7.  [Collect a sequence of characters](#46.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are [ASCII digits](#46.html_ascii-digits). If the collected sequence is not exactly two characters long, then fail. Otherwise, interpret the resulting sequence as a base-ten integer. Let that number be the `week`.

8.  Let `maxweek` be the [week number of the last day](#46.html_week-number-of-the-last-day) of year `year`.

9.  If `week` is not a number in the range 1 ≤ `week` ≤ `maxweek`, then fail.

10.  If `position` is *not* beyond the end of `input`, then fail.

11.  Return the week-year number `year` and the week number `week`.

##### 2.4.5.9 Durations

A <dfn id="46.html_concept-duration" data-anolis-xref="concept-duration">duration</dfn> consists of a number of seconds.

Since months and seconds are not comparable (a month is not a precise number of seconds, but is instead a period whose exact length depends on the precise day from which it is measured) a [duration](#46.html_concept-duration) as defined in this specification cannot include months (or years, which are equivalent to twelve months). Only durations that describe a specific number of seconds can be described.

A string is a <dfn id="46.html_valid-duration-string">valid duration string</dfn> representing a [duration](#46.html_concept-duration) `t` if it consists of either of the following:

*   A literal U+0050 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER P character followed by one or more of the following subcomponents, in the order given, where the number of days, hours, minutes, and seconds corresponds to the same number of seconds as in `t`:

    1.  One or more [ASCII digits](#46.html_ascii-digits) followed by a U+0044 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER D character, representing a number of days.

    2.  A U+0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T character followed by one or more of the following subcomponents, in the order given:

        1.  One or more [ASCII digits](#46.html_ascii-digits) followed by a U+0048 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER H character, representing a number of hours.

        2.  One or more [ASCII digits](#46.html_ascii-digits) followed by a U+004D LATIN CAPITAL LETTER M character, representing a number of minutes.

        3.  The following components:

            1.  One or more [ASCII digits](#46.html_ascii-digits), representing a number of seconds.

            2.  Optionally, a "." (U+002E) character followed by one, two, or three [ASCII digits](#46.html_ascii-digits), representing a fraction of a second.

            3.  A U+0053 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S character.

    This, as with a number of other date- and time-related microsyntaxes defined in this specification, is based on one of the formats defined in ISO 8601\. [[ISO8601]](#46.html_refsISO8601)

*   One or more [duration time components](#46.html_duration-time-component), each with a different [duration time component scale](#46.html_duration-time-component-scale), in any order; the sum of the represented seconds being equal to the number of seconds in `t`.

    A <dfn id="46.html_duration-time-component">duration time component</dfn> is a string consisting of the following components:

    1.  Zero or more [space characters](#46.html_space-character).

    2.  One or more [ASCII digits](#46.html_ascii-digits), representing a number of time units, scaled by the [duration time component scale](#46.html_duration-time-component-scale) specified (see below) to represent a number of seconds.

    3.  If the [duration time component scale](#46.html_duration-time-component-scale) specified is 1 (i.e. the units are seconds), then, optionally, a "." (U+002E) character followed by one, two, or three [ASCII digits](#46.html_ascii-digits), representing a fraction of a second.

    4.  Zero or more [space characters](#46.html_space-character).

    5.  One of the following characters, representing the <dfn id="46.html_duration-time-component-scale">duration time component scale</dfn> of the time unit used in the numeric part of the [duration time component](#46.html_duration-time-component):

        U+0057 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER W character
        U+0077 LATIN SMALL LETTER W character

        Weeks. The scale is 604800.

        U+0044 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER D character
        U+0064 LATIN SMALL LETTER D character

        Days. The scale is 86400.

        U+0048 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER H character
        U+0068 LATIN SMALL LETTER H character

        Hours. The scale is 3600.

        U+004D LATIN CAPITAL LETTER M character
        U+006D LATIN SMALL LETTER M character

        Minutes. The scale is 60.

        U+0053 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S character
        U+0073 LATIN SMALL LETTER S character

        Seconds. The scale is 1.

    6.  Zero or more [space characters](#46.html_space-character).

    This is not based on any of the formats in ISO 8601\. It is intended to be a more human-readable alternative to the ISO 8601 duration format.

The rules to <dfn id="46.html_parse-a-duration-string">parse a duration string</dfn> are as follows. This will return either a [duration](#46.html_concept-duration) or nothing. If at any point the algorithm says that it "fails", this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing.

1.  Let `input` be the string being parsed.

2.  Let `position` be a pointer into `input`, initially pointing at the start of the string.

3.  Let `months`, `seconds`, and `component count` all be zero.

4.  Let `M-disambiguator` be *minutes*.

    This flag's other value is *months*. It is used to disambiguate the "M" unit in ISO8601 durations, which use the same unit for months and minutes. Months are not allowed, but are parsed for future compatibility and to avoid misinterpreting ISO8601 durations that would be valid in other contexts.

5.  [Skip whitespace](#46.html_skip-whitespace).

6.  If `position` is past the end of `input`, then fail.

7.  If the character in `input` pointed to by `position` is a U+0050 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER P character, then advance `position` to the next character, set `M-disambiguator` to *months*, and [skip whitespace](#46.html_skip-whitespace).

8.  Run the following substeps in a loop, until a step requiring the loop to be broken or the entire algorithm to fail is reached:

    1.  Let `units` be undefined. It will be assigned one of the following values: *years*, *months*, *weeks*, *days*, *hours*, *minutes*, and *seconds*.

    2.  Let `next character` be undefined. It is used to process characters from the `input`.

    3.  If `position` is past the end of `input`, then break the loop.

    4.  If the character in `input` pointed to by `position` is a U+0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T character, then advance `position` to the next character, set `M-disambiguator` to *minutes*, [skip whitespace](#46.html_skip-whitespace), and return to the top of the loop.

    5.  Set `next character` to the character in `input` pointed to by `position`.

    6.  If `next character` is a "." (U+002E) character, then let `N` equal zero. (Do not advance `position`. That is taken care of below.)

        Otherwise, if `next character` is an [ASCII digit](#46.html_ascii-digits), then [collect a sequence of characters](#46.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are [ASCII digits](#46.html_ascii-digits), interpret the resulting sequence as a base-ten integer, and let `N` be that number.

        Otherwise `next character` is not part of a number; fail.

    7.  If `position` is past the end of `input`, then fail.

    8.  Set `next character` to the character in `input` pointed to by `position`, and this time advance `position` to the next character. (If `next character` was a U+002E FULL STOP character (.) before, it will still be that character this time.)

    9.  If `next character` is a "." (U+002E) character, then run these substeps:

        1.  [Collect a sequence of characters](#46.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are [ASCII digits](#46.html_ascii-digits). Let `s` be the resulting sequence.

        2.  If `s` is the empty string, then fail.

        3.  Let `length` be the number of characters in `s`.

        4.  Let `fraction` be the result of interpreting `s` as a base-ten integer, and then dividing that number by 10^(`length`).

        5.  Increment `N` by `fraction`.

        6.  [Skip whitespace](#46.html_skip-whitespace).

        7.  If `position` is past the end of `input`, then fail.

        8.  Set `next character` to the character in `input` pointed to by `position`, and advance `position` to the next character.

        9.  If `next character` is neither a U+0053 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S character nor a U+0073 LATIN SMALL LETTER S character, then fail.

        10.  Set `units` to *seconds*.

        Otherwise, run these substeps:

        1.  If `next character` is a [space character](#46.html_space-character), then [skip whitespace](#46.html_skip-whitespace), set `next character` to the character in `input` pointed to by `position`, and advance `position` to the next character.

        2.  If `next character` is a U+0059 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Y character, or a U+0079 LATIN SMALL LETTER Y character, set `units` to *years* and set `M-disambiguator` to *months*.

            If `next character` is a U+004D LATIN CAPITAL LETTER M character or a U+006D LATIN SMALL LETTER M character, and `M-disambiguator` is *months*, then set `units` to *months*.

            If `next character` is a U+0057 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER W character or a U+0077 LATIN SMALL LETTER W character, set `units` to *weeks* and set `M-disambiguator` to *minutes*.

            If `next character` is a U+0044 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER D character or a U+0064 LATIN SMALL LETTER D character, set `units` to *days* and set `M-disambiguator` to *minutes*.

            If `next character` is a U+0048 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER H character or a U+0068 LATIN SMALL LETTER H character, set `units` to *hours* and set `M-disambiguator` to *minutes*.

            If `next character` is a U+004D LATIN CAPITAL LETTER M character or a U+006D LATIN SMALL LETTER M character, and `M-disambiguator` is *minutes*, then set `units` to *minutes*.

            If `next character` is a U+0053 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S character or a U+0073 LATIN SMALL LETTER S character, set `units` to *seconds* and set `M-disambiguator` to *minutes*.

            Otherwise if `next character` is none of the above characters, then fail.

    10.  Increment `component count`.

    11.  Let `multiplier` be 1.

    12.  If `units` is *years*, multiply `multiplier` by 12 and set `units` to *months*.

    13.  If `units` is *months*, add the product of `N` and `multiplier` to `months`.

        Otherwise, run these substeps:

        1.  If `units` is *weeks*, multiply `multiplier` by 7 and set `units` to *days*.

        2.  If `units` is *days*, multiply `multiplier` by 24 and set `units` to *hours*.

        3.  If `units` is *hours*, multiply `multiplier` by 60 and set `units` to *minutes*.

        4.  If `units` is *minutes*, multiply `multiplier` by 60 and set `units` to *seconds*.

        5.  Forcibly, `units` is now *seconds*. Add the product of `N` and `multiplier` to `seconds`.

    14.  [Skip whitespace](#46.html_skip-whitespace).

9.  If `component count` is zero, fail.

10.  If `months` is not zero, fail.

11.  Return the [duration](#46.html_concept-duration) consisting of `seconds` seconds.

##### 2.4.5.10 Vaguer moments in time

A string is a <dfn id="46.html_valid-date-string-with-optional-time">valid date string with optional time</dfn> if it is also one of the following:

*   A [valid date string](#46.html_valid-date-string)
*   A [valid global date and time string](#46.html_valid-global-date-and-time-string)

* * *

The rules to <dfn id="46.html_parse-a-date-or-time-string">parse a date or time string</dfn> are as follows. The algorithm will return either a [date](#46.html_concept-date), a [time](#46.html_concept-time), a [global date and time](#46.html_concept-datetime), or nothing. If at any point the algorithm says that it "fails", this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing.

1.  Let `input` be the string being parsed.

2.  Let `position` be a pointer into `input`, initially pointing at the start of the string.

3.  Set `start position` to the same position as `position`.

4.  Set the `date present` and `time present` flags to true.

5.  [Parse a date component](#46.html_parse-a-date-component) to obtain `year`, `month`, and `day`. If this fails, then set the `date present` flag to false.

6.  If `date present` is true, and `position` is not beyond the end of `input`, and the character at `position` is either a "T" (U+0054) character or a U+0020 SPACE character, then advance `position` to the next character in `input`.

    Otherwise, if `date present` is true, and either `position` is beyond the end of `input` or the character at `position` is neither a "T" (U+0054) character nor a U+0020 SPACE character, then set `time present` to false.

    Otherwise, if `date present` is false, set `position` back to the same position as `start position`.

7.  If the `time present` flag is true, then [parse a time component](#46.html_parse-a-time-component) to obtain `hour`, `minute`, and `second`. If this returns nothing, then fail.

8.  If the `date present` and `time present` flags are both true, but `position` is beyond the end of `input`, then fail.

9.  If the `date present` and `time present` flags are both true, [parse a time-zone offset component](#46.html_parse-a-time-zone-offset-component) to obtain `timezone`[`hours`] and `timezone`[`minutes`]. If this returns nothing, then fail.

10.  If `position` is *not* beyond the end of `input`, then fail.

11.  If the `date present` flag is true and the `time present` flag is false, then let `date` be the date with year `year`, month `month`, and day `day`, and return `date`.

    Otherwise, if the `time present` flag is true and the `date present` flag is false, then let `time` be the time with hour `hour`, minute `minute`, and second `second`, and return `time`.

    Otherwise, let `time` be the moment in time at year `year`, month `month`, day `day`, hours `hour`, minute `minute`, second `second`, subtracting `timezone`[`hours`] hours and `timezone`[`minutes`] minutes, that moment in time being a moment in the UTC time zone; let `timezone` be `timezone`[`hours`] hours and `timezone`[`minutes`] minutes from UTC; and return `time` and `timezone`.

#### 2.4.6 Colors

A <dfn id="47.html_simple-color">simple color</dfn> consists of three 8-bit numbers in the range 0..255, representing the red, green, and blue components of the color respectively, in the sRGB color space. [[SRGB]](#47.html_refsSRGB)

A string is a <dfn id="47.html_valid-simple-color">valid simple color</dfn> if it is exactly seven characters long, and the first character is a "#" (U+0023) character, and the remaining six characters are all [ASCII hex digits](#47.html_ascii-hex-digits), with the first two digits representing the red component, the middle two digits representing the green component, and the last two digits representing the blue component, in hexadecimal.

A string is a <dfn id="47.html_valid-lowercase-simple-color">valid lowercase simple color</dfn> if it is a [valid simple color](#47.html_valid-simple-color) and doesn't use any characters in the range U+0041 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A to U+0046 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER F.

The <dfn id="47.html_rules-for-parsing-simple-color-values">rules for parsing simple color values</dfn> are as given in the following algorithm. When invoked, the steps must be followed in the order given, aborting at the first step that returns a value. This algorithm will return either a [simple color](#47.html_simple-color) or an error.

1.  Let `input` be the string being parsed.

2.  If `input` is not exactly seven characters long, then return an error.

3.  If the first character in `input` is not a U+0023 NUMBER SIGN character (#), then return an error.

4.  If the last six characters of `input` are not all [ASCII hex digits](#47.html_ascii-hex-digits), then return an error.

5.  Let `result` be a [simple color](#47.html_simple-color).

6.  Interpret the second and third characters as a hexadecimal number and let the result be the red component of `result`.

7.  Interpret the fourth and fifth characters as a hexadecimal number and let the result be the green component of `result`.

8.  Interpret the sixth and seventh characters as a hexadecimal number and let the result be the blue component of `result`.

9.  Return `result`.

The <dfn id="47.html_rules-for-serializing-simple-color-values">rules for serializing simple color values</dfn> given a [simple color](#47.html_simple-color) are as given in the following algorithm:

1.  Let `result` be a string consisting of a single "#" (U+0023) character.

2.  Convert the red, green, and blue components in turn to two-digit hexadecimal numbers using [lowercase ASCII hex digits](#47.html_lowercase-ascii-hex-digits), zero-padding if necessary, and append these numbers to `result`, in the order red, green, blue.

3.  Return `result`, which will be a [valid lowercase simple color](#47.html_valid-lowercase-simple-color).

* * *

Some obsolete legacy attributes parse colors in a more complicated manner, using the <dfn id="47.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value">rules for parsing a legacy color value</dfn>, which are given in the following algorithm. When invoked, the steps must be followed in the order given, aborting at the first step that returns a value. This algorithm will return either a [simple color](#47.html_simple-color) or an error.

1.  Let `input` be the string being parsed.

2.  If `input` is the empty string, then return an error.

3.  [Strip leading and trailing whitespace](#47.html_strip-leading-and-trailing-whitespace) from `input`.

4.  If `input` is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#47.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`transparent`", then return an error.

5.  If `input` is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#47.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for one of the keywords listed in the [SVG color keywords](http://www.w3.org/TR/css3-color/#svg-color) section of the CSS3 Color specification, then return the [simple color](#47.html_simple-color) corresponding to that keyword. [[CSSCOLOR]](#47.html_refsCSSCOLOR)

    [CSS2 System Colors](http://www.w3.org/TR/css3-color/#css2-system) are not recognised.

6.  If `input` is four characters long, and the first character in `input` is a "#" (U+0023) character, and the last three characters of `input` are all [ASCII hex digits](#47.html_ascii-hex-digits), then run these substeps:

    1.  Let `result` be a [simple color](#47.html_simple-color).

    2.  Interpret the second character of `input` as a hexadecimal digit; let the red component of `result` be the resulting number multiplied by 17.

    3.  Interpret the third character of `input` as a hexadecimal digit; let the green component of `result` be the resulting number multiplied by 17.

    4.  Interpret the fourth character of `input` as a hexadecimal digit; let the blue component of `result` be the resulting number multiplied by 17.

    5.  Return `result`.

7.  Replace any characters in `input` that have a Unicode code point greater than U+FFFF (i.e. any characters that are not in the basic multilingual plane) with the two-character string "`00`".

8.  If `input` is longer than 128 characters, truncate `input`, leaving only the first 128 characters.

9.  If the first character in `input` is a "#" (U+0023) character, remove it.

10.  Replace any character in `input` that is not an [ASCII hex digit](#47.html_ascii-hex-digits) with the character "0" (U+0030).

11.  While `input`'s length is zero or not a multiple of three, append a "0" (U+0030) character to `input`.

12.  Split `input` into three strings of equal length, to obtain three components. Let `length` be the length of those components (one third the length of `input`).

13.  If `length` is greater than 8, then remove the leading `length`-8 characters in each component, and let `length` be 8.

14.  While `length` is greater than two and the first character in each component is a "0" (U+0030) character, remove that character and reduce `length` by one.

15.  If `length` is *still* greater than two, truncate each component, leaving only the first two characters in each.

16.  Let `result` be a [simple color](#47.html_simple-color).

17.  Interpret the first component as a hexadecimal number; let the red component of `result` be the resulting number.

18.  Interpret the second component as a hexadecimal number; let the green component of `result` be the resulting number.

19.  Interpret the third component as a hexadecimal number; let the blue component of `result` be the resulting number.

20.  Return `result`.

* * *

#### 2.4.7 Space-separated tokens

A <dfn id="48.html_set-of-space-separated-tokens">set of space-separated tokens</dfn> is a string containing zero or more words (known as tokens) separated by one or more [space characters](#48.html_space-character), where words consist of any string of one or more characters, none of which are [space characters](#48.html_space-character).

A string containing a [set of space-separated tokens](#48.html_set-of-space-separated-tokens) may have leading or trailing [space characters](#48.html_space-character).

An <dfn id="48.html_unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens">unordered set of unique space-separated tokens</dfn> is a [set of space-separated tokens](#48.html_set-of-space-separated-tokens) where none of the tokens are duplicated.

An <dfn id="48.html_ordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens">ordered set of unique space-separated tokens</dfn> is a [set of space-separated tokens](#48.html_set-of-space-separated-tokens) where none of the tokens are duplicated but where the order of the tokens is meaningful.

[Sets of space-separated tokens](#48.html_set-of-space-separated-tokens) sometimes have a defined set of allowed values. When a set of allowed values is defined, the tokens must all be from that list of allowed values; other values are non-conforming. If no such set of allowed values is provided, then all values are conforming.

How tokens in a [set of space-separated tokens](#48.html_set-of-space-separated-tokens) are to be compared (e.g. case-sensitively or not) is defined on a per-set basis.

When a user agent has to <dfn id="48.html_split-a-string-on-spaces">split a string on spaces</dfn>, it must use the following algorithm:

1.  Let `input` be the string being parsed.

2.  Let `position` be a pointer into `input`, initially pointing at the start of the string.

3.  Let `tokens` be an ordered list of tokens, initially empty.

4.  [Skip whitespace](#48.html_skip-whitespace)

5.  While `position` is not past the end of `input`:

    1.  [Collect a sequence of characters](#48.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are not [space characters](#48.html_space-character).

    2.  Append the string collected in the previous step to `tokens`.

    3.  [Skip whitespace](#48.html_skip-whitespace)

6.  Return `tokens`.

#### 2.4.8 Comma-separated tokens

A <dfn id="49.html_set-of-comma-separated-tokens">set of comma-separated tokens</dfn> is a string containing zero or more tokens each separated from the next by a single "," (U+002C) character, where tokens consist of any string of zero or more characters, neither beginning nor ending with [space characters](#49.html_space-character), nor containing any "," (U+002C) characters, and optionally surrounded by [space characters](#49.html_space-character).

For instance, the string "` a ,b,,d d `" consists of four tokens: "a", "b", the empty string, and "d d". Leading and trailing whitespace around each token doesn't count as part of the token, and the empty string can be a token.

[Sets of comma-separated tokens](#49.html_set-of-comma-separated-tokens) sometimes have further restrictions on what consists a valid token. When such restrictions are defined, the tokens must all fit within those restrictions; other values are non-conforming. If no such restrictions are specified, then all values are conforming.

When a user agent has to <dfn id="49.html_split-a-string-on-commas">split a string on commas</dfn>, it must use the following algorithm:

1.  Let `input` be the string being parsed.

2.  Let `position` be a pointer into `input`, initially pointing at the start of the string.

3.  Let `tokens` be an ordered list of tokens, initially empty.

4.  *Token*: If `position` is past the end of `input`, jump to the last step.

5.  [Collect a sequence of characters](#49.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are not "," (U+002C) characters. Let `s` be the resulting sequence (which might be the empty string).

6.  [Strip leading and trailing whitespace](#49.html_strip-leading-and-trailing-whitespace) from `s`.

7.  Append `s` to `tokens`.

8.  If `position` is not past the end of `input`, then the character at `position` is a "," (U+002C) character; advance `position` past that character.

9.  Jump back to the step labeled *token*.

10.  Return `tokens`.

#### 2.4.9 References

A <dfn id="50.html_valid-hash-name-reference">valid hash-name reference</dfn> to an element of type `type` is a string consisting of a "#" (U+0023) character followed by a string which exactly matches the value of the `name` attribute of an element with type `type` in the document.

The <dfn id="50.html_rules-for-parsing-a-hash-name-reference">rules for parsing a hash-name reference</dfn> to an element of type `type` are as follows:

1.  If the string being parsed does not contain a U+0023 NUMBER SIGN character, or if the first such character in the string is the last character in the string, then return null and abort these steps.

2.  Let `s` be the string from the character immediately after the first U+0023 NUMBER SIGN character in the string being parsed up to the end of that string.

3.  Return the first element of type `type` that has an [`id`](#50.html_the-id-attribute) attribute whose value is a [case-sensitive](#50.html_case-sensitive) match for `s` or a `name` attribute whose value is a [compatibility caseless](#50.html_compatibility-caseless) match for `s`.

#### 2.4.10 Media queries

A string is a <dfn id="51.html_valid-media-query">valid media query</dfn> if it matches the `media_query_list` production of the Media Queries specification. [[MQ]](#51.html_refsMQ)

A string <dfn id="51.html_matches-the-environment">matches the environment</dfn> of the user if it is the empty string, a string consisting of only [space characters](#51.html_space-character), or is a media query that matches the user's environment according to the definitions given in the Media Queries specification. [[MQ]](#51.html_refsMQ)

### 2.5 URLs

#### 2.5.1 Terminology

A URL is a <dfn id="53.html_valid-url">valid URL</dfn> if it conforms to the authoring conformance requirements in the URL standard. [[URL]](#53.html_refsURL)

A string is a <dfn id="53.html_valid-non-empty-url">valid non-empty URL</dfn> if it is a [valid URL](#53.html_valid-url) but it is not the empty string.

A string is a <dfn id="53.html_valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces">valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces</dfn> if, after [stripping leading and trailing whitespace](#53.html_strip-leading-and-trailing-whitespace) from it, it is a [valid URL](#53.html_valid-url).

A string is a <dfn id="53.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces">valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces</dfn> if, after [stripping leading and trailing whitespace](#53.html_strip-leading-and-trailing-whitespace) from it, it is a [valid non-empty URL](#53.html_valid-non-empty-url).

This specification defines the URL <dfn id="53.html_about:legacy-compat">`about:legacy-compat`</dfn> as a reserved, though unresolvable, `about:` URL, for use in [DOCTYPE](#53.html_syntax-doctype)s in [HTML documents](#53.html_html-documents) when needed for compatibility with XML tools. [[ABOUT]](#53.html_refsABOUT)

This specification defines the URL <dfn id="53.html_about:srcdoc">`about:srcdoc`</dfn> as a reserved, though unresolvable, `about:` URL, that is used as [the document's address](#53.html_the-document's-address) of [`iframe` `srcdoc` documents](#53.html_an-iframe-srcdoc-document). [[ABOUT]](#53.html_refsABOUT)

The <dfn id="53.html_fallback-base-url">fallback base URL</dfn> of a [`Document`](#53.html_document) object is the [absolute URL](#53.html_absolute-url) obtained by running these substeps:

1.  If the [`Document`](#53.html_document) is [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#53.html_an-iframe-srcdoc-document), then return the [document base URL](#53.html_document-base-url) of the [`Document`](#53.html_document)'s [browsing context](#53.html_browsing-context)'s [browsing context container](#53.html_browsing-context-container)'s [`Document`](#53.html_document) and abort these steps.

2.  If [the document's address](#53.html_the-document's-address) is [`about:blank`](#53.html_about:blank), and the [`Document`](#53.html_document)'s [browsing context](#53.html_browsing-context) has a [creator browsing context](#53.html_creator-browsing-context), then return the [document base URL](#53.html_document-base-url) of the [creator `Document`](#53.html_creator-document), and abort these steps.

3.  Return [the document's address](#53.html_the-document's-address).

The <dfn id="53.html_document-base-url">document base URL</dfn> of a [`Document`](#53.html_document) object is the [absolute URL](#53.html_absolute-url) obtained by running these substeps:

1.  If there is no [`base`](#53.html_the-base-element) element that has an [`href`](#53.html_attr-base-href) attribute in the [`Document`](#53.html_document), then the [document base URL](#53.html_document-base-url) is the [`Document`](#53.html_document)'s [fallback base URL](#53.html_fallback-base-url); abort these steps.

2.  Otherwise, the [document base URL](#53.html_document-base-url) is the [frozen base URL](#53.html_frozen-base-url) of the first [`base`](#53.html_the-base-element) element in the [`Document`](#53.html_document) that has an [`href`](#53.html_attr-base-href) attribute, in [tree order](#53.html_tree-order).

#### 2.5.2 Resolving URLs

Resolving a URL is the process of taking a [relative URL](#54.html_relative-url) and obtaining the [absolute URL](#54.html_absolute-url) that it implies.

To <dfn id="54.html_resolve-a-url">resolve a URL</dfn> to an [absolute URL](#54.html_absolute-url) relative to either another [absolute URL](#54.html_absolute-url) or an element, the user agent must use the following steps. Resolving a URL can result in an error, in which case the URL is not resolvable.

1.  Let `url` be the URL being resolved.

2.  Let `encoding` be determined as follows:

    If the URL had a character encoding defined when the URL was created or defined or when this algorithm was invoked

    The URL character encoding is as defined.

    If the URL came from a script (e.g. as an argument to a method)

    The URL character encoding is the [API URL character encoding](#54.html_api-url-character-encoding) specified by the script's [settings object](#54.html_settings-object).

    If the URL came from a DOM node (e.g. from an element)

    The node has a [`Document`](#54.html_document), and the URL character encoding is the [document's character encoding](#54.html_document's-character-encoding).

3.  If `encoding` is [a UTF-16 encoding](#54.html_a-utf-16-encoding), then change the value of `encoding` to UTF-8.

4.  If the algorithm was invoked with an [absolute URL](#54.html_absolute-url) to use as the base URL, let `base` be that [absolute URL](#54.html_absolute-url).

    Otherwise, let `base` be [the element's base URL](#54.html_the-element's-base-url).

5.  Apply the [URL parser](#54.html_url-parser-0) to `url`, with `base` as the base URL, with `encoding` as the encoding.

6.  If this returns failure, then abort these steps with an error.

7.  Let `parsed URL` be the result of the [URL parser](#54.html_url-parser-0).

8.  Let `serialized URL` be the result of apply the [URL serializer](#54.html_concept-url-serializer) to `parsed URL`.

9.  Return `serialized URL` as the <dfn id="54.html_resulting-absolute-url">resulting absolute URL</dfn> and `parsed URL` as the <dfn id="54.html_resulting-parsed-url">resulting parsed URL</dfn>.

Given an element, <dfn id="54.html_the-element's-base-url">the element's base URL</dfn> is the *base URI of the element*, as defined by the XML Base specification, with *the base URI of the document entity* being defined as the [document base URL](#54.html_document-base-url) of the [`Document`](#54.html_document) that owns the element. [[XMLBASE]](#54.html_refsXMLBASE)

For the purposes of the XML Base specification, user agents must act as if all [`Document`](#54.html_document) objects represented XML documents.

It is possible for [`xml:base`](#54.html_the-xml:base-attribute-(xml-only)) attributes to be present even in HTML fragments, as such attributes can be added dynamically using script. (Such scripts would not be conforming, however, as [`xml:base`](#54.html_the-xml:base-attribute-(xml-only)) attributes are not allowed in [HTML documents](#54.html_html-documents).)

#### 2.5.3 Dynamic changes to base URLs

When an [`xml:base`](#55.html_the-xml:base-attribute-(xml-only)) attribute is set, changed, or removed, the attribute's element, and all descendant elements, are [affected by a base URL change](#55.html_affected-by-a-base-url-change).

When a document's [document base URL](#55.html_document-base-url) changes, all elements in that document are [affected by a base URL change](#55.html_affected-by-a-base-url-change).

The following are [base URL change steps](#55.html_base-url-change-steps), which run when an element is [affected by a base URL change](#55.html_affected-by-a-base-url-change) (as defined by the DOM specification):

If the element creates a [hyperlink](#55.html_hyperlink)

If the [absolute URL](#55.html_absolute-url) identified by the hyperlink is being shown to the user, or if any data derived from that URL is affecting the display, then the [`href`](#55.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute should be [re-resolved](#55.html_resolve-a-url) relative to the element and the UI updated appropriately.

For example, the CSS [`:link`](#55.html_selector-link)/[`:visited`](#55.html_selector-visited) pseudo-classes might have been affected.

If the element is a [`q`](#55.html_the-q-element), [`blockquote`](#55.html_the-blockquote-element), [`ins`](#55.html_the-ins-element), or [`del`](#55.html_the-del-element) element with a `cite` attribute

If the [absolute URL](#55.html_absolute-url) identified by the `cite` attribute is being shown to the user, or if any data derived from that URL is affecting the display, then the URL should be [re-resolved](#55.html_resolve-a-url) relative to the element and the UI updated appropriately.

Otherwise

The element is not directly affected.

For instance, changing the base URL doesn't affect the image displayed by [`img`](#55.html_the-img-element) elements, although subsequent accesses of the [`src`](#55.html_dom-img-src) IDL attribute from script will return a new [absolute URL](#55.html_absolute-url) that might no longer correspond to the image being shown.

### 2.6 Fetching resources

#### 2.6.1 Terminology

User agents can implement a variety of transfer protocols, but this specification mostly defines behavior in terms of HTTP. [[HTTP]](#57.html_refsHTTP)

The <dfn id="57.html_concept-http-equivalent-get" data-anolis-xref="concept-http-equivalent-get">HTTP GET method</dfn> is equivalent to the default retrieval action of the protocol. For example, RETR in FTP. Such actions are idempotent and safe, in HTTP terms.

The <dfn id="57.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes" data-anolis-xref="concept-http-equivalent-codes">HTTP response codes</dfn> are equivalent to statuses in other protocols that have the same basic meanings. For example, a "file not found" error is equivalent to a 404 code, a server error is equivalent to a 5xx code, and so on.

The <dfn id="57.html_concept-http-equivalent-headers" data-anolis-xref="concept-http-equivalent-headers">HTTP headers</dfn> are equivalent to fields in other protocols that have the same basic meaning. For example, the HTTP authentication headers are equivalent to the authentication aspects of the FTP protocol.

A <dfn id="57.html_referrer-source">referrer source</dfn> is either a [`Document`](#57.html_document) or a URL.

#### 2.6.2 Processing model

When a user agent is to <dfn id="58.html_fetch">fetch</dfn> a resource or URL, optionally **from** an origin *origin*, optionally **using** a specific [referrer source](#58.html_referrer-source) as an *override referrer source*, and optionally with any of a *synchronous flag*, a *manual redirect flag*, a *force same-origin flag*, and a *block cookies flag*, the following steps must be run. (When a *URL* is to be fetched, the URL identifies a resource to be obtained.)

1.  If there is a specific *override referrer source*, and it is a URL, then let `referrer` be the *override referrer source*, and jump to the step labeled *clean referrer*.

2.  Let `document` be the appropriate [`Document`](#58.html_document) as given by the following list:

    If there is a specific *override referrer source*

    The *override referrer source*.

    When [navigating](#58.html_navigate)

    The [active document](#58.html_active-document) of the [source browsing context](#58.html_source-browsing-context).

    When fetching resources for an element

    The element's [`Document`](#58.html_document).

3.  While `document` is [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#58.html_an-iframe-srcdoc-document), let `document` be `document`'s [browsing context](#58.html_browsing-context)'s [browsing context container](#58.html_browsing-context-container)'s [`Document`](#58.html_document) instead.

4.  If the [origin](#58.html_origin-0) of `Document` is not a scheme/host/port tuple, then set `referrer` to the empty string and jump to the step labeled *clean referrer*.

5.  Let `referrer` be [the document's address](#58.html_the-document's-address) of `document`.

6.  *Clean referrer*: Apply the [URL parser](#58.html_url-parser-0) to `referrer` and let `parsed referrer` be the [resulting parsed URL](#58.html_resulting-parsed-url).

7.  Let `referrer` be the result of applying the [URL serializer](#58.html_concept-url-serializer) to `parsed referrer`, with the *exclude fragment flag* set.

8.  If `referrer` is not the empty string, is not a [`data:` URL](#58.html_data-protocol), and is not the URL "[`about:blank`](#58.html_about:blank)", then generate the *address of the resource from which Request-URIs are obtained* as required by HTTP for the `Referer` (sic) header from `referrer`. [[HTTP]](#58.html_refsHTTP)

    Otherwise, the `Referer` (sic) header must be omitted, regardless of its value.

9.  If the algorithm was not invoked with the *synchronous flag*, perform the remaining steps asynchronously.

10.  If the [`Document`](#58.html_document) with which any [tasks](#58.html_concept-task) [queued](#58.html_queue-a-task) by this algorithm would be associated doesn't have an associated [browsing context](#58.html_browsing-context), then abort these steps.

11.  This is the *main step*.

    If the resource is to be obtained from an [application cache](#58.html_application-cache), then use the data from that [application cache](#58.html_application-cache), as if it had been obtained in the manner appropriate given its URL.

    If the resource is identified by an [absolute URL](#58.html_absolute-url), and the resource is to be obtained using an idempotent action (such as an HTTP GET [or equivalent](#58.html_concept-http-equivalent-get)), and it is already being downloaded for other reasons (e.g. another invocation of this algorithm), and this request would be identical to the previous one (e.g. same `Accept` and `Origin` headers), and the user agent is configured such that it is to reuse the data from the existing download instead of initiating a new one, then use the results of the existing download instead of starting a new one.

    Otherwise, if the resource is identified by an [absolute URL](#58.html_absolute-url) with a scheme that does not define a mechanism to obtain the resource (e.g. it is a `mailto:` URL) or that the user agent does not support, then act as if the resource was an HTTP 204 No Content response with no other metadata.

    Otherwise, if the resource is identified by the URL <dfn id="58.html_about:blank">`about:blank`</dfn>, then the resource is immediately available and consists of the empty string, with no metadata.

    Otherwise, at a time convenient to the user and the user agent, download (or otherwise obtain) the resource, applying the semantics of the relevant specifications (e.g. performing an HTTP GET or POST operation, or reading the file from disk, or expanding [`data:` URLs](#58.html_data-protocol), etc).

    For the purposes of the `Referer` (sic) header, use the *address of the resource from which Request-URIs are obtained* generated in the earlier step.

    For the purposes of the `Origin` header, if the [fetching algorithm](#58.html_fetch) was explicitly initiated from an *origin*, then *the origin that initiated the HTTP request* is *origin*. Otherwise, this is *a request from a "privacy-sensitive" context*. [[ORIGIN]](#58.html_refsORIGIN)

12.  If the algorithm was not invoked with the *block cookies flag*, and there are cookies to be set, then the user agent must run the following substeps:

    1.  Wait until ownership of the [storage mutex](#58.html_storage-mutex) can be taken by this instance of the [fetching](#58.html_fetch) algorithm.

    2.  Take ownership of the [storage mutex](#58.html_storage-mutex).

    3.  Update the cookies. [[COOKIES]](#58.html_refsCOOKIES) [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/1f728a53673beb31aff6f0d3ad29dcc8.jpg)](#58.html_fingerprinting-vector)

    4.  Release the [storage mutex](#58.html_storage-mutex) so that it is once again free.

13.  If the fetched resource is an HTTP redirect [or equivalent](#58.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes), then:

    If the *force same-origin flag* is set and the URL of the target of the redirect does not have the [same origin](#58.html_same-origin) as the URL for which the [fetch](#58.html_fetch) algorithm was invoked

    Abort these steps and return failure from this algorithm, as if the remote host could not be contacted.

    If the *manual redirect flag* is set

    Continue, using the fetched resource (the redirect) as the result of the algorithm. If the calling algorithm subsequently requires the user agent to <dfn id="58.html_transparently-follow-the-redirect">transparently follow the redirect</dfn>, then the user agent must resume this algorithm from the *main step*, but using the target of the redirect as the resource to fetch, rather than the original resource.

    Otherwise

    First, apply any relevant requirements for redirects (such as showing any appropriate prompts). Then, redo *main step*, but using the target of the redirect as the resource to fetch, rather than the original resource. For HTTP requests, the new request must include the same headers as the original request, except for headers for which other requirements are specified (such as the `Host` header). [[HTTP]](#58.html_refsHTTP)

    The HTTP specification requires that 301, 302, and 307 redirects, when applied to methods other than the safe methods, not be followed without user confirmation. That would be an appropriate prompt for the purposes of the requirement in the paragraph above. [[HTTP]](#58.html_refsHTTP)

14.  If the algorithm was not invoked with the *synchronous flag*: When the resource is available, or if there is an error of some description, [queue a task](#58.html_queue-a-task) that uses the resource as appropriate. If the resource can be processed incrementally, as, for instance, with a progressively interlaced JPEG or an HTML file, additional tasks may be queued to process the data as it is downloaded. The [task source](#58.html_task-source) for these [tasks](#58.html_concept-task) is the [networking task source](#58.html_networking-task-source).

    Otherwise, return the resource or error information to the calling algorithm.

If the user agent can determine the actual length of the resource being [fetched](#58.html_fetch) for an instance of this algorithm, and if that length is finite, then that length is the file's <dfn id="58.html_concept-fetch-total" data-anolis-xref="concept-fetch-total">size</dfn>. Otherwise, the subject of the algorithm (that is, the resource being fetched) has no known [size](#58.html_concept-fetch-total). (For example, the HTTP `Content-Length` header might provide this information.)

The user agent must also keep track of the <dfn id="58.html_concept-fetch-loaded" data-anolis-xref="concept-fetch-loaded">number of bytes downloaded</dfn> for each instance of this algorithm. This number must exclude any out-of-band metadata, such as HTTP headers.

The [application cache](#58.html_application-cache) processing model introduces some [changes to the networking model](#58.html_changesToNetworkingModel) to handle the returning of cached resources.

The [navigation](#58.html_navigate) processing model handles redirects itself, overriding the redirection handling that would be done by the fetching algorithm.

Whether the [type sniffing rules](#58.html_content-type-sniffing) apply to the fetched resource depends on the algorithm that invokes the rules — they are not always applicable.

#### 2.6.3 Encrypted HTTP and related security concerns

Anything in this specification that refers to HTTP also applies to HTTP-over-TLS, as represented by URLs representing the `https` scheme. [[HTTP]](#59.html_refsHTTP)

User agents should report certificate errors to the user and must either refuse to download resources sent with erroneous certificates or must act as if such resources were in fact served with no encryption.

User agents should warn the user that there is a potential problem whenever the user visits a page that the user has previously visited, if the page uses less secure encryption on the second visit.

Not doing so can result in users not noticing man-in-the-middle attacks.

If a user connects to a server with a self-signed certificate, the user agent could allow the connection but just act as if there had been no encryption. If the user agent instead allowed the user to override the problem and then displayed the page as if it was fully and safely encrypted, the user could be easily tricked into accepting man-in-the-middle connections.

If a user connects to a server with full encryption, but the page then refers to an external resource that has an expired certificate, then the user agent will act as if the resource was unavailable, possibly also reporting the problem to the user. If the user agent instead allowed the resource to be used, then an attacker could just look for "secure" sites that used resources from a different host and only apply man-in-the-middle attacks to that host, for example taking over scripts in the page.

If a user bookmarks a site that uses a CA-signed certificate, and then later revisits that site directly but the site has started using a self-signed certificate, the user agent could warn the user that a man-in-the-middle attack is likely underway, instead of simply acting as if the page was not encrypted.

#### 2.6.4 Determining the type of a resource

The <dfn id="60.html_content-type" data-anolis-xref="Content-Type">Content-Type metadata</dfn> of a resource must be obtained and interpreted in a manner consistent with the requirements of the MIME Sniffing specification. [[MIMESNIFF]](#60.html_refsMIMESNIFF)

The <dfn id="60.html_content-type-sniffing-0" data-anolis-xref="Content-Type sniffing">sniffed type of a resource</dfn> must be found in a manner consistent with the requirements given in the MIME Sniffing specification for finding the *sniffed media type* of the relevant sequence of octets. [[MIMESNIFF]](#60.html_refsMIMESNIFF)

The <dfn id="60.html_content-type-sniffing:-image" data-anolis-xref="Content-Type sniffing: image">rules for sniffing images specifically</dfn> and the <dfn id="60.html_content-type-sniffing:-text-or-binary" data-anolis-xref="Content-Type sniffing: text or binary">rules for distinguishing if a resource is text or binary</dfn> are also defined in the MIME Sniffing specification. Both sets of rules return a [MIME type](#60.html_mime-type) as their result. [[MIMESNIFF]](#60.html_refsMIMESNIFF)

It is imperative that the rules in the MIME Sniffing specification be followed exactly. When a user agent uses different heuristics for content type detection than the server expects, security problems can occur. For more details, see the MIME Sniffing specification. [[MIMESNIFF]](#60.html_refsMIMESNIFF)

#### 2.6.5 Extracting character encodings from [`meta`](#61.html_the-meta-element) elements

The <dfn id="61.html_algorithm-for-extracting-a-character-encoding-from-a-meta-element">algorithm for extracting a character encoding from a `meta` element</dfn>, given a string `s`, is as follows. It either returns a character encoding or nothing.

1.  Let `position` be a pointer into `s`, initially pointing at the start of the string.

2.  *Loop*: Find the first seven characters in `s` after `position` that are an [ASCII case-insensitive](#61.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the word "`charset`". If no such match is found, return nothing and abort these steps.

3.  Skip any [space characters](#61.html_space-character) that immediately follow the word "`charset`" (there might not be any).

4.  If the next character is not a "=" (U+003D), then move `position` to point just before that next character, and jump back to the step labeled *loop*.

5.  Skip any [space characters](#61.html_space-character) that immediately follow the equals sign (there might not be any).

6.  Process the next character as follows:

    If it is a """ (U+0022) character and there is a later """ (U+0022) character in `s`
    If it is a "'" (U+0027) character and there is a later "'" (U+0027) character in `s`

    Return the result of [getting an encoding](#61.html_getting-an-encoding) from the substring that is between this character and the next earliest occurrence of this character.

    If it is an unmatched """ (U+0022) character
    If it is an unmatched "'" (U+0027) character
    If there is no next character

    Return nothing.

    Otherwise

    Return the result of [getting an encoding](#61.html_getting-an-encoding) from the substring that consists of this character up to but not including the first [space character](#61.html_space-character) or ";" (U+003B) character, or the end of `s`, whichever comes first.

This algorithm is distinct from those in the HTTP specification (for example, HTTP doesn't allow the use of single quotes and requires supporting a backslash-escape mechanism that is not supported by this algorithm). While the algorithm is used in contexts that, historically, were related to HTTP, the syntax as supported by implementations diverged some time ago. [[HTTP]](#61.html_refsHTTP)

#### 2.6.6 CORS settings attributes

A <dfn id="62.html_cors-settings-attribute">CORS settings attribute</dfn> is an [enumerated attribute](#62.html_enumerated-attribute). The following table lists the keywords and states for the attribute — the keywords in the left column map to the states in the cell in the second column on the same row as the keyword.

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <dfn id="62.html_attr-crossorigin-anonymous-keyword" data-anolis-xref="attr-crossorigin-anonymous-keyword">`anonymous`</dfn> | <dfn id="62.html_attr-crossorigin-anonymous" data-anolis-xref="attr-crossorigin-anonymous">Anonymous</dfn> | Cross-origin CORS requests for the element will have the *[omit credentials flag](#62.html_omit-credentials-flag)* set. |
| <dfn id="62.html_attr-crossorigin-use-credentials-keyword" data-anolis-xref="attr-crossorigin-use-credentials-keyword">`use-credentials`</dfn> | <dfn id="62.html_attr-crossorigin-use-credentials" data-anolis-xref="attr-crossorigin-use-credentials">Use Credentials</dfn> | Cross-origin CORS requests for the element will not have the *[omit credentials flag](#62.html_omit-credentials-flag)* set. |

The empty string is also a valid keyword, and maps to the [Anonymous](#62.html_attr-crossorigin-anonymous) state. The attribute's *invalid value default* is the [Anonymous](#62.html_attr-crossorigin-anonymous) state. For the purposes of [reflection](#62.html_reflect), the canonical case for the [Anonymous](#62.html_attr-crossorigin-anonymous) state is the [`anonymous`](#62.html_attr-crossorigin-anonymous-keyword) keyword. The *missing value default*, used when the attribute is omitted, is the <dfn id="62.html_attr-crossorigin-none" data-anolis-xref="attr-crossorigin-none">No CORS</dfn> state.

#### 2.6.7 CORS-enabled fetch

When the user agent is required to perform a <dfn id="63.html_potentially-cors-enabled-fetch">potentially CORS-enabled fetch</dfn> of an [absolute URL](#63.html_absolute-url) `URL` with a mode `mode` that is either "[No CORS](#63.html_attr-crossorigin-none)", "[Anonymous](#63.html_attr-crossorigin-anonymous)", or "[Use Credentials](#63.html_attr-crossorigin-use-credentials)", optionally using a [referrer source](#63.html_referrer-source) `referrer source`, with an [origin](#63.html_origin-0) `origin`, and with a default origin behaviour `default` which is either "*taint*" or "*fail*", it must run the first applicable set of steps from the following list. The default origin behaviour is only used if `mode` is "[No CORS](#63.html_attr-crossorigin-none)". This algorithm wraps the [fetch](#63.html_fetch) algorithm above, and labels the obtained resource as either <dfn id="63.html_cors-same-origin">CORS-same-origin</dfn> or <dfn id="63.html_cors-cross-origin">CORS-cross-origin</dfn>, or blocks the resource entirely.

If the `URL` has the [same origin](#63.html_same-origin) as `origin`
If the `URL` is a [`data:` URL](#63.html_data-protocol)
If the `URL` is [`about:blank`](#63.html_about:blank)

Run these substeps:

1.  [Fetch](#63.html_fetch) `URL`, using `referrer source` if one was specified, with the *manual redirect flag* set.

2.  *Loop*: Wait for the [fetch](#63.html_fetch) algorithm to know if the result is a redirect or not.

3.  Follow the first appropriate steps from the following list:

    If the result of the [fetch](#63.html_fetch) is a redirect, and the [origin](#63.html_origin-0) of the target URL of the redirect is not the [same origin](#63.html_same-origin) as `origin`

    Set `URL` to the target URL of the redirect and return to the top of the [potentially CORS-enabled fetch](#63.html_potentially-cors-enabled-fetch) algorithm (this time, one of the other branches below might be taken, based on the value of `mode`).

    If the result of the [fetch](#63.html_fetch) is a redirect

    The [origin](#63.html_origin-0) of the target URL of the redirect is the [same origin](#63.html_same-origin) as `origin`.

    [Transparently follow the redirect](#63.html_transparently-follow-the-redirect) and jump to the step labeled *loop* above.

    Otherwise

    The resource is available, it is not a redirect, and its [origin](#63.html_origin-0) is the [same origin](#63.html_same-origin) as `origin`.

    The [tasks](#63.html_concept-task) from the [fetch](#63.html_fetch) algorithm are [queued](#63.html_queue-a-task) normally, and for the purposes of the calling algorithm, the obtained resource is [CORS-same-origin](#63.html_cors-same-origin).

If `mode` is "[No CORS](#63.html_attr-crossorigin-none)" and `default` is *taint*

The `URL` does not have the [same origin](#63.html_same-origin) as `origin`.

[Fetch](#63.html_fetch) `URL`, using `referrer source` if one was specified.

The [tasks](#63.html_concept-task) from the [fetch](#63.html_fetch) algorithm are [queued](#63.html_queue-a-task) normally, but for the purposes of the calling algorithm, the obtained resource is [CORS-cross-origin](#63.html_cors-cross-origin). The user agent may report a cross-origin resource access failure to the user (e.g. in a debugging console).

If `mode` is "[No CORS](#63.html_attr-crossorigin-none)"

The `URL` does not have the [same origin](#63.html_same-origin) as `origin`, and `default` is *fail*.

Discard any data fetched as part of this algorithm, and prevent any [tasks](#63.html_concept-task) from such invocations of the [fetch](#63.html_fetch) algorithm from being [queued](#63.html_queue-a-task). For the purposes of the calling algorithm, the user agent must act as if there was a fatal network error and no resource was obtained. The user agent may report a cross-origin resource access failure to the user (e.g. in a debugging console).

If `mode` is "[Anonymous](#63.html_attr-crossorigin-anonymous)" or "[Use Credentials](#63.html_attr-crossorigin-use-credentials)"

The `URL` does not have the [same origin](#63.html_same-origin) as `origin`.

Run these steps:

1.  Perform a [cross-origin request](#63.html_cross-origin-request) with the *request URL* set to `URL`, with the CORS *referrer source* set to `referrer source` if one was specified, the *source origin* set to `origin`, and with the *[omit credentials flag](#63.html_omit-credentials-flag)* set if `mode` is "[Anonymous](#63.html_attr-crossorigin-anonymous)" and not set otherwise. [[CORS]](#63.html_refsCORS)

2.  Wait for the CORS [cross-origin request status](#63.html_cross-origin-request-status) to have a value.

3.  Jump to the appropriate step from the following list:

    If the CORS [cross-origin request status](#63.html_cross-origin-request-status) is not *success*

    Discard all fetched data and prevent any [tasks](#63.html_concept-task) from the [fetch](#63.html_fetch) algorithm from being [queued](#63.html_queue-a-task). For the purposes of the calling algorithm, the user agent must act as if there was a fatal network error and no resource was obtained. If a CORS [resource sharing check](#63.html_resource-sharing-check) failed, the user agent may report a cross-origin resource access failure to the user (e.g. in a debugging console).

    If the CORS [cross-origin request status](#63.html_cross-origin-request-status) is *success*

    The [tasks](#63.html_concept-task) from the [fetch](#63.html_fetch) algorithm are [queued](#63.html_queue-a-task) normally, and for the purposes of the calling algorithm, the obtained resource is [CORS-same-origin](#63.html_cors-same-origin).

### 2.7 Common DOM interfaces

#### 2.7.1 Reflecting content attributes in IDL attributes

Some IDL attributes are defined to <dfn id="65.html_reflect">reflect</dfn> a particular content attribute. This means that on getting, the IDL attribute returns the current value of the content attribute, and on setting, the IDL attribute changes the value of the content attribute to the given value.

In general, on getting, if the content attribute is not present, the IDL attribute must act as if the content attribute's value is the empty string; and on setting, if the content attribute is not present, it must first be added.

If a reflecting IDL attribute is a `DOMString` attribute whose content attribute is defined to contain a URL, then on getting, the IDL attribute must [resolve](#65.html_resolve-a-url) the value of the content attribute relative to the element and return the resulting [absolute URL](#65.html_absolute-url) if that was successful, or the empty string otherwise; and on setting, must set the content attribute to the specified literal value. If the content attribute is absent, the IDL attribute must return the default value, if the content attribute has one, or else the empty string.

If a reflecting IDL attribute is a `DOMString` attribute whose content attribute is defined to contain one or more URLs, then on getting, the IDL attribute must [split the content attribute on spaces](#65.html_split-a-string-on-spaces) and return the concatenation of [resolving](#65.html_resolve-a-url) each token URL to an [absolute URL](#65.html_absolute-url) relative to the element, with a single U+0020 SPACE character between each URL, ignoring any tokens that did not resolve successfully. If the content attribute is absent, the IDL attribute must return the default value, if the content attribute has one, or else the empty string. On setting, the IDL attribute must set the content attribute to the specified literal value.

If a reflecting IDL attribute is a `DOMString` attribute whose content attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#65.html_enumerated-attribute), and the IDL attribute is <dfn id="65.html_limited-to-only-known-values">limited to only known values</dfn>, then, on getting, the IDL attribute must return the conforming value associated with the state the attribute is in (in its canonical case), if any, or the empty string if the attribute is in a state that has no associated keyword value or if the attribute is not in a defined state (e.g. the attribute is missing and there is no *missing value default*); and on setting, the content attribute must be set to the specified new value.

If a reflecting IDL attribute is a `DOMString` attribute but doesn't fall into any of the above categories, then the getting and setting must be done in a transparent, case-preserving manner.

If a reflecting IDL attribute is a `boolean` attribute, then on getting the IDL attribute must return true if the content attribute is set, and false if it is absent. On setting, the content attribute must be removed if the IDL attribute is set to false, and must be set to the empty string if the IDL attribute is set to true. (This corresponds to the rules for [boolean content attributes](#65.html_boolean-attribute).)

If a reflecting IDL attribute has a signed integer type (`long`) then, on getting, the content attribute must be parsed according to the [rules for parsing signed integers](#65.html_rules-for-parsing-integers), and if that is successful, and the value is in the range of the IDL attribute's type, the resulting value must be returned. If, on the other hand, it fails or returns an out of range value, or if the attribute is absent, then the default value must be returned instead, or 0 if there is no default value. On setting, the given value must be converted to the shortest possible string representing the number as a [valid integer](#65.html_valid-integer) and then that string must be used as the new content attribute value.

If a reflecting IDL attribute has a signed integer type (`long`) that is <dfn id="65.html_limited-to-only-non-negative-numbers">limited to only non-negative numbers</dfn> then, on getting, the content attribute must be parsed according to the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#65.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers), and if that is successful, and the value is in the range of the IDL attribute's type, the resulting value must be returned. If, on the other hand, it fails or returns an out of range value, or if the attribute is absent, the default value must be returned instead, or ?1 if there is no default value. On setting, if the value is negative, the user agent must throw an [`IndexSizeError`](#65.html_indexsizeerror) exception. Otherwise, the given value must be converted to the shortest possible string representing the number as a [valid non-negative integer](#65.html_valid-non-negative-integer) and then that string must be used as the new content attribute value.

If a reflecting IDL attribute has an *unsigned* integer type (`unsigned long`) then, on getting, the content attribute must be parsed according to the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#65.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers), and if that is successful, and the value is in the range 0 to 2147483647 inclusive, the resulting value must be returned. If, on the other hand, it fails or returns an out of range value, or if the attribute is absent, the default value must be returned instead, or 0 if there is no default value. On setting, first, if the new value is in the range 0 to 2147483647, then let `n` be the new value, otherwise let `n` be the default value, or 0 if there is no default value; then, `n` must be converted to the shortest possible string representing the number as a [valid non-negative integer](#65.html_valid-non-negative-integer) and that string must be used as the new content attribute value.

If a reflecting IDL attribute has an unsigned integer type (`unsigned long`) that is <dfn id="65.html_limited-to-only-non-negative-numbers-greater-than-zero">limited to only non-negative numbers greater than zero</dfn>, then the behavior is similar to the previous case, but zero is not allowed. On getting, the content attribute must first be parsed according to the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#65.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers), and if that is successful, and the value is in the range 1 to 2147483647 inclusive, the resulting value must be returned. If, on the other hand, it fails or returns an out of range value, or if the attribute is absent, the default value must be returned instead, or 1 if there is no default value. On setting, if the value is zero, the user agent must throw an [`IndexSizeError`](#65.html_indexsizeerror) exception. Otherwise, first, if the new value is in the range 1 to 2147483647, then let `n` be the new value, otherwise let `n` be the default value, or 1 if there is no default value; then, `n` must be converted to the shortest possible string representing the number as a [valid non-negative integer](#65.html_valid-non-negative-integer) and that string must be used as the new content attribute value.

If a reflecting IDL attribute has a floating-point number type (`double` or `unrestricted double`), then, on getting, the content attribute must be parsed according to the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#65.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values), and if that is successful, the resulting value must be returned. If, on the other hand, it fails, or if the attribute is absent, the default value must be returned instead, or 0.0 if there is no default value. On setting, the given value must be converted to the [best representation of the number as a floating-point number](#65.html_best-representation-of-the-number-as-a-floating-point-number) and then that string must be used as the new content attribute value.

If a reflecting IDL attribute has a floating-point number type (`double` or `unrestricted double`) that is <dfn id="65.html_limited-to-numbers-greater-than-zero">limited to numbers greater than zero</dfn>, then the behavior is similar to the previous case, but zero and negative values are not allowed. On getting, the content attribute must be parsed according to the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#65.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values), and if that is successful and the value is greater than 0.0, the resulting value must be returned. If, on the other hand, it fails or returns an out of range value, or if the attribute is absent, the default value must be returned instead, or 0.0 if there is no default value. On setting, if the value is less than or equal to zero, then the value must be ignored. Otherwise, the given value must be converted to the [best representation of the number as a floating-point number](#65.html_best-representation-of-the-number-as-a-floating-point-number) and then that string must be used as the new content attribute value.

The values Infinity and Not-a-Number (NaN) values throw an exception on setting, as defined in the Web IDL specification. [[WEBIDL]](#65.html_refsWEBIDL)

If a reflecting IDL attribute has the type [`DOMTokenList`](#65.html_domtokenlist) or [`DOMSettableTokenList`](#65.html_domsettabletokenlist), then on getting it must return a [`DOMTokenList`](#65.html_domtokenlist) or [`DOMSettableTokenList`](#65.html_domsettabletokenlist) object (as appropriate) whose associated element is the element in question and whose associated attribute's local name is the name of the attribute in question. The same [`DOMTokenList`](#65.html_domtokenlist) or [`DOMSettableTokenList`](#65.html_domsettabletokenlist) object must be returned every time for each attribute.

If a reflecting IDL attribute has the type [`HTMLElement`](#65.html_htmlelement), or an interface that descends from [`HTMLElement`](#65.html_htmlelement), then, on getting, it must run the following algorithm (stopping at the first point where a value is returned):

1.  If the corresponding content attribute is absent, then the IDL attribute must return null.
2.  Let `candidate` be the element that the [`document.getElementById()`](#65.html_dom-document-getelementbyid) method would find when called on the content attribute's document if it were passed as its argument the current value of the corresponding content attribute.
3.  If `candidate` is null, or if it is not type-compatible with the IDL attribute, then the IDL attribute must return null.
4.  Otherwise, it must return `candidate`.

On setting, if the given element has an [`id`](#65.html_the-id-attribute) attribute, and has the same [home subtree](#65.html_home-subtree) as the element of the attribute being set, and the given element is the first element in that [home subtree](#65.html_home-subtree) whose [ID](#65.html_concept-id) is the value of that [`id`](#65.html_the-id-attribute) attribute, then the content attribute must be set to the value of that [`id`](#65.html_the-id-attribute) attribute. Otherwise, the content attribute must be set to the empty string.

#### 2.7.2 Collections

The [`HTMLAllCollection`](#66.html_htmlallcollection-0), [`HTMLFormControlsCollection`](#66.html_htmlformcontrolscollection-0), [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#66.html_htmloptionscollection-0), interfaces are [collections](#66.html_collections-0) derived from the [`HTMLCollection`](#66.html_htmlcollection) interface.

##### 2.7.2.1 HTMLAllCollection

The [`HTMLAllCollection`](#66.html_htmlallcollection-0) interface is used for generic [collections](#66.html_collections-0) of elements just like [`HTMLCollection`](#66.html_htmlcollection), with the exception that its [`namedItem()`](#66.html_dom-htmlallcollection-nameditem) method returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#66.html_htmlcollection) object when there are multiple matching elements, and that its `item()` method can be used as a synonym for its [`namedItem()`](#66.html_dom-htmlallcollection-nameditem) method. It is intended only for the legacy [`document.all`](#66.html_dom-document-all) attribute.

```
interface HTMLAllCollection : HTMLCollection {
  // inherits length and item(unsigned long index)
  (HTMLCollection or Element)? item(DOMString name);
  legacycaller getter (HTMLCollection or Element)? namedItem(DOMString name); // shadows inherited namedItem()
  HTMLAllCollection tags(DOMString tagName);
};
```

`collection` . `length`

Returns the number of elements in the collection.

`element` = `collection` . [`item`](#66.html_dom-htmlcollection-item)(`index`)
`collection`[`index`]

Returns the item with index `index` from the collection. The items are sorted in [tree order](#66.html_tree-order).

`element` = `collection` . [`item`](#66.html_dom-htmlallcollection-item-string)(`name`)
`collection` = `collection` . [`item`](#66.html_dom-htmlallcollection-item-string)(`name`)
`element` = `collection` . [`namedItem`](#66.html_dom-htmlallcollection-nameditem)(`name`)
`collection` = `collection` . [`namedItem`](#66.html_dom-htmlallcollection-nameditem)(`name`)
`collection`[`name`]
`collection`(`name`)

Returns the item with [ID](#66.html_concept-id) or name `name` from the collection.

If there are multiple matching items, then an [`HTMLCollection`](#66.html_htmlcollection) object containing all those elements is returned.

Only [`a`](#66.html_the-a-element), [`applet`](#66.html_the-applet-element), [`area`](#66.html_the-area-element), [`embed`](#66.html_the-embed-element), [`form`](#66.html_the-form-element), [`frame`](#66.html_frame), [`frameset`](#66.html_frameset), [`iframe`](#66.html_the-iframe-element), [`img`](#66.html_the-img-element), and [`object`](#66.html_the-object-element) elements can have a name for the purpose of this method; their name is given by the value of their `name` attribute.

`collection` = `collection` . [`tags`](#66.html_dom-htmlallcollection-tags)(`tagName`)

Returns a collection that is a filtered view of the current collection, containing only elements with the given tag name.

The object's [supported property indices](#66.html_supported-property-indices) are as defined for [`HTMLCollection`](#66.html_htmlcollection) objects.

The [supported property names](#66.html_supported-property-names) consist of the non-empty values of all the [`id`](#66.html_the-id-attribute) attributes of all the elements [represented by the collection](#66.html_represented-by-the-collection), and the non-empty values of all the `name` attributes of all the [`a`](#66.html_the-a-element), [`applet`](#66.html_the-applet-element), [`area`](#66.html_the-area-element), [`embed`](#66.html_the-embed-element), [`form`](#66.html_the-form-element), [`frame`](#66.html_frame), [`frameset`](#66.html_frameset), [`iframe`](#66.html_the-iframe-element), [`img`](#66.html_the-img-element), and [`object`](#66.html_the-object-element) elements [represented by the collection](#66.html_represented-by-the-collection), in [tree order](#66.html_tree-order), ignoring later duplicates, with the [`id`](#66.html_the-id-attribute) of an element preceding its `name` if it contributes both, they differ from each other, and neither is the duplicate of an earlier entry.

The <dfn id="66.html_dom-htmlallcollection-item-string" data-anolis-xref="dom-HTMLAllCollection-item-string">`item(``name``)`</dfn> and <dfn id="66.html_dom-htmlallcollection-nameditem" data-anolis-xref="dom-HTMLAllCollection-namedItem">`namedItem(``name``)`</dfn> methods must act according to the following algorithm:

1.  If `name` is the empty string, return null and stop the algorithm.
2.  Let `collection` be an [`HTMLCollection`](#66.html_htmlcollection) object rooted at the same node as the [`HTMLAllCollection`](#66.html_htmlallcollection-0) object on which the method was invoked, whose filter matches only elements that already match the filter of the [`HTMLAllCollection`](#66.html_htmlallcollection-0) object on which the method was invoked and that are either:

    *   [`a`](#66.html_the-a-element), [`applet`](#66.html_the-applet-element), [`area`](#66.html_the-area-element), [`embed`](#66.html_the-embed-element), [`form`](#66.html_the-form-element), [`frame`](#66.html_frame), [`frameset`](#66.html_frameset), [`iframe`](#66.html_the-iframe-element), [`img`](#66.html_the-img-element), or [`object`](#66.html_the-object-element) elements with a `name` attribute equal to `name`, or,
    *   elements with an [ID](#66.html_concept-id) equal to `name`.
3.  If, at the time the method is called, there is exactly one node in `collection`, then return that node and stop the algorithm.
4.  Otherwise, if, at the time the method is called, `collection` is empty, return null and stop the algorithm.
5.  Otherwise, return `collection`.

The <dfn id="66.html_dom-htmlallcollection-tags" data-anolis-xref="dom-HTMLAllCollection-tags">`tags(``tagName``)`</dfn> method must return an [`HTMLAllCollection`](#66.html_htmlallcollection-0) rooted at the same node as the [`HTMLAllCollection`](#66.html_htmlallcollection-0) object on which the method was invoked, whose filter matches only [HTML elements](#66.html_html-elements) whose local name is the `tagName` argument and that already match the filter of the [`HTMLAllCollection`](#66.html_htmlallcollection-0) object on which the method was invoked. In [HTML documents](#66.html_html-documents), the argument must first be [converted to ASCII lowercase](#66.html_converted-to-ascii-lowercase).

##### 2.7.2.2 HTMLFormControlsCollection

The [`HTMLFormControlsCollection`](#66.html_htmlformcontrolscollection-0) interface is used for [collections](#66.html_collections-0) of [listed elements](#66.html_category-listed) in [`form`](#66.html_the-form-element) and [`fieldset`](#66.html_the-fieldset-element) elements.

```
interface HTMLFormControlsCollection : HTMLCollection {
  // inherits length and item()
  legacycaller getter (RadioNodeList or Element)? namedItem(DOMString name); // shadows inherited namedItem()
};

interface RadioNodeList : NodeList {
          attribute DOMString value;
};
```

`collection` . `length`

Returns the number of elements in the collection.

`element` = `collection` . [`item`](#66.html_dom-htmlcollection-item)(`index`)
`collection`[`index`]

Returns the item with index `index` from the collection. The items are sorted in [tree order](#66.html_tree-order).

`element` = `collection` . [`namedItem`](#66.html_dom-htmlformcontrolscollection-nameditem)(`name`)
`radioNodeList` = `collection` . [`namedItem`](#66.html_dom-htmlformcontrolscollection-nameditem)(`name`)
`collection`[`name`]
`collection`(`name`)

Returns the item with [ID](#66.html_concept-id) or [`name`](#66.html_attr-fe-name) `name` from the collection.

If there are multiple matching items, then a [`RadioNodeList`](#66.html_radionodelist) object containing all those elements is returned.

`radioNodeList` . `value` [ = `value` ]

Returns the value of the first checked radio button represented by the object.

Can be set, to check the first radio button with the given value represented by the object.

The object's [supported property indices](#66.html_supported-property-indices) are as defined for [`HTMLCollection`](#66.html_htmlcollection) objects.

The [supported property names](#66.html_supported-property-names) consist of the non-empty values of all the [`id`](#66.html_the-id-attribute) and [`name`](#66.html_attr-fe-name) attributes of all the elements [represented by the collection](#66.html_represented-by-the-collection), in [tree order](#66.html_tree-order), ignoring later duplicates, with the [`id`](#66.html_the-id-attribute) of an element preceding its [`name`](#66.html_attr-fe-name) if it contributes both, they differ from each other, and neither is the duplicate of an earlier entry.

The <dfn id="66.html_dom-htmlformcontrolscollection-nameditem" data-anolis-xref="dom-HTMLFormControlsCollection-namedItem">`namedItem(``name``)`</dfn> method must act according to the following algorithm:

1.  If `name` is the empty string, return null and stop the algorithm.
2.  If, at the time the method is called, there is exactly one node in the collection that has either an [`id`](#66.html_the-id-attribute) attribute or a [`name`](#66.html_attr-fe-name) attribute equal to `name`, then return that node and stop the algorithm.
3.  Otherwise, if there are no nodes in the collection that have either an [`id`](#66.html_the-id-attribute) attribute or a [`name`](#66.html_attr-fe-name) attribute equal to `name`, then return null and stop the algorithm.
4.  Otherwise, create a new [`RadioNodeList`](#66.html_radionodelist) object representing a [live](#66.html_live) view of the [`HTMLFormControlsCollection`](#66.html_htmlformcontrolscollection-0) object, further filtered so that the only nodes in the [`RadioNodeList`](#66.html_radionodelist) object are those that have either an [`id`](#66.html_the-id-attribute) attribute or a [`name`](#66.html_attr-fe-name) attribute equal to `name`.
