The nodes in the [`RadioNodeList`](#66.html_radionodelist) object must be sorted in [tree order](#66.html_tree-order).
5.  Return that [`RadioNodeList`](#66.html_radionodelist) object.

* * *

Members of the [`RadioNodeList`](#66.html_radionodelist) interface inherited from the [`NodeList`](#66.html_nodelist) interface must behave as they would on a [`NodeList`](#66.html_nodelist) object.

The <dfn id="66.html_dom-radionodelist-value" data-anolis-xref="dom-RadioNodeList-value">`value`</dfn> IDL attribute on the [`RadioNodeList`](#66.html_radionodelist) object, on getting, must return the value returned by running the following steps:

1.  Let `element` be the first element in [tree order](#66.html_tree-order) represented by the [`RadioNodeList`](#66.html_radionodelist) object that is an [`input`](#66.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#66.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#66.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state and whose [checkedness](#66.html_concept-fe-checked) is true. Otherwise, let it be null.

2.  If `element` is null, or if it is an element with no [`value`](#66.html_attr-input-value) attribute, return the empty string.

3.  Otherwise, return the value of `element`'s [`value`](#66.html_attr-input-value) attribute.

On setting, the [`value`](#66.html_dom-radionodelist-value) IDL attribute must run the following steps:

1.  Let `element` be the first element in [tree order](#66.html_tree-order) represented by the [`RadioNodeList`](#66.html_radionodelist) object that is an [`input`](#66.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#66.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#66.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state and whose [`value`](#66.html_attr-input-value) content attribute is present and equal to the new value, if any. Otherwise, let it be null.

2.  If `element` is not null, then set its [checkedness](#66.html_concept-fe-checked) to true.

##### 2.7.2.3 HTMLOptionsCollection

The [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#66.html_htmloptionscollection-0) interface is used for [collections](#66.html_collections-0) of [`option`](#66.html_the-option-element) elements. It is always rooted on a [`select`](#66.html_the-select-element) element and has attributes and methods that manipulate that element's descendants.

```
interface HTMLOptionsCollection : HTMLCollection {
  // inherits item()
           attribute unsigned long length; // shadows inherited length
  legacycaller HTMLOptionElement? (DOMString name);
  setter creator void (unsigned long index, HTMLOptionElement? option);
  void add((HTMLOptionElement or HTMLOptGroupElement) element, optional (HTMLElement or long)? before = null);
  void remove(long index);
           attribute long selectedIndex;
};
```

`collection` . [`length`](#66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-length) [ = `value` ]

Returns the number of elements in the collection.

When set to a smaller number, truncates the number of [`option`](#66.html_the-option-element) elements in the corresponding container.

When set to a greater number, adds new blank [`option`](#66.html_the-option-element) elements to that container.

`element` = `collection` . [`item`](#66.html_dom-htmlcollection-item)(`index`)
`collection`[`index`]

Returns the item with index `index` from the collection. The items are sorted in [tree order](#66.html_tree-order).

`element` = `collection` . [`namedItem`](#66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-nameditem)(`name`)
`nodeList` = `collection` . [`namedItem`](#66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-nameditem)(`name`)
`collection`[`name`]
`collection`(`name`)

Returns the item with [ID](#66.html_concept-id) or [`name`](#66.html_attr-option-name) `name` from the collection.

If there are multiple matching items, then the first is returned.

`collection` . [`add`](#66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-add)(`element` [, `before` ] )

Inserts `element` before the node given by `before`.

The `before` argument can be a number, in which case `element` is inserted before the item with that number, or an element from the collection, in which case `element` is inserted before that element.

If `before` is omitted, null, or a number out of range, then `element` will be added at the end of the list.

This method will throw a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#66.html_hierarchyrequesterror) exception if `element` is an ancestor of the element into which it is to be inserted.

`collection` . [`selectedIndex`](#66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-selectedindex) [ = `value` ]

Returns the index of the first selected item, if any, or ?1 if there is no selected item.

Can be set, to change the selection.

The object's [supported property indices](#66.html_supported-property-indices) are as defined for [`HTMLCollection`](#66.html_htmlcollection) objects.

On getting, the <dfn id="66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-length" data-anolis-xref="dom-HTMLOptionsCollection-length">`length`</dfn> attribute must return the number of nodes [represented by the collection](#66.html_represented-by-the-collection).

On setting, the behavior depends on whether the new value is equal to, greater than, or less than the number of nodes [represented by the collection](#66.html_represented-by-the-collection) at that time. If the number is the same, then setting the attribute must do nothing. If the new value is greater, then `n` new [`option`](#66.html_the-option-element) elements with no attributes and no child nodes must be appended to the [`select`](#66.html_the-select-element) element on which the [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#66.html_htmloptionscollection-0) is rooted, where `n` is the difference between the two numbers (new value minus old value). Mutation events must be fired as if a [`DocumentFragment`](#66.html_documentfragment) containing the new [`option`](#66.html_the-option-element) elements had been inserted. If the new value is lower, then the last `n` nodes in the collection must be removed from their parent nodes, where `n` is the difference between the two numbers (old value minus new value).

Setting [`length`](#66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-length) never removes or adds any [`optgroup`](#66.html_the-optgroup-element) elements, and never adds new children to existing [`optgroup`](#66.html_the-optgroup-element) elements (though it can remove children from them).

The [supported property names](#66.html_supported-property-names) consist of the non-empty values of all the [`id`](#66.html_the-id-attribute) and [`name`](#66.html_attr-option-name) attributes of all the elements [represented by the collection](#66.html_represented-by-the-collection), in [tree order](#66.html_tree-order), ignoring later duplicates, with the [`id`](#66.html_the-id-attribute) of an element preceding its [`name`](#66.html_attr-option-name) if it contributes both, they differ from each other, and neither is the duplicate of an earlier entry.

The <dfn id="66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-nameditem" data-anolis-xref="dom-HTMLOptionsCollection-namedItem">legacy caller</dfn> of the [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#66.html_htmloptionscollection-0) interface must act like the `namedItem()` method on the ancestor [`HTMLCollection`](#66.html_htmlcollection) interface.

When the user agent is to <dfn id="66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-setter" data-anolis-xref="dom-HTMLOptionsCollection-setter">set the value of a new indexed property or set the value of an existing indexed property</dfn> for a given property index `index` to a new value `value`, it must run the following algorithm:

1.  If `value` is null, invoke the steps for the [`remove`](#66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-remove) method with `index` as the argument, and abort these steps.

2.  Let `length` be the number of nodes [represented by the collection](#66.html_represented-by-the-collection).

3.  Let `n` be `index` minus `length`.

4.  If `n` is greater than zero, then [append](#66.html_concept-node-append) a [`DocumentFragment`](#66.html_documentfragment) consisting of `n`-1 new [`option`](#66.html_the-option-element) elements with no attributes and no child nodes to the [`select`](#66.html_the-select-element) element on which the [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#66.html_htmloptionscollection-0) is rooted.

5.  If `n` is greater than or equal to zero, [append](#66.html_concept-node-append) `value` to the [`select`](#66.html_the-select-element) element. Otherwise, [replace](#66.html_concept-node-replace) the `index`th element in the collection by `value`.

The <dfn id="66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-add" data-anolis-xref="dom-HTMLOptionsCollection-add">`add(``element``,` `before``)`</dfn> method must act according to the following algorithm:

1.  If `element` is an ancestor of the [`select`](#66.html_the-select-element) element on which the [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#66.html_htmloptionscollection-0) is rooted, then throw a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#66.html_hierarchyrequesterror) exception and abort these steps.

2.  If `before` is an element, but that element isn't a descendant of the [`select`](#66.html_the-select-element) element on which the [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#66.html_htmloptionscollection-0) is rooted, then throw a [`NotFoundError`](#66.html_notfounderror) exception and abort these steps.

3.  If `element` and `before` are the same element, then return and abort these steps.

4.  If `before` is a node, then let `reference` be that node. Otherwise, if `before` is an integer, and there is a `before`th node in the collection, let `reference` be that node. Otherwise, let `reference` be null.

5.  If `reference` is not null, let `parent` be the parent node of `reference`. Otherwise, let `parent` be the [`select`](#66.html_the-select-element) element on which the [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#66.html_htmloptionscollection-0) is rooted.

6.  Act as if the DOM [`insertBefore()`](#66.html_dom-node-insertbefore) method was invoked on the `parent` node, with `element` as the first argument and `reference` as the second argument.

The <dfn id="66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-remove" data-anolis-xref="dom-HTMLOptionsCollection-remove">`remove(``index``)`</dfn> method must act according to the following algorithm:

1.  If the number of nodes [represented by the collection](#66.html_represented-by-the-collection) is zero, abort these steps.

2.  If `index` is not a number greater than or equal to 0 and less than the number of nodes [represented by the collection](#66.html_represented-by-the-collection), abort these steps.

3.  Let `element` be the `index`th element in the collection.

4.  Remove `element` from its parent node.

The <dfn id="66.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-selectedindex" data-anolis-xref="dom-HTMLOptionsCollection-selectedIndex">`selectedIndex`</dfn> IDL attribute must act like the identically named attribute on the [`select`](#66.html_the-select-element) element on which the [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#66.html_htmloptionscollection-0) is rooted

#### 2.7.3 DOMStringMap

The [`DOMStringMap`](#67.html_domstringmap-0) interface represents a set of name-value pairs. It exposes these using the scripting language's native mechanisms for property access.

When a [`DOMStringMap`](#67.html_domstringmap-0) object is instantiated, it is associated with three algorithms, one for getting the list of name-value pairs, one for setting names to certain values, and one for deleting names.

```
[OverrideBuiltins]
interface DOMStringMap {
  getter DOMString (DOMString name);
  setter creator void (DOMString name, DOMString value);
  deleter void (DOMString name);
};
```

The [supported property names](#67.html_supported-property-names) on a [`DOMStringMap`](#67.html_domstringmap-0) object at any instant are the names of each pair returned from the algorithm for getting the list of name-value pairs at that instant, in the order returned.

To <dfn id="67.html_dom-domstringmap-nameditem" data-anolis-xref="dom-DOMStringMap-namedItem">determine the value of a named property</dfn> `name` in a [`DOMStringMap`](#67.html_domstringmap-0), the user agent must return the value component of the name-value pair whose name component is `name` in the list returned by the algorithm for getting the list of name-value pairs.

To set the value of a <dfn id="67.html_dom-domstringmap-additem" data-anolis-xref="dom-DOMStringMap-addItem">new</dfn> or <dfn id="67.html_dom-domstringmap-setitem" data-anolis-xref="dom-DOMStringMap-setItem">existing</dfn> named property `name` to value `value`, the algorithm for setting names to certain values must be run, passing `name` as the name and the result of converting `value` to a `DOMString` as the value.

To <dfn id="67.html_dom-domstringmap-removeitem" data-anolis-xref="dom-DOMStringMap-removeItem">delete an existing named property</dfn> `name`, the algorithm for deleting names must be run, passing `name` as the name.

The [`DOMStringMap`](#67.html_domstringmap-0) interface definition here is only intended for JavaScript environments. Other language bindings will need to define how [`DOMStringMap`](#67.html_domstringmap-0) is to be implemented for those languages.

The [`dataset`](#67.html_dom-dataset) attribute on elements exposes the [`data-*`](#67.html_attr-data-*) attributes on the element.

Given the following fragment and elements with similar constructions:

```
<img class="tower" id="tower5" data-x="12" data-y="5"
     data-ai="robotarget" data-hp="46" data-ability="flames"
     src="towers/rocket.png alt="Rocket Tower">
```

...one could imagine a function `splashDamage()` that takes some arguments, the first of which is the element to process:

```
function splashDamage(node, x, y, damage) {
  if (node.classList.contains('tower') && // checking the 'class' attribute
      node.dataset.x == x && // reading the 'data-x' attribute
      node.dataset.y == y) { // reading the 'data-y' attribute
    var hp = parseInt(node.dataset.hp); // reading the 'data-hp' attribute
    hp = hp - damage;
    if (hp < 0) {
      hp = 0;
      node.dataset.ai = 'dead'; // setting the 'data-ai' attribute
      delete node.dataset.ability; // removing the 'data-ability' attribute
    }
    node.dataset.hp = hp; // setting the 'data-hp' attribute
  }
}
```

#### 2.7.4 Transferable objects

Some objects support being copied and closed in one operation. This is called *transferring* the object, and is used in particular to transfer ownership of unsharable or expensive resources across worker boundaries.

The following [`Transferable`](#68.html_transferable) types exist:

*   [`ArrayBuffer`](#68.html_arraybuffer) [[TYPEDARRAY]](#68.html_refsTYPEDARRAY)
*   [`MessagePort`](#68.html_messageport)

The following IDL block formalizes this:

```
[NoInterfaceObject]
interface Transferable { };
ArrayBuffer implements Transferable;
MessagePort implements Transferable;
```

To <dfn id="68.html_transfer-a-transferable-object">transfer a `Transferable` object</dfn> to a new owner, the user agent must run the steps defined for the type of object in question. The steps will return a new object of the same type, and will permanently <dfn id="68.html_concept-transferable-neutered" data-anolis-xref="concept-Transferable-neutered">neuter</dfn> the original object. (This is an irreversible and non-idempotent operation; once an object has been transferred, it cannot be transferred, or indeed used, again.)

To [transfer](#68.html_transfer-a-transferable-object) an [`ArrayBuffer`](#68.html_arraybuffer) object `old` to a new owner `owner`, a user agent must create a new [`ArrayBuffer`](#68.html_arraybuffer) object pointing at the same underlying data as `old`, thus obtaining `new`, must [neuter](#68.html_concept-transferable-neutered) the `old` object, and must finally return `new`. [[TYPEDARRAY]](#68.html_refsTYPEDARRAY)

Rules for how to [transfer a `MessagePort` object](#68.html_refsWEBMSG) are given in the relevant sections of this specification.

#### 2.7.5 Safe passing of structured data

When a user agent is required to obtain a <dfn id="69.html_structured-clone">structured clone</dfn> of a value, optionally with a *transfer map*, it must run the following algorithm, which either returns a separate value, or throws an exception. If a *transfer map* is provided, it consists of an association list of [`Transferable`](#69.html_transferable) objects to placeholder objects.

1.  Let `input` be the value being cloned.

2.  Let `transfer map` be the *transfer map* passed to the algorithm, if any, or the empty list otherwise.

3.  Let `memory` be an association list of pairs of objects, initially empty. This is used to handle duplicate references. In each pair of objects, one is called the *[source](#69.html_the-source-element)* object and the other the *destination* object.

4.  For each mapping in `transfer map`, add a mapping from the [`Transferable`](#69.html_transferable) object (the source object) to the placeholder object (the destination object) to `memory`.

5.  Let `output` be the value resulting from calling the [internal structured cloning algorithm](#69.html_internal-structured-cloning-algorithm) with `input` as the "`input`" argument, and `memory` as the "`memory`" argument.

6.  Return `output`.

The <dfn id="69.html_internal-structured-cloning-algorithm">internal structured cloning algorithm</dfn> is always called with two arguments, `input` and `memory`, and its behavior is as follows:

1.  If `input` is the source object of a pair of objects in `memory`, then return the destination object in that pair of objects and abort these steps.

2.  If `input` is a primitive value, then return that value and abort these steps.

3.  Let `deep clone` be *none*.

4.  The `input` value is an object. Jump to the appropriate step below:

    If `input` is a `Boolean` object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed Boolean object with the same value as `input`.

    If `input` is a `Number` object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed Number object with the same value as `input`.

    If `input` is a `String` object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed String object with the same value as `input`.

    If `input` is a `Date` object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed `Date` object with the same value as `input`.

    If `input` is a `RegExp` object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed `RegExp` object with the same pattern and flags as `input`.

    The value of the `lastIndex` property is not copied.

    If `input` is a [`Blob`](#69.html_blob) object

    If `input` has been disabled through the [`close()`](#69.html_dom-blob-close) method, throw a [`DataCloneError`](#69.html_datacloneerror) exception and abort the overall [structured clone](#69.html_structured-clone) algorithm. Otherwise, let `output` be a newly constructed object of the same class as `input`, corresponding to the same underlying data.

    If `input` is a [`FileList`](#69.html_filelist) object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed [`FileList`](#69.html_filelist) object containing a list of newly constructed [`File`](#69.html_file) objects corresponding to the same underlying data as those in `input`, maintaining their relative order.

    If `input` is an `ImageData` object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed `ImageData` object whose `width`, `height`, and `resolution` attributes have values equal to the corresponding attributes on `input`, and whose `data` attribute has the value obtained from invoking the [internal structured cloning algorithm](#69.html_internal-structured-cloning-algorithm) recursively with the value of the `data` attribute on `input` as the new "`input`" argument and `memory` as the new "`memory`" argument.

    If `input` is an [`ArrayBuffer`](#69.html_arraybuffer) object

    If `input` has been [neutered](#69.html_concept-transferable-neutered), throw a [`DataCloneError`](#69.html_datacloneerror) exception and abort the overall [structured clone](#69.html_structured-clone) algorithm. Otherwise, let `output` be a newly constructed [`ArrayBuffer`](#69.html_arraybuffer) object whose contents are a copy of `input`'s contents, with the same length.

    If `input` is an [`ArrayBufferView`](#69.html_arraybufferview) object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed object of the same class as `input`, with each IDL attribute defined for that class being set to the value obtained from invoking the [internal structured cloning algorithm](#69.html_internal-structured-cloning-algorithm) recursively with the value of the attribute on `input` as the new "`input`" argument and `memory` as the new "`memory`" argument.

    Only IDL attributes defined on the class (including the [`ArrayBufferView`](#69.html_arraybufferview) attributes) are cloned. Properties added by a script, for example, are not cloned.

    If `input` is an `Array` object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed empty `Array` object whose `length` is equal to the `length` of `input`, and set `deep clone` to *own*.

    This means that the length of sparse arrays is preserved.

    If `input` is an `Object` object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed empty `Object` object, and set `deep clone` to *own*.

    If `input` is a [`Map`](#69.html_the-map-element) object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed empty `Map` object, and set `deep clone` to *[map](#69.html_the-map-element)*.

    If `input` is a `Set` object

    Let `output` be a newly constructed empty `Set` object, and set `deep clone` to *set*.

    If `input` is an object that another specification defines how to clone

    Let `output` be a clone of the object as defined by the other specification.

    If `input` is another native object type (e.g. `Error`, `Function`)
    If `input` is a host object (e.g. a DOM node)

    Throw a [`DataCloneError`](#69.html_datacloneerror) exception and abort the overall [structured clone](#69.html_structured-clone) algorithm.

    For the purposes of the algorithm above, an object is a particular type of object `class` if its [[Class]] internal property is equal to `class`.

    For example, "`input` is an `Object` object" if `input`'s [[Class]] internal property is equal to the string "`Object`".

5.  Add a mapping from `input` (the source object) to `output` (the destination object) to `memory`.

6.  If `deep clone` is set to *[map](#69.html_the-map-element)*, then run these substeps. These substeps use the terminology and typographic conventions used in the JavaScript specification's definition of Maps. [[ECMA262]](#69.html_refsECMA262)

    1.  Let `source` be the List that is the value of `input`'s [[MapData]] internal slot, if any. If there is no such slot, then instead throw a [`DataCloneError`](#69.html_datacloneerror) exception and abort the overall [structured clone](#69.html_structured-clone) algorithm. [[ECMA262]](#69.html_refsECMA262)

    2.  Let `target` be the List that is the value of `output`'s [[MapData]] internal slot.

    3.  For each Record {[[key]], [[value]]} `entry` that is an element of `source`, run the following substeps:

        1.  Let `key` have the value obtained from invoking the [internal structured cloning algorithm](#69.html_internal-structured-cloning-algorithm) recursively with `entry`.[[key]] as the new "`input`" argument and `memory` as the new "`memory`" argument.

        2.  Let `value` have the value obtained from invoking the [internal structured cloning algorithm](#69.html_internal-structured-cloning-algorithm) recursively with `entry`.[[value]] as the new "`input`" argument and `memory` as the new "`memory`" argument.

        3.  Let `new entry` be the Record {[[key]]: `key`, [[value]]: `value`}.

        4.  Append `new entry` as the last element of `target`.

    4.  Set `deep clone` to *own*.

7.  If `deep clone` is set to *set*, then run these substeps. These substeps use the terminology and typographic conventions used in the JavaScript specification's definition of Sets. [[ECMA262]](#69.html_refsECMA262)

    1.  Let `source` be the List that is the value of `input`'s [[SetData]] internal slot, if any. If there is no such slot, then instead throw a [`DataCloneError`](#69.html_datacloneerror) exception and abort the overall [structured clone](#69.html_structured-clone) algorithm. [[ECMA262]](#69.html_refsECMA262)

    2.  Let `target` be the List that is the value of `output`'s [[SetData]] internal slot.

    3.  For each `entry` that is an element of `source` that is not *empty*, run the following substeps:

        1.  Let `new entry` have the value obtained from invoking the [internal structured cloning algorithm](#69.html_internal-structured-cloning-algorithm) recursively with `entry` as the new "`input`" argument and `memory` as the new "`memory`" argument.

        2.  Append `new entry` as the last element of `target`.

    4.  Set `deep clone` to *own*.

8.  If `deep clone` is set to *own*, then, for each enumerable own property in `input`, run the following steps:

    1.  Let `name` be the name of the property.

    2.  Let `source value` be the result of calling the [[Get]] internal method of `input` with the argument `name`. If the [[Get]] internal method of a property involved executing script, and that script threw an uncaught exception, then abort the overall [structured clone](#69.html_structured-clone) algorithm, with that exception being passed through to the caller.

    3.  Let `cloned value` be the result of invoking the [internal structured cloning algorithm](#69.html_internal-structured-cloning-algorithm) recursively with `source value` as the "`input`" argument and `memory` as the "`memory`" argument. If this results in an exception, then abort the overall [structured clone](#69.html_structured-clone) algorithm, with that exception being passed through to the caller.

    4.  Add a new property to `output` having the name `name`, and having the value `cloned value`.

    The order of the properties in the `input` and `output` objects must be the same, and any properties whose [[Get]] internal method involves running script must be processed in that same order.

    This does not walk the prototype chain.

    Property descriptors, setters, getters, and analogous features are not copied in this process. For example, the property in the input could be marked as read-only, but in the output it would just have the default state (typically read-write, though that could depend on the scripting environment).

    Properties of Array objects are not treated any differently than those of other Objects. In particular, this means that non-index properties of arrays are copied as well.

9.  Return `output`.

This algorithm preserves cycles and preserves the identity of duplicate objects in graphs.

#### 2.7.6 Callbacks

The following callback function type is used in various APIs that interact with [`File`](#70.html_file) objects:

```
callback FileCallback = void (File file);
```

#### 2.7.7 Garbage collection

There is an <dfn id="71.html_implied-strong-reference">implied strong reference</dfn> from any IDL attribute that returns a pre-existing object to that object.

For example, the `document.location` attribute means that there is a strong reference from a [`Document`](#71.html_document) object to its [`Location`](#71.html_location) object. Similarly, there is always a strong reference from a [`Document`](#71.html_document) to any descendant nodes, and from any node to its owner [`Document`](#71.html_document).

### 2.8 Namespaces

The <dfn id="72.html_html-namespace-0">HTML namespace</dfn> is: `http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml`

The <dfn id="72.html_mathml-namespace">MathML namespace</dfn> is: `http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML`

The <dfn id="72.html_svg-namespace">SVG namespace</dfn> is: `http://www.w3.org/2000/svg`

The <dfn id="72.html_xlink-namespace">XLink namespace</dfn> is: `http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink`

The <dfn id="72.html_xml-namespace">XML namespace</dfn> is: `http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace`

The <dfn id="72.html_xmlns-namespace">XMLNS namespace</dfn> is: `http://www.w3.org/2000/xmlns/`

* * *

Data mining tools and other user agents that perform operations on content without running scripts, evaluating CSS or XPath expressions, or otherwise exposing the resulting DOM to arbitrary content, may "support namespaces" by just asserting that their DOM node analogues are in certain namespaces, without actually exposing the above strings.

* * *

In [the HTML syntax](#72.html_syntax), namespace prefixes and namespace declarations do not have the same effect as in XML. For instance, the colon has no special meaning in HTML element names.

## 3 Semantics, structure, and APIs of HTML documents

### 3.1 Documents

Every XML and HTML document in an HTML UA is represented by a [`Document`](#74.html_document) object. [[DOM]](#74.html_refsDOM)

<dfn id="74.html_the-document's-address">The document's address</dfn> is an [absolute URL](#74.html_absolute-url) that is initially set when the [`Document`](#74.html_document) is created but that can change during the lifetime of the [`Document`](#74.html_document), for example when the user [navigates](#74.html_navigate) to a [fragment identifier](#74.html_scroll-to-fragid) on the page or when the [`pushState()`](#74.html_dom-history-pushstate) method is called with a new URL.

Interactive user agents typically expose [the document's address](#74.html_the-document's-address) in their user interface. This is the primary mechanism by which a user can tell if a site is attempting to impersonate another.

When a [`Document`](#74.html_document) is created by a [script](#74.html_concept-script) using the [`createDocument()`](#74.html_dom-domimplementation-createdocument) or [`createHTMLDocument()`](#74.html_dom-domimplementation-createhtmldocument) APIs, [the document's address](#74.html_the-document's-address) is the same as [the document's address](#74.html_the-document's-address) of the [responsible document](#74.html_responsible-document) specified by the script's [settings object](#74.html_settings-object), and the [`Document`](#74.html_document) is both [ready for post-load tasks](#74.html_ready-for-post-load-tasks) and [completely loaded](#74.html_completely-loaded) immediately.

<dfn id="74.html_the-document's-referrer">The document's referrer</dfn> is an [absolute URL](#74.html_absolute-url) that can be set when the [`Document`](#74.html_document) is created. If it is not explicitly set, then its value is the empty string.

Each [`Document`](#74.html_document) object has a <dfn id="74.html_reload-override-flag">reload override flag</dfn> that is originally unset. The flag is set by the [`document.open()`](#74.html_dom-document-open) and [`document.write()`](#74.html_dom-document-open) methods in certain situations. When the flag is set, the [`Document`](#74.html_document) also has a <dfn id="74.html_reload-override-buffer">reload override buffer</dfn> which is a Unicode string that is used as the source of the document when it is reloaded.

When the user agent is to perform <dfn id="74.html_an-overridden-reload">an overridden reload</dfn>, given a [source browsing context](#74.html_source-browsing-context), it must act as follows:

1.  Let `source` be the value of the [browsing context](#74.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#74.html_active-document)'s [reload override buffer](#74.html_reload-override-buffer).

2.  Let `address` be the [browsing context](#74.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#74.html_active-document)'s [address](#74.html_the-document's-address).

3.  [Navigate](#74.html_navigate) the [browsing context](#74.html_browsing-context) to a resource whose source is `source`, with [replacement enabled](#74.html_replacement-enabled) and [exceptions enabled](#74.html_exceptions-enabled). The [source browsing context](#74.html_source-browsing-context) is that given to the [overridden reload](#74.html_an-overridden-reload) algorithm. When the [navigate](#74.html_navigate) algorithm creates a [`Document`](#74.html_document) object for this purpose, set that [`Document`](#74.html_document)'s [reload override flag](#74.html_reload-override-flag) and set its [reload override buffer](#74.html_reload-override-buffer) to `source`.

    When it comes time to [set the document's address](#74.html_set-the-document's-address) in the [navigation algorithm](#74.html_navigate), use `address` as the [override URL](#74.html_override-url).

#### 3.1.1 The [`Document`](#75.html_document) object

The DOM specification defines a [`Document`](#75.html_dom-document) interface, which this specification extends significantly:

```
enum DocumentReadyState { "loading", "interactive", "complete" };

[OverrideBuiltins]
partial /*sealed*/ interface Document {
  // resource metadata management
  [PutForwards=href, Unforgeable] readonly attribute Location? location;
           attribute DOMString domain;
  readonly attribute DOMString referrer;
           attribute DOMString cookie;
  readonly attribute DOMString lastModified;
  readonly attribute DocumentReadyState readyState;

  // DOM tree accessors
  getter object (DOMString name);
           attribute DOMString title;
           attribute DOMString dir;
           attribute HTMLElement? body;
  readonly attribute HTMLHeadElement? head;
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection images;
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection embeds;
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection plugins;
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection links;
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection forms;
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection scripts;
  NodeList getElementsByName(DOMString elementName);

  // dynamic markup insertion
  Document open(optional DOMString type = "text/html", optional DOMString replace = "");
  WindowProxy open(DOMString url, DOMString name, DOMString features, optional boolean replace = false);
  void close();
  void write(DOMString... text);
  void writeln(DOMString... text);

  // user interaction
  readonly attribute WindowProxy? defaultView;
  readonly attribute Element? activeElement;
  boolean hasFocus();
           attribute DOMString designMode;
  boolean execCommand(DOMString commandId, optional boolean showUI = false, optional DOMString value = "");
  boolean queryCommandEnabled(DOMString commandId);
  boolean queryCommandIndeterm(DOMString commandId);
  boolean queryCommandState(DOMString commandId);
  boolean queryCommandSupported(DOMString commandId);
  DOMString queryCommandValue(DOMString commandId);

  // special event handler IDL attributes that only apply to Document objects
  [LenientThis] attribute EventHandler onreadystatechange;
};
Document implements GlobalEventHandlers;
```

#### 3.1.2 <dfn>Resource metadata management</dfn>

`document` . [`referrer`](#76.html_dom-document-referrer)

Returns [the address](#76.html_the-document's-address) of the [`Document`](#76.html_document) from which the user navigated to this one, unless it was blocked or there was no such document, in which case it returns the empty string.

The [`noreferrer`](#76.html_link-type-noreferrer) link type can be used to block the referrer.

The <dfn id="76.html_dom-document-referrer" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-referrer">`referrer`</dfn> attribute must return [the document's referrer](#76.html_the-document's-referrer).

In the case of HTTP, the [`referrer`](#76.html_dom-document-referrer) IDL attribute will match the `Referer` (sic) header that was sent when [fetching](#76.html_fetch) the current page.

Typically user agents are configured to not report referrers in the case where the referrer uses an encrypted protocol and the current page does not (e.g. when navigating from an `https:` page to an `http:` page).

* * *

`document` . [`cookie`](#76.html_dom-document-cookie) [ = `value` ]

Returns the HTTP cookies that apply to the [`Document`](#76.html_document). If there are no cookies or cookies can't be applied to this resource, the empty string will be returned.

Can be set, to add a new cookie to the element's set of HTTP cookies.

If the contents are [sandboxed into a unique origin](#76.html_sandboxed-origin-browsing-context-flag) (e.g. in an [`iframe`](#76.html_the-iframe-element) with the [`sandbox`](#76.html_attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute), a [`SecurityError`](#76.html_securityerror) exception will be thrown on getting and setting.

The <dfn id="76.html_dom-document-cookie" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-cookie">`cookie`</dfn> attribute represents the cookies of the resource identified by [the document's address](#76.html_the-document's-address).

A [`Document`](#76.html_document) object that falls into one of the following conditions is a <dfn id="76.html_cookie-averse-document-object">cookie-averse `Document` object</dfn>:

*   A [`Document`](#76.html_document) that has no [browsing context](#76.html_browsing-context).
*   A [`Document`](#76.html_document) whose [address](#76.html_the-document's-address) does not use a server-based naming authority.

On getting, if the document is a [cookie-averse `Document` object](#76.html_cookie-averse-document-object), then the user agent must return the empty string. Otherwise, if the [`Document`](#76.html_document)'s [origin](#76.html_origin-0) is not a scheme/host/port tuple, the user agent must throw a [`SecurityError`](#76.html_securityerror) exception. Otherwise, the user agent must first [obtain the storage mutex](#76.html_obtain-the-storage-mutex) and then return the cookie-string for [the document's address](#76.html_the-document's-address) for a "non-HTTP" API, decoded using the [UTF-8 decoder](#76.html_utf-8-decoder). [[COOKIES]](#76.html_refsCOOKIES) [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/3b31360aee12a981464d233e49df16cd.jpg)](#76.html_fingerprinting-vector)

On setting, if the document is a [cookie-averse `Document` object](#76.html_cookie-averse-document-object), then the user agent must do nothing. Otherwise, if the [`Document`](#76.html_document)'s [origin](#76.html_origin-0) is not a scheme/host/port tuple, the user agent must throw a [`SecurityError`](#76.html_securityerror) exception. Otherwise, the user agent must [obtain the storage mutex](#76.html_obtain-the-storage-mutex) and then act as it would when [receiving a set-cookie-string](#76.html_receives-a-set-cookie-string) for [the document's address](#76.html_the-document's-address) via a "non-HTTP" API, consisting of the new value encoded as UTF-8\. [[COOKIES]](#76.html_refsCOOKIES) [[RFC3629]](#76.html_refsRFC3629)

Since the [`cookie`](#76.html_dom-document-cookie) attribute is accessible across frames, the path restrictions on cookies are only a tool to help manage which cookies are sent to which parts of the site, and are not in any way a security feature.

* * *

`document` . [`lastModified`](#76.html_dom-document-lastmodified)

Returns the date of the last modification to the document, as reported by the server, in the form "`MM/DD/YYYY hh:mm:ss`", in the user's local time zone.

If the last modification date is not known, the current time is returned instead.

The <dfn id="76.html_dom-document-lastmodified" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-lastModified">`lastModified`</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return the date and time of the [`Document`](#76.html_document)'s source file's last modification, in the user's local time zone, in the following format:

1.  The month component of the date.
2.  A "/" (U+002F) character.
3.  The day component of the date.
4.  A "/" (U+002F) character.
5.  The year component of the date.
6.  A U+0020 SPACE character.
7.  The hours component of the time.
8.  A ":" (U+003A) character.
9.  The minutes component of the time.
10.  A ":" (U+003A) character.
11.  The seconds component of the time.

All the numeric components above, other than the year, must be given as two [ASCII digits](#76.html_ascii-digits) representing the number in base ten, zero-padded if necessary. The year must be given as the shortest possible string of four or more [ASCII digits](#76.html_ascii-digits) representing the number in base ten, zero-padded if necessary.

The [`Document`](#76.html_document)'s source file's last modification date and time must be derived from relevant features of the networking protocols used, e.g. from the value of the HTTP `Last-Modified` header of the document, or from metadata in the file system for local files. If the last modification date and time are not known, the attribute must return the current date and time in the above format.

* * *

`document` . [`readyState`](#76.html_dom-document-readystate)

Returns "`loading`" while the [`Document`](#76.html_document) is loading, "`interactive`" once it is finished parsing but still loading sub-resources, and "`complete`" once it has loaded.

The [`readystatechange`](#76.html_event-readystatechange) event fires on the [`Document`](#76.html_document) object when this value changes.

Each document has a <dfn id="76.html_current-document-readiness">current document readiness</dfn>. When a [`Document`](#76.html_document) object is created, it must have its [current document readiness](#76.html_current-document-readiness) set to the string "`loading`" if the document is associated with an [HTML parser](#76.html_html-parser), an [XML parser](#76.html_xml-parser), or an XSLT processor, and to the string "`complete`" otherwise. Various algorithms during page loading affect this value. When the value is set, the user agent must [fire a simple event](#76.html_fire-a-simple-event) named <dfn id="76.html_event-readystatechange" data-anolis-xref="event-readystatechange">`readystatechange`</dfn> at the [`Document`](#76.html_document) object.

A [`Document`](#76.html_document) is said to have an <dfn id="76.html_active-parser">active parser</dfn> if it is associated with an [HTML parser](#76.html_html-parser) or an [XML parser](#76.html_xml-parser) that has not yet been [stopped](#76.html_stop-parsing) or [aborted](#76.html_abort-a-parser).

The <dfn id="76.html_dom-document-readystate" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-readyState">`readyState`</dfn> IDL attribute must, on getting, return the [current document readiness](#76.html_current-document-readiness).

#### 3.1.3 <dfn>DOM tree accessors</dfn>

<dfn id="77.html_the-html-element-0">The `html` element</dfn> of a document is the document's root element, if there is one and it's an [`html`](#77.html_the-html-element) element, or null otherwise.

* * *

`document` . [`head`](#77.html_dom-document-head)

Returns [the `head` element](#77.html_the-head-element-0).

<dfn id="77.html_the-head-element-0">The `head` element</dfn> of a document is the first [`head`](#77.html_the-head-element) element that is a child of [the `html` element](#77.html_the-html-element-0), if there is one, or null otherwise.

The <dfn id="77.html_dom-document-head" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-head">`head`</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return [the `head` element](#77.html_the-head-element-0) of the document (a [`head`](#77.html_the-head-element) element or null).

* * *

`document` . [`title`](#77.html_document.title) [ = `value` ]

Returns the document's title, as given by [the `title` element](#77.html_the-title-element-0).

Can be set, to update the document's title. If there is no [`head` element](#77.html_the-head-element-0), the new value is ignored.

In SVG documents, the `SVGDocument` interface's `title` attribute takes precedence.

<dfn id="77.html_the-title-element-0">The `title` element</dfn> of a document is the first [`title`](#77.html_the-title-element) element in the document (in tree order), if there is one, or null otherwise.

The <dfn id="77.html_document.title" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-title">`title`</dfn> attribute must, on getting, run the following algorithm:

1.  If the [root element](#77.html_root-element) is an [`svg`](#77.html_svg-0) element in the "`http://www.w3.org/2000/svg`" namespace, and the user agent supports SVG, then return the value that would have been returned by the IDL attribute of the same name on the `SVGDocument` interface. [[SVG]](#77.html_refsSVG)

2.  Otherwise, let `value` be a concatenation of the data of all the child [`Text`](#77.html_text-0) nodes of [the `title` element](#77.html_the-title-element-0), in [tree order](#77.html_tree-order), or the empty string if [the `title` element](#77.html_the-title-element-0) is null.

3.  [Strip and collapse whitespace](#77.html_strip-and-collapse-whitespace) in `value`.

4.  Return `value`.

On setting, the following algorithm must be run. Mutation events must be fired as appropriate.

1.  If the [root element](#77.html_root-element) is an [`svg`](#77.html_svg-0) element in the "`http://www.w3.org/2000/svg`" namespace, and the user agent supports SVG, then the setter must act as if it was the setter for the IDL attribute of the same name on the [`Document`](#77.html_document) interface defined by the SVG specification. Stop the algorithm here. [[SVG]](#77.html_refsSVG)

2.  If [the `title` element](#77.html_the-title-element-0) is null and [the `head` element](#77.html_the-head-element-0) is null, then the attribute must do nothing. Stop the algorithm here.
3.  If [the `title` element](#77.html_the-title-element-0) is null, then a new [`title`](#77.html_the-title-element) element must be created and appended to [the `head` element](#77.html_the-head-element-0). Let `element` be that element. Otherwise, let `element` be [the `title` element](#77.html_the-title-element-0).
4.  The children of `element` (if any) must all be removed.
5.  A single [`Text`](#77.html_text-0) node whose data is the new value being assigned must be appended to `element`.

The [`title`](#77.html_document.title) IDL attribute defined above must replace the attribute of the same name on the [`Document`](#77.html_document) interface defined by the SVG specification when the user agent supports both HTML and SVG. [[SVG]](#77.html_refsSVG)

* * *

`document` . [`body`](#77.html_dom-document-body) [ = `value` ]

Returns [the body element](#77.html_the-body-element-0).

Can be set, to replace [the body element](#77.html_the-body-element-0).

If the new value is not a [`body`](#77.html_the-body-element) or [`frameset`](#77.html_frameset) element, this will throw a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#77.html_hierarchyrequesterror) exception.

<dfn id="77.html_the-body-element-0">The body element</dfn> of a document is the first child of [the `html` element](#77.html_the-html-element-0) that is either a [`body`](#77.html_the-body-element) element or a [`frameset`](#77.html_frameset) element. If there is no such element, it is null.

The <dfn id="77.html_dom-document-body" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-body">`body`</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return [the body element](#77.html_the-body-element-0) of the document (either a [`body`](#77.html_the-body-element) element, a [`frameset`](#77.html_frameset) element, or null). On setting, the following algorithm must be run:

1.  If the new value is not a [`body`](#77.html_the-body-element) or [`frameset`](#77.html_frameset) element, then throw a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#77.html_hierarchyrequesterror) exception and abort these steps.
2.  Otherwise, if the new value is the same as [the body element](#77.html_the-body-element-0), do nothing. Abort these steps.
3.  Otherwise, if [the body element](#77.html_the-body-element-0) is not null, then replace that element with the new value in the DOM, as if the root element's `replaceChild()` method had been called with the new value and [the incumbent body element](#77.html_the-body-element-0) as its two arguments respectively, then abort these steps.
4.  Otherwise, if there is no root element, throw a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#77.html_hierarchyrequesterror) exception and abort these steps.
5.  Otherwise, [the body element](#77.html_the-body-element-0) is null, but there's a root element. Append the new value to the root element.

* * *

`document` . [`images`](#77.html_dom-document-images)

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#77.html_htmlcollection) of the [`img`](#77.html_the-img-element) elements in the [`Document`](#77.html_document).

`document` . [`embeds`](#77.html_dom-document-embeds)
`document` . [`plugins`](#77.html_dom-document-plugins)

Return an [`HTMLCollection`](#77.html_htmlcollection) of the [`embed`](#77.html_the-embed-element) elements in the [`Document`](#77.html_document).

`document` . [`links`](#77.html_dom-document-links)

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#77.html_htmlcollection) of the [`a`](#77.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#77.html_the-area-element) elements in the [`Document`](#77.html_document) that have [`href`](#77.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attributes.

`document` . [`forms`](#77.html_dom-document-forms)

Return an [`HTMLCollection`](#77.html_htmlcollection) of the [`form`](#77.html_the-form-element) elements in the [`Document`](#77.html_document).

`document` . [`scripts`](#77.html_dom-document-scripts)

Return an [`HTMLCollection`](#77.html_htmlcollection) of the [`script`](#77.html_the-script-element) elements in the [`Document`](#77.html_document).

The <dfn id="77.html_dom-document-images" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-images">`images`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#77.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#77.html_document) node, whose filter matches only [`img`](#77.html_the-img-element) elements.

The <dfn id="77.html_dom-document-embeds" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-embeds">`embeds`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#77.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#77.html_document) node, whose filter matches only [`embed`](#77.html_the-embed-element) elements.

The <dfn id="77.html_dom-document-plugins" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-plugins">`plugins`</dfn> attribute must return the same object as that returned by the [`embeds`](#77.html_dom-document-embeds) attribute.

The <dfn id="77.html_dom-document-links" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-links">`links`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#77.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#77.html_document) node, whose filter matches only [`a`](#77.html_the-a-element) elements with [`href`](#77.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attributes and [`area`](#77.html_the-area-element) elements with [`href`](#77.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attributes.

The <dfn id="77.html_dom-document-forms" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-forms">`forms`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#77.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#77.html_document) node, whose filter matches only [`form`](#77.html_the-form-element) elements.

The <dfn id="77.html_dom-document-scripts" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-scripts">`scripts`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#77.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#77.html_document) node, whose filter matches only [`script`](#77.html_the-script-element) elements.

* * *

`collection` = `document` . [`getElementsByName`](#77.html_dom-document-getelementsbyname)(`name`)

Returns a [`NodeList`](#77.html_nodelist) of elements in the [`Document`](#77.html_document) that have a `name` attribute with the value `name`.

The <dfn id="77.html_dom-document-getelementsbyname" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-getElementsByName">`getElementsByName(``name``)`</dfn> method takes a string `name`, and must return a [live](#77.html_live) [`NodeList`](#77.html_nodelist) containing all the [HTML elements](#77.html_html-elements) in that document that have a `name` attribute whose value is equal to the `name` argument (in a [case-sensitive](#77.html_case-sensitive) manner), in [tree order](#77.html_tree-order). When the method is invoked on a [`Document`](#77.html_document) object again with the same argument, the user agent may return the same as the object returned by the earlier call. In other cases, a new [`NodeList`](#77.html_nodelist) object must be returned.

* * *

The [`Document`](#77.html_document) interface [supports named properties](#77.html_support-named-properties). The [supported property names](#77.html_supported-property-names) at any moment consist of the values of the `name` content attributes of all the [`applet`](#77.html_the-applet-element), [exposed](#77.html_exposed) [`embed`](#77.html_the-embed-element), [`form`](#77.html_the-form-element), [`iframe`](#77.html_the-iframe-element), [`img`](#77.html_the-img-element), and [exposed](#77.html_exposed) [`object`](#77.html_the-object-element) elements in the [`Document`](#77.html_document) that have non-empty `name` content attributes, and the values of the [`id`](#77.html_the-id-attribute) content attributes of all the [`applet`](#77.html_the-applet-element) and [exposed](#77.html_exposed) [`object`](#77.html_the-object-element) elements in the [`Document`](#77.html_document) that have non-empty [`id`](#77.html_the-id-attribute) content attributes, and the values of the [`id`](#77.html_the-id-attribute) content attributes of all the [`img`](#77.html_the-img-element) elements in the [`Document`](#77.html_document) that have both non-empty `name` content attributes and non-empty [`id`](#77.html_the-id-attribute) content attributes. The [supported property names](#77.html_supported-property-names) must be in [tree order](#77.html_tree-order), ignoring later duplicates, with values from [`id`](#77.html_the-id-attribute) attributes coming before values from `name` attributes when the same element contributes both.

To [determine the value of a named property](#77.html_determine-the-value-of-a-named-property) `name` when <dfn id="77.html_dom-document-nameditem" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-namedItem">the `Document` object is indexed for property retrieval</dfn>, the user agent must return the value obtained using the following steps:

1.  Let `elements` be the list of [named elements](#77.html_dom-document-nameditem-filter) with the name `name` in the [`Document`](#77.html_document).

    There will be at least one such element, by definition.

2.  If `elements` has only one element, and that element is an [`iframe`](#77.html_the-iframe-element) element, then return the [`WindowProxy`](#77.html_windowproxy) object of the [nested browsing context](#77.html_nested-browsing-context) represented by that [`iframe`](#77.html_the-iframe-element) element, and abort these steps.

3.  Otherwise, if `elements` has only one element, return that element and abort these steps.

4.  Otherwise return an [`HTMLCollection`](#77.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#77.html_document) node, whose filter matches only [named elements](#77.html_dom-document-nameditem-filter) with the name `name`.

<dfn id="77.html_dom-document-nameditem-filter" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-nameditem-filter">Named elements</dfn> with the name `name`, for the purposes of the above algorithm, are those that are either:

*   [`applet`](#77.html_the-applet-element), [exposed](#77.html_exposed) [`embed`](#77.html_the-embed-element), [`form`](#77.html_the-form-element), [`iframe`](#77.html_the-iframe-element), [`img`](#77.html_the-img-element), or [exposed](#77.html_exposed) [`object`](#77.html_the-object-element) elements that have a `name` content attribute whose value is `name`, or
*   [`applet`](#77.html_the-applet-element) or [exposed](#77.html_exposed) [`object`](#77.html_the-object-element) elements that have an [`id`](#77.html_the-id-attribute) content attribute whose value is `name`, or
*   [`img`](#77.html_the-img-element) elements that have an [`id`](#77.html_the-id-attribute) content attribute whose value is `name`, and that have a non-empty `name` content attribute present also.

An [`embed`](#77.html_the-embed-element) or [`object`](#77.html_the-object-element) element is said to be <dfn id="77.html_exposed">exposed</dfn> if it has no [exposed](#77.html_exposed) [`object`](#77.html_the-object-element) ancestor, and, for [`object`](#77.html_the-object-element) elements, is additionally either not showing its [fallback content](#77.html_fallback-content) or has no [`object`](#77.html_the-object-element) or [`embed`](#77.html_the-embed-element) descendants.

* * *

The [`dir`](#77.html_dom-document-dir) attribute on the [`Document`](#77.html_document) interface is defined along with the [`dir`](#77.html_the-dir-attribute) content attribute.

### 3.2 Elements

#### 3.2.1 Semantics

Elements, attributes, and attribute values in HTML are defined (by this specification) to have certain meanings (semantics). For example, the [`ol`](#79.html_the-ol-element) element represents an ordered list, and the [`lang`](#79.html_attr-lang) attribute represents the language of the content.

These definitions allow HTML processors, such as Web browsers or search engines, to present and use documents and applications in a wide variety of contexts that the author might not have considered.

As a simple example, consider a Web page written by an author who only considered desktop computer Web browsers:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html>
 <head>
  <title>My Page</title>
 </head>
 <body>
  <h1>Welcome to my page</h1>
  <p>I like cars and lorries and have a big Jeep!</p>
  <h2>Where I live</h2>
  <p>I live in a small hut on a mountain!</p>
 </body>
</html>
```

Because HTML conveys *meaning*, rather than presentation, the same page can also be used by a small browser on a mobile phone, without any change to the page. Instead of headings being in large letters as on the desktop, for example, the browser on the mobile phone might use the same size text for the whole the page, but with the headings in bold.

But it goes further than just differences in screen size: the same page could equally be used by a blind user using a browser based around speech synthesis, which instead of displaying the page on a screen, reads the page to the user, e.g. using headphones. Instead of large text for the headings, the speech browser might use a different volume or a slower voice.

That's not all, either. Since the browsers know which parts of the page are the headings, they can create a document outline that the user can use to quickly navigate around the document, using keys for "jump to next heading" or "jump to previous heading". Such features are especially common with speech browsers, where users would otherwise find quickly navigating a page quite difficult.

Even beyond browsers, software can make use of this information. Search engines can use the headings to more effectively index a page, or to provide quick links to subsections of the page from their results. Tools can use the headings to create a table of contents (that is in fact how this very specification's table of contents is generated).

This example has focused on headings, but the same principle applies to all of the semantics in HTML.

Authors must not use elements, attributes, or attribute values for purposes other than their appropriate intended semantic purpose, as doing so prevents software from correctly processing the page.

For example, the following document is non-conforming, despite being syntactically correct:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en-GB">
 <head> <title> Demonstration </title> </head>
 <body>
  <table>
   <tr> <td> My favourite animal is the cat. </td> </tr>
   <tr>
    <td>
     —<a href="http://example.org/~ernest/"><cite>Ernest</cite></a>,
     in an essay from 1992
    </td>
   </tr>
  </table>
 </body>
</html>
```

...because the data placed in the cells is clearly not tabular data (and the [`cite`](#79.html_the-cite-element) element mis-used). This would make software that relies on these semantics fail: for example, a speech browser that allowed a blind user to navigate tables in the document would report the quote above as a table, confusing the user; similarly, a tool that extracted titles of works from pages would extract "Ernest" as the title of a work, even though it's actually a person's name, not a title.

A corrected version of this document might be:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en-GB">
 <head> <title> Demonstration </title> </head>
 <body>
  <blockquote>
   <p> My favourite animal is the cat. </p>
  </blockquote>
  <p>
   —<a href="http://example.org/~ernest/">Ernest</a>,
   in an essay from 1992
  </p>
 </body>
</html>
```

Authors must not use elements, attributes, or attribute values that are not permitted by this specification or [other applicable specifications](#79.html_other-applicable-specifications), as doing so makes it significantly harder for the language to be extended in the future.

In the next example, there is a non-conforming attribute value ("carpet") and a non-conforming attribute ("texture"), which is not permitted by this specification:

```
<label>Carpet: <input type="carpet" name="c" texture="deep pile"></label>
```

Here would be an alternative and correct way to mark this up:

```
<label>Carpet: <input type="text" class="carpet" name="c" data-texture="deep pile"></label>
```

Through scripting and using other mechanisms, the values of attributes, text, and indeed the entire structure of the document may change dynamically while a user agent is processing it. The semantics of a document at an instant in time are those represented by the state of the document at that instant in time, and the semantics of a document can therefore change over time. User agents must update their presentation of the document as this occurs.

HTML has a [`progress`](#79.html_the-progress-element) element that describes a progress bar. If its "value" attribute is dynamically updated by a script, the UA would update the rendering to show the progress changing.

#### 3.2.2 Elements in the DOM

The nodes representing [HTML elements](#80.html_html-elements) in the DOM must implement, and expose to scripts, the interfaces listed for them in the relevant sections of this specification. This includes [HTML elements](#80.html_html-elements) in [XML documents](#80.html_xml-documents), even when those documents are in another context (e.g. inside an XSLT transform).

Elements in the DOM <dfn id="80.html_represents" data-anolis-xref="represents">represent</dfn> things; that is, they have intrinsic *meaning*, also known as semantics.

For example, an [`ol`](#80.html_the-ol-element) element represents an ordered list.

The basic interface, from which all the [HTML elements](#80.html_html-elements)' interfaces inherit, and which must be used by elements that have no additional requirements, is the [`HTMLElement`](#80.html_htmlelement) interface.

```
interface HTMLElement : Element {
  // metadata attributes
           attribute DOMString title;
           attribute DOMString lang;
           attribute boolean translate;
           attribute DOMString dir;
  readonly attribute DOMStringMap dataset;

  // user interaction
           attribute boolean hidden;
  void click();
           attribute long tabIndex;
  void focus();
  void blur();
           attribute DOMString accessKey;
  readonly attribute DOMString accessKeyLabel;
           attribute DOMString contentEditable;
  readonly attribute boolean isContentEditable;
           attribute boolean spellcheck;
};
HTMLElement implements GlobalEventHandlers;

interface HTMLUnknownElement : HTMLElement { };
```

The [`HTMLElement`](#80.html_htmlelement) interface holds methods and attributes related to a number of disparate features, and the members of this interface are therefore described in various different sections of this specification.

The [`HTMLUnknownElement`](#80.html_htmlunknownelement) interface must be used for [HTML elements](#80.html_html-elements) that are not defined by this specification (or [other applicable specifications](#80.html_other-applicable-specifications)).

#### 3.2.3 Element definitions

Each element in this specification has a definition that includes the following information:

<dfn id="81.html_element-dfn-categories" data-anolis-xref="element-dfn-categories">Categories</dfn>

A list of [categories](#81.html_content-categories) to which the element belongs. These are used when defining the [content models](#81.html_content-models) for each element.

<dfn id="81.html_element-dfn-contexts" data-anolis-xref="element-dfn-contexts">Contexts in which this element can be used</dfn>

A *non-normative* description of where the element can be used. This information is redundant with the content models of elements that allow this one as a child, and is provided only as a convenience.

For simplicity, only the most specific expectations are listed. For example, an element that is both [flow content](#81.html_flow-content-1) and [phrasing content](#81.html_phrasing-content-1) can be used anywhere that either [flow content](#81.html_flow-content-1) or [phrasing content](#81.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected, but since anywhere that [flow content](#81.html_flow-content-1) is expected, [phrasing content](#81.html_phrasing-content-1) is also expected (since all [phrasing content](#81.html_phrasing-content-1) is [flow content](#81.html_flow-content-1)), only "where [phrasing content](#81.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected" will be listed.

<dfn id="81.html_element-dfn-content-model" data-anolis-xref="element-dfn-content-model">Content model</dfn>

A normative description of what content must be included as children and descendants of the element.

<dfn id="81.html_element-dfn-tag-omission" data-anolis-xref="element-dfn-tag-omission">Tag omission in text/html</dfn>

A *non-normative* description of whether, in the [`text/html`](#81.html_text/html) syntax, the [start](#81.html_syntax-start-tag) and [end](#81.html_syntax-end-tag) tags can be omitted. This information is redundant with the normative requirements given in the [optional tags](#81.html_syntax-tag-omission) section, and is provided in the element definitions only as a convenience.

<dfn id="81.html_element-dfn-attributes" data-anolis-xref="element-dfn-attributes">Content attributes</dfn>

A normative list of attributes that may be specified on the element (except where otherwise disallowed), along with non-normative descriptions of those attributes. (The content to the left of the dash is normative, the content to the right of the dash is not.)

<dfn id="81.html_element-dfn-dom" data-anolis-xref="element-dfn-dom">DOM interface</dfn>

A normative definition of a DOM interface that such elements must implement.

This is then followed by a description of what the element [represents](#81.html_represents), along with any additional normative conformance criteria that may apply to authors and implementations. Examples are sometimes also included.

##### 3.2.3.1 Attributes

Except where otherwise specified, attributes on [HTML elements](#81.html_html-elements) may have any string value, including the empty string. Except where explicitly stated, there is no restriction on what text can be specified in such attributes.

#### 3.2.4 <dfn>Content models</dfn>

Each element defined in this specification has a content model: a description of the element's expected [contents](#82.html_concept-html-contents). An [HTML element](#82.html_html-elements) must have contents that match the requirements described in the element's content model. The <dfn id="82.html_concept-html-contents" data-anolis-xref="concept-html-contents">contents</dfn> of an element are its children in the DOM, except for [`template`](#82.html_the-template-element) elements, where the children are those in the [template contents](#82.html_template-contents) (a separate [`DocumentFragment`](#82.html_documentfragment) assigned to the element when the element is created).

The [space characters](#82.html_space-character) are always allowed between elements. User agents represent these characters between elements in the source markup as [`Text`](#82.html_text-0) nodes in the DOM. Empty [`Text`](#82.html_text-0) nodes and [`Text`](#82.html_text-0) nodes consisting of just sequences of those characters are considered <dfn id="82.html_inter-element-whitespace">inter-element whitespace</dfn>.

[Inter-element whitespace](#82.html_inter-element-whitespace), comment nodes, and processing instruction nodes must be ignored when establishing whether an element's contents match the element's content model or not, and must be ignored when following algorithms that define document and element semantics.

Thus, an element `A` is said to be *preceded or followed* by a second element `B` if `A` and `B` have the same parent node and there are no other element nodes or [`Text`](#82.html_text-0) nodes (other than [inter-element whitespace](#82.html_inter-element-whitespace)) between them. Similarly, a node is the *only child* of an element if that element contains no other nodes other than [inter-element whitespace](#82.html_inter-element-whitespace), comment nodes, and processing instruction nodes.

Authors must not use [HTML elements](#82.html_html-elements) anywhere except where they are explicitly allowed, as defined for each element, or as explicitly required by other specifications. For XML compound documents, these contexts could be inside elements from other namespaces, if those elements are defined as providing the relevant contexts.

For example, the Atom specification defines a `content` element. When its `type` attribute has the value `xhtml`, the Atom specification requires that it contain a single HTML [`div`](#82.html_the-div-element) element. Thus, a [`div`](#82.html_the-div-element) element is allowed in that context, even though this is not explicitly normatively stated by this specification. [[ATOM]](#82.html_refsATOM)

In addition, [HTML elements](#82.html_html-elements) may be orphan nodes (i.e. without a parent node).

For example, creating a [`td`](#82.html_the-td-element) element and storing it in a global variable in a script is conforming, even though [`td`](#82.html_the-td-element) elements are otherwise only supposed to be used inside [`tr`](#82.html_the-tr-element) elements.

```
var data = {
  name: "Banana",
  cell: document.createElement('td'),
};
```

##### 3.2.4.1 Kinds of content

Each element in HTML falls into zero or more <dfn id="82.html_content-categories" data-anolis-xref="content categories">categories</dfn> that group elements with similar characteristics together. The following broad categories are used in this specification:

*   [Metadata content](#82.html_metadata-content-0)
*   [Flow content](#82.html_flow-content-1)
*   [Sectioning content](#82.html_sectioning-content-0)
*   [Heading content](#82.html_heading-content-0)
*   [Phrasing content](#82.html_phrasing-content-1)
*   [Embedded content](#82.html_embedded-content-2)
*   [Interactive content](#82.html_interactive-content-0)

Some elements also fall into other categories, which are defined in other parts of this specification.

These categories are related as follows:

![](Images/dcab54ef8909527b5fddfdf09701f1d9.jpg)

Sectioning content, heading content, phrasing content, embedded content, and interactive content are all types of flow content. Metadata is sometimes flow content. Metadata and interactive content are sometimes phrasing content. Embedded content is also a type of phrasing content, and sometimes is interactive content.

Other categories are also used for specific purposes, e.g. form controls are specified using a number of categories to define common requirements. Some elements have unique requirements and do not fit into any particular category.

###### 3.2.4.1.1 Metadata content

<dfn id="82.html_metadata-content-0">Metadata content</dfn> is content that sets up the presentation or behavior of the rest of the content, or that sets up the relationship of the document with other documents, or that conveys other "out of band" information.

*   [`base`](#82.html_the-base-element)
*   [`link`](#82.html_the-link-element)
*   [`meta`](#82.html_the-meta-element)
*   [`noscript`](#82.html_the-noscript-element)
*   [`script`](#82.html_the-script-element)
*   [`style`](#82.html_the-style-element)
*   [`template`](#82.html_the-template-element)
*   [`title`](#82.html_the-title-element)

Elements from other namespaces whose semantics are primarily metadata-related (e.g. RDF) are also [metadata content](#82.html_metadata-content-0).

Thus, in the XML serialization, one can use RDF, like this:

```
<html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"
      xmlns:r="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#">
 <head>
  <title>Hedral's Home Page</title>
  <r:RDF>
   <Person xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/10/swap/pim/contact#"
           r:about="http://hedral.example.com/#">
    <fullName>Cat Hedral</fullName>
    <mailbox r:resource="mailto:hedral@damowmow.com"/>
    <personalTitle>Sir</personalTitle>
   </Person>
  </r:RDF>
 </head>
 <body>
  <h1>My home page</h1>
  <p>I like playing with string, I guess. Sister says squirrels are fun
  too so sometimes I follow her to play with them.</p>
 </body>
</html>
```

This isn't possible in the HTML serialization, however.

###### 3.2.4.1.3 Sectioning content

<dfn id="82.html_sectioning-content-0">Sectioning content</dfn> is content that defines the scope of [headings](#82.html_heading-content-0) and [footers](#82.html_the-footer-element).

*   [`article`](#82.html_the-article-element)
*   [`aside`](#82.html_the-aside-element)
*   [`nav`](#82.html_the-nav-element)
*   [`section`](#82.html_the-section-element)

Each [sectioning content](#82.html_sectioning-content-0) element potentially has a heading and an [outline](#82.html_outline). See the section on [headings and sections](#82.html_headings-and-sections) for further details.

There are also certain elements that are [sectioning roots](#82.html_sectioning-root). These are distinct from [sectioning content](#82.html_sectioning-content-0), but they can also have an [outline](#82.html_outline).

###### 3.2.4.1.4 Heading content

<dfn id="82.html_heading-content-0">Heading content</dfn> defines the header of a section (whether explicitly marked up using [sectioning content](#82.html_sectioning-content-0) elements, or implied by the heading content itself).

*   [`h1`](#82.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)
*   [`h2`](#82.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)

*   [`h6`](#82.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)
