Most elements that are categorized as phrasing content can only contain elements that are themselves categorized as phrasing content, not any flow content.

<dfn id="82.html_text-content" data-anolis-xref="text content">Text</dfn>, in the context of content models, means either nothing, or [`Text`](#82.html_text-0) nodes. [Text](#82.html_text-content) is sometimes used as a content model on its own, but is also [phrasing content](#82.html_phrasing-content-1), and can be [inter-element whitespace](#82.html_inter-element-whitespace) (if the [`Text`](#82.html_text-0) nodes are empty or contain just [space characters](#82.html_space-character)).

[`Text`](#82.html_text-0) nodes and attribute values must consist of [Unicode characters](#82.html_unicode-character), must not contain U+0000 characters, must not contain permanently undefined Unicode characters (noncharacters), and must not contain [control characters](#82.html_control-characters) other than [space characters](#82.html_space-character). This specification includes extra constraints on the exact value of [`Text`](#82.html_text-0) nodes and attribute values depending on their precise context.

###### 3.2.4.1.6 Embedded content

<dfn id="82.html_embedded-content-2">Embedded content</dfn> is content that imports another resource into the document, or content from another vocabulary that is inserted into the document.

*   [`audio`](#82.html_the-audio-element)
*   [`canvas`](#82.html_the-canvas-element)
*   [`embed`](#82.html_the-embed-element)
*   [`iframe`](#82.html_the-iframe-element)
*   [`img`](#82.html_the-img-element)
*   [`math`](#82.html_math)
*   [`object`](#82.html_the-object-element)
*   [`svg`](#82.html_svg-0)
*   [`video`](#82.html_the-video-element)

Elements that are from namespaces other than the [HTML namespace](#82.html_html-namespace-0) and that convey content but not metadata, are [embedded content](#82.html_embedded-content-2) for the purposes of the content models defined in this specification. (For example, MathML, or SVG.)

Some embedded content elements can have <dfn id="82.html_fallback-content">fallback content</dfn>: content that is to be used when the external resource cannot be used (e.g. because it is of an unsupported format). The element definitions state what the fallback is, if any.

###### 3.2.4.1.7 Interactive content

<dfn id="82.html_interactive-content-0">Interactive content</dfn> is content that is specifically intended for user interaction.

*   [`a`](#82.html_the-a-element)
*   [`audio`](#82.html_the-audio-element) (if the [`controls`](#82.html_attr-media-controls) attribute is present)
*   [`button`](#82.html_the-button-element)
*   [`embed`](#82.html_the-embed-element)
*   [`iframe`](#82.html_the-iframe-element)
*   [`img`](#82.html_the-img-element) (if the [`usemap`](#82.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap) attribute is present)
*   [`input`](#82.html_the-input-element) (if the [`type`](#82.html_attr-input-type) attribute is *not* in the [Hidden](#82.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state)
*   [`keygen`](#82.html_the-keygen-element)
*   [`label`](#82.html_the-label-element)
*   [`object`](#82.html_the-object-element) (if the [`usemap`](#82.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap) attribute is present)
*   [`select`](#82.html_the-select-element)
*   [`textarea`](#82.html_the-textarea-element)
*   [`video`](#82.html_the-video-element) (if the [`controls`](#82.html_attr-media-controls) attribute is present)

Certain elements in HTML have an [activation behavior](#82.html_activation-behavior), which means that the user can activate them. This triggers a sequence of events dependent on the activation mechanism, and normally culminating in a [`click`](#82.html_event-click) event, as described below.

The user agent should allow the user to manually trigger elements that have an [activation behavior](#82.html_activation-behavior), for instance using keyboard or voice input, or through mouse clicks. When the user triggers an element with a defined [activation behavior](#82.html_activation-behavior) in a manner other than clicking it, the default action of the interaction event must be to [run synthetic click activation steps](#82.html_run-synthetic-click-activation-steps) on the element.

Each element has a `click in progress` flag, initially set to false.

When a user agent is to <dfn id="82.html_run-synthetic-click-activation-steps">run synthetic click activation steps</dfn> on an element, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  If the element's `click in progress` flag is set to true, then abort these steps.

2.  Set the `click in progress` flag on the element to true.

3.  [Run pre-click activation steps](#82.html_run-pre-click-activation-steps) on the element.

4.  [Fire a `click` event](#82.html_fire-a-click-event) at the element. If the [run synthetic click activation steps](#82.html_run-synthetic-click-activation-steps) algorithm was invoked because the [`click()`](#82.html_dom-click) method was invoked, then the [`isTrusted`](#82.html_dom-event-istrusted) attribute must be initialized to false.

5.  If this [`click`](#82.html_event-click) event is not canceled, [run post-click activation steps](#82.html_run-post-click-activation-steps) on the element.

    If the event *is* canceled, the user agent must [run canceled activation steps](#82.html_run-canceled-activation-steps) on the element instead.

6.  Set the `click in progress` flag on the element to false.

When a pointing device is clicked, the user agent must run these steps:

1.  If the element's `click in progress` flag is set to true, then abort these steps.

2.  Set the `click in progress` flag on the element to true.

3.  Let `e` be the [nearest activatable element](#82.html_nearest-activatable-element) of the element designated by the user (defined below), if any.

4.  If there is an element `e`, [run pre-click activation steps](#82.html_run-pre-click-activation-steps) on it.

5.  [Dispatch](#82.html_concept-event-dispatch) the required [`click`](#82.html_event-click) event.

    If there is an element `e` and the [`click`](#82.html_event-click) event is not canceled, [run post-click activation steps](#82.html_run-post-click-activation-steps) on element `e`.

    If there is an element `e` and the event *is* canceled, [run canceled activation steps](#82.html_run-canceled-activation-steps) on element `e`.

6.  Set the `click in progress` flag on the element to false.

The algorithms above don't run for arbitrary synthetic events dispatched by author script. The [`click()`](#82.html_dom-click) method can be used to make the [run synthetic click activation steps](#82.html_run-synthetic-click-activation-steps) algorithm happen programmatically.

Click-focusing behavior (e.g. the focusing of a text field when user clicks in one) typically happens before the click, when the mouse button is first depressed, and is therefore not discussed here.

Given an element `target`, the <dfn id="82.html_nearest-activatable-element">nearest activatable element</dfn> is the element returned by the following algorithm:

1.  If `target` has a defined [activation behavior](#82.html_activation-behavior), then return `target` and abort these steps.

2.  If `target` has a parent element, then set `target` to that parent element and return to the first step.

3.  Otherwise, there is no [nearest activatable element](#82.html_nearest-activatable-element).

When a user agent is to <dfn id="82.html_run-pre-click-activation-steps">run pre-click activation steps</dfn> on an element, it must run the <dfn id="82.html_pre-click-activation-steps">pre-click activation steps</dfn> defined for that element, if any.

When a user agent is to <dfn id="82.html_run-canceled-activation-steps">run canceled activation steps</dfn> on an element, it must run the <dfn id="82.html_canceled-activation-steps">canceled activation steps</dfn> defined for that element, if any.

When a user agent is to <dfn id="82.html_run-post-click-activation-steps">run post-click activation steps</dfn> on an element, it must run the <dfn id="82.html_activation-behavior">activation behavior</dfn> defined for that element, if any. Activation behaviors can refer to the [`click`](#82.html_event-click) event that was fired by the steps above leading up to this point.

###### 3.2.4.1.8 Palpable content

As a general rule, elements whose content model allows any [flow content](#82.html_flow-content-1) or [phrasing content](#82.html_phrasing-content-1) should have at least one node in its [contents](#82.html_concept-html-contents) that is <dfn id="82.html_palpable-content-0">palpable content</dfn> and that does not have the [`hidden`](#82.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute specified.

This requirement is not a hard requirement, however, as there are many cases where an element can be empty legitimately, for example when it is used as a placeholder which will later be filled in by a script, or when the element is part of a template and would on most pages be filled in but on some pages is not relevant.

Conformance checkers are encouraged to provide a mechanism for authors to find elements that fail to fulfill this requirement, as an authoring aid.

The following elements are palpable content:

*   [`a`](#82.html_the-a-element)
*   [`abbr`](#82.html_the-abbr-element)
*   [`address`](#82.html_the-address-element)

###### 3.2.4.1.9 Script-supporting elements

<dfn id="82.html_script-supporting-elements-0">Script-supporting elements</dfn> are those that do not [represent](#82.html_represents) anything themselves (i.e. they are not rendered), but are used to support scripts, e.g. to provide functionality for the user.

The following elements are script-supporting elements:

*   [`script`](#82.html_the-script-element)
*   [`template`](#82.html_the-template-element)

##### 3.2.4.2 Transparent content models

Some elements are described as <dfn id="82.html_transparent">transparent</dfn>; they have "transparent" in the description of their content model. The content model of a [transparent](#82.html_transparent) element is derived from the content model of its parent element: the elements required in the part of the content model that is "transparent" are the same elements as required in the part of the content model of the parent of the transparent element in which the transparent element finds itself.

For instance, an [`ins`](#82.html_the-ins-element) element inside a [`ruby`](#82.html_the-ruby-element) element cannot contain an [`rt`](#82.html_the-rt-element) element, because the part of the [`ruby`](#82.html_the-ruby-element) element's content model that allows [`ins`](#82.html_the-ins-element) elements is the part that allows [phrasing content](#82.html_phrasing-content-1), and the [`rt`](#82.html_the-rt-element) element is not [phrasing content](#82.html_phrasing-content-1).

In some cases, where transparent elements are nested in each other, the process has to be applied iteratively.

Consider the following markup fragment:

```
<p><object><param><ins><map><a href="/">Apples</a></map></ins></object></p>
```

To check whether "Apples" is allowed inside the [`a`](#82.html_the-a-element) element, the content models are examined. The [`a`](#82.html_the-a-element) element's content model is transparent, as is the [`map`](#82.html_the-map-element) element's, as is the [`ins`](#82.html_the-ins-element) element's, as is the part of the [`object`](#82.html_the-object-element) element's in which the [`ins`](#82.html_the-ins-element) element is found. The [`object`](#82.html_the-object-element) element is found in the [`p`](#82.html_the-p-element) element, whose content model is [phrasing content](#82.html_phrasing-content-1). Thus, "Apples" is allowed, as text is phrasing content.

When a transparent element has no parent, then the part of its content model that is "transparent" must instead be treated as accepting any [flow content](#82.html_flow-content-1).

##### 3.2.4.3 Paragraphs

The term [paragraph](#82.html_paragraph) as defined in this section is used for more than just the definition of the [`p`](#82.html_the-p-element) element. The [paragraph](#82.html_paragraph) concept defined here is used to describe how to interpret documents. The [`p`](#82.html_the-p-element) element is merely one of several ways of marking up a [paragraph](#82.html_paragraph).

A <dfn id="82.html_paragraph">paragraph</dfn> is typically a run of [phrasing content](#82.html_phrasing-content-1) that forms a block of text with one or more sentences that discuss a particular topic, as in typography, but can also be used for more general thematic grouping. For instance, an address is also a paragraph, as is a part of a form, a byline, or a stanza in a poem.

In the following example, there are two paragraphs in a section. There is also a heading, which contains phrasing content that is not a paragraph. Note how the comments and [inter-element whitespace](#82.html_inter-element-whitespace) do not form paragraphs.

```
<section>
  <h1>Example of paragraphs</h1>
  This is the <em>first</em> paragraph in this example.
  <p>This is the second.</p>
  <!-- This is not a paragraph. -->
</section>
```

Paragraphs in [flow content](#82.html_flow-content-1) are defined relative to what the document looks like without the [`a`](#82.html_the-a-element), [`ins`](#82.html_the-ins-element), [`del`](#82.html_the-del-element), and [`map`](#82.html_the-map-element) elements complicating matters, since those elements, with their hybrid content models, can straddle paragraph boundaries, as shown in the first two examples below.

Generally, having elements straddle paragraph boundaries is best avoided. Maintaining such markup can be difficult.

The following example takes the markup from the earlier example and puts [`ins`](#82.html_the-ins-element) and [`del`](#82.html_the-del-element) elements around some of the markup to show that the text was changed (though in this case, the changes admittedly don't make much sense). Notice how this example has exactly the same paragraphs as the previous one, despite the [`ins`](#82.html_the-ins-element) and [`del`](#82.html_the-del-element) elements — the [`ins`](#82.html_the-ins-element) element straddles the heading and the first paragraph, and the [`del`](#82.html_the-del-element) element straddles the boundary between the two paragraphs.

```
<section>
  <ins><h1>Example of paragraphs</h1>
  This is the <em>first</em> paragraph in</ins> this example<del>.
  <p>This is the second.</p></del>
  <!-- This is not a paragraph. -->
</section>
```

Let `view` be a view of the DOM that replaces all [`a`](#82.html_the-a-element), [`ins`](#82.html_the-ins-element), [`del`](#82.html_the-del-element), and [`map`](#82.html_the-map-element) elements in the document with their [contents](#82.html_concept-html-contents). Then, in `view`, for each run of sibling [phrasing content](#82.html_phrasing-content-1) nodes uninterrupted by other types of content, in an element that accepts content other than [phrasing content](#82.html_phrasing-content-1) as well as [phrasing content](#82.html_phrasing-content-1), let `first` be the first node of the run, and let `last` be the last node of the run. For each such run that consists of at least one node that is neither [embedded content](#82.html_embedded-content-2) nor [inter-element whitespace](#82.html_inter-element-whitespace), a paragraph exists in the original DOM from immediately before `first` to immediately after `last`. (Paragraphs can thus span across [`a`](#82.html_the-a-element), [`ins`](#82.html_the-ins-element), [`del`](#82.html_the-del-element), and [`map`](#82.html_the-map-element) elements.)

Conformance checkers may warn authors of cases where they have paragraphs that overlap each other (this can happen with [`object`](#82.html_the-object-element), [`video`](#82.html_the-video-element), [`audio`](#82.html_the-audio-element), and [`canvas`](#82.html_the-canvas-element) elements, and indirectly through elements in other namespaces that allow HTML to be further embedded therein, like [`svg`](#82.html_svg-0) or [`math`](#82.html_math)).

A [paragraph](#82.html_paragraph) is also formed explicitly by [`p`](#82.html_the-p-element) elements.

The [`p`](#82.html_the-p-element) element can be used to wrap individual paragraphs when there would otherwise not be any content other than phrasing content to separate the paragraphs from each other.

In the following example, the link spans half of the first paragraph, all of the heading separating the two paragraphs, and half of the second paragraph. It straddles the paragraphs and the heading.

```
<header>
 Welcome!
 <a href="about.html">
  This is home of...
  <h1>The Falcons!</h1>
  The Lockheed Martin multirole jet fighter aircraft!
 </a>
 This page discusses the F-16 Fighting Falcon's innermost secrets.
</header>
```

Here is another way of marking this up, this time showing the paragraphs explicitly, and splitting the one link element into three:

```
<header>
 <p>Welcome! <a href="about.html">This is home of...</a></p>
 <h1><a href="about.html">The Falcons!</a></h1>
 <p><a href="about.html">The Lockheed Martin multirole jet
 fighter aircraft!</a> This page discusses the F-16 Fighting
 Falcon's innermost secrets.</p>
</header>
```

It is possible for paragraphs to overlap when using certain elements that define fallback content. For example, in the following section:

```
<section>
 <h1>My Cats</h1>
 You can play with my cat simulator.
 <object data="cats.sim">
  To see the cat simulator, use one of the following links:
  <ul>
   <li><a href="cats.sim">Download simulator file</a>
   <li><a href="http://sims.example.com/watch?v=LYds5xY4INU">Use online simulator</a>
  </ul>
  Alternatively, upgrade to the Mellblom Browser.
 </object>
 I'm quite proud of it.
</section>
```

There are five paragraphs:

1.  The paragraph that says "You can play with my cat simulator. *object* I'm quite proud of it.", where *object* is the [`object`](#82.html_the-object-element) element.
2.  The paragraph that says "To see the cat simulator, use one of the following links:".
3.  The paragraph that says "Download simulator file".
4.  The paragraph that says "Use online simulator".
5.  The paragraph that says "Alternatively, upgrade to the Mellblom Browser.".

The first paragraph is overlapped by the other four. A user agent that supports the "cats.sim" resource will only show the first one, but a user agent that shows the fallback will confusingly show the first sentence of the first paragraph as if it was in the same paragraph as the second one, and will show the last paragraph as if it was at the start of the second sentence of the first paragraph.

To avoid this confusion, explicit [`p`](#82.html_the-p-element) elements can be used. For example:

```
<section>
 <h1>My Cats</h1>
 <p>You can play with my cat simulator.</p>
 <object data="cats.sim">
  <p>To see the cat simulator, use one of the following links:</p>
  <ul>
   <li><a href="cats.sim">Download simulator file</a>
   <li><a href="http://sims.example.com/watch?v=LYds5xY4INU">Use online simulator</a>
  </ul>
  <p>Alternatively, upgrade to the Mellblom Browser.</p>
 </object>
 <p>I'm quite proud of it.</p>
</section>
```

#### 3.2.5 <dfn>Global attributes</dfn>

The following attributes are common to and may be specified on all [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements) (even those not defined in this specification):

*   [`accesskey`](#83.html_the-accesskey-attribute)
*   [`class`](#83.html_classes)
*   [`contenteditable`](#83.html_attr-contenteditable)
*   [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute)
*   [`hidden`](#83.html_the-hidden-attribute)
*   [`id`](#83.html_the-id-attribute)
*   [`lang`](#83.html_attr-lang)
*   [`spellcheck`](#83.html_attr-spellcheck)
*   [`style`](#83.html_the-style-attribute)
*   [`tabindex`](#83.html_attr-tabindex)
*   [`title`](#83.html_attr-title)
*   [`translate`](#83.html_attr-translate)

These attributes are only defined by this specification as attributes for [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements). When this specification refers to elements having these attributes, elements from namespaces that are not defined as having these attributes must not be considered as being elements with these attributes.

For example, in the following XML fragment, the "`bogus`" element does not have a [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute as defined in this specification, despite having an attribute with the literal name "`dir`". Thus, [the directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) of the inner-most [`span`](#83.html_the-span-element) element is '[rtl](#83.html_concept-rtl)', inherited from the [`div`](#83.html_the-div-element) element indirectly through the "`bogus`" element.

```
<div xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" dir="rtl">
 <bogus xmlns="http://example.net/ns" dir="ltr">
  <span xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">
  </span>
 </bogus>
</div>
```

* * *

To enable assistive technology products to expose a more fine-grained interface than is otherwise possible with HTML elements and attributes, a set of [annotations for assistive technology products](#83.html_wai-aria) can be specified (the ARIA [`role`](#83.html_attr-aria-role) and `aria-*` attributes). [[ARIA]](#83.html_refsARIA)
