* * *

[Custom data attributes](#83.html_custom-data-attribute) (e.g. `data-foldername` or `data-msgid`) can be specified on any [HTML element](#83.html_html-elements), to store custom data specific to the page.

* * *

In [HTML documents](#83.html_html-documents), elements in the [HTML namespace](#83.html_html-namespace-0) may have an `xmlns` attribute specified, if, and only if, it has the exact value "`http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml`". This does not apply to [XML documents](#83.html_xml-documents).

In HTML, the `xmlns` attribute has absolutely no effect. It is basically a talisman. It is allowed merely to make migration to and from XHTML mildly easier. When parsed by an [HTML parser](#83.html_html-parser), the attribute ends up in no namespace, not the "`http://www.w3.org/2000/xmlns/`" namespace like namespace declaration attributes in XML do.

In XML, an `xmlns` attribute is part of the namespace declaration mechanism, and an element cannot actually have an `xmlns` attribute in no namespace specified.

* * *

The XML specification also allows the use of the `xml:space` attribute in the [XML namespace](#83.html_xml-namespace) on any element in an [XML document](#83.html_xml-documents). This attribute has no effect on [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements), as the default behavior in HTML is to preserve whitespace. [[XML]](#83.html_refsXML)

There is no way to serialize the `xml:space` attribute on [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements) in the [`text/html`](#83.html_text/html) syntax.

##### 3.2.5.1 The <dfn id="83.html_attr-id" data-anolis-xref="attr-id">`id`</dfn> attribute

The [`id`](#83.html_the-id-attribute) attribute specifies its element's [unique identifier (ID)](#83.html_concept-id). [[DOM]](#83.html_refsDOM)

The value must be unique amongst all the [IDs](#83.html_concept-id) in the element's [home subtree](#83.html_home-subtree) and must contain at least one character. The value must not contain any [space characters](#83.html_space-character).

There are no other restrictions on what form an ID can take; in particular, IDs can consist of just digits, start with a digit, start with an underscore, consist of just punctuation, etc.

An element's [unique identifier](#83.html_concept-id) can be used for a variety of purposes, most notably as a way to link to specific parts of a document using fragment identifiers, as a way to target an element when scripting, and as a way to style a specific element from CSS.

Identifiers are opaque strings. Particular meanings should not be derived from the value of the [`id`](#83.html_the-id-attribute) attribute.

##### 3.2.5.2 The [`title`](#83.html_attr-title) attribute

The <dfn id="83.html_attr-title" data-anolis-xref="attr-title">`title`</dfn> attribute [represents](#83.html_represents) advisory information for the element, such as would be appropriate for a tooltip. On a link, this could be the title or a description of the target resource; on an image, it could be the image credit or a description of the image; on a paragraph, it could be a footnote or commentary on the text; on a citation, it could be further information about the source; on [interactive content](#83.html_interactive-content-0), it could be a label for, or instructions for, use of the element; and so forth. The value is text.

Relying on the [`title`](#83.html_attr-title) attribute is currently discouraged as many user agents do not expose the attribute in an accessible manner as required by this specification (e.g. requiring a pointing device such as a mouse to cause a tooltip to appear, which excludes keyboard-only users and touch-only users, such as anyone with a modern phone or tablet).

If this attribute is omitted from an element, then it implies that the [`title`](#83.html_attr-title) attribute of the nearest ancestor [HTML element](#83.html_html-elements) with a [`title`](#83.html_attr-title) attribute set is also relevant to this element. Setting the attribute overrides this, explicitly stating that the advisory information of any ancestors is not relevant to this element. Setting the attribute to the empty string indicates that the element has no advisory information.

If the [`title`](#83.html_attr-title) attribute's value contains "LF" (U+000A) characters, the content is split into multiple lines. Each "LF" (U+000A) character represents a line break.

Caution is advised with respect to the use of newlines in [`title`](#83.html_attr-title) attributes.

For instance, the following snippet actually defines an abbreviation's expansion *with a line break in it*:

```
<p>My logs show that there was some interest in <abbr title="Hypertext
Transport Protocol">HTTP</abbr> today.</p>
```

Some elements, such as [`link`](#83.html_the-link-element), [`abbr`](#83.html_the-abbr-element), and [`input`](#83.html_the-input-element), define additional semantics for the [`title`](#83.html_attr-title) attribute beyond the semantics described above.

The <dfn id="83.html_advisory-information">advisory information</dfn> of an element is the value that the following algorithm returns, with the algorithm being aborted once a value is returned. When the algorithm returns the empty string, then there is no advisory information.

1.  If the element is a [`link`](#83.html_the-link-element), [`style`](#83.html_the-style-element), [`dfn`](#83.html_the-dfn-element), or [`abbr`](#83.html_the-abbr-element) element, then: if the element has a `title` attribute, return the value of that attribute, otherwise, return the empty string.

2.  Otherwise, if the element has a [`title`](#83.html_attr-title) attribute, then return its value.

3.  Otherwise, if the element has a parent element, then return the parent element's [advisory information](#83.html_advisory-information).

4.  Otherwise, return the empty string.

User agents should inform the user when elements have [advisory information](#83.html_advisory-information), otherwise the information would not be discoverable.

* * *

The <dfn id="83.html_dom-title" data-anolis-xref="dom-title">`title`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#83.html_reflect) the [`title`](#83.html_attr-title) content attribute.

##### 3.2.5.3 The [`lang`](#83.html_attr-lang) and [`xml:lang`](#83.html_attr-xml-lang) attributes

The <dfn id="83.html_attr-lang" data-anolis-xref="attr-lang">`lang`</dfn> attribute (in no namespace) specifies the primary language for the element's contents and for any of the element's attributes that contain text. Its value must be a valid BCP 47 language tag, or the empty string. Setting the attribute to the empty string indicates that the primary language is unknown. [[BCP47]](#83.html_refsBCP47)

The <dfn id="83.html_attr-xml-lang" data-anolis-xref="attr-xml-lang">`lang`</dfn> attribute in the [XML namespace](#83.html_xml-namespace) is defined in XML. [[XML]](#83.html_refsXML)

If these attributes are omitted from an element, then the language of this element is the same as the language of its parent element, if any.

The [`lang`](#83.html_attr-lang) attribute in no namespace may be used on any [HTML element](#83.html_html-elements).

The [`lang` attribute in the XML namespace](#83.html_attr-xml-lang) may be used on [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements) in [XML documents](#83.html_xml-documents), as well as elements in other namespaces if the relevant specifications allow it (in particular, MathML and SVG allow [`lang` attributes in the XML namespace](#83.html_attr-xml-lang) to be specified on their elements). If both the [`lang`](#83.html_attr-lang) attribute in no namespace and the [`lang` attribute in the XML namespace](#83.html_attr-xml-lang) are specified on the same element, they must have exactly the same value when compared in an [ASCII case-insensitive](#83.html_ascii-case-insensitive) manner.

Authors must not use the [`lang` attribute in the XML namespace](#83.html_attr-xml-lang) on [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements) in [HTML documents](#83.html_html-documents). To ease migration to and from XHTML, authors may specify an attribute in no namespace with no prefix and with the literal localname "`xml:lang`" on [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements) in [HTML documents](#83.html_html-documents), but such attributes must only be specified if a [`lang`](#83.html_attr-lang) attribute in no namespace is also specified, and both attributes must have the same value when compared in an [ASCII case-insensitive](#83.html_ascii-case-insensitive) manner.

The attribute in no namespace with no prefix and with the literal localname "`xml:lang`" has no effect on language processing.

* * *

To determine the <dfn id="83.html_language">language</dfn> of a node, user agents must look at the nearest ancestor element (including the element itself if the node is an element) that has a [`lang` attribute in the XML namespace](#83.html_attr-xml-lang) set or is an [HTML element](#83.html_html-elements) and has a [`lang`](#83.html_attr-lang) in no namespace attribute set. That attribute specifies the language of the node (regardless of its value).

If both the [`lang`](#83.html_attr-lang) attribute in no namespace and the [`lang` attribute in the XML namespace](#83.html_attr-xml-lang) are set on an element, user agents must use the [`lang` attribute in the XML namespace](#83.html_attr-xml-lang), and the [`lang`](#83.html_attr-lang) attribute in no namespace must be [ignored](#83.html_ignore) for the purposes of determining the element's language.

If neither the node nor any of the node's ancestors, including the [root element](#83.html_root-element), have either attribute set, but there is a [pragma-set default language](#83.html_pragma-set-default-language) set, then that is the language of the node. If there is no [pragma-set default language](#83.html_pragma-set-default-language) set, then language information from a higher-level protocol (such as HTTP), if any, must be used as the final fallback language instead. In the absence of any such language information, and in cases where the higher-level protocol reports multiple languages, the language of the node is unknown, and the corresponding language tag is the empty string.

If the resulting value is not a recognized language tag, then it must be treated as an unknown language having the given language tag, distinct from all other languages. For the purposes of round-tripping or communicating with other services that expect language tags, user agents should pass unknown language tags through unmodified, and tagged as being BCP 47 language tags, so that subsequent services do not interpret the data as another type of language description. [[BCP47]](#83.html_refsBCP47)

Thus, for instance, an element with `lang="xyzzy"` would be matched by the selector `:lang(xyzzy)` (e.g. in CSS), but it would not be matched by `:lang(abcde)`, even though both are equally invalid. Similarly, if a Web browser and screen reader working in unison communicated about the language of the element, the browser would tell the screen reader that the language was "xyzzy", even if it knew it was invalid, just in case the screen reader actually supported a language with that tag after all. Even if the screen reader supported both BCP 47 and another syntax for encoding language names, and in that other syntax the string "xyzzy" was a way to denote the Belarusian language, it would be *incorrect* for the screen reader to then start treating text as Belarusian, because "xyzzy" is not how Belarusian is described in BCP 47 codes (BCP 47 uses the code "be" for Belarusian).

If the resulting value is the empty string, then it must be interpreted as meaning that the language of the node is explicitly unknown.

* * *

User agents may use the element's language to determine proper processing or rendering (e.g. in the selection of appropriate fonts or pronunciations, for dictionary selection, or for the user interfaces of form controls such as date pickers).

* * *

The <dfn id="83.html_dom-lang" data-anolis-xref="dom-lang">`lang`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#83.html_reflect) the [`lang`](#83.html_attr-lang) content attribute in no namespace.

##### 3.2.5.4 The [`translate`](#83.html_attr-translate) attribute

The <dfn id="83.html_attr-translate" data-anolis-xref="attr-translate">`translate`</dfn> attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#83.html_enumerated-attribute) that is used to specify whether an element's attribute values and the values of its [`Text`](#83.html_text-0) node children are to be translated when the page is localized, or whether to leave them unchanged.

The attribute's keywords are the empty string, `yes`, and `no`. The empty string and the `yes` keyword map to the *yes* state. The `no` keyword maps to the *no* state. In addition, there is a third state, the *inherit* state, which is the *missing value default* (and the *invalid value default*).

Each element (even non-HTML elements) has a <dfn id="83.html_translation-mode">translation mode</dfn>, which is in either the [translate-enabled](#83.html_translate-enabled) state or the [no-translate](#83.html_no-translate) state. If an [HTML element](#83.html_html-elements)'s [`translate`](#83.html_attr-translate) attribute is in the *yes* state, then the element's [translation mode](#83.html_translation-mode) is in the [translate-enabled](#83.html_translate-enabled) state; otherwise, if the element's [`translate`](#83.html_attr-translate) attribute is in the *no* state, then the element's [translation mode](#83.html_translation-mode) is in the [no-translate](#83.html_no-translate) state. Otherwise, either the element's [`translate`](#83.html_attr-translate) attribute is in the *inherit* state, or the element is not an [HTML element](#83.html_html-elements) and thus does not have a [`translate`](#83.html_attr-translate) attribute; in either case, the element's [translation mode](#83.html_translation-mode) is in the same state as its parent element's, if any, or in the [translate-enabled](#83.html_translate-enabled) state, if the element is a [root element](#83.html_root-element).

When an element is in the <dfn id="83.html_translate-enabled">translate-enabled</dfn> state, the element's [translatable attributes](#83.html_translatable-attributes) and the values of its [`Text`](#83.html_text-0) node children are to be translated when the page is localized. Attributes of the element that are not listed as [translatable attributes](#83.html_translatable-attributes) should not be translated.

When an element is in the <dfn id="83.html_no-translate">no-translate</dfn> state, the element's attribute values (including the values of [translatable attributes](#83.html_translatable-attributes)) and the values of its [`Text`](#83.html_text-0) node children are to be left as-is when the page is localized, e.g. because the element contains a person's name or a the name of a computer program.

The following attributes are <dfn id="83.html_translatable-attributes">translatable attributes</dfn>:

*   [`abbr`](#83.html_attr-th-abbr) on [`th`](#83.html_the-th-element) elements
*   `alt` on [`area`](#83.html_attr-area-alt), [`img`](#83.html_attr-img-alt), and [`input`](#83.html_attr-input-alt) elements
*   [`content`](#83.html_attr-meta-content) on [`meta`](#83.html_the-meta-element) elements, if the [`name`](#83.html_attr-meta-name) attribute specifies a metadata name whose value is known to be translatable
*   `download` on `a` and `area` elements
*   `label` on [`optgroup`](#83.html_attr-optgroup-label), [`option`](#83.html_attr-option-label), and [`track`](#83.html_attr-track-label) elements
*   [`lang`](#83.html_attr-lang) on [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements); must be "translated" to match the language used in the translation
*   `placeholder` on [`input`](#83.html_attr-input-placeholder) and [`textarea`](#83.html_attr-textarea-placeholder) elements
*   [`srcdoc`](#83.html_attr-iframe-srcdoc) on [`iframe`](#83.html_the-iframe-element) elements; must be parsed and recursively processed
*   [`style`](#83.html_the-style-attribute) on [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements); must be parsed and recursively processed (e.g. for the values of 'content' properties)
*   [`title`](#83.html_attr-title) on all [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements)
*   [`value`](#83.html_attr-input-value) on [`input`](#83.html_the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#83.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Button](#83.html_button-state-(type=button)) state or the [Reset Button](#83.html_reset-button-state-(type=reset)) state

* * *

The <dfn id="83.html_dom-translate" data-anolis-xref="dom-translate">`translate`</dfn> IDL attribute must, on getting, return true if the element's [translation mode](#83.html_translation-mode) is [translate-enabled](#83.html_translate-enabled), and false otherwise. On setting, it must set the content attribute's value to "`yes`" if the new value is true, and set the content attribute's value to "`no`" otherwise.

In this example, everything in the document is to be translated when the page is localized, except the sample keyboard input and sample program output:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html> <!-- default on the root element is translate=yes -->
 <head>
  <title>The Bee Game</title> <!-- implied translate=yes inherited from ancestors -->
 </head>
 <body>
  <p>The Bee Game is a text adventure game in English.</p>
  <p>When the game launches, the first thing you should do is type
  <kbd translate=no>eat honey</kbd>. The game will respond with:</p>
  <pre><samp translate=no>Yum yum! That was some good honey!</samp></pre>
 </body>
</html>
```

##### 3.2.5.5 The <dfn id="83.html_attr-xml-base" data-anolis-xref="attr-xml-base">`xml:base`</dfn> attribute (XML only)

The [`xml:base`](#83.html_the-xml:base-attribute-(xml-only)) attribute is defined in XML Base. [[XMLBASE]](#83.html_refsXMLBASE)

The [`xml:base`](#83.html_the-xml:base-attribute-(xml-only)) attribute may be used on [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements) of [XML documents](#83.html_xml-documents). Authors must not use the [`xml:base`](#83.html_the-xml:base-attribute-(xml-only)) attribute on [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements) in [HTML documents](#83.html_html-documents).

##### 3.2.5.6 The <dfn id="83.html_attr-dir" data-anolis-xref="attr-dir">`dir`</dfn> attribute

The [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute specifies the element's text directionality. The attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#83.html_enumerated-attribute) with the following keywords and states:

The <dfn id="83.html_attr-dir-ltr" data-anolis-xref="attr-dir-ltr">`ltr`</dfn> keyword, which maps to the <dfn id="83.html_attr-dir-ltr-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-dir-ltr-state">ltr</dfn> state

Indicates that the contents of the element are explicitly directionally isolated left-to-right text.

The <dfn id="83.html_attr-dir-rtl" data-anolis-xref="attr-dir-rtl">`rtl`</dfn> keyword, which maps to the <dfn id="83.html_attr-dir-rtl-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-dir-rtl-state">rtl</dfn> state

Indicates that the contents of the element are explicitly directionally isolated right-to-left text.

The <dfn id="83.html_attr-dir-auto" data-anolis-xref="attr-dir-auto">`auto`</dfn> keyword, which maps to the <dfn id="83.html_attr-dir-auto-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-dir-auto-state">auto</dfn> state

Indicates that the contents of the element are explicitly directionally isolated text, but that the direction is to be determined programmatically using the contents of the element (as described below).

The heuristic used by this state is very crude (it just looks at the first character with a strong directionality, in a manner analogous to the Paragraph Level determination in the bidirectional algorithm). Authors are urged to only use this value as a last resort when the direction of the text is truly unknown and no better server-side heuristic can be applied. [[BIDI]](#83.html_refsBIDI)

For [`textarea`](#83.html_the-textarea-element) and [`pre`](#83.html_the-pre-element) elements, the heuristic is applied on a per-paragraph level.

The attribute has no *invalid value default* and no *missing value default*.

* * *

<dfn id="83.html_the-directionality">The directionality</dfn> of an element (any element, not just an [HTML element](#83.html_html-elements)) is either '<dfn id="83.html_concept-ltr" data-anolis-xref="concept-ltr">ltr</dfn>' or '<dfn id="83.html_concept-rtl" data-anolis-xref="concept-rtl">rtl</dfn>', and is determined as per the first appropriate set of steps from the following list:

If the element's [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute is in the [ltr](#83.html_attr-dir-ltr-state) state
If the element is a [root element](#83.html_root-element) and the [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute is not in a defined state (i.e. it is not present or has an invalid value)
If the element is an [`input`](#83.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#83.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Telephone](#83.html_telephone-state-(type=tel)) state, and the [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute is not in a defined state (i.e. it is not present or has an invalid value)

[The directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) of the element is '[ltr](#83.html_concept-ltr)'.

If the element's [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute is in the [rtl](#83.html_attr-dir-rtl-state) state

[The directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) of the element is '[rtl](#83.html_concept-rtl)'.

If the element is an [`input`](#83.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#83.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Text](#83.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [Search](#83.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [Telephone](#83.html_telephone-state-(type=tel)), [URL](#83.html_url-state-(type=url)), or [E-mail](#83.html_e-mail-state-(type=email)) state, and the [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute is in the [auto](#83.html_attr-dir-auto-state) state
If the element is a [`textarea`](#83.html_the-textarea-element) element and the [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute is in the [auto](#83.html_attr-dir-auto-state) state

If the element's [value](#83.html_concept-fe-value) contains a character of bidirectional character type AL or R, and there is no character of bidirectional character type L anywhere before it in the element's [value](#83.html_concept-fe-value), then [the directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) of the element is '[rtl](#83.html_concept-rtl)'. [[BIDI]](#83.html_refsBIDI)

Otherwise, if the element's [value](#83.html_concept-fe-value) is not the empty string, or if the element is a [root element](#83.html_root-element), [the directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) of the element is '[ltr](#83.html_concept-ltr)'.

Otherwise, [the directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) of the element is the same as the element's parent element's [directionality](#83.html_the-directionality).

If the element's [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute is in the [auto](#83.html_attr-dir-auto-state) state
If the element is a [`bdi`](#83.html_the-bdi-element) element and the [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute is not in a defined state (i.e. it is not present or has an invalid value)

Find the first character in [tree order](#83.html_tree-order) that matches the following criteria:

*   The character is from a [`Text`](#83.html_text-0) node that is a descendant of the element whose [directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) is being determined.

*   The character is of bidirectional character type L, AL, or R. [[BIDI]](#83.html_refsBIDI)

*   The character is not in a [`Text`](#83.html_text-0) node that has an ancestor element that is a descendant of the element whose [directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) is being determined and that is either:

    *   A [`bdi`](#83.html_the-bdi-element) element.
    *   A [`script`](#83.html_the-script-element) element.
    *   A [`style`](#83.html_the-style-element) element.
    *   A [`textarea`](#83.html_the-textarea-element) element.
    *   An element with a [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute in a defined state.

If such a character is found and it is of bidirectional character type AL or R, [the directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) of the element is '[rtl](#83.html_concept-rtl)'.

If such a character is found and it is of bidirectional character type L, [the directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) of the element is '[ltr](#83.html_concept-ltr)'.

Otherwise, if the element is empty and is not a [root element](#83.html_root-element), [the directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) of the element is the same as the element's parent element's [directionality](#83.html_the-directionality).

Otherwise, [the directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) of the element is '[ltr](#83.html_concept-ltr)'.

If the element has a parent element and the [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute is not in a defined state (i.e. it is not present or has an invalid value)

[The directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) of the element is the same as the element's parent element's [directionality](#83.html_the-directionality).

Since the [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute is only defined for [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements), it cannot be present on elements from other namespaces. Thus, elements from other namespaces always just inherit their [directionality](#83.html_the-directionality) from their parent element, or, if they don't have one, default to '[ltr](#83.html_concept-ltr)'.

This attribute [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#83.html_bidireq).

* * *

The <dfn id="83.html_directionality-of-the-attribute" data-anolis-xref="directionality of the attribute">directionality of an attribute</dfn> of an [HTML element](#83.html_html-elements), which is used when the text of that attribute is to be included in the rendering in some manner, is determined as per the first appropriate set of steps from the following list:

If the attribute is a [directionality-capable attribute](#83.html_directionality-capable-attribute) and the element's [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute is in the [auto](#83.html_attr-dir-auto-state) state

Find the first character (in logical order) of the attribute's value that is of bidirectional character type L, AL, or R. [[BIDI]](#83.html_refsBIDI)

If such a character is found and it is of bidirectional character type AL or R, the [directionality of the attribute](#83.html_directionality-of-the-attribute) is '[rtl](#83.html_concept-rtl)'.

Otherwise, the [directionality of the attribute](#83.html_directionality-of-the-attribute) is '[ltr](#83.html_concept-ltr)'.

Otherwise

The [directionality of the attribute](#83.html_directionality-of-the-attribute) is the same as [the element's directionality](#83.html_the-directionality).

The following attributes are <dfn id="83.html_directionality-capable-attribute" data-anolis-xref="directionality-capable
  attribute">directionality-capable attributes</dfn>:

*   [`abbr`](#83.html_attr-th-abbr) on [`th`](#83.html_the-th-element) elements
*   `alt` on [`area`](#83.html_attr-area-alt), [`img`](#83.html_attr-img-alt), and [`input`](#83.html_attr-input-alt) elements
*   [`content`](#83.html_attr-meta-content) on [`meta`](#83.html_the-meta-element) elements, if the [`name`](#83.html_attr-meta-name) attribute specifies a metadata name whose value is primarily intended to be human-readable rather than machine-readable
*   `label` on [`optgroup`](#83.html_attr-optgroup-label), [`option`](#83.html_attr-option-label), and [`track`](#83.html_attr-track-label) elements
*   `placeholder` on [`input`](#83.html_attr-input-placeholder) and [`textarea`](#83.html_attr-textarea-placeholder) elements
*   [`title`](#83.html_attr-title) on all [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements)

* * *

`document` . [`dir`](#83.html_dom-dir) [ = `value` ]

Returns [the `html` element](#83.html_the-html-element-0)'s [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute's value, if any.

Can be set, to either "`ltr`", "`rtl`", or "`auto`" to replace [the `html` element](#83.html_the-html-element-0)'s [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute's value.

If there is no [`html` element](#83.html_the-html-element-0), returns the empty string and ignores new values.

The <dfn id="83.html_dom-dir" data-anolis-xref="dom-dir">`dir`</dfn> IDL attribute on an element must [reflect](#83.html_reflect) the [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) content attribute of that element, [limited to only known values](#83.html_limited-to-only-known-values).

The <dfn id="83.html_dom-document-dir" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-dir">`dir`</dfn> IDL attribute on [`Document`](#83.html_document) objects must [reflect](#83.html_reflect) the [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) content attribute of [the `html` element](#83.html_the-html-element-0), if any, [limited to only known values](#83.html_limited-to-only-known-values). If there is no such element, then the attribute must return the empty string and do nothing on setting.

Authors are strongly encouraged to use the [`dir`](#83.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute to indicate text direction rather than using CSS, since that way their documents will continue to render correctly even in the absence of CSS (e.g. as interpreted by search engines).

This markup fragment is of an IM conversation.

```
<p dir=auto class="u1"><b><bdi>Student</bdi>:</b> How do you write "What's your name?" in Arabic?</p>
<p dir=auto class="u2"><b><bdi>Teacher</bdi>:</b> ?? ?????</p>
<p dir=auto class="u1"><b><bdi>Student</bdi>:</b> Thanks.</p>
<p dir=auto class="u2"><b><bdi>Teacher</bdi>:</b> That's written "?????".</p>
<p dir=auto class="u2"><b><bdi>Teacher</bdi>:</b> Do you know how to write "Please"?</p>
<p dir=auto class="u1"><b><bdi>Student</bdi>:</b> "?? ????", right?</p>
```

Given a suitable style sheet and the default alignment styles for the [`p`](#83.html_the-p-element) element, namely to align the text to the *start edge* of the paragraph, the resulting rendering could be as follows:

![Each paragraph rendered as a separate block, with the paragraphs left-aligned except the second paragraph and the last one, which would be right aligned, with the usernames ('Student' and 'Teacher' in this example) flush right, with a colon to their left, and the text first to the left of that.](Images/2b0fe066d499a6491be9413cba2dca6b.jpg)

As noted earlier, the [`auto`](#83.html_attr-dir-auto) value is not a panacea. The final paragraph in this example is misinterpreted as being right-to-left text, since it begins with an Arabic character, which causes the "right?" to be to the left of the Arabic text.

##### 3.2.5.7 The <dfn id="83.html_attr-class" data-anolis-xref="attr-class">`class`</dfn> attribute

Every [HTML element](#83.html_html-elements) may have a [`class`](#83.html_classes) attribute specified.

The attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [set of space-separated tokens](#83.html_set-of-space-separated-tokens) representing the various classes that the element belongs to.

The classes that an [HTML element](#83.html_html-elements) has assigned to it consists of all the classes returned when the value of the [`class`](#83.html_classes) attribute is [split on spaces](#83.html_split-a-string-on-spaces). (Duplicates are ignored.)

Assigning classes to an element affects class matching in selectors in CSS, the `getElementsByClassName()` method in the DOM, and other such features.

There are no additional restrictions on the tokens authors can use in the [`class`](#83.html_classes) attribute, but authors are encouraged to use values that describe the nature of the content, rather than values that describe the desired presentation of the content.

* * *

The <dfn id="83.html_dom-classname" data-anolis-xref="dom-className">`className`</dfn> and <dfn id="83.html_dom-classlist" data-anolis-xref="dom-classList">`classList`</dfn> IDL attributes, defined in the DOM specification, [reflect](#83.html_reflect) the [`class`](#83.html_classes) content attribute. [[DOM]](#83.html_refsDOM)

##### 3.2.5.8 The <dfn id="83.html_attr-style" data-anolis-xref="attr-style">`style`</dfn> attribute

All [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements) may have the [`style`](#83.html_the-style-attribute) content attribute set. This is a [CSS styling attribute](#83.html_css-styling-attribute) as defined by the CSS Styling Attribute Syntax specification. [[CSSATTR]](#83.html_refsCSSATTR)

In user agents that support CSS, the attribute's value must be parsed when the attribute is added or has its value changed, according to the rules given for [CSS styling attributes](#83.html_css-styling-attribute). [[CSSATTR]](#83.html_refsCSSATTR)

Documents that use [`style`](#83.html_the-style-attribute) attributes on any of their elements must still be comprehensible and usable if those attributes were removed.

In particular, using the [`style`](#83.html_the-style-attribute) attribute to hide and show content, or to convey meaning that is otherwise not included in the document, is non-conforming. (To hide and show content, use the [`hidden`](#83.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute.)

* * *

`element` . [`style`](#83.html_dom-style)

Returns a [`CSSStyleDeclaration`](#83.html_cssstyledeclaration) object for the element's [`style`](#83.html_the-style-attribute) attribute.

The <dfn id="83.html_dom-style" data-anolis-xref="dom-style">`style`</dfn> IDL attribute is defined in the CSS Object Model (CSSOM) specification. [[CSSOM]](#83.html_refsCSSOM)

In the following example, the words that refer to colors are marked up using the [`span`](#83.html_the-span-element) element and the [`style`](#83.html_the-style-attribute) attribute to make those words show up in the relevant colors in visual media.

```
<p>My sweat suit is <span style="color: green; background:
transparent">green</span> and my eyes are <span style="color: blue;
background: transparent">blue</span>.</p>
```

##### 3.2.5.9 <dfn>Embedding custom non-visible data</dfn> with the [`data-*`](#83.html_attr-data-*) attributes

A <dfn id="83.html_custom-data-attribute">custom data attribute</dfn> is an attribute in no namespace whose name starts with the string "<dfn id="83.html_attr-data-*" data-anolis-xref="attr-data-*">`data-`</dfn>", has at least one character after the hyphen, is [XML-compatible](#83.html_xml-compatible), and contains no [uppercase ASCII letters](#83.html_uppercase-ascii-letters).

All attribute names on [HTML elements](#83.html_html-elements) in [HTML documents](#83.html_html-documents) get ASCII-lowercased automatically, so the restriction on ASCII uppercase letters doesn't affect such documents.

[Custom data attributes](#83.html_custom-data-attribute) are intended to store custom data private to the page or application, for which there are no more appropriate attributes or elements.

These attributes are not intended for use by software that is independent of the site that uses the attributes.

For instance, a site about music could annotate list items representing tracks in an album with custom data attributes containing the length of each track. This information could then be used by the site itself to allow the user to sort the list by track length, or to filter the list for tracks of certain lengths.

```
<ol>
 <li data-length="2m11s">Beyond The Sea</li>
 ...
</ol>
```

It would be inappropriate, however, for the user to use generic software not associated with that music site to search for tracks of a certain length by looking at this data.

This is because these attributes are intended for use by the site's own scripts, and are not a generic extension mechanism for publicly-usable metadata.

Every [HTML element](#83.html_html-elements) may have any number of [custom data attributes](#83.html_custom-data-attribute) specified, with any value.

* * *

`element` . [`dataset`](#83.html_dom-dataset)

Returns a [`DOMStringMap`](#83.html_domstringmap-0) object for the element's [`data-*`](#83.html_attr-data-*) attributes.

Hyphenated names become camel-cased. For example, `data-foo-bar=""` becomes `element.dataset.fooBar`.

The <dfn id="83.html_dom-dataset" data-anolis-xref="dom-dataset">`dataset`</dfn> IDL attribute provides convenient accessors for all the [`data-*`](#83.html_attr-data-*) attributes on an element. On getting, the [`dataset`](#83.html_dom-dataset) IDL attribute must return a [`DOMStringMap`](#83.html_domstringmap-0) object, associated with the following algorithms, which expose these attributes on their element:

The algorithm for getting the list of name-value pairs

1.  Let `list` be an empty list of name-value pairs.
2.  For each content attribute on the element whose first five characters are the string "`data-`" and whose remaining characters (if any) do not include any [uppercase ASCII letters](#83.html_uppercase-ascii-letters), in the order that those attributes are listed in the element's [attribute list](#83.html_attribute-list), add a name-value pair to `list` whose name is the attribute's name with the first five characters removed and whose value is the attribute's value.
3.  For each name in `list`, for each "-" (U+002D) character in the name that is followed by a [lowercase ASCII letter](#83.html_lowercase-ascii-letters), remove the "-" (U+002D) character and replace the character that followed it by the same character [converted to ASCII uppercase](#83.html_converted-to-ascii-uppercase).
4.  Return `list`.

The algorithm for setting names to certain values

1.  Let `name` be the name passed to the algorithm.
2.  Let `value` be the value passed to the algorithm.
3.  If `name` contains a "-" (U+002D) character followed by a [lowercase ASCII letter](#83.html_lowercase-ascii-letters), throw a [`SyntaxError`](#83.html_syntaxerror) exception and abort these steps.
4.  For each [uppercase ASCII letter](#83.html_uppercase-ascii-letters) in `name`, insert a "-" (U+002D) character before the character and replace the character with the same character [converted to ASCII lowercase](#83.html_converted-to-ascii-lowercase).
5.  Insert the string `data-` at the front of `name`.
6.  Set the value of the attribute with the name `name`, to the value `value`, replacing any previous value if the attribute already existed. If `setAttribute()` would have thrown an exception when setting an attribute with the name `name`, then this must throw the same exception.

The algorithm for deleting names

1.  Let `name` be the name passed to the algorithm.
2.  For each [uppercase ASCII letter](#83.html_uppercase-ascii-letters) in `name`, insert a "-" (U+002D) character before the character and replace the character with the same character [converted to ASCII lowercase](#83.html_converted-to-ascii-lowercase).
3.  Insert the string `data-` at the front of `name`.
4.  Remove the attribute with the name `name`, if such an attribute exists. Do nothing otherwise.

This algorithm will only get invoked by the WebIDL specification for names that are given by the earlier algorithm for getting the list of name-value pairs. [[WEBIDL]](#83.html_refsWEBIDL)

The same object must be returned each time.

If a Web page wanted an element to represent a space ship, e.g. as part of a game, it would have to use the [`class`](#83.html_classes) attribute along with [`data-*`](#83.html_attr-data-*) attributes:

```
<div class="spaceship" data-ship-id="92432"
     data-weapons="laser 2" data-shields="50%"

     data-x="30" data-y="10" data-z="90">
 <button class="fire"
         onclick="spaceships[this.parentNode.dataset.shipId].fire()">
  Fire
 </button>
</div>
```

Notice how the hyphenated attribute name becomes camel-cased in the API.

Authors should carefully design such extensions so that when the attributes are ignored and any associated CSS dropped, the page is still usable.

User agents must not derive any implementation behavior from these attributes or values. Specifications intended for user agents must not define these attributes to have any meaningful values.

JavaScript libraries may use the [custom data attributes](#83.html_custom-data-attribute), as they are considered to be part of the page on which they are used. Authors of libraries that are reused by many authors are encouraged to include their name in the attribute names, to reduce the risk of clashes. Where it makes sense, library authors are also encouraged to make the exact name used in the attribute names customizable, so that libraries whose authors unknowingly picked the same name can be used on the same page, and so that multiple versions of a particular library can be used on the same page even when those versions are not mutually compatible.

For example, a library called "DoQuery" could use attribute names like `data-doquery-range`, and a library called "jJo" could use attributes names like `data-jjo-range`. The jJo library could also provide an API to set which prefix to use (e.g. `J.setDataPrefix('j2')`, making the attributes have names like `data-j2-range`).

#### 3.2.6 Requirements relating to the bidirectional algorithm

##### 3.2.6.1 Authoring conformance criteria for bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters

[Text content](#84.html_text-content) in [HTML elements](#84.html_html-elements) with [`Text`](#84.html_text-0) nodes in their [contents](#84.html_concept-html-contents), and text in attributes of [HTML elements](#84.html_html-elements) that allow free-form text, may contain characters in the ranges U+202A to U+202E and U+2066 to U+2069 (the bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters). However, the use of these characters is restricted so that any embedding or overrides generated by these characters do not start and end with different parent elements, and so that all such embeddings and overrides are explicitly terminated by a U+202C POP DIRECTIONAL FORMATTING character. This helps reduce incidences of text being reused in a manner that has unforeseen effects on the bidirectional algorithm. [[BIDI]](#84.html_refsBIDI)

The aforementioned restrictions are defined by specifying that certain parts of documents form [bidirectional-algorithm formatting character ranges](#84.html_bidirectional-algorithm-formatting-character-ranges), and then imposing a requirement on such ranges.

The strings resulting from applying the following algorithm to an [HTML element](#84.html_html-elements) `element` are [bidirectional-algorithm formatting character ranges](#84.html_bidirectional-algorithm-formatting-character-ranges):

1.  Let `output` be an empty list of strings.

2.  Let `string` be an empty string.

3.  Let `node` be the first child node of `element`, if any, or null otherwise.

4.  *Loop*: If `node` is null, jump to the step labeled *end*.

5.  Process `node` according to the first matching step from the following list:

    If `node` is a [`Text`](#84.html_text-0) node

    Append the text data of `node` to `string`.

    If `node` is a [`br`](#84.html_the-br-element) element
    If `node` is an [HTML element](#84.html_html-elements) that is [flow content](#84.html_flow-content-1) but that is not also [phrasing content](#84.html_phrasing-content-1)

    If `string` is not the empty string, push `string` onto `output`, and let `string` be empty string.

    Otherwise

    Do nothing.

6.  Let `node` be `node`'s next sibling, if any, or null otherwise.

7.  Jump to the step labeled *loop*.

8.  *End*: If `string` is not the empty string, push `string` onto `output`.

9.  Return `output` as the [bidirectional-algorithm formatting character ranges](#84.html_bidirectional-algorithm-formatting-character-ranges).

The value of a namespace-less attribute of an [HTML element](#84.html_html-elements) is a [bidirectional-algorithm formatting character range](#84.html_bidirectional-algorithm-formatting-character-ranges).

Any strings that, as described above, are <dfn id="84.html_bidirectional-algorithm-formatting-character-ranges">bidirectional-algorithm formatting character ranges</dfn> must match the `string` production in the following ABNF, the character set for which is Unicode. [[ABNF]](#84.html_refsABNF)

```
string        = *( plaintext ( embedding / override / isolation ) ) plaintext
embedding     = ( lre / rle ) string pdf
override      = ( lro / rlo ) string pdf
isolation     = ( lri / rli / fsi ) string pdi
lre           = %x202A ; U+202A LEFT-TO-RIGHT EMBEDDING
rle           = %x202B ; U+202B RIGHT-TO-LEFT EMBEDDING
lro           = %x202D ; U+202D LEFT-TO-RIGHT OVERRIDE
rlo           = %x202E ; U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE
pdf           = %x202C ; U+202C POP DIRECTIONAL FORMATTING
lri           = %x2066 ; U+2066 LEFT-TO-RIGHT ISOLATE
rli           = %x2067 ; U+2067 RIGHT-TO-LEFT ISOLATE
fsi           = %x2068 ; U+2068 FIRST STRONG ISOLATE
pdi           = %x2069 ; U+2069 POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE
plaintext     = *( %x0000-2029 / %x202F-2065 / %x206A-10FFFF )
                ; any string with no bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters
```

While the U+2069 POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE character implicitly also ends open embeddings and overrides, text that relies on this implicit scope closure is not conforming to this specification. All strings of embeddings, overrides, and isolations need to be explicitly terminated to conform to this section's requirements.

Authors are encouraged to use the [`dir`](#84.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute, the [`bdo`](#84.html_the-bdo-element) element, and the [`bdi`](#84.html_the-bdi-element) element, rather than maintaining the bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters manually. The bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters interact poorly with CSS.

##### 3.2.6.2 User agent conformance criteria

User agents must implement the Unicode bidirectional algorithm to determine the proper ordering of characters when rendering documents and parts of documents. [[BIDI]](#84.html_refsBIDI)

The mapping of HTML to the Unicode bidirectional algorithm must be done in one of three ways. Either the user agent must implement CSS, including in particular the CSS 'unicode-bidi', 'direction', and 'content' properties, and must have, in its user agent style sheet, the rules using those properties given in this specification's [rendering](#84.html_rendering) section, or, alternatively, the user agent must act as if it implemented just the aforementioned properties and had a user agent style sheet that included all the aforementioned rules, but without letting style sheets specified in documents override them, or, alternatively, the user agent must implement another styling language with equivalent semantics. [[CSSWM]](#84.html_refsCSSWM) [[CSSGC]](#84.html_refsCSSGC)

The following elements and attributes have requirements defined by the [rendering](#84.html_rendering) section that, due to the requirements in this section, are requirements on all user agents (not just those that [support the suggested default rendering](#84.html_renderingUA)):

*   [`dir`](#84.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute
*   [`bdi`](#84.html_the-bdi-element) element
*   [`bdo`](#84.html_the-bdo-element) element
*   [`br`](#84.html_the-br-element) element
*   [`pre`](#84.html_the-pre-element) element
*   [`textarea`](#84.html_the-textarea-element) element
*   [`wbr`](#84.html_the-wbr-element) element

#### 3.2.7 <dfn>WAI-ARIA</dfn>

Authors are encouraged to make use of the following documents for guidance on using ARIA in HTML beyond that which is provided in this section:

*   [Using WAI-ARIA in HTML](http://rawgithub.com/w3c/aria-in-html/master/index.html) - A practical guide for developers on how to to add accessibility information to HTML elements using the Accessible Rich Internet Applications specification [[ARIA]](#85.html_refsARIA). In particular the [Recommendations Table](http://rawgithub.com/w3c/aria-in-html/master/index.html#recommendations-table) provides a complete reference for authors as to which ARIA roles, states and properties are appropriate to use on each HTML element.
*   [WAI-ARIA 1.0 Authoring Practices](http://www.w3.org/WAI/PF/aria-practices/) - An author's guide to understanding and implementing Accessible Rich Internet Applications.

Authors may use the ARIA [`role`](#85.html_attr-aria-role) and `aria-*` attributes on [HTML elements](#85.html_html-elements), in accordance with the requirements described in the ARIA specifications, except where these conflict with the [strong native semantics](#85.html_strong-native-semantics) described below. These exceptions are intended to prevent authors from making assistive technology products report nonsensical states that do not represent the actual state of the document. [[ARIA]](#85.html_refsARIA)

User agents are required to implement ARIA semantics on all [HTML elements](#85.html_html-elements), as defined in the ARIA specifications. The [default implicit ARIA semantics](#85.html_default-implicit-aria-semantics) defined below must be recognized by implementations for the purposes of ARIA processing. [[ARIAIMPL]](#85.html_refsARIAIMPL)

The ARIA attributes defined in the ARIA specifications, and the [strong native semantics](#85.html_strong-native-semantics) and [default implicit ARIA semantics](#85.html_default-implicit-aria-semantics) defined below, do not have any effect on CSS pseudo-class matching, user interface modalities that don't use assistive technologies, or the default actions of user interaction events as described in this specification.

##### 3.2.7.1 ARIA Role Attribute

Every HTML element may have an ARIA [`role`](#85.html_attr-aria-role) attribute specified. This is an ARIA Role attribute as defined by [[ARIA]](#85.html_refsARIA) [Section 5.4 Definition of Roles](http://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/roles#role_definitions).

The attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a set of space-separated tokens representing the various WAI-ARIA roles that the element belongs to.

The WAI-ARIA role that an HTML element has assigned to it is the first non-abstract role found in the list of values generated when the [`role`](#85.html_attr-aria-role) attribute is split on spaces.

##### 3.2.7.2 State and Property Attributes

Every HTML element may have ARIA state and property attributes specified. These attributes are defined by [[ARIA]](#85.html_refsARIA) in [Section 6.6, Definitions of States and Properties (all aria-* attributes)](http://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/states_and_properties#state_prop_def).

A subset of the ARIA State and Property attributes are defined as "<dfn id="85.html_aria-global-attributes">Global States and Properties</dfn>" in [Section 6.4\. Global States and Properties](http://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/states_and_properties#global_states) of the [[ARIA]](#85.html_refsARIA) Specification.

These attributes, if specified, must have a value that is the ARIA value type in the "Value" field of the definition for the state or property, mapped to the appropriate HTML value type according to [[ARIA]](#85.html_refsARIA) [Section 10.2 Mapping WAI-ARIA Value types to languages](http://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/appendices#typemapping) using the HTML 5 mapping.

ARIA State and Property attributes can be used on any element. They are not always meaningful, however, and in such cases user agents might not perform any processing aside from including them in the DOM. State and property attributes are processed according to the requirements of the sections [Strong Native Semantics](#85.html_sec-strong-native-semantics) and [Implicit ARIA semantics](#85.html_sec-implicit-aria-semantics), as well as [[ARIA]](#85.html_refsARIA) and [[ARIAIMPL]](#85.html_refsARIAIMPL).

##### 3.2.7.3 Strong Native Semantics

The following table defines the [strong native semantics](#85.html_strong-native-semantics) and corresponding [default implicit ARIA semantics](#85.html_default-implicit-aria-semantics) that apply to [HTML elements](#85.html_html-elements). Each language feature (element or attribute) in a cell in the first column implies the ARIA semantics (any role, states, and properties) given in the cell in the second column of the same row. When multiple rows apply to an element, the role from the last row to define a role must be applied, and the states and properties from all the rows must be combined.

Documents must not use any [`role`](#85.html_attr-aria-role) values with elements in the following table other than the corresponding role value (if any) as listed for that element in the second column, or the [`role`](#85.html_attr-aria-role) value "`presentation`", if the second column indicates that element's semantics can be removed by using the "`presentation`" [`role`](#85.html_attr-aria-role) value.

In the majority of cases setting an ARIA [`role`](#85.html_attr-aria-role) and/or `aria-*` attribute that matches the [default implicit ARIA semantics](#85.html_default-implicit-aria-semantics) is unnecessary and not recommended as these properties are already set by the browser.

| Language feature | [Strong native semantics](#85.html_strong-native-semantics) and [default implicit ARIA semantics](#85.html_default-implicit-aria-semantics) |
| --- | --- |
| [`area`](#85.html_the-area-element) element that creates a [hyperlink](#85.html_hyperlink) | `link` role |
| [`base`](#85.html_the-base-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`datalist`](#85.html_the-datalist-element) element | `listbox` role, with the `aria-multiselectable` property set to "false" |
| [`fieldset`](#85.html_the-fieldset-element) element | `group` role (semantics may be removed by using the `presentation` role) |
| [`footer`](#85.html_the-footer-element) element that is not a descendant of an [`article`](#85.html_the-article-element) or [`section`](#85.html_the-section-element) element. | `contentinfo` role (semantics may be removed by using the `presentation` role) |
| [`head`](#85.html_the-head-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`header`](#85.html_the-header-element) element that is not a descendant of an [`article`](#85.html_the-article-element) or [`section`](#85.html_the-section-element) element. | `banner` role (semantics may be removed by using the `presentation` role) |
| [`hr`](#85.html_the-hr-element) element | `separator` role (semantics may be removed by using the `presentation` role) |
| [`html`](#85.html_the-html-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`img`](#85.html_the-img-element) element whose [`alt`](#85.html_attr-img-alt) attribute's value is empty | `presentation` role |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Checkbox](#85.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) state | `aria-checked` state set to "mixed" if the element's [`indeterminate`](#85.html_dom-input-indeterminate) IDL attribute is true, or "true" if the element's [checkedness](#85.html_concept-fe-checked) is true, or "false" otherwise |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Color](#85.html_color-state-(type=color)) state | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Date](#85.html_date-state-(type=date)) state | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none), with the `aria-readonly` property set to "true" if the element has a [`readonly`](#85.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [E-mail](#85.html_e-mail-state-(type=email)) state with no [suggestions source element](#85.html_concept-input-list) | `textbox` role, with the `aria-readonly` property set to "true" if the element has a [`readonly`](#85.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [File Upload](#85.html_file-upload-state-(type=file)) state | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Hidden](#85.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Number](#85.html_number-state-(type=number)) state | `spinbutton` role, with the `aria-readonly` property set to "true" if the element has a [`readonly`](#85.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute, the `aria-valuemax` property set to the element's [maximum](#85.html_concept-input-max), the `aria-valuemin` property set to the element's [minimum](#85.html_concept-input-min), and, if the result of applying the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#85.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) to the element's [value](#85.html_concept-fe-value) is a number, with the `aria-valuenow` property set to that number |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Password](#85.html_password-state-(type=password)) state | `textbox` role, with the `aria-readonly` property set to "true" if the element has a [`readonly`](#85.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Radio Button](#85.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state | `aria-checked` state set to "true" if the element's [checkedness](#85.html_concept-fe-checked) is true, or "false" otherwise |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Range](#85.html_range-state-(type=range)) state | `slider` role, with the `aria-valuemax` property set to the element's [maximum](#85.html_concept-input-max), the `aria-valuemin` property set to the element's [minimum](#85.html_concept-input-min), and the `aria-valuenow` property set to the result of applying the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#85.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) to the element's [value](#85.html_concept-fe-value), if that results in a number, or the [default value](#85.html_concept-input-value-default-range) otherwise |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Reset Button](#85.html_reset-button-state-(type=reset)) state | `button` role |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Search](#85.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) state with no [suggestions source element](#85.html_concept-input-list) | `textbox` role, with the `aria-readonly` property set to "true" if the element has a [`readonly`](#85.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Submit Button](#85.html_submit-button-state-(type=submit)) state | `button` role |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Telephone](#85.html_telephone-state-(type=tel)) state with no [suggestions source element](#85.html_concept-input-list) | `textbox` role, with the `aria-readonly` property set to "true" if the element has a [`readonly`](#85.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Text](#85.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) state with no [suggestions source element](#85.html_concept-input-list) | `textbox` role, with the `aria-readonly` property set to "true" if the element has a [`readonly`](#85.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Text](#85.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [Search](#85.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [Telephone](#85.html_telephone-state-(type=tel)), [URL](#85.html_url-state-(type=url)), or [E-mail](#85.html_e-mail-state-(type=email)) states with a [suggestions source element](#85.html_concept-input-list) | `combobox` role, with the `aria-owns` property set to the same value as the [`list`](#85.html_attr-input-list) attribute, and the `aria-readonly` property set to "true" if the element has a [`readonly`](#85.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Time](#85.html_time-state-(type=time)) state | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none), with the `aria-readonly` property set to "true" if the element has a [`readonly`](#85.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [URL](#85.html_url-state-(type=url)) state with no [suggestions source element](#85.html_concept-input-list) | `textbox` role, with the `aria-readonly` property set to "true" if the element has a [`readonly`](#85.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute |
| [`keygen`](#85.html_the-keygen-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`label`](#85.html_the-label-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`link`](#85.html_the-link-element) element that creates a [hyperlink](#85.html_hyperlink) | `link` role |
| [`main`](#85.html_the-main-element) element | `main` role (semantics may be removed by using the `presentation` role) |
| [`meta`](#85.html_the-meta-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`meter`](#85.html_the-meter-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`nav`](#85.html_the-nav-element) element | `navigation` role (semantics may be removed by using the `presentation` role) |
| [`noscript`](#85.html_the-noscript-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`optgroup`](#85.html_the-optgroup-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`option`](#85.html_the-option-element) element that is in a [list of options](#85.html_concept-select-option-list) or that represents a suggestion in a [`datalist`](#85.html_the-datalist-element) element | `option` role, with the `aria-selected` state set to "true" if the element's [selectedness](#85.html_concept-option-selectedness) is true, or "false" otherwise. |
| [`param`](#85.html_the-param-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`progress`](#85.html_the-progress-element) element | `progressbar` role, with, if the progress bar is determinate, the `aria-valuemax` property set to the maximum value of the progress bar, the `aria-valuemin` property set to zero, and the `aria-valuenow` property set to the current value of the progress bar |
| [`script`](#85.html_the-script-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`select`](#85.html_the-select-element) element with a [`multiple`](#85.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute | `listbox` role, with the `aria-multiselectable` property set to "true" |
| [`select`](#85.html_the-select-element) element with no [`multiple`](#85.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute | `listbox` role, with the `aria-multiselectable` property set to "false" |
| [`source`](#85.html_the-source-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`style`](#85.html_the-style-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`template`](#85.html_the-template-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| [`textarea`](#85.html_the-textarea-element) element | `textbox` role, with the `aria-multiline` property set to "true", and the `aria-readonly` property set to "true" if the element has a [`readonly`](#85.html_attr-textarea-readonly) attribute |
| [`title`](#85.html_the-title-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) |
| Element that is [disabled](#85.html_concept-fe-disabled) | The `aria-disabled` state set to "true" |
| Element that is [inert](#85.html_inert) | The `aria-disabled` state set to "true" |
| Element that is a [candidate for constraint validation](#85.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation) but that does not [satisfy its constraints](#85.html_concept-fv-valid) | The `aria-invalid` state set to "true" |

##### 3.2.7.4 Implicit ARIA Semantics

Some [HTML elements](#85.html_html-elements) have native semantics that can be overridden. The following table lists these elements and their [default implicit ARIA semantics](#85.html_default-implicit-aria-semantics), along with the restrictions that apply to those elements. Each language feature (element or attribute) in a cell in the first column implies, unless otherwise overridden, the ARIA semantic (role, state, or property) given in the cell in the second column of the same row, but this semantic may be overridden under the conditions listed in the cell in the third column of that row.

| Language feature | Default implicit ARIA semantic | Restrictions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`a`](#85.html_the-a-element) element that creates a [hyperlink](#85.html_hyperlink) | `link` role | If specified, role must be one of the following: `link`, `button`, `checkbox`, `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox`,`menuitemradio`, `option`, `radio`, `tab`, or `treeitem` |
| [`address`](#85.html_the-address-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be `contentinfo` |
| [`article`](#85.html_the-article-element) element | `article` role | If specified, role must be one of the following: `article`, `document`, `application`, or `main` |
| [`aside`](#85.html_the-aside-element) element | `complementary` role | If specified, role must be one of the following: `complementary`, `note`, `search` or `presentation` |
| [`audio`](#85.html_the-audio-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be `application` |
| [`body`](#85.html_the-body-element) element | `document` role | If specified, role must be either `document` or `application` |
| [`button`](#85.html_the-button-element) element | `button` role | If specified, role must be one of the following: `button`, `link`, `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox`, `menuitemradio` or `radio` |
| [`embed`](#85.html_the-embed-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be one of the following: `application`, `document`, or `img` |
| [`h1`](#85.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be one of the following: `heading`, `tab` or `presentation` |
| [`h2`](#85.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be one of the following: `heading`, `tab` or `presentation` |
| [`h3`](#85.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be one of the following: `heading`, `tab` or `presentation` |
| [`h4`](#85.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be one of the following: `heading`, `tab` or `presentation` |
| [`h5`](#85.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be one of the following: `heading`, `tab` or `presentation` |
| [`h6`](#85.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be one of the following: `heading`, `tab` or `presentation` |
| [`iframe`](#85.html_the-iframe-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be one of the following: `application`, `document`, `img`, or `presentation` |
| [`img`](#85.html_the-img-element) element whose [`alt`](#85.html_attr-img-alt) attribute's value is absent | `img` role | No restrictions |
| [`img`](#85.html_the-img-element) element whose [`alt`](#85.html_attr-img-alt) attribute's value is present and not empty | `img` role | No restrictions |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Button](#85.html_button-state-(type=button)) state | `button` role | If specified, role must be one of the following: `button`, `link`, `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox`, `menuitemradio` or `radio` |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Checkbox](#85.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) state | `checkbox` role | If specified, role must be either `checkbox` or `menuitemcheckbox` |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Image Button](#85.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state | `button` role | If specified, role must be one of the following: `button`, `link`, `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox`, `menuitemradio` or `radio` |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#85.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Radio Button](#85.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state | `radio` role | If specified, role must be either `radio` or `menuitemradio` |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element), [`select`](#85.html_the-select-element) or [`textarea`](#85.html_the-textarea-element) element with a `required` attribute | The `aria-required` state set to "true" | If specified, the `aria-required` state must be set to "true" |
| [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element), [`select`](#85.html_the-select-element) or [`textarea`](#85.html_the-textarea-element) element without a `required` attribute | `aria-required` set to "false" | If specified, the `aria-required` state set to "true" or "false" |
| [`li`](#85.html_the-li-element) element whose parent is an [`ol`](#85.html_the-ol-element) or [`ul`](#85.html_the-ul-element) element | `listitem` role | If specified, role must be one of the following: `listitem`, `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox`, `menuitemradio`, `option`, `radio`, `tab`, `treeitem` or `presentation` |
| `menu` element with a `type` attribute in the toolbar state | `toolbar` role | If specified, role must be one of the following: `directory`, `list`, `listbox`, `menu`, `menubar`, `tablist`, `toolbar`, or `tree` or `presentation` |
| [`object`](#85.html_the-object-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be one of the following: `application`, `document`, `img`, or `presentation` |
| [`ol`](#85.html_the-ol-element) element | `list` role | If specified, role must be one of the following: `directory`, `list`, `listbox`, `menu`, `menubar`, `radiogroup`, `tablist`, `toolbar`, `tree` or `presentation` |
| [`output`](#85.html_the-output-element) element | `status` role | No restrictions |
| [`section`](#85.html_the-section-element) element | `region` role**Note:**It is strongly recommended that user agents such as screen readers only convey the presence of, and provide navigation for [`section`](#85.html_the-section-element) elements, when the [`section`](#85.html_the-section-element) element has an accessible name. | If specified, role must be one of the following: `alert`, `alertdialog`, `application`, `contentinfo`, `dialog`, `document`, `log`, `main`, `marquee`, `region`, `search`, `status` or `presentation` |
| [`ul`](#85.html_the-ul-element) element | `list` role | If specified, role must be one of the following: `directory`, `group`, `list`, `listbox`, `menu`, `menubar`, `radiogroup`, `tablist`, `toolbar`, `tree` or `presentation` |
| [`video`](#85.html_the-video-element) element | [No role](#85.html_concept-role-none) | If specified, role must be `application` |
| Element with a [`hidden`](#85.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute | The `aria-hidden` state set to "true" | If specified, the `aria-hidden` state set to "true" or "false" |
| Element without a [`hidden`](#85.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute | The `aria-hidden` state set to "false" | If specified, the `aria-hidden` state set to "true" or "false" |

The entry "<dfn id="85.html_concept-role-none" data-anolis-xref="concept-role-none">no role</dfn>", when used as a [strong native semantic](#85.html_strong-native-semantics), means that no role can be used and that the user agent has no default mapping to ARIA roles. (However, it could have its own mappings to the accessibility layer.) When used as a [default implicit ARIA semantic](#85.html_default-implicit-aria-semantics), it means the user agent has no default mapping to ARIA roles. (However, it could have its own mappings to the accessibility layer.)

The WAI-ARIA specification neither requires or forbids user agents from enhancing native presentation and interaction behaviors on the basis of WAI- ARIA markup. Even mainstream user agents might choose to expose metadata or navigational features directly or via user-installed extensions; for example, exposing required form fields or landmark navigation. User agents are encouraged to maximize their usefulness to users, including users without disabilities.

Conformance checkers are encouraged to phrase errors such that authors are encouraged to use more appropriate elements rather than remove accessibility annotations. For example, if an [`a`](#85.html_the-a-element) element is marked as having the `button` role, a conformance checker could say "Use a more appropriate element to represent a button, for example a [`button`](#85.html_the-button-element) element or an [`input`](#85.html_the-input-element) element" rather than "The `button` role cannot be used with [`a`](#85.html_the-a-element) elements".

These features can be used to make accessibility tools render content to their users in more useful ways. For example, ASCII art, which is really an image, appears to be text, and in the absence of appropriate annotations would end up being rendered by screen readers as a very painful reading of lots of punctuation. Using the features described in this section, one can instead make the ATs skip the ASCII art and just read the caption:

```
<figure role="img" aria-labelledby="fish-caption"> 
 <pre>
 o           .'`/
     '      /  (
   O    .-'` ` `'-._      .')
      _/ (o)        '.  .' /
      )       )))     ><  <
      `\  |_\      _.'  '. \
        '-._  _ .-'       '.)
    jgs     `\__\
 </pre>
 <figcaption id="fish-caption">
  Joan G. Stark, "<cite>fish</cite>".
  October 1997\. ASCII on electrons. 28×8.
 </figcaption> 
</figure> 
```

## 4 The elements of HTML

### 4.1 The root element

#### 4.1.1 The <dfn>`html`</dfn> element

[Categories](#88.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#88.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As the root element of a document.

Wherever a subdocument fragment is allowed in a compound document.

[Content model](#88.html_element-dfn-content-model):

A [`head`](#88.html_the-head-element) element followed by a [`body`](#88.html_the-body-element) element.

[Content attributes](#88.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#88.html_global-attributes)

[`manifest`](#88.html_attr-html-manifest) — [Application cache manifest](#88.html_application-cache)

[Tag omission in text/html](#88.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

An [`html`](#88.html_the-html-element) element's [start tag](#88.html_syntax-start-tag) can be omitted if the first thing inside the [`html`](#88.html_the-html-element) element is not a [comment](#88.html_syntax-comments).

An [`html`](#88.html_the-html-element) element's [end tag](#88.html_syntax-end-tag) can be omitted if the [`html`](#88.html_the-html-element) element is not immediately followed by a [comment](#88.html_syntax-comments).

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#88.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

none

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#88.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#88.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#88.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLHtmlElement : HTMLElement {};
```

The [`html`](#88.html_the-html-element) element [represents](#88.html_represents) the root of an HTML document.

Authors are encouraged to specify a [`lang`](#88.html_attr-lang) attribute on the root [`html`](#88.html_the-html-element) element, giving the document's language. This aids speech synthesis tools to determine what pronunciations to use, translation tools to determine what rules to use, and so forth.

The <dfn id="88.html_attr-html-manifest" data-anolis-xref="attr-html-manifest">`manifest`</dfn> attribute gives the address of the document's [application cache](#88.html_application-cache) [manifest](#88.html_concept-appcache-manifest), if there is one. If the attribute is present, the attribute's value must be a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#88.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces).

The [`manifest`](#88.html_attr-html-manifest) attribute only [has an effect](#88.html_concept-appcache-init) during the early stages of document load. Changing the attribute dynamically thus has no effect (and thus, no DOM API is provided for this attribute).

For the purposes of [application cache selection](#88.html_concept-appcache-init), later [`base`](#88.html_the-base-element) elements cannot affect the [resolving of relative URLs](#88.html_resolve-a-url) in [`manifest`](#88.html_attr-html-manifest) attributes, as the attributes are processed before those elements are seen.

The [`window.applicationCache`](#88.html_dom-applicationcache) IDL attribute provides scripted access to the offline [application cache](#88.html_application-cache) mechanism.

The [`html`](#88.html_the-html-element) element in the following example declares that the document's language is English.

```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<title>Swapping Songs</title>
</head>
<body>
<h1>Swapping Songs</h1>
<p>Tonight I swapped some of the songs I wrote with some friends, who
gave me some of the songs they wrote. I love sharing my music.</p>
</body>
</html>
```

### 4.2 Document metadata

#### 4.2.1 The <dfn>`head`</dfn> element

[Categories](#90.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#90.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As the first element in an [`html`](#90.html_the-html-element) element.

[Content model](#90.html_element-dfn-content-model):

If the document is [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#90.html_an-iframe-srcdoc-document) or if title information is available from a higher-level protocol: Zero or more elements of [metadata content](#90.html_metadata-content-0), of which no more than one is a [`title`](#90.html_the-title-element) element and no more than one is a [`base`](#90.html_the-base-element) element.

Otherwise: One or more elements of [metadata content](#90.html_metadata-content-0), of which exactly one is a [`title`](#90.html_the-title-element) element and no more than one is a [`base`](#90.html_the-base-element) element.

[Content attributes](#90.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#90.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#90.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

A [`head`](#90.html_the-head-element) element's [start tag](#90.html_syntax-start-tag) may be omitted if the element is empty, or if the first thing inside the [`head`](#90.html_the-head-element) element is an element.

A [`head`](#90.html_the-head-element) element's [end tag](#90.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`head`](#90.html_the-head-element) element is not immediately followed by a [space character](#90.html_space-character) or a [comment](#90.html_syntax-comments).

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#90.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

none

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#90.html_state-and-property-attributes):
