[Global aria-* attributes](#90.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#90.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLHeadElement : HTMLElement {};
```

The [`head`](#90.html_the-head-element) element [represents](#90.html_represents) a collection of metadata for the [`Document`](#90.html_document).

The collection of metadata in a [`head`](#90.html_the-head-element) element can be large or small. Here is an example of a very short one:

```
<!doctype html>
<html>
 <head>
  <title>A document with a short head</title>
 </head>
 <body>
 ...
```

Here is an example of a longer one:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<HTML>
 <HEAD>
  <META CHARSET="UTF-8">
  <BASE HREF="http://www.example.com/">
  <TITLE>An application with a long head</TITLE>
  <LINK REL="STYLESHEET" HREF="default.css">
  <LINK REL="STYLESHEET ALTERNATE" HREF="big.css" TITLE="Big Text">
  <SCRIPT SRC="support.js"></SCRIPT>
  <META NAME="APPLICATION-NAME" CONTENT="Long headed application">
 </HEAD>
 <BODY>
 ...
```

The [`title`](#90.html_the-title-element) element is a required child in most situations, but when a higher-level protocol provides title information, e.g. in the Subject line of an e-mail when HTML is used as an e-mail authoring format, the [`title`](#90.html_the-title-element) element can be omitted.

#### 4.2.2 The <dfn>`title`</dfn> element

[Categories](#91.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Metadata content](#91.html_metadata-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#91.html_element-dfn-contexts):

In a [`head`](#91.html_the-head-element) element containing no other [`title`](#91.html_the-title-element) elements.

[Content model](#91.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Text](#91.html_text-content) that is not [inter-element whitespace](#91.html_inter-element-whitespace).

[Content attributes](#91.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#91.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#91.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#91.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

none

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#91.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#91.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#91.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTitleElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString text;
};
```

The [`title`](#91.html_the-title-element) element [represents](#91.html_represents) the document's title or name. Authors should use titles that identify their documents even when they are used out of context, for example in a user's history or bookmarks, or in search results. The document's title is often different from its first heading, since the first heading does not have to stand alone when taken out of context.

There must be no more than one [`title`](#91.html_the-title-element) element per document.

If it's reasonable for the [`Document`](#91.html_document) to have no title, then the [`title`](#91.html_the-title-element) element is probably not required. See the [`head`](#91.html_the-head-element) element's content model for a description of when the element is required.

`title` . [`text`](#91.html_dom-title-text) [ = `value` ]

Returns the contents of the element, ignoring child nodes that aren't [`Text`](#91.html_text-0) nodes.

Can be set, to replace the element's children with the given value.

The IDL attribute <dfn id="91.html_dom-title-text" data-anolis-xref="dom-title-text">`text`</dfn> must return a concatenation of the contents of all the [`Text`](#91.html_text-0) nodes that are children of the [`title`](#91.html_the-title-element) element (ignoring any other nodes such as comments or elements), in tree order. On setting, it must act the same way as the [`textContent`](#91.html_textcontent) IDL attribute.

Here are some examples of appropriate titles, contrasted with the top-level headings that might be used on those same pages.

```
 <title>Introduction to The Mating Rituals of Bees</title>
    ...
  <h1>Introduction</h1>
  <p>This companion guide to the highly successful
  <cite>Introduction to Medieval Bee-Keeping</cite> book is...
```

The next page might be a part of the same site. Note how the title describes the subject matter unambiguously, while the first heading assumes the reader knows what the context is and therefore won't wonder if the dances are Salsa or Waltz:

```
 <title>Dances used during bee mating rituals</title>
    ...
  <h1>The Dances</h1>
```

The string to use as the document's title is given by the [`document.title`](#91.html_document.title) IDL attribute.

User agents should use the document's title when referring to the document in their user interface. When the contents of a [`title`](#91.html_the-title-element) element are used in this way, [the directionality](#91.html_the-directionality) of that [`title`](#91.html_the-title-element) element should be used to set the directionality of the document's title in the user interface.

#### 4.2.3 The <dfn>`base`</dfn> element

[Categories](#92.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Metadata content](#92.html_metadata-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#92.html_element-dfn-contexts):

In a [`head`](#92.html_the-head-element) element containing no other [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) elements.

[Content model](#92.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#92.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#92.html_global-attributes)

[`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) — [Document base URL](#92.html_document-base-url)

[`target`](#92.html_attr-base-target) — Default [browsing context](#92.html_browsing-context) for [hyperlink](#92.html_hyperlink) [navigation](#92.html_navigate) and [form submission](#92.html_form-submission)

[Tag omission in text/html](#92.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

No end tag.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#92.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

none

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#92.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#92.html_index-aria-global).

[DOM interface](#92.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLBaseElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString href;
           attribute DOMString target;
};
```

The [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element allows authors to specify the [document base URL](#92.html_document-base-url) for the purposes of [resolving relative URLs](#92.html_resolve-a-url), and the name of the default [browsing context](#92.html_browsing-context) for the purposes of [following hyperlinks](#92.html_following-hyperlinks). The element does not [represent](#92.html_represents) any content beyond this information.

There must be no more than one [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element per document.

A [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element must have either an [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) attribute, a [`target`](#92.html_attr-base-target) attribute, or both.

The <dfn id="92.html_attr-base-href" data-anolis-xref="attr-base-href">`href`</dfn> content attribute, if specified, must contain a [valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#92.html_valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces).

A [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element, if it has an [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) attribute, must come before any other elements in the tree that have attributes defined as taking URLs, except the [`html`](#92.html_the-html-element) element (its [`manifest`](#92.html_attr-html-manifest) attribute isn't affected by [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) elements).

If there are multiple [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) elements with [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) attributes, all but the first are ignored.

The <dfn id="92.html_attr-base-target" data-anolis-xref="attr-base-target">`target`</dfn> attribute, if specified, must contain a [valid browsing context name or keyword](#92.html_valid-browsing-context-name-or-keyword), which specifies which [browsing context](#92.html_browsing-context) is to be used as the default when [hyperlinks](#92.html_hyperlink) and [forms](#92.html_the-form-element) in the [`Document`](#92.html_document) cause [navigation](#92.html_navigate).

A [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element, if it has a [`target`](#92.html_attr-base-target) attribute, must come before any elements in the tree that represent [hyperlinks](#92.html_hyperlink).

If there are multiple [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) elements with [`target`](#92.html_attr-base-target) attributes, all but the first are ignored.

A [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element that is the first [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element with an [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) content attribute in a particular [`Document`](#92.html_document) has a <dfn id="92.html_frozen-base-url">frozen base URL</dfn>. The [frozen base URL](#92.html_frozen-base-url) must be [set](#92.html_set-the-frozen-base-url), synchronously, whenever any of the following situations occur:

*   The [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element becomes the first [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element in [tree order](#92.html_tree-order) with an [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) content attribute in its [`Document`](#92.html_document).
*   The [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element is the first [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element in [tree order](#92.html_tree-order) with an [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) content attribute in its [`Document`](#92.html_document), and its [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) content attribute is changed.

To <dfn id="92.html_set-the-frozen-base-url">set the frozen base URL</dfn>, [resolve](#92.html_resolve-a-url) the value of the element's [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) content attribute relative to the [`Document`](#92.html_document)'s [fallback base URL](#92.html_fallback-base-url); if this is successful, set the [frozen base URL](#92.html_frozen-base-url) to the [resulting absolute URL](#92.html_resulting-absolute-url), otherwise, set the [frozen base URL](#92.html_frozen-base-url) to the [fallback base URL](#92.html_fallback-base-url).

The <dfn id="92.html_dom-base-href" data-anolis-xref="dom-base-href">`href`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the result of running the following algorithm:

1.  If the [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element has no [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) content attribute, then return the [document base URL](#92.html_document-base-url) and abort these steps.

2.  Let `fallback base url` be the [`Document`](#92.html_document)'s [fallback base URL](#92.html_fallback-base-url).

3.  Let `url` be the value of the [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) attribute of the [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element.

4.  [Resolve](#92.html_resolve-a-url) `url` relative to `fallback base url` (thus, the [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) attribute isn't affected by [`xml:base`](#92.html_the-xml:base-attribute-(xml-only)) attributes or [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) elements).

5.  If the previous step was successful, return the resulting [absolute URL](#92.html_absolute-url) and abort these steps.

6.  Otherwise, return the empty string.

The [`href`](#92.html_dom-base-href) IDL attribute, on setting, must set the [`href`](#92.html_attr-base-href) content attribute to the given new value.

The <dfn id="92.html_dom-base-target" data-anolis-xref="dom-base-target">`target`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#92.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

In this example, a [`base`](#92.html_the-base-element) element is used to set the [document base URL](#92.html_document-base-url):

```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
    <head>
        <title>This is an example for the &lt;base&gt; element</title>
        <base href="http://www.example.com/news/index.html">
    </head>
    <body>
        <p>Visit the <a href="archives.html">archives</a>.</p>
    </body>
</html>
```

The link in the above example would be a link to "`http://www.example.com/news/archives.html`".

#### 4.2.4 The <dfn>`link`</dfn> element

[Categories](#93.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Metadata content](#93.html_metadata-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#93.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [metadata content](#93.html_metadata-content-0) is expected.

In a [`noscript`](#93.html_the-noscript-element) element that is a child of a [`head`](#93.html_the-head-element) element.

[Content model](#93.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#93.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#93.html_global-attributes)

[`href`](#93.html_attr-link-href) — Address of the [hyperlink](#93.html_hyperlink)

[`crossorigin`](#93.html_attr-link-crossorigin) — How the element handles crossorigin requests

[`rel`](#93.html_attr-link-rel) — Relationship between the document containing the hyperlink and the destination resource

[`media`](#93.html_attr-link-media) — Applicable media

[`hreflang`](#93.html_attr-link-hreflang) — Language of the linked resource

[`type`](#93.html_attr-link-type) — Hint for the type of the referenced resource

[`sizes`](#93.html_attr-link-sizes) — Sizes of the icons (for [`rel`](#93.html_attr-link-rel)="[`icon`](#93.html_rel-icon)")

Also, the [`title`](#93.html_attr-link-title) attribute has special semantics on this element: Title of the link; alternative style sheet set name.

[Tag omission in text/html](#93.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

No [end tag](#93.html_syntax-end-tag).

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#93.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`link`](#93.html_index-aria-link) (default - [*do not set*](#93.html_aria-usage-note)).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#93.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#93.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#93.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

For `role` value

[DOM interface](#93.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLLinkElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute boolean disabled;
           attribute DOMString href;
           attribute DOMString crossOrigin;
           attribute DOMString rel;
           attribute DOMString rev;
  readonly attribute DOMTokenList relList;
           attribute DOMString media;
           attribute DOMString hreflang;
           attribute DOMString type;
  [PutForwards=value] readonly attribute DOMSettableTokenList sizes;
};
HTMLLinkElement implements LinkStyle;
```

The [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element allows authors to link their document to other resources.

The destination of the link(s) is given by the <dfn id="93.html_attr-link-href" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-href">`href`</dfn> attribute, which must be present and must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#93.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces). If the [`href`](#93.html_attr-link-href) attribute is absent, then the element does not define a link.

A [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element must have a [`rel`](#93.html_attr-link-rel) attribute.

If the [`rel`](#93.html_attr-link-rel) attribute is used, the element is restricted to the [`head`](#93.html_the-head-element) element.

The types of link indicated (the relationships) are given by the value of the <dfn id="93.html_attr-link-rel" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-rel">`rel`</dfn> attribute, which, if present, must have a value that is a [set of space-separated tokens](#93.html_set-of-space-separated-tokens). The [allowed keywords and their meanings](#93.html_linkTypes) are defined in a later section. If the [`rel`](#93.html_attr-link-rel) attribute is absent, has no keywords, or if none of the keywords used are allowed according to the definitions in this specification, then the element does not create any links.

Two categories of links can be created using the [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element: [Links to external resources](#93.html_external-resource-link) and [hyperlinks](#93.html_hyperlink). The [link types section](#93.html_linkTypes) defines whether a particular link type is an external resource or a hyperlink. One [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element can create multiple links (of which some might be external resource links and some might be hyperlinks); exactly which and how many links are created depends on the keywords given in the [`rel`](#93.html_attr-link-rel) attribute. User agents must process the links on a per-link basis, not a per-element basis.

Each link created for a [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element is handled separately. For instance, if there are two [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) elements with `rel="stylesheet"`, they each count as a separate external resource, and each is affected by its own attributes independently. Similarly, if a single [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element has a [`rel`](#93.html_attr-link-rel) attribute with the value `next stylesheet`, it creates both a [hyperlink](#93.html_hyperlink) (for the [`next`](#93.html_link-type-next) keyword) and an [external resource link](#93.html_external-resource-link) (for the [`stylesheet`](#93.html_link-type-stylesheet) keyword), and they are affected by other attributes (such as [`media`](#93.html_attr-link-media) or [`title`](#93.html_attr-link-title)) differently.

For example, the following [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element creates two hyperlinks (to the same page):

```
<link rel="author license" href="/about">
```

The two links created by this element are one whose semantic is that the target page has information about the current page's author, and one whose semantic is that the target page has information regarding the license under which the current page is provided.

The <dfn id="93.html_attr-link-crossorigin" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-crossorigin">`crossorigin`</dfn> attribute is a [CORS settings attribute](#93.html_cors-settings-attribute). It is intended for use with external resource links.

The exact behavior for links to external resources depends on the exact relationship, as defined for the relevant link type. Some of the attributes control whether or not the external resource is to be applied (as defined below).

For external resources that are represented in the DOM (for example, style sheets), the DOM representation must be made available (modulo cross-origin restrictions) even if the resource is not applied. To <dfn id="93.html_concept-link-obtain" data-anolis-xref="concept-link-obtain">obtain the resource</dfn>, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  If the [`href`](#93.html_attr-link-href) attribute's value is the empty string, then abort these steps.

2.  [Resolve](#93.html_resolve-a-url) the URL given by the [`href`](#93.html_attr-link-href) attribute, relative to the element.

3.  If the previous step fails, then abort these steps.

4.  Do a [potentially CORS-enabled fetch](#93.html_potentially-cors-enabled-fetch) of the resulting [absolute URL](#93.html_absolute-url), with the *mode* being the current state of the element's [`crossorigin`](#93.html_attr-link-crossorigin) content attribute, the *origin* being the [origin](#93.html_origin-0) of the [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element's [`Document`](#93.html_document), and the *default origin behaviour* set to *taint*.

    The resource obtained in this fashion can be either [CORS-same-origin](#93.html_cors-same-origin) or [CORS-cross-origin](#93.html_cors-cross-origin).

User agents may opt to only try to obtain such resources when they are needed, instead of pro-actively [fetching](#93.html_fetch) all the external resources that are not applied.

The semantics of the protocol used (e.g. HTTP) must be followed when fetching external resources. (For example, redirects will be followed and 404 responses will cause the external resource to not be applied.)

Once the attempts to obtain the resource and its [critical subresources](#93.html_critical-subresources) are complete, the user agent must, if the loads were successful, [queue a task](#93.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#93.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `load` at the [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element, or, if the resource or one of its [critical subresources](#93.html_critical-subresources) failed to completely load for any reason (e.g. DNS error, HTTP 404 response, a connection being prematurely closed, unsupported Content-Type), [queue a task](#93.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#93.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `error` at the [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element. Non-network errors in processing the resource or its subresources (e.g. CSS parse errors, PNG decoding errors) are not failures for the purposes of this paragraph.

The [task source](#93.html_task-source) for these [tasks](#93.html_concept-task) is the [DOM manipulation task source](#93.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

The element must [delay the load event](#93.html_delay-the-load-event) of the element's document until all the attempts to obtain the resource and its [critical subresources](#93.html_critical-subresources) are complete. (Resources that the user agent has not yet attempted to obtain, e.g. because it is waiting for the resource to be needed, do not [delay the load event](#93.html_delay-the-load-event).)

* * *

Interactive user agents may provide users with a means to [follow the hyperlinks](#93.html_following-hyperlinks) created using the [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element, somewhere within their user interface. The exact interface is not defined by this specification, but it could include the following information (obtained from the element's attributes, again as defined below), in some form or another (possibly simplified), for each hyperlink created with each [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element in the document:

*   The relationship between this document and the resource (given by the [`rel`](#93.html_attr-link-rel) attribute)
*   The title of the resource (given by the [`title`](#93.html_attr-link-title) attribute).
*   The address of the resource (given by the [`href`](#93.html_attr-link-href) attribute).
*   The language of the resource (given by the [`hreflang`](#93.html_attr-link-hreflang) attribute).
*   The optimum media for the resource (given by the [`media`](#93.html_attr-link-media) attribute).

User agents could also include other information, such as the type of the resource (as given by the [`type`](#93.html_attr-link-type) attribute).

Hyperlinks created with the [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element and its [`rel`](#93.html_attr-link-rel) attribute apply to the whole page. This contrasts with the [`rel`](#93.html_attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute of [`a`](#93.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#93.html_the-area-element) elements, which indicates the type of a link whose context is given by the link's location within the document.

The <dfn id="93.html_attr-link-media" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-media">`media`</dfn> attribute says which media the resource applies to. The value must be a [valid media query](#93.html_valid-media-query).

If the link is a [hyperlink](#93.html_hyperlink) then the [`media`](#93.html_attr-link-media) attribute is purely advisory, and describes for which media the document in question was designed.

However, if the link is an [external resource link](#93.html_external-resource-link), then the [`media`](#93.html_attr-link-media) attribute is prescriptive. The user agent must apply the external resource when the [`media`](#93.html_attr-link-media) attribute's value [matches the environment](#93.html_matches-the-environment) and the other relevant conditions apply, and must not apply it otherwise.

The external resource might have further restrictions defined within that limit its applicability. For example, a CSS style sheet might have some `@media` blocks. This specification does not override such further restrictions or requirements.

The default, if the [`media`](#93.html_attr-link-media) attribute is omitted, is "`all`", meaning that by default links apply to all media.

The <dfn id="93.html_attr-link-hreflang" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-hreflang">`hreflang`</dfn> attribute on the [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element has the same semantics as the [`hreflang` attribute on `a` and `area` elements](#93.html_attr-hyperlink-hreflang).

The <dfn id="93.html_attr-link-type" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-type">`type`</dfn> attribute gives the [MIME type](#93.html_mime-type) of the linked resource. It is purely advisory. The value must be a [valid MIME type](#93.html_valid-mime-type).

For [external resource links](#93.html_external-resource-link), the [`type`](#93.html_attr-link-type) attribute is used as a hint to user agents so that they can avoid fetching resources they do not support. If the attribute is present, then the user agent must assume that the resource is of the given type (even if that is not a [valid MIME type](#93.html_valid-mime-type), e.g. the empty string). If the attribute is omitted, but the external resource link type has a default type defined, then the user agent must assume that the resource is of that type. If the UA does not support the given [MIME type](#93.html_mime-type) for the given link relationship, then the UA should not [obtain](#93.html_concept-link-obtain) the resource; if the UA does support the given [MIME type](#93.html_mime-type) for the given link relationship, then the UA should [obtain](#93.html_concept-link-obtain) the resource at the appropriate time as specified for the [external resource link](#93.html_external-resource-link)'s particular type. If the attribute is omitted, and the external resource link type does not have a default type defined, but the user agent would [obtain](#93.html_concept-link-obtain) the resource if the type was known and supported, then the user agent should [obtain](#93.html_concept-link-obtain) the resource under the assumption that it will be supported.

User agents must not consider the [`type`](#93.html_attr-link-type) attribute authoritative — upon fetching the resource, user agents must not use the [`type`](#93.html_attr-link-type) attribute to determine its actual type. Only the actual type (as defined in the next paragraph) is used to determine whether to *apply* the resource, not the aforementioned assumed type.

If the external resource link type defines rules for processing the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#93.html_content-type), then those rules apply. Otherwise, if the resource is expected to be an image, user agents may apply the [image sniffing rules](#93.html_content-type-sniffing:-image), with the `official type` being the type determined from the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#93.html_content-type), and use the resulting sniffed type of the resource as if it was the actual type. Otherwise, if neither of these conditions apply or if the user agent opts not to apply the image sniffing rules, then the user agent must use the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#93.html_content-type) to determine the type of the resource. If there is no type metadata, but the external resource link type has a default type defined, then the user agent must assume that the resource is of that type.

The [`stylesheet`](#93.html_link-type-stylesheet) link type defines rules for processing the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#93.html_content-type).

Once the user agent has established the type of the resource, the user agent must apply the resource if it is of a supported type and the other relevant conditions apply, and must ignore the resource otherwise.

If a document contains style sheet links labeled as follows:

```
<link rel="stylesheet" href="A" type="text/plain">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="B" type="text/css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="C">
```

...then a compliant UA that supported only CSS style sheets would fetch the B and C files, and skip the A file (since `text/plain` is not the [MIME type](#93.html_mime-type) for CSS style sheets).

For files B and C, it would then check the actual types returned by the server. For those that are sent as `text/css`, it would apply the styles, but for those labeled as `text/plain`, or any other type, it would not.

If one of the two files was returned without a [Content-Type](#93.html_content-type) metadata, or with a syntactically incorrect type like `Content-Type: "null"`, then the default type for [`stylesheet`](#93.html_link-type-stylesheet) links would kick in. Since that default type is `text/css`, the style sheet *would* nonetheless be applied.

The <dfn id="93.html_attr-link-title" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-title">`title`</dfn> attribute gives the title of the link. With one exception, it is purely advisory. The value is text. The exception is for style sheet links, where the [`title`](#93.html_attr-link-title) attribute defines [alternative style sheet sets](#93.html_alternative-style-sheet-sets).

The [`title`](#93.html_attr-link-title) attribute on [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) elements differs from the global [`title`](#93.html_attr-title) attribute of most other elements in that a link without a title does not inherit the title of the parent element: it merely has no title.

The [`sizes`](#93.html_attr-link-sizes) attribute is used with the [`icon`](#93.html_rel-icon) link type. The attribute must not be specified on [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) elements that do not have a [`rel`](#93.html_attr-link-rel) attribute that specifies the [`icon`](#93.html_rel-icon) keyword.

The [activation behavior](#93.html_activation-behavior) of [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) elements that create [hyperlinks](#93.html_hyperlink) is to run the following steps:

1.  If the [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element's [`Document`](#93.html_document) is not [fully active](#93.html_fully-active), then abort these steps.

2.  [Follow the hyperlink](#93.html_following-hyperlinks) created by the [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element.

HTTP `Link:` headers, if supported, must be assumed to come before any links in the document, in the order that they were given in the HTTP message. These headers are to be processed according to the rules given in the relevant specifications. [[HTTP]](#93.html_refsHTTP) [[WEBLINK]](#93.html_refsWEBLINK)

Registration of relation types in HTTP Link: headers is distinct from [HTML link types](#93.html_linkTypes), and thus their semantics can be different from same-named HTML types.

The IDL attributes <dfn id="93.html_dom-link-href" data-anolis-xref="dom-link-href">`href`</dfn>, <dfn id="93.html_dom-link-rel" data-anolis-xref="dom-link-rel">`rel`</dfn>, <dfn id="93.html_dom-link-rev" data-anolis-xref="dom-link-rev">`rev`</dfn>, <dfn id="93.html_dom-link-media" data-anolis-xref="dom-link-media">`media`</dfn>, <dfn id="93.html_dom-link-hreflang" data-anolis-xref="dom-link-hreflang">`hreflang`</dfn>, <dfn id="93.html_dom-link-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-link-type">`type`</dfn>, and <dfn id="93.html_dom-link-sizes" data-anolis-xref="dom-link-sizes">`sizes`</dfn> each must [reflect](#93.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

The <dfn id="93.html_dom-link-crossorigin" data-anolis-xref="dom-link-crossOrigin">`crossOrigin`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#93.html_reflect) the [`crossorigin`](#93.html_attr-link-crossorigin) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#93.html_limited-to-only-known-values).

The IDL attribute <dfn id="93.html_dom-link-rellist" data-anolis-xref="dom-link-rellist">`relList`</dfn> must [reflect](#93.html_reflect) the [`rel`](#93.html_attr-link-rel) content attribute.

The IDL attribute <dfn id="93.html_dom-link-disabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-link-disabled">`disabled`</dfn> only applies to style sheet links. When the [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) element defines a style sheet link, then the [`disabled`](#93.html_dom-link-disabled) attribute behaves as defined [for the alternative style sheets DOM](#93.html_dom-linkstyle-disabled). For all other [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) elements it always return false and does nothing on setting.

The [`LinkStyle`](#93.html_linkstyle) interface is also implemented by this element; the [styling processing model](#93.html_styling) defines how. [[CSSOM]](#93.html_refsCSSOM)

Here, a set of [`link`](#93.html_the-link-element) elements provide some style sheets:

```
<!-- a persistent style sheet -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="default.css">

<!-- the preferred alternate style sheet -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="green.css" title="Green styles">

<!-- some alternate style sheets -->
<link rel="alternate stylesheet" href="contrast.css" title="High contrast">
<link rel="alternate stylesheet" href="big.css" title="Big fonts">
<link rel="alternate stylesheet" href="wide.css" title="Wide screen">
```

The following example shows how you can specify versions of the page that use alternative formats, are aimed at other languages, and that are intended for other media:

```
<link rel=alternate href="/en/html" hreflang=en type=text/html title="English HTML">
<link rel=alternate href="/fr/html" hreflang=fr type=text/html title="French HTML">
<link rel=alternate href="/en/html/print" hreflang=en type=text/html media=print title="English HTML (for printing)">
<link rel=alternate href="/fr/html/print" hreflang=fr type=text/html media=print title="French HTML (for printing)">
<link rel=alternate href="/en/pdf" hreflang=en type=application/pdf title="English PDF">
<link rel=alternate href="/fr/pdf" hreflang=fr type=application/pdf title="French PDF">
```

#### 4.2.5 The <dfn id="94.html_meta">`meta`</dfn> element

[Categories](#94.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Metadata content](#94.html_metadata-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#94.html_element-dfn-contexts):

If the [`charset`](#94.html_attr-meta-charset) attribute is present, or if the element's [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute is in the [encoding declaration state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type): in a [`head`](#94.html_the-head-element) element.

If the [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute is present but not in the [encoding declaration state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type): in a [`head`](#94.html_the-head-element) element.

If the [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute is present but not in the [encoding declaration state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type): in a [`noscript`](#94.html_the-noscript-element) element that is a child of a [`head`](#94.html_the-head-element) element.

If the [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) attribute is present: where [metadata content](#94.html_metadata-content-0) is expected.

[Content model](#94.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#94.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#94.html_global-attributes)

[`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) — Metadata name

[`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) — Pragma directive

[`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) — Value of the element

[`charset`](#94.html_attr-meta-charset) — [Character encoding declaration](#94.html_character-encoding-declaration)

[Tag omission in text/html](#94.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

No [end tag](#94.html_syntax-end-tag).

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#94.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

none

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#94.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#94.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#94.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLMetaElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString name;
           attribute DOMString httpEquiv;
           attribute DOMString content;
};
```

The [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element [represents](#94.html_represents) various kinds of metadata that cannot be expressed using the [`title`](#94.html_the-title-element), [`base`](#94.html_the-base-element), [`link`](#94.html_the-link-element), [`style`](#94.html_the-style-element), and [`script`](#94.html_the-script-element) elements.

The [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element can represent document-level metadata with the [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) attribute, pragma directives with the [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute, and the file's [character encoding declaration](#94.html_character-encoding-declaration) when an HTML document is serialized to string form (e.g. for transmission over the network or for disk storage) with the [`charset`](#94.html_attr-meta-charset) attribute.

Exactly one of the [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name), [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv), and [`charset`](#94.html_attr-meta-charset), attributes must be specified.

If either [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) or [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) is specified, then the [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute must also be specified. Otherwise, it must be omitted.

The <dfn id="94.html_attr-meta-charset" data-anolis-xref="attr-meta-charset">`charset`</dfn> attribute specifies the character encoding used by the document. This is a [character encoding declaration](#94.html_character-encoding-declaration). If the attribute is present in an [XML document](#94.html_xml-documents), its value must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](#94.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`UTF-8`" (and the document is therefore forced to use UTF-8 as its encoding).

The [`charset`](#94.html_attr-meta-charset) attribute on the [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element has no effect in XML documents, and is only allowed in order to facilitate migration to and from XHTML.

There must not be more than one [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with a [`charset`](#94.html_attr-meta-charset) attribute per document.

The <dfn id="94.html_attr-meta-content" data-anolis-xref="attr-meta-content">`content`</dfn> attribute gives the value of the document metadata or pragma directive when the element is used for those purposes. The allowed values depend on the exact context, as described in subsequent sections of this specification.

If a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element has a <dfn id="94.html_attr-meta-name" data-anolis-xref="attr-meta-name">`name`</dfn> attribute, it sets document metadata. Document metadata is expressed in terms of name-value pairs, the [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) attribute on the [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element giving the name, and the [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute on the same element giving the value. The name specifies what aspect of metadata is being set; valid names and the meaning of their values are described in the following sections. If a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element has no [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute, then the value part of the metadata name-value pair is the empty string.

The <dfn id="94.html_dom-meta-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-meta-name">`name`</dfn> and <dfn id="94.html_dom-meta-content" data-anolis-xref="dom-meta-content">`content`</dfn> IDL attributes must [reflect](#94.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name. The IDL attribute <dfn id="94.html_dom-meta-httpequiv" data-anolis-xref="dom-meta-httpEquiv">`httpEquiv`</dfn> must [reflect](#94.html_reflect) the content attribute [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv).

##### 4.2.5.1 Standard metadata names

This specification defines a few names for the [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) attribute of the [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element.

Names are case-insensitive, and must be compared in an [ASCII case-insensitive](#94.html_ascii-case-insensitive) manner.

<dfn id="94.html_meta-application-name" data-anolis-xref="meta-application-name">`application-name`</dfn>

The value must be a short free-form string giving the name of the Web application that the page represents. If the page is not a Web application, the [`application-name`](#94.html_meta-application-name) metadata name must not be used. Translations of the Web application's name may be given, using the [](#94.html_attr-lang)attribute to specify the language of each name.

There must not be more than one [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with a given [language](#94.html_language) and with its [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) attribute set to the value [`application-name`](#94.html_meta-application-name) per document.

User agents may use the application name in UI in preference to the page's [`title`](#94.html_the-title-element), since the title might include status messages and the like relevant to the status of the page at a particular moment in time instead of just being the name of the application.

To find the application name to use given an ordered list of languages (e.g. British English, American English, and English), user agents must run the following steps:

1.  Let `languages` be the list of languages.

2.  Let `default language` be the [language](#94.html_language) of the [`Document`](#94.html_document)'s [root element](#94.html_root-element-of-a-document-object), if any, and if that language is not unknown.

3.  If there is a `default language`, and if it is not the same language as any of the languages is `languages`, append it to `languages`.

4.  Let `winning language` be the first language in `languages` for which there is a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element in the [`Document`](#94.html_document) that has its [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) attribute set to the value [`application-name`](#94.html_meta-application-name) and whose [language](#94.html_language) is the language in question.

    If none of the languages have such a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element, then abort these steps; there's no given application name.

5.  Return the value of the [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute of the first [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element in the [`Document`](#94.html_document) in [tree order](#94.html_tree-order) that has its [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) attribute set to the value [`application-name`](#94.html_meta-application-name) and whose [language](#94.html_language) is `winning language`.

<dfn id="94.html_meta-author" data-anolis-xref="meta-author">`author`</dfn>

The value must be a free-form string giving the name of one of the page's authors.

<dfn id="94.html_meta-description" data-anolis-xref="meta-description">`description`</dfn>

The value must be a free-form string that describes the page. The value must be appropriate for use in a directory of pages, e.g. in a search engine. There must not be more than one [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with its [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) attribute set to the value [`description`](#94.html_meta-description) per document.

<dfn id="94.html_meta-generator" data-anolis-xref="meta-generator">`generator`</dfn>

The value must be a free-form string that identifies one of the software packages used to generate the document. This value must not be used on pages whose markup is not generated by software, e.g. pages whose markup was written by a user in a text editor.

Here is what a tool called "Frontweaver" could include in its output, in the page's [`head`](#94.html_the-head-element) element, to identify itself as the tool used to generate the page:

```
<meta name=generator content="Frontweaver 8.2">
```

<dfn id="94.html_meta-keywords" data-anolis-xref="meta-keywords">`keywords`</dfn>

The value must be a [set of comma-separated tokens](#94.html_set-of-comma-separated-tokens), each of which is a keyword relevant to the page.

This page about typefaces on British motorways uses a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element to specify some keywords that users might use to look for the page:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html>
 <head>
  <title>Typefaces on UK motorways</title>
  <meta name="keywords" content="british,type face,font,fonts,highway,highways">
 </head>
 <body>
  ...
```

Many search engines do not consider such keywords, because this feature has historically been used unreliably and even misleadingly as a way to spam search engine results in a way that is not helpful for users.

To obtain the list of keywords that the author has specified as applicable to the page, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `keywords` be an empty list.

2.  For each [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with a [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) attribute and a [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute and whose [`name`](#94.html_attr-meta-name) attribute's value is [`keywords`](#94.html_meta-keywords), run the following substeps:

    1.  [Split the value of the element's `content` attribute on commas](#94.html_split-a-string-on-commas).

    2.  Add the resulting tokens, if any, to `keywords`.

3.  Remove any duplicates from `keywords`.

4.  Return `keywords`. This is the list of keywords that the author has specified as applicable to the page.

User agents should not use this information when there is insufficient confidence in the reliability of the value.

For instance, it would be reasonable for a content management system to use the keyword information of pages within the system to populate the index of a site-specific search engine, but a large-scale content aggregator that used this information would likely find that certain users would try to game its ranking mechanism through the use of inappropriate keywords.

##### 4.2.5.2 Other metadata names

<dfn id="94.html_concept-meta-extensions" data-anolis-xref="concept-meta-extensions">Extensions to the predefined set of metadata names</dfn> may be registered in the [WHATWG Wiki MetaExtensions page](http://wiki.whatwg.org/wiki/MetaExtensions). [[WHATWGWIKI]](#94.html_refsWHATWGWIKI)

Anyone is free to edit the WHATWG Wiki MetaExtensions page at any time to add a type. These new names must be specified with the following information:

Keyword

The actual name being defined. The name should not be confusingly similar to any other defined name (e.g. differing only in case).

Brief description

A short non-normative description of what the metadata name's meaning is, including the format the value is required to be in.

Specification

A link to a more detailed description of the metadata name's semantics and requirements. It could be another page on the Wiki, or a link to an external page.

Synonyms

A list of other names that have exactly the same processing requirements. Authors should not use the names defined to be synonyms, they are only intended to allow user agents to support legacy content. Anyone may remove synonyms that are not used in practice; only names that need to be processed as synonyms for compatibility with legacy content are to be registered in this way.

Status

One of the following:

Proposed

The name has not received wide peer review and approval. Someone has proposed it and is, or soon will be, using it.

Ratified

The name has received wide peer review and approval. It has a specification that unambiguously defines how to handle pages that use the name, including when they use it in incorrect ways.

Discontinued

The metadata name has received wide peer review and it has been found wanting. Existing pages are using this metadata name, but new pages should avoid it. The "brief description" and "specification" entries will give details of what authors should use instead, if anything.

If a metadata name is found to be redundant with existing values, it should be removed and listed as a synonym for the existing value.

If a metadata name is registered in the "proposed" state for a period of a month or more without being used or specified, then it may be removed from the registry.

If a metadata name is added with the "proposed" status and found to be redundant with existing values, it should be removed and listed as a synonym for the existing value. If a metadata name is added with the "proposed" status and found to be harmful, then it should be changed to "discontinued" status.

Anyone can change the status at any time, but should only do so in accordance with the definitions above.

Conformance checkers may use the information given on the WHATWG Wiki MetaExtensions page to establish if a value is allowed or not: values defined in this specification or marked as "proposed" or "ratified" must be accepted, whereas values marked as "discontinued" or not listed in either this specification or on the aforementioned page must be reported as invalid. Conformance checkers may cache this information (e.g. for performance reasons or to avoid the use of unreliable network connectivity).

When an author uses a new metadata name not defined by either this specification or the Wiki page, conformance checkers should offer to add the value to the Wiki, with the details described above, with the "proposed" status.

Metadata names whose values are to be URLs must not be proposed or accepted. Links must be represented using the [`link`](#94.html_the-link-element) element, not the [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element.

##### 4.2.5.3 Pragma directives

When the <dfn id="94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv" data-anolis-xref="attr-meta-http-equiv">`http-equiv`</dfn> attribute is specified on a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element, the element is a pragma directive.

The [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#94.html_enumerated-attribute). The following table lists the keywords defined for this attribute. The states given in the first cell of the rows with keywords give the states to which those keywords map. Some of the keywords are non-conforming, as noted in the last column.

| State | Keyword | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Content Language](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-language) | `content-language` | Non-conforming |
| [Encoding declaration](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type) | `content-type` |  |
| [Default style](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-default-style) | `default-style` |  |
| [Refresh](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-refresh) | `refresh` |  |
| [Cookie setter](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-set-cookie) | `set-cookie` | Non-conforming |

When a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element is [inserted into the document](#94.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document), if its [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute is present and represents one of the above states, then the user agent must run the algorithm appropriate for that state, as described in the following list:

<dfn id="94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-language" data-anolis-xref="attr-meta-http-equiv-content-language">Content language state</dfn> (`http-equiv="content-language"`)

This feature is non-conforming. Authors are encouraged to use the [`lang`](#94.html_attr-lang) attribute instead.

This pragma sets the <dfn id="94.html_pragma-set-default-language">pragma-set default language</dfn>. Until such a pragma is successfully processed, there is no [pragma-set default language](#94.html_pragma-set-default-language).

1.  If the [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element has no [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute, then abort these steps.

2.  If the element's [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute contains a "," (U+002C) character then abort these steps.

3.  Let `input` be the value of the element's [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute.

4.  Let `position` point at the first character of `input`.

5.  [Skip whitespace](#94.html_skip-whitespace).

6.  [Collect a sequence of characters](#94.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are not [space characters](#94.html_space-character).

7.  Let `candidate` be the string that resulted from the previous step.

8.  If `candidate` is the empty string, abort these steps.

9.  Set the [pragma-set default language](#94.html_pragma-set-default-language) to `candidate`.

This pragma is almost, but not quite, entirely unlike the HTTP `Content-Language` header of the same name. [[HTTP]](#94.html_refsHTTP)

<dfn id="94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type" data-anolis-xref="attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type">encoding declaration state</dfn> (`http-equiv="content-type"`)

The [encoding declaration state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type) is just an alternative form of setting the `charset` attribute: it is a [character encoding declaration](#94.html_character-encoding-declaration). This state's user agent requirements are all handled by the parsing section of the specification.

For [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) elements with an [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the [Encoding declaration state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type), the [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute must have a value that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#94.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for a string that consists of: the literal string "`text/html;`", optionally followed by any number of [space characters](#94.html_space-character), followed by the literal string "`charset=`", followed by one of the [labels](#94.html_encoding-label) of the [character encoding](#94.html_encoding) of the [character encoding declaration](#94.html_character-encoding-declaration).

A document must not contain both a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with an [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the [encoding declaration state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type) and a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with the [`charset`](#94.html_attr-meta-charset) attribute present.

The [encoding declaration state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type) may be used in [HTML documents](#94.html_html-documents) and in [XML Documents](#94.html_xml-documents). If the [encoding declaration state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type) is used in [XML Documents](#94.html_xml-documents), the name of the [character encoding](#94.html_encoding) must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](#94.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`UTF-8`" (and the document is therefore forced to use UTF-8 as its encoding).

The [encoding declaration state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type) has no effect in XML documents, and is only allowed in order to facilitate migration to and from XHTML.

<dfn id="94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-default-style" data-anolis-xref="attr-meta-http-equiv-default-style">Default style state</dfn> (`http-equiv="default-style"`)

This pragma sets the name of the default [alternative style sheet set](#94.html_alternative-style-sheet-sets).

1.  If the [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element has no [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute, or if that attribute's value is the empty string, then abort these steps.

2.  Set the [preferred style sheet set](#94.html_preferred-style-sheet-set) to the value of the element's [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute. [[CSSOM]](#94.html_refsCSSOM)

<dfn id="94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-refresh" data-anolis-xref="attr-meta-http-equiv-refresh">Refresh state</dfn> (`http-equiv="refresh"`)

This pragma acts as timed redirect.

1.  If another [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with an [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the [Refresh state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-refresh) has already been successfully processed (i.e. when it was inserted the user agent processed it and reached the last step of this list of steps), then abort these steps.

2.  If the [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element has no [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute, or if that attribute's value is the empty string, then abort these steps.

3.  Let `input` be the value of the element's [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute.

4.  Let `position` point at the first character of `input`.

5.  [Skip whitespace](#94.html_skip-whitespace).

6.  [Collect a sequence of characters](#94.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are [ASCII digits](#94.html_ascii-digits), and parse the resulting string using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#94.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers). If the sequence of characters collected is the empty string, then no number will have been parsed; abort these steps. Otherwise, let `time` be the parsed number.

7.  [Collect a sequence of characters](#94.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are [ASCII digits](#94.html_ascii-digits) and "." (U+002E) characters. Ignore any collected characters.

8.  [Skip whitespace](#94.html_skip-whitespace).

9.  Let `url` be the address of the current page.

10.  If the character in `input` pointed to by `position` is a ";" (U+003B) character or a "," (U+002C) character, then advance `position` to the next character. Otherwise, jump to the last step.

11.  [Skip whitespace](#94.html_skip-whitespace).

12.  If the character in `input` pointed to by `position` is a "U" (U+0055) character or a U+0075 LATIN SMALL LETTER U character (u), then advance `position` to the next character. Otherwise, jump to the last step.

13.  If the character in `input` pointed to by `position` is a "R" (U+0052) character or a U+0072 LATIN SMALL LETTER R character (r), then advance `position` to the next character. Otherwise, jump to the last step.

14.  If the character in `input` pointed to by `position` is s "L" (U+004C) character or a U+006C LATIN SMALL LETTER L character (l), then advance `position` to the next character. Otherwise, jump to the last step.

15.  [Skip whitespace](#94.html_skip-whitespace).

16.  If the character in `input` pointed to by `position` is a "=" (U+003D), then advance `position` to the next character. Otherwise, jump to the last step.

17.  [Skip whitespace](#94.html_skip-whitespace).

18.  If the character in `input` pointed to by `position` is either a "'" (U+0027) character or """ (U+0022) character, then let `quote` be that character, and advance `position` to the next character. Otherwise, let `quote` be the empty string.

19.  Let `url` be equal to the substring of `input` from the character at `position` to the end of the string.

20.  If `quote` is not the empty string, and there is a character in `url` equal to `quote`, then truncate `url` at that character, so that it and all subsequent characters are removed.

21.  Strip any trailing [space characters](#94.html_space-character) from the end of `url`.

22.  Strip any "tab" (U+0009), "LF" (U+000A), and "CR" (U+000D) characters from `url`.

23.  [Resolve](#94.html_resolve-a-url) the `url` value to an [absolute URL](#94.html_absolute-url), relative to the [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element. If this fails, abort these steps.

24.  Perform one or more of the following steps:

    *   After the refresh has come due (as defined below), if the user has not canceled the redirect and if the [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element's [`Document`](#94.html_document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#94.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) does not have the [sandboxed automatic features browsing context flag](#94.html_sandboxed-automatic-features-browsing-context-flag) set, [navigate](#94.html_navigate) the [`Document`](#94.html_document)'s [browsing context](#94.html_browsing-context) to `url`, with [replacement enabled](#94.html_replacement-enabled), and with the [`Document`](#94.html_document)'s [browsing context](#94.html_browsing-context) as the [source browsing context](#94.html_source-browsing-context).

        For the purposes of the previous paragraph, a refresh is said to have come due as soon as the *later* of the following two conditions occurs:

        *   At least `time` seconds have elapsed since the document has [completely loaded](#94.html_completely-loaded), adjusted to take into account user or user agent preferences.
        *   At least `time` seconds have elapsed since the [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element was [inserted into the `Document`](#94.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document), adjusted to take into account user or user agent preferences.
    *   Provide the user with an interface that, when selected, [navigates](#94.html_navigate) a [browsing context](#94.html_browsing-context) to `url`, with the [`Document`](#94.html_document)'s [browsing context](#94.html_browsing-context) as the [source browsing context](#94.html_source-browsing-context).

    *   Do nothing.

    In addition, the user agent may, as with anything, inform the user of any and all aspects of its operation, including the state of any timers, the destinations of any timed redirects, and so forth.

For [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) elements with an [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the [Refresh state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-refresh), the [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute must have a value consisting either of:

*   just a [valid non-negative integer](#94.html_valid-non-negative-integer), or
*   a [valid non-negative integer](#94.html_valid-non-negative-integer), followed by a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;), followed by one or more [space characters](#94.html_space-character), followed by a substring that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#94.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`URL`", followed by a "=" (U+003D) character, followed by a [valid URL](#94.html_valid-url) that does not start with a literal "'" (U+0027) or """ (U+0022) character.

In the former case, the integer represents a number of seconds before the page is to be reloaded; in the latter case the integer represents a number of seconds before the page is to be replaced by the page at the given URL.

A news organization's front page could include the following markup in the page's [`head`](#94.html_the-head-element) element, to ensure that the page automatically reloads from the server every five minutes:

```
<meta http-equiv="Refresh" content="300">
```

A sequence of pages could be used as an automated slide show by making each page refresh to the next page in the sequence, using markup such as the following:

```
<meta http-equiv="Refresh" content="20; URL=page4.html">
```

<dfn id="94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-set-cookie" data-anolis-xref="attr-meta-http-equiv-set-cookie">Cookie setter</dfn> (`http-equiv="set-cookie"`)

This pragma sets an HTTP cookie. [[COOKIES]](#94.html_refsCOOKIES)

It is non-conforming. Real HTTP headers should be used instead.

1.  If the [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element has no [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute, or if that attribute's value is the empty string, then abort these steps.

2.  [Obtain the storage mutex](#94.html_obtain-the-storage-mutex).

3.  Act as if [receiving a set-cookie-string](#94.html_receives-a-set-cookie-string) for [the document's address](#94.html_the-document's-address) via a "non-HTTP" API, consisting of the value of the element's [`content`](#94.html_attr-meta-content) attribute encoded as UTF-8\. [[COOKIES]](#94.html_refsCOOKIES) [[RFC3629]](#94.html_refsRFC3629)

There must not be more than one [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with any particular state in the document at a time.

##### 4.2.5.4 Other pragma directives

<dfn id="94.html_concept-http-equiv-extensions" data-anolis-xref="concept-http-equiv-extensions">Extensions to the predefined set of pragma directives</dfn> may, under certain conditions, be registered in the [WHATWG Wiki PragmaExtensions page](http://wiki.whatwg.org/wiki/PragmaExtensions). [[WHATWGWIKI]](#94.html_refsWHATWGWIKI)

Such extensions must use a name that is identical to an HTTP header registered in the Permanent Message Header Field Registry, and must have behavior identical to that described for the HTTP header. [[IANAPERMHEADERS]](#94.html_refsIANAPERMHEADERS)

Pragma directives corresponding to headers describing metadata, or not requiring specific user agent processing, must not be registered; instead, use [metadata names](#94.html_concept-meta-extensions). Pragma directives corresponding to headers that affect the HTTP processing model (e.g. caching) must not be registered, as they would result in HTTP-level behavior being different for user agents that implement HTML than for user agents that do not.

Anyone is free to edit the WHATWG Wiki PragmaExtensions page at any time to add a pragma directive satisfying these conditions. Such registrations must specify the following information:

Keyword

The actual name being defined. The name must match a previously-registered HTTP name with the same requirements.

Brief description

A short non-normative description of the purpose of the pragma directive.

Specification

A link to the specification defining the corresponding HTTP header.

Conformance checkers must use the information given on the WHATWG Wiki PragmaExtensions page to establish if a value is allowed or not: values defined in this specification or listed on the aforementioned page must be accepted, whereas values not listed in either this specification or on the aforementioned page must be rejected as invalid. Conformance checkers may cache this information (e.g. for performance reasons or to avoid the use of unreliable network connectivity).

##### 4.2.5.5 Specifying the document's character encoding

A <dfn id="94.html_character-encoding-declaration">character encoding declaration</dfn> is a mechanism by which the [character encoding](#94.html_encoding) used to store or transmit a document is specified.

The following restrictions apply to [character encoding declarations](#94.html_character-encoding-declaration):

*   The character encoding name given must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](#94.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for one of the [labels](#94.html_encoding-label) of the [character encoding](#94.html_encoding) used to serialize the file. [[ENCODING]](#94.html_refsENCODING)
*   The character encoding declaration must be serialized without the use of [character references](#94.html_syntax-charref) or character escapes of any kind.
*   The element containing the character encoding declaration must be serialized completely within the first 1024 bytes of the document.

In addition, due to a number of restrictions on [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) elements, there can only be one [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element)-based character encoding declaration per document.

If an [HTML document](#94.html_html-documents) does not start with a BOM, and its [encoding](#94.html_encoding) is not explicitly given by [Content-Type metadata](#94.html_content-type), and the document is not [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#94.html_an-iframe-srcdoc-document), then the character encoding used must be an [ASCII-compatible character encoding](#94.html_ascii-compatible-character-encoding), and the encoding must be specified using a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with a [`charset`](#94.html_attr-meta-charset) attribute or a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with an [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the [encoding declaration state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type).

A character encoding declaration is required (either in the [Content-Type metadata](#94.html_content-type) or explicitly in the file) even if the encoding is US-ASCII, because a character encoding is needed to process non-ASCII characters entered by the user in forms, in URLs generated by scripts, and so forth.

If the document is [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#94.html_an-iframe-srcdoc-document), the document must not have a [character encoding declaration](#94.html_character-encoding-declaration). (In this case, the source is already decoded, since it is part of the document that contained the [`iframe`](#94.html_the-iframe-element).)

If an [HTML document](#94.html_html-documents) contains a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with a [`charset`](#94.html_attr-meta-charset) attribute or a [`meta`](#94.html_the-meta-element) element with an [`http-equiv`](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv) attribute in the [encoding declaration state](#94.html_attr-meta-http-equiv-content-type), then the character encoding used must be an [ASCII-compatible character encoding](#94.html_ascii-compatible-character-encoding).

Authors should use UTF-8\. Conformance checkers may advise authors against using legacy encodings. [[RFC3629]](#94.html_refsRFC3629)

Authoring tools should default to using UTF-8 for newly-created documents. [[RFC3629]](#94.html_refsRFC3629)

Encodings in which a series of bytes in the range 0x20 to 0x7E can encode characters other than the corresponding characters in the range U+0020 to U+007E represent a potential security vulnerability: a user agent that does not support the encoding (or does not support the label used to declare the encoding, or does not use the same mechanism to detect the encoding of unlabeled content as another user agent) might end up interpreting technically benign plain text content as HTML tags and JavaScript. Authors should therefore not use these encodings. For example, this applies to encodings in which the bytes corresponding to "`<script>`" in ASCII can encode a different string. Authors should not use such encodings, which are known to include JIS_C6226-1983, JIS_X0212-1990, HZ-GB-2312, JOHAB (Windows code page 1361), encodings based on ISO-2022, and encodings based on EBCDIC. Furthermore, authors must not use the CESU-8, UTF-7, BOCU-1 and SCSU encodings, which also fall into this category; these encodings were never intended for use for Web content. [[RFC1345]](#94.html_refsRFC1345) [[RFC1842]](#94.html_refsRFC1842) [[RFC1468]](#94.html_refsRFC1468) [[RFC2237]](#94.html_refsRFC2237) [[RFC1554]](#94.html_refsRFC1554) [[CP50220]](#94.html_refsCP50220) [[RFC1922]](#94.html_refsRFC1922) [[RFC1557]](#94.html_refsRFC1557) [[CESU8]](#94.html_refsCESU8) [[UTF7]](#94.html_refsUTF7) [[BOCU1]](#94.html_refsBOCU1) [[SCSU]](#94.html_refsSCSU)

Authors should not use UTF-32, as the encoding detection algorithms described in this specification intentionally do not distinguish it from UTF-16\. [[UNICODE]](#94.html_refsUNICODE)

Using non-UTF-8 encodings can have unexpected results on form submission and URL encodings, which use the [document's character encoding](#94.html_document's-character-encoding) by default.

In XHTML, the XML declaration should be used for inline character encoding information, if necessary.

In HTML, to declare that the character encoding is UTF-8, the author could include the following markup near the top of the document (in the [`head`](#94.html_the-head-element) element):

```
<meta charset="utf-8">
```

In XML, the XML declaration would be used instead, at the very top of the markup:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
```

#### 4.2.6 The <dfn>`style`</dfn> element

[Categories](#95.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Metadata content](#95.html_metadata-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#95.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [metadata content](#95.html_metadata-content-0) is expected.

In a [`noscript`](#95.html_the-noscript-element) element that is a child of a [`head`](#95.html_the-head-element) element.

[Content model](#95.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Depends on the value of the [`type`](#95.html_attr-style-type) attribute, but must match requirements described in prose below.

[Content attributes](#95.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#95.html_global-attributes)

[`media`](#95.html_attr-style-media) — Applicable media

[`type`](#95.html_attr-style-type) — Type of embedded resource

Also, the [`title`](#95.html_attr-style-title) attribute has special semantics on this element: Alternative style sheet set name.

[Tag omission in text/html](#95.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#95.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

none

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#95.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#95.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#95.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLStyleElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute boolean disabled;
           attribute DOMString media;
           attribute DOMString type;
};
HTMLStyleElement implements LinkStyle;
```

The [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) element allows authors to embed style information in their documents. The [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) element is one of several inputs to the [styling processing model](#95.html_styling). The element does not [represent](#95.html_represents) content for the user.

The <dfn id="95.html_attr-style-type" data-anolis-xref="attr-style-type">`type`</dfn> attribute gives the styling language. If the attribute is present, its value must be a [valid MIME type](#95.html_valid-mime-type) that designates a styling language. The `charset` parameter must not be specified. The default value for the [`type`](#95.html_attr-style-type) attribute, which is used if the attribute is absent, is "`text/css`". [[RFC2318]](#95.html_refsRFC2318)

When examining types to determine if they support the language, user agents must not ignore unknown MIME parameters — types with unknown parameters must be assumed to be unsupported. The `charset` parameter must be treated as an unknown parameter for the purpose of comparing [MIME types](#95.html_mime-type) here.

The <dfn id="95.html_attr-style-media" data-anolis-xref="attr-style-media">`media`</dfn> attribute says which media the styles apply to. The value must be a [valid media query](#95.html_valid-media-query). The user agent must apply the styles when the [`media`](#95.html_attr-style-media) attribute's value [matches the environment](#95.html_matches-the-environment) and the other relevant conditions apply, and must not apply them otherwise.

The styles might be further limited in scope, e.g. in CSS with the use of `@media` blocks. This specification does not override such further restrictions or requirements.

The default, if the [`media`](#95.html_attr-style-media) attribute is omitted, is "`all`", meaning that by default styles apply to all media.

The <dfn id="95.html_attr-style-title" data-anolis-xref="attr-style-title">`title`</dfn> attribute on [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) elements defines [alternative style sheet sets](#95.html_alternative-style-sheet-sets). If the [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) element has no [`title`](#95.html_attr-style-title) attribute, then it has no title; the [`title`](#95.html_attr-title) attribute of ancestors does not apply to the [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) element. [[CSSOM]](#95.html_refsCSSOM)

The [`title`](#95.html_attr-style-title) attribute on [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) elements, like the [`title`](#95.html_attr-link-title) attribute on [`link`](#95.html_the-link-element) elements, differs from the global [`title`](#95.html_attr-title) attribute in that a [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) block without a title does not inherit the title of the parent element: it merely has no title.

The [`textContent`](#95.html_textcontent) of a [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) element must match the `style` production in the following ABNF, the character set for which is Unicode. [[ABNF]](#95.html_refsABNF)

```
style         = no-c-start *( c-start no-c-end c-end no-c-start )
no-c-start    = < any string that doesn't contain a substring that matches c-start >
c-start       = "<!--"
no-c-end      = < any string that doesn't contain a substring that matches c-end >
c-end         = "-->"
```

All descendant elements must be processed, according to their semantics, before the [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) element itself is evaluated. For styling languages that consist of pure text (as opposed to XML), user agents must evaluate [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) elements by passing the concatenation of the contents of all the [`Text`](#95.html_text-0) nodes that are children of the [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) element (not any other nodes such as comments or elements), in [tree order](#95.html_tree-order), to the style system. For XML-based styling languages, user agents must pass all the child nodes of the [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) element to the style system.

All URLs found by the styling language's processor must be [resolved](#95.html_resolve-a-url), relative to the element (or as defined by the styling language), when the processor is invoked.

Once the attempts to obtain the style sheet's [critical subresources](#95.html_critical-subresources), if any, are complete, or, if the style sheet has no [critical subresources](#95.html_critical-subresources), once the style sheet has been parsed and processed, the user agent must, if the loads were successful or there were none, [queue a task](#95.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#95.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `load` at the [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) element, or, if one of the style sheet's [critical subresources](#95.html_critical-subresources) failed to completely load for any reason (e.g. DNS error, HTTP 404 response, a connection being prematurely closed, unsupported Content-Type), [queue a task](#95.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#95.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `error` at the [`style`](#95.html_the-style-element) element. Non-network errors in processing the style sheet or its subresources (e.g. CSS parse errors, PNG decoding errors) are not failures for the purposes of this paragraph.

The [task source](#95.html_task-source) for these [tasks](#95.html_concept-task) is the [DOM manipulation task source](#95.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

The element must [delay the load event](#95.html_delay-the-load-event) of the element's document until all the attempts to obtain the style sheet's [critical subresources](#95.html_critical-subresources), if any, are complete.

This specification does not specify a style system, but CSS is expected to be supported by most Web browsers. [[CSS]](#95.html_refsCSS)

The <dfn id="95.html_dom-style-media" data-anolis-xref="dom-style-media">`media`</dfn> and <dfn id="95.html_dom-style-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-style-type">`type`</dfn> IDL attributes must [reflect](#95.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

The <dfn id="95.html_dom-style-disabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-style-disabled">`disabled`</dfn> IDL attribute behaves as defined [for the alternative style sheets DOM](#95.html_dom-linkstyle-disabled).

The [`LinkStyle`](#95.html_linkstyle) interface is also implemented by this element; the [styling processing model](#95.html_styling) defines how. [[CSSOM]](#95.html_refsCSSOM)

The following document has its stress emphasis styled as bright red text rather than italics text, while leaving titles of works and Latin words in their default italics. It shows how using appropriate elements enables easier restyling of documents.

```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en-US">
 <head>
  <title>My favorite book</title>
  <style>
   body { color: black; background: white; }
   em { font-style: normal; color: red; }
  </style>
 </head>
 <body>
  <p>My <em>favorite</em> book of all time has <em>got</em> to be
  <cite>A Cat's Life</cite>. It is a book by P. Rahmel that talks
  about the <i lang="la">Felis Catus</i> in modern human society.</p>
 </body>
</html>
```

#### 4.2.7 <dfn id="96.html_styling-processing-model" data-anolis-xref="styling processing model">Styling</dfn>

The [`link`](#96.html_the-link-element) and [`style`](#96.html_the-style-element) elements can provide styling information for the user agent to use when rendering the document. The CSS and CSSOM specifications specify what styling information is to be used by the user agent and how it is to be used. [[CSS]](#96.html_refsCSS) [[CSSOM]](#96.html_refsCSSOM)
