The [`style`](#96.html_the-style-element) and [`link`](#96.html_the-link-element) elements implement the [`LinkStyle`](#96.html_linkstyle) interface. [[CSSOM]](#96.html_refsCSSOM)

For [`style`](#96.html_the-style-element) elements, if the user agent does not support the specified styling language, then the [`sheet`](#96.html_dom-linkstyle-sheet) attribute of the element's [`LinkStyle`](#96.html_linkstyle) interface must return null. Similarly, [`link`](#96.html_the-link-element) elements that do not represent [external resource links that contribute to the styling processing model](#96.html_link-type-stylesheet) (i.e. that do not have a [`stylesheet`](#96.html_link-type-stylesheet) keyword in their [`rel`](#96.html_attr-link-rel) attribute), for which [the link is an alternative stylesheet](#96.html_the-link-is-an-alternative-stylesheet) but whose [`title`](#96.html_dom-title) content attribute is absent or empty, or whose resource is [CORS-cross-origin](#96.html_cors-cross-origin), must have their [`LinkStyle`](#96.html_linkstyle) interface's [`sheet`](#96.html_dom-linkstyle-sheet) attribute return null.

Otherwise, the [`LinkStyle`](#96.html_linkstyle) interface's [`sheet`](#96.html_dom-linkstyle-sheet) attribute must return null if the corresponding element is not [in a `Document`](#96.html_in-a-document), and otherwise must return a [`StyleSheet`](#96.html_stylesheet) object with the following properties: [[CSSOM]](#96.html_refsCSSOM)

The style sheet type

The style sheet type must be the same as the style's specified type. For [`style`](#96.html_the-style-element) elements, this is the same as the [`type`](#96.html_attr-style-type) content attribute's value, or `text/css` if that is omitted. For [`link`](#96.html_the-link-element) elements, this is the [Content-Type metadata of the specified resource](#96.html_content-type).

The style sheet location

For [`link`](#96.html_the-link-element) elements, the location must be the result of [resolving](#96.html_resolve-a-url) the URL given by the element's [`href`](#96.html_attr-link-href) content attribute, relative to the element, or the empty string if that fails. For [`style`](#96.html_the-style-element) elements, there is no location.

The style sheet media

The media must be the same as the value of the element's `media` content attribute, or the empty string, if the attribute is omitted.

The style sheet title

The title must be the same as the value of the element's [`title`](#96.html_dom-title) content attribute, if the attribute is present and has a non-empty value. If the attribute is absent or its value is the empty string, then the style sheet does not have a title (it is the empty string). The title is used for defining [alternative style sheet sets](#96.html_alternative-style-sheet-sets).

The style sheet alternate flag

For [`link`](#96.html_the-link-element) elements, true if [the link is an alternative stylesheet](#96.html_the-link-is-an-alternative-stylesheet). In all other cases, false.

The same object must be returned each time.

The <dfn id="96.html_dom-linkstyle-disabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-LinkStyle-disabled">`disabled`</dfn> IDL attribute on [`link`](#96.html_the-link-element) and [`style`](#96.html_the-style-element) elements must return false and do nothing on setting, if the [`sheet`](#96.html_dom-linkstyle-sheet) attribute of their [`LinkStyle`](#96.html_linkstyle) interface is null. Otherwise, it must return the value of the [`StyleSheet`](#96.html_stylesheet) interface's [`disabled`](#96.html_dom-stylesheet-disabled) attribute on getting, and forward the new value to that same attribute on setting.

The rules for handling alternative style sheets are defined in the CSS object model specification. [[CSSOM]](#96.html_refsCSSOM)

* * *

Style sheets, whether added by a [`link`](#96.html_the-link-element) element, a [`style`](#96.html_the-style-element) element, an `<?xml-stylesheet>` PI, an HTTP `Link:` header, or some other mechanism, have a <dfn id="96.html_style-sheet-ready">style sheet ready</dfn> flag, which is initially unset.

When a style sheet is ready to be applied, its [style sheet ready](#96.html_style-sheet-ready) flag must be set. If the style sheet referenced no other resources (e.g. it was an internal style sheet given by a [`style`](#96.html_the-style-element) element with no `@import` rules), then the style rules must be synchronously made available to script; otherwise, the style rules must only be made available to script once the [event loop](#96.html_event-loop) reaches its "update the rendering" step.

A style sheet in the context of the [`Document`](#96.html_document) of an [HTML parser](#96.html_html-parser) or [XML parser](#96.html_xml-parser) is said to be <dfn id="96.html_a-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts">a style sheet that is blocking scripts</dfn> if the element was created by that [`Document`](#96.html_document)'s parser, and the element is either a [`style`](#96.html_the-style-element) element or a [`link`](#96.html_the-link-element) element that was an [external resource link that contributes to the styling processing model](#96.html_link-type-stylesheet) when the element was created by the parser, and the element's style sheet was enabled when the element was created by the parser, and the element's [style sheet ready](#96.html_style-sheet-ready) flag is not yet set, and, the last time the [event loop](#96.html_event-loop) reached step 1, the element was [in that `Document`](#96.html_in-a-document), and the user agent hasn't given up on that particular style sheet yet. A user agent may give up on a style sheet at any time.

Giving up on a style sheet before the style sheet loads, if the style sheet eventually does still load, means that the script might end up operating with incorrect information. For example, if a style sheet sets the color of an element to green, but a script that inspects the resulting style is executed before the sheet is loaded, the script will find that the element is black (or whatever the default color is), and might thus make poor choices (e.g. deciding to use black as the color elsewhere on the page, instead of green). Implementors have to balance the likelihood of a script using incorrect information with the performance impact of doing nothing while waiting for a slow network request to finish.

A [`Document`](#96.html_document) <dfn id="96.html_has-a-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts">has a style sheet that is blocking scripts</dfn> if there is either [a style sheet that is blocking scripts](#96.html_a-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts) in the context of that [`Document`](#96.html_document), or if that [`Document`](#96.html_document) is in a [browsing context](#96.html_browsing-context) that has a [parent browsing context](#96.html_parent-browsing-context), and the [active document](#96.html_active-document) of that [parent browsing context](#96.html_parent-browsing-context) itself [has a style sheet that is blocking scripts](#96.html_has-a-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts).

A [`Document`](#96.html_document) <dfn id="96.html_has-no-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts">has no style sheet that is blocking scripts</dfn> if it does not [have a style sheet that is blocking scripts](#96.html_has-a-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts) as defined in the previous paragraph.

### 4.3 Sections

#### 4.3.1 The <dfn>`body`</dfn> element

[Categories](#98.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Sectioning root](#98.html_sectioning-root).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#98.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As the second element in an [`html`](#98.html_the-html-element) element.

[Content model](#98.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Flow content](#98.html_flow-content-1).

[Content attributes](#98.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#98.html_global-attributes)

[`onafterprint`](#98.html_handler-window-onafterprint)

[`onbeforeprint`](#98.html_handler-window-onbeforeprint)

[`onbeforeunload`](#98.html_handler-window-onbeforeunload)

[`onhashchange`](#98.html_handler-window-onhashchange)

[`onmessage`](#98.html_handler-window-onmessage)

[`onoffline`](#98.html_handler-window-onoffline)

[`ononline`](#98.html_handler-window-ononline)

[`onpagehide`](#98.html_handler-window-onpagehide)

[`onpageshow`](#98.html_handler-window-onpageshow)

[`onpopstate`](#98.html_handler-window-onpopstate)

[`onstorage`](#98.html_handler-window-onstorage)

[`onunload`](#98.html_handler-window-onunload)

[Tag omission in text/html](#98.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

A [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element's [start tag](#98.html_syntax-start-tag) may be omitted if the element is empty, or if the first thing inside the [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element is not a [space character](#98.html_space-character) or a [comment](#98.html_syntax-comments), except if the first thing inside the [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element is a [`meta`](#98.html_the-meta-element), [`link`](#98.html_the-link-element), [`script`](#98.html_the-script-element), [`style`](#98.html_the-style-element), or [`template`](#98.html_the-template-element) element.

A [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element's [end tag](#98.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element is not immediately followed by a [comment](#98.html_syntax-comments).

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#98.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`document`](#98.html_index-aria-document) role (default - [*do not set*](#98.html_aria-usage-note)), [`application`](#98.html_index-aria-application).

Allowed [ARIA State and Property Attributes](#98.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#98.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#98.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#98.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLBodyElement : HTMLElement {
};
HTMLBodyElement implements WindowEventHandlers;
```

The [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element [represents](#98.html_represents) the content of the document.

In conforming documents, there is only one [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element. The [`document.body`](#98.html_dom-document-body) IDL attribute provides scripts with easy access to a document's [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element.

Some DOM operations are defined in terms of "[the body element](#98.html_the-body-element-0)". This refers to a particular element in the DOM, as per the definition of the term, and not any arbitrary [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element.

The [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element exposes as [event handler content attributes](#98.html_event-handler-content-attributes) a number of the [event handlers](#98.html_event-handlers) of the [`Window`](#98.html_window) object. It also mirrors their [event handler IDL attributes](#98.html_event-handler-idl-attributes).

The [`onblur`](#98.html_handler-onblur), [`onerror`](#98.html_handler-onerror), [`onfocus`](#98.html_handler-onfocus), [`onload`](#98.html_handler-onload), [`onresize`](#98.html_handler-onresize), and [`onscroll`](#98.html_handler-onscroll) [event handlers](#98.html_event-handlers) of the [`Window`](#98.html_window) object, exposed on the [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element, replace the generic [event handlers](#98.html_event-handlers) with the same names normally supported by [HTML elements](#98.html_html-elements).

Thus, for example, a bubbling `error` event dispatched on a child of [the body element](#98.html_the-body-element-0) of a [`Document`](#98.html_document) would first trigger the [`onerror`](#98.html_handler-onerror) [event handler content attributes](#98.html_event-handler-content-attributes) of that element, then that of the root [`html`](#98.html_the-html-element) element, and only *then* would it trigger the [`onerror`](#98.html_handler-onerror) [event handler content attribute](#98.html_event-handler-content-attributes) on the [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) element. This is because the event would bubble from the target, to the [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element), to the [`html`](#98.html_the-html-element), to the [`Document`](#98.html_document), to the [`Window`](#98.html_window), and the [event handler](#98.html_event-handlers) on the [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) is watching the [`Window`](#98.html_window) not the [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element). A regular event listener attached to the [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) using `addEventListener()`, however, would be run when the event bubbled through the [`body`](#98.html_the-body-element) and not when it reaches the [`Window`](#98.html_window) object.

This page updates an indicator to show whether or not the user is online:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html>
 <head>
  <title>Online or offline?</title>
  <script>
   function update(online) {
     document.getElementById('status').textContent =
       online ? 'Online' : 'Offline';
   }
  </script>
 </head>
 <body ononline="update(true)"
       onoffline="update(false)"
       onload="update(navigator.onLine)">
  <p>You are: <span id="status">(Unknown)</span></p>
 </body>
</html>
```

#### 4.3.2 The <dfn>`article`</dfn> element

[Categories](#99.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#99.html_flow-content-1), but with no [`main`](#99.html_the-main-element) element descendants.

[Sectioning content](#99.html_sectioning-content-0).

[Palpable content](#99.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#99.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [flow content](#99.html_flow-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#99.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Flow content](#99.html_flow-content-1).

[Content attributes](#99.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#99.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#99.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#99.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`article`](#99.html_index-aria-article) (default - [*do not set*](#99.html_aria-usage-note)), [`application`](#99.html_index-aria-application), [`document`](#99.html_index-aria-document) or [`main`](#99.html_index-aria-main).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#99.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#99.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#99.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#99.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#99.html_htmlelement).

The [`article`](#99.html_the-article-element) element [represents](#99.html_represents) a complete, or self-contained, composition in a document, page, application, or site and that is, in principle, independently distributable or reusable, e.g. in syndication. This could be a forum post, a magazine or newspaper article, a blog entry, a user-submitted comment, an interactive widget or gadget, or any other independent item of content.

When [`article`](#99.html_the-article-element) elements are nested, the inner [`article`](#99.html_the-article-element) elements represent articles that are in principle related to the contents of the outer article. For instance, a blog entry on a site that accepts user-submitted comments could represent the comments as [`article`](#99.html_the-article-element) elements nested within the [`article`](#99.html_the-article-element) element for the blog entry.

Author information associated with an [`article`](#99.html_the-article-element) element (q.v. the [`address`](#99.html_the-address-element) element) does not apply to nested [`article`](#99.html_the-article-element) elements.

When used specifically with content to be redistributed in syndication, the [`article`](#99.html_the-article-element) element is similar in purpose to the `entry` element in Atom. [[ATOM]](#99.html_refsATOM)

When the main content of the page (i.e. excluding footers, headers, navigation blocks, and sidebars) is all one single self-contained composition, the content should be marked up with a [`main`](#99.html_the-main-element) element and the content may also be marked with an [`article`](#99.html_the-article-element), but it is technically redundant in this case (since it's self-evident that the page is a single composition, as it is a single document).

This example shows a blog post using the [`article`](#99.html_the-article-element) element, with some schema.org annotations:

```
<article itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/BlogPosting">
 <header>
  <h1 itemprop="headline">The Very First Rule of Life</h1>
  <p><time itemprop="datePublished" datetime="2009-10-09">3 days ago</time></p>
  <link itemprop="url" href="?comments=0">
 </header>
 <p>If there's a microphone anywhere near you, assume it's hot and
 sending whatever you're saying to the world. Seriously.</p>
 <p>...</p>
 <footer>
  <a itemprop="discussionUrl" href="?comments=1">Show comments...</a>
 </footer>
</article>
```

Here is that same blog post, but showing some of the comments:

```
<article itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/BlogPosting">
 <header>
  <h1 itemprop="headline">The Very First Rule of Life</h1>
  <p><time itemprop="datePublished" datetime="2009-10-09">3 days ago</time></p>
  <link itemprop="url" href="?comments=0">
 </header>
 <p>If there's a microphone anywhere near you, assume it's hot and
 sending whatever you're saying to the world. Seriously.</p>
 <p>...</p>
 <section>
  <h1>Comments</h1>
  <article itemprop="comment" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/UserComments" id="c1">
   <link itemprop="url" href="#c1">
   <footer>
    <p>Posted by: <span itemprop="creator" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person">
     <span itemprop="name">George Washington</span>
    </span></p>
    <p><time itemprop="commentTime" datetime="2009-10-10">15 minutes ago</time></p>
   </footer>
   <p>Yeah! Especially when talking about your lobbyist friends!</p>
  </article>
  <article itemprop="comment" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/UserComments" id="c2">
   <link itemprop="url" href="#c2">
   <footer>
    <p>Posted by: <span itemprop="creator" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person">
     <span itemprop="name">George Hammond</span>
    </span></p>
    <p><time itemprop="commentTime" datetime="2009-10-10">5 minutes ago</time></p>
   </footer>
   <p>Hey, you have the same first name as me.</p>
  </article>
 </section>
</article>
```

Notice the use of [`footer`](#99.html_the-footer-element) to give the information for each comment (such as who wrote it and when): the [`footer`](#99.html_the-footer-element) element *can* appear at the start of its section when appropriate, such as in this case. (Using [`header`](#99.html_the-header-element) in this case wouldn't be wrong either; it's mostly a matter of authoring preference.)

#### 4.3.3 The <dfn>`section`</dfn> element

[Categories](#100.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#100.html_flow-content-1).

[Sectioning content](#100.html_sectioning-content-0).

[Palpable content](#100.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#100.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [flow content](#100.html_flow-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#100.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Flow content](#100.html_flow-content-1).

[Content attributes](#100.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#100.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#100.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#100.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`region`](#100.html_index-aria-region) role (default - [*do not set*](#100.html_aria-usage-note)), [`alert`](#100.html_index-aria-alert), [`alertdialog`](#100.html_index-aria-alertdialog), [`application`](#100.html_index-aria-application), [`contentinfo`](#100.html_index-aria-contentinfo), [`dialog`](#100.html_index-aria-dialog), [`document`](#100.html_index-aria-document), [`log`](#100.html_index-aria-log), [`main`](#100.html_index-aria-main), [`marquee`](#100.html_index-aria-marquee), [`presentation`](#100.html_index-aria-presentation), [`search`](#100.html_index-aria-search) or [`status`](#100.html_index-aria-status).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#100.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#100.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#100.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#100.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#100.html_htmlelement).

The [`section`](#100.html_the-section-element) element [represents](#100.html_represents) a generic section of a document or application. A section, in this context, is a thematic grouping of content. The theme of each [`section`](#100.html_the-section-element) should be identified, typically by including a heading ([`h1`](#100.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)-[`h6`](#100.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element) as a child of the [`section`](#100.html_the-section-element) element.

Examples of sections would be chapters, the various tabbed pages in a tabbed dialog box, or the numbered sections of a thesis. A Web site's home page could be split into sections for an introduction, news items, and contact information.

Authors are encouraged to use the [`article`](#100.html_the-article-element) element instead of the [`section`](#100.html_the-section-element) element when it would make sense to syndicate the contents of the element.

The [`section`](#100.html_the-section-element) element is not a generic container element. When an element is needed only for styling purposes or as a convenience for scripting, authors are encouraged to use the [`div`](#100.html_the-div-element) element instead. A general rule is that the [`section`](#100.html_the-section-element) element is appropriate only if the element's contents would be listed explicitly in the document's [outline](#100.html_outline).

In the following example, we see an article (part of a larger Web page) about apples, containing two short sections.

```
<article>
 <header>
  <h2>Apples</h2>
  <p>Tasty, delicious fruit!</p>
 </header>
 <p>The apple is the pomaceous fruit of the apple tree.</p>
 <section>
  <h3>Red Delicious</h3>
  <p>These bright red apples are the most common found in many
  supermarkets.</p>
 </section>
 <section>
  <h3>Granny Smith</h3>
  <p>These juicy, green apples make a great filling for
  apple pies.</p>
 </section>
</article>
```

Here is a graduation programme with two sections, one for the list of people graduating, and one for the description of the ceremony. (The markup in this example features an uncommon style sometimes used to minimize the amount of [inter-element whitespace](#100.html_inter-element-whitespace).)

```
<!DOCTYPE Html>
<Html
 ><Head
   ><Title
     >Graduation Ceremony Summer 2022</Title
   ></Head
 ><Body
   ><H1
     >Graduation</H1
   ><Section
     ><H2
       >Ceremony</H2
     ><P
       >Opening Procession</P
     ><P
       >Speech by Validactorian</P
     ><P
       >Speech by Class President</P
     ><P
       >Presentation of Diplomas</P
     ><P
       >Closing Speech by Headmaster</P
   ></Section
   ><Section
     ><H2
       >Graduates</H2
     ><Ul
       ><Li
         >Molly Carpenter</Li
       ><Li
         >Anastasia Luccio</Li
       ><Li
         >Ebenezar McCoy</Li
       ><Li
         >Karrin Murphy</Li
       ><Li
         >Thomas Raith</Li
       ><Li
         >Susan Rodriguez</Li
     ></Ul
   ></Section
 ></Body
></Html>
```

In this example, a book author has marked up some sections as chapters and some as appendices, and uses CSS to style the headers in these two classes of section differently. The whole book is wrapped in an [`article`](#100.html_the-article-element) element as part of an even larger document containing other books.

```
<article class="book">
 <style>
  section { border: double medium; margin: 2em; }
  section.chapter h1 { font: 2em Roboto, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif; }
  section.appendix h1 { font: small-caps 2em Roboto, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif; }
 </style>
 <header>
   <h2>My Book</h2>
   <p>A sample with not much content</p>
  <p><small>Published by Dummy Publicorp Ltd.</small></p>
 </header>

 <section class="chapter">
  <h3>My First Chapter</h3>
  <p>This is the first of my chapters. It doesn't say much.</p>
  <p>But it has two paragraphs!</p>
 </section>
 <section class="chapter">
  <h3>It Continutes: The Second Chapter</h3>
  <p>Bla dee bla, dee bla dee bla. Boom.</p>
 </section>
 <section class="chapter">
  <h3>Chapter Three: A Further Example</h3>
  <p>It's not like a battle between brightness and earthtones would go
  unnoticed.</p>
  <p>But it might ruin my story.</p>
 </section>
 <section class="appendix">
  <h3>Appendix A: Overview of Examples</h3>
  <p>These are demonstrations.</p>
 </section>
 <section class="appendix">
  <h3>Appendix B: Some Closing Remarks</h3>
  <p>Hopefully this long example shows that you <em>can</em> style
  sections, so long as they are used to indicate actual sections.</p>
 </section>
</article>
```

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#101.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#101.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#101.html_htmlelement).

The [`nav`](#101.html_the-nav-element) element [represents](#101.html_represents) a section of a page that links to other pages or to parts within the page: a section with navigation links.

In cases where the content of a [`nav`](#101.html_the-nav-element) element represents a list of items, use list markup to aid understanding and navigation.

Not all groups of links on a page need to be in a [`nav`](#101.html_the-nav-element) element — the element is primarily intended for sections that consist of major navigation blocks. In particular, it is common for footers to have a short list of links to various pages of a site, such as the terms of service, the home page, and a copyright page. The [`footer`](#101.html_the-footer-element) element alone is sufficient for such cases; while a [`nav`](#101.html_the-nav-element) element can be used in such cases, it is usually unnecessary.

User agents (such as screen readers) that are targeted at users who can benefit from navigation information being omitted in the initial rendering, or who can benefit from navigation information being immediately available, can use this element as a way to determine what content on the page to initially skip or provide on request (or both).

In the following example, the page has several places where links are present, but only one of those places is considered a navigation section.

```
<body itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Blog">
 <header>
  <h1>Wake up sheeple!</h1>
  <p><a href="news.html">News</a> -
     <a href="blog.html">Blog</a> -
     <a href="forums.html">Forums</a></p>
  <p>Last Modified: <span itemprop="dateModified">2009-04-01</span></p>
  <nav>
   <h1>Navigation</h1>
   <ul>
    <li><a href="articles.html">Index of all articles</a></li>
    <li><a href="today.html">Things sheeple need to wake up for today</a></li>
    <li><a href="successes.html">Sheeple we have managed to wake</a></li>
   </ul>
  </nav>
 </header>
 <main>
  <article itemprop="blogPosts" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/BlogPosting">
   <header>
    <h1 itemprop="headline">My Day at the Beach</h1>
   </header>
   <div itemprop="articleBody">
    <p>Today I went to the beach and had a lot of fun.</p>
    ...more content...
   </div>
   <footer>
    <p>Posted <time itemprop="datePublished" datetime="2009-10-10">Thursday</time>.</p>
   </footer>
  </article>
  ...more blog posts...
 </main>
 <footer>
  <p>Copyright ?
   <span itemprop="copyrightYear">2010</span>
   <span itemprop="copyrightHolder">The Example Company</span>
  </p>
  <p><a href="about.html">About</a> -
     <a href="policy.html">Privacy Policy</a> -
     <a href="contact.html">Contact Us</a></p>
 </footer>
</body>
```

Notice the [`main`](#101.html_the-main-element) element being used to wrap the main content of the page. In this case, all content other than the page header and footer.

You can also see microdata annotations in the above example that use the schema.org vocabulary to provide the publication date and other metadata about the blog post.

In the following example, there are two [`nav`](#101.html_the-nav-element) elements, one for primary navigation around the site, and one for secondary navigation around the page itself.

```
<body>
 <h1>The Wiki Center Of Exampland</h1>
 <nav>
  <ul>
   <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
   <li><a href="/events">Current Events</a></li>
   ...more...
  </ul>
 </nav>
 <main>
  <header>
   <h1>Demos in Exampland</h1>
   <p>Written by A. N. Other.</p>
  </header>
  <nav>
   <ul>
    <li><a href="#public">Public demonstrations</a></li>
    <li><a href="#destroy">Demolitions</a></li>
    ...more...
   </ul>
  </nav>
  <div>
   <section id="public">
    <h1>Public demonstrations</h1>
    <p>...more...</p>
   </section>
   <section id="destroy">
    <h1>Demolitions</h1>
    <p>...more...</p>
   </section>
   ...more...
  </div>
  <footer>
   <p><a href="?edit">Edit</a> | <a href="?delete">Delete</a> | <a href="?Rename">Rename</a></p>
  </footer>
 </main>
 <footer>
  <p><small>? copyright 1998 Exampland Emperor</small></p>
 </footer>
</body>
```

A [`nav`](#101.html_the-nav-element) element doesn't have to contain a list, it can contain other kinds of content as well. In this navigation block, links are provided in prose:

```
<nav>
 <h1>Navigation</h1>
 <p>You are on my home page. To the north lies <a href="/blog">my
 blog</a>, from whence the sounds of battle can be heard. To the east
 you can see a large mountain, upon which many <a
 href="/school">school papers</a> are littered. Far up thus mountain
 you can spy a little figure who appears to be me, desperately
 scribbling a <a href="/school/thesis">thesis</a>.</p>
 <p>To the west are several exits. One fun-looking exit is labeled <a
 href="http://games.example.com/">"games"</a>. Another more
 boring-looking exit is labeled <a
 href="http://isp.example.net/">ISP?</a>.</p>
 <p>To the south lies a dark and dank <a href="/about">contacts
 page</a>. Cobwebs cover its disused entrance, and at one point you
 see a rat run quickly out of the page.</p>
</nav>
```

#### 4.3.5 The <dfn>`aside`</dfn> element

[Categories](#102.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#102.html_flow-content-1).

[Sectioning content](#102.html_sectioning-content-0).

[Palpable content](#102.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#102.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [flow content](#102.html_flow-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#102.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Flow content](#102.html_flow-content-1), but with no [`main`](#102.html_the-main-element) element descendants.

[Content attributes](#102.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#102.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#102.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#102.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`complementary`](#102.html_index-aria-complementary) role (default - [*do not set*](#102.html_aria-usage-note)), [`note`](#102.html_index-aria-note), [`search`](#102.html_index-aria-search) or [`presentation`](#102.html_index-aria-presentation).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#102.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#102.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#102.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#102.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#102.html_htmlelement).

The [`aside`](#102.html_the-aside-element) element [represents](#102.html_represents) a section of a page that consists of content that is tangentially related to the content around the [`aside`](#102.html_the-aside-element) element, and which could be considered separate from that content. Such sections are often represented as sidebars in printed typography.

The element can be used for typographical effects like pull quotes or sidebars, for advertising, for groups of [`nav`](#102.html_the-nav-element) elements, and for other content that is considered separate from the main content of the page.

It's not appropriate to use the [`aside`](#102.html_the-aside-element) element just for parentheticals, since those are part of the main flow of the document.

The following example shows how an aside is used to mark up background material on Switzerland in a much longer news story on Europe.

```
<aside>
 <h1>Switzerland</h1>
 <p>Switzerland, a land-locked country in the middle of geographic
 Europe, has not joined the geopolitical European Union, though it is
 a signatory to a number of European treaties.</p>
</aside>
```

The following example shows how an aside is used to mark up a pull quote in a longer article.

```
...

<p>He later joined a large company, continuing on the same work.
<q>I love my job. People ask me what I do for fun when I'm not at
work. But I'm paid to do my hobby, so I never know what to
answer. Some people wonder what they would do if they didn't have to
work... but I know what I would do, because I was unemployed for a
year, and I filled that time doing exactly what I do now.</q></p>

<aside>
 <q> People ask me what I do for fun when I'm not at work. But I'm
 paid to do my hobby, so I never know what to answer. </q>
</aside>

<p>Of course his work — or should that be hobby? —
isn't his only passion. He also enjoys other pleasures.</p>

...
```

The following extract shows how [`aside`](#102.html_the-aside-element) can be used for blogrolls and other side content on a blog:

```
<body>
 <header>
  <h1>My wonderful blog</h1>
  <p>My tagline</p>
 </header>
 <aside>
  <!-- this aside contains two sections that are tangentially related
  to the page, namely, links to other blogs, and links to blog posts
  from this blog -->
  <nav>
   <h1>My blogroll</h1>
   <ul>
    <li><a href="http://blog.example.com/">Example Blog</a>
   </ul>
  </nav>
  <nav>
   <h1>Archives</h1>
   <ol reversed>
    <li><a href="/last-post">My last post</a>
    <li><a href="/first-post">My first post</a>
   </ol>
  </nav>
 </aside>
 <aside>
  <!-- this aside is tangentially related to the page also, it
  contains twitter messages from the blog author -->
  <h1>Twitter Feed</h1>
  <blockquote cite="http://twitter.example.net/t31351234">
   I'm on vacation, writing my blog.
  </blockquote>
  <blockquote cite="http://twitter.example.net/t31219752">
   I'm going to go on vacation soon.
  </blockquote>
 </aside>
 <article>
  <!-- this is a blog post -->
  <h1>My last post</h1>
  <p>This is my last post.</p>
  <footer>
   <p><a href="/last-post" rel=bookmark>Permalink</a>
  </footer>
 </article>
 <article>
  <!-- this is also a blog post -->
  <h1>My first post</h1>
  <p>This is my first post.</p>
  <aside>
   <!-- this aside is about the blog post, since it's inside the
   <article> element; it would be wrong, for instance, to put the
   blogroll here, since the blogroll isn't really related to this post
   specifically, only to the page as a whole -->
   <h1>Posting</h1>
   <p>While I'm thinking about it, I wanted to say something about
   posting. Posting is fun!</p>
  </aside>
  <footer>
   <p><a href="/first-post" rel=bookmark>Permalink</a>
  </footer>
 </article>
 <footer>
  <nav>
   <a href="/archives">Archives</a> —
   <a href="/about">About me</a> —
   <a href="/copyright">Copyright</a>
  </nav>
 </footer>
</body>
```

#### 4.3.6 The <dfn id="103.html_the-h1-element">`h1`</dfn>, <dfn id="103.html_the-h2-element">`h2`</dfn>, <dfn id="103.html_the-h3-element">`h3`</dfn>, <dfn id="103.html_the-h4-element">`h4`</dfn>, <dfn id="103.html_the-h5-element">`h5`</dfn>, and <dfn id="103.html_the-h6-element">`h6`</dfn> elements

[Categories](#103.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#103.html_flow-content-1).

[Heading content](#103.html_heading-content-0).

[Palpable content](#103.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#103.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [flow content](#103.html_flow-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#103.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#103.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#103.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#103.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#103.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#103.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`heading`](#103.html_index-aria-heading) role (default - [*do not set*](#103.html_aria-usage-note)), [`tab`](#103.html_index-aria-tab) or [`presentation`](#103.html_index-aria-presentation).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#103.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#103.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#103.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#103.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLHeadingElement : HTMLElement {};
```

These elements [represent](#103.html_represents) headings for their sections.

The semantics and meaning of these elements are defined in the section on [headings and sections](#103.html_headings-and-sections).

These elements have a <dfn id="103.html_rank">rank</dfn> given by the number in their name. The [`h1`](#103.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element is said to have the highest rank, the [`h6`](#103.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element has the lowest rank, and two elements with the same name have equal rank.

[`h1`](#103.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)–[`h6`](#103.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) elements must not be used to markup subheadings, subtitles, alternative titles and taglines unless intended to be the heading for a new section or subsection. Instead use the markup patterns in the [Common idioms without dedicated elements](#103.html_common-idioms) section of the specification.

As far as their respective document outlines (their heading and section structures) are concerned, these two snippets are semantically equivalent:

```
<body>
<h1>Let's call it a draw(ing surface)</h1>
<h2>Diving in</h2>
<h2>Simple shapes</h2>
<h2>Canvas coordinates</h2>
<h3>Canvas coordinates diagram</h3>
<h2>Paths</h2>
</body>
```

```
<body>
 <h1>Let's call it a draw(ing surface)</h1>
 <section>
  <h1>Diving in</h1>
 </section>
 <section>
  <h1>Simple shapes</h1>
 </section>
 <section>
  <h1>Canvas coordinates</h1>
  <section>
   <h1>Canvas coordinates diagram</h1>
  </section>
 </section>
 <section>
  <h1>Paths</h1>
 </section>
</body>
```

Authors might prefer the former style for its terseness, or the latter style for its convenience in the face of heavy editing; which is best is purely an issue of preferred authoring style.

#### 4.3.7 The <dfn>`header`</dfn> element

[Categories](#104.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#104.html_flow-content-1).

[Palpable content](#104.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#104.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [flow content](#104.html_flow-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#104.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Flow content](#104.html_flow-content-1), but with no [`header`](#104.html_the-header-element), [`footer`](#104.html_the-footer-element), or [`main`](#104.html_the-main-element) element descendants.

[Content attributes](#104.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#104.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#104.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#104.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`banner`](#104.html_index-aria-banner) role (default - [*do not set*](#104.html_aria-usage-note)) or [`presentation`](#104.html_index-aria-presentation).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#104.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#104.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#104.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#104.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#104.html_htmlelement).

The [`header`](#104.html_the-header-element) element [represents](#104.html_represents) introductory content for its nearest ancestor [sectioning content](#104.html_sectioning-content-0) or [sectioning root](#104.html_sectioning-root) element. A [`header`](#104.html_the-header-element) typically contains a group of introductory or navigational aids.

When the nearest ancestor [sectioning content](#104.html_sectioning-content-0) or [sectioning root](#104.html_sectioning-root) element is [the body element](#104.html_the-body-element-0), then it applies to the whole page.

A [`header`](#104.html_the-header-element) element is intended to usually contain the section's heading (an [`h1`](#104.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)–[`h6`](#104.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element), but this is not required. The [`header`](#104.html_the-header-element) element can also be used to wrap a section's table of contents, a search form, or any relevant logos.

Here are some sample headers. This first one is for a game:

```
<header>
 <p>Welcome to...</p>
 <h1>Voidwars!</h1>
</header>
```

The following snippet shows how the element can be used to mark up a specification's header:

```
<header>
  <h1>Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) 1.2</h1>
  <p>W3C Working Draft 27 October 2004</p>
 <dl>
  <dt>This version:</dt>
  <dd><a href="http://www.w3.org/TR/2004/WD-SVG12-20041027/">http://www.w3.org/TR/2004/WD-SVG12-20041027/</a></dd>
  <dt>Previous version:</dt>
  <dd><a href="http://www.w3.org/TR/2004/WD-SVG12-20040510/">http://www.w3.org/TR/2004/WD-SVG12-20040510/</a></dd>
  <dt>Latest version of SVG 1.2:</dt>
  <dd><a href="http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG12/">http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG12/</a></dd>
  <dt>Latest SVG Recommendation:</dt>
  <dd><a href="http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/">http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/</a></dd>
  <dt>Editor:</dt>
  <dd>Dean Jackson, W3C, <a href="mailto:dean@w3.org">dean@w3.org</a></dd>
  <dt>Authors:</dt>
  <dd>See <a href="#authors">Author List</a></dd>
 </dl>
 <p class="copyright"><a href="http://www.w3.org/Consortium/Legal/ipr-notic ...
</header>
```

The [`header`](#104.html_the-header-element) element is not [sectioning content](#104.html_sectioning-content-0); it doesn't introduce a new section.

In this example, the page has a page heading given by the [`h1`](#104.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element, and two subsections whose headings are given by [`h2`](#104.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) elements. The content after the [`header`](#104.html_the-header-element) element is still part of the last subsection started in the [`header`](#104.html_the-header-element) element, because the [`header`](#104.html_the-header-element) element doesn't take part in the [outline](#104.html_outline) algorithm.

```
<body>
 <header>
  <h1>Little Green Guys With Guns</h1>
  <nav>
   <ul>
    <li><a href="/games">Games</a>
    <li><a href="/forum">Forum</a>
    <li><a href="/download">Download</a>
   </ul>
  </nav>
  <h2>Important News</h2> <!-- this starts a second subsection -->
  <!-- this is part of the subsection entitled "Important News" -->
  <p>To play today's games you will need to update your client.</p>
  <h2>Games</h2> <!-- this starts a third subsection -->
 </header>
 <p>You have three active games:</p>
 <!-- this is still part of the subsection entitled "Games" -->
 ...
```

#### 4.3.8 The <dfn>`footer`</dfn> element

[Categories](#105.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#105.html_flow-content-1).

[Palpable content](#105.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#105.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [flow content](#105.html_flow-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#105.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Flow content](#105.html_flow-content-1), but with no [`header`](#105.html_the-header-element), [`footer`](#105.html_the-footer-element), or [`main`](#105.html_the-main-element) element descendants.

[Content attributes](#105.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#105.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#105.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#105.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`contentinfo`](#105.html_index-aria-contentinfo) role (default - [*do not set*](#105.html_aria-usage-note)) or [`presentation`](#105.html_index-aria-presentation).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#105.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#105.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#105.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#105.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#105.html_htmlelement).

The [`footer`](#105.html_the-footer-element) element [represents](#105.html_represents) a footer for its nearest ancestor [sectioning content](#105.html_sectioning-content-0) or [sectioning root](#105.html_sectioning-root) element. A footer typically contains information about its section such as who wrote it, links to related documents, copyright data, and the like.

When the [`footer`](#105.html_the-footer-element) element contains entire sections, they [represent](#105.html_represents) appendices, indexes, long colophons, verbose license agreements, and other such content.

Contact information for the author or editor of a section belongs in an [`address`](#105.html_the-address-element) element, possibly itself inside a [`footer`](#105.html_the-footer-element). Bylines and other information that could be suitable for both a [`header`](#105.html_the-header-element) or a [`footer`](#105.html_the-footer-element) can be placed in either (or neither). The primary purpose of these elements is merely to help the author write self-explanatory markup that is easy to maintain and style; they are not intended to impose specific structures on authors.

Footers don't necessarily have to appear at the *end* of a section, though they usually do.

When the nearest ancestor [sectioning content](#105.html_sectioning-content-0) or [sectioning root](#105.html_sectioning-root) element is [the body element](#105.html_the-body-element-0), then it applies to the whole page.

The [`footer`](#105.html_the-footer-element) element is not [sectioning content](#105.html_sectioning-content-0); it doesn't introduce a new section.

Here is a page with two footers, one at the top and one at the bottom, with the same content:

```
<body>
 <footer><a href="../">Back to index...</a></footer>
 <div>
  <h1>Lorem ipsum</h1>
  <p>The ipsum of all lorems</p>
 </div>
 <p>A dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod
 tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim
 veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex
 ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in
 voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla
 pariatur. Excepteur sint occaecat cupidatat non proident, sunt in
 culpa qui officia deserunt mollit anim id est laborum.</p>
 <footer><a href="../">Back to index...</a></footer>
</body>
```

Here is an example which shows the [`footer`](#105.html_the-footer-element) element being used both for a site-wide footer and for a section footer.

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<HTML><HEAD>
<TITLE>The Ramblings of a Scientist</TITLE>
<BODY>
<H1>The Ramblings of a Scientist</H1>
<MAIN>
 <ARTICLE>
 <H1>Episode 15</H1>
 <VIDEO SRC="/fm/015.ogv" CONTROLS PRELOAD>
  <P><A HREF="/fm/015.ogv">Download video</A>.</P>
 </VIDEO>
 <FOOTER> <!-- footer for article -->
  <P>Published <TIME DATETIME="2009-10-21T18:26-07:00">on 2009/10/21 at 6:26pm</TIME></P>
 </FOOTER>
</ARTICLE>
<ARTICLE>
 <H1>My Favorite Trains</H1>
 <P>I love my trains. My favorite train of all time is a K?f.</P>
 <P>It is fun to see them pull some coal cars because they look so
 dwarfed in comparison.</P>
 <FOOTER> <!-- footer for article -->
  <P>Published <TIME DATETIME="2009-09-15T14:54-07:00">on 2009/09/15 at 2:54pm</TIME></P>
 </FOOTER>
 </ARTICLE>
</MAIN>
<FOOTER> <!-- site wide footer -->
 <NAV>
  <P><A HREF="/credits.html">Credits</A> —
     <A HREF="/tos.html">Terms of Service</A> —
     <A HREF="/index.html">Blog Index</A></P>
 </NAV>
 <P>Copyright ? 2009 Gordon Freeman</P>
</FOOTER>
</BODY>
</HTML>
```

Some site designs have what is sometimes referred to as "fat footers" — footers that contain a lot of material, including images, links to other articles, links to pages for sending feedback, special offers... in some ways, a whole "front page" in the footer.

This fragment shows the bottom of a page on a site with a "fat footer":

```
...
 <footer>
  <nav>
   <section>
    <h1>Articles</h1>
    <p><img src="https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/images/somersaults.jpeg" alt=""> Go to the gym with
    our somersaults class! Our teacher Jim takes you through the paces
    in this two-part article. <a href="articles/somersaults/1">Part
    1</a> · <a href="articles/somersaults/2">Part 2</a></p>
    <p><img src="https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/images/kindplus.jpeg"> Tired of walking on the edge of
    a clif<!-- sic -->? Our guest writer Lara shows you how to bumble
    your way through the bars. <a href="articles/kindplus/1">Read
    more...</a></p>
    <p><img src="https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/images/crisps.jpeg"> The chips are down, now all
    that's left is a potato. What can you do with it? <a
    href="articles/crisps/1">Read more...</a></p>
   </section>
   <ul>
    <li> <a href="/about">About us...</a>
    <li> <a href="/feedback">Send feedback!</a>
    <li> <a href="/sitemap">Sitemap</a>
   </ul>
  </nav>
  <p><small>Copyright ? 2015 The Snacker —
  <a href="/tos">Terms of Service</a></small></p>
 </footer>
</body>
```

#### 4.3.9 The <dfn>`address`</dfn> element

[Categories](#106.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#106.html_flow-content-1).

[Palpable content](#106.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#106.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [flow content](#106.html_flow-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#106.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Flow content](#106.html_flow-content-1), but with no [heading content](#106.html_heading-content-0) descendants, no [sectioning content](#106.html_sectioning-content-0) descendants, and no [`header`](#106.html_the-header-element), [`footer`](#106.html_the-footer-element), or [`address`](#106.html_the-address-element) element descendants.

[Content attributes](#106.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#106.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#106.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#106.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`contentinfo`](#106.html_index-aria-contentinfo) role.

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#106.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#106.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#106.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#106.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#106.html_htmlelement).

The [`address`](#106.html_the-address-element) element [represents](#106.html_represents) the contact information for its nearest [`article`](#106.html_the-article-element) or [`body`](#106.html_the-body-element) element ancestor. If that is [the body element](#106.html_the-body-element-0), then the contact information applies to the document as a whole.

For example, a page at the W3C Web site related to HTML might include the following contact information:

```
<ADDRESS>
 <A href="../People/Raggett/">Dave Raggett</A>,
 <A href="../People/Arnaud/">Arnaud Le Hors</A>,
 contact persons for the <A href="Activity">W3C HTML Activity</A>
</ADDRESS>
```

The [`address`](#106.html_the-address-element) element must not be used to represent arbitrary addresses (e.g. postal addresses), unless those addresses are in fact the relevant contact information. (The [`p`](#106.html_the-p-element) element is the appropriate element for marking up postal addresses in general.)

The [`address`](#106.html_the-address-element) element must not contain information other than contact information.

For example, the following is non-conforming use of the [`address`](#106.html_the-address-element) element:

```
<ADDRESS>Last Modified: 1999/12/24 23:37:50</ADDRESS>
```

Typically, the [`address`](#106.html_the-address-element) element would be included along with other information in a [`footer`](#106.html_the-footer-element) element.

The contact information for a node `node` is a collection of [`address`](#106.html_the-address-element) elements defined by the first applicable entry from the following list:

If `node` is an [`article`](#106.html_the-article-element) element
If `node` is a [`body`](#106.html_the-body-element) element

The contact information consists of all the [`address`](#106.html_the-address-element) elements that have `node` as an ancestor and do not have another [`body`](#106.html_the-body-element) or [`article`](#106.html_the-article-element) element ancestor that is a descendant of `node`.

If `node` has an ancestor element that is an [`article`](#106.html_the-article-element) element
If `node` has an ancestor element that is a [`body`](#106.html_the-body-element) element

The contact information of `node` is the same as the contact information of the nearest [`article`](#106.html_the-article-element) or [`body`](#106.html_the-body-element) element ancestor, whichever is nearest.

If `node`'s [`Document`](#106.html_document) has [a body element](#106.html_the-body-element-0)

The contact information of `node` is the same as the contact information of [the body element](#106.html_the-body-element-0) of the [`Document`](#106.html_document).

Otherwise

There is no contact information for `node`.

User agents may expose the contact information of a node to the user, or use it for other purposes, such as indexing sections based on the sections' contact information.

In this example the footer contains contact information and a copyright notice.

```
<footer>
 <address>
  For more details, contact
  <a href="mailto:js@example.com">John Smith</a>.
 </address>
 <p><small>? copyright 2038 Example Corp.</small></p>
</footer>
```

#### 4.3.10 <dfn>Headings and sections</dfn>

The [`h1`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)–[`h6`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) elements are headings.

The first element of [heading content](#107.html_heading-content-0) in an element of [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) [represents](#107.html_represents) the heading for that section. Subsequent headings of equal or higher [rank](#107.html_rank) start new (implied) sections, headings of lower [rank](#107.html_rank) start implied subsections that are part of the previous one. In both cases, the element [represents](#107.html_represents) the heading of the implied section.

[`h1`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)–[`h6`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) elements must not be used to markup subheadings, subtitles, alternative titles and taglines unless intended to be the heading for a new section or subsection. Instead use the markup patterns in the [Common idioms without dedicated elements](#107.html_common-idioms) section of the specification.

Certain elements are said to be <dfn id="107.html_sectioning-root" data-anolis-xref="sectioning
  root">sectioning roots</dfn>, including [`blockquote`](#107.html_the-blockquote-element) and [`td`](#107.html_the-td-element) elements. These elements can have their own outlines, but the sections and headings inside these elements do not contribute to the outlines of their ancestors.

*   [`blockquote`](#107.html_the-blockquote-element)
*   [`body`](#107.html_the-body-element)
*   [`fieldset`](#107.html_the-fieldset-element)
*   [`figure`](#107.html_the-figure-element)
*   [`td`](#107.html_the-td-element)

[Sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) elements are always considered subsections of their nearest ancestor [sectioning root](#107.html_sectioning-root) or their nearest ancestor element of [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0), whichever is nearest, regardless of what implied sections other headings may have created.

For the following fragment:

```
<body>
 <h1>Foo</h1>
 <h2>Bar</h2>
 <blockquote>
  <h3>Bla</h3>
 </blockquote>
 <p>Baz</p>
 <h2>Quux</h2>
 <section>
  <h3>Thud</h3>
 </section>
 <p>Grunt</p>
</body>
```

...the structure would be:

1.  Foo (heading of explicit [`body`](#107.html_the-body-element) section, containing the "Grunt" paragraph)
    1.  Bar (heading starting implied section, containing a block quote and the "Baz" paragraph)
    2.  Quux (heading starting implied section with no content other than the heading itself)
    3.  Thud (heading of explicit [`section`](#107.html_the-section-element) section)

Notice how the [`section`](#107.html_the-section-element) ends the earlier implicit section so that a later paragraph ("Grunt") is back at the top level.

Sections may contain headings of any [rank](#107.html_rank), and authors are strongly encouraged to use headings of the appropriate [rank](#107.html_rank) for the section's nesting level.

Authors are also encouraged to explicitly wrap sections in elements of [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0), instead of relying on the implicit sections generated by having multiple headings in one element of [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0).

For example, the following is correct:

```
<body>
 <h4>Apples</h4>
 <p>Apples are fruit.</p>
 <section>
  <h2>Taste</h2>
  <p>They taste lovely.</p>
  <h6>Sweet</h6>
  <p>Red apples are sweeter than green ones.</p>
  <h1>Color</h1>
  <p>Apples come in various colors.</p>
 </section>
</body>
```

However, the same document would be more clearly expressed as:

```
<body>
 <h1>Apples</h1>
 <p>Apples are fruit.</p>
 <section>
  <h2>Taste</h2>
  <p>They taste lovely.</p>
  <section>
   <h3>Sweet</h3>
   <p>Red apples are sweeter than green ones.</p>
  </section>
 </section>
 <section>
  <h2>Color</h2>
  <p>Apples come in various colors.</p>
 </section>
</body>
```

Both of the documents above are semantically identical and would produce the same outline in compliant user agents.

This third example is also semantically identical, and might be easier to maintain (e.g. if sections are often moved around in editing):

```
<body>
 <h1>Apples</h1>
 <p>Apples are fruit.</p>
 <section>
  <h1>Taste</h1>
  <p>They taste lovely.</p>
  <section>
   <h1>Sweet</h1>
   <p>Red apples are sweeter than green ones.</p>
  </section>
 </section>
 <section>
  <h1>Color</h1>
  <p>Apples come in various colors.</p>
 </section>
</body>
```

This final example would need explicit style rules to be rendered well in legacy browsers. Legacy browsers without CSS support would render all the headings as top-level headings.

##### 4.3.10.1 Creating an outline

There are currently no known implementations of the outline algorithm in graphical browsers or assistive technology user agents, although the algorithm is implemented in other software such as conformance checkers. Therefore the [outline](#107.html_outline) algorithm cannot be relied upon to convey document structure to users. Authors are advised to use heading [rank](#107.html_rank) ([`h1`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)-[`h6`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)) to convey document structure.

This section defines an algorithm for creating an outline for a [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) element or a [sectioning root](#107.html_sectioning-root) element. It is defined in terms of a walk over the nodes of a DOM tree, in tree order, with each node being visited when it is *entered* and when it is *exited* during the walk.

The <dfn id="107.html_outline">outline</dfn> for a [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) element or a [sectioning root](#107.html_sectioning-root) element consists of a list of one or more potentially nested [sections](#107.html_concept-section). A <dfn id="107.html_concept-section" data-anolis-xref="concept-section">section</dfn> is a container that corresponds to some nodes in the original DOM tree. Each section can have one heading associated with it, and can contain any number of further nested sections. The algorithm for the outline also associates each node in the DOM tree with a particular section and potentially a heading. (The sections in the outline aren't [`section`](#107.html_the-section-element) elements, though some may correspond to such elements — they are merely conceptual sections.)

The following markup fragment:

```
<body>
 <h1>A</h1>
 <p>B</p>
 <h2>C</h2>
 <p>D</p>
 <h2>E</h2>
 <p>F</p>
</body>
```

...results in the following outline being created for the [`body`](#107.html_the-body-element) node (and thus the entire document):

1.  Section created for [`body`](#107.html_the-body-element) node.

    Associated with heading "A".

    Also associated with paragraph "B".

    Nested sections:

    1.  Section implied for first [`h2`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element.

        Associated with heading "C".

        Also associated with paragraph "D".

        No nested sections.

    2.  Section implied for second [`h2`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element.

        Associated with heading "E".

        Also associated with paragraph "F".

        No nested sections.

The algorithm that must be followed during a walk of a DOM subtree rooted at a [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) element or a [sectioning root](#107.html_sectioning-root) element to determine that element's [outline](#107.html_outline) is as follows:

1.  Let `current outline target` be null. (It holds the element whose [outline](#107.html_outline) is being created.)

2.  Let `current section` be null. (It holds a pointer to a [section](#107.html_concept-section), so that elements in the DOM can all be associated with a section.)

3.  Create a stack to hold elements, which is used to handle nesting. Initialize this stack to empty.

4.  Walk over the DOM in [tree order](#107.html_tree-order), starting with the [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) element or [sectioning root](#107.html_sectioning-root) element at the root of the subtree for which an outline is to be created, and trigger the first relevant step below for each element as the walk enters and exits it.

    When exiting an element, if that element is the element at the top of the stack

    The element being exited is a [heading content](#107.html_heading-content-0) element or an element with a [`hidden`](#107.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute.

    Pop that element from the stack.

    If the top of the stack is a [heading content](#107.html_heading-content-0) element or an element with a [`hidden`](#107.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute

    Do nothing.

    When entering an element with a [`hidden`](#107.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute

    Push the element being entered onto the stack. (This causes the algorithm to skip that element and any descendants of the element.)

    When entering a [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) element

    Run these steps:

    1.  If `current outline target` is not null, run these substeps:

        1.  If the `current section` has no heading, create an implied heading and let that be the heading for the `current section`.

        2.  Push `current outline target` onto the stack.

    2.  Let `current outline target` be the element that is being entered.

    3.  Let `current section` be a newly created [section](#107.html_concept-section) for the `current outline target` element.

    4.  Associate `current outline target` with `current section`.

    5.  Let there be a new [outline](#107.html_outline) for the new `current outline target`, initialized with just the new `current section` as the only [section](#107.html_concept-section) in the outline.

    When exiting a [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) element, if the stack is not empty

    Run these steps:

    1.  If the `current section` has no heading, create an implied heading and let that be the heading for the `current section`.

    2.  Pop the top element from the stack, and let the `current outline target` be that element.

    3.  Let `current section` be the last section in the [outline](#107.html_outline) of the `current outline target` element.

    4.  Append the [outline](#107.html_outline) of the [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) element being exited to the `current section`. (This does not change which section is the last section in the [outline](#107.html_outline).)

    When entering a [sectioning root](#107.html_sectioning-root) element

    Run these steps:

    1.  If `current outline target` is not null, push `current outline target` onto the stack.

    2.  Let `current outline target` be the element that is being entered.

    3.  Let `current outline target`'s *parent section* be `current section`.

    4.  Let `current section` be a newly created [section](#107.html_concept-section) for the `current outline target` element.

    5.  Let there be a new [outline](#107.html_outline) for the new `current outline target`, initialized with just the new `current section` as the only [section](#107.html_concept-section) in the outline.

    When exiting a [sectioning root](#107.html_sectioning-root) element, if the stack is not empty

    Run these steps:

    1.  If the `current section` has no heading, create an implied heading and let that be the heading for the `current section`.

    2.  Let `current section` be `current outline target`'s *parent section*.

    3.  Pop the top element from the stack, and let the `current outline target` be that element.

    When exiting a [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) element or a [sectioning root](#107.html_sectioning-root) element (when the stack is empty)

    The `current outline target` is the element being exited, and it is the [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) element or a [sectioning root](#107.html_sectioning-root) element at the root of the subtree for which an outline is being generated.

    If the `current section` has no heading, create an implied heading and let that be the heading for the `current section`.

    Skip to the next step in the overall set of steps. (The walk is over.)

    When entering a [heading content](#107.html_heading-content-0) element

    If the `current section` has no heading, let the element being entered be the heading for the `current section`.

    Otherwise, if the element being entered has a [rank](#107.html_rank) equal to or higher than the heading of the last section of the [outline](#107.html_outline) of the `current outline target`, or if the heading of the last section of the [outline](#107.html_outline) of the `current outline target` is an implied heading, then create a new [section](#107.html_concept-section) and append it to the [outline](#107.html_outline) of the `current outline target` element, so that this new section is the new last section of that outline. Let `current section` be that new section. Let the element being entered be the new heading for the `current section`.

    Otherwise, run these substeps:

    1.  Let `candidate section` be `current section`.

    2.  *Heading loop*: If the element being entered has a [rank](#107.html_rank) lower than the [rank](#107.html_rank) of the heading of the `candidate section`, then create a new [section](#107.html_concept-section), and append it to `candidate section`. (This does not change which section is the last section in the outline.) Let `current section` be this new section. Let the element being entered be the new heading for the `current section`. Abort these substeps.

    3.  Let `new candidate section` be the [section](#107.html_concept-section) that contains `candidate section` in the [outline](#107.html_outline) of `current outline target`.

    4.  Let `candidate section` be `new candidate section`.

    5.  Return to the step labeled *heading loop*.

    Push the element being entered onto the stack. (This causes the algorithm to skip any descendants of the element.)

    Recall that [`h1`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) has the *highest* rank, and [`h6`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) has the lowest rank.

    Otherwise

    Do nothing.

    In addition, whenever the walk exits a node, after doing the steps above, if the node is not associated with a [section](#107.html_concept-section) yet, associate the node with the [section](#107.html_concept-section) `current section`.

5.  Associate all nodes with the heading of the [section](#107.html_concept-section) with which they are associated, if any.

The tree of sections created by the algorithm above, or a proper subset thereof, must be used when generating document outlines, for example when generating tables of contents.

The outline created for [the body element](#107.html_the-body-element-0) of a [`Document`](#107.html_document) is the [outline](#107.html_outline) of the entire document.

When creating an interactive table of contents, entries should jump the user to the relevant [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) element, if the [section](#107.html_concept-section) was created for a real element in the original document, or to the relevant [heading content](#107.html_heading-content-0) element, if the [section](#107.html_concept-section) in the tree was generated for a heading in the above process.

Selecting the first [section](#107.html_concept-section) of the document therefore always takes the user to the top of the document, regardless of where the first heading in the [`body`](#107.html_the-body-element) is to be found.

The <dfn id="107.html_outline-depth">outline depth</dfn> of a [heading content](#107.html_heading-content-0) element associated with a [section](#107.html_concept-section) `section` is the number of [sections](#107.html_concept-section) that are ancestors of `section` in the outermost [outline](#107.html_outline) that `section` finds itself in when the [outlines](#107.html_outline) of its [`Document`](#107.html_document)'s elements are created, plus 1\. The [outline depth](#107.html_outline-depth) of a [heading content](#107.html_heading-content-0) element not associated with a [section](#107.html_concept-section) is 1.

User agents should provide default headings for sections that do not have explicit section headings.

Consider the following snippet:

```
<body>
 <nav>
  <p><a href="/">Home</a></p>
 </nav>
 <p>Hello world.</p>
 <aside>
  <p>My cat is cute.</p>
 </aside>
</body>
```

Although it contains no headings, this snippet has three sections: a document (the [`body`](#107.html_the-body-element)) with two subsections (a [`nav`](#107.html_the-nav-element) and an [`aside`](#107.html_the-aside-element)). A user agent could present the outline as follows:

1.  Untitled document
    1.  Navigation
    2.  Sidebar

These default headings ("Untitled document", "Navigation", "Sidebar") are not specified by this specification, and might vary with the user's language, the page's language, the user's preferences, the user agent implementor's preferences, etc.

The following JavaScript function shows how the tree walk could be implemented. The `root` argument is the root of the tree to walk (either a [sectioning content](#107.html_sectioning-content-0) element or a [sectioning root](#107.html_sectioning-root) element), and the `enter` and `exit` arguments are callbacks that are called with the nodes as they are entered and exited. [[ECMA262]](#107.html_refsECMA262)

```
function (root, enter, exit) {
  var node = root;
  start: while (node) {
    enter(node);
    if (node.firstChild) {
      node = node.firstChild;
      continue start;
    }
    while (node) {
      exit(node);
      if (node == root) {
        node = null;
      } else if (node.nextSibling) {
        node = node.nextSibling;
        continue start;
      } else {
        node = node.parentNode;
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### 4.3.10.2 Sample outlines

*This section is non-normative.*

The following document shows a straight-forward application of the [outline](#107.html_outline) algorithm. First, here is the document, which is a book with very short chapters and subsections:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<title>The Tax Book (all in one page)</title>
<h1>The Tax Book</h1>
<h2>Earning money</h2>
<p>Earning money is good.</p>
<h3>Getting a job</h3>
<p>To earn money you typically need a job.</p>
<h2>Spending money</h2>
<p>Spending is what money is mainly used for.</p>
<h3>Cheap things</h3>
<p>Buying cheap things often not cost-effective.</p>
<h3>Expensive things</h3>
<p>The most expensive thing is often not the most cost-effective either.</p>
<h2>Investing money</h2>
<p>You can lend your money to other people.</p>
<h2>Losing money</h2>
<p>If you spend money or invest money, sooner or later you will lose money.
<h3>Poor judgement</h3>
<p>Usually if you lose money it's because you made a mistake.</p>
```

This book would form the following outline:

1.  The Tax Book
    1.  Earning money
        1.  Getting a job
    2.  Spending money
        1.  Cheap things
        2.  Expensive things
    3.  Investing money
    4.  Losing money
        1.  Poor judgement

Notice that the [`title`](#107.html_the-title-element) element does not participate in the outline.

Here is a similar document, but this time using [`section`](#107.html_the-section-element) elements to get the same effect:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<title>The Tax Book (all in one page)</title>
<h1>The Tax Book</h1>
<section>
 <h1>Earning money</h1>
 <p>Earning money is good.</p>
 <section>
  <h1>Getting a job</h1>
  <p>To earn money you typically need a job.</p>
 </section>
</section>
<section>
 <h1>Spending money</h1>
 <p>Spending is what money is mainly used for.</p>
 <section>
  <h1>Cheap things</h1>
  <p>Buying cheap things often not cost-effective.</p>
 </section>
 <section>
  <h1>Expensive things</h1>
  <p>The most expensive thing is often not the most cost-effective either.</p>
 </section>
</section>
<section>
 <h1>Investing money</h1>
 <p>You can lend your money to other people.</p>
</section>
<section>
 <h1>Losing money</h1>
 <p>If you spend money or invest money, sooner or later you will lose money.
 <section>
  <h1>Poor judgement</h1>
  <p>Usually if you lose money it's because you made a mistake.</p>
 </section>
</section>
```

This book would form the same outline:

1.  The Tax Book
    1.  Earning money
        1.  Getting a job
    2.  Spending money
        1.  Cheap things
        2.  Expensive things
    3.  Investing money
    4.  Losing money
        1.  Poor judgement

A document can contain multiple top-level headings:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<title>Alphabetic Fruit</title>
<h1>Apples</h1>
<p>Pomaceous.</p>
<h1>Bananas</h1>
<p>Edible.</p>
<h1>Carambola</h1>
<p>Star.</p>
```

This would form the following simple outline consisting of three top-level sections:

1.  Apples
2.  Bananas
3.  Carambola

Effectively, the [`body`](#107.html_the-body-element) element is split into three.

Mixing both the [`h1`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)–[`h6`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) model and the [`section`](#107.html_the-section-element)/[`h1`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) model can lead to some unintuitive results.

Consider for example the following, which is just the previous example but with the contents of the (implied) [`body`](#107.html_the-body-element) wrapped in a [`section`](#107.html_the-section-element):

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<title>Alphabetic Fruit</title>
<section>
 <h1>Apples</h1>
 <p>Pomaceous.</p>
 <h1>Bananas</h1>
 <p>Edible.</p>
 <h1>Carambola</h1>
 <p>Star.</p>
</section>
```

The resulting outline would be:

1.  *(untitled page)*
    1.  Apples
    2.  Bananas
    3.  Carambola

This result is described as *unintuitive* because it results in three subsections even though there's only one [`section`](#107.html_the-section-element) element. Effectively, the [`section`](#107.html_the-section-element) is split into three, just like the implied [`body`](#107.html_the-body-element) element in the previous example.

(In this example, "*(untitled page)*" is the implied heading for the [`body`](#107.html_the-body-element) element, since it has no explicit heading.)

Headings never rise above other sections. Thus, in the following example, the first [`h1`](#107.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) does not actually describe the page header; it describes the header for the second half of the page:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<title>Feathers on The Site of Encyclopedic Knowledge</title>
<section>
 <h1>A plea from our caretakers</h1>
 <p>Please, we beg of you, send help! We're stuck in the server room!</p>
</section>
<h1>Feathers</h1>
<p>Epidermal growths.</p>
```

The resulting outline would be:

1.  *(untitled page)*
    1.  A plea from our caretakers
2.  Feathers

Thus, when an [`article`](#107.html_the-article-element) element starts with a [`nav`](#107.html_the-nav-element) block and only later has its heading, the result is that the [`nav`](#107.html_the-nav-element) block is not part of the same section as the rest of the [`article`](#107.html_the-article-element) in the outline. For instance, take this document:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<title>We're adopting a child! — Ray's blog</title>
...

<h1>Ray's blog</h1>

<main>
 <article>
<header>
  <nav>
   <a href="?t=-1d">Yesterday</a>;
   <a href="?t=-7d">Last week</a>;
   <a href="?t=-1m">Last month</a>
  </nav> 
</header>
  <h2>We're adopting a child!</h2>

  <p>As of today, Janine and I have signed the papers to become
  the proud parents of baby Diane! We've been looking forward to
  this day for weeks.</p>
</article> 
</main>
...
```

The resulting outline would be:

1.  Ray's blog
    1.  *Untitled article*
        1.  *Untitled navigation section*
    2.  We're adopting a child!

Also worthy of note in this example is that the [`header`](#107.html_the-header-element) and [`main`](#107.html_the-main-element) elements have no effect whatsoever on the document outline.
