Let the <dfn id="125.html_hyperlink-suffix">`hyperlink suffix`</dfn> be a U+003F QUESTION MARK character, the value of `x` expressed as a base-ten integer using [ASCII digits](#125.html_ascii-digits), a "," (U+002C) character, and the value of `y` expressed as a base-ten integer using [ASCII digits](#125.html_ascii-digits).
4.  Finally, the user agent must [follow the hyperlink](#125.html_following-hyperlinks) or [download the hyperlink](#125.html_downloading-hyperlinks) created by the [`a`](#125.html_the-a-element) element, as determined by the [`download`](#125.html_attr-hyperlink-download) attribute and any expressed user preference. If the steps above defined a [`hyperlink suffix`](#125.html_hyperlink-suffix), then take that into account when following or downloading the hyperlink.

`a` . [`text`](#125.html_dom-a-text)

Same as [`textContent`](#125.html_textcontent).

The IDL attributes <dfn id="125.html_dom-a-download" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-download">`download`</dfn>, <dfn id="125.html_dom-a-target" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-target">`target`</dfn>, <dfn id="125.html_dom-a-rel" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-rel">`rel`</dfn>, <dfn id="125.html_dom-a-rev" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-rev">`rev`</dfn>, <dfn id="125.html_dom-a-hreflang" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-hreflang">`hreflang`</dfn>, and <dfn id="125.html_dom-a-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-type">`type`</dfn>, must [reflect](#125.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

The IDL attribute <dfn id="125.html_dom-a-rellist" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-rellist">`relList`</dfn> must [reflect](#125.html_reflect) the [`rel`](#125.html_attr-hyperlink-rel) content attribute.

The <dfn id="125.html_dom-a-text" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-text">`text`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the same value as the [`textContent`](#125.html_textcontent) IDL attribute on the element, and on setting, must act as if the [`textContent`](#125.html_textcontent) IDL attribute on the element had been set to the new value.

* * *

The [`a`](#125.html_the-a-element) element also supports the [`URLUtils`](#125.html_urlutils) interface. [[URL]](#125.html_refsURL)

When the element is created, and whenever the element's [`href`](#125.html_attr-hyperlink-href) content attribute is set, changed, or removed, the user agent must invoke the element's [`URLUtils`](#125.html_urlutils) interface's [set the input](#125.html_concept-uu-set-the-input) algorithm with the value of the [`href`](#125.html_attr-hyperlink-href) content attribute, if any, or the empty string otherwise, as the given value.

The element's [`URLUtils`](#125.html_urlutils) interface's [get the base](#125.html_concept-uu-get-the-base) algorithm must simply return [the element's base URL](#125.html_the-element's-base-url).

The element's [`URLUtils`](#125.html_urlutils) interface's [query encoding](#125.html_concept-uu-query-encoding) is the [document's character encoding](#125.html_document's-character-encoding).

When the element's [`URLUtils`](#125.html_urlutils) interface invokes its [update steps](#125.html_concept-uu-update) with a string `value`, the user agent must set the element's [`href`](#125.html_attr-hyperlink-href) content attribute to the string `value`.

The [`a`](#125.html_the-a-element) element may be wrapped around entire paragraphs, lists, tables, and so forth, even entire sections, so long as there is no interactive content within (e.g. buttons or other links). This example shows how this can be used to make an entire advertising block into a link:

```
<aside class="advertising">
 <h1>Advertising</h1>
 <a href="http://ad.example.com/?adid=1929&amp;pubid=1422">
  <section>
   <h1>Mellblomatic 9000!</h1>
   <p>Turn all your widgets into mellbloms!</p>
   <p>Only $9.99 plus shipping and handling.</p>
  </section>
 </a>
 <a href="http://ad.example.com/?adid=375&amp;pubid=1422">
  <section>
   <h1>The Mellblom Browser</h1>
   <p>Web browsing at the speed of light.</p>
   <p>No other browser goes faster!</p>
  </section>
 </a>
</aside>
```

#### 4.5.2 The <dfn>`em`</dfn> element

[Categories](#126.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#126.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#126.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#126.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#126.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#126.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#126.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#126.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#126.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#126.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#126.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#126.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#126.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#126.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#126.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#126.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#126.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#126.html_htmlelement).

The [`em`](#126.html_the-em-element) element [represents](#126.html_represents) stress emphasis of its contents.

The level of stress that a particular piece of content has is given by its number of ancestor [`em`](#126.html_the-em-element) elements.

The placement of stress emphasis changes the meaning of the sentence. The element thus forms an integral part of the content. The precise way in which stress is used in this way depends on the language.

These examples show how changing the stress emphasis changes the meaning. First, a general statement of fact, with no stress:

```
<p>Cats are cute animals.</p>
```

By emphasizing the first word, the statement implies that the kind of animal under discussion is in question (maybe someone is asserting that dogs are cute):

```
<p><em>Cats</em> are cute animals.</p>
```

Moving the stress to the verb, one highlights that the truth of the entire sentence is in question (maybe someone is saying cats are not cute):

```
<p>Cats <em>are</em> cute animals.</p>
```

By moving it to the adjective, the exact nature of the cats is reasserted (maybe someone suggested cats were *mean* animals):

```
<p>Cats are <em>cute</em> animals.</p>
```

Similarly, if someone asserted that cats were vegetables, someone correcting this might emphasize the last word:

```
<p>Cats are cute <em>animals</em>.</p>
```

By emphasizing the entire sentence, it becomes clear that the speaker is fighting hard to get the point across. This kind of stress emphasis also typically affects the punctuation, hence the exclamation mark here.

```
<p><em>Cats are cute animals!</em></p>
```

Anger mixed with emphasizing the cuteness could lead to markup such as:

```
<p><em>Cats are <em>cute</em> animals!</em></p>
```

The [`em`](#126.html_the-em-element) element isn't a generic "italics" element. Sometimes, text is intended to stand out from the rest of the paragraph, as if it was in a different mood or voice. For this, the [`i`](#126.html_the-i-element) element is more appropriate.

The [`em`](#126.html_the-em-element) element also isn't intended to convey importance; for that purpose, the [`strong`](#126.html_the-strong-element) element is more appropriate.

#### 4.5.3 The <dfn>`strong`</dfn> element

[Categories](#127.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#127.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#127.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#127.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#127.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#127.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#127.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#127.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#127.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#127.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#127.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#127.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#127.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#127.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#127.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#127.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#127.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#127.html_htmlelement).

The [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element) element [represents](#127.html_represents) strong importance, seriousness, or urgency for its contents.

**Importance**: The [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element) element can be used in a heading, caption, or paragraph to distinguish the part that really matters from other parts of the that might be more detailed, more jovial, or merely boilerplate.

For example, the first word of the previous paragraph is marked up with [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element) to distinguish it from the more detailed text in the rest of the paragraph.

**Seriousness**: The [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element) element can be used to mark up a warning or caution notice.

**Urgency**: The [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element) element can be used to denote contents that the user needs to see sooner than other parts of the document.

The relative level of importance of a piece of content is given by its number of ancestor [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element) elements; each [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element) element increases the importance of its contents.

Changing the importance of a piece of text with the [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element) element does not change the meaning of the sentence.

Here, the word "chapter" and the actual chapter number are mere boilerplate, and the actual name of the chapter is marked up with [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element):

```
<h1>Chapter 1: <strong>The Praxis</strong></h1>
```

In the following example, the name of the diagram in the caption is marked up with [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element), to distinguish it from boilerplate text (before) and the description (after):

```
<figcaption>Figure 1\. <strong>Ant colony dynamics</strong>. The ants in this colony are
affected by the heat source (upper left) and the food source (lower right).</figcaption>
```

In this example, the heading is really "Flowers, Bees, and Honey", but the author has added a light-hearted addition to the heading. The [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element) element is thus used to mark up the first part to distinguish it from the latter part.

```
<h1><strong>Flowers, Bees, and Honey</strong> and other things I don't understand</h1>
```

Here is an example of a warning notice in a game, with the various parts marked up according to how important they are:

```
<p><strong>Warning.</strong> This dungeon is dangerous.
<strong>Avoid the ducks.</strong> Take any gold you find.
<strong><strong>Do not take any of the diamonds</strong>,
they are explosive and <strong>will destroy anything within
ten meters.</strong></strong> You have been warned.</p>
```

In this example, the [`strong`](#127.html_the-strong-element) element is used to denote the part of the text that the user is intended to read first.

```
<p>Welcome to Remy, the reminder system.</p>
<p>Your tasks for today:</p>
<ul>
 <li><p><strong>Turn off the oven.</strong></p></li>
 <li><p>Put out the trash.</p></li>
 <li><p>Do the laundry.</p></li>
</ul>
```

#### 4.5.4 The <dfn>`small`</dfn> element

[Categories](#128.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#128.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#128.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#128.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#128.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#128.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#128.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#128.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#128.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#128.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#128.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#128.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#128.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#128.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#128.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#128.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#128.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#128.html_htmlelement).

The [`small`](#128.html_the-small-element) element [represents](#128.html_represents) side comments such as small print.

Small print typically features disclaimers, caveats, legal restrictions, or copyrights. Small print is also sometimes used for attribution, or for satisfying licensing requirements.

The [`small`](#128.html_the-small-element) element does not "de-emphasize" or lower the importance of text emphasized by the [`em`](#128.html_the-em-element) element or marked as important with the [`strong`](#128.html_the-strong-element) element. To mark text as not emphasized or important, simply do not mark it up with the [`em`](#128.html_the-em-element) or [`strong`](#128.html_the-strong-element) elements respectively.

The [`small`](#128.html_the-small-element) element should not be used for extended spans of text, such as multiple paragraphs, lists, or sections of text. It is only intended for short runs of text. The text of a page listing terms of use, for instance, would not be a suitable candidate for the [`small`](#128.html_the-small-element) element: in such a case, the text is not a side comment, it is the main content of the page.

In this example, the [`small`](#128.html_the-small-element) element is used to indicate that value-added tax is not included in a price of a hotel room:

```
<dl>
 <dt>Single room
 <dd>199 € <small>breakfast included, VAT not included</small>
 <dt>Double room
 <dd>239 € <small>breakfast included, VAT not included</small>
</dl>
```

In this second example, the [`small`](#128.html_the-small-element) element is used for a side comment in an article.

```
<p>Example Corp today announced record profits for the
second quarter <small>(Full Disclosure: Foo News is a subsidiary of
Example Corp)</small>, leading to speculation about a third quarter
merger with Demo Group.</p>
```

This is distinct from a sidebar, which might be multiple paragraphs long and is removed from the main flow of text. In the following example, we see a sidebar from the same article. This sidebar also has small print, indicating the source of the information in the sidebar.

```
<aside>
 <h1>Example Corp</h1>
 <p>This company mostly creates small software and Web
 sites.</p>
 <p>The Example Corp company mission is "To provide entertainment
 and news on a sample basis".</p>
 <p><small>Information obtained from <a
 href="http://example.com/about.html">example.com</a> home
 page.</small></p>
</aside>
```

In this last example, the [`small`](#128.html_the-small-element) element is marked as being *important* small print.

```
<p><strong><small>Continued use of this service will result in a kiss.</small></strong></p>
```

#### 4.5.5 The <dfn>`s`</dfn> element

Where [phrasing content](#129.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content attributes](#129.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#129.html_global-attributes)

Tag omission in text/html

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#129.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

The [`s`](#129.html_the-s-element) element [represents](#129.html_represents) contents that are no longer accurate or no longer relevant.

The [`s`](#129.html_the-s-element) element is not appropriate when indicating document edits; to mark a span of text as having been removed from a document, use the [`del`](#129.html_the-del-element) element.

In this example a recommended retail price has been marked as no longer relevant as the product in question has a new sale price.

```
<p>Buy our Iced Tea and Lemonade!</p>
<p><s>Recommended retail price: $3.99 per bottle</s></p>
<p><strong>Now selling for just $2.99 a bottle!</strong></p>
```

#### 4.5.6 The <dfn>`cite`</dfn> element

[Categories](#130.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#130.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#130.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#130.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#130.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#130.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#130.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#130.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#130.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#130.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#130.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#130.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#130.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#130.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#130.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#130.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#130.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#130.html_htmlelement).

The [`cite`](#130.html_the-cite-element) element [represents](#130.html_represents) a reference to a creative work. It must include the title of the work or the name of the author(person, people or organization) or an URL reference, which may be in an abbreviated form as per the conventions used for the addition of citation metadata.

Creative works include a book, a paper, an essay, a poem, a score, a song, a script, a film, a TV show, a game, a sculpture, a painting, a theatre production, a play, an opera, a musical, an exhibition, a legal case report, a web site, a web page, a blog post or comment, a forum post or comment, a tweet, a written or oral statement, etc.

Here is an example of the author of a quote referenced using the [`cite`](#130.html_the-cite-element) element:

```
 <p>In the words of <cite>Charles Bukowski</cite> -  
  <q>An intellectual says a simple thing in a hard way. An artist says a hard thing in a simple way.</q></p> 
```

This second example identifies the author of a tweet by referencing the authors name using the [`cite`](#130.html_the-cite-element) element:

```
 <blockquote class="twitter-tweet">
  <p>? Bukowski in <a href="https://twitter.com/search?q=%23HTML5&src=hash">#HTML5</a> spec examples
  <a href="http://t.co/0FIEiYN1pC">http://t.co/0FIEiYN1pC</a></p><cite>— karl dubost (@karlpro) 
  <a href="https://twitter.com/karlpro/statuses/370905307293442048">August 23, 2013</a></cite>
  </blockquote> 
```

In this example the [`cite`](#130.html_the-cite-element) element is used to reference the title of a work in a bibliography:

```
<p><cite>Universal Declaration of Human Rights</cite>, United Nations,
December 1948\. Adopted by General Assembly resolution 217 A (III).</p>
```

In this example the [`cite`](#130.html_the-cite-element) element is used to reference the title of a television show:

```
<p>Who is your favorite doctor (in <cite>Doctor Who</cite>)?</p>
```

A very common use for the [`cite`](#130.html_the-cite-element) element is to identify the author of a comment in a blog post or forum, as in this example:

```
 <article id="comment-1"> 
  Comment by <cite><a href="http://oli.jp">Oli Studholme</a></cite> 
  <time datetime="2013-08-19T16:01">August 19th, 2013 at 4:01 pm</time>
  <p>Unfortunately I don't think adding names back into the definition of <code>cite</code>
  solves the problem: of the 12 blockquote examples in
  <a href="http://oli.jp/example/blockquote-metadata/">Examples of block quote metadata</a>,
  there's not even one that's <em>just</em> a person’s name.</p>
  <p>A subset of the problem, maybe…</p>
  </article>
```

Another common use for the [`cite`](#130.html_the-cite-element) element is to reference the `URL` of a search result, as in this example:

```
 <div id="resultStats">About 416,000,000 results 0.33 seconds) </div>
  ...
  <p><a href="http://www.w3.org/html/wg/">W3C <i>HTML Working Group</i></a></p>
  <p><cite>www.w3.org/<b>html</b>/wg/</cite></p>
  <p>15 Apr 2013 - The <i>HTML Working Group</i> is currently chartered to continue its 
  work through 31 December 2014\. A Plan 2014 document published by the...</p>
  ... 
```

A *citation* is not a *quote* (for which the [`q`](#130.html_the-q-element) element is appropriate).

This is incorrect usage, because [`cite`](#130.html_the-cite-element) is not for quotes:

```
<p><cite>This is wrong!, said Hillary.</cite> is a quote from the 
   popular daytime TV drama When Ian became Hillary.</p>
```

This is an example of the correct usage:

```
<p><q>This is correct, said Hillary.</q> is a quote from the 
   popular daytime TV drama <cite>When Ian became Hillary</cite>.</p>
```

#### 4.5.7 The <dfn>`q`</dfn> element

[Categories](#131.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#131.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#131.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#131.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#131.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#131.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#131.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#131.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#131.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#131.html_global-attributes)

[`cite`](#131.html_attr-q-cite) - Link to the source of the quotation or more information about the edit

[Tag omission in text/html](#131.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#131.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#131.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#131.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#131.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#131.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#131.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLQuoteElement`](#131.html_htmlquoteelement).

The [`q`](#131.html_the-q-element) element [represents](#131.html_represents) some [phrasing content](#131.html_phrasing-content-1) quoted from another source.

Quotation punctuation (such as quotation marks) that is quoting the contents of the element must not appear immediately before, after, or inside [`q`](#131.html_the-q-element) elements; they will be inserted into the rendering by the user agent.

Content inside a [`q`](#131.html_the-q-element) element must be quoted from another source, whose address, if it has one, may be cited in the <dfn id="131.html_attr-q-cite" data-anolis-xref="attr-q-cite">`cite`</dfn> attribute. The source may be fictional, as when quoting characters in a novel or screenplay.

If the [`cite`](#131.html_attr-q-cite) attribute is present, it must be a [valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#131.html_valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces). To obtain the corresponding citation link, the value of the attribute must be [resolved](#131.html_resolve-a-url) relative to the element. User agents may allow users to follow such citation links, but they are primarily intended for private use (e.g. by server-side scripts collecting statistics about a site's use of quotations), not for readers.

The [`q`](#131.html_the-q-element) element must not be used in place of quotation marks that do not represent quotes; for example, it is inappropriate to use the [`q`](#131.html_the-q-element) element for marking up sarcastic statements.

The use of [`q`](#131.html_the-q-element) elements to mark up quotations is entirely optional; using explicit quotation punctuation without [`q`](#131.html_the-q-element) elements is just as correct.

Here is a simple example of the use of the [`q`](#131.html_the-q-element) element:

```
<p>The man said <q>Things that are impossible just take
longer</q>. I disagreed with him.</p>
```

Here is an example with both an explicit citation link in the [`q`](#131.html_the-q-element) element, and an explicit citation outside:

```
<p>The W3C page <cite>About W3C</cite> says the W3C's
mission is <q cite="http://www.w3.org/Consortium/">To lead the
World Wide Web to its full potential by developing protocols and
guidelines that ensure long-term growth for the Web</q>. I
disagree with this mission.</p>
```

In the following example, the quotation itself contains a quotation:

```
<p>In <cite>Example One</cite>, he writes <q>The man
said <q>Things that are impossible just take longer</q>. I
disagreed with him</q>. Well, I disagree even more!</p>
```

In the following example, quotation marks are used instead of the [`q`](#131.html_the-q-element) element:

```
<p>His best argument was ?I disagree?, which
I thought was laughable.</p>
```

In the following example, there is no quote — the quotation marks are used to name a word. Use of the [`q`](#131.html_the-q-element) element in this case would be inappropriate.

```
<p>The word "ineffable" could have been used to describe the disaster
resulting from the campaign's mismanagement.</p>
```

#### 4.5.8 The <dfn>`dfn`</dfn> element

[Categories](#132.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#132.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#132.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#132.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#132.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#132.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#132.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#132.html_phrasing-content-1), but there must be no [`dfn`](#132.html_the-dfn-element) element descendants.

[Content attributes](#132.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#132.html_global-attributes)

Also, the [`title`](#132.html_attr-dfn-title) attribute has special semantics on this element.

[Tag omission in text/html](#132.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#132.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#132.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#132.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#132.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#132.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#132.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#132.html_htmlelement).

The [`dfn`](#132.html_the-dfn-element) element [represents](#132.html_represents) the defining instance of a term. The [paragraph](#132.html_paragraph), [description list group](#132.html_the-dl-element), or [section](#132.html_sectioning-content-0) that is the nearest ancestor of the [`dfn`](#132.html_the-dfn-element) element must also contain the definition(s) for the [term](#132.html_defining-term) given by the [`dfn`](#132.html_the-dfn-element) element.

<dfn id="132.html_defining-term">Defining term</dfn>: If the [`dfn`](#132.html_the-dfn-element) element has a <dfn id="132.html_attr-dfn-title" data-anolis-xref="attr-dfn-title">`title`</dfn> attribute, then the exact value of that attribute is the term being defined. Otherwise, if it contains exactly one element child node and no child [`Text`](#132.html_text-0) nodes, and that child element is an [`abbr`](#132.html_the-abbr-element) element with a [`title`](#132.html_attr-abbr-title) attribute, then the exact value of *that* attribute is the term being defined. Otherwise, it is the exact [`textContent`](#132.html_textcontent) of the [`dfn`](#132.html_the-dfn-element) element that gives the term being defined.

If the [`title`](#132.html_attr-dfn-title) attribute of the [`dfn`](#132.html_the-dfn-element) element is present, then it must contain only the term being defined.

The [`title`](#132.html_attr-title) attribute of ancestor elements does not affect [`dfn`](#132.html_the-dfn-element) elements.

An [`a`](#132.html_the-a-element) element that links to a [`dfn`](#132.html_the-dfn-element) element represents an instance of the term defined by the [`dfn`](#132.html_the-dfn-element) element.

In the following fragment, the term "Garage Door Opener" is first defined in the first paragraph, then used in the second. In both cases, its abbreviation is what is actually displayed.

```
<p>The <dfn><abbr title="Garage Door Opener">GDO</abbr></dfn>
is a device that allows off-world teams to open the iris.</p>
<!-- ... later in the document: -->
<p>Teal'c activated his <abbr title="Garage Door Opener">GDO</abbr>
and so Hammond ordered the iris to be opened.</p>
```

With the addition of an [`a`](#132.html_the-a-element) element, the reference can be made explicit:

```
<p>The <dfn id=gdo><abbr title="Garage Door Opener">GDO</abbr></dfn>
is a device that allows off-world teams to open the iris.</p>
<!-- ... later in the document: -->
<p>Teal'c activated his <a href=#gdo><abbr title="Garage Door Opener">GDO</abbr></a>
and so Hammond ordered the iris to be opened.</p>
```

#### 4.5.9 The <dfn>`abbr`</dfn> element

[Categories](#133.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#133.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#133.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#133.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#133.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#133.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#133.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#133.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#133.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#133.html_global-attributes)

Also, the [`title`](#133.html_attr-abbr-title) attribute has special semantics on this element.

[Tag omission in text/html](#133.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#133.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#133.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#133.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#133.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#133.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#133.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#133.html_htmlelement).

The [`abbr`](#133.html_the-abbr-element) element [represents](#133.html_represents) an abbreviation or acronym, optionally with its expansion. The <dfn id="133.html_attr-abbr-title" data-anolis-xref="attr-abbr-title">`title`</dfn> attribute may be used to provide an expansion of the abbreviation. The attribute, if specified, must contain an expansion of the abbreviation, and nothing else.

The paragraph below contains an abbreviation marked up with the [`abbr`](#133.html_the-abbr-element) element. This paragraph [defines the term](#133.html_defining-term) "Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group".

```
<p>The <dfn id=whatwg><abbr
title="Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group">WHATWG</abbr></dfn>
is a loose unofficial collaboration of Web browser manufacturers and
interested parties who wish to develop new technologies designed to
allow authors to write and deploy Applications over the World Wide
Web.</p>
```

An alternative way to write this would be:

```
<p>The <dfn id=whatwg>Web Hypertext Application Technology
Working Group</dfn> (<abbr
title="Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group">WHATWG</abbr>)
is a loose unofficial collaboration of Web browser manufacturers and
interested parties who wish to develop new technologies designed to
allow authors to write and deploy Applications over the World Wide
Web.</p>
```

This paragraph has two abbreviations. Notice how only one is defined; the other, with no expansion associated with it, does not use the [`abbr`](#133.html_the-abbr-element) element.

```
<p>The
<abbr title="Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group">WHATWG</abbr>
started working on HTML5 in 2004.</p>
```

This paragraph links an abbreviation to its definition.

```
<p>The <a href="#whatwg"><abbr
title="Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group">WHATWG</abbr></a>
community does not have much representation from Asia.</p>
```

This paragraph marks up an abbreviation without giving an expansion, possibly as a hook to apply styles for abbreviations (e.g. smallcaps).

```
<p>Philip` and Dashiva both denied that they were going to
get the issue counts from past revisions of the specification to
backfill the <abbr>WHATWG</abbr> issue graph.</p>
```

If an abbreviation is pluralized, the expansion's grammatical number (plural vs singular) must match the grammatical number of the contents of the element.

Here the plural is outside the element, so the expansion is in the singular:

```
<p>Two <abbr title="Working Group">WG</abbr>s worked on
this specification: the <abbr>WHATWG</abbr> and the
<abbr>HTMLWG</abbr>.</p>
```

Here the plural is inside the element, so the expansion is in the plural:

```
<p>Two <abbr title="Working Groups">WGs</abbr> worked on
this specification: the <abbr>WHATWG</abbr> and the
<abbr>HTMLWG</abbr>.</p>
```

Abbreviations do not have to be marked up using this element. It is expected to be useful in the following cases:

*   Abbreviations for which the author wants to give expansions, where using the [`abbr`](#133.html_the-abbr-element) element with a [`title`](#133.html_attr-title) attribute is an alternative to including the expansion inline (e.g. in parentheses).
*   Abbreviations that are likely to be unfamiliar to the document's readers, for which authors are encouraged to either mark up the abbreviation using an [`abbr`](#133.html_the-abbr-element) element with a [`title`](#133.html_attr-title) attribute or include the expansion inline in the text the first time the abbreviation is used.
*   Abbreviations whose presence needs to be semantically annotated, e.g. so that they can be identified from a style sheet and given specific styles, for which the [`abbr`](#133.html_the-abbr-element) element can be used without a [`title`](#133.html_attr-title) attribute.

Providing an expansion in a [`title`](#133.html_attr-title) attribute once will not necessarily cause other [`abbr`](#133.html_the-abbr-element) elements in the same document with the same contents but without a [`title`](#133.html_attr-title) attribute to behave as if they had the same expansion. Every [`abbr`](#133.html_the-abbr-element) element is independent.

#### 4.5.10 The <dfn>`data`</dfn> element

[Categories](#134.html_element-dfn-categories):

Where [phrasing content](#134.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#134.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#134.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#134.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#134.html_global-attributes)

[`value`](#134.html_attr-data-value) - Machine-readable value

[Tag omission in text/html](#134.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#134.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#134.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#134.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#134.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#134.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#134.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLDataElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString value;
};
```

The [`data`](#134.html_the-data-element) element [represents](#134.html_represents) its contents, along with a machine-readable form of those contents in the [`value`](#134.html_attr-data-value) attribute.

The <dfn id="134.html_attr-data-value" data-anolis-xref="attr-data-value">`value`</dfn> attribute must be present. Its value must be a representation of the element's contents in a machine-readable format.

When the value is date- or time-related, the more specific [`time`](#134.html_the-time-element) element can be used instead.

The element can be used for several purposes.

When combined with microformats or microdata, the element serves to provide both a machine-readable value for the purposes of data processors, and a human-readable value for the purposes of rendering in a Web browser. In this case, the format to be used in the [`value`](#134.html_attr-data-value) attribute is determined by the microformats or microdata vocabulary in use.

The element can also, however, be used in conjunction with scripts in the page, for when a script has a literal value to store alongside a human-readable value. In such cases, the format to be used depends only on the needs of the script. (The [`data-*`](#134.html_attr-data-*) attributes can also be useful in such situations.)

The <dfn id="134.html_dom-data-value" data-anolis-xref="dom-data-value">`value`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#134.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

[Categories](#135.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Palpable content](#135.html_palpable-content-0).

Where [phrasing content](#135.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content attributes](#135.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Tag omission in text/html](#135.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#135.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#135.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#135.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTimeElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString dateTime;
};
```

The [`time`](#135.html_the-time-element) element [represents](#135.html_represents) its contents, along with a machine-readable form of those contents in the [`datetime`](#135.html_attr-time-datetime) attribute. The kind of content is limited to various kinds of dates, times, time-zone offsets, and durations, as described below.

The <dfn id="135.html_attr-time-datetime" data-anolis-xref="attr-time-datetime">`datetime`</dfn> attribute may be present. If present, its value must be a representation of the element's contents in a machine-readable format.

A [`time`](#135.html_the-time-element) element that does not have a [`datetime`](#135.html_attr-time-datetime) content attribute must not have any element descendants.

The <dfn id="135.html_datetime-value">datetime value</dfn> of a [`time`](#135.html_the-time-element) element is the value of the element's [`datetime`](#135.html_attr-time-datetime) content attribute, if it has one, or the element's [`textContent`](#135.html_textcontent), if it does not.

The [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) of a [`time`](#135.html_the-time-element) element must match one of the following syntaxes.

A [valid month string](#135.html_valid-month-string)

```
<time>2011-11</time>
```

A [valid date string](#135.html_valid-date-string)

```
<time>2011-11-12</time>
```

A [valid yearless date string](#135.html_valid-yearless-date-string)

```
<time>11-12</time>
```

A [valid time string](#135.html_valid-time-string)

```
<time>14:54</time>
```

```
<time>14:54:39</time>
```

```
<time>14:54:39.929</time>
```

A [valid floating date and time string](#135.html_valid-floating-date-and-time-string)

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54:39</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54:39.929</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54:39</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54:39.929</time>
```

Times with dates but without a time zone offset are useful for specifying events that are observed at the same specific time in each time zone, throughout a day. For example, the 2020 new year is celebrated at 2020-01-01 00:00 in each time zone, not at the same precise moment across all time zones. For events that occur at the same time across all time zones, for example a videoconference meeting, a [valid global date and time string](#135.html_valid-global-date-and-time-string) is likely more useful.

A [valid time-zone offset string](#135.html_valid-time-zone-offset-string)

```
<time>Z</time>
```

```
<time>+0000</time>
```

```
<time>+00:00</time>
```

```
<time>-0800</time>
```

```
<time>-08:00</time>
```

For times without dates (or times referring to events that recur on multiple dates), specifying the geographic location that controls the time is usually more useful than specifying a time zone offset, because geographic locations change time zone offsets with daylight savings time. In some cases, geographic locations even change time zone, e.g. when the boundaries of those time zones are redrawn, as happened with Samoa at the end of 2011\. There exists a time zone database that describes the boundaries of time zones and what rules apply within each such zone, known as the *time zone database*. [[TZDATABASE]](#135.html_refsTZDATABASE)

A [valid global date and time string](#135.html_valid-global-date-and-time-string)

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54Z</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54:39Z</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54:39.929Z</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54+0000</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54:39+0000</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54:39.929+0000</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54+00:00</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54:39+00:00</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T14:54:39.929+00:00</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T06:54-0800</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T06:54:39-0800</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T06:54:39.929-0800</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T06:54-08:00</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T06:54:39-08:00</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12T06:54:39.929-08:00</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54Z</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54:39Z</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54:39.929Z</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54+0000</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54:39+0000</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54:39.929+0000</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54+00:00</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54:39+00:00</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 14:54:39.929+00:00</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 06:54-0800</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 06:54:39-0800</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 06:54:39.929-0800</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 06:54-08:00</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 06:54:39-08:00</time>
```

```
<time>2011-11-12 06:54:39.929-08:00</time>
```

Times with dates and a time zone offset are useful for specifying specific events, or recurring virtual events where the time is not anchored to a specific geographic location. For example, the precise time of an asteroid impact, or a particular meeting in a series of meetings held at 1400 UTC every day, regardless of whether any particular part of the world is observing daylight savings time or not. For events where the precise time varies by the local time zone offset of a specific geographic location, a [valid floating date and time string](#135.html_valid-floating-date-and-time-string) combined with that geographic location is likely more useful.

A [valid week string](#135.html_valid-week-string)

```
<time>2011-W46</time>
```

Four or more [ASCII digits](#135.html_ascii-digits), at least one of which is not "0" (U+0030)

```
<time>2011</time>
```

```
<time>0001</time>
```

A [valid duration string](#135.html_valid-duration-string)

```
<time>PT4H18M3S</time>
```

```
<time>4h 18m 3s</time>
```

Many of the preceding valid syntaxes describe "floating" date and/or time values (they do not include a [time-zone offset](#135.html_concept-timezone)). Care is needed when converting floating time values to or from global ("incremental") time values (e.g., JavaScript's Date object). In many cases, an implicit time-of-day and time zone are used in the conversion and may result in unexpected changes to the value of the date itself. [[TIMEZONES]](#135.html_refsTIMEZONES)

The <dfn id="135.html_machine-readable-equivalent-of-the-element's-contents">machine-readable equivalent of the element's contents</dfn> must be obtained from the element's [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) by using the following algorithm:

1.  If [parsing a month string](#135.html_parse-a-month-string) from the element's [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) returns a [month](#135.html_concept-month), that is the machine-readable equivalent; abort these steps.

2.  If [parsing a date string](#135.html_parse-a-date-string) from the element's [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) returns a [date](#135.html_concept-date), that is the machine-readable equivalent; abort these steps.

3.  If [parsing a yearless date string](#135.html_parse-a-yearless-date-string) from the element's [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) returns a [yearless date](#135.html_concept-yearless-date), that is the machine-readable equivalent; abort these steps.

4.  If [parsing a time string](#135.html_parse-a-time-string) from the element's [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) returns a [time](#135.html_concept-time), that is the machine-readable equivalent; abort these steps.

5.  If [parsing a floating date and time string](#135.html_parse-a-floating-date-and-time-string) from the element's [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) returns a [floating date and time](#135.html_concept-datetime-floating), that is the machine-readable equivalent; abort these steps.

6.  If [parsing a time-zone offset string](#135.html_parse-a-time-zone-offset-string) from the element's [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) returns a [time-zone offset](#135.html_concept-timezone), that is the machine-readable equivalent; abort these steps.

7.  If [parsing a global date and time string](#135.html_parse-a-global-date-and-time-string) from the element's [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) returns a [global date and time](#135.html_concept-datetime), that is the machine-readable equivalent; abort these steps.

8.  If [parsing a week string](#135.html_parse-a-week-string) from the element's [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) returns a [week](#135.html_concept-week), that is the machine-readable equivalent; abort these steps.

9.  If the element's [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) consists of only [ASCII digits](#135.html_ascii-digits), at least one of which is not "0" (U+0030), then the machine-readable equivalent is the base-ten interpretation of those digits, representing a year; abort these steps.

10.  If [parsing a duration string](#135.html_parse-a-duration-string) from the element's [datetime value](#135.html_datetime-value) returns a [duration](#135.html_concept-duration), that is the machine-readable equivalent; abort these steps.

11.  There is no machine-readable equivalent.

The algorithms referenced above are intended to be designed such that for any arbitrary string `s`, only one of the algorithms returns a value. A more efficient approach might be to create a single algorithm that parses all these data types in one pass; developing such an algorithm is left as an exercise to the reader.

The <dfn id="135.html_dom-time-datetime" data-anolis-xref="dom-time-dateTime">`dateTime`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#135.html_reflect) the element's [`datetime`](#135.html_attr-time-datetime) content attribute.

The [`time`](#135.html_the-time-element) element can be used to encode dates, for example in microformats. The following shows a hypothetical way of encoding an event using a variant on hCalendar that uses the [`time`](#135.html_the-time-element) element:

```
<div class="vevent">
 <a class="url" href="http://www.web2con.com/">http://www.web2con.com/</a>
  <span class="summary">Web 2.0 Conference</span>:
  <time class="dtstart" datetime="2005-10-05">October 5</time> -
  <time class="dtend" datetime="2005-10-07">7</time>,
  at the <span class="location">Argent Hotel, San Francisco, CA</span>
 </div>
```

Here, a fictional microdata vocabulary based on the Atom vocabulary is used with the [`time`](#135.html_the-time-element) element to mark up a blog post's publication date.

```
<article itemscope itemtype="http://n.example.org/rfc4287">
 <h1 itemprop="title">Big tasks</h1>
 <footer>Published <time itemprop="published" datetime="2009-08-29">two days ago</time>.</footer>
 <p itemprop="content">Today, I went out and bought a bike for my kid.</p>
</article>
```

In this example, another article's publication date is marked up using [`time`](#135.html_the-time-element), this time using the schema.org microdata vocabulary:

```
<article itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/BlogPosting">
 <h1 itemprop="headline">Small tasks</h1>
 <footer>Published <time itemprop="datePublished" datetime="2009-08-30">yesterday</time>.</footer>
 <p itemprop="articleBody">I put a bike bell on his bike.</p>
</article>
```

In the following snippet, the [`time`](#135.html_the-time-element) element is used to encode a date in the ISO8601 format, for later processing by a script:

```
<p>Our first date was <time datetime="2006-09-23">a Saturday</time>.</p>
```

In this second snippet, the value includes a time:

```
<p>We stopped talking at <time datetime="2006-09-24T05:00-07:00">5am the next morning</time>.</p>
```

A script loaded by the page (and thus privy to the page's internal convention of marking up dates and times using the [`time`](#135.html_the-time-element) element) could scan through the page and look at all the [`time`](#135.html_the-time-element) elements therein to create an index of dates and times.

For example, this element conveys the string "Tuesday" with the additional semantic that the 12th of November 2011 is the meaning that corresponds to "Tuesday":

```
Today is <time datetime="2011-11-12">Tuesday</time>.
```

In this example, a specific time in the Pacific Standard Time timezone is specified:

```
Your next meeting is at <time datetime="2011-11-12T15:00-08:00">3pm</time>.
```

#### 4.5.12 The <dfn>`code`</dfn> element

[Categories](#136.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#136.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#136.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#136.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#136.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#136.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#136.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#136.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#136.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#136.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#136.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#136.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#136.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#136.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#136.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#136.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#136.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#136.html_htmlelement).

The [`code`](#136.html_the-code-element) element [represents](#136.html_represents) a fragment of computer code. This could be an XML element name, a file name, a computer program, or any other string that a computer would recognize.

There is no formal way to indicate the language of computer code being marked up. Authors who wish to mark [`code`](#136.html_the-code-element) elements with the language used, e.g. so that syntax highlighting scripts can use the right rules, can use the [`class`](#136.html_classes) attribute, e.g. by adding a class prefixed with "`language-`" to the element.

The following example shows how the element can be used in a paragraph to mark up element names and computer code, including punctuation.

```
<p>The <code>code</code> element represents a fragment of computer
code.</p>

<p>When you call the <code>activate()</code> method on the
<code>robotSnowman</code> object, the eyes glow.</p>

<p>The example below uses the <code>begin</code> keyword to indicate
the start of a statement block. It is paired with an <code>end</code>
keyword, which is followed by the <code>.</code> punctuation character
(full stop) to indicate the end of the program.</p>
```

The following example shows how a block of code could be marked up using the [`pre`](#136.html_the-pre-element) and [`code`](#136.html_the-code-element) elements.

```
<pre><code class="language-pascal">var i: Integer;
begin
   i := 1;
end.</code></pre>
```

A class is used in that example to indicate the language used.

See the [`pre`](#136.html_the-pre-element) element for more details.

#### 4.5.13 The <dfn>`var`</dfn> element

[Categories](#137.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#137.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#137.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#137.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#137.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#137.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#137.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#137.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#137.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#137.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#137.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#137.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#137.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#137.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#137.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#137.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#137.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#137.html_htmlelement).

The [`var`](#137.html_the-var-element) element [represents](#137.html_represents) a variable. This could be an actual variable in a mathematical expression or programming context, an identifier representing a constant, a symbol identifying a physical quantity, a function parameter, or just be a term used as a placeholder in prose.

In the paragraph below, the letter "n" is being used as a variable in prose:

```
<p>If there are <var>n</var> pipes leading to the ice
cream factory then I expect at <em>least</em> <var>n</var>
flavors of ice cream to be available for purchase!</p>
```

For mathematics, in particular for anything beyond the simplest of expressions, MathML is more appropriate. However, the [`var`](#137.html_the-var-element) element can still be used to refer to specific variables that are then mentioned in MathML expressions.

In this example, an equation is shown, with a legend that references the variables in the equation. The expression itself is marked up with MathML, but the variables are mentioned in the figure's legend using [`var`](#137.html_the-var-element).

```
<figure>
 <math>
  <mi>a</mi>
  <mo>=</mo>
  <msqrt>
   <msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup>
   <mi>+</mi>
   <msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup>
  </msqrt>
 </math>
 <figcaption>
  Using Pythagoras' theorem to solve for the hypotenuse <var>a</var> of
  a triangle with sides <var>b</var> and <var>c</var>
 </figcaption>
</figure>
```

Here, the equation describing mass-energy equivalence is used in a sentence, and the [`var`](#137.html_the-var-element) element is used to mark the variables and constants in that equation:

```
<p>Then he turned to the blackboard and picked up the chalk. After a few moment's
thought, he wrote <var>E</var> = <var>m</var> <var>c</var><sup>2</sup>. The teacher
looked pleased.</p>
```

Where [phrasing content](#138.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#138.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#138.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#138.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#138.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#138.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#138.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#138.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#138.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#138.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#138.html_element-dfn-dom):

The [`samp`](#138.html_the-samp-element) element [represents](#138.html_represents) (sample) output from a program or computing system.

See the [`pre`](#138.html_the-pre-element) and [`kbd`](#138.html_the-kbd-element) elements for more details.

This example shows the [`samp`](#138.html_the-samp-element) element being used inline:

```
<p>The computer said <samp>Too much cheese in tray
two</samp> but I didn't know what that meant.</p>
```

This second example shows a block of sample output. Nested [`samp`](#138.html_the-samp-element) and [`kbd`](#138.html_the-kbd-element) elements allow for the styling of specific elements of the sample output using a style sheet. There's also a few parts of the [`samp`](#138.html_the-samp-element) that are annotated with even more detailed markup, to enable very precise styling. To achieve this, [`span`](#138.html_the-span-element) elements are used.

```
<pre><samp><span class="prompt">jdoe@mowmow:~$</span> <kbd>ssh demo.example.com</kbd>
Last login: Tue Apr 12 09:10:17 2005 from mowmow.example.com on pts/1
Linux demo 2.6.10-grsec+gg3+e+fhs6b+nfs+gr0501+++p3+c4a+gr2b-reslog-v6.189 #1 SMP Tue Feb 1 11:22:36 PST 2005 i686 unknown

<span class="prompt">jdoe@demo:~$</span> <span class="cursor">_</span></samp></pre>
```

#### 4.5.15 The <dfn>`kbd`</dfn> element

[Categories](#139.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#139.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#139.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#139.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#139.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#139.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#139.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#139.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#139.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#139.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#139.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#139.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#139.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#139.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#139.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#139.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#139.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#139.html_htmlelement).

The [`kbd`](#139.html_the-kbd-element) element [represents](#139.html_represents) user input (typically keyboard input, although it may also be used to represent other input, such as voice commands).

When the [`kbd`](#139.html_the-kbd-element) element is nested inside a [`samp`](#139.html_the-samp-element) element, it represents the input as it was echoed by the system.

When the [`kbd`](#139.html_the-kbd-element) element *contains* a [`samp`](#139.html_the-samp-element) element, it represents input based on system output, for example invoking a menu item.

When the [`kbd`](#139.html_the-kbd-element) element is nested inside another [`kbd`](#139.html_the-kbd-element) element, it represents an actual key or other single unit of input as appropriate for the input mechanism.

Here the [`kbd`](#139.html_the-kbd-element) element is used to indicate keys to press:

```
<p>To make George eat an apple, press <kbd><kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F3</kbd></kbd></p>
```

In this second example, the user is told to pick a particular menu item. The outer [`kbd`](#139.html_the-kbd-element) element marks up a block of input, with the inner [`kbd`](#139.html_the-kbd-element) elements representing each individual step of the input, and the [`samp`](#139.html_the-samp-element) elements inside them indicating that the steps are input based on something being displayed by the system, in this case menu labels:

```
<p>To make George eat an apple, select
    <kbd><kbd><samp>File</samp></kbd>|<kbd><samp>Eat Apple...</samp></kbd></kbd>
</p>
```

Such precision isn't necessary; the following is equally fine:

```
<p>To make George eat an apple, select <kbd>File | Eat Apple...</kbd></p>
```

The [`sup`](#140.html_the-sub-and-sup-elements) element [represents](#140.html_represents) a superscript and the [`sub`](#140.html_the-sub-and-sup-elements) element [represents](#140.html_represents) a subscript.

These elements must be used only to mark up typographical conventions with specific meanings, not for typographical presentation for presentation's sake. For example, it would be inappropriate for the [`sub`](#140.html_the-sub-and-sup-elements) and [`sup`](#140.html_the-sub-and-sup-elements) elements to be used in the name of the LaTeX document preparation system. In general, authors should use these elements only if the *absence* of those elements would change the meaning of the content.

In certain languages, superscripts are part of the typographical conventions for some abbreviations.

```
<p>The most beautiful women are
<span lang="fr"><abbr>M<sup>lle</sup></abbr> Gwendoline</span> and
<span lang="fr"><abbr>M<sup>me</sup></abbr> Denise</span>.</p>
```

The [`sub`](#140.html_the-sub-and-sup-elements) element can be used inside a [`var`](#140.html_the-var-element) element, for variables that have subscripts.

Here, the [`sub`](#140.html_the-sub-and-sup-elements) element is used to represent the subscript that identifies the variable in a family of variables:

```
<p>The coordinate of the <var>i</var>th point is
(<var>x<sub><var>i</var></sub></var>, <var>y<sub><var>i</var></sub></var>).
For example, the 10th point has coordinate
(<var>x<sub>10</sub></var>, <var>y<sub>10</sub></var>).</p>
```

Mathematical expressions often use subscripts and superscripts. Authors are encouraged to use MathML for marking up mathematics, but authors may opt to use [`sub`](#140.html_the-sub-and-sup-elements) and [`sup`](#140.html_the-sub-and-sup-elements) if detailed mathematical markup is not desired. [[MATHML]](#140.html_refsMATHML)

```
<var>E</var>=<var>m</var><var>c</var><sup>2</sup>
```

```
f(<var>x</var>, <var>n</var>) = log<sub>4</sub><var>x</var><sup><var>n</var></sup>
```

#### 4.5.17 The <dfn>`i`</dfn> element

[Categories](#141.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#141.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#141.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#141.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#141.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#141.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#141.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#141.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#141.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#141.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#141.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#141.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#141.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#141.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#141.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#141.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#141.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#141.html_htmlelement).

The [`i`](#141.html_the-i-element) element [represents](#141.html_represents) a span of text in an alternate voice or mood, or otherwise offset from the normal prose in a manner indicating a different quality of text, such as a taxonomic designation, a technical term, an idiomatic phrase from another language, transliteration, a thought, or a ship name in Western texts.

Terms in languages different from the main text should be annotated with [`lang`](#141.html_attr-lang) attributes (or, in XML, [`lang` attributes in the XML namespace](#141.html_attr-xml-lang)).

The examples below show uses of the [`i`](#141.html_the-i-element) element:

```
<p>The <i class="taxonomy">Felis silvestris catus</i> is cute.</p>
<p>The term <i>prose content</i> is defined above.</p>
<p>There is a certain <i lang="fr">je ne sais quoi</i> in the air.</p>
```

In the following example, a dream sequence is marked up using [`i`](#141.html_the-i-element) elements.

```
<p>Raymond tried to sleep.</p>
<p><i>The ship sailed away on Thursday</i>, he
dreamt. <i>The ship had many people aboard, including a beautiful
princess called Carey. He watched her, day-in, day-out, hoping she
would notice him, but she never did.</i></p>
<p><i>Finally one night he picked up the courage to speak with
her—</i></p>
<p>Raymond woke with a start as the fire alarm rang out.</p>
```

Authors can use the [`class`](#141.html_classes) attribute on the [`i`](#141.html_the-i-element) element to identify why the element is being used, so that if the style of a particular use (e.g. dream sequences as opposed to taxonomic terms) is to be changed at a later date, the author doesn't have to go through the entire document (or series of related documents) annotating each use.

Authors are encouraged to consider whether other elements might be more applicable than the [`i`](#141.html_the-i-element) element, for instance the [`em`](#141.html_the-em-element) element for marking up stress emphasis, or the [`dfn`](#141.html_the-dfn-element) element to mark up the defining instance of a term.

Style sheets can be used to format [`i`](#141.html_the-i-element) elements, just like any other element can be restyled. Thus, it is not the case that content in [`i`](#141.html_the-i-element) elements will necessarily be italicized.

#### 4.5.18 The <dfn>`b`</dfn> element

[Categories](#142.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#142.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#142.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#142.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#142.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#142.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#142.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#142.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#142.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#142.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#142.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#142.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#142.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#142.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#142.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#142.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#142.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#142.html_htmlelement).

The [`b`](#142.html_the-b-element) element [represents](#142.html_represents) a span of text to which attention is being drawn for utilitarian purposes without conveying any extra importance and with no implication of an alternate voice or mood, such as key words in a document abstract, product names in a review, actionable words in interactive text-driven software, or an article lede.

The following example shows a use of the [`b`](#142.html_the-b-element) element to highlight key words without marking them up as important:

```
<p>The <b>frobonitor</b> and <b>barbinator</b> components are fried.</p>
```

In the following example, objects in a text adventure are highlighted as being special by use of the [`b`](#142.html_the-b-element) element.

```
<p>You enter a small room. Your <b>sword</b> glows
brighter. A <b>rat</b> scurries past the corner wall.</p>
```

Another case where the [`b`](#142.html_the-b-element) element is appropriate is in marking up the lede (or lead) sentence or paragraph. The following example shows how a [BBC article about kittens adopting a rabbit as their own](http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/scotland/north_east/7101506.stm) could be marked up:

```
<article>
 <h2>Kittens 'adopted' by pet rabbit</h2>
 <p><b class="lede">Six abandoned kittens have found an
 unexpected new mother figure — a pet rabbit.</b></p>
 <p>Veterinary nurse Melanie Humble took the three-week-old
 kittens to her Aberdeen home.</p>
[...]
```

As with the [`i`](#142.html_the-i-element) element, authors can use the [`class`](#142.html_classes) attribute on the [`b`](#142.html_the-b-element) element to identify why the element is being used, so that if the style of a particular use is to be changed at a later date, the author doesn't have to go through annotating each use.

The [`b`](#142.html_the-b-element) element should be used as a last resort when no other element is more appropriate. In particular, headings should use the [`h1`](#142.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) to [`h6`](#142.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) elements, stress emphasis should use the [`em`](#142.html_the-em-element) element, importance should be denoted with the [`strong`](#142.html_the-strong-element) element, and text marked or highlighted should use the [`mark`](#142.html_the-mark-element) element.

The following would be *incorrect* usage:

```
<p><b>WARNING!</b> Do not frob the barbinator!</p>
```

In the previous example, the correct element to use would have been [`strong`](#142.html_the-strong-element), not [`b`](#142.html_the-b-element).

Style sheets can be used to format [`b`](#142.html_the-b-element) elements, just like any other element can be restyled. Thus, it is not the case that content in [`b`](#142.html_the-b-element) elements will necessarily be boldened.

#### 4.5.19 The <dfn>`u`</dfn> element

[Categories](#143.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Palpable content](#143.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#143.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#143.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Phrasing content](#143.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#143.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#143.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#143.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#143.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#143.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#143.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#143.html_index-aria-global)
