[DOM interface](#143.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#143.html_htmlelement).

The [`u`](#143.html_the-u-element) element [represents](#143.html_represents) a span of text with an unarticulated, though explicitly rendered, non-textual annotation, such as labeling the text as being a proper name in Chinese text (a Chinese proper name mark), or labeling the text as being misspelt.

In most cases, another element is likely to be more appropriate: for marking stress emphasis, the [`em`](#143.html_the-em-element) element should be used; for marking key words or phrases either the [`b`](#143.html_the-b-element) element or the [`mark`](#143.html_the-mark-element) element should be used, depending on the context; for marking book titles, the [`cite`](#143.html_the-cite-element) element should be used; for labeling text with explicit textual annotations, the [`ruby`](#143.html_the-ruby-element) element should be used; for labeling ship names in Western texts, the [`i`](#143.html_the-i-element) element should be used.

The default rendering of the [`u`](#143.html_the-u-element) element in visual presentations clashes with the conventional rendering of hyperlinks (underlining). Authors are encouraged to avoid using the [`u`](#143.html_the-u-element) element where it could be confused for a hyperlink.

#### 4.5.20 The <dfn>`mark`</dfn> element

[Categories](#144.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#144.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#144.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#144.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#144.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#144.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#144.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#144.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#144.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#144.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#144.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#144.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#144.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#144.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#144.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#144.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#144.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#144.html_htmlelement).

The [`mark`](#144.html_the-mark-element) element [represents](#144.html_represents) a run of text in one document marked or highlighted for reference purposes, due to its relevance in another context. When used in a quotation or other block of text referred to from the prose, it indicates a highlight that was not originally present but which has been added to bring the reader's attention to a part of the text that might not have been considered important by the original author when the block was originally written, but which is now under previously unexpected scrutiny. When used in the main prose of a document, it indicates a part of the document that has been highlighted due to its likely relevance to the user's current activity.

This example shows how the [`mark`](#144.html_the-mark-element) element can be used to bring attention to a particular part of a quotation:

```
<p lang="en-US">Consider the following quote:</p>
<blockquote lang="en-GB">
 <p>Look around and you will find, no-one's really
 <mark>colour</mark> blind.</p>
</blockquote>
<p lang="en-US">As we can tell from the <em>spelling</em> of the word,
the person writing this quote is clearly not American.</p>
```

(If the goal was to mark the element as misspelt, however, the [`u`](#144.html_the-u-element) element, possibly with a class, would be more appropriate.)

Another example of the [`mark`](#144.html_the-mark-element) element is highlighting parts of a document that are matching some search string. If someone looked at a document, and the server knew that the user was searching for the word "kitten", then the server might return the document with one paragraph modified as follows:

```
<p>I also have some <mark>kitten</mark>s who are visiting me
these days. They're really cute. I think they like my garden! Maybe I
should adopt a <mark>kitten</mark>.</p>
```

In the following snippet, a paragraph of text refers to a specific part of a code fragment.

```
<p>The highlighted part below is where the error lies:</p>
<pre><code>var i: Integer;
begin
   i := <mark>1.1</mark>;
end.</code></pre>
```

This is separate from *syntax highlighting*, for which [`span`](#144.html_the-span-element) is more appropriate. Combining both, one would get:

```
<p>The highlighted part below is where the error lies:</p>
<pre><code><span class=keyword>var</span> <span class=ident>i</span>: <span class=type>Integer</span>;
<span class=keyword>begin</span>
   <span class=ident>i</span> := <span class=literal><mark>1.1</mark></span>;
<span class=keyword>end</span>.</code></pre>
```

This is another example showing the use of [`mark`](#144.html_the-mark-element) to highlight a part of quoted text that was originally not emphasized. In this example, common typographic conventions have led the author to explicitly style [`mark`](#144.html_the-mark-element) elements in quotes to render in italics.

```
<article>
 <style>
  blockquote mark, q mark {
    font: inherit; font-style: italic;
    text-decoration: none;
    background: transparent; color: inherit;
  }
  .bubble em {
    font: inherit; font-size: larger;
    text-decoration: underline;
  }
 </style>
 <h1>She knew</h1>
 <p>Did you notice the subtle joke in the joke on panel 4?</p>
 <blockquote>
  <p class="bubble">I didn't <em>want</em> to believe. <mark>Of course
  on some level I realized it was a known-plaintext attack.</mark> But I
  couldn't admit it until I saw for myself.</p>
 </blockquote>
 <p>(Emphasis mine.) I thought that was great. It's so pedantic, yet it
 explains everything neatly.</p>
</article>
```

Note, incidentally, the distinction between the [`em`](#144.html_the-em-element) element in this example, which is part of the original text being quoted, and the [`mark`](#144.html_the-mark-element) element, which is highlighting a part for comment.

The following example shows the difference between denoting the *importance* of a span of text ([`strong`](#144.html_the-strong-element)) as opposed to denoting the *relevance* of a span of text ([`mark`](#144.html_the-mark-element)). It is an extract from a textbook, where the extract has had the parts relevant to the exam highlighted. The safety warnings, important though they may be, are apparently not relevant to the exam.

```
<h3>Wormhole Physics Introduction</h3>

<p><mark>A wormhole in normal conditions can be held open for a
maximum of just under 39 minutes.</mark> Conditions that can increase
the time include a powerful energy source coupled to one or both of
the gates connecting the wormhole, and a large gravity well (such as a
black hole).</p>

<p><mark>Momentum is preserved across the wormhole. Electromagnetic
radiation can travel in both directions through a wormhole,
but matter cannot.</mark></p>

<p>When a wormhole is created, a vortex normally forms.
<strong>Warning: The vortex caused by the wormhole opening will
annihilate anything in its path.</strong> Vortexes can be avoided when
using sufficiently advanced dialing technology.</p>

<p><mark>An obstruction in a gate will prevent it from accepting a
wormhole connection.</mark></p>
```

#### 4.5.21 The <dfn>`ruby`</dfn> element

[Categories](#145.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#145.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#145.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#145.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#145.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#145.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#145.html_element-dfn-content-model):

See prose.

[Content attributes](#145.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#145.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#145.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#145.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#145.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#145.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#145.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#145.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#145.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#145.html_htmlelement).

The [`ruby`](#145.html_the-ruby-element) element allows one or more spans of phrasing content to be marked with ruby annotations. Ruby annotations are short runs of text presented alongside base text, primarily used in East Asian typography as a guide for pronunciation or to include other annotations. In Japanese, this form of typography is also known as *furigana*. Ruby text can appear on either side, and sometimes both sides, of the base text, and it is possible to control its position using CSS. A more complete introduction to ruby can be found in the Use Cases & Exploratory Approaches for Ruby Markup document as well as in CSS Ruby Module Level 1. [[RUBY-UC]](#145.html_refsRUBY-UC) [[CSSRUBY]](#145.html_refsCSSRUBY)

The content model of [`ruby`](#145.html_the-ruby-element) elements consists of one or more of the following sequences:

1.  One or more [phrasing content](#145.html_phrasing-content-1) nodes or [`rb`](#145.html_the-rb-element) elements.
2.  One or more [`rt`](#145.html_the-rt-element) or [`rtc`](#145.html_the-rtc-element) elements, each of which either immediately preceded or followed by an [`rp`](#145.html_the-rp-element) elements.

The [`ruby`](#145.html_the-ruby-element), [`rb`](#145.html_the-rb-element), [`rtc`](#145.html_the-rtc-element), and [`rt`](#145.html_the-rt-element) elements can be used for a variety of kinds of annotations, including in particular (though by no means limited to) those described below. For more details on Japanese Ruby in particular, and how to render Ruby for Japanese, see Requirements for Japanese Text Layout. [[JLREQ]](#145.html_refsJLREQ) The [`rp`](#145.html_the-rp-element) element can be used as fallback content when ruby rendering is not supported.

Mono-ruby for individual base characters

Annotations (the ruby text) are associated individually with each ideographic character (the base text). In Japanese this is typically hiragana or katakana characters used to provide readings of kanji characters.

```
<ruby>base<rt>annotation</ruby>
```

When no [`rb`](#145.html_the-rb-element) element is used, the base is implied, as above. But you can also make it explicit. This can be useful notably for styling, or when consecutive bases are to be treated as a group, as in the jukugo ruby example further down.

```
<ruby><rb>base<rt>annotation</ruby>
```

In the following example, notice how each annotation corresponds to a single base character.

```
<ruby>日<rt>に</rt></ruby><ruby>本<rt>ほん</rt></ruby>
<ruby>語<rt>ご</rt></ruby>で<ruby>書<rt>か</rt></ruby>
いた<ruby>作<rt>さく</rt></ruby><ruby>文<rt>ぶん</rt></ruby>です。 
```

Ruby text interspersed in regular text provides structure akin to the following image:

![An example of ruby text mixed up with regular text.](Images/378be585cc69283c5fd60fa3993f5e83.jpg)

This example can also be written as follows, using one [`ruby`](#145.html_the-ruby-element) element with two segments of base text and two annotations (one for each) rather than two back-to-back [`ruby`](#145.html_the-ruby-element) elements each with one base text segment and annotation (as in the markup above):

```
<ruby>日<rt>に</rt>本<rt>ほん</rt>語<rt>ご</rt></ruby>
で<ruby>書<rt>か</rt></ruby>
いた<ruby>作<rt>さく</rt>文<rt>ぶん</rt></ruby>です。 
```

Group ruby

Group ruby is often used where phonetic annotations don't map to discreet base characters, or for semantic glosses that span the whole base text. For example, the word "today" is written with the characters 今日, literally "this day". But it's pronounced きょう (kyou), which can't be broken down into a "this" part and a "day" part. In typical rendering, you can't split text that is annotated with group ruby; it has to wrap as a single unit onto the next line. When a [ruby text annotation](#145.html_ruby-text-annotation) maps to a base that is comprised of more than one character, then that base is grouped.

The following group ruby:

![Group ruby example with きょう annotating 今日](Images/fbc9e85097918486949d4c4337fa1b2d.jpg)

Can be marked up as follows:

```
<ruby>今日<rt>きょう</ruby>
```

Jukugo ruby

*Jukugo* refers to a Japanese compound noun, i.e. a word made up of more than one kanji character. *Jukugo ruby* is a term that is used not to describe ruby annotations over jukugo text, but rather to describe ruby with a behaviour slightly different from mono or group ruby. Jukugo ruby is similar to mono ruby, in that there is a strong association between ruby text and individual base characters, but the ruby text is typically rendered as grouped together over multiple ideographs when they are on the same line.

The distinction is captured in this example:

![Example of jukugo ruby](Images/5c424af6104ffbb0b20fede177a743c5.jpg)

Which can be marked up as follows:

```
<ruby>法<rb>華<rb>経<rt>ほ<rt>け<rt>きょう</ruby>
```

In this example, each [`rt`](#145.html_the-rt-element) element is paired with its respective [`rb`](#145.html_the-rb-element) element, the difference with an interleaved [`rb`](#145.html_the-rb-element)/[`rt`](#145.html_the-rt-element) approach being that the sequences of both base text and ruby annotations are implicitly placed in common containers so that the grouping information is captured.

For more details on [Jukugo Ruby rendering](http://www.w3.org/TR/jlreq/#positioning_of_jukugoruby), see Appendix F in the Requirements for Japanese Text Layout and Use Case C: Jukugo ruby in the Use Cases & Exploratory Approaches for Ruby Markup. [[JLREQ]](#145.html_refsJLREQ) [[RUBY-UC]](#145.html_refsRUBY-UC)

Inline ruby

In some contexts, for instance when the font size or line height are too small for ruby to be readable, it is desirable to inline the ruby annotation such that it appears in parentheses after the text it annotates. This also provides a convenient fallback strategy for user agents that do not support rendering ruby annotations.

Inlining takes grouping into account. For example, Tokyo is written with two kanji characters, 東, which is pronounced とう, and 京, which is pronounced きょう. Each base character should be annotated individually, but the fallback should be 東京(とうきょう) not 東(とう)京(きょう). This can be marked up as follows:

```
<ruby>東<rb>京<rt>とう<rt>きょう</ruby>
```

Note that the above markup will enable the usage of parentheses when inlining for browsers that support ruby layout, but for those that don't it will fail to provide parenthetical fallback. This is where the [`rp`](#145.html_the-rp-element) element is useful. It can be inserted into the above example to provide the appropriate fallback when ruby layout is not supported:

```
<ruby>東<rb>京<rp>(<rt>とう<rt>きょう<rp>)</ruby>
```

Text with both phonetic and semantic annotations (double-sided ruby)

Sometimes, ruby can be used to annotate a base twice.

In the following example, the Chinese word for San Francisco (旧金山, i.e. “old gold mountain”) is annotated both using pinyin to give the pronunciation, and with the original English.

![San Francisco in Chinese, with both pinyin and the original English as annotations.](Images/23b4dd64cdfeff422ae2a76f1d598373.jpg)

Which is marked up as follows:

```
<ruby><rb>旧<rb>金<rb>山<rt>jiù<rt>jīn<rt>shān<rtc>San Francisco</ruby> 
```

In this example, a single base run of three base characters is annotated with three pinyin ruby text segments in a first (implicit) container, and an [`rtc`](#145.html_the-rtc-element) element is introduced in order to provide a second single [ruby text annotation](#145.html_ruby-text-annotation) being the city's English name.

We can also revisit our jukugo example above with 上手 ("skill") to show how it can be annotation in both kana and romaji phonetics while at the same time maintaining the pairing to bases and annotation grouping information.

![上手 ("skill") annotated in both kana and romaji, shown in both jukugo and mono styles.](Images/fcd2ae513f0df88f122bf737c7fb27ab.jpg)

Which is marked up as follows:

```
<ruby><rb>上<rb>手<rt>じよう<rt>ず<rtc><rt>jou<rt>zu</ruby> 
```

Text that is a direct child of the [`rtc`](#145.html_the-rtc-element) element implicitly produces a ruby text segment as if it were contained in an [`rt`](#145.html_the-rt-element) element. In this contrived example, this is shown with some symbols that are given names in English and French with annotations intended to appear on either side of the base symbol.

```
<ruby>
  ?<rt>Heart<rtc lang=fr>C?ur</rtc>
  ?<rt>Shamrock<rtc lang=fr>Trèfle</rtc>
  ?<rt>Star<rtc lang=fr>étoile
</ruby> 
```

Similarly, text directly inside a [`ruby`](#145.html_the-ruby-element) element implicitly produces a ruby base as if it were contained in an [`rb`](#145.html_the-rb-element) element, and [`rt`](#145.html_the-rt-element) children of [`ruby`](#145.html_the-ruby-element) are implicitly contained in an [`rtc`](#145.html_the-rtc-element) container. In effect, the above example is equivalent (in meaning, though not in the DOM it produces) to the following:

```
<ruby>
  <rb>?</rb><rtc><rt>Heart</rt></rtc><rtc lang=fr><rt>C?ur</rt></rtc>
  <rb>?</rb><rtc><rt>Shamrock</rt></rtc><rtc lang=fr><rt>Trèfle</rt></rtc>
  <rb>?</rb><rtc><rt>Star</rt></rtc><rtc lang=fr><rt>étoile</rt></rtc>
</ruby> 
```

* * *

Within a ruby element, content is parcelled into a series of ruby segments. Each <dfn id="145.html_ruby-segment">ruby segment</dfn> is described by:

*   Zero or more <dfn id="145.html_ruby-base" data-anolis-xref="ruby base">ruby bases</dfn>, each of which is a DOM range that may contain phrasing content or an [`rb`](#145.html_the-rb-element) element.
*   A base range, that is a DOM range including all the bases. This is the <dfn id="145.html_ruby-base-container">ruby base container</dfn>.
*   Zero or more [ruby text containers](#145.html_ruby-text-container) which may correspond to explicit [`rtc`](#145.html_the-rtc-element) elements, or to sequences of [`rt`](#145.html_the-rt-element) elements implicitly recognised as contained in an anonymous [ruby text container](#145.html_ruby-text-container).

Each <dfn id="145.html_ruby-text-container">ruby text container</dfn> is described by zero or more <dfn id="145.html_ruby-text-annotation" data-anolis-xref="ruby text
      annotation">ruby text annotations</dfn> each of which is a DOM range that may contain phrasing content or an [`rt`](#145.html_the-rt-element) element, and an annotations range that is a range including all the annotations for that container. A [ruby text container](#145.html_ruby-text-container) is also known (primarily in a CSS context) as a <dfn id="145.html_ruby-annotation-container">ruby annotation container</dfn>.

Furthermore, a ruby element contains <dfn id="145.html_ignored-ruby-content">ignored ruby content</dfn>. Ignored ruby content does not form part of the document's semantics. It consists of some [inter-element whitespace](#145.html_inter-element-whitespace) and [`rp`](#145.html_the-rp-element) elements, the latter of which are used for legacy user agents that do not support ruby at all.

The process of <dfn id="145.html_annotation-pairing">annotation pairing</dfn> associates [ruby annotations](#145.html_ruby-text-annotation) with [ruby bases](#145.html_ruby-base). Within each [ruby segment](#145.html_ruby-segment), each [ruby base](#145.html_ruby-base) in the [ruby base container](#145.html_ruby-base-container) is paired with one [ruby text annotation](#145.html_ruby-text-annotation) from the [ruby text container](#145.html_ruby-text-container), in order. If there are not enough [ruby text annotations](#145.html_ruby-text-annotation) in a [ruby annotation container](#145.html_ruby-annotation-container), the last one is associated with any excess [ruby bases](#145.html_ruby-base). (If there are not any in the [ruby annotation container](#145.html_ruby-annotation-container), an anonymous empty one is assumed to exist.) If there are not enough [ruby bases](#145.html_ruby-base), any remaining [ruby text annotations](#145.html_ruby-text-annotation) are assumed to be associated with empty, anonymous bases inserted at the end of the [ruby base container](#145.html_ruby-base-container).

Note that the terms [ruby segment](#145.html_ruby-segment), [ruby base](#145.html_ruby-base), [ruby text annotation](#145.html_ruby-text-annotation), [ruby text container](#145.html_ruby-text-container), [ruby base container](#145.html_ruby-base-container), and [ruby annotation container](#145.html_ruby-annotation-container) have their equivalents in CSS Ruby Module Level 1. [[CSSRUBY]](#145.html_refsCSSRUBY)

Informally, the segmentation and categorisation algorithm below performs a simple set of tasks. First it processes adjacent [`rb`](#145.html_the-rb-element) elements, text nodes, and non-ruby elements into a list of bases. Then it processes any number of [`rtc`](#145.html_the-rtc-element) elements or sequences of [`rt`](#145.html_the-rt-element) elements that are considered to automatically map to an anonymous [ruby text container](#145.html_ruby-text-container). Put together these data items form a [ruby segment](#145.html_ruby-segment) as detailed in the data model above. It will continue to produce such segments until it reaches the end of the content of a given [`ruby`](#145.html_the-ruby-element) element. The complexity of the algorithm below compared to this informal description stems from the need to support an author-friendly syntax and being mindful of inter-element white space.

At any particular time, the <dfn id="145.html_segmentation-and-categorisation-of-ruby" data-anolis-xref="segmentation and categorisation of
      ruby">segmentation and categorisation of content of a `ruby`</dfn> element is the result that would be obtained from running the following algorithm:

1.  Let `root` be the [`ruby`](#145.html_the-ruby-element) element for which the algorithm is being run.
2.  Let `index` be 0.
3.  Let `ruby segments` be an empty list.
4.  Let `current bases` be an empty list of DOM ranges.
5.  Let `current bases range` be null.
6.  Let `current bases range start` be null.
7.  Let `current annotations` be an empty list of DOM ranges.
8.  Let `current annotations range` be null.
9.  Let `current annotations range start` be null.
10.  Let `current annotation containers` be an empty list.
11.  Let `current automatic base nodes` be an empty list of DOM Nodes.
12.  Let `current automatic base range start` be null.
13.  *Process a ruby child*: If `index` is equal to or greater than the number of child nodes in `root`, then run the steps to [commit a ruby segment](#145.html_commit-a-ruby-segment), return `ruby segments`, and abort these steps.
14.  Let `current child` be the `index`th node in `root`.
15.  If `current child` is not a [Text](#145.html_text-0) node and is not an [Element](#145.html_element) node, then increment `index` by one and jump to the step labelled *process a ruby child*.
16.  If `current child` is an [`rp`](#145.html_the-rp-element) element, then increment `index` by one and jump to the step labelled *process a ruby child*. (Note that this has the effect of including this element in any range that we are currently processing. This is done intentionally so that misplaced [`rp`](#145.html_the-rp-element) can be processed correctly; semantically they are ignored all the same.)
17.  If `current child` is an [`rt`](#145.html_the-rt-element) element, then run these substeps:
    1.  Run the steps to [commit an automatic base](#145.html_commit-an-automatic-base).
    2.  Run the steps to [commit the base range](#145.html_commit-the-base-range).
    3.  If `current annotations` is empty, set `current annotations range start` to the value of `index`.
    4.  Create a new DOM range whose [start](#145.html_concept-range-start) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index`) and whose [end](#145.html_concept-range-end) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index` plus one), and append it at the end of `current annotations`.
    5.  Increment `index` by one and jump to the step labelled *process a ruby child*.
18.  If `current child` is an [`rtc`](#145.html_the-rtc-element) element, then run these substeps:
    1.  Run the steps to [commit an automatic base](#145.html_commit-an-automatic-base).
    2.  Run the steps to [commit the base range](#145.html_commit-the-base-range).
    3.  Run the steps to [commit current annotations](#145.html_commit-current-annotations).
    4.  Create a new [ruby annotation container](#145.html_ruby-annotation-container). It is described by the list of annotations returned by running the steps to [process an `rtc` element](#145.html_process-an-rtc-element) and a DOM range whose [start](#145.html_concept-range-start) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index`) and whose [end](#145.html_concept-range-end) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index` plus one). Append this new [ruby annotation container](#145.html_ruby-annotation-container) at the end of `current annotation containers`.
    5.  Increment `index` by one and jump to the step labelled *process a ruby child*.
19.  If `current child` is a [Text](#145.html_text-0) node and is [inter-element whitespace](#145.html_inter-element-whitespace), then run these substeps:
    1.  If `current annotations` is not empty, increment `index` by one and jump to the step labelled *process a ruby child*.
    2.  Run the following substeps:
        1.  Let `lookahead index` be set to the value of `index`.
        2.  *Peek ahead*: Increment `lookahead index` by one.
        3.  If `lookahead index` is equal to or greater than the number of child nodes in `root`, then abort these substeps.
        4.  Let `peek child` be the `lookahead index`th node in `root`.
        5.  If `peek child` is a [Text](#145.html_text-0) node and is [inter-element whitespace](#145.html_inter-element-whitespace), then jump to the step labelled *peek ahead*.
        6.  If `peek child` is an [`rt`](#145.html_the-rt-element) element, an [`rtc`](#145.html_the-rtc-element) element, or an [`rp`](#145.html_the-rp-element) element, then set `index` to the value of `lookahead index` and jump to the step labelled *process a ruby child*.
20.  If `current annotations` is not empty or if `current annotation containers` is not empty, then run the steps to [commit a ruby segment](#145.html_commit-a-ruby-segment).
21.  If `current child` is an [`rb`](#145.html_the-rb-element) element, then run these substeps:
    1.  Run the steps to [commit an automatic base](#145.html_commit-an-automatic-base).
    2.  If `current bases` is empty, then set `current bases range start` to the value of `index`.
    3.  Create a new DOM range whose [start](#145.html_concept-range-start) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index`) and whose [end](#145.html_concept-range-end) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index` plus one), and append it at the end of `current bases`.
    4.  Increment `index` by one and jump to the step labelled *process a ruby child*.
22.  If `current automatic base nodes` is empty, set `current automatic base range start` to the value of `index`.
23.  Append `current child` at the end of `current automatic base nodes`.
24.  Increment `index` by one and jump to the step labelled *process a ruby child*.

When the steps above say to <dfn id="145.html_commit-a-ruby-segment">commit a ruby segment</dfn>, it means to run the following steps at that point in the algorithm:

1.  Run the steps to [commit an automatic base](#145.html_commit-an-automatic-base).
2.  If `current bases`, `current annotations`, and `current annotation containers` are all empty, abort these steps.
3.  Run the steps to [commit the base range](#145.html_commit-the-base-range).
4.  Run the steps to [commit current annotations](#145.html_commit-current-annotations).
5.  Create a new [ruby segment](#145.html_ruby-segment). It is described by a list of bases set to `current bases`, a base DOM range set to `current bases range`, and a list of [ruby annotation containers](#145.html_ruby-annotation-container) that are the `current annotation containers` list. Append this new [ruby segment](#145.html_ruby-segment) at the end of `ruby segments`.
6.  Let `current bases` be an empty list.
7.  Let `current bases range` be null.
8.  Let `current bases range start` be null.
9.  Let `current annotation containers` be an empty list.

When the steps above say to <dfn id="145.html_commit-the-base-range">commit the base range</dfn>, it means to run the following steps at that point in the algorithm:

1.  If `current bases` is empty, abort these steps.
2.  If `current bases range` is not null, abort these steps.
3.  Let `current bases range` be a DOM range whose [start](#145.html_concept-range-start) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `current bases range start`) and whose [end](#145.html_concept-range-end) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index`).

When the steps above say to <dfn id="145.html_commit-current-annotations">commit current annotations</dfn>, it means to run the following steps at that point in the algorithm:

1.  If `current annotations` is not empty and `current annotations range` is null let `current annotations range` be a DOM range whose [start](#145.html_concept-range-start) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `current annotations range start`) and whose [end](#145.html_concept-range-end) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index`).
2.  If `current annotations` is not empty, create a new [ruby annotation container](#145.html_ruby-annotation-container). It is described by an annotations list set to `current annotations` and a range set to `current annotations range`. Append this new [ruby annotation container](#145.html_ruby-annotation-container) at the end of `current annotation containers`.
3.  Let `current annotations` be an empty list of DOM ranges.
4.  Let `current annotations range` be null.
5.  Let `current annotations range start` be null.

When the steps above say to <dfn id="145.html_commit-an-automatic-base">commit an automatic base</dfn>, it means to run the following steps at that point in the algorithm:

1.  If `current automatic base nodes` is empty, abort these steps.
2.  If `current automatic base nodes` contains nodes that are not [Text](#145.html_text-0) nodes, or [Text](#145.html_text-0) nodes that are not [inter-element whitespace](#145.html_inter-element-whitespace), then run these substeps:
    1.  It `current bases` is empty, set `current bases range start` to the value of `current automatic base range start`.
    2.  Create a new DOM range whose [start](#145.html_concept-range-start) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `current automatic base range start`) and whose [end](#145.html_concept-range-end) is the [boundary point](#145.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index`), and append it at the end of `current bases`.
3.  Let `current automatic base nodes` be an empty list of DOM Nodes.
4.  Let `current automatic base range start` be null.

#### 4.5.22 The <dfn>`rb`</dfn> element

[Categories](#146.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#146.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As a child of a [`ruby`](#146.html_the-ruby-element) element.

[Content model](#146.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#146.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#146.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#146.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#146.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

An [`rb`](#146.html_the-rb-element) element's [end tag](#146.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`rb`](#146.html_the-rb-element) element is immediately followed by an [`rb`](#146.html_the-rb-element), [`rt`](#146.html_the-rt-element), [`rtc`](#146.html_the-rtc-element) or [`rp`](#146.html_the-rp-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#146.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#146.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#146.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#146.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#146.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#146.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#146.html_htmlelement).

The [`rb`](#146.html_the-rb-element) element marks the base text component of a ruby annotation. When it is the child of a [`ruby`](#146.html_the-ruby-element) element, it doesn't [represent](#146.html_represents) anything itself, but its parent [`ruby`](#146.html_the-ruby-element) element uses it as part of determining what *it* [represents](#146.html_represents).

An [`rb`](#146.html_the-rb-element) element that is not a child of a [`ruby`](#146.html_the-ruby-element) element [represents](#146.html_represents) the same thing as its children.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#147.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#147.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#147.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[DOM interface](#147.html_element-dfn-dom):

The [`rt`](#147.html_the-rt-element) element marks the ruby text component of a ruby annotation. When it is the child of a [`ruby`](#147.html_the-ruby-element) element or of an [`rtc`](#147.html_the-rtc-element) element that is itself the child of a [`ruby`](#147.html_the-ruby-element) element, it doesn't [represent](#147.html_represents) anything itself, but its ancestor [`ruby`](#147.html_the-ruby-element) element uses it as part of determining what *it* [represents](#147.html_represents).

An [`rt`](#147.html_the-rt-element) element that is not a child of a [`ruby`](#147.html_the-ruby-element) element or of an [`rtc`](#147.html_the-rtc-element) element that is itself the child of a [`ruby`](#147.html_the-ruby-element) element [represents](#147.html_represents) the same thing as its children.

#### 4.5.24 The <dfn>`rtc`</dfn> element

[Categories](#148.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#148.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As a child of a [`ruby`](#148.html_the-ruby-element) element.

[Content model](#148.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#148.html_phrasing-content-1) or [`rt`](#148.html_the-rt-element) elements.

[Content attributes](#148.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#148.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#148.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

An [`rtc`](#148.html_the-rtc-element) element's [end tag](#148.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`rtc`](#148.html_the-rtc-element) element is immediately followed by an [`rb`](#148.html_the-rb-element), [`rtc`](#148.html_the-rtc-element) or [`rp`](#148.html_the-rp-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#148.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#148.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#148.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#148.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#148.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#148.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#148.html_htmlelement).

The [`rtc`](#148.html_the-rtc-element) element marks a [ruby text container](#148.html_ruby-text-container) for ruby text components in a ruby annotation. When it is the child of a [`ruby`](#148.html_the-ruby-element) element it doesn't [represent](#148.html_represents) anything itself, but its parent [`ruby`](#148.html_the-ruby-element) element uses it as part of determining what *it* [represents](#148.html_represents).

An [`rtc`](#148.html_the-rtc-element) element that is not a child of a [`ruby`](#148.html_the-ruby-element) element [represents](#148.html_represents) the same thing as its children.

When an [`rtc`](#148.html_the-rtc-element) element is processed as part of the segmentation and categorisation of content for a [`ruby`](#148.html_the-ruby-element) element, the following algorithm defines how to <dfn id="148.html_process-an-rtc-element">process an `rtc` element</dfn>:

1.  Let `root` be the [`rtc`](#148.html_the-rtc-element) element for which the algorithm is being run.
2.  Let `index` be 0.
3.  Let `annotations` be an empty list of DOM ranges.
4.  Let `current automatic annotation nodes` be an empty list of DOM nodes.
5.  Let `current automatic annotation range start` be null.
6.  *Process an rtc child*: If `index` is equal to or greater than the number of child nodes in `root`, then run the steps to [commit an automatic annotation](#148.html_commit-an-automatic-annotation), return `annotations`, and abort these steps.
7.  Let `current child` be the `index`th node in `root`.
8.  If `current child` is an [`rt`](#148.html_the-rt-element) element, then run these substeps:
    1.  Run the steps to [commit an automatic annotation](#148.html_commit-an-automatic-annotation).
    2.  Create a new DOM range whose [start](#148.html_concept-range-start) is the [boundary point](#148.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index`) and whose [end](#148.html_concept-range-end) is the [boundary point](#148.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index` plus one), and append it at the end of `annotations`.
    3.  Increment `index` by one and jump to the step labelled *process an rtc child*.
9.  If `current automatic annotation nodes` is empty, set `current automatic annotation range start` to the value of `index`.
10.  Append `current child` at the end of `current automatic annotation nodes`.
11.  Increment `index` by one and jump to the step labelled *process an rtc child*.

When the steps above say to <dfn id="148.html_commit-an-automatic-annotation">commit an automatic annotation</dfn>, it means to run the following steps at that point in the algorithm:

1.  If `current automatic annotation nodes` is empty, abort these steps.
2.  If `current automatic annotation nodes` contains nodes that are not [Text](#148.html_text-0) nodes, or [Text](#148.html_text-0) nodes that are not [inter-element whitespace](#148.html_inter-element-whitespace), then create a new DOM range whose [start](#148.html_concept-range-start) is the [boundary point](#148.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `current automatic annotation range start`) and whose [end](#148.html_concept-range-end) is the [boundary point](#148.html_concept-range-bp) (`root`, `index`), and append it at the end of `annotations`.
3.  Let `current automatic annotation nodes` be an empty list of DOM nodes.
4.  Let `current automatic annotation range start` be null.

As a child of a [`ruby`](#149.html_the-ruby-element) element, either immediately before or immediately after an [`rt`](#149.html_the-rt-element) or [`rtc`](#149.html_the-rtc-element) element, but not between [`rt`](#149.html_the-rt-element) elements.

[Content model](#149.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#149.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#149.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#149.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#149.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

An [`rp`](#149.html_the-rp-element) element's [end tag](#149.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`rp`](#149.html_the-rp-element) element is immediately followed by an [`rb`](#149.html_the-rb-element), [`rt`](#149.html_the-rt-element), [`rtc`](#149.html_the-rtc-element) or [`rp`](#149.html_the-rp-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#149.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#149.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#149.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#149.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#149.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#149.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#149.html_htmlelement).

The [`rp`](#149.html_the-rp-element) element is used to provide fallback text to be shown by user agents that don't support ruby annotations. One widespread convention is to provide parentheses around the ruby text component of a ruby annotation.

The contents of the [`rp`](#149.html_the-rp-element) elements are typically not displayed by user agents which do support ruby annotations

An [`rp`](#149.html_the-rp-element) element that is a child of a [`ruby`](#149.html_the-ruby-element) element [represents](#149.html_represents) nothing. An [`rp`](#149.html_the-rp-element) element whose parent element is not a [`ruby`](#149.html_the-ruby-element) element [represents](#149.html_represents) its children.

The example shown previously, in which each ideograph in the text 漢字 is annotated with its phonetic reading, could be expanded to use [`rp`](#149.html_the-rp-element) so that in legacy user agents the readings are in parentheses (please note that white space has been introduced into this example in order to make it more readable):

```
...
<ruby>
  漢
  <rb>字</rb>
  <rp> (</rp>
  <rt>かん</rt>
  <rt>じ</rt>
  <rp>) </rp>
</ruby>
... 
```

In conforming user agents the rendering would be as above, but in user agents that do not support ruby, the rendering would be:

```
... 漢字 (かんじ) ...
```

When there are multiple annotations for a segment, [`rp`](#149.html_the-rp-element) elements can also be placed between the annotations. Here is another copy of an earlier contrived example showing some symbols with names given in English and French using double-sided annotations, but this time with [`rp`](#149.html_the-rp-element) elements as well:

```
<ruby>
  ?<rp>: </rp><rt>Heart</rt><rp>, </rp><rtc><rt lang=fr>C?ur</rt></rtc><rp>.</rp>
  ?<rp>: </rp><rt>Shamrock</rt><rp>, </rp><rtc><rt lang=fr>Trèfle</rt></rtc><rp>.</rp>
  ?<rp>: </rp><rt>Star</rt><rp>, </rp><rtc><rt lang=fr>étoile</rt></rtc><rp>.</rp>
</ruby> 
```

This would make the example render as follows in non-ruby-capable user agents:

```
?: Heart, C?ur.
?: Shamrock, Trèfle.
?: Star, étoile. 
```

#### 4.5.26 The <dfn>`bdi`</dfn> element

[Categories](#150.html_element-dfn-categories):

Where [phrasing content](#150.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#150.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#150.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#150.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#150.html_global-attributes)

Also, the [`dir`](#150.html_the-dir-attribute) global attribute has special semantics on this element.

[Tag omission in text/html](#150.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#150.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#150.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#150.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#150.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#150.html_htmlelement).

The [`bdi`](#150.html_the-bdi-element) element [represents](#150.html_represents) a span of text that is to be isolated from its surroundings for the purposes of bidirectional text formatting. [[BIDI]](#150.html_refsBIDI)

The [`dir`](#150.html_the-dir-attribute) global attribute defaults to [`auto`](#150.html_attr-dir-auto) on this element (it never inherits from the parent element like with other elements).

This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#150.html_bidireq).

This element is especially useful when embedding user-generated content with an unknown directionality.

In this example, usernames are shown along with the number of posts that the user has submitted. If the [`bdi`](#150.html_the-bdi-element) element were not used, the username of the Arabic user would end up confusing the text (the bidirectional algorithm would put the colon and the number "3" next to the word "User" rather than next to the word "posts").

```
<ul>
 <li>User <bdi>jcranmer</bdi>: 12 posts.
 <li>User <bdi>hober</bdi>: 5 posts.
 <li>User <bdi>????</bdi>: 3 posts.
</ul>
```

The [`bdo`](#151.html_the-bdo-element) element [represents](#151.html_represents) explicit text directionality formatting control for its children. It allows authors to override the Unicode bidirectional algorithm by explicitly specifying a direction override. [[BIDI]](#151.html_refsBIDI)

Authors must specify the [`dir`](#151.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute on this element, with the value [`ltr`](#151.html_attr-dir-ltr) to specify a left-to-right override and with the value [`rtl`](#151.html_attr-dir-rtl) to specify a right-to-left override. The [`auto`](#151.html_attr-dir-auto) value must not be specified.

This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#151.html_bidireq).

[Palpable content](#152.html_palpable-content-0).

Where [phrasing content](#152.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#152.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#152.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#152.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Any role value](#152.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#152.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#152.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#152.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#152.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLSpanElement : HTMLElement {};
```

The [`span`](#152.html_the-span-element) element doesn't mean anything on its own, but can be useful when used together with the [global attributes](#152.html_global-attributes), e.g. [`class`](#152.html_classes), [`lang`](#152.html_attr-lang), or [`dir`](#152.html_the-dir-attribute). It [represents](#152.html_represents) its children.

In this example, a code fragment is marked up using [`span`](#152.html_the-span-element) elements and [`class`](#152.html_classes) attributes so that its keywords and identifiers can be color-coded from CSS:

```
<pre><code class="lang-c"><span class="keyword">for</span> (<span class="ident">j</span> = 0; <span class="ident">j</span> &lt; 256; <span class="ident">j</span>++) {
  <span class="ident">i_t3</span> = (<span class="ident">i_t3</span> & 0x1ffff) | (<span class="ident">j</span> &lt;&lt; 17);
  <span class="ident">i_t6</span> = (((((((<span class="ident">i_t3</span> >> 3) ^ <span class="ident">i_t3</span>) >> 1) ^ <span class="ident">i_t3</span>) >> 8) ^ <span class="ident">i_t3</span>) >> 5) & 0xff;
  <span class="keyword">if</span> (<span class="ident">i_t6</span> == <span class="ident">i_t1</span>)
    <span class="keyword">break</span>;
}</code></pre>
```

#### 4.5.29 The <dfn>`br`</dfn> element

[Categories](#153.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#153.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#153.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#153.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#153.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#153.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#153.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#153.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#153.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

No [end tag](#153.html_syntax-end-tag)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#153.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#153.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#153.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#153.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#153.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#153.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLBRElement : HTMLElement {};
```

The [`br`](#153.html_the-br-element) element [represents](#153.html_represents) a line break.

While line breaks are usually represented in visual media by physically moving subsequent text to a new line, a style sheet or user agent would be equally justified in causing line breaks to be rendered in a different manner, for instance as green dots, or as extra spacing.

[`br`](#153.html_the-br-element) elements must be used only for line breaks that are actually part of the content, as in poems or addresses.

The following example is correct usage of the [`br`](#153.html_the-br-element) element:

```
<p>P. Sherman<br>
42 Wallaby Way<br>
Sydney</p>
```

[`br`](#153.html_the-br-element) elements must not be used for separating thematic groups in a paragraph.

The following examples are non-conforming, as they abuse the [`br`](#153.html_the-br-element) element:

```
<p><a ...>34 comments.</a><br>
<a ...>Add a comment.</a></p>
```

```
<p><label>Name: <input name="name"></label><br>
<label>Address: <input name="address"></label></p>
```

Here are alternatives to the above, which are correct:

```
<p><a ...>34 comments.</a></p>
<p><a ...>Add a comment.</a></p>
```

```
<p><label>Name: <input name="name"></label></p>
<p><label>Address: <input name="address"></label></p>
```

If a [paragraph](#153.html_paragraph) consists of nothing but a single [`br`](#153.html_the-br-element) element, it represents a placeholder blank line (e.g. as in a template). Such blank lines must not be used for presentation purposes.

Any content inside [`br`](#153.html_the-br-element) elements must not be considered part of the surrounding text.

This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#153.html_bidireq).

[Categories](#154.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Phrasing content](#154.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#154.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#154.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#154.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#154.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#154.html_global-attributes)

[Tag omission in text/html](#154.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

No [end tag](#154.html_syntax-end-tag)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#154.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#154.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#154.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#154.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#154.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#154.html_htmlelement).

The [`wbr`](#154.html_the-wbr-element) element [represents](#154.html_represents) a line break opportunity.

In the following example, someone is quoted as saying something which, for effect, is written as one long word. However, to ensure that the text can be wrapped in a readable fashion, the individual words in the quote are separated using a [`wbr`](#154.html_the-wbr-element) element.

```
<p>So then he pointed at the tiger and screamed
"there<wbr>is<wbr>no<wbr>way<wbr>you<wbr>are<wbr>ever<wbr>going<wbr>to<wbr>catch<wbr>me"!</p>
```

Here, especially long lines of code in a program listing have suggested wrapping points given using [`wbr`](#154.html_the-wbr-element) elements.

```
<pre>...
Heading heading = Helm.HeadingFactory(HeadingCoordinates[1], <wbr>HeadingCoordinates[2], <wbr>HeadingCoordinates[3], <wbr>HeadingCoordinates[4]);
Course course = Helm.CourseFactory(Heading, <wbr>Maps.MapFactoryFromHeading(heading), <wbr>Speeds.GetMaximumSpeed().ConvertToWarp());
...</pre>
```

Any content inside [`wbr`](#154.html_the-wbr-element) elements must not be considered part of the surrounding text.

This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#154.html_bidireq).

### 4.6 Edits

The [`ins`](#156.html_the-ins-element) and [`del`](#156.html_the-del-element) elements represent edits to the document.

#### 4.6.1 The <dfn>`ins`</dfn> element

[Categories](#157.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#157.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#157.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#157.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#157.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#157.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#157.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Transparent](#157.html_transparent).

[Content attributes](#157.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#157.html_global-attributes)

[`cite`](#157.html_attr-mod-cite) - Link to the source of the quotation or more information about the edit

[`datetime`](#157.html_attr-mod-datetime) - Date and (optionally) time of the change

[Tag omission in text/html](#157.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#157.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#157.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#157.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#157.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#157.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#157.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses the [`HTMLModElement`](#157.html_htmlmodelement) interface.

The [`ins`](#157.html_the-ins-element) element [represents](#157.html_represents) an addition to the document.

The following represents the addition of a single paragraph:

```
<aside>
 <ins>
  <p> I like fruit. </p>
 </ins>
</aside>
```

As does the following, because everything in the [`aside`](#157.html_the-aside-element) element here counts as [phrasing content](#157.html_phrasing-content-1) and therefore there is just one [paragraph](#157.html_paragraph):

```
<aside>
 <ins>
  Apples are <em>tasty</em>.
 </ins>
 <ins>
  So are pears.
 </ins>
</aside>
```

[`ins`](#157.html_the-ins-element) elements should not cross [implied paragraph](#157.html_paragraph) boundaries.

The following example represents the addition of two paragraphs, the second of which was inserted in two parts. The first [`ins`](#157.html_the-ins-element) element in this example thus crosses a paragraph boundary, which is considered poor form.

```
<aside>
 <!-- don't do this -->
 <ins datetime="2005-03-16 00:00Z">
  <p> I like fruit. </p>
  Apples are <em>tasty</em>.
 </ins>
 <ins datetime="2007-12-19 00:00Z">
  So are pears.
 </ins>
</aside>
```

Here is a better way of marking this up. It uses more elements, but none of the elements cross implied paragraph boundaries.

```
<aside>
 <ins datetime="2005-03-16 00:00Z">
  <p> I like fruit. </p>
 </ins>
 <ins datetime="2005-03-16 00:00Z">
  Apples are <em>tasty</em>.
 </ins>
 <ins datetime="2007-12-19 00:00Z">
  So are pears.
 </ins>
</aside>
```

[Phrasing content](#158.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#158.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#158.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Transparent](#158.html_transparent).

[Content attributes](#158.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#158.html_global-attributes)

[`cite`](#158.html_attr-mod-cite) - Link to the source of the quotation or more information about the edit

[`datetime`](#158.html_attr-mod-datetime) - Date and (optionally) time of the change

[Tag omission in text/html](#158.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#158.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#158.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

The [`del`](#158.html_the-del-element) element [represents](#158.html_represents) a removal from the document.

[`del`](#158.html_the-del-element) elements should not cross [implied paragraph](#158.html_paragraph) boundaries.

The following shows a "to do" list where items that have been done are crossed-off with the date and time of their completion.

```
<h1>To Do</h1>
<ul>
 <li>Empty the dishwasher</li>
 <li><del datetime="2009-10-11T01:25-07:00">Watch Walter Lewin's lectures</del></li>
 <li><del datetime="2009-10-10T23:38-07:00">Download more tracks</del></li>
 <li>Buy a printer</li>
</ul>
```

#### 4.6.3 Attributes common to [`ins`](#159.html_the-ins-element) and [`del`](#159.html_the-del-element) elements

The <dfn id="159.html_attr-mod-cite" data-anolis-xref="attr-mod-cite">`cite`</dfn> attribute may be used to specify the address of a document that explains the change. When that document is long, for instance the minutes of a meeting, authors are encouraged to include a fragment identifier pointing to the specific part of that document that discusses the change.

If the [`cite`](#159.html_attr-mod-cite) attribute is present, it must be a [valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#159.html_valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces) that explains the change. To obtain the corresponding citation link, the value of the attribute must be [resolved](#159.html_resolve-a-url) relative to the element. User agents may allow users to follow such citation links, but they are primarily intended for private use (e.g. by server-side scripts collecting statistics about a site's edits), not for readers.

The <dfn id="159.html_attr-mod-datetime" data-anolis-xref="attr-mod-datetime">`datetime`</dfn> attribute may be used to specify the time and date of the change.

If present, the [`datetime`](#159.html_attr-mod-datetime) attribute's value must be a [valid date string with optional time](#159.html_valid-date-string-with-optional-time).

User agents must parse the [`datetime`](#159.html_attr-mod-datetime) attribute according to the [parse a date or time string](#159.html_parse-a-date-or-time-string) algorithm. If that doesn't return a [date](#159.html_concept-date) or a [global date and time](#159.html_concept-datetime), then the modification has no associated timestamp (the value is non-conforming; it is not a [valid date string with optional time](#159.html_valid-date-string-with-optional-time)). Otherwise, the modification is marked as having been made at the given [date](#159.html_concept-date) or [global date and time](#159.html_concept-datetime). If the given value is a [global date and time](#159.html_concept-datetime) then user agents should use the associated time-zone offset information to determine which time zone to present the given datetime in.

This value may be shown to the user, but it is primarily intended for private use.

The [`ins`](#159.html_the-ins-element) and [`del`](#159.html_the-del-element) elements must implement the [`HTMLModElement`](#159.html_htmlmodelement) interface:

```
interface HTMLModElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString cite;
           attribute DOMString dateTime;
};
```

The <dfn id="159.html_dom-mod-cite" data-anolis-xref="dom-mod-cite">`cite`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#159.html_reflect) the element's [`cite`](#159.html_attr-mod-cite) content attribute. The <dfn id="159.html_dom-mod-datetime" data-anolis-xref="dom-mod-dateTime">`dateTime`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#159.html_reflect) the element's [`datetime`](#159.html_attr-mod-datetime) content attribute.

#### 4.6.4 Edits and paragraphs

*This section is non-normative.*

Since the [`ins`](#160.html_the-ins-element) and [`del`](#160.html_the-del-element) elements do not affect [paragraphing](#160.html_paragraph), it is possible, in some cases where paragraphs are [implied](#160.html_paragraph) (without explicit [`p`](#160.html_the-p-element) elements), for an [`ins`](#160.html_the-ins-element) or [`del`](#160.html_the-del-element) element to span both an entire paragraph or other non-[phrasing content](#160.html_phrasing-content-1) elements and part of another paragraph. For example:

```
<section>
 <ins>
  <p>
   This is a paragraph that was inserted.
  </p>
  This is another paragraph whose first sentence was inserted
  at the same time as the paragraph above.
 </ins>
 This is a second sentence, which was there all along.
</section>
```

By only wrapping some paragraphs in [`p`](#160.html_the-p-element) elements, one can even get the end of one paragraph, a whole second paragraph, and the start of a third paragraph to be covered by the same [`ins`](#160.html_the-ins-element) or [`del`](#160.html_the-del-element) element (though this is very confusing, and not considered good practice):

```
<section>
 This is the first paragraph. <ins>This sentence was
 inserted.
 <p>This second paragraph was inserted.</p>
 This sentence was inserted too.</ins> This is the
 third paragraph in this example.
 <!-- (don't do this) -->
</section>
```

However, due to the way [implied paragraphs](#160.html_paragraph) are defined, it is not possible to mark up the end of one paragraph and the start of the very next one using the same [`ins`](#160.html_the-ins-element) or [`del`](#160.html_the-del-element) element. You instead have to use one (or two) [`p`](#160.html_the-p-element) element(s) and two [`ins`](#160.html_the-ins-element) or [`del`](#160.html_the-del-element) elements, as for example:

```
<section>
 <p>This is the first paragraph. <del>This sentence was
 deleted.</del></p>
 <p><del>This sentence was deleted too.</del> That
 sentence needed a separate &lt;del&gt; element.</p>
</section>
```

Partly because of the confusion described above, authors are strongly encouraged to always mark up all paragraphs with the [`p`](#160.html_the-p-element) element, instead of having [`ins`](#160.html_the-ins-element) or [`del`](#160.html_the-del-element) elements that cross [implied paragraphs](#160.html_paragraph) boundaries.

#### 4.6.5 Edits and lists

*This section is non-normative.*

The content models of the [`ol`](#161.html_the-ol-element) and [`ul`](#161.html_the-ul-element) elements do not allow [`ins`](#161.html_the-ins-element) and [`del`](#161.html_the-del-element) elements as children. Lists always represent all their items, including items that would otherwise have been marked as deleted.

To indicate that an item is inserted or deleted, an [`ins`](#161.html_the-ins-element) or [`del`](#161.html_the-del-element) element can be wrapped around the contents of the [`li`](#161.html_the-li-element) element. To indicate that an item has been replaced by another, a single [`li`](#161.html_the-li-element) element can have one or more [`del`](#161.html_the-del-element) elements followed by one or more [`ins`](#161.html_the-ins-element) elements.

In the following example, a list that started empty had items added and removed from it over time. The bits in the example that have been emphasized show the parts that are the "current" state of the list. The list item numbers don't take into account the edits, though.

```
<h1>Stop-ship bugs</h1>
<ol>
 <li><ins datetime="2008-02-12T15:20Z">Bug 225:
 Rain detector doesn't work in snow</ins></li>
 <li><del datetime="2008-03-01T20:22Z"><ins datetime="2008-02-14T12:02Z">Bug 228:
 Water buffer overflows in April</ins></del></li>
 <li><ins datetime="2008-02-16T13:50Z">Bug 230:
 Water heater doesn't use renewable fuels</ins></li>
 <li><del datetime="2008-02-20T21:15Z"><ins datetime="2008-02-16T14:25Z">Bug 232:
 Carbon dioxide emissions detected after startup</ins></del></li>
</ol>
```

In the following example, a list that started with just fruit was replaced by a list with just colors.

```
<h1>List of <del>fruits</del><ins>colors</ins></h1>
<ul>
 <li><del>Lime</del><ins>Green</ins></li>
 <li><del>Apple</del></li>
 <li>Orange</li>
 <li><del>Pear</del></li>
 <li><ins>Teal</ins></li>
 <li><del>Lemon</del><ins>Yellow</ins></li>
 <li>Olive</li>
 <li><ins>Purple</ins></li>
</ul>
```

#### 4.6.6 Edits and tables

*This section is non-normative.*

The elements that form part of the table model have complicated content model requirements that do not allow for the [`ins`](#162.html_the-ins-element) and [`del`](#162.html_the-del-element) elements, so indicating edits to a table can be difficult.

To indicate that an entire row or an entire column has been added or removed, the entire contents of each cell in that row or column can be wrapped in [`ins`](#162.html_the-ins-element) or [`del`](#162.html_the-del-element) elements (respectively).

Here, a table's row has been added:

```
<table>
 <thead>
  <tr> <th> Game name           <th> Game publisher   <th> Verdict
 <tbody>
  <tr> <td> Diablo 2            <td> Blizzard         <td> 8/10
  <tr> <td> Portal              <td> Valve            <td> 10/10
  <tr> <td> <ins>Portal 2</ins> <td> <ins>Valve</ins> <td> <ins>10/10</ins>
</table>
```

Here, a column has been removed (the time at which it was removed is given also, as is a link to the page explaining why):

```
<table>
 <thead>
  <tr> <th> Game name           <th> Game publisher   <th> <del cite="/edits/r192" datetime="2011-05-02 14:23Z">Verdict</del>
 <tbody>
  <tr> <td> Diablo 2            <td> Blizzard         <td> <del cite="/edits/r192" datetime="2011-05-02 14:23Z">8/10</del>
  <tr> <td> Portal              <td> Valve            <td> <del cite="/edits/r192" datetime="2011-05-02 14:23Z">10/10</del>
  <tr> <td> Portal 2            <td> Valve            <td> <del cite="/edits/r192" datetime="2011-05-02 14:23Z">10/10</del>
</table>
```

Generally speaking, there is no good way to indicate more complicated edits (e.g. that a cell was removed, moving all subsequent cells up or to the left).

### 4.7 Embedded content

#### 4.7.1 The <dfn>`img`</dfn> element

[Categories](#164.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#164.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#164.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Embedded content](#164.html_embedded-content-2).

[Form-associated element](#164.html_form-associated-element).

If the element has a [`usemap`](#164.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap) attribute: [Interactive content](#164.html_interactive-content-0).

[Palpable content](#164.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#164.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [embedded content](#164.html_embedded-content-2) is expected.

[Content model](#164.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#164.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#164.html_global-attributes)

[`alt`](#164.html_attr-img-alt) - Replacement text for use when images are not available

[`src`](#164.html_attr-img-src) - Address of the resource

[`crossorigin`](#164.html_attr-img-crossorigin) - How the element handles crossorigin requests

[`usemap`](#164.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap) - Name of [image map](#164.html_image-map) to use

[`ismap`](#164.html_attr-img-ismap) - Whether the image is a server-side image map

[`width`](#164.html_attr-dim-width) - Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#164.html_attr-dim-height) - Vertical dimension

[Tag omission in text/html](#164.html_element-dfn-tag-omission):

No [end tag](#164.html_syntax-end-tag).

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#164.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`presentation`](#164.html_index-aria-presentation) role only, for an [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element whose `alt` attribute's value is empty (`alt=""`), otherwise [any role value](#164.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#164.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#164.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#164.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#164.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
[NamedConstructor=Image(optional unsigned long width, optional unsigned long height)]
interface HTMLImageElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString alt;
           attribute DOMString src;

           attribute DOMString crossOrigin;
           attribute DOMString useMap;
           attribute boolean isMap;
           attribute unsigned long width;
           attribute unsigned long height;
  readonly attribute unsigned long naturalWidth;
  readonly attribute unsigned long naturalHeight;
  readonly attribute boolean complete;
};
```

An [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element represents an image.

The image given by the <dfn id="164.html_attr-img-src" data-anolis-xref="attr-img-src">`src`</dfn> attributes is the embedded content; the value of the <dfn id="164.html_attr-img-alt" data-anolis-xref="attr-img-alt">`alt`</dfn> attribute provides equivalent content for those who cannot process images or who have image loading disabled.

The requirements on the [`alt`](#164.html_attr-img-alt) attribute's value are described [in the next section](#164.html_alt).

The [`src`](#164.html_attr-img-src) attribute must be present, and must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#164.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces) referencing a non-interactive, optionally animated, image resource that is neither paged nor scripted.

The requirements above imply that images can be static bitmaps (e.g. PNGs, GIFs, JPEGs), single-page vector documents (single-page PDFs, XML files with an SVG root element), animated bitmaps (APNGs, animated GIFs), animated vector graphics (XML files with an SVG root element that use declarative SMIL animation), and so forth. However, these definitions preclude SVG files with script, multipage PDF files, interactive MNG files, HTML documents, plain text documents, and so forth. [[PNG]](#164.html_refsPNG) [[GIF]](#164.html_refsGIF) [[JPEG]](#164.html_refsJPEG) [[PDF]](#164.html_refsPDF) [[XML]](#164.html_refsXML) [[APNG]](#164.html_refsAPNG) [[SVG]](#164.html_refsSVG) [[MNG]](#164.html_refsMNG)

The [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element must not be used as a layout tool. In particular, [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) elements should not be used to display transparent images, as such images rarely convey meaning and rarely add anything useful to the document.

* * *

The <dfn id="164.html_attr-img-crossorigin" data-anolis-xref="attr-img-crossorigin">`crossorigin`</dfn> attribute is a [CORS settings attribute](#164.html_cors-settings-attribute). Its purpose is to allow images from third-party sites that allow cross-origin access to be used with [`canvas`](#164.html_the-canvas-element).

* * *

An [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) is always in one of the following states:

<dfn id="164.html_img-none" data-anolis-xref="img-none">Unavailable</dfn>

The user agent hasn't obtained any image data.

<dfn id="164.html_img-inc" data-anolis-xref="img-inc">Partially available</dfn>

The user agent has obtained some of the image data.

<dfn id="164.html_img-all" data-anolis-xref="img-all">Completely available</dfn>

The user agent has obtained all of the image data and at least the image dimensions are available.

<dfn id="164.html_img-error" data-anolis-xref="img-error">Broken</dfn>

The user agent has obtained all of the image data that it can, but it cannot even decode the image enough to get the image dimensions (e.g. the image is corrupted, or the format is not supported, or no data could be obtained).

When an [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element is either in the [partially available](#164.html_img-inc) state or in the [completely available](#164.html_img-all) state, it is said to be <dfn id="164.html_img-available" data-anolis-xref="img-available">available</dfn>.

An [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element is initially [unavailable](#164.html_img-none).

When an [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element is [available](#164.html_img-available), it [provides a paint source](#164.html_provides-a-paint-source) whose width is the image's intrinsic width, whose height is the image's intrinsic height, and whose appearance is the intrinsic appearance of the image.

In a [browsing context](#164.html_browsing-context) where [scripting is disabled](#164.html_concept-bc-noscript), user agents may obtain images immediately or on demand. In a [browsing context](#164.html_browsing-context) where [scripting is enabled](#164.html_concept-bc-noscript), user agents must obtain images immediately.

A user agent that obtains images immediately must synchronously [update the image data](#164.html_update-the-image-data) of an [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element whenever that element is created with a [`src`](#164.html_attr-img-src) attribute. A user agent that obtains images immediately must also synchronously [update the image data](#164.html_update-the-image-data) of an [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element whenever that element has its [`src`](#164.html_attr-img-src) or [`crossorigin`](#164.html_attr-img-crossorigin) attribute set, changed, or removed.

A user agent that obtains images on demand must [update the image data](#164.html_update-the-image-data) of an [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element whenever it needs the image data (i.e. on demand), but only if the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element has a [`src`](#164.html_attr-img-src) attribute, and only if the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element is in the [unavailable](#164.html_img-none) state. When an [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element's [`src`](#164.html_attr-img-src) or [`crossorigin`](#164.html_attr-img-crossorigin) attribute set, changed, or removed, if the user agent only obtains images on demand, the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element must return to the [unavailable](#164.html_img-none) state.

Each [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element has a <dfn id="164.html_last-selected-source">last selected source</dfn>, which must initially be null, and a <dfn id="164.html_current-pixel-density">current pixel density</dfn>, which must initially be undefined.

When an [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element has a [current pixel density](#164.html_current-pixel-density) that is not 1.0, the element's image data must be treated as if its resolution, in device pixels per CSS pixels, was the [current pixel density](#164.html_current-pixel-density).

For example, if the [current pixel density](#164.html_current-pixel-density) is 3.125, that means that there are 300 device pixels per CSS inch, and thus if the image data is 300x600, it has an intrinsic dimension of 96 CSS pixels by 192 CSS pixels.

Each [`Document`](#164.html_document) object must have a <dfn id="164.html_list-of-available-images">list of available images</dfn>. Each image in this list is identified by a tuple consisting of an [absolute URL](#164.html_absolute-url), a [CORS settings attribute](#164.html_cors-settings-attribute) mode, and, if the mode is not [No CORS](#164.html_attr-crossorigin-none), an [origin](#164.html_origin-0). User agents may copy entries from one [`Document`](#164.html_document) object's [list of available images](#164.html_list-of-available-images) to another at any time (e.g. when the [`Document`](#164.html_document) is created, user agents can add to it all the images that are loaded in other [`Document`](#164.html_document)s), but must not change the keys of entries copied in this way when doing so. User agents may also remove images from such lists at any time (e.g. to save memory).

When the user agent is to <dfn id="164.html_update-the-image-data">update the image data</dfn> of an [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element, it must run the following steps:

1.  Return the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element to the [unavailable](#164.html_img-none) state.

2.  If an instance of the [fetching](#164.html_fetch) algorithm is still running for this element, then abort that algorithm, discarding any pending [tasks](#164.html_concept-task) generated by that algorithm.

3.  Forget the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element's current image data, if any.

4.  If the user agent cannot support images, or its support for images has been disabled, then abort these steps.

5.  Otherwise, if the element has a [`src`](#164.html_attr-img-src) attribute specified and its value is not the empty string, let `selected source` be the value of the element's [`src`](#164.html_attr-img-src) attribute, and `selected pixel density` be 1.0\. Otherwise, let `selected source` be null and `selected pixel density` be undefined.
6.  Let the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element's [last selected source](#164.html_last-selected-source) be `selected source` and the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element's [current pixel density](#164.html_current-pixel-density) be `selected pixel density`.

7.  If `selected source` is not null, run these substeps:

    1.  [Resolve](#164.html_resolve-a-url) `selected source`, relative to the element. If that is not successful, abort these steps.

    2.  Let `key` be a tuple consisting of the resulting [absolute URL](#164.html_absolute-url), the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element's [`crossorigin`](#164.html_attr-img-crossorigin) attribute's mode, and, if that mode is not [No CORS](#164.html_attr-crossorigin-none), the [`Document`](#164.html_document) object's [origin](#164.html_origin-0).

    3.  If the [list of available images](#164.html_list-of-available-images) contains an entry for `key`, then set the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element to the [completely available](#164.html_img-all) state, update the presentation of the image appropriately, [queue a task](#164.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#164.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `load` at the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element, and abort these steps.

8.  Asynchronously [await a stable state](#164.html_await-a-stable-state), allowing the [task](#164.html_concept-task) that invoked this algorithm to continue. The [synchronous section](#164.html_synchronous-section) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm until the algorithm says the [synchronous section](#164.html_synchronous-section) has ended. (Steps in [synchronous sections](#164.html_synchronous-section) are marked with ?.)

9.  ? If another instance of this algorithm for this [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element was started after this instance (even if it aborted and is no longer running), then abort these steps.

    Only the last instance takes effect, to avoid multiple requests when, for example, the [`src`](#164.html_attr-img-src) and [`crossorigin`](#164.html_attr-img-crossorigin) attributes are all set in succession.

10.  ? If `selected source` is null, then set the element to the [broken](#164.html_img-error) state, [queue a task](#164.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#164.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `error` at the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element, and abort these steps.

11.  ? [Queue a task](#164.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a progress event](#164.html_fire-a-progress-event) named `loadstart` at the [`img`](#164.html_the-img-element) element.

12.  ?
