If, when the element is created, the [`srcdoc`](#165.html_attr-iframe-srcdoc) attribute is not set, and the [`src`](#165.html_attr-iframe-src) attribute is either also not set or set but its value cannot be [resolved](#165.html_resolve-a-url), the browsing context will remain at the initial [`about:blank`](#165.html_about:blank) page.

If the user [navigates](#165.html_navigate) away from this page, the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element)'s corresponding [`WindowProxy`](#165.html_windowproxy) object will proxy new [`Window`](#165.html_window) objects for new [`Document`](#165.html_document) objects, but the [`src`](#165.html_attr-iframe-src) attribute will not change.

* * *

The <dfn id="165.html_attr-iframe-name" data-anolis-xref="attr-iframe-name">`name`</dfn> attribute, if present, must be a [valid browsing context name](#165.html_valid-browsing-context-name). The given value is used to name the [nested browsing context](#165.html_nested-browsing-context). When the browsing context is created, if the attribute is present, the [browsing context name](#165.html_browsing-context-name) must be set to the value of this attribute; otherwise, the [browsing context name](#165.html_browsing-context-name) must be set to the empty string.

Whenever the [`name`](#165.html_attr-iframe-name) attribute is set, the nested [browsing context](#165.html_browsing-context)'s [name](#165.html_browsing-context-name) must be changed to the new value. If the attribute is removed, the [browsing context name](#165.html_browsing-context-name) must be set to the empty string.

* * *

The <dfn id="165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox" data-anolis-xref="attr-iframe-sandbox">`sandbox`</dfn> attribute, when specified, enables a set of extra restrictions on any content hosted by the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element). Its value must be an [unordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#165.html_unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens) that are [ASCII case-insensitive](#165.html_ascii-case-insensitive). The allowed values are [`allow-forms`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-forms), [`allow-pointer-lock`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-pointer-lock), [`allow-popups`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-popups), [`allow-same-origin`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin), [`allow-scripts`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-scripts), and [`allow-top-navigation`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation).

When the attribute is set, the content is treated as being from a unique [origin](#165.html_origin-0), forms, scripts, and various potentially annoying APIs are disabled, links are prevented from targeting other [browsing contexts](#165.html_browsing-context), and plugins are secured. The [`allow-same-origin`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin) keyword causes the content to be treated as being from its real origin instead of forcing it into a unique origin; the [`allow-top-navigation`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation) keyword allows the content to [navigate](#165.html_navigate) its [top-level browsing context](#165.html_top-level-browsing-context); and the [`allow-forms`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-forms), [`allow-pointer-lock`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-pointer-lock), [`allow-popups`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-popups) and [`allow-scripts`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-scripts) keywords re-enable forms, the pointer lock API, popups, and scripts respectively. [[POINTERLOCK]](#165.html_refsPOINTERLOCK)

Setting both the [`allow-scripts`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-scripts) and [`allow-same-origin`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin) keywords together when the embedded page has the [same origin](#165.html_same-origin) as the page containing the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) allows the embedded page to simply remove the [`sandbox`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute and then reload itself, effectively breaking out of the sandbox altogether.

These flags only take effect when the [nested browsing context](#165.html_nested-browsing-context) of the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) is [navigated](#165.html_navigate). Removing them, or removing the entire [`sandbox`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute, has no effect on an already-loaded page.

Potentially hostile files should not be served from the same server as the file containing the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element. Sandboxing hostile content is of minimal help if an attacker can convince the user to just visit the hostile content directly, rather than in the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element). To limit the damage that can be caused by hostile HTML content, it should be served from a separate dedicated domain. Using a different domain ensures that scripts in the files are unable to attack the site, even if the user is tricked into visiting those pages directly, without the protection of the [`sandbox`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute.

When an [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element with a [`sandbox`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute has its [nested browsing context](#165.html_nested-browsing-context) created (before the initial [`about:blank`](#165.html_about:blank) [`Document`](#165.html_document) is created), and when an [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element's [`sandbox`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute is set or changed while it has a [nested browsing context](#165.html_nested-browsing-context), the user agent must [parse the sandboxing directive](#165.html_parse-a-sandboxing-directive) using the attribute's value as the `input`, and the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element's [nested browsing context](#165.html_nested-browsing-context)'s [`iframe` sandboxing flag set](#165.html_iframe-sandboxing-flag-set) as the output.

When an [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element's [`sandbox`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute is removed while it has a [nested browsing context](#165.html_nested-browsing-context), the user agent must empty the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element's [nested browsing context](#165.html_nested-browsing-context)'s [`iframe` sandboxing flag set](#165.html_iframe-sandboxing-flag-set) as the output.

In this example, some completely-unknown, potentially hostile, user-provided HTML content is embedded in a page. Because it is served from a separate domain, it is affected by all the normal cross-site restrictions. In addition, the embedded page has scripting disabled, plugins disabled, forms disabled, and it cannot navigate any frames or windows other than itself (or any frames or windows it itself embeds).

```
<p>We're not scared of you! Here is your content, unedited:</p>
<iframe sandbox src="http://usercontent.example.net/getusercontent.cgi?id=12193"></iframe>
```

It is important to use a separate domain so that if the attacker convinces the user to visit that page directly, the page doesn't run in the context of the site's origin, which would make the user vulnerable to any attack found in the page.

In this example, a gadget from another site is embedded. The gadget has scripting and forms enabled, and the origin sandbox restrictions are lifted, allowing the gadget to communicate with its originating server. The sandbox is still useful, however, as it disables plugins and popups, thus reducing the risk of the user being exposed to malware and other annoyances.

```
<iframe sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-scripts"
        src="http://maps.example.com/embedded.html"></iframe>
```

Suppose a file A contained the following fragment:

```
<iframe sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-forms" src=B></iframe>
```

Suppose that file B contained an iframe also:

```
<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" src=C></iframe>
```

Further, suppose that file C contained a link:

```
<a href=D>Link</a>
```

For this example, suppose all the files were served as [`text/html`](#165.html_text/html).

Page C in this scenario has all the sandboxing flags set. Scripts are disabled, because the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) in A has scripts disabled, and this overrides the [`allow-scripts`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-scripts) keyword set on the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) in B. Forms are also disabled, because the inner [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) (in B) does not have the [`allow-forms`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-forms) keyword set.

Suppose now that a script in A removes all the [`sandbox`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox) attributes in A and B. This would change nothing immediately. If the user clicked the link in C, loading page D into the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) in B, page D would now act as if the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) in B had the [`allow-same-origin`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin) and [`allow-forms`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-forms) keywords set, because that was the state of the [nested browsing context](#165.html_nested-browsing-context) in the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) in A when page B was loaded.

Generally speaking, dynamically removing or changing the [`sandbox`](#165.html_attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute is ill-advised, because it can make it quite hard to reason about what will be allowed and what will not.

* * *

The [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element supports [dimension attributes](#165.html_dimension-attributes) for cases where the embedded content has specific dimensions (e.g. ad units have well-defined dimensions).

An [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element never has [fallback content](#165.html_fallback-content), as it will always create a nested [browsing context](#165.html_browsing-context), regardless of whether the specified initial contents are successfully used.

* * *

Descendants of [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) elements represent nothing. (In legacy user agents that do not support [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) elements, the contents would be parsed as markup that could act as fallback content.)

When used in [HTML documents](#165.html_html-documents), the allowed content model of [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) elements is text, except that invoking the [HTML fragment parsing algorithm](#165.html_html-fragment-parsing-algorithm) with the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element as the [`context`](#165.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element and the text contents as the `input` must result in a list of nodes that are all [phrasing content](#165.html_phrasing-content-1), with no [parse errors](#165.html_parse-error) having occurred, with no [`script`](#165.html_the-script-element) elements being anywhere in the list or as descendants of elements in the list, and with all the elements in the list (including their descendants) being themselves conforming.

The [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element must be empty in [XML documents](#165.html_xml-documents).

The [HTML parser](#165.html_html-parser) treats markup inside [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) elements as text.

* * *

The IDL attributes <dfn id="165.html_dom-iframe-src" data-anolis-xref="dom-iframe-src">`src`</dfn>, <dfn id="165.html_dom-iframe-srcdoc" data-anolis-xref="dom-iframe-srcdoc">`srcdoc`</dfn>, <dfn id="165.html_dom-iframe-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-iframe-name">`name`</dfn>, and <dfn id="165.html_dom-iframe-sandbox" data-anolis-xref="dom-iframe-sandbox">`sandbox`</dfn> must [reflect](#165.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

The <dfn id="165.html_dom-iframe-contentdocument" data-anolis-xref="dom-iframe-contentDocument">`contentDocument`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the [`Document`](#165.html_document) object of the [active document](#165.html_active-document) of the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element's [nested browsing context](#165.html_nested-browsing-context), if any and if its [effective script origin](#165.html_effective-script-origin) is the [same origin](#165.html_same-origin) as the [effective script origin](#165.html_effective-script-origin) specified by the [incumbent settings object](#165.html_incumbent-settings-object), or null otherwise.

The <dfn id="165.html_dom-iframe-contentwindow" data-anolis-xref="dom-iframe-contentWindow">`contentWindow`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the [`WindowProxy`](#165.html_windowproxy) object of the [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) element's [nested browsing context](#165.html_nested-browsing-context), if any, or null otherwise.

Here is an example of a page using an [`iframe`](#165.html_the-iframe-element) to include advertising from an advertising broker:

```
<iframe src="http://ads.example.com/?customerid=923513721&amp;format=banner"
        width="468" height="60"></iframe>
```

#### 4.7.3 The <dfn>`embed`</dfn> element

[Categories](#166.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#166.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#166.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Embedded content](#166.html_embedded-content-2).

[Interactive content](#166.html_interactive-content-0).

[Palpable content](#166.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#166.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [embedded content](#166.html_embedded-content-2) is expected.

[Content model](#166.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#166.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#166.html_global-attributes)

[`src`](#166.html_attr-embed-src) - Address of the resource

[`type`](#166.html_attr-embed-type) - Type of embedded resource

[`width`](#166.html_attr-dim-width) - Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#166.html_attr-dim-height)- Vertical dimension

Any other attribute that has no namespace (see prose).

Tag omission in text/html:

No [end tag](#166.html_syntax-end-tag)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#166.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`application`](#166.html_index-aria-application), [`document`](#166.html_index-aria-document) or [`img`](#166.html_index-aria-img) or [`presentation`](#166.html_index-aria-presentation).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#166.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#166.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#166.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLEmbedElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString src;
           attribute DOMString type;
           attribute DOMString width;
           attribute DOMString height;
  legacycaller any (any... arguments);
};
```

Depending on the type of content instantiated by the [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element, the node may also support other interfaces.

The [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element provides an integration point for an external (typically non-HTML) application or interactive content.

The <dfn id="166.html_attr-embed-src" data-anolis-xref="attr-embed-src">`src`</dfn> attribute gives the address of the resource being embedded. The attribute, if present, must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#166.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces).

The <dfn id="166.html_attr-embed-type" data-anolis-xref="attr-embed-type">`type`</dfn> attribute, if present, gives the [MIME type](#166.html_mime-type) by which the plugin to instantiate is selected. The value must be a [valid MIME type](#166.html_valid-mime-type). If both the [`type`](#166.html_attr-embed-type) attribute and the [`src`](#166.html_attr-embed-src) attribute are present, then the [`type`](#166.html_attr-embed-type) attribute must specify the same type as the [explicit Content-Type metadata](#166.html_content-type) of the resource given by the [`src`](#166.html_attr-embed-src) attribute.

When the element is created with neither a [`src`](#166.html_attr-embed-src) attribute nor a [`type`](#166.html_attr-embed-type) attribute, and when attributes are removed such that neither attribute is present on the element anymore, and when the element has a [media element](#166.html_media-element) ancestor, and when the element has an ancestor [`object`](#166.html_the-object-element) element that is *not* showing its [fallback content](#166.html_fallback-content), any [plugin](#166.html_plugin) instantiated for the element must be removed, and the [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element then represents nothing.

An [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element is said to be <dfn id="166.html_concept-embed-active" data-anolis-xref="concept-embed-active">potentially active</dfn> when the following conditions are all met simultaneously:

*   The element is [in a `Document`](#166.html_in-a-document) or was [in a `Document`](#166.html_in-a-document) the last time the [event loop](#166.html_event-loop) reached step 1.
*   The element's [`Document`](#166.html_document) is [fully active](#166.html_fully-active).
*   The element has either a [`src`](#166.html_attr-embed-src) attribute set or a [`type`](#166.html_attr-embed-type) attribute set (or both).
*   The element's [`src`](#166.html_attr-embed-src) attribute is either absent or its value is not the empty string.
*   The element is not a descendant of a [media element](#166.html_media-element).
*   The element is not a descendant of an [`object`](#166.html_the-object-element) element that is not showing its [fallback content](#166.html_fallback-content).
*   The element is [being rendered](#166.html_being-rendered), or was [being rendered](#166.html_being-rendered) the last time the [event loop](#166.html_event-loop) reached step 1.

Whenever an [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element that was not [potentially active](#166.html_concept-embed-active) becomes [potentially active](#166.html_concept-embed-active), and whenever a [potentially active](#166.html_concept-embed-active) [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element that is remaining [potentially active](#166.html_concept-embed-active) and has its [`src`](#166.html_attr-embed-type) attribute set, changed, or removed or its [`type`](#166.html_attr-embed-type) attribute set, changed, or removed, the user agent must [queue a task](#166.html_queue-a-task) using the <dfn id="166.html_embed-task-source">embed task source</dfn> to run [the `embed` element setup steps](#166.html_the-embed-element-setup-steps).

<dfn id="166.html_the-embed-element-setup-steps">The `embed` element setup steps</dfn> are as follows:

1.  If another [task](#166.html_concept-task) has since been queued to run [the `embed` element setup steps](#166.html_the-embed-element-setup-steps) for this element, then abort these steps.

2.  If the element has a [`src`](#166.html_attr-embed-src) attribute set

    The user agent must [resolve](#166.html_resolve-a-url) the value of the element's [`src`](#166.html_attr-embed-src) attribute, relative to the element. If that is successful, the user agent should [fetch](#166.html_fetch) the resulting [absolute URL](#166.html_absolute-url), from the element's [browsing context scope origin](#166.html_browsing-context-scope-origin) if it has one. The [task](#166.html_concept-task) that is [queued](#166.html_queue-a-task) by the [networking task source](#166.html_networking-task-source) once the resource has been [fetched](#166.html_fetch) must run the following steps:

    1.  If another [task](#166.html_concept-task) has since been queued to run [the `embed` element setup steps](#166.html_the-embed-element-setup-steps) for this element, then abort these steps.

    2.  Determine the <dfn id="166.html_concept-embed-type" data-anolis-xref="concept-embed-type">type of the content</dfn> being embedded, as follows (stopping at the first substep that determines the type):

        1.  If the element has a [`type`](#166.html_attr-embed-type) attribute, and that attribute's value is a type that a [plugin](#166.html_plugin) supports, then the value of the [`type`](#166.html_attr-embed-type) attribute is the [content's type](#166.html_concept-embed-type).

        2.  Otherwise, if applying the [URL parser](#166.html_url-parser-0) algorithm to the URL of the specified resource (after any redirects) results in a [parsed URL](#166.html_parsed-url) whose [path](#166.html_concept-url-path) component matches a pattern that a [plugin](#166.html_plugin) supports, then the [content's type](#166.html_concept-embed-type) is the type that that plugin can handle.

            For example, a plugin might say that it can handle resources with [path](#166.html_concept-url-path) components that end with the four character string "`.swf`".

        3.  Otherwise, if the specified resource has [explicit Content-Type metadata](#166.html_content-type), then that is the [content's type](#166.html_concept-embed-type).

        4.  Otherwise, the content has no [type](#166.html_concept-embed-type) and there can be no appropriate [plugin](#166.html_plugin) for it.

    3.  If the previous step determined that the [content's type](#166.html_concept-embed-type) is `image/svg+xml`, then run the following substeps:

        1.  If the [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element is not associated with a [nested browsing context](#166.html_nested-browsing-context), associate the element with a newly created [nested browsing context](#166.html_nested-browsing-context), and, if the element has a [`name`](#166.html_attr-embed-name) attribute, set the [browsing context name](#166.html_browsing-context-name) of the element's [nested browsing context](#166.html_nested-browsing-context) to the value of this attribute.

        2.  [Navigate](#166.html_navigate) the [nested browsing context](#166.html_nested-browsing-context) to the fetched resource, with [replacement enabled](#166.html_replacement-enabled), and with the [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element's document's [browsing context](#166.html_browsing-context) as the [source browsing context](#166.html_source-browsing-context). (The [`src`](#166.html_attr-embed-src) attribute of the [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element doesn't get updated if the browsing context gets further navigated to other locations.)

        3.  The [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element now [represents](#166.html_represents) its associated [nested browsing context](#166.html_nested-browsing-context).

    4.  Otherwise, find and instantiate an appropriate [plugin](#166.html_plugin) based on the [content's type](#166.html_concept-embed-type), and hand that [plugin](#166.html_plugin) the content of the resource, replacing any previously instantiated plugin for the element. The [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element now represents this [plugin](#166.html_plugin) instance.

    Whether the resource is fetched successfully or not (e.g. whether the response code was a 2xx code [or equivalent](#166.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes)) must be ignored when determining the [content's type](#166.html_concept-embed-type) and when handing the resource to the plugin.

    This allows servers to return data for plugins even with error responses (e.g. HTTP 500 Internal Server Error codes can still contain plugin data).

    Fetching the resource must [delay the load event](#166.html_delay-the-load-event) of the element's document.

    If the element has no [`src`](#166.html_attr-embed-src) attribute set

    The user agent should find and instantiate an appropriate [plugin](#166.html_plugin) based on the value of the [`type`](#166.html_attr-embed-type) attribute. The [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element now represents this [plugin](#166.html_plugin) instance.

The [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element has no [fallback content](#166.html_fallback-content). If the user agent can't find a suitable plugin when attempting to find and instantiate one for the algorithm above, then the user agent must use a default plugin. This default could be as simple as saying "Unsupported Format".

Whenever an [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element that was [potentially active](#166.html_concept-embed-active) stops being [potentially active](#166.html_concept-embed-active), any [plugin](#166.html_plugin) that had been instantiated for that element must be unloaded.

When a [plugin](#166.html_plugin) is to be instantiated but it cannot be [secured](#166.html_concept-plugin-secure) and the [sandboxed plugins browsing context flag](#166.html_sandboxed-plugins-browsing-context-flag) is set on the [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element's [`Document`](#166.html_document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#166.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set), then the user agent must not instantiate the [plugin](#166.html_plugin), and must instead render the [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element in a manner that conveys that the [plugin](#166.html_plugin) was disabled. The user agent may offer the user the option to override the sandbox and instantiate the [plugin](#166.html_plugin) anyway; if the user invokes such an option, the user agent must act as if the conditions above did not apply for the purposes of this element.

Plugins that cannot be [secured](#166.html_concept-plugin-secure) are disabled in sandboxed browsing contexts because they might not honor the restrictions imposed by the sandbox (e.g. they might allow scripting even when scripting in the sandbox is disabled). User agents should convey the danger of overriding the sandbox to the user if an option to do so is provided.

Any namespace-less attribute other than [`name`](#166.html_attr-embed-name), [`align`](#166.html_attr-embed-align), [`hspace`](#166.html_attr-embed-hspace), and [`vspace`](#166.html_attr-embed-vspace) may be specified on the [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element, so long as its name is [XML-compatible](#166.html_xml-compatible) and contains no [uppercase ASCII letters](#166.html_uppercase-ascii-letters). These attributes are then passed as parameters to the [plugin](#166.html_plugin).

All attributes in [HTML documents](#166.html_html-documents) get lowercased automatically, so the restriction on uppercase letters doesn't affect such documents.

The four exceptions are to exclude legacy attributes that have side-effects beyond just sending parameters to the [plugin](#166.html_plugin).

The user agent should pass the names and values of all the attributes of the [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element that have no namespace to the [plugin](#166.html_plugin) used, when one is instantiated.

The [`HTMLEmbedElement`](#166.html_htmlembedelement) object representing the element must expose the scriptable interface of the [plugin](#166.html_plugin) instantiated for the [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element, if any. At a minimum, this interface must implement the <dfn id="166.html_dom-embed-caller" data-anolis-xref="dom-embed-caller">legacy caller operation</dfn>. (It is suggested that the default behavior of this legacy caller operation, e.g. the behavior of the default plugin's legacy caller operation, be to throw a [`NotSupportedError`](#166.html_notsupportederror) exception.)

The [`embed`](#166.html_the-embed-element) element supports [dimension attributes](#166.html_dimension-attributes).

The IDL attributes <dfn id="166.html_dom-embed-src" data-anolis-xref="dom-embed-src">`src`</dfn> and <dfn id="166.html_dom-embed-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-embed-type">`type`</dfn> each must [reflect](#166.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

Here's a way to embed a resource that requires a proprietary plugin, like Flash:

```
<embed src="catgame.swf">
```

If the user does not have the plugin (for example if the plugin vendor doesn't support the user's platform), then the user will be unable to use the resource.

To pass the plugin a parameter "quality" with the value "high", an attribute can be specified:

```
<embed src="catgame.swf" quality="high">
```

This would be equivalent to the following, when using an [`object`](#166.html_the-object-element) element instead:

```
<object data="catgame.swf">
 <param name="quality" value="high">
</object>
```

#### 4.7.4 The <dfn>`object`</dfn> element

[Categories](#167.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#167.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#167.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Embedded content](#167.html_embedded-content-2).

If the element has a [`usemap`](#167.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap) attribute: [Interactive content](#167.html_interactive-content-0).

[Listed](#167.html_category-listed), [submittable](#167.html_category-submit), and [reassociateable](#167.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#167.html_form-associated-element).

[Palpable content](#167.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#167.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [embedded content](#167.html_embedded-content-2) is expected.

[Content model](#167.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Zero or more [`param`](#167.html_the-param-element) elements, then, [transparent](#167.html_transparent).

[Content attributes](#167.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#167.html_global-attributes)

[`data`](#167.html_attr-object-data) - Address of the resource

[`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) - Type of embedded resource

[`typemustmatch`](#167.html_attr-object-typemustmatch) - Whether the [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute and the [Content-Type](#167.html_content-type) value need to match for the resource to be used

[`name`](#167.html_attr-object-name) - Name of [nested browsing context](#167.html_nested-browsing-context)

[`usemap`](#167.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap) - Name of [image map](#167.html_image-map) to use

[`form`](#167.html_attr-fae-form) - Associates the control with a [`form`](#167.html_the-form-element) element

[`width`](#167.html_attr-dim-width) - Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#167.html_attr-dim-height) - Vertical dimension

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#167.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`application`](#167.html_index-aria-application), [`document`](#167.html_index-aria-document) or [`img`](#167.html_index-aria-img) or [`presentation`](#167.html_index-aria-presentation).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#167.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#167.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#167.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#167.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLObjectElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString data;
           attribute DOMString type;
           attribute boolean typeMustMatch;
           attribute DOMString name;
           attribute DOMString useMap;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
           attribute DOMString width;
           attribute DOMString height;
  readonly attribute Document? contentDocument;
  readonly attribute WindowProxy? contentWindow;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  void setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  legacycaller any (any... arguments);
};
```

Depending on the type of content instantiated by the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element, the node also supports other interfaces.

The [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element can represent an external resource, which, depending on the type of the resource, will either be treated as an image, as a [nested browsing context](#167.html_nested-browsing-context), or as an external resource to be processed by a [plugin](#167.html_plugin).

The <dfn id="167.html_attr-object-data" data-anolis-xref="attr-object-data">`data`</dfn> attribute, if present, specifies the address of the resource. If present, the attribute must be a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#167.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces).

Authors who reference resources from other [origins](#167.html_origin-0) that they do not trust are urged to use the [`typemustmatch`](#167.html_attr-object-typemustmatch) attribute defined below. Without that attribute, it is possible in certain cases for an attacker on the remote host to use the plugin mechanism to run arbitrary scripts, even if the author has used features such as the Flash "allowScriptAccess" parameter.

The <dfn id="167.html_attr-object-type" data-anolis-xref="attr-object-type">`type`</dfn> attribute, if present, specifies the type of the resource. If present, the attribute must be a [valid MIME type](#167.html_valid-mime-type).

At least one of either the [`data`](#167.html_attr-object-data) attribute or the [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute must be present.

The <dfn id="167.html_attr-object-typemustmatch" data-anolis-xref="attr-object-typemustmatch">`typemustmatch`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#167.html_boolean-attribute) whose presence indicates that the resource specified by the [`data`](#167.html_attr-object-data) attribute is only to be used if the value of the [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute and the [Content-Type](#167.html_content-type) of the aforementioned resource match.

The [`typemustmatch`](#167.html_attr-object-typemustmatch) attribute must not be specified unless both the [`data`](#167.html_attr-object-data) attribute and the [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute are present.

The <dfn id="167.html_attr-object-name" data-anolis-xref="attr-object-name">`name`</dfn> attribute, if present, must be a [valid browsing context name](#167.html_valid-browsing-context-name). The given value is used to name the [nested browsing context](#167.html_nested-browsing-context), if applicable.

Whenever one of the following conditions occur:

*   the element is created,
*   the element is popped off the [stack of open elements](#167.html_stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#167.html_html-parser) or [XML parser](#167.html_xml-parser),
*   the element is not on the [stack of open elements](#167.html_stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#167.html_html-parser) or [XML parser](#167.html_xml-parser), and it is either [inserted into a document](#167.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document) or [removed from a document](#167.html_remove-an-element-from-a-document),
*   the element's [`Document`](#167.html_document) changes whether it is [fully active](#167.html_fully-active),
*   one of the element's ancestor [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) elements changes to or from showing its [fallback content](#167.html_fallback-content),
*   the element's [`classid`](#167.html_attr-object-classid) attribute is set, changed, or removed,
*   the element's [`classid`](#167.html_attr-object-classid) attribute is not present, and its [`data`](#167.html_attr-object-data) attribute is set, changed, or removed,
*   neither the element's [`classid`](#167.html_attr-object-classid) attribute nor its [`data`](#167.html_attr-object-data) attribute are present, and its [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute is set, changed, or removed,
*   the element changes from [being rendered](#167.html_being-rendered) to not being rendered, or vice versa,

...the user agent must [queue a task](#167.html_queue-a-task) to run the following steps to (re)determine what the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element represents. The [task source](#167.html_task-source) for this [task](#167.html_concept-task) is the [DOM manipulation task source](#167.html_dom-manipulation-task-source). This [task](#167.html_concept-task) being [queued](#167.html_queue-a-task) or actively running must [delay the load event](#167.html_delay-the-load-event) of the element's document.

1.  If the user has indicated a preference that this [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element's [fallback content](#167.html_fallback-content) be shown instead of the element's usual behavior, then jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

    For example, a user could ask for the element's [fallback content](#167.html_fallback-content) to be shown because that content uses a format that the user finds more accessible.

2.  If the element has an ancestor [media element](#167.html_media-element), or has an ancestor [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element that is *not* showing its [fallback content](#167.html_fallback-content), or if the element is not [in a `Document`](#167.html_in-a-document) with a [browsing context](#167.html_browsing-context), or if the element's [`Document`](#167.html_document) is not [fully active](#167.html_fully-active), or if the element is still in the [stack of open elements](#167.html_stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#167.html_html-parser) or [XML parser](#167.html_xml-parser), or if the element is not [being rendered](#167.html_being-rendered), then jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

3.  If the [`classid`](#167.html_attr-object-classid) attribute is present, and has a value that isn't the empty string, then: if the user agent can find a [plugin](#167.html_plugin) suitable according to the value of the [`classid`](#167.html_attr-object-classid) attribute, and either [plugins aren't being sandboxed](#167.html_sandboxPluginObject) or that [plugin](#167.html_plugin) can be [secured](#167.html_concept-plugin-secure), then that [plugin](#167.html_plugin) [should be used](#167.html_object-plugin), and the value of the [`data`](#167.html_attr-object-data) attribute, if any, should be passed to the [plugin](#167.html_plugin). If no suitable [plugin](#167.html_plugin) can be found, or if the [plugin](#167.html_plugin) reports an error, jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

4.  If the [`data`](#167.html_attr-object-data) attribute is present and its value is not the empty string, then:

    1.  If the [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute is present and its value is not a type that the user agent supports, and is not a type that the user agent can find a [plugin](#167.html_plugin) for, then the user agent may jump to the step below labeled *fallback* without fetching the content to examine its real type.

    2.  [Resolve](#167.html_resolve-a-url) the URL specified by the [`data`](#167.html_attr-object-data) attribute, relative to the element.

    3.  If that failed, [fire a simple event](#167.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `error` at the element, then jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

    4.  [Fetch](#167.html_fetch) the resulting [absolute URL](#167.html_absolute-url), from the element's [browsing context scope origin](#167.html_browsing-context-scope-origin) if it has one.

        Fetching the resource must [delay the load event](#167.html_delay-the-load-event) of the element's document until the [task](#167.html_concept-task) that is [queued](#167.html_queue-a-task) by the [networking task source](#167.html_networking-task-source) once the resource has been [fetched](#167.html_fetch) (defined next) has been run.

        For the purposes of the [application cache](#167.html_application-cache) networking model, this [fetch](#167.html_fetch) operation is not for a [child browsing context](#167.html_child-browsing-context) (though it might end up being used for one after all, as defined below).

    5.  If the resource is not yet available (e.g. because the resource was not available in the cache, so that loading the resource required making a request over the network), then jump to the step below labeled *fallback*. The [task](#167.html_concept-task) that is [queued](#167.html_queue-a-task) by the [networking task source](#167.html_networking-task-source) once the resource is available must restart this algorithm from this step. Resources can load incrementally; user agents may opt to consider a resource "available" whenever enough data has been obtained to begin processing the resource.

    6.  If the load failed (e.g. there was an HTTP 404 error, there was a DNS error), [fire a simple event](#167.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `error` at the element, then jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

    7.  Determine the `resource type`, as follows:

        1.  Let the `resource type` be unknown.

        2.  If the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element has a [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute and a [`typemustmatch`](#167.html_attr-object-typemustmatch) attribute, and the resource has [associated Content-Type metadata](#167.html_content-type), and the type specified in [the resource's Content-Type metadata](#167.html_content-type) is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#167.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the value of the element's [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute, then let `resource type` be that type and jump to the step below labeled *handler*.

        3.  If the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element has a [`typemustmatch`](#167.html_attr-object-typemustmatch) attribute, jump to the step below labeled *handler*.

        4.  If the user agent is configured to strictly obey Content-Type headers for this resource, and the resource has [associated Content-Type metadata](#167.html_content-type), then let the `resource type` be the type specified in [the resource's Content-Type metadata](#167.html_content-type), and jump to the step below labeled *handler*.

            This can introduce a vulnerability, wherein a site is trying to embed a resource that uses a particular plugin, but the remote site overrides that and instead furnishes the user agent with a resource that triggers a different plugin with different security characteristics.

        5.  If there is a [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute present on the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element, and that attribute's value is not a type that the user agent supports, but it *is* a type that a [plugin](#167.html_plugin) supports, then let the `resource type` be the type specified in that [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute, and jump to the step below labeled *handler*.

        6.  Run the appropriate set of steps from the following list:

            If the resource has [associated Content-Type metadata](#167.html_content-type)

            1.  Let `binary` be false.

            2.  If the type specified in [the resource's Content-Type metadata](#167.html_content-type) is "`text/plain`", and the result of applying the [rules for distinguishing if a resource is text or binary](#167.html_content-type-sniffing:-text-or-binary) to the resource is that the resource is not `text/plain`, then set `binary` to true.

            3.  If the type specified in [the resource's Content-Type metadata](#167.html_content-type) is "`application/octet-stream`", then set `binary` to true.

            4.  If `binary` is false, then let the `resource type` be the type specified in [the resource's Content-Type metadata](#167.html_content-type), and jump to the step below labeled *handler*.

            5.  If there is a [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute present on the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element, and its value is not `application/octet-stream`, then run the following steps:

                1.  If the attribute's value is a type that a [plugin](#167.html_plugin) supports, or the attribute's value is a type that starts with "`image/`" that is not also an [XML MIME type](#167.html_xml-mime-type), then let the `resource type` be the type specified in that [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute.

                2.  Jump to the step below labeled *handler*.

            Otherwise, if the resource does not have [associated Content-Type metadata](#167.html_content-type)

            1.  If there is a [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute present on the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element, then let the `tentative type` be the type specified in that [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute.

                Otherwise, let `tentative type` be the [sniffed type of the resource](#167.html_content-type-sniffing-0).

            2.  If `tentative type` is *not* `application/octet-stream`, then let `resource type` be `tentative type` and jump to the step below labeled *handler*.

        7.  If applying the [URL parser](#167.html_url-parser-0) algorithm to the URL of the specified resource (after any redirects) results in a [parsed URL](#167.html_parsed-url) whose [path](#167.html_concept-url-path) component matches a pattern that a [plugin](#167.html_plugin) supports, then let `resource type` be the type that that plugin can handle.

            For example, a plugin might say that it can handle resources with [path](#167.html_concept-url-path) components that end with the four character string "`.swf`".

        It is possible for this step to finish, or for one of the substeps above to jump straight to the next step, with `resource type` still being unknown. In both cases, the next step will trigger fallback.

    8.  *Handler*: Handle the content as given by the first of the following cases that matches:

        If the `resource type` is not a type that the user agent supports, but it *is* a type that a [plugin](#167.html_plugin) supports

        If [plugins are being sandboxed](#167.html_sandboxPluginObject) and the plugin that supports `resource type` cannot be [secured](#167.html_concept-plugin-secure), jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

        Otherwise, the user agent should [use the plugin that supports `resource type`](#167.html_object-plugin) and pass the content of the resource to that [plugin](#167.html_plugin). If the [plugin](#167.html_plugin) reports an error, then jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

        If the `resource type` is an [XML MIME type](#167.html_xml-mime-type), or if the `resource type` does not start with "`image/`"

        The [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element must be associated with a newly created [nested browsing context](#167.html_nested-browsing-context), if it does not already have one.

        If the URL of the given resource is not [`about:blank`](#167.html_about:blank), the element's [nested browsing context](#167.html_nested-browsing-context) must then be [navigated](#167.html_navigate) to that resource, with [replacement enabled](#167.html_replacement-enabled), and with the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element's document's [browsing context](#167.html_browsing-context) as the [source browsing context](#167.html_source-browsing-context). (The [`data`](#167.html_attr-object-data) attribute of the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element doesn't get updated if the browsing context gets further navigated to other locations.)

        If the URL of the given resource *is* [`about:blank`](#167.html_about:blank), then, instead, the user agent must [queue a task](#167.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#167.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `load` at the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element. No `load` event is fired at the [`about:blank`](#167.html_about:blank) document itself.

        The [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element [represents](#167.html_represents) the [nested browsing context](#167.html_nested-browsing-context).

        If the [`name`](#167.html_attr-object-name) attribute is present, the [browsing context name](#167.html_browsing-context-name) must be set to the value of this attribute; otherwise, the [browsing context name](#167.html_browsing-context-name) must be set to the empty string.

        In certain situations, e.g. if the resource was [fetched](#167.html_fetch) from an [application cache](#167.html_application-cache) but it is an HTML file with a [`manifest`](#167.html_attr-html-manifest) attribute that points to a different [application cache manifest](#167.html_concept-appcache-manifest), the [navigation](#167.html_navigate) of the [browsing context](#167.html_browsing-context) will be restarted so as to load the resource afresh from the network or a different [application cache](#167.html_application-cache). Even if the resource is then found to have a different type, it is still used as part of a [nested browsing context](#167.html_nested-browsing-context): only the [navigate](#167.html_navigate) algorithm is restarted, not this [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) algorithm.

        If the `resource type` starts with "`image/`", and support for images has not been disabled

        Apply the [image sniffing](#167.html_content-type-sniffing:-image) rules to determine the type of the image.

        The [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element [represents](#167.html_represents) the specified image. The image is not a [nested browsing context](#167.html_nested-browsing-context).

        If the image cannot be rendered, e.g. because it is malformed or in an unsupported format, jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

        Otherwise

        The given `resource type` is not supported. Jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

        If the previous step ended with the `resource type` being unknown, this is the case that is triggered.

    9.  The element's contents are not part of what the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element represents.

    10.  Once the resource is completely loaded, [queue a task](#167.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#167.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `load` at the element.

        The [task source](#167.html_task-source) for this task is the [DOM manipulation task source](#167.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

5.  If the [`data`](#167.html_attr-object-data) attribute is absent but the [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute is present, and the user agent can find a [plugin](#167.html_plugin) suitable according to the value of the [`type`](#167.html_attr-object-type) attribute, and either [plugins aren't being sandboxed](#167.html_sandboxPluginObject) or the [plugin](#167.html_plugin) can be [secured](#167.html_concept-plugin-secure), then that [plugin](#167.html_plugin) [should be used](#167.html_object-plugin). If these conditions cannot be met, or if the [plugin](#167.html_plugin) reports an error, jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

6.  *Fallback*: The [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element [represents](#167.html_represents) the element's children, ignoring any leading [`param`](#167.html_the-param-element) element children. This is the element's [fallback content](#167.html_fallback-content). If the element has an instantiated [plugin](#167.html_plugin), then unload it.

When the algorithm above instantiates a [plugin](#167.html_plugin), the user agent should pass to the [plugin](#167.html_plugin) used the names and values of all the attributes on the element, in the order they were added to the element, with the attributes added by the parser being ordered in source order, followed by a parameter named "PARAM" whose value is null, followed by all the names and values of [parameters](#167.html_concept-param-parameter) given by [`param`](#167.html_the-param-element) elements that are children of the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element, in [tree order](#167.html_tree-order). If the [plugin](#167.html_plugin) supports a scriptable interface, the [`HTMLObjectElement`](#167.html_htmlobjectelement) object representing the element should expose that interface. The [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element [represents](#167.html_represents) the [plugin](#167.html_plugin). The [plugin](#167.html_plugin) is not a nested [browsing context](#167.html_browsing-context).

Plugins are considered sandboxed for the purpose of an [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element if the [sandboxed plugins browsing context flag](#167.html_sandboxed-plugins-browsing-context-flag) is set on the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element's [`Document`](#167.html_document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#167.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set).

Due to the algorithm above, the contents of [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) elements act as [fallback content](#167.html_fallback-content), used only when referenced resources can't be shown (e.g. because it returned a 404 error). This allows multiple [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) elements to be nested inside each other, targeting multiple user agents with different capabilities, with the user agent picking the first one it supports.

Whenever the [`name`](#167.html_attr-object-name) attribute is set, if the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element has a nested [browsing context](#167.html_browsing-context), its [name](#167.html_browsing-context-name) must be changed to the new value. If the attribute is removed, if the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element has a [browsing context](#167.html_browsing-context), the [browsing context name](#167.html_browsing-context-name) must be set to the empty string.

The [`usemap`](#167.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap) attribute, if present while the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element represents an image, can indicate that the object has an associated [image map](#167.html_image-map). The attribute must be ignored if the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element doesn't represent an image.

The [`form`](#167.html_attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element with its [form owner](#167.html_form-owner).

**Constraint validation**: [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) elements are always [barred from constraint validation](#167.html_barred-from-constraint-validation).

The [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element supports [dimension attributes](#167.html_dimension-attributes).

The IDL attributes <dfn id="167.html_dom-object-data" data-anolis-xref="dom-object-data">`data`</dfn>, <dfn id="167.html_dom-object-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-object-type">`type`</dfn> and <dfn id="167.html_dom-object-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-object-name">`name`</dfn> each must [reflect](#167.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name. The <dfn id="167.html_dom-object-typemustmatch" data-anolis-xref="dom-object-typeMustMatch">`typeMustMatch`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#167.html_reflect) the [`typemustmatch`](#167.html_attr-object-typemustmatch) content attribute. The <dfn id="167.html_dom-object-usemap" data-anolis-xref="dom-object-useMap">`useMap`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#167.html_reflect) the [`usemap`](#167.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap) content attribute.

The <dfn id="167.html_dom-object-contentdocument" data-anolis-xref="dom-object-contentDocument">`contentDocument`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the [`Document`](#167.html_document) object of the [active document](#167.html_active-document) of the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element's [nested browsing context](#167.html_nested-browsing-context), if any and if its [effective script origin](#167.html_effective-script-origin) is the [same origin](#167.html_same-origin) as the [effective script origin](#167.html_effective-script-origin) specified by the [incumbent settings object](#167.html_incumbent-settings-object), or null otherwise.

The <dfn id="167.html_dom-object-contentwindow" data-anolis-xref="dom-object-contentWindow">`contentWindow`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the [`WindowProxy`](#167.html_windowproxy) object of the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element's [nested browsing context](#167.html_nested-browsing-context), if it has one; otherwise, it must return null.

The [`willValidate`](#167.html_dom-cva-willvalidate), [`validity`](#167.html_dom-cva-validity), and [`validationMessage`](#167.html_dom-cva-validationmessage) attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#167.html_dom-cva-checkvalidity), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#167.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#167.html_the-constraint-validation-api). The [`form`](#167.html_dom-fae-form) IDL attribute is part of the element's forms API.

All [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) elements have a <dfn id="167.html_dom-object-caller" data-anolis-xref="dom-object-caller">legacy caller operation</dfn>. If the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element has an instantiated [plugin](#167.html_plugin) that supports a scriptable interface that defines a legacy caller operation, then that must be the behavior of the object's legacy caller operation. Otherwise, the object's legacy caller operation must be to throw a [`NotSupportedError`](#167.html_notsupportederror) exception.

In the following example, a Java applet is embedded in a page using the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element. (Generally speaking, it is better to avoid using applets like these and instead use native JavaScript and HTML to provide the functionality, since that way the application will work on all Web browsers without requiring a third-party plugin. Many devices, especially embedded devices, do not support third-party technologies like Java.)

```
<figure>
 <object type="application/x-java-applet">
  <param name="code" value="MyJavaClass">
  <p>You do not have Java available, or it is disabled.</p>
 </object>
 <figcaption>My Java Clock</figcaption>
</figure>
```

In this example, an HTML page is embedded in another using the [`object`](#167.html_the-object-element) element.

```
<figure>
 <object data="clock.html"></object>
 <figcaption>My HTML Clock</figcaption>
</figure>
```

The following example shows how a plugin can be used in HTML (in this case the Flash plugin, to show a video file). Fallback is provided for users who do not have Flash enabled, in this case using the [`video`](#167.html_the-video-element) element to show the video for those using user agents that support [`video`](#167.html_the-video-element), and finally providing a link to the video for those who have neither Flash nor a [`video`](#167.html_the-video-element)-capable browser.

```
<p>Look at my video:
 <object type="application/x-shockwave-flash">
  <param name=movie value="http://video.example.com/library/watch.swf">
  <param name=allowfullscreen value=true>
  <param name=flashvars value="http://video.example.com/vids/315981">
  <video controls src="http://video.example.com/vids/315981">
   <a href="http://video.example.com/vids/315981">View video</a>.
  </video>
 </object>
</p>
```

#### 4.7.5 The <dfn>`param`</dfn> element

[Categories](#168.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#168.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As a child of an [`object`](#168.html_the-object-element) element, before any [flow content](#168.html_flow-content-1).

[Content model](#168.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#168.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#168.html_global-attributes)

[`name`](#168.html_attr-param-name) - Name of parameter

[`value`](#168.html_attr-param-value) - Value of parameter

Tag omission in text/html:

No [end tag](#168.html_syntax-end-tag)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#168.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#168.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#168.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#168.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLParamElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString name;
           attribute DOMString value;
};
```

The [`param`](#168.html_the-param-element) element defines parameters for plugins invoked by [`object`](#168.html_the-object-element) elements. It does not [represent](#168.html_represents) anything on its own.

The <dfn id="168.html_attr-param-name" data-anolis-xref="attr-param-name">`name`</dfn> attribute gives the name of the parameter.

The <dfn id="168.html_attr-param-value" data-anolis-xref="attr-param-value">`value`</dfn> attribute gives the value of the parameter.

Both attributes must be present. They may have any value.

If both attributes are present, and if the parent element of the [`param`](#168.html_the-param-element) is an [`object`](#168.html_the-object-element) element, then the element defines a <dfn id="168.html_concept-param-parameter" data-anolis-xref="concept-param-parameter">parameter</dfn> with the given name-value pair.

If either the name or value of a [parameter](#168.html_concept-param-parameter) defined by a [`param`](#168.html_the-param-element) element that is the child of an [`object`](#168.html_the-object-element) element that [represents](#168.html_represents) an instantiated [plugin](#168.html_plugin) changes, and if that [plugin](#168.html_plugin) is communicating with the user agent using an API that features the ability to update the [plugin](#168.html_plugin) when the name or value of a [parameter](#168.html_concept-param-parameter) so changes, then the user agent must appropriately exercise that ability to notify the [plugin](#168.html_plugin) of the change.

The IDL attributes <dfn id="168.html_dom-param-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-param-name">`name`</dfn> and <dfn id="168.html_dom-param-value" data-anolis-xref="dom-param-value">`value`</dfn> must both [reflect](#168.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

The following example shows how the [`param`](#168.html_the-param-element) element can be used to pass a parameter to a plugin, in this case the O3D plugin.

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
   <title>O3D Utah Teapot</title>
  </head>
  <body>
   <p>
    <object type="application/vnd.o3d.auto">
     <param name="o3d_features" value="FloatingPointTextures">
     <img src="o3d-teapot.png"
          title="3D Utah Teapot illustration rendered using O3D."
          alt="When O3D renders the Utah Teapot, it appears as a squat
          teapot with a shiny metallic finish on which the
          surroundings are reflected, with a faint shadow caused by
          the lighting.">
     <p>To see the teapot actually rendered by O3D on your
     computer, please download and install the <a
     href="http://code.google.com/apis/o3d/docs/gettingstarted.html#install">O3D plugin</a>.</p>
    </object>
    <script src="o3d-teapot.js"></script>
   </p>
  </body>
</html>
```

#### 4.7.6 The <dfn id="169.html_video">`video`</dfn> element

[Categories](#169.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#169.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#169.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Embedded content](#169.html_embedded-content-2).

If the element has a [`controls`](#169.html_attr-media-controls) attribute: [Interactive content](#169.html_interactive-content-0).

[Palpable content](#169.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#169.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [embedded content](#169.html_embedded-content-2) is expected.

[Content model](#169.html_element-dfn-content-model):

If the element has a [`src`](#169.html_attr-media-src) attribute: zero or more [`track`](#169.html_the-track-element) elements, then [transparent](#169.html_transparent), but with no [media element](#169.html_media-element) descendants.

If the element does not have a [`src`](#169.html_attr-media-src) attribute: zero or more [`source`](#169.html_the-source-element) elements, then zero or more [`track`](#169.html_the-track-element) elements, then [transparent](#169.html_transparent), but with no [media element](#169.html_media-element) descendants.

[Content attributes](#169.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#169.html_global-attributes)

[`src`](#169.html_attr-media-src) - Address of the resource

[`crossorigin`](#169.html_attr-media-crossorigin) - How the element handles crossorigin requests

[`poster`](#169.html_attr-video-poster) - Poster frame to show prior to video playback

[`preload`](#169.html_attr-media-preload) - Hints how much buffering the [media resource](#169.html_media-resource) will likely need

[`autoplay`](#169.html_attr-media-autoplay) - Hint that the [media resource](#169.html_media-resource) can be started automatically when the page is loaded

[`mediagroup`](#169.html_attr-media-mediagroup) - Groups [media elements](#169.html_media-element) together with an implicit [`MediaController`](#169.html_mediacontroller)

[`loop`](#169.html_attr-media-loop) - Whether to loop the [media resource](#169.html_media-resource)

[`muted`](#169.html_attr-media-muted) - Whether to mute the [media resource](#169.html_media-resource) by default

[`controls`](#169.html_attr-media-controls) - Show user agent controls

[`width`](#169.html_attr-dim-width) - Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#169.html_attr-dim-height) - Vertical dimension

Tag omission in text/html

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#169.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`application`](#169.html_index-aria-application).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#169.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#169.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#169.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#169.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLVideoElement : HTMLMediaElement {
           attribute unsigned long width;
           attribute unsigned long height;
  readonly attribute unsigned long videoWidth;
  readonly attribute unsigned long videoHeight;
           attribute DOMString poster;
};
```

A [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element is used for playing videos or movies, and audio files with captions.

Content may be provided inside the [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element. User agents should not show this content to the user; it is intended for older Web browsers which do not support [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element), so that legacy video plugins can be tried, or to show text to the users of these older browsers informing them of how to access the video contents.

In particular, this content is not intended to address accessibility concerns. To make video content accessible to the partially sighted, the blind, the hard-of-hearing, the deaf, and those with other physical or cognitive disabilities, a variety of features are available. Captions can be provided, either embedded in the video stream or as external files using the [`track`](#169.html_the-track-element) element. Sign-language tracks can be provided, again either embedded in the video stream or by synchronizing multiple [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) elements using the [`mediagroup`](#169.html_attr-media-mediagroup) attribute or a [`MediaController`](#169.html_mediacontroller) object. Audio descriptions can be provided, either as a separate track embedded in the video stream, or a separate audio track in an [`audio`](#169.html_the-audio-element) element [slaved](#169.html_slaved-media-elements) to the same controller as the [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element(s), or in text form using a [WebVTT file](#169.html_webvtt-file) referenced using the [`track`](#169.html_the-track-element) element and synthesized into speech by the user agent. WebVTT can also be used to provide chapter titles. For users who would rather not use a media element at all, transcripts or other textual alternatives can be provided by simply linking to them in the prose near the [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element. [[WEBVTT]](#169.html_refsWEBVTT)

The [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element is a [media element](#169.html_media-element) whose [media data](#169.html_media-data) is ostensibly video data, possibly with associated audio data.

The [`src`](#169.html_attr-media-src), [`preload`](#169.html_attr-media-preload), [`autoplay`](#169.html_attr-media-autoplay), [`mediagroup`](#169.html_attr-media-mediagroup), [`loop`](#169.html_attr-media-loop), [`muted`](#169.html_attr-media-muted), and [`controls`](#169.html_attr-media-controls) attributes are [the attributes common to all media elements](#169.html_media-element-attributes).

The <dfn id="169.html_attr-video-poster" data-anolis-xref="attr-video-poster">`poster`</dfn> attribute gives the address of an image file that the user agent can show while no video data is available. The attribute, if present, must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#169.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces).

If the specified resource is to be used, then, when the element is created or when the [`poster`](#169.html_attr-video-poster) attribute is set, changed, or removed, the user agent must run the following steps to determine the element's <dfn id="169.html_poster-frame">poster frame</dfn> (regardless of the value of the element's [show poster flag](#169.html_show-poster-flag)):

1.  If there is an existing instance of this algorithm running for this [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element, abort that instance of this algorithm without changing the [poster frame](#169.html_poster-frame).

2.  If the [`poster`](#169.html_attr-video-poster) attribute's value is the empty string or if the attribute is absent, then there is no [poster frame](#169.html_poster-frame); abort these steps.

3.  [Resolve](#169.html_resolve-a-url) the [`poster`](#169.html_attr-video-poster) attribute's value relative to the element. If this fails, then there is no [poster frame](#169.html_poster-frame); abort these steps.

4.  [Fetch](#169.html_fetch) the resulting [absolute URL](#169.html_absolute-url), from the element's [`Document`](#169.html_document)'s [origin](#169.html_origin-0). This must [delay the load event](#169.html_delay-the-load-event) of the element's document.

5.  If an image is thus obtained, the [poster frame](#169.html_poster-frame) is that image. Otherwise, there is no [poster frame](#169.html_poster-frame).

The image given by the [`poster`](#169.html_attr-video-poster) attribute, the *[poster frame](#169.html_poster-frame)*, is intended to be a representative frame of the video (typically one of the first non-blank frames) that gives the user an idea of what the video is like.

* * *

A [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element represents what is given for the first matching condition in the list below:

When no video data is available (the element's [`readyState`](#169.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute is either [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#169.html_dom-media-have_nothing), or [`HAVE_METADATA`](#169.html_dom-media-have_metadata) but no video data has yet been obtained at all, or the element's [`readyState`](#169.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute is any subsequent value but the [media resource](#169.html_media-resource) does not have a video channel)

The [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element [represents](#169.html_represents) its [poster frame](#169.html_poster-frame), if any, or else transparent black with no intrinsic dimensions.

When the [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element is [paused](#169.html_dom-media-paused), the [current playback position](#169.html_current-playback-position) is the first frame of video, and the element's [show poster flag](#169.html_show-poster-flag) is set

The [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element [represents](#169.html_represents) its [poster frame](#169.html_poster-frame), if any, or else the first frame of the video.

When the [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element is [paused](#169.html_dom-media-paused), and the frame of video corresponding to the [current playback position](#169.html_current-playback-position) is not available (e.g. because the video is seeking or buffering)
When the [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element is neither [potentially playing](#169.html_potentially-playing) nor [paused](#169.html_dom-media-paused) (e.g. when seeking or stalled)

The [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element [represents](#169.html_represents) the last frame of the video to have been rendered.

When the [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element is [paused](#169.html_dom-media-paused)

The [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element [represents](#169.html_represents) the frame of video corresponding to the [current playback position](#169.html_current-playback-position).

Otherwise (the [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element has a video channel and is [potentially playing](#169.html_potentially-playing))

The [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element [represents](#169.html_represents) the frame of video at the continuously increasing ["current" position](#169.html_current-playback-position). When the [current playback position](#169.html_current-playback-position) changes such that the last frame rendered is no longer the frame corresponding to the [current playback position](#169.html_current-playback-position) in the video, the new frame must be rendered.

Which frame in a video stream corresponds to a particular playback position is defined by the video stream's format.

The [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element also [represents](#169.html_represents) any [text track cues](#169.html_text-track-cue) whose [text track cue active flag](#169.html_text-track-cue-active-flag) is set and whose [text track](#169.html_text-track) is in the [showing](#169.html_text-track-showing) mode, and any audio from the [media resource](#169.html_media-resource), at the [current playback position](#169.html_current-playback-position).

Any audio associated with the [media resource](#169.html_media-resource) must, if played, be played synchronized with the [current playback position](#169.html_current-playback-position), at the element's [effective media volume](#169.html_effective-media-volume).

In addition to the above, the user agent may provide messages to the user (such as "buffering", "no video loaded", "error", or more detailed information) by overlaying text or icons on the video or other areas of the element's playback area, or in another appropriate manner.

User agents that cannot render the video may instead make the element [represent](#169.html_represents) a link to an external video playback utility or to the video data itself.

When a [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element's [media resource](#169.html_media-resource) has a video channel, the element [provides a paint source](#169.html_provides-a-paint-source) whose width is the [media resource](#169.html_media-resource)'s [intrinsic width](#169.html_concept-video-intrinsic-width), whose height is the [media resource](#169.html_media-resource)'s [intrinsic height](#169.html_concept-video-intrinsic-height), and whose appearance is the frame of video corresponding to the [current playback position](#169.html_current-playback-position), if that is available, or else (e.g. when the video is seeking or buffering) its previous appearance, if any, or else (e.g. because the video is still loading the first frame) blackness.

* * *

`video` . [`videoWidth`](#169.html_dom-video-videowidth)
`video` . [`videoHeight`](#169.html_dom-video-videoheight)

These attributes return the intrinsic dimensions of the video, or zero if the dimensions are not known.

The <dfn id="169.html_concept-video-intrinsic-width" data-anolis-xref="concept-video-intrinsic-width">intrinsic width</dfn> and <dfn id="169.html_concept-video-intrinsic-height" data-anolis-xref="concept-video-intrinsic-height">intrinsic height</dfn> of the [media resource](#169.html_media-resource) are the dimensions of the resource in CSS pixels after taking into account the resource's dimensions, aspect ratio, clean aperture, resolution, and so forth, as defined for the format used by the resource. If an anamorphic format does not define how to apply the aspect ratio to the video data's dimensions to obtain the "correct" dimensions, then the user agent must apply the ratio by increasing one dimension and leaving the other unchanged.

The <dfn id="169.html_dom-video-videowidth" data-anolis-xref="dom-video-videoWidth">`videoWidth`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the [intrinsic width](#169.html_concept-video-intrinsic-width) of the video in CSS pixels. The <dfn id="169.html_dom-video-videoheight" data-anolis-xref="dom-video-videoHeight">`videoHeight`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the [intrinsic height](#169.html_concept-video-intrinsic-height) of the video in CSS pixels. If the element's [`readyState`](#169.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute is [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#169.html_dom-media-have_nothing), then the attributes must return 0.

Whenever the [intrinsic width](#169.html_concept-video-intrinsic-width) or [intrinsic height](#169.html_concept-video-intrinsic-height) of the video changes (including, for example, because the [selected video track](#169.html_dom-videotrack-selected) was changed), if the element's [`readyState`](#169.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute is not [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#169.html_dom-media-have_nothing), the user agent must [queue a task](#169.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#169.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`resize`](#169.html_event-media-resize) at the [media element](#169.html_media-element).

The [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element supports [dimension attributes](#169.html_dimension-attributes).

In the absence of style rules to the contrary, video content should be rendered inside the element's playback area such that the video content is shown centered in the playback area at the largest possible size that fits completely within it, with the video content's aspect ratio being preserved. Thus, if the aspect ratio of the playback area does not match the aspect ratio of the video, the video will be shown letterboxed or pillarboxed. Areas of the element's playback area that do not contain the video represent nothing.

In user agents that implement CSS, the above requirement can be implemented by using the [style rule suggested in the rendering section](#169.html_video-object-fit).

The intrinsic width of a [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element's playback area is the intrinsic width of the [poster frame](#169.html_poster-frame), if that is available and the element currently [represents](#169.html_represents) its poster frame; otherwise, it is the [intrinsic width](#169.html_concept-video-intrinsic-width) of the video resource, if that is available; otherwise the intrinsic width is missing.

The intrinsic height of a [`video`](#169.html_the-video-element) element's playback area is the intrinsic height of the [poster frame](#169.html_poster-frame), if that is available and the element currently [represents](#169.html_represents) its poster frame; otherwise it is the [intrinsic height](#169.html_concept-video-intrinsic-height) of the video resource, if that is available; otherwise the intrinsic height is missing.

The [default object size](#169.html_default-object-size) is a width of 300 CSS pixels and a height of 150 CSS pixels. [[CSSIMAGES]](#169.html_refsCSSIMAGES)

* * *

User agents should provide controls to enable or disable the display of closed captions, audio description tracks, and other additional data associated with the video stream, though such features should, again, not interfere with the page's normal rendering.

User agents may allow users to view the video content in manners more suitable to the user (e.g. full-screen or in an independent resizable window). As for the other user interface features, controls to enable this should not interfere with the page's normal rendering unless the user agent is [exposing a user interface](#169.html_expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user). In such an independent context, however, user agents may make full user interfaces visible, with, e.g., play, pause, seeking, and volume controls, even if the [`controls`](#169.html_attr-media-controls) attribute is absent.
