User agents may allow video playback to affect system features that could interfere with the user's experience; for example, user agents could disable screensavers while video playback is in progress.

* * *

The <dfn id="169.html_dom-video-poster" data-anolis-xref="dom-video-poster">`poster`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#169.html_reflect) the [`poster`](#169.html_attr-video-poster) content attribute.

This example shows how to detect when a video has failed to play correctly:

```
<script>
 function failed(e) {
   // video playback failed - show a message saying why
   switch (e.target.error.code) {
     case e.target.error.MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED:
       alert('You aborted the video playback.');
       break;
     case e.target.error.MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK:
       alert('A network error caused the video download to fail part-way.');
       break;
     case e.target.error.MEDIA_ERR_DECODE:
       alert('The video playback was aborted due to a corruption problem or because the video used features your browser did not support.');
       break;
     case e.target.error.MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED:
       alert('The video could not be loaded, either because the server or network failed or because the format is not supported.');
       break;
     default:
       alert('An unknown error occurred.');
       break;
   }
 }
</script>
<p><video src="tgif.vid" autoplay controls onerror="failed(event)"></video></p>
<p><a href="tgif.vid">Download the video file</a>.</p>
```

#### 4.7.7 The <dfn id="170.html_audio">`audio`</dfn> element

[Categories](#170.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#170.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#170.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Embedded content](#170.html_embedded-content-2).

If the element has a [`controls`](#170.html_attr-media-controls) attribute: [Interactive content](#170.html_interactive-content-0).

If the element has a [`controls`](#170.html_attr-media-controls) attribute: [Palpable content](#170.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#170.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [embedded content](#170.html_embedded-content-2) is expected.

[Content model](#170.html_element-dfn-content-model):

If the element has a [`src`](#170.html_attr-media-src) attribute: zero or more [`track`](#170.html_the-track-element) elements, then [transparent](#170.html_transparent), but with no [media element](#170.html_media-element) descendants.

If the element does not have a [`src`](#170.html_attr-media-src) attribute: zero or more [`source`](#170.html_the-source-element) elements, then zero or more [`track`](#170.html_the-track-element) elements, then [transparent](#170.html_transparent), but with no [media element](#170.html_media-element) descendants.

[Content attributes](#170.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#170.html_global-attributes)

[`src`](#170.html_attr-media-src) - Address of the resource

[`crossorigin`](#170.html_attr-media-crossorigin) - How the element handles crossorigin requests

[`preload`](#170.html_attr-media-preload) - Hints how much buffering the [media resource](#170.html_media-resource) will likely need

[`autoplay`](#170.html_attr-media-autoplay) - Hint that the [media resource](#170.html_media-resource) can be started automatically when the page is loaded

[`mediagroup`](#170.html_attr-media-mediagroup) - Groups [media elements](#170.html_media-element) together with an implicit [`MediaController`](#170.html_mediacontroller)

[`loop`](#170.html_attr-media-loop) - Whether to loop the [media resource](#170.html_media-resource)

[`muted`](#170.html_attr-media-muted) - Whether to mute the [media resource](#170.html_media-resource) by default

[`controls`](#170.html_attr-media-controls) - Show user agent controls

Tag omission in text/html

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#170.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`application`](#170.html_index-aria-application).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#170.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#170.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#170.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#170.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
[NamedConstructor=Audio(optional DOMString src)]
interface HTMLAudioElement : HTMLMediaElement {};
```

An [`audio`](#170.html_the-audio-element) element [represents](#170.html_represents) a sound or audio stream.

Content may be provided inside the [`audio`](#170.html_the-audio-element) element. User agents should not show this content to the user; it is intended for older Web browsers which do not support [`audio`](#170.html_the-audio-element), so that legacy audio plugins can be tried, or to show text to the users of these older browsers informing them of how to access the audio contents.

In particular, this content is not intended to address accessibility concerns. To make audio content accessible to the deaf or to those with other physical or cognitive disabilities, a variety of features are available. If captions or a sign language video are available, the [`video`](#170.html_the-video-element) element can be used instead of the [`audio`](#170.html_the-audio-element) element to play the audio, allowing users to enable the visual alternatives. Chapter titles can be provided to aid navigation, using the [`track`](#170.html_the-track-element) element and a [WebVTT file](#170.html_webvtt-file). And, naturally, transcripts or other textual alternatives can be provided by simply linking to them in the prose near the [`audio`](#170.html_the-audio-element) element. [[WEBVTT]](#170.html_refsWEBVTT)

The [`audio`](#170.html_the-audio-element) element is a [media element](#170.html_media-element) whose [media data](#170.html_media-data) is ostensibly audio data.

The [`src`](#170.html_attr-media-src), [`preload`](#170.html_attr-media-preload), [`autoplay`](#170.html_attr-media-autoplay), [`mediagroup`](#170.html_attr-media-mediagroup), [`loop`](#170.html_attr-media-loop), [`muted`](#170.html_attr-media-muted), and [`controls`](#170.html_attr-media-controls) attributes are [the attributes common to all media elements](#170.html_media-element-attributes).

When an [`audio`](#170.html_the-audio-element) element is [potentially playing](#170.html_potentially-playing), it must have its audio data played synchronized with the [current playback position](#170.html_current-playback-position), at the element's [effective media volume](#170.html_effective-media-volume).

When an [`audio`](#170.html_the-audio-element) element is not [potentially playing](#170.html_potentially-playing), audio must not play for the element.

`audio` = new [`Audio`](#170.html_dom-audio)( [ `url` ] )

Returns a new [`audio`](#170.html_the-audio-element) element, with the [`src`](#170.html_attr-media-src) attribute set to the value passed in the argument, if applicable.

A constructor is provided for creating [`HTMLAudioElement`](#170.html_htmlaudioelement) objects (in addition to the factory methods from DOM such as `createElement()`): <dfn id="170.html_dom-audio" data-anolis-xref="dom-Audio">`Audio(``src``)`</dfn>. When invoked as a constructor, it must return a new [`HTMLAudioElement`](#170.html_htmlaudioelement) object (a new [`audio`](#170.html_the-audio-element) element). The element must have its [`preload`](#170.html_attr-media-preload) attribute set to the literal value "[`auto`](#170.html_attr-media-preload-auto)". If the `src` argument is present, the object created must have its [`src`](#170.html_attr-media-src) content attribute set to the provided value, and the user agent must invoke the object's [resource selection algorithm](#170.html_concept-media-load-algorithm) before returning. The element's document must be the [active document](#170.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#170.html_browsing-context) of the [`Window`](#170.html_window) object on which the interface object of the invoked constructor is found.

#### 4.7.8 The <dfn>`source`</dfn> element

[Categories](#171.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#171.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As a child of a [media element](#171.html_media-element), before any [flow content](#171.html_flow-content-1) or [`track`](#171.html_the-track-element) elements.

[Content model](#171.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#171.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#171.html_global-attributes)

[`src`](#171.html_attr-source-src) - Address of the resource

[`type`](#171.html_attr-source-type) - Type of embedded resource

Tag omission in text/html:

No [end tag](#171.html_syntax-end-tag)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#171.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#171.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#171.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#171.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLSourceElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString src;
           attribute DOMString type;
           attribute DOMString media;
};
```

The [`source`](#171.html_the-source-element) element allows authors to specify multiple alternative [media resources](#171.html_media-resource) for [media elements](#171.html_media-element). It does not [represent](#171.html_represents) anything on its own.

The <dfn id="171.html_attr-source-src" data-anolis-xref="attr-source-src">`src`</dfn> attribute gives the address of the [media resource](#171.html_media-resource). The value must be a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#171.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces). This attribute must be present.

Dynamically modifying a [`source`](#171.html_the-source-element) element and its attribute when the element is already inserted in a [`video`](#171.html_the-video-element) or [`audio`](#171.html_the-audio-element) element will have no effect. To change what is playing, just use the [`src`](#171.html_attr-media-src) attribute on the [media element](#171.html_media-element) directly, possibly making use of the [`canPlayType()`](#171.html_dom-navigator-canplaytype) method to pick from amongst available resources. Generally, manipulating [`source`](#171.html_the-source-element) elements manually after the document has been parsed is an unnecessarily complicated approach.

The <dfn id="171.html_attr-source-type" data-anolis-xref="attr-source-type">`type`</dfn> attribute gives the type of the [media resource](#171.html_media-resource), to help the user agent determine if it can play this [media resource](#171.html_media-resource) before fetching it. If specified, its value must be a [valid MIME type](#171.html_valid-mime-type). The `codecs` parameter, which certain MIME types define, might be necessary to specify exactly how the resource is encoded. [[RFC6381]](#171.html_refsRFC6381)

The following list shows some examples of how to use the `codecs=` MIME parameter in the [`type`](#171.html_attr-source-type) attribute.

H.264 Constrained baseline profile video (main and extended video compatible) level 3 and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container

```
<source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="avc1.42E01E, mp4a.40.2"'>
```

H.264 Extended profile video (baseline-compatible) level 3 and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container

```
<source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="avc1.58A01E, mp4a.40.2"'>
```

H.264 Main profile video level 3 and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container

```
<source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="avc1.4D401E, mp4a.40.2"'>
```

H.264 'High' profile video (incompatible with main, baseline, or extended profiles) level 3 and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container

```
<source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="avc1.64001E, mp4a.40.2"'>
```

MPEG-4 Visual Simple Profile Level 0 video and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container

```
<source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="mp4v.20.8, mp4a.40.2"'>
```

MPEG-4 Advanced Simple Profile Level 0 video and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container

```
<source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="mp4v.20.240, mp4a.40.2"'>
```

MPEG-4 Visual Simple Profile Level 0 video and AMR audio in 3GPP container

```
<source src='video.3gp' type='video/3gpp; codecs="mp4v.20.8, samr"'>
```

Theora video and Vorbis audio in Ogg container

```
<source src='video.ogv' type='video/ogg; codecs="theora, vorbis"'>
```

Theora video and Speex audio in Ogg container

```
<source src='video.ogv' type='video/ogg; codecs="theora, speex"'>
```

Vorbis audio alone in Ogg container

```
<source src='audio.ogg' type='audio/ogg; codecs=vorbis'>
```

Speex audio alone in Ogg container

```
<source src='audio.spx' type='audio/ogg; codecs=speex'>
```

FLAC audio alone in Ogg container

```
<source src='audio.oga' type='audio/ogg; codecs=flac'>
```

Dirac video and Vorbis audio in Ogg container

```
<source src='video.ogv' type='video/ogg; codecs="dirac, vorbis"'>
```

The <dfn id="171.html_attr-source-media" data-anolis-xref="attr-source-media">`media`</dfn> attribute gives the intended media type of the [media resource](#171.html_media-resource), to help the user agent determine if this [media resource](#171.html_media-resource) is useful to the user before fetching it. Its value must be a [valid media query](#171.html_valid-media-query).

The [resource selection algorithm](#171.html_concept-media-load-algorithm) is defined in such a way that when the [`media`](#171.html_attr-source-media) attribute is omitted the user agent acts the same as if the value was "`all`", i.e. by default the [media resource](#171.html_media-resource) is suitable for all media.

If a [`source`](#171.html_the-source-element) element is inserted as a child of a [media element](#171.html_media-element) that has no [`src`](#171.html_attr-media-src) attribute and whose [`networkState`](#171.html_dom-media-networkstate) has the value [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#171.html_dom-media-network_empty), the user agent must invoke the [media element](#171.html_media-element)'s [resource selection algorithm](#171.html_concept-media-load-algorithm).

The IDL attributes <dfn id="171.html_dom-source-src" data-anolis-xref="dom-source-src">`src`</dfn>, <dfn id="171.html_dom-source-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-source-type">`type`</dfn>, and <dfn id="171.html_dom-source-media" data-anolis-xref="dom-source-media">`media`</dfn> must [reflect](#171.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

If the author isn't sure if user agents will all be able to render the media resources provided, the author can listen to the `error` event on the last [`source`](#171.html_the-source-element) element and trigger fallback behavior:

```
<script>
 function fallback(video) {
   // replace <video> with its contents
   while (video.hasChildNodes()) {
     if (video.firstChild instanceof HTMLSourceElement)
       video.removeChild(video.firstChild);
     else
       video.parentNode.insertBefore(video.firstChild, video);
   }
   video.parentNode.removeChild(video);
 }
</script>
<video controls autoplay>
 <source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="avc1.42E01E, mp4a.40.2"'>
 <source src='video.ogv' type='video/ogg; codecs="theora, vorbis"'
         onerror="fallback(parentNode)">
 ...
</video>
```

#### 4.7.9 The <dfn>`track`</dfn> element

[Categories](#172.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#172.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As a child of a [media element](#172.html_media-element), before any [flow content](#172.html_flow-content-1).

[Content model](#172.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#172.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#172.html_global-attributes)

[`kind`](#172.html_attr-track-kind) - The type of text track

[`src`](#172.html_attr-track-src) - Address of the resource

[`srclang`](#172.html_attr-track-srclang) - Language of the text track

[`label`](#172.html_attr-track-label) - User-visible label

[`default`](#172.html_attr-track-default) - Enable the track if no other [text track](#172.html_text-track) is more suitable

Tag omission in text/html:

No [end tag](#172.html_syntax-end-tag)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#172.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#172.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#172.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#172.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTrackElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString kind;
           attribute DOMString src;
           attribute DOMString srclang;
           attribute DOMString label;
           attribute boolean default;

  const unsigned short NONE = 0;
  const unsigned short LOADING = 1;
  const unsigned short LOADED = 2;
  const unsigned short ERROR = 3;
  readonly attribute unsigned short readyState;

  readonly attribute TextTrack track;
};
```

The [`track`](#172.html_the-track-element) element allows authors to specify explicit external timed [text tracks](#172.html_text-track) for [media elements](#172.html_media-element). It does not [represent](#172.html_represents) anything on its own.

The <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-kind" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-kind">`kind`</dfn> attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#172.html_enumerated-attribute). The following table lists the keywords defined for this attribute. The keyword given in the first cell of each row maps to the state given in the second cell.

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-kind-keyword-subtitles" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-kind-keyword-subtitles">`subtitles`</dfn> | <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-kind-subtitles" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-kind-subtitles">Subtitles</dfn> | Transcription or translation of the dialogue, suitable for when the sound is available but not understood (e.g. because the user does not understand the language of the [media resource](#172.html_media-resource)'s audio track). Overlaid on the video. |
| <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-kind-keyword-captions" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-kind-keyword-captions">`captions`</dfn> | <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-kind-captions" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-kind-captions">Captions</dfn> | Transcription or translation of the dialogue, sound effects, relevant musical cues, and other relevant audio information, suitable for when sound is unavailable or not clearly audible (e.g. because it is muted, drowned-out by ambient noise, or because the user is deaf). Overlaid on the video; labeled as appropriate for the hard-of-hearing. |
| <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-kind-keyword-descriptions" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-kind-keyword-descriptions">`descriptions`</dfn> | <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-kind-descriptions" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-kind-descriptions">Descriptions</dfn> | Textual descriptions of the video component of the [media resource](#172.html_media-resource), intended for audio synthesis when the visual component is obscured, unavailable, or not usable (e.g. because the user is interacting with the application without a screen while driving, or because the user is blind). Synthesized as audio. |
| <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-kind-keyword-chapters" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-kind-keyword-chapters">`chapters`</dfn> | <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-kind-chapters" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-kind-chapters">Chapters</dfn> | Chapter titles, intended to be used for navigating the [media resource](#172.html_media-resource). Displayed as an interactive (potentially nested) list in the user agent's interface. |
| <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-kind-keyword-metadata" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-kind-keyword-metadata">`metadata`</dfn> | <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-kind-metadata" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-kind-metadata">Metadata</dfn> | Tracks intended for use from script. Not displayed by the user agent. |

The attribute may be omitted. The *missing value default* is the [subtitles](#172.html_attr-track-kind-subtitles) state.

The <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-src" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-src">`src`</dfn> attribute gives the address of the text track data. The value must be a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#172.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces). This attribute must be present.

If the element has a [`src`](#172.html_attr-track-src) attribute whose value is not the empty string and whose value, when the attribute was set, could be successfully [resolved](#172.html_resolve-a-url) relative to the element, then the element's <dfn id="172.html_track-url">track URL</dfn> is the resulting [absolute URL](#172.html_absolute-url). Otherwise, the element's [track URL](#172.html_track-url) is the empty string.

If the element's [track URL](#172.html_track-url) identifies a [WebVTT](#172.html_webvtt) resource, and the element's [`kind`](#172.html_attr-track-kind) attribute is not in the [metadata](#172.html_attr-track-kind-metadata) state, then the [WebVTT](#172.html_webvtt) file must be a [WebVTT file using cue text](#172.html_webvtt-file-using-cue-text). [[WEBVTT]](#172.html_refsWEBVTT)

Furthermore, if the element's [track URL](#172.html_track-url) identifies a [WebVTT](#172.html_webvtt) resource, and the element's [`kind`](#172.html_attr-track-kind) attribute is in the [chapters](#172.html_attr-track-kind-chapters) state, then the [WebVTT](#172.html_webvtt) file must be both a [WebVTT file using chapter title text](#172.html_webvtt-file-using-chapter-title-text) and a [WebVTT file using only nested cues](#172.html_webvtt-file-using-only-nested-cues). [[WEBVTT]](#172.html_refsWEBVTT)

The <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-srclang" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-srclang">`srclang`</dfn> attribute gives the language of the text track data. The value must be a valid BCP 47 language tag. This attribute must be present if the element's [`kind`](#172.html_attr-track-kind) attribute is in the [subtitles](#172.html_attr-track-kind-subtitles) state. [[BCP47]](#172.html_refsBCP47)

If the element has a [`srclang`](#172.html_attr-track-srclang) attribute whose value is not the empty string, then the element's <dfn id="172.html_track-language">track language</dfn> is the value of the attribute. Otherwise, the element has no [track language](#172.html_track-language).

The <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-label" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-label">`label`</dfn> attribute gives a user-readable title for the track. This title is used by user agents when listing [subtitle](#172.html_attr-track-kind-subtitles), [caption](#172.html_attr-track-kind-captions), and [audio description](#172.html_attr-track-kind-descriptions) tracks in their user interface.

The value of the [`label`](#172.html_attr-track-label) attribute, if the attribute is present, must not be the empty string. Furthermore, there must not be two [`track`](#172.html_the-track-element) element children of the same [media element](#172.html_media-element) whose [`kind`](#172.html_attr-track-kind) attributes are in the same state, whose [`srclang`](#172.html_attr-track-srclang) attributes are both missing or have values that represent the same language, and whose [`label`](#172.html_attr-track-label) attributes are again both missing or both have the same value.

If the element has a [`label`](#172.html_attr-track-label) attribute whose value is not the empty string, then the element's <dfn id="172.html_track-label">track label</dfn> is the value of the attribute. Otherwise, the element's [track label](#172.html_track-label) is an empty string.

The <dfn id="172.html_attr-track-default" data-anolis-xref="attr-track-default">`default`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#172.html_boolean-attribute), which, if specified, indicates that the track is to be enabled if the user's preferences do not indicate that another track would be more appropriate.

Each [media element](#172.html_media-element) must have no more than one [`track`](#172.html_the-track-element) element child whose [`kind`](#172.html_attr-track-kind) attribute is in the [subtitles](#172.html_attr-track-kind-subtitles) or [captions](#172.html_attr-track-kind-captions) state and whose [`default`](#172.html_attr-track-default) attribute is specified.

Each [media element](#172.html_media-element) must have no more than one [`track`](#172.html_the-track-element) element child whose [`kind`](#172.html_attr-track-kind) attribute is in the [description](#172.html_attr-track-kind-descriptions) state and whose [`default`](#172.html_attr-track-default) attribute is specified.

Each [media element](#172.html_media-element) must have no more than one [`track`](#172.html_the-track-element) element child whose [`kind`](#172.html_attr-track-kind) attribute is in the [chapters](#172.html_attr-track-kind-chapters) state and whose [`default`](#172.html_attr-track-default) attribute is specified.

There is no limit on the number of [`track`](#172.html_the-track-element) elements whose [`kind`](#172.html_attr-track-kind) attribute is in the [metadata](#172.html_attr-track-kind-metadata) state and whose [`default`](#172.html_attr-track-default) attribute is specified.

`track` . [`readyState`](#172.html_dom-track-readystate)

Returns the [text track readiness state](#172.html_text-track-readiness-state), represented by a number from the following list:

`track` . [`NONE`](#172.html_dom-track-none) (0)

The [text track not loaded](#172.html_text-track-not-loaded) state.

`track` . [`LOADING`](#172.html_dom-track-loading) (1)

The [text track loading](#172.html_text-track-loading) state.

`track` . [`LOADED`](#172.html_dom-track-loaded) (2)

The [text track loaded](#172.html_text-track-loaded) state.

`track` . [`ERROR`](#172.html_dom-track-error) (3)

The [text track failed to load](#172.html_text-track-failed-to-load) state.

`track` . [`track`](#172.html_dom-track-track)

Returns the [`TextTrack`](#172.html_texttrack) object corresponding to the [text track](#172.html_text-track) of the [`track`](#172.html_the-track-element) element.

The <dfn id="172.html_dom-track-readystate" data-anolis-xref="dom-track-readyState">`readyState`</dfn> attribute must return the numeric value corresponding to the [text track readiness state](#172.html_text-track-readiness-state) of the [`track`](#172.html_the-track-element) element's [text track](#172.html_text-track), as defined by the following list:

<dfn id="172.html_dom-track-none" data-anolis-xref="dom-track-NONE">`NONE`</dfn> (numeric value 0)

The [text track not loaded](#172.html_text-track-not-loaded) state.

<dfn id="172.html_dom-track-loading" data-anolis-xref="dom-track-LOADING">`LOADING`</dfn> (numeric value 1)

The [text track loading](#172.html_text-track-loading) state.

<dfn id="172.html_dom-track-loaded" data-anolis-xref="dom-track-LOADED">`LOADED`</dfn> (numeric value 2)

The [text track loaded](#172.html_text-track-loaded) state.

<dfn id="172.html_dom-track-error" data-anolis-xref="dom-track-ERROR">`ERROR`</dfn> (numeric value 3)

The [text track failed to load](#172.html_text-track-failed-to-load) state.

The <dfn id="172.html_dom-track-track" data-anolis-xref="dom-track-track">`track`</dfn> IDL attribute must, on getting, return the [`track`](#172.html_the-track-element) element's [text track](#172.html_text-track)'s corresponding [`TextTrack`](#172.html_texttrack) object.

The <dfn id="172.html_dom-track-src" data-anolis-xref="dom-track-src">`src`</dfn>, <dfn id="172.html_dom-track-srclang" data-anolis-xref="dom-track-srclang">`srclang`</dfn>, <dfn id="172.html_dom-track-label" data-anolis-xref="dom-track-label">`label`</dfn>, and <dfn id="172.html_dom-track-default" data-anolis-xref="dom-track-default">`default`</dfn> IDL attributes must [reflect](#172.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name. The <dfn id="172.html_dom-track-kind" data-anolis-xref="dom-track-kind">`kind`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#172.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name, [limited to only known values](#172.html_limited-to-only-known-values).

This video has subtitles in several languages:

```
<video src="brave.webm">
 <track kind=subtitles src=brave.en.vtt srclang=en label="English">
 <track kind=captions src=brave.en.hoh.vtt srclang=en label="English for the Hard of Hearing">
 <track kind=subtitles src=brave.fr.vtt srclang=fr lang=fr label="Fran?ais">
 <track kind=subtitles src=brave.de.vtt srclang=de lang=de label="Deutsch">
</video>
```

(The [`lang`](#172.html_attr-lang) attributes on the last two describe the language of the [`label`](#172.html_attr-track-label) attribute, not the language of the subtitles themselves. The language of the subtitles is given by the [`srclang`](#172.html_attr-track-srclang) attribute.)

#### 4.7.10 Media elements

<dfn id="173.html_media-element" data-anolis-xref="media element">Media elements</dfn> ([`audio`](#173.html_the-audio-element) and [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element), in this specification) implement the following interface:

```
enum CanPlayTypeEnum { "" /* empty string */, "maybe", "probably" };
interface HTMLMediaElement : HTMLElement {

  // error state
  readonly attribute MediaError? error;

  // network state
           attribute DOMString src;
  readonly attribute DOMString currentSrc;
           attribute DOMString crossOrigin;
  const unsigned short NETWORK_EMPTY = 0;
  const unsigned short NETWORK_IDLE = 1;
  const unsigned short NETWORK_LOADING = 2;
  const unsigned short NETWORK_NO_SOURCE = 3;
  readonly attribute unsigned short networkState;
           attribute DOMString preload;
  readonly attribute TimeRanges buffered;
  void load();
  CanPlayTypeEnum canPlayType(DOMString type);

  // ready state
  const unsigned short HAVE_NOTHING = 0;
  const unsigned short HAVE_METADATA = 1;
  const unsigned short HAVE_CURRENT_DATA = 2;
  const unsigned short HAVE_FUTURE_DATA = 3;
  const unsigned short HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA = 4;
  readonly attribute unsigned short readyState;
  readonly attribute boolean seeking;

  // playback state
           attribute double currentTime;
  readonly attribute unrestricted double duration;
  Date getStartDate();
  readonly attribute boolean paused;
           attribute double defaultPlaybackRate;
           attribute double playbackRate;
  readonly attribute TimeRanges played;
  readonly attribute TimeRanges seekable;
  readonly attribute boolean ended;
           attribute boolean autoplay;
           attribute boolean loop;
  void play();
  void pause();

  // media controller
           attribute DOMString mediaGroup;
           attribute MediaController? controller;

  // controls
           attribute boolean controls;
           attribute double volume;
           attribute boolean muted;
           attribute boolean defaultMuted;

  // tracks
  readonly attribute AudioTrackList audioTracks;
  readonly attribute VideoTrackList videoTracks;
  readonly attribute TextTrackList textTracks;
  TextTrack addTextTrack(TextTrackKind kind, optional DOMString label = "", optional DOMString language = "");
};
```

The <dfn id="173.html_media-element-attributes">media element attributes</dfn>, [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src), [`crossorigin`](#173.html_attr-media-crossorigin), [`preload`](#173.html_attr-media-preload), [`autoplay`](#173.html_attr-media-autoplay), [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup), [`loop`](#173.html_attr-media-loop), [`muted`](#173.html_attr-media-muted), and [`controls`](#173.html_attr-media-controls), apply to all [media elements](#173.html_media-element). They are defined in this section.

[Media elements](#173.html_media-element) are used to present audio data, or video and audio data, to the user. This is referred to as <dfn id="173.html_media-data">media data</dfn> in this section, since this section applies equally to [media elements](#173.html_media-element) for audio or for video. The term <dfn id="173.html_media-resource">media resource</dfn> is used to refer to the complete set of media data, e.g. the complete video file, or complete audio file.

A [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) can have multiple audio and video tracks. For the purposes of a [media element](#173.html_media-element), the video data of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is only that of the currently selected track (if any) given by the element's [`videoTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-videotracks) attribute, and the audio data of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is the result of mixing all the currently enabled tracks (if any) given by the element's [`audioTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-audiotracks) attribute.

Both [`audio`](#173.html_the-audio-element) and [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) elements can be used for both audio and video. The main difference between the two is simply that the [`audio`](#173.html_the-audio-element) element has no playback area for visual content (such as video or captions), whereas the [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) element does.

Except where otherwise explicitly specified, the [task source](#173.html_task-source) for all the tasks [queued](#173.html_queue-a-task) in this section and its subsections is the <dfn id="173.html_media-element-event-task-source">media element event task source</dfn> of the [media element](#173.html_media-element) in question.

##### 4.7.10.1 Error codes

`media` . [`error`](#173.html_dom-media-error)

Returns a [`MediaError`](#173.html_mediaerror) object representing the current error state of the element.

Returns null if there is no error.

All [media elements](#173.html_media-element) have an associated error status, which records the last error the element encountered since its [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm) was last invoked. The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-error" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-error">`error`</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return the [`MediaError`](#173.html_mediaerror) object created for this last error, or null if there has not been an error.

```
interface MediaError {
  const unsigned short MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED = 1;
  const unsigned short MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK = 2;
  const unsigned short MEDIA_ERR_DECODE = 3;
  const unsigned short MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED = 4;
  readonly attribute unsigned short code;
};
```

`media` . [`error`](#173.html_dom-media-error) . [`code`](#173.html_dom-mediaerror-code)

Returns the current error's error code, from the list below.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediaerror-code" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaError-code">`code`</dfn> attribute of a [`MediaError`](#173.html_mediaerror) object must return the code for the error, which must be one of the following:

<dfn id="173.html_dom-mediaerror-media_err_aborted" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaError-MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED">`MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED`</dfn> (numeric value 1)

The fetching process for the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) was aborted by the user agent at the user's request.

<dfn id="173.html_dom-mediaerror-media_err_network" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaError-MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK">`MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK`</dfn> (numeric value 2)

A network error of some description caused the user agent to stop fetching the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), after the resource was established to be usable.

<dfn id="173.html_dom-mediaerror-media_err_decode" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaError-MEDIA_ERR_DECODE">`MEDIA_ERR_DECODE`</dfn> (numeric value 3)

An error of some description occurred while decoding the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), after the resource was established to be usable.

<dfn id="173.html_dom-mediaerror-media_err_src_not_supported" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaError-MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED">`MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED`</dfn> (numeric value 4)

The [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) indicated by the [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute was not suitable.

##### 4.7.10.2 Location of the media resource

The <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-src" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-src">`src`</dfn> content attribute on [media elements](#173.html_media-element) gives the address of the media resource (video, audio) to show. The attribute, if present, must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#173.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces).

The <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-crossorigin" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-crossorigin">`crossorigin`</dfn> content attribute on [media elements](#173.html_media-element) is a [CORS settings attribute](#173.html_cors-settings-attribute).

If a [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute of a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is set or changed, the user agent must invoke the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [media element load algorithm](#173.html_media-element-load-algorithm). (*Removing* the [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute does not do this, even if there are [`source`](#173.html_the-source-element) elements present.)

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-src" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-src">`src`</dfn> IDL attribute on [media elements](#173.html_media-element) must [reflect](#173.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-crossorigin" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-crossOrigin">`crossOrigin`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#173.html_reflect) the [`crossorigin`](#173.html_attr-media-crossorigin) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#173.html_limited-to-only-known-values).

`media` . [`currentSrc`](#173.html_dom-media-currentsrc)

Returns the address of the current [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).

Returns the empty string when there is no [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-currentsrc" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-currentSrc">`currentSrc`</dfn> IDL attribute is initially the empty string. Its value is changed by the [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm) defined below.

There are two ways to specify a [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), the [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute, or [`source`](#173.html_the-source-element) elements. The attribute overrides the elements.

##### 4.7.10.3 MIME types

A [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) can be described in terms of its *type*, specifically a [MIME type](#173.html_mime-type), in some cases with a `codecs` parameter. (Whether the `codecs` parameter is allowed or not depends on the MIME type.) [[RFC6381]](#173.html_refsRFC6381)

Types are usually somewhat incomplete descriptions; for example "`video/mpeg`" doesn't say anything except what the container type is, and even a type like "`video/mp4; codecs="avc1.42E01E, mp4a.40.2"`" doesn't include information like the actual bitrate (only the maximum bitrate). Thus, given a type, a user agent can often only know whether it *might* be able to play media of that type (with varying levels of confidence), or whether it definitely *cannot* play media of that type.

<dfn id="173.html_a-type-that-the-user-agent-knows-it-cannot-render">A type that the user agent knows it cannot render</dfn> is one that describes a resource that the user agent definitely does not support, for example because it doesn't recognize the container type, or it doesn't support the listed codecs.

The [MIME type](#173.html_mime-type) "`application/octet-stream`" with no parameters is never [a type that the user agent knows it cannot render](#173.html_a-type-that-the-user-agent-knows-it-cannot-render). User agents must treat that type as equivalent to the lack of any explicit [Content-Type metadata](#173.html_content-type) when it is used to label a potential [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).

Only the [MIME type](#173.html_mime-type) "`application/octet-stream`" with no parameters is special-cased here; if any parameter appears with it, it will be treated just like any other [MIME type](#173.html_mime-type). This is a deviation from the rule that unknown [MIME type](#173.html_mime-type) parameters should be ignored.

`media` . [`canPlayType`](#173.html_dom-navigator-canplaytype)(`type`)

Returns the empty string (a negative response), "maybe", or "probably" based on how confident the user agent is that it can play media resources of the given type.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-navigator-canplaytype" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-canPlayType">`canPlayType(``type``)`</dfn> method must return <dfn id="173.html_dom-canplaytypeenum-nil" data-anolis-xref="dom-CanPlayTypeEnum-nil">the empty string</dfn> if `type` is [a type that the user agent knows it cannot render](#173.html_a-type-that-the-user-agent-knows-it-cannot-render) or is the type "`application/octet-stream`"; it must return "<dfn id="173.html_dom-canplaytypeenum-probably" data-anolis-xref="dom-CanPlayTypeEnum-probably">`probably`</dfn>" if the user agent is confident that the type represents a [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) that it can render if used in with this [`audio`](#173.html_the-audio-element) or [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) element; and it must return "<dfn id="173.html_dom-canplaytypeenum-maybe" data-anolis-xref="dom-CanPlayTypeEnum-maybe">`maybe`</dfn>" otherwise. Implementors are encouraged to return "[`maybe`](#173.html_dom-canplaytypeenum-maybe)" unless the type can be confidently established as being supported or not. Generally, a user agent should never return "[`probably`](#173.html_dom-canplaytypeenum-probably)" for a type that allows the `codecs` parameter if that parameter is not present.

This script tests to see if the user agent supports a (fictional) new format to dynamically decide whether to use a [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) element or a plugin:

```
<section id="video">
 <p><a href="playing-cats.nfv">Download video</a></p>
</section>
<script>
 var videoSection = document.getElementById('video');
 var videoElement = document.createElement('video');
 var support = videoElement.canPlayType('video/x-new-fictional-format;codecs="kittens,bunnies"');
 if (support != "probably" && "New Fictional Video Plugin" in navigator.plugins) {
   // not confident of browser support
   // but we have a plugin
   // so use plugin instead
   videoElement = document.createElement("embed");
 } else if (support == "") {
   // no support from browser and no plugin
   // do nothing
   videoElement = null;
 }
 if (videoElement) {
   while (videoSection.hasChildNodes())
     videoSection.removeChild(videoSection.firstChild);
   videoElement.setAttribute("src", "playing-cats.nfv");
   videoSection.appendChild(videoElement);
 }
</script>
```

The [`type`](#173.html_attr-source-type) attribute of the [`source`](#173.html_the-source-element) element allows the user agent to avoid downloading resources that use formats it cannot render.

##### 4.7.10.4 Network states

`media` . [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate)

Returns the current state of network activity for the element, from the codes in the list below.

As [media elements](#173.html_media-element) interact with the network, their current network activity is represented by the <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-networkstate" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-networkState">`networkState`</dfn> attribute. On getting, it must return the current network state of the element, which must be one of the following values:

<dfn id="173.html_dom-media-network_empty" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-NETWORK_EMPTY">`NETWORK_EMPTY`</dfn> (numeric value 0)

The element has not yet been initialized. All attributes are in their initial states.

<dfn id="173.html_dom-media-network_idle" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-NETWORK_IDLE">`NETWORK_IDLE`</dfn> (numeric value 1)

The element's [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm) is active and has selected a [resource](#173.html_media-resource), but it is not actually using the network at this time.

<dfn id="173.html_dom-media-network_loading" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-NETWORK_LOADING">`NETWORK_LOADING`</dfn> (numeric value 2)

The user agent is actively trying to download data.

<dfn id="173.html_dom-media-network_no_source" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-NETWORK_NO_SOURCE">`NETWORK_NO_SOURCE`</dfn> (numeric value 3)

The element's [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm) is active, but it has not yet found a [resource](#173.html_media-resource) to use.

The [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm) defined below describes exactly when the [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute changes value and what events fire to indicate changes in this state.

##### 4.7.10.5 Loading the media resource

`media` . [`load`](#173.html_dom-media-load)()

Causes the element to reset and start selecting and loading a new [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) from scratch.

All [media elements](#173.html_media-element) have an <dfn id="173.html_autoplaying-flag">autoplaying flag</dfn>, which must begin in the true state, and a <dfn id="173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag">delaying-the-load-event flag</dfn>, which must begin in the false state. While the [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) is true, the element must [delay the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event) of its document.

When the <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-load" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-load">`load()`</dfn> method on a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is invoked, the user agent must run the [media element load algorithm](#173.html_media-element-load-algorithm).

The <dfn id="173.html_media-element-load-algorithm">media element load algorithm</dfn> consists of the following steps.

1.  Abort any already-running instance of the [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm) for this element.

2.  If there are any [tasks](#173.html_concept-task) from the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [media element event task source](#173.html_media-element-event-task-source) in one of the [task queues](#173.html_task-queue), then remove those tasks.

    If there are any [tasks](#173.html_concept-task) that were [queued](#173.html_queue-a-task) by the [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm) (including the algorithms that it itself invokes) for this same [media element](#173.html_media-element) from the [DOM manipulation task source](#173.html_dom-manipulation-task-source) in one of the [task queues](#173.html_task-queue), then remove those tasks.

    Basically, pending events and callbacks for the media element are discarded when the media element starts loading a new resource.

3.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) is set to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#173.html_dom-media-network_loading) or [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_idle), [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`abort`](#173.html_event-media-abort) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

4.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) is not set to [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#173.html_dom-media-network_empty), then run these substeps:

    1.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`emptied`](#173.html_event-media-emptied) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

    2.  If a fetching process is in progress for the [media element](#173.html_media-element), the user agent should stop it.

    3.  [Forget the media element's media-resource-specific tracks](#173.html_forget-the-media-element's-media-resource-specific-tracks).

    4.  If [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) is not set to [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#173.html_dom-media-have_nothing), then set it to that state.

    5.  If the [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute is false, then set it to true.

    6.  If [`seeking`](#173.html_dom-media-seeking) is true, set it to false.

    7.  Set the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) to 0.

        Set the [official playback position](#173.html_official-playback-position) to 0.

        If this changed the [official playback position](#173.html_official-playback-position), then [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

    8.  Set the [initial playback position](#173.html_initial-playback-position) to 0.

    9.  Set the [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset) to Not-a-Number (NaN).

    10.  Update the [`duration`](#173.html_dom-media-duration) attribute to Not-a-Number (NaN).

        The user agent [will not](#173.html_durationChange) fire a [`durationchange`](#173.html_event-media-durationchange) event for this particular change of the duration.

5.  Set the [`playbackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-playbackrate) attribute to the value of the [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-defaultplaybackrate) attribute.

6.  Set the [`error`](#173.html_dom-media-error) attribute to null and the [autoplaying flag](#173.html_autoplaying-flag) to true.

7.  Invoke the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm).

8.  Playback of any previously playing [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) for this element stops.

The <dfn id="173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm" data-anolis-xref="concept-media-load-algorithm">resource selection algorithm</dfn> for a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is as follows. This algorithm is always invoked synchronously, but one of the first steps in the algorithm is to return and continue running the remaining steps asynchronously, meaning that it runs in the background with scripts and other [tasks](#173.html_concept-task) running in parallel. In addition, this algorithm interacts closely with the [event loop](#173.html_event-loop) mechanism; in particular, it has [synchronous sections](#173.html_synchronous-section) (which are triggered as part of the [event loop](#173.html_event-loop) algorithm). Steps in such sections are marked with ?.

1.  Set the element's [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute to the [`NETWORK_NO_SOURCE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_no_source) value.

2.  Set the element's [show poster flag](#173.html_show-poster-flag) to true.

3.  Set the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) to true (this [delays the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event)).

4.  Asynchronously [await a stable state](#173.html_await-a-stable-state), allowing the [task](#173.html_concept-task) that invoked this algorithm to continue. The [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm until the algorithm says the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) has ended. (Steps in [synchronous sections](#173.html_synchronous-section) are marked with ?.)

5.  ? If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [blocked-on-parser](#173.html_blocked-on-parser) flag is false, then [populate the list of pending text tracks](#173.html_populate-the-list-of-pending-text-tracks).

6.  ? If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute, then let `mode` be *attribute*.

    ? Otherwise, if the [media element](#173.html_media-element) does not have a [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute but has a [`source`](#173.html_the-source-element) element child, then let `mode` be *children* and let `candidate` be the first such [`source`](#173.html_the-source-element) element child in [tree order](#173.html_tree-order).

    ? Otherwise the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has neither a [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute nor a [`source`](#173.html_the-source-element) element child: set the [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) to [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#173.html_dom-media-network_empty), and abort these steps; the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) ends.

7.  ? Set the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#173.html_dom-media-network_loading).

8.  ? [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`loadstart`](#173.html_event-media-loadstart) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

9.  If `mode` is *attribute*, then run these substeps:

    1.  ? If the [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute's value is the empty string, then end the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section), and jump down to the *failed with attribute* step below.

    2.  ? Let `absolute URL` be the [absolute URL](#173.html_absolute-url) that would have resulted from [resolving](#173.html_resolve-a-url) the URL specified by the [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute's value relative to the [media element](#173.html_media-element) when the [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute was last changed.

    3.  ? If `absolute URL` was obtained successfully, set the [`currentSrc`](#173.html_dom-media-currentsrc) attribute to `absolute URL`.

    4.  End the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section), continuing the remaining steps asynchronously.

    5.  If `absolute URL` was obtained successfully, run the [resource fetch algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-resource) with `absolute URL`. If that algorithm returns without aborting *this* one, then the load failed.

    6.  *Failed with attribute*: Reaching this step indicates that the media resource failed to load or that the given URL could not be [resolved](#173.html_resolve-a-url). [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to run the following steps, using the [DOM manipulation task source](#173.html_dom-manipulation-task-source):

        1.  Set the [`error`](#173.html_dom-media-error) attribute to a new [`MediaError`](#173.html_mediaerror) object whose [`code`](#173.html_dom-mediaerror-code) attribute is set to [`MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED`](#173.html_dom-mediaerror-media_err_src_not_supported).

        2.  [Forget the media element's media-resource-specific tracks](#173.html_forget-the-media-element's-media-resource-specific-tracks).

        3.  Set the element's [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute to the [`NETWORK_NO_SOURCE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_no_source) value.

        4.  Set the element's [show poster flag](#173.html_show-poster-flag) to true.

        5.  [Fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`error`](#173.html_event-media-error) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

        6.  Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event).

    7.  Wait for the [task](#173.html_concept-task) queued by the previous step to have executed.

    8.  Abort these steps. Until the [`load()`](#173.html_dom-media-load) method is invoked or the [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute is changed, the element won't attempt to load another resource.

    Otherwise, the [`source`](#173.html_the-source-element) elements will be used; run these substeps:

    1.  ? Let `pointer` be a position defined by two adjacent nodes in the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s child list, treating the start of the list (before the first child in the list, if any) and end of the list (after the last child in the list, if any) as nodes in their own right. One node is the node before `pointer`, and the other node is the node after `pointer`. Initially, let `pointer` be the position between the `candidate` node and the next node, if there are any, or the end of the list, if it is the last node.

        As nodes are inserted and removed into the [media element](#173.html_media-element), `pointer` must be updated as follows:

        If a new node is inserted between the two nodes that define `pointer`

        Let `pointer` be the point between the node before `pointer` and the new node. In other words, insertions at `pointer` go after `pointer`.

        If the node before `pointer` is removed

        Let `pointer` be the point between the node after `pointer` and the node before the node after `pointer`. In other words, `pointer` doesn't move relative to the remaining nodes.

        If the node after `pointer` is removed

        Let `pointer` be the point between the node before `pointer` and the node after the node before `pointer`. Just as with the previous case, `pointer` doesn't move relative to the remaining nodes.

        Other changes don't affect `pointer`.

    2.  ? *Process candidate*: If `candidate` does not have a [`src`](#173.html_attr-source-src) attribute, or if its [`src`](#173.html_attr-source-src) attribute's value is the empty string, then end the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section), and jump down to the *failed with elements* step below.

    3.  ? Let `absolute URL` be the [absolute URL](#173.html_absolute-url) that would have resulted from [resolving](#173.html_resolve-a-url) the URL specified by `candidate`'s [`src`](#173.html_attr-source-src) attribute's value relative to the `candidate` when the [`src`](#173.html_attr-source-src) attribute was last changed.

    4.  ? If `absolute URL` was not obtained successfully, then end the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section), and jump down to the *failed with elements* step below.

    5.  ? If `candidate` has a [`type`](#173.html_attr-source-type) attribute whose value, when parsed as a [MIME type](#173.html_mime-type) (including any codecs described by the `codecs` parameter, for types that define that parameter), represents [a type that the user agent knows it cannot render](#173.html_a-type-that-the-user-agent-knows-it-cannot-render), then end the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section), and jump down to the *failed with elements* step below.

    6.  ? If `candidate` has a [`media`](#173.html_attr-source-media) attribute whose value does not [match the environment](#173.html_matches-the-environment), then end the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section), and jump down to the *failed with elements* step below.

    7.  ? Set the [`currentSrc`](#173.html_dom-media-currentsrc) attribute to `absolute URL`.

    8.  End the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section), continuing the remaining steps asynchronously.

    9.  Run the [resource fetch algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-resource) with `absolute URL`. If that algorithm returns without aborting *this* one, then the load failed.

    10.  *Failed with elements*: [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task), using the [DOM manipulation task source](#173.html_dom-manipulation-task-source), to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `error` at the `candidate` element.

    11.  Asynchronously [await a stable state](#173.html_await-a-stable-state). The [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm until the algorithm says the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) has ended. (Steps in [synchronous sections](#173.html_synchronous-section) are marked with ?.)

    12.  ? [Forget the media element's media-resource-specific tracks](#173.html_forget-the-media-element's-media-resource-specific-tracks).

    13.  ? *Find next candidate*: Let `candidate` be null.

    14.  ? *Search loop*: If the node after `pointer` is the end of the list, then jump to the *waiting* step below.

    15.  ? If the node after `pointer` is a [`source`](#173.html_the-source-element) element, let `candidate` be that element.

    16.  ? Advance `pointer` so that the node before `pointer` is now the node that was after `pointer`, and the node after `pointer` is the node after the node that used to be after `pointer`, if any.

    17.  ? If `candidate` is null, jump back to the *search loop* step. Otherwise, jump back to the *process candidate* step.

    18.  ? *Waiting*: Set the element's [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute to the [`NETWORK_NO_SOURCE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_no_source) value.

    19.  ? Set the element's [show poster flag](#173.html_show-poster-flag) to true.

    20.  ? Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event).

    21.  End the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section), continuing the remaining steps asynchronously.

    22.  Wait until the node after `pointer` is a node other than the end of the list. (This step might wait forever.)

    23.  Asynchronously [await a stable state](#173.html_await-a-stable-state). The [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm until the algorithm says the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) has ended. (Steps in [synchronous sections](#173.html_synchronous-section) are marked with ?.)

    24.  ? Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) back to true (this [delays the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event) again, in case it hasn't been fired yet).

    25.  ? Set the [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) back to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#173.html_dom-media-network_loading).

    26.  ? Jump back to the *find next candidate* step above.

The <dfn id="173.html_concept-media-load-resource" data-anolis-xref="concept-media-load-resource">resource fetch algorithm</dfn> for a [media element](#173.html_media-element) and a given [absolute URL](#173.html_absolute-url) is as follows:

1.  Let the `current media resource` be the resource given by the [absolute URL](#173.html_absolute-url) passed to this algorithm. This is now the element's [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).

2.  Remove all [media-resource-specific text tracks](#173.html_media-resource-specific-text-track) from the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [list of pending text tracks](#173.html_list-of-pending-text-tracks), if any.

3.  Optionally, run the following substeps. This is the expected behavior if the user agent intends to not attempt to fetch the resource until the user requests it explicitly (e.g. as a way to implement the [`preload`](#173.html_attr-media-preload) attribute's [`none`](#173.html_attr-media-preload-none) keyword).

    1.  Set the [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) to [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_idle).

    2.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`suspend`](#173.html_event-media-suspend) at the element, using the [DOM manipulation task source](#173.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

    3.  Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event).

    4.  Wait for the task to be run.

    5.  Wait for an implementation-defined event (e.g. the user requesting that the media element begin playback).

    6.  Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) back to true (this [delays the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event) again, in case it hasn't been fired yet).

    7.  Set the [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#173.html_dom-media-network_loading).

4.  Perform a [potentially CORS-enabled fetch](#173.html_potentially-cors-enabled-fetch) of the `current media resource`'s [absolute URL](#173.html_absolute-url), with the *mode* being the state of the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`crossorigin`](#173.html_attr-media-crossorigin) content attribute, the *origin* being the [origin](#173.html_origin-0) of the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`Document`](#173.html_document), and the *default origin behaviour* set to *taint*.

    The resource obtained in this fashion, if any, contains the [media data](#173.html_media-data). It can be [CORS-same-origin](#173.html_cors-same-origin) or [CORS-cross-origin](#173.html_cors-cross-origin); this affects whether subtitles referenced in the [media data](#173.html_media-data) are exposed in the API and, for [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) elements, whether a [`canvas`](#173.html_the-canvas-element) gets tainted when the video is drawn on it.

    While the load is not suspended (see below), every 350ms (±200ms) or for every byte received, whichever is *least* frequent, [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`progress`](#173.html_event-media-progress) at the element.

    The <dfn id="173.html_stall-timeout">stall timeout</dfn> is a user-agent defined length of time, which should be about three seconds. When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) that is actively attempting to obtain [media data](#173.html_media-data) has failed to receive any data for a duration equal to the [stall timeout](#173.html_stall-timeout), the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`stalled`](#173.html_event-media-stalled) at the element.

    User agents may allow users to selectively block or slow [media data](#173.html_media-data) downloads. When a [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s download has been blocked altogether, the user agent must act as if it was stalled (as opposed to acting as if the connection was closed). The rate of the download may also be throttled automatically by the user agent, e.g. to balance the download with other connections sharing the same bandwidth.

    User agents may decide to not download more content at any time, e.g. after buffering five minutes of a one hour media resource, while waiting for the user to decide whether to play the resource or not, while waiting for user input in an interactive resource, or when the user navigates away from the page. When a [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s download has been suspended, the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task), using the [DOM manipulation task source](#173.html_dom-manipulation-task-source), to set the [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) to [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_idle) and [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`suspend`](#173.html_event-media-suspend) at the element. If and when downloading of the resource resumes, the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to set the [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#173.html_dom-media-network_loading). Between the queuing of these tasks, the load is suspended (so [`progress`](#173.html_event-media-progress) events don't fire, as described above).

    The [`preload`](#173.html_attr-media-preload) attribute provides a hint regarding how much buffering the author thinks is advisable, even in the absence of the [`autoplay`](#173.html_attr-media-autoplay) attribute.

    When a user agent decides to completely stall a download, e.g. if it is waiting until the user starts playback before downloading any further content, the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) must be set to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event).

    The user agent may use whatever means necessary to fetch the resource (within the constraints put forward by this and other specifications); for example, reconnecting to the server in the face of network errors, using HTTP range retrieval requests, or switching to a streaming protocol. The user agent must consider a resource erroneous only if it has given up trying to fetch it.

    This specification does not currently say whether or how to check the MIME types of the media resources, or whether or how to perform file type sniffing using the actual file data. Implementors differ in their intentions on this matter and it is therefore unclear what the right solution is. In the absence of any requirement here, the HTTP specification's strict requirement to follow the Content-Type header prevails ("Content-Type specifies the media type of the underlying data." ... "If and only if the media type is not given by a Content-Type field, the recipient MAY attempt to guess the media type via inspection of its content and/or the name extension(s) of the URI used to identify the resource.").

    The [networking task source](#173.html_networking-task-source) [tasks](#173.html_concept-task) to process the data as it is being fetched must, when appropriate, include the relevant substeps from the following list:

    If the [media data](#173.html_media-data) cannot be fetched at all, due to network errors, causing the user agent to give up trying to fetch the resource
    If the [media data](#173.html_media-data) can be fetched but is found by inspection to be in an unsupported format, or can otherwise not be rendered at all

    DNS errors, HTTP 4xx and 5xx errors (and equivalents in other protocols), and other fatal network errors that occur before the user agent has established whether the `current media resource` is usable, as well as the file using an unsupported container format, or using unsupported codecs for all the data, must cause the user agent to execute the following steps:

    1.  The user agent should cancel the fetching process.

    2.  Abort this subalgorithm, returning to the [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm).

    If the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is found to have an audio track

    1.  Create an [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) object to represent the audio track.

    2.  Update the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`audioTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-audiotracks) attribute's [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) object with the new [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) object.

    3.  [Fire](#173.html_concept-event-fire) a [trusted](#173.html_concept-events-trusted) event with the name [`addtrack`](#173.html_event-media-addtrack), that does not bubble and is not cancelable, and that uses the [`TrackEvent`](#173.html_trackevent) interface, with the [`track`](#173.html_dom-trackevent-track) attribute initialized to the new [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) object, at this [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) object.

    If the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is found to have a video track

    1.  Create a [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) object to represent the video track.

    2.  Update the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`videoTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-videotracks) attribute's [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object with the new [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) object.

    3.  [Fire](#173.html_concept-event-fire) a [trusted](#173.html_concept-events-trusted) event with the name [`addtrack`](#173.html_event-media-addtrack), that does not bubble and is not cancelable, and that uses the [`TrackEvent`](#173.html_trackevent) interface, with the [`track`](#173.html_dom-trackevent-track) attribute initialized to the new [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) object, at this [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object.

    Once enough of the [media data](#173.html_media-data) has been fetched to determine the duration of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), its dimensions, and other metadata

    This indicates that the resource is usable. The user agent must follow these substeps:

    1.  [Establish the media timeline](#173.html_defineTimeline) for the purposes of the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position), the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position), and the [initial playback position](#173.html_initial-playback-position), based on the [media data](#173.html_media-data).

    2.  Update the [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset) to the date and time that corresponds to the zero time in the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline) established in the previous step, if any. If no explicit time and date is given by the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), the [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset) must be set to Not-a-Number (NaN).

    3.  Set the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) and the [official playback position](#173.html_official-playback-position) to the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position).

    4.  Update the [`duration`](#173.html_dom-media-duration) attribute with the time of the last frame of the resource, if known, on the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline) established above. If it is not known (e.g. a stream that is in principle infinite), update the [`duration`](#173.html_dom-media-duration) attribute to the value positive Infinity.

        The user agent [will](#173.html_durationChange) [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`durationchange`](#173.html_event-media-durationchange) at the element at this point.

    5.  For [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) elements, set the [`videoWidth`](#173.html_dom-video-videowidth) and [`videoHeight`](#173.html_dom-video-videoheight) attributes, and [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`resize`](#173.html_event-media-resize) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

        Further [`resize`](#173.html_event-media-resize) events will be fired if the dimensions subsequently change.

    6.  Set the [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute to [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata).

        A [`loadedmetadata`](#173.html_event-media-loadedmetadata) DOM event [will be fired](#173.html_fire-loadedmetadata) as part of setting the [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute to a new value.

    7.  Let `jumped` be false.

    8.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [default playback start position](#173.html_default-playback-start-position) is greater than zero, then [seek](#173.html_dom-media-seek) to that time, and let `jumped` be true.

    9.  Let the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [default playback start position](#173.html_default-playback-start-position) be zero.

    10.  If either the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) or the address of the `current media resource` indicate a particular start time, then set the [initial playback position](#173.html_initial-playback-position) to that time and, if `jumped` is still false, [seek](#173.html_dom-media-seek) to that time and let `jumped` be true.

        For example, with media formats that support the Media Fragments URI fragment identifier syntax, the fragment identifier can be used to indicate a start position. [[MEDIAFRAG]](#173.html_refsMEDIAFRAG)

    11.  If either the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) or the address of the `current media resource` indicate a particular set of audio or video tracks to enable, or if the user agent has information that would enable it to select specific tracks to improve the user's experience, then the relevant audio tracks must be enabled in the element's [`audioTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-audiotracks) object, and, of the relevant video tracks, the one that is listed first in the element's [`videoTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-videotracks) object must be selected. All other tracks must be disabled.

        This could again be triggered by Media Fragments URI fragment identifier syntax, but it could also be triggered e.g. by the user agent selecting a 5.1 surround sound audio track over a stereo audio track. [[MEDIAFRAG]](#173.html_refsMEDIAFRAG)

    12.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), then: if `jumped` is true and the [initial playback position](#173.html_initial-playback-position), relative to the [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller)'s timeline, is greater than the [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller)'s [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position), then [seek the media controller](#173.html_seek-the-media-controller) to the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [initial playback position](#173.html_initial-playback-position), relative to the [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller)'s timeline; otherwise, [seek](#173.html_dom-media-seek) the [media element](#173.html_media-element) to the [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position), relative to the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s timeline.

    Once the [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute reaches [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data), [after the `loadeddata` event has been fired](#173.html_fire-loadeddata), set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event).

    A user agent that is attempting to reduce network usage while still fetching the metadata for each [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) would also stop buffering at this point, following [the rules described previously](#173.html_resourceSuspend), which involve the [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute switching to the [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_idle) value and a `suspend` event firing.

    The user agent is *required* to determine the duration of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) and go through this step before playing.

    Once the entire [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) has been [fetched](#173.html_fetch) (but potentially before any of it has been decoded)

    [Fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`progress`](#173.html_event-media-progress) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

    Set the [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) to [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_idle) and [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`suspend`](#173.html_event-media-suspend) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

    If the user agent ever discards any [media data](#173.html_media-data) and then needs to resume the network activity to obtain it again, then it must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to set the [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#173.html_dom-media-network_loading).

    If the user agent can keep the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) loaded, then the algorithm will continue to its final step below, which aborts the algorithm.

    If the connection is interrupted after some [media data](#173.html_media-data) has been received, causing the user agent to give up trying to fetch the resource
