    Fatal network errors that occur after the user agent has established whether the `current media resource` is usable (i.e. once the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute is no longer [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#173.html_dom-media-have_nothing)) must cause the user agent to execute the following steps:

    1.  The user agent should cancel the fetching process.

    2.  Set the [`error`](#173.html_dom-media-error) attribute to a new [`MediaError`](#173.html_mediaerror) object whose [`code`](#173.html_dom-mediaerror-code) attribute is set to [`MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK`](#173.html_dom-mediaerror-media_err_network).

    3.  [Fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`error`](#173.html_event-media-error) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

    4.  Set the element's [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute to the [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_idle) value.

    5.  Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event).

    6.  Abort the overall [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm).

    If the [media data](#173.html_media-data) is corrupted

    Fatal errors in decoding the [media data](#173.html_media-data) that occur after the user agent has established whether the `current media resource` is usable must cause the user agent to execute the following steps:

    1.  The user agent should cancel the fetching process.

    2.  Set the [`error`](#173.html_dom-media-error) attribute to a new [`MediaError`](#173.html_mediaerror) object whose [`code`](#173.html_dom-mediaerror-code) attribute is set to [`MEDIA_ERR_DECODE`](#173.html_dom-mediaerror-media_err_decode).

    3.  [Fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`error`](#173.html_event-media-error) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

    4.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute has a value equal to [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#173.html_dom-media-have_nothing), set the element's [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute to the [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#173.html_dom-media-network_empty) value, set the element's [show poster flag](#173.html_show-poster-flag) to true, and [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`emptied`](#173.html_event-media-emptied) at the element.

        Otherwise, set the element's [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute to the [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_idle) value.

    5.  Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event).

    6.  Abort the overall [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm).

    If the [media data](#173.html_media-data) fetching process is aborted by the user

    The fetching process is aborted by the user, e.g. because the user pressed a "stop" button, the user agent must execute the following steps. These steps are not followed if the [`load()`](#173.html_dom-media-load) method itself is invoked while these steps are running, as the steps above handle that particular kind of abort.

    1.  The user agent should cancel the fetching process.

    2.  Set the [`error`](#173.html_dom-media-error) attribute to a new [`MediaError`](#173.html_mediaerror) object whose [`code`](#173.html_dom-mediaerror-code) attribute is set to [`MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED`](#173.html_dom-mediaerror-media_err_aborted).

    3.  [Fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`abort`](#173.html_event-media-abort) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

    4.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute has a value equal to [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#173.html_dom-media-have_nothing), set the element's [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute to the [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#173.html_dom-media-network_empty) value, set the element's [show poster flag](#173.html_show-poster-flag) to true, and [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`emptied`](#173.html_event-media-emptied) at the element.

        Otherwise, set the element's [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute to the [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_idle) value.

    5.  Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#173.html_delaying-the-load-event-flag) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#173.html_delay-the-load-event).

    6.  Abort the overall [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm).

    If the [media data](#173.html_media-data) can be fetched but has non-fatal errors or uses, in part, codecs that are unsupported, preventing the user agent from rendering the content completely correctly but not preventing playback altogether

    The server returning data that is partially usable but cannot be optimally rendered must cause the user agent to render just the bits it can handle, and ignore the rest.

    If the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is found to declare a [media-resource-specific text track](#173.html_media-resource-specific-text-track) that the user agent supports

    If the [media data](#173.html_media-data) is [CORS-same-origin](#173.html_cors-same-origin), run the [steps to expose a media-resource-specific text track](#173.html_steps-to-expose-a-media-resource-specific-text-track) with the relevant data.

    Cross-origin videos do not expose their subtitles, since that would allow attacks such as hostile sites reading subtitles from confidential videos on a user's intranet.

    When the [networking task source](#173.html_networking-task-source) has [queued](#173.html_queue-a-task) the last [task](#173.html_concept-task) as part of [fetching](#173.html_fetch) the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) (i.e. once the download has completed), if the fetching process completes without errors, including decoding the media data, and if all of the data is available to the user agent without network access, then, the user agent must move on to the next step. This might never happen, e.g. when streaming an infinite resource such as Web radio, or if the resource is longer than the user agent's ability to cache data.

    While the user agent might still need network access to obtain parts of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), the user agent must remain on this step.

    For example, if the user agent has discarded the first half of a video, the user agent will remain at this step even once the [playback has ended](#173.html_ended-playback), because there is always the chance the user will seek back to the start. In fact, in this situation, once [playback has ended](#173.html_ended-playback), the user agent will end up firing a [`suspend`](#173.html_event-media-suspend) event, as described earlier.

5.  If the user agent ever reaches this step (which can only happen if the entire resource gets loaded and kept available): abort the overall [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm).

When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is to <dfn id="173.html_forget-the-media-element's-media-resource-specific-tracks">forget the media element's media-resource-specific tracks</dfn>, the user agent must remove from the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [list of text tracks](#173.html_list-of-text-tracks) all the [media-resource-specific text tracks](#173.html_media-resource-specific-text-track), then empty the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`audioTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-audiotracks) attribute's [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) object, then empty the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`videoTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-videotracks) attribute's [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object. No events (in particular, no [`removetrack`](#173.html_event-media-removetrack) events) are fired as part of this; the [`error`](#173.html_event-media-error) and [`emptied`](#173.html_event-media-emptied) events, fired by the algorithms that invoke this one, can be used instead.

* * *

The <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-preload" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-preload">`preload`</dfn> attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#173.html_enumerated-attribute). The following table lists the keywords and states for the attribute — the keywords in the left column map to the states in the cell in the second column on the same row as the keyword. The attribute can be changed even once the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is being buffered or played; the descriptions in the table below are to be interpreted with that in mind.

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-preload-none" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-preload-none">`none`</dfn> | <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-preload-none-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-preload-none-state">None</dfn> | Hints to the user agent that either the author does not expect the user to need the media resource, or that the server wants to minimize unnecessary traffic. This state does not provide a hint regarding how aggressively to actually download the media resource if buffering starts anyway (e.g. once the user hits "play"). |
| <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-preload-metadata" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-preload-metadata">`metadata`</dfn> | <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-preload-metadata-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-preload-metadata-state">Metadata</dfn> | Hints to the user agent that the author does not expect the user to need the media resource, but that fetching the resource metadata (dimensions, track list, duration, etc), and maybe even the first few frames, is reasonable. If the user agent precisely fetches no more than the metadata, then the [media element](#173.html_media-element) will end up with its [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute set to [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata); typically though, some frames will be obtained as well and it will probably be [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data) or [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data). When the media resource is playing, hints to the user agent that bandwidth is to be considered scarce, e.g. suggesting throttling the download so that the media data is obtained at the slowest possible rate that still maintains consistent playback. |
| <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-preload-auto" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-preload-auto">`auto`</dfn> | <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-preload-auto-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-preload-auto-state">Automatic</dfn> | Hints to the user agent that the user agent can put the user's needs first without risk to the server, up to and including optimistically downloading the entire resource. |

The empty string is also a valid keyword, and maps to the [Automatic](#173.html_attr-media-preload-auto-state) state. The attribute's *missing value default* is user-agent defined, though the [Metadata](#173.html_attr-media-preload-metadata-state) state is suggested as a compromise between reducing server load and providing an optimal user experience.

Authors might switch the attribute from "[`none`](#173.html_attr-media-preload-none)" or "[`metadata`](#173.html_attr-media-preload-metadata)" to "[`auto`](#173.html_attr-media-preload-auto)" dynamically once the user begins playback. For example, on a page with many videos this might be used to indicate that the many videos are not to be downloaded unless requested, but that once one *is* requested it is to be downloaded aggressively.

The [`preload`](#173.html_attr-media-preload) attribute is intended to provide a hint to the user agent about what the author thinks will lead to the best user experience. The attribute may be ignored altogether, for example based on explicit user preferences or based on the available connectivity.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-preload" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-preload">`preload`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#173.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name, [limited to only known values](#173.html_limited-to-only-known-values).

The [`autoplay`](#173.html_attr-media-autoplay) attribute can override the [`preload`](#173.html_attr-media-preload) attribute (since if the media plays, it naturally has to buffer first, regardless of the hint given by the [`preload`](#173.html_attr-media-preload) attribute). Including both is not an error, however.

* * *

`media` . [`buffered`](#173.html_dom-media-buffered)

Returns a [`TimeRanges`](#173.html_timeranges) object that represents the ranges of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) that the user agent has buffered.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-buffered" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-buffered">`buffered`</dfn> attribute must return a new static [normalized `TimeRanges` object](#173.html_normalized-timeranges-object) that represents the ranges of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), if any, that the user agent has buffered, at the time the attribute is evaluated. Users agents must accurately determine the ranges available, even for media streams where this can only be determined by tedious inspection.

Typically this will be a single range anchored at the zero point, but if, e.g. the user agent uses HTTP range requests in response to seeking, then there could be multiple ranges.

User agents may discard previously buffered data.

Thus, a time position included within a range of the objects return by the [`buffered`](#173.html_dom-media-buffered) attribute at one time can end up being not included in the range(s) of objects returned by the same attribute at later times.

##### 4.7.10.6 Offsets into the media resource

`media` . [`duration`](#173.html_dom-media-duration)

Returns the length of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), in seconds, assuming that the start of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is at time zero.

Returns NaN if the duration isn't available.

Returns Infinity for unbounded streams.

`media` . [`currentTime`](#173.html_dom-media-currenttime) [ = `value` ]

Returns the [official playback position](#173.html_official-playback-position), in seconds.

Can be set, to seek to the given time.

Will throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#173.html_invalidstateerror) exception if there is no selected [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) or if there is a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

A [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) has a <dfn id="173.html_media-timeline">media timeline</dfn> that maps times (in seconds) to positions in the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource). The origin of a timeline is its earliest defined position. The duration of a timeline is its last defined position.

<dfn id="173.html_defineTimeline" data-anolis-xref="establish the media timeline">Establishing the media timeline</dfn>: If the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) somehow specifies an explicit timeline whose origin is not negative (i.e. gives each frame a specific time offset and gives the first frame a zero or positive offset), then the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline) should be that timeline. (Whether the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) can specify a timeline or not depends on the [media resource's](#173.html_media-resource) format.) If the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) specifies an explicit start time *and date*, then that time and date should be considered the zero point in the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline); the [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset) will be the time and date, exposed using the [`getStartDate()`](#173.html_dom-media-getstartdate) method.

If the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) has a discontinuous timeline, the user agent must extend the timeline used at the start of the resource across the entire resource, so that the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline) of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) increases linearly starting from the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position) (as defined below), even if the underlying [media data](#173.html_media-data) has out-of-order or even overlapping time codes.

For example, if two clips have been concatenated into one video file, but the video format exposes the original times for the two clips, the video data might expose a timeline that goes, say, 00:15..00:29 and then 00:05..00:38\. However, the user agent would not expose those times; it would instead expose the times as 00:15..00:29 and 00:29..01:02, as a single video.

In the rare case of a [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) that does not have an explicit timeline, the zero time on the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline) should correspond to the first frame of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource). In the even rarer case of a [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) with no explicit timings of any kind, not even frame durations, the user agent must itself determine the time for each frame in a user-agent-defined manner. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/fdc3317bb5adce541cf9d7dc13ff9f41.jpg)](#173.html_fingerprinting-vector)

An example of a file format with no explicit timeline but with explicit frame durations is the Animated GIF format. An example of a file format with no explicit timings at all is the JPEG-push format ([`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#173.html_multipart/x-mixed-replace) with JPEG frames, often used as the format for MJPEG streams).

If, in the case of a resource with no timing information, the user agent will nonetheless be able to seek to an earlier point than the first frame originally provided by the server, then the zero time should correspond to the earliest seekable time of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource); otherwise, it should correspond to the first frame received from the server (the point in the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) at which the user agent began receiving the stream).

At the time of writing, there is no known format that lacks explicit frame time offsets yet still supports seeking to a frame before the first frame sent by the server.

Consider a stream from a TV broadcaster, which begins streaming on a sunny Friday afternoon in October, and always sends connecting user agents the media data on the same media timeline, with its zero time set to the start of this stream. Months later, user agents connecting to this stream will find that the first frame they receive has a time with millions of seconds. The [`getStartDate()`](#173.html_dom-media-getstartdate) method would always return the date that the broadcast started; this would allow controllers to display real times in their scrubber (e.g. "2:30pm") rather than a time relative to when the broadcast began ("8 months, 4 hours, 12 minutes, and 23 seconds").

Consider a stream that carries a video with several concatenated fragments, broadcast by a server that does not allow user agents to request specific times but instead just streams the video data in a predetermined order, with the first frame delivered always being identified as the frame with time zero. If a user agent connects to this stream and receives fragments defined as covering timestamps 2010-03-20 23:15:00 UTC to 2010-03-21 00:05:00 UTC and 2010-02-12 14:25:00 UTC to 2010-02-12 14:35:00 UTC, it would expose this with a [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline) starting at 0s and extending to 3,600s (one hour). Assuming the streaming server disconnected at the end of the second clip, the [`duration`](#173.html_dom-media-duration) attribute would then return 3,600\. The [`getStartDate()`](#173.html_dom-media-getstartdate) method would return a `Date` object with a time corresponding to 2010-03-20 23:15:00 UTC. However, if a different user agent connected five minutes later, *it* would (presumably) receive fragments covering timestamps 2010-03-20 23:20:00 UTC to 2010-03-21 00:05:00 UTC and 2010-02-12 14:25:00 UTC to 2010-02-12 14:35:00 UTC, and would expose this with a [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline) starting at 0s and extending to 3,300s (fifty five minutes). In this case, the [`getStartDate()`](#173.html_dom-media-getstartdate) method would return a `Date` object with a time corresponding to 2010-03-20 23:20:00 UTC.

In both of these examples, the [`seekable`](#173.html_dom-media-seekable) attribute would give the ranges that the controller would want to actually display in its UI; typically, if the servers don't support seeking to arbitrary times, this would be the range of time from the moment the user agent connected to the stream up to the latest frame that the user agent has obtained; however, if the user agent starts discarding earlier information, the actual range might be shorter.

In any case, the user agent must ensure that the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position) (as defined below) using the established [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline), is greater than or equal to zero.

The [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline) also has an associated clock. Which clock is used is user-agent defined, and may be [media resource](#173.html_media-resource)-dependent, but it should approximate the user's wall clock.

All the [media elements](#173.html_media-element) that share [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) use the same clock for their [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline).

[Media elements](#173.html_media-element) have a <dfn id="173.html_current-playback-position">current playback position</dfn>, which must initially (i.e. in the absence of [media data](#173.html_media-data)) be zero seconds. The [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) is a time on the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline).

[Media elements](#173.html_media-element) also have an <dfn id="173.html_official-playback-position">official playback position</dfn>, which must initially be set to zero seconds. The [official playback position](#173.html_official-playback-position) is an approximation of the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) that is kept stable while scripts are running.

[Media elements](#173.html_media-element) also have a <dfn id="173.html_default-playback-start-position">default playback start position</dfn>, which must initially be set to zero seconds. This time is used to allow the element to be seeked even before the media is loaded.

Each [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a <dfn id="173.html_show-poster-flag">show poster flag</dfn>. When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is created, this flag must be set to true. This flag is used to control when the user agent is to show a poster frame for a [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) element instead of showing the video contents.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-currenttime" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-currentTime">`currentTime`</dfn> attribute must, on getting, return the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [default playback start position](#173.html_default-playback-start-position), unless that is zero, in which case it must return the element's [official playback position](#173.html_official-playback-position). The returned value must be expressed in seconds. On setting, if the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), then the user agent must throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#173.html_invalidstateerror) exception; otherwise, if the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) is [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#173.html_dom-media-have_nothing), then it must set the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [default playback start position](#173.html_default-playback-start-position) to the new value; otherwise, it must set the [official playback position](#173.html_official-playback-position) to the new value and then [seek](#173.html_dom-media-seek) to the new value. The new value must be interpreted as being in seconds.

[Media elements](#173.html_media-element) have an <dfn id="173.html_initial-playback-position">initial playback position</dfn>, which must initially (i.e. in the absence of [media data](#173.html_media-data)) be zero seconds. The [initial playback position](#173.html_initial-playback-position) is updated when a [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is loaded. The [initial playback position](#173.html_initial-playback-position) is a time on the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline).

If the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is a streaming resource, then the user agent might be unable to obtain certain parts of the resource after it has expired from its buffer. Similarly, some [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) might have a [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline) that doesn't start at zero. The <dfn id="173.html_earliest-possible-position">earliest possible position</dfn> is the earliest position in the stream or resource that the user agent can ever obtain again. It is also a time on the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline).

The [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position) is not explicitly exposed in the API; it corresponds to the start time of the first range in the [`seekable`](#173.html_dom-media-seekable) attribute's [`TimeRanges`](#173.html_timeranges) object, if any, or the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) otherwise.

When the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position) changes, then: if the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) is before the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position), the user agent must [seek](#173.html_dom-media-seek) to the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position); otherwise, if the user agent has not fired a [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) event at the element in the past 15 to 250ms and is not still running event handlers for such an event, then the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) at the element.

Because of the above requirement and the requirement in the [resource fetch algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-resource) that kicks in [when the metadata of the clip becomes known](#173.html_getting-media-metadata), the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) can never be less than the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position).

If at any time the user agent learns that an audio or video track has ended and all [media data](#173.html_media-data) relating to that track corresponds to parts of the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline) that are *before* the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position), the user agent may [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to first remove the track from the [`audioTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-audiotracks) attribute's [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) object or the [`videoTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-videotracks) attribute's [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object as appropriate and then [fire](#173.html_concept-event-fire) a [trusted](#173.html_concept-events-trusted) event with the name [`removetrack`](#173.html_event-media-removetrack), that does not bubble and is not cancelable, and that uses the [`TrackEvent`](#173.html_trackevent) interface, with the [`track`](#173.html_dom-trackevent-track) attribute initialized to the [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) or [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) object representing the track, at the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s aforementioned [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) or [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-duration" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-duration">`duration`</dfn> attribute must return the time of the end of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), in seconds, on the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline). If no [media data](#173.html_media-data) is available, then the attributes must return the Not-a-Number (NaN) value. If the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is not known to be bounded (e.g. streaming radio, or a live event with no announced end time), then the attribute must return the positive Infinity value.

The user agent must determine the duration of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) before playing any part of the [media data](#173.html_media-data) and before setting [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) to a value equal to or greater than [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata), even if doing so requires fetching multiple parts of the resource.

When the length of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) changes to a known value (e.g. from being unknown to known, or from a previously established length to a new length) the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`durationchange`](#173.html_event-media-durationchange) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element). (The event is not fired when the duration is reset as part of loading a new media resource.) If the duration is changed such that the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) ends up being greater than the time of the end of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), then the user agent must also [seek](#173.html_dom-media-seek) to the time of the end of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).

If an "infinite" stream ends for some reason, then the duration would change from positive Infinity to the time of the last frame or sample in the stream, and the [`durationchange`](#173.html_event-media-durationchange) event would be fired. Similarly, if the user agent initially estimated the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource)'s duration instead of determining it precisely, and later revises the estimate based on new information, then the duration would change and the [`durationchange`](#173.html_event-media-durationchange) event would be fired.

Some video files also have an explicit date and time corresponding to the zero time in the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline), known as the <dfn id="173.html_timeline-offset">timeline offset</dfn>. Initially, the [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset) must be set to Not-a-Number (NaN).

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-getstartdate" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-getStartDate">`getStartDate()`</dfn> method must return [a new `Date` object](#173.html_create-a-date-object) representing the current [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset).

* * *

The <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-loop" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-loop">`loop`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#173.html_boolean-attribute) that, if specified, indicates that the [media element](#173.html_media-element) is to seek back to the start of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) upon reaching the end.

The [`loop`](#173.html_attr-media-loop) attribute has no effect while the element has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-loop" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-loop">`loop`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#173.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

##### 4.7.10.7 Ready states

`media` . [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate)

Returns a value that expresses the current state of the element with respect to rendering the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position), from the codes in the list below.

[Media elements](#173.html_media-element) have a *ready state*, which describes to what degree they are ready to be rendered at the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position). The possible values are as follows; the ready state of a media element at any particular time is the greatest value describing the state of the element:

<dfn id="173.html_dom-media-have_nothing" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-HAVE_NOTHING">`HAVE_NOTHING`</dfn> (numeric value 0)

No information regarding the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is available. No data for the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) is available. [Media elements](#173.html_media-element) whose [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute are set to [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#173.html_dom-media-network_empty) are always in the [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#173.html_dom-media-have_nothing) state.

<dfn id="173.html_dom-media-have_metadata" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-HAVE_METADATA">`HAVE_METADATA`</dfn> (numeric value 1)

Enough of the resource has been obtained that the duration of the resource is available. In the case of a [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) element, the dimensions of the video are also available. The API will no longer throw an exception when seeking. No [media data](#173.html_media-data) is available for the immediate [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position).

<dfn id="173.html_dom-media-have_current_data" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-HAVE_CURRENT_DATA">`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`</dfn> (numeric value 2)

Data for the immediate [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) is available, but either not enough data is available that the user agent could successfully advance the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) in the [direction of playback](#173.html_direction-of-playback) at all without immediately reverting to the [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata) state, or there is no more data to obtain in the [direction of playback](#173.html_direction-of-playback). For example, in video this corresponds to the user agent having data from the current frame, but not the next frame, when the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) is at the end of the current frame; and to when [playback has ended](#173.html_ended-playback).

<dfn id="173.html_dom-media-have_future_data" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-HAVE_FUTURE_DATA">`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`</dfn> (numeric value 3)

Data for the immediate [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) is available, as well as enough data for the user agent to advance the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) in the [direction of playback](#173.html_direction-of-playback) at least a little without immediately reverting to the [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata) state, and [the text tracks are ready](#173.html_the-text-tracks-are-ready). For example, in video this corresponds to the user agent having data for at least the current frame and the next frame when the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) is at the instant in time between the two frames, or to the user agent having the video data for the current frame and audio data to keep playing at least a little when the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) is in the middle of a frame. The user agent cannot be in this state if [playback has ended](#173.html_ended-playback), as the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) can never advance in this case.

<dfn id="173.html_dom-media-have_enough_data" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA">`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`</dfn> (numeric value 4)

All the conditions described for the [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data) state are met, and, in addition, either of the following conditions is also true:

*   The user agent estimates that data is being fetched at a rate where the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position), if it were to advance at the [effective playback rate](#173.html_effective-playback-rate), would not overtake the available data before playback reaches the end of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).
*   The user agent has entered a state where waiting longer will not result in further data being obtained, and therefore nothing would be gained by delaying playback any further. (For example, the buffer might be full.)

In practice, the difference between [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata) and [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data) is negligible. Really the only time the difference is relevant is when painting a [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) element onto a [`canvas`](#173.html_the-canvas-element), where it distinguishes the case where something will be drawn ([`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data) or greater) from the case where nothing is drawn ([`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata) or less). Similarly, the difference between [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data) (only the current frame) and [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data) (at least this frame and the next) can be negligible (in the extreme, only one frame). The only time that distinction really matters is when a page provides an interface for "frame-by-frame" navigation.

When the ready state of a [media element](#173.html_media-element) whose [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) is not [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#173.html_dom-media-network_empty) changes, the user agent must follow the steps given below:

1.  Apply the first applicable set of substeps from the following list:

    If the previous ready state was [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#173.html_dom-media-have_nothing), and the new ready state is [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata)

    [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`loadedmetadata`](#173.html_event-media-loadedmetadata) at the element.

    Before this task is run, as part of the [event loop](#173.html_event-loop) mechanism, the rendering will have been updated to resize the [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) element if appropriate.

    If the previous ready state was [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata) and the new ready state is [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data) or greater

    If this is the first time this occurs for this [media element](#173.html_media-element) since the [`load()`](#173.html_dom-media-load) algorithm was last invoked, the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`loadeddata`](#173.html_event-media-loadeddata) at the element.

    If the new ready state is [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data) or [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_enough_data), then the relevant steps below must then be run also.

    If the previous ready state was [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data) or more, and the new ready state is [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data) or less

    If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) was [potentially playing](#173.html_potentially-playing) before its [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute changed to a value lower than [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data), and the element has not [ended playback](#173.html_ended-playback), and playback has not [stopped due to errors](#173.html_stopped-due-to-errors), [paused for user interaction](#173.html_paused-for-user-interaction), or [paused for in-band content](#173.html_paused-for-in-band-content), the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) at the element, and [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`waiting`](#173.html_event-media-waiting) at the element.

    If the previous ready state was [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data) or less, and the new ready state is [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data)

    The user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`canplay`](#173.html_event-media-canplay) at the element.

    If the element's [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute is false, the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`playing`](#173.html_event-media-playing) at the element.

    If the new ready state is [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_enough_data)

    If the previous ready state was [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data) or less, the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`canplay`](#173.html_event-media-canplay) at the element, and, if the element's [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute is false, [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`playing`](#173.html_event-media-playing) at the element.

    If the [autoplaying flag](#173.html_autoplaying-flag) is true, and the [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute is true, and the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has an [`autoplay`](#173.html_attr-media-autoplay) attribute specified, and the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`Document`](#173.html_document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#173.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) does not have the [sandboxed automatic features browsing context flag](#173.html_sandboxed-automatic-features-browsing-context-flag) set, then the user agent may also run the following substeps:

    1.  Set the [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute to false.
    2.  If the element's [show poster flag](#173.html_show-poster-flag) is true, set it to false and run the *[time marches on](#173.html_time-marches-on)* steps.
    3.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`play`](#173.html_event-media-play) at the element.
    4.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`playing`](#173.html_event-media-playing) at the element.

    User agents do not need to support autoplay, and it is suggested that user agents honor user preferences on the matter. Authors are urged to use the [`autoplay`](#173.html_attr-media-autoplay) attribute rather than using script to force the video to play, so as to allow the user to override the behavior if so desired.

    In any case, the user agent must finally [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`canplaythrough`](#173.html_event-media-canplaythrough) at the element.

2.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), then [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

It is possible for the ready state of a media element to jump between these states discontinuously. For example, the state of a media element can jump straight from [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata) to [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_enough_data) without passing through the [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data) and [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data) states.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-readystate" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-readyState">`readyState`</dfn> IDL attribute must, on getting, return the value described above that describes the current ready state of the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

The <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-autoplay" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-autoplay">`autoplay`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#173.html_boolean-attribute). When present, the user agent (as described in the algorithm described herein) will automatically begin playback of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) as soon as it can do so without stopping.

Authors are urged to use the [`autoplay`](#173.html_attr-media-autoplay) attribute rather than using script to trigger automatic playback, as this allows the user to override the automatic playback when it is not desired, e.g. when using a screen reader. Authors are also encouraged to consider not using the automatic playback behavior at all, and instead to let the user agent wait for the user to start playback explicitly.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-autoplay" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-autoplay">`autoplay`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#173.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

##### 4.7.10.8 Playing the media resource

`media` . [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused)

Returns true if playback is paused; false otherwise.

`media` . [`ended`](#173.html_dom-media-ended)

Returns true if playback has reached the end of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).

`media` . [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-defaultplaybackrate) [ = `value` ]

Returns the default rate of playback, for when the user is not fast-forwarding or reversing through the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).

Can be set, to change the default rate of playback.

The default rate has no direct effect on playback, but if the user switches to a fast-forward mode, when they return to the normal playback mode, it is expected that the rate of playback will be returned to the default rate of playback.

When the element has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), the [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-defaultplaybackrate) attribute is ignored and the [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller)'s [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-defaultplaybackrate) is used instead.

`media` . [`playbackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-playbackrate) [ = `value` ]

Returns the current rate playback, where 1.0 is normal speed.

Can be set, to change the rate of playback.

When the element has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), the [`playbackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-playbackrate) attribute is ignored and the [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller)'s [`playbackRate`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-playbackrate) is used instead.

`media` . [`played`](#173.html_dom-media-played)

Returns a [`TimeRanges`](#173.html_timeranges) object that represents the ranges of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) that the user agent has played.

`media` . [`play`](#173.html_dom-media-play)()

Sets the [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute to false, loading the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) and beginning playback if necessary. If the playback had ended, will restart it from the start.

`media` . [`pause`](#173.html_dom-media-pause)()

Sets the [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute to true, loading the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) if necessary.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-paused" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-paused">`paused`</dfn> attribute represents whether the [media element](#173.html_media-element) is paused or not. The attribute must initially be true.

A [media element](#173.html_media-element) is a <dfn id="173.html_blocked-media-element">blocked media element</dfn> if its [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute is in the [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#173.html_dom-media-have_nothing) state, the [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata) state, or the [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data) state, or if the element has [paused for user interaction](#173.html_paused-for-user-interaction) or [paused for in-band content](#173.html_paused-for-in-band-content).

A [media element](#173.html_media-element) is said to be <dfn id="173.html_potentially-playing">potentially playing</dfn> when its [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute is false, the element has not [ended playback](#173.html_ended-playback), playback has not [stopped due to errors](#173.html_stopped-due-to-errors), the element either has no [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) or has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) but is not [blocked on its media controller](#173.html_blocked-on-its-media-controller), and the element is not a [blocked media element](#173.html_blocked-media-element).

A [`waiting`](#173.html_event-media-waiting) DOM event [can be fired](#173.html_fire-waiting-when-waiting) as a result of an element that is [potentially playing](#173.html_potentially-playing) stopping playback due to its [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute changing to a value lower than [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data).

A [media element](#173.html_media-element) is said to have <dfn id="173.html_ended-playback">ended playback</dfn> when:

*   The element's [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute is [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata) or greater, and
*   Either:

    *   The [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) is the end of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), and
    *   The [direction of playback](#173.html_direction-of-playback) is forwards, and
    *   Either the [media element](#173.html_media-element) does not have a [`loop`](#173.html_attr-media-loop) attribute specified, or the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

    Or:

    *   The [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) is the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position), and
    *   The [direction of playback](#173.html_direction-of-playback) is backwards.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-ended" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-ended">`ended`</dfn> attribute must return true if, the last time the [event loop](#173.html_event-loop) reached step 1, the [media element](#173.html_media-element) had [ended playback](#173.html_ended-playback) and the [direction of playback](#173.html_direction-of-playback) was forwards, and false otherwise.

A [media element](#173.html_media-element) is said to have <dfn id="173.html_stopped-due-to-errors">stopped due to errors</dfn> when the element's [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute is [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata) or greater, and the user agent [encounters a non-fatal error](#173.html_non-fatal-media-error) during the processing of the [media data](#173.html_media-data), and due to that error, is not able to play the content at the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position).

A [media element](#173.html_media-element) is said to have <dfn id="173.html_paused-for-user-interaction">paused for user interaction</dfn> when its [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute is false, the [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute is either [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data) or [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_enough_data) and the user agent has reached a point in the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) where the user has to make a selection for the resource to continue. If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) when this happens, then the user agent must [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller). If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) when the user makes a selection, allowing playback to resume, the user agent must similarly [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

It is possible for a [media element](#173.html_media-element) to have both [ended playback](#173.html_ended-playback) and [paused for user interaction](#173.html_paused-for-user-interaction) at the same time.

When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) that is [potentially playing](#173.html_potentially-playing) stops playing because it has [paused for user interaction](#173.html_paused-for-user-interaction), the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) at the element.

A [media element](#173.html_media-element) is said to have <dfn id="173.html_paused-for-in-band-content">paused for in-band content</dfn> when its [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute is false, the [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute is either [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data) or [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_enough_data) and the user agent has suspended playback of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) in order to play content that is temporally anchored to the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) and has a non-zero length, or to play content that is temporally anchored to a segment of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) but has a length longer than that segment. If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) when this happens, then the user agent must [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller). If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) when the user agent unsuspends playback, the user agent must similarly [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

One example of when a [media element](#173.html_media-element) would be [paused for in-band content](#173.html_paused-for-in-band-content) is when the user agent is playing [audio descriptions](#173.html_attr-track-kind-descriptions) from an external WebVTT file, and the synthesized speech generated for a cue is longer than the time between the [text track cue start time](#173.html_text-track-cue-start-time) and the [text track cue end time](#173.html_text-track-cue-end-time).

* * *

When the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) reaches the end of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) when the [direction of playback](#173.html_direction-of-playback) is forwards, then the user agent must follow these steps:

1.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [`loop`](#173.html_attr-media-loop) attribute specified and does not have a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), then [seek](#173.html_dom-media-seek) to the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position) of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) and abort these steps.

2.  As defined above, the [`ended`](#173.html_dom-media-ended) IDL attribute starts returning true once the [event loop](#173.html_event-loop)'s current [task](#173.html_concept-task) ends.

3.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

4.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) that, if the [media element](#173.html_media-element) does not have a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), and the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has still [ended playback](#173.html_ended-playback), and the [direction of playback](#173.html_direction-of-playback) is still forwards, and [paused](#173.html_dom-media-paused) is false, changes [paused](#173.html_dom-media-paused) to true and [fires a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`pause`](#173.html_event-media-pause) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

5.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`ended`](#173.html_event-media-ended) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

6.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), then [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

When the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) reaches the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position) of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) when the [direction of playback](#173.html_direction-of-playback) is backwards, then the user agent must only [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) at the element.

* * *

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-defaultplaybackrate" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-defaultPlaybackRate">`defaultPlaybackRate`</dfn> attribute gives the desired speed at which the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is to play, as a multiple of its intrinsic speed. The attribute is mutable: on getting it must return the last value it was set to, or 1.0 if it hasn't yet been set; on setting the attribute must be set to the new value.

The [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-defaultplaybackrate) is used by the user agent when it [exposes a user interface to the user](#173.html_expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user).

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-playbackrate" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-playbackRate">`playbackRate`</dfn> attribute gives the [effective playback rate](#173.html_effective-playback-rate) (assuming there is no [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) overriding it), which is the speed at which the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) plays, as a multiple of its intrinsic speed. If it is not equal to the [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-defaultplaybackrate), then the implication is that the user is using a feature such as fast forward or slow motion playback. The attribute is mutable: on getting it must return the last value it was set to, or 1.0 if it hasn't yet been set; on setting the attribute must be set to the new value, and the playback will change speed (if the element is [potentially playing](#173.html_potentially-playing) and there is no [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller)).

When the [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-defaultplaybackrate) or [`playbackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-playbackrate) attributes change value (either by being set by script or by being changed directly by the user agent, e.g. in response to user control) the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`ratechange`](#173.html_event-media-ratechange) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

The [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-defaultplaybackrate) and [`playbackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-playbackrate) attributes have no effect when the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller); the namesake attributes on the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object are used instead in that situation.

* * *

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-played" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-played">`played`</dfn> attribute must return a new static [normalized `TimeRanges` object](#173.html_normalized-timeranges-object) that represents the ranges of points on the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline) of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) reached through the usual monotonic increase of the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) during normal playback, if any, at the time the attribute is evaluated.

* * *

When the <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-play" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-play">`play()`</dfn> method on a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is invoked, the user agent must run the following steps.

1.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute has the value [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#173.html_dom-media-network_empty), invoke the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm).

2.  If the [playback has ended](#173.html_ended-playback) and the [direction of playback](#173.html_direction-of-playback) is forwards, and the [media element](#173.html_media-element) does not have a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), [seek](#173.html_dom-media-seek) to the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position) of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).

    This [will cause](#173.html_seekUpdate) the user agent to [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

3.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), then [bring the media element up to speed with its new media controller](#173.html_bring-the-media-element-up-to-speed-with-its-new-media-controller).

4.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute is true, run the following substeps:

    1.  Change the value of [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) to false.

    2.  If the [show poster flag](#173.html_show-poster-flag) is true, set the element's [show poster flag](#173.html_show-poster-flag) to false and run the *[time marches on](#173.html_time-marches-on)* steps.

    3.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`play`](#173.html_event-media-play) at the element.

    4.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute has the value [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#173.html_dom-media-have_nothing), [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata), or [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data), [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`waiting`](#173.html_event-media-waiting) at the element.

        Otherwise, the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute has the value [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data) or [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_enough_data): [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`playing`](#173.html_event-media-playing) at the element.

5.  Set the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [autoplaying flag](#173.html_autoplaying-flag) to false.

6.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), then [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

* * *

When the <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-pause" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-pause">`pause()`</dfn> method is invoked, and when the user agent is required to pause the [media element](#173.html_media-element), the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute has the value [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#173.html_dom-media-network_empty), invoke the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm).

2.  Set the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [autoplaying flag](#173.html_autoplaying-flag) to false.

3.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute is false, run the following steps:

    1.  Change the value of [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) to true.

    2.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) at the element.

    3.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`pause`](#173.html_event-media-pause) at the element.

    4.  Set the [official playback position](#173.html_official-playback-position) to the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position).

4.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), then [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

* * *

The <dfn id="173.html_effective-playback-rate">effective playback rate</dfn> is not necessarily the element's [`playbackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-playbackrate). When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), its [effective playback rate](#173.html_effective-playback-rate) is the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller playback rate](#173.html_media-controller-playback-rate). Otherwise, the [effective playback rate](#173.html_effective-playback-rate) is just the element's [`playbackRate`](#173.html_dom-media-playbackrate). Thus, the [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) overrides the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

If the [effective playback rate](#173.html_effective-playback-rate) is positive or zero, then the <dfn id="173.html_direction-of-playback">direction of playback</dfn> is forwards. Otherwise, it is backwards.

When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is [potentially playing](#173.html_potentially-playing) and its [`Document`](#173.html_document) is a [fully active](#173.html_fully-active) [`Document`](#173.html_document), its [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) must increase monotonically at [effective playback rate](#173.html_effective-playback-rate) units of media time per unit time of the [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline)'s clock. (This specification always refers to this as an *increase*, but that increase could actually be a *de*crease if the [effective playback rate](#173.html_effective-playback-rate) is negative.)

The [effective playback rate](#173.html_effective-playback-rate) can be 0.0, in which case the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) doesn't move, despite playback not being paused ([`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) doesn't become true, and the [`pause`](#173.html_event-media-pause) event doesn't fire).

This specification doesn't define how the user agent achieves the appropriate playback rate — depending on the protocol and media available, it is plausible that the user agent could negotiate with the server to have the server provide the media data at the appropriate rate, so that (except for the period between when the rate is changed and when the server updates the stream's playback rate) the client doesn't actually have to drop or interpolate any frames.

Any time the user agent [provides a stable state](#173.html_provide-a-stable-state), the [official playback position](#173.html_official-playback-position) must be set to the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position).

When the [direction of playback](#173.html_direction-of-playback) is backwards, any corresponding audio must be muted. When the [effective playback rate](#173.html_effective-playback-rate) is so low or so high that the user agent cannot play audio usefully, the corresponding audio must also be muted. If the [effective playback rate](#173.html_effective-playback-rate) is not 1.0, the user agent may apply pitch adjustments to the audio as necessary to render it faithfully.

[Media elements](#173.html_media-element) that are [potentially playing](#173.html_potentially-playing) while not [in a `Document`](#173.html_in-a-document) must not play any video, but should play any audio component. Media elements must not stop playing just because all references to them have been removed; only once a media element is in a state where no further audio could ever be played by that element may the element be garbage collected.

It is possible for an element to which no explicit references exist to play audio, even if such an element is not still actively playing: for instance, it could have a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) that still has references and can still be unpaused, or it could be unpaused but stalled waiting for content to buffer.

* * *

Each [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a <dfn id="173.html_list-of-newly-introduced-cues">list of newly introduced cues</dfn>, which must be initially empty. Whenever a [text track cue](#173.html_text-track-cue) is added to the [list of cues](#173.html_text-track-list-of-cues) of a [text track](#173.html_text-track) that is in the [list of text tracks](#173.html_list-of-text-tracks) for a [media element](#173.html_media-element), that [cue](#173.html_text-track-cue) must be added to the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [list of newly introduced cues](#173.html_list-of-newly-introduced-cues). Whenever a [text track](#173.html_text-track) is added to the [list of text tracks](#173.html_list-of-text-tracks) for a [media element](#173.html_media-element), all of the [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) in that [text track](#173.html_text-track)'s [list of cues](#173.html_text-track-list-of-cues) must be added to the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [list of newly introduced cues](#173.html_list-of-newly-introduced-cues). When a [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [list of newly introduced cues](#173.html_list-of-newly-introduced-cues) has new cues added while the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [show poster flag](#173.html_show-poster-flag) is not set, then the user agent must run the *[time marches on](#173.html_time-marches-on)* steps.

When a [text track cue](#173.html_text-track-cue) is removed from the [list of cues](#173.html_text-track-list-of-cues) of a [text track](#173.html_text-track) that is in the [list of text tracks](#173.html_list-of-text-tracks) for a [media element](#173.html_media-element), and whenever a [text track](#173.html_text-track) is removed from the [list of text tracks](#173.html_list-of-text-tracks) of a [media element](#173.html_media-element), if the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [show poster flag](#173.html_show-poster-flag) is not set, then the user agent must run the *[time marches on](#173.html_time-marches-on)* steps.

When the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) of a [media element](#173.html_media-element) changes (e.g. due to playback or seeking), the user agent must run the *[time marches on](#173.html_time-marches-on)* steps. If the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) changes while the steps are running, then the user agent must wait for the steps to complete, and then must immediately rerun the steps. (These steps are thus run as often as possible or needed — if one iteration takes a long time, this can cause certain [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) to be skipped over as the user agent rushes ahead to "catch up".)

The <dfn id="173.html_time-marches-on">*time marches on*</dfn> steps are as follows:

1.  Let `current cues` be a list of [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue), initialized to contain all the [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) of all the [hidden](#173.html_text-track-hidden) or [showing](#173.html_text-track-showing) [text tracks](#173.html_text-track) of the [media element](#173.html_media-element) (not the [disabled](#173.html_text-track-disabled) ones) whose [start times](#173.html_text-track-cue-start-time) are less than or equal to the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) and whose [end times](#173.html_text-track-cue-end-time) are greater than the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position).

2.  Let `other cues` be a list of [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue), initialized to contain all the [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) of [hidden](#173.html_text-track-hidden) and [showing](#173.html_text-track-showing) [text tracks](#173.html_text-track) of the [media element](#173.html_media-element) that are not present in `current cues`.

3.  Let `last time` be the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) at the time this algorithm was last run for this [media element](#173.html_media-element), if this is not the first time it has run.

4.  If the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) has, since the last time this algorithm was run, only changed through its usual monotonic increase during normal playback, then let `missed cues` be the list of [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) in `other cues` whose [start times](#173.html_text-track-cue-start-time) are greater than or equal to `last time` and whose [end times](#173.html_text-track-cue-end-time) are less than or equal to the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position). Otherwise, let `missed cues` be an empty list.

5.  Remove all the [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) in `missed cues` that are also in the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [list of newly introduced cues](#173.html_list-of-newly-introduced-cues), and then empty the element's [list of newly introduced cues](#173.html_list-of-newly-introduced-cues).

6.  If the time was reached through the usual monotonic increase of the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) during normal playback, and if the user agent has not fired a [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) event at the element in the past 15 to 250ms and is not still running event handlers for such an event, then the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) at the element. (In the other cases, such as explicit seeks, relevant events get fired as part of the overall process of changing the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position).)

    The event thus is not to be fired faster than about 66Hz or slower than 4Hz (assuming the event handlers don't take longer than 250ms to run). User agents are encouraged to vary the frequency of the event based on the system load and the average cost of processing the event each time, so that the UI updates are not any more frequent than the user agent can comfortably handle while decoding the video.

7.  If all of the [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) in `current cues` have their [text track cue active flag](#173.html_text-track-cue-active-flag) set, none of the [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) in `other cues` have their [text track cue active flag](#173.html_text-track-cue-active-flag) set, and `missed cues` is empty, then abort these steps.

8.  If the time was reached through the usual monotonic increase of the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) during normal playback, and there are [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) in `other cues` that have their [text track cue pause-on-exit flag](#173.html_text-track-cue-pause-on-exit-flag) set and that either have their [text track cue active flag](#173.html_text-track-cue-active-flag) set or are also in `missed cues`, then immediately [pause](#173.html_dom-media-pause) the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

    In the other cases, such as explicit seeks, playback is not paused by going past the end time of a [cue](#173.html_text-track-cue), even if that [cue](#173.html_text-track-cue) has its [text track cue pause-on-exit flag](#173.html_text-track-cue-pause-on-exit-flag) set.

9.  Let `events` be a list of [tasks](#173.html_concept-task), initially empty. Each [task](#173.html_concept-task) in this list will be associated with a [text track](#173.html_text-track), a [text track cue](#173.html_text-track-cue), and a time, which are used to sort the list before the [tasks](#173.html_concept-task) are queued.

    Let `affected tracks` be a list of [text tracks](#173.html_text-track), initially empty.

    When the steps below say to <dfn id="173.html_prepare-an-event">prepare an event</dfn> named `event` for a [text track cue](#173.html_text-track-cue) `target` with a time `time`, the user agent must run these substeps:

    1.  Let `track` be the [text track](#173.html_text-track) with which the [text track cue](#173.html_text-track-cue) `target` is associated.

    2.  Create a [task](#173.html_concept-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `event` at `target`.

    3.  Add the newly created [task](#173.html_concept-task) to `events`, associated with the time `time`, the [text track](#173.html_text-track) `track`, and the [text track cue](#173.html_text-track-cue) `target`.

    4.  Add `track` to `affected tracks`.

10.  For each [text track cue](#173.html_text-track-cue) in `missed cues`, [prepare an event](#173.html_prepare-an-event) named `enter` for the [`TextTrackCue`](#173.html_texttrackcue) object with the [text track cue start time](#173.html_text-track-cue-start-time).

11.  For each [text track cue](#173.html_text-track-cue) in `other cues` that either has its [text track cue active flag](#173.html_text-track-cue-active-flag) set or is in `missed cues`, [prepare an event](#173.html_prepare-an-event) named `exit` for the [`TextTrackCue`](#173.html_texttrackcue) object with the later of the [text track cue end time](#173.html_text-track-cue-end-time) and the [text track cue start time](#173.html_text-track-cue-start-time).

12.  For each [text track cue](#173.html_text-track-cue) in `current cues` that does not have its [text track cue active flag](#173.html_text-track-cue-active-flag) set, [prepare an event](#173.html_prepare-an-event) named `enter` for the [`TextTrackCue`](#173.html_texttrackcue) object with the [text track cue start time](#173.html_text-track-cue-start-time).

13.  Sort the [tasks](#173.html_concept-task) in `events` in ascending time order ([tasks](#173.html_concept-task) with earlier times first).

    Further sort [tasks](#173.html_concept-task) in `events` that have the same time by the relative [text track cue order](#173.html_text-track-cue-order) of the [text track cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) associated with these [tasks](#173.html_concept-task).
