    Finally, sort [tasks](#173.html_concept-task) in `events` that have the same time and same [text track cue order](#173.html_text-track-cue-order) by placing [tasks](#173.html_concept-task) that fire `enter` events before those that fire `exit` events.

14.  [Queue](#173.html_queue-a-task) each [task](#173.html_concept-task) in `events`, in list order.

15.  Sort `affected tracks` in the same order as the [text tracks](#173.html_text-track) appear in the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [list of text tracks](#173.html_list-of-text-tracks), and remove duplicates.

16.  For each [text track](#173.html_text-track) in `affected tracks`, in the list order, [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `cuechange` at the [`TextTrack`](#173.html_texttrack) object, and, if the [text track](#173.html_text-track) has a corresponding [`track`](#173.html_the-track-element) element, to then [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `cuechange` at the [`track`](#173.html_the-track-element) element as well.

17.  Set the [text track cue active flag](#173.html_text-track-cue-active-flag) of all the [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) in the `current cues`, and unset the [text track cue active flag](#173.html_text-track-cue-active-flag) of all the [cues](#173.html_text-track-cue) in the `other cues`.

18.  Run the [rules for updating the text track rendering](#173.html_rules-for-updating-the-text-track-rendering) of each of the [text tracks](#173.html_text-track) in `affected tracks` that are [showing](#173.html_text-track-showing). For example, for [text tracks](#173.html_text-track) based on [WebVTT](#173.html_webvtt), the [rules for updating the display of WebVTT text tracks](#173.html_rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks). [[WEBVTT]](#173.html_refsWEBVTT)

For the purposes of the algorithm above, a [text track cue](#173.html_text-track-cue) is considered to be part of a [text track](#173.html_text-track) only if it is listed in the [text track list of cues](#173.html_text-track-list-of-cues), not merely if it is associated with the [text track](#173.html_text-track).

If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`Document`](#173.html_document) stops being a [fully active](#173.html_fully-active) document, then the playback will [stop](#173.html_media-playback) until the document is active again.

When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is [removed from a `Document`](#173.html_remove-an-element-from-a-document), the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Asynchronously [await a stable state](#173.html_await-a-stable-state), allowing the [task](#173.html_concept-task) that removed the [media element](#173.html_media-element) from the [`Document`](#173.html_document) to continue. The [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm. (Steps in the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) are marked with ?.)

2.  ? If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) is [in a `Document`](#173.html_in-a-document), abort these steps.

3.  ? If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) attribute has the value [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#173.html_dom-media-network_empty), abort these steps.

4.  ? [Pause](#173.html_dom-media-pause) the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

##### 4.7.10.9 Seeking

`media` . [`seeking`](#173.html_dom-media-seeking)

Returns true if the user agent is currently seeking.

`media` . [`seekable`](#173.html_dom-media-seekable)

Returns a [`TimeRanges`](#173.html_timeranges) object that represents the ranges of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) to which it is possible for the user agent to seek.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-seeking" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-seeking">`seeking`</dfn> attribute must initially have the value false.

When the user agent is required to <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-seek" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-seek">seek</dfn> to a particular `new playback position` in the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), optionally with the *approximate-for-speed* flag set, it means that the user agent must run the following steps. This algorithm interacts closely with the [event loop](#173.html_event-loop) mechanism; in particular, it has a [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) (which is triggered as part of the [event loop](#173.html_event-loop) algorithm). Steps in that section are marked with ?.

1.  Set the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [show poster flag](#173.html_show-poster-flag) to false.

2.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) is [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#173.html_dom-media-have_nothing), abort these steps.

3.  If the element's [`seeking`](#173.html_dom-media-seeking) IDL attribute is true, then another instance of this algorithm is already running. Abort that other instance of the algorithm without waiting for the step that it is running to complete.

4.  Set the [`seeking`](#173.html_dom-media-seeking) IDL attribute to true.

5.  If the seek was in response to a DOM method call or setting of an IDL attribute, then continue the script. The remainder of these steps must be run asynchronously. With the exception of the steps marked with ?, they could be aborted at any time by another instance of this algorithm being invoked.

6.  If the `new playback position` is later than the end of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), then let it be the end of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) instead.

7.  If the `new playback position` is less than the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position), let it be that position instead.

8.  If the (possibly now changed) `new playback position` is not in one of the ranges given in the [`seekable`](#173.html_dom-media-seekable) attribute, then let it be the position in one of the ranges given in the [`seekable`](#173.html_dom-media-seekable) attribute that is the nearest to the `new playback position`. If two positions both satisfy that constraint (i.e. the `new playback position` is exactly in the middle between two ranges in the [`seekable`](#173.html_dom-media-seekable) attribute) then use the position that is closest to the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position). If there are no ranges given in the [`seekable`](#173.html_dom-media-seekable) attribute then set the [`seeking`](#173.html_dom-media-seeking) IDL attribute to false and abort these steps.

9.  If the *approximate-for-speed* flag is set, adjust the `new playback position` to a value that will allow for playback to resume promptly. If `new playback position` before this step is before [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position), then the adjusted `new playback position` must also be before the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position). Similarly, if the `new playback position` before this step is after [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position), then the adjusted `new playback position` must also be after the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position).

    For example, the user agent could snap to the nearest key frame, so that it doesn't have to spend time decoding then discarding intermediate frames before resuming playback.

10.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`seeking`](#173.html_event-media-seeking) at the element.

11.  Set the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) to the given `new playback position`.

    If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) was [potentially playing](#173.html_potentially-playing) immediately before it started seeking, but seeking caused its [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute to change to a value lower than [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data), then a [`waiting`](#173.html_event-media-waiting) [will be fired](#173.html_fire-waiting-when-waiting) at the element.

    The [`currentTime`](#173.html_dom-media-currenttime) attribute does not get updated asynchronously, as it returns the [official playback position](#173.html_official-playback-position), not the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position).

12.  Wait until the user agent has established whether or not the [media data](#173.html_media-data) for the `new playback position` is available, and, if it is, until it has decoded enough data to play back that position.

13.  [Await a stable state](#173.html_await-a-stable-state). The [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm. (Steps in the [synchronous section](#173.html_synchronous-section) are marked with ?.)

14.  ? Set the [`seeking`](#173.html_dom-media-seeking) IDL attribute to false.

15.  ? Run the [time marches on](#173.html_time-marches-on) steps.

16.  ? [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-media-timeupdate) at the element.

17.  ? [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`seeked`](#173.html_event-media-seeked) at the element.

* * *

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-seekable" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-seekable">`seekable`</dfn> attribute must return a new static [normalized `TimeRanges` object](#173.html_normalized-timeranges-object) that represents the ranges of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), if any, that the user agent is able to seek to, at the time the attribute is evaluated.

If the user agent can seek to anywhere in the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), e.g. because it is a simple movie file and the user agent and the server support HTTP Range requests, then the attribute would return an object with one range, whose start is the time of the first frame (the [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position), typically zero), and whose end is the same as the time of the first frame plus the [`duration`](#173.html_dom-media-duration) attribute's value (which would equal the time of the last frame, and might be positive Infinity).

The range might be continuously changing, e.g. if the user agent is buffering a sliding window on an infinite stream. This is the behavior seen with DVRs viewing live TV, for instance.

[Media resources](#173.html_media-resource) might be internally scripted or interactive. Thus, a [media element](#173.html_media-element) could play in a non-linear fashion. If this happens, the user agent must act as if the algorithm for [seeking](#173.html_dom-media-seek) was used whenever the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) changes in a discontinuous fashion (so that the relevant events fire). If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), then the user agent must [seek the media controller](#173.html_seek-the-media-controller) appropriately instead.

##### 4.7.10.10 Media resources with multiple media tracks

A [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) can have multiple embedded audio and video tracks. For example, in addition to the primary video and audio tracks, a [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) could have foreign-language dubbed dialogues, director's commentaries, audio descriptions, alternative angles, or sign-language overlays.

`media` . [`audioTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-audiotracks)

Returns an [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) object representing the audio tracks available in the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).

`media` . [`videoTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-videotracks)

Returns a [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object representing the video tracks available in the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-audiotracks" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-audioTracks">`audioTracks`</dfn> attribute of a [media element](#173.html_media-element) must return a [live](#173.html_live) [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) object representing the audio tracks available in the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [media resource](#173.html_media-resource). The same object must be returned each time.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-videotracks" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-videoTracks">`videoTracks`</dfn> attribute of a [media element](#173.html_media-element) must return a [live](#173.html_live) [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object representing the video tracks available in the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [media resource](#173.html_media-resource). The same object must be returned each time.

There are only ever one [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) object and one [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object per [media element](#173.html_media-element), even if another [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is loaded into the element: the objects are reused. (The [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) and [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) objects are not, though.)

In this example, a script defines a function that takes a URL to a video and a reference to an element where the video is to be placed. That function then tries to load the video, and, once it is loaded, checks to see if there is a sign-language track available. If there is, it also displays that track. Both tracks are just placed in the given container; it's assumed that styles have been applied to make this work in a pretty way!

```
<script>
 function loadVideo(url, container) {
   var controller = new MediaController();
   var video = document.createElement('video');
   video.src = url;
   video.autoplay = true;
   video.controls = true;
   video.controller = controller;
   container.appendChild(video);
   video.onloadedmetadata = function (event) {
     for (var i = 0; i < video.videoTracks.length; i += 1) {
       if (video.videoTracks[i].kind == 'sign') {
         var sign = document.createElement('video');
         sign.src = url + '#track=' + video.videoTracks[i].id; 
         sign.autoplay = true;
         sign.controller = controller;
         container.appendChild(sign);
         return;
       }
     }
   };
 }
</script>
```

###### 4.7.10.10.1 [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) and [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) objects

The [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) and [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) interfaces are used by attributes defined in the previous section.

```
interface AudioTrackList : EventTarget {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter AudioTrack (unsigned long index);
  AudioTrack? getTrackById(DOMString id);

           attribute EventHandler onchange;
           attribute EventHandler onaddtrack;
           attribute EventHandler onremovetrack;
};

interface AudioTrack {
  readonly attribute DOMString id;
  readonly attribute DOMString kind;
  readonly attribute DOMString label;
  readonly attribute DOMString language;
           attribute boolean enabled;
};

interface VideoTrackList : EventTarget {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter VideoTrack (unsigned long index);
  VideoTrack? getTrackById(DOMString id);
  readonly attribute long selectedIndex;

           attribute EventHandler onchange;
           attribute EventHandler onaddtrack;
           attribute EventHandler onremovetrack;
};

interface VideoTrack {
  readonly attribute DOMString id;
  readonly attribute DOMString kind;
  readonly attribute DOMString label;
  readonly attribute DOMString language;
           attribute boolean selected;
};
```

`media` . [`audioTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-audiotracks) . [`length`](#173.html_dom-audiotracklist-length)
`media` . [`videoTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-videotracks) . [`length`](#173.html_dom-videotracklist-length)

Returns the number of tracks in the list.

`audioTrack` = `media` . [`audioTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-audiotracks)[`index`]
`videoTrack` = `media` . [`videoTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-videotracks)[`index`]

Returns the specified [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) or [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) object.

`audioTrack` = `media` . [`audioTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-audiotracks) . [`getTrackById`](#173.html_dom-audiotracklist-gettrackbyid)( `id` )
`videoTrack` = `media` . [`videoTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-videotracks) . [`getTrackById`](#173.html_dom-videotracklist-gettrackbyid)( `id` )

Returns the [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) or [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) object with the given identifier, or null if no track has that identifier.

`audioTrack` . [`id`](#173.html_dom-audiotrack-id)
`videoTrack` . [`id`](#173.html_dom-videotrack-id)

Returns the ID of the given track. This is the ID that can be used with a fragment identifier if the format supports the Media Fragments URI syntax, and that can be used with the `getTrackById()` method. [[MEDIAFRAG]](#173.html_refsMEDIAFRAG)

`audioTrack` . [`kind`](#173.html_dom-audiotrack-kind)
`videoTrack` . [`kind`](#173.html_dom-videotrack-kind)

Returns the category the given track falls into. The [possible track categories](#173.html_dom-TrackList-getKind-categories) are given below.

`audioTrack` . [`label`](#173.html_dom-audiotrack-label)
`videoTrack` . [`label`](#173.html_dom-videotrack-label)

Returns the label of the given track, if known, or the empty string otherwise.

`audioTrack` . [`language`](#173.html_dom-audiotrack-language)
`videoTrack` . [`language`](#173.html_dom-videotrack-language)

Returns the language of the given track, if known, or the empty string otherwise.

`audioTrack` . [`enabled`](#173.html_dom-audiotrack-enabled) [ = `value` ]

Returns true if the given track is active, and false otherwise.

Can be set, to change whether the track is enabled or not. If multiple audio tracks are enabled simultaneously, they are mixed.

`media` . [`videoTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-videotracks) . [`selectedIndex`](#173.html_dom-videotracklist-selectedindex)

Returns the index of the currently selected track, if any, or ?1 otherwise.

`videoTrack` . [`selected`](#173.html_dom-videotrack-selected) [ = `value` ]

Returns true if the given track is active, and false otherwise.

Can be set, to change whether the track is selected or not. Either zero or one video track is selected; selecting a new track while a previous one is selected will unselect the previous one.

An [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) object represents a dynamic list of zero or more audio tracks, of which zero or more can be enabled at a time. Each audio track is represented by an [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) object.

A [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object represents a dynamic list of zero or more video tracks, of which zero or one can be selected at a time. Each video track is represented by a [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) object.

Tracks in [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) and [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) objects must be consistently ordered. If the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is in a format that defines an order, then that order must be used; otherwise, the order must be the relative order in which the tracks are declared in the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource). The order used is called the *natural order* of the list.

Each track in a `TrackList` thus has an index; the first has the index 0, and each subsequent track is numbered one higher than the previous one. If a [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) dynamically adds or removes audio or video tracks, then the indices of the tracks will change dynamically. If the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) changes entirely, then all the previous tracks will be removed and replaced with new tracks.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-audiotracklist-length" data-anolis-xref="dom-AudioTrackList-length">`AudioTrackList.length`</dfn> and <dfn id="173.html_dom-videotracklist-length" data-anolis-xref="dom-VideoTrackList-length">`VideoTrackList.length`</dfn> attributes must return the number of tracks represented by their objects at the time of getting.

The [supported property indices](#173.html_supported-property-indices) of [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) and [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) objects at any instant are the numbers from zero to the number of tracks represented by the respective object minus one, if any tracks are represented. If an [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) or [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object represents no tracks, it has no [supported property indices](#173.html_supported-property-indices).

To [determine the value of an indexed property](#173.html_determine-the-value-of-an-indexed-property) for a given index `index` in an [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) or [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object `list`, the user agent must return the [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) or [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) object that represents the `index`th track in `list`.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-audiotracklist-gettrackbyid" data-anolis-xref="dom-AudioTrackList-getTrackById">`AudioTrackList.getTrackById(``id``)`</dfn> and <dfn id="173.html_dom-videotracklist-gettrackbyid" data-anolis-xref="dom-VideoTrackList-getTrackById">`VideoTrackList.getTrackById(``id``)`</dfn> methods must return the first [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) or [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) object (respectively) in the [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) or [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object (respectively) whose identifier is equal to the value of the `id` argument (in the natural order of the list, as defined above). When no tracks match the given argument, the methods must return null.

The [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) and [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) objects represent specific tracks of a [media resource](#173.html_media-resource). Each track can have an identifier, category, label, and language. These aspects of a track are permanent for the lifetime of the track; even if a track is removed from a [media resource](#173.html_media-resource)'s [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) or [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) objects, those aspects do not change.

In addition, [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) objects can each be enabled or disabled; this is the audio track's *enabled state*. When an [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) is created, its *enabled state* must be set to false (disabled). The [resource fetch algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-resource) can override this.

Similarly, a single [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) object per [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object can be selected, this is the video track's *selection state*. When a [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) is created, its *selection state* must be set to false (not selected). The [resource fetch algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-resource) can override this.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-audiotrack-id" data-anolis-xref="dom-AudioTrack-id">`AudioTrack.id`</dfn> and <dfn id="173.html_dom-videotrack-id" data-anolis-xref="dom-VideoTrack-id">`VideoTrack.id`</dfn> attributes must return the identifier of the track, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise. If the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is in a format that supports the Media Fragments URI fragment identifier syntax, the identifier returned for a particular track must be the same identifier that would enable the track if used as the name of a track in the track dimension of such a fragment identifier. [[MEDIAFRAG]](#173.html_refsMEDIAFRAG)

For example, in Ogg files, this would be the Name header field of the track. [[OGGSKELETONHEADERS]](#173.html_refsOGGSKELETONHEADERS)

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-audiotrack-kind" data-anolis-xref="dom-AudioTrack-kind">`AudioTrack.kind`</dfn> and <dfn id="173.html_dom-videotrack-kind" data-anolis-xref="dom-VideoTrack-kind">`VideoTrack.kind`</dfn> attributes must return the category of the track, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise.

The category of a track is the string given in the first column of the table below that is the most appropriate for the track based on the definitions in the table's second and third columns, as determined by the metadata included in the track in the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource). The cell in the third column of a row says what the category given in the cell in the first column of that row applies to; a category is only appropriate for an audio track if it applies to audio tracks, and a category is only appropriate for video tracks if it applies to video tracks. Categories must only be returned for [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) objects if they are appropriate for audio, and must only be returned for [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) objects if they are appropriate for video.

Return values for [`AudioTrack.kind()`](#173.html_dom-audiotrack-kind) and [`VideoTrack.kind()`](#173.html_dom-videotrack-kind)

| Category | Definition | Applies to... |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "<dfn id="173.html_value-track-kind-alternate" data-anolis-xref="value-track-kind-alternate">`alternative`</dfn>" | A possible alternative to the main track, e.g. a different take of a song (audio), or a different angle (video). | Audio and video. |
| "<dfn id="173.html_value-track-kind-caption" data-anolis-xref="value-track-kind-caption">`captions`</dfn>" | A version of the main video track with captions burnt in. (For legacy content; new content would use text tracks.) | Video only. |
| "<dfn id="173.html_value-track-kind-descriptions" data-anolis-xref="value-track-kind-descriptions">`descriptions`</dfn>" | An audio description of a video track. | Audio only. |
| "<dfn id="173.html_value-track-kind-main" data-anolis-xref="value-track-kind-main">`main`</dfn>" | The primary audio or video track. | Audio and video. |
| "<dfn id="173.html_value-track-kind-main-desc" data-anolis-xref="value-track-kind-main-desc">`main-desc`</dfn>" | The primary audio track, mixed with audio descriptions. | Audio only. |
| "<dfn id="173.html_value-track-kind-sign" data-anolis-xref="value-track-kind-sign">`sign`</dfn>" | A sign-language interpretation of an audio track. | Video only. |
| "<dfn id="173.html_value-track-kind-subtitle" data-anolis-xref="value-track-kind-subtitle">`subtitles`</dfn>" | A version of the main video track with subtitles burnt in. (For legacy content; new content would use text tracks.) | Video only. |
| "<dfn id="173.html_value-track-kind-translation" data-anolis-xref="value-track-kind-translation">`translation`</dfn>" | A translated version of the main audio track. | Audio only. |
| "<dfn id="173.html_value-track-kind-commentary" data-anolis-xref="value-track-kind-commentary">`commentary`</dfn>" | Commentary on the primary audio or video track, e.g. a director's commentary. | Audio and video. |
| "" (empty string) | No explicit kind, or the kind given by the track's metadata is not recognised by the user agent. | Audio and video. |

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-audiotrack-label" data-anolis-xref="dom-AudioTrack-label">`AudioTrack.label`</dfn> and <dfn id="173.html_dom-videotrack-label" data-anolis-xref="dom-VideoTrack-label">`VideoTrack.label`</dfn> attributes must return the label of the track, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-audiotrack-language" data-anolis-xref="dom-AudioTrack-language">`AudioTrack.language`</dfn> and <dfn id="173.html_dom-videotrack-language" data-anolis-xref="dom-VideoTrack-language">`VideoTrack.language`</dfn> attributes must return the BCP 47 language tag of the language of the track, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise. If the user agent is not able to express that language as a BCP 47 language tag (for example because the language information in the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource)'s format is a free-form string without a defined interpretation), then the method must return the empty string, as if the track had no language.

Source attribute values for id, kind, label and language of multitrack audio and video tracks as described for the relevant [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) format. [[INBANDTRACKS]](#173.html_refsINBANDTRACKS)

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-audiotrack-enabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-AudioTrack-enabled">`AudioTrack.enabled`</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return true if the track is currently enabled, and false otherwise. On setting, it must enable the track if the new value is true, and disable it otherwise. (If the track is no longer in an [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) object, then the track being enabled or disabled has no effect beyond changing the value of the attribute on the [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack) object.)

Whenever an audio track in an [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) is enabled or disabled, the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`change`](#173.html_event-media-change) at the [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) object.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-videotracklist-selectedindex" data-anolis-xref="dom-VideoTrackList-selectedIndex">`VideoTrackList.selectedIndex`</dfn> attribute must return the index of the currently selected track, if any. If the [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object does not currently represent any tracks, or if none of the tracks are selected, it must instead return ?1.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-videotrack-selected" data-anolis-xref="dom-VideoTrack-selected">`VideoTrack.selected`</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return true if the track is currently selected, and false otherwise. On setting, it must select the track if the new value is true, and unselect it otherwise. If the track is in a [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist), then all the other [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) objects in that list must be unselected. (If the track is no longer in a [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object, then the track being selected or unselected has no effect beyond changing the value of the attribute on the [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack) object.)

Whenever a track in a [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) that was previously not selected is selected, the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`change`](#173.html_event-media-change) at the [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) object. This [task](#173.html_concept-task) must be [queued](#173.html_queue-a-task) before the [task](#173.html_concept-task) that fires the [`resize`](#173.html_event-media-resize) event, if any.

* * *

The following are the [event handlers](#173.html_event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#173.html_event-handler-event-type)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#173.html_event-handler-idl-attributes), by all objects implementing the [`AudioTrackList`](#173.html_audiotracklist) and [`VideoTrackList`](#173.html_videotracklist) interfaces:

| [Event handler](#173.html_event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#173.html_event-handler-event-type) |
| --- | --- |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-tracklist-onchange" data-anolis-xref="handler-TrackList-onchange">`onchange`</dfn> | [`change`](#173.html_event-media-change) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-tracklist-onaddtrack" data-anolis-xref="handler-TrackList-onaddtrack">`onaddtrack`</dfn> | [`addtrack`](#173.html_event-media-addtrack) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-tracklist-onremovetrack" data-anolis-xref="handler-TrackList-onremovetrack">`onremovetrack`</dfn> | [`removetrack`](#173.html_event-media-removetrack) |

* * *

The [task source](#173.html_task-source) for the [tasks](#173.html_concept-task) listed in this section is the [DOM manipulation task source](#173.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

###### 4.7.10.10.2 Selecting specific audio and video tracks declaratively

The [`audioTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-audiotracks) and [`videoTracks`](#173.html_dom-media-videotracks) attributes allow scripts to select which track should play, but it is also possible to select specific tracks declaratively, by specifying particular tracks in the fragment identifier of the URL of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource). The format of the fragment identifier depends on the [MIME type](#173.html_mime-type) of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource). [[RFC2046]](#173.html_refsRFC2046) [[URL]](#173.html_refsURL)

In this example, a video that uses a format that supports the Media Fragments URI fragment identifier syntax is embedded in such a way that the alternative angles labeled "Alternative" are enabled instead of the default video track. [[MEDIAFRAG]](#173.html_refsMEDIAFRAG)

```
<video src="myvideo#track=Alternative"></video>
```

##### 4.7.10.11 Synchronising multiple media elements

###### 4.7.10.11.1 Introduction

Each [media element](#173.html_media-element) can have a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller). A [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is an object that coordinates the playback of multiple [media elements](#173.html_media-element), for instance so that a sign-language interpreter track can be overlaid on a video track, with the two being kept in sync.

By default, a [media element](#173.html_media-element) has no [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller). An implicit [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) can be assigned using the [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) content attribute. An explicit [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) can be assigned directly using the [`controller`](#173.html_dom-media-controller) IDL attribute.

[Media elements](#173.html_media-element) with a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) are said to be *slaved* to their controller. The [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) modifies the playback rate and the playback volume of each of the [media elements](#173.html_media-element) slaved to it, and ensures that when any of its slaved [media elements](#173.html_media-element) unexpectedly stall, the others are stopped at the same time.

When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is slaved to a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller), its playback rate is fixed to that of the other tracks in the same [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller), and any looping is disabled.

###### 4.7.10.11.2 Media controllers

```
enum MediaControllerPlaybackState { "waiting", "playing", "ended" };
[Constructor]
interface MediaController : EventTarget {
  readonly attribute unsigned short readyState; // uses HTMLMediaElement.readyState's values

  readonly attribute TimeRanges buffered;
  readonly attribute TimeRanges seekable;
  readonly attribute unrestricted double duration;
           attribute double currentTime;

  readonly attribute boolean paused;
  readonly attribute MediaControllerPlaybackState playbackState;
  readonly attribute TimeRanges played;
  void pause();
  void unpause();
  void play(); // calls play() on all media elements as well

           attribute double defaultPlaybackRate;
           attribute double playbackRate;

           attribute double volume;
           attribute boolean muted;

           attribute EventHandler onemptied;
           attribute EventHandler onloadedmetadata;
           attribute EventHandler onloadeddata;
           attribute EventHandler oncanplay;
           attribute EventHandler oncanplaythrough;
           attribute EventHandler onplaying;
           attribute EventHandler onended;
           attribute EventHandler onwaiting;

           attribute EventHandler ondurationchange;
           attribute EventHandler ontimeupdate;
           attribute EventHandler onplay;
           attribute EventHandler onpause;
           attribute EventHandler onratechange;
           attribute EventHandler onvolumechange;
};
```

`controller` = new [`MediaController`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller)()

Returns a new [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object.

`media` . [`controller`](#173.html_dom-media-controller) [ = `controller` ]

Returns the current [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) for the [media element](#173.html_media-element), if any; returns null otherwise.

Can be set, to set an explicit [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller). Doing so removes the [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) attribute, if any.

`controller` . [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-readystate)

Returns the state that the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) was in the last time it fired events as a result of [reporting the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state). The values of this attribute are the same as for the [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) attribute of [media elements](#173.html_media-element).

`controller` . [`buffered`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-buffered)

Returns a [`TimeRanges`](#173.html_timeranges) object that represents the intersection of the time ranges for which the user agent has all relevant media data for all the slaved [media elements](#173.html_media-element).

`controller` . [`seekable`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-seekable)

Returns a [`TimeRanges`](#173.html_timeranges) object that represents the intersection of the time ranges into which the user agent can seek for all the slaved [media elements](#173.html_media-element).

`controller` . [`duration`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-duration)

Returns the difference between the earliest playable moment and the latest playable moment (not considering whether the data in question is actually buffered or directly seekable, but not including time in the future for infinite streams). Will return zero if there is no media.

`controller` . [`currentTime`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-currenttime) [ = `value` ]

Returns the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position), in seconds, as a position between zero time and the current [`duration`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-duration).

Can be set, to seek to the given time.

`controller` . [`paused`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-paused)

Returns true if playback is paused; false otherwise. When this attribute is true, any [media element](#173.html_media-element) slaved to this controller will be stopped.

`controller` . [`playbackState`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-playbackstate)

Returns the state that the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) was in the last time it fired events as a result of [reporting the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state). The value of this attribute is either "[`playing`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-playing)", indicating that the media is actively playing, "[`ended`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-ended)", indicating that the media is not playing because playback has reached the end of all the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements), or "[`waiting`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-waiting)", indicating that the media is not playing for some other reason (e.g. the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is paused).

`controller` . [`pause`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-pause)()

Sets the [`paused`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-paused) attribute to true.

`controller` . [`unpause`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-unpause)()

Sets the [`paused`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-paused) attribute to false.

`controller` . [`play`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-play)()

Sets the [`paused`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-paused) attribute to false and invokes the [`play()`](#173.html_dom-media-play) method of each [slaved media element](#173.html_slaved-media-elements).

`controller` . [`played`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-played)

Returns a [`TimeRanges`](#173.html_timeranges) object that represents the union of the time ranges in all the slaved [media elements](#173.html_media-element) that have been played.

`controller` . [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-defaultplaybackrate) [ = `value` ]

Returns the default rate of playback.

Can be set, to change the default rate of playback.

This default rate has no direct effect on playback, but if the user switches to a fast-forward mode, when they return to the normal playback mode, it is expected that rate of playback ([`playbackRate`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-playbackrate)) will be returned to this default rate.

`controller` . [`playbackRate`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-playbackrate) [ = `value` ]

Returns the current rate of playback.

Can be set, to change the rate of playback.

`controller` . [`volume`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-volume) [ = `value` ]

Returns the current playback volume multiplier, as a number in the range 0.0 to 1.0, where 0.0 is the quietest and 1.0 the loudest.

Can be set, to change the volume multiplier.

Throws an [`IndexSizeError`](#173.html_indexsizeerror) exception if the new value is not in the range 0.0 .. 1.0.

`controller` . [`muted`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-muted) [ = `value` ]

Returns true if all audio is muted (regardless of other attributes either on the controller or on any [media elements](#173.html_media-element) slaved to this controller), and false otherwise.

Can be set, to change whether the audio is muted or not.

A [media element](#173.html_media-element) can have a <dfn id="173.html_current-media-controller">current media controller</dfn>, which is a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object. When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is created without a [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) attribute, it does not have a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller). (If it is created *with* such an attribute, then that attribute initializes the [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), as defined below.)

The <dfn id="173.html_slaved-media-elements">slaved media elements</dfn> of a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) are the [media elements](#173.html_media-element) whose [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) is that [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller). All the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) of a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) must use the same clock for their definition of their [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline)'s unit time. When the user agent is required to act on each [slaved media element](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) in turn, they must be processed in the order that they were last associated with the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

* * *

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-controller" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-controller">`controller`</dfn> attribute on a [media element](#173.html_media-element), on getting, must return the element's [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), if any, or null otherwise. On setting, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `m` be the [media element](#173.html_media-element) in question.

2.  Let `old controller` be `m`'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), if it currently has one, and null otherwise.

3.  Let `new controller` be null.

4.  Let `m` have no [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), if it currently has one.

5.  Remove the element's [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) content attribute, if any.

6.  If the new value is null, then jump to the *update controllers* step below.

7.  Let `m`'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) be the new value.

8.  Let `new controller` be `m`'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

9.  [Bring the media element up to speed with its new media controller](#173.html_bring-the-media-element-up-to-speed-with-its-new-media-controller).

10.  *Update controllers*: If `old controller` and `new controller` are the same (whether both null or both the same controller) then abort these steps.

11.  If `old controller` is not null and still has one or more [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements), then [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for `old controller`.

12.  If `new controller` is not null, then [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for `new controller`.

* * *

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController">`MediaController()`</dfn> constructor, when invoked, must return a newly created [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object.

* * *

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-readystate" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-readyState">`readyState`</dfn> attribute must return the value to which it was most recently set. When the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object is created, the attribute must be set to the value 0 ([`HAVE_NOTHING`](#173.html_dom-media-have_nothing)). The value is updated by the [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) algorithm below.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-seekable" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-seekable">`seekable`</dfn> attribute must return a new static [normalized `TimeRanges` object](#173.html_normalized-timeranges-object) that represents the intersection of the ranges of the [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) of the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) that the user agent is able to seek to, at the time the attribute is evaluated.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-buffered" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-buffered">`buffered`</dfn> attribute must return a new static [normalized `TimeRanges` object](#173.html_normalized-timeranges-object) that represents the intersection of the ranges of the [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) of the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) that the user agent has buffered, at the time the attribute is evaluated. Users agents must accurately determine the ranges available, even for media streams where this can only be determined by tedious inspection.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-duration" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-duration">`duration`</dfn> attribute must return the [media controller duration](#173.html_media-controller-duration).

Every 15 to 250ms, or whenever the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller duration](#173.html_media-controller-duration) changes, whichever happens least often, the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`durationchange`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-durationchange) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller). If the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller duration](#173.html_media-controller-duration) decreases such that the [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position) is greater than the [media controller duration](#173.html_media-controller-duration), the user agent must immediately [seek the media controller](#173.html_seek-the-media-controller) to [media controller duration](#173.html_media-controller-duration).

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-currenttime" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-currentTime">`currentTime`</dfn> attribute must return the [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position) on getting, and on setting must [seek the media controller](#173.html_seek-the-media-controller) to the new value.

Every 15 to 250ms, or whenever the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position) changes, whichever happens least often, the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-timeupdate) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

* * *

When a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is created it is a <dfn id="173.html_playing-media-controller">playing media controller</dfn>. It can be changed into a <dfn id="173.html_paused-media-controller">paused media controller</dfn> and back either via the user agent's user interface (when the element is [exposing a user interface to the user](#173.html_expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user)) or by script using the APIs defined in this section (see below).

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-paused" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-paused">`paused`</dfn> attribute must return true if the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object is a [paused media controller](#173.html_paused-media-controller), and false otherwise.

When the <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-pause" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-pause">`pause()`</dfn> method is invoked, if the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is a [playing media controller](#173.html_playing-media-controller) then the user agent must change the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) into a [paused media controller](#173.html_paused-media-controller), [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`pause`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-pause) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller), and then [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

When the <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-unpause" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-unpause">`unpause()`</dfn> method is invoked, if the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is a [paused media controller](#173.html_paused-media-controller), the user agent must change the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) into a [playing media controller](#173.html_playing-media-controller), [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`play`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-play) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller), and then [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

When the <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-play" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-play">`play()`</dfn> method is invoked, the user agent must invoke the [`play()`](#173.html_dom-media-play) method of each [slaved media element](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) in turn, and then invoke the [`unpause`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-unpause) method of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-playbackstate" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-playbackState">`playbackState`</dfn> attribute must return the value to which it was most recently set. When the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object is created, the attribute must be set to the value "[`waiting`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-waiting)". The value is updated by the [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) algorithm below.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-played" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-played">`played`</dfn> attribute must return a new static [normalized `TimeRanges` object](#173.html_normalized-timeranges-object) that represents the union of the ranges of points on the [media timelines](#173.html_media-timeline) of the [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) of the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) that the user agent has so far reached through the usual monotonic increase of their [current playback positions](#173.html_current-playback-position) during normal playback, at the time the attribute is evaluated.

* * *

A [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) has a <dfn id="173.html_media-controller-default-playback-rate">media controller default playback rate</dfn> and a <dfn id="173.html_media-controller-playback-rate">media controller playback rate</dfn>, which must both be set to 1.0 when the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object is created.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-defaultplaybackrate" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-defaultPlaybackRate">`defaultPlaybackRate`</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller default playback rate](#173.html_media-controller-default-playback-rate), and on setting, must set the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller default playback rate](#173.html_media-controller-default-playback-rate) to the new value, then [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`ratechange`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-ratechange) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-playbackrate" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-playbackRate">`playbackRate`</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller playback rate](#173.html_media-controller-playback-rate), and on setting, must set the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller playback rate](#173.html_media-controller-playback-rate) to the new value, then [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`ratechange`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-ratechange) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

* * *

A [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) has a <dfn id="173.html_media-controller-volume-multiplier">media controller volume multiplier</dfn>, which must be set to 1.0 when the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object is created, and a <dfn id="173.html_media-controller-mute-override">media controller mute override</dfn>, much must initially be false.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-volume" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-volume">`volume`</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller volume multiplier](#173.html_media-controller-volume-multiplier), and on setting, if the new value is in the range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive, must set the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller volume multiplier](#173.html_media-controller-volume-multiplier) to the new value and [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`volumechange`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-volumechange) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller). If the new value is outside the range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive, then, on setting, an [`IndexSizeError`](#173.html_indexsizeerror) exception must be thrown instead.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-muted" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-muted">`muted`</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller mute override](#173.html_media-controller-mute-override), and on setting, must set the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller mute override](#173.html_media-controller-mute-override) to the new value and [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`volumechange`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-volumechange) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

* * *

The [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) of all the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) of a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) have a defined temporal relationship which provides relative offsets between the zero time of each such [media resource](#173.html_media-resource): for [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) with a [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset), their relative offsets are the difference between their [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset); the zero times of all the [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) without a [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset) are not offset from each other (i.e. the origins of their timelines are cotemporal); and finally, the zero time of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) with the earliest [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset) (if any) is not offset from the zero times of the [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) without a [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset) (i.e. the origins of [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) without a [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset) are further cotemporal with the earliest defined point on the timeline of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) with the earliest [timeline offset](#173.html_timeline-offset)).

The <dfn id="173.html_media-resource-end-position">media resource end position</dfn> of a [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) in a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is defined as follows: if the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) has a finite and known duration, the [media resource end position](#173.html_media-resource-end-position) is the duration of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource)'s timeline (the last defined position on that timeline); otherwise, the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource)'s duration is infinite or unknown, and the [media resource end position](#173.html_media-resource-end-position) is the time of the last frame of [media data](#173.html_media-data) currently available for that [media resource](#173.html_media-resource).

Each [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) also has its own defined timeline. On this timeline, all the [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) of all the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) are temporally aligned according to their defined offsets. The <dfn id="173.html_media-controller-duration">media controller duration</dfn> of that [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is the time from the earliest [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position), relative to this [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) timeline, of any of the [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) of the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller), to the time of the latest [media resource end position](#173.html_media-resource-end-position) of the [media resources](#173.html_media-resource) of the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller), again relative to this [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) timeline.

Each [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) has a <dfn id="173.html_media-controller-position">media controller position</dfn>. This is the time on the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s timeline at which the user agent is trying to play the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements). When a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is created, its [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position) is initially zero.

When the user agent is to <dfn id="173.html_bring-the-media-element-up-to-speed-with-its-new-media-controller" data-anolis-xref="bring the media element up to speed with its new media
  controller">bring a media element up to speed with its new media controller</dfn>, it must [seek](#173.html_dom-media-seek) that [media element](#173.html_media-element) to the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position) relative to the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s timeline.

When the user agent is to <dfn id="173.html_seek-the-media-controller">seek the media controller</dfn> to a particular `new playback position`, it must follow these steps:

1.  If the `new playback position` is less than zero, then set it to zero.

2.  If the `new playback position` is greater than the [media controller duration](#173.html_media-controller-duration), then set it to the [media controller duration](#173.html_media-controller-duration).

3.  Set the [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position) to the `new playback position`.

4.  [Seek](#173.html_dom-media-seek) each [slaved media element](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) to the `new playback position` relative to the [media element](#173.html_media-element) timeline.

A [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is a <dfn id="173.html_restrained-media-controller">restrained media controller</dfn> if the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is a [playing media controller](#173.html_playing-media-controller), and none of its [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) are [blocked media elements](#173.html_blocked-media-element), but either at least one of its [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) whose [autoplaying flag](#173.html_autoplaying-flag) is true still has its [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute set to true, or, all of its [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) have their [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute set to true.

A [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is a <dfn id="173.html_blocked-media-controller">blocked media controller</dfn> if the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is a [paused media controller](#173.html_paused-media-controller), or if any of its [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) are [blocked media elements](#173.html_blocked-media-element), or if any of its [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) whose [autoplaying flag](#173.html_autoplaying-flag) is true still have their [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute set to true, or if all of its [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) have their [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute set to true.

A [media element](#173.html_media-element) is <dfn id="173.html_blocked-on-its-media-controller">blocked on its media controller</dfn> if the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is a [blocked media controller](#173.html_blocked-media-controller), or if its [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position) is either before the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource)'s [earliest possible position](#173.html_earliest-possible-position) relative to the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s timeline or after the end of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) relative to the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s timeline.

When a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is not a [blocked media controller](#173.html_blocked-media-controller) and it has at least one [slaved media element](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) whose [`Document`](#173.html_document) is a [fully active](#173.html_fully-active) [`Document`](#173.html_document), the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position) must increase monotonically at [media controller playback rate](#173.html_media-controller-playback-rate) units of time on the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s timeline per unit time of the clock used by its [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements).

When the zero point on the timeline of a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) moves relative to the timelines of the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) by a time difference `ΔT`, the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position) must be decremented by `ΔT`.

In some situations, e.g. when playing back a live stream without buffering anything, the [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position) would increase monotonically as described above at the same rate as the `ΔT` described in the previous paragraph decreases it, with the end result that for all intents and purposes, the [media controller position](#173.html_media-controller-position) would appear to remain constant (probably with the value 0).

* * *

A [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) has a <dfn id="173.html_most-recently-reported-readiness-state">most recently reported readiness state</dfn>, which is a number from 0 to 4 derived from the numbers used for the [media element](#173.html_media-element) `readyState` attribute, and a <dfn id="173.html_most-recently-reported-playback-state">most recently reported playback state</dfn>, which is either *playing*, *waiting*, or *ended*.

When a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is created, its [most recently reported readiness state](#173.html_most-recently-reported-readiness-state) must be set to 0, and its [most recently reported playback state](#173.html_most-recently-reported-playback-state) must be set to *waiting*.

When a user agent is required to <dfn id="173.html_report-the-controller-state">report the controller state</dfn> for a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller), the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  If the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) has no [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements), let `new readiness state` be 0.

    Otherwise, let it have the lowest value of the [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) IDL attributes of all of its [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements).

2.  If the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [most recently reported readiness state](#173.html_most-recently-reported-readiness-state) is less than the `new readiness state`, then run these substeps:

    1.  Let `next state` be the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [most recently reported readiness state](#173.html_most-recently-reported-readiness-state).

    2.  *Loop*: Increment `next state` by one.

    3.  [Queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to run the following steps:

        1.  Set the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-readystate) attribute to the value `next state`.

        2.  [Fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object, whose name is the event name corresponding to the value of `next state` given in the table below.

    4.  If `next state` is less than `new readiness state`, then return to the step labeled *loop*.

    Otherwise, if the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [most recently reported readiness state](#173.html_most-recently-reported-readiness-state) is greater than `new readiness state` then [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object, whose name is the event name corresponding to the value of `new readiness state` given in the table below.

    | Value of `new readiness state` | Event name |
    | --- | --- |
    | 0 | [`emptied`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-emptied) |
    | 1 | [`loadedmetadata`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-loadedmetadata) |
    | 2 | [`loadeddata`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-loadeddata) |
    | 3 | [`canplay`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-canplay) |
    | 4 | [`canplaythrough`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-canplaythrough) |

3.  Let the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [most recently reported readiness state](#173.html_most-recently-reported-readiness-state) be `new readiness state`.

4.  Initialize `new playback state` by setting it to the state given for the first matching condition from the following list:

    If the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) has no [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements)

    Let `new playback state` be *waiting*.

    If all of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) have [ended playback](#173.html_ended-playback) and the [media controller playback rate](#173.html_media-controller-playback-rate) is positive or zero

    Let `new playback state` be *ended*.

    If the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) is a [blocked media controller](#173.html_blocked-media-controller)

    Let `new playback state` be *waiting*.

    Otherwise

    Let `new playback state` be *playing*.

5.  If the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [most recently reported playback state](#173.html_most-recently-reported-playback-state) is not equal to `new playback state` and the `new playback state` is *ended*, then [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) that, if the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object is a [playing media controller](#173.html_playing-media-controller), and all of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) have still [ended playback](#173.html_ended-playback), and the [media controller playback rate](#173.html_media-controller-playback-rate) is still positive or zero, changes the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object to a [paused media controller](#173.html_paused-media-controller) and then [fires a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`pause`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-pause) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object.

6.  If the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [most recently reported playback state](#173.html_most-recently-reported-playback-state) is not equal to `new playback state` then [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to run the following steps:

    1.  Set the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [`playbackState`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-playbackstate) attribute to the value given in the second column of the row of the following table whose first column contains the `new playback state`.

    2.  [Fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) at the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object, whose name is the value given in the third column of the row of the following table whose first column contains the `new playback state`.

    | New playback state | New value for [`playbackState`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-playbackstate) | Event name |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | *playing* | "<dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-playing" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-playing">`playing`</dfn>" | [`playing`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-playing) |
    | *waiting* | "<dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-waiting" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-waiting">`waiting`</dfn>" | [`waiting`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-waiting) |
    | *ended* | "<dfn id="173.html_dom-mediacontroller-ended" data-anolis-xref="dom-MediaController-ended">`ended`</dfn>" | [`ended`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-ended) |

7.  Let the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s [most recently reported playback state](#173.html_most-recently-reported-playback-state) be `new playback state`.

* * *

The following are the [event handlers](#173.html_event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#173.html_event-handler-event-type)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#173.html_event-handler-idl-attributes), by all objects implementing the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) interface:

| [Event handler](#173.html_event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#173.html_event-handler-event-type) |
| --- | --- |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-onemptied" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-onemptied">`onemptied`</dfn> | [`emptied`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-emptied) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-onloadedmetadata" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-onloadedmetadata">`onloadedmetadata`</dfn> | [`loadedmetadata`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-loadedmetadata) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-onloadeddata" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-onloadeddata">`onloadeddata`</dfn> | [`loadeddata`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-loadeddata) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-oncanplay" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-oncanplay">`oncanplay`</dfn> | [`canplay`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-canplay) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-oncanplaythrough" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-oncanplaythrough">`oncanplaythrough`</dfn> | [`canplaythrough`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-canplaythrough) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-onplaying" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-onplaying">`onplaying`</dfn> | [`playing`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-playing) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-onended" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-onended">`onended`</dfn> | [`ended`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-ended) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-onwaiting" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-onwaiting">`onwaiting`</dfn> | [`waiting`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-waiting) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-ondurationchange" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-ondurationchange">`ondurationchange`</dfn> | [`durationchange`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-durationchange) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-ontimeupdate" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-ontimeupdate">`ontimeupdate`</dfn> | [`timeupdate`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-timeupdate) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-onplay" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-onplay">`onplay`</dfn> | [`play`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-play) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-onpause" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-onpause">`onpause`</dfn> | [`pause`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-pause) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-onratechange" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-onratechange">`onratechange`</dfn> | [`ratechange`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-ratechange) |
| <dfn id="173.html_handler-mediacontroller-onvolumechange" data-anolis-xref="handler-MediaController-onvolumechange">`onvolumechange`</dfn> | [`volumechange`](#173.html_event-mediacontroller-volumechange) |

* * *

The [task source](#173.html_task-source) for the [tasks](#173.html_concept-task) listed in this section is the [DOM manipulation task source](#173.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

###### 4.7.10.11.3 Assigning a media controller declaratively

The <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-mediagroup" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-mediagroup">`mediagroup`</dfn> content attribute on [media elements](#173.html_media-element) can be used to link multiple [media elements](#173.html_media-element) together by implicitly creating a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller). The value is text; [media elements](#173.html_media-element) with the same value are automatically linked by the user agent.

When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is created with a [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) attribute, and when a [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) attribute is set, changed, or removed, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `m` be the [media element](#173.html_media-element) in question.

2.  Let `old controller` be `m`'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), if it currently has one, and null otherwise.

3.  Let `new controller` be null.

4.  Let `m` have no [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), if it currently has one.

5.  If `m`'s [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) attribute is being removed, then jump to the *update controllers* step below.

6.  If there is another [media element](#173.html_media-element) whose [`Document`](#173.html_document) is the same as `m`'s [`Document`](#173.html_document) (even if one or both of these elements are not actually [*in* the `Document`](#173.html_in-a-document)), and which also has a [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) attribute, and whose [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) attribute has the same value as the new value of `m`'s [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) attribute, then let `controller` be that [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

    Otherwise, let `controller` be a newly created [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

7.  Let `m`'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) be `controller`.

8.  Let `new controller` be `m`'s [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller).

9.  [Bring the media element up to speed with its new media controller](#173.html_bring-the-media-element-up-to-speed-with-its-new-media-controller).

10.  *Update controllers*: If `old controller` and `new controller` are the same (whether both null or both the same controller) then abort these steps.

11.  If `old controller` is not null and still has one or more [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements), then [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for `old controller`.

12.  If `new controller` is not null, then [report the controller state](#173.html_report-the-controller-state) for `new controller`.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-mediagroup" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-mediaGroup">`mediaGroup`</dfn> IDL attribute on [media elements](#173.html_media-element) must [reflect](#173.html_reflect) the [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) content attribute.

Multiple [media elements](#173.html_media-element) referencing the same [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) will share a single network request. This can be used to efficiently play two (video) tracks from the same [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) in two different places on the screen. Used with the [`mediagroup`](#173.html_attr-media-mediagroup) attribute, these elements can also be kept synchronised.

In this example, a sign-languge interpreter track from a movie file is overlaid on the primary video track of that same video file using two [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) elements, some CSS, and an implicit [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller):

```
<article>
 <style>
  div { margin: 1em auto; position: relative; width: 400px; height: 300px; }
  video { position; absolute; bottom: 0; right: 0; }
  video:first-child { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
  video:last-child { width: 30%; }
 </style>
 <div>
  <video src="movie.vid#track=Video&amp;track=English" autoplay controls mediagroup=movie></video>
  <video src="movie.vid#track=sign" autoplay mediagroup=movie></video>
 </div>
</article>
```

##### 4.7.10.12 Timed text tracks

###### 4.7.10.12.1 Text track model

A [media element](#173.html_media-element) can have a group of associated <dfn id="173.html_text-track" data-anolis-xref="text track">text tracks</dfn>, known as the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s <dfn id="173.html_list-of-text-tracks">list of text tracks</dfn>. The [text tracks](#173.html_text-track) are sorted as follows:
