##### 4.7.10.13 User interface

The <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-controls" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-controls">`controls`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#173.html_boolean-attribute). If present, it indicates that the author has not provided a scripted controller and would like the user agent to provide its own set of controls.

If the attribute is present, or if [scripting is disabled](#173.html_concept-n-noscript) for the [media element](#173.html_media-element), then the user agent should <dfn id="173.html_expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user">expose a user interface to the user</dfn>. This user interface should include features to begin playback, pause playback, seek to an arbitrary position in the content (if the content supports arbitrary seeking), change the volume, change the display of closed captions or embedded sign-language tracks, select different audio tracks or turn on audio descriptions, and show the media content in manners more suitable to the user (e.g. full-screen video or in an independent resizable window). Other controls may also be made available.

If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), then the user agent should expose audio tracks from all the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) (although avoiding duplicates if the same [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) is being used several times). If a [media resource](#173.html_media-resource)'s audio track exposed in this way has no known name, and it is the only audio track for a particular [media element](#173.html_media-element), the user agent should use the element's [`title`](#173.html_attr-title) attribute, if any, as the name (or as part of the name) of that track.

Even when the attribute is absent, however, user agents may provide controls to affect playback of the media resource (e.g. play, pause, seeking, and volume controls), but such features should not interfere with the page's normal rendering. For example, such features could be exposed in the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s context menu. The user agent may implement this simply by [exposing a user interface to the user](#173.html_expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user) as described above (as if the [`controls`](#173.html_attr-media-controls) attribute was present).

If the user agent [exposes a user interface to the user](#173.html_expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user) by displaying controls over the [media element](#173.html_media-element), then the user agent should suppress any user interaction events while the user agent is interacting with this interface. (For example, if the user clicks on a video's playback control, `mousedown` events and so forth would not simultaneously be fired at elements on the page.)

Where possible (specifically, for starting, stopping, pausing, and unpausing playback, for seeking, for changing the rate of playback, for fast-forwarding or rewinding, for listing, enabling, and disabling text tracks, and for muting or changing the volume of the audio), user interface features exposed by the user agent must be implemented in terms of the DOM API described above, so that, e.g., all the same events fire.

When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), the user agent's user interface for pausing and unpausing playback, for seeking, for changing the rate of playback, for fast-forwarding or rewinding, and for muting or changing the volume of audio of the entire group must be implemented in terms of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) API exposed on that [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller). When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), and all the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) of that [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) are paused, the user agent should also unpause all the [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements) when the user invokes a user agent interface control for beginning playback.

The "play" function in the user agent's interface must set the `playbackRate` attribute to the value of the `defaultPlaybackRate` attribute before invoking the `play()` method. When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), the attributes and method with those names on that [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object must be used. Otherwise, the attributes and method with those names on the [media element](#173.html_media-element) itself must be used.

Features such as fast-forward or rewind must be implemented by only changing the `playbackRate` attribute (and not the `defaultPlaybackRate` attribute). Again, when a [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), the attributes with those names on that [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object must be used; otherwise, the attributes with those names on the [media element](#173.html_media-element) itself must be used.

When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), seeking must be implemented in terms of the [`currentTime`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-currenttime) attribute on that [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object. Otherwise, the user agent must directly [seek](#173.html_dom-media-seek) to the requested position in the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline). For media resources where seeking to an arbitrary position would be slow, user agents are encouraged to use the *approximate-for-speed* flag when seeking in response to the user manipulating an approximate position interface such as a seek bar.

When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), user agents may additionally provide the user with controls that directly manipulate an individual [media element](#173.html_media-element) without affecting the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller), but such features are considered relatively advanced and unlikely to be useful to most users.

The [activation behavior](#173.html_activation-behavior) of a [media element](#173.html_media-element) that is [exposing a user interface to the user](#173.html_expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user) must be to run the following steps:

1.  If the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), and that [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) is a [restrained media controller](#173.html_restrained-media-controller), then invoke the [`play()`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-play) method of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

2.  Otherwise, if the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), and that [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) is a [paused media controller](#173.html_paused-media-controller), then invoke the [`unpause()`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-unpause) method of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

3.  Otherwise, if the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), then that [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) is a [playing media controller](#173.html_playing-media-controller); invoke the [`pause()`](#173.html_dom-mediacontroller-pause) method of the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller).

4.  Otherwise, the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has no [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller); if the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute is true, then invoke the [`play()`](#173.html_dom-media-play) method on the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

5.  Otherwise, the [media element](#173.html_media-element) has no [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), and the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) attribute is false; invoke the [`pause()`](#173.html_dom-media-pause) method on the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

For the purposes of listing chapters in the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), only [text tracks](#173.html_text-track) in the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s [list of text tracks](#173.html_list-of-text-tracks) that are [showing](#173.html_text-track-showing) and whose [text track kind](#173.html_text-track-kind) is [`chapters`](#173.html_dom-texttrack-kind-chapters) should be used. Such tracks must be interpreted according to the [rules for constructing the chapter tree from a text track](#173.html_rules-for-constructing-the-chapter-tree-from-a-text-track). When seeking in response to a user maniplating a chapter selection interface, user agents should not use the *approximate-for-speed* flag.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-controls" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-controls">`controls`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#173.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

* * *

`media` . [`volume`](#173.html_dom-media-volume) [ = `value` ]

Returns the current playback volume, as a number in the range 0.0 to 1.0, where 0.0 is the quietest and 1.0 the loudest.

Can be set, to change the volume.

Throws an [`IndexSizeError`](#173.html_indexsizeerror) exception if the new value is not in the range 0.0 .. 1.0.

`media` . [`muted`](#173.html_dom-media-muted) [ = `value` ]

Returns true if audio is muted, overriding the [`volume`](#173.html_dom-media-volume) attribute, and false if the [`volume`](#173.html_dom-media-volume) attribute is being honored.

Can be set, to change whether the audio is muted or not.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-volume" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-volume">`volume`</dfn> attribute must return the playback volume of any audio portions of the [media element](#173.html_media-element), in the range 0.0 (silent) to 1.0 (loudest). Initially, the volume should be 1.0, but user agents may remember the last set value across sessions, on a per-site basis or otherwise, so the volume may start at other values. On setting, if the new value is in the range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive, the playback volume of any audio portions of the [media element](#173.html_media-element) must be set to the new value. If the new value is outside the range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive, then, on setting, an [`IndexSizeError`](#173.html_indexsizeerror) exception must be thrown instead.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-muted" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-muted">`muted`</dfn> attribute must return true if the audio output is muted and false otherwise. Initially, the audio output should not be muted (false), but user agents may remember the last set value across sessions, on a per-site basis or otherwise, so the muted state may start as muted (true). On setting, if the new value is true then the audio output should be muted and if the new value is false it should be unmuted.

Whenever either of the values that would be returned by the [`volume`](#173.html_dom-media-volume) and [`muted`](#173.html_dom-media-muted) attributes change, the user agent must [queue a task](#173.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#173.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`volumechange`](#173.html_event-media-volumechange) at the [media element](#173.html_media-element).

An element's <dfn id="173.html_effective-media-volume">effective media volume</dfn> is determined as follows:

1.  If the user has indicated that the user agent is to override the volume of the element, then the element's [effective media volume](#173.html_effective-media-volume) is the volume desired by the user. Abort these steps.

2.  If the element's audio output is muted, the element's [effective media volume](#173.html_effective-media-volume) is zero. Abort these steps.

3.  If the element has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller) and that [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object's [media controller mute override](#173.html_media-controller-mute-override) is true, the element's [effective media volume](#173.html_effective-media-volume) is zero. Abort these steps.

4.  Let `volume` be the playback volume of the audio portions of the [media element](#173.html_media-element), in range 0.0 (silent) to 1.0 (loudest).

5.  If the element has a [current media controller](#173.html_current-media-controller), multiply `volume` by that [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller) object's [media controller volume multiplier](#173.html_media-controller-volume-multiplier).

6.  The element's [effective media volume](#173.html_effective-media-volume) is `volume`, interpreted relative to the range 0.0 to 1.0, with 0.0 being silent, and 1.0 being the loudest setting, values in between increasing in loudness. The range need not be linear. The loudest setting may be lower than the system's loudest possible setting; for example the user could have set a maximum volume.

The <dfn id="173.html_attr-media-muted" data-anolis-xref="attr-media-muted">`muted`</dfn> attribute on [media elements](#173.html_media-element) is a [boolean attribute](#173.html_boolean-attribute) that controls the default state of the audio output of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource), potentially overriding user preferences.

When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) is created, if it has a [`muted`](#173.html_attr-media-muted) attribute specified, the user agent must mute the [media element](#173.html_media-element)'s audio output, overriding any user preference.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-media-defaultmuted" data-anolis-xref="dom-media-defaultMuted">`defaultMuted`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#173.html_reflect) the [`muted`](#173.html_attr-media-muted) content attribute.

This attribute has no dynamic effect (it only controls the default state of the element).

This video (an advertisement) autoplays, but to avoid annoying users, it does so without sound, and allows the user to turn the sound on.

```
<video src="adverts.cgi?kind=video" controls autoplay loop muted></video>
```

##### 4.7.10.14 Time ranges

Objects implementing the [`TimeRanges`](#173.html_timeranges) interface represent a list of ranges (periods) of time.

```
interface TimeRanges {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  double start(unsigned long index);
  double end(unsigned long index);
};
```

`media` . [`length`](#173.html_dom-timeranges-length)

Returns the number of ranges in the object.

`time` = `media` . [`start`](#173.html_dom-timeranges-start)(`index`)

Returns the time for the start of the range with the given index.

Throws an [`IndexSizeError`](#173.html_indexsizeerror) exception if the index is out of range.

`time` = `media` . [`end`](#173.html_dom-timeranges-end)(`index`)

Returns the time for the end of the range with the given index.

Throws an [`IndexSizeError`](#173.html_indexsizeerror) exception if the index is out of range.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-timeranges-length" data-anolis-xref="dom-TimeRanges-length">`length`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the number of ranges represented by the object.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-timeranges-start" data-anolis-xref="dom-TimeRanges-start">`start(``index``)`</dfn> method must return the position of the start of the `index`th range represented by the object, in seconds measured from the start of the timeline that the object covers.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-timeranges-end" data-anolis-xref="dom-TimeRanges-end">`end(``index``)`</dfn> method must return the position of the end of the `index`th range represented by the object, in seconds measured from the start of the timeline that the object covers.

These methods must throw [`IndexSizeError`](#173.html_indexsizeerror) exceptions if called with an `index` argument greater than or equal to the number of ranges represented by the object.

When a [`TimeRanges`](#173.html_timeranges) object is said to be a <dfn id="173.html_normalized-timeranges-object">normalized `TimeRanges` object</dfn>, the ranges it represents must obey the following criteria:

*   The start of a range must be greater than the end of all earlier ranges.
*   The start of a range must be less than the end of that same range.

In other words, the ranges in such an object are ordered, don't overlap, aren't empty, and don't touch (adjacent ranges are folded into one bigger range).

Ranges in a [`TimeRanges`](#173.html_timeranges) object must be inclusive.

Thus, the end of a range would be equal to the start of a following adjacent (touching but not overlapping) range. Similarly, a range covering a whole timeline anchored at zero would have a start equal to zero and an end equal to the duration of the timeline.

The timelines used by the objects returned by the [`buffered`](#173.html_dom-media-buffered), [`seekable`](#173.html_dom-media-seekable) and [`played`](#173.html_dom-media-played) IDL attributes of [media elements](#173.html_media-element) must be that element's [media timeline](#173.html_media-timeline).

##### 4.7.10.15 Event definitions

```
[Constructor(DOMString type, optional TrackEventInit eventInitDict)]
interface TrackEvent : Event {
  readonly attribute (VideoTrack or AudioTrack or TextTrack) track;
};

dictionary TrackEventInit : EventInit {
  (VideoTrack or AudioTrack or TextTrack) track;
};
```

`event` . [`track`](#173.html_dom-trackevent-track)

Returns the track object ([`TextTrack`](#173.html_texttrack), [`AudioTrack`](#173.html_audiotrack), or [`VideoTrack`](#173.html_videotrack)) to which the event relates.

The <dfn id="173.html_dom-trackevent-track" data-anolis-xref="dom-TrackEvent-track">`track`</dfn> attribute must return the value it was initialized to. When the object is created, this attribute must be initialized to null. It represents the context information for the event.

##### 4.7.10.16 Event summary

*This section is non-normative.*

The following events fire on [media elements](#173.html_media-element) as part of the processing model described above:

| Event name | Interface | Fired when... | Preconditions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <dfn id="173.html_event-media-loadstart" data-anolis-xref="event-media-loadstart">`loadstart`</dfn> | [`Event`](#173.html_event) | The user agent begins looking for [media data](#173.html_media-data), as part of the [resource selection algorithm](#173.html_concept-media-load-algorithm). | [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) equals [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#173.html_dom-media-network_loading) |
| <dfn id="173.html_event-media-progress" data-anolis-xref="event-media-progress">`progress`</dfn> | [`Event`](#173.html_event) | The user agent is fetching [media data](#173.html_media-data). | [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) equals [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#173.html_dom-media-network_loading) |
| <dfn id="173.html_event-media-suspend" data-anolis-xref="event-media-suspend">`suspend`</dfn> | [`Event`](#173.html_event) | The user agent is intentionally not currently fetching [media data](#173.html_media-data). | [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) equals [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_idle) |
| <dfn id="173.html_event-media-abort" data-anolis-xref="event-media-abort">`abort`</dfn> | [`Event`](#173.html_event) | The user agent stops fetching the [media data](#173.html_media-data) before it is completely downloaded, but not due to an error. | [`error`](#173.html_dom-media-error) is an object with the code [`MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED`](#173.html_dom-mediaerror-media_err_aborted). [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) equals either [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#173.html_dom-media-network_empty) or [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_idle), depending on when the download was aborted. |
| <dfn id="173.html_event-media-error" data-anolis-xref="event-media-error">`error`</dfn> | [`Event`](#173.html_event) | An error occurs while fetching the [media data](#173.html_media-data). | [`error`](#173.html_dom-media-error) is an object with the code [`MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK`](#173.html_dom-mediaerror-media_err_network) or higher. [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) equals either [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#173.html_dom-media-network_empty) or [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#173.html_dom-media-network_idle), depending on when the download was aborted. |

| <dfn id="173.html_event-media-stalled" data-anolis-xref="event-media-stalled">`stalled`</dfn> | [`Event`](#173.html_event) | The user agent is trying to fetch [media data](#173.html_media-data), but data is unexpectedly not forthcoming. | [`networkState`](#173.html_dom-media-networkstate) is [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#173.html_dom-media-network_loading). |
| <dfn id="173.html_event-media-loadedmetadata" data-anolis-xref="event-media-loadedmetadata">`loadedmetadata`</dfn> | [`Event`](#173.html_event) | The user agent has just determined the duration and dimensions of the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) and [the text tracks are ready](#173.html_the-text-tracks-are-ready). | [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) is newly equal to [`HAVE_METADATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_metadata) or greater for the first time. |
| <dfn id="173.html_event-media-loadeddata" data-anolis-xref="event-media-loadeddata">`loadeddata`</dfn> | [`Event`](#173.html_event) | The user agent can render the [media data](#173.html_media-data) at the [current playback position](#173.html_current-playback-position) for the first time. | [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) newly increased to [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_current_data) or greater for the first time. |
| <dfn id="173.html_event-media-canplay" data-anolis-xref="event-media-canplay">`canplay`</dfn> | [`Event`](#173.html_event) | The user agent can resume playback of the [media data](#173.html_media-data), but estimates that if playback were to be started now, the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) could not be rendered at the current playback rate up to its end without having to stop for further buffering of content. | [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) newly increased to [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data) or greater. |
| <dfn id="173.html_event-media-canplaythrough" data-anolis-xref="event-media-canplaythrough">`canplaythrough`</dfn> | [`Event`](#173.html_event) | The user agent estimates that if playback were to be started now, the [media resource](#173.html_media-resource) could be rendered at the current playback rate all the way to its end without having to stop for further buffering. | [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) is newly equal to [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_enough_data). |
| <dfn id="173.html_event-media-playing" data-anolis-xref="event-media-playing">`playing`</dfn> | [`Event`](#173.html_event) | Playback is ready to start after having been paused or delayed due to lack of [media data](#173.html_media-data). | [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) is newly equal to or greater than [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data) and [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) is false, or [`paused`](#173.html_dom-media-paused) is newly false and [`readyState`](#173.html_dom-media-readystate) is equal to or greater than [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#173.html_dom-media-have_future_data). ##### 4.7.10.17 Security and privacy considerations

The main security and privacy implications of the [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) and [`audio`](#173.html_the-audio-element) elements come from the ability to embed media cross-origin. There are two directions that threats can flow: from hostile content to a victim page, and from a hostile page to victim content.

* * *

If a victim page embeds hostile content, the threat is that the content might contain scripted code that attempts to interact with the [`Document`](#173.html_document) that embeds the content. To avoid this, user agents must ensure that there is no access from the content to the embedding page. In the case of media content that uses DOM concepts, the embedded content must be treated as if it was in its own unrelated [top-level browsing context](#173.html_top-level-browsing-context).

For instance, if an SVG animation was embedded in a [`video`](#173.html_the-video-element) element, the user agent would not give it access to the DOM of the outer page. From the perspective of scripts in the SVG resource, the SVG file would appear to be in a lone top-level browsing context with no parent.

* * *

If a hostile page embeds victim content, the threat is that the embedding page could obtain information from the content that it would not otherwise have access to. The API does expose some information: the existence of the media, its type, its duration, its size, and the performance characteristics of its host. Such information is already potentially problematic, but in practice the same information can more or less be obtained using the [`img`](#173.html_the-img-element) element, and so it has been deemed acceptable.

However, significantly more sensitive information could be obtained if the user agent further exposes metadata within the content such as subtitles or chapter titles. Such information is therefore only exposed if the video resource passes a CORS [resource sharing check](#173.html_resource-sharing-check). The [`crossorigin`](#173.html_attr-media-crossorigin) attribute allows authors to control how this check is performed. [[CORS]](#173.html_refsCORS)

Without this restriction, an attacker could trick a user running within a corporate network into visiting a site that attempts to load a video from a previously leaked location on the corporation's intranet. If such a video included confidential plans for a new product, then being able to read the subtitles would present a serious confidentiality breach.

##### 4.7.10.18 Best practices for authors using media elements

*This section is non-normative.*

Playing audio and video resources on small devices such as set-top boxes or mobile phones is often constrained by limited hardware resources in the device. For example, a device might only support three simultaneous videos. For this reason, it is a good practice to release resources held by [media elements](#173.html_media-element) when they are done playing, either by being very careful about removing all references to the element and allowing it to be garbage collected, or, even better, by removing the element's [`src`](#173.html_attr-media-src) attribute and any [`source`](#173.html_the-source-element) element descendants, and invoking the element's [`load()`](#173.html_dom-media-load) method.

Similarly, when the playback rate is not exactly 1.0, hardware, software, or format limitations can cause video frames to be dropped and audio to be choppy or muted.

##### 4.7.10.19 Best practices for implementors of media elements

*This section is non-normative.*

How accurately various aspects of the [media element](#173.html_media-element) API are implemented is considered a quality-of-implementation issue.

For example, when implementing the `buffered` attribute, how precise an implementation reports the ranges that have been buffered depends on how carefully the user agent inspects the data. Since the API reports ranges as times, but the data is obtained in byte streams, a user agent receiving a variable-bit-rate stream might only be able to determine precise times by actually decoding all of the data. User agents aren't required to do this, however; they can instead return estimates (e.g. based on the average bit rate seen so far) which get revised as more information becomes available.

As a general rule, user agents are urged to be conservative rather than optimistic. For example, it would be bad to report that everything had been buffered when it had not.

Another quality-of-implementation issue would be playing a video backwards when the codec is designed only for forward playback (e.g. there aren't many key frames, and they are far apart, and the intervening frames only have deltas from the previous frame). User agents could do a poor job, e.g. only showing key frames; however, better implementations would do more work and thus do a better job, e.g. actually decoding parts of the video forwards, storing the complete frames, and then playing the frames backwards.

Similarly, while implementations are allowed to drop buffered data at any time (there is no requirement that a user agent keep all the media data obtained for the lifetime of the media element), it is again a quality of implementation issue: user agents with sufficient resources to keep all the data around are encouraged to do so, as this allows for a better user experience. For example, if the user is watching a live stream, a user agent could allow the user only to view the live video; however, a better user agent would buffer everything and allow the user to seek through the earlier material, pause it, play it forwards and backwards, etc.

When multiple tracks are synchronised with a [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller), it is possible for scripts to add and remove media elements from the [`MediaController`](#173.html_mediacontroller)'s list of [slaved media elements](#173.html_slaved-media-elements), even while these tracks are playing. How smoothly the media plays back in such situations is another quality-of-implementation issue.

* * *

When a [media element](#173.html_media-element) that is paused is [removed from a document](#173.html_remove-an-element-from-a-document) and not reinserted before the next time the [event loop](#173.html_event-loop) spins, implementations that are resource constrained are encouraged to take that opportunity to release all hardware resources (like video planes, networking resources, and data buffers) used by the [media element](#173.html_media-element). (User agents still have to keep track of the playback position and so forth, though, in case playback is later restarted.)

#### 4.7.11 The <dfn>`map`</dfn> element

[Categories](#174.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#174.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#174.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Palpable content](#174.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#174.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#174.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#174.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Transparent](#174.html_transparent).

[Content attributes](#174.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#174.html_global-attributes)

[`name`](#174.html_attr-map-name) - Name of [image map](#174.html_image-map) to reference from the [`usemap`](#174.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap) attribute

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#174.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#174.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#174.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#174.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLMapElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString name;
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection areas;
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection images;
};
```

The [`map`](#174.html_the-map-element) element, in conjunction with an [`img`](#174.html_the-img-element) element and any [`area`](#174.html_the-area-element) element descendants, defines an [image map](#174.html_image-map). The element [represents](#174.html_represents) its children.

The <dfn id="174.html_attr-map-name" data-anolis-xref="attr-map-name">`name`</dfn> attribute gives the map a name so that it can be referenced. The attribute must be present and must have a non-empty value with no [space characters](#174.html_space-character). The value of the [`name`](#174.html_attr-map-name) attribute must not be a [compatibility-caseless](#174.html_compatibility-caseless) match for the value of the [`name`](#174.html_attr-map-name) attribute of another [`map`](#174.html_the-map-element) element in the same document. If the [`id`](#174.html_the-id-attribute) attribute is also specified, both attributes must have the same value.

`map` . [`areas`](#174.html_dom-map-areas)

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#174.html_htmlcollection) of the [`area`](#174.html_the-area-element) elements in the [`map`](#174.html_the-map-element).

`map` . [`images`](#174.html_dom-map-images)

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#174.html_htmlcollection) of the [`img`](#174.html_the-img-element) and [`object`](#174.html_the-object-element) elements that use the [`map`](#174.html_the-map-element).

The <dfn id="174.html_dom-map-areas" data-anolis-xref="dom-map-areas">`areas`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#174.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`map`](#174.html_the-map-element) element, whose filter matches only [`area`](#174.html_the-area-element) elements.

The <dfn id="174.html_dom-map-images" data-anolis-xref="dom-map-images">`images`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#174.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#174.html_document) node, whose filter matches only [`img`](#174.html_the-img-element) and [`object`](#174.html_the-object-element) elements that are associated with this [`map`](#174.html_the-map-element) element according to the [image map](#174.html_image-map) processing model.

The IDL attribute <dfn id="174.html_dom-map-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-map-name">`name`</dfn> must [reflect](#174.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

Image maps can be defined in conjunction with other content on the page, to ease maintenance. This example is of a page with an image map at the top of the page and a corresponding set of text links at the bottom.

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<TITLE>Babies?: Toys</TITLE>
<HEADER>
 <H1>Toys</H1>
 <IMG SRC="/images/menu.gif"
      ALT="Babies? navigation menu. Select a department to go to its page."
      USEMAP="#NAV">
</HEADER>
 ...
<FOOTER>
 <MAP NAME="NAV">
  <P>
   <A HREF="/clothes/">Clothes</A>
   <AREA ALT="Clothes" COORDS="0,0,100,50" HREF="/clothes/"> |
   <A HREF="/toys/">Toys</A>
   <AREA ALT="Toys" COORDS="0,0,100,50" HREF="/toys/"> |
   <A HREF="/food/">Food</A>
   <AREA ALT="Food" COORDS="0,0,100,50" HREF="/food/"> |
   <A HREF="/books/">Books</A>
   <AREA ALT="Books" COORDS="0,0,100,50" HREF="/books/">
 </MAP>
</FOOTER>
```

[Content attributes](#175.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#175.html_global-attributes)

[`alt`](#175.html_attr-area-alt) - Replacement text for use when images are not available

[`coords`](#175.html_attr-area-coords) - Coordinates for the shape to be created in an [image map](#175.html_image-map)

[`download`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-download) - Whether to download the resource instead of navigating to it, and its file name if so

[`href`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-href) - Address of the [hyperlink](#175.html_hyperlink)

[`hreflang`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-hreflang) - Language of the linked resource

[`rel`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-rel) Relationship between the document containing the hyperlink and the destination resource

[`shape`](#175.html_attr-area-shape) - The kind of shape to be created in an [image map](#175.html_image-map)

[`target`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-target) - [Browsing context](#175.html_browsing-context) for [hyperlink](#175.html_hyperlink) [navigation](#175.html_navigate)

[`type`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-type) - Hint for the type of the referenced resource

Tag omission in text/html:

No [end tag](#175.html_syntax-end-tag)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#175.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`link`](#175.html_index-aria-link) role (default - [*do not set*](#175.html_aria-usage-note)).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#175.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#175.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#175.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#175.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLAreaElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString alt;
           attribute DOMString coords;
           attribute DOMString shape;
           attribute DOMString target;
           attribute DOMString download;

           attribute DOMString rel;
  readonly attribute DOMTokenList relList;
           attribute DOMString hreflang;
           attribute DOMString type;
};
HTMLAreaElement implements URLUtils;
```

The [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) element [represents](#175.html_represents) either a hyperlink with some text and a corresponding area on an [image map](#175.html_image-map), or a dead area on an image map.

An [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) element with a parent node must have a [`map`](#175.html_the-map-element) element ancestor or a [`template`](#175.html_the-template-element) element ancestor.

If the [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) element has an [`href`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute, then the [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) element represents a [hyperlink](#175.html_hyperlink). In this case, the <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-alt" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-alt">`alt`</dfn> attribute must be present. It specifies the text of the hyperlink. Its value must be text that, when presented with the texts specified for the other hyperlinks of the [image map](#175.html_image-map), and with the alternative text of the image, but without the image itself, provides the user with the same kind of choice as the hyperlink would when used without its text but with its shape applied to the image. The [`alt`](#175.html_attr-area-alt) attribute may be left blank if there is another [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) element in the same [image map](#175.html_image-map) that points to the same resource and has a non-blank [`alt`](#175.html_attr-area-alt) attribute.

If the [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) element has no [`href`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute, then the area represented by the element cannot be selected, and the [`alt`](#175.html_attr-area-alt) attribute must be omitted.

In both cases, the [`shape`](#175.html_attr-area-shape) and [`coords`](#175.html_attr-area-coords) attributes specify the area.

The <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape">`shape`</dfn> attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#175.html_enumerated-attribute). The following table lists the keywords defined for this attribute. The states given in the first cell of the rows with keywords give the states to which those keywords map. Some of the keywords are non-conforming, as noted in the last column.

| State | Keywords | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Circle state](#175.html_attr-area-shape-circle) | <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape-keyword-circle" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape-keyword-circle">`circle`</dfn> |  |
| <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape-keyword-circ" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape-keyword-circ">`circ`</dfn> | Non-conforming |
| [Default state](#175.html_attr-area-shape-default) | <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape-keyword-default" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape-keyword-default">`default`</dfn> |  |
| [Polygon state](#175.html_attr-area-shape-poly) | <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape-keyword-poly" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape-keyword-poly">`poly`</dfn> |  |
| <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape-keyword-polygon" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape-keyword-polygon">`polygon`</dfn> | Non-conforming |
| [Rectangle state](#175.html_attr-area-shape-rect) | <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape-keyword-rect" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape-keyword-rect">`rect`</dfn> |  |
| <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape-keyword-rectangle" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape-keyword-rectangle">`rectangle`</dfn> | Non-conforming |

The attribute may be omitted. The *missing value default* is the [rectangle](#175.html_attr-area-shape-rect) state.

The <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-coords" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-coords">`coords`</dfn> attribute must, if specified, contain a [valid list of integers](#175.html_valid-list-of-integers). This attribute gives the coordinates for the shape described by the [`shape`](#175.html_attr-area-shape) attribute. The processing for this attribute is described as part of the [image map](#175.html_image-map) processing model.

In the <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape-circle" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape-circle">circle state</dfn>, [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) elements must have a [`coords`](#175.html_attr-area-coords) attribute present, with three integers, the last of which must be non-negative. The first integer must be the distance in CSS pixels from the left edge of the image to the center of the circle, the second integer must be the distance in CSS pixels from the top edge of the image to the center of the circle, and the third integer must be the radius of the circle, again in CSS pixels.

In the <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape-default" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape-default">default state</dfn> state, [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) elements must not have a [`coords`](#175.html_attr-area-coords) attribute. (The area is the whole image.)

In the <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape-poly" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape-poly">polygon state</dfn>, [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) elements must have a [`coords`](#175.html_attr-area-coords) attribute with at least six integers, and the number of integers must be even. Each pair of integers must represent a coordinate given as the distances from the left and the top of the image in CSS pixels respectively, and all the coordinates together must represent the points of the polygon, in order.

In the <dfn id="175.html_attr-area-shape-rect" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-shape-rect">rectangle state</dfn>, [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) elements must have a [`coords`](#175.html_attr-area-coords) attribute with exactly four integers, the first of which must be less than the third, and the second of which must be less than the fourth. The four points must represent, respectively, the distance from the left edge of the image to the left side of the rectangle, the distance from the top edge to the top side, the distance from the left edge to the right side, and the distance from the top edge to the bottom side, all in CSS pixels.

When user agents allow users to [follow hyperlinks](#175.html_following-hyperlinks) or [download hyperlinks](#175.html_downloading-hyperlinks) created using the [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) element, as described in the next section, the [`href`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-href), [`target`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-target), [`download`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-download), and attributes decide how the link is followed. The [`rel`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-rel), [`hreflang`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-hreflang), and [`type`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-type) attributes may be used to indicate to the user the likely nature of the target resource before the user follows the link.

The [`target`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-target), [`download`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-download), [`rel`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-rel), [`hreflang`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-hreflang), and [`type`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-type) attributes must be omitted if the [`href`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute is not present.

The [activation behavior](#175.html_activation-behavior) of [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) elements is to run the following steps:

1.  If the [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) element's [`Document`](#175.html_document) is not [fully active](#175.html_fully-active), then abort these steps.

2.  If the [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) element has a [`download`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-download) attribute and the algorithm is not [allowed to show a popup](#175.html_allowed-to-show-a-popup), or the element's [`target`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-target) attribute is present and applying [the rules for choosing a browsing context given a browsing context name](#175.html_the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name), using the value of the [`target`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-target) attribute as the browsing context name, would result in there not being a chosen browsing context, then run these substeps:

    1.  If there is an [entry settings object](#175.html_entry-settings-object), throw an [`InvalidAccessError`](#175.html_invalidaccesserror) exception.

    2.  Abort these steps without following the hyperlink.

3.  Otherwise, the user agent must [follow the hyperlink](#175.html_following-hyperlinks) or [download the hyperlink](#175.html_downloading-hyperlinks) created by the [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) element, if any, and as determined by the [`download`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-download) attribute and any expressed user preference.

The IDL attributes <dfn id="175.html_dom-area-alt" data-anolis-xref="dom-area-alt">`alt`</dfn>, <dfn id="175.html_dom-area-coords" data-anolis-xref="dom-area-coords">`coords`</dfn>, <dfn id="175.html_dom-area-target" data-anolis-xref="dom-area-target">`target`</dfn>, <dfn id="175.html_dom-area-download" data-anolis-xref="dom-area-download">`download`</dfn>, <dfn id="175.html_dom-area-rel" data-anolis-xref="dom-area-rel">`rel`</dfn>, <dfn id="175.html_dom-area-hreflang" data-anolis-xref="dom-area-hreflang">`hreflang`</dfn>, and <dfn id="175.html_dom-area-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-area-type">`type`</dfn>, each must [reflect](#175.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

The IDL attribute <dfn id="175.html_dom-area-shape" data-anolis-xref="dom-area-shape">`shape`</dfn> must [reflect](#175.html_reflect) the [`shape`](#175.html_attr-area-shape) content attribute.

The IDL attribute <dfn id="175.html_dom-area-rellist" data-anolis-xref="dom-area-rellist">`relList`</dfn> must [reflect](#175.html_reflect) the [`rel`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-rel) content attribute.

* * *

The [`area`](#175.html_the-area-element) element also supports the [`URLUtils`](#175.html_urlutils) interface. [[URL]](#175.html_refsURL)

When the element is created, and whenever the element's [`href`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-href) content attribute is set, changed, or removed, the user agent must invoke the element's [`URLUtils`](#175.html_urlutils) interface's [set the input](#175.html_concept-uu-set-the-input) algorithm with the value of the [`href`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-href) content attribute, if any, or the empty string otherwise, as the given value.

The element's [`URLUtils`](#175.html_urlutils) interface's [get the base](#175.html_concept-uu-get-the-base) algorithm must simply return [the element's base URL](#175.html_the-element's-base-url).

The element's [`URLUtils`](#175.html_urlutils) interface's [query encoding](#175.html_concept-uu-query-encoding) is the [document's character encoding](#175.html_document's-character-encoding).

When the element's [`URLUtils`](#175.html_urlutils) interface invokes its [update steps](#175.html_concept-uu-update) with a string `value`, the user agent must set the element's [`href`](#175.html_attr-hyperlink-href) content attribute to the string `value`.

#### 4.7.13 Image maps

##### 4.7.13.1 Authoring

An <dfn id="176.html_image-map">image map</dfn> allows geometric areas on an image to be associated with [hyperlinks](#176.html_hyperlink).

An image, in the form of an [`img`](#176.html_the-img-element) element or an [`object`](#176.html_the-object-element) element representing an image, may be associated with an image map (in the form of a [`map`](#176.html_the-map-element) element) by specifying a <dfn id="176.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap" data-anolis-xref="attr-hyperlink-usemap">`usemap`</dfn> attribute on the [`img`](#176.html_the-img-element) or [`object`](#176.html_the-object-element) element. The [`usemap`](#176.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap) attribute, if specified, must be a [valid hash-name reference](#176.html_valid-hash-name-reference) to a [`map`](#176.html_the-map-element) element.

Consider an image that looks as follows:

![A line with four shapes in it, equally spaced: a red hollow box, a green circle, a blue triangle, and a yellow four-pointed star.](Images/9532591f1210e45326b286a1bf49c17a.jpg)

If we wanted just the colored areas to be clickable, we could do it as follows:

```
<p>
 Please select a shape:
 <img src="shapes.png" usemap="#shapes"
      alt="Four shapes are available: a red hollow box, a green circle, a blue triangle, and a yellow four-pointed star.">
 <map name="shapes">
  <area shape=rect coords="50,50,100,100"> <!-- the hole in the red box -->
  <area shape=rect coords="25,25,125,125" href="red.html" alt="Red box.">
  <area shape=circle coords="200,75,50" href="green.html" alt="Green circle.">
  <area shape=poly coords="325,25,262,125,388,125" href="blue.html" alt="Blue triangle.">
  <area shape=poly coords="450,25,435,60,400,75,435,90,450,125,465,90,500,75,465,60"
        href="yellow.html" alt="Yellow star.">
 </map>
</p>
```

##### 4.7.13.2 Processing model

If an [`img`](#176.html_the-img-element) element or an [`object`](#176.html_the-object-element) element representing an image has a [`usemap`](#176.html_attr-hyperlink-usemap) attribute specified, user agents must process it as follows:

1.  First, [rules for parsing a hash-name reference](#176.html_rules-for-parsing-a-hash-name-reference) to a [`map`](#176.html_the-map-element) element must be followed. This will return either an element (the `map`) or null.

2.  If that returned null, then abort these steps. The image is not associated with an image map after all.

3.  Otherwise, the user agent must collect all the [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) elements that are descendants of the `map`. Let those be the `areas`.

Having obtained the list of [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) elements that form the image map (the `areas`), interactive user agents must process the list in one of two ways.

If the user agent intends to show the text that the [`img`](#176.html_the-img-element) element represents, then it must use the following steps.

In user agents that do not support images, or that have images disabled, [`object`](#176.html_the-object-element) elements cannot represent images, and thus this section never applies (the [fallback content](#176.html_fallback-content) is shown instead). The following steps therefore only apply to [`img`](#176.html_the-img-element) elements.

1.  Remove all the [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) elements in `areas` that have no [`href`](#176.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute.

2.  Remove all the [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) elements in `areas` that have no [`alt`](#176.html_attr-area-alt) attribute, or whose [`alt`](#176.html_attr-area-alt) attribute's value is the empty string, *if* there is another [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) element in `areas` with the same value in the [`href`](#176.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute and with a non-empty [`alt`](#176.html_attr-area-alt) attribute.

3.  Each remaining [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) element in `areas` represents a [hyperlink](#176.html_hyperlink). Those hyperlinks should all be made available to the user in a manner associated with the text of the [`img`](#176.html_the-img-element).

    In this context, user agents may represent [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) and [`img`](#176.html_the-img-element) elements with no specified `alt` attributes, or whose `alt` attributes are the empty string or some other non-visible text, in a user-agent-defined fashion intended to indicate the lack of suitable author-provided text.

If the user agent intends to show the image and allow interaction with the image to select hyperlinks, then the image must be associated with a set of layered shapes, taken from the [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) elements in `areas`, in reverse tree order (so the last specified [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) element in the `map` is the bottom-most shape, and the first element in the `map`, in tree order, is the top-most shape).

Each [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) element in `areas` must be processed as follows to obtain a shape to layer onto the image:

1.  Find the state that the element's [`shape`](#176.html_attr-area-shape) attribute represents.

2.  Use the [rules for parsing a list of integers](#176.html_rules-for-parsing-a-list-of-integers) to parse the element's [`coords`](#176.html_attr-area-coords) attribute, if it is present, and let the result be the `coords` list. If the attribute is absent, let the `coords` list be the empty list.

3.  If the number of items in the `coords` list is less than the minimum number given for the [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) element's current state, as per the following table, then the shape is empty; abort these steps.

    | State | Minimum number of items |
    | --- | --- |
    | [Circle state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-circle) | 3 |
    | [Default state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-default) | 0 |
    | [Polygon state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-poly) | 6 |
    | [Rectangle state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-rect) | 4 |

4.  Check for excess items in the `coords` list as per the entry in the following list corresponding to the [`shape`](#176.html_attr-area-shape) attribute's state:

    [Circle state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-circle)

    Drop any items in the list beyond the third.

    [Default state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-default)

    Drop all items in the list.

    [Polygon state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-poly)

    Drop the last item if there's an odd number of items.

    [Rectangle state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-rect)

    Drop any items in the list beyond the fourth.

5.  If the [`shape`](#176.html_attr-area-shape) attribute represents the [rectangle state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-rect), and the first number in the list is numerically less than the third number in the list, then swap those two numbers around.

6.  If the [`shape`](#176.html_attr-area-shape) attribute represents the [rectangle state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-rect), and the second number in the list is numerically less than the fourth number in the list, then swap those two numbers around.

7.  If the [`shape`](#176.html_attr-area-shape) attribute represents the [circle state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-circle), and the third number in the list is less than or equal to zero, then the shape is empty; abort these steps.

8.  Now, the shape represented by the element is the one described for the entry in the list below corresponding to the state of the [`shape`](#176.html_attr-area-shape) attribute:

    [Circle state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-circle)

    Let `x` be the first number in `coords`, `y` be the second number, and `r` be the third number.

    The shape is a circle whose center is `x` CSS pixels from the left edge of the image and `y` CSS pixels from the top edge of the image, and whose radius is `r` pixels.

    [Default state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-default)

    The shape is a rectangle that exactly covers the entire image.

    [Polygon state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-poly)

    Let `x`[`i`] be the (2`i`)th entry in `coords`, and `y`[`i`] be the (2`i`+1)th entry in `coords` (the first entry in `coords` being the one with index 0).

    Let `the coordinates` be (`x`[`i`], `y`[`i`]), interpreted in CSS pixels measured from the top left of the image, for all integer values of `i` from 0 to (`N`/2)-1, where `N` is the number of items in `coords`.

    The shape is a polygon whose vertices are given by `the coordinates`, and whose interior is established using the even-odd rule. [[GRAPHICS]](#176.html_refsGRAPHICS)

    [Rectangle state](#176.html_attr-area-shape-rect)

    Let `x`[`1`] be the first number in `coords`, `y`[`1`] be the second number, `x`[`2`] be the third number, and `y`[`2`] be the fourth number.

    The shape is a rectangle whose top-left corner is given by the coordinate (`x`[`1`], `y`[`1`]) and whose bottom right corner is given by the coordinate (`x`[`2`], `y`[`2`]), those coordinates being interpreted as CSS pixels from the top left corner of the image.

    For historical reasons, the coordinates must be interpreted relative to the *displayed* image after any stretching caused by the CSS 'width' and 'height' properties (or, for non-CSS browsers, the image element's `width` and `height` attributes — CSS browsers map those attributes to the aforementioned CSS properties).

    Browser zoom features and transforms applied using CSS or SVG do not affect the coordinates.

Pointing device interaction with an image associated with a set of layered shapes per the above algorithm must result in the relevant user interaction events being first fired to the top-most shape covering the point that the pointing device indicated, if any, or to the image element itself, if there is no shape covering that point. User agents may also allow individual [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) elements representing [hyperlinks](#176.html_hyperlink) to be selected and activated (e.g. using a keyboard).

Because a [`map`](#176.html_the-map-element) element (and its [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) elements) can be associated with multiple [`img`](#176.html_the-img-element) and [`object`](#176.html_the-object-element) elements, it is possible for an [`area`](#176.html_the-area-element) element to correspond to multiple focusable areas of the document.

Image maps are [live](#176.html_live); if the DOM is mutated, then the user agent must act as if it had rerun the algorithms for image maps.

#### 4.7.14 MathML

The <dfn id="177.html_math">`math`</dfn> element from the [MathML namespace](#177.html_mathml-namespace) falls into the [embedded content](#177.html_embedded-content-2), [phrasing content](#177.html_phrasing-content-1), and [flow content](#177.html_flow-content-1) categories for the purposes of the content models in this specification.

User agents must handle text other than [inter-element whitespace](#177.html_inter-element-whitespace) found in MathML elements whose content models do not allow straight text by pretending for the purposes of MathML content models, layout, and rendering that that text is actually wrapped in an `mtext` element in the [MathML namespace](#177.html_mathml-namespace). (Such text is not, however, conforming.)

User agents must act as if any MathML element whose contents does not match the element's content model was replaced, for the purposes of MathML layout and rendering, by an `merror` element in the [MathML namespace](#177.html_mathml-namespace) containing some appropriate error message.

To enable authors to use MathML tools that only accept MathML in its XML form, interactive HTML user agents are encouraged to provide a way to export any MathML fragment as an XML namespace-well-formed XML fragment.

The semantics of MathML elements are defined by the MathML specification and [other applicable specifications](#177.html_other-applicable-specifications). [[MATHML]](#177.html_refsMATHML)

Here is an example of the use of MathML in an HTML document:

```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
 <head>
  <title>The quadratic formula</title>
 </head>
 <body>
  <h1>The quadratic formula</h1>
  <p>
   <math>
    <mi>x</mi>
    <mo>=</mo>
    <mfrac>
     <mrow>
      <mo form="prefix">?</mo> <mi>b</mi>
      <mo>±</mo>
      <msqrt>
       <msup> <mi>b</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msup>
       <mo>?</mo>
       <mn>4</mn> <mo>?</mo> <mi>a</mi> <mo>?</mo> <mi>c</mi>
      </msqrt>
     </mrow>
     <mrow>
      <mn>2</mn> <mo>?</mo> <mi>a</mi>
     </mrow>
    </mfrac>
   </math>
  </p>
 </body>
</html>
```

#### 4.7.15 SVG

The <dfn id="178.html_svg-0">`svg`</dfn> element from the [SVG namespace](#178.html_svg-namespace) falls into the [embedded content](#178.html_embedded-content-2), [phrasing content](#178.html_phrasing-content-1), and [flow content](#178.html_flow-content-1) categories for the purposes of the content models in this specification.

To enable authors to use SVG tools that only accept SVG in its XML form, interactive HTML user agents are encouraged to provide a way to export any SVG fragment as an XML namespace-well-formed XML fragment.

When the SVG `foreignObject` element contains elements from the [HTML namespace](#178.html_html-namespace-0), such elements must all be [flow content](#178.html_flow-content-1). [[SVG]](#178.html_refsSVG)

The content model for `title` elements in the [SVG namespace](#178.html_svg-namespace) inside [HTML documents](#178.html_html-documents) is [phrasing content](#178.html_phrasing-content-1). (This further constrains the requirements given in the SVG specification.)

The semantics of SVG elements are defined by the SVG specification and [other applicable specifications](#178.html_other-applicable-specifications). [[SVG]](#178.html_refsSVG)

The SVG specification includes requirements regarding the handling of elements in the DOM that are not in the SVG namespace, that are in SVG fragments, and that are not included in a `foreignObject` element. *This* specification does not define any processing for elements in SVG fragments that are not in the HTML namespace; they are considered neither conforming nor non-conforming from the perspective of this specification.

#### 4.7.16 <dfn>Dimension attributes</dfn>

**Author requirements**: The <dfn id="179.html_attr-dim-width" data-anolis-xref="attr-dim-width">`width`</dfn> and <dfn id="179.html_attr-dim-height" data-anolis-xref="attr-dim-height">`height`</dfn> attributes on [`img`](#179.html_the-img-element), [`iframe`](#179.html_the-iframe-element), [`embed`](#179.html_the-embed-element), [`object`](#179.html_the-object-element), [`video`](#179.html_the-video-element), and, when their [`type`](#179.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Image Button](#179.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, [`input`](#179.html_the-input-element) elements may be specified to give the dimensions of the visual content of the element (the width and height respectively, relative to the nominal direction of the output medium), in CSS pixels. The attributes, if specified, must have values that are [valid non-negative integers](#179.html_valid-non-negative-integer).

The specified dimensions given may differ from the dimensions specified in the resource itself, since the resource may have a resolution that differs from the CSS pixel resolution. (On screens, CSS pixels have a resolution of 96ppi, but in general the CSS pixel resolution depends on the reading distance.) If both attributes are specified, then one of the following statements must be true:

*   `specified width` - 0.5 ≤ `specified height` * `target ratio` ≤ `specified width` + 0.5
*   `specified height` - 0.5 ≤ `specified width` / `target ratio` ≤ `specified height` + 0.5
*   `specified height` = `specified width` = 0

The `target ratio` is the ratio of the intrinsic width to the intrinsic height in the resource. The `specified width` and `specified height` are the values of the [`width`](#179.html_attr-dim-width) and [`height`](#179.html_attr-dim-height) attributes respectively.

The two attributes must be omitted if the resource in question does not have both an intrinsic width and an intrinsic height.

If the two attributes are both zero, it indicates that the element is not intended for the user (e.g. it might be a part of a service to count page views).

The dimension attributes are not intended to be used to stretch the image.

**User agent requirements**: User agents are expected to use these attributes [as hints for the rendering](#179.html_dimRendering).

The <dfn id="179.html_dom-dim-width" data-anolis-xref="dom-dim-width">`width`</dfn> and <dfn id="179.html_dom-dim-height" data-anolis-xref="dom-dim-height">`height`</dfn> IDL attributes on the [`iframe`](#179.html_the-iframe-element), [`embed`](#179.html_the-embed-element), [`object`](#179.html_the-object-element), and [`video`](#179.html_the-video-element) elements must [reflect](#179.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

For [`iframe`](#179.html_the-iframe-element), [`embed`](#179.html_the-embed-element), and [`object`](#179.html_the-object-element) the IDL attributes are `DOMString`; for [`video`](#179.html_the-video-element) the IDL attributes are `unsigned long`.

The corresponding IDL attributes for [`img`](#179.html_dom-img-height) and [`input`](#179.html_dom-input-height) elements are defined in those respective elements' sections, as they are slightly more specific to those elements' other behaviors.

### 4.8 Links

Links are a conceptual construct, created by [`a`](#180.html_the-a-element), [`area`](#180.html_the-area-element), and [`link`](#180.html_the-link-element) elements, that [represent](#180.html_represents) a connection between two resources, one of which is the current [`Document`](#180.html_document). There are two kinds of links in HTML:

<dfn id="180.html_external-resource-link" data-anolis-xref="external resource link">Links to external resources</dfn>

These are links to resources that are to be used to augment the current document, generally automatically processed by the user agent.

<dfn id="180.html_hyperlink" data-anolis-xref="hyperlink">Hyperlinks</dfn>

These are links to other resources that are generally exposed to the user by the user agent so that the user can cause the user agent to [navigate](#180.html_navigate) to those resources, e.g. to visit them in a browser or download them.

For [`link`](#180.html_the-link-element) elements with an [`href`](#180.html_attr-link-href) attribute and a [`rel`](#180.html_attr-link-rel) attribute, links must be created for the keywords of the [`rel`](#180.html_attr-link-rel) attribute, as defined for those keywords in the [link types](#180.html_linkTypes) section.

Similarly, for [`a`](#180.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#180.html_the-area-element) elements with an [`href`](#180.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute and a [`rel`](#180.html_attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute, links must be created for the keywords of the [`rel`](#180.html_attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute as defined for those keywords in the [link types](#180.html_linkTypes) section. Unlike [`link`](#180.html_the-link-element) elements, however, [`a`](#180.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#180.html_the-area-element) element with an [`href`](#180.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute that either do not have a [`rel`](#180.html_attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute, or whose [`rel`](#180.html_attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute has no keywords that are defined as specifying [hyperlinks](#180.html_hyperlink), must also create a [hyperlink](#180.html_hyperlink). This implied hyperlink has no special meaning (it has no [link type](#180.html_linkTypes)) beyond linking the element's document to the resource given by the element's [`href`](#180.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute.

A [hyperlink](#180.html_hyperlink) can have one or more <dfn id="180.html_hyperlink-annotation" data-anolis-xref="hyperlink annotation">hyperlink annotations</dfn> that modify the processing semantics of that hyperlink.

#### 4.8.1 Links created by [`a`](#181.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#181.html_the-area-element) elements

The <dfn id="181.html_attr-hyperlink-href" data-anolis-xref="attr-hyperlink-href">`href`</dfn> attribute on [`a`](#181.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#181.html_the-area-element) elements must have a value that is a [valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#181.html_valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces).

The [`href`](#181.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute on [`a`](#181.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#181.html_the-area-element) elements is not required; when those elements do not have [`href`](#181.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attributes they do not create hyperlinks.

The <dfn id="181.html_attr-hyperlink-target" data-anolis-xref="attr-hyperlink-target">`target`</dfn> attribute, if present, must be a [valid browsing context name or keyword](#181.html_valid-browsing-context-name-or-keyword). It gives the name of the [browsing context](#181.html_browsing-context) that will be used. User agents use this name when [following hyperlinks](#181.html_following-hyperlinks).

When an [`a`](#181.html_the-a-element) or [`area`](#181.html_the-area-element) element's [activation behavior](#181.html_activation-behavior) is invoked, the user agent may allow the user to indicate a preference regarding whether the hyperlink is to be used for [navigation](#181.html_navigate) or whether the resource it specifies is to be downloaded.

In the absence of a user preference, the default should be navigation if the element has no [`download`](#181.html_attr-hyperlink-download) attribute, and should be to download the specified resource if it does.

Whether determined by the user's preferences or via the presence or absence of the attribute, if the decision is to use the hyperlink for [navigation](#181.html_navigate) then the user agent must [follow the hyperlink](#181.html_following-hyperlinks), and if the decision is to use the hyperlink to download a resource, the user agent must [download the hyperlink](#181.html_downloading-hyperlinks). These terms are defined in subsequent sections below.

The <dfn id="181.html_attr-hyperlink-download" data-anolis-xref="attr-hyperlink-download">`download`</dfn> attribute, if present, indicates that the author intends the hyperlink to be used for downloading a resource. The attribute may have a value; the value, if any, specifies the default file name that the author recommends for use in labeling the resource in a local file system. There are no restrictions on allowed values, but authors are cautioned that most file systems have limitations with regard to what punctuation is supported in file names, and user agents are likely to adjust file names accordingly.

The <dfn id="181.html_attr-hyperlink-rel" data-anolis-xref="attr-hyperlink-rel">`rel`</dfn> attribute on [`a`](#181.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#181.html_the-area-element) elements controls what kinds of links the elements create. The attribute's value must be a [set of space-separated tokens](#181.html_set-of-space-separated-tokens). The [allowed keywords and their meanings](#181.html_linkTypes) are defined below.

The [`rel`](#181.html_attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute has no default value. If the attribute is omitted or if none of the values in the attribute are recognized by the user agent, then the document has no particular relationship with the destination resource other than there being a hyperlink between the two.

The <dfn id="181.html_attr-hyperlink-hreflang" data-anolis-xref="attr-hyperlink-hreflang">`hreflang`</dfn> attribute on [`a`](#181.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#181.html_the-area-element) elements that create [hyperlinks](#181.html_hyperlink), if present, gives the language of the linked resource. It is purely advisory. The value must be a valid BCP 47 language tag. [[BCP47]](#181.html_refsBCP47) User agents must not consider this attribute authoritative — upon fetching the resource, user agents must use only language information associated with the resource to determine its language, not metadata included in the link to the resource.

The <dfn id="181.html_attr-hyperlink-type" data-anolis-xref="attr-hyperlink-type">`type`</dfn> attribute, if present, gives the [MIME type](#181.html_mime-type) of the linked resource. It is purely advisory. The value must be a [valid MIME type](#181.html_valid-mime-type). User agents must not consider the [`type`](#181.html_attr-hyperlink-type) attribute authoritative — upon fetching the resource, user agents must not use metadata included in the link to the resource to determine its type.

#### 4.8.2 Following hyperlinks

When a user <dfn id="182.html_following-hyperlinks" data-anolis-xref="following hyperlinks">follows a hyperlink</dfn> created by an element `subject`, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `replace` be false.

2.  Let `source` be the [browsing context](#182.html_browsing-context) that contains the [`Document`](#182.html_document) object with which `subject` in question is associated.

3.  If the user indicated a specific [browsing context](#182.html_browsing-context) when following the hyperlink, or if the user agent is configured to follow hyperlinks by navigating a particular browsing context, then let `target` be that [browsing context](#182.html_browsing-context).

    Otherwise, if `subject` is an [`a`](#182.html_the-a-element) or [`area`](#182.html_the-area-element) element that has a [`target`](#182.html_attr-hyperlink-target) attribute, then let `target` be the [browsing context](#182.html_browsing-context) that is chosen by applying [the rules for choosing a browsing context given a browsing context name](#182.html_the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name), using the value of the [`target`](#182.html_attr-hyperlink-target) attribute as the browsing context name. If these rules result in the creation of a new [browsing context](#182.html_browsing-context), set `replace` to true.

    Otherwise, if `target` is an [`a`](#182.html_the-a-element) or [`area`](#182.html_the-area-element) element with no [`target`](#182.html_attr-hyperlink-target) attribute, but the [`Document`](#182.html_document) contains a [`base`](#182.html_the-base-element) element with a [`target`](#182.html_attr-base-target) attribute, then let `target` be the [browsing context](#182.html_browsing-context) that is chosen by applying [the rules for choosing a browsing context given a browsing context name](#182.html_the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name), using the value of the [`target`](#182.html_attr-base-target) attribute of the first such [`base`](#182.html_the-base-element) element as the browsing context name. If these rules result in the creation of a new [browsing context](#182.html_browsing-context), set `replace` to true.

    Otherwise, let `target` be the [browsing context](#182.html_browsing-context) that `subject` itself is in.

4.  [Resolve](#182.html_resolve-a-url) the URL given by the [`href`](#182.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute of that element, relative to that element.

5.  If that is successful, let `URL` be the [resulting absolute URL](#182.html_resulting-absolute-url).

    Otherwise, if [resolving](#182.html_resolve-a-url) the URL failed, the user agent may report the error to the user in a user-agent-specific manner, may [queue a task](#182.html_queue-a-task) to [navigate](#182.html_navigate) the `target` [browsing context](#182.html_browsing-context) to an error page to report the error, or may ignore the error and do nothing. In any case, the user agent must then abort these steps.

6.  In the case of server-side image maps, append the [`hyperlink suffix`](#182.html_hyperlink-suffix) to `URL`.

7.  [Queue a task](#182.html_queue-a-task) to [navigate](#182.html_navigate) the `target` [browsing context](#182.html_browsing-context) to `URL`. If `replace` is true, the navigation must be performed with [replacement enabled](#182.html_replacement-enabled). The [source browsing context](#182.html_source-browsing-context) must be `source`.

The [task source](#182.html_task-source) for the tasks mentioned above is the [DOM manipulation task source](#182.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

#### 4.8.3 Downloading resources

In some cases, resources are intended for later use rather than immediate viewing. To indicate that a resource is intended to be downloaded for use later, rather than immediately used, the [`download`](#183.html_attr-hyperlink-download) attribute can be specified on the [`a`](#183.html_the-a-element) or [`area`](#183.html_the-area-element) element that creates the [hyperlink](#183.html_hyperlink) to that resource.

The attribute can furthermore be given a value, to specify the file name that user agents are to use when storing the resource in a file system. This value can be overridden by the `Content-Disposition` HTTP header's filename parameters. [[RFC6266]](#183.html_refsRFC6266)

In cross-origin situations, the [`download`](#183.html_attr-hyperlink-download) attribute has to be combined with the `Content-Disposition` HTTP header, specifically with the `attachment` disposition type, to avoid the user being warned of possibly nefarious activity. (This is to protect users from being made to download sensitive personal or confidential information without their full understanding.)

* * *

When a user <dfn id="183.html_downloading-hyperlinks" data-anolis-xref="downloading hyperlinks">downloads a hyperlink</dfn> created by an element, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  [Resolve](#183.html_resolve-a-url) the URL given by the [`href`](#183.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute of that element, relative to that element.

2.  If [resolving](#183.html_resolve-a-url) the URL fails, the user agent may report the error to the user in a user-agent-specific manner, may [navigate](#183.html_navigate) to an error page to report the error, or may ignore the error and do nothing. In either case, the user agent must abort these steps.

3.  Otherwise, let `URL` be the resulting [absolute URL](#183.html_absolute-url).

4.  In the case of server-side image maps, append the [`hyperlink suffix`](#183.html_hyperlink-suffix) to `URL`.

5.  Return to whatever algorithm invoked these steps and continue these steps asynchronously.

6.  [Fetch](#183.html_fetch) `URL` and handle the resulting resource [as a download](#183.html_as-a-download).

When a user agent is to handle a resource obtained from a [fetch](#183.html_fetch) algorithm <dfn id="183.html_as-a-download">as a download</dfn>, it should provide the user with a way to save the resource for later use, if a resource is successfully obtained; or otherwise should report any problems downloading the file to the user.

If the user agent needs a file name for a resource being handled [as a download](#183.html_as-a-download), it should select one using the following algorithm.

This algorithm is intended to mitigate security dangers involved in downloading files from untrusted sites, and user agents are strongly urged to follow it.

1.  Let `filename` be the void value.

2.  If the resource has a `Content-Disposition` header, that header specifies the `attachment` disposition type, and the header includes file name information, then let `filename` have the value specified by the header, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below. [[RFC6266]](#183.html_refsRFC6266)

3.  Let `interface origin` be the [origin](#183.html_origin-0) of the [`Document`](#183.html_document) in which the [download](#183.html_downloading-hyperlinks) or [navigate](#183.html_navigate) action resulting in the download was initiated, if any.

4.  Let `resource origin` be the [origin](#183.html_origin-0) of the URL of the resource being downloaded, unless that URL's [scheme](#183.html_concept-url-scheme) component is `data`, in which case let `resource origin` be the same as the `interface origin`, if any.

5.  If there is no `interface origin`, then let `trusted operation` be true. Otherwise, let `trusted operation` be true if `resource origin` is the [same origin](#183.html_same-origin) as `interface origin`, and false otherwise.
