6.  If `trusted operation` is true and the resource has a `Content-Disposition` header and that header includes file name information, then let `filename` have the value specified by the header, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below. [[RFC6266]](#183.html_refsRFC6266)

7.  If the download was not initiated from a [hyperlink](#183.html_hyperlink) created by an [`a`](#183.html_the-a-element) or [`area`](#183.html_the-area-element) element, or if the element of the [hyperlink](#183.html_hyperlink) from which it was initiated did not have a [`download`](#183.html_attr-hyperlink-download) attribute when the download was initiated, or if there was such an attribute but its value when the download was initiated was the empty string, then jump to the step labeled *no proposed file name*.

8.  Let `proposed filename` have the value of the [`download`](#183.html_attr-hyperlink-download) attribute of the element of the [hyperlink](#183.html_hyperlink) that initiated the download at the time the download was initiated.

9.  If `trusted operation` is true, let `filename` have the value of `proposed filename`, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below.

10.  If the resource has a `Content-Disposition` header and that header specifies the `attachment` disposition type, let `filename` have the value of `proposed filename`, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below. [[RFC6266]](#183.html_refsRFC6266)

11.  *No proposed file name*: If `trusted operation` is true, or if the user indicated a preference for having the resource in question downloaded, let `filename` have a value derived from the URL of the resource in a user-agent-defined manner, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below.

12.  Act in a user-agent-defined manner to safeguard the user from a potentially hostile cross-origin download. If the download is not to be aborted, then let `filename` be set to the user's preferred file name or to a file name selected by the user agent, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below.

    If the algorithm reaches this step, then a download was begun from a different origin than the resource being downloaded, and the origin did not mark the file as suitable for downloading, and the download was not initiated by the user. This could be because a [`download`](#183.html_attr-hyperlink-download) attribute was used to trigger the download, or because the resource in question is not of a type that the user agent supports.

    This could be dangerous, because, for instance, a hostile server could be trying to get a user to unknowingly download private information and then re-upload it to the hostile server, by tricking the user into thinking the data is from the hostile server.

    Thus, it is in the user's interests that the user be somehow notified that the resource in question comes from quite a different source, and to prevent confusion, any suggested file name from the potentially hostile `interface origin` should be ignored.

13.  *Sanitize*: Optionally, allow the user to influence `filename`. For example, a user agent could prompt the user for a file name, potentially providing the value of `filename` as determined above as a default value.

14.  Adjust `filename` to be suitable for the local file system.

    For example, this could involve removing characters that are not legal in file names, or trimming leading and trailing whitespace.

15.  If the platform conventions do not in any way use [extensions](#183.html_concept-extension) to determine the types of file on the file system, then return `filename` as the file name and abort these steps.

16.  Let `claimed type` be the type given by the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#183.html_content-type), if any is known. Let `named type` be the type given by `filename`'s [extension](#183.html_concept-extension), if any is known. For the purposes of this step, a *type* is a mapping of a [MIME type](#183.html_mime-type) to an [extension](#183.html_concept-extension).

17.  If `named type` is consistent with the user's preferences (e.g. because the value of `filename` was determined by prompting the user), then return `filename` as the file name and abort these steps.

18.  If `claimed type` and `named type` are the same type (i.e. the type given by the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#183.html_content-type) is consistent with the type given by `filename`'s [extension](#183.html_concept-extension)), then return `filename` as the file name and abort these steps.

19.  If the `claimed type` is known, then alter `filename` to add an [extension](#183.html_concept-extension) corresponding to `claimed type`.

    Otherwise, if `named type` is known to be potentially dangerous (e.g. it will be treated by the platform conventions as a native executable, shell script, HTML application, or executable-macro-capable document) then optionally alter `filename` to add a known-safe [extension](#183.html_concept-extension) (e.g. "`.txt`").

    This last step would make it impossible to download executables, which might not be desirable. As always, implementors are forced to balance security and usability in this matter.

20.  Return `filename` as the file name.

For the purposes of this algorithm, a file <dfn id="183.html_concept-extension" data-anolis-xref="concept-extension">extension</dfn> consists of any part of the file name that platform conventions dictate will be used for identifying the type of the file. For example, many operating systems use the part of the file name following the last dot ("`.`") in the file name to determine the type of the file, and from that the manner in which the file is to be opened or executed.

User agents should ignore any directory or path information provided by the resource itself, its URL, and any [`download`](#183.html_attr-hyperlink-download) attribute, in deciding where to store the resulting file in the user's file system.

#### 4.8.4 Link types

The following table summarizes the link types that are defined by this specification. This table is non-normative; the actual definitions for the link types are given in the next few sections.

In this section, the term *referenced document* refers to the resource identified by the element representing the link, and the term *current document* refers to the resource within which the element representing the link finds itself.

To determine which link types apply to a [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), or [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) element, the element's `rel` attribute must be [split on spaces](#184.html_split-a-string-on-spaces). The resulting tokens are the link types that apply to that element.

Except where otherwise specified, a keyword must not be specified more than once per [`rel`](#184.html_attr-hyperlink-rel) attribute.

Link types are always [ASCII case-insensitive](#184.html_ascii-case-insensitive), and must be compared as such.

Thus, `rel="next"` is the same as `rel="NEXT"`.

| Link type | Effect on... | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) | [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) |
| --- | --- |
| [`alternate`](#184.html_rel-alternate) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | Gives alternate representations of the current document. |
| [`author`](#184.html_link-type-author) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | Gives a link to the author of the current document or article. |
| [`bookmark`](#184.html_link-type-bookmark) | *not allowed* | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | Gives the permalink for the nearest ancestor section. |
| [`help`](#184.html_link-type-help) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | Provides a link to context-sensitive help. |
| [`icon`](#184.html_rel-icon) | [External Resource](#184.html_external-resource-link) | *not allowed* | Imports an icon to represent the current document. |
| [`license`](#184.html_link-type-license) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | Indicates that the main content of the current document is covered by the copyright license described by the referenced document. |
| [`next`](#184.html_link-type-next) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | Indicates that the current document is a part of a series, and that the next document in the series is the referenced document. |
| [`nofollow`](#184.html_link-type-nofollow) | *not allowed* | [Annotation](#184.html_hyperlink-annotation) | Indicates that the current document's original author or publisher does not endorse the referenced document. |
| [`noreferrer`](#184.html_link-type-noreferrer) | *not allowed* | [Annotation](#184.html_hyperlink-annotation) | Requires that the user agent not send an HTTP `Referer` (sic) header if the user follows the hyperlink. |
| [`prefetch`](#184.html_link-type-prefetch) | [External Resource](#184.html_external-resource-link) | [External Resource](#184.html_external-resource-link) | Specifies that the target resource should be preemptively cached. |
| [`prev`](#184.html_link-type-prev) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | Indicates that the current document is a part of a series, and that the previous document in the series is the referenced document. |
| [`search`](#184.html_link-type-search) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | Gives a link to a resource that can be used to search through the current document and its related pages. |
| [`stylesheet`](#184.html_link-type-stylesheet) | [External Resource](#184.html_external-resource-link) | *not allowed* | Imports a stylesheet. |
| [`tag`](#184.html_link-type-tag) | *not allowed* | [Hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) | Gives a tag (identified by the given address) that applies to the current document. |

Some of the types described below list synonyms for these values. These are to be handled as specified by user agents, but must not be used in documents.

##### 4.8.4.1 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-alternate-0" data-anolis-xref="rel-alternate">`alternate`</dfn>"

The [`alternate`](#184.html_rel-alternate) keyword may be used with [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements.

The meaning of this keyword depends on the values of the other attributes.

If the element is a [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) element and the [`rel`](#184.html_attr-link-rel) attribute also contains the keyword [`stylesheet`](#184.html_link-type-stylesheet)

The [`alternate`](#184.html_rel-alternate) keyword modifies the meaning of the [`stylesheet`](#184.html_link-type-stylesheet) keyword in the way described for that keyword. The [`alternate`](#184.html_rel-alternate) keyword does not create a link of its own.

If the [`alternate`](#184.html_rel-alternate) keyword is used with the [`type`](#184.html_attr-hyperlink-type) attribute set to the value `application/rss+xml` or the value `application/atom+xml`

The keyword creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) referencing a syndication feed (though not necessarily syndicating exactly the same content as the current page).

The first [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), or [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) element in the document (in tree order) with the [`alternate`](#184.html_rel-alternate) keyword used with the [`type`](#184.html_attr-hyperlink-type) attribute set to the value `application/rss+xml` or the value `application/atom+xml` must be treated as the default syndication feed for the purposes of feed autodiscovery.

The following [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) element gives the syndication feed for the current page:

```
<link rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml" href="data.xml">
```

The following extract offers various different syndication feeds:

```
<p>You can access the planets database using Atom feeds:</p>
<ul>
 <li><a href="recently-visited-planets.xml" rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml">Recently Visited Planets</a></li>
 <li><a href="known-bad-planets.xml" rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml">Known Bad Planets</a></li>
 <li><a href="unexplored-planets.xml" rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml">Unexplored Planets</a></li>
</ul>
```

Otherwise

The keyword creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink) referencing an alternate representation of the current document.

The nature of the referenced document is given by the [`hreflang`](#184.html_attr-hyperlink-hreflang), and [`type`](#184.html_attr-hyperlink-type) attributes.

If the [`alternate`](#184.html_rel-alternate) keyword is used with the [`hreflang`](#184.html_attr-hyperlink-hreflang) attribute, and that attribute's value differs from the [root element](#184.html_root-element)'s [language](#184.html_language), it indicates that the referenced document is a translation.

If the [`alternate`](#184.html_rel-alternate) keyword is used with the [`type`](#184.html_attr-hyperlink-type) attribute, it indicates that the referenced document is a reformulation of the current document in the specified format.

The [`hreflang`](#184.html_attr-hyperlink-hreflang) and [`type`](#184.html_attr-hyperlink-type) attributes can be combined when specified with the [`alternate`](#184.html_rel-alternate) keyword.

For example, the following link is a French translation that uses the PDF format:

```
<link rel=alternate type=application/pdf hreflang=fr href=manual-fr>
```

This relationship is transitive — that is, if a document links to two other documents with the link type "[`alternate`](#184.html_rel-alternate)", then, in addition to implying that those documents are alternative representations of the first document, it is also implying that those two documents are alternative representations of each other.

##### 4.8.4.2 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-author" data-anolis-xref="rel-author">`author`</dfn>"

The [`author`](#184.html_link-type-author) keyword may be used with [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink).

For [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements, the [`author`](#184.html_link-type-author) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides further information about the author of the nearest [`article`](#184.html_the-article-element) element ancestor of the element defining the hyperlink, if there is one, or of the page as a whole, otherwise.

For [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) elements, the [`author`](#184.html_link-type-author) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides further information about the author for the page as a whole.

The "referenced document" can be, and often is, a `mailto:` URL giving the e-mail address of the author. [[MAILTO]](#184.html_refsMAILTO)

**Synonyms**: For historical reasons, user agents must also treat [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements that have a `rev` attribute with the value "`made`" as having the [`author`](#184.html_link-type-author) keyword specified as a link relationship.

##### 4.8.4.3 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-bookmark" data-anolis-xref="rel-bookmark">`bookmark`</dfn>"

The [`bookmark`](#184.html_link-type-bookmark) keyword may be used with [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink).

The [`bookmark`](#184.html_link-type-bookmark) keyword gives a permalink for the nearest ancestor [`article`](#184.html_the-article-element) element of the linking element in question, or of [the section the linking element is most closely associated with](#184.html_associatedSection), if there are no ancestor [`article`](#184.html_the-article-element) elements.

The following snippet has three permalinks. A user agent could determine which permalink applies to which part of the spec by looking at where the permalinks are given.

```
 ...
 <body>
  <h1>Example of permalinks</h1>
  <div id="a">
   <h2>First example</h2>
   <p><a href="a.html" rel="bookmark">This permalink applies to
   only the content from the first H2 to the second H2</a>. The DIV isn't
   exactly that section, but it roughly corresponds to it.</p>
  </div>
  <h2>Second example</h2>
  <article id="b">
   <p><a href="b.html" rel="bookmark">This permalink applies to
   the outer ARTICLE element</a> (which could be, e.g., a blog post).</p>
   <article id="c">
    <p><a href="c.html" rel="bookmark">This permalink applies to
    the inner ARTICLE element</a> (which could be, e.g., a blog comment).</p>
   </article>
  </article>
 </body>
 ...
```

##### 4.8.4.4 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-help" data-anolis-xref="rel-help">`help`</dfn>"

The [`help`](#184.html_link-type-help) keyword may be used with [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink).

For [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements, the [`help`](#184.html_link-type-help) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides further help information for the parent of the element defining the hyperlink, and its children.

In the following example, the form control has associated context-sensitive help. The user agent could use this information, for example, displaying the referenced document if the user presses the "Help" or "F1" key.

```
 <p><label> Topic: <input name=topic> <a href="help/topic.html" rel="help">(Help)</a></label></p>
```

For [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) elements, the [`help`](#184.html_link-type-help) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides help for the page as a whole.

For [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements, on some browsers, the [`help`](#184.html_link-type-help) keyword causes the link to use a different cursor.

##### 4.8.4.5 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-icon-0" data-anolis-xref="rel-icon">`icon`</dfn>"

The [`icon`](#184.html_rel-icon) keyword may be used with [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#184.html_external-resource-link).

The specified resource is an icon representing the page or site, and should be used by the user agent when representing the page in the user interface.

Icons could be auditory icons, visual icons, or other kinds of icons. If multiple icons are provided, the user agent must select the most appropriate icon according to the [`type`](#184.html_attr-link-type), [`media`](#184.html_attr-link-media), and [`sizes`](#184.html_attr-link-sizes) attributes. If there are multiple equally appropriate icons, user agents must use the last one declared in [tree order](#184.html_tree-order) at the time that the user agent collected the list of icons. If the user agent tries to use an icon but that icon is determined, upon closer examination, to in fact be inappropriate (e.g. because it uses an unsupported format), then the user agent must try the next-most-appropriate icon as determined by the attributes.

User agents are not required to update icons when the list of icons changes, but are encouraged to do so.

There is no default type for resources given by the [`icon`](#184.html_rel-icon) keyword. However, for the purposes of [determining the type of the resource](#184.html_concept-link-type-sniffing), user agents must expect the resource to be an image.

The <dfn id="184.html_attr-link-sizes" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-sizes">`sizes`</dfn> attribute gives the sizes of icons for visual media. Its value, if present, is merely advisory. User agents may use the value to decide which icon(s) to use if multiple icons are available.

If specified, the attribute must have a value that is an [unordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#184.html_unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens) which are [ASCII case-insensitive](#184.html_ascii-case-insensitive). Each value must be either an [ASCII case-insensitive](#184.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "[`any`](#184.html_attr-link-sizes-any)", or a value that consists of two [valid non-negative integers](#184.html_valid-non-negative-integer) that do not have a leading "0" (U+0030) character and that are separated by a single U+0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X or U+0058 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER X character.

The keywords represent icon sizes in raw pixels (as opposed to CSS pixels).

An icon that is 50 CSS pixels wide intended for displays with a device pixel density of two device pixels per CSS pixel (2x, 192dpi) would have a width of 100 raw pixels. This feature does not support indicating that a different resource is to be used for small high-resolution icons vs large low-resolution icons (e.g. 50×50 2x vs 100×100 1x).

To parse and process the attribute's value, the user agent must first [split the attribute's value on spaces](#184.html_split-a-string-on-spaces), and must then parse each resulting keyword to determine what it represents.

The <dfn id="184.html_attr-link-sizes-any" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-sizes-any">`any`</dfn> keyword represents that the resource contains a scalable icon, e.g. as provided by an SVG image.

Other keywords must be further parsed as follows to determine what they represent:

*   If the keyword doesn't contain exactly one U+0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X or U+0058 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER X character, then this keyword doesn't represent anything. Abort these steps for that keyword.

*   Let `width string` be the string before the "`x`" or "`X`".

*   Let `height string` be the string after the "`x`" or "`X`".

*   If either `width string` or `height string` start with a "0" (U+0030) character or contain any characters other than [ASCII digits](#184.html_ascii-digits), then this keyword doesn't represent anything. Abort these steps for that keyword.

*   Apply the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#184.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) to `width string` to obtain `width`.

*   Apply the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#184.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) to `height string` to obtain `height`.

*   The keyword represents that the resource contains a bitmap icon with a width of `width` device pixels and a height of `height` device pixels.

The keywords specified on the [`sizes`](#184.html_attr-link-sizes) attribute must not represent icon sizes that are not actually available in the linked resource.

In the absence of a [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) with the [`icon`](#184.html_rel-icon) keyword, for [`Document`](#184.html_document)s obtained over HTTP or HTTPS, user agents may instead attempt to [fetch](#184.html_fetch) and use an icon with the [absolute URL](#184.html_absolute-url) obtained by resolving the URL "`/favicon.ico`" against [the document's address](#184.html_the-document's-address), as if the page had declared that icon using the [`icon`](#184.html_rel-icon) keyword.

The following snippet shows the top part of an application with several icons.

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html>
 <head>
  <title>lsForums — Inbox</title>
  <link rel=icon href=favicon.png sizes="16x16" type="image/png">
  <link rel=icon href=windows.ico sizes="32x32 48x48" type="image/vnd.microsoft.icon">
  <link rel=icon href=mac.icns sizes="128x128 512x512 8192x8192 32768x32768">
  <link rel=icon href=iphone.png sizes="57x57" type="image/png">
  <link rel=icon href=gnome.svg sizes="any" type="image/svg+xml">
  <link rel=stylesheet href=lsforums.css>
  <script src=lsforums.js></script>
  <meta name=application-name content="lsForums">
 </head>
 <body>
  ...
```

For historical reasons, the [`icon`](#184.html_rel-icon) keyword may be preceded by the keyword "`shortcut`". If the "`shortcut`" keyword is present, it must be come immediately before the [`icon`](#184.html_rel-icon) keyword and the two keywords must be separated by only a single U+0020 SPACE character.

##### 4.8.4.6 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-license" data-anolis-xref="rel-license">`license`</dfn>"

The [`license`](#184.html_link-type-license) keyword may be used with [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink).

The [`license`](#184.html_link-type-license) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides the copyright license terms under which the main content of the current document is provided.

This specification defines the main content of a document and content that is not deemed to be part of that main content via the [`main`](#184.html_the-main-element) element. The distinction should be made clear to the user.

Consider a photo sharing site. A page on that site might describe and show a photograph, and the page might be marked up as follows:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html>
 <head>
  <title>Exampl Pictures: Kissat</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="/style/default">
 </head>
 <body>
  <h1>Kissat</h1>
  <nav>
   <a href="../">Return to photo index</a>
  </nav>

  <main>
  <figure>
   <img src="/pix/39627052_fd8dcd98b5.jpg">
   <figcaption>Kissat</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <p>One of them has six toes!</p>
  <p><small>This photograph is <a rel="license" href="http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php">MIT Licensed</a></small></p>
  </main>
  <footer>
   <a href="/">Home</a> | <a href="../">Photo index</a>
   <p><small>? copyright 2009 Exampl Pictures. All Rights Reserved.</small></p>
  </footer>
 </body>
</html>
```

In this case the [`license`](#184.html_link-type-license) applies to just the photo (the main content of the document), not the whole document. In particular not the design of the page itself, which is covered by the copyright given at the bottom of the document. This should be made clear in the text referencing the licensing link and could also be made clearer in the styling (e.g. making the license link prominently positioned near the photograph, while having the page copyright in small text at the foot of the page, or adding a border to the [`main`](#184.html_the-main-element) element.)

**Synonyms**: For historical reasons, user agents must also treat the keyword "`copyright`" like the [`license`](#184.html_link-type-license) keyword.

##### 4.8.4.7 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-nofollow" data-anolis-xref="rel-nofollow">`nofollow`</dfn>"

The [`nofollow`](#184.html_link-type-nofollow) keyword may be used with [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements. This keyword does not create a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink), but [annotates](#184.html_hyperlink-annotation) any other hyperlinks created by the element (the implied hyperlink, if no other keywords create one).

The [`nofollow`](#184.html_link-type-nofollow) keyword indicates that the link is not endorsed by the original author or publisher of the page, or that the link to the referenced document was included primarily because of a commercial relationship between people affiliated with the two pages.

##### 4.8.4.8 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-noreferrer" data-anolis-xref="rel-noreferrer">`noreferrer`</dfn>"

The [`noreferrer`](#184.html_link-type-noreferrer) keyword may be used with [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements. This keyword does not create a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink), but [annotates](#184.html_hyperlink-annotation) any other hyperlinks created by the element (the implied hyperlink, if no other keywords create one).

It indicates that no referrer information is to be leaked when following the link.

If a user agent follows a link defined by an [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) or [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) element that has the [`noreferrer`](#184.html_link-type-noreferrer) keyword, the user agent must not include a `Referer` (sic) HTTP header ([or equivalent](#184.html_concept-http-equivalent-headers) for other protocols) in the request.

This keyword also [causes the `opener` attribute to remain null](#184.html_noopener) if the hyperlink creates a new [browsing context](#184.html_browsing-context).

##### 4.8.4.9 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-prefetch" data-anolis-xref="rel-prefetch">`prefetch`</dfn>"

The [`prefetch`](#184.html_link-type-prefetch) keyword may be used with [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#184.html_external-resource-link).

The [`prefetch`](#184.html_link-type-prefetch) keyword indicates that preemptively fetching and caching the specified resource is likely to be beneficial, as it is highly likely that the user will require this resource.

There is no default type for resources given by the [`prefetch`](#184.html_link-type-prefetch) keyword.

##### 4.8.4.10 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-search" data-anolis-xref="rel-search">`search`</dfn>"

The [`search`](#184.html_link-type-search) keyword may be used with [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink).

The [`search`](#184.html_link-type-search) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides an interface specifically for searching the document and its related resources.

OpenSearch description documents can be used with [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) elements and the [`search`](#184.html_link-type-search) link type to enable user agents to autodiscover search interfaces. [[OPENSEARCH]](#184.html_refsOPENSEARCH)

##### 4.8.4.11 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-stylesheet" data-anolis-xref="rel-stylesheet">`stylesheet`</dfn>"

The [`stylesheet`](#184.html_link-type-stylesheet) keyword may be used with [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#184.html_external-resource-link) that contributes to the [styling processing model](#184.html_styling).

The specified resource is a resource that describes how to present the document. Exactly how the resource is to be processed depends on the actual type of the resource.

If the [`alternate`](#184.html_rel-alternate) keyword is also specified on the [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) element, then <dfn id="184.html_the-link-is-an-alternative-stylesheet">the link is an alternative stylesheet</dfn>; in this case, the [`title`](#184.html_attr-title) attribute must be specified on the [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) element, with a non-empty value.

The default type for resources given by the [`stylesheet`](#184.html_link-type-stylesheet) keyword is `text/css`.

The appropriate times to [obtain](#184.html_concept-link-obtain) the resource are:

*   When the [external resource link](#184.html_external-resource-link)'s [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) element is [inserted into a document](#184.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document).

*   When the [external resource link](#184.html_external-resource-link) is created on a [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) element that is already [in a `Document`](#184.html_in-a-document).

*   When the [`href`](#184.html_attr-link-href) attribute of the [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#184.html_external-resource-link) that is already [in a `Document`](#184.html_in-a-document) is changed.

**Quirk**: If the document has been set to [quirks mode](#184.html_quirks-mode), has the [same origin](#184.html_same-origin) as the URL of the external resource, and the [Content-Type metadata](#184.html_content-type) of the external resource is not a supported style sheet type, the user agent must instead assume it to be `text/css`.

##### 4.8.4.12 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-tag" data-anolis-xref="rel-tag">`tag`</dfn>"

The [`tag`](#184.html_link-type-tag) keyword may be used with [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink).

The [`tag`](#184.html_link-type-tag) keyword indicates that the *tag* that the referenced document represents applies to the current document.

Since it indicates that the tag *applies to the current document*, it would be inappropriate to use this keyword in the markup of a [tag cloud](#184.html_tag-cloud), which lists the popular tags across a set of pages.

This document is about some gems, and so it is *tagged* with "`http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemstone`" to unambiguously categorise it as applying to the "jewel" kind of gems, and not to, say, the towns in the US, the Ruby package format, or the Swiss locomotive class:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html>
 <head>
  <title>My Precious</title>
 </head>
 <body>
  <header><h1>My precious</h1> <p>Summer 2012</p></header>
  <p>Recently I managed to dispose of a red gem that had been
  bothering me. I now have a much nicer blue sapphire.</p>
  <p>The red gem had been found in a bauxite stone while I was digging
  out the office level, but nobody was willing to haul it away. The
  same red gem stayed there for literally years.</p>
  <footer>
   Tags: <a rel=tag href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemstone">Gemstone</a>
  </footer>
 </body>
</html>
```

In *this* document, there are two articles. The "[`tag`](#184.html_link-type-tag)" link, however, applies to the whole page (and would do so wherever it was placed, including if it was within the [`article`](#184.html_the-article-element) elements).

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html>
 <head>
  <title>Gem 4/4</title>
 </head>
 <body>
  <article>
   <h1>801: Steinbock</h1>
   <p>The number 801 Gem 4/4 electro-diesel has an ibex and was rebuilt in 2002.</p>
  </article>
  <article>
   <h1>802: Murmeltier</h1>
   <figure>
    <img src="../Images/5806324774f83ce2f1eb2eca140a8bb1.jpg"
         alt="The 802 was red with pantographs and tall vents on the side.">
    <figcaption>The 802 in the 1980s, above Lago Bianco.</figcaption>
   </figure>
   <p>The number 802 Gem 4/4 electro-diesel has a marmot and was rebuilt in 2003.</p>
  </article>
  <p class="topic"><a rel=tag href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhaetian_Railway_Gem_4/4">Gem 4/4</a></p>
 </body>
</html>
```

##### 4.8.4.13 Sequential link types

Some documents form part of a sequence of documents.

A sequence of documents is one where each document can have a *previous sibling* and a *next sibling*. A document with no previous sibling is the start of its sequence, a document with no next sibling is the end of its sequence.

A document may be part of multiple sequences.

###### 4.8.4.13.1 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-next" data-anolis-xref="rel-next">`next`</dfn>"

The [`next`](#184.html_link-type-next) keyword may be used with [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink).

The [`next`](#184.html_link-type-next) keyword indicates that the document is part of a sequence, and that the link is leading to the document that is the next logical document in the sequence.

###### 4.8.4.13.2 Link type "<dfn id="184.html_rel-prev" data-anolis-xref="rel-prev">`prev`</dfn>"

The [`prev`](#184.html_link-type-prev) keyword may be used with [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink).

The [`prev`](#184.html_link-type-prev) keyword indicates that the document is part of a sequence, and that the link is leading to the document that is the previous logical document in the sequence.

**Synonyms**: For historical reasons, user agents must also treat the keyword "`previous`" like the [`prev`](#184.html_link-type-prev) keyword.

##### 4.8.4.14 Other link types

<dfn id="184.html_concept-rel-extensions" data-anolis-xref="concept-rel-extensions">Extensions to the predefined set of link types</dfn> may be registered in the [microformats wiki existing-rel-values page](http://microformats.org/wiki/existing-rel-values#HTML5_link_type_extensions). [[MFREL]](#184.html_refsMFREL)

Anyone is free to edit the microformats wiki existing-rel-values page at any time to add a type. Extension types must be specified with the following information:

Keyword

The actual value being defined. The value should not be confusingly similar to any other defined value (e.g. differing only in case).

If the value contains a ":" (U+003A) character, it must also be an [absolute URL](#184.html_absolute-url).

Effect on... [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element)

One of the following:

Not allowed

The keyword must not be specified on [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) elements.

Hyperlink

The keyword may be specified on a [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) element; it creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink).

External Resource

The keyword may be specified on a [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element) element; it creates an [external resource link](#184.html_external-resource-link).

Effect on... [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element)

One of the following:

Not allowed

The keyword must not be specified on [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements.

Hyperlink

The keyword may be specified on [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements; it creates a [hyperlink](#184.html_hyperlink).

External Resource

The keyword may be specified on [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements; it creates an [external resource link](#184.html_external-resource-link).

Hyperlink Annotation

The keyword may be specified on [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element) and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements; it [annotates](#184.html_hyperlink-annotation) other [hyperlinks](#184.html_hyperlink) created by the element.

Brief description

A short non-normative description of what the keyword's meaning is.

Specification

A link to a more detailed description of the keyword's semantics and requirements. It could be another page on the Wiki, or a link to an external page.

Synonyms

A list of other keyword values that have exactly the same processing requirements. Authors should not use the values defined to be synonyms, they are only intended to allow user agents to support legacy content. Anyone may remove synonyms that are not used in practice; only names that need to be processed as synonyms for compatibility with legacy content are to be registered in this way.

Status

One of the following:

Proposed

The keyword has not received wide peer review and approval. Someone has proposed it and is, or soon will be, using it.

Ratified

The keyword has received wide peer review and approval. It has a specification that unambiguously defines how to handle pages that use the keyword, including when they use it in incorrect ways.

Discontinued

The keyword has received wide peer review and it has been found wanting. Existing pages are using this keyword, but new pages should avoid it. The "brief description" and "specification" entries will give details of what authors should use instead, if anything.

If a keyword is found to be redundant with existing values, it should be removed and listed as a synonym for the existing value.

If a keyword is registered in the "proposed" state for a period of a month or more without being used or specified, then it may be removed from the registry.

If a keyword is added with the "proposed" status and found to be redundant with existing values, it should be removed and listed as a synonym for the existing value. If a keyword is added with the "proposed" status and found to be harmful, then it should be changed to "discontinued" status.

Anyone can change the status at any time, but should only do so in accordance with the definitions above.

Conformance checkers may use the information given on the microformats wiki existing-rel-values page to establish if a value is allowed or not: values defined in this specification or marked as "proposed" or "ratified" must be accepted when used on the elements for which they apply as described in the "Effect on..." field, whereas values marked as "discontinued" or values not containing a U+003A COLON character but not listed in either this specification or on the aforementioned page must be reported as invalid. The remaining values must be accepted as valid if they are absolute URLs containing US-ASCII characters only and rejected otherwise. Conformance checkers may cache this information (e.g. for performance reasons or to avoid the use of unreliable network connectivity).

Note: Even URL-valued link types are compared ASCII-case-insensitively. Validators might choose to warn about characters U+0041 (LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A) through U+005A (LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Z) (inclusive) in the pre-case-folded form of link types that contain a colon.

When an author uses a new type not defined by either this specification or the Wiki page, conformance checkers should offer to add the value to the Wiki, with the details described above, with the "proposed" status.

Types defined as extensions in the [microformats wiki existing-rel-values page](http://microformats.org/wiki/existing-rel-values#HTML5_link_type_extensions) with the status "proposed" or "ratified" may be used with the `rel` attribute on [`link`](#184.html_the-link-element), [`a`](#184.html_the-a-element), and [`area`](#184.html_the-area-element) elements in accordance to the "Effect on..." field. [[MFREL]](#184.html_refsMFREL)

### 4.9 Tabular data

#### 4.9.1 The <dfn>`table`</dfn> element

[Categories](#186.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#186.html_flow-content-1).

[Palpable content](#186.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#186.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [flow content](#186.html_flow-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#186.html_element-dfn-content-model):

In this order: optionally a [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element, followed by zero or more [`colgroup`](#186.html_the-colgroup-element) elements, followed optionally by a [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element, followed optionally by a [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element, followed by either zero or more [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) elements or one or more [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) elements, followed optionally by a [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element (but there can only be one [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element child in total), optionally intermixed with one or more [script-supporting elements](#186.html_script-supporting-elements-0).

[Content attributes](#186.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#186.html_global-attributes)

[`border`](#186.html_attr-table-border)

`sortable` - Enables a sorting interface for the table

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#186.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#186.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#186.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#186.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#186.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#186.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTableElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute HTMLTableCaptionElement? caption;
  HTMLElement createCaption();
  void deleteCaption();
           attribute HTMLTableSectionElement? tHead;
  HTMLElement createTHead();
  void deleteTHead();
           attribute HTMLTableSectionElement? tFoot;
  HTMLElement createTFoot();
  void deleteTFoot();
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection tBodies;
  HTMLElement createTBody();
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection rows;
  HTMLElement insertRow(optional long index = -1);
  void deleteRow(long index);
           attribute DOMString border;
};
```

The [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element [represents](#186.html_represents) data with more than one dimension, in the form of a [table](#186.html_concept-table).

The [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element takes part in the [table model](#186.html_table-model). Tables have rows, columns, and cells given by their descendants. The rows and columns form a grid; a table's cells must completely cover that grid without overlap.

Precise rules for determining whether this conformance requirement is met are described in the description of the [table model](#186.html_table-model).

Authors are encouraged to provide information describing how to interpret complex tables. Guidance on how to [provide such information](#186.html_table-descriptions-techniques) is given below.

Tables should not be used as layout aids. Historically, many Web authors have tables in HTML as a way to control their page layout making it difficult to extract tabular data from such documents. In particular, users of accessibility tools, like screen readers, are likely to find it very difficult to navigate pages with tables used for layout. If a table is to be used for layout it must be marked with the attribute role="presentation" for a user agent to properly represent the table to an assistive technology and to properly convey the intent of the author to tools that wish to extract tabular data from the document.

There are a variety of alternatives to using HTML tables for layout, primarily using CSS positioning and the CSS table model. [[CSS]](#186.html_refsCSS)

The <dfn id="186.html_attr-table-border" data-anolis-xref="attr-table-border">`border`</dfn> attribute may be specified on a [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element to explicitly indicate that the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element is not being used for layout purposes. If specified, the attribute's value must either be the empty string or the value "`1`". The attribute is used by certain user agents as an indication that borders should be drawn around cells of the table.

* * *

Tables can be complicated to understand and navigate. To help users with this, user agents should clearly delineate cells in a table from each other, unless the user agent has classified the table as a layout table.

Authors and implementors are encouraged to consider using some of the [table design techniques](#186.html_table-layout-techniques) described below to make tables easier to navigate for users.

User agents, especially those that do table analysis on arbitrary content, are encouraged to find heuristics to determine which tables actually contain data and which are merely being used for layout. This specification does not define a precise heuristic, but the following are suggested as possible indicators:

| Feature | Indication |
| --- | --- |
| The use of the [`role`](#186.html_attr-aria-role) attribute with the value `presentation` | Probably a layout table |
| The use of the [`border`](#186.html_attr-table-border) attribute with the non-conforming value 0 | Probably a layout table |
| The use of the non-conforming [`cellspacing`](#186.html_attr-table-cellspacing) and [`cellpadding`](#186.html_attr-table-cellpadding) attributes with the value 0 | Probably a layout table |
| The use of [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element), [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element), or [`th`](#186.html_the-th-element) elements | Probably a non-layout table |
| The use of the [`headers`](#186.html_attr-tdth-headers) and [`scope`](#186.html_attr-th-scope) attributes | Probably a non-layout table |
| The use of the [`border`](#186.html_attr-table-border) attribute with a value other than 0 | Probably a non-layout table |
| Explicit visible borders set using CSS | Probably a non-layout table |
| The use of the [`summary`](#186.html_attr-table-summary) attribute | Not a good indicator (both layout and non-layout tables have historically been given this attribute) |

It is quite possible that the above suggestions are wrong. Implementors are urged to provide feedback elaborating on their experiences with trying to create a layout table detection heuristic.

* * *

`table` . [`caption`](#186.html_dom-table-caption) [ = `value` ]

Returns the table's [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element.

Can be set, to replace the [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element. If the new value is not a [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element, throws a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#186.html_hierarchyrequesterror) exception.

`caption` = `table` . [`createCaption`](#186.html_dom-table-createcaption)()

Ensures the table has a [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element, and returns it.

`table` . [`deleteCaption`](#186.html_dom-table-deletecaption)()

Ensures the table does not have a [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element.

`table` . [`tHead`](#186.html_dom-table-thead) [ = `value` ]

Returns the table's [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element.

Can be set, to replace the [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element. If the new value is not a [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element, throws a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#186.html_hierarchyrequesterror) exception.

`thead` = `table` . [`createTHead`](#186.html_dom-table-createthead)()

Ensures the table has a [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element, and returns it.

`table` . [`deleteTHead`](#186.html_dom-table-deletethead)()

Ensures the table does not have a [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element.

`table` . [`tFoot`](#186.html_dom-table-tfoot) [ = `value` ]

Returns the table's [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element.

Can be set, to replace the [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element. If the new value is not a [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element, throws a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#186.html_hierarchyrequesterror) exception.

`tfoot` = `table` . [`createTFoot`](#186.html_dom-table-createtfoot)()

Ensures the table has a [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element, and returns it.

`table` . [`deleteTFoot`](#186.html_dom-table-deletetfoot)()

Ensures the table does not have a [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element.

`table` . [`tBodies`](#186.html_dom-table-tbodies)

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#186.html_htmlcollection) of the [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) elements of the table.

`tbody` = `table` . [`createTBody`](#186.html_dom-table-createtbody)()

Creates a [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) element, inserts it into the table, and returns it.

`table` . [`rows`](#186.html_dom-table-rows)

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#186.html_htmlcollection) of the [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) elements of the table.

`tr` = `table` . [`insertRow`](#186.html_dom-table-insertrow)( [ `index` ] )

Creates a [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element, along with a [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) if required, inserts them into the table at the position given by the argument, and returns the [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element).

The position is relative to the rows in the table. The index ?1, which is the default if the argument is omitted, is equivalent to inserting at the end of the table.

If the given position is less than ?1 or greater than the number of rows, throws an [`IndexSizeError`](#186.html_indexsizeerror) exception.

`table` . [`deleteRow`](#186.html_dom-table-deleterow)(`index`)

Removes the [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element with the given position in the table.

The position is relative to the rows in the table. The index ?1 is equivalent to deleting the last row of the table.

If the given position is less than ?1 or greater than the index of the last row, or if there are no rows, throws an [`IndexSizeError`](#186.html_indexsizeerror) exception.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-caption" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-caption">`caption`</dfn> IDL attribute must return, on getting, the first [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any, or null otherwise. On setting, if the new value is a [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element, the first [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any, must be removed, and the new value must be inserted as the first node of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element. If the new value is not a [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element, then a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#186.html_hierarchyrequesterror) DOM exception must be thrown instead.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-createcaption" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-createCaption">`createCaption()`</dfn> method must return the first [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any; otherwise a new [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element must be created, inserted as the first node of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, and then returned.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-deletecaption" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-deleteCaption">`deleteCaption()`</dfn> method must remove the first [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-thead" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-tHead">`tHead`</dfn> IDL attribute must return, on getting, the first [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any, or null otherwise. On setting, if the new value is a [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element, the first [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any, must be removed, and the new value must be inserted immediately before the first element in the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element that is neither a [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element nor a [`colgroup`](#186.html_the-colgroup-element) element, if any, or at the end of the table if there are no such elements. If the new value is not a [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element, then a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#186.html_hierarchyrequesterror) DOM exception must be thrown instead.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-createthead" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-createTHead">`createTHead()`</dfn> method must return the first [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any; otherwise a new [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element must be created and inserted immediately before the first element in the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element that is neither a [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element nor a [`colgroup`](#186.html_the-colgroup-element) element, if any, or at the end of the table if there are no such elements, and then that new element must be returned.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-deletethead" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-deleteTHead">`deleteTHead()`</dfn> method must remove the first [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-tfoot" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-tFoot">`tFoot`</dfn> IDL attribute must return, on getting, the first [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any, or null otherwise. On setting, if the new value is a [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element, the first [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any, must be removed, and the new value must be inserted immediately before the first element in the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element that is neither a [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element, a [`colgroup`](#186.html_the-colgroup-element) element, nor a [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element, if any, or at the end of the table if there are no such elements. If the new value is not a [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element, then a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#186.html_hierarchyrequesterror) DOM exception must be thrown instead.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-createtfoot" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-createTFoot">`createTFoot()`</dfn> method must return the first [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any; otherwise a new [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element must be created and inserted immediately before the first element in the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element that is neither a [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element) element, a [`colgroup`](#186.html_the-colgroup-element) element, nor a [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) element, if any, or at the end of the table if there are no such elements, and then that new element must be returned.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-deletetfoot" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-deleteTFoot">`deleteTFoot()`</dfn> method must remove the first [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element child of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-tbodies" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-tBodies">`tBodies`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#186.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) node, whose filter matches only [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) elements that are children of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-createtbody" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-createTBody">`createTBody()`</dfn> method must create a new [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) element, insert it immediately after the last [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) element child in the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, if any, or at the end of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element if the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element has no [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) element children, and then must return the new [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) element.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-rows" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-rows">`rows`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#186.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) node, whose filter matches only [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) elements that are either children of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, or children of [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element), or [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) elements that are themselves children of the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element. The elements in the collection must be ordered such that those elements whose parent is a [`thead`](#186.html_the-thead-element) are included first, in tree order, followed by those elements whose parent is either a [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) or [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) element, again in tree order, followed finally by those elements whose parent is a [`tfoot`](#186.html_the-tfoot-element) element, still in tree order.

The behavior of the <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-insertrow" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-insertRow">`insertRow(``index``)`</dfn> method depends on the state of the table. When it is called, the method must act as required by the first item in the following list of conditions that describes the state of the table and the `index` argument:

If `index` is less than ?1 or greater than the number of elements in [`rows`](#186.html_dom-table-rows) collection:

The method must throw an [`IndexSizeError`](#186.html_indexsizeerror) exception.

If the [`rows`](#186.html_dom-table-rows) collection has zero elements in it, and the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) has no [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) elements in it:

The method must create a [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) element, then create a [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element, then append the [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element to the [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) element, then append the [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) element to the [`table`](#186.html_the-table-element) element, and finally return the [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element.

If the [`rows`](#186.html_dom-table-rows) collection has zero elements in it:

The method must create a [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element, append it to the last [`tbody`](#186.html_the-tbody-element) element in the table, and return the [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element.

If `index` is ?1 or equal to the number of items in [`rows`](#186.html_dom-table-rows) collection:

The method must create a [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element, and append it to the parent of the last [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element in the [`rows`](#186.html_dom-table-rows) collection. Then, the newly created [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element must be returned.

Otherwise:

The method must create a [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element, insert it immediately before the `index`th [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element in the [`rows`](#186.html_dom-table-rows) collection, in the same parent, and finally must return the newly created [`tr`](#186.html_the-tr-element) element.

When the <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-deleterow" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-deleteRow">`deleteRow(``index``)`</dfn> method is called, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  If `index` is equal to ?1, then `index` must be set to the number of items in the [`rows`](#186.html_dom-table-rows) collection, minus one.

2.  Now, if `index` is less than zero, or greater than or equal to the number of elements in the [`rows`](#186.html_dom-table-rows) collection, the method must instead throw an [`IndexSizeError`](#186.html_indexsizeerror) exception, and these steps must be aborted.

3.  Otherwise, the method must remove the `index`th element in the [`rows`](#186.html_dom-table-rows) collection from its parent.

The <dfn id="186.html_dom-table-border" data-anolis-xref="dom-table-border">`border`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#186.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

Here is an example of a table being used to mark up a Sudoku puzzle. Observe the lack of headers, which are not necessary in such a table.

```
<section>
 <style>
  table { border-collapse: collapse; border: solid thick; }
  colgroup, tbody { border: solid medium; }
  td { border: solid thin; height: 1.4em; width: 1.4em; text-align: center; padding: 0; }
 </style>
 <h1>Today's Sudoku</h1>
 <table>
  <colgroup><col><col><col>
  <colgroup><col><col><col>
  <colgroup><col><col><col>
  <tbody>
   <tr> <td> 1 <td>   <td> 3 <td> 6 <td>   <td> 4 <td> 7 <td>   <td> 9
   <tr> <td>   <td> 2 <td>   <td>   <td> 9 <td>   <td>   <td> 1 <td>
   <tr> <td> 7 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 6
  <tbody>
   <tr> <td> 2 <td>   <td> 4 <td>   <td> 3 <td>   <td> 9 <td>   <td> 8
   <tr> <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>
   <tr> <td> 5 <td>   <td>   <td> 9 <td>   <td> 7 <td>   <td>   <td> 1
  <tbody>
   <tr> <td> 6 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 5 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 2
   <tr> <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 7 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>
   <tr> <td> 9 <td>   <td>   <td> 8 <td>   <td> 2 <td>   <td>   <td> 5
 </table>
</section>
```

##### 4.9.1.1 Techniques for describing tables

For tables that consist of more than just a grid of cells with headers in the first row and headers in the first column, and for any table in general where the reader might have difficulty understanding the content, authors should include explanatory information introducing the table. This information is useful for all users, but is especially useful for users who cannot see the table, e.g. users of screen readers.

Such explanatory information should introduce the purpose of the table, outline its basic cell structure, highlight any trends or patterns, and generally teach the user how to use the table.

For instance, the following table:

Characteristics with positive and negative sides

| Negative | Characteristic | Positive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sad | Mood | Happy |
| Failing | Grade | Passing |

...might benefit from a description explaining the way the table is laid out, something like "Characteristics are given in the second column, with the negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right column".

There are a variety of ways to include this information, such as:

In prose, surrounding the table

```
<p id="summary">In the following table, characteristics are 
given in the second column, with the negative side in the left column and the positive
side in the right column.</p>
<table aria-describedby="summary">
 <caption>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</caption>
 <thead>
  <tr>
   <th id="n"> Negative
   <th> Characteristic
   <th> Positive
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td headers="n r1"> Sad
   <th id="r1"> Mood
   <td> Happy
  <tr>
   <td headers="n r2"> Failing
   <th id="r2"> Grade
   <td> Passing
</table>
```

In the example above the [`aria-describedby`](http://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/states_and_properties#aria-describedby) attribute is used to explicitly associate the information with the table for assistive technology users.

In the table's [`caption`](#186.html_the-caption-element)

```
<table>
 <caption>
  <strong>Characteristics with positive and negative sides.</strong>
  <p>Characteristics are given in the second column, with the
  negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right
  column.</p>
 </caption>
 <thead>
  <tr>
   <th id="n"> Negative
   <th> Characteristic
   <th> Positive
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <td headers="n r1"> Sad
   <th id="r1"> Mood
   <td> Happy
  <tr>
   <td headers="n r2"> Failing
   <th id="r2"> Grade
   <td> Passing
</table>
```

Next to the table, in the same [`figure`](#186.html_the-figure-element)

```
<figure>
 <figcaption>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</figcaption>
 <p>Characteristics are given in the second column, with the
 negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right
 column.</p>
 <table>
  <thead>
   <tr>
    <th id="n"> Negative
    <th> Characteristic
    <th> Positive
  <tbody>
   <tr>
    <td headers="n r1"> Sad
    <th id="r1"> Mood
    <td> Happy
   <tr>
    <td headers="n r2"> Failing
    <th id="r2"> Grade
    <td> Passing
 </table>
</figure>
```

Next to the table, in a [`figure`](#186.html_the-figure-element)'s [`figcaption`](#186.html_the-figcaption-element)

```
<figure>
 <figcaption>
  <strong>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</strong>
  <p>Characteristics are given in the second column, with the
  negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right
  column.</p>
 </figcaption>
 <table>
  <thead>
   <tr>
    <th id="n"> Negative
    <th> Characteristic
    <th> Positive
  <tbody>
   <tr>
    <td headers="n r1"> Sad
    <th id="r1"> Mood
    <td> Happy
   <tr>
    <td headers="n r2"> Failing
    <th id="r2"> Grade
    <td> Passing
 </table>
</figure>
```

Authors may also use other techniques, or combinations of the above techniques, as appropriate.

The best option, of course, rather than writing a description explaining the way the table is laid out, is to adjust the table such that no explanation is needed.

In the case of the table used in the examples above, a simple rearrangement of the table so that the headers are on the top and left sides removes the need for an explanation as well as removing the need for the use of [`headers`](#186.html_attr-tdth-headers) attributes:

```
<table>
 <caption>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</caption>
 <thead>
  <tr>
   <th> Characteristic
   <th> Negative
   <th> Positive
 <tbody>
  <tr>
   <th> Mood
   <td> Sad
   <td> Happy
  <tr>
   <th> Grade
   <td> Failing
   <td> Passing
</table>
```

##### 4.9.1.2 Techniques for table design

Good table design is key to making tables more readable and usable.

In visual media, providing column and row borders and alternating row backgrounds can be very effective to make complicated tables more readable.

For tables with large volumes of numeric content, using monospaced fonts can help users see patterns, especially in situations where a user agent does not render the borders. (Unfortunately, for historical reasons, not rendering borders on tables is a common default.)

In speech media, table cells can be distinguished by reporting the corresponding headers before reading the cell's contents, and by allowing users to navigate the table in a grid fashion, rather than serializing the entire contents of the table in source order.

Authors are encouraged to use CSS to achieve these effects.

User agents are encouraged to render tables using these techniques whenever the page does not use CSS and the table is not classified as a layout table.

#### 4.9.2 The <dfn>`caption`</dfn> element

[Categories](#187.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#187.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As the first element child of a [`table`](#187.html_the-table-element) element.

[Content model](#187.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Flow content](#187.html_flow-content-1), but with no descendant [`table`](#187.html_the-table-element) elements.

[Content attributes](#187.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#187.html_global-attributes)

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#187.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#187.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#187.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#187.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#187.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#187.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTableCaptionElement : HTMLElement {};
```

The [`caption`](#187.html_the-caption-element) element [represents](#187.html_represents) the title of the [`table`](#187.html_the-table-element) that is its parent, if it has a parent and that is a [`table`](#187.html_the-table-element) element.

The [`caption`](#187.html_the-caption-element) element takes part in the [table model](#187.html_table-model).

When a [`table`](#187.html_the-table-element) element is the only content in a [`figure`](#187.html_the-figure-element) element other than the [`figcaption`](#187.html_the-figcaption-element), the [`caption`](#187.html_the-caption-element) element should be omitted in favor of the [`figcaption`](#187.html_the-figcaption-element).

A caption can introduce context for a table, making it significantly easier to understand.

Consider, for instance, the following table:

|  | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
| 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
| 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 |
| 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 |
| 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 |

In the abstract, this table is not clear. However, with a caption giving the table's number (for reference in the main prose) and explaining its use, it makes more sense:

```
<caption>
<p>Table 1.
<p>This table shows the total score obtained from rolling two
six-sided dice. The first row represents the value of the first die,
the first column the value of the second die. The total is given in
the cell that corresponds to the values of the two dice.
</caption>
```

This provides the user with more context:

Table 1.

This table shows the total score obtained from rolling two six-sided dice. The first row represents the value of the first die, the first column the value of the second die. The total is given in the cell that corresponds to the values of the two dice.

|  | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
| 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
| 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
| 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 |
| 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 |
| 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 |

#### 4.9.3 The <dfn>`colgroup`</dfn> element

[Categories](#188.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#188.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As a child of a [`table`](#188.html_the-table-element) element, after any [`caption`](#188.html_the-caption-element) elements and before any [`thead`](#188.html_the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#188.html_the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#188.html_the-tfoot-element), and [`tr`](#188.html_the-tr-element) elements.

[Content model](#188.html_element-dfn-content-model):

If the [`span`](#188.html_attr-colgroup-span) attribute is present: Empty.

If the [`span`](#188.html_attr-colgroup-span) attribute is absent: Zero or more [`col`](#188.html_the-col-element) and [`template`](#188.html_the-template-element) elements.

[Content attributes](#188.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#188.html_global-attributes)

[`span`](#188.html_attr-colgroup-span) - Number of columns spanned by the element

Tag omission in text/html:

A [`colgroup`](#188.html_the-colgroup-element) element's [end tag](#188.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`colgroup`](#188.html_the-colgroup-element) element is not immediately followed by a [space character](#188.html_space-character) or a [comment](#188.html_syntax-comments). A [`colgroup`](#188.html_the-colgroup-element) element's [end tag](#188.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`colgroup`](#188.html_the-colgroup-element) element is not immediately followed by a [space character](#188.html_space-character) or a [comment](#188.html_syntax-comments).

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#188.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#188.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#188.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#188.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTableColElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute unsigned long span;
};
```

The [`colgroup`](#188.html_the-colgroup-element) element [represents](#188.html_represents) a [group](#188.html_concept-column-group) of one or more [columns](#188.html_concept-column) in the [`table`](#188.html_the-table-element) that is its parent, if it has a parent and that is a [`table`](#188.html_the-table-element) element.

If the [`colgroup`](#188.html_the-colgroup-element) element contains no [`col`](#188.html_the-col-element) elements, then the element may have a <dfn id="188.html_attr-colgroup-span" data-anolis-xref="attr-colgroup-span">`span`</dfn> content attribute specified, whose value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#188.html_valid-non-negative-integer) greater than zero.

The [`colgroup`](#188.html_the-colgroup-element) element and its [`span`](#188.html_attr-colgroup-span) attribute take part in the [table model](#188.html_table-model).

The <dfn id="188.html_dom-colgroup-span" data-anolis-xref="dom-colgroup-span">`span`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#188.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name. The value must be [limited to only non-negative numbers greater than zero](#188.html_limited-to-only-non-negative-numbers-greater-than-zero).
