#### 4.9.5 The <dfn>`tbody`</dfn> element

[Categories](#190.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#190.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As a child of a [`table`](#190.html_the-table-element) element, after any [`caption`](#190.html_the-caption-element), [`colgroup`](#190.html_the-colgroup-element), and [`thead`](#190.html_the-thead-element) elements, but only if there are no [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) elements that are children of the [`table`](#190.html_the-table-element) element.

[Content model](#190.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Zero or more [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) and [script-supporting](#190.html_script-supporting-elements-0) elements

[Content attributes](#190.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#190.html_global-attributes)

Tag omission in text/html:

A [`tbody`](#190.html_the-tbody-element) element's [start tag](#190.html_syntax-start-tag) may be omitted if the first thing inside the [`tbody`](#190.html_the-tbody-element) element is a [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) element, and if the element is not immediately preceded by a [`tbody`](#190.html_the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#190.html_the-thead-element), or [`tfoot`](#190.html_the-tfoot-element) element whose [end tag](#190.html_syntax-end-tag) has been omitted. (It can't be omitted if the element is empty.). A [`tbody`](#190.html_the-tbody-element) element's [end tag](#190.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`tbody`](#190.html_the-tbody-element) element is immediately followed by a [`tbody`](#190.html_the-tbody-element) or [`tfoot`](#190.html_the-tfoot-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#190.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#190.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#190.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#190.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#190.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#190.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTableSectionElement : HTMLElement {
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection rows;
  HTMLElement insertRow(optional long index = -1);
  void deleteRow(long index);
};
```

The [`HTMLTableSectionElement`](#190.html_htmltablesectionelement) interface is also used for [`thead`](#190.html_the-thead-element) and [`tfoot`](#190.html_the-tfoot-element) elements.

The [`tbody`](#190.html_the-tbody-element) element [represents](#190.html_represents) a [block](#190.html_concept-row-group) of [rows](#190.html_concept-row) that consist of a body of data for the parent [`table`](#190.html_the-table-element) element, if the [`tbody`](#190.html_the-tbody-element) element has a parent and it is a [`table`](#190.html_the-table-element).

The [`tbody`](#190.html_the-tbody-element) element takes part in the [table model](#190.html_table-model).

`tbody` . [`rows`](#190.html_dom-tbody-rows)

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#190.html_htmlcollection) of the [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) elements of the table section.

`tr` = `tbody` . [`insertRow`](#190.html_dom-tbody-insertrow)( [ `index` ] )

Creates a [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) element, inserts it into the table section at the position given by the argument, and returns the [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element).

The position is relative to the rows in the table section. The index ?1, which is the default if the argument is omitted, is equivalent to inserting at the end of the table section.

If the given position is less than ?1 or greater than the number of rows, throws an [`IndexSizeError`](#190.html_indexsizeerror) exception.

`tbody` . [`deleteRow`](#190.html_dom-tbody-deleterow)(`index`)

Removes the [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) element with the given position in the table section.

The position is relative to the rows in the table section. The index ?1 is equivalent to deleting the last row of the table section.

If the given position is less than ?1 or greater than the index of the last row, or if there are no rows, throws an [`IndexSizeError`](#190.html_indexsizeerror) exception.

The <dfn id="190.html_dom-tbody-rows" data-anolis-xref="dom-tbody-rows">`rows`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#190.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the element, whose filter matches only [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) elements that are children of the element.

The <dfn id="190.html_dom-tbody-insertrow" data-anolis-xref="dom-tbody-insertRow">`insertRow(``index``)`</dfn> method must, when invoked on an element `table section`, act as follows:

If `index` is less than ?1 or greater than the number of elements in the [`rows`](#190.html_dom-tbody-rows) collection, the method must throw an [`IndexSizeError`](#190.html_indexsizeerror) exception.

If `index` is ?1 or equal to the number of items in the [`rows`](#190.html_dom-tbody-rows) collection, the method must create a [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) element, append it to the element `table section`, and return the newly created [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) element.

Otherwise, the method must create a [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) element, insert it as a child of the `table section` element, immediately before the `index`th [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) element in the [`rows`](#190.html_dom-tbody-rows) collection, and finally must return the newly created [`tr`](#190.html_the-tr-element) element.

The <dfn id="190.html_dom-tbody-deleterow" data-anolis-xref="dom-tbody-deleteRow">`deleteRow(``index``)`</dfn> method must remove the `index`th element in the [`rows`](#190.html_dom-tbody-rows) collection from its parent. If `index` is less than zero or greater than or equal to the number of elements in the [`rows`](#190.html_dom-tbody-rows) collection, the method must instead throw an [`IndexSizeError`](#190.html_indexsizeerror) exception.

Notice the use of both [`th`](#191.html_the-th-element) and [`td`](#191.html_the-td-element) elements in the [`thead`](#191.html_the-thead-element) element: the first row is the headers, and the second row is an explanation of how to fill in the table.

```
 <thead>

  <tr>

 <tbody>

   <td>$45
  <tr>

   <td><input id=e2 type=text name=what required form=f>
   <td><input id=e3 type=url name=pic form=f>
   <td><input id=e4 type=number step=0.01 min=0 value=0 required form=f>
</table>
<form id=f action="/auction.cgi">
 <input type=button name=add value="Submit">
</form>
```

As a child of a [`table`](#193.html_the-table-element) element, after any [`caption`](#193.html_the-caption-element), [`colgroup`](#193.html_the-colgroup-element), and [`thead`](#193.html_the-thead-element) elements, but only if there are no [`tbody`](#193.html_the-tbody-element) elements that are children of the [`table`](#193.html_the-table-element) element.

[Content model](#193.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Zero or more [`td`](#193.html_the-td-element), [`th`](#193.html_the-th-element), and [script-supporting](#193.html_script-supporting-elements-0) elements

[Content attributes](#193.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#193.html_global-attributes)

Tag omission in text/html:

A [`tr`](#193.html_the-tr-element) element's [end tag](#193.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`tr`](#193.html_the-tr-element) element is immediately followed by another [`tr`](#193.html_the-tr-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#193.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#193.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#193.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#193.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#193.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#193.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTableRowElement : HTMLElement {
  readonly attribute long rowIndex;
  readonly attribute long sectionRowIndex;
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection cells;
  HTMLElement insertCell(optional long index = -1);
  void deleteCell(long index);
};
```

The [`tr`](#193.html_the-tr-element) element [represents](#193.html_represents) a [row](#193.html_concept-row) of [cells](#193.html_concept-cell) in a [table](#193.html_concept-table).

The [`tr`](#193.html_the-tr-element) element takes part in the [table model](#193.html_table-model).

`tr` . [`rowIndex`](#193.html_dom-tr-rowindex)

Returns the position of the row in the table's [`rows`](#193.html_dom-table-rows) list.

Returns ?1 if the element isn't in a table.

`tr` . [`sectionRowIndex`](#193.html_dom-tr-sectionrowindex)

Returns the position of the row in the table section's [`rows`](#193.html_dom-tbody-rows) list.

Returns ?1 if the element isn't in a table section.

`tr` . [`cells`](#193.html_dom-tr-cells)

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#193.html_htmlcollection) of the [`td`](#193.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#193.html_the-th-element) elements of the row.

`cell` = `tr` . [`insertCell`](#193.html_dom-tr-insertcell)( [ `index` ] )

Creates a [`td`](#193.html_the-td-element) element, inserts it into the table row at the position given by the argument, and returns the [`td`](#193.html_the-td-element).

The position is relative to the cells in the row. The index ?1, which is the default if the argument is omitted, is equivalent to inserting at the end of the row.

If the given position is less than ?1 or greater than the number of cells, throws an [`IndexSizeError`](#193.html_indexsizeerror) exception.

`tr` . [`deleteCell`](#193.html_dom-tr-deletecell)(`index`)

Removes the [`td`](#193.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#193.html_the-th-element) element with the given position in the row.

The position is relative to the cells in the row. The index ?1 is equivalent to deleting the last cell of the row.

If the given position is less than ?1 or greater than the index of the last cell, or if there are no cells, throws an [`IndexSizeError`](#193.html_indexsizeerror) exception.

The <dfn id="193.html_dom-tr-rowindex" data-anolis-xref="dom-tr-rowIndex">`rowIndex`</dfn> attribute must, if the element has a parent [`table`](#193.html_the-table-element) element, or a parent [`tbody`](#193.html_the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#193.html_the-thead-element), or [`tfoot`](#193.html_the-tfoot-element) element and a *grandparent* [`table`](#193.html_the-table-element) element, return the index of the [`tr`](#193.html_the-tr-element) element in that [`table`](#193.html_the-table-element) element's [`rows`](#193.html_dom-table-rows) collection. If there is no such [`table`](#193.html_the-table-element) element, then the attribute must return ?1.

The <dfn id="193.html_dom-tr-sectionrowindex" data-anolis-xref="dom-tr-sectionRowIndex">`sectionRowIndex`</dfn> attribute must, if the element has a parent [`table`](#193.html_the-table-element), [`tbody`](#193.html_the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#193.html_the-thead-element), or [`tfoot`](#193.html_the-tfoot-element) element, return the index of the [`tr`](#193.html_the-tr-element) element in the parent element's `rows` collection (for tables, that's the [`HTMLTableElement.rows`](#193.html_dom-table-rows) collection; for table sections, that's the [`HTMLTableRowElement.rows`](#193.html_dom-tbody-rows) collection). If there is no such parent element, then the attribute must return ?1.

The <dfn id="193.html_dom-tr-cells" data-anolis-xref="dom-tr-cells">`cells`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#193.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`tr`](#193.html_the-tr-element) element, whose filter matches only [`td`](#193.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#193.html_the-th-element) elements that are children of the [`tr`](#193.html_the-tr-element) element.

The <dfn id="193.html_dom-tr-insertcell" data-anolis-xref="dom-tr-insertCell">`insertCell(``index``)`</dfn> method must act as follows:

If `index` is less than ?1 or greater than the number of elements in the [`cells`](#193.html_dom-tr-cells) collection, the method must throw an [`IndexSizeError`](#193.html_indexsizeerror) exception.

If `index` is equal to ?1 or equal to the number of items in [`cells`](#193.html_dom-tr-cells) collection, the method must create a [`td`](#193.html_the-td-element) element, append it to the [`tr`](#193.html_the-tr-element) element, and return the newly created [`td`](#193.html_the-td-element) element.

Otherwise, the method must create a [`td`](#193.html_the-td-element) element, insert it as a child of the [`tr`](#193.html_the-tr-element) element, immediately before the `index`th [`td`](#193.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#193.html_the-th-element) element in the [`cells`](#193.html_dom-tr-cells) collection, and finally must return the newly created [`td`](#193.html_the-td-element) element.

The <dfn id="193.html_dom-tr-deletecell" data-anolis-xref="dom-tr-deleteCell">`deleteCell(``index``)`</dfn> method must remove the `index`th element in the [`cells`](#193.html_dom-tr-cells) collection from its parent. If `index` is less than zero or greater than or equal to the number of elements in the [`cells`](#193.html_dom-tr-cells) collection, the method must instead throw an [`IndexSizeError`](#193.html_indexsizeerror) exception.

#### 4.9.9 The <dfn>`td`</dfn> element

[Categories](#194.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Sectioning root](#194.html_sectioning-root).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#194.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As a child of a [`tr`](#194.html_the-tr-element) element.

[Content model](#194.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Flow content](#194.html_flow-content-1).

[Content attributes](#194.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#194.html_global-attributes)

[`colspan`](#194.html_attr-tdth-colspan) - Number of columns that the cell is to span

[`rowspan`](#194.html_attr-tdth-rowspan) - Number of rows that the cell is to span

[`headers`](#194.html_attr-tdth-headers) - The header cells for this cell

Tag omission in text/html:

A [`td`](#194.html_the-td-element) element's [end tag](#194.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`td`](#194.html_the-td-element) element is immediately followed by a [`td`](#194.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#194.html_the-th-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#194.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#194.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#194.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#194.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#194.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#194.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTableDataCellElement : HTMLTableCellElement {};
```

The [`td`](#194.html_the-td-element) element [represents](#194.html_represents) a data [cell](#194.html_concept-cell) in a table.

The [`td`](#194.html_the-td-element) element and its [`colspan`](#194.html_attr-tdth-colspan), [`rowspan`](#194.html_attr-tdth-rowspan), and [`headers`](#194.html_attr-tdth-headers) attributes take part in the [table model](#194.html_table-model).

User agents, especially in non-visual environments or where displaying the table as a 2D grid is impractical, may give the user context for the cell when rendering the contents of a cell; for instance, giving its position in the [table model](#194.html_table-model), or listing the cell's header cells (as determined by the [algorithm for assigning header cells](#194.html_algorithm-for-assigning-header-cells)). When a cell's header cells are being listed, user agents may use the value of [`abbr`](#194.html_attr-th-abbr) attributes on those header cells, if any, instead of the contents of the header cells themselves.

#### 4.9.10 The <dfn>`th`</dfn> element

[Categories](#195.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#195.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As a child of a [`tr`](#195.html_the-tr-element) element.

[Content model](#195.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Flow content](#195.html_flow-content-1), but with no [`header`](#195.html_the-header-element), [`footer`](#195.html_the-footer-element), [sectioning content](#195.html_sectioning-content-0), or [heading content](#195.html_heading-content-0) descendants.

[Content attributes](#195.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#195.html_global-attributes)

[`colspan`](#195.html_attr-tdth-colspan) - Number of columns that the cell is to span

[`rowspan`](#195.html_attr-tdth-rowspan) - Number of rows that the cell is to span

[`headers`](#195.html_attr-tdth-headers) - The headers for this cell

[`scope`](#195.html_attr-th-scope) - Specifies which cells the header cell applies to

[`abbr`](#195.html_attr-th-abbr) - Alternative label to use for the header cell when referencing the cell in other contexts

`sorted` - Column sort direction and ordinality

Tag omission in text/html:

A [`th`](#195.html_the-th-element) element's [end tag](#195.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`th`](#195.html_the-th-element) element is immediately followed by a [`td`](#195.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#195.html_the-th-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#195.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#195.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#195.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#195.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#195.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#195.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTableHeaderCellElement : HTMLTableCellElement {
           attribute DOMString scope;
           attribute DOMString abbr;
};
```

The [`th`](#195.html_the-th-element) element [represents](#195.html_represents) a header [cell](#195.html_concept-cell) in a table.

The [`th`](#195.html_the-th-element) element may have a <dfn id="195.html_attr-th-scope" data-anolis-xref="attr-th-scope">`scope`</dfn> content attribute specified. The [`scope`](#195.html_attr-th-scope) attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#195.html_enumerated-attribute) with five states, four of which have explicit keywords:

The <dfn id="195.html_attr-th-scope-row" data-anolis-xref="attr-th-scope-row">`row`</dfn> keyword, which maps to the *row* state

The *row* state means the header cell applies to some of the subsequent cells in the same row(s).

The <dfn id="195.html_attr-th-scope-col" data-anolis-xref="attr-th-scope-col">`col`</dfn> keyword, which maps to the *column* state

The *column* state means the header cell applies to some of the subsequent cells in the same column(s).

The <dfn id="195.html_attr-th-scope-rowgroup" data-anolis-xref="attr-th-scope-rowgroup">`rowgroup`</dfn> keyword, which maps to the *row group* state

The *row group* state means the header cell applies to all the remaining cells in the row group. A [`th`](#195.html_the-th-element) element's [`scope`](#195.html_attr-th-scope) attribute must not be in the [row group](#195.html_attr-th-scope-rowgroup) state if the element is not anchored in a [row group](#195.html_concept-row-group).

The <dfn id="195.html_attr-th-scope-colgroup" data-anolis-xref="attr-th-scope-colgroup">`colgroup`</dfn> keyword, which maps to the *column group* state

The *column group* state means the header cell applies to all the remaining cells in the column group. A [`th`](#195.html_the-th-element) element's [`scope`](#195.html_attr-th-scope) attribute must not be in the [column group](#195.html_attr-th-scope-colgroup) state if the element is not anchored in a [column group](#195.html_concept-column-group).

The <dfn id="195.html_attr-th-scope-auto" data-anolis-xref="attr-th-scope-auto">auto</dfn> state

The *auto* state makes the header cell apply to a set of cells selected based on context.

The [`scope`](#195.html_attr-th-scope) attribute's *missing value default* is the *auto* state.

The [`th`](#195.html_the-th-element) element may have an <dfn id="195.html_attr-th-abbr" data-anolis-xref="attr-th-abbr">`abbr`</dfn> content attribute specified. Its value must be an alternative label for the header cell, to be used when referencing the cell in other contexts (e.g. when describing the header cells that apply to a data cell). It is typically an abbreviated form of the full header cell, but can also be an expansion, or merely a different phrasing.

The [`th`](#195.html_the-th-element) element and its [`colspan`](#195.html_attr-tdth-colspan), [`rowspan`](#195.html_attr-tdth-rowspan), [`headers`](#195.html_attr-tdth-headers), and [`scope`](#195.html_attr-th-scope) attributes take part in the [table model](#195.html_table-model).

The <dfn id="195.html_dom-th-scope" data-anolis-xref="dom-th-scope">`scope`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#195.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name, [limited to only known values](#195.html_limited-to-only-known-values).

The following example shows how the [`scope`](#195.html_attr-th-scope) attribute's [`rowgroup`](#195.html_attr-th-scope-rowgroup) value affects which data cells a header cell applies to.

Here is a markup fragment showing a table:

The [`tbody`](#195.html_the-tbody-element) elements in this example identify the range of the row groups.

```
<table>
   <caption>Measurement of legs and tails in Cats and English speakers</caption>
 <thead>
  <tr> <th> ID <th> Measurement <th> Average <th> Maximum
 <tbody>
  <tr> <td> <th scope=rowgroup> Cats <td> <td>
  <tr> <td> 93 <th scope=row> Legs <td> 3.5 <td> 4
  <tr> <td> 10 <th scope=row> Tails <td> 1 <td> 1
 </tbody>
 <tbody>
  <tr> <td> <th scope=rowgroup> English speakers <td> <td>
  <tr> <td> 32 <th scope=row> Legs <td> 2.67 <td> 4
  <tr> <td> 35 <th scope=row> Tails <td> 0.33 <td> 1
 </tbody>
  </table>
```

This would result in the following table:

Measurement of legs and tails in Cats and English speakers

| ID | Measurement | Average | Maximum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | Cats |  |  |
| 93 | Legs | 3.5 | 4 |
| 10 | Tails | 1 | 1 |
|  | English speakers |  |  |
| 32 | Legs | 2.67 | 4 |
| 35 | Tails | 0.33 | 1 |

The header cells in row 1 ('ID', 'Measurement', 'Average' and 'Maximum') each apply only to the cells in their column.

The header cells with a `scope=rowgroup` ('Cats' and 'English speakers') apply to all the cells in their row group other than the cells (to their left) in column 1:

The header 'Cats' (row 2, column 2) applies to the headers 'Legs' (row 3, column 2) and 'Tails' (row 4, column 2) and to the data cells in rows 2, 3 and 4 of the 'Average' and 'Maximum' columns.

The header 'English speakers' (row 5, column 2) applies to the headers 'Legs' (row 6, column 2) and 'Tails' (row 7, column 2) and to the data cells in rows 5, 6 and 7 of the 'Average' and 'Maximum' columns.

Each of the 'Legs' and 'Tails' header cells has a `scope=row` and therefore apply to the data cells (to the right) in their row, from the 'Average' and 'Maximum' columns.

![Representation of the example table overlayed with arrows indicating which cells each header applies to.](Images/769f9c3751ef66aa662e2a9c86f67b73.jpg)

#### 4.9.11 Attributes common to [`td`](#196.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) elements

The [`td`](#196.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) elements may have a <dfn id="196.html_attr-tdth-colspan" data-anolis-xref="attr-tdth-colspan">`colspan`</dfn> content attribute specified, whose value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#196.html_valid-non-negative-integer) greater than zero.

The [`td`](#196.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) elements may also have a <dfn id="196.html_attr-tdth-rowspan" data-anolis-xref="attr-tdth-rowspan">`rowspan`</dfn> content attribute specified, whose value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#196.html_valid-non-negative-integer). For this attribute, the value zero means that the cell is to span all the remaining rows in the row group.

These attributes give the number of columns and rows respectively that the cell is to span. These attributes must not be used to overlap cells, as described in the description of the [table model](#196.html_table-model).

* * *

The [`td`](#196.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) element may have a <dfn id="196.html_attr-tdth-headers" data-anolis-xref="attr-tdth-headers">`headers`</dfn> content attribute specified. The [`headers`](#196.html_attr-tdth-headers) attribute, if specified, must contain a string consisting of an [unordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#196.html_unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens) that are [case-sensitive](#196.html_case-sensitive), each of which must have the value of an [ID](#196.html_concept-id) of a [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) element taking part in the same [table](#196.html_concept-table) as the [`td`](#196.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) element (as defined by the [table model](#196.html_table-model)).

A [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) element with [ID](#196.html_concept-id) `id` is said to be *directly targeted* by all [`td`](#196.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) elements in the same [table](#196.html_concept-table) that have [`headers`](#196.html_attr-tdth-headers) attributes whose values include as one of their tokens the [ID](#196.html_concept-id) `id`. A [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) element `A` is said to be *targeted* by a [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) or [`td`](#196.html_the-td-element) element `B` if either `A` is *directly targeted* by `B` or if there exists an element `C` that is itself *targeted* by the element `B` and `A` is *directly targeted* by `C`.

A [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) element must not be *targeted* by itself.

The [`colspan`](#196.html_attr-tdth-colspan), [`rowspan`](#196.html_attr-tdth-rowspan), and [`headers`](#196.html_attr-tdth-headers) attributes take part in the [table model](#196.html_table-model).

* * *

The [`td`](#196.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#196.html_the-th-element) elements implement interfaces that inherit from the [`HTMLTableCellElement`](#196.html_htmltablecellelement) interface:

```
interface HTMLTableCellElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute unsigned long colSpan;
           attribute unsigned long rowSpan;
  [PutForwards=value] readonly attribute DOMSettableTokenList headers;
  readonly attribute long cellIndex;
};
```

`cell` . [`cellIndex`](#196.html_dom-tdth-cellindex)

Returns the position of the cell in the row's [`cells`](#196.html_dom-tr-cells) list. This does not necessarily correspond to the `x`-position of the cell in the table, since earlier cells might cover multiple rows or columns.

Returns ?1 if the element isn't in a row.

The <dfn id="196.html_dom-tdth-colspan" data-anolis-xref="dom-tdth-colSpan">`colSpan`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#196.html_reflect) the [`colspan`](#196.html_attr-tdth-colspan) content attribute. Its default value is 1.

The <dfn id="196.html_dom-tdth-rowspan" data-anolis-xref="dom-tdth-rowSpan">`rowSpan`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#196.html_reflect) the [`rowspan`](#196.html_attr-tdth-rowspan) content attribute. Its default value is 1.

The <dfn id="196.html_dom-tdth-headers" data-anolis-xref="dom-tdth-headers">`headers`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#196.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

The <dfn id="196.html_dom-tdth-cellindex" data-anolis-xref="dom-tdth-cellIndex">`cellIndex`</dfn> IDL attribute must, if the element has a parent [`tr`](#196.html_the-tr-element) element, return the index of the cell's element in the parent element's [`cells`](#196.html_dom-tr-cells) collection. If there is no such parent element, then the attribute must return ?1.

#### 4.9.12 Processing model

The various table elements and their content attributes together define the <dfn id="197.html_table-model">table model</dfn>.

A <dfn id="197.html_concept-table" data-anolis-xref="concept-table">table</dfn> consists of cells aligned on a two-dimensional grid of <dfn id="197.html_concept-slots" data-anolis-xref="concept-slots">slots</dfn> with coordinates (`x`, `y`). The grid is finite, and is either empty or has one or more slots. If the grid has one or more slots, then the `x` coordinates are always in the range 0 ≤ `x` < `x`[`width`], and the `y` coordinates are always in the range 0 ≤ `y` < `y`[`height`]. If one or both of `x`[`width`] and `y`[`height`] are zero, then the table is empty (has no slots). Tables correspond to [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element) elements.

A <dfn id="197.html_concept-cell" data-anolis-xref="concept-cell">cell</dfn> is a set of slots anchored at a slot (`cell`[`x`], `cell`[`y`]), and with a particular `width` and `height` such that the cell covers all the slots with coordinates (`x`, `y`) where `cell`[`x`] ≤ `x` < `cell`[`x`]+`width` and `cell`[`y`] ≤ `y` < `cell`[`y`]+`height`. Cells can either be *data cells* or *header cells*. Data cells correspond to [`td`](#197.html_the-td-element) elements, and header cells correspond to [`th`](#197.html_the-th-element) elements. Cells of both types can have zero or more associated header cells.

It is possible, in certain error cases, for two cells to occupy the same slot.

A <dfn id="197.html_concept-row" data-anolis-xref="concept-row">row</dfn> is a complete set of slots from `x`=0 to `x`=`x`[`width`]-1, for a particular value of `y`. Rows usually correspond to [`tr`](#197.html_the-tr-element) elements, though a [row group](#197.html_concept-row-group) can have some implied [rows](#197.html_concept-row) at the end in some cases involving [cells](#197.html_concept-cell) spanning multiple rows.

A <dfn id="197.html_concept-column" data-anolis-xref="concept-column">column</dfn> is a complete set of slots from `y`=0 to `y`=`y`[`height`]-1, for a particular value of `x`. Columns can correspond to [`col`](#197.html_the-col-element) elements. In the absence of [`col`](#197.html_the-col-element) elements, columns are implied.

A <dfn id="197.html_concept-row-group" data-anolis-xref="concept-row-group">row group</dfn> is a set of [rows](#197.html_concept-row) anchored at a slot (0, `group`[`y`]) with a particular `height` such that the row group covers all the slots with coordinates (`x`, `y`) where 0 ≤ `x` < `x`[`width`] and `group`[`y`] ≤ `y` < `group`[`y`]+`height`. Row groups correspond to [`tbody`](#197.html_the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#197.html_the-thead-element), and [`tfoot`](#197.html_the-tfoot-element) elements. Not every row is necessarily in a row group.

A <dfn id="197.html_concept-column-group" data-anolis-xref="concept-column-group">column group</dfn> is a set of [columns](#197.html_concept-column) anchored at a slot (`group`[`x`], 0) with a particular `width` such that the column group covers all the slots with coordinates (`x`, `y`) where `group`[`x`] ≤ `x` < `group`[`x`]+`width` and 0 ≤ `y` < `y`[`height`]. Column groups correspond to [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element) elements. Not every column is necessarily in a column group.

[Row groups](#197.html_concept-row-group) cannot overlap each other. Similarly, [column groups](#197.html_concept-column-group) cannot overlap each other.

A [cell](#197.html_concept-cell) cannot cover slots that are from two or more [row groups](#197.html_concept-row-group). It is, however, possible for a cell to be in multiple [column groups](#197.html_concept-column-group). All the slots that form part of one cell are part of zero or one [row groups](#197.html_concept-row-group) and zero or more [column groups](#197.html_concept-column-group).

In addition to [cells](#197.html_concept-cell), [columns](#197.html_concept-column), [rows](#197.html_concept-row), [row groups](#197.html_concept-row-group), and [column groups](#197.html_concept-column-group), [tables](#197.html_concept-table) can have a [`caption`](#197.html_the-caption-element) element associated with them. This gives the table a heading, or legend.

A <dfn id="197.html_table-model-error">table model error</dfn> is an error with the data represented by [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element) elements and their descendants. Documents must not have table model errors.

##### 4.9.12.1 Forming a table

To determine which elements correspond to which slots in a [table](#197.html_concept-table) associated with a [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element) element, to determine the dimensions of the table (`x`[`width`] and `y`[`height`]), and to determine if there are any [table model errors](#197.html_table-model-error), user agents must use the following algorithm:

1.  Let `x`[`width`] be zero.

2.  Let `y`[`height`] be zero.

3.  Let `pending` [`tfoot`](#197.html_the-tfoot-element) `elements` be a list of [`tfoot`](#197.html_the-tfoot-element) elements, initially empty.

4.  Let `the table` be the [table](#197.html_concept-table) represented by the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element) element. The `x`[`width`] and `y`[`height`] variables give `the table`'s dimensions. `The table` is initially empty.

5.  If the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element) element has no children elements, then return `the table` (which will be empty), and abort these steps.

6.  Associate the first [`caption`](#197.html_the-caption-element) element child of the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element) element with `the table`. If there are no such children, then it has no associated [`caption`](#197.html_the-caption-element) element.

7.  Let the `current element` be the first element child of the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element) element.

    If a step in this algorithm ever requires the `current element` to be <dfn id="197.html_concept-table-advance" data-anolis-xref="concept-table-advance">advanced to the next child of the `table`</dfn> when there is no such next child, then the user agent must jump to the step labeled *end*, near the end of this algorithm.

8.  While the `current element` is not one of the following elements, [advance](#197.html_concept-table-advance) the `current element` to the next child of the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element):

    *   [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element)
    *   [`thead`](#197.html_the-thead-element)
    *   [`tbody`](#197.html_the-tbody-element)
    *   [`tfoot`](#197.html_the-tfoot-element)
    *   [`tr`](#197.html_the-tr-element)
9.  If the `current element` is a [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element), follow these substeps:

    1.  *Column groups*: Process the `current element` according to the appropriate case below:

        If the `current element` has any [`col`](#197.html_the-col-element) element children

        Follow these steps:

        1.  Let `x`[`start`] have the value of `x`[`width`].

        2.  Let the `current column` be the first [`col`](#197.html_the-col-element) element child of the [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element) element.

        3.  *Columns*: If the `current column` [`col`](#197.html_the-col-element) element has a [`span`](#197.html_attr-col-span) attribute, then parse its value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#197.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers).

            If the result of parsing the value is not an error or zero, then let `span` be that value.

            Otherwise, if the [`col`](#197.html_the-col-element) element has no [`span`](#197.html_attr-col-span) attribute, or if trying to parse the attribute's value resulted in an error or zero, then let `span` be 1.

        4.  Increase `x`[`width`] by `span`.

        5.  Let the last `span` [columns](#197.html_concept-column) in `the table` correspond to the `current column` [`col`](#197.html_the-col-element) element.

        6.  If `current column` is not the last [`col`](#197.html_the-col-element) element child of the [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element) element, then let the `current column` be the next [`col`](#197.html_the-col-element) element child of the [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element) element, and return to the step labeled *columns*.

        7.  Let all the last [columns](#197.html_concept-column) in `the table` from x=`x`[`start`] to x=`x`[`width`]-1 form a new [column group](#197.html_concept-column-group), anchored at the slot (`x`[`start`], 0), with width `x`[`width`]-`x`[`start`], corresponding to the [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element) element.

        If the `current element` has no [`col`](#197.html_the-col-element) element children

        1.  If the [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element) element has a [`span`](#197.html_attr-colgroup-span) attribute, then parse its value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#197.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers).

            If the result of parsing the value is not an error or zero, then let `span` be that value.

            Otherwise, if the [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element) element has no [`span`](#197.html_attr-colgroup-span) attribute, or if trying to parse the attribute's value resulted in an error or zero, then let `span` be 1.

        2.  Increase `x`[`width`] by `span`.

        3.  Let the last `span` [columns](#197.html_concept-column) in `the table` form a new [column group](#197.html_concept-column-group), anchored at the slot (`x`[`width`]-`span`, 0), with width `span`, corresponding to the [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element) element.

    2.  [Advance](#197.html_concept-table-advance) the `current element` to the next child of the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element).

    3.  While the `current element` is not one of the following elements, [advance](#197.html_concept-table-advance) the `current element` to the next child of the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element):

        *   [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element)
        *   [`thead`](#197.html_the-thead-element)
        *   [`tbody`](#197.html_the-tbody-element)
        *   [`tfoot`](#197.html_the-tfoot-element)
        *   [`tr`](#197.html_the-tr-element)
    4.  If the `current element` is a [`colgroup`](#197.html_the-colgroup-element) element, jump to the step labeled *column groups* above.

10.  Let `y`[`current`] be zero.

11.  Let the `list of downward-growing cells` be an empty list.

12.  *Rows*: While the `current element` is not one of the following elements, [advance](#197.html_concept-table-advance) the `current element` to the next child of the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element):

    *   [`thead`](#197.html_the-thead-element)
    *   [`tbody`](#197.html_the-tbody-element)
    *   [`tfoot`](#197.html_the-tfoot-element)
    *   [`tr`](#197.html_the-tr-element)
13.  If the `current element` is a [`tr`](#197.html_the-tr-element), then run the [algorithm for processing rows](#197.html_algorithm-for-processing-rows), [advance](#197.html_concept-table-advance) the `current element` to the next child of the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element), and return to the step labeled *rows*.

14.  Run the [algorithm for ending a row group](#197.html_algorithm-for-ending-a-row-group).

15.  If the `current element` is a [`tfoot`](#197.html_the-tfoot-element), then add that element to the list of `pending` [`tfoot`](#197.html_the-tfoot-element) `elements`, [advance](#197.html_concept-table-advance) the `current element` to the next child of the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element), and return to the step labeled *rows*.

16.  The `current element` is either a [`thead`](#197.html_the-thead-element) or a [`tbody`](#197.html_the-tbody-element).

    Run the [algorithm for processing row groups](#197.html_algorithm-for-processing-row-groups).

17.  [Advance](#197.html_concept-table-advance) the `current element` to the next child of the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element).

18.  Return to the step labeled *rows*.

19.  *End*: For each [`tfoot`](#197.html_the-tfoot-element) element in the list of `pending` [`tfoot`](#197.html_the-tfoot-element) `elements`, in tree order, run the [algorithm for processing row groups](#197.html_algorithm-for-processing-row-groups).

20.  If there exists a [row](#197.html_concept-row) or [column](#197.html_concept-column) in `the table` containing only [slots](#197.html_concept-slots) that do not have a [cell](#197.html_concept-cell) anchored to them, then this is a [table model error](#197.html_table-model-error).

21.  Return `the table`.

The <dfn id="197.html_algorithm-for-processing-row-groups">algorithm for processing row groups</dfn>, which is invoked by the set of steps above for processing [`thead`](#197.html_the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#197.html_the-tbody-element), and [`tfoot`](#197.html_the-tfoot-element) elements, is:

1.  Let `y`[`start`] have the value of `y`[`height`].

2.  For each [`tr`](#197.html_the-tr-element) element that is a child of the element being processed, in tree order, run the [algorithm for processing rows](#197.html_algorithm-for-processing-rows).

3.  If `y`[`height`] > `y`[`start`], then let all the last [rows](#197.html_concept-row) in `the table` from y=`y`[`start`] to y=`y`[`height`]-1 form a new [row group](#197.html_concept-row-group), anchored at the slot with coordinate (0, `y`[`start`]), with height `y`[`height`]-`y`[`start`], corresponding to the element being processed.

4.  Run the [algorithm for ending a row group](#197.html_algorithm-for-ending-a-row-group).

The <dfn id="197.html_algorithm-for-ending-a-row-group">algorithm for ending a row group</dfn>, which is invoked by the set of steps above when starting and ending a block of rows, is:

1.  While `y`[`current`] is less than `y`[`height`], follow these steps:

    1.  Run the [algorithm for growing downward-growing cells](#197.html_algorithm-for-growing-downward-growing-cells).

    2.  Increase `y`[`current`] by 1.

2.  Empty the `list of downward-growing cells`.

The <dfn id="197.html_algorithm-for-processing-rows">algorithm for processing rows</dfn>, which is invoked by the set of steps above for processing [`tr`](#197.html_the-tr-element) elements, is:

1.  If `y`[`height`] is equal to `y`[`current`], then increase `y`[`height`] by 1\. (`y`[`current`] is never *greater* than `y`[`height`].)

2.  Let `x`[`current`] be 0.

3.  Run the [algorithm for growing downward-growing cells](#197.html_algorithm-for-growing-downward-growing-cells).

4.  If the [`tr`](#197.html_the-tr-element) element being processed has no [`td`](#197.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#197.html_the-th-element) element children, then increase `y`[`current`] by 1, abort this set of steps, and return to the algorithm above.

5.  Let `current cell` be the first [`td`](#197.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#197.html_the-th-element) element child in the [`tr`](#197.html_the-tr-element) element being processed.

6.  *Cells*: While `x`[`current`] is less than `x`[`width`] and the slot with coordinate (`x`[`current`], `y`[`current`]) already has a cell assigned to it, increase `x`[`current`] by 1.

7.  If `x`[`current`] is equal to `x`[`width`], increase `x`[`width`] by 1\. (`x`[`current`] is never *greater* than `x`[`width`].)

8.  If the `current cell` has a [`colspan`](#197.html_attr-tdth-colspan) attribute, then [parse that attribute's value](#197.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers), and let `colspan` be the result.

    If parsing that value failed, or returned zero, or if the attribute is absent, then let `colspan` be 1, instead.

9.  If the `current cell` has a [`rowspan`](#197.html_attr-tdth-rowspan) attribute, then [parse that attribute's value](#197.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers), and let `rowspan` be the result.

    If parsing that value failed or if the attribute is absent, then let `rowspan` be 1, instead.

10.  If `rowspan` is zero and the [`table`](#197.html_the-table-element) element's [`Document`](#197.html_document) is not set to [quirks mode](#197.html_quirks-mode), then let `cell grows downward` be true, and set `rowspan` to 1\. Otherwise, let `cell grows downward` be false.

11.  If `x`[`width`] < `x`[`current`]+`colspan`, then let `x`[`width`] be `x`[`current`]+`colspan`.

12.  If `y`[`height`] < `y`[`current`]+`rowspan`, then let `y`[`height`] be `y`[`current`]+`rowspan`.

13.  Let the slots with coordinates (`x`, `y`) such that `x`[`current`] ≤ `x` < `x`[`current`]+`colspan` and `y`[`current`] ≤ `y` < `y`[`current`]+`rowspan` be covered by a new [cell](#197.html_concept-cell) `c`, anchored at (`x`[`current`], `y`[`current`]), which has width `colspan` and height `rowspan`, corresponding to the `current cell` element.

    If the `current cell` element is a [`th`](#197.html_the-th-element) element, let this new cell `c` be a header cell; otherwise, let it be a data cell.

    To establish which header cells apply to the `current cell` element, use the [algorithm for assigning header cells](#197.html_algorithm-for-assigning-header-cells) described in the next section.

    If any of the slots involved already had a [cell](#197.html_concept-cell) covering them, then this is a [table model error](#197.html_table-model-error). Those slots now have two cells overlapping.

14.  If `cell grows downward` is true, then add the tuple {`c`, `x`[`current`], `colspan`} to the `list of downward-growing cells`.

15.  Increase `x`[`current`] by `colspan`.

16.  If `current cell` is the last [`td`](#197.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#197.html_the-th-element) element child in the [`tr`](#197.html_the-tr-element) element being processed, then increase `y`[`current`] by 1, abort this set of steps, and return to the algorithm above.

17.  Let `current cell` be the next [`td`](#197.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#197.html_the-th-element) element child in the [`tr`](#197.html_the-tr-element) element being processed.

18.  Return to the step labeled *cells*.

When the algorithms above require the user agent to run the <dfn id="197.html_algorithm-for-growing-downward-growing-cells">algorithm for growing downward-growing cells</dfn>, the user agent must, for each {`cell`, `cell`[`x`], `width`} tuple in the `list of downward-growing cells`, if any, extend the [cell](#197.html_concept-cell) `cell` so that it also covers the slots with coordinates (`x`, `y`[`current`]), where `cell`[`x`] ≤ `x` < `cell`[`x`]+`width`.

##### 4.9.12.2 Forming relationships between data cells and header cells

Each cell can be assigned zero or more header cells. The <dfn id="197.html_algorithm-for-assigning-header-cells">algorithm for assigning header cells</dfn> to a cell `principal cell` is as follows.

1.  Let `header list` be an empty list of cells.

2.  Let (`principal`[`x`], `principal`[`y`]) be the coordinate of the slot to which the `principal cell` is anchored.

3.  If the `principal cell` has a [`headers`](#197.html_attr-tdth-headers) attribute specified

    1.  Take the value of the `principal cell`'s [`headers`](#197.html_attr-tdth-headers) attribute and [split it on spaces](#197.html_split-a-string-on-spaces), letting `id list` be the list of tokens obtained.

    2.  For each token in the `id list`, if the first element in the [`Document`](#197.html_document) with an [ID](#197.html_concept-id) equal to the token is a cell in the same [table](#197.html_concept-table), and that cell is not the `principal cell`, then add that cell to `header list`.

    If `principal cell` does not have a [`headers`](#197.html_attr-tdth-headers) attribute specified

    1.  Let `principal`[`width`] be the width of the `principal cell`.

    2.  Let `principal`[`height`] be the height of the `principal cell`.

    3.  For each value of `y` from `principal`[`y`] to `principal`[`y`]+`principal`[`height`]-1, run the [internal algorithm for scanning and assigning header cells](#197.html_internal-algorithm-for-scanning-and-assigning-header-cells), with the `principal cell`, the `header list`, the initial coordinate (`principal`[`x`],`y`), and the increments Δ`x`=?1 and Δ`y`=0.

    4.  For each value of `x` from `principal`[`x`] to `principal`[`x`]+`principal`[`width`]-1, run the [internal algorithm for scanning and assigning header cells](#197.html_internal-algorithm-for-scanning-and-assigning-header-cells), with the `principal cell`, the `header list`, the initial coordinate (`x`,`principal`[`y`]), and the increments Δ`x`=0 and Δ`y`=?1.

    5.  If the `principal cell` is anchored in a [row group](#197.html_concept-row-group), then add all header cells that are [row group headers](#197.html_row-group-header) and are anchored in the same row group with an `x`-coordinate less than or equal to `principal`[`x`]+`principal`[`width`]-1 and a `y`-coordinate less than or equal to `principal`[`y`]+`principal`[`height`]-1 to `header list`.

    6.  If the `principal cell` is anchored in a [column group](#197.html_concept-column-group), then add all header cells that are [column group headers](#197.html_column-group-header) and are anchored in the same column group with an `x`-coordinate less than or equal to `principal`[`x`]+`principal`[`width`]-1 and a `y`-coordinate less than or equal to `principal`[`y`]+`principal`[`height`]-1 to `header list`.

4.  Remove all the [empty cells](#197.html_empty-cell) from the `header list`.

5.  Remove any duplicates from the `header list`.

6.  Remove `principal cell` from the `header list` if it is there.

7.  Assign the headers in the `header list` to the `principal cell`.

The <dfn id="197.html_internal-algorithm-for-scanning-and-assigning-header-cells">internal algorithm for scanning and assigning header cells</dfn>, given a `principal cell`, a `header list`, an initial coordinate (`initial`[`x`], `initial`[`y`]), and Δ`x` and Δ`y` increments, is as follows:

1.  Let `x` equal `initial`[`x`].

2.  Let `y` equal `initial`[`y`].

3.  Let `opaque headers` be an empty list of cells.

4.  If `principal cell` is a header cell

    Let `in header block` be true, and let `headers from current header block` be a list of cells containing just the `principal cell`.

    Otherwise

    Let `in header block` be false and let `headers from current header block` be an empty list of cells.

5.  *Loop*: Increment `x` by Δ`x`; increment `y` by Δ`y`.

    For each invocation of this algorithm, one of Δ`x` and Δ`y` will be ?1, and the other will be 0.

6.  If either `x` or `y` is less than 0, then abort this internal algorithm.

7.  If there is no cell covering slot (`x`, `y`), or if there is more than one cell covering slot (`x`, `y`), return to the substep labeled *loop*.

8.  Let `current cell` be the cell covering slot (`x`, `y`).

9.  If `current cell` is a header cell

    1.  Set `in header block` to true.

    2.  Add `current cell` to `headers from current header block`.

    3.  Let `blocked` be false.

    4.  If Δ`x` is 0

        If there are any cells in the `opaque headers` list anchored with the same `x`-coordinate as the `current cell`, and with the same width as `current cell`, then let `blocked` be true.

        If the `current cell` is not a [column header](#197.html_column-header), then let `blocked` be true.

        If Δ`y` is 0

        If there are any cells in the `opaque headers` list anchored with the same `y`-coordinate as the `current cell`, and with the same height as `current cell`, then let `blocked` be true.

        If the `current cell` is not a [row header](#197.html_row-header), then let `blocked` be true.

    5.  If `blocked` is false, then add the `current cell` to the `headers list`.

    If `current cell` is a data cell and `in header block` is true

    Set `in header block` to false. Add all the cells in `headers from current header block` to the `opaque headers` list, and empty the `headers from current header block` list.

10.  Return to the step labeled *loop*.

A header cell anchored at the slot with coordinate (`x`, `y`) with width `width` and height `height` is said to be a <dfn id="197.html_column-header">column header</dfn> if any of the following conditions are true:

*   The cell's [`scope`](#197.html_attr-th-scope) attribute is in the [column](#197.html_attr-th-scope-col) state, or
*   The cell's [`scope`](#197.html_attr-th-scope) attribute is in the [auto](#197.html_attr-th-scope-auto) state, and there are no data cells in any of the cells covering slots with `y`-coordinates `y` .. `y`+`height`-1.

A header cell anchored at the slot with coordinate (`x`, `y`) with width `width` and height `height` is said to be a <dfn id="197.html_row-header">row header</dfn> if any of the following conditions are true:

*   The cell's [`scope`](#197.html_attr-th-scope) attribute is in the [row](#197.html_attr-th-scope-row) state, or
*   The cell's [`scope`](#197.html_attr-th-scope) attribute is in the [auto](#197.html_attr-th-scope-auto) state, the cell is not a [column header](#197.html_column-header), and there are no data cells in any of the cells covering slots with `x`-coordinates `x` .. `x`+`width`-1.

A header cell is said to be a <dfn id="197.html_column-group-header">column group header</dfn> if its [`scope`](#197.html_attr-th-scope) attribute is in the [column group](#197.html_attr-th-scope-colgroup) state.

A header cell is said to be a <dfn id="197.html_row-group-header">row group header</dfn> if its [`scope`](#197.html_attr-th-scope) attribute is in the [row group](#197.html_attr-th-scope-rowgroup) state.

A cell is said to be an <dfn id="197.html_empty-cell">empty cell</dfn> if it contains no elements and its text content, if any, consists only of [White_Space](#197.html_white_space) characters.

### 4.10 Forms

#### 4.10.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

A form is a component of a Web page that has form controls, such as text fields, buttons, checkboxes, range controls, or color pickers. A user can interact with such a form, providing data that can then be sent to the server for further processing (e.g. returning the results of a search or calculation). No client-side scripting is needed in many cases, though an API is available so that scripts can augment the user experience or use forms for purposes other than submitting data to a server.

Writing a form consists of several steps, which can be performed in any order: writing the user interface, implementing the server-side processing, and configuring the user interface to communicate with the server.

##### 4.10.1.1 Writing a form's user interface

*This section is non-normative.*

For the purposes of this brief introduction, we will create a pizza ordering form.

Any form starts with a [`form`](#199.html_the-form-element) element, inside which are placed the controls. Most controls are represented by the [`input`](#199.html_the-input-element) element, which by default provides a one-line text field. To label a control, the [`label`](#199.html_the-label-element) element is used; the label text and the control itself go inside the [`label`](#199.html_the-label-element) element. Each part of a form is considered a [paragraph](#199.html_paragraph), and is typically separated from other parts using [`p`](#199.html_the-p-element) elements. Putting this together, here is how one might ask for the customer's name:

```
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
</form>
```

To let the user select the size of the pizza, we can use a set of radio buttons. Radio buttons also use the [`input`](#199.html_the-input-element) element, this time with a [`type`](#199.html_attr-input-type) attribute with the value [`radio`](#199.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)). To make the radio buttons work as a group, they are given a common name using the [`name`](#199.html_attr-fe-name) attribute. To group a batch of controls together, such as, in this case, the radio buttons, one can use the [`fieldset`](#199.html_the-fieldset-element) element. The title of such a group of controls is given by the first element in the [`fieldset`](#199.html_the-fieldset-element), which has to be a [`legend`](#199.html_the-legend-element) element.

```
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
</form>
```

Changes from the previous step are highlighted.

To pick toppings, we can use checkboxes. These use the [`input`](#199.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#199.html_attr-input-type) attribute with the value [`checkbox`](#199.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)):

```
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
</form>
```

The pizzeria for which this form is being written is always making mistakes, so it needs a way to contact the customer. For this purpose, we can use form controls specifically for telephone numbers ([`input`](#199.html_the-input-element) elements with their [`type`](#199.html_attr-input-type) attribute set to [`tel`](#199.html_telephone-state-(type=tel))) and e-mail addresses ([`input`](#199.html_the-input-element) elements with their [`type`](#199.html_attr-input-type) attribute set to [`email`](#199.html_e-mail-state-(type=email))):

```
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel></label></p>
 <p><label>E-mail address: <input type=email></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
</form>
```

We can use an [`input`](#199.html_the-input-element) element with its [`type`](#199.html_attr-input-type) attribute set to [`time`](#199.html_time-state-(type=time)) to ask for a delivery time. Many of these form controls have attributes to control exactly what values can be specified; in this case, three attributes of particular interest are [`min`](#199.html_attr-input-min), [`max`](#199.html_attr-input-max), and [`step`](#199.html_attr-input-step). These set the minimum time, the maximum time, and the interval between allowed values (in seconds). This pizzeria only delivers between 11am and 9pm, and doesn't promise anything better than 15 minute increments, which we can mark up as follows:

```
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel></label></p>
 <p><label>E-mail address: <input type=email></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900"></label></p>
</form>
```

The [`textarea`](#199.html_the-textarea-element) element can be used to provide a free-form text field. In this instance, we are going to use it to provide a space for the customer to give delivery instructions:

```
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel></label></p>
 <p><label>E-mail address: <input type=email></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900"></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea></textarea></label></p>
</form>
```

Finally, to make the form submittable we use the [`button`](#199.html_the-button-element) element:

```
<form>
 <p><label>Customer name: <input></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel></label></p>
 <p><label>E-mail address: <input type=email></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900"></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea></textarea></label></p>
 <p><button>Submit order</button></p>
</form>
```

##### 4.10.1.2 Implementing the server-side processing for a form

*This section is non-normative.*

The exact details for writing a server-side processor are out of scope for this specification. For the purposes of this introduction, we will assume that the script at `https://pizza.example.com/order.cgi` is configured to accept submissions using the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#199.html_attr-fs-enctype-urlencoded) format, expecting the following parameters sent in an HTTP POST body:

`custname`

Customer's name

`custtel`

Customer's telephone number

`custemail`

Customer's e-mail address

`size`

The pizza size, either `small`, `medium`, or `large`

`topping`

A topping, specified once for each selected topping, with the allowed values being `bacon`, `cheese`, `onion`, and `mushroom`

`delivery`

The requested delivery time

`comments`

The delivery instructions

##### 4.10.1.3 Configuring a form to communicate with a server

*This section is non-normative.*

Form submissions are exposed to servers in a variety of ways, most commonly as HTTP GET or POST requests. To specify the exact method used, the [`method`](#199.html_attr-fs-method) attribute is specified on the [`form`](#199.html_the-form-element) element. This doesn't specify how the form data is encoded, though; to specify that, you use the [`enctype`](#199.html_attr-fs-enctype) attribute. You also have to specify the URL of the service that will handle the submitted data, using the [`action`](#199.html_attr-fs-action) attribute.

For each form control you want submitted, you then have to give a name that will be used to refer to the data in the submission. We already specified the name for the group of radio buttons; the same attribute ([`name`](#199.html_attr-fe-name)) also specifies the submission name. Radio buttons can be distinguished from each other in the submission by giving them different values, using the [`value`](#199.html_attr-input-value) attribute.

Multiple controls can have the same name; for example, here we give all the checkboxes the same name, and the server distinguishes which checkbox was checked by seeing which values are submitted with that name — like the radio buttons, they are also given unique values with the [`value`](#199.html_attr-input-value) attribute.

Given the settings in the previous section, this all becomes:

```
<form method="post"
      enctype="application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
      action="https://pizza.example.com/order.cgi">
 <p><label>Customer name: <input name="custname"></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel name="custtel"></label></p>
 <p><label>E-mail address: <input type=email name="custemail"></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size value="small"> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size value="medium"> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size value="large"> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="bacon"> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="cheese"> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="onion"> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="mushroom"> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900" name="delivery"></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea name="comments"></textarea></label></p>
 <p><button>Submit order</button></p>
</form>
```

There is no particular significance to the way some of the attributes have their values quoted and others don't. The HTML syntax allows a variety of equally valid ways to specify attributes, as discussed [in the syntax section](#199.html_syntax-attributes).

For example, if the customer entered "Denise Lawrence" as their name, "555-321-8642" as their telephone number, did not specify an e-mail address, asked for a medium-sized pizza, selected the Extra Cheese and Mushroom toppings, entered a delivery time of 7pm, and left the delivery instructions text field blank, the user agent would submit the following to the online Web service:

```
custname=Denise+Lawrence&custtel=555-321-8624&custemail=&size=medium&topping=cheese&topping=mushroom&delivery=19%3A00&comments=
```

##### 4.10.1.4 Client-side form validation

*This section is non-normative.*

Forms can be annotated in such a way that the user agent will check the user's input before the form is submitted. The server still has to verify the input is valid (since hostile users can easily bypass the form validation), but it allows the user to avoid the wait incurred by having the server be the sole checker of the user's input.

The simplest annotation is the [`required`](#199.html_attr-input-required) attribute, which can be specified on [`input`](#199.html_the-input-element) elements to indicate that the form is not to be submitted until a value is given. By adding this attribute to the customer name, pizza size, and delivery time fields, we allow the user agent to notify the user when the user submits the form without filling in those fields:

```
<form method="post"
      enctype="application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
      action="https://pizza.example.com/order.cgi">
 <p><label>Customer name: <input name="custname" required></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel name="custtel"></label></p>
 <p><label>E-mail address: <input type=email name="custemail"></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="small"> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="medium"> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="large"> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="bacon"> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="cheese"> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="onion"> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="mushroom"> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900" name="delivery" required></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea name="comments"></textarea></label></p>
 <p><button>Submit order</button></p>
</form>
```

It is also possible to limit the length of the input, using the [`maxlength`](#199.html_attr-fe-maxlength) attribute. By adding this to the [`textarea`](#199.html_the-textarea-element) element, we can limit users to 1000 characters, preventing them from writing huge essays to the busy delivery drivers instead of staying focused and to the point:

```
<form method="post"
      enctype="application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
      action="https://pizza.example.com/order.cgi">
 <p><label>Customer name: <input name="custname" required></label></p>
 <p><label>Telephone: <input type=tel name="custtel"></label></p>
 <p><label>E-mail address: <input type=email name="custemail"></label></p>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Size </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="small"> Small </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="medium"> Medium </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=radio name=size required value="large"> Large </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset>
  <legend> Pizza Toppings </legend>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="bacon"> Bacon </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="cheese"> Extra Cheese </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="onion"> Onion </label></p>
  <p><label> <input type=checkbox name="topping" value="mushroom"> Mushroom </label></p>
 </fieldset>
 <p><label>Preferred delivery time: <input type=time min="11:00" max="21:00" step="900" name="delivery" required></label></p>
 <p><label>Delivery instructions: <textarea name="comments" maxlength=1000></textarea></label></p>
 <p><button>Submit order</button></p>
</form>
```

When a form is submitted, `invalid` events are fired at each form control that is invalid, and then at the [`form`](#199.html_the-form-element) element itself. This can be useful for displaying a summary of the problems with the form, since typically the browser itself will only report one problem at a time.

##### 4.10.1.5 Date, time, and number formats

*This section is non-normative.*

In this pizza delivery example, the times are specified in the format "HH:MM": two digits for the hour, in 24-hour format, and two digits for the time. (Seconds could also be specified, though they are not necessary in this example.)

In some locales, however, times are often expressed differently when presented to users. For example, in the United States, it is still common to use the 12-hour clock with an am/pm indicator, as in "2pm". In France, it is common to separate the hours from the minutes using an "h" character, as in "14h00".

Similar issues exist with dates, with the added complication that even the order of the components is not always consistent — for example, in Cyprus the first of February 2003 would typically be written "1/2/03", while that same date in Japan would typically be written as "2003年02月01日" — and even with numbers, where locales differ, for example, in what punctuation is used as the decimal separator and the thousands separator.

It is therefore important to distinguish the time, date, and number formats used in HTML and in form submissions, which are always the formats defined in this specification (and based on the well-established ISO 8601 standard for computer-readable date and time formats), from the time, date, and number formats presented to the user by the browser and accepted as input from the user by the browser.

The format used "on the wire", i.e. in HTML markup and in form submissions, is intended to be computer-readable and consistent irrespective of the user's locale. Dates, for instance, are always written in the format "YYYY-MM-DD", as in "2003-02-01". Users are not expected to ever see this format.

The time, date, or number given by the page in the wire format is then translated to the user's preferred presentation (based on user preferences or on the locale of the page itself), before being displayed to the user. Similarly, after the user inputs a time, date, or number using their preferred format, the user agent converts it back to the wire format before putting it in the DOM or submitting it.

This allows scripts in pages and on servers to process times, dates, and numbers in a consistent manner without needing to support dozens of different formats, while still supporting the users' needs.

See also the [implementation notes](#199.html_input-impl-notes) regarding localization of form controls.

#### 4.10.2 Categories

Mostly for historical reasons, elements in this section fall into several overlapping (but subtly different) categories in addition to the usual ones like [flow content](#200.html_flow-content-1), [phrasing content](#200.html_phrasing-content-1), and [interactive content](#200.html_interactive-content-0).

A number of the elements are <dfn id="200.html_form-associated-element" data-anolis-xref="form-associated element">form-associated elements</dfn>, which means they can have a [form owner](#200.html_form-owner).

*   [`button`](#200.html_the-button-element)
*   [`fieldset`](#200.html_the-fieldset-element)
*   [`input`](#200.html_the-input-element)
*   [`keygen`](#200.html_the-keygen-element)
*   [`label`](#200.html_the-label-element)
*   [`object`](#200.html_the-object-element)
*   [`output`](#200.html_the-output-element)
*   [`select`](#200.html_the-select-element)
*   [`textarea`](#200.html_the-textarea-element)
*   [`img`](#200.html_the-img-element)

The [form-associated elements](#200.html_form-associated-element) fall into several subcategories:

<dfn id="200.html_category-listed" data-anolis-xref="category-listed">Listed elements</dfn>

Denotes elements that are listed in the [`form``.elements`](#200.html_dom-form-elements) and [`fieldset``.elements`](#200.html_dom-fieldset-elements) APIs.

*   [`button`](#200.html_the-button-element)
*   [`fieldset`](#200.html_the-fieldset-element)
*   [`input`](#200.html_the-input-element)
*   [`keygen`](#200.html_the-keygen-element)
*   [`object`](#200.html_the-object-element)
*   [`output`](#200.html_the-output-element)
*   [`select`](#200.html_the-select-element)
*   [`textarea`](#200.html_the-textarea-element)

<dfn id="200.html_category-submit" data-anolis-xref="category-submit">Submittable elements</dfn>

Denotes elements that can be used for [constructing the form data set](#200.html_constructing-form-data-set) when a [`form`](#200.html_the-form-element) element is [submitted](#200.html_concept-form-submit).

*   [`button`](#200.html_the-button-element)
*   [`input`](#200.html_the-input-element)
*   [`keygen`](#200.html_the-keygen-element)
*   [`object`](#200.html_the-object-element)
*   [`select`](#200.html_the-select-element)
*   [`textarea`](#200.html_the-textarea-element)

Some [submittable elements](#200.html_category-submit) can be, depending on their attributes, <dfn id="200.html_concept-button" data-anolis-xref="concept-button">buttons</dfn>. The prose below defines when an element is a button. Some buttons are specifically <dfn id="200.html_concept-submit-button" data-anolis-xref="concept-submit-button">submit buttons</dfn>.

<dfn id="200.html_category-reset" data-anolis-xref="category-reset">Resettable elements</dfn>

Denotes elements that can be affected when a [`form`](#200.html_the-form-element) element is [reset](#200.html_concept-form-reset).

*   [`input`](#200.html_the-input-element)
*   [`keygen`](#200.html_the-keygen-element)
*   [`output`](#200.html_the-output-element)
*   [`select`](#200.html_the-select-element)
*   [`textarea`](#200.html_the-textarea-element)

<dfn id="200.html_category-form-attr" data-anolis-xref="category-form-attr">Reassociateable elements</dfn>

Denotes elements that have a [`form`](#200.html_attr-fae-form) content attribute, and a matching [`form`](#200.html_dom-fae-form) IDL attribute, that allow authors to specify an explicit [form owner](#200.html_form-owner).

*   [`button`](#200.html_the-button-element)
*   [`fieldset`](#200.html_the-fieldset-element)
*   [`input`](#200.html_the-input-element)
*   [`keygen`](#200.html_the-keygen-element)
*   [`label`](#200.html_the-label-element)
*   [`object`](#200.html_the-object-element)
*   [`output`](#200.html_the-output-element)
*   [`select`](#200.html_the-select-element)
*   [`textarea`](#200.html_the-textarea-element)

Some elements, not all of them [form-associated](#200.html_form-associated-element), are categorized as <dfn id="200.html_category-label" data-anolis-xref="category-label">labelable elements</dfn>. These are elements that can be associated with a [`label`](#200.html_the-label-element) element.

*   [`button`](#200.html_the-button-element)
*   [`input`](#200.html_the-input-element) (if the [`type`](#200.html_attr-input-type) attribute is *not* in the [Hidden](#200.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state)
*   [`keygen`](#200.html_the-keygen-element)
*   [`meter`](#200.html_the-meter-element)
*   [`output`](#200.html_the-output-element)
*   [`progress`](#200.html_the-progress-element)
*   [`select`](#200.html_the-select-element)
*   [`textarea`](#200.html_the-textarea-element)

#### 4.10.3 The <dfn>`form`</dfn> element

[Categories](#201.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#201.html_flow-content-1).

[Palpable content](#201.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#201.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [flow content](#201.html_flow-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#201.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Flow content](#201.html_flow-content-1), but with no [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element descendants.

[Content attributes](#201.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#201.html_global-attributes)

[`accept-charset`](#201.html_attr-form-accept-charset) - Character encodings to use for [form submission](#201.html_form-submission-0)

[`action`](#201.html_attr-fs-action) - URL to use for [form submission](#201.html_form-submission-0)

[`autocomplete`](#201.html_attr-form-autocomplete) - Default setting for autofill feature for controls in the form

[`enctype`](#201.html_attr-fs-enctype) - Form data set encoding type to use for [form submission](#201.html_form-submission-0)

[`method`](#201.html_attr-fs-method) - HTTP method to use for [form submission](#201.html_form-submission-0)

[`name`](#201.html_attr-form-name) - Name of form to use in the [`document.forms`](#201.html_dom-document-forms) API

[`novalidate`](#201.html_attr-fs-novalidate) - Bypass form control validation for [form submission](#201.html_form-submission-0)

[`target`](#201.html_attr-fs-target) - [Browsing context](#201.html_browsing-context) for [form submission](#201.html_form-submission-0)

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#201.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#201.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#201.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#201.html_index-aria-global)
