Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#201.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#201.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
[OverrideBuiltins]
interface HTMLFormElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString acceptCharset;
           attribute DOMString action;
           attribute DOMString autocomplete;
           attribute DOMString enctype;
           attribute DOMString encoding;
           attribute DOMString method;
           attribute DOMString name;
           attribute boolean noValidate;
           attribute DOMString target;

  readonly attribute HTMLFormControlsCollection elements;
  readonly attribute long length;
  getter Element (unsigned long index);
  getter (RadioNodeList or Element) (DOMString name);

  void submit();
  void reset();
  boolean checkValidity();
};
```

The [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element [represents](#201.html_represents) a collection of [form-associated elements](#201.html_form-associated-element), some of which can represent editable values that can be submitted to a server for processing.

The <dfn id="201.html_attr-form-accept-charset" data-anolis-xref="attr-form-accept-charset">`accept-charset`</dfn> attribute gives the character encodings that are to be used for the submission. If specified, the value must be an [ordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#201.html_ordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens) that are [ASCII case-insensitive](#201.html_ascii-case-insensitive), and each token must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](#201.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for one of the [labels](#201.html_encoding-label) of an [ASCII-compatible character encoding](#201.html_ascii-compatible-character-encoding). [[ENCODING]](#201.html_refsENCODING)

The <dfn id="201.html_attr-form-name" data-anolis-xref="attr-form-name">`name`</dfn> attribute represents the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element)'s name within the [`forms`](#201.html_dom-document-forms) collection. The value must not be the empty string, and the value must be unique amongst the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) elements in the [`forms`](#201.html_dom-document-forms) collection that it is in, if any.

The <dfn id="201.html_attr-form-autocomplete" data-anolis-xref="attr-form-autocomplete">`autocomplete`</dfn> attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#201.html_enumerated-attribute). The attribute has two states. The `on` keyword maps to the <dfn id="201.html_attr-form-autocomplete-on-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-form-autocomplete-on-state">on</dfn> state, and the `off` keyword maps to the <dfn id="201.html_attr-form-autocomplete-off-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-form-autocomplete-off-state">off</dfn> state. The attribute may also be omitted. The *missing value default* is the [on](#201.html_attr-form-autocomplete-on-state) state. The [off](#201.html_attr-form-autocomplete-off-state) state indicates that by default, form controls in the form will have their autofill field name set to "[`off`](#201.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-off)"; the [on](#201.html_attr-form-autocomplete-on-state) state indicates that by default, form controls in the form will have their autofill field name set to "[`on`](#201.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-on)".

The [`action`](#201.html_attr-fs-action), [`enctype`](#201.html_attr-fs-enctype), [`method`](#201.html_attr-fs-method), [`novalidate`](#201.html_attr-fs-novalidate), and [`target`](#201.html_attr-fs-target) attributes are [attributes for form submission](#201.html_attributes-for-form-submission).

`form` . [`elements`](#201.html_dom-form-elements)

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#201.html_htmlcollection) of the form controls in the form (excluding image buttons for historical reasons).

`form` . [`length`](#201.html_dom-form-length)

Returns the number of form controls in the form (excluding image buttons for historical reasons).

`form`[`index`]

Returns the `index`th element in the form (excluding image buttons for historical reasons).

`form`[`name`]

Returns the form control (or, if there are several, a [`RadioNodeList`](#201.html_radionodelist) of the form controls) in the form with the given [ID](#201.html_concept-id) or [`name`](#201.html_attr-fe-name) (excluding image buttons for historical reasons); or, if there are none, returns the [`img`](#201.html_the-img-element) element with the given ID.

Once an element has been referenced using a particular name, that name will continue being available as a way to reference that element in this method, even if the element's actual [ID](#201.html_concept-id) or [`name`](#201.html_attr-fe-name) changes, for as long as the element remains in the [`Document`](#201.html_document).

If there are multiple matching items, then a [`RadioNodeList`](#201.html_radionodelist) object containing all those elements is returned.

`form` . [`submit`](#201.html_dom-form-submit)()

Submits the form.

`form` . [`reset`](#201.html_dom-form-reset)()

Resets the form.

`form` . [`checkValidity`](#201.html_dom-form-checkvalidity)()

Returns true if the form's controls are all valid; otherwise, returns false.

The <dfn id="201.html_dom-form-autocomplete" data-anolis-xref="dom-form-autocomplete">`autocomplete`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#201.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name, [limited to only known values](#201.html_limited-to-only-known-values).

The <dfn id="201.html_dom-form-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-form-name">`name`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#201.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

The <dfn id="201.html_dom-form-acceptcharset" data-anolis-xref="dom-form-acceptCharset">`acceptCharset`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#201.html_reflect) the [`accept-charset`](#201.html_attr-form-accept-charset) content attribute.

* * *

The <dfn id="201.html_dom-form-elements" data-anolis-xref="dom-form-elements">`elements`</dfn> IDL attribute must return an [`HTMLFormControlsCollection`](#201.html_htmlformcontrolscollection-0) rooted at the [`Document`](#201.html_document) node while the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element is [in a `Document`](#201.html_in-a-document) and rooted at the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element itself when it is not, whose filter matches [listed elements](#201.html_category-listed) whose [form owner](#201.html_form-owner) is the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element, with the exception of [`input`](#201.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#201.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Image Button](#201.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, which must, for historical reasons, be excluded from this particular collection.

The <dfn id="201.html_dom-form-length" data-anolis-xref="dom-form-length">`length`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the number of nodes [represented](#201.html_represented-by-the-collection) by the [`elements`](#201.html_dom-form-elements) collection.

The [supported property indices](#201.html_supported-property-indices) at any instant are the indices supported by the object returned by the [`elements`](#201.html_dom-form-elements) attribute at that instant.

When a [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element is <dfn id="201.html_dom-form-item" data-anolis-xref="dom-form-item">indexed for indexed property retrieval</dfn>, the user agent must return the value returned by the `item` method on the [`elements`](#201.html_dom-form-elements) collection, when invoked with the given index as its argument.

* * *

Each [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element has a mapping of names to elements called the <dfn id="201.html_past-names-map">past names map</dfn>. It is used to persist names of controls even when they change names.

The [supported property names](#201.html_supported-property-names) consist of the names obtained from the following algorithm, in the order obtained from this algorithm:

1.  Let `sourced names` be an initially empty ordered list of tuples consisting of a string, an element, a source, where the source is either *id*, *name*, or *past*, and, if the source is *past*, an age.

2.  For each [listed element](#201.html_category-listed) `candidate` whose [form owner](#201.html_form-owner) is the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element, with the exception of any [`input`](#201.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#201.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Image Button](#201.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, run these substeps:

    1.  If `candidate` has an [`id`](#201.html_the-id-attribute) attribute, add an entry to `sourced names` with that [`id`](#201.html_the-id-attribute) attribute's value as the string, `candidate` as the element, and *id* as the source.

    2.  If `candidate` has a [`name`](#201.html_attr-fe-name) attribute, add an entry to `sourced names` with that [`name`](#201.html_attr-fe-name) attribute's value as the string, `candidate` as the element, and *name* as the source.

3.  For each [`img`](#201.html_the-img-element) element `candidate` whose [form owner](#201.html_form-owner) is the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element, run these substeps:

    1.  If `candidate` has an [`id`](#201.html_the-id-attribute) attribute, add an entry to `sourced names` with that [`id`](#201.html_the-id-attribute) attribute's value as the string, `candidate` as the element, and *id* as the source.

    2.  If `candidate` has a [`name`](#201.html_attr-img-name) attribute, add an entry to `sourced names` with that [`name`](#201.html_attr-img-name) attribute's value as the string, `candidate` as the element, and *name* as the source.

4.  For each entry `past entry` in the [past names map](#201.html_past-names-map) add an entry to `sourced names` with the `past entry`'s name as the string, `past entry`'s element as the element, *past* as the source, and the length of time `past entry` has been in the [past names map](#201.html_past-names-map) as the age.

5.  Sort `sourced names` by [tree order](#201.html_tree-order) of the element entry of each tuple, sorting entries with the same element by putting entries whose source is *id* first, then entries whose source is *name*, and finally entries whose source is *past*, and sorting entries with the same element and source by their age, oldest first.

6.  Remove any entries in `sourced names` that have the empty string as their name.

7.  Remove any entries in `sourced names` that have the same name as an earlier entry in the map.

8.  Return the list of names from `sourced names`, maintaining their relative order.

The properties exposed in this way must not be enumerable.

When a [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element is <dfn id="201.html_dom-form-nameditem" data-anolis-xref="dom-form-namedItem">indexed for named property retrieval</dfn>, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `candidates` be a [live](#201.html_live) [`RadioNodeList`](#201.html_radionodelist) object containing all the [listed elements](#201.html_category-listed) whose [form owner](#201.html_form-owner) is the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element that have either an [`id`](#201.html_the-id-attribute) attribute or a [`name`](#201.html_attr-fe-name) attribute equal to `name`, with the exception of [`input`](#201.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#201.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Image Button](#201.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, in [tree order](#201.html_tree-order).

2.  If `candidates` is empty, let `candidates` be a [live](#201.html_live) [`RadioNodeList`](#201.html_radionodelist) object containing all the [`img`](#201.html_the-img-element) elements that are descendants of the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element and that have either an [`id`](#201.html_the-id-attribute) attribute or a [`name`](#201.html_attr-img-name) attribute equal to `name`, in [tree order](#201.html_tree-order).

3.  If `candidates` is empty, `name` is the name of one of the entries in the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element's [past names map](#201.html_past-names-map): return the object associated with `name` in that map.

4.  If `candidates` contains more than one node, return `candidates` and abort these steps.

5.  Otherwise, `candidates` contains exactly one node. Add a mapping from `name` to the node in `candidates` in the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element's [past names map](#201.html_past-names-map), replacing the previous entry with the same name, if any.

6.  Return the node in `candidates`.

If an element listed in a [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element's [past names map](#201.html_past-names-map) changes [form owner](#201.html_form-owner), then its entries must be removed from that map.

* * *

The <dfn id="201.html_dom-form-submit" data-anolis-xref="dom-form-submit">`submit()`</dfn> method, when invoked, must [submit](#201.html_concept-form-submit) the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element from the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element itself, with the `submitted from` [`submit()`](#201.html_dom-form-submit) `method` flag set.

The <dfn id="201.html_dom-form-reset" data-anolis-xref="dom-form-reset">`reset()`</dfn> method, when invoked, must run the following steps:

1.  If the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element is marked as *[locked for reset](#201.html_locked-for-reset)*, then abort these steps.

2.  Mark the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element as <dfn id="201.html_locked-for-reset">locked for reset</dfn>.

3.  [Reset](#201.html_concept-form-reset) the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element.

4.  Unmark the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element as *[locked for reset](#201.html_locked-for-reset)*.

If the <dfn id="201.html_dom-form-checkvalidity" data-anolis-xref="dom-form-checkValidity">`checkValidity()`</dfn> method is invoked, the user agent must [statically validate the constraints](#201.html_statically-validate-the-constraints) of the [`form`](#201.html_the-form-element) element, and return true if the constraint validation return a *positive* result, and false if it returned a *negative* result.

This example shows two search forms:

```
<form action="http://www.google.com/search" method="get">
 <label>Google: <input type="search" name="q"></label> <input type="submit" value="Search...">
</form>
<form action="http://www.bing.com/search" method="get">
 <label>Bing: <input type="search" name="q"></label> <input type="submit" value="Search...">
</form>
```

#### 4.10.4 The <dfn>`label`</dfn> element

[Categories](#202.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#202.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#202.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Interactive content](#202.html_interactive-content-0).

[Reassociateable](#202.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#202.html_form-associated-element).

[Palpable content](#202.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#202.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#202.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#202.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#202.html_phrasing-content-1), but with no descendant [labelable elements](#202.html_category-label) unless it is the element's [labeled control](#202.html_labeled-control), and no descendant [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) elements.

[Content attributes](#202.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#202.html_global-attributes)

[`form`](#202.html_attr-fae-form) - Associates the control with a [`form`](#202.html_the-form-element) element

[`for`](#202.html_attr-label-for) - Associate the label with form control

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissable

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#202.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#202.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#202.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#202.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLLabelElement : HTMLElement {
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
           attribute DOMString htmlFor;
  readonly attribute HTMLElement? control;
};
```

The [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element [represents](#202.html_represents) a caption in a user interface. The caption can be associated with a specific form control, known as the [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element's <dfn id="202.html_labeled-control">labeled control</dfn>, either using the [`for`](#202.html_attr-label-for) attribute, or by putting the form control inside the [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element itself.

Except where otherwise specified by the following rules, a [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element has no [labeled control](#202.html_labeled-control).

The <dfn id="202.html_attr-label-for" data-anolis-xref="attr-label-for">`for`</dfn> attribute may be specified to indicate a form control with which the caption is to be associated. If the attribute is specified, the attribute's value must be the [ID](#202.html_concept-id) of a [labelable element](#202.html_category-label) in the same [`Document`](#202.html_document) as the [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element. If the attribute is specified and there is an element in the [`Document`](#202.html_document) whose [ID](#202.html_concept-id) is equal to the value of the [`for`](#202.html_attr-label-for) attribute, and the first such element is a [labelable element](#202.html_category-label), then that element is the [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element's [labeled control](#202.html_labeled-control).

If the [`for`](#202.html_attr-label-for) attribute is not specified, but the [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element has a [labelable element](#202.html_category-label) descendant, then the first such descendant in [tree order](#202.html_tree-order) is the [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element's [labeled control](#202.html_labeled-control).

The [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element's exact default presentation and behavior, in particular what its [activation behavior](#202.html_activation-behavior) might be, if anything, should match the platform's label behavior. The [activation behavior](#202.html_activation-behavior) of a [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element for events targeted at [interactive content](#202.html_interactive-content-0) descendants of a [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element, and any descendants of those [interactive content](#202.html_interactive-content-0) descendants, must be to do nothing.

For example, on platforms where clicking a checkbox label checks the checkbox, clicking the [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) in the following snippet could trigger the user agent to [run synthetic click activation steps](#202.html_run-synthetic-click-activation-steps) on the [`input`](#202.html_the-input-element) element, as if the element itself had been triggered by the user:

```
<label><input type=checkbox name=lost> Lost</label>
```

On other platforms, the behavior might be just to focus the control, or do nothing.

The [`form`](#202.html_attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element with its [form owner](#202.html_form-owner).

The following example shows three form controls each with a label, two of which have small text showing the right format for users to use.

```
<p><label>Full name: <input name=fn> <small>Format: First Last</small></label></p>
<p><label>Age: <input name=age type=number min=0></label></p>
<p><label>Post code: <input name=pc> <small>Format: AB12 3CD</small></label></p>
```

`label` . [`control`](#202.html_dom-label-control)

Returns the form control that is associated with this element.

The <dfn id="202.html_dom-label-htmlfor" data-anolis-xref="dom-label-htmlFor">`htmlFor`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#202.html_reflect) the [`for`](#202.html_attr-label-for) content attribute.

The <dfn id="202.html_dom-label-control" data-anolis-xref="dom-label-control">`control`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) element's [labeled control](#202.html_labeled-control), if any, or null if there isn't one.

The [`form`](#202.html_dom-fae-form) IDL attribute is part of the element's forms API.

* * *

`control` . [`labels`](#202.html_dom-lfe-labels)

Returns a [`NodeList`](#202.html_nodelist) of all the [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) elements that the form control is associated with.

[Labelable elements](#202.html_category-label) have a [`NodeList`](#202.html_nodelist) object associated with them that represents the list of [`label`](#202.html_the-label-element) elements, in [tree order](#202.html_tree-order), whose [labeled control](#202.html_labeled-control) is the element in question. The <dfn id="202.html_dom-lfe-labels" data-anolis-xref="dom-lfe-labels">`labels`</dfn> IDL attribute of [labelable elements](#202.html_category-label), on getting, must return that [`NodeList`](#202.html_nodelist) object.

#### 4.10.5 The <dfn>`input`</dfn> element

[Categories](#203.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#203.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#203.html_phrasing-content-1).

If the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is *not* in the [Hidden](#203.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state: [Interactive content](#203.html_interactive-content-0).

If the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is *not* in the [Hidden](#203.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state: [Listed](#203.html_category-listed), [labelable](#203.html_category-label), [submittable](#203.html_category-submit), [resettable](#203.html_category-reset), and [reassociateable](#203.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#203.html_form-associated-element).

If the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Hidden](#203.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state: [Listed](#203.html_category-listed), [submittable](#203.html_category-submit), [resettable](#203.html_category-reset), and [reassociateable](#203.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#203.html_form-associated-element).

If the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is *not* in the [Hidden](#203.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state: [Palpable content](#203.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#203.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#203.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#203.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#203.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#203.html_global-attributes)

[`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept) - Hint for expected file type in [file upload controls](#203.html_file-upload-state-(type=file))

[`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt) - Replacement text for use when images are not available

[`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete) - Hint for form autofill feature

[`autofocus`](#203.html_attr-fe-autofocus) - Automatically focus the form control when the page is loaded

[`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked) - Whether the command or control is checked

[`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname) - Name of form field to use for sending the element's [directionality](#203.html_the-directionality) in [form submission](#203.html_form-submission-0)

[`disabled`](#203.html_attr-fe-disabled) - Whether the form control is disabled

[`form`](#203.html_attr-fae-form) - Associates the control with a [`form`](#203.html_the-form-element) element

[`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction) - URL to use for [form submission](#203.html_form-submission-0)

[`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype) - Form data set encoding type to use for [form submission](#203.html_form-submission-0)

[`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod) - HTTP method to use for [form submission](#203.html_form-submission-0)

[`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate) - Bypass form control validation for [form submission](#203.html_form-submission-0)

[`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget) - [Browsing context](#203.html_browsing-context) for [form submission](#203.html_form-submission-0)

[`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height) - Vertical dimension

`inputmode` - Hint for selecting an input modality

[`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list) - List of autocomplete options

[`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max) - Maximum value

[`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength) - Maximum length of value

[`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) - Minimum value

[`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength) - Minimum length of value

[`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) - Whether to allow multiple values

[`name`](#203.html_attr-fe-name) - Name of form control to use for [form submission](#203.html_form-submission-0) and in the [`form.elements`](#203.html_dom-form-elements) API

[`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern) - Pattern to be matched by the form control's value

[`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder) - User-visible label to be placed within the form control

[`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly) - Whether to allow the value to be edited by the user

[`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required) - Whether the control is required for [form submission](#203.html_form-submission-0)

[`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size) - Size of the control

[`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src) - Address of the resource

[`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step) - Granularity to be matched by the form control's value

[`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) - Type of form control

[`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) - Value of the form control

[`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width) - Horizontal dimension

Also, the `title` attribute has special semantics on this element when used in conjunction with the [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern) attribute.

Tag omission in text/html:

No [end tag](#203.html_syntax-end-tag)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

Depends upon [state of the `type` attribute](#203.html_states-of-the-type-attribute).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#203.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLInputElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString accept;
           attribute DOMString alt;
           attribute DOMString autocomplete;
           attribute boolean autofocus;
           attribute boolean defaultChecked;
           attribute boolean checked;
           attribute DOMString dirName;
           attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  readonly attribute FileList? files;
           attribute DOMString formAction;
           attribute DOMString formEnctype;
           attribute DOMString formMethod;
           attribute boolean formNoValidate;
           attribute DOMString formTarget;
           attribute unsigned long height;
           attribute boolean indeterminate;
  readonly attribute HTMLElement? list;
           attribute DOMString max;
           attribute long maxLength;
           attribute DOMString min;
           attribute long minLength;
           attribute boolean multiple;
           attribute DOMString name;
           attribute DOMString pattern;
           attribute DOMString placeholder;
           attribute boolean readOnly;
           attribute boolean required;
           attribute unsigned long size;
           attribute DOMString src;
           attribute DOMString step;
           attribute DOMString type;
           attribute DOMString defaultValue;
  [TreatNullAs=EmptyString] attribute DOMString value;
           attribute Date? valueAsDate;
           attribute unrestricted double valueAsNumber;
           attribute unsigned long width;

  void stepUp(optional long n = 1);
  void stepDown(optional long n = 1);

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  void setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;

  void select();
           attribute unsigned long selectionStart;
           attribute unsigned long selectionEnd;
           attribute DOMString selectionDirection;
  void setRangeText(DOMString replacement);
  void setRangeText(DOMString replacement, unsigned long start, unsigned long end, optional SelectionMode selectionMode = "preserve");
  void setSelectionRange(unsigned long start, unsigned long end, optional DOMString direction);
};
```

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a typed data field, usually with a form control to allow the user to edit the data.

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type">`type`</dfn> attribute controls the data type (and associated control) of the element. It is an [enumerated attribute](#203.html_enumerated-attribute). The following table lists the keywords and states for the attribute — the keywords in the left column map to the states in the cell in the second column on the same row as the keyword.

| Keyword | State | Data type | Control type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-hidden-keyword" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-hidden-keyword">`hidden`</dfn> | [Hidden](#203.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) | An arbitrary string | n/a |
| <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-text-keyword" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-text-keyword">`text`</dfn> | [Text](#203.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) | Text with no line breaks | A text field |

Which of the [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), content attributes, the [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files), [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate), [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber), and [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list) IDL attributes, the [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select) method, the [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-apply" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-apply">apply</dfn> to an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element depends on the state of its [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute. The subsections that define each type also clearly define in normative "bookkeeping" sections which of these feature apply, and which <dfn id="203.html_do-not-apply">do not apply</dfn>, to each type. The behavior of these features depends on whether they apply or not, as defined in their various sections (q.v. for [content attributes](#203.html_common-input-element-attributes), for [APIs](#203.html_common-input-element-apis), for [events](#203.html_common-input-element-events)).

Some states of the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute define a <dfn id="203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm">value sanitization algorithm</dfn>.

Each [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element has a [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), which is exposed by the [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute. Some states define an <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-value-string-number" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-value-string-number">algorithm to convert a string to a number</dfn>, an <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-value-number-string" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-value-number-string">algorithm to convert a number to a string</dfn>, an <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-value-string-date" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-value-string-date">algorithm to convert a string to a `Date` object</dfn>, and an <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-value-date-string" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-value-date-string">algorithm to convert a `Date` object to a string</dfn>, which are used by [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step), [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate), [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber), [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown), and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup).

Each [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element has a boolean <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-value-dirty-flag" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-value-dirty-flag">dirty value flag</dfn>. The [dirty value flag](#203.html_concept-input-value-dirty-flag) must be initially set to false when the element is created, and must be set to true whenever the user interacts with the control in a way that changes the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value). (It is also set to true when the value is programmatically changed, as described in the definition of the [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute.)

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-value" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-value">`value`</dfn> content attribute gives the default [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element. When the [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) content attribute is added, set, or removed, if the control's [dirty value flag](#203.html_concept-input-value-dirty-flag) is false, the user agent must set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element to the value of the [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) content attribute, if there is one, or the empty string otherwise, and then run the current [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm), if one is defined.

Each [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element has a [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked), which is exposed by the [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked) IDL attribute.

Each [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element has a boolean <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-checked-dirty-flag" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-checked-dirty-flag">dirty checkedness flag</dfn>. When it is true, the element is said to have a <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-checked-dirty" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-checked-dirty">*dirty checkedness*</dfn>. The [dirty checkedness flag](#203.html_concept-input-checked-dirty-flag) must be initially set to false when the element is created, and must be set to true whenever the user interacts with the control in a way that changes the [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked).

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-checked" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-checked">`checked`</dfn> content attribute is a [boolean attribute](#203.html_boolean-attribute) that gives the default [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) of the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element. When the [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked) content attribute is added, if the control does not have *[dirty checkedness](#203.html_concept-input-checked-dirty)*, the user agent must set the [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) of the element to true; when the [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked) content attribute is removed, if the control does not have *[dirty checkedness](#203.html_concept-input-checked-dirty)*, the user agent must set the [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) of the element to false.

The [reset algorithm](#203.html_concept-form-reset-control) for [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) elements is to set the [dirty value flag](#203.html_concept-input-value-dirty-flag) and [dirty checkedness flag](#203.html_concept-input-checked-dirty-flag) back to false, set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element to the value of the [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) content attribute, if there is one, or the empty string otherwise, set the [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) of the element to true if the element has a [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked) content attribute and false if it does not, empty the list of [selected files](#203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected), and then invoke the [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm), if the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state defines one.

Each [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element can be *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*. Except where otherwise specified, an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element is always *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*. Similarly, except where otherwise specified, the user agent should not allow the user to modify the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) or [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element is [disabled](#203.html_concept-fe-disabled), it is not *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*.

The [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute can also in some cases (e.g. for the [Date](#203.html_date-state-(type=date)) state, but not the [Checkbox](#203.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) state) stop an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element from being *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*.

The [cloning steps](#203.html_concept-node-clone-ext) for [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) elements must propagate the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), [dirty value flag](#203.html_concept-input-value-dirty-flag), [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked), and [dirty checkedness flag](#203.html_concept-input-checked-dirty-flag) from the node being cloned to the copy.

* * *

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element is first created, the element's rendering and behavior must be set to the rendering and behavior defined for the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's state, and the [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm), if one is defined for the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's state, must be invoked.

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute changes state, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  If the previous state of the element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute put the [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute in the *[value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value)* mode, and the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) is not the empty string, and the new state of the element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute puts the [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute in either the *[default](#203.html_dom-input-value-default)* mode or the *[default/on](#203.html_dom-input-value-default-on)* mode, then set the element's [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) content attribute to the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

2.  Otherwise, if the previous state of the element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute put the [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute in any mode other than the *[value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value)* mode, and the new state of the element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute puts the [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute in the *[value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value)* mode, then set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element to the value of the [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) content attribute, if there is one, or the empty string otherwise, and then set the control's [dirty value flag](#203.html_concept-input-value-dirty-flag) to false.

3.  Update the element's rendering and behavior to the new state's.

4.  Invoke the [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm), if one is defined for the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's new state.

* * *

The [`name`](#203.html_attr-fe-name) attribute represents the element's name. The [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname) attribute controls how the element's [directionality](#203.html_the-directionality) is submitted. The [`disabled`](#203.html_attr-fe-disabled) attribute is used to make the control non-interactive and to prevent its value from being submitted. The [`form`](#203.html_attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element with its [form owner](#203.html_form-owner). The [`autofocus`](#203.html_attr-fe-autofocus) attribute controls focus. The [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete) attribute controls how the user agent provides autofill behavior.

The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-indeterminate" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-indeterminate">`indeterminate`</dfn> IDL attribute must initially be set to false. On getting, it must return the last value it was set to. On setting, it must be set to the new value. It has no effect except for changing the appearance of [checkbox](#203.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) controls.

The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-accept" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-accept">`accept`</dfn>, <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-alt" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-alt">`alt`</dfn>, <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-max" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-max">`max`</dfn>, <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-min" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-min">`min`</dfn>, <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-multiple" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-multiple">`multiple`</dfn>, <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-pattern" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-pattern">`pattern`</dfn>, <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-placeholder" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-placeholder">`placeholder`</dfn>, <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-required" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-required">`required`</dfn>, <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-size" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-size">`size`</dfn>, <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-src" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-src">`src`</dfn>, and <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-step" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-step">`step`</dfn> IDL attributes must [reflect](#203.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name. The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-readonly" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-readOnly">`readOnly`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#203.html_reflect) the [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly) content attribute. The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-defaultchecked" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-defaultChecked">`defaultChecked`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#203.html_reflect) the [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked) content attribute. The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-defaultvalue" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-defaultValue">`defaultValue`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#203.html_reflect) the [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) content attribute.

The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-type">`type`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#203.html_reflect) the respective content attribute of the same name, [limited to only known values](#203.html_limited-to-only-known-values). The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-maxlength" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-maxLength">`maxLength`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#203.html_reflect) the [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength) content attribute, [limited to only non-negative numbers](#203.html_limited-to-only-non-negative-numbers). The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-minlength" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-minLength">`minLength`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#203.html_reflect) the [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength) content attribute, [limited to only non-negative numbers](#203.html_limited-to-only-non-negative-numbers).

The IDL attributes <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-width" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-width">`width`</dfn> and <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-height" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-height">`height`</dfn> must return the rendered width and height of the image, in CSS pixels, if an image is [being rendered](#203.html_being-rendered), and is being rendered to a visual medium; or else the intrinsic width and height of the image, in CSS pixels, if an image is *[available](#203.html_input-img-available)* but not being rendered to a visual medium; or else 0, if no image is *[available](#203.html_input-img-available)*. On setting, they must act as if they [reflected](#203.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

##### 4.10.5.1 States of the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute

###### 4.10.5.1.1 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-hidden" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-hidden">Hidden</dfn> state (`type=hidden`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Hidden](#203.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a value that is not intended to be examined or manipulated by the user.

**Constraint validation**: If an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Hidden](#203.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state, it is [barred from constraint validation](#203.html_barred-from-constraint-validation).

If the [`name`](#203.html_attr-fe-name) attribute is present and has a value that is a [case-sensitive](#203.html_case-sensitive) match for the string "[`_charset_`](#203.html_attr-fe-name-charset)", then the element's [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute must be omitted.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to this element and is in mode [default](#203.html_dom-input-value-default).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required), [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

###### 4.10.5.1.2 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-text" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-text">Text</dfn> (`type=text`) state and <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-search" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-search">Search</dfn> state (`type=search`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`textbox`](#203.html_index-aria-textbox) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)) or [`combobox`](#203.html_index-aria-combobox).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Text](#203.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) state or the [Search](#203.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a one line plain text edit control for the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

The difference between the [Text](#203.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) state and the [Search](#203.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) state is primarily stylistic: on platforms where search fields are distinguished from regular text fields, the [Search](#203.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) state might result in an appearance consistent with the platform's search fields rather than appearing like a regular text field.

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, its [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) should be editable by the user. User agents must not allow users to insert "LF" (U+000A) or "CR" (U+000D) characters into the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, the user agent should allow the user to change the writing direction of the element, setting it either to a left-to-right writing direction or a right-to-left writing direction. If the user does so, the user agent must then run the following steps:

1.  Set the element's [`dir`](#203.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute to "[`ltr`](#203.html_attr-dir-ltr)" if the user selected a left-to-right writing direction, and "[`rtl`](#203.html_attr-dir-rtl)" if the user selected a right-to-left writing direction.

2.  [Queue a task](#203.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element.

The [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, if specified, must have a value that contains no "LF" (U+000A) or "CR" (U+000D) characters.

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm) is as follows**: [Strip line breaks](#203.html_strip-line-breaks) from the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

The following common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required), and [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size) content attributes; [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list), [`selectionStart`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), [`selectionDirection`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection), and [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`setRangeText()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange) methods.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value).

The [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files), [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate), and [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) IDL attributes; [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown) and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.3 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-tel" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-tel">Telephone</dfn> state (`type=tel`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`textbox`](#203.html_index-aria-textbox) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)) or [`combobox`](#203.html_index-aria-combobox).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Telephone](#203.html_telephone-state-(type=tel)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a control for editing a telephone number given in the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, its [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) should be editable by the user. User agents may change the spacing and, with care, the punctuation of [values](#203.html_concept-fe-value) that the user enters. User agents must not allow users to insert "LF" (U+000A) or "CR" (U+000D) characters into the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

The [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, if specified, must have a value that contains no "LF" (U+000A) or "CR" (U+000D) characters.

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm) is as follows**: [Strip line breaks](#203.html_strip-line-breaks) from the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

Unlike the [URL](#203.html_url-state-(type=url)) and [E-mail](#203.html_e-mail-state-(type=email)) types, the [Telephone](#203.html_telephone-state-(type=tel)) type does not enforce a particular syntax. This is intentional; in practice, telephone number fields tend to be free-form fields, because there are a wide variety of valid phone numbers. Systems that need to enforce a particular format are encouraged to use the [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern) attribute or the [`setCustomValidity()`](#203.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) method to hook into the client-side validation mechanism.

The following common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required), and [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size) content attributes; [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list), [`selectionStart`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), [`selectionDirection`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection), and [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`setRangeText()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange) methods.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value).

The [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files), [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate), and [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) IDL attributes; [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown) and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.4 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-url" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-url">URL</dfn> state (`type=url`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`textbox`](#203.html_index-aria-textbox) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)) or [`combobox`](#203.html_index-aria-combobox).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [URL](#203.html_url-state-(type=url)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a control for editing a single [absolute URL](#203.html_absolute-url) given in the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, the user agent should allow the user to change the URL represented by its [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value). User agents may allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a string that is not a [valid](#203.html_valid-url) [absolute URL](#203.html_absolute-url), but may also or instead automatically escape characters entered by the user so that the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) is always a [valid](#203.html_valid-url) [absolute URL](#203.html_absolute-url) (even if that isn't the actual value seen and edited by the user in the interface). User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the empty string. User agents must not allow users to insert "LF" (U+000A) or "CR" (U+000D) characters into the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

The [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a [valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#203.html_valid-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces) that is also an [absolute URL](#203.html_absolute-url).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm) is as follows**: [Strip line breaks](#203.html_strip-line-breaks) from the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), then [strip leading and trailing whitespace](#203.html_strip-leading-and-trailing-whitespace) from the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

**Constraint validation**: While the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element is neither the empty string nor a [valid](#203.html_valid-url) [absolute URL](#203.html_absolute-url), the element is [suffering from a type mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-type-mismatch).

The following common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required), and [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size) content attributes; [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list), [`selectionStart`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), [`selectionDirection`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection), and [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`setRangeText()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange) methods.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value).

The [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files), [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate), and [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) IDL attributes; [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown) and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods.

If a document contained the following markup:

```
<input type="url" name="location" list="urls">
<datalist id="urls">
 <option label="MIME: Format of Internet Message Bodies" value="http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2045">
 <option label="HTML 4.01 Specification" value="http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/">
 <option label="Form Controls" value="http://www.w3.org/TR/xforms/slice8.html#ui-commonelems-hint">
 <option label="Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) 1.1 Specification" value="http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/">
 <option label="Feature Sets - SVG 1.1 - 20030114" value="http://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/feature.html">
 <option label="The Single UNIX Specification, Version 3" value="http://www.unix-systems.org/version3/">
</datalist>
```

...and the user had typed "`www.w3`", and the user agent had also found that the user had visited `http://www.w3.org/Consortium/#membership` and `http://www.w3.org/TR/XForms/` in the recent past, then the rendering might look like this:

![A text box with an icon on the left followed by the text "www.w3" and a cursor, with a drop down button on the right hand side; with, below, a drop down box containing a list of six URLs on the left, with the first four having grayed out labels on the right; and a scroll bar to the right of the drop down box, indicating further values are available.](Images/83a966b432abc7c738e48d0c67746b87.jpg)

The first four URLs in this sample consist of the four URLs in the author-specified list that match the text the user has entered, sorted in some UA-defined manner (maybe by how frequently the user refers to those URLs). Note how the UA is using the knowledge that the values are URLs to allow the user to omit the scheme part and perform intelligent matching on the domain name.

The last two URLs (and probably many more, given the scrollbar's indications of more values being available) are the matches from the user agent's session history data. This data is not made available to the page DOM. In this particular case, the UA has no titles to provide for those values.

###### 4.10.5.1.5 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-email" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-email">E-mail</dfn> state (`type=email`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`textbox`](#203.html_index-aria-textbox) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)) or [`combobox`](#203.html_index-aria-combobox).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [E-mail](#203.html_e-mail-state-(type=email)) state, the rules in this section apply.

How the [E-mail](#203.html_e-mail-state-(type=email)) state operates depends on whether the [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute is specified or not.

When the [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute is not specified on the element

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a control for editing an e-mail address given in the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, the user agent should allow the user to change the e-mail address represented by its [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value). User agents may allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a string that is not a [valid e-mail address](#203.html_valid-e-mail-address). The user agent should act in a manner consistent with expecting the user to provide a single e-mail address. User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the empty string. User agents must not allow users to insert "LF" (U+000A) or "CR" (U+000D) characters into the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value). User agents may transform the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) for display and editing; in particular, user agents should convert punycode in the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to IDN in the display and vice versa.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface is representing input that the user agent cannot convert to punycode, the control is [suffering from bad input](#203.html_suffering-from-bad-input).

The [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a single [valid e-mail address](#203.html_valid-e-mail-address).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm) is as follows**: [Strip line breaks](#203.html_strip-line-breaks) from the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), then [strip leading and trailing whitespace](#203.html_strip-leading-and-trailing-whitespace) from the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

When the [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute is removed, the user agent must run the [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm).

**Constraint validation**: While the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element is neither the empty string nor a single [valid e-mail address](#203.html_valid-e-mail-address), the element is [suffering from a type mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-type-mismatch).

When the [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute *is* specified on the element

The element's [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-values) are the result of [splitting on commas](#203.html_split-a-string-on-commas) the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a control for adding, removing, and editing the e-mail addresses given in the element's [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-values).

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, the user agent should allow the user to add, remove, and edit the e-mail addresses represented by its [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-values). User agents may allow the user to set any individual value in the list of [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a string that is not a [valid e-mail address](#203.html_valid-e-mail-address), but must not allow users to set any individual value to a string containing "," (U+002C), "LF" (U+000A), or "CR" (U+000D) characters. User agents should allow the user to remove all the addresses in the element's [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-values). User agents may transform the [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-values) for display and editing; in particular, user agents should convert punycode in the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to IDN in the display and vice versa.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes a situation where an individual value contains a "," (U+002C) or is representing input that the user agent cannot convert to punycode, the control is [suffering from bad input](#203.html_suffering-from-bad-input).

Whenever the user changes the element's [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-value), the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `latest values` be a copy of the element's [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

2.  [Strip leading and trailing whitespace](#203.html_strip-leading-and-trailing-whitespace) from each value in `latest values`.

3.  Let the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) be the result of concatenating all the values in `latest values`, separating each value from the next by a single "," (U+002C) character, maintaining the list's order.

The [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid e-mail address list](#203.html_valid-e-mail-address-list).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm) is as follows**:

1.  [Split on commas](#203.html_split-a-string-on-commas) the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), [strip leading and trailing whitespace](#203.html_strip-leading-and-trailing-whitespace) from each resulting token, if any, and let the element's [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-values) be the (possibly empty) resulting list of (possibly empty) tokens, maintaining the original order.

2.  Let the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) be the result of concatenating the element's [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-values), separating each value from the next by a single "," (U+002C) character, maintaining the list's order.

When the [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute is set, the user agent must run the [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm).

**Constraint validation**: While the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element is not a [valid e-mail address list](#203.html_valid-e-mail-address-list), the element is [suffering from a type mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-type-mismatch).

A <dfn id="203.html_valid-e-mail-address">valid e-mail address</dfn> is a string that matches the `email` production of the following ABNF, the character set for which is Unicode. This ABNF implements the extensions described in RFC 1123\. [[ABNF]](#203.html_refsABNF) [[RFC5322]](#203.html_refsRFC5322) [[RFC1034]](#203.html_refsRFC1034) [[RFC1123]](#203.html_refsRFC1123)

```
email         = 1*( atext / "." ) "@" label *( "." label )
label         = let-dig [ [ ldh-str ] let-dig ]  ; limited to a length of 63 characters by RFC 1034 section 3.5
atext         = < as defined in RFC 5322 section 3.2.3 >
let-dig       = < as defined in RFC 1034 section 3.5 >
ldh-str       = < as defined in RFC 1034 section 3.5 >
```

This requirement is a [willful violation](#203.html_willful-violation) of RFC 5322, which defines a syntax for e-mail addresses that is simultaneously too strict (before the "@" character), too vague (after the "@" character), and too lax (allowing comments, whitespace characters, and quoted strings in manners unfamiliar to most users) to be of practical use here.

The following JavaScript- and Perl-compatible regular expression is an implementation of the above definition.

```
/^[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*$/
```

A <dfn id="203.html_valid-e-mail-address-list">valid e-mail address list</dfn> is a [set of comma-separated tokens](#203.html_set-of-comma-separated-tokens), where each token is itself a [valid e-mail address](#203.html_valid-e-mail-address). To obtain the list of tokens from a [valid e-mail address list](#203.html_valid-e-mail-address-list), and implementation must [split the string on commas](#203.html_split-a-string-on-commas).

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value).

###### 4.10.5.1.7 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-date" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-date">Date</dfn> state (`type=date`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Date](#203.html_date-state-(type=date)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a control for setting the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a string representing a specific [date](#203.html_concept-date).

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, the user agent should allow the user to change the [date](#203.html_concept-date) represented by its [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), as obtained by [parsing a date](#203.html_parse-a-date-string) from it. User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a non-empty string that is not a [valid date string](#203.html_valid-date-string). If the user agent provides a user interface for selecting a [date](#203.html_concept-date), then the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) must be set to a [valid date string](#203.html_valid-date-string) representing the user's selection. User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the empty string.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes input that the user agent cannot convert to a [valid date string](#203.html_valid-date-string), the control is [suffering from bad input](#203.html_suffering-from-bad-input).

See the [introduction section](#203.html_input-author-notes) for a discussion of the difference between the input format and submission format for date, time, and number form controls, and the [implementation notes](#203.html_input-impl-notes) regarding localization of form controls.

The [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a [valid date string](#203.html_valid-date-string).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm) is as follows**: If the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element is not a [valid date string](#203.html_valid-date-string), then set it to the empty string instead.

The [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid date string](#203.html_valid-date-string). The [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid date string](#203.html_valid-date-string).

The [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step) attribute is expressed in days. The [step scale factor](#203.html_concept-input-step-scale) is 86,400,000 (which converts the days to milliseconds, as used in the other algorithms). The [default step](#203.html_concept-input-step-default) is 1 day.

When the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch), the user agent may round the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the nearest [date](#203.html_concept-date) for which the element would not [suffer from a step mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch).

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number), given a string `input`, is as follows**: If [parsing a date](#203.html_parse-a-date-string) from `input` results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return the number of milliseconds elapsed from midnight UTC on the morning of 1970-01-01 (the time represented by the value "`1970-01-01T00:00:00.0Z`") to midnight UTC on the morning of the parsed [date](#203.html_concept-date), ignoring leap seconds.

**The [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#203.html_concept-input-value-number-string), given a number `input`, is as follows**: Return a [valid date string](#203.html_valid-date-string) that represents the [date](#203.html_concept-date) that, in UTC, is current `input` milliseconds after midnight UTC on the morning of 1970-01-01 (the time represented by the value "`1970-01-01T00:00:00.0Z`").

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a `Date` object](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-date), given a string `input`, is as follows**: If [parsing a date](#203.html_parse-a-date-string) from `input` results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return [a new `Date` object](#203.html_create-a-date-object) representing midnight UTC on the morning of the parsed [date](#203.html_concept-date).

**The [algorithm to convert a `Date` object to a string](#203.html_concept-input-value-date-string), given a `Date` object `input`, is as follows**: Return a [valid date string](#203.html_valid-date-string) that represents the [date](#203.html_concept-date) current at the time represented by `input` in the UTC time zone.
