User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the empty string.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes input that the user agent cannot convert to a [valid time string](#203.html_valid-time-string), the control is [suffering from bad input](#203.html_suffering-from-bad-input).

See the [introduction section](#203.html_input-author-notes) for a discussion of the difference between the input format and submission format for date, time, and number form controls, and the [implementation notes](#203.html_input-impl-notes) regarding localization of form controls.

The [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a [valid time string](#203.html_valid-time-string).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm) is as follows**: If the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element is not a [valid time string](#203.html_valid-time-string), then set it to the empty string instead.

The form control [has a periodic domain](#203.html_has-a-periodic-domain).

The [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid time string](#203.html_valid-time-string). The [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid time string](#203.html_valid-time-string).

The [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step) attribute is expressed in seconds. The [step scale factor](#203.html_concept-input-step-scale) is 1000 (which converts the seconds to milliseconds, as used in the other algorithms). The [default step](#203.html_concept-input-step-default) is 60 seconds.

When the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch), the user agent may round the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the nearest [time](#203.html_concept-time) for which the element would not [suffer from a step mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch).

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number), given a string `input`, is as follows**: If [parsing a time](#203.html_parse-a-time-string) from `input` results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return the number of milliseconds elapsed from midnight to the parsed [time](#203.html_concept-time) on a day with no time changes.

**The [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#203.html_concept-input-value-number-string), given a number `input`, is as follows**: Return a [valid time string](#203.html_valid-time-string) that represents the [time](#203.html_concept-time) that is `input` milliseconds after midnight on a day with no time changes.

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a `Date` object](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-date), given a string `input`, is as follows**: If [parsing a time](#203.html_parse-a-time-string) from `input` results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return [a new `Date` object](#203.html_create-a-date-object) representing the parsed [time](#203.html_concept-time) in UTC on 1970-01-01.

**The [algorithm to convert a `Date` object to a string](#203.html_concept-input-value-date-string), given a `Date` object `input`, is as follows**: Return a [valid time string](#203.html_valid-time-string) that represents the UTC [time](#203.html_concept-time) component that is represented by `input`.

The following common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required), and [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step) content attributes; [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list), [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value), [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate), and [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) IDL attributes; [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown) and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value).

The [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files), [`selectionStart`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), and [`selectionDirection`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`setRangeText()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.9 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-number" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-number">Number</dfn> state (`type=number`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`spinbutton`](#203.html_index-aria-spinbutton) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Number](#203.html_number-state-(type=number)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a control for setting the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a string representing a number.

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, the user agent should allow the user to change the number represented by its [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), as obtained from applying the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#203.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) to it. User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a non-empty string that is not a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number). If the user agent provides a user interface for selecting a number, then the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) must be set to the [best representation of the number representing the user's selection as a floating-point number](#203.html_best-representation-of-the-number-as-a-floating-point-number). User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the empty string.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes input that the user agent cannot convert to a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number), the control is [suffering from bad input](#203.html_suffering-from-bad-input).

This specification does not define what user interface user agents are to use; user agent vendors are encouraged to consider what would best serve their users' needs. For example, a user agent in Persian or Arabic markets might support Persian and Arabic numeric input (converting it to the format required for submission as described above). Similarly, a user agent designed for Romans might display the value in Roman numerals rather than in decimal; or (more realistically) a user agent designed for the French market might display the value with apostrophes between thousands and commas before the decimals, and allow the user to enter a value in that manner, internally converting it to the submission format described above.

The [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm) is as follows**: If the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element is not a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number), then set it to the empty string instead.

The [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number). The [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number).

The [step scale factor](#203.html_concept-input-step-scale) is 1. The [default step](#203.html_concept-input-step-default) is 1 (allowing only integers to be selected by the user, unless the [step base](#203.html_concept-input-min-zero) has a non-integer value).

When the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch), the user agent may round the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the nearest number for which the element would not [suffer from a step mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch). If there are two such numbers, user agents are encouraged to pick the one nearest positive infinity.

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number), given a string `input`, is as follows**: If applying the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#203.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) to `input` results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return the resulting number.

**The [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#203.html_concept-input-value-number-string), given a number `input`, is as follows**: Return a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number) that represents `input`.

The following common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required), and [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step) content attributes; [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list), [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value), and [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) IDL attributes; [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown) and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value).

The [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files), [`selectionStart`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), [`selectionDirection`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection), and [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`setRangeText()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange) methods.

Here is an example of using a numeric input control:

```
<label>How much do you want to charge? $<input type=number min=0 step=0.01 name=price></label>
```

As described above, a user agent might support numeric input in the user's local format, converting it to the format required for submission as described above. This might include handling grouping separators (as in "872,000,000,000") and various decimal separators (such as "3,99" vs "3.99") or using local digits (such as those in Arabic, Devanagari, Persian, and Thai).

The `type=number` state is not appropriate for input that happens to only consist of numbers but isn't strictly speaking a number. For example, it would be inappropriate for credit card numbers or US postal codes. A simple way of determining whether to use `type=number` is to consider whether it would make sense for the input control to have a spinbox interface (e.g. with "up" and "down" arrows). Getting a credit card number wrong by 1 in the last digit isn't a minor mistake, it's as wrong as getting every digit incorrect. So it would not make sense for the user to select a credit card number using "up" and "down" buttons. When a spinbox interface is not appropriate, `type=text` is probably the right choice (possibly with a [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern) attribute).

###### 4.10.5.1.10 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-range" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-range">Range</dfn> state (`type=range`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`slider`](#203.html_index-aria-slider) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Range](#203.html_range-state-(type=range)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a control for setting the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a string representing a number, but with the caveat that the exact value is not important, letting UAs provide a simpler interface than they do for the [Number](#203.html_number-state-(type=number)) state.

In this state, the range and step constraints are enforced even during user input, and there is no way to set the value to the empty string.

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, the user agent should allow the user to change the number represented by its [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), as obtained from applying the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#203.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) to it. User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a string that is not a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number). If the user agent provides a user interface for selecting a number, then the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) must be set to a [best representation of the number representing the user's selection as a floating-point number](#203.html_best-representation-of-the-number-as-a-floating-point-number). User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the empty string.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes input that the user agent cannot convert to a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number), the control is [suffering from bad input](#203.html_suffering-from-bad-input).

The [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm) is as follows**: If the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element is not a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number), then set it to a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number) that represents the [default value](#203.html_concept-input-value-default-range).

The [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number). The [default minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min-default) is 0. The [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number). The [default maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max-default) is 100.

The <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-value-default-range" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-value-default-range">default value</dfn> is the [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min) plus half the difference between the [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min) and the [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max), unless the [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max) is less than the [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min), in which case the [default value](#203.html_concept-input-value-default-range) is the [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min).

When the element is [suffering from an underflow](#203.html_suffering-from-an-underflow), the user agent must set the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number) that represents the [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min).

When the element is [suffering from an overflow](#203.html_suffering-from-an-overflow), if the [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max) is not less than the [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min), the user agent must set the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number) that represents the [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max).

The [step scale factor](#203.html_concept-input-step-scale) is 1. The [default step](#203.html_concept-input-step-default) is 1 (allowing only integers, unless the [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) attribute has a non-integer value).

When the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch), the user agent must round the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the nearest number for which the element would not [suffer from a step mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch), and which is greater than or equal to the [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min), and, if the [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max) is not less than the [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min), which is less than or equal to the [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max), if there is a number that matches these constraints. If two numbers match these constraints, then user agents must use the one nearest to positive infinity.

For example, the markup `<input type="range" min=0 max=100 step=20 value=50>` results in a range control whose initial value is 60.

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number), given a string `input`, is as follows**: If applying the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#203.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) to `input` results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return the resulting number.

**The [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#203.html_concept-input-value-number-string), given a number `input`, is as follows**: Return a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number) that represents `input`.

The following common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), and [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step) content attributes; [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list), [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value), and [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) IDL attributes; [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown) and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value).

The [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required), [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files), [`selectionStart`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), [`selectionDirection`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection), and [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`setRangeText()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange) methods.

Here is an example of a range control using an autocomplete list with the [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list) attribute. This could be useful if there are values along the full range of the control that are especially important, such as preconfigured light levels or typical speed limits in a range control used as a speed control. The following markup fragment:

```
<input type="range" min="-100" max="100" value="0" step="10" name="power" list="powers">
<datalist id="powers">
 <option value="0">
 <option value="-30">
 <option value="30">
 <option value="++50">
</datalist>
```

...with the following style sheet applied:

```
input { height: 75px; width: 49px; background: #D5CCBB; color: black; }
```

...might render as:

![A vertical slider control whose primary color is black and whose background color is beige, with the slider having five tick marks, one long one at each extremity, and three short ones clustered around the midpoint.](Images/9fad551be5fad3297c38e09b9b0a5dab.jpg)

Note how the UA determined the orientation of the control from the ratio of the style-sheet-specified height and width properties. The colors were similarly derived from the style sheet. The tick marks, however, were derived from the markup. In particular, the [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step) attribute has not affected the placement of tick marks, the UA deciding to only use the author-specified completion values and then adding longer tick marks at the extremes.

Note also how the invalid value `++50` was completely ignored.

For another example, consider the following markup fragment:

```
<input name=x type=range min=100 max=700 step=9.09090909 value=509.090909>
```

A user agent could display in a variety of ways, for instance:

![As a dial.](Images/36402076e6ce9185c6aa9c660faa45c5.jpg)

Or, alternatively, for instance:

![As a long horizontal slider with tick marks.](Images/6a588dfa3d5e69e4a407678dc4f745a9.jpg)

The user agent could pick which one to display based on the dimensions given in the style sheet. This would allow it to maintain the same resolution for the tick marks, despite the differences in width.

Finally, here is an example of a range control with two labeled values:

```
<input type="range" name="a" list="a-values">
<datalist id="a-values">
 <option value="10" label="Low">
 <option value="90" label="High">
</datalist>
```

With styles that make the control draw vertically, it might look as follows:

![A vertical slider control with two tick marks, one near the top labeled 'High', and one near the bottom labeled 'Low'.](Images/db2de487ad5cd4c6ebcf92d3a2e13622.jpg)

###### 4.10.5.1.11 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-color" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-color">Color</dfn> state (`type=color`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Color](#203.html_color-state-(type=color)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a color well control, for setting the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a string representing a [simple color](#203.html_simple-color).

In this state, there is always a color picked, and there is no way to set the value to the empty string.

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, the user agent should allow the user to change the color represented by its [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), as obtained from applying the [rules for parsing simple color values](#203.html_rules-for-parsing-simple-color-values) to it. User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to a string that is not a [valid lowercase simple color](#203.html_valid-lowercase-simple-color). If the user agent provides a user interface for selecting a color, then the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) must be set to the result of using the [rules for serializing simple color values](#203.html_rules-for-serializing-simple-color-values) to the user's selection. User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the empty string.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes input that the user agent cannot convert to a [valid lowercase simple color](#203.html_valid-lowercase-simple-color), the control is [suffering from bad input](#203.html_suffering-from-bad-input).

The [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a [valid simple color](#203.html_valid-simple-color).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm) is as follows**: If the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element is a [valid simple color](#203.html_valid-simple-color), then set it to the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element [converted to ASCII lowercase](#203.html_converted-to-ascii-lowercase); otherwise, set it to the string "`#000000`".

The following common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element content attributes and IDL attributes [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete) and [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list) content attributes; [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list) and [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attributes.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value).

The [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply).

###### 4.10.5.1.12 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-checkbox" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-checkbox">Checkbox</dfn> state (`type=checkbox`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`checkbox`](#203.html_index-aria-checkbox) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)) or [`menuitemcheckbox`](#203.html_index-aria-menuitemcheckbox).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Checkbox](#203.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a two-state control that represents the element's [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) state. If the element's [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) state is true, the control represents a positive selection, and if it is false, a negative selection. If the element's [`indeterminate`](#203.html_dom-input-indeterminate) IDL attribute is set to true, then the control's selection should be obscured as if the control was in a third, indeterminate, state.

The control is never a true tri-state control, even if the element's [`indeterminate`](#203.html_dom-input-indeterminate) IDL attribute is set to true. The [`indeterminate`](#203.html_dom-input-indeterminate) IDL attribute only gives the appearance of a third state.

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, then: The [pre-click activation steps](#203.html_pre-click-activation-steps) consist of setting the element's [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) to its opposite value (i.e. true if it is false, false if it is true), and of setting the element's [`indeterminate`](#203.html_dom-input-indeterminate) IDL attribute to false. The [canceled activation steps](#203.html_canceled-activation-steps) consist of setting the [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) and the element's [`indeterminate`](#203.html_dom-input-indeterminate) IDL attribute back to the values they had before the [pre-click activation steps](#203.html_pre-click-activation-steps) were run. The [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior) is to [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the element and then [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `change` at the element.

If the element is not *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, it has no [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior).

**Constraint validation**: If the element is *[required](#203.html_concept-input-required)* and its [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) is false, then the element is [suffering from being missing](#203.html_suffering-from-being-missing).

`input` . [`indeterminate`](#203.html_dom-input-indeterminate) [ = `value` ]

When set, overrides the rendering of [checkbox](#203.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) controls so that the current value is not visible.

The following common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element content attributes and IDL attributes [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), and [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required) content attributes; [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked) and [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attributes.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [default/on](#203.html_dom-input-value-default-on).

The [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

###### 4.10.5.1.13 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-radio" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-radio">Radio Button</dfn> state (`type=radio`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`radio`](#203.html_index-aria-radio) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)) or [`menuitemradio`](#203.html_index-aria-menuitemradio).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#203.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a control that, when used in conjunction with other [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) elements, forms a *[radio button group](#203.html_radio-button-group)* in which only one control can have its [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) state set to true. If the element's [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) state is true, the control represents the selected control in the group, and if it is false, it indicates a control in the group that is not selected.

The <dfn id="203.html_radio-button-group">*radio button group*</dfn> that contains an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element `a` also contains all the other [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) elements `b` that fulfill all of the following conditions:

*   The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element `b`'s [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#203.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state.
*   Either `a` and `b` have the same [form owner](#203.html_form-owner), or they both have no [form owner](#203.html_form-owner).
*   Both `a` and `b` are in the same [home subtree](#203.html_home-subtree).
*   They both have a [`name`](#203.html_attr-fe-name) attribute, their [`name`](#203.html_attr-fe-name) attributes are not empty, and the value of `a`'s [`name`](#203.html_attr-fe-name) attribute is a [compatibility caseless](#203.html_compatibility-caseless) match for the value of `b`'s [`name`](#203.html_attr-fe-name) attribute.

A document must not contain an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element whose *[radio button group](#203.html_radio-button-group)* contains only that element.

When any of the following phenomena occur, if the element's [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) state is true after the occurrence, the [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) state of all the other elements in the same *[radio button group](#203.html_radio-button-group)* must be set to false:

*   The element's [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) state is set to true (for whatever reason).
*   The element's [`name`](#203.html_attr-fe-name) attribute is set, changed, or removed.
*   The element's [form owner](#203.html_form-owner) changes.

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, then: The [pre-click activation steps](#203.html_pre-click-activation-steps) consist of setting the element's [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) to true. The [canceled activation steps](#203.html_canceled-activation-steps) consist of setting the element's [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) to false. The [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior) is to [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the element and then [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `change` at the element. .

If the element is not *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, it has no [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior).

**Constraint validation**: If an element in the *[radio button group](#203.html_radio-button-group)* is *[required](#203.html_concept-input-required)*, and all of the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) elements in the *[radio button group](#203.html_radio-button-group)* have a [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) that is false, then the element is [suffering from being missing](#203.html_suffering-from-being-missing).

If none of the radio buttons in a [radio button group](#203.html_radio-button-group) are checked when they are inserted into the document, then they will all be initially unchecked in the interface, until such time as one of them is checked (either by the user or by script).

The following common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element content attributes and IDL attributes [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked) and [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required) content attributes; [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked) and [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attributes.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [default/on](#203.html_dom-input-value-default-on).

The [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

###### 4.10.5.1.14 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-file" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-file">File Upload</dfn> state (`type=file`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [File Upload](#203.html_file-upload-state-(type=file)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a list of <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-type-file-selected">selected files</dfn>, each file consisting of a file name, a file type, and a file body (the contents of the file).

File names must not contain path components, even in the case that a user has selected an entire directory hierarchy or multiple files with the same name from different directories.

Unless the [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute is set, there must be no more than one file in the list of [selected files](#203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected).

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, then the element's [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior) is to run the following steps:

1.  If the algorithm is not [allowed to show a popup](#203.html_allowed-to-show-a-popup), then abort these steps without doing anything else.

2.  Return, but continue running these steps asynchronously.

3.  Optionally, wait until any prior execution of this algorithm has terminated.

4.  Display a prompt to the user requesting that the user specify some files. If the [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute is not set, there must be no more than one file selected; otherwise, any number may be selected. Files can be from the filesystem or created on the fly, e.g. a picture taken from a camera connected to the user's device.

5.  Wait for the user to have made their selection.

6.  [Queue a task](#203.html_queue-a-task) to first update the element's [selected files](#203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected) so that it represents the user's selection, then [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element, and finally [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `change` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element.

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, the user agent should allow the user to change the files on the list in other ways also, e.g. adding or removing files by drag-and-drop. When the user does so, the user agent must [queue a task](#203.html_queue-a-task) to first update the element's [selected files](#203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected) so that it represents the user's new selection, then [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element, and finally [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `change` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element.

If the element is not *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, it has no [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior) and the user agent must not allow the user to change the element's selection.

**Constraint validation**: If the element is *[required](#203.html_concept-input-required)* and the list of [selected files](#203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected) is empty, then the element is [suffering from being missing](#203.html_suffering-from-being-missing).

* * *

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-accept" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-accept">`accept`</dfn> attribute may be specified to provide user agents with a hint of what file types will be accepted.

If specified, the attribute must consist of a [set of comma-separated tokens](#203.html_set-of-comma-separated-tokens), each of which must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](#203.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for one of the following:

The string `audio/*`

Indicates that sound files are accepted.

The string `video/*`

Indicates that video files are accepted.

The string `image/*`

Indicates that image files are accepted.

A [valid MIME type with no parameters](#203.html_valid-mime-type-with-no-parameters)

Indicates that files of the specified type are accepted.

A string whose first character is a "." (U+002E) character

Indicates that files with the specified file extension are accepted.

The tokens must not be [ASCII case-insensitive](#203.html_ascii-case-insensitive) matches for any of the other tokens (i.e. duplicates are not allowed). To obtain the list of tokens from the attribute, the user agent must [split the attribute value on commas](#203.html_split-a-string-on-commas).

User agents may use the value of this attribute to display a more appropriate user interface than a generic file picker. For instance, given the value `image/*`, a user agent could offer the user the option of using a local camera or selecting a photograph from their photo collection; given the value `audio/*`, a user agent could offer the user the option of recording a clip using a headset microphone.

User agents should prevent the user from selecting files that are not accepted by one (or more) of these tokens.

Authors are encouraged to specify both any MIME types and any corresponding extensions when looking for data in a specific format.

For example, consider an application that converts Microsoft Word documents to Open Document Format files. Since Microsoft Word documents are described with a wide variety of MIME types and extensions, the site can list several, as follows:

```
<input type="file" accept=".doc,.docx,.xml,application/msword,application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document">
```

On platforms that only use file extensions to describe file types, the extensions listed here can be used to filter the allowed documents, while the MIME types can be used with the system's type registration table (mapping MIME types to extensions used by the system), if any, to determine any other extensions to allow. Similarly, on a system that does not have file names or extensions but labels documents with MIME types internally, the MIME types can be used to pick the allowed files, while the extensions can be used if the system has an extension registration table that maps known extensions to MIME types used by the system.

Extensions tend to be ambiguous (e.g. there are an untold number of formats that use the "`.dat`" extension, and users can typically quite easily rename their files to have a "`.doc`" extension even if they are not Microsoft Word documents), and MIME types tend to be unreliable (e.g. many formats have no formally registered types, and many formats are in practice labeled using a number of different MIME types). Authors are reminded that, as usual, data received from a client should be treated with caution, as it may not be in an expected format even if the user is not hostile and the user agent fully obeyed the [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept) attribute's requirements.

For historical reasons, the [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute prefixes the file name with the string "`C:\fakepath\`". Some legacy user agents actually included the full path (which was a security vulnerability). As a result of this, obtaining the file name from the [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute in a backwards-compatible way is non-trivial. The following function extracts the file name in a suitably compatible manner:

```
function extractFilename(path) {
  if (path.substr(0, 12) == "C:\\fakepath\\")
    return path.substr(12); // modern browser
  var x;
  x = path.lastIndexOf('/');
  if (x >= 0) // Unix-based path
    return path.substr(x+1);
  x = path.lastIndexOf('\\');
  if (x >= 0) // Windows-based path
    return path.substr(x+1);
  return path; // just the file name
}
```

This can be used as follows:

```
<p><input type=file name=image onchange="updateFilename(this.value)"></p>
<p>The name of the file you picked is: <span id="filename">(none)</span></p>
<script>
 function updateFilename(path) {
   var name = extractFilename(path);
   document.getElementById('filename').textContent = name;
 }
</script>
```

* * *

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [filename](#203.html_dom-input-value-filename).

The element's [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute must be omitted.

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list), [`selectionStart`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), [`selectionDirection`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection), [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate), and [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`setRangeText()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), [`setSelectionRange()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange), [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown), and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.15 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-submit" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-submit">Submit Button</dfn> state (`type=submit`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`button`](#203.html_index-aria-button) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Submit Button](#203.html_submit-button-state-(type=submit)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a button that, when activated, submits the form. If the element has a [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, the button's label must be the value of that attribute; otherwise, it must be an implementation-defined string that means "Submit" or some such. The element is a [button](#203.html_concept-button), specifically a [submit button](#203.html_concept-submit-button). [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/6cb93ce3b50cff7c3d208ab7696a9b07.jpg)](#203.html_fingerprinting-vector)

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, then the element's [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior) is as follows: if the element has a [form owner](#203.html_form-owner), and the element's [`Document`](#203.html_document) is [fully active](#203.html_fully-active), [submit](#203.html_concept-form-submit) the [form owner](#203.html_form-owner) from the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element; otherwise, do nothing.

If the element is not *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, it has no [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior).

The [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), and [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget) attributes are [attributes for form submission](#203.html_attributes-for-form-submission).

The [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate) attribute can be used to make submit buttons that do not trigger the constraint validation.

The following common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element content attributes and IDL attributes [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the element: [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), and [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget) content attributes; [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [default](#203.html_dom-input-value-default).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required), [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files), [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list), [`selectionStart`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), [`selectionDirection`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection), [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate), and [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`setRangeText()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), [`setSelectionRange()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange), [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown), and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.16 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-image" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-image">Image Button</dfn> state (`type=image`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`button`](#203.html_index-aria-button) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)), [`link`](#203.html_index-aria-link), [`menuitem`](#203.html_index-aria-menuitem), [`menuitemcheckbox`](#203.html_index-aria-menuitemcheckbox), [`menuitemradio`](#203.html_index-aria-menuitemradio) or [`radio`](#203.html_index-aria-radio).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Image Button](#203.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) either an image from which a user can select a coordinate and submit the form, or alternatively a button from which the user can submit the form. The element is a [button](#203.html_concept-button), specifically a [submit button](#203.html_concept-submit-button).

The coordinate is sent to the server [during form submission](#203.html_constructing-the-form-data-set) by sending two entries for the element, derived from the name of the control but with "`.x`" and "`.y`" appended to the name with the `x` and `y` components of the coordinate respectively.

* * *

The image is given by the <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-src" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-src">`src`</dfn> attribute. The [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src) attribute must be present, and must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#203.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces) referencing a non-interactive, optionally animated, image resource that is neither paged nor scripted.

When any of the following events occur, unless the user agent cannot support images, or its support for images has been disabled, or the user agent only fetches elements on demand, or the [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src) attribute's value is the empty string, the user agent must [resolve](#203.html_resolve-a-url) the value of the [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src) attribute, relative to the element, and if that is successful, must [fetch](#203.html_fetch) the resulting [absolute URL](#203.html_absolute-url):

*   The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is first set to the [Image Button](#203.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state (possibly when the element is first created), and the [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src) attribute is present.
*   The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is changed back to the [Image Button](#203.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, and the [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src) attribute is present, and its value has changed since the last time the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute was in the [Image Button](#203.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state.
*   The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Image Button](#203.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, and the [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src) attribute is set or changed.

Fetching the image must [delay the load event](#203.html_delay-the-load-event) of the element's document until the [task](#203.html_concept-task) that is [queued](#203.html_queue-a-task) by the [networking task source](#203.html_networking-task-source) once the resource has been [fetched](#203.html_fetch) (defined below) has been run.

If the image was successfully obtained, with no network errors, and the image's type is a supported image type, and the image is a valid image of that type, then the image is said to be <dfn id="203.html_input-img-available" data-anolis-xref="input-img-available">*available*</dfn>. If this is true before the image is completely downloaded, each [task](#203.html_concept-task) that is [queued](#203.html_queue-a-task) by the [networking task source](#203.html_networking-task-source) while the image is being [fetched](#203.html_fetch) must update the presentation of the image appropriately.

The user agent should apply the [image sniffing rules](#203.html_content-type-sniffing:-image) to determine the type of the image, with the image's [associated Content-Type headers](#203.html_content-type) giving the `official type`. If these rules are not applied, then the type of the image must be the type given by the image's [associated Content-Type headers](#203.html_content-type).

User agents must not support non-image resources with the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element. User agents must not run executable code embedded in the image resource. User agents must only display the first page of a multipage resource. User agents must not allow the resource to act in an interactive fashion, but should honor any animation in the resource.

The [task](#203.html_concept-task) that is [queued](#203.html_queue-a-task) by the [networking task source](#203.html_networking-task-source) once the resource has been [fetched](#203.html_fetch), must, if the download was successful and the image is *[available](#203.html_input-img-available)*, [queue a task](#203.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `load` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element; and otherwise, if the fetching process fails without a response from the remote server, or completes but the image is not a valid or supported image, [queue a task](#203.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `error` on the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element.

* * *

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-alt" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-alt">`alt`</dfn> attribute provides the textual label for the button for users and user agents who cannot use the image. The [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt) attribute must be present, and must contain a non-empty string giving the label that would be appropriate for an equivalent button if the image was unavailable.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element supports [dimension attributes](#203.html_dimension-attributes).

* * *

If the [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src) attribute is set, and the image is *[available](#203.html_input-img-available)* and the user agent is configured to display that image, then: The element [represents](#203.html_represents) a control for selecting a [coordinate](#203.html_concept-input-type-image-coordinate) from the image specified by the [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src) attribute; if the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, the user agent should allow the user to select this [coordinate](#203.html_concept-input-type-image-coordinate), and the element's [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior) is as follows: if the element has a [form owner](#203.html_form-owner), and the element's [`Document`](#203.html_document) is [fully active](#203.html_fully-active), take the user's selected [coordinate](#203.html_concept-input-type-image-coordinate), and [submit](#203.html_concept-form-submit) the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [form owner](#203.html_form-owner) from the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element. If the user activates the control without explicitly selecting a coordinate, then the coordinate (0,0) must be assumed.

Otherwise, the element [represents](#203.html_represents) a submit button whose label is given by the value of the [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt) attribute; if the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, then the element's [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior) is as follows: if the element has a [form owner](#203.html_form-owner), and the element's [`Document`](#203.html_document) is [fully active](#203.html_fully-active), set the [selected coordinate](#203.html_concept-input-type-image-coordinate) to (0,0), and [submit](#203.html_concept-form-submit) the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [form owner](#203.html_form-owner) from the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element.

In either case, if the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)* but has no [form owner](#203.html_form-owner) or the element's [`Document`](#203.html_document) is not [fully active](#203.html_fully-active), then its [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior) must be to do nothing. If the element is not *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, it has no [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior).

The <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-type-image-coordinate" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-type-image-coordinate">selected coordinate</dfn> must consist of an `x`-component and a `y`-component. The coordinates represent the position relative to the edge of the image, with the coordinate space having the positive `x` direction to the right, and the positive `y` direction downwards.

The `x`-component must be a [valid integer](#203.html_valid-integer) representing a number `x` in the range ?(`border`[`left`]+`padding`[`left`]) ≤ `x` ≤ `width`+`border`[`right`]+`padding`[`right`], where `width` is the rendered width of the image, `border`[`left`] is the width of the border on the left of the image, `padding`[`left`] is the width of the padding on the left of the image, `border`[`right`] is the width of the border on the right of the image, and `padding`[`right`] is the width of the padding on the right of the image, with all dimensions given in CSS pixels.

The `y`-component must be a [valid integer](#203.html_valid-integer) representing a number `y` in the range ?(`border`[`top`]+`padding`[`top`]) ≤ `y` ≤ `height`+`border`[`bottom`]+`padding`[`bottom`], where `height` is the rendered height of the image, `border`[`top`] is the width of the border above the image, `padding`[`top`] is the width of the padding above the image, `border`[`bottom`] is the width of the border below the image, and `padding`[`bottom`] is the width of the padding below the image, with all dimensions given in CSS pixels.

Where a border or padding is missing, its width is zero CSS pixels.

* * *

The [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), and [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget) attributes are [attributes for form submission](#203.html_attributes-for-form-submission).

`image` . [`width`](#203.html_dom-input-width) [ = `value` ]
`image` . [`height`](#203.html_dom-input-height) [ = `value` ]

These attributes return the actual rendered dimensions of the image, or zero if the dimensions are not known.

They can be set, to change the corresponding content attributes.

The following common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element content attributes and IDL attributes [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the element: [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width) content attributes; [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute.

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute is in mode [default](#203.html_dom-input-value-default).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required), [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size), and [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step).

The element's [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute must be omitted.

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files), [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list), [`selectionStart`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), [`selectionDirection`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection), [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate), and [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`setRangeText()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), [`setSelectionRange()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange), [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown), and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods.

The [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply).

Many aspects of this state's behavior are similar to the behavior of the [`img`](#203.html_the-img-element) element. Readers are encouraged to read that section, where many of the same requirements are described in more detail.

Take the following form:

```
<form action="process.cgi">
 <input type=image src=map.png name=where alt="Show location list">
</form>
```

If the user clicked on the image at coordinate (127,40) then the URL used to submit the form would be "`process.cgi?where.x=127&where.y=40`".

(In this example, it's assumed that for users who don't see the map, and who instead just see a button labeled "Show location list", clicking the button will cause the server to show a list of locations to pick from instead of the map.)

###### 4.10.5.1.17 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-reset" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-reset">Reset Button</dfn> state (`type=reset`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`button`](#203.html_index-aria-button) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Reset Button](#203.html_reset-button-state-(type=reset)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a button that, when activated, resets the form. If the element has a [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, the button's label must be the value of that attribute; otherwise, it must be an implementation-defined string that means "Reset" or some such. The element is a [button](#203.html_concept-button). [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/6cb93ce3b50cff7c3d208ab7696a9b07.jpg)](#203.html_fingerprinting-vector)

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, then the element's [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior), if the element has a [form owner](#203.html_form-owner) and the element's [`Document`](#203.html_document) is [fully active](#203.html_fully-active), is to [reset](#203.html_concept-form-reset) the [form owner](#203.html_form-owner); otherwise, it is to do nothing.

If the element is not *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, it has no [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior).

**Constraint validation**: The element is [barred from constraint validation](#203.html_barred-from-constraint-validation).

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to this element and is in mode [default](#203.html_dom-input-value-default).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required), [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files), [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list), [`selectionStart`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), [`selectionDirection`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection), [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate), and [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`setRangeText()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), [`setSelectionRange()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange), [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown), and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.18 <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-type-button" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-type-button">Button</dfn> state (`type=button`)

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#203.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`button`](#203.html_index-aria-button) (default - [*do not set*](#203.html_aria-usage-note)), [`link`](#203.html_index-aria-link), [`menuitem`](#203.html_index-aria-menuitem), [`menuitemcheckbox`](#203.html_index-aria-menuitemcheckbox), [`menuitemradio`](#203.html_index-aria-menuitemradio) or [`radio`](#203.html_index-aria-radio).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#203.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#203.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#203.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Button](#203.html_button-state-(type=button)) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element [represents](#203.html_represents) a button with no default behavior. A label for the button must be provided in the [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, though it may be the empty string. If the element has a [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, the button's label must be the value of that attribute; otherwise, it must be the empty string. The element is a [button](#203.html_concept-button).

If the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, the element's [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior) is to do nothing.

If the element is not *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, it has no [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior).

**Constraint validation**: The element is [barred from constraint validation](#203.html_barred-from-constraint-validation).

The [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to this element and is in mode [default](#203.html_dom-input-value-default).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`accept`](#203.html_attr-input-accept), [`alt`](#203.html_attr-input-alt), [`autocomplete`](#203.html_attr-fe-autocomplete), [`checked`](#203.html_attr-input-checked), [`dirname`](#203.html_attr-fe-dirname), [`formaction`](#203.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#203.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#203.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#203.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), [`formtarget`](#203.html_attr-fs-formtarget), [`height`](#203.html_attr-dim-height), [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list), [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max), [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min), [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength), [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple), [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern), [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder), [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly), [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required), [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size), [`src`](#203.html_attr-input-src), [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step), and [`width`](#203.html_attr-dim-width).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the element: [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked), [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files), [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list), [`selectionStart`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), [`selectionDirection`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection), [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate), and [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`setRangeText()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), [`setSelectionRange()`](#203.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange), [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown), and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods.

The [`input`](#203.html_event-input-input) and [`change`](#203.html_event-input-change) events [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply).

##### 4.10.5.2 Implemention notes regarding localization of form controls

*This section is non-normative.*

The formats shown to the user in date, time, and number controls is independent of the format used for form submission.

Browsers are encouraged to use user interfaces that present dates, times, and numbers according to the conventions of either the locale implied by the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [language](#203.html_language) or the user's preferred locale. Using the page's locale will ensure consistency with page-provided data.

For example, it would be confusing to users if an American English page claimed that a Cirque De Soleil show was going to be showing on 02/03, but their browser, configured to use the British English locale, only showed the date 03/02 in the ticket purchase date picker. Using the page's locale would at least ensure that the date was presented in the same format everywhere. (There's still a risk that the user would end up arriving a month late, of course, but there's only so much that can be done about such cultural differences...)

##### 4.10.5.3 Common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element attributes

These attributes only [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element if its [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in a state whose definition declares that the attribute [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply). When an attribute [doesn't apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element, user agents must [ignore](#203.html_ignore) the attribute, regardless of the requirements and definitions below.

###### 4.10.5.3.1 The [`maxlength`](#203.html_attr-input-maxlength) and [`minlength`](#203.html_attr-input-minlength) attributes

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-maxlength" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-maxlength">`maxlength`</dfn> attribute, when it [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply), is a [form control `maxlength` attribute](#203.html_attr-fe-maxlength) controlled by the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [dirty value flag](#203.html_concept-input-value-dirty-flag).
