The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-minlength" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-minlength">`minlength`</dfn> attribute, when it [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply), is a [form control `minlength` attribute](#203.html_attr-fe-minlength) controlled by the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [dirty value flag](#203.html_concept-input-value-dirty-flag).

If the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element has a [maximum allowed value length](#203.html_maximum-allowed-value-length), then the [code-unit length](#203.html_code-unit-length) of the value of the element's [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute must be equal to or less than the element's [maximum allowed value length](#203.html_maximum-allowed-value-length).

The following extract shows how a messaging client's text entry could be arbitrarily restricted to a fixed number of characters, thus forcing any conversation through this medium to be terse and discouraging intelligent discourse.

```
<label>What are you doing? <input name=status maxlength=140></label>
```

Here, a password is given a minimum length:

```
<p><label>Username: <input name=u required></label>
<p><label>Password: <input name=p required minlength=12></label>
```

###### 4.10.5.3.2 The [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size) attribute

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-size" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-size">`size`</dfn> attribute gives the number of characters that, in a visual rendering, the user agent is to allow the user to see while editing the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value).

The [`size`](#203.html_attr-input-size) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid non-negative integer](#203.html_valid-non-negative-integer) greater than zero.

If the attribute is present, then its value must be parsed using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#203.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers), and if the result is a number greater than zero, then the user agent should ensure that at least that many characters are visible.

The [`size`](#203.html_dom-input-size) IDL attribute is [limited to only non-negative numbers greater than zero](#203.html_limited-to-only-non-negative-numbers-greater-than-zero) and has a default value of 20.

###### 4.10.5.3.3 The [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-readonly" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-readonly">`readonly`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#203.html_boolean-attribute) that controls whether or not the user can edit the form control. When specified, the element is not *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*.

**Constraint validation**: If the [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute is specified on an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element, the element is [barred from constraint validation](#203.html_barred-from-constraint-validation).

The difference between [`disabled`](#203.html_attr-fe-disabled) and [`readonly`](#203.html_attr-input-readonly) is that read-only controls are still focusable, so the user can still select the text and interact with it, whereas disabled controls are entirely non-interactive. (For this reason, only text controls can be made read-only: it wouldn't make sense for checkboxes or buttons, for instances.)

In the following example, the existing product identifiers cannot be modified, but they are still displayed as part of the form, for consistency with the row representing a new product (where the identifier is not yet filled in).

```
<form action="products.cgi" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
 <table>
  <tr> <th> Product ID <th> Product name <th> Price <th> Action
  <tr>
   <td> <input readonly="readonly" name="1.pid" value="H412">
   <td> <input required="required" name="1.pname" value="Floor lamp Ulke">
   <td> $<input required="required" type="number" min="0" step="0.01" name="1.pprice" value="49.99">
   <td> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="delete:1">Delete</button>
  <tr>
   <td> <input readonly="readonly" name="2.pid" value="FG28">
   <td> <input required="required" name="2.pname" value="Table lamp Ulke">
   <td> $<input required="required" type="number" min="0" step="0.01" name="2.pprice" value="24.99">
   <td> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="delete:2">Delete</button>
  <tr>
   <td> <input required="required" name="3.pid" value="" pattern="[A-Z0-9]+">
   <td> <input required="required" name="3.pname" value="">
   <td> $<input required="required" type="number" min="0" step="0.01" name="3.pprice" value="">
   <td> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="delete:3">Delete</button>
 </table>
 <p> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="add">Add</button> </p>
 <p> <button name="action" value="update">Save</button> </p>
</form>
```

###### 4.10.5.3.4 The [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required) attribute

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-required" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-required">`required`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#203.html_boolean-attribute). When specified, the element is <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-required" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-required">*required*</dfn>.

**Constraint validation**: If the element is *[required](#203.html_concept-input-required)*, and its [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) IDL attribute [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply) and is in the mode [value](#203.html_dom-input-value-value), and the element is *[mutable](#203.html_concept-fe-mutable)*, and the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) is the empty string, then the element is [suffering from being missing](#203.html_suffering-from-being-missing).

The following form has two required fields, one for an e-mail address and one for a password. It also has a third field that is only considered valid if the user types the same password in the password field and this third field.

```
<h1>Create new account</h1>
<form action="/newaccount" method=post
      oninput="up2.setCustomValidity(up2.value != up.value ? 'Passwords do not match.' : '')">
 <p>
  <label for="username">E-mail address:</label>
  <input id="username" type=email required name=un>
 <p>
  <label for="password1">Password:</label>
  <input id="password1" type=password required name=up>
 <p>
  <label for="password2">Confirm password:</label>
  <input id="password2" type=password name=up2>
 <p>
  <input type=submit value="Create account">
</form>
```

For radio buttons, the [`required`](#203.html_attr-input-required) attribute is satisfied if any of the radio buttons in the [group](#203.html_radio-button-group) is selected. Thus, in the following example, any of the radio buttons can be checked, not just the one marked as required:

```
<fieldset>
 <legend>Did the movie pass the Bechdel test?</legend>
 <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="no-characters"> No, there are not even two female characters in the movie. </label>
 <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="no-names"> No, the female characters never talk to each other. </label>
 <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="no-topic"> No, when female characters talk to each other it's always about a male character. </label>
 <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="yes" required> Yes. </label>
 <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="unknown"> I don't know. </label>
</fieldset>
```

To avoid confusion as to whether a [radio button group](#203.html_radio-button-group) is required or not, authors are encouraged to specify the attribute on all the radio buttons in a group. Indeed, in general, authors are encouraged to avoid having radio button groups that do not have any initially checked controls in the first place, as this is a state that the user cannot return to, and is therefore generally considered a poor user interface.

###### 4.10.5.3.5 The [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-multiple" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-multiple">`multiple`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#203.html_boolean-attribute) that indicates whether the user is to be allowed to specify more than one value.

The following extract shows how an e-mail client's "Cc" field could accept multiple e-mail addresses.

```
<label>Cc: <input type=email multiple name=cc></label>
```

If the user had, amongst many friends in his user contacts database, two friends "Arthur Dent" (with address "art@example.net") and "Adam Josh" (with address "adamjosh@example.net"), then, after the user has typed "a", the user agent might suggest these two e-mail addresses to the user.

![Form control group containing 'Send', 'Save now' and 'Discard' buttons, a 'To:' combo box with an 'a' displayed in the text box and 2 list items below.](Images/2f402d74c34069d7dbe443bd430cbb60.jpg)

The page could also link in the user's contacts database from the site:

```
<label>Cc: <input type=email multiple name=cc list=contacts></label>
...
<datalist id="contacts">
 <option value="hedral@damowmow.com">
 <option value="pillar@example.com">
 <option value="astrophy@cute.example">
 <option value="astronomy@science.example.org">
</datalist>
```

Suppose the user had entered "bob@example.net" into this text field, and then started typing a second e-mail address starting with "a". The user agent might show both the two friends mentioned earlier, as well as the "astrophy" and "astronomy" values given in the [`datalist`](#203.html_the-datalist-element) element.

![Form control group containing 'send', 'save now' and 'discard' buttons and a 'To:' combo box with 'bob@example.net,a' displayed in the text box and 4 list items below.](Images/be659c71e258c01fefe3a222a3d5fd50.jpg)

The following extract shows how an e-mail client's "Attachments" field could accept multiple files for upload.

```
<label>Attachments: <input type=file multiple name=att></label>
```

###### 4.10.5.3.6 The [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern) attribute

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-pattern" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-pattern">`pattern`</dfn> attribute specifies a regular expression against which the control's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), or, when the [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply) and is set, the control's [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-values), are to be checked.

If specified, the attribute's value must match the JavaScript *Pattern* production. [[ECMA262]](#203.html_refsECMA262)

If an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element has a [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern) attribute specified, and the attribute's value, when compiled as a JavaScript regular expression with the `global`, `ignoreCase`, and `multiline` flags *disabled* (see ECMA262 Edition 5, sections 15.10.7.2 through 15.10.7.4), compiles successfully, then the resulting regular expression is the element's <dfn id="203.html_compiled-pattern-regular-expression">compiled pattern regular expression</dfn>. If the element has no such attribute, or if the value doesn't compile successfully, then the element has no [compiled pattern regular expression](#203.html_compiled-pattern-regular-expression). [[ECMA262]](#203.html_refsECMA262)

**Constraint validation**: If the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) is not the empty string, and either the element's [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute is not specified or it [does not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply) to the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element given its [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state, and the element has a [compiled pattern regular expression](#203.html_compiled-pattern-regular-expression) but that regular expression does not match the entirety of the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), then the element is [suffering from a pattern mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-pattern-mismatch).

**Constraint validation**: If the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) is not the empty string, and the element's [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute is specified and [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply) to the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element, and the element has a [compiled pattern regular expression](#203.html_compiled-pattern-regular-expression) but that regular expression does not match the entirety of each of the element's [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-values), then the element is [suffering from a pattern mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-pattern-mismatch).

The [compiled pattern regular expression](#203.html_compiled-pattern-regular-expression), when matched against a string, must have its start anchored to the start of the string and its end anchored to the end of the string.

This implies that the regular expression language used for this attribute is the same as that used in JavaScript, except that the [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern) attribute is matched against the entire value, not just any subset (somewhat as if it implied a `^(?:` at the start of the pattern and a `)$` at the end).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element has a [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern) attribute specified, authors should provide a description of the pattern in text near the control. Authors may also include a [`title`](#203.html_attr-title) attribute to give a description of the pattern. User agents may use the contents of this attribute, if it is present, when informing the user that the pattern is not matched, or at any other suitable time, such as in a tooltip or read out by assistive technology when the control gains focus.

Relying on the [`title`](#203.html_attr-title) attribute alone is currently discouraged as many user agents do not expose the attribute in an accessible manner as required by this specification (e.g. requiring a pointing device such as a mouse to cause a tooltip to appear, which excludes keyboard-only users and touch-only users, such as anyone with a modern phone or tablet).

For example, the following snippet includes the pattern description in text below the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element), the pattern description is also included in the [`title`](#203.html_attr-title) attribute:

```
<label> Part number:
        <input pattern="[0-9][A-Z]{3}" name="part"
        data-x="A part number is a digit followed by three uppercase letters."/>
        </label>
        <p>A part number is a digit followed by three uppercase letters.</p>
```

The presence of the pattern description in text makes the advice available to any user regardless of device.

The presence of the pattern description in the title attribute, results in the description being announced by assistive technology such as screen readers when the input receives focus.

If the user has attempted to submit the form with incorrect information, the presence of the title attribute text could also cause the UA to display an alert such as:

```
A part number is a digit followed by three uppercase letters.
    You cannot submit this form when the field is incorrect.
```

In this example, the pattern description is in text below the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element), but not in the [`title`](#203.html_attr-title) attribute. The [`aria-describedby`](http://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/states_and_properties#aria-describedby) attribute is used to explicitly associate the text description with the control, the description is announced by assistive technology such as screen readers when the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) receives focus:

```
<label> Part number:
        <input pattern="[0-9][A-Z]{3}" name="part" aria-describedby="description">
        </label>
        <p id="description">A part number is a digit followed by three uppercase letters.</p>
```

When a control has a [`pattern`](#203.html_attr-input-pattern) attribute, the `title` attribute, if used, must describe the pattern. Additional information could also be included, so long as it assists the user in filling in the control. Otherwise, assistive technology would be impaired.

For instance, if the title attribute contained the caption of the control, assistive technology could end up saying something like <samp>The text you have entered does not match the required pattern. Birthday</samp>, which is not useful.

UAs may still show the [`title`](#203.html_attr-title) in non-error situations (for example, as a tooltip when hovering over the control), so authors should be careful not to word `title`s as if an error has necessarily occurred.

###### 4.10.5.3.7 The [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) and [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max) attributes

Some form controls can have explicit constraints applied limiting the allowed range of values that the user can provide. Normally, such a range would be linear and continuous. A form control can <dfn id="203.html_has-a-periodic-domain" data-anolis-xref="has a periodic domain">have a periodic domain</dfn>, however, in which case the form control's broadest possible range is finite, and authors can specify explicit ranges within it that span the boundaries.

Specifically, the broadest range of a [`type=time`](#203.html_time-state-(type=time)) control is midnight to midnight (24 hours), and authors can set both continuous linear ranges (such as 9pm to 11pm) and discontinuous ranges spanning midnight (such as 11pm to 1am).

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-min" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-min">`min`</dfn> and <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-max" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-max">`max`</dfn> attributes indicate the allowed range of values for the element.

Their syntax is defined by the section that defines the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state.

If the element has a [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) attribute, and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number) to the value of the [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) attribute is a number, then that number is the element's <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-min" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-min">minimum</dfn>; otherwise, if the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state defines a <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-min-default" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-min-default">default minimum</dfn>, then that is the [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min); otherwise, the element has no [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min).

The [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) attribute also defines the [step base](#203.html_concept-input-min-zero).

If the element has a [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max) attribute, and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number) to the value of the [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max) attribute is a number, then that number is the element's <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-max" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-max">maximum</dfn>; otherwise, if the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state defines a <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-max-default" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-max-default">default maximum</dfn>, then that is the [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max); otherwise, the element has no [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max).

If the element does not [have a periodic domain](#203.html_has-a-periodic-domain), the [`max`](#203.html_attr-input-max) attribute's value (the [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max)) must not be less than the [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) attribute's value (its [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min)).

If an element that does not [have a periodic domain](#203.html_has-a-periodic-domain) has a [maximum](#203.html_attr-input-max) that is less than its [minimum](#203.html_attr-input-min), then so long as the element has a [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), it will either be [suffering from an underflow](#203.html_suffering-from-an-underflow) or [suffering from an overflow](#203.html_suffering-from-an-overflow).

An element <dfn id="203.html_has-a-reversed-range">has a reversed range</dfn> if it [has a periodic domain](#203.html_has-a-periodic-domain) and its [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max) is less than its [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min).

An element <dfn id="203.html_have-range-limitations" data-anolis-xref="have range limitations">has range limitations</dfn> if it has a defined [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min) or a defined [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max).

**Constraint validation**: When the element has a [minimum](#203.html_attr-input-min) and does not [have a reversed range](#203.html_has-a-reversed-range), and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number) to the string given by the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) is a number, and the number obtained from that algorithm is less than the [minimum](#203.html_attr-input-min), the element is [suffering from an underflow](#203.html_suffering-from-an-underflow).

**Constraint validation**: When the element has a [maximum](#203.html_attr-input-max) and does not [have a reversed range](#203.html_has-a-reversed-range), and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number) to the string given by the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) is a number, and the number obtained from that algorithm is more than the [maximum](#203.html_attr-input-max), the element is [suffering from an overflow](#203.html_suffering-from-an-overflow).

**Constraint validation**: When an element [has a reversed range](#203.html_has-a-reversed-range), and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number) to the string given by the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) is a number, and the number obtained from that algorithm is more than the [maximum](#203.html_attr-input-max) *and* less than the [minimum](#203.html_attr-input-min), the element is simultaneously [suffering from an underflow](#203.html_suffering-from-an-underflow) and [suffering from an overflow](#203.html_suffering-from-an-overflow).

The following date control limits input to dates that are before the 1980s:

```
<input name=bday type=date max="1979-12-31">
```

The following number control limits input to whole numbers greater than zero:

```
<input name=quantity required="" type="number" min="1" value="1">
```

The following time control limits input to those minutes that occur between 9pm and 6am, defaulting to midnight:

```
<input name="sleepStart" type=time min="21:00" max="06:00" step="60" value="00:00">
```

###### 4.10.5.3.8 The [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step) attribute

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-step" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-step">`step`</dfn> attribute indicates the granularity that is expected (and required) of the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), by limiting the allowed values. The section that defines the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state also defines the <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-step-default" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-step-default">default step</dfn>, the <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-step-scale" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-step-scale">step scale factor</dfn>, and in some cases the <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-step-default-base" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-step-default-base">default step base</dfn>, which are used in processing the attribute as described below.

The [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step) attribute, if specified, must either have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#203.html_valid-floating-point-number) that [parses](#203.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) to a number that is greater than zero, or must have a value that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#203.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`any`".

The attribute provides the <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-step" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-step">allowed value step</dfn> for the element, as follows:

1.  If the attribute is absent, then the [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step) is the [default step](#203.html_concept-input-step-default) multiplied by the [step scale factor](#203.html_concept-input-step-scale).
2.  Otherwise, if the attribute's value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#203.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`any`", then there is no [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step).
3.  Otherwise, if the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#203.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values), when they are applied to the attribute's value, return an error, zero, or a number less than zero, then the [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step) is the [default step](#203.html_concept-input-step-default) multiplied by the [step scale factor](#203.html_concept-input-step-scale).
4.  Otherwise, the [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step) is the number returned by the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#203.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) when they are applied to the attribute's value, multiplied by the [step scale factor](#203.html_concept-input-step-scale).

The <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-min-zero" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-min-zero">step base</dfn> is the value returned by the following algorithm:

1.  If the element has a [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) content attribute, and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number) to the value of the [`min`](#203.html_attr-input-min) content attribute is not an error, then return that result and abort these steps.

2.  If the element has a [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) content attribute, and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number) to the value of the [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) content attribute is not an error, then return that result and abort these steps.

3.  If a [default step base](#203.html_concept-input-step-default-base) is defined for this element given its [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's state, then return it and abort these steps.

4.  Return zero.

**Constraint validation**: When the element has an [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step), and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number) to the string given by the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) is a number, and that number subtracted from the [step base](#203.html_concept-input-min-zero) is not an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step), the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#203.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch).

The following range control only accepts values in the range 0..1, and allows 256 steps in that range:

```
<input name=opacity type=range min=0 max=1 step=0.00392156863>
```

The following control allows any time in the day to be selected, with any accuracy (e.g. thousandth-of-a-second accuracy or more):

```
<input name=favtime type=time step=any>
```

Normally, time controls are limited to an accuracy of one minute.

###### 4.10.5.3.9 The [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list) attribute

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-list" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-list">`list`</dfn> attribute is used to identify an element that lists predefined options suggested to the user.

If present, its value must be the [ID](#203.html_concept-id) of a [`datalist`](#203.html_the-datalist-element) element in the same document.

The <dfn id="203.html_concept-input-list" data-anolis-xref="concept-input-list">suggestions source element</dfn> is the first element in the document in [tree order](#203.html_tree-order) to have an [ID](#203.html_concept-id) equal to the value of the [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list) attribute, if that element is a [`datalist`](#203.html_the-datalist-element) element. If there is no [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list) attribute, or if there is no element with that [ID](#203.html_concept-id), or if the first element with that [ID](#203.html_concept-id) is not a [`datalist`](#203.html_the-datalist-element) element, then there is no [suggestions source element](#203.html_concept-input-list).

If there is a [suggestions source element](#203.html_concept-input-list), then, when the user agent is allowing the user to edit the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), the user agent should offer the suggestions represented by the [suggestions source element](#203.html_concept-input-list) to the user in a manner suitable for the type of control used. The user agent may use the suggestion's [label](#203.html_concept-option-label) to identify the suggestion if appropriate.

How user selections of suggestions are handled depends on whether the element is a control accepting a single value only, or whether it accepts multiple values:

If the element does not have a [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute specified or if the [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute does not apply

When the user selects a suggestion, the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) must be set to the selected suggestion's [value](#203.html_concept-option-value), as if the user had written that value himself.

If the element *does* have a [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute specified, and the [`multiple`](#203.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute does [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply)

When the user selects a suggestion, the user agent must either add a new entry to the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-values), whose value is the selected suggestion's [value](#203.html_concept-option-value), or change an existing entry in the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [value*s*](#203.html_concept-fe-values) to have the value given by the selected suggestion's [value](#203.html_concept-option-value), as if the user had himself added an entry with that value, or edited an existing entry to be that value. Which behavior is to be applied depends on the user interface in a user-agent-defined manner.

* * *

If the [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list) attribute [does not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply), there is no [suggestions source element](#203.html_concept-input-list).

This URL field offers some suggestions.

```
<label>Homepage: <input name=hp type=url list=hpurls></label>
<datalist id=hpurls>
 <option value="http://www.google.com/" label="Google">
 <option value="http://www.reddit.com/" label="Reddit">
</datalist>
```

Other URLs from the user's history might show also; this is up to the user agent.

This example demonstrates how to design a form that uses the autocompletion list feature while still degrading usefully in legacy user agents.

If the autocompletion list is merely an aid, and is not important to the content, then simply using a [`datalist`](#203.html_the-datalist-element) element with children [`option`](#203.html_the-option-element) elements is enough. To prevent the values from being rendered in legacy user agents, they need to be placed inside the [`value`](#203.html_attr-option-value) attribute instead of inline.

```
<p>
 <label>
  Enter a breed:
  <input type="text" name="breed" list="breeds">
  <datalist id="breeds">
   <option value="Abyssinian">
   <option value="Alpaca">
   <!-- ... -->
  </datalist>
 </label>
</p>
```

However, if the values need to be shown in legacy UAs, then fallback content can be placed inside the [`datalist`](#203.html_the-datalist-element) element, as follows:

```
<p>
 <label>
  Enter a breed:
  <input type="text" name="breed" list="breeds">
 </label>
 <datalist id="breeds">
  <label>
   or select one from the list:
   <select name="breed">
    <option value=""> (none selected)
    <option>Abyssinian
    <option>Alpaca
    <!-- ... -->
   </select>
  </label>
 </datalist>
</p>
```

The fallback content will only be shown in UAs that don't support [`datalist`](#203.html_the-datalist-element). The options, on the other hand, will be detected by all UAs, even though they are not children of the [`datalist`](#203.html_the-datalist-element) element.

Note that if an [`option`](#203.html_the-option-element) element used in a [`datalist`](#203.html_the-datalist-element) is [`selected`](#203.html_attr-option-selected), it will be selected by default by legacy UAs (because it affects the [`select`](#203.html_the-select-element)), but it will not have any effect on the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element in UAs that support [`datalist`](#203.html_the-datalist-element).

###### 4.10.5.3.10 The [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder) attribute

The <dfn id="203.html_attr-input-placeholder" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-placeholder">`placeholder`</dfn> attribute represents a *short* hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value. A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format. The attribute, if specified, must have a value that contains no "LF" (U+000A) or "CR" (U+000D) characters.

The [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder) attribute should not be used as a replacement for a [`label`](#203.html_the-label-element). For a longer hint or other advisory text, place the text next to the control.

Use of the [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder) attribute as a replacement for a [`label`](#203.html_the-label-element) can reduce the accessibility and usability of the control for a range of users including older users and users with cognitive, mobility, fine motor skill or vision impairments. While the hint given by the control's [`label`](#203.html_the-label-element) is shown at all times, the short hint given in the [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder) attribute is only shown before the user enters a value. Furthermore, [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder) text may be mistaken for a pre-filled value, and as commonly implemented the default color of the placeholder text provides insufficient contrast and the lack of a separate visible [`label`](#203.html_the-label-element) reduces the size of the hit region available for setting focus on the control.

User agents should present this hint to the user, after having [stripped line breaks](#203.html_strip-line-breaks) from it, when the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) is the empty string and the control is not focused (i.e., by displaying it inside a blank unfocused control).

Here is an example of a mail configuration user interface that uses the [`placeholder`](#203.html_attr-input-placeholder) attribute:

```
<fieldset>
 <legend>Mail Account</legend>
 <p><label>Name: <input type="text" name="fullname" placeholder="John Ratzenberger"></label></p>
 <p><label>Address: <input type="email" name="address" placeholder="john@example.net"></label></p>
 <p><label>Password: <input type="password" name="password"></label></p>
 <p><label>Description: <input type="text" name="desc" placeholder="My Email Account"></label></p>
</fieldset>
```

In situations where the control's content has one directionality but the placeholder needs to have a different directionality, Unicode's bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters can be used in the attribute value:

```
<input name=t1 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B;???? ?????? 1?&#x202E;">
<input name=t2 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B;???? ?????? 2?&#x202E;">
```

For slightly more clarity, here's the same example using numeric character references instead of inline Arabic:

```
<input name=t1 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B;&#1585;&#1602;&#1605; &#1575;&#1604;&#1607;&#1575;&#1578;&#1601; 1&#x202E;">
<input name=t2 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B;&#1585;&#1602;&#1605; &#1575;&#1604;&#1607;&#1575;&#1578;&#1601; 2&#x202E;">
```

##### 4.10.5.4 Common [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element APIs

`input` . [`value`](#203.html_dom-input-value) [ = `value` ]

Returns the current [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the form control.

Can be set, to change the value.

Throws an [`InvalidStateError`](#203.html_invalidstateerror) exception if it is set to any value other than the empty string when the control is a file upload control.

`input` . [`checked`](#203.html_dom-input-checked) [ = `value` ]

Returns the current [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) of the form control.

Can be set, to change the [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked).

`input` . [`files`](#203.html_dom-input-files)

Returns a [`FileList`](#203.html_filelist) object listing the [selected files](#203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected) of the form control.

Returns null if the control isn't a file control.

`input` . [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate) [ = `value` ]

Returns a `Date` object representing the form control's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), if applicable; otherwise, returns null.

Can be set, to change the value.

Throws an [`InvalidStateError`](#203.html_invalidstateerror) exception if the control isn't date- or time-based.

`input` . [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) [ = `value` ]

Returns a number representing the form control's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), if applicable; otherwise, returns NaN.

Can be set, to change the value. Setting this to NaN will set the underlying value to the empty string.

Throws an [`InvalidStateError`](#203.html_invalidstateerror) exception if the control is neither date- or time-based nor numeric.

`input` . [`stepUp`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup)( [ `n` ] )
`input` . [`stepDown`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown)( [ `n` ] )

Changes the form control's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) by the value given in the [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step) attribute, multiplied by `n`. The default value for `n` is 1.

Throws [`InvalidStateError`](#203.html_invalidstateerror) exception if the control is neither date- or time-based nor numeric, or if the [`step`](#203.html_attr-input-step) attribute's value is "`any`".

`input` . [`list`](#203.html_dom-input-list)

Returns the [`datalist`](#203.html_the-datalist-element) element indicated by the [`list`](#203.html_attr-input-list) attribute.

The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-value" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-value">`value`</dfn> IDL attribute allows scripts to manipulate the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element. The attribute is in one of the following modes, which define its behavior:

<dfn id="203.html_dom-input-value-value" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-value-value">value</dfn>

On getting, it must return the current [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element. On setting, it must set the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to the new value, set the element's [dirty value flag](#203.html_concept-input-value-dirty-flag) to true, invoke the [value sanitization algorithm](#203.html_value-sanitization-algorithm), if the element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state defines one, and then, if the element has a text entry cursor position, should move the text entry cursor position to the end of the text field, unselecting any selected text and resetting the selection direction to *none*.

<dfn id="203.html_dom-input-value-default" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-value-default">default</dfn>

On getting, if the element has a [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, it must return that attribute's value; otherwise, it must return the empty string. On setting, it must set the element's [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute to the new value.

<dfn id="203.html_dom-input-value-default-on" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-value-default-on">default/on</dfn>

On getting, if the element has a [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute, it must return that attribute's value; otherwise, it must return the string "`on`". On setting, it must set the element's [`value`](#203.html_attr-input-value) attribute to the new value.

<dfn id="203.html_dom-input-value-filename" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-value-filename">filename</dfn>

On getting, it must return the string "`C:\fakepath\`" followed by the name of the first file in the list of [selected files](#203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected), if any, or the empty string if the list is empty. On setting, if the new value is the empty string, it must empty the list of [selected files](#203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected); otherwise, it must throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#203.html_invalidstateerror) exception.

This "fakepath" requirement is a sad accident of history. See [the example in the File Upload state section](#203.html_fakepath-srsly) for more information.

* * *

The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-checked" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-checked">`checked`</dfn> IDL attribute allows scripts to manipulate the [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) of an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element. On getting, it must return the current [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) of the element; and on setting, it must set the element's [checkedness](#203.html_concept-fe-checked) to the new value and set the element's [dirty checkedness flag](#203.html_concept-input-checked-dirty-flag) to true.

* * *

The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-files" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-files">`files`</dfn> IDL attribute allows scripts to access the element's [selected files](#203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected). On getting, if the IDL attribute [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply), it must return a [`FileList`](#203.html_filelist) object that represents the current [selected files](#203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected). The same object must be returned until the list of [selected files](#203.html_concept-input-type-file-selected) changes. If the IDL attribute [does not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply), then it must instead return null. [[FILEAPI]](#203.html_refsFILEAPI)

* * *

The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-valueasdate" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-valueAsDate">`valueAsDate`</dfn> IDL attribute represents the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element, interpreted as a date.

On getting, if the [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate) attribute [does not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply), as defined for the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state, then return null. Otherwise, run the [algorithm to convert a string to a `Date` object](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-date) defined for that state; if the algorithm returned a `Date` object, then return it, otherwise, return null.

On setting, if the [`valueAsDate`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate) attribute [does not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply), as defined for the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state, then throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#203.html_invalidstateerror) exception; otherwise, if the new value is null or a `Date` object representing the NaN time value, then set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element to the empty string; otherwise, run the [algorithm to convert a `Date` object to a string](#203.html_concept-input-value-date-string), as defined for that state, on the new value, and set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element to the resulting string.

* * *

The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-valueAsNumber">`valueAsNumber`</dfn> IDL attribute represents the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element, interpreted as a number.

On getting, if the [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) attribute [does not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply), as defined for the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state, then return a Not-a-Number (NaN) value. Otherwise, if the [`valueAs`*`Date`*](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate) attribute [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply), run the [algorithm to convert a string to a `Date` object](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-date) defined for that state; if the algorithm returned a `Date` object, then return the *time value* of the object (the number of milliseconds from midnight UTC the morning of 1970-01-01 to the time represented by the `Date` object), otherwise, return a Not-a-Number (NaN) value. Otherwise, run the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number) defined for that state; if the algorithm returned a number, then return it, otherwise, return a Not-a-Number (NaN) value.

On setting, if the new value is infinite, then throw a `TypeError` exception. Otherwise, if the [`valueAsNumber`](#203.html_dom-input-valueasnumber) attribute [does not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply), as defined for the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state, then throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#203.html_invalidstateerror) exception. Otherwise, if the new value is a Not-a-Number (NaN) value, then set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element to the empty string. Otherwise, if the [`valueAs`*`Date`*](#203.html_dom-input-valueasdate) attribute [applies](#203.html_concept-input-apply), run the [algorithm to convert a `Date` object to a string](#203.html_concept-input-value-date-string) defined for that state, passing it a `Date` object whose *time value* is the new value, and set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element to the resulting string. Otherwise, run the [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#203.html_concept-input-value-number-string), as defined for that state, on the new value, and set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element to the resulting string.

* * *

The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-stepdown" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-stepDown">`stepDown(``n``)`</dfn> and <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-stepup" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-stepUp">`stepUp(``n``)`</dfn> methods, when invoked, must run the following algorithm:

1.  If the [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown) and [`stepUp()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepup) methods [do not apply](#203.html_do-not-apply), as defined for the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state, then throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#203.html_invalidstateerror) exception, and abort these steps.

2.  If the element has no [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step), then throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#203.html_invalidstateerror) exception, and abort these steps.

3.  If the element has a [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min) and a [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max) and the [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min) is greater than the [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max), then abort these steps.

4.  If the element has a [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min) and a [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max) and there is no value greater than or equal to the element's [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min) and less than or equal to the element's [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-max) that, when subtracted from the [step base](#203.html_concept-input-min-zero), is an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step), then abort these steps.

5.  If applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#203.html_concept-input-value-string-number) to the string given by the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) does not result in an error, then let `value` be the result of that algorithm. Otherwise, let `value` be zero.

6.  If `value` subtracted from the [step base](#203.html_concept-input-min-zero) is not an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step), then set `value` to the nearest value that, when subtracted from the [step base](#203.html_concept-input-min-zero), is an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step), and that is less than `value` if the method invoked was the [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown) and more than `value` otherwise.

    Otherwise (`value` subtracted from the [step base](#203.html_concept-input-min-zero) is an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step)), run the following substeps:

    1.  Let `n` be the argument.

    2.  Let `delta` be the [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step) multiplied by `n`.

    3.  If the method invoked was the [`stepDown()`](#203.html_dom-input-stepdown) method, negate `delta`.

    4.  Let `value` be the result of adding `delta` to `value`.

7.  If the element has a [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min), and `value` is less than that [minimum](#203.html_concept-input-min), then set `value` to the smallest value that, when subtracted from the [step base](#203.html_concept-input-min-zero), is an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step), and that is more than or equal to `minimum`.

8.  If the element has a [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-min), and `value` is greater than that [maximum](#203.html_concept-input-min), then set `value` to the largest value that, when subtracted from the [step base](#203.html_concept-input-min-zero), is an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#203.html_concept-input-step), and that is less than or equal to `maximum`.

9.  Let `value as string` be the result of running the [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#203.html_concept-input-value-number-string), as defined for the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's current state, on `value`.

10.  Set the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) of the element to `value as string`.

* * *

The <dfn id="203.html_dom-input-list" data-anolis-xref="dom-input-list">`list`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the current [suggestions source element](#203.html_concept-input-list), if any, or null otherwise.

##### 4.10.5.5 Common event behaviors

When the `input` and `change` events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply) (which is the case for all [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) controls other than [buttons](#203.html_concept-button) and those with the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Hidden](#203.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state), the events are fired to indicate that the user has interacted with the control. The <dfn id="203.html_event-input-input" data-anolis-xref="event-input-input">`input`</dfn> event fires whenever the user has modified the data of the control. The <dfn id="203.html_event-input-change" data-anolis-xref="event-input-change">`change`</dfn> event fires when the value is committed, if that makes sense for the control, or else when the control loses focus. In all cases, the `input` event comes before the corresponding `change` event (if any).

When an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element has a defined [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior), the rules for dispatching these events, if they [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply), are given in the section above that defines the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute's state. (This is the case for all [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) controls with the [`type`](#203.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Checkbox](#203.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) state, the [Radio Button](#203.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state, or the [File Upload](#203.html_file-upload-state-(type=file)) state.)

For [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) elements without a defined [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior), but to which these events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply), and for which the user interface involves both interactive manipulation and an explicit commit action, then when the user changes the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), the user agent must [queue a task](#203.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element, and any time the user commits the change, the user agent must [queue a task](#203.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `change` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element.

An example of a user interface involving both interactive manipulation and a commit action would be a [Range](#203.html_range-state-(type=range)) controls that use a slider, when manipulated using a pointing device. While the user is dragging the control's knob, `input` events would fire whenever the position changed, whereas the `change` event would only fire when the user let go of the knob, committing to a specific value.

For [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) elements without a defined [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior), but to which these events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply), and for which the user interface involves an explicit commit action but no intermediate manipulation, then any time the user commits a change to the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value), the user agent must [queue a task](#203.html_queue-a-task) to first [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element, and then [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `change` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element.

An example of a user interface with a commit action would be a [Color](#203.html_color-state-(type=color)) control that consists of a single button that brings up a color wheel: if the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) only changes when the dialog is closed, then that would be the explicit commit action. On the other hand, if the control can be focused and manipulating the control changes the color interactively, then there might be no commit action.

Another example of a user interface with a commit action would be a [Date](#203.html_date-state-(type=date)) control that allows both text-based user input and user selection from a drop-down calendar: while text input might not have an explicit commit step, selecting a date from the drop down calendar and then dismissing the drop down would be a commit action.

For [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) elements without a defined [activation behavior](#203.html_activation-behavior), but to which these events [apply](#203.html_concept-input-apply), any time the user causes the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) to change without an explicit commit action, the user agent must [queue a task](#203.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element. The corresponding `change` event, if any, will be fired when the control [loses focus](#203.html_unfocusing-steps).

Examples of a user changing the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) would include the user typing into a text field, pasting a new value into the field, or undoing an edit in that field. Some user interactions do not cause changes to the value, e.g. hitting the "delete" key in an empty text field, or replacing some text in the field with text from the clipboard that happens to be exactly the same text.

A [Range](#203.html_range-state-(type=range)) control in the form of a slider that the user has focused and is interacting with using a keyboard would be another example of the user changing the element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) without a commit step.

In the case of [tasks](#203.html_concept-task) that just fire an `input` event, user agents may wait for a suitable break in the user's interaction before [queuing](#203.html_queue-a-task) the tasks; for example, a user agent could wait for the user to have not hit a key for 100ms, so as to only fire the event when the user pauses, instead of continuously for each keystroke.

When the user agent is to change an [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element's [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) on behalf of the user (e.g. as part of a form prefilling feature), the user agent must [queue a task](#203.html_queue-a-task) to first update the [value](#203.html_concept-fe-value) accordingly, then [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element, then [fire a simple event](#203.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `change` at the [`input`](#203.html_the-input-element) element.

These events are not fired in response to changes made to the values of form controls by scripts. (This is to make it easier to update the values of form controls in response to the user manipulating the controls, without having to then filter out the script's own changes to avoid an infinite loop.)

The [task source](#203.html_task-source) for these [tasks](#203.html_concept-task) is the [user interaction task source](#203.html_user-interaction-task-source).

#### 4.10.6 The <dfn>`button`</dfn> element

[Categories](#204.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#204.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#204.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Interactive content](#204.html_interactive-content-0).

[Listed](#204.html_category-listed), [labelable](#204.html_category-label), [submittable](#204.html_category-submit), and [reassociateable](#204.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#204.html_form-associated-element).

[Palpable content](#204.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#204.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#204.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#204.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#204.html_phrasing-content-1), but there must be no [interactive content](#204.html_interactive-content-0) descendant.

[Content attributes](#204.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#204.html_global-attributes)

[`autofocus`](#204.html_attr-fe-autofocus) - Automatically focus the form control when the page is loaded

[`disabled`](#204.html_attr-fe-disabled) - Whether the form control is disabled

[`form`](#204.html_attr-fae-form) - Associates the control with a [`form`](#204.html_the-form-element) element

[`formaction`](#204.html_attr-fs-formaction) - URL to use for [form submission](#204.html_form-submission-0)

[`formenctype`](#204.html_attr-fs-formenctype) - Form data set encoding type to use for [form submission](#204.html_form-submission-0)

[`formmethod`](#204.html_attr-fs-formmethod) - HTTP method to use for [form submission](#204.html_form-submission-0)

[`formnovalidate`](#204.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate) - Bypass form control validation for [form submission](#204.html_form-submission-0)

[`formtarget`](#204.html_attr-fs-formtarget) - [Browsing context](#204.html_browsing-context) for [form submission](#204.html_form-submission-0)

`menu` - Specifies the element's designated pop-up menu

[`name`](#204.html_attr-fe-name) - Name of form control to use for [form submission](#204.html_form-submission-0) and in the [`form.elements`](#204.html_dom-form-elements) API

[`type`](#204.html_attr-button-type) - Type of button

[`value`](#204.html_attr-button-value) - Value to be used for [form submission](#204.html_form-submission-0)

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#204.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`button`](#204.html_index-aria-button) (default - [*do not set*](#204.html_aria-usage-note)), [`link`](#204.html_index-aria-link), [`menuitem`](#204.html_index-aria-menuitem), [`menuitemcheckbox`](#204.html_index-aria-menuitemcheckbox), [`menuitemradio`](#204.html_index-aria-menuitemradio) or [`radio`](#204.html_index-aria-radio).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#204.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#204.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#204.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#204.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLButtonElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute boolean autofocus;
           attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
           attribute DOMString formAction;
           attribute DOMString formEnctype;
           attribute DOMString formMethod;
           attribute boolean formNoValidate;
           attribute DOMString formTarget;
           attribute DOMString name;
           attribute DOMString type;
           attribute DOMString value;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  void setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`button`](#204.html_the-button-element) element [represents](#204.html_represents) a button labeled by its contents.

The element is a [button](#204.html_concept-button).

The <dfn id="204.html_attr-button-type" data-anolis-xref="attr-button-type">`type`</dfn> attribute controls the behavior of the button when it is activated. It is an [enumerated attribute](#204.html_enumerated-attribute). The following table lists the keywords and states for the attribute — the keywords in the left column map to the states in the cell in the second column on the same row as the keyword.

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <dfn id="204.html_attr-button-type-submit" data-anolis-xref="attr-button-type-submit">`submit`</dfn> | [Submit Button](#204.html_attr-button-type-submit-state) | Submits the form. |
| <dfn id="204.html_attr-button-type-reset" data-anolis-xref="attr-button-type-reset">`reset`</dfn> | [Reset Button](#204.html_attr-button-type-reset-state) | Resets the form. |
| <dfn id="204.html_attr-button-type-button" data-anolis-xref="attr-button-type-button">`button`</dfn> | [Button](#204.html_attr-button-type-button-state) | Does nothing. |

The *missing value default* is the [Submit Button](#204.html_attr-button-type-submit-state) state.

If the [`type`](#204.html_attr-button-type) attribute is in the [Submit Button](#204.html_attr-button-type-submit-state) state, the element is specifically a [submit button](#204.html_concept-submit-button).

**Constraint validation**: If the [`type`](#204.html_attr-button-type) attribute is in the [Reset Button](#204.html_attr-button-type-reset-state) state, or the [Button](#204.html_attr-button-type-button-state) state, the element is [barred from constraint validation](#204.html_barred-from-constraint-validation).

When a [`button`](#204.html_the-button-element) element is not [disabled](#204.html_concept-fe-disabled), its [activation behavior](#204.html_activation-behavior) element is to run the steps defined in the following list for the current state of the element's [`type`](#204.html_attr-button-type) attribute:

<dfn id="204.html_attr-button-type-submit-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-button-type-submit-state">Submit Button</dfn>

If the element has a [form owner](#204.html_form-owner) and the element's [`Document`](#204.html_document) is [fully active](#204.html_fully-active), the element must [submit](#204.html_concept-form-submit) the [form owner](#204.html_form-owner) from the [`button`](#204.html_the-button-element) element.

<dfn id="204.html_attr-button-type-reset-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-button-type-reset-state">Reset Button</dfn>

If the element has a [form owner](#204.html_form-owner) and the element's [`Document`](#204.html_document) is [fully active](#204.html_fully-active), the element must [reset](#204.html_concept-form-reset) the [form owner](#204.html_form-owner).

<dfn id="204.html_attr-button-type-button-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-button-type-button-state">Button</dfn>

Do nothing.

The [`form`](#204.html_attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`button`](#204.html_the-button-element) element with its [form owner](#204.html_form-owner). The [`name`](#204.html_attr-fe-name) attribute represents the element's name. The [`disabled`](#204.html_attr-fe-disabled) attribute is used to make the control non-interactive and to prevent its value from being submitted. The [`autofocus`](#204.html_attr-fe-autofocus) attribute controls focus. The [`formaction`](#204.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#204.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#204.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#204.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), and [`formtarget`](#204.html_attr-fs-formtarget) attributes are [attributes for form submission](#204.html_attributes-for-form-submission).

The [`formnovalidate`](#204.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate) attribute can be used to make submit buttons that do not trigger the constraint validation.

The [`formaction`](#204.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#204.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#204.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#204.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), and [`formtarget`](#204.html_attr-fs-formtarget) must not be specified if the element's [`type`](#204.html_attr-button-type) attribute is not in the [Submit Button](#204.html_attr-button-type-submit-state) state.

The <dfn id="204.html_attr-button-value" data-anolis-xref="attr-button-value">`value`</dfn> attribute gives the element's value for the purposes of form submission. The element's [value](#204.html_concept-fe-value) is the value of the element's [`value`](#204.html_attr-button-value) attribute, if there is one, or the empty string otherwise.

A button (and its value) is only included in the form submission if the button itself was used to initiate the form submission.

* * *

The <dfn id="204.html_dom-button-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-button-type">`type`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#204.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name, [limited to only known values](#204.html_limited-to-only-known-values).

The [`willValidate`](#204.html_dom-cva-willvalidate), [`validity`](#204.html_dom-cva-validity), and [`validationMessage`](#204.html_dom-cva-validationmessage) IDL attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#204.html_dom-cva-checkvalidity), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#204.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#204.html_the-constraint-validation-api). The [`labels`](#204.html_dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#204.html_the-label-element)s. The [`autofocus`](#204.html_dom-fe-autofocus), [`disabled`](#204.html_dom-fe-disabled), [`form`](#204.html_dom-fae-form), and [`name`](#204.html_dom-fe-name) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

The following button is labeled "Show hint" and pops up a dialog box when activated:

```
<button type=button
        onclick="alert('This 15-20 minute piece was composed by George Gershwin.')">
 Show hint
</button>
```

#### 4.10.7 The <dfn>`select`</dfn> element

[Categories](#205.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#205.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#205.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Interactive content](#205.html_interactive-content-0).

[Listed](#205.html_category-listed), [labelable](#205.html_category-label), [submittable](#205.html_category-submit), [resettable](#205.html_category-reset), and [reassociateable](#205.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#205.html_form-associated-element).

[Palpable content](#205.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#205.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#205.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#205.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Zero or more [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element), [`optgroup`](#205.html_the-optgroup-element), and [script-supporting](#205.html_script-supporting-elements-0) elements.

[Content attributes](#205.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#205.html_global-attributes)

[`autofocus`](#205.html_attr-fe-autofocus) - Automatically focus the form control when the page is loaded

[`disabled`](#205.html_attr-fe-disabled) - Whether the form control is disabled

[`form`](#205.html_attr-fae-form) - Associates the control with a [`form`](#205.html_the-form-element) element

[`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) - Whether to allow multiple values

[`name`](#205.html_attr-fe-name) - Name of form control to use for [form submission](#205.html_form-submission-0) and in the [`form.elements`](#205.html_dom-form-elements) API

[`required`](#205.html_attr-select-required) - Whether the control is required for [form submission](#205.html_form-submission-0)

[`size`](#205.html_attr-select-size) - Size of the control

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#205.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`listbox`](#205.html_index-aria-listbox) (default - [*do not set*](#205.html_aria-usage-note)) or [`menu`](#205.html_index-aria-menu).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#205.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#205.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#205.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#205.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLSelectElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute boolean autofocus;
           attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
           attribute boolean multiple;
           attribute DOMString name;
           attribute boolean required;
           attribute unsigned long size;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;

  readonly attribute HTMLOptionsCollection options;
           attribute unsigned long length;
  getter Element? item(unsigned long index);
  HTMLOptionElement? namedItem(DOMString name);
  void add((HTMLOptionElement or HTMLOptGroupElement) element, optional (HTMLElement or long)? before = null);
  void remove(); // ChildNode overload
  void remove(long index);
  setter creator void (unsigned long index, HTMLOptionElement? option);

  readonly attribute HTMLCollection selectedOptions;
           attribute long selectedIndex;
           attribute DOMString value;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  void setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element represents a control for selecting amongst a set of options.

The <dfn id="205.html_attr-select-multiple" data-anolis-xref="attr-select-multiple">`multiple`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#205.html_boolean-attribute). If the attribute is present, then the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element [represents](#205.html_represents) a control for selecting zero or more options from the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list). If the attribute is absent, then the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element [represents](#205.html_represents) a control for selecting a single option from the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list).

The <dfn id="205.html_attr-select-size" data-anolis-xref="attr-select-size">`size`</dfn> attribute gives the number of options to show to the user. The [`size`](#205.html_attr-select-size) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid non-negative integer](#205.html_valid-non-negative-integer) greater than zero.

The <dfn id="205.html_concept-select-size" data-anolis-xref="concept-select-size">display size</dfn> of a [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element is the result of applying the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#205.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) to the value of element's [`size`](#205.html_attr-select-size) attribute, if it has one and parsing it is successful. If applying those rules to the attribute's value is not successful, or if the [`size`](#205.html_attr-select-size) attribute is absent, then the element's [display size](#205.html_concept-select-size) is 4 if the element's [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) content attribute is present, and 1 otherwise.

The <dfn id="205.html_concept-select-option-list" data-anolis-xref="concept-select-option-list">list of options</dfn> for a [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element consists of all the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element children of the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element, and all the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element children of all the [`optgroup`](#205.html_the-optgroup-element) element children of the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element, in [tree order](#205.html_tree-order).

The <dfn id="205.html_attr-select-required" data-anolis-xref="attr-select-required">`required`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#205.html_boolean-attribute). When specified, the user will be required to select a value before submitting the form.

If a [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element has a [`required`](#205.html_attr-select-required) attribute specified, does not have a [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute specified, and has a [display size](#205.html_concept-select-size) of 1; and if the [value](#205.html_concept-option-value) of the first [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element in the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element's [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) (if any) is the empty string, and that [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element's parent node is the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element (and not an [`optgroup`](#205.html_the-optgroup-element) element), then that [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) is the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element's <dfn id="205.html_placeholder-label-option">placeholder label option</dfn>.

If a [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element has a [`required`](#205.html_attr-select-required) attribute specified, does not have a [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute specified, and has a [display size](#205.html_concept-select-size) of 1, then the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element must have a [placeholder label option](#205.html_placeholder-label-option).

**Constraint validation**: If the element has its [`required`](#205.html_attr-select-required) attribute specified, and either none of the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) elements in the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element's [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) have their [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true, or the only [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element in the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element's [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) with its [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true is the [placeholder label option](#205.html_placeholder-label-option), then the element is [suffering from being missing](#205.html_suffering-from-being-missing).

If the [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute is absent, and the element is not [disabled](#205.html_concept-fe-disabled), then the user agent should allow the user to pick an [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element in its [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) that is itself not [disabled](#205.html_concept-option-disabled). Upon this [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element being <dfn id="205.html_concept-select-pick" data-anolis-xref="concept-select-pick">picked</dfn> (either through a click, or through unfocusing the element after changing its value, or through any other mechanism), and before the relevant user interaction event is queued (e.g. before the [`click`](#205.html_event-click) event), the user agent must set the [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) of the picked [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element to true, set its [dirtiness](#205.html_concept-option-dirtiness) to true, and then [send `select` update notifications](#205.html_send-select-update-notifications).

If the [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute is absent, whenever an [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element in the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element's [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) has its [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true, and whenever an [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element with its [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true is added to the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element's [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list), the user agent must set the [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) of all the other [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) elements in its [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) to false.

If the [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute is absent and the element's [display size](#205.html_concept-select-size) is greater than 1, then the user agent should also allow the user to request that the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) whose [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) is true, if any, be unselected. Upon this request being conveyed to the user agent, and before the relevant user interaction event is queued (e.g. before the [`click`](#205.html_event-click) event), the user agent must set the [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) of that [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element to false, set its [dirtiness](#205.html_concept-option-dirtiness) to true, and then [send `select` update notifications](#205.html_send-select-update-notifications).

If [nodes are inserted](#205.html_nodes-are-inserted) or [nodes are removed](#205.html_nodes-are-removed) causing the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) to gain or lose one or more [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) elements, or if an [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element in the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) <dfn id="205.html_ask-for-a-reset" data-anolis-xref="ask for a reset">asks for a reset</dfn>, then, if the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element's [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute is absent, the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element's [display size](#205.html_concept-select-size) is 1, and no [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) elements in the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element's [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) have their [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true, the user agent must set the [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) of the first [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element in the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) in [tree order](#205.html_tree-order) that is not [disabled](#205.html_concept-option-disabled), if any, to true.
