If the [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute is present, and the element is not [disabled](#205.html_concept-fe-disabled), then the user agent should allow the user to <dfn id="205.html_concept-select-toggle" data-anolis-xref="concept-select-toggle">toggle</dfn> the [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) of the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) elements in its [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) that are themselves not [disabled](#205.html_concept-option-disabled). Upon such an element being [toggled](#205.html_concept-select-toggle) (either through a click, or any other mechanism), and before the relevant user interaction event is queued (e.g. before a related [`click`](#205.html_event-click) event), the [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) of the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element must be changed (from true to false or false to true), the [dirtiness](#205.html_concept-option-dirtiness) of the element must be set to true, and the user agent must [send `select` update notifications](#205.html_send-select-update-notifications).

When the user agent is to <dfn id="205.html_send-select-update-notifications">send `select` update notifications</dfn>, [queue a task](#205.html_queue-a-task) to first [fire a simple event](#205.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element, and then [fire a simple event](#205.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `change` at the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element, using the [user interaction task source](#205.html_user-interaction-task-source) as the task source.

The [reset algorithm](#205.html_concept-form-reset-control) for [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) elements is to go through all the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) elements in the element's [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list), set their [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) to true if the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element has a [`selected`](#205.html_attr-option-selected) attribute, and false otherwise, set their [dirtiness](#205.html_concept-option-dirtiness) to false, and then have the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) elements [ask for a reset](#205.html_ask-for-a-reset).

The [`form`](#205.html_attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element with its [form owner](#205.html_form-owner). The [`name`](#205.html_attr-fe-name) attribute represents the element's name. The [`disabled`](#205.html_attr-fe-disabled) attribute is used to make the control non-interactive and to prevent its value from being submitted. The [`autofocus`](#205.html_attr-fe-autofocus) attribute controls focus.

A [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element that is not [disabled](#205.html_concept-fe-disabled) is *[mutable](#205.html_concept-fe-mutable)*.

`select` . [`type`](#205.html_dom-select-type)

Returns "`select-multiple`" if the element has a [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute, and "`select-one`" otherwise.

`select` . [`options`](#205.html_dom-select-options)

Returns an [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#205.html_htmloptionscollection-0) of the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list).

`select` . [`length`](#205.html_dom-select-length) [ = `value` ]

Returns the number of elements in the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list).

When set to a smaller number, truncates the number of [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) elements in the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element).

When set to a greater number, adds new blank [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) elements to the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element).

`element` = `select` . [`item`](#205.html_dom-select-item)(`index`)
`select`[`index`]

Returns the item with index `index` from the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list). The items are sorted in [tree order](#205.html_tree-order).

`element` = `select` . [`namedItem`](#205.html_dom-select-item)(`name`)

Returns the first item with [ID](#205.html_concept-id) or [`name`](#205.html_attr-option-name) `name` from the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list).

Returns null if no element with that [ID](#205.html_concept-id) could be found.

`select` . [`add`](#205.html_dom-select-add)(`element` [, `before` ])

Inserts `element` before the node given by `before`.

The `before` argument can be a number, in which case `element` is inserted before the item with that number, or an element from the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list), in which case `element` is inserted before that element.

If `before` is omitted, null, or a number out of range, then `element` will be added at the end of the list.

This method will throw a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#205.html_hierarchyrequesterror) exception if `element` is an ancestor of the element into which it is to be inserted.

`select` . [`selectedOptions`](#205.html_dom-select-selectedoptions)

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#205.html_htmlcollection) of the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) that are selected.

`select` . [`selectedIndex`](#205.html_dom-select-selectedindex) [ = `value` ]

Returns the index of the first selected item, if any, or ?1 if there is no selected item.

Can be set, to change the selection.

`select` . [`value`](#205.html_dom-select-value) [ = `value` ]

Returns the [value](#205.html_concept-fe-value) of the first selected item, if any, or the empty string if there is no selected item.

Can be set, to change the selection.

The <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-type">`type`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the string "`select-one`" if the [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute is absent, and the string "`select-multiple`" if the [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute is present.

The <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-options" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-options">`options`</dfn> IDL attribute must return an [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#205.html_htmloptionscollection-0) rooted at the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) node, whose filter matches the elements in the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list).

The [`options`](#205.html_dom-select-options) collection is also mirrored on the [`HTMLSelectElement`](#205.html_htmlselectelement) object. The [supported property indices](#205.html_supported-property-indices) at any instant are the indices supported by the object returned by the [`options`](#205.html_dom-select-options) attribute at that instant.

The <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-length" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-length">`length`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the number of nodes [represented](#205.html_represented-by-the-collection) by the [`options`](#205.html_dom-select-options) collection. On setting, it must act like the attribute of the same name on the [`options`](#205.html_dom-select-options) collection.

The <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-item" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-item">`item(``index``)`</dfn> method must return the value returned by [the method of the same name](#205.html_dom-htmlcollection-item) on the [`options`](#205.html_dom-select-options) collection, when invoked with the same argument.

The <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-nameditem" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-namedItem">`namedItem(``name``)`</dfn> method must return the value returned by [the method of the same name](#205.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-nameditem) on the [`options`](#205.html_dom-select-options) collection, when invoked with the same argument.

When the user agent is to <dfn id="205.html_dom-htmlselectelement-setter" data-anolis-xref="dom-HTMLSelectElement-setter">set the value of a new indexed property</dfn> for a given property index `index` to a new value `value`, it must instead [set the value of a new indexed property](#205.html_dom-htmloptionscollection-setter) with the given property index `index` to the new value `value` on the [`options`](#205.html_dom-select-options) collection.

Similarly, the <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-add" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-add">`add()`</dfn> method must act like its namesake method on that same [`options`](#205.html_dom-select-options) collection.

The <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-remove" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-remove">`remove()`</dfn> method must act like its namesake method on that same [`options`](#205.html_dom-select-options) collection when it has arguments, and like its namesake method on the [`ChildNode`](#205.html_childnode) interface implemented by the [`HTMLSelectElement`](#205.html_htmlselectelement) ancestor interface [`Element`](#205.html_element) when it has no arguments.

The <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-selectedoptions" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-selectedOptions">`selectedOptions`</dfn> IDL attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#205.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) node, whose filter matches the elements in the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) that have their [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true.

The <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-selectedindex" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-selectedIndex">`selectedIndex`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the [index](#205.html_concept-option-index) of the first [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element in the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) in [tree order](#205.html_tree-order) that has its [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true, if any. If there isn't one, then it must return ?1.

On setting, the [`selectedIndex`](#205.html_dom-select-selectedindex) attribute must set the [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) of all the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) elements in the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) to false, and then the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element in the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) whose [index](#205.html_concept-option-index) is the given new value, if any, must have its [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true and its [dirtiness](#205.html_concept-option-dirtiness) set to true.

This can result in no element having a [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true even in the case of the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element having no [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute and a [display size](#205.html_concept-select-size) of 1.

The <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-value" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-value">`value`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the [value](#205.html_concept-option-value) of the first [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element in the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) in [tree order](#205.html_tree-order) that has its [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true, if any. If there isn't one, then it must return the empty string.

On setting, the [`value`](#205.html_dom-select-value) attribute must set the [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) of all the [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) elements in the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list) to false, and then the first [`option`](#205.html_the-option-element) element in the [list of options](#205.html_concept-select-option-list), in [tree order](#205.html_tree-order), whose [value](#205.html_concept-option-value) is equal to the given new value, if any, must have its [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true and its [dirtiness](#205.html_concept-option-dirtiness) set to true.

This can result in no element having a [selectedness](#205.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true even in the case of the [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element having no [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute and a [display size](#205.html_concept-select-size) of 1.

The <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-multiple" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-multiple">`multiple`</dfn>, <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-required" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-required">`required`</dfn>, and <dfn id="205.html_dom-select-size" data-anolis-xref="dom-select-size">`size`</dfn> IDL attributes must [reflect](#205.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name. The [`size`](#205.html_dom-select-size) IDL attribute has a default value of zero.

For historical reasons, the default value of the [`size`](#205.html_dom-select-size) IDL attribute does not return the actual size used, which, in the absence of the [`size`](#205.html_attr-select-size) content attribute, is either 1 or 4 depending on the presence of the [`multiple`](#205.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute.

The [`willValidate`](#205.html_dom-cva-willvalidate), [`validity`](#205.html_dom-cva-validity), and [`validationMessage`](#205.html_dom-cva-validationmessage) IDL attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#205.html_dom-cva-checkvalidity), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#205.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#205.html_the-constraint-validation-api). The [`labels`](#205.html_dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#205.html_the-label-element)s. The [`autofocus`](#205.html_dom-fe-autofocus), [`disabled`](#205.html_dom-fe-disabled), [`form`](#205.html_dom-fae-form), and [`name`](#205.html_dom-fe-name) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

The following example shows how a [`select`](#205.html_the-select-element) element can be used to offer the user with a set of options from which the user can select a single option. The default option is preselected.

```
<p>
 <label for="unittype">Select unit type:</label>
 <select id="unittype" name="unittype">
  <option value="1"> Miner </option>
  <option value="2"> Puffer </option>
  <option value="3" selected> Snipey </option>
  <option value="4"> Max </option>
  <option value="5"> Firebot </option>
 </select>
</p>
```

When there is no default option, a placeholder can be used instead:

```
<select name="unittype" required>
 <option value=""> Select unit type </option>
 <option value="1"> Miner </option>
 <option value="2"> Puffer </option>
 <option value="3"> Snipey </option>
 <option value="4"> Max </option>
 <option value="5"> Firebot </option>
</select>
```

Here, the user is offered a set of options from which he can select any number. By default, all five options are selected.

```
<p>
 <label for="allowedunits">Select unit types to enable on this map:</label>
 <select id="allowedunits" name="allowedunits" multiple>
  <option value="1" selected> Miner </option>
  <option value="2" selected> Puffer </option>
  <option value="3" selected> Snipey </option>
  <option value="4" selected> Max </option>
  <option value="5" selected> Firebot </option>
 </select>
</p>
```

Sometimes, a user has to select one or more items. This example shows such an interface.

```
<p>Select the songs from that you would like on your Act II Mix Tape:</p>
<select multiple required name="act2">
 <option value="s1">It Sucks to Be Me (Reprise)
 <option value="s2">There is Life Outside Your Apartment
 <option value="s3">The More You Ruv Someone
 <option value="s4">Schadenfreude
 <option value="s5">I Wish I Could Go Back to College
 <option value="s6">The Money Song
 <option value="s7">School for Monsters
 <option value="s8">The Money Song (Reprise)
 <option value="s9">There's a Fine, Fine Line (Reprise)
 <option value="s10">What Do You Do With a B.A. in English? (Reprise)
 <option value="s11">For Now
</select>
```

#### 4.10.8 The <dfn>`datalist`</dfn> element

[Categories](#206.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#206.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#206.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#206.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#206.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#206.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Either: [phrasing content](#206.html_phrasing-content-1) (with zero or more [`option`](#206.html_the-option-element) elements descendants).

Or: Zero or more [`option`](#206.html_the-option-element) elements.

[Content attributes](#206.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#206.html_global-attributes)

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#206.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`listbox`](#206.html_index-aria-listbox) (default - [*do not set*](#206.html_aria-usage-note)).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#206.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#206.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#206.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#206.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLDataListElement : HTMLElement {
  readonly attribute HTMLCollection options;
};
```

The [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element) element represents a set of [`option`](#206.html_the-option-element) elements that represent predefined options for other controls. In the rendering, the [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element) element [represents](#206.html_represents) nothing and it, along with its children, should be hidden.

The [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element) element can be used in two ways. In the simplest case, the [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element) element has just [`option`](#206.html_the-option-element) element children.

```
<label>
 Sex:
 <input name=sex list=sexes>
 <datalist id=sexes>
  <option value="Female">
  <option value="Male">
 </datalist>
</label>
```

In the more elaborate case, the [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element) element can be given contents that are to be displayed for down-level clients that don't support [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element). In this case, the [`option`](#206.html_the-option-element) elements are provided inside a [`select`](#206.html_the-select-element) element inside the [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element) element.

```
<label>
 Sex:
 <input name=sex list=sexes>
</label>
<datalist id=sexes>
 <label>
  or select from the list:
  <select name=sex>
   <option value="">
   <option>Female
   <option>Male
  </select>
 </label>
</datalist>
```

The [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element) element is hooked up to an [`input`](#206.html_the-input-element) element using the [`list`](#206.html_attr-input-list) attribute on the [`input`](#206.html_the-input-element) element.

Each [`option`](#206.html_the-option-element) element that is a descendant of the [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element) element, that is not [disabled](#206.html_concept-option-disabled), and whose [value](#206.html_concept-option-value) is a string that isn't the empty string, represents a suggestion. Each suggestion has a [value](#206.html_concept-option-value) and a [label](#206.html_concept-option-label).

`datalist` . [`options`](#206.html_dom-datalist-options)

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](#206.html_htmlcollection) of the `options` elements of the [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element) element.

The <dfn id="206.html_dom-datalist-options" data-anolis-xref="dom-datalist-options">`options`</dfn> IDL attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#206.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element) node, whose filter matches [`option`](#206.html_the-option-element) elements.

**Constraint validation**: If an element has a [`datalist`](#206.html_the-datalist-element) element ancestor, it is [barred from constraint validation](#206.html_barred-from-constraint-validation).

#### 4.10.9 The <dfn>`optgroup`</dfn> element

[Categories](#207.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#207.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As a child of a [`select`](#207.html_the-select-element) element.

[Content model](#207.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Zero or more [`option`](#207.html_the-option-element) and [script-supporting](#207.html_script-supporting-elements-0) elements.

[Content attributes](#207.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#207.html_global-attributes)

[`disabled`](#207.html_attr-optgroup-disabled) - Whether the form control is disabled

[`label`](#207.html_attr-optgroup-label) - User-visible label

Tag omission in text/html:

An [`optgroup`](#207.html_the-optgroup-element) element's [end tag](#207.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`optgroup`](#207.html_the-optgroup-element) element is immediately followed by another [`optgroup`](#207.html_the-optgroup-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#207.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#207.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#207.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#207.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLOptGroupElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute boolean disabled;
           attribute DOMString label;
};
```

The [`optgroup`](#207.html_the-optgroup-element) element [represents](#207.html_represents) a group of [`option`](#207.html_the-option-element) elements with a common label.

The element's group of [`option`](#207.html_the-option-element) elements consists of the [`option`](#207.html_the-option-element) elements that are children of the [`optgroup`](#207.html_the-optgroup-element) element.

When showing [`option`](#207.html_the-option-element) elements in [`select`](#207.html_the-select-element) elements, user agents should show the [`option`](#207.html_the-option-element) elements of such groups as being related to each other and separate from other [`option`](#207.html_the-option-element) elements.

The <dfn id="207.html_attr-optgroup-disabled" data-anolis-xref="attr-optgroup-disabled">`disabled`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#207.html_boolean-attribute) and can be used to [disable](#207.html_concept-option-disabled) a group of [`option`](#207.html_the-option-element) elements together.

The <dfn id="207.html_attr-optgroup-label" data-anolis-xref="attr-optgroup-label">`label`</dfn> attribute must be specified. Its value gives the name of the group, for the purposes of the user interface. User agents should use this attribute's value when labeling the group of [`option`](#207.html_the-option-element) elements in a [`select`](#207.html_the-select-element) element.

The <dfn id="207.html_dom-optgroup-disabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-optgroup-disabled">`disabled`</dfn> and <dfn id="207.html_dom-optgroup-label" data-anolis-xref="dom-optgroup-label">`label`</dfn> attributes must [reflect](#207.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

The following snippet shows how a set of lessons from three courses could be offered in a [`select`](#207.html_the-select-element) drop-down widget:

```
<form action="courseselector.dll" method="get">
 <p>Which course would you like to watch today?
 <p><label>Course:
  <select name="c">
   <optgroup label="8.01 Physics I: Classical Mechanics">
    <option value="8.01.1">Lecture 01: Powers of Ten
    <option value="8.01.2">Lecture 02: 1D Kinematics
    <option value="8.01.3">Lecture 03: Vectors
   <optgroup label="8.02 Electricity and Magnestism">
    <option value="8.02.1">Lecture 01: What holds our world together?
    <option value="8.02.2">Lecture 02: Electric Field
    <option value="8.02.3">Lecture 03: Electric Flux
   <optgroup label="8.03 Physics III: Vibrations and Waves">
    <option value="8.03.1">Lecture 01: Periodic Phenomenon
    <option value="8.03.2">Lecture 02: Beats
    <option value="8.03.3">Lecture 03: Forced Oscillations with Damping
  </select>
 </label>
 <p><input type=submit value="? Play">
</form>
```

#### 4.10.10 The <dfn>`option`</dfn> element

[Categories](#208.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#208.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As a child of a [`select`](#208.html_the-select-element) element.

As a child of a [`datalist`](#208.html_the-datalist-element) element.

As a child of an [`optgroup`](#208.html_the-optgroup-element) element.

[Content model](#208.html_element-dfn-content-model):

If the element has a [`label`](#208.html_attr-option-label) attribute and a [`value`](#208.html_attr-option-value) attribute: Empty.

If the element has a [`label`](#208.html_attr-option-label) attribute but no [`value`](#208.html_attr-option-value) attribute: [Text](#208.html_text-content).

If the element has no [`label`](#208.html_attr-option-label) attribute: [Text](#208.html_text-content) that is not [inter-element whitespace](#208.html_inter-element-whitespace).

[Content attributes](#208.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#208.html_global-attributes)

[`disabled`](#208.html_attr-option-disabled) - Whether the form control is disabled

[`label`](#208.html_attr-option-label) - User-visible label

[`selected`](#208.html_attr-option-selected) - Whether the option is selected by default

[`value`](#208.html_attr-option-value) - Value to be used for [form submission](#208.html_form-submission-0)

Tag omission in text/html:

An [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element's [end tag](#208.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element is immediately followed by another [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element, or if it is immediately followed by an [`optgroup`](#208.html_the-optgroup-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#208.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`option`](#208.html_index-aria-option) (default - [*do not set*](#208.html_aria-usage-note)), [`menuitem`](#208.html_index-aria-menuitem), [`menuitemradio`](#208.html_index-aria-menuitemradio) or [`separator`](#208.html_index-aria-separator).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#208.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#208.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#208.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#208.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
[NamedConstructor=Option(optional DOMString text = "", optional DOMString value, optional boolean defaultSelected = false, optional boolean selected = false)]
interface HTMLOptionElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
           attribute DOMString label;
           attribute boolean defaultSelected;
           attribute boolean selected;
           attribute DOMString value;

           attribute DOMString text;
  readonly attribute long index;
};
```

The [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element [represents](#208.html_represents) an option in a [`select`](#208.html_the-select-element) element or as part of a list of suggestions in a [`datalist`](#208.html_the-datalist-element) element.

In certain circumstances described in the definition of the [`select`](#208.html_the-select-element) element, an [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element can be a [`select`](#208.html_the-select-element) element's [placeholder label option](#208.html_placeholder-label-option). A [placeholder label option](#208.html_placeholder-label-option) does not represent an actual option, but instead represents a label for the [`select`](#208.html_the-select-element) control.

The <dfn id="208.html_attr-option-disabled" data-anolis-xref="attr-option-disabled">`disabled`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#208.html_boolean-attribute). An [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element is <dfn id="208.html_concept-option-disabled" data-anolis-xref="concept-option-disabled">disabled</dfn> if its [`disabled`](#208.html_attr-option-disabled) attribute is present or if it is a child of an [`optgroup`](#208.html_the-optgroup-element) element whose [`disabled`](#208.html_attr-optgroup-disabled) attribute is present.

An [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element that is [disabled](#208.html_attr-option-disabled) must prevent any [`click`](#208.html_event-click) events that are [queued](#208.html_queue-a-task) on the [user interaction task source](#208.html_user-interaction-task-source) from being dispatched on the element.

The <dfn id="208.html_attr-option-label" data-anolis-xref="attr-option-label">`label`</dfn> attribute provides a label for element. The <dfn id="208.html_concept-option-label" data-anolis-xref="concept-option-label">label</dfn> of an [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element is the value of the [`label`](#208.html_attr-option-label) content attribute, if there is one, or, if there is not, the value of the element's [`text`](#208.html_dom-option-text) IDL attribute.

The [`label`](#208.html_attr-option-label) content attribute, if specified, must not be empty.

The <dfn id="208.html_attr-option-value" data-anolis-xref="attr-option-value">`value`</dfn> attribute provides a value for element. The <dfn id="208.html_concept-option-value" data-anolis-xref="concept-option-value">value</dfn> of an [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element is the value of the [`value`](#208.html_attr-option-value) content attribute, if there is one, or, if there is not, the value of the element's [`text`](#208.html_dom-option-text) IDL attribute.

The <dfn id="208.html_attr-option-selected" data-anolis-xref="attr-option-selected">`selected`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#208.html_boolean-attribute). It represents the default [selectedness](#208.html_concept-option-selectedness) of the element.

The <dfn id="208.html_concept-option-dirtiness" data-anolis-xref="concept-option-dirtiness">dirtiness</dfn> of an [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element is a boolean state, initially false. It controls whether adding or removing the [`selected`](#208.html_attr-option-selected) content attribute has any effect.

The <dfn id="208.html_concept-option-selectedness" data-anolis-xref="concept-option-selectedness">selectedness</dfn> of an [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element is a boolean state, initially false. Except where otherwise specified, when the element is created, its [selectedness](#208.html_concept-option-selectedness) must be set to true if the element has a [`selected`](#208.html_attr-option-selected) attribute. Whenever an [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element's [`selected`](#208.html_attr-option-selected) attribute is added, if its [dirtiness](#208.html_concept-option-dirtiness) is false, its [selectedness](#208.html_concept-option-selectedness) must be set to true. Whenever an [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element's [`selected`](#208.html_attr-option-selected) attribute is *removed*, if its [dirtiness](#208.html_concept-option-dirtiness) is false, its [selectedness](#208.html_concept-option-selectedness) must be set to false.

The [`Option()`](#208.html_dom-option) constructor, when called with three or fewer arguments, overrides the initial state of the [selectedness](#208.html_concept-option-selectedness) state to always be false even if the third argument is true (implying that a [`selected`](#208.html_attr-option-selected) attribute is to be set). The fourth argument can be used to explicitly set the initial [selectedness](#208.html_concept-option-selectedness) state when using the constructor.

A [`select`](#208.html_the-select-element) element whose [`multiple`](#208.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute is not specified must not have more than one descendant [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element with its [`selected`](#208.html_attr-option-selected) attribute set.

An [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element's <dfn id="208.html_concept-option-index" data-anolis-xref="concept-option-index">index</dfn> is the number of [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) elements that are in the same [list of options](#208.html_concept-select-option-list) but that come before it in [tree order](#208.html_tree-order). If the [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element is not in a [list of options](#208.html_concept-select-option-list), then the [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element's [index](#208.html_concept-option-index) is zero.

`option` . [`selected`](#208.html_dom-option-selected)

Returns true if the element is selected, and false otherwise.

Can be set, to override the current state of the element.

`option` . [`index`](#208.html_dom-option-index)

Returns the index of the element in its [`select`](#208.html_the-select-element) element's [`options`](#208.html_dom-select-options) list.

`option` . [`form`](#208.html_dom-option-form)

Returns the element's [`form`](#208.html_the-form-element) element, if any, or null otherwise.

`option` . [`text`](#208.html_dom-option-text)

Same as [`textContent`](#208.html_textcontent), except that spaces are collapsed and [`script`](#208.html_the-script-element) elements are skipped.

`option` = new [`Option`](#208.html_dom-option)( [ `text` [, `value` [, `defaultSelected` [, `selected` ] ] ] ] )

Returns a new [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element.

The `text` argument sets the contents of the element.

The `value` argument sets the [`value`](#208.html_attr-option-value) attribute.

The `defaultSelected` argument sets the [`selected`](#208.html_attr-option-selected) attribute.

The `selected` argument sets whether or not the element is selected. If it is omitted, even if the `defaultSelected` argument is true, the element is not selected.

The <dfn id="208.html_dom-option-disabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-option-disabled">`disabled`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#208.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name. The <dfn id="208.html_dom-option-defaultselected" data-anolis-xref="dom-option-defaultSelected">`defaultSelected`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#208.html_reflect) the [`selected`](#208.html_attr-option-selected) content attribute.

The <dfn id="208.html_dom-option-label" data-anolis-xref="dom-option-label">`label`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the element's [label](#208.html_concept-option-label). On setting, the element's [`label`](#208.html_attr-option-label) content attribute must be set to the new value.

The <dfn id="208.html_dom-option-value" data-anolis-xref="dom-option-value">`value`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the element's [value](#208.html_concept-option-value). On setting, the element's [`value`](#208.html_attr-option-value) content attribute must be set to the new value.

The <dfn id="208.html_dom-option-selected" data-anolis-xref="dom-option-selected">`selected`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return true if the element's [selectedness](#208.html_concept-option-selectedness) is true, and false otherwise. On setting, it must set the element's [selectedness](#208.html_concept-option-selectedness) to the new value, set its [dirtiness](#208.html_concept-option-dirtiness) to true, and then cause the element to [ask for a reset](#208.html_ask-for-a-reset).

The <dfn id="208.html_dom-option-index" data-anolis-xref="dom-option-index">`index`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the element's [index](#208.html_concept-option-index).

The <dfn id="208.html_dom-option-text" data-anolis-xref="dom-option-text">`text`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the result of [stripping and collapsing whitespace](#208.html_strip-and-collapse-whitespace) from the concatenation of [data](#208.html_concept-cd-data) of all the [`Text`](#208.html_text-0) node descendants of the [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element, in [tree order](#208.html_tree-order), excluding any that are descendants of descendants of the [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element that are themselves [`script`](#208.html_the-script-element) elements in the [HTML namespace](#208.html_html-namespace-0) or `script` elements in the [SVG namespace](#208.html_svg-namespace).

On setting, the [`text`](#208.html_dom-option-text) attribute must act as if the [`textContent`](#208.html_textcontent) IDL attribute on the element had been set to the new value.

The <dfn id="208.html_dom-option-form" data-anolis-xref="dom-option-form">`form`</dfn> IDL attribute's behavior depends on whether the [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element is in a [`select`](#208.html_the-select-element) element or not. If the [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) has a [`select`](#208.html_the-select-element) element as its parent, or has an [`optgroup`](#208.html_the-optgroup-element) element as its parent and that [`optgroup`](#208.html_the-optgroup-element) element has a [`select`](#208.html_the-select-element) element as its parent, then the [`form`](#208.html_dom-option-form) IDL attribute must return the same value as the [`form`](#208.html_dom-fae-form) IDL attribute on that [`select`](#208.html_the-select-element) element. Otherwise, it must return null.

A constructor is provided for creating [`HTMLOptionElement`](#208.html_htmloptionelement) objects (in addition to the factory methods from DOM such as `createElement()`): <dfn id="208.html_dom-option" data-anolis-xref="dom-option">`Option(``text``,` `value``,` `defaultSelected``,` `selected``)`</dfn>. When invoked as a constructor, it must return a new [`HTMLOptionElement`](#208.html_htmloptionelement) object (a new [`option`](#208.html_the-option-element) element). If the first argument is not the empty string, the new object must have as its only child a [`Text`](#208.html_text-0) node whose data is the value of that argument. Otherwise, it must have no children. If the `value` argument is present, the new object must have a [`value`](#208.html_attr-option-value) attribute set with the value of the argument as its value. If the `defaultSelected` argument is true, the new object must have a [`selected`](#208.html_attr-option-selected) attribute set with no value. If the `selected` argument is true, the new object must have its [selectedness](#208.html_concept-option-selectedness) set to true; otherwise the [selectedness](#208.html_concept-option-selectedness) must be set to false, even if the `defaultSelected` argument is true. The element's document must be the [active document](#208.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#208.html_browsing-context) of the [`Window`](#208.html_window) object on which the interface object of the invoked constructor is found.

#### 4.10.11 The <dfn>`textarea`</dfn> element

[Categories](#209.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#209.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#209.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Interactive content](#209.html_interactive-content-0).

[Listed](#209.html_category-listed), [labelable](#209.html_category-label), [submittable](#209.html_category-submit), [resettable](#209.html_category-reset), and [reassociateable](#209.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#209.html_form-associated-element).

[Palpable content](#209.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#209.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#209.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#209.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Text](#209.html_text-content).

[Content attributes](#209.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#209.html_global-attributes)

[`autocomplete`](#209.html_attr-fe-autocomplete) - - Hint for form autofill feature

[`autofocus`](#209.html_attr-fe-autofocus) - Automatically focus the form control when the page is loaded

[`cols`](#209.html_attr-textarea-cols) - Maximum number of characters per line

[`dirname`](#209.html_attr-fe-dirname) - Name of form field to use for sending the element's [directionality](#209.html_the-directionality) in [form submission](#209.html_form-submission-0)

[`disabled`](#209.html_attr-fe-disabled) - Whether the form control is disabled

[`form`](#209.html_attr-fae-form) - Associates the control with a [`form`](#209.html_the-form-element) element

`inputmode` - Hint for selecting an input modality

[`maxlength`](#209.html_attr-textarea-maxlength) - Maximum length of value

[`minlength`](#209.html_attr-textarea-minlength) - Minimum length of value

[`name`](#209.html_attr-fe-name) - Name of form control to use for [form submission](#209.html_form-submission-0) and in the [`form.elements`](#209.html_dom-form-elements) API

[`placeholder`](#209.html_attr-textarea-placeholder) - User-visible label to be placed within the form control

[`readonly`](#209.html_attr-textarea-readonly) - Whether to allow the value to be edited by the user

[`required`](#209.html_attr-textarea-required) - Whether the control is required for [form submission](#209.html_form-submission-0)

[`rows`](#209.html_attr-textarea-rows) - Number of lines to show

[`wrap`](#209.html_attr-textarea-wrap) - How the value of the form control is to be wrapped for [form submission](#209.html_form-submission-0)

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#209.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`textbox`](#209.html_index-aria-textbox) (default - [*do not set*](#209.html_aria-usage-note)).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#209.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#209.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#209.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#209.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTextAreaElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString autocomplete;
           attribute boolean autofocus;
           attribute unsigned long cols;
           attribute DOMString dirName;
           attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
           attribute long maxLength;
           attribute long minLength;
           attribute DOMString name;
           attribute DOMString placeholder;
           attribute boolean readOnly;
           attribute boolean required;
           attribute unsigned long rows;
           attribute DOMString wrap;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;
           attribute DOMString defaultValue;
  [TreatNullAs=EmptyString] attribute DOMString value;
  readonly attribute unsigned long textLength;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  void setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;

  void select();
           attribute unsigned long selectionStart;
           attribute unsigned long selectionEnd;
           attribute DOMString selectionDirection;
  void setRangeText(DOMString replacement);
  void setRangeText(DOMString replacement, unsigned long start, unsigned long end, optional SelectionMode selectionMode = "preserve");
  void setSelectionRange(unsigned long start, unsigned long end, optional DOMString direction);
};
```

The [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element [represents](#209.html_represents) a multiline plain text edit control for the element's <dfn id="209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value" data-anolis-xref="concept-textarea-raw-value">raw value</dfn>. The contents of the control represent the control's default value.

The [raw value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) of a [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) control must be initially the empty string.

This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#209.html_bidireq).

The <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-readonly" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-readonly">`readonly`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#209.html_boolean-attribute) used to control whether the text can be edited by the user or not.

In this example, a text field is marked read-only because it represents a read-only file:

```
Filename: <code>/etc/bash.bashrc</code>
<textarea name="buffer" readonly>
# System-wide .bashrc file for interactive bash(1) shells.

# To enable the settings / commands in this file for login shells as well,
# this file has to be sourced in /etc/profile.

# If not running interactively, don't do anything
[ -z "$PS1" ] &amp;&amp; return

...</textarea>
```

**Constraint validation**: If the [`readonly`](#209.html_attr-textarea-readonly) attribute is specified on a [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element, the element is [barred from constraint validation](#209.html_barred-from-constraint-validation).

A [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element is [mutable](#209.html_concept-fe-mutable) if it is neither [disabled](#209.html_concept-fe-disabled) nor has a [`readonly`](#209.html_attr-textarea-readonly) attribute specified.

When a [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) is [mutable](#209.html_concept-fe-mutable), its [raw value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) should be editable by the user: the user agent should allow the user to edit, insert, and remove text, and to insert and remove line breaks in the form of "LF" (U+000A) characters. Any time the user causes the element's [raw value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) to change, the user agent must [queue a task](#209.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#209.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element. User agents may wait for a suitable break in the user's interaction before queuing the task; for example, a user agent could wait for the user to have not hit a key for 100ms, so as to only fire the event when the user pauses, instead of continuously for each keystroke.

A [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element has a <dfn id="209.html_concept-textarea-dirty" data-anolis-xref="concept-textarea-dirty">dirty value flag</dfn>, which must be initially set to false, and must be set to true whenever the user interacts with the control in a way that changes the [raw value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value).

When the [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element's [`textContent`](#209.html_textcontent) IDL attribute changes value, if the element's [dirty value flag](#209.html_concept-textarea-dirty) is false, then the element's [raw value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) must be set to the value of the element's [`textContent`](#209.html_textcontent) IDL attribute.

The [reset algorithm](#209.html_concept-form-reset-control) for [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) elements is to set the element's [value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) to the value of the element's [`textContent`](#209.html_textcontent) IDL attribute.

If the element is [mutable](#209.html_concept-fe-mutable), the user agent should allow the user to change the writing direction of the element, setting it either to a left-to-right writing direction or a right-to-left writing direction. If the user does so, the user agent must then run the following steps:

1.  Set the element's [`dir`](#209.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute to "[`ltr`](#209.html_attr-dir-ltr)" if the user selected a left-to-right writing direction, and "[`rtl`](#209.html_attr-dir-rtl)" if the user selected a right-to-left writing direction.

2.  [Queue a task](#209.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#209.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `input` at the [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element.

The <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-cols" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-cols">`cols`</dfn> attribute specifies the expected maximum number of characters per line. If the [`cols`](#209.html_attr-textarea-cols) attribute is specified, its value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#209.html_valid-non-negative-integer) greater than zero. If applying the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#209.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) to the attribute's value results in a number greater than zero, then the element's <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-cols-value" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-cols-value">character width</dfn> is that value; otherwise, it is 20.

The user agent may use the [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element's [character width](#209.html_attr-textarea-cols-value) as a hint to the user as to how many characters the server prefers per line (e.g. for visual user agents by making the width of the control be that many characters). In visual renderings, the user agent should wrap the user's input in the rendering so that each line is no wider than this number of characters.

The <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-rows" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-rows">`rows`</dfn> attribute specifies the number of lines to show. If the [`rows`](#209.html_attr-textarea-rows) attribute is specified, its value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#209.html_valid-non-negative-integer) greater than zero. If applying the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#209.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) to the attribute's value results in a number greater than zero, then the element's <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-rows-value" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-rows-value">character height</dfn> is that value; otherwise, it is 2.

Visual user agents should set the height of the control to the number of lines given by [character height](#209.html_attr-textarea-rows-value).

The <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-wrap" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-wrap">`wrap`</dfn> attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#209.html_enumerated-attribute) with two keywords and states: the <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-wrap-soft" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-wrap-soft">`soft`</dfn> keyword which maps to the [Soft](#209.html_attr-textarea-wrap-soft-state) state, and the <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-wrap-hard" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-wrap-hard">`hard`</dfn> keyword which maps to the [Hard](#209.html_attr-textarea-wrap-hard-state) state. The *missing value default* is the [Soft](#209.html_attr-textarea-wrap-soft-state) state.

The <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-wrap-soft-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-wrap-soft-state">Soft</dfn> state indicates that the text in the [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) is not to be wrapped when it is submitted (though it can still be wrapped in the rendering).

The <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-wrap-hard-state" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-wrap-hard-state">Hard</dfn> state indicates that the text in the [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) is to have newlines added by the user agent so that the text is wrapped when it is submitted.

If the element's [`wrap`](#209.html_attr-textarea-wrap) attribute is in the [Hard](#209.html_attr-textarea-wrap-hard-state) state, the [`cols`](#209.html_attr-textarea-cols) attribute must be specified.

For historical reasons, the element's value is normalised in three different ways for three different purposes. The [raw value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) is the value as it was originally set. It is not normalized. The [API value](#209.html_concept-textarea-api-value) is the value used in the [`value`](#209.html_dom-textarea-value) IDL attribute. It is normalized so that line breaks use "LF" (U+000A) characters. Finally, there is the form submission [value](#209.html_concept-fe-value). It is normalized so that line breaks use U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN "CRLF" (U+000A) character pairs, and in addition, if necessary given the element's [`wrap`](#209.html_attr-textarea-wrap) attribute, additional line breaks are inserted to wrap the text at the given width.

The element's <dfn id="209.html_concept-textarea-api-value" data-anolis-xref="concept-textarea-api-value">API value</dfn> is defined to be the element's [raw value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) with the following transformation applied:

1.  Replace every U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN "CRLF" (U+000A) character pair from the [raw value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) with a single "LF" (U+000A) character.

2.  Replace every remaining U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN character from the [raw value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) with a single "LF" (U+000A) character.

The element's [value](#209.html_concept-fe-value) is defined to be the element's [raw value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) with the following transformation applied:

1.  Replace every occurrence of a "CR" (U+000D) character not followed by a "LF" (U+000A) character, and every occurrence of a "LF" (U+000A) character not preceded by a "CR" (U+000D) character, by a two-character string consisting of a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN "CRLF" (U+000A) character pair.

2.  If the element's [`wrap`](#209.html_attr-textarea-wrap) attribute is in the [Hard](#209.html_attr-textarea-wrap-hard-state) state, insert U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN "CRLF" (U+000A) character pairs into the string using a UA-defined algorithm so that each line has no more than [character width](#209.html_attr-textarea-cols-value) characters. For the purposes of this requirement, lines are delimited by the start of the string, the end of the string, and U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN "CRLF" (U+000A) character pairs.

The <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-maxlength" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-maxlength">`maxlength`</dfn> attribute is a [form control `maxlength` attribute](#209.html_attr-fe-maxlength) controlled by the [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element's [dirty value flag](#209.html_concept-textarea-dirty).

If the [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element has a [maximum allowed value length](#209.html_maximum-allowed-value-length), then the element's children must be such that the [code-unit length](#209.html_code-unit-length) of the value of the element's [`textContent`](#209.html_textcontent) IDL attribute is equal to or less than the element's [maximum allowed value length](#209.html_maximum-allowed-value-length).

The <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-minlength" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-minlength">`minlength`</dfn> attribute is a [form control `minlength` attribute](#209.html_attr-fe-minlength) controlled by the [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element's [dirty value flag](#209.html_concept-textarea-dirty).

The <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-required" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-required">`required`</dfn> attribute is a [boolean attribute](#209.html_boolean-attribute). When specified, the user will be required to enter a value before submitting the form.

**Constraint validation**: If the element has its [`required`](#209.html_attr-textarea-required) attribute specified, and the element is [mutable](#209.html_concept-fe-mutable), and the element's [value](#209.html_concept-fe-value) is the empty string, then the element is [suffering from being missing](#209.html_suffering-from-being-missing).

The <dfn id="209.html_attr-textarea-placeholder" data-anolis-xref="attr-textarea-placeholder">`placeholder`</dfn> attribute represents a *short* hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value. A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

The [`placeholder`](#209.html_attr-input-placeholder) attribute should not be used as a replacement for a [`label`](#209.html_the-label-element). For a longer hint or other advisory text, place the text next to the control.

Use of the [`placeholder`](#209.html_attr-input-placeholder) attribute as a replacement for a [`label`](#209.html_the-label-element) can reduce the accessibility and usability of the control for a range of users including older users and users with cognitive, mobility, fine motor skill or vision impairments. While the hint given by the control's [`label`](#209.html_the-label-element) is shown at all times, the short hint given in the [`placeholder`](#209.html_attr-input-placeholder) attribute is only shown before the user enters a value. Furthermore, [`placeholder`](#209.html_attr-input-placeholder) text may be mistaken for a pre-filled value, and as commonly implemented the default color of the placeholder text provides insufficient contrast and the lack of a separate visible [`label`](#209.html_the-label-element) reduces the size of the hit region available for setting focus on the control.

User agents should present this hint to the user when the element's [value](#209.html_concept-fe-value) is the empty string and the control is not focused (e.g. by displaying it inside a blank unfocused control). All U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED character pairs (CRLF) in the hint, as well as all other "CR" (U+000D) and "LF" (U+000A) characters in the hint, must be treated as line breaks when rendering the hint.

The [`name`](#209.html_attr-fe-name) attribute represents the element's name. The [`dirname`](#209.html_attr-fe-dirname) attribute controls how the element's [directionality](#209.html_the-directionality) is submitted. The [`disabled`](#209.html_attr-fe-disabled) attribute is used to make the control non-interactive and to prevent its value from being submitted. The [`form`](#209.html_attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) element with its [form owner](#209.html_form-owner). The [`autofocus`](#209.html_attr-fe-autofocus) attribute controls focus. The [`autocomplete`](#209.html_attr-fe-autocomplete) attribute controls how the user agent provides autofill behavior.

`textarea` . `type`

Returns the string "`textarea`".

`textarea` . `value`

Returns the current value of the element.

Can be set, to change the value.

The <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-cols" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-cols">`cols`</dfn>, <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-placeholder" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-placeholder">`placeholder`</dfn>, <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-required" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-required">`required`</dfn>, <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-rows" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-rows">`rows`</dfn>, and <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-wrap" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-wrap">`wrap`</dfn> attributes must [reflect](#209.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name. The [`cols`](#209.html_dom-textarea-cols) and [`rows`](#209.html_dom-textarea-rows) attributes are [limited to only non-negative numbers greater than zero](#209.html_limited-to-only-non-negative-numbers-greater-than-zero). The [`cols`](#209.html_dom-textarea-cols) attribute's default value is 20\. The [`rows`](#209.html_dom-textarea-rows) attribute's default value is 2\. The <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-dirname" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-dirName">`dirName`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#209.html_reflect) the [`dirname`](#209.html_attr-fe-dirname) content attribute. The <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-maxlength" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-maxLength">`maxLength`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#209.html_reflect) the [`maxlength`](#209.html_attr-textarea-maxlength) content attribute, [limited to only non-negative numbers](#209.html_limited-to-only-non-negative-numbers). The <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-minlength" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-minLength">`minLength`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#209.html_reflect) the [`minlength`](#209.html_attr-textarea-minlength) content attribute, [limited to only non-negative numbers](#209.html_limited-to-only-non-negative-numbers). The <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-readonly" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-readOnly">`readOnly`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#209.html_reflect) the [`readonly`](#209.html_attr-textarea-readonly) content attribute.

The <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-type">`type`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the value "`textarea`".

The <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-defaultvalue" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-defaultValue">`defaultValue`</dfn> IDL attribute must act like the element's [`textContent`](#209.html_textcontent) IDL attribute.

The <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-value" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-value">`value`</dfn> attribute must, on getting, return the element's [API value](#209.html_concept-textarea-api-value); on setting, it must set the element's [raw value](#209.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) to the new value, set the element's [dirty value flag](#209.html_concept-textarea-dirty) to true, and should then move the text entry cursor position to the end of the text field, unselecting any selected text and resetting the selection direction to *none*.

The <dfn id="209.html_dom-textarea-textlength" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea-textLength">`textLength`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the [code-unit length](#209.html_code-unit-length) of the element's [API value](#209.html_concept-textarea-api-value).

The [`willValidate`](#209.html_dom-cva-willvalidate), [`validity`](#209.html_dom-cva-validity), and [`validationMessage`](#209.html_dom-cva-validationmessage) IDL attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#209.html_dom-cva-checkvalidity), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#209.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#209.html_the-constraint-validation-api). The [`labels`](#209.html_dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#209.html_the-label-element)s. The [`select()`](#209.html_dom-textarea/input-select), [`selectionStart`](#209.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart), [`selectionEnd`](#209.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend), [`selectionDirection`](#209.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection), [`setRangeText()`](#209.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#209.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange) methods and IDL attributes expose the element's text selection. The [`autofocus`](#209.html_dom-fe-autofocus), [`disabled`](#209.html_dom-fe-disabled), [`form`](#209.html_dom-fae-form), and [`name`](#209.html_dom-fe-name) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

Here is an example of a [`textarea`](#209.html_the-textarea-element) being used for unrestricted free-form text input in a form:

```
<p>If you have any comments, please let us know: <textarea cols=80 name=comments></textarea></p>
```

To specify a maximum length for the comments, one can use the [`maxlength`](#209.html_attr-textarea-maxlength) attribute:

```
<p>If you have any short comments, please let us know: <textarea cols=80 name=comments maxlength=200></textarea></p>
```

To give a default value, text can be included inside the element:

```
<p>If you have any comments, please let us know: <textarea cols=80 name=comments>You rock!</textarea></p>
```

You can also give a minimum length. Here, a letter needs to be filled out by the user; a template (which is shorter than the minimum length) is provided, but is insufficient to submit the form:

```
<textarea required minlength="500">Dear Madam Speaker,

Regarding your letter dated ...

...

Yours Sincerely,

...</textarea>
```

A placeholder can be given as well, to suggest the basic form to the user, without providing an explicit template:

```
<textarea placeholder="Dear Francine,

They closed the parks this week, so we won't be able to
meet your there. Should we just have dinner?

Love,
Daddy"></textarea>
```

To have the browser submit [the directionality](#209.html_the-directionality) of the element along with the value, the [`dirname`](#209.html_attr-fe-dirname) attribute can be specified:

```
<p>If you have any comments, please let us know (you may use either English or Hebrew for your comments):
<textarea cols=80 name=comments dirname=comments.dir></textarea></p>
```

#### 4.10.12 The <dfn>`keygen`</dfn> element

[Categories](#210.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#210.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#210.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Interactive content](#210.html_interactive-content-0).

[Listed](#210.html_category-listed), [labelable](#210.html_category-label), [submittable](#210.html_category-submit), [resettable](#210.html_category-reset), and [reassociateable](#210.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#210.html_form-associated-element).

[Palpable content](#210.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#210.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#210.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#210.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Empty.

[Content attributes](#210.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#210.html_global-attributes)

[`autofocus`](#210.html_attr-fe-autofocus) - Automatically focus the form control when the page is loaded

[`challenge`](#210.html_attr-keygen-challenge) - String to package with the generated and signed public key

[`disabled`](#210.html_attr-fe-disabled) - Whether the form control is disabled

[`form`](#210.html_attr-fae-form) - Associates the control with a [`form`](#210.html_the-form-element) element

[`keytype`](#210.html_attr-keygen-keytype) - The type of cryptographic key to generate

[`name`](#210.html_attr-fe-name) - Name of form control to use for [form submission](#210.html_form-submission-0) and in the [`form.elements`](#210.html_dom-form-elements) API

Tag omission in text/html:

No [end tag](#210.html_syntax-end-tag).

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#210.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#210.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#210.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#210.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLKeygenElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute boolean autofocus;
           attribute DOMString challenge;
           attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
           attribute DOMString keytype;
           attribute DOMString name;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  void setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`keygen`](#210.html_the-keygen-element) element [represents](#210.html_represents) a key pair generator control. When the control's form is submitted, the private key is stored in the local keystore, and the public key is packaged and sent to the server.

The <dfn id="210.html_attr-keygen-challenge" data-anolis-xref="attr-keygen-challenge">`challenge`</dfn> attribute may be specified. Its value will be packaged with the submitted key.

The <dfn id="210.html_attr-keygen-keytype" data-anolis-xref="attr-keygen-keytype">`keytype`</dfn> attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#210.html_enumerated-attribute). The following table lists the keywords and states for the attribute — the keywords in the left column map to the states listed in the cell in the second column on the same row as the keyword. User agents are not required to support these values, and must only recognize values whose corresponding algorithms they support.

| Keyword | State |
| --- | --- |
| `rsa` | *RSA* |

The *invalid value default* state is the *unknown* state. The *missing value default* state is the *RSA* state, if it is supported, or the *unknown* state otherwise.

This specification does not specify what key types user agents are to support — it is possible for a user agent to not support any key types at all.

The user agent may expose a user interface for each [`keygen`](#210.html_the-keygen-element) element to allow the user to configure settings of the element's key pair generator, e.g. the key length.

The [reset algorithm](#210.html_concept-form-reset-control) for [`keygen`](#210.html_the-keygen-element) elements is to set these various configuration settings back to their defaults.

The element's [value](#210.html_concept-fe-value) is the string returned from the following algorithm:

1.  Use the appropriate step from the following list:

    If the [`keytype`](#210.html_attr-keygen-keytype) attribute is in the *RSA* state

    Generate an RSA key pair using the settings given by the user, if appropriate, using the `md5WithRSAEncryption` RSA signature algorithm (the signature algorithm with MD5 and the RSA encryption algorithm) referenced in section 2.2.1 ("RSA Signature Algorithm") of RFC 3279, and defined in RFC 3447\. [[RFC3279]](#210.html_refsRFC3279) [[RFC3447]](#210.html_refsRFC3447)

    Otherwise, the [`keytype`](#210.html_attr-keygen-keytype) attribute is in the *unknown* state

    The given key type is not supported. Return the empty string and abort this algorithm.

    Let `private key` be the generated private key.

    Let `public key` be the generated public key.

    Let `signature algorithm` be the selected signature algorithm.

2.  If the element has a [`challenge`](#210.html_attr-keygen-challenge) attribute, then let `challenge` be that attribute's value. Otherwise, let `challenge` be the empty string.

3.  Let `algorithm` be an ASN.1 `AlgorithmIdentifier` structure as defined by RFC 5280, with the `algorithm` field giving the ASN.1 OID used to identify `signature algorithm`, using the OIDs defined in section 2.2 ("Signature Algorithms") of RFC 3279, and the `parameters` field set up as required by RFC 3279 for `AlgorithmIdentifier` structures for that algorithm. [[X690]](#210.html_refsX690) [[RFC5280]](#210.html_refsRFC5280) [[RFC3279]](#210.html_refsRFC3279)

4.  Let `spki` be an ASN.1 `SubjectPublicKeyInfo` structure as defined by RFC 5280, with the `algorithm` field set to the `algorithm` structure from the previous step, and the `subjectPublicKey` field set to the BIT STRING value resulting from ASN.1 DER encoding the `public key`. [[X690]](#210.html_refsX690) [[RFC5280]](#210.html_refsRFC5280)

5.  Let `publicKeyAndChallenge` be an ASN.1 [`PublicKeyAndChallenge`](#210.html_publickeyandchallenge) structure as defined below, with the `spki` field set to the `spki` structure from the previous step, and the `challenge` field set to the string `challenge` obtained earlier. [[X690]](#210.html_refsX690)

6.  Let `signature` be the BIT STRING value resulting from ASN.1 DER encoding the signature generated by applying the `signature algorithm` to the byte string obtained by ASN.1 DER encoding the `publicKeyAndChallenge` structure, using `private key` as the signing key. [[X690]](#210.html_refsX690)

7.  Let `signedPublicKeyAndChallenge` be an ASN.1 [`SignedPublicKeyAndChallenge`](#210.html_signedpublickeyandchallenge) structure as defined below, with the `publicKeyAndChallenge` field set to the `publicKeyAndChallenge` structure, the `signatureAlgorithm` field set to the `algorithm` structure, and the `signature` field set to the BIT STRING `signature` from the previous step. [[X690]](#210.html_refsX690)

8.  Return the result of base64 encoding the result of ASN.1 DER encoding the `signedPublicKeyAndChallenge` structure. [[RFC4648]](#210.html_refsRFC4648) [[X690]](#210.html_refsX690)

The data objects used by the above algorithm are defined as follows. These definitions use the same "ASN.1-like" syntax defined by RFC 5280. [[RFC5280]](#210.html_refsRFC5280)

```
[](#cb589-1)PublicKeyAndChallenge ::= SEQUENCE {
[](#cb589-2)    spki SubjectPublicKeyInfo,
[](#cb589-3)    challenge IA5STRING
[](#cb589-4)}
[](#cb589-5)
[](#cb589-6)SignedPublicKeyAndChallenge ::= SEQUENCE {
[](#cb589-7)    publicKeyAndChallenge PublicKeyAndChallenge,
[](#cb589-8)    signatureAlgorithm AlgorithmIdentifier,
[](#cb589-9)    signature BIT STRING
[](#cb589-10)}
```

* * *

**Constraint validation**: The [`keygen`](#210.html_the-keygen-element) element is [barred from constraint validation](#210.html_barred-from-constraint-validation).

The [`form`](#210.html_attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`keygen`](#210.html_the-keygen-element) element with its [form owner](#210.html_form-owner). The [`name`](#210.html_attr-fe-name) attribute represents the element's name. The [`disabled`](#210.html_attr-fe-disabled) attribute is used to make the control non-interactive and to prevent its value from being submitted. The [`autofocus`](#210.html_attr-fe-autofocus) attribute controls focus.

`keygen` . `type`

Returns the string "`keygen`".

The <dfn id="210.html_dom-keygen-challenge" data-anolis-xref="dom-keygen-challenge">`challenge`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#210.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

The <dfn id="210.html_dom-keygen-keytype" data-anolis-xref="dom-keygen-keytype">`keytype`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#210.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name, [limited to only known values](#210.html_limited-to-only-known-values).

The <dfn id="210.html_dom-keygen-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-keygen-type">`type`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the value "`keygen`".

The [`willValidate`](#210.html_dom-cva-willvalidate), [`validity`](#210.html_dom-cva-validity), and [`validationMessage`](#210.html_dom-cva-validationmessage) IDL attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#210.html_dom-cva-checkvalidity), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#210.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#210.html_the-constraint-validation-api). The [`labels`](#210.html_dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#210.html_the-label-element)s. The [`autofocus`](#210.html_dom-fe-autofocus), [`disabled`](#210.html_dom-fe-disabled), [`form`](#210.html_dom-fae-form), and [`name`](#210.html_dom-fe-name) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

This specification does not specify how the private key generated is to be used. It is expected that after receiving the [`SignedPublicKeyAndChallenge`](#210.html_signedpublickeyandchallenge) (SPKAC) structure, the server will generate a client certificate and offer it back to the user for download; this certificate, once downloaded and stored in the key store along with the private key, can then be used to authenticate to services that use TLS and certificate authentication.

To generate a key pair, add the private key to the user's key store, and submit the public key to the server, markup such as the following can be used:

```
<form action="processkey.cgi" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
 <p><keygen name="key"></p>
 <p><input type=submit value="Submit key..."></p>
</form>
```

The server will then receive a form submission with a packaged RSA public key as the value of "`key`". This can then be used for various purposes, such as generating a client certificate, as mentioned above.

#### 4.10.13 The <dfn>`output`</dfn> element

[Categories](#211.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#211.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#211.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Listed](#211.html_category-listed), [labelable](#211.html_category-label), [resettable](#211.html_category-reset), and [reassociateable](#211.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#211.html_form-associated-element).

[Palpable content](#211.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#211.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#211.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#211.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#211.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#211.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#211.html_global-attributes)

[`for`](#211.html_attr-output-for) - Specifies controls from which the output was calculated

[`form`](#211.html_attr-fae-form) - Associates the control with a [`form`](#211.html_the-form-element) element

[`name`](#211.html_attr-fe-name) - Name of form control to use for [form submission](#211.html_form-submission-0) and in the [`form.elements`](#211.html_dom-form-elements) API

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#211.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`status`](#211.html_index-aria-status) (default - [*do not set*](#211.html_aria-usage-note)), [any role value](#211.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[Global aria-* attributes](#211.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#211.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#211.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLOutputElement : HTMLElement {
  [PutForwards=value] readonly attribute DOMSettableTokenList htmlFor;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
           attribute DOMString name;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;
           attribute DOMString defaultValue;
           attribute DOMString value;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  void setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`output`](#211.html_the-output-element) element [represents](#211.html_represents) the result of a calculation or user action.

The <dfn id="211.html_attr-output-for" data-anolis-xref="attr-output-for">`for`</dfn> content attribute allows an explicit relationship to be made between the result of a calculation and the elements that represent the values that went into the calculation or that otherwise influenced the calculation. The [`for`](#211.html_attr-output-for) attribute, if specified, must contain a string consisting of an [unordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#211.html_unordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens) that are [case-sensitive](#211.html_case-sensitive), each of which must have the value of an [ID](#211.html_concept-id) of an element in the same [`Document`](#211.html_document).

The [`form`](#211.html_attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`output`](#211.html_the-output-element) element with its [form owner](#211.html_form-owner). The [`name`](#211.html_attr-fe-name) attribute represents the element's name.

The element has a <dfn id="211.html_concept-output-mode" data-anolis-xref="concept-output-mode">value mode flag</dfn> which is either *value* or *default*. Initially, the [value mode flag](#211.html_concept-output-mode) must be set to *default*.

The element also has a <dfn id="211.html_concept-output-defaultvalue" data-anolis-xref="concept-output-defaultValue">default value</dfn>. Initially, the [default value](#211.html_concept-output-defaultvalue) must be the empty string.

When the [value mode flag](#211.html_concept-output-mode) is in mode *default*, the contents of the element represent both the value of the element and its [default value](#211.html_concept-output-defaultvalue). When the [value mode flag](#211.html_concept-output-mode) is in mode *value*, the contents of the element represent the value of the element only, and the [default value](#211.html_concept-output-defaultvalue) is only accessible using the [`defaultValue`](#211.html_dom-output-defaultvalue) IDL attribute.

Whenever the element's descendants are changed in any way, if the [value mode flag](#211.html_concept-output-mode) is in mode *default*, the element's [default value](#211.html_concept-output-defaultvalue) must be set to the value of the element's [`textContent`](#211.html_textcontent) IDL attribute.

The [reset algorithm](#211.html_concept-form-reset-control) for [`output`](#211.html_the-output-element) elements is to set the element's [value mode flag](#211.html_concept-output-mode) to *default* and then to set the element's [`textContent`](#211.html_textcontent) IDL attribute to the value of the element's [default value](#211.html_concept-output-defaultvalue) (thus replacing the element's child nodes).
