`output` . [`value`](#211.html_dom-output-value) [ = `value` ]

Returns the element's current value.

Can be set, to change the value.

`output` . [`defaultValue`](#211.html_dom-output-defaultvalue) [ = `value` ]

Returns the element's current default value.

Can be set, to change the default value.

`output` . [`type`](#211.html_dom-output-type)

Returns the string "`output`".

The <dfn id="211.html_dom-output-value" data-anolis-xref="dom-output-value">`value`</dfn> IDL attribute must act like the element's [`textContent`](#211.html_textcontent) IDL attribute, except that on setting, in addition, before the child nodes are changed, the element's [value mode flag](#211.html_concept-output-mode) must be set to *value*.

The <dfn id="211.html_dom-output-defaultvalue" data-anolis-xref="dom-output-defaultValue">`defaultValue`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the element's [default value](#211.html_concept-output-defaultvalue). On setting, the attribute must set the element's [default value](#211.html_concept-output-defaultvalue), and, if the element's [value mode flag](#211.html_concept-output-mode) is in the mode *default*, set the element's [`textContent`](#211.html_textcontent) IDL attribute as well.

The <dfn id="211.html_dom-output-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-output-type">`type`</dfn> attribute must return the string "`output`".

The <dfn id="211.html_dom-output-htmlfor" data-anolis-xref="dom-output-htmlFor">`htmlFor`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#211.html_reflect) the [`for`](#211.html_attr-output-for) content attribute.

The [`willValidate`](#211.html_dom-cva-willvalidate), [`validity`](#211.html_dom-cva-validity), and [`validationMessage`](#211.html_dom-cva-validationmessage) IDL attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#211.html_dom-cva-checkvalidity), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#211.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#211.html_the-constraint-validation-api). The [`labels`](#211.html_dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#211.html_the-label-element)s. The [`form`](#211.html_dom-fae-form) and [`name`](#211.html_dom-fe-name) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

A simple calculator could use [`output`](#211.html_the-output-element) for its display of calculated results:

```
<form onsubmit="return false" oninput="o.value = a.valueAsNumber + b.valueAsNumber">
 <input name=a type=number step=any> +
 <input name=b type=number step=any> =
 <output name=o for="a b"></output>
</form>
```

In this example, an [`output`](#211.html_the-output-element) element is used to report the results from a remote server, as they come in:

```
<output id="result"></output>
<script>
 var primeSource = new WebSocket('ws://primes.example.net/');
 primeSource.onmessage = function (event) {
   document.getElementById('result').value = event.data;
 }
</script>
```

#### 4.10.14 The <dfn>`progress`</dfn> element

[Categories](#212.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#212.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#212.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Labelable element](#212.html_category-label).

[Palpable content](#212.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#212.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#212.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#212.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#212.html_phrasing-content-1), but there must be no [`progress`](#212.html_the-progress-element) element descendants.

[Content attributes](#212.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#212.html_global-attributes)

[`value`](#212.html_attr-progress-value) - Current value of the element

[`max`](#212.html_attr-progress-max) - Upper bound of range

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#212.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`progressbar`](#212.html_index-aria-progressbar) (default - [*do not set*](#212.html_aria-usage-note)).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#212.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#212.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#212.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#212.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLProgressElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute double value;
           attribute double max;
  readonly attribute double position;
  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`progress`](#212.html_the-progress-element) element [represents](#212.html_represents) the completion progress of a task. The progress is either indeterminate, indicating that progress is being made but that it is not clear how much more work remains to be done before the task is complete (e.g. because the task is waiting for a remote host to respond), or the progress is a number in the range zero to a maximum, giving the fraction of work that has so far been completed.

There are two attributes that determine the current task completion represented by the element. The <dfn id="212.html_attr-progress-value" data-anolis-xref="attr-progress-value">`value`</dfn> attribute specifies how much of the task has been completed, and the <dfn id="212.html_attr-progress-max" data-anolis-xref="attr-progress-max">`max`</dfn> attribute specifies how much work the task requires in total. The units are arbitrary and not specified.

To make a determinate progress bar, add a [`value`](#212.html_attr-progress-value) attribute with the current progress (either a number from 0.0 to 1.0, or, if the [`max`](#212.html_attr-progress-max) attribute is specified, a number from 0 to the value of the [`max`](#212.html_attr-progress-max) attribute). To make an indeterminate progress bar, remove the [`value`](#212.html_attr-progress-value) attribute.

Authors are encouraged to also include the current value and the maximum value inline as text inside the element, so that the progress is made available to users of legacy user agents.

Here is a snippet of a Web application that shows the progress of some automated task:

```
<section>
 <h2>Task Progress</h2>
 <p>Progress: <progress id="p" max=100><span>0</span>%</progress></p>
 <script>
  var progressBar = document.getElementById('p');
  function updateProgress(newValue) {
    progressBar.value = newValue;
    progressBar.getElementsByTagName('span')[0].textContent = newValue;
  }
 </script>
</section>
```

(The `updateProgress()` method in this example would be called by some other code on the page to update the actual progress bar as the task progressed.)

The [`value`](#212.html_attr-progress-value) and [`max`](#212.html_attr-progress-max) attributes, when present, must have values that are [valid floating-point numbers](#212.html_valid-floating-point-number). The [`value`](#212.html_attr-progress-value) attribute, if present, must have a value equal to or greater than zero, and less than or equal to the value of the [`max`](#212.html_attr-progress-max) attribute, if present, or 1.0, otherwise. The [`max`](#212.html_attr-progress-max) attribute, if present, must have a value greater than zero.

The [`progress`](#212.html_the-progress-element) element is the wrong element to use for something that is just a gauge, as opposed to task progress. For instance, indicating disk space usage using [`progress`](#212.html_the-progress-element) would be inappropriate. Instead, the [`meter`](#212.html_the-meter-element) element is available for such use cases.

**User agent requirements**: If the [`value`](#212.html_attr-progress-value) attribute is omitted, then the progress bar is an indeterminate progress bar. Otherwise, it is a determinate progress bar.

If the progress bar is a determinate progress bar and the element has a [`max`](#212.html_attr-progress-max) attribute, the user agent must parse the [`max`](#212.html_attr-progress-max) attribute's value according to the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#212.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values). If this does not result in an error, and if the parsed value is greater than zero, then the <dfn id="212.html_concept-progress-maximum" data-anolis-xref="concept-progress-maximum">maximum value</dfn> of the progress bar is that value. Otherwise, if the element has no [`max`](#212.html_attr-progress-max) attribute, or if it has one but parsing it resulted in an error, or if the parsed value was less than or equal to zero, then the [maximum value](#212.html_concept-progress-maximum) of the progress bar is 1.0.

If the progress bar is a determinate progress bar, user agents must parse the [`value`](#212.html_attr-progress-value) attribute's value according to the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#212.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values). If this does not result in an error, and if the parsed value is less than the [maximum value](#212.html_concept-progress-maximum) and greater than zero, then the <dfn id="212.html_concept-progress-value" data-anolis-xref="concept-progress-value">current value</dfn> of the progress bar is that parsed value. Otherwise, if the parsed value was greater than or equal to the [maximum value](#212.html_concept-progress-maximum), then the [current value](#212.html_concept-progress-value) of the progress bar is the [maximum value](#212.html_concept-progress-maximum) of the progress bar. Otherwise, if parsing the [`value`](#212.html_attr-progress-value) attribute's value resulted in an error, or a number less than or equal to zero, then the [current value](#212.html_concept-progress-value) of the progress bar is zero.

**UA requirements for showing the progress bar**: When representing a [`progress`](#212.html_the-progress-element) element to the user, the UA should indicate whether it is a determinate or indeterminate progress bar, and in the former case, should indicate the relative position of the [current value](#212.html_concept-progress-value) relative to the [maximum value](#212.html_concept-progress-maximum).

`progress` . [`position`](#212.html_dom-progress-position)

For a determinate progress bar (one with known current and maximum values), returns the result of dividing the current value by the maximum value.

For an indeterminate progress bar, returns ?1.

If the progress bar is an indeterminate progress bar, then the <dfn id="212.html_dom-progress-position" data-anolis-xref="dom-progress-position">`position`</dfn> IDL attribute must return ?1\. Otherwise, it must return the result of dividing the [current value](#212.html_concept-progress-value) by the [maximum value](#212.html_concept-progress-maximum).

If the progress bar is an indeterminate progress bar, then the <dfn id="212.html_dom-progress-value" data-anolis-xref="dom-progress-value">`value`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return 0\. Otherwise, it must return the [current value](#212.html_concept-progress-value). On setting, the given value must be converted to the [best representation of the number as a floating-point number](#212.html_best-representation-of-the-number-as-a-floating-point-number) and then the [`value`](#212.html_dom-progress-value) content attribute must be set to that string.

Setting the [`value`](#212.html_dom-progress-value) IDL attribute to itself when the corresponding content attribute is absent would change the progress bar from an indeterminate progress bar to a determinate progress bar with no progress.

The <dfn id="212.html_dom-progress-max" data-anolis-xref="dom-progress-max">`max`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#212.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name, [limited to numbers greater than zero](#212.html_limited-to-numbers-greater-than-zero). The default value for [`max`](#212.html_dom-progress-max) is 1.0.

The [`labels`](#212.html_dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#212.html_the-label-element)s.

#### 4.10.15 The <dfn>`meter`</dfn> element

[Categories](#213.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#213.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#213.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Labelable element](#213.html_category-label).

[Palpable content](#213.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#213.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [phrasing content](#213.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#213.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#213.html_phrasing-content-1), but there must be no [`meter`](#213.html_the-meter-element) element descendants.

[Content attributes](#213.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#213.html_global-attributes)

[`value`](#213.html_attr-meter-value) - Current value of the element

[`min`](#213.html_attr-meter-min) - Lower bound of range

[`max`](#213.html_attr-meter-max) - Upper bound of range

[`low`](#213.html_attr-meter-low) - High limit of low range

[`high`](#213.html_attr-meter-high) - Low limit of high range

[`optimum`](#213.html_attr-meter-optimum) - Optimum value in gauge

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#213.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#213.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#213.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#213.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLMeterElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute double value;
           attribute double min;
           attribute double max;
           attribute double low;
           attribute double high;
           attribute double optimum;
  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`meter`](#213.html_the-meter-element) element [represents](#213.html_represents) a scalar measurement within a known range, or a fractional value; for example disk usage, the relevance of a query result, or the fraction of a voting population to have selected a particular candidate.

This is also known as a gauge.

The [`meter`](#213.html_the-meter-element) element should not be used to indicate progress (as in a progress bar). For that role, HTML provides a separate [`progress`](#213.html_the-progress-element) element.

The [`meter`](#213.html_the-meter-element) element also does not represent a scalar value of arbitrary range — for example, it would be wrong to use this to report a weight, or height, unless there is a known maximum value.

There are six attributes that determine the semantics of the gauge represented by the element.

The <dfn id="213.html_attr-meter-min" data-anolis-xref="attr-meter-min">`min`</dfn> attribute specifies the lower bound of the range, and the <dfn id="213.html_attr-meter-max" data-anolis-xref="attr-meter-max">`max`</dfn> attribute specifies the upper bound. The <dfn id="213.html_attr-meter-value" data-anolis-xref="attr-meter-value">`value`</dfn> attribute specifies the value to have the gauge indicate as the "measured" value.

The other three attributes can be used to segment the gauge's range into "low", "medium", and "high" parts, and to indicate which part of the gauge is the "optimum" part. The <dfn id="213.html_attr-meter-low" data-anolis-xref="attr-meter-low">`low`</dfn> attribute specifies the range that is considered to be the "low" part, and the <dfn id="213.html_attr-meter-high" data-anolis-xref="attr-meter-high">`high`</dfn> attribute specifies the range that is considered to be the "high" part. The <dfn id="213.html_attr-meter-optimum" data-anolis-xref="attr-meter-optimum">`optimum`</dfn> attribute gives the position that is "optimum"; if that is higher than the "high" value then this indicates that the higher the value, the better; if it's lower than the "low" mark then it indicates that lower values are better, and naturally if it is in between then it indicates that neither high nor low values are good.

**Authoring requirements**: The [`value`](#213.html_attr-meter-value) attribute must be specified. The [`value`](#213.html_attr-meter-value), [`min`](#213.html_attr-meter-min), [`low`](#213.html_attr-meter-low), [`high`](#213.html_attr-meter-high), [`max`](#213.html_attr-meter-max), and [`optimum`](#213.html_attr-meter-optimum) attributes, when present, must have values that are [valid floating-point numbers](#213.html_valid-floating-point-number).

In addition, the attributes' values are further constrained:

Let `value` be the [`value`](#213.html_attr-meter-value) attribute's number.

If the [`min`](#213.html_attr-meter-min) attribute is specified, then let `minimum` be that attribute's value; otherwise, let it be zero.

If the [`max`](#213.html_attr-meter-max) attribute is specified, then let `maximum` be that attribute's value; otherwise, let it be 1.0.

The following inequalities must hold, as applicable:

*   `minimum` ≤ `value` ≤ `maximum`
*   `minimum` ≤ [`low`](#213.html_attr-meter-low) ≤ `maximum` (if [`low`](#213.html_attr-meter-low) is specified)
*   `minimum` ≤ [`high`](#213.html_attr-meter-high) ≤ `maximum` (if [`high`](#213.html_attr-meter-high) is specified)
*   `minimum` ≤ [`optimum`](#213.html_attr-meter-optimum) ≤ `maximum` (if [`optimum`](#213.html_attr-meter-optimum) is specified)
*   [`low`](#213.html_attr-meter-low) ≤ [`high`](#213.html_attr-meter-high) (if both [`low`](#213.html_attr-meter-low) and [`high`](#213.html_attr-meter-high) are specified)

If no minimum or maximum is specified, then the range is assumed to be 0..1, and the value thus has to be within that range.

Authors are encouraged to include a textual representation of the gauge's state in the element's contents, for users of user agents that do not support the [`meter`](#213.html_the-meter-element) element.

The following examples show three gauges that would all be three-quarters full:

```
Storage space usage: <meter value=6 max=8>6 blocks used (out of 8 total)</meter>
Voter turnout: <meter value=0.75><img alt="75%" src="graph75.png"></meter>
Tickets sold: <meter min="0" max="100" value="75"></meter>
```

The following example is incorrect use of the element, because it doesn't give a range (and since the default maximum is 1, both of the gauges would end up looking maxed out):

```
<p>The grapefruit pie had a radius of <meter value=12>12cm</meter>
and a height of <meter value=2>2cm</meter>.</p> <!-- BAD! -->
```

Instead, one would either not include the meter element, or use the meter element with a defined range to give the dimensions in context compared to other pies:

```
<p>The grapefruit pie had a radius of 12cm and a height of
2cm.</p>
<dl>
 <dt>Radius: <dd> <meter min=0 max=20 value=12>12cm</meter>
 <dt>Height: <dd> <meter min=0 max=10 value=2>2cm</meter>
</dl>
```

There is no explicit way to specify units in the [`meter`](#213.html_the-meter-element) element, but the units may be specified in the [`title`](#213.html_attr-title) attribute in free-form text.

The example above could be extended to mention the units:

```
<dl>
 <dt>Radius: <dd> <meter min=0 max=20 value=12 title="centimeters">12cm</meter>
 <dt>Height: <dd> <meter min=0 max=10 value=2 title="centimeters">2cm</meter>
</dl>
```

**User agent requirements**: User agents must parse the [`min`](#213.html_attr-meter-min), [`max`](#213.html_attr-meter-max), [`value`](#213.html_attr-meter-value), [`low`](#213.html_attr-meter-low), [`high`](#213.html_attr-meter-high), and [`optimum`](#213.html_attr-meter-optimum) attributes using the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#213.html_rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values).

User agents must then use all these numbers to obtain values for six points on the gauge, as follows. (The order in which these are evaluated is important, as some of the values refer to earlier ones.)

The <dfn id="213.html_concept-meter-minimum" data-anolis-xref="concept-meter-minimum">minimum value</dfn>

If the [`min`](#213.html_attr-meter-min) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then the minimum value is that value. Otherwise, the minimum value is zero.

The <dfn id="213.html_concept-meter-maximum" data-anolis-xref="concept-meter-maximum">maximum value</dfn>

If the [`max`](#213.html_attr-meter-max) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then the candidate maximum value is that value. Otherwise, the candidate maximum value is 1.0.

If the candidate maximum value is greater than or equal to the minimum value, then the maximum value is the candidate maximum value. Otherwise, the maximum value is the same as the minimum value.

The <dfn id="213.html_concept-meter-actual" data-anolis-xref="concept-meter-actual">actual value</dfn>

If the [`value`](#213.html_attr-meter-value) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then that value is the candidate actual value. Otherwise, the candidate actual value is zero.

If the candidate actual value is less than the minimum value, then the actual value is the minimum value.

Otherwise, if the candidate actual value is greater than the maximum value, then the actual value is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the actual value is the candidate actual value.

The <dfn id="213.html_concept-meter-low" data-anolis-xref="concept-meter-low">low boundary</dfn>

If the [`low`](#213.html_attr-meter-low) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then the candidate low boundary is that value. Otherwise, the candidate low boundary is the same as the minimum value.

If the candidate low boundary is less than the minimum value, then the low boundary is the minimum value.

Otherwise, if the candidate low boundary is greater than the maximum value, then the low boundary is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the low boundary is the candidate low boundary.

The <dfn id="213.html_concept-meter-high" data-anolis-xref="concept-meter-high">high boundary</dfn>

If the [`high`](#213.html_attr-meter-high) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then the candidate high boundary is that value. Otherwise, the candidate high boundary is the same as the maximum value.

If the candidate high boundary is less than the low boundary, then the high boundary is the low boundary.

Otherwise, if the candidate high boundary is greater than the maximum value, then the high boundary is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the high boundary is the candidate high boundary.

The <dfn id="213.html_concept-meter-optimum" data-anolis-xref="concept-meter-optimum">optimum point</dfn>

If the [`optimum`](#213.html_attr-meter-optimum) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then the candidate optimum point is that value. Otherwise, the candidate optimum point is the midpoint between the minimum value and the maximum value.

If the candidate optimum point is less than the minimum value, then the optimum point is the minimum value.

Otherwise, if the candidate optimum point is greater than the maximum value, then the optimum point is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the optimum point is the candidate optimum point.

All of which will result in the following inequalities all being true:

*   minimum value ≤ actual value ≤ maximum value
*   minimum value ≤ low boundary ≤ high boundary ≤ maximum value
*   minimum value ≤ optimum point ≤ maximum value

**UA requirements for regions of the gauge**: If the optimum point is equal to the low boundary or the high boundary, or anywhere in between them, then the region between the low and high boundaries of the gauge must be treated as the optimum region, and the low and high parts, if any, must be treated as suboptimal. Otherwise, if the optimum point is less than the low boundary, then the region between the minimum value and the low boundary must be treated as the optimum region, the region from the low boundary up to the high boundary must be treated as a suboptimal region, and the remaining region must be treated as an even less good region. Finally, if the optimum point is higher than the high boundary, then the situation is reversed; the region between the high boundary and the maximum value must be treated as the optimum region, the region from the high boundary down to the low boundary must be treated as a suboptimal region, and the remaining region must be treated as an even less good region.

**UA requirements for showing the gauge**: When representing a [`meter`](#213.html_the-meter-element) element to the user, the UA should indicate the relative position of the actual value to the minimum and maximum values, and the relationship between the actual value and the three regions of the gauge.

The following markup:

```
<h3>Suggested groups</h3>
<ul>
 <li>
  <p><a href="/group/comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets/view">comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets</a> -
     <a href="/group/comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets/subscribe">join</a></p>
  <p>Group description: <strong>Layout/presentation on the WWW.</strong></p>
  <p><meter value="0.5">Moderate activity,</meter> Usenet, 618 subscribers</p>
 </li>
 <li>
  <p><a href="/group/netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall/view">netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall</a> -
     <a href="/group/netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall/subscribe">join</a></p>
  <p>Group description: <strong>Mozilla XPInstall discussion.</strong></p>
  <p><meter value="0.25">Low activity,</meter> Usenet, 22 subscribers</p>
 </li>
 <li>
  <p><a href="/group/mozilla.dev.general/view">mozilla.dev.general</a> -
     <a href="/group/mozilla.dev.general/subscribe">join</a></p>
  <p><meter value="0.25">Low activity,</meter> Usenet, 66 subscribers</p>
 </li>
</ul>
```

Might be rendered as follows:

![With the <meter> elements rendered as inline green bars of varying lengths.](Images/18b27d434b51b6e74b60ee7dba7d7e46.jpg)

User agents may combine the value of the [`title`](#213.html_attr-title) attribute and the other attributes to provide context-sensitive help or inline text detailing the actual values.

For example, the following snippet:

```
<meter min=0 max=60 value=23.2 title=seconds></meter>
```

...might cause the user agent to display a gauge with a tooltip saying "Value: 23.2 out of 60." on one line and "seconds" on a second line.

The <dfn id="213.html_dom-meter-value" data-anolis-xref="dom-meter-value">`value`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the [actual value](#213.html_concept-meter-actual). On setting, the given value must be converted to the [best representation of the number as a floating-point number](#213.html_best-representation-of-the-number-as-a-floating-point-number) and then the [`value`](#213.html_dom-meter-value) content attribute must be set to that string.

The <dfn id="213.html_dom-meter-min" data-anolis-xref="dom-meter-min">`min`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the [minimum value](#213.html_concept-meter-minimum). On setting, the given value must be converted to the [best representation of the number as a floating-point number](#213.html_best-representation-of-the-number-as-a-floating-point-number) and then the [`min`](#213.html_dom-meter-min) content attribute must be set to that string.

The <dfn id="213.html_dom-meter-max" data-anolis-xref="dom-meter-max">`max`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the [maximum value](#213.html_concept-meter-maximum). On setting, the given value must be converted to the [best representation of the number as a floating-point number](#213.html_best-representation-of-the-number-as-a-floating-point-number) and then the [`max`](#213.html_dom-meter-max) content attribute must be set to that string.

The <dfn id="213.html_dom-meter-low" data-anolis-xref="dom-meter-low">`low`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the [low boundary](#213.html_concept-meter-low). On setting, the given value must be converted to the [best representation of the number as a floating-point number](#213.html_best-representation-of-the-number-as-a-floating-point-number) and then the [`low`](#213.html_dom-meter-low) content attribute must be set to that string.

The <dfn id="213.html_dom-meter-high" data-anolis-xref="dom-meter-high">`high`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the [high boundary](#213.html_concept-meter-high). On setting, the given value must be converted to the [best representation of the number as a floating-point number](#213.html_best-representation-of-the-number-as-a-floating-point-number) and then the [`high`](#213.html_dom-meter-high) content attribute must be set to that string.

The <dfn id="213.html_dom-meter-optimum" data-anolis-xref="dom-meter-optimum">`optimum`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the [optimum value](#213.html_concept-meter-optimum). On setting, the given value must be converted to the [best representation of the number as a floating-point number](#213.html_best-representation-of-the-number-as-a-floating-point-number) and then the [`optimum`](#213.html_dom-meter-optimum) content attribute must be set to that string.

The [`labels`](#213.html_dom-lfe-labels) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#213.html_the-label-element)s.

The following example shows how a gauge could fall back to localized or pretty-printed text.

```
<p>Disk usage: <meter min=0 value=170261928 max=233257824>170?261?928 bytes used
out of 233?257?824 bytes available</meter></p>
```

#### 4.10.16 The <dfn>`fieldset`</dfn> element

[Categories](#214.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#214.html_flow-content-1).

[Sectioning root](#214.html_sectioning-root).

[Listed](#214.html_category-listed) and [reassociateable](#214.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#214.html_form-associated-element).

[Palpable content](#214.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#214.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [flow content](#214.html_flow-content-1) is expected.

[Content model](#214.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Optionally a [`legend`](#214.html_the-legend-element) element, followed by [flow content](#214.html_flow-content-1).

[Content attributes](#214.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#214.html_global-attributes)

[`disabled`](#214.html_attr-fieldset-disabled) - Whether the form control is disabled

[`form`](#214.html_attr-fae-form) - Associates the control with a [`form`](#214.html_the-form-element) element

[`name`](#214.html_attr-fe-name) - Name of form control to use for [form submission](#214.html_form-submission-0) and in the [`form.elements`](#214.html_dom-form-elements) API

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#214.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[`group`](#214.html_index-aria-group) (default - [*do not set*](#214.html_aria-usage-note)) or [`presentation`](#214.html_index-aria-presentation).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#214.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#214.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#214.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#214.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLFieldSetElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
           attribute DOMString name;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;

  readonly attribute HTMLFormControlsCollection elements;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  void setCustomValidity(DOMString error);
};
```

The [`fieldset`](#214.html_the-fieldset-element) element [represents](#214.html_represents) a set of form controls optionally grouped under a common name.

The name of the group is given by the first [`legend`](#214.html_the-legend-element) element that is a child of the [`fieldset`](#214.html_the-fieldset-element) element, if any. The remainder of the descendants form the group.

The <dfn id="214.html_attr-fieldset-disabled" data-anolis-xref="attr-fieldset-disabled">`disabled`</dfn> attribute, when specified, causes all the form control descendants of the [`fieldset`](#214.html_the-fieldset-element) element, excluding those that are descendants of the [`fieldset`](#214.html_the-fieldset-element) element's first [`legend`](#214.html_the-legend-element) element child, if any, to be [disabled](#214.html_concept-fe-disabled).

The [`form`](#214.html_attr-fae-form) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`fieldset`](#214.html_the-fieldset-element) element with its [form owner](#214.html_form-owner). The [`name`](#214.html_attr-fe-name) attribute represents the element's name.

`fieldset` . [`type`](#214.html_dom-fieldset-type)

Returns the string "fieldset".

`fieldset` . [`elements`](#214.html_dom-form-elements)

Returns an [`HTMLFormControlsCollection`](#214.html_htmlformcontrolscollection-0) of the form controls in the element.

The <dfn id="214.html_dom-fieldset-disabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-fieldset-disabled">`disabled`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#214.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

The <dfn id="214.html_dom-fieldset-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-fieldset-type">`type`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the string "`fieldset`".

The <dfn id="214.html_dom-fieldset-elements" data-anolis-xref="dom-fieldset-elements">`elements`</dfn> IDL attribute must return an [`HTMLFormControlsCollection`](#214.html_htmlformcontrolscollection-0) rooted at the [`fieldset`](#214.html_the-fieldset-element) element, whose filter matches [listed elements](#214.html_category-listed).

The [`willValidate`](#214.html_dom-cva-willvalidate), [`validity`](#214.html_dom-cva-validity), and [`validationMessage`](#214.html_dom-cva-validationmessage) attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#214.html_dom-cva-checkvalidity), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#214.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#214.html_the-constraint-validation-api). The [`form`](#214.html_dom-fae-form) and [`name`](#214.html_dom-fe-name) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

This example shows a [`fieldset`](#214.html_the-fieldset-element) element being used to group a set of related controls:

```
<fieldset>
 <legend>Display</legend>
 <div><label><input type=radio name=c value=0 checked> Black on White</label></div>
 <div><label><input type=radio name=c value=1> White on Black</label></div>
 <div><label><input type=checkbox name=g> Use grayscale</label></div>
 <div><label>Enhance contrast <input type=range name=e list=contrast min=0 max=100 value=0 step=1></label></div>
 <datalist id=contrast>
  <option label=Normal value=0>
  <option label=Maximum value=100>
 </datalist>
</fieldset>
```

The div elements used in the code samples above and below are not intended to convey any semantic meaning and are used only to create a non-inline rendering of the grouped fieldset controls.

The following snippet shows a fieldset with a checkbox in the legend that controls whether or not the fieldset is enabled. The contents of the fieldset consist of two required text fields and an optional year/month control.

```
<fieldset name="clubfields" disabled>
 <legend> <label>
  <input type=checkbox name=club onchange="form.clubfields.disabled = !checked">
  Use Club Card
 </label> </legend>
 <div><label>Name on card: <input name=clubname required></label></div>
 <div><label>Card number: <input name=clubnum required pattern="[-0-9]+"></label></div>
 <div><label>Expiry date: <input name=clubexp type=date></label></div>
</fieldset>
```

You can also nest [`fieldset`](#214.html_the-fieldset-element) elements. Here is an example expanding on the previous one that does so:

```
<fieldset name="clubfields" disabled>
 <legend> <label>
  <input type=checkbox name=club onchange="form.clubfields.disabled = !checked">
  Use Club Card
 </label> </legend>
 <div><label>Name on card: <input name=clubname required></label></div>
 <fieldset name="numfields">
  <legend> <label>
   <input type=radio checked name=clubtype onchange="form.numfields.disabled = !checked">
   My card has numbers on it
  </label> </legend>
  <div><label>Card number: <input name=clubnum required pattern="[-0-9]+"></label></div>
 </fieldset>
 <fieldset name="letfields" disabled>
  <legend> <label>
   <input type=radio name=clubtype onchange="form.letfields.disabled = !checked">
   My card has letters on it
  </label> </legend>
  <div><label>Card code: <input name=clublet required pattern="[A-Za-z]+"></label></>
 </fieldset>
</fieldset>
```

In this example, if the outer "Use Club Card" checkbox is not checked, everything inside the outer [`fieldset`](#214.html_the-fieldset-element), including the two radio buttons in the legends of the two nested [`fieldset`](#214.html_the-fieldset-element)s, will be disabled. However, if the checkbox is checked, then the radio buttons will both be enabled and will let you select which of the two inner [`fieldset`](#214.html_the-fieldset-element)s is to be enabled.

#### 4.10.17 The <dfn>`legend`</dfn> element

[Categories](#215.html_element-dfn-categories):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#215.html_element-dfn-contexts):

As the first child of a [`fieldset`](#215.html_the-fieldset-element) element.

[Content model](#215.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Phrasing content](#215.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Content attributes](#215.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#215.html_global-attributes)

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#215.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#215.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#215.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#215.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#215.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[DOM interface](#215.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLLegendElement : HTMLElement {
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
};
```

The [`legend`](#215.html_the-legend-element) element [represents](#215.html_represents) a caption for the rest of the contents of the [`legend`](#215.html_the-legend-element) element's parent [`fieldset`](#215.html_the-fieldset-element) element, if any.

`legend` . [`form`](#215.html_dom-legend-form)

Returns the element's [`form`](#215.html_the-form-element) element, if any, or null otherwise.

The <dfn id="215.html_dom-legend-form" data-anolis-xref="dom-legend-form">`form`</dfn> IDL attribute's behavior depends on whether the [`legend`](#215.html_the-legend-element) element is in a [`fieldset`](#215.html_the-fieldset-element) element or not. If the [`legend`](#215.html_the-legend-element) has a [`fieldset`](#215.html_the-fieldset-element) element as its parent, then the [`form`](#215.html_dom-legend-form) IDL attribute must return the same value as the [`form`](#215.html_dom-fae-form) IDL attribute on that [`fieldset`](#215.html_the-fieldset-element) element. Otherwise, it must return null.

#### 4.10.18 Form control infrastructure

##### 4.10.18.1 A form control's value

Form controls have a <dfn id="216.html_concept-fe-value" data-anolis-xref="concept-fe-value">value</dfn> and a <dfn id="216.html_concept-fe-checked" data-anolis-xref="concept-fe-checked">checkedness</dfn>. (The latter is only used by [`input`](#216.html_the-input-element) elements.) These are used to describe how the user interacts with the control.

To define the behaviour of constraint validation in the face of the [`input`](#216.html_the-input-element) element's [`multiple`](#216.html_attr-input-multiple) attribute, [`input`](#216.html_the-input-element) elements can also have separately defined <dfn id="216.html_concept-fe-values" data-anolis-xref="concept-fe-values">value*s*</dfn>.

##### 4.10.18.2 Mutability

A form control can be designated as <dfn id="216.html_concept-fe-mutable" data-anolis-xref="concept-fe-mutable">*mutable*</dfn>.

This determines (by means of definitions and requirements in this specification that rely on whether an element is so designated) whether or not the user can modify the [value](#216.html_concept-fe-value) or [checkedness](#216.html_concept-fe-checked) of a form control, or whether or not a control can be automatically prefilled.

##### 4.10.18.3 Association of controls and forms

A [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) can have a relationship with a [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) element, which is called the element's <dfn id="216.html_form-owner">form owner</dfn>. If a [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) is not associated with a [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) element, its [form owner](#216.html_form-owner) is said to be null.

A [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) is, by default, associated with its nearest ancestor [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) element (as described below), but, if it is [reassociateable](#216.html_category-form-attr), may have a <dfn id="216.html_attr-fae-form" data-anolis-xref="attr-fae-form">`form`</dfn> attribute specified to override this.

This feature allows authors to work around the lack of support for nested [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) elements.

If a [reassociateable](#216.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) has a [`form`](#216.html_attr-fae-form) attribute specified, then that attribute's value must be the [ID](#216.html_concept-id) of a [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) element in the element's owner [`Document`](#216.html_document).

The rules in this section are complicated by the fact that although conforming documents will never contain nested [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) elements, it is quite possible (e.g. using a script that performs DOM manipulation) to generate documents that have such nested elements. They are also complicated by rules in the HTML parser that, for historical reasons, can result in a [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) being associated with a [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) element that is not its ancestor.

When a [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) is created, its [form owner](#216.html_form-owner) must be initialized to null (no owner).

When a [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) is to be <dfn id="216.html_concept-form-association" data-anolis-xref="concept-form-association">associated</dfn> with a form, its [form owner](#216.html_form-owner) must be set to that form.

When a [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) or one of its ancestors is [inserted into a `Document`](#216.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document), then the user agent must [reset the form owner](#216.html_reset-the-form-owner) of that [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element). The [HTML parser](#216.html_html-parser) overrides this requirement when inserting form controls.

When an element is [removed from a `Document`](#216.html_remove-an-element-from-a-document) resulting in a [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) and its [form owner](#216.html_form-owner) (if any) no longer being in the same [home subtree](#216.html_home-subtree), then the user agent must [reset the form owner](#216.html_reset-the-form-owner) of that [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element).

When a [reassociateable](#216.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element)'s [`form`](#216.html_attr-fae-form) attribute is set, changed, or removed, then the user agent must [reset the form owner](#216.html_reset-the-form-owner) of that element.

When a [reassociateable](#216.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) has a [`form`](#216.html_attr-fae-form) attribute and the [ID](#216.html_concept-id) of any of the elements in the [`Document`](#216.html_document) changes, then the user agent must [reset the form owner](#216.html_reset-the-form-owner) of that [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element).

When a [reassociateable](#216.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) has a [`form`](#216.html_attr-fae-form) attribute and an element with an [ID](#216.html_concept-id) is [inserted into](#216.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document) or [removed from](#216.html_remove-an-element-from-a-document) the [`Document`](#216.html_document), then the user agent must [reset the form owner](#216.html_reset-the-form-owner) of that [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element).

When the user agent is to <dfn id="216.html_reset-the-form-owner">reset the form owner</dfn> of a [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element), it must run the following steps:

1.  If the element's [form owner](#216.html_form-owner) is not null, and either the element is not [reassociateable](#216.html_category-form-attr) or its [`form`](#216.html_attr-fae-form) content attribute is not present, and the element's [form owner](#216.html_form-owner) is its nearest [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) element ancestor after the change to the ancestor chain, then do nothing, and abort these steps.

2.  Let the element's [form owner](#216.html_form-owner) be null.

3.  If the element is [reassociateable](#216.html_category-form-attr), has a [`form`](#216.html_attr-fae-form) content attribute, and is itself [in a `Document`](#216.html_in-a-document), then run these substeps:

    1.  If the first element [in the `Document`](#216.html_in-a-document) to have an [ID](#216.html_concept-id) that is [case-sensitively](#216.html_case-sensitive) equal to the element's [`form`](#216.html_attr-fae-form) content attribute's value is a [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) element, then [associate](#216.html_concept-form-association) the [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) with that [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) element.

    2.  Abort the "reset the form owner" steps.

4.  Otherwise, if the [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) in question has an ancestor [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) element, then [associate](#216.html_concept-form-association) the [form-associated element](#216.html_form-associated-element) with the nearest such ancestor [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) element.

5.  Otherwise, the element is left unassociated.

In the following non-conforming snippet:

```
...
 <form id="a">
  <div id="b"></div>
 </form>
 <script>
  document.getElementById('b').innerHTML =
     '<table><tr><td><form id="c"><input id="d"></table>' +
     '<input id="e">';
 </script>
...
```

The [form owner](#216.html_form-owner) of "d" would be the inner nested form "c", while the [form owner](#216.html_form-owner) of "e" would be the outer form "a".

This happens as follows: First, the "e" node gets associated with "c" in the [HTML parser](#216.html_html-parser). Then, the [`innerHTML`](#216.html_dom-innerhtml) algorithm moves the nodes from the temporary document to the "b" element. At this point, the nodes see their ancestor chain change, and thus all the "magic" associations done by the parser are reset to normal ancestor associations.

This example is a non-conforming document, though, as it is a violation of the content models to nest [`form`](#216.html_the-form-element) elements.

`element` . [`form`](#216.html_dom-fae-form)

Returns the element's [form owner](#216.html_form-owner).

Returns null if there isn't one.

[Reassociateable](#216.html_category-form-attr) [form-associated elements](#216.html_form-associated-element) have a <dfn id="216.html_dom-fae-form" data-anolis-xref="dom-fae-form">`form`</dfn> IDL attribute, which, on getting, must return the element's [form owner](#216.html_form-owner), or null if there isn't one.

#### 4.10.19 <dfn>Attributes common to form controls</dfn>

##### 4.10.19.1 Naming form controls: the [`name`](#217.html_attr-fe-name) attribute

The <dfn id="217.html_attr-fe-name" data-anolis-xref="attr-fe-name">`name`</dfn> content attribute gives the name of the form control, as used in [form submission](#217.html_form-submission-0) and in the [`form`](#217.html_the-form-element) element's [`elements`](#217.html_dom-form-elements) object. If the attribute is specified, its value must not be the empty string.

Any non-empty value for [`name`](#217.html_attr-form-name) is allowed, but the names "[`_charset_`](#217.html_attr-fe-name-charset)" and "[`isindex`](#217.html_attr-fe-name-isindex)" are special:

<dfn id="217.html_attr-fe-name-isindex" data-anolis-xref="attr-fe-name-isindex">`isindex`</dfn>

This value, if used as the name of a [Text](#217.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) control that is the first control in a form that is submitted using the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#217.html_attr-fs-enctype-urlencoded) mechanism, causes the submission to only include the value of this control, with no name.

<dfn id="217.html_attr-fe-name-charset" data-anolis-xref="attr-fe-name-charset">`_charset_`</dfn>

This value, if used as the name of a [Hidden](#217.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) control with no [`value`](#217.html_attr-input-value) attribute, is automatically given a value during submission consisting of the submission character encoding.

The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fe-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-fe-name">`name`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the [`name`](#217.html_attr-fe-name) content attribute.

##### 4.10.19.2 Submitting element directionality: the [`dirname`](#217.html_attr-fe-dirname) attribute

The <dfn id="217.html_attr-fe-dirname" data-anolis-xref="attr-fe-dirname">`dirname`</dfn> attribute on a form control element enables the submission of [the directionality](#217.html_the-directionality) of the element, and gives the name of the field that contains this value during [form submission](#217.html_form-submission-0). If such an attribute is specified, its value must not be the empty string.

In this example, a form contains a text field and a submission button:

```
<form action="addcomment.cgi" method=post>
 <p><label>Comment: <input type=text name="comment" dirname="comment.dir" required></label></p>
 <p><button name="mode" type=submit value="add">Post Comment</button></p>
</form>
```

When the user submits the form, the user agent includes three fields, one called "comment", one called "comment.dir", and one called "mode"; so if the user types "Hello", the submission body might be something like:

```
comment=Hello&comment.dir=ltr&mode=add
```

If the user manually switches to a right-to-left writing direction and enters "?????", the submission body might be something like:

```
comment=%D9%85%D8%B1%D8%AD%D8%A8%D8%A7&comment.dir=rtl&mode=add
```

##### 4.10.19.3 Limiting user input length: the [`maxlength`](#217.html_attr-fe-maxlength) attribute

A <dfn id="217.html_attr-fe-maxlength" data-anolis-xref="attr-fe-maxlength">form control `maxlength` attribute</dfn>, controlled by a `dirty value flag`, declares a limit on the number of characters a user can input.

If an element has its [form control `maxlength` attribute](#217.html_attr-fe-maxlength) specified, the attribute's value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#217.html_valid-non-negative-integer). If the attribute is specified and applying the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#217.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) to its value results in a number, then that number is the element's <dfn id="217.html_maximum-allowed-value-length">maximum allowed value length</dfn>. If the attribute is omitted or parsing its value results in an error, then there is no [maximum allowed value length](#217.html_maximum-allowed-value-length).

**Constraint validation**: If an element has a [maximum allowed value length](#217.html_maximum-allowed-value-length), its `dirty value flag` is true, its [value](#217.html_concept-fe-value) was last changed by a user edit (as opposed to a change made by a script), and the [code-unit length](#217.html_code-unit-length) of the element's [value](#217.html_concept-fe-value) is greater than the element's [maximum allowed value length](#217.html_maximum-allowed-value-length), then the element is [suffering from being too long](#217.html_suffering-from-being-too-long).

User agents may prevent the user from causing the element's [value](#217.html_concept-fe-value) to be set to a value whose [code-unit length](#217.html_code-unit-length) is greater than the element's [maximum allowed value length](#217.html_maximum-allowed-value-length).

##### 4.10.19.4 Setting minimum input length requirements: the [`minlength`](#217.html_attr-fe-minlength) attribute

A <dfn id="217.html_attr-fe-minlength" data-anolis-xref="attr-fe-minlength">form control `minlength` attribute</dfn>, controlled by a `dirty value flag`, declares a lower bound on the number of characters a user can input.

The [`minlength`](#217.html_attr-fe-minlength) attribute does not imply the `required` attribute. If the form control has no [`minlength`](#217.html_attr-fe-minlength) attribute, then the value can still be omitted; the [`minlength`](#217.html_attr-fe-minlength) attribute only kicks in once the user has entered a value at all. If the empty string is not allowed, then the `required` attribute also needs to be set.

If an element has its [form control `minlength` attribute](#217.html_attr-fe-minlength) specified, the attribute's value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#217.html_valid-non-negative-integer). If the attribute is specified and applying the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#217.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) to its value results in a number, then that number is the element's <dfn id="217.html_minimum-allowed-value-length">minimum allowed value length</dfn>. If the attribute is omitted or parsing its value results in an error, then there is no [minimum allowed value length](#217.html_minimum-allowed-value-length).

If an element has both a [maximum allowed value length](#217.html_maximum-allowed-value-length) and a [minimum allowed value length](#217.html_minimum-allowed-value-length), the [minimum allowed value length](#217.html_minimum-allowed-value-length) must be smaller than or equal to the [maximum allowed value length](#217.html_maximum-allowed-value-length).

**Constraint validation**: If an element has a [minimum allowed value length](#217.html_minimum-allowed-value-length), its [value](#217.html_concept-fe-value) is not the empty string, and the [code-unit length](#217.html_code-unit-length) of the element's [value](#217.html_concept-fe-value) is less than the element's [minimum allowed value length](#217.html_minimum-allowed-value-length), then the element is [suffering from being too short](#217.html_suffering-from-being-too-short).

In this example, there are four text fields. The first is required, and has to be at least 5 characters long. The other three are optional, but if the user fills one in, the user has to enter at least 10 characters.

```
<form action="/events/menu.cgi" method="post">
 <p><label>Name of Event: <input required minlength=5 maxlength=50 name=event></label></p>
 <p><label>Describe what you would like for breakfast, if anything:
    <textarea name="breakfast" minlength="10"></textarea></label></p>
 <p><label>Describe what you would like for lunch, if anything:
    <textarea name="lunch" minlength="10"></textarea></label></p>
 <p><label>Describe what you would like for dinner, if anything:
    <textarea name="dinner" minlength="10"></textarea></label></p>
 <p><input type=submit value="Submit Request"></p>
</form>
```

##### 4.10.19.5 Enabling and disabling form controls: the [`disabled`](#217.html_attr-fe-disabled) attribute

The <dfn id="217.html_attr-fe-disabled" data-anolis-xref="attr-fe-disabled">`disabled`</dfn> content attribute is a [boolean attribute](#217.html_boolean-attribute).

A form control is <dfn id="217.html_concept-fe-disabled" data-anolis-xref="concept-fe-disabled">disabled</dfn> if its [`disabled`](#217.html_attr-fe-disabled) attribute is set, or if it is a descendant of a [`fieldset`](#217.html_the-fieldset-element) element whose [`disabled`](#217.html_attr-fieldset-disabled) attribute is set and is *not* a descendant of that [`fieldset`](#217.html_the-fieldset-element) element's first [`legend`](#217.html_the-legend-element) element child, if any.

A form control that is [disabled](#217.html_concept-fe-disabled) must prevent any [`click`](#217.html_event-click) events that are [queued](#217.html_queue-a-task) on the [user interaction task source](#217.html_user-interaction-task-source) from being dispatched on the element.

**Constraint validation**: If an element is [disabled](#217.html_concept-fe-disabled), it is [barred from constraint validation](#217.html_barred-from-constraint-validation).

The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fe-disabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-fe-disabled">`disabled`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the [`disabled`](#217.html_attr-fe-disabled) content attribute.

##### 4.10.19.6 Form submission

<dfn id="217.html_attributes-for-form-submission">Attributes for form submission</dfn> can be specified both on [`form`](#217.html_the-form-element) elements and on [submit buttons](#217.html_concept-submit-button) (elements that represent buttons that submit forms, e.g. an [`input`](#217.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#217.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Submit Button](#217.html_submit-button-state-(type=submit)) state).

The [attributes for form submission](#217.html_attributes-for-form-submission) that may be specified on [`form`](#217.html_the-form-element) elements are [`action`](#217.html_attr-fs-action), [`enctype`](#217.html_attr-fs-enctype), [`method`](#217.html_attr-fs-method), [`novalidate`](#217.html_attr-fs-novalidate), and [`target`](#217.html_attr-fs-target).

The corresponding [attributes for form submission](#217.html_attributes-for-form-submission) that may be specified on [submit buttons](#217.html_concept-submit-button) are [`formaction`](#217.html_attr-fs-formaction), [`formenctype`](#217.html_attr-fs-formenctype), [`formmethod`](#217.html_attr-fs-formmethod), [`formnovalidate`](#217.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate), and [`formtarget`](#217.html_attr-fs-formtarget). When omitted, they default to the values given on the corresponding attributes on the [`form`](#217.html_the-form-element) element.

* * *

The <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-action" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-action">`action`</dfn> and <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-formaction" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-formaction">`formaction`</dfn> content attributes, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#217.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces).

The <dfn id="217.html_concept-fs-action" data-anolis-xref="concept-fs-action">action</dfn> of an element is the value of the element's [`formaction`](#217.html_attr-fs-formaction) attribute, if the element is a [submit button](#217.html_concept-submit-button) and has such an attribute, or the value of its [form owner](#217.html_form-owner)'s [`action`](#217.html_attr-fs-action) attribute, if *it* has one, or else the empty string.

* * *

The <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-method" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-method">`method`</dfn> and <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-formmethod" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-formmethod">`formmethod`</dfn> content attributes are [enumerated attributes](#217.html_enumerated-attribute) with the following keywords and states:

*   The keyword <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-method-get-keyword" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-method-GET-keyword">`get`</dfn>, mapping to the state <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-method-get" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-method-GET">GET</dfn>, indicating the HTTP GET method.
*   The keyword <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-method-post-keyword" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-method-POST-keyword">`post`</dfn>, mapping to the state <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-method-post" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-method-POST">POST</dfn>, indicating the HTTP POST method.

The *invalid value default* for these attributes is the [GET](#217.html_attr-fs-method-get) state. The *missing value default* for the [`method`](#217.html_attr-fs-method) attribute is also the [GET](#217.html_attr-fs-method-get) state. (There is no *missing value default* for the [`formmethod`](#217.html_attr-fs-formmethod) attribute.)

The <dfn id="217.html_concept-fs-method" data-anolis-xref="concept-fs-method">method</dfn> of an element is one of those states. If the element is a [submit button](#217.html_concept-submit-button) and has a [`formmethod`](#217.html_attr-fs-formmethod) attribute, then the element's [method](#217.html_concept-fs-method) is that attribute's state; otherwise, it is the [form owner](#217.html_form-owner)'s [`method`](#217.html_attr-fs-method) attribute's state.

Here the [`method`](#217.html_attr-fs-method) attribute is used to explicitly specify the default value, "[`get`](#217.html_attr-fs-method-get-keyword)", so that the search query is submitted in the URL:

```
<form method="get" action="/search.cgi">
 <p><label>Search terms: <input type=search name=q></label></p>
 <p><input type=submit></p>
</form>
```

On the other hand, here the [`method`](#217.html_attr-fs-method) attribute is used to specify the value "[`post`](#217.html_attr-fs-method-post-keyword)", so that the user's message is submitted in the HTTP request's body:

```
<form method="post" action="/post-message.cgi">
 <p><label>Message: <input type=text name=m></label></p>
 <p><input type=submit value="Submit message"></p>
</form>
```

* * *

The <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-enctype" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-enctype">`enctype`</dfn> and <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-formenctype" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-formenctype">`formenctype`</dfn> content attributes are [enumerated attributes](#217.html_enumerated-attribute) with the following keywords and states:

*   The "<dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-enctype-urlencoded" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-enctype-urlencoded">`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`</dfn>" keyword and corresponding state.
*   The "<dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-enctype-formdata" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-enctype-formdata">`multipart/form-data`</dfn>" keyword and corresponding state.
*   The "<dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-enctype-text" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-enctype-text">`text/plain`</dfn>" keyword and corresponding state.

The *invalid value default* for these attributes is the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#217.html_attr-fs-enctype-urlencoded) state. The *missing value default* for the [`enctype`](#217.html_attr-fs-enctype) attribute is also the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#217.html_attr-fs-enctype-urlencoded) state. (There is no *missing value default* for the [`formenctype`](#217.html_attr-fs-formenctype) attribute.)

The <dfn id="217.html_concept-fs-enctype" data-anolis-xref="concept-fs-enctype">enctype</dfn> of an element is one of those three states. If the element is a [submit button](#217.html_concept-submit-button) and has a [`formenctype`](#217.html_attr-fs-formenctype) attribute, then the element's [enctype](#217.html_concept-fs-enctype) is that attribute's state; otherwise, it is the [form owner](#217.html_form-owner)'s [`enctype`](#217.html_attr-fs-enctype) attribute's state.

* * *

The <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-target" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-target">`target`</dfn> and <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-formtarget" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-formtarget">`formtarget`</dfn> content attributes, if specified, must have values that are [valid browsing context names or keywords](#217.html_valid-browsing-context-name-or-keyword).

The <dfn id="217.html_concept-fs-target" data-anolis-xref="concept-fs-target">target</dfn> of an element is the value of the element's [`formtarget`](#217.html_attr-fs-formtarget) attribute, if the element is a [submit button](#217.html_concept-submit-button) and has such an attribute; or the value of its [form owner](#217.html_form-owner)'s [`target`](#217.html_attr-fs-target) attribute, if *it* has such an attribute; or, if the [`Document`](#217.html_document) contains a [`base`](#217.html_the-base-element) element with a [`target`](#217.html_attr-base-target) attribute, then the value of the [`target`](#217.html_attr-base-target) attribute of the first such [`base`](#217.html_the-base-element) element; or, if there is no such element, the empty string.

* * *

The <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-novalidate" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-novalidate">`novalidate`</dfn> and <dfn id="217.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate" data-anolis-xref="attr-fs-formnovalidate">`formnovalidate`</dfn> content attributes are [boolean attributes](#217.html_boolean-attribute). If present, they indicate that the form is not to be validated during submission.

The <dfn id="217.html_concept-fs-novalidate" data-anolis-xref="concept-fs-novalidate">no-validate state</dfn> of an element is true if the element is a [submit button](#217.html_concept-submit-button) and the element's [`formnovalidate`](#217.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate) attribute is present, or if the element's [form owner](#217.html_form-owner)'s [`novalidate`](#217.html_attr-fs-novalidate) attribute is present, and false otherwise.

This attribute is useful to include "save" buttons on forms that have validation constraints, to allow users to save their progress even though they haven't fully entered the data in the form. The following example shows a simple form that has two required fields. There are three buttons: one to submit the form, which requires both fields to be filled in; one to save the form so that the user can come back and fill it in later; and one to cancel the form altogether.

```
<form action="editor.cgi" method="post">
 <p><label>Name: <input required name=fn></label></p>
 <p><label>Essay: <textarea required name=essay></textarea></label></p>
 <p><input type=submit name=submit value="Submit essay"></p>
 <p><input type=submit formnovalidate name=save value="Save essay"></p>
 <p><input type=submit formnovalidate name=cancel value="Cancel"></p>
</form>
```

* * *

The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fs-action" data-anolis-xref="dom-fs-action">`action`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name, except that on getting, when the content attribute is missing or its value is the empty string, [the document's address](#217.html_the-document's-address) must be returned instead. The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fs-target" data-anolis-xref="dom-fs-target">`target`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name. The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fs-method" data-anolis-xref="dom-fs-method">`method`</dfn> and <dfn id="217.html_dom-fs-enctype" data-anolis-xref="dom-fs-enctype">`enctype`</dfn> IDL attributes must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name, [limited to only known values](#217.html_limited-to-only-known-values). The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fs-encoding" data-anolis-xref="dom-fs-encoding">`encoding`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the [`enctype`](#217.html_attr-fs-enctype) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#217.html_limited-to-only-known-values). The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fs-novalidate" data-anolis-xref="dom-fs-noValidate">`noValidate`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the [`novalidate`](#217.html_attr-fs-novalidate) content attribute. The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fs-formaction" data-anolis-xref="dom-fs-formAction">`formAction`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the [`formaction`](#217.html_attr-fs-formaction) content attribute, except that on getting, when the content attribute is missing or its value is the empty string, [the document's address](#217.html_the-document's-address) must be returned instead. The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fs-formenctype" data-anolis-xref="dom-fs-formEnctype">`formEnctype`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the [`formenctype`](#217.html_attr-fs-formenctype) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#217.html_limited-to-only-known-values). The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fs-formmethod" data-anolis-xref="dom-fs-formMethod">`formMethod`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the [`formmethod`](#217.html_attr-fs-formmethod) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#217.html_limited-to-only-known-values). The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fs-formnovalidate" data-anolis-xref="dom-fs-formNoValidate">`formNoValidate`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the [`formnovalidate`](#217.html_attr-fs-formnovalidate) content attribute. The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fs-formtarget" data-anolis-xref="dom-fs-formTarget">`formTarget`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the [`formtarget`](#217.html_attr-fs-formtarget) content attribute.

##### 4.10.19.7 Autofocusing a form control: the [`autofocus`](#217.html_attr-fe-autofocus) attribute

The <dfn id="217.html_attr-fe-autofocus" data-anolis-xref="attr-fe-autofocus">`autofocus`</dfn> content attribute allows the author to indicate that a control is to be focused as soon as the page is loaded, allowing the user to just start typing without having to manually focus the main control.

The [`autofocus`](#217.html_attr-fe-autofocus) attribute is a [boolean attribute](#217.html_boolean-attribute).

An element's <dfn id="217.html_nearest-ancestor-autofocus-scoping-root-element">nearest ancestor autofocus scoping root element</dfn> is the element's [root element](#217.html_root-element).

There must not be two elements with the same [nearest ancestor autofocus scoping root element](#217.html_nearest-ancestor-autofocus-scoping-root-element) that both have the [`autofocus`](#217.html_attr-fe-autofocus) attribute specified.

When an element with the [`autofocus`](#217.html_attr-fe-autofocus) attribute specified is [inserted into a document](#217.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document), user agents should run the following steps:

1.  Let `target` be the element's [`Document`](#217.html_document).

2.  If `target` has no [browsing context](#217.html_browsing-context), abort these steps.

3.  If `target`'s [browsing context](#217.html_browsing-context) has no [top-level browsing context](#217.html_top-level-browsing-context) (e.g. it is a [nested browsing context](#217.html_nested-browsing-context) with no [parent browsing context](#217.html_parent-browsing-context)), abort these steps.

4.  If `target`'s [active sandboxing flag set](#217.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) has the [sandboxed automatic features browsing context flag](#217.html_sandboxed-automatic-features-browsing-context-flag), abort these steps.

5.  If `target`'s [origin](#217.html_origin-0) is not the [same](#217.html_same-origin) as the [origin](#217.html_origin-0) of the [`Document`](#217.html_document) of the currently focused element in `target`'s [top-level browsing context](#217.html_top-level-browsing-context), abort these steps.

6.  If `target`'s [origin](#217.html_origin-0) is not the [same](#217.html_same-origin) as the [origin](#217.html_origin-0) of the [active document](#217.html_active-document) of `target`'s [top-level browsing context](#217.html_top-level-browsing-context), abort these steps.

7.  If the user agent has already reached the last step of this list of steps in response to an element being [inserted](#217.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document) into a [`Document`](#217.html_document) whose [top-level browsing context](#217.html_top-level-browsing-context)'s [active document](#217.html_active-document) is the same as `target`'s [top-level browsing context](#217.html_top-level-browsing-context)'s [active document](#217.html_active-document), abort these steps.

8.  If the user has indicated (for example, by starting to type in a form control) that he does not wish focus to be changed, then optionally abort these steps.

9.  [Queue a task](#217.html_queue-a-task) that checks to see if the element is [focusable](#217.html_focusable), and if so, runs the [focusing steps](#217.html_focusing-steps) for that element. User agents may also change the scrolling position of the document, or perform some other action that brings the element to the user's attention. The [task source](#217.html_task-source) for this task is the [user interaction task source](#217.html_user-interaction-task-source).

This handles the automatic focusing during document load.

Focusing the control does not imply that the user agent must focus the browser window if it has lost focus.

The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fe-autofocus" data-anolis-xref="dom-fe-autofocus">`autofocus`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

In the following snippet, the text control would be focused when the document was loaded.

```
<input maxlength="256" name="q" value="" autofocus>
<input type="submit" value="Search">
```

##### 4.10.19.8 Autofilling form controls: the [`autocomplete`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete) attribute

User agents sometimes have features for helping users fill forms in, for example prefilling the user's address based on earlier user input. The <dfn id="217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete" data-anolis-xref="attr-fe-autocomplete">`autocomplete`</dfn> content attribute can be used to hint to the user agent how to, or indeed whether to, provide such a feature.

The attribute, if present, must have a value that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#217.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "[`off`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-off)", or a single token that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#217.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "[`on`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-on)"

The "<dfn id="217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-off" data-anolis-xref="attr-fe-autocomplete-off">`off`</dfn>" keyword indicates either that the control's input data is particularly sensitive (for example the activation code for a nuclear weapon); or that it is a value that will never be reused (for example a one-time-key for a bank login) and the user will therefore have to explicitly enter the data each time, instead of being able to rely on the UA to prefill the value for him; or that the document provides its own autocomplete mechanism and does not want the user agent to provide autocompletion values.

The "<dfn id="217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-on" data-anolis-xref="attr-fe-autocomplete-on">`on`</dfn>" keyword indicates that the user agent is allowed to provide the user with autocompletion values, but does not provide any further information about what kind of data the user might be expected to enter. User agents would have to use heuristics to decide what autocompletion values to suggest.

If the [`autocomplete`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete) attribute is omitted, the default value corresponding to the state of the element's [form owner](#217.html_form-owner)'s [`autocomplete`](#217.html_attr-form-autocomplete) attribute is used instead (either "[`on`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-on)" or "[`off`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-off)"). If there is no [form owner](#217.html_form-owner), then the value "[`on`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-on)" is used.

When an element's autofill field name is "[`off`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-off)", the user agent should not remember the control's [value](#217.html_concept-fe-value), and should not offer past values to the user.

In addition, when an element's autofill field name is "[`off`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-off)", [values are reset](#217.html_history-autocomplete) when [traversing the history](#217.html_traverse-the-history).

Banks frequently do not want UAs to prefill login information:

```
<p><label>Account: <input type="text" name="ac" autocomplete="off"></label></p>
<p><label>PIN: <input type="password" name="pin" autocomplete="off"></label></p>
```

When an element's autofill field name is *not* "[`off`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-off)", the user agent may store the control's [value](#217.html_concept-fe-value), and may offer previously stored values to the user.

When the autofill field name is "[`on`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-on)", the user agent should attempt to use heuristics to determine the most appropriate values to offer the user, e.g. based on the element's [`name`](#217.html_attr-fe-name) value, the position of the element in the document's DOM, what other fields exist in the form, and so forth.

The autocompletion mechanism must be implemented by the user agent acting as if the user had modified the element's [value](#217.html_concept-fe-value), and must be done at a time where the element is *[mutable](#217.html_concept-fe-mutable)* (e.g. just after the element has been inserted into the document, or when the user agent [stops parsing](#217.html_stop-parsing)). User agents must only prefill controls using values that the user could have entered.

A user agent prefilling a form control's [value](#217.html_concept-fe-value) must not cause that control to [suffer from a type mismatch](#217.html_suffering-from-a-type-mismatch), [suffer from a pattern mismatch](#217.html_suffering-from-a-pattern-mismatch), [suffer from being too long](#217.html_suffering-from-being-too-long), [suffer from being too short](#217.html_suffering-from-being-too-short), [suffer from an underflow](#217.html_suffering-from-an-underflow), [suffer from an overflow](#217.html_suffering-from-an-overflow), or [suffer from a step mismatch](#217.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch). Where possible given the control's constraints, user agents must use the format given as canonical in the aforementioned table. Where it's not possible for the canonical format to be used, user agents should use heuristics to attempt to convert values so that they can be used.

A user agent may allow the user to override an element's autofill field name, e.g. to change it from "[`off`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-off)" to "[`on`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-on)" to allow values to be remembered and prefilled despite the page author's objections, or to always "[`off`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-off)", never remembering values. However, user agents should not allow users to trivially override the autofill field name from "[`off`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-off)" to "[`on`](#217.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-on)" or other values, as there are significant security implications for the user if all values are always remembered, regardless of the site's preferences.

The <dfn id="217.html_dom-fe-autocomplete" data-anolis-xref="dom-fe-autocomplete">`autocomplete`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the element's IDL-exposed autofill value, and on setting, must [reflect](#217.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

#### 4.10.20 APIs for the text field selections

The [`input`](#218.html_the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#218.html_the-textarea-element) elements define the following members in their DOM interfaces for handling their selection:

```
 void select();
           attribute unsigned long selectionStart;
           attribute unsigned long selectionEnd;
           attribute DOMString selectionDirection;
  void setRangeText(DOMString replacement);
  void setRangeText(DOMString replacement, unsigned long start, unsigned long end, optional SelectionMode selectionMode = "preserve");
  void setSelectionRange(unsigned long start, unsigned long end, optional DOMString direction = "preserve");
```

The [`setRangeText`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext) method uses the following enumeration:

```
enum SelectionMode {
  "select",
  "start",
  "end",
```
