```
  "preserve" // default
};
```

These methods and attributes expose and control the selection of [`input`](#218.html_the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#218.html_the-textarea-element) text fields.

`element` . [`select`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-select)()

Selects everything in the text field.

`element` . `selectionStart` [ = `value` ]

Returns the offset to the start of the selection.

Can be set, to change the start of the selection.

`element` . `selectionEnd` [ = `value` ]

Returns the offset to the end of the selection.

Can be set, to change the end of the selection.

`element` . `selectionDirection` [ = `value` ]

Returns the current direction of the selection.

Can be set, to change the direction of the selection.

The possible values are "`forward`", "`backward`", and "`none`".

`element` . [`setSelectionRange`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange)(`start`, `end` [, `direction`] )

Changes the selection to cover the given substring in the given direction. If the direction is omitted, it will be reset to be the platform default (none or forward).

`element` . [`setRangeText`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext)(`replacement` [, `start`, `end` [, `selectionMode` ] ] )

Replaces a range of text with the new text. If the `start` and `end` arguments are not provided, the range is assumed to be the selection.

The final argument determines how the selection should be set after the text has been replaced. The possible values are:

"[`select`](#218.html_dom-selectionmode-select)"

Selects the newly inserted text.

"[`start`](#218.html_dom-selectionmode-start)"

Moves the selection to just before the inserted text.

"[`end`](#218.html_dom-selectionmode-end)"

Moves the selection to just after the selected text.

"[`preserve`](#218.html_dom-selectionmode-preserve)"

Attempts to preserve the selection. This is the default.

For [`input`](#218.html_the-input-element) elements, calling these methods while they [don't apply](#218.html_do-not-apply), and getting or setting these attributes while they [don't apply](#218.html_do-not-apply), must throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#218.html_invalidstateerror) exception. Otherwise, they must act as described below.

For [`input`](#218.html_the-input-element) elements, these methods and attributes must operate on the element's [value](#218.html_concept-fe-value). For [`textarea`](#218.html_the-textarea-element) elements, these methods and attributes must operate on the element's [raw value](#218.html_concept-textarea-raw-value).

Where possible, user interface features for changing the text selection in [`input`](#218.html_the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#218.html_the-textarea-element) elements must be implemented in terms of the DOM API described in this section, so that, e.g., all the same events fire.

The selections of [`input`](#218.html_the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#218.html_the-textarea-element) elements have a *direction*, which is either *forward*, *backward*, or *none*. This direction is set when the user manipulates the selection. The exact meaning of the selection direction depends on the platform.

On Windows, the direction indicates the position of the caret relative to the selection: a *forward* selection has the caret at the end of the selection and a *backward* selection has the caret at the start of the selection. Windows has no *none* direction. On Mac, the direction indicates which end of the selection is affected when the user adjusts the size of the selection using the arrow keys with the Shift modifier: the forward direction means the end of the selection is modified, and the backwards direction means the start of the selection is modified. The none direction is the default on Mac, it indicates that no particular direction has yet been selected. The user sets the direction implicitly when first adjusting the selection, based on which directional arrow key was used.

The <dfn id="218.html_dom-textarea/input-select" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea/input-select">`select()`</dfn> method must cause the contents of the text field to be fully selected, with the selection direction being none, if the platform support selections with the direction *none*, or otherwise *forward*. The user agent must then [queue a task](#218.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#218.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `select` at the element, using the [user interaction task source](#218.html_user-interaction-task-source) as the task source.

The <dfn id="218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea/input-selectionStart">`selectionStart`</dfn> attribute must, on getting, return the offset (in logical order) to the character that immediately follows the start of the selection. If there is no selection, then it must return the offset (in logical order) to the character that immediately follows the text entry cursor.

On setting, it must act as if the [`setSelectionRange()`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange) method had been called, with the new value as the first argument; the current value of the [`selectionEnd`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend) attribute as the second argument, unless the current value of the [`selectionEnd`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend) is less than the new value, in which case the second argument must also be the new value; and the current value of the [`selectionDirection`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection) as the third argument.

The <dfn id="218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea/input-selectionEnd">`selectionEnd`</dfn> attribute must, on getting, return the offset (in logical order) to the character that immediately follows the end of the selection. If there is no selection, then it must return the offset (in logical order) to the character that immediately follows the text entry cursor.

On setting, it must act as if the [`setSelectionRange()`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange) method had been called, with the current value of the [`selectionStart`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart) attribute as the first argument, the new value as the second argument, and the current value of the [`selectionDirection`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection) as the third argument.

The <dfn id="218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectiondirection" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea/input-selectionDirection">`selectionDirection`</dfn> attribute must, on getting, return the string corresponding to the current selection direction: if the direction is *forward*, "`forward`"; if the direction is *backward*, "`backward`"; and otherwise, "`none`".

On setting, it must act as if the [`setSelectionRange()`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange) method had been called, with the current value of the [`selectionStart`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart) attribute as the first argument, the current value of the [`selectionEnd`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend) attribute as the second argument, and the new value as the third argument.

The <dfn id="218.html_dom-textarea/input-setselectionrange" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea/input-setSelectionRange">`setSelectionRange(``start``,` `end``,` `direction``)`</dfn> method must set the selection of the text field to the sequence of characters starting with the character at the `start`th position (in logical order) and ending with the character at the (`end`-1)th position. Arguments greater than the length of the value of the text field must be treated as pointing at the end of the text field. If `end` is less than or equal to `start` then the start of the selection and the end of the selection must both be placed immediately before the character with offset `end`. In UAs where there is no concept of an empty selection, this must set the cursor to be just before the character with offset `end`. The direction of the selection must be set to *backward* if `direction` is a [case-sensitive](#218.html_case-sensitive) match for the string "`backward`", *forward* if `direction` is a [case-sensitive](#218.html_case-sensitive) match for the string "`forward`" or if the platform does not support selections with the direction *none*, and *none* otherwise (including if the argument is omitted). The user agent must then [queue a task](#218.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#218.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `select` at the element, using the [user interaction task source](#218.html_user-interaction-task-source) as the task source.

The <dfn id="218.html_dom-textarea/input-setrangetext" data-anolis-xref="dom-textarea/input-setRangeText">`setRangeText(``replacement``,` `start``,` `end``,` `selectMode``)`</dfn> method must run the following steps:

1.  If the method has only one argument, then let `start` and `end` have the values of the [`selectionStart`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart) attribute and the [`selectionEnd`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend) attribute respectively.

    Otherwise, let `start`, `end` have the values of the second and third arguments respectively.

2.  If `start` is greater than `end`, then throw an [`IndexSizeError`](#218.html_indexsizeerror) exception and abort these steps.

3.  If `start` is greater than the length of the value of the text field, then set it to the length of the value of the text field.

4.  If `end` is greater than the length of the value of the text field, then set it to the length of the value of the text field.

5.  Let `selection start` be the current value of the [`selectionStart`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionstart) attribute.

6.  Let `selection end` be the current value of the [`selectionEnd`](#218.html_dom-textarea/input-selectionend) attribute.

7.  If `start` is less than `end`, delete the sequence of characters starting with the character at the `start`th position (in logical order) and ending with the character at the (`end`-1)th position.

8.  Insert the value of the first argument into the text of the value of the text field, immediately before the `start`th character.

9.  Let `new length` be the length of the value of the first argument.

10.  Let `new end` be the sum of `start` and `new length`.

11.  Run the appropriate set of substeps from the following list:

    If the fourth argument's value is "<dfn id="218.html_dom-selectionmode-select" data-anolis-xref="dom-SelectionMode-select">`select`</dfn>"

    Let `selection start` be `start`.

    Let `selection end` be `new end`.

    If the fourth argument's value is "<dfn id="218.html_dom-selectionmode-start" data-anolis-xref="dom-SelectionMode-start">`start`</dfn>"

    Let `selection start` and `selection end` be `start`.

    If the fourth argument's value is "<dfn id="218.html_dom-selectionmode-end" data-anolis-xref="dom-SelectionMode-end">`end`</dfn>"

    Let `selection start` and `selection end` be `new end`.

    If the fourth argument's value is "<dfn id="218.html_dom-selectionmode-preserve" data-anolis-xref="dom-SelectionMode-preserve">`preserve`</dfn>" (the default)

    1.  Let `old length` be `end` minus `start`.

    2.  Let `delta` be `new length` minus `old length`.

    3.  If `selection start` is greater than `end`, then increment it by `delta`. (If `delta` is negative, i.e. the new text is shorter than the old text, then this will *decrease* the value of `selection start`.)

        Otherwise: if `selection start` is greater than `start`, then set it to `start`. (This snaps the start of the selection to the start of the new text if it was in the middle of the text that it replaced.)

    4.  If `selection end` is greater than `end`, then increment it by `delta` in the same way.

        Otherwise: if `selection end` is greater than `start`, then set it to `new end`. (This snaps the end of the selection to the end of the new text if it was in the middle of the text that it replaced.)

12.  Set the selection of the text field to the sequence of characters starting with the character at the `selection start`th position (in logical order) and ending with the character at the (`selection end`-1)th position. In UAs where there is no concept of an empty selection, this must set the cursor to be just before the character with offset `end`. The direction of the selection must be set to *forward* if the platform does not support selections with the direction *none*, and *none* otherwise.

13.  [Queue a task](#218.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#218.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `select` at the element, using the [user interaction task source](#218.html_user-interaction-task-source) as the task source.

All elements to which this API [applies](#218.html_concept-input-apply) have either a selection or a text entry cursor position at all times (even for elements that are not [being rendered](#218.html_being-rendered)). User agents should follow platform conventions to determine their initial state.

Characters with no visible rendering, such as U+200D ZERO WIDTH JOINER, still count as characters. Thus, for instance, the selection can include just an invisible character, and the text insertion cursor can be placed to one side or another of such a character.

To obtain the currently selected text, the following JavaScript suffices:

```
var selectionText = control.value.substring(control.selectionStart, control.selectionEnd);
```

...where `control` is the [`input`](#218.html_the-input-element) or [`textarea`](#218.html_the-textarea-element) element.

To add some text at the start of a text control, while maintaining the text selection, the three attributes must be preserved:

```
var oldStart = control.selectionStart;
var oldEnd = control.selectionEnd;
var oldDirection = control.selectionDirection;
var prefix = "http://";
control.value = prefix + control.value;
control.setSelectionRange(oldStart + prefix.length, oldEnd + prefix.length, oldDirection);
```

...where `control` is the [`input`](#218.html_the-input-element) or [`textarea`](#218.html_the-textarea-element) element.

#### 4.10.21 Constraints

##### 4.10.21.1 Definitions

A [submittable element](#219.html_category-submit) is a <dfn id="219.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation">candidate for constraint validation</dfn> except when a condition has <dfn id="219.html_barred-from-constraint-validation" data-anolis-xref="barred from constraint validation">barred the element from constraint validation</dfn>. (For example, an element is [barred from constraint validation](#219.html_barred-from-constraint-validation) if it is an [`object`](#219.html_the-object-element) element.)

An element can have a <dfn id="219.html_custom-validity-error-message">custom validity error message</dfn> defined. Initially, an element must have its [custom validity error message](#219.html_custom-validity-error-message) set to the empty string. When its value is not the empty string, the element is [suffering from a custom error](#219.html_suffering-from-a-custom-error). It can be set using the [`setCustomValidity()`](#219.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) method. The user agent should use the [custom validity error message](#219.html_custom-validity-error-message) when alerting the user to the problem with the control.

An element can be constrained in various ways. The following is the list of <dfn id="219.html_validity-states">validity states</dfn> that a form control can be in, making the control invalid for the purposes of constraint validation. (The definitions below are non-normative; other parts of this specification define more precisely when each state applies or does not.)

<dfn id="219.html_suffering-from-being-missing">Suffering from being missing</dfn>

When a control has no [value](#219.html_concept-fe-value) but has a `required` attribute ([`input`](#219.html_the-input-element) [`required`](#219.html_attr-input-required), [`select`](#219.html_the-select-element) [`required`](#219.html_attr-select-required), [`textarea`](#219.html_the-textarea-element) [`required`](#219.html_attr-textarea-required)), or, in the case of an element in a *[radio button group](#219.html_radio-button-group)*, any of the other elements in the group has a [`required`](#219.html_attr-input-required) attribute.

<dfn id="219.html_suffering-from-a-type-mismatch">Suffering from a type mismatch</dfn>

When a control that allows arbitrary user input has a [value](#219.html_concept-fe-value) that is not in the correct syntax ([E-mail](#219.html_e-mail-state-(type=email)), [URL](#219.html_url-state-(type=url))).

<dfn id="219.html_suffering-from-a-pattern-mismatch">Suffering from a pattern mismatch</dfn>

When a control has a [value](#219.html_concept-fe-value) that doesn't satisfy the [`pattern`](#219.html_attr-input-pattern) attribute.

<dfn id="219.html_suffering-from-being-too-long">Suffering from being too long</dfn>

When a control has a [value](#219.html_concept-fe-value) that is too long for the [form control `maxlength` attribute](#219.html_attr-fe-maxlength) ([`input`](#219.html_the-input-element) [`maxlength`](#219.html_attr-input-maxlength), [`textarea`](#219.html_the-textarea-element) [`maxlength`](#219.html_attr-textarea-maxlength)).

<dfn id="219.html_suffering-from-being-too-short">Suffering from being too short</dfn>

When a control has a [value](#219.html_concept-fe-value) that is too short for the [form control `minlength` attribute](#219.html_attr-fe-minlength) ([`input`](#219.html_the-input-element) [`minlength`](#219.html_attr-input-minlength), [`textarea`](#219.html_the-textarea-element) [`minlength`](#219.html_attr-textarea-minlength)).

<dfn id="219.html_suffering-from-an-underflow">Suffering from an underflow</dfn>

When a control has a [value](#219.html_concept-fe-value) that is too low for the [`min`](#219.html_attr-input-min) attribute.

<dfn id="219.html_suffering-from-an-overflow">Suffering from an overflow</dfn>

When a control has a [value](#219.html_concept-fe-value) that is too high for the [`max`](#219.html_attr-input-max) attribute.

<dfn id="219.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch">Suffering from a step mismatch</dfn>

When a control has a [value](#219.html_concept-fe-value) that doesn't fit the rules given by the [`step`](#219.html_attr-input-step) attribute.

<dfn id="219.html_suffering-from-bad-input">Suffering from bad input</dfn>

When a control has incomplete input and the user agent does not think the user ought to be able to submit the form in its current state.

<dfn id="219.html_suffering-from-a-custom-error">Suffering from a custom error</dfn>

When a control's [custom validity error message](#219.html_custom-validity-error-message) (as set by the element's [`setCustomValidity()`](#219.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) method) is not the empty string.

An element can still suffer from these states even when the element is [disabled](#219.html_concept-fe-disabled); thus these states can be represented in the DOM even if validating the form during submission wouldn't indicate a problem to the user.

An element <dfn id="219.html_concept-fv-valid" data-anolis-xref="concept-fv-valid">satisfies its constraints</dfn> if it is not suffering from any of the above [validity states](#219.html_validity-states).

##### 4.10.21.2 Constraint validation

When the user agent is required to <dfn id="219.html_statically-validate-the-constraints">statically validate the constraints</dfn> of [`form`](#219.html_the-form-element) element `form`, it must run the following steps, which return either a *positive* result (all the controls in the form are valid) or a *negative* result (there are invalid controls) along with a (possibly empty) list of elements that are invalid and for which no script has claimed responsibility:

1.  Let `controls` be a list of all the [submittable elements](#219.html_category-submit) whose [form owner](#219.html_form-owner) is `form`, in [tree order](#219.html_tree-order).

2.  Let `invalid controls` be an initially empty list of elements.

3.  For each element `field` in `controls`, in [tree order](#219.html_tree-order), run the following substeps:

    1.  If `field` is not a [candidate for constraint validation](#219.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation), then move on to the next element.

    2.  Otherwise, if `field` [satisfies its constraints](#219.html_concept-fv-valid), then move on to the next element.

    3.  Otherwise, add `field` to `invalid controls`.

4.  If `invalid controls` is empty, then return a *positive* result and abort these steps.

5.  Let `unhandled invalid controls` be an initially empty list of elements.

6.  For each element `field` in `invalid controls`, if any, in [tree order](#219.html_tree-order), run the following substeps:

    1.  [Fire a simple event](#219.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `invalid` that is cancelable at `field`.

    2.  If the event was not canceled, then add `field` to `unhandled invalid controls`.

7.  Return a *negative* result with the list of elements in the `unhandled invalid controls` list.

If a user agent is to <dfn id="219.html_interactively-validate-the-constraints">interactively validate the constraints</dfn> of [`form`](#219.html_the-form-element) element `form`, then the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  [Statically validate the constraints](#219.html_statically-validate-the-constraints) of `form`, and let `unhandled invalid controls` be the list of elements returned if the result was *negative*.

2.  If the result was *positive*, then return that result and abort these steps.

3.  Report the problems with the constraints of at least one of the elements given in `unhandled invalid controls` to the user. User agents may focus one of those elements in the process, by running the [focusing steps](#219.html_focusing-steps) for that element, and may change the scrolling position of the document, or perform some other action that brings the element to the user's attention. User agents may report more than one constraint violation. User agents may coalesce related constraint violation reports if appropriate (e.g. if multiple radio buttons in a [group](#219.html_radio-button-group) are marked as required, only one error need be reported). If one of the controls is not [being rendered](#219.html_being-rendered) (e.g. it has the [`hidden`](#219.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute set) then user agents may report a script error.

4.  Return a *negative* result.

##### 4.10.21.3 The <dfn>constraint validation API</dfn>

`element` . [`willValidate`](#219.html_dom-cva-willvalidate)

Returns true if the element will be validated when the form is submitted; false otherwise.

`element` . [`setCustomValidity`](#219.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity)(`message`)

Sets a custom error, so that the element would fail to validate. The given message is the message to be shown to the user when reporting the problem to the user.

If the argument is the empty string, clears the custom error.

`element` . [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) . [`valueMissing`](#219.html_dom-validitystate-valuemissing)

Returns true if the element has no value but is a required field; false otherwise.

`element` . [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) . [`typeMismatch`](#219.html_dom-validitystate-typemismatch)

Returns true if the element's value is not in the correct syntax; false otherwise.

`element` . [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) . [`patternMismatch`](#219.html_dom-validitystate-patternmismatch)

Returns true if the element's value doesn't match the provided pattern; false otherwise.

`element` . [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) . [`tooLong`](#219.html_dom-validitystate-toolong)

Returns true if the element's value is longer than the provided maximum length; false otherwise.

`element` . [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) . [`tooShort`](#219.html_dom-validitystate-tooshort)

Returns true if the element's value, if it is not the empty string, is shorter than the provided minimum length; false otherwise.

`element` . [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) . [`rangeUnderflow`](#219.html_dom-validitystate-rangeunderflow)

Returns true if the element's value is lower than the provided minimum; false otherwise.

`element` . [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) . [`rangeOverflow`](#219.html_dom-validitystate-rangeoverflow)

Returns true if the element's value is higher than the provided maximum; false otherwise.

`element` . [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) . [`stepMismatch`](#219.html_dom-validitystate-stepmismatch)

Returns true if the element's value doesn't fit the rules given by the [`step`](#219.html_attr-input-step) attribute; false otherwise.

`element` . [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) . [`badInput`](#219.html_dom-validitystate-badinput)

Returns true if the user has provided input in the user interface that the user agent is unable to convert to a value; false otherwise.

`element` . [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) . [`customError`](#219.html_dom-validitystate-customerror)

Returns true if the element has a custom error; false otherwise.

`element` . [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) . [`valid`](#219.html_dom-validitystate-valid)

Returns true if the element's value has no validity problems; false otherwise.

`valid` = `element` . [`checkValidity`](#219.html_dom-cva-checkvalidity)()

Returns true if the element's value has no validity problems; false otherwise. Fires an `invalid` event at the element in the latter case.

`element` . [`validationMessage`](#219.html_dom-cva-validationmessage)

Returns the error message that would be shown to the user if the element was to be checked for validity.

The <dfn id="219.html_dom-cva-willvalidate" data-anolis-xref="dom-cva-willValidate">`willValidate`</dfn> attribute must return true if an element is a [candidate for constraint validation](#219.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation), and false otherwise (i.e. false if any conditions are [barring it from constraint validation](#219.html_barred-from-constraint-validation)).

The <dfn id="219.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity" data-anolis-xref="dom-cva-setCustomValidity">`setCustomValidity(``message``)`</dfn>, when invoked, must set the [custom validity error message](#219.html_custom-validity-error-message) to the value of the given `message` argument.

In the following example, a script checks the value of a form control each time it is edited, and whenever it is not a valid value, uses the [`setCustomValidity()`](#219.html_dom-cva-setcustomvalidity) method to set an appropriate message.

```
<label>Feeling: <input name=f type="text" oninput="check(this)"></label>
<script>
 function check(input) {
   if (input.value == "good" ||
       input.value == "fine" ||
       input.value == "tired") {
     input.setCustomValidity('"' + input.value + '" is not a feeling.');
   } else {
     // input is fine -- reset the error message
     input.setCustomValidity('');
   }
 }
</script>
```

The <dfn id="219.html_dom-cva-validity" data-anolis-xref="dom-cva-validity">`validity`</dfn> attribute must return a [`ValidityState`](#219.html_validitystate) object that represents the [validity states](#219.html_validity-states) of the element. This object is [live](#219.html_live), and the same object must be returned each time the element's [`validity`](#219.html_dom-cva-validity) attribute is retrieved.

```
interface ValidityState {
  readonly attribute boolean valueMissing;
  readonly attribute boolean typeMismatch;
  readonly attribute boolean patternMismatch;
  readonly attribute boolean tooLong;
  readonly attribute boolean tooShort;
  readonly attribute boolean rangeUnderflow;
  readonly attribute boolean rangeOverflow;
  readonly attribute boolean stepMismatch;
  readonly attribute boolean badInput;
  readonly attribute boolean customError;
  readonly attribute boolean valid;
};
```

A [`ValidityState`](#219.html_validitystate) object has the following attributes. On getting, they must return true if the corresponding condition given in the following list is true, and false otherwise.

<dfn id="219.html_dom-validitystate-valuemissing" data-anolis-xref="dom-ValidityState-valueMissing">`valueMissing`</dfn>

The control is [suffering from being missing](#219.html_suffering-from-being-missing).

<dfn id="219.html_dom-validitystate-typemismatch" data-anolis-xref="dom-ValidityState-typeMismatch">`typeMismatch`</dfn>

The control is [suffering from a type mismatch](#219.html_suffering-from-a-type-mismatch).

<dfn id="219.html_dom-validitystate-patternmismatch" data-anolis-xref="dom-ValidityState-patternMismatch">`patternMismatch`</dfn>

The control is [suffering from a pattern mismatch](#219.html_suffering-from-a-pattern-mismatch).

<dfn id="219.html_dom-validitystate-toolong" data-anolis-xref="dom-ValidityState-tooLong">`tooLong`</dfn>

The control is [suffering from being too long](#219.html_suffering-from-being-too-long).

<dfn id="219.html_dom-validitystate-tooshort" data-anolis-xref="dom-ValidityState-tooShort">`tooShort`</dfn>

The control is [suffering from being too short](#219.html_suffering-from-being-too-short).

<dfn id="219.html_dom-validitystate-rangeunderflow" data-anolis-xref="dom-ValidityState-rangeUnderflow">`rangeUnderflow`</dfn>

The control is [suffering from an underflow](#219.html_suffering-from-an-underflow).

<dfn id="219.html_dom-validitystate-rangeoverflow" data-anolis-xref="dom-ValidityState-rangeOverflow">`rangeOverflow`</dfn>

The control is [suffering from an overflow](#219.html_suffering-from-an-overflow).

<dfn id="219.html_dom-validitystate-stepmismatch" data-anolis-xref="dom-ValidityState-stepMismatch">`stepMismatch`</dfn>

The control is [suffering from a step mismatch](#219.html_suffering-from-a-step-mismatch).

<dfn id="219.html_dom-validitystate-badinput" data-anolis-xref="dom-ValidityState-badInput">`badInput`</dfn>

The control is [suffering from bad input](#219.html_suffering-from-bad-input).

<dfn id="219.html_dom-validitystate-customerror" data-anolis-xref="dom-ValidityState-customError">`customError`</dfn>

The control is [suffering from a custom error](#219.html_suffering-from-a-custom-error).

<dfn id="219.html_dom-validitystate-valid" data-anolis-xref="dom-ValidityState-valid">`valid`</dfn>

None of the other conditions are true.

When the <dfn id="219.html_dom-cva-checkvalidity" data-anolis-xref="dom-cva-checkValidity">`checkValidity()`</dfn> method is invoked, if the element is a [candidate for constraint validation](#219.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation) and does not [satisfy its constraints](#219.html_concept-fv-valid), the user agent must [fire a simple event](#219.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `invalid` that is cancelable (but in this case has no default action) at the element and return false. Otherwise, it must only return true without doing anything else.

The <dfn id="219.html_dom-cva-validationmessage" data-anolis-xref="dom-cva-validationMessage">`validationMessage`</dfn> attribute must return the empty string if the element is not a [candidate for constraint validation](#219.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation) or if it is one but it [satisfies its constraints](#219.html_concept-fv-valid); otherwise, it must return a suitably localized message that the user agent would show the user if this were the only form control with a validity constraint problem. If the user agent would not actually show a textual message in such a situation (e.g. it would show a graphical cue instead), then the attribute must return a suitably localized message that expresses (one or more of) the validity constraint(s) that the control does not satisfy. If the element is a [candidate for constraint validation](#219.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation) and is [suffering from a custom error](#219.html_suffering-from-a-custom-error), then the [custom validity error message](#219.html_custom-validity-error-message) should be present in the return value.

##### 4.10.21.4 Security

Servers should not rely on client-side validation. Client-side validation can be intentionally bypassed by hostile users, and unintentionally bypassed by users of older user agents or automated tools that do not implement these features. The constraint validation features are only intended to improve the user experience, not to provide any kind of security mechanism.

#### 4.10.22 <dfn>Form submission</dfn>

##### 4.10.22.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

When a form is submitted, the data in the form is converted into the structure specified by the [enctype](#220.html_concept-fs-enctype), and then sent to the destination specified by the [action](#220.html_concept-fs-action) using the given [method](#220.html_concept-fs-method).

For example, take the following form:

```
<form action="/find.cgi" method=get>
 <input type=text name=t>
 <input type=search name=q>
 <input type=submit>
</form>
```

If the user types in "cats" in the first field and "fur" in the second, and then hits the submit button, then the user agent will load `/find.cgi?t=cats&q=fur`.

On the other hand, consider this form:

```
<form action="/find.cgi" method=post enctype="multipart/form-data">
 <input type=text name=t>
 <input type=search name=q>
 <input type=submit>
</form>
```

Given the same user input, the result on submission is quite different: the user agent instead does an HTTP POST to the given URL, with as the entity body something like the following text:

```
------kYFrd4jNJEgCervE
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="t"

cats
------kYFrd4jNJEgCervE
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="q"

fur
------kYFrd4jNJEgCervE--
```

##### 4.10.22.2 Implicit submission

A [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element's <dfn id="220.html_default-button">default button</dfn> is the first [submit button](#220.html_concept-submit-button) in [tree order](#220.html_tree-order) whose [form owner](#220.html_form-owner) is that [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element.

If the user agent supports letting the user submit a form implicitly (for example, on some platforms hitting the "enter" key while a text field is focused implicitly submits the form), then doing so for a form whose [default button](#220.html_default-button) has a defined [activation behavior](#220.html_activation-behavior) must cause the user agent to [run synthetic click activation steps](#220.html_run-synthetic-click-activation-steps) on that [default button](#220.html_default-button).

Consequently, if the [default button](#220.html_default-button) is [disabled](#220.html_concept-fe-disabled), the form is not submitted when such an implicit submission mechanism is used. (A button has no [activation behavior](#220.html_activation-behavior) when disabled.)

There are pages on the Web that are only usable if there is a way to implicitly submit forms, so user agents are strongly encouraged to support this.

If the form has no [submit button](#220.html_concept-submit-button), then the implicit submission mechanism must do nothing if the form has more than one *field that blocks implicit submission*, and must [submit](#220.html_concept-form-submit) the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element from the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element itself otherwise.

For the purpose of the previous paragraph, an element is a *field that blocks implicit submission* of a [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element if it is an [`input`](#220.html_the-input-element) element whose [form owner](#220.html_form-owner) is that [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element and whose [`type`](#220.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in one of the following states: [Text](#220.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [Search](#220.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [URL](#220.html_url-state-(type=url)), [Telephone](#220.html_telephone-state-(type=tel)), [E-mail](#220.html_e-mail-state-(type=email)), [Password](#220.html_password-state-(type=password)), [Date](#220.html_date-state-(type=date)), [Time](#220.html_time-state-(type=time)), [Number](#220.html_number-state-(type=number))

##### 4.10.22.3 Form submission algorithm

When a [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element `form` is <dfn id="220.html_concept-form-submit" data-anolis-xref="concept-form-submit">submitted</dfn> from an element `submitter` (typically a button), optionally with a `submitted from` [`submit()`](#220.html_dom-form-submit) `method` flag set, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `form document` be the `form`'s [`Document`](#220.html_document).

2.  If `form document` has no associated [browsing context](#220.html_browsing-context) or its [active sandboxing flag set](#220.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) has its [sandboxed forms browsing context flag](#220.html_sandboxed-forms-browsing-context-flag) set, then abort these steps without doing anything.

3.  Let `form browsing context` be the [browsing context](#220.html_browsing-context) of `form document`.

4.  If the `submitted from` [`submit()`](#220.html_dom-form-submit) `method` flag is not set, and the `submitter` element's [no-validate state](#220.html_concept-fs-novalidate) is false, then [interactively validate the constraints](#220.html_interactively-validate-the-constraints) of `form` and examine the result: if the result is negative (the constraint validation concluded that there were invalid fields and probably informed the user of this) then [fire a simple event](#220.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `invalid` at the `form` element and then abort these steps.

5.  If the `submitted from` [`submit()`](#220.html_dom-form-submit) `method` flag is not set, then [fire a simple event](#220.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles and is cancelable named `submit`, at `form`. If the event's default action is prevented (i.e. if the event is canceled) then abort these steps. Otherwise, continue (effectively the default action is to perform the submission).

6.  Let `form data set` be the result of [constructing the form data set](#220.html_constructing-the-form-data-set) for `form` in the context of `submitter`.

7.  Let `action` be the `submitter` element's [action](#220.html_concept-fs-action).

8.  If `action` is the empty string, let `action` be [the document's address](#220.html_the-document's-address) of the `form document`.

9.  [Resolve](#220.html_resolve-a-url) the URL `action`, relative to the `submitter` element. If this fails, abort these steps.

10.  Let `action` be the resulting [absolute URL](#220.html_absolute-url).

11.  Let `action components` be the resulting [parsed URL](#220.html_parsed-url).

12.  Let `scheme` be the [scheme](#220.html_concept-url-scheme) of the resulting [parsed URL](#220.html_parsed-url).

13.  Let `enctype` be the `submitter` element's [enctype](#220.html_concept-fs-enctype).

14.  Let `method` be the `submitter` element's [method](#220.html_concept-fs-method).

15.  Let `target` be the `submitter` element's [target](#220.html_concept-fs-target).

16.  If the user indicated a specific [browsing context](#220.html_browsing-context) to use when submitting the form, then let `target browsing context` be that [browsing context](#220.html_browsing-context). Otherwise, apply [the rules for choosing a browsing context given a browsing context name](#220.html_the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name) using `target` as the name and `form browsing context` as the context in which the algorithm is executed, and let `target browsing context` be the resulting [browsing context](#220.html_browsing-context).

17.  If `target browsing context` was created in the previous step, or, alternatively, if the `form document` has not yet [completely loaded](#220.html_completely-loaded) and the `submitted from` [`submit()`](#220.html_dom-form-submit) `method` flag is set, then let `replace` be true. Otherwise, let it be false.

18.  Otherwise, select the appropriate row in the table below based on the value of `scheme` as given by the first cell of each row. Then, select the appropriate cell on that row based on the value of `method` as given in the first cell of each column. Then, jump to the steps named in that cell and defined below the table.

    |  | [GET](#220.html_attr-fs-method-get) | [POST](#220.html_attr-fs-method-post) |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `http` | [Mutate action URL](#220.html_submit-mutate-action) | [Submit as entity body](#220.html_submit-body) |
    | `https` | [Mutate action URL](#220.html_submit-mutate-action) | [Submit as entity body](#220.html_submit-body) |
    | `ftp` | [Get action URL](#220.html_submit-get-action) | [Get action URL](#220.html_submit-get-action) |
    | `javascript` | [Get action URL](#220.html_submit-get-action) | [Get action URL](#220.html_submit-get-action) |
    | `data` | [Get action URL](#220.html_submit-get-action) | [Post to data:](#220.html_submit-data-post) |
    | `mailto` | [Mail with headers](#220.html_submit-mailto-headers) | [Mail as body](#220.html_submit-mailto-body) |

    If `scheme` is not one of those listed in this table, then the behavior is not defined by this specification. User agents should, in the absence of another specification defining this, act in a manner analogous to that defined in this specification for similar schemes.

    Each [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element has a <dfn id="220.html_planned-navigation">planned navigation</dfn>, which is either null or a [task](#220.html_concept-task); when the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) is first created, its [planned navigation](#220.html_planned-navigation) must be set to null. In the behaviours described below, when the user agent is required to <dfn id="220.html_plan-to-navigate">plan to navigate</dfn> to a particular resource `destination`, it must run the following steps:

    1.  If the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) has a non-null [planned navigation](#220.html_planned-navigation), remove it from its [task queue](#220.html_task-queue).

    2.  Let the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element)'s [planned navigation](#220.html_planned-navigation) be a new [task](#220.html_concept-task) that consists of running the following steps:

        1.  Let the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element)'s [planned navigation](#220.html_planned-navigation) be null.

        2.  [Navigate](#220.html_navigate) `target browsing context` to the particular resource `destination`. If `replace` is true, then `target browsing context` must be navigated with [replacement enabled](#220.html_replacement-enabled).

        For the purposes of this task, `target browsing context` and `replace` are the variables that were set up when the overall form submission algorithm was run, with their values as they stood when this [planned navigation](#220.html_planned-navigation) was [queued](#220.html_queue-a-task).

    3.  [Queue the task](#220.html_queue-a-task) that is the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element)'s new [planned navigation](#220.html_planned-navigation).

        The [task source](#220.html_task-source) for this task is the [DOM manipulation task source](#220.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

    The behaviors are as follows:

    <dfn id="220.html_submit-mutate-action" data-anolis-xref="submit-mutate-action">Mutate action URL</dfn>

    Let `query` be the result of encoding the `form data set` using the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` encoding algorithm](#220.html_application/x-www-form-urlencoded-encoding-algorithm), interpreted as a US-ASCII string.

    Set `parsed action`'s [query](#220.html_concept-url-query) component to `query`.

    Let `destination` be a new URL formed by applying the [URL serializer](#220.html_concept-url-serializer) algorithm to `parsed action`.

    [Plan to navigate](#220.html_plan-to-navigate) to `destination`.

    <dfn id="220.html_submit-body" data-anolis-xref="submit-body">Submit as entity body</dfn>

    Let `entity body` be the result of encoding the `form data set` using the [appropriate form encoding algorithm](#220.html_appropriate-form-encoding-algorithm).

    Let `MIME type` be determined as follows:

    If `enctype` is [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#220.html_attr-fs-enctype-urlencoded)

    Let `MIME type` be "`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`".

    If `enctype` is [`multipart/form-data`](#220.html_attr-fs-enctype-formdata)

    Let `MIME type` be the concatenation of the string "`multipart/form-data;`", a U+0020 SPACE character, the string "`boundary=`", and the [`multipart/form-data` boundary string](#220.html_multipart/form-data-boundary-string) generated by the [`multipart/form-data` encoding algorithm](#220.html_multipart/form-data-encoding-algorithm).

    If `enctype` is [`text/plain`](#220.html_attr-fs-enctype-text)

    Let `MIME type` be "`text/plain`".

    Otherwise, [plan to navigate](#220.html_plan-to-navigate) to `action` using the HTTP method given by `method` and with `entity body` as the entity body, of type `MIME type`.

    <dfn id="220.html_submit-get-action" data-anolis-xref="submit-get-action">Get action URL</dfn>

    [Plan to navigate](#220.html_plan-to-navigate) to `action`.

    The `form data set` is discarded.

    <dfn id="220.html_submit-data-post" data-anolis-xref="submit-data-post">Post to data:</dfn>

    Let `data` be the result of encoding the `form data set` using the [appropriate form encoding algorithm](#220.html_appropriate-form-encoding-algorithm).

    If `action` contains the string "`%%%%`" (four U+0025 PERCENT SIGN characters), then [percent encode](#220.html_percent-encode) all bytes in `data` that, if interpreted as US-ASCII, are not characters in the URL [default encode set](#220.html_default-encode-set), and then, treating the result as a US-ASCII string, [UTF-8 percent encode](#220.html_utf-8-percent-encode) all the U+0025 PERCENT SIGN characters in the resulting string and replace the first occurrence of "`%%%%`" in `action` with the resulting doubly-escaped string. [[URL]](#220.html_refsURL)

    Otherwise, if `action` contains the string "`%%`" (two U+0025 PERCENT SIGN characters in a row, but not four), then [UTF-8 percent encode](#220.html_utf-8-percent-encode) all characters in `data` that, if interpreted as US-ASCII, are not characters in the URL [default encode set](#220.html_default-encode-set), and then, treating the result as a US-ASCII string, replace the first occurrence of "`%%`" in `action` with the resulting escaped string. [[URL]](#220.html_refsURL)

    [Plan to navigate](#220.html_plan-to-navigate) to the potentially modified `action` (which will be a [`data:` URL](#220.html_data-protocol)).

    <dfn id="220.html_submit-mailto-headers" data-anolis-xref="submit-mailto-headers">Mail with headers</dfn>

    Let `headers` be the resulting encoding the `form data set` using the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` encoding algorithm](#220.html_application/x-www-form-urlencoded-encoding-algorithm), interpreted as a US-ASCII string.

    Replace occurrences of "+" (U+002B) characters in `headers` with the string "`%20`".

    Let `destination` consist of all the characters from the first character in `action` to the character immediately before the first "?" (U+003F) character, if any, or the end of the string if there are none.

    Append a single "?" (U+003F) character to `destination`.

    Append `headers` to `destination`.

    [Plan to navigate](#220.html_plan-to-navigate) to `destination`.

    <dfn id="220.html_submit-mailto-body" data-anolis-xref="submit-mailto-body">Mail as body</dfn>

    Let `body` be the resulting of encoding the `form data set` using the [appropriate form encoding algorithm](#220.html_appropriate-form-encoding-algorithm) and then [percent encoding](#220.html_percent-encode) all the bytes in the resulting byte string that, when interpreted as US-ASCII, are not characters in the URL [default encode set](#220.html_default-encode-set). [[URL]](#220.html_refsURL)

    Let `destination` have the same value as `action`.

    If `destination` does not contain a "?" (U+003F) character, append a single "?" (U+003F) character to `destination`. Otherwise, append a single U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&).

    Append the string "`body=`" to `destination`.

    Append `body`, interpreted as a US-ASCII string, to `destination`.

    [Plan to navigate](#220.html_plan-to-navigate) to `destination`.

    The <dfn id="220.html_appropriate-form-encoding-algorithm">appropriate form encoding algorithm</dfn> is determined as follows:

    If `enctype` is [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#220.html_attr-fs-enctype-urlencoded)

    Use the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` encoding algorithm](#220.html_application/x-www-form-urlencoded-encoding-algorithm).

    If `enctype` is [`multipart/form-data`](#220.html_attr-fs-enctype-formdata)

    Use the [`multipart/form-data` encoding algorithm](#220.html_multipart/form-data-encoding-algorithm).

    If `enctype` is [`text/plain`](#220.html_attr-fs-enctype-text)

    Use the [`text/plain` encoding algorithm](#220.html_text/plain-encoding-algorithm).

##### 4.10.22.4 Constructing the form data set

The algorithm to <dfn id="220.html_constructing-the-form-data-set" data-anolis-xref="constructing the form data set">construct the form data set</dfn> for a form `form` optionally in the context of a submitter `submitter` is as follows. If not specified otherwise, `submitter` is null.

1.  Let `controls` be a list of all the [submittable elements](#220.html_category-submit) whose [form owner](#220.html_form-owner) is `form`, in [tree order](#220.html_tree-order).

2.  Let the `form data set` be a list of name-value-type tuples, initially empty.

3.  *Loop*: For each element `field` in `controls`, in [tree order](#220.html_tree-order), run the following substeps:

    1.  If any of the following conditions are met, then skip these substeps for this element:

        *   The `field` element has a [`datalist`](#220.html_the-datalist-element) element ancestor.
        *   The `field` element is [disabled](#220.html_concept-fe-disabled).
        *   The `field` element is a [button](#220.html_concept-button) but it is not `submitter`.
        *   The `field` element is an [`input`](#220.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#220.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Checkbox](#220.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) state and whose [checkedness](#220.html_concept-fe-checked) is false.
        *   The `field` element is an [`input`](#220.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#220.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#220.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state and whose [checkedness](#220.html_concept-fe-checked) is false.
        *   The `field` element is not an [`input`](#220.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#220.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Image Button](#220.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, and either the `field` element does not have a [`name`](#220.html_attr-fe-name) attribute specified, or its [`name`](#220.html_attr-fe-name) attribute's value is the empty string.
        *   The `field` element is an [`object`](#220.html_the-object-element) element that is not using a [plugin](#220.html_plugin).

        Otherwise, process `field` as follows:

    2.  Let `type` be the value of the `type` IDL attribute of `field`.

    3.  If the `field` element is an [`input`](#220.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#220.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Image Button](#220.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, then run these further nested substeps:

        1.  If the `field` element has a [`name`](#220.html_attr-fe-name) attribute specified and its value is not the empty string, let `name` be that value followed by a single "." (U+002E) character. Otherwise, let `name` be the empty string.

        2.  Let `name`[`x`] be the string consisting of the concatenation of `name` and a single U+0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X character (x).

        3.  Let `name`[`y`] be the string consisting of the concatenation of `name` and a single U+0079 LATIN SMALL LETTER Y character (y).

        4.  The `field` element is `submitter`, and before this algorithm was invoked the user [indicated a coordinate](#220.html_concept-input-type-image-coordinate). Let `x` be the `x`-component of the coordinate selected by the user, and let `y` be the `y`-component of the coordinate selected by the user.

        5.  Append an entry to the `form data set` with the name `name`[`x`], the value `x`, and the type `type`.

        6.  Append an entry to the `form data set` with the name `name`[`y`] and the value `y`, and the type `type`.

        7.  Skip the remaining substeps for this element: if there are any more elements in `controls`, return to the top of the *loop* step, otherwise, jump to the *end* step below.

    4.  Let `name` be the value of the `field` element's [`name`](#220.html_attr-fe-name) attribute.

    5.  If the `field` element is a [`select`](#220.html_the-select-element) element, then for each [`option`](#220.html_the-option-element) element in the [`select`](#220.html_the-select-element) element's [list of options](#220.html_concept-select-option-list) whose [selectedness](#220.html_concept-option-selectedness) is true and that is not [disabled](#220.html_concept-option-disabled), append an entry to the `form data set` with the `name` as the name, the [value](#220.html_concept-option-value) of the [`option`](#220.html_the-option-element) element as the value, and `type` as the type.

    6.  Otherwise, if the `field` element is an [`input`](#220.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#220.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Checkbox](#220.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) state or the [Radio Button](#220.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state, then run these further nested substeps:

        1.  If the `field` element has a [`value`](#220.html_attr-input-value) attribute specified, then let `value` be the value of that attribute; otherwise, let `value` be the string "`on`".

        2.  Append an entry to the `form data set` with `name` as the name, `value` as the value, and `type` as the type.

    7.  Otherwise, if the `field` element is an [`input`](#220.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#220.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [File Upload](#220.html_file-upload-state-(type=file)) state, then for each file [selected](#220.html_concept-input-type-file-selected) in the [`input`](#220.html_the-input-element) element, append an entry to the `form data set` with the `name` as the name, the file (consisting of the name, the type, and the body) as the value, and `type` as the type. If there are no [selected files](#220.html_concept-input-type-file-selected), then append an entry to the `form data set` with the `name` as the name, the empty string as the value, and `application/octet-stream` as the type.

    8.  Otherwise, if the `field` element is an [`object`](#220.html_the-object-element) element: try to obtain a form submission value from the [plugin](#220.html_plugin), and if that is successful, append an entry to the `form data set` with `name` as the name, the returned form submission value as the value, and the string "`object`" as the type.

    9.  Otherwise, append an entry to the `form data set` with `name` as the name, the [value](#220.html_concept-fe-value) of the `field` element as the value, and `type` as the type.

    10.  If the element has a [`dirname`](#220.html_attr-fe-dirname) attribute, and that attribute's value is not the empty string, then run these substeps:

        1.  Let `dirname` be the value of the element's [`dirname`](#220.html_attr-fe-dirname) attribute.

        2.  Let `dir` be the string "`ltr`" if [the directionality](#220.html_the-directionality) of the element is '[ltr](#220.html_concept-ltr)', and "`rtl`" otherwise (i.e. when [the directionality](#220.html_the-directionality) of the element is '[rtl](#220.html_concept-rtl)').

        3.  Append an entry to the `form data set` with `dirname` as the name, `dir` as the value, and the string "`direction`" as the type.

        An element can only have a [`dirname`](#220.html_attr-fe-dirname) attribute if it is a [`textarea`](#220.html_the-textarea-element) element or an [`input`](#220.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#220.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in either the [Text](#220.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) state or the [Search](#220.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) state.

4.  *End*: For the name of each entry in the `form data set`, and for the value of each entry in the `form data set` whose type is not "`file`" or "`textarea`", replace every occurrence of a "CR" (U+000D) character not followed by a "LF" (U+000A) character, and every occurrence of a "LF" (U+000A) character not preceded by a "CR" (U+000D) character, by a two-character string consisting of a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN "CRLF" (U+000A) character pair.

    In the case of the [value](#220.html_concept-fe-value) of [`textarea`](#220.html_the-textarea-element) elements, this newline normalization is already performed during the conversion of the control's [raw value](#220.html_concept-textarea-raw-value) into the control's [value](#220.html_concept-fe-value) (which also performs any necessary line wrapping). In the case of [`input`](#220.html_the-input-element) elements [`type`](#220.html_attr-input-type) attributes in the [File Upload](#220.html_file-upload-state-(type=file)) state, the value is not normalized.

5.  Return the `form data set`.

##### 4.10.22.5 Selecting a form submission encoding

If the user agent is to <dfn id="220.html_picking-an-encoding-for-the-form" data-anolis-xref="picking an encoding for the form">pick an encoding for a form</dfn>, optionally with an *allow non-ASCII-compatible encodings* flag set, it must run the following substeps:

1.  Let `input` be the value of the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element's [`accept-charset`](#220.html_attr-form-accept-charset) attribute.

2.  Let `candidate encoding labels` be the result of [splitting `input` on spaces](#220.html_split-a-string-on-spaces).

3.  Let `candidate encodings` be an empty list of [character encodings](#220.html_encoding).

4.  For each token in `candidate encoding labels` in turn (in the order in which they were found in `input`), [get an encoding](#220.html_getting-an-encoding) for the token and, if this does not result in failure, append the [encoding](#220.html_encoding) to `candidate encodings`.

5.  If the *allow non-ASCII-compatible encodings* flag is not set, remove any encodings that are not [ASCII-compatible character encodings](#220.html_ascii-compatible-character-encoding) from `candidate encodings`.

6.  If `candidate encodings` is empty, return UTF-8 and abort these steps.

7.  Each character encoding in `candidate encodings` can represent a finite number of characters. (For example, UTF-8 can represent all 1.1 million or so Unicode code points, while Windows-1252 can only represent 256.)

    For each encoding in `candidate encodings`, determine how many of the characters in the names and values of the entries in the `form data set` the encoding can represent (without ignoring duplicates). Let `max` be the highest such count. (For UTF-8, `max` would equal the number of characters in the names and values of the entries in the `form data set`.)

    Return the first encoding in `candidate encodings` that can encode `max` characters in the names and values of the entries in the `form data set`.

##### 4.10.22.6 URL-encoded form data

This form data set encoding is in many ways an aberrant monstrosity, the result of many years of implementation accidents and compromises leading to a set of requirements necessary for interoperability, but in no way representing good design practices. In particular, readers are cautioned to pay close attention to the twisted details involving repeated (and in some cases nested) conversions between character encodings and byte sequences.

The <dfn id="220.html_application/x-www-form-urlencoded-encoding-algorithm">`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` encoding algorithm</dfn> is as follows:

1.  Let `result` be the empty string.

2.  If the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element has an [`accept-charset`](#220.html_attr-form-accept-charset) attribute, let the selected character encoding be the result of [picking an encoding for the form](#220.html_picking-an-encoding-for-the-form).

    Otherwise, if the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element has no [`accept-charset`](#220.html_attr-form-accept-charset) attribute, but the [document's character encoding](#220.html_document's-character-encoding) is an [ASCII-compatible character encoding](#220.html_ascii-compatible-character-encoding), then that is the selected character encoding.

    Otherwise, let the selected character encoding be UTF-8.

3.  Let `charset` be the [name](#220.html_encoding-name) of the selected [character encoding](#220.html_encoding).

4.  For each entry in the `form data set`, perform these substeps:

    1.  If the entry's name is "[`_charset_`](#220.html_attr-fe-name-charset)" and its type is "`hidden`", replace its value with `charset`.

    2.  If the entry's type is "`file`", replace its value with the file's name only.

    3.  For each character in the entry's name and value that cannot be expressed using the selected character encoding, replace the character by a string consisting of a U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&), a "#" (U+0023) character, one or more [ASCII digits](#220.html_ascii-digits) representing the Unicode code point of the character in base ten, and finally a ";" (U+003B) character.

    4.  Encode the entry's name and value using the [encoder](#220.html_encoder) for the selected character encoding. The entry's name and value are now byte strings.

    5.  For each byte in the entry's name and value, apply the appropriate subsubsteps from the following list:

        If the byte is 0x20 (U+0020 SPACE if interpreted as ASCII)

        Replace the byte with a single 0x2B byte ("+" (U+002B) character if interpreted as ASCII).

        If the byte is in the range 0x2A, 0x2D, 0x2E, 0x30 to 0x39, 0x41 to 0x5A, 0x5F, 0x61 to 0x7A

        Leave the byte as is.

        Otherwise

        1.  Let `s` be a string consisting of a U+0025 PERCENT SIGN character (%) followed by [uppercase ASCII hex digits](#220.html_uppercase-ascii-hex-digits) representing the hexadecimal value of the byte in question (zero-padded if necessary).

        2.  Encode the string `s` as US-ASCII, so that it is now a byte string.

        3.  Replace the byte in question in the name or value being processed by the bytes in `s`, preserving their relative order.

    6.  Interpret the entry's name and value as Unicode strings encoded in US-ASCII. (All of the bytes in the string will be in the range 0x00 to 0x7F; the high bit will be zero throughout.) The entry's name and value are now Unicode strings again.

    7.  If the entry's name is "[`isindex`](#220.html_attr-fe-name-isindex)", its type is "`text`", and this is the first entry in the `form data set`, then append the value to `result` and skip the rest of the substeps for this entry, moving on to the next entry, if any, or the next step in the overall algorithm otherwise.

    8.  If this is not the first entry, append a single U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&) to `result`.

    9.  Append the entry's name to `result`.

    10.  Append a single "=" (U+003D) character to `result`.

    11.  Append the entry's value to `result`.

5.  Encode `result` as US-ASCII and return the resulting byte stream.

To <dfn id="220.html_application/x-www-form-urlencoded-decoding-algorithm" data-anolis-xref="application/x-www-form-urlencoded decoding algorithm">decode `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` payloads</dfn>, the following algorithm should be used. This algorithm uses as inputs the payload itself, `payload`, consisting of a Unicode string using only characters in the range U+0000 to U+007F; a default character encoding `encoding`; and optionally an `isindex` flag indicating that the payload is to be processed as if it had been generated for a form containing an [`isindex`](#220.html_attr-fe-name-isindex) control. The output of this algorithm is a sorted list of name-value pairs. If the `isindex` flag is set and the first control really was an [`isindex`](#220.html_attr-fe-name-isindex) control, then the first name-value pair will have as its name the empty string.

Which default character encoding to use can only be determined on a case-by-case basis, but generally the best character encoding to use as a default is the one that was used to encode the page on which the form used to create the payload was itself found. In the absence of a better default, UTF-8 is suggested.

The `isindex` flag is for legacy use only. Forms in conforming HTML documents will not generate payloads that need to be decoded with this flag set.

1.  Let `strings` be the result of [strictly splitting the string](#220.html_strictly-split-a-string) `payload` on U+0026 AMPERSAND characters (&).

2.  If the `isindex` flag is set and the first string in `strings` does not contain a "=" (U+003D) character, insert a "=" (U+003D) character at the start of the first string in `strings`.

3.  Let `pairs` be an empty list of name-value pairs.

4.  For each string `string` in `strings`, run these substeps:

    1.  If `string` contains a "=" (U+003D) character, then let `name` be the substring of `string` from the start of `string` up to but excluding its first "=" (U+003D) character, and let `value` be the substring from the first character, if any, after the first "=" (U+003D) character up to the end of `string`. If the first "=" (U+003D) character is the first character, then `name` will be the empty string. If it is the last character, then `value` will be the empty string.

        Otherwise, `string` contains no "=" (U+003D) characters. Let `name` have the value of `string` and let `value` be the empty string.

    2.  Replace any "+" (U+002B) characters in `name` and `value` with U+0020 SPACE characters.

    3.  Replace any escape in `name` and `value` with the character represented by the escape. This replacement must not be recursive.

        An escape is a "%" (U+0025) character followed by two [ASCII hex digits](#220.html_ascii-hex-digits).

        The character represented by an escape is the Unicode character whose code point is equal to the value of the two characters after the "%" (U+0025) character, interpreted as a hexadecimal number (in the range 0..255).

        So for instance the string "`A%2BC`" would become "`A+C`". Similarly, the string "`100%25AA%21`" becomes the string "`100%AA!`".

    4.  Convert the `name` and `value` strings to their byte representation in ISO-8859-1 (i.e. convert the Unicode string to a byte string, mapping code points to byte values directly).

    5.  Add a pair consisting of `name` and `value` to `pairs`.

5.  If any of the name-value pairs in `pairs` have a name component consisting of the string "`_charset_`" encoded in US-ASCII, and the value component of the first such pair, when decoded as US-ASCII, is the name of a supported character encoding, then let `encoding` be that character encoding (replacing the default passed to the algorithm).

6.  Convert the name and value components of each name-value pair in `pairs` to Unicode by interpreting the bytes according to the encoding `encoding`.

7.  Return `pairs`.

Parameters on the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#220.html_application/x-www-form-urlencoded) MIME type are ignored. In particular, this MIME type does not support the `charset` parameter.

##### 4.10.22.7 Multipart form data

The <dfn id="220.html_multipart/form-data-encoding-algorithm">`multipart/form-data` encoding algorithm</dfn> is as follows:

1.  Let `result` be the empty string.

2.  If the algorithm was invoked with an explicit character encoding, let the selected character encoding be that encoding. (This algorithm is used by other specifications, which provide an explicit character encoding to avoid the dependency on the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element described in the next paragraph.)

    Otherwise, if the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element has an [`accept-charset`](#220.html_attr-form-accept-charset) attribute, let the selected character encoding be the result of [picking an encoding for the form](#220.html_picking-an-encoding-for-the-form).

    Otherwise, if the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element has no [`accept-charset`](#220.html_attr-form-accept-charset) attribute, but the [document's character encoding](#220.html_document's-character-encoding) is an [ASCII-compatible character encoding](#220.html_ascii-compatible-character-encoding), then that is the selected character encoding.

    Otherwise, let the selected character encoding be UTF-8.

3.  Let `charset` be the [name](#220.html_encoding-name) of the selected [character encoding](#220.html_encoding).

4.  For each entry in the `form data set`, perform these substeps:

    1.  If the entry's name is "[`_charset_`](#220.html_attr-fe-name-charset)" and its type is "`hidden`", replace its value with `charset`.

    2.  For each character in the entry's name and value that cannot be expressed using the selected character encoding, replace the character by a string consisting of a U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&), a "#" (U+0023) character, one or more [ASCII digits](#220.html_ascii-digits) representing the Unicode code point of the character in base ten, and finally a ";" (U+003B) character.

5.  Encode the (now mutated) `form data set` using the rules described by RFC 2388, Returning Values from Forms: `multipart/form-data`, and return the resulting byte stream. [[RFC2388]](#220.html_refsRFC2388)

    Each entry in the `form data set` is a *field*, the name of the entry is the *field name* and the value of the entry is the *field value*.

    The order of parts must be the same as the order of fields in the `form data set`. Multiple entries with the same name must be treated as distinct fields.

    In particular, this means that multiple files submitted as part of a single `<input type=file multiple>` element will result in each file having its own field; the "sets of files" feature ("`multipart/mixed`") of RFC 2388 is not used.

    The parts of the generated `multipart/form-data` resource that correspond to non-file fields must not have a [`Content-Type`](#220.html_content-type) header specified. Their names and values must be encoded using the character encoding selected above (field names in particular do not get converted to a 7-bit safe encoding as suggested in RFC 2388).

    File names included in the generated `multipart/form-data` resource (as part of file fields) must use the character encoding selected above, though the precise name may be approximated if necessary (e.g. newlines could be removed from file names, quotes could be changed to "%22", and characters not expressible in the selected character encoding could be replaced by other characters). User agents must not use the RFC 2231 encoding suggested by RFC 2388.

    The boundary used by the user agent in generating the return value of this algorithm is the <dfn id="220.html_multipart/form-data-boundary-string">`multipart/form-data` boundary string</dfn>. (This value is used to generate the MIME type of the form submission payload generated by this algorithm.)

For details on how to interpret `multipart/form-data` payloads, see RFC 2388\. [[RFC2388]](#220.html_refsRFC2388)

##### 4.10.22.8 Plain text form data

The <dfn id="220.html_text/plain-encoding-algorithm">`text/plain` encoding algorithm</dfn> is as follows:

1.  Let `result` be the empty string.

2.  If the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element has an [`accept-charset`](#220.html_attr-form-accept-charset) attribute, let the selected character encoding be the result of [picking an encoding for the form](#220.html_picking-an-encoding-for-the-form), with the *allow non-ASCII-compatible encodings* flag unset.

    Otherwise, if the [`form`](#220.html_the-form-element) element has no [`accept-charset`](#220.html_attr-form-accept-charset) attribute, then that is the selected character encoding.

3.  Let `charset` be the [name](#220.html_encoding-name) of the selected [character encoding](#220.html_encoding).

4.  If the entry's name is "[`_charset_`](#220.html_attr-fe-name-charset)" and its type is "`hidden`", replace its value with `charset`.

5.  If the entry's type is "`file`", replace its value with the file's name only.

6.  For each entry in the `form data set`, perform these substeps:

    1.  Append the entry's name to `result`.

    2.  Append a single "=" (U+003D) character to `result`.

    3.  Append the entry's value to `result`.

    4.  Append a "CR" (U+000D) "LF" (U+000A) character pair to `result`.

7.  Encode `result` using the [encoder](#220.html_encoder) for the selected character encoding and return the resulting byte stream.

Payloads using the `text/plain` format are intended to be human readable. They are not reliably interpretable by computer, as the format is ambiguous (for example, there is no way to distinguish a literal newline in a value from the newline at the end of the value).

#### 4.10.23 Resetting a form

When a [`form`](#221.html_the-form-element) element `form` is <dfn id="221.html_concept-form-reset" data-anolis-xref="concept-form-reset">reset</dfn>, the user agent must [fire a simple event](#221.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `reset`, that bubbles and is cancelable, at `form`, and then, if that event is not canceled, must invoke the [reset algorithm](#221.html_concept-form-reset-control) of each [resettable element](#221.html_category-reset) whose [form owner](#221.html_form-owner) is `form`.

Each [resettable element](#221.html_category-reset) defines its own <dfn id="221.html_concept-form-reset-control" data-anolis-xref="concept-form-reset-control">reset algorithm</dfn>. Changes made to form controls as part of these algorithms do not count as changes caused by the user (and thus, e.g., do not cause `input` events to fire).

### 4.11 Scripting

Scripts allow authors to add interactivity to their documents.

Authors are encouraged to use declarative alternatives to scripting where possible, as declarative mechanisms are often more maintainable, and many users disable scripting.

Authors are also encouraged to make their applications degrade gracefully in the absence of scripting support.

#### 4.11.1 The <dfn id="223.html_script">`script`</dfn> element

[Categories](#223.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Metadata content](#223.html_metadata-content-0).

[Flow content](#223.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#223.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Script-supporting element](#223.html_script-supporting-elements-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#223.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [metadata content](#223.html_metadata-content-0) is expected.

Where [phrasing content](#223.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

Where [script-supporting elements](#223.html_script-supporting-elements-0) are expected.

[Content model](#223.html_element-dfn-content-model):

If there is no [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute, depends on the value of the [`type`](#223.html_attr-script-type) attribute, but must match [script content restrictions](#223.html_restrictions-for-contents-of-script-elements).

If there *is* a [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute, the element must be either empty or contain only [script documentation](#223.html_inline-documentation-for-external-scripts) that also matches [script content restrictions](#223.html_restrictions-for-contents-of-script-elements).

[Content attributes](#223.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#223.html_global-attributes)

[`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) - Address of the resource

[`type`](#223.html_attr-script-type) - Type of embedded resource

[`charset`](#223.html_attr-script-charset) - Character encoding of the external script resource

[`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) - Execute script asynchronously

[`defer`](#223.html_attr-script-defer) - Defer script execution

[`crossorigin`](#223.html_attr-script-crossorigin) - How the element handles crossorigin requests

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#223.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#223.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#223.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#223.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLScriptElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString src;
           attribute DOMString type;
           attribute DOMString charset;
           attribute boolean async;
           attribute boolean defer;
           attribute DOMString crossOrigin;
           attribute DOMString text;
};
```

The [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element allows authors to include dynamic script and data blocks in their documents. The element does not [represent](#223.html_represents) content for the user.

When used to include dynamic scripts, the scripts may either be embedded inline or may be imported from an external file using the [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute. If the language is not that described by "`text/javascript`", then the [`type`](#223.html_attr-script-type) attribute must be present, as described below. Whatever language is used, the contents of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element must conform with the requirements of that language's specification.

When used to include data blocks (as opposed to scripts), the data must be embedded inline, the format of the data must be given using the [`type`](#223.html_attr-script-type) attribute, the [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute must not be specified, and the contents of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element must conform to the requirements defined for the format used.

The <dfn id="223.html_attr-script-type" data-anolis-xref="attr-script-type">`type`</dfn> attribute gives the language of the script or format of the data. If the attribute is present, its value must be a [valid MIME type](#223.html_valid-mime-type). The `charset` parameter must not be specified. The default, which is used if the attribute is absent, is "`text/javascript`".

The <dfn id="223.html_attr-script-src" data-anolis-xref="attr-script-src">`src`</dfn> attribute, if specified, gives the address of the external script resource to use. The value of the attribute must be a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#223.html_valid-non-empty-url-potentially-surrounded-by-spaces) identifying a script resource of the type given by the [`type`](#223.html_attr-script-type) attribute, if the attribute is present, or of the type "`text/javascript`", if the attribute is absent. A resource is a script resource of a given type if that type identifies a scripting language and the resource conforms with the requirements of that language's specification.

The <dfn id="223.html_attr-script-charset" data-anolis-xref="attr-script-charset">`charset`</dfn> attribute gives the character encoding of the external script resource. The attribute must not be specified if the [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute is not present.
