If the attribute is set, its value must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](#223.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for one of the [labels](#223.html_encoding-label) of an [encoding](#223.html_encoding), and must specify the same [encoding](#223.html_encoding) as the `charset` parameter of the [Content-Type metadata](#223.html_content-type) of the external file, if any. [[ENCODING]](#223.html_refsENCODING)

The <dfn id="223.html_attr-script-async" data-anolis-xref="attr-script-async">`async`</dfn> and <dfn id="223.html_attr-script-defer" data-anolis-xref="attr-script-defer">`defer`</dfn> attributes are [boolean attributes](#223.html_boolean-attribute) that indicate how the script should be executed. The [`defer`](#223.html_attr-script-defer) and [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) attributes must not be specified if the [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute is not present.

There are three possible modes that can be selected using these attributes. If the [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) attribute is present, then the script will be executed asynchronously, as soon as it is available. If the [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) attribute is not present but the [`defer`](#223.html_attr-script-defer) attribute is present, then the script is executed when the page has finished parsing. If neither attribute is present, then the script is fetched and executed immediately, before the user agent continues parsing the page.

The exact processing details for these attributes are, for mostly historical reasons, somewhat non-trivial, involving a number of aspects of HTML. The implementation requirements are therefore by necessity scattered throughout the specification. The algorithms below (in this section) describe the core of this processing, but these algorithms reference and are referenced by the parsing rules for [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) [start](#223.html_scriptTag) and [end](#223.html_scriptEndTag) tags in HTML, [in foreign content](#223.html_scriptForeignEndTag), and [in XML](#223.html_scriptTagXML), the rules for the [`document.write()`](#223.html_dom-document-write) method, the handling of [scripting](#223.html_scripting), etc.

The [`defer`](#223.html_attr-script-defer) attribute may be specified even if the [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) attribute is specified, to cause legacy Web browsers that only support [`defer`](#223.html_attr-script-defer) (and not [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async)) to fall back to the [`defer`](#223.html_attr-script-defer) behavior instead of the synchronous blocking behavior that is the default.

The <dfn id="223.html_attr-script-crossorigin" data-anolis-xref="attr-script-crossorigin">`crossorigin`</dfn> attribute is a [CORS settings attribute](#223.html_cors-settings-attribute). It controls, for scripts that are obtained from other [origins](#223.html_origin-0), whether error information will be exposed.

Changing the [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src), [`type`](#223.html_attr-script-type), [`charset`](#223.html_attr-script-charset), [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async), [`defer`](#223.html_attr-script-defer), and [`crossorigin`](#223.html_attr-script-crossorigin) attributes dynamically has no direct effect; these attribute are only used at specific times described below.

A [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element has several associated pieces of state.

The first is a flag indicating whether or not the script block has been <dfn id="223.html_already-started">"already started"</dfn>. Initially, [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements must have this flag unset (script blocks, when created, are not "already started"). The [cloning steps](#223.html_concept-node-clone-ext) for [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements must set the "already started" flag on the copy if it is set on the element being cloned.

The second is a flag indicating whether the element was <dfn id="223.html_parser-inserted">"parser-inserted"</dfn>. Initially, [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements must have this flag unset. It is set by the [HTML parser](#223.html_html-parser) and the [XML parser](#223.html_xml-parser) on [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements they insert and affects the processing of those elements.

The third is a flag indicating whether the element will <dfn id="223.html_force-async">"force-async"</dfn>. Initially, [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements must have this flag set. It is unset by the [HTML parser](#223.html_html-parser) and the [XML parser](#223.html_xml-parser) on [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements they insert. In addition, whenever a [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element whose ["force-async"](#223.html_force-async) flag is set has a [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) content attribute added, the element's ["force-async"](#223.html_force-async) flag must be unset.

The fourth is a flag indicating whether or not the script block is <dfn id="223.html_ready-to-be-parser-executed">"ready to be parser-executed"</dfn>. Initially, [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements must have this flag unset (script blocks, when created, are not "ready to be parser-executed"). This flag is used only for elements that are also ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted), to let the parser know when to execute the script.

The last few pieces of state are <dfn id="223.html_the-script-block's-type">`the script block's type`</dfn>, <dfn id="223.html_the-script-block's-character-encoding">`the script block's character encoding`</dfn>, and <dfn id="223.html_the-script-block's-fallback-character-encoding">`the script block's fallback character encoding`</dfn>. They are determined when the script is prepared, based on the attributes on the element at that time, and the [`Document`](#223.html_document) of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element.

When a [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element that is not marked as being ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted) experiences one of the events listed in the following list, the user agent must synchronously [prepare](#223.html_prepare-a-script) the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element:

*   The [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element gets [inserted into a document](#223.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document), at the time the [node is inserted](#223.html_nodes-are-inserted) according to the DOM, after any other [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements inserted at the same time that are earlier in the [`Document`](#223.html_document) in [tree order](#223.html_tree-order).
*   The [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element is [in a `Document`](#223.html_in-a-document) and a node or document fragment is [inserted](#223.html_nodes-are-inserted) into the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element, after any [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements [inserted](#223.html_nodes-are-inserted) at that time.
*   The [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element is [in a `Document`](#223.html_in-a-document) and has a [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute set where previously the element had no such attribute.

To <dfn id="223.html_prepare-a-script" data-anolis-xref="prepare a script">prepare a script</dfn>, the user agent must act as follows:

1.  If the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element is marked as having ["already started"](#223.html_already-started), then the user agent must abort these steps at this point. The script is not executed.

2.  If the element has its ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted) flag set, then set `was-parser-inserted` to true and unset the element's ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted) flag. Otherwise, set `was-parser-inserted` to false.

    This is done so that if parser-inserted [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements fail to run when the parser tries to run them, e.g. because they are empty or specify an unsupported scripting language, another script can later mutate them and cause them to run again.

3.  If `was-parser-inserted` is true and the element does not have an [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) attribute, then set the element's ["force-async"](#223.html_force-async) flag to true.

    This is done so that if a parser-inserted [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element fails to run when the parser tries to run it, but it is later executed after a script dynamically updates it, it will execute asynchronously even if the [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) attribute isn't set.

4.  If the element has no [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute, and its child nodes, if any, consist only of comment nodes and empty [`Text`](#223.html_text-0) nodes, then the user agent must abort these steps at this point. The script is not executed.

5.  If the element is not [in a `Document`](#223.html_in-a-document), then the user agent must abort these steps at this point. The script is not executed.

6.  If either:

    *   the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element has a [`type`](#223.html_attr-script-type) attribute and its value is the empty string, or
    *   the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element has no [`type`](#223.html_attr-script-type) attribute but it has a [`language`](#223.html_attr-script-language) attribute and *that* attribute's value is the empty string, or
    *   the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element has neither a [`type`](#223.html_attr-script-type) attribute nor a [`language`](#223.html_attr-script-language) attribute, then

    ...let [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type) for this [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element be "`text/javascript`".

    Otherwise, if the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element has a [`type`](#223.html_attr-script-type) attribute, let [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type) for this [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element be the value of that attribute with any leading or trailing sequences of [space characters](#223.html_space-character) removed.

    Otherwise, the element has a non-empty [`language`](#223.html_attr-script-language) attribute; let [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type) for this [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element be the concatenation of the string "`text/`" followed by the value of the [`language`](#223.html_attr-script-language) attribute.

    The [`language`](#223.html_attr-script-language) attribute is never conforming, and is always ignored if there is a [`type`](#223.html_attr-script-type) attribute present.

7.  If the user agent does not [support the scripting language](#223.html_support-the-scripting-language) given by [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type) for this [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element, then the user agent must abort these steps at this point. The script is not executed.

8.  If `was-parser-inserted` is true, then flag the element as ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted) again, and set the element's ["force-async"](#223.html_force-async) flag to false.

9.  The user agent must set the element's ["already started"](#223.html_already-started) flag.

    The state of the element at this moment [is later used](#223.html_establish-script-block-source) to determine the script source.

10.  If the element is flagged as ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted), but the element's [`Document`](#223.html_document) is not the [`Document`](#223.html_document) of the parser that created the element, then abort these steps.

11.  If [scripting is disabled](#223.html_concept-n-noscript) for the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element, then the user agent must abort these steps at this point. The script is not executed.

    The definition of [scripting is disabled](#223.html_concept-n-noscript) means that, amongst others, the following scripts will not execute: scripts in [`XMLHttpRequest`](#223.html_xmlhttprequest)'s `responseXML` documents, scripts in `DOMParser`-created documents, scripts in documents created by `XSLTProcessor`'s `transformToDocument` feature, and scripts that are first inserted by a script into a [`Document`](#223.html_document) that was created using the [`createDocument()`](#223.html_dom-domimplementation-createdocument) API. [[XHR]](#223.html_refsXHR) [[DOMPARSING]](#223.html_refsDOMPARSING) [[DOM]](#223.html_refsDOM)

12.  If the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element has an [`event`](#223.html_attr-script-event) attribute and a [`for`](#223.html_attr-script-for) attribute, then run these substeps:

    1.  Let `for` be the value of the [`for`](#223.html_attr-script-for) attribute.

    2.  Let `event` be the value of the [`event`](#223.html_attr-script-event) attribute.

    3.  [Strip leading and trailing whitespace](#223.html_strip-leading-and-trailing-whitespace) from `event` and `for`.

    4.  If `for` is not an [ASCII case-insensitive](#223.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`window`", then the user agent must abort these steps at this point. The script is not executed.

    5.  If `event` is not an [ASCII case-insensitive](#223.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for either the string "`onload`" or the string "`onload()`", then the user agent must abort these steps at this point. The script is not executed.

13.  If the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element has a [`charset`](#223.html_attr-script-charset) attribute, then let [`the script block's character encoding`](#223.html_the-script-block's-character-encoding) for this [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element be the result of [getting an encoding](#223.html_getting-an-encoding) from the value of the [`charset`](#223.html_attr-script-charset) attribute.

    Otherwise, let [`the script block's fallback character encoding`](#223.html_the-script-block's-fallback-character-encoding) for this [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element be the same as [the encoding of the document itself](#223.html_document's-character-encoding).

    Only one of these two pieces of state is set.

14.  If the element has a [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) content attribute, run these substeps:

    1.  Let `src` be the value of the element's [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute.

    2.  If `src` is the empty string, [queue a task](#223.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#223.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `error` at the element, and abort these steps.

    3.  [Resolve](#223.html_resolve-a-url) `src` relative to the element.

    4.  If the previous step failed, [queue a task](#223.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#223.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `error` at the element, and abort these steps.

    5.  Do a [potentially CORS-enabled fetch](#223.html_potentially-cors-enabled-fetch) of the resulting [absolute URL](#223.html_absolute-url), with the *mode* being the current state of the element's [`crossorigin`](#223.html_attr-script-crossorigin) content attribute, the *origin* being the [origin](#223.html_origin-0) of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element's [`Document`](#223.html_document), and the *default origin behaviour* set to *taint*.

        The resource obtained in this fashion can be either [CORS-same-origin](#223.html_cors-same-origin) or [CORS-cross-origin](#223.html_cors-cross-origin). This only affects how error reporting happens.

        For performance reasons, user agents may start fetching the script (as defined above) as soon as the [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute is set, instead, in the hope that the element will be inserted into the document (and that the [`crossorigin`](#223.html_attr-script-crossorigin) attribute won't change value in the meantime). Either way, once the element is [inserted into the document](#223.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document), the load must have started as described in this step. If the UA performs such prefetching, but the element is never inserted in the document, or the [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute is dynamically changed, or the [`crossorigin`](#223.html_attr-script-crossorigin) attribute is dynamically changed, then the user agent will not execute the script so obtained, and the fetching process will have been effectively wasted.

15.  Then, the first of the following options that describes the situation must be followed:

    If the element has a [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute, and the element has a [`defer`](#223.html_attr-script-defer) attribute, and the element has been flagged as ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted), and the element does not have an [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) attribute

    The element must be added to the end of the <dfn id="223.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-when-the-document-has-finished-parsing">list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing</dfn> associated with the [`Document`](#223.html_document) of the parser that created the element.

    The [task](#223.html_concept-task) that the [networking task source](#223.html_networking-task-source) places on the [task queue](#223.html_task-queue) once the [fetching algorithm](#223.html_fetch) has completed must set the element's ["ready to be parser-executed"](#223.html_ready-to-be-parser-executed) flag. The parser will handle executing the script.

    If the element has a [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute, and the element has been flagged as ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted), and the element does not have an [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) attribute

    The element is the [pending parsing-blocking script](#223.html_pending-parsing-blocking-script) of the [`Document`](#223.html_document) of the parser that created the element. (There can only be one such script per [`Document`](#223.html_document) at a time.)

    The [task](#223.html_concept-task) that the [networking task source](#223.html_networking-task-source) places on the [task queue](#223.html_task-queue) once the [fetching algorithm](#223.html_fetch) has completed must set the element's ["ready to be parser-executed"](#223.html_ready-to-be-parser-executed) flag. The parser will handle executing the script.

    If the element does not have a [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute, and the element has been flagged as ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted), and either the parser that created the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) is an [XML parser](#223.html_xml-parser) or it's an [HTML parser](#223.html_html-parser) whose [script nesting level](#223.html_script-nesting-level) is not greater than one, and the [`Document`](#223.html_document) of the [HTML parser](#223.html_html-parser) or [XML parser](#223.html_xml-parser) that created the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element [has a style sheet that is blocking scripts](#223.html_has-a-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts)

    The element is the [pending parsing-blocking script](#223.html_pending-parsing-blocking-script) of the [`Document`](#223.html_document) of the parser that created the element. (There can only be one such script per [`Document`](#223.html_document) at a time.)

    Set the element's ["ready to be parser-executed"](#223.html_ready-to-be-parser-executed) flag. The parser will handle executing the script.

    If the element has a [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute, does not have an [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) attribute, and does not have the ["force-async"](#223.html_force-async) flag set

    The element must be added to the end of the <dfn id="223.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-in-order-as-soon-as-possible">list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible</dfn> associated with the [`Document`](#223.html_document) of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element at the time the [prepare a script](#223.html_prepare-a-script) algorithm started.

    The [task](#223.html_concept-task) that the [networking task source](#223.html_networking-task-source) places on the [task queue](#223.html_task-queue) once the [fetching algorithm](#223.html_fetch) has completed must run the following steps:

    1.  If the element is not now the first element in the [list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible](#223.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-in-order-as-soon-as-possible) to which it was added above, then mark the element as ready but abort these steps without executing the script yet.

    2.  *Execution*: [Execute the script block](#223.html_execute-the-script-block) corresponding to the first script element in this [list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible](#223.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-in-order-as-soon-as-possible).

    3.  Remove the first element from this [list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible](#223.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-in-order-as-soon-as-possible).

    4.  If this [list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible](#223.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-in-order-as-soon-as-possible) is still not empty and the first entry has already been marked as ready, then jump back to the step labeled *execution*.

    If the element has a [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute

    The element must be added to the <dfn id="223.html_set-of-scripts-that-will-execute-as-soon-as-possible">set of scripts that will execute as soon as possible</dfn> of the [`Document`](#223.html_document) of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element at the time the [prepare a script](#223.html_prepare-a-script) algorithm started.

    The [task](#223.html_concept-task) that the [networking task source](#223.html_networking-task-source) places on the [task queue](#223.html_task-queue) once the [fetching algorithm](#223.html_fetch) has completed must [execute the script block](#223.html_execute-the-script-block) and then remove the element from the [set of scripts that will execute as soon as possible](#223.html_set-of-scripts-that-will-execute-as-soon-as-possible).

    Otherwise

    The user agent must immediately [execute the script block](#223.html_execute-the-script-block), even if other scripts are already executing.

Fetching an external script must [delay the load event](#223.html_delay-the-load-event) of the element's document until the [task](#223.html_concept-task) that is [queued](#223.html_queue-a-task) by the [networking task source](#223.html_networking-task-source) once the resource has been [fetched](#223.html_fetch) (defined above) has been run.

The <dfn id="223.html_pending-parsing-blocking-script">pending parsing-blocking script</dfn> of a [`Document`](#223.html_document) is used by the [`Document`](#223.html_document)'s parser(s).

If a [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element that blocks a parser gets moved to another [`Document`](#223.html_document) before it would normally have stopped blocking that parser, it nonetheless continues blocking that parser until the condition that causes it to be blocking the parser no longer applies (e.g. if the script is a [pending parsing-blocking script](#223.html_pending-parsing-blocking-script) because there was [a style sheet that is blocking scripts](#223.html_a-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts) when it was parsed, but then the script is moved to another [`Document`](#223.html_document) before the style sheet loads, the script still blocks the parser until the style sheets are all loaded, at which time the script executes and the parser is unblocked).

When the user agent is required to <dfn id="223.html_execute-the-script-block" data-anolis-xref="execute the script block">execute a script block</dfn>, it must run the following steps:

1.  If the element is flagged as ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted), but the element's [`Document`](#223.html_document) is not the [`Document`](#223.html_document) of the parser that created the element, then abort these steps.

2.  Jump to the appropriate set of steps from the list below:

    If the load resulted in an error (for example a DNS error, or an HTTP 404 error)

    Executing the script block must just consist of [firing a simple event](#223.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `error` at the element.

    If the load was successful

    Executing the script block must consist of running the following steps. For the purposes of these steps, the script is considered to be from an *external file* if, while the [prepare a script](#223.html_prepare-a-script) algorithm above was running for this script, the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element had a [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute specified.

    1.  Initialize <dfn id="223.html_the-script-block's-source">`the script block's source`</dfn> as follows:

        If the script is from an external file and [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type) is a text-based language

        The contents of that file, interpreted as a Unicode string, are the script source.

        To obtain the Unicode string, the user agent run the following steps:

        1.  If the resource's [Content Type metadata](#223.html_content-type), if any, specifies a character encoding, and the user agent supports that encoding, then let `character encoding` be that encoding, and jump to the bottom step in this series of steps.

        2.  If the algorithm above set [`the script block's character encoding`](#223.html_the-script-block's-character-encoding), then let `character encoding` be that encoding, and jump to the bottom step in this series of steps.

        3.  Let `character encoding` be [`the script block's fallback character encoding`](#223.html_the-script-block's-fallback-character-encoding).

        4.  If the specification for [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type) gives specific rules for decoding files in that format to Unicode, follow them, using `character encoding` as the character encoding specified by higher-level protocols, if necessary.

            Otherwise, [decode](#223.html_decode) the file to Unicode, using `character encoding` as the fallback encoding.

            The [decode](#223.html_decode) algorithm overrides `character encoding` if the file contains a BOM.

        If the script is from an external file and [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type) is an XML-based language

        The external file is the script source. When it is later executed, it must be interpreted in a manner consistent with the specification defining the language given by [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type).

        If the script is inline and [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type) is a text-based language

        The value of the [`text`](#223.html_dom-script-text) IDL attribute at the time the element's ["already started"](#223.html_already-started) flag was last set is the script source.

        If the script is inline and [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type) is an XML-based language

        The child nodes of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element at the time the element's ["already started"](#223.html_already-started) flag was last set are the script source.

    2.  [Fire a simple event](#223.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `beforescriptexecute` that bubbles and is cancelable at the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element.

        If the event is canceled, then abort these steps.

    3.  If the script is from an external file, then increment the [ignore-destructive-writes counter](#223.html_ignore-destructive-writes-counter) of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element's [`Document`](#223.html_document). Let `neutralized doc` be that [`Document`](#223.html_document).

    4.  [Create a script](#223.html_create-a-script), using [`the script block's source`](#223.html_the-script-block's-source), the URL from which the script was obtained, [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type) as the scripting language, and the [script settings object](#223.html_script-settings-object) of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element's [`Document`](#223.html_document)'s [`Window`](#223.html_window) object.

        If the script came from a resource that was [fetched](#223.html_fetch) in the steps above, and the resource was [CORS-cross-origin](#223.html_cors-cross-origin), then pass the `muted errors` flag to the [create a script](#223.html_create-a-script) algorithm as well.

        This is where the script is compiled and actually executed.

    5.  Decrement the [ignore-destructive-writes counter](#223.html_ignore-destructive-writes-counter) of `neutralized doc`, if it was incremented in the earlier step.

    6.  [Fire a simple event](#223.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `afterscriptexecute` that bubbles (but is not cancelable) at the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element.

    7.  If the script is from an external file, [fire a simple event](#223.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `load` at the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element.

        Otherwise, the script is internal; [queue a task](#223.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#223.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `load` at the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element.

The IDL attributes <dfn id="223.html_dom-script-src" data-anolis-xref="dom-script-src">`src`</dfn>, <dfn id="223.html_dom-script-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-script-type">`type`</dfn>, <dfn id="223.html_dom-script-charset" data-anolis-xref="dom-script-charset">`charset`</dfn>, <dfn id="223.html_dom-script-defer" data-anolis-xref="dom-script-defer">`defer`</dfn>, each must [reflect](#223.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

The <dfn id="223.html_dom-script-crossorigin" data-anolis-xref="dom-script-crossOrigin">`crossOrigin`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#223.html_reflect) the [`crossorigin`](#223.html_attr-script-crossorigin) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#223.html_limited-to-only-known-values).

The <dfn id="223.html_dom-script-async" data-anolis-xref="dom-script-async">`async`</dfn> IDL attribute controls whether the element will execute asynchronously or not. If the element's ["force-async"](#223.html_force-async) flag is set, then, on getting, the [`async`](#223.html_dom-script-async) IDL attribute must return true, and on setting, the ["force-async"](#223.html_force-async) flag must first be unset, and then the content attribute must be removed if the IDL attribute's new value is false, and must be set to the empty string if the IDL attribute's new value is true. If the element's ["force-async"](#223.html_force-async) flag is *not* set, the IDL attribute must [reflect](#223.html_reflect) the [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) content attribute.

`script` . [`text`](#223.html_dom-script-text) [ = `value` ]

Returns the contents of the element, ignoring child nodes that aren't [`Text`](#223.html_text-0) nodes.

Can be set, to replace the element's children with the given value.

The IDL attribute <dfn id="223.html_dom-script-text" data-anolis-xref="dom-script-text">`text`</dfn> must return a concatenation of the contents of all the [`Text`](#223.html_text-0) nodes that are children of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element (ignoring any other nodes such as comments or elements), in tree order. On setting, it must act the same way as the [`textContent`](#223.html_textcontent) IDL attribute.

When inserted using the [`document.write()`](#223.html_dom-document-write) method, [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements execute (typically synchronously), but when inserted using [`innerHTML`](#223.html_dom-innerhtml) and [`outerHTML`](#223.html_dom-outerhtml) attributes, they do not execute at all.

In this example, two [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements are used. One embeds an external script, and the other includes some data.

```
<script src="game-engine.js"></script>
<script type="text/x-game-map">
........U.........e
o............A....e
.....A.....AAA....e
.A..AAA...AAAAA...e
</script>
```

The data in this case might be used by the script to generate the map of a video game. The data doesn't have to be used that way, though; maybe the map data is actually embedded in other parts of the page's markup, and the data block here is just used by the site's search engine to help users who are looking for particular features in their game maps.

The following sample shows how a script element can be used to define a function that is then used by other parts of the document. It also shows how a [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element can be used to invoke script while the document is being parsed, in this case to initialize the form's output.

```
<script>
 function calculate(form) {
   var price = 52000;
   if (form.elements.brakes.checked)
     price += 1000;
   if (form.elements.radio.checked)
     price += 2500;
   if (form.elements.turbo.checked)
     price += 5000;
   if (form.elements.sticker.checked)
     price += 250;
   form.elements.result.value = price;
 }
</script>
<form name="pricecalc" onsubmit="return false" onchange="calculate(this)">
 <fieldset>
  <legend>Work out the price of your car</legend>
  <p>Base cost: ￡52000.</p>
  <p>Select additional options:</p>
  <ul>
   <li><label><input type=checkbox name=brakes> Ceramic brakes (￡1000)</label></li>
   <li><label><input type=checkbox name=radio> Satellite radio (￡2500)</label></li>
   <li><label><input type=checkbox name=turbo> Turbo charger (￡5000)</label></li>
   <li><label><input type=checkbox name=sticker> "XZ" sticker (￡250)</label></li>
  </ul>
  <p>Total: ￡<output name=result></output></p>
 </fieldset>
 <script>
  calculate(document.forms.pricecalc);
 </script>
</form>
```

##### 4.11.1.1 Scripting languages

A user agent is said to <dfn id="223.html_support-the-scripting-language">support the scripting language</dfn> if each component of [`the script block's type`](#223.html_the-script-block's-type) is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#223.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the corresponding component in the [MIME type](#223.html_mime-type) string of a scripting language that the user agent implements.

The following lists the [MIME type](#223.html_mime-type) strings that user agents must recognize, and the languages to which they refer:

"`application/ecmascript`"
"`application/javascript`"
"`application/x-ecmascript`"
"`application/x-javascript`"
"`text/ecmascript`"
"`text/javascript`"
"`text/javascript1.0`"
"`text/javascript1.1`"
"`text/javascript1.2`"
"`text/javascript1.3`"
"`text/javascript1.4`"
"`text/javascript1.5`"
"`text/jscript`"
"`text/livescript`"
"`text/x-ecmascript`"
"`text/x-javascript`"

JavaScript. [[ECMA262]](#223.html_refsECMA262)

User agents may support other [MIME types](#223.html_mime-type) for other languages, but must not support other [MIME types](#223.html_mime-type) for the languages in the list above. User agents are not required to support the languages listed above.

The following [MIME types](#223.html_mime-type) (with or without parameters) must not be interpreted as scripting languages:

*   "`text/plain`"
*   "`text/xml`"
*   "`application/octet-stream`"
*   "`application/xml`"

These types are explicitly listed here because they are poorly-defined types that are nonetheless likely to be used as formats for data blocks, and it would be problematic if they were suddenly to be interpreted as script by a user agent.

When examining types to determine if they represent supported languages, user agents must not ignore MIME parameters. Types are to be compared including all parameters.

For example, types that include the `charset` parameter will not be recognized as referencing any of the scripting languages listed above.

##### 4.11.1.2 <dfn id="223.html_script-content-restrictions" data-anolis-xref="script content restrictions">Restrictions for contents of `script` elements</dfn>

The easiest and safest way to avoid the rather strange restrictions described in this section is to always escape "`<!--`" as "`<\!--`", "`<script`" as "`<\script`", and "`</script`" as "`<\/script`" when these sequences appear in literals in scripts (e.g. in strings, regular expressions, or comments), and to avoid writing code that uses such constructs in expressions. Doing so avoids the pitfalls that the restrictions in this section are prone to triggering: namely, that, for historical reasons, parsing of [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) blocks in HTML is a strange and exotic practice that acts unintuitively in the face of these sequences.

The [`textContent`](#223.html_textcontent) of a [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element must match the `script` production in the following ABNF, the character set for which is Unicode. [[ABNF]](#223.html_refsABNF)

```
script        = outer *( comment-open inner comment-close outer )

outer         = < any string that doesn't contain a substring that matches not-in-outer >
not-in-outer  = comment-open
inner         = < any string that doesn't contain a substring that matches not-in-inner >
not-in-inner  = comment-close / script-open

comment-open  = "<!--"
comment-close = "-->"
script-open   = "<" s c r i p t tag-end

s             =  %x0053 ; U+0053 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S
s             =/ %x0073 ; U+0073 LATIN SMALL LETTER S
c             =  %x0043 ; U+0043 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER C
c             =/ %x0063 ; U+0063 LATIN SMALL LETTER C
r             =  %x0052 ; U+0052 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER R
r             =/ %x0072 ; U+0072 LATIN SMALL LETTER R
i             =  %x0049 ; U+0049 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I
i             =/ %x0069 ; U+0069 LATIN SMALL LETTER I
p             =  %x0050 ; U+0050 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER P
p             =/ %x0070 ; U+0070 LATIN SMALL LETTER P
t             =  %x0054 ; U+0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T
t             =/ %x0074 ; U+0074 LATIN SMALL LETTER T

tag-end       =  %x0009 ; "tab" (U+0009)
tag-end       =/ %x000A ; "LF" (U+000A)
tag-end       =/ %x000C ; "FF" (U+000C)
tag-end       =/ %x0020 ; U+0020 SPACE
tag-end       =/ %x002F ; "/" (U+002F)
tag-end       =/ %x003E ; ">" (U+003E)
```

When a [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element contains [script documentation](#223.html_inline-documentation-for-external-scripts), there are further restrictions on the contents of the element, as described in the section below.

The following script illustrates this issue. Suppose you have a script that contains a string, as in:

```
var example = 'Consider this string: <!-- <script>';
console.log(example);
```

If one were to put this string directly in a [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) block, it would violate the restrictions above:

```
<script>
  var example = 'Consider this string: <!-- <script>';
  console.log(example);
</script>
```

The bigger problem, though, and the reason why it would violate those restrictions, is that actually the script would get parsed weirdly: *the script block above is not terminated*. That is, what looks like a "`</script>`" end tag in this snippet is actually still part of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) block. The script doesn't execute (since it's not terminated); if it somehow were to execute, as it might if the markup looked as follows, it would fail because the script (highlighted here) is not valid JavaScript:

```
<script>
  var example = 'Consider this string: <!-- <script>';
  console.log(example);
</script>
<!-- despite appearances, this is actually part of the script still! -->
<script>
 ... // this is the same script block still...
</script>
```

What is going on here is that for legacy reasons, "`<!--`" and "`<script`" strings in [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements in HTML need to be balanced in order for the parser to consider closing the block.

By escaping the problematic strings as mentioned at the top of this section, the problem is avoided entirely:

```
<script>
  var example = 'Consider this string: <\!-- <\script>';
  console.log(example);
</script>
<!-- this is just a comment between script blocks -->
<script>
 ... // this is a new script block
</script>
```

It is possible for these sequences to naturally occur in script expressions, as in the following examples:

```
if (x<!--y) { ... }
if ( player<script ) { ... }
```

In such cases the characters cannot be escaped, but the expressions can be rewritten so that the sequences don't occur, as in:

```
if (x < !--y) { ... }
if (!--y > x) { ... }
if (!(--y) > x) { ... }
if (player < script) { ... }
if (script > player) { ... }
```

Doing this also avoids a different pitfall as well: for related historical reasons, the string "<!--" in JavaScript is actually treated as a line comment start, just like "//".

##### 4.11.1.3 <dfn id="223.html_script-documentation" data-anolis-xref="script documentation">Inline documentation for external scripts</dfn>

If a [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element's [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute is specified, then the contents of the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element, if any, must be such that the value of the [`text`](#223.html_dom-script-text) IDL attribute, which is derived from the element's contents, matches the `documentation` production in the following ABNF, the character set for which is Unicode. [[ABNF]](#223.html_refsABNF)

```
documentation = *( *( space / tab / comment ) [ line-comment ] newline )
comment       = slash star *( not-star / star not-slash ) 1*star slash
line-comment  = slash slash *not-newline

; characters
tab           = %x0009 ; "tab" (U+0009)
newline       = %x000A ; "LF" (U+000A)
space         = %x0020 ; U+0020 SPACE
star          = %x002A ; "*" (U+002A)
slash         = %x002F ; "/" (U+002F)
not-newline   = %x0000-0009 / %x000B-10FFFF
                ; a Unicode character other than "LF" (U+000A)
not-star      = %x0000-0029 / %x002B-10FFFF
                ; a Unicode character other than "*" (U+002A)
not-slash     = %x0000-002E / %x0030-10FFFF
                ; a Unicode character other than "/" (U+002F)
```

This corresponds to putting the contents of the element in JavaScript comments.

This requirement is in addition to the earlier restrictions on the syntax of contents of [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements.

This allows authors to include documentation, such as license information or API information, inside their documents while still referring to external script files. The syntax is constrained so that authors don't accidentally include what looks like valid script while also providing a [`src`](#223.html_attr-script-src) attribute.

```
<script src="cool-effects.js">
 // create new instances using:
 //    var e = new Effect();
 // start the effect using .play, stop using .stop:
 //    e.play();
 //    e.stop();
</script>
```

##### 4.11.1.4 Interaction of [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements and XSLT

*This section is non-normative.*

This specification does not define how XSLT interacts with the [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) element. However, in the absence of another specification actually defining this, here are some guidelines for implementors, based on existing implementations:

*   When an XSLT transformation program is triggered by an `<?xml-stylesheet?>` processing instruction and the browser implements a direct-to-DOM transformation, [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements created by the XSLT processor need to be marked ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted) and run in document order (modulo scripts marked [`defer`](#223.html_attr-script-defer) or [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async)), asynchronously while the transformation is occurring.

*   The `XSLTProcessor.transformToDocument()` method adds elements to a [`Document`](#223.html_document) that is not in a [browsing context](#223.html_browsing-context), and, accordingly, any [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements they create need to have their ["already started"](#223.html_already-started) flag set in the [prepare a script](#223.html_prepare-a-script) algorithm and never get executed ([scripting is disabled](#223.html_concept-bc-noscript)). Such [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements still need to be marked ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted), though, such that their [`async`](#223.html_dom-script-async) IDL attribute will return false in the absence of an [`async`](#223.html_attr-script-async) content attribute.

*   The `XSLTProcessor.transformToFragment()` method needs to create a fragment that is equivalent to one built manually by creating the elements using [`document.createElementNS()`](#223.html_dom-document-createelementns). For instance, it needs to create [`script`](#223.html_the-script-element) elements that aren't ["parser-inserted"](#223.html_parser-inserted) and that don't have their ["already started"](#223.html_already-started) flag set, so that they will execute when the fragment is inserted into a document.

The main distinction between the first two cases and the last case is that the first two operate on [`Document`](#223.html_document)s and the last operates on a fragment.

#### 4.11.2 The <dfn>`noscript`</dfn> element

[Categories](#224.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Metadata content](#224.html_metadata-content-0).

[Flow content](#224.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#224.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#224.html_element-dfn-contexts):

In a [`head`](#224.html_the-head-element) element of an [HTML document](#224.html_html-documents), if there are no ancestor [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) elements.

Where [phrasing content](#224.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected in [HTML documents](#224.html_html-documents), if there are no ancestor [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) elements.

[Content model](#224.html_element-dfn-content-model):

When [scripting is disabled](#224.html_concept-n-noscript), in a [`head`](#224.html_the-head-element) element: in any order, zero or more [`link`](#224.html_the-link-element) elements, zero or more [`style`](#224.html_the-style-element) elements, and zero or more [`meta`](#224.html_the-meta-element) elements.

When [scripting is disabled](#224.html_concept-n-noscript), not in a [`head`](#224.html_the-head-element) element: [transparent](#224.html_transparent), but there must be no [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element descendants.

Otherwise: text that conforms to the requirements given in the prose.

[Content attributes](#224.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#224.html_global-attributes)

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#224.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#224.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#224.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#224.html_element-dfn-dom):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#224.html_htmlelement).

The [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element [represents](#224.html_represents) nothing if [scripting is enabled](#224.html_concept-n-script), and [represents](#224.html_represents) its children if [scripting is disabled](#224.html_concept-n-noscript). It is used to present different markup to user agents that support scripting and those that don't support scripting, by affecting how the document is parsed.

When used in [HTML documents](#224.html_html-documents), the allowed content model is as follows:

In a [`head`](#224.html_the-head-element) element, if [scripting is disabled](#224.html_concept-n-noscript) for the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element

The [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element must contain only [`link`](#224.html_the-link-element), [`style`](#224.html_the-style-element), and [`meta`](#224.html_the-meta-element) elements.

In a [`head`](#224.html_the-head-element) element, if [scripting is enabled](#224.html_concept-n-script) for the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element

The [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element must contain only text, except that invoking the [HTML fragment parsing algorithm](#224.html_html-fragment-parsing-algorithm) with the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element as the [`context`](#224.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element and the text contents as the `input` must result in a list of nodes that consists only of [`link`](#224.html_the-link-element), [`style`](#224.html_the-style-element), and [`meta`](#224.html_the-meta-element) elements that would be conforming if they were children of the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element, and no [parse errors](#224.html_parse-error).

Outside of [`head`](#224.html_the-head-element) elements, if [scripting is disabled](#224.html_concept-n-noscript) for the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element

The [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element's content model is [transparent](#224.html_transparent), with the additional restriction that a [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element must not have a [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element as an ancestor (that is, [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) can't be nested).

Outside of [`head`](#224.html_the-head-element) elements, if [scripting is enabled](#224.html_concept-n-script) for the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element

The [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element must contain only text, except that the text must be such that running the following algorithm results in a conforming document with no [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) elements and no [`script`](#224.html_the-script-element) elements, and such that no step in the algorithm causes an [HTML parser](#224.html_html-parser) to flag a [parse error](#224.html_parse-error):

1.  Remove every [`script`](#224.html_the-script-element) element from the document.
2.  Make a list of every [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element in the document. For every [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element in that list, perform the following steps:
    1.  Let the `parent element` be the parent element of the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element.
    2.  Take all the children of the `parent element` that come before the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element, and call these elements `the before children`.
    3.  Take all the children of the `parent element` that come *after* the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element, and call these elements `the after children`.
    4.  Let `s` be the concatenation of all the [`Text`](#224.html_text-0) node children of the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element.
    5.  Set the [`innerHTML`](#224.html_dom-innerhtml) attribute of the `parent element` to the value of `s`. (This, as a side-effect, causes the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element to be removed from the document.)
    6.  Insert `the before children` at the start of the `parent element`, preserving their original relative order.
    7.  Insert `the after children` at the end of the `parent element`, preserving their original relative order.

All these contortions are required because, for historical reasons, the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element is handled differently by the [HTML parser](#224.html_html-parser) based on whether [scripting was enabled or not](#224.html_scripting-flag) when the parser was invoked.

The [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element must not be used in [XML documents](#224.html_xml-documents).

The [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element is only effective in [the HTML syntax](#224.html_syntax), it has no effect in [the XHTML syntax](#224.html_the-xhtml-syntax). This is because the way it works is by essentially "turning off" the parser when scripts are enabled, so that the contents of the element are treated as pure text and not as real elements. XML does not define a mechanism by which to do this.

The [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element has no other requirements. In particular, children of the [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element are not exempt from [form submission](#224.html_form-submission-0), scripting, and so forth, even when [scripting is enabled](#224.html_concept-n-script) for the element.

In the following example, a [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element is used to provide fallback for a script.

```
<form action="calcSquare.php">
 <p>
  <label for=x>Number</label>:
  <input id="x" name="x" type="number">
 </p>
 <script>
  var x = document.getElementById('x');
  var output = document.createElement('p');
  output.textContent = 'Type a number; it will be squared right then!';
  x.form.appendChild(output);
  x.form.onsubmit = function () { return false; }
  x.oninput = function () {
    var v = x.valueAsNumber;
    output.textContent = v + ' squared is ' + v * v;
  };
 </script>
 <noscript>
  <input type=submit value="Calculate Square">
 </noscript>
</form>
```

When script is disabled, a button appears to do the calculation on the server side. When script is enabled, the value is computed on-the-fly instead.

The [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) element is a blunt instrument. Sometimes, scripts might be enabled, but for some reason the page's script might fail. For this reason, it's generally better to avoid using [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element), and to instead design the script to change the page from being a scriptless page to a scripted page on the fly, as in the next example:

```
<form action="calcSquare.php">
 <p>
  <label for=x>Number</label>:
  <input id="x" name="x" type="number">
 </p>
 <input id="submit" type=submit value="Calculate Square">
 <script>
  var x = document.getElementById('x');
  var output = document.createElement('p');
  output.textContent = 'Type a number; it will be squared right then!';
  x.form.appendChild(output);
  x.form.onsubmit = function () { return false; }
  x.oninput = function () {
    var v = x.valueAsNumber;
    output.textContent = v + ' squared is ' + v * v;
  };
  var submit = document.getElementById('submit');
  submit.parentNode.removeChild(submit);
 </script>
</form>
```

The above technique is also useful in XHTML, since [`noscript`](#224.html_the-noscript-element) is not supported in [the XHTML syntax](#224.html_the-xhtml-syntax).

#### 4.11.3 The <dfn>`template`</dfn> element

[Categories](#225.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Metadata content](#225.html_metadata-content-0).

[Flow content](#225.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#225.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Script-supporting element](#225.html_script-supporting-elements-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#225.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [metadata content](#225.html_metadata-content-0) is expected.

Where [phrasing content](#225.html_phrasing-content-1) is expected.

Where [script-supporting elements](#225.html_script-supporting-elements-0) are expected.

As a child of a [`colgroup`](#225.html_the-colgroup-element) element that doesn't have a [`span`](#225.html_attr-colgroup-span) attribute.

[Content model](#225.html_element-dfn-content-model):

Either: [Metadata content](#225.html_metadata-content-0).

Or: [Flow content](#225.html_flow-content-1).

Or: The content model of [`ol`](#225.html_the-ol-element) and [`ul`](#225.html_the-ul-element) elements.

Or: The content model of [`dl`](#225.html_the-dl-element) elements.

Or: The content model of [`figure`](#225.html_the-figure-element) elements.

Or: The content model of [`ruby`](#225.html_the-ruby-element) elements.

Or: The content model of [`object`](#225.html_the-object-element) elements.

Or: The content model of [`video`](#225.html_the-video-element) and [`audio`](#225.html_the-audio-element) elements.

Or: The content model of [`table`](#225.html_the-table-element) elements.

Or: The content model of [`colgroup`](#225.html_the-colgroup-element) elements.

Or: The content model of [`thead`](#225.html_the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#225.html_the-tbody-element), and [`tfoot`](#225.html_the-tfoot-element) elements.

Or: The content model of [`tr`](#225.html_the-tr-element) elements.

Or: The content model of [`fieldset`](#225.html_the-fieldset-element) elements.

Or: The content model of [`select`](#225.html_the-select-element) elements.

[Content attributes](#225.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#225.html_global-attributes)

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#225.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

None

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#225.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#225.html_index-aria-global)

[DOM interface](#225.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
interface HTMLTemplateElement : HTMLElement {
  readonly attribute DocumentFragment content;
};
```

The [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element is used to declare fragments of HTML that can be cloned and inserted in the document by script.

Templates provide a method for declaring inert DOM subtrees and manipulating them to instantiate document fragments with identical contents.

When web pages dynamically alter the contents of their documents (e.g. in response to user interaction or new data arriving from the server), it is common that they require fragments of HTML which may require further modification before use, such as the insertion of values appropriate for the usage context.

The [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element allows for the declaration of document fragments which are unused by the document when loaded, but are parsed as HTML and are available at runtime for use by the web page.

In a rendering, the [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element [represents](#225.html_represents) nothing.

`template` . [`content`](#225.html_dom-template-content)

Returns the contents of the [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element), which are stored in a [`DocumentFragment`](#225.html_documentfragment) associated with a different [`Document`](#225.html_document) so as to avoid the [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) contents interfering with the main [`Document`](#225.html_document). (For example, this avoids form controls from being submitted, scripts from executing, and so forth.)

Each [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element has an associated [`DocumentFragment`](#225.html_documentfragment) object that is its <dfn id="225.html_template-contents">template contents</dfn>. When a [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element is created, the user agent must run the following steps to establish the [template contents](#225.html_template-contents):

1.  Let `doc` be the [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element's [`ownerDocument`](#225.html_dom-node-ownerdocument)'s [appropriate template contents owner document](#225.html_appropriate-template-contents-owner-document).

2.  Create a [`DocumentFragment`](#225.html_documentfragment) object whose [`ownerDocument`](#225.html_dom-node-ownerdocument) is `doc`.

3.  Set the [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element's [template contents](#225.html_template-contents) to the newly created [`DocumentFragment`](#225.html_documentfragment) object.

A [`Document`](#225.html_document) `doc`'s <dfn id="225.html_appropriate-template-contents-owner-document">appropriate template contents owner document</dfn> is the [`Document`](#225.html_document) returned by the following algorithm:

1.  If `doc` is not a [`Document`](#225.html_document) created by this algorithm, run these substeps:

    1.  If `doc` does not yet have an <dfn id="225.html_associated-inert-template-document">associated inert template document</dfn> then run these substeps:

        1.  Let `new doc` be a new [`Document`](#225.html_document) (that does not have a [browsing context](#225.html_browsing-context)). This is "a [`Document`](#225.html_document) created by this algorithm" for the purposes of the step above.

        2.  If `doc` is an [HTML document](#225.html_html-documents), mark `new doc` as an [HTML document](#225.html_html-documents) also.

        3.  Let `doc`'s [associated inert template document](#225.html_associated-inert-template-document) be `new doc`.

    2.  Set `doc` to `doc`'s [associated inert template document](#225.html_associated-inert-template-document).

    Each [`Document`](#225.html_document) not created by this algorithm thus gets a single [`Document`](#225.html_document) to act as its proxy for owning the [template contents](#225.html_template-contents) of all its [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) elements, so that they aren't in a [browsing context](#225.html_browsing-context) and thus remain inert (e.g. scripts do not run). Meanwhile, [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) elements inside [`Document`](#225.html_document) objects that *are* created by this algorithm just reuse the same [`Document`](#225.html_document) owner for their contents.

2.  Return `doc`.

When a [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element changes [`ownerDocument`](#225.html_dom-node-ownerdocument), the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `doc` be the [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element's new [`ownerDocument`](#225.html_dom-node-ownerdocument)'s [appropriate template contents owner document](#225.html_appropriate-template-contents-owner-document).

2.  [Adopt](#225.html_concept-node-adopt) the [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element's [template contents](#225.html_template-contents) (a [`DocumentFragment`](#225.html_documentfragment) object) into `doc`.

The <dfn id="225.html_dom-template-content" data-anolis-xref="dom-template-content">`content`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element's [template contents](#225.html_template-contents).

* * *

The [cloning steps](#225.html_concept-node-clone-ext) for a [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element `node` being cloned to a copy `copy` must run the following steps:

1.  If the `clone children flag` is not set in the calling [clone](#225.html_concept-node-clone) algorithm, abort these steps.

2.  Let `copied contents` be the result of [cloning](#225.html_concept-node-clone) all the children of `node`'s [template contents](#225.html_template-contents), with `ownerDocument` set to `copy`'s [template contents](#225.html_template-contents)'s [`ownerDocument`](#225.html_dom-node-ownerdocument), and with the `clone children flag` set.

3.  Append `copied contents` to `copy`'s [template contents](#225.html_template-contents).

In this example, a script populates a table with data from a data structure, using a [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) to provide the element structure instead of manually generating the structure from markup.

```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<title>Cat data</title>
<script>
 // Data is hard-coded here, but could come from the server
 var data = [
   { name: 'Pillar', color: 'Ticked Tabby', sex: 'Female (neutered)', legs: 3 },
   { name: 'Hedral', color: 'Tuxedo', sex: 'Male (neutered)', legs: 4 },
 ];
</script>
<table>
 <thead>
  <tr>
   <th>Name <th>Color <th>Sex <th>Legs
 <tbody>
  <template id="row">
   <tr><td><td><td><td>
  </template>
</table>
<script>
 var template = document.querySelector('#row');
 for (var i = 0; i < data.length; i += 1) {
   var cat = data[i];
   var clone = template.content.cloneNode(true);
   var cells = clone.querySelectorAll('td');
   cells[0].textContent = cat.name;
   cells[1].textContent = cat.color;
   cells[2].textContent = cat.sex;
   cells[3].textContent = cat.legs;
   template.parentNode.appendChild(clone);
 }
</script>
```

##### 4.11.3.1 Interaction of [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) elements with XSLT and XPath

*This section is non-normative.*

This specification does not define how XSLT and XPath interact with the [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element. However, in the absence of another specification actually defining this, here are some guidelines for implementors, which are intended to be consistent with other processing described in this specification:

*   An XSLT processor based on an XML parser that acts [as described in this specification](#225.html_xml-parser) needs to act as if [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) elements contain as descendants their [template contents](#225.html_template-contents) for the purposes of the transform.

*   An XSLT processor that outputs a DOM needs to ensure that nodes that would go into a [`template`](#225.html_the-template-element) element are instead placed into the element's [template contents](#225.html_template-contents).

*   XPath evaluation using the XPath DOM API when applied to a [`Document`](#225.html_document) parsed using the [HTML parser](#225.html_html-parser) or the [XML parser](#225.html_xml-parser) described in this specification needs to ignore [template contents](#225.html_template-contents).

#### 4.11.4 The <dfn id="226.html_canvas">`canvas`</dfn> element

[Categories](#226.html_element-dfn-categories):

[Flow content](#226.html_flow-content-1).

[Phrasing content](#226.html_phrasing-content-1).

[Embedded content](#226.html_embedded-content-2).

[Palpable content](#226.html_palpable-content-0).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#226.html_element-dfn-contexts):

Where [embedded content](#226.html_embedded-content-2) is expected.

[Content model](#226.html_element-dfn-content-model):

[Transparent](#226.html_transparent).

[Content attributes](#226.html_element-dfn-attributes):

[Global attributes](#226.html_global-attributes)

[`width`](#226.html_attr-canvas-width) - Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#226.html_attr-canvas-height) - Vertical dimension

Tag omission in text/html:

Neither tag is omissible

Allowed [ARIA role attribute](#226.html_aria-role-attribute) values:

[Any role value](#226.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

Allowed [ARIA state and property attributes](#226.html_state-and-property-attributes):

[Global aria-* attributes](#226.html_index-aria-global)

Any `aria-*` attributes [applicable to the allowed roles](#226.html_allowed-aria-roles,-states-and-properties).

[`width`](#226.html_attr-canvas-width)

[`height`](#226.html_attr-canvas-height)

[DOM interface](#226.html_element-dfn-dom):

```
typedef (CanvasRenderingContext2D or WebGLRenderingContext) RenderingContext;

interface HTMLCanvasElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute unsigned long width;
           attribute unsigned long height;

  RenderingContext? getContext(DOMString contextId, any... arguments);

  DOMString toDataURL(optional DOMString type, any... arguments);
  void toBlob(FileCallback? _callback, optional DOMString type, any... arguments);
};
```

The [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element provides scripts with a resolution-dependent bitmap canvas, which can be used for rendering graphs, game graphics, art, or other visual images on the fly.

Authors should not use the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element in a document when a more suitable element is available. For example, it is inappropriate to use a [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element to render a page heading: if the desired presentation of the heading is graphically intense, it should be marked up using appropriate elements (typically [`h1`](#226.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)) and then styled using CSS and supporting technologies such as XBL.

When authors use the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element, they must also provide content that, when presented to the user, conveys essentially the same function or purpose as the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element)' bitmap. This content may be placed as content of the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element. The contents of the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element, if any, are the element's [fallback content](#226.html_fallback-content).

* * *

In interactive visual media, if [scripting is enabled](#226.html_concept-n-script) for the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element, and if support for [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) elements has been enabled, the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element [represents](#226.html_represents) [embedded content](#226.html_embedded-content-2) consisting of a dynamically created image, the element's bitmap.

In non-interactive, static, visual media, if the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element has been previously associated with a rendering context (e.g. if the page was viewed in an interactive visual medium and is now being printed, or if some script that ran during the page layout process painted on the element), then the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element [represents](#226.html_represents) [embedded content](#226.html_embedded-content-2) with the element's current bitmap and size. Otherwise, the element represents its [fallback content](#226.html_fallback-content) instead.

In non-visual media, and in visual media if [scripting is disabled](#226.html_concept-n-noscript) for the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element or if support for [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) elements has been disabled, the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element [represents](#226.html_represents) its [fallback content](#226.html_fallback-content) instead.

When a [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element [represents](#226.html_represents) [embedded content](#226.html_embedded-content-2), the user can still focus descendants of the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element (in the [fallback content](#226.html_fallback-content)). When an element is focused, it is the target of keyboard interaction events (even though the element itself is not visible). This allows authors to make an interactive canvas keyboard-accessible: authors should have a one-to-one mapping of interactive regions to focusable elements in the [fallback content](#226.html_fallback-content). (Focus has no effect on mouse interaction events.) [[DOMEVENTS]](#226.html_refsDOMEVENTS)

* * *

The [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element has two attributes to control the size of the element's bitmap: <dfn id="226.html_attr-canvas-width" data-anolis-xref="attr-canvas-width">`width`</dfn> and <dfn id="226.html_attr-canvas-height" data-anolis-xref="attr-canvas-height">`height`</dfn>. These attributes, when specified, must have values that are [valid non-negative integers](#226.html_valid-non-negative-integer). The [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#226.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) must be used to obtain their numeric values. If an attribute is missing, or if parsing its value returns an error, then the default value must be used instead. The [`width`](#226.html_attr-canvas-width) attribute defaults to 300, and the [`height`](#226.html_attr-canvas-height) attribute defaults to 150.

The intrinsic dimensions of the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element when it [represents](#226.html_represents) [embedded content](#226.html_embedded-content-2) are equal to the dimensions of the element's bitmap.

A [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element can be sized arbitrarily by a style sheet, its bitmap is then subject to the 'object-fit' CSS property. [[CSSIMAGES]](#226.html_refsCSSIMAGES)

* * *

The bitmaps of [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) elements, as well as some of the bitmaps of rendering contexts, such as those described in the HTML Canvas 2D Context specification [[CANVAS2D]](#226.html_refsCANVAS2D), have an <dfn id="226.html_concept-canvas-origin-clean" data-anolis-xref="concept-canvas-origin-clean">origin-clean</dfn> flag, which can be set to true or false. Initially, when the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element is created, its bitmap's [origin-clean](#226.html_concept-canvas-origin-clean) flag must be set to true.

A [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) bitmap can also have a hit region list, as described in the `CanvasRenderingContext2D` section below.

A [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element can have a rendering context bound to it. Initially, it does not have a bound rendering context. To keep track of whether it has a rendering context or not, and what kind of rendering context it is, a [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) also has a <dfn id="226.html_concept-canvas-context-mode" data-anolis-xref="concept-canvas-context-mode">canvas context mode</dfn>, which is initially <dfn id="226.html_concept-canvas-none" data-anolis-xref="concept-canvas-none">none</dfn> but can be changed to either <dfn id="226.html_concept-canvas-direct-2d" data-anolis-xref="concept-canvas-direct-2d">direct-2d</dfn>, <dfn id="226.html_concept-canvas-direct-webgl" data-anolis-xref="concept-canvas-direct-webgl">direct-webgl</dfn>, <dfn id="226.html_concept-canvas-indirect" data-anolis-xref="concept-canvas-indirect">indirect</dfn>, or <dfn id="226.html_concept-canvas-proxied" data-anolis-xref="concept-canvas-proxied">proxied</dfn> by algorithms defined in this specification.

When its [canvas context mode](#226.html_concept-canvas-context-mode) is [none](#226.html_concept-canvas-none), a [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element has no rendering context, and its bitmap must be fully transparent black with an intrinsic width equal to the numeric value of the element's [`width`](#226.html_attr-canvas-width) attribute and an intrinsic height equal to the numeric value of the element's [`height`](#226.html_attr-canvas-height) attribute, those values being interpreted in CSS pixels, and being updated as the attributes are set, changed, or removed.

When a [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element represents [embedded content](#226.html_embedded-content-2), it [provides a paint source](#226.html_provides-a-paint-source) whose width is the element's intrinsic width, whose height is the element's intrinsic height, and whose appearance is the element's bitmap.

Whenever the [`width`](#226.html_attr-canvas-width) and [`height`](#226.html_attr-canvas-height) content attributes are set, removed, changed, or redundantly set to the value they already have, if the [canvas context mode](#226.html_concept-canvas-context-mode) is [direct-2d](#226.html_concept-canvas-direct-2d), the user agent must [set bitmap dimensions](#226.html_concept-canvas-set-bitmap-dimensions) to the numeric values of the [`width`](#226.html_attr-canvas-width) and [`height`](#226.html_attr-canvas-height) content attributes.

The <dfn id="226.html_dom-canvas-width" data-anolis-xref="dom-canvas-width">`width`</dfn> and <dfn id="226.html_dom-canvas-height" data-anolis-xref="dom-canvas-height">`height`</dfn> IDL attributes must [reflect](#226.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name, with the same defaults.

The bitmaps used with [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) elements can have arbitrary pixel densities. Typically, the density will match that of the user's screen.

* * *

`context` = `canvas` . [`getContext`](#226.html_dom-canvas-getcontext)(`contextId` [, ... ])

Returns an object that exposes an API for drawing on the canvas. The first argument specifies the desired API, either "[`2d`](#226.html_canvas-context-2d)" or "[`webgl`](#226.html_canvas-context-webgl)". Subsequent arguments are handled by that API.

The list of defined contexts is given on the [WHATWG Wiki CanvasContexts page](http://wiki.whatwg.org/wiki/CanvasContexts). [[WHATWGWIKI]](#226.html_refsWHATWGWIKI)

Example contexts are the "[`2d`](#226.html_canvas-context-2d)" [[CANVAS2D]](#226.html_refsCANVAS2D) and the "[`webgl`](#226.html_canvas-context-webgl)" context [[WEBGL]](#226.html_refsWEBGL).

Returns null if the given context ID is not supported or if the canvas has already been initialized with some other (incompatible) context type (e.g. trying to get a "[`2d`](#226.html_canvas-context-2d)" context after getting a "[`webgl`](#226.html_canvas-context-webgl)" context).

Each rendering context has a <dfn id="226.html_concept-canvas-context-bitmap-mode" data-anolis-xref="concept-canvas-context-bitmap-mode">context bitmap mode</dfn>, which is one of <dfn id="226.html_concept-canvas-fixed" data-anolis-xref="concept-canvas-fixed">fixed</dfn>, <dfn id="226.html_concept-canvas-unbound" data-anolis-xref="concept-canvas-unbound">unbound</dfn>, or <dfn id="226.html_concept-canvas-bound" data-anolis-xref="concept-canvas-bound">bound</dfn>. Initially, rendering contexts must be in the [unbound](#226.html_concept-canvas-bound) mode.

* * *

The <dfn id="226.html_dom-canvas-getcontext" data-anolis-xref="dom-canvas-getContext">`getContext(``contextId``,` `arguments...``)`</dfn> method of the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element, when invoked, must run the steps in the cell of the following table whose column header describes the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element's [canvas context mode](#226.html_concept-canvas-context-mode) and whose row header describes the method's first argument.

|  | [none](#226.html_concept-canvas-none) | [direct-2d](#226.html_concept-canvas-direct-2d) | [direct-webgl](#226.html_concept-canvas-direct-webgl) | [indirect](#226.html_concept-canvas-indirect) | [proxied](#226.html_concept-canvas-proxied) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| "<dfn id="226.html_canvas-context-2d" data-anolis-xref="canvas-context-2d">`2d`</dfn>" | Set the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element's [context mode](#226.html_concept-canvas-context-mode) to [direct-2d](#226.html_concept-canvas-direct-2d), obtain a `CanvasRenderingContext2D` object as defined in the HTML Canvas 2D Context specification [[CANVAS2D]](#226.html_refsCANVAS2D), set the obtained `CanvasRenderingContext2D` object's [context bitmap mode](#226.html_concept-canvas-context-bitmap-mode) to [fixed](#226.html_concept-canvas-fixed), and return the `CanvasRenderingContext2D` object | Return the same object as was return the last time the method was invoked with this same argument. | Return null. | Throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#226.html_invalidstateerror) exception. | Throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#226.html_invalidstateerror) exception. |
| "<dfn id="226.html_canvas-context-webgl" data-anolis-xref="canvas-context-webgl">`webgl`</dfn>", if the user agent supports the WebGL feature in its current configuration | Follow the instructions given in the WebGL specification's *Context Creation* section to obtain either a [`WebGLRenderingContext`](#226.html_webglrenderingcontext) or null; if the returned value is null, then return null and abort these steps, otherwise, set the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element's [context mode](#226.html_concept-canvas-context-mode) to [direct-webgl](#226.html_concept-canvas-direct-webgl), set the new [`WebGLRenderingContext`](#226.html_webglrenderingcontext) object's [context bitmap mode](#226.html_concept-canvas-context-bitmap-mode) to [fixed](#226.html_concept-canvas-fixed), and return the [`WebGLRenderingContext`](#226.html_webglrenderingcontext) object? [[WEBGL]](#226.html_refsWEBGL) | Return null. | Return the same object as was return the last time the method was invoked with this same argument. | Throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#226.html_invalidstateerror) exception. | Throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#226.html_invalidstateerror) exception. |
