| A vendor-specific extension* | Behave as defined for the extension. | Behave as defined for the extension. | Behave as defined for the extension. | Throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#226.html_invalidstateerror) exception. | Throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#226.html_invalidstateerror) exception. |
| An unsupported value? | Return null. | Return null. | Return null. | Throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#226.html_invalidstateerror) exception. | Throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#226.html_invalidstateerror) exception. |

* Vendors may define experimental contexts using the syntax `vendorname``-``context`, for example, `moz-3d`.

? For example, the "[`webgl`](#226.html_canvas-context-webgl)" value in the case of a user agent having exhausted the graphics hardware's abilities and having no software fallback implementation.

? The second (and subsequent) argument(s) to the method, if any, are ignored in all cases except this one. See the WebGL specification for details.

`url` = `canvas` . [`toDataURL`](#226.html_dom-canvas-todataurl)( [ `type`, ... ] )

Returns a [`data:` URL](#226.html_data-protocol) for the image in the canvas.

The first argument, if provided, controls the type of the image to be returned (e.g. PNG or JPEG). The default is `image/png`; that type is also used if the given type isn't supported. The other arguments are specific to the type, and control the way that the image is generated, as given [in the table below](#226.html_canvas-serialization-arguments).

When trying to use types other than "`image/png`", authors can check if the image was really returned in the requested format by checking to see if the returned string starts with one of the exact strings "`data:image/png,`" or "`data:image/png;`". If it does, the image is PNG, and thus the requested type was not supported. (The one exception to this is if the canvas has either no height or no width, in which case the result might simply be "`data:,`".)

The [`toDataURL()`](#226.html_dom-canvas-todataurl) method returns the data at a resolution of 96dpi.

`canvas` . [`toBlob`](#226.html_dom-canvas-toblob)(`callback` [, `type`, ... ])

Creates a [`Blob`](#226.html_blob) object representing a file containing the image in the canvas, and invokes a callback with a handle to that object.

The second argument, if provided, controls the type of the image to be returned (e.g. PNG or JPEG). The default is `image/png`; that type is also used if the given type isn't supported. The other arguments are specific to the type, and control the way that the image is generated, as given [in the table below](#226.html_canvas-serialization-arguments).

The [`toBlob()`](#226.html_dom-canvas-toblob) method provides the data at a resolution of 96dpi.

The <dfn id="226.html_dom-canvas-todataurl" data-anolis-xref="dom-canvas-toDataURL">`toDataURL()`</dfn> method must run the following steps:

1.  If the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element's bitmap's [origin-clean](#226.html_concept-canvas-origin-clean) flag is set to false, throw a [`SecurityError`](#226.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps.

2.  If the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element's bitmap has no pixels (i.e. either its horizontal dimension or its vertical dimension is zero) then return the string "`data:,`" and abort these steps. (This is the shortest [`data:` URL](#226.html_data-protocol); it represents the empty string in a `text/plain` resource.)

3.  Let `file` be [a serialization of the `canvas` element's bitmap as a file](#226.html_a-serialization-of-the-bitmap-as-a-file), using the method's arguments (if any) as the `arguments`.

4.  Return a [`data:` URL](#226.html_data-protocol) representing `file`. [[RFC2397]](#226.html_refsRFC2397)

The <dfn id="226.html_dom-canvas-toblob" data-anolis-xref="dom-canvas-toBlob">`toBlob()`</dfn> method must run the following steps:

1.  If the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element's bitmap's [origin-clean](#226.html_concept-canvas-origin-clean) flag is set to false, throw a [`SecurityError`](#226.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps.

2.  Let `callback` be the first argument.

3.  Let `arguments` be the second and subsequent arguments to the method, if any.

4.  If the [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element's bitmap has no pixels (i.e. either its horizontal dimension or its vertical dimension is zero) then let `result` be null.

    Otherwise, let `result` be a [`Blob`](#226.html_blob) object representing [a serialization of the `canvas` element's bitmap as a file](#226.html_a-serialization-of-the-bitmap-as-a-file), using `arguments`. [[FILEAPI]](#226.html_refsFILEAPI)

5.  Return, but continue running these steps asynchronously.

6.  If `callback` is null, abort these steps.

7.  [Queue a task](#226.html_queue-a-task) to invoke the [`FileCallback`](#226.html_filecallback) `callback` with `result` as its argument. The [task source](#226.html_task-source) for this task is the <dfn id="226.html_canvas-blob-serialization-task-source">canvas blob serialization task source</dfn>.

##### 4.11.4.1 Color spaces and color correction

The [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) APIs must perform color correction at only two points: when rendering images with their own gamma correction and color space information onto a bitmap, to convert the image to the color space used by the bitmaps (e.g. using the 2D Context's `drawImage()` method with an [`HTMLImageElement`](#226.html_htmlimageelement) object), and when rendering the actual canvas bitmap to the output device.

Thus, in the 2D context, colors used to draw shapes onto the canvas will exactly match colors obtained through the `getImageDataHD()` method.

The [`toDataURL()`](#226.html_dom-canvas-todataurl) method must not include color space information in the resources it returns. Where the output format allows it, the color of pixels in resources created by [`toDataURL()`](#226.html_dom-canvas-todataurl) must match those returned by the `getImageData()` method.

In user agents that support CSS, the color space used by a [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element must match the color space used for processing any colors for that element in CSS.

The gamma correction and color space information of images must be handled in such a way that an image rendered directly using an [`img`](#226.html_the-img-element) element would use the same colors as one painted on a [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) element that is then itself rendered. Furthermore, the rendering of images that have no color correction information (such as those returned by the [`toDataURL()`](#226.html_dom-canvas-todataurl) method) must be rendered with no color correction.

##### 4.11.4.2 Serializing bitmaps to a file

When a user agent is to create <dfn id="226.html_a-serialization-of-the-bitmap-as-a-file">a serialization of the bitmap as a file</dfn>, optionally with some given `arguments`, it must create an image file in the format given by the first value of `arguments`, or, if there are no `arguments`, in the PNG format. [[PNG]](#226.html_refsPNG)

If if the bitmap has one pixel per coordinate space unit then the image file must have the same pixel data (before compression, if applicable) as the bitmap, and if the file format used supports encoding resolution metadata, the resolution of that bitmap (device pixels per coordinate space units being interpreted as image pixels per CSS pixel) must be given as well.

Otherwise, the image file's pixel data must be the bitmap's pixel data scaled to one image pixel per coordinate space unit, and if the file format used supports encoding resolution metadata, the resolution must be given as 96dpi (one image pixel per CSS pixel).

If `arguments` is not empty, the first value must be interpreted as a [MIME type](#226.html_mime-type) giving the format to use. If the type has any parameters, it must be treated as not supported.

For example, the value "`image/png`" would mean to generate a PNG image, the value "`image/jpeg`" would mean to generate a JPEG image, and the value "`image/svg+xml`" would mean to generate an SVG image (which would require that the user agent track how the bitmap was generated, an unlikely, though potentially awesome, feature).

User agents must support PNG ("`image/png`"). User agents may support other types. If the user agent does not support the requested type, it must create the file using the PNG format. [[PNG]](#226.html_refsPNG)

User agents must [convert the provided type to ASCII lowercase](#226.html_converted-to-ascii-lowercase) before establishing if they support that type.

For image types that do not support an alpha channel, the serialized image must be the bitmap image composited onto a solid black background using the source-over operator.

If the first argument in `arguments` gives a type corresponding to one of the types given in the first column of the following table, and the user agent supports that type, then the subsequent arguments, if any, must be treated as described in the second cell of that row.

Arguments for serialization methods

| Type | Other arguments | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image/jpeg` | The second argument, if it is a number in the range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive, must be treated as the desired quality level. If it is not a number or is outside that range, the user agent must use its default value, as if the argument had been omitted. | [[JPEG]](#226.html_refsJPEG) |

For the purposes of these rules, an argument is considered to be a number if it is converted to an IDL double value by the rules for handling arguments of type `any` in the Web IDL specification. [[WEBIDL]](#226.html_refsWEBIDL)

Other arguments must be ignored and must not cause the user agent to throw an exception. A future version of this specification will probably define other parameters to be passed to these methods to allow authors to more carefully control compression settings, image metadata, etc.

##### 4.11.4.3 Security with [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) elements

*This section is non-normative.*

**Information leakage** can occur if scripts from one [origin](#226.html_origin-0) can access information (e.g. read pixels) from images from another origin (one that isn't the [same](#226.html_same-origin)).

To mitigate this, bitmaps used with [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element) elements are defined to have a flag indicating whether they are [origin-clean](#226.html_concept-canvas-origin-clean). All bitmaps start with their [origin-clean](#226.html_concept-canvas-origin-clean) set to true. The flag is set to false when cross-origin images or fonts are used.

The [`toDataURL()`](#226.html_dom-canvas-todataurl), [`toBlob()`](#226.html_dom-canvas-toblob), `getImageData()`, and `getImageDataHD()` methods check the flag and will throw a [`SecurityError`](#226.html_securityerror) exception rather than leak cross-origin data.

The flag can be reset in certain situations; for example, when a `CanvasRenderingContext2D` is bound to a new [`canvas`](#226.html_the-canvas-element), the bitmap is cleared and its flag reset.

### 4.12 Common idioms without dedicated elements

#### 4.12.1 Subheadings, subtitles, alternative titles and taglines

HTML does not have a dedicated mechanism for marking up subheadings, alternative titles or taglines. Here are the suggested alternatives.

[`h1`](#228.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)–[`h6`](#228.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) elements must not be used to markup subheadings, subtitles, alternative titles and taglines unless intended to be the heading for a new section or subsection.

In the following example the title and subtitles of a web page are grouped using a [`header`](#228.html_the-header-element) element. As the author does not want the subtitles to be included the table of contents and they are not intended to signify the start of a new section, they are marked up using [`p`](#228.html_the-p-element) elements. A sample CSS styled rendering of the title and subtitles is provided below the code example.

```
 <header>
   <h1>HTML 5.1 Nightly</h1>
   <p>A vocabulary and associated APIs for HTML and XHTML</p>
   <p>Editor's Draft 9 May 2013</p>
   </header> 
```

![Title:'HTML 5.1 Nightly' in a mid blue Sans Serif font. Subtitle 1:'A vocabulary and associated APIs for HTML and XHTML' on a new line, same style smaller font size. Subtitle 2:'Editor's Draft 9 May 2013' on a new line, same style and size as subtitle 1.](Images/4db261f38395a13577765363dd607d1e.jpg)

In the following example the subtitle of a book is on the same line as the title separated by a colon. A sample CSS styled rendering of the title and subtitle is provided below the code example.

```
<h1>The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers</h1>
```

![Title and subtitle:'The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers' in a gold coloured Gothic style Serif font on a black background.](Images/df3e442f58d7a1a186a2856b7a8da3a3.jpg)

In the following example part of an album title is included in a [`span`](#228.html_the-span-element) element, allowing it to be styled differently from the rest of the title. A [`br`](#228.html_the-br-element) element is used to place the album title on a new line. A sample CSS styled rendering of the heading is provided below the code example.

```
 <h1>Ramones <br>
   <span>Hey! Ho! Let's Go</span> 
   </h1>
```

![ Line 1:'Ramones' displayed in a large bold angular hand writing style font with a spray can paint effect. Line 2:'Hey! Ho! Let's Go' displayed in a smaller, standard sans serif style font.](Images/deb851cbc47c2293457826a6c7d4d1e0.jpg)

In the following example the title and tagline for a news article are grouped using a [`header`](#228.html_the-header-element) element. The title is marked up using a [`h2`](#228.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element and the tagline is in a [`p`](#228.html_the-p-element) element. A sample CSS styled rendering of the title and tagline is provided below the code example.

```
 <header>
   <h2>3D films set for popularity slide </h2>
   <p>First drop in 3D box office projected for this year despite hotly tipped summer blockbusters,
    according to Fitch Ratings report</p>
   </header> 
```

![ Title:'3D films set for popularity slide' in a large, bold, dark blue Serif font style. Paragraph: 'First drop in 3D box office projected for this year despite...' in a smaller, dark grey, Sans Serif font style.](Images/a74500959648b7c4f58256a0343b4597.jpg)

In this last example the title and taglines for a news magazine are grouped using a [`header`](#228.html_the-header-element) element. The title is marked up using a [`h1`](#228.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element and the taglines are each in a [`p`](#228.html_the-p-element) element. A sample CSS styled rendering of the title and taglines is provided below the code example.

```
 <header>
   <p>Magazine of the Decade</p>
   <h1>THE MONTH</h1>
   <p>The Best of UK and Foreign Media</p>
   </header> 
```

![Tagline above the heading:'Magazine of the Decade'. Tagline below the heading 'The Best of UK and Foreign Media' both in a small,all caps, sans-serif font style. Heading:'The Month' in a large, Serif font style. All text is black against a red background.](Images/aceee6228aaa7e157ce16eb2ea13a80c.jpg)

#### 4.12.2 Bread crumb navigation

This specification does not provide a machine-readable way of describing bread-crumb navigation menus. Authors are encouraged to markup bread-crumb navigation as a list. The [`nav`](#229.html_the-nav-element) element can be used to mark the list containing links as being a navigation block.

In the following example, the current page can be reached via the path indicated. The path is indicated using the right arrow symbol "→". A text label is provided to give the user context. The links are structured as a list, which provides users with an indication of item number.

```
 <nav>
   <h2>You are here:</h2>
   <ul id="navlist">
   <li><a href="/">Main</a> →</li> 
   <li><a href="/products/">Products</a> →</li> 
   <li><a href="/products/dishwashers/">Dishwashers</a> →</li> 
   <li><a>Second hand</a></li> 
   </ul>
   </nav> 
```

The breadcrumb code example could be styled as a horizonatal list using CSS:

![The heading and the links are displayed on one line.](Images/d2e550caca70b506886b1e4d53c84b6f.jpg)

The use of the right angle bracket symbol ">" to indicate path direction is discouraged as its meaning, in the context used, is not clearly conveyed to all users.

#### 4.12.3 Tag clouds

This specification does not define any markup specifically for marking up lists of keywords that apply to a group of pages (also known as *tag clouds*). In general, authors are encouraged to either mark up such lists using [`ul`](#230.html_the-ul-element) elements with explicit inline counts that are then hidden and turned into a presentational effect using a style sheet, or to use SVG.

Here, three tags are included in a short tag cloud:

```
<style>
@media screen, print, handheld, tv {
  /* should be ignored by non-visual browsers */
  .tag-cloud > li > span { display: none; }
  .tag-cloud > li { display: inline; }
  .tag-cloud-1 { font-size: 0.7em; }
  .tag-cloud-2 { font-size: 0.9em; }
  .tag-cloud-3 { font-size: 1.1em; }
  .tag-cloud-4 { font-size: 1.3em; }
  .tag-cloud-5 { font-size: 1.5em; }
}
</style>
...
<ul class="tag-cloud">
 <li class="tag-cloud-4"><a title="28 instances" href="/t/apple">apple</a> <span>(popular)</span>
 <li class="tag-cloud-2"><a title="6 instances"  href="/t/kiwi">kiwi</a> <span>(rare)</span>
 <li class="tag-cloud-5"><a title="41 instances" href="/t/pear">pear</a> <span>(very popular)</span>
</ul>
```

The actual frequency of each tag is given using the [`title`](#230.html_attr-title) attribute. A CSS style sheet is provided to convert the markup into a cloud of differently-sized words, but for user agents that do not support CSS or are not visual, the markup contains annotations like "(popular)" or "(rare)" to categorize the various tags by frequency, thus enabling all users to benefit from the information.

The [`ul`](#230.html_the-ul-element) element is used (rather than [`ol`](#230.html_the-ol-element)) because the order is not particularly important: while the list is in fact ordered alphabetically, it would convey the same information if ordered by, say, the length of the tag.

The [`tag`](#230.html_link-type-tag) [`rel`](#230.html_attr-hyperlink-rel)-keyword is *not* used on these [`a`](#230.html_the-a-element) elements because they do not represent tags that apply to the page itself; they are just part of an index listing the tags themselves.

#### 4.12.4 Conversations

This specification does not define a specific element for marking up conversations, meeting minutes, chat transcripts, dialogues in screenplays, instant message logs, and other situations where different players take turns in discourse.

Instead, authors are encouraged to mark up conversations using [`p`](#231.html_the-p-element) elements and punctuation. Authors who need to mark the speaker for styling purposes are encouraged to use [`span`](#231.html_the-span-element) or [`b`](#231.html_the-b-element). Paragraphs with their text wrapped in the [`i`](#231.html_the-i-element) element can be used for marking up stage directions.

This example demonstrates this using an extract from Abbot and Costello's famous sketch, Who's on first:

```
<p> Costello: Look, you gotta first baseman?
<p> Abbott: Certainly.
<p> Costello: Who's playing first?
<p> Abbott: That's right.
<p> Costello becomes exasperated.
<p> Costello: When you pay off the first baseman every month, who gets the money?
<p> Abbott: Every dollar of it.
```

The following extract shows how an IM conversation log could be marked up, using the [`data`](#231.html_the-data-element) element to provide Unix timestamps for each line. Note that the timestamps are provided in a format that the [`time`](#231.html_the-time-element) element does not support, so the [`data`](#231.html_the-data-element) element is used instead (namely, Unix `time_t` timestamps). Had the author wished to mark up the data using one of the date and time formats supported by the [`time`](#231.html_the-time-element) element, that element could have been used instead of [`data`](#231.html_the-data-element). This could be advantageous as it would allow data analysis tools to detect the timestamps unambiguously, without coordination with the page author.

```
<p> <data value="1319898155">14:22</data> <b>egof</b> I'm not that nerdy, I've only seen 30% of the star trek episodes
<p> <data value="1319898192">14:23</data> <b>kaj</b> if you know what percentage of the star trek episodes you have seen, you are inarguably nerdy
<p> <data value="1319898200">14:23</data> <b>egof</b> it's unarguably
<p> <data value="1319898228">14:23</data> <i>* kaj blinks</i>
<p> <data value="1319898260">14:24</data> <b>kaj</b> you are not helping your case
```

HTML does not have a good way to mark up graphs, so descriptions of interactive conversations from games are more difficult to mark up. This example shows one possible convention using [`dl`](#231.html_the-dl-element) elements to list the possible responses at each point in the conversation. Another option to consider is describing the conversation in the form of a DOT file, and outputting the result as an SVG image to place in the document. [[DOT]](#231.html_refsDOT)

```
<p> Next, you meet a fisherman. You can say one of several greetings:
<dl>
 <dt> "Hello there!"
 <dd>
  <p> He responds with "Hello, how may I help you?"; you can respond with:
  <dl>
   <dt> "I would like to buy a fish."
   <dd> <p> He sells you a fish and the conversation finishes.
   <dt> "Can I borrow your boat?"
   <dd>
    <p> He is surprised and asks "What are you offering in return?".
    <dl>
     <dt> "Five gold." (if you have enough)
     <dt> "Ten gold." (if you have enough)
     <dt> "Fifteen gold." (if you have enough)
     <dd> <p> He lends you his boat. The conversation ends.
     <dt> "A fish." (if you have one)
     <dt> "A newspaper." (if you have one)
     <dt> "A pebble." (if you have one)
     <dd> <p> "No thanks", he replies. Your conversation options        
     at this point are the same as they were after asking to borrow
     his boat, minus any options you've suggested before.
    </dl>
   </dd>
  </dl>
 </dd>
 <dt> "Vote for me in the next election!"
 <dd> <p> He turns away. The conversation finishes.
 <dt> "Sir, are you aware that your fish are running away?"
 <dd>
  <p> He looks at you skeptically and says "Fish cannot run, sir".
  <dl>
   <dt> "You got me!"
   <dd> <p> The fisherman sighs and the conversation ends.
   <dt> "Only kidding."
   <dd> <p> "Good one!" he retorts. Your conversation options at this
   point are the same as those following "Hello there!" above.
   <dt> "Oh, then what are they doing?"
   <dd> <p> He looks at his fish, giving you an opportunity to steal
   his boat, which you do. The conversation ends.
  </dl>
 </dd>
</dl>
```

In some games, conversations are simpler: each character merely has a fixed set of lines that they say. In this example, a game FAQ/walkthrough lists some of the known possible responses for each character:

```
<section>
 <h1>Dialogue</h1>
 <p><small>Some characters repeat their lines in order each time you interact
 with them, others randomly pick from amongst their lines. Those who respond in
 order have numbered entries in the lists below.</small>
 <h2>The Shopkeeper</h2>
 <ul>
  <li>How may I help you?
  <li>Fresh apples!
  <li>A loaf of bread for madam?
 </ul>
 <h2>The pilot</h2>
 <p>Before the accident:
 <ul>
  </li>I'm about to fly out, sorry!
  </li>Sorry, I'm just waiting for flight clearance and then I'll be off!
 </ul>
 <p>After the accident:
 <ol>
  <li>I'm about to fly out, sorry!
  <li>Ok, I'm not leaving right now, my plane is being cleaned.
  <li>Ok, it's not being cleaned, it needs a minor repair first.
  <li>Ok, ok, stop bothering me! Truth is, I had a crash.
 </ol>
 <h2>Clan Leader</h2>
 <p>During the first clan meeting:
 <ul>
  <li>Hey, have you seen my daughter? I bet she's up to something nefarious again...
  <li>Nice weather we're having today, eh?
  <li>The name is Bailey, Jeff Bailey. How can I help you today?
  <li>A glass of water? Fresh from the well!
 </ul>
 <p>After the earthquake:
 <ol>
  <li>Everyone is safe in the shelter, we just have to put out the fire!
  <li>I'll go and tell the fire brigade, you keep hosing it down!
 </ol>
</section>
```

#### 4.12.5 Footnotes

HTML does not have a dedicated mechanism for marking up footnotes. Here are the suggested alternatives.

* * *

For annotations, the [`a`](#232.html_the-a-element) element should be used, pointing to an element later in the document. The convention is that the contents of the link be a number in square brackets.

In this example, a footnote in the dialogue links to a paragraph below the dialogue. The paragraph then reciprocally links back to the dialogue, allowing the user to return to the location of the footnote.

```
<p> Announcer: Number 16: The <i>hand</i>.
<p> Interviewer: Good evening. I have with me in the studio tonight
Mr Norman St John Polevaulter, who for the past few years has been
contradicting people. Mr Polevaulter, why <em>do</em> you
contradict people?
<p> Norman: I don't. <sup><a href="#fn1" id="r1">[1]</a></sup>
<p> Interviewer: You told me you did!
...
<section>
 <p id="fn1"><a href="#r1">[1]</a> This is, naturally, a lie,
 but paradoxically if it were true he could not say so without
 contradicting the interviewer and thus making it false.</p>
</section>
```

* * *

For side notes, longer annotations that apply to entire sections of the text rather than just specific words or sentences, the [`aside`](#232.html_the-aside-element) element should be used.

In this example, a sidebar is given after a dialogue, giving it some context.

```
<p> <span class="speaker">Customer</span>: I will not buy this record, it is scratched.
<p> <span class="speaker">Shopkeeper</span>: I'm sorry?
<p> <span class="speaker">Customer</span>: I will not buy this record, it is scratched.
<p> <span class="speaker">Shopkeeper</span>: No no no, this's'a tobacconist's.
<aside>
 <p>In 1970, the British Empire lay in ruins, and foreign
 nationalists frequented the streets — many of them Hungarians
 (not the streets — the foreign nationals). Sadly, Alexander
 Yalt has been publishing incompetently-written phrase books.
</aside>
```

* * *

For figures or tables, footnotes can be included in the relevant [`figcaption`](#232.html_the-figcaption-element) or [`caption`](#232.html_the-caption-element) element, or in surrounding prose.

In this example, a table has cells with footnotes that are given in prose. A [`figure`](#232.html_the-figure-element) element is used to give a single legend to the combination of the table and its footnotes.

```
<figure>
 <figcaption>Table 1\. Alternative activities for knights.</figcaption>
 <table>
  <tr>
   <th> Activity
   <th> Location
   <th> Cost
  <tr>
   <td> Dance
   <td> Wherever possible
   <td> ￡0<sup><a href="#fn1">1</a></sup>
  <tr>
   <td> Routines, chorus scenes<sup><a href="#fn2">2</a></sup>
   <td> Undisclosed
   <td> Undisclosed
  <tr>
   <td> Dining<sup><a href="#fn3">3</a></sup>
   <td> Camelot
   <td> Cost of ham, jam, and spam<sup><a href="#fn4">4</a></sup>
 </table>
 <p id="fn1">1\. Assumed.</p>
 <p id="fn2">2\. Footwork impeccable.</p>
 <p id="fn3">3\. Quality described as "well".</p>
 <p id="fn4">4\. A lot.</p>
</figure>
```

### 4.13 Disabled elements

An element is said to be <dfn id="233.html_concept-element-disabled" data-anolis-xref="concept-element-disabled">actually disabled</dfn> if it falls into one of the following categories:

*   [`button`](#233.html_the-button-element) elements that are [disabled](#233.html_concept-fe-disabled)
*   [`input`](#233.html_the-input-element) elements that are [disabled](#233.html_concept-fe-disabled)
*   [`select`](#233.html_the-select-element) elements that are [disabled](#233.html_concept-fe-disabled)
*   [`textarea`](#233.html_the-textarea-element) elements that are [disabled](#233.html_concept-fe-disabled)
*   [`optgroup`](#233.html_the-optgroup-element) elements that have a [`disabled`](#233.html_attr-optgroup-disabled) attribute
*   [`option`](#233.html_the-option-element) elements that are [disabled](#233.html_concept-option-disabled)
*   [`fieldset`](#233.html_the-fieldset-element) elements that have a [`disabled`](#233.html_attr-fieldset-disabled) attribute

This definition is used to determine what elements can be [focused](#233.html_specially-focusable) and which elements match the [`:disabled`](#233.html_selector-disabled) pseudo-class.

### 4.14 Matching HTML elements using selectors

#### 4.14.1 Case-sensitivity

The Selectors specification leaves the case-sensitivity of IDs, classes, element names, attribute names, and attribute values to be defined by the host language. [[SELECTORS]](#235.html_refsSELECTORS)

The [unique identifier](#235.html_concept-id) of [HTML elements](#235.html_html-elements) in documents that are in [quirks mode](#235.html_quirks-mode) must be treated as [ASCII case-insensitive](#235.html_ascii-case-insensitive) for the purposes of selector matching.

Classes from the [`class`](#235.html_classes) attribute of [HTML elements](#235.html_html-elements) in documents that are in [quirks mode](#235.html_quirks-mode) must be treated as [ASCII case-insensitive](#235.html_ascii-case-insensitive) for the purposes of selector matching.

When comparing a CSS element type selector to the names of [HTML elements](#235.html_html-elements) in [HTML documents](#235.html_html-documents), the CSS element type selector must first be [converted to ASCII lowercase](#235.html_converted-to-ascii-lowercase). The same selector when compared to other elements must be compared according to its original case. In both cases, the comparison is [case-sensitive](#235.html_case-sensitive).

When comparing the name part of a CSS attribute selector to the names of namespace-less attributes on [HTML elements](#235.html_html-elements) in [HTML documents](#235.html_html-documents), the name part of the CSS attribute selector must first be [converted to ASCII lowercase](#235.html_converted-to-ascii-lowercase). The same selector when compared to other attributes must be compared according to its original case. In both cases, the comparison is [case-sensitive](#235.html_case-sensitive).

Everything else (attribute values on [HTML elements](#235.html_html-elements), IDs and classes in [no-quirks mode](#235.html_no-quirks-mode) and [limited-quirks mode](#235.html_limited-quirks-mode), and element names, attribute names, and attribute values in [XML documents](#235.html_xml-documents)) must be treated as [case-sensitive](#235.html_case-sensitive) for the purposes of selector matching.

#### 4.14.2 Pseudo-classes

There are a number of dynamic selectors that can be used with HTML. This section defines when these selectors match HTML elements. [[SELECTORS]](#236.html_refsSELECTORS)

<dfn id="236.html_selector-link" data-anolis-xref="selector-link">`:link`</dfn>
<dfn id="236.html_selector-visited" data-anolis-xref="selector-visited">`:visited`</dfn>

All [`a`](#236.html_the-a-element) elements that have an [`href`](#236.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute, all [`area`](#236.html_the-area-element) elements that have an [`href`](#236.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute, and all [`link`](#236.html_the-link-element) elements that have an [`href`](#236.html_attr-link-href) attribute, must match one of [`:link`](#236.html_selector-link) and [`:visited`](#236.html_selector-visited).

Other specifications might apply more specific rules regarding how these elements are to match these pseudo-classes, to mitigate some privacy concerns that apply with straightforward implementations of this requirement.

<dfn id="236.html_selector-active" data-anolis-xref="selector-active">`:active`</dfn>

The [`:active`](#236.html_selector-active) pseudo-class is defined to match an element “while an element is *being activated* by the user”. For the purposes of defining the [`:active`](#236.html_selector-active) pseudo-class only, an HTML user agent must consider an element as *being activated* if it is:

*   An element falling into one of the following categories between the time the user begins to indicate an intent to trigger the element's [activation behavior](#236.html_activation-behavior) and either the time the user stops indicating an intent to trigger the element's [activation behavior](#236.html_activation-behavior), or the time the element's [activation behavior](#236.html_activation-behavior) has finished running, which ever comes first:

    *   [`a`](#236.html_the-a-element) elements that have an [`href`](#236.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute
    *   [`area`](#236.html_the-area-element) elements that have an [`href`](#236.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute
    *   [`link`](#236.html_the-link-element) elements that have an [`href`](#236.html_attr-link-href) attribute
    *   [`button`](#236.html_the-button-element) elements that are not [disabled](#236.html_concept-fe-disabled)
    *   [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#236.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Submit Button](#236.html_submit-button-state-(type=submit)), [Image Button](#236.html_image-button-state-(type=image)), [Reset Button](#236.html_reset-button-state-(type=reset)), or [Button](#236.html_button-state-(type=button)) state
    *   elements that have their [tabindex focus flag](#236.html_specially-focusable) set

    For example, if the user is using a keyboard to push a [`button`](#236.html_the-button-element) element by pressing the space bar, the element would match this pseudo-class in between the time that the element received the `keydown` event and the time the element received the `keyup` event.

*   An element that the user indicates using a pointing device while that pointing device is in the "down" state (e.g. for a mouse, between the time the mouse button is pressed and the time it is depressed).

*   An element that has a descendant that is currently matching the [`:active`](#236.html_selector-active) pseudo-class.

<dfn id="236.html_selector-hover" data-anolis-xref="selector-hover">`:hover`</dfn>

The [`:hover`](#236.html_selector-hover) pseudo-class is defined to match an element “while the user *designates* an element with a pointing device”. For the purposes of defining the [`:hover`](#236.html_selector-hover) pseudo-class only, an HTML user agent must consider an element as being one that the user *designates* if it is:

*   An element that the user indicates using a pointing device.

*   An element that has a descendant that the user indicates using a pointing device.

*   An element that is the [labeled control](#236.html_labeled-control) of a [`label`](#236.html_the-label-element) element that is currently matching [:hover](#236.html_selector-hover).

Consider in particular a fragment such as:

```
<p> <label for=c> <input id=a> </label> <span id=b> <input id=c> </span> </p>
```

If the user designates the element with ID "`a`" with their pointing device, then the [`p`](#236.html_the-p-element) element (and all its ancestors not shown in the snippet above), the [`label`](#236.html_the-label-element) element, the element with ID "`a`", and the element with ID "`c`" will match the [:hover](#236.html_selector-hover) pseudo-class. The element with ID "`a`" matches it from condition 1, the [`label`](#236.html_the-label-element) and [`p`](#236.html_the-p-element) elements match it because of condition 2 (one of their descendants is designated), and the element with ID "`c`" matches it through condition 3 (its [`label`](#236.html_the-label-element) element matches [:hover](#236.html_selector-hover)). However, the element with ID "`b`" does *not* match [:hover](#236.html_selector-hover): its descendant is not designated, even though it matches [:hover](#236.html_selector-hover).

<dfn id="236.html_selector-enabled" data-anolis-xref="selector-enabled">`:enabled`</dfn>

The [`:enabled`](#236.html_selector-enabled) pseudo-class must match any element falling into one of the following categories:

*   [`a`](#236.html_the-a-element) elements that have an [`href`](#236.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute
*   [`area`](#236.html_the-area-element) elements that have an [`href`](#236.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute
*   [`link`](#236.html_the-link-element) elements that have an [`href`](#236.html_attr-link-href) attribute
*   [`button`](#236.html_the-button-element) elements that are not [disabled](#236.html_concept-fe-disabled)
*   [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements that are not [disabled](#236.html_concept-fe-disabled)
*   [`select`](#236.html_the-select-element) elements that are not [disabled](#236.html_concept-fe-disabled)
*   [`textarea`](#236.html_the-textarea-element) elements that are not [disabled](#236.html_concept-fe-disabled)
*   [`optgroup`](#236.html_the-optgroup-element) elements that do not have a [`disabled`](#236.html_attr-optgroup-disabled) attribute
*   [`option`](#236.html_the-option-element) elements that are not [disabled](#236.html_concept-option-disabled)
*   [`fieldset`](#236.html_the-fieldset-element) elements that do not have a [`disabled`](#236.html_attr-fieldset-disabled) attribute

<dfn id="236.html_selector-disabled" data-anolis-xref="selector-disabled">`:disabled`</dfn>

The [`:disabled`](#236.html_selector-disabled) pseudo-class must match any element that is [actually disabled](#236.html_concept-element-disabled).

<dfn id="236.html_selector-checked" data-anolis-xref="selector-checked">`:checked`</dfn>

The [`:checked`](#236.html_selector-checked) pseudo-class must match any element falling into one of the following categories:

*   [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#236.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Checkbox](#236.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) state and whose [checkedness](#236.html_concept-fe-checked) state is true
*   [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#236.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#236.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state and whose [checkedness](#236.html_concept-fe-checked) state is true
*   [`option`](#236.html_the-option-element) elements whose [selectedness](#236.html_concept-option-selectedness) is true

<dfn id="236.html_selector-indeterminate" data-anolis-xref="selector-indeterminate">`:indeterminate`</dfn>

The [`:indeterminate`](#236.html_selector-indeterminate) pseudo-class must match any element falling into one of the following categories:

*   [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#236.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Checkbox](#236.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) state and whose [`indeterminate`](#236.html_dom-input-indeterminate) IDL attribute is set to true
*   [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#236.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#236.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state and whose [radio button group](#236.html_radio-button-group) contains no [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements whose [checkedness](#236.html_concept-fe-checked) state is true.
*   [`progress`](#236.html_the-progress-element) elements with no [`value`](#236.html_attr-progress-value) content attribute

<dfn id="236.html_selector-default" data-anolis-xref="selector-default">`:default`</dfn>

The [`:default`](#236.html_selector-default) pseudo-class must match any element falling into one of the following categories:

*   [`button`](#236.html_the-button-element) elements that are their form's [default button](#236.html_default-button)
*   [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#236.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Submit Button](#236.html_submit-button-state-(type=submit)) or [Image Button](#236.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, and that are their form's [default button](#236.html_default-button)
*   [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements to which the [`checked`](#236.html_attr-input-checked) attribute applies and that have a [`checked`](#236.html_attr-input-checked) attribute
*   [`option`](#236.html_the-option-element) elements that have a [`selected`](#236.html_attr-option-selected) attribute

<dfn id="236.html_selector-valid" data-anolis-xref="selector-valid">`:valid`</dfn>

The [`:valid`](#236.html_selector-valid) pseudo-class must match any element falling into one of the following categories:

*   elements that are [candidates for constraint validation](#236.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation) and that [satisfy their constraints](#236.html_concept-fv-valid)
*   [`form`](#236.html_the-form-element) elements that are not the [form owner](#236.html_form-owner) of any elements that themselves are [candidates for constraint validation](#236.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation) but do not [satisfy their constraints](#236.html_concept-fv-valid)
*   [`fieldset`](#236.html_the-fieldset-element) elements that have no descendant elements that themselves are [candidates for constraint validation](#236.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation) but do not [satisfy their constraints](#236.html_concept-fv-valid)

<dfn id="236.html_selector-invalid" data-anolis-xref="selector-invalid">`:invalid`</dfn>

The [`:invalid`](#236.html_selector-invalid) pseudo-class must match any element falling into one of the following categories:

*   elements that are [candidates for constraint validation](#236.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation) but that do not [satisfy their constraints](#236.html_concept-fv-valid)
*   [`form`](#236.html_the-form-element) elements that are the [form owner](#236.html_form-owner) of one or more elements that themselves are [candidates for constraint validation](#236.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation) but do not [satisfy their constraints](#236.html_concept-fv-valid)
*   [`fieldset`](#236.html_the-fieldset-element) elements that have of one or more descendant elements that themselves are [candidates for constraint validation](#236.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation) but do not [satisfy their constraints](#236.html_concept-fv-valid)

<dfn id="236.html_selector-in-range" data-anolis-xref="selector-in-range">`:in-range`</dfn>

The [`:in-range`](#236.html_selector-in-range) pseudo-class must match all elements that are [candidates for constraint validation](#236.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation), [have range limitations](#236.html_have-range-limitations), and that are neither [suffering from an underflow](#236.html_suffering-from-an-underflow) nor [suffering from an overflow](#236.html_suffering-from-an-overflow).

<dfn id="236.html_selector-out-of-range" data-anolis-xref="selector-out-of-range">`:out-of-range`</dfn>

The [`:out-of-range`](#236.html_selector-out-of-range) pseudo-class must match all elements that are [candidates for constraint validation](#236.html_candidate-for-constraint-validation), [have range limitations](#236.html_have-range-limitations), and that are either [suffering from an underflow](#236.html_suffering-from-an-underflow) or [suffering from an overflow](#236.html_suffering-from-an-overflow).

<dfn id="236.html_selector-required" data-anolis-xref="selector-required">`:required`</dfn>

The [`:required`](#236.html_selector-required) pseudo-class must match any element falling into one of the following categories:

*   [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements that are *[required](#236.html_concept-input-required)*
*   [`select`](#236.html_the-select-element) elements that have a [`required`](#236.html_attr-select-required) attribute
*   [`textarea`](#236.html_the-textarea-element) elements that have a [`required`](#236.html_attr-textarea-required) attribute

<dfn id="236.html_selector-optional" data-anolis-xref="selector-optional">`:optional`</dfn>

The [`:optional`](#236.html_selector-optional) pseudo-class must match any element falling into one of the following categories:

*   [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements to which the [`required`](#236.html_attr-input-required) attribute applies that are not *[required](#236.html_concept-input-required)*
*   [`select`](#236.html_the-select-element) elements that do not have a [`required`](#236.html_attr-select-required) attribute
*   [`textarea`](#236.html_the-textarea-element) elements that do not have a [`required`](#236.html_attr-textarea-required) attribute

<dfn id="236.html_selector-read-only" data-anolis-xref="selector-read-only">`:read-only`</dfn>
<dfn id="236.html_selector-read-write" data-anolis-xref="selector-read-write">`:read-write`</dfn>

The [`:read-write`](#236.html_selector-read-write) pseudo-class must match any element falling into one of the following categories, which for the purposes of Selectors are thus considered *user-alterable*: [[SELECTORS]](#236.html_refsSELECTORS)

*   [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements to which the [`readonly`](#236.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute applies, and that are *[mutable](#236.html_concept-fe-mutable)* (i.e. that do not have the [`readonly`](#236.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute specified and that are not [disabled](#236.html_concept-fe-disabled))
*   [`textarea`](#236.html_the-textarea-element) elements that do not have a [`readonly`](#236.html_attr-textarea-readonly) attribute, and that are not [disabled](#236.html_concept-fe-disabled)
*   elements that are [editing hosts](#236.html_editing-host) or [editable](#236.html_editable) and are neither [`input`](#236.html_the-input-element) elements nor [`textarea`](#236.html_the-textarea-element) elements

The [`:read-only`](#236.html_selector-read-only) pseudo-class must match all other [HTML elements](#236.html_html-elements).

Another section of this specification defines the *[target element](#236.html_target-element)* used with the `:target` pseudo-class.

This specification does not define when an element matches the `:focus` or `:lang()` dynamic pseudo-classes, as those are all defined in sufficient detail in a language-agnostic fashion in the Selectors specification. [[SELECTORS]](#236.html_refsSELECTORS)

## 5 Loading Web pages

This section describes features that apply most directly to Web browsers. Having said that, except where specified otherwise, the requirements defined in this section *do* apply to all user agents, whether they are Web browsers or not.

### 5.1 Browsing contexts

A <dfn id="238.html_browsing-context">browsing context</dfn> is an environment in which [`Document`](#238.html_document) objects are presented to the user.

A tab or window in a Web browser typically contains a [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context), as does an [`iframe`](#238.html_the-iframe-element) or [`frame`](#238.html_frame)s in a [`frameset`](#238.html_frameset).

Each [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) has a corresponding [`WindowProxy`](#238.html_windowproxy) object.

A [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) has a [session history](#238.html_session-history), which lists the [`Document`](#238.html_document) objects that that [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) has presented, is presenting, or will present. At any time, one [`Document`](#238.html_document) in each [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) is designated the <dfn id="238.html_active-document">active document</dfn>. A [`Document`](#238.html_document)'s [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) is that [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) whose [session history](#238.html_session-history) contains the [`Document`](#238.html_document), if any. (A [`Document`](#238.html_document) created using an API such as [`createDocument()`](#238.html_dom-domimplementation-createdocument) has no [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context).)

Each [`Document`](#238.html_document) in a [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) is <dfn id="238.html_concept-document-window" data-anolis-xref="concept-document-window">associated</dfn> with a [`Window`](#238.html_window) object. A [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context)'s [`WindowProxy`](#238.html_windowproxy) object forwards everything to the [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#238.html_active-document)'s [`Window`](#238.html_window) object.

In general, there is a 1-to-1 mapping from the [`Window`](#238.html_window) object to the [`Document`](#238.html_document) object. There are two exceptions. First, a [`Window`](#238.html_window) can be reused for the presentation of a second [`Document`](#238.html_document) in the same [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context), such that the mapping is then 1-to-2\. This occurs when a [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) is [navigated](#238.html_navigate) from the initial [`about:blank`](#238.html_about:blank) [`Document`](#238.html_document) to another, with [replacement enabled](#238.html_replacement-enabled). Second, a [`Document`](#238.html_document) can end up being reused for several [`Window`](#238.html_window) objects when the [`document.open()`](#238.html_dom-document-open) method is used, such that the mapping is then many-to-1.

A [`Document`](#238.html_document) does not necessarily have a [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) associated with it. In particular, data mining tools are likely to never instantiate browsing contexts.

* * *

A [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) can have a <dfn id="238.html_creator-browsing-context">creator browsing context</dfn>, the [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) that was responsible for its creation. If a [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) has a [parent browsing context](#238.html_parent-browsing-context), then that is its [creator browsing context](#238.html_creator-browsing-context). Otherwise, if the [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) has an [opener browsing context](#238.html_opener-browsing-context), then *that* is its [creator browsing context](#238.html_creator-browsing-context). Otherwise, the [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) has no [creator browsing context](#238.html_creator-browsing-context).

If a [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) `A` has a [creator browsing context](#238.html_creator-browsing-context), then the [`Document`](#238.html_document) that was the [active document](#238.html_active-document) of that [creator browsing context](#238.html_creator-browsing-context) at the time `A` was created is the <dfn id="238.html_creator-document">creator `Document`</dfn>.

When a [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) is first created, it must be created with a single [`Document`](#238.html_document) in its session history, whose [address](#238.html_the-document's-address) is [`about:blank`](#238.html_about:blank), which is marked as being an [HTML document](#238.html_html-documents), whose [character encoding](#238.html_document's-character-encoding) is UTF-8, and which is both [ready for post-load tasks](#238.html_ready-for-post-load-tasks) and [completely loaded](#238.html_completely-loaded) immediately, along with a new [`Window`](#238.html_window) object that the [`Document`](#238.html_document) is associated with. The [`Document`](#238.html_document) must have a single child [`html`](#238.html_the-html-element) node, which itself has two empty child nodes: a [`head`](#238.html_the-head-element) element, and a [`body`](#238.html_the-body-element) element. As soon as this [`Document`](#238.html_document) is created, the user agent must [implement the sandboxing](#238.html_implement-the-sandboxing) for it. If the [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) has a [creator `Document`](#238.html_creator-document), then the [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context)'s [`Document`](#238.html_document)'s [referrer](#238.html_the-document's-referrer) must be set to [the address](#238.html_the-document's-address) of that [creator `Document`](#238.html_creator-document) at the time of the [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context)'s creation.

If the [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) is created specifically to be immediately navigated, then that initial navigation will have [replacement enabled](#238.html_replacement-enabled).

The [origin](#238.html_origin-0) and [effective script origin](#238.html_effective-script-origin) of the [`about:blank`](#238.html_about:blank) [`Document`](#238.html_document) are set when the [`Document`](#238.html_document) is created. If the new [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) has a [creator browsing context](#238.html_creator-browsing-context), then the [origin](#238.html_origin-0) of the [`about:blank`](#238.html_about:blank) [`Document`](#238.html_document) is an [alias](#238.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#238.html_origin-0) of the [creator `Document`](#238.html_creator-document) and the [effective script origin](#238.html_effective-script-origin) of the [`about:blank`](#238.html_about:blank) [`Document`](#238.html_document) is initially an [alias](#238.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [effective script origin](#238.html_effective-script-origin) of the [creator `Document`](#238.html_creator-document). Otherwise, the [origin](#238.html_origin-0) of the [`about:blank`](#238.html_about:blank) [`Document`](#238.html_document) is a globally unique identifier assigned when the new [browsing context](#238.html_browsing-context) is created and the [effective script origin](#238.html_effective-script-origin) of the [`about:blank`](#238.html_about:blank) [`Document`](#238.html_document) is initially an [alias](#238.html_concept-origin-alias) to its [origin](#238.html_origin-0).

#### 5.1.1 Nested browsing contexts

Certain elements (for example, [`iframe`](#239.html_the-iframe-element) elements) can instantiate further [browsing contexts](#239.html_browsing-context). These are called <dfn id="239.html_nested-browsing-context" data-anolis-xref="nested browsing
  context">nested browsing contexts</dfn>. If a browsing context `P` has a [`Document`](#239.html_document) `D` with an element `E` that nests another browsing context `C` inside it, then `C` is said to be <dfn id="239.html_browsing-context-nested-through" data-anolis-xref="browsing context nested through">nested through</dfn> `D`, and `E` is said to be the <dfn id="239.html_browsing-context-container">browsing context container</dfn> of `C`. If the [browsing context container](#239.html_browsing-context-container) element `E` is [in](#239.html_in-a-document) the [`Document`](#239.html_document) `D`, then `P` is said to be the <dfn id="239.html_parent-browsing-context">parent browsing context</dfn> of `C` and `C` is said to be a <dfn id="239.html_child-browsing-context">child browsing context</dfn> of `P`. Otherwise, the [nested browsing context](#239.html_nested-browsing-context) `C` has no [parent browsing context](#239.html_parent-browsing-context).

A browsing context `A` is said to be an <dfn id="239.html_ancestor-browsing-context" data-anolis-xref="ancestor browsing
  context">ancestor</dfn> of a browsing context `B` if there exists a browsing context `A'` that is a [child browsing context](#239.html_child-browsing-context) of `A` and that is itself an [ancestor](#239.html_ancestor-browsing-context) of `B`, or if the browsing context `A` is the [parent browsing context](#239.html_parent-browsing-context) of `B`.

A browsing context that is not a [nested browsing context](#239.html_nested-browsing-context) has no [parent browsing context](#239.html_parent-browsing-context), and is the <dfn id="239.html_top-level-browsing-context">top-level browsing context</dfn> of all the browsing contexts for which it is an [ancestor browsing context](#239.html_ancestor-browsing-context).

The transitive closure of [parent browsing contexts](#239.html_parent-browsing-context) for a [nested browsing context](#239.html_nested-browsing-context) gives the list of [ancestor browsing contexts](#239.html_ancestor-browsing-context).

The <dfn id="239.html_list-of-the-descendant-browsing-contexts">list of the descendant browsing contexts</dfn> of a [`Document`](#239.html_document) `d` is the (ordered) list returned by the following algorithm:

1.  Let `list` be an empty list.

2.  For each [child browsing context](#239.html_child-browsing-context) of `d` that is [nested through](#239.html_browsing-context-nested-through) an element that is [in the `Document`](#239.html_in-a-document) `d`, in the [tree order](#239.html_tree-order) of the elements nesting those [browsing contexts](#239.html_browsing-context), run these substeps:

    1.  Append that [child browsing context](#239.html_child-browsing-context) to the list `list`.

    2.  Append the [list of the descendant browsing contexts](#239.html_list-of-the-descendant-browsing-contexts) of the [active document](#239.html_active-document) of that [child browsing context](#239.html_child-browsing-context) to the list `list`.

3.  Return the constructed `list`.

A [`Document`](#239.html_document) is said to be <dfn id="239.html_fully-active">fully active</dfn> when it is the [active document](#239.html_active-document) of its [browsing context](#239.html_browsing-context), and either its browsing context is a [top-level browsing context](#239.html_top-level-browsing-context), or it has a [parent browsing context](#239.html_parent-browsing-context) and the [`Document`](#239.html_document) [through which](#239.html_browsing-context-nested-through) it is [nested](#239.html_nested-browsing-context) is itself [fully active](#239.html_fully-active).

Because they are nested through an element, [child browsing contexts](#239.html_child-browsing-context) are always tied to a specific [`Document`](#239.html_document) in their [parent browsing context](#239.html_parent-browsing-context). User agents must not allow the user to interact with [child browsing contexts](#239.html_child-browsing-context) of elements that are in [`Document`](#239.html_document)s that are not themselves [fully active](#239.html_fully-active).

A [nested browsing context](#239.html_nested-browsing-context) can be put into a <dfn id="239.html_delaying-load-events-mode">delaying `load` events mode</dfn>. This is used when it is [navigated](#239.html_navigate), to [delay the load event](#239.html_delay-the-load-event) of the [browsing context container](#239.html_browsing-context-container) [`iframe`](#239.html_the-iframe-element) element before the new [`Document`](#239.html_document) is created.

The <dfn id="239.html_document-family">document family</dfn> of a [browsing context](#239.html_browsing-context) consists of the union of all the [`Document`](#239.html_document) objects in that [browsing context](#239.html_browsing-context)'s [session history](#239.html_session-history) and the [document families](#239.html_document-family) of all those [`Document`](#239.html_document) objects. The [document family](#239.html_document-family) of a [`Document`](#239.html_document) object consists of the union of all the [document families](#239.html_document-family) of the [browsing contexts](#239.html_browsing-context) that are [nested through](#239.html_browsing-context-nested-through) the [`Document`](#239.html_document) object.

##### 5.1.1.1 Navigating nested browsing contexts in the DOM

`window` . [`top`](#239.html_dom-top)

Returns the [`WindowProxy`](#239.html_windowproxy) for the [top-level browsing context](#239.html_top-level-browsing-context).

`window` . [`parent`](#239.html_dom-parent)

Returns the [`WindowProxy`](#239.html_windowproxy) for the [parent browsing context](#239.html_parent-browsing-context).

`window` . [`frameElement`](#239.html_dom-frameelement)

Returns the [`Element`](#239.html_element) for the [browsing context container](#239.html_browsing-context-container).

Returns null if there isn't one.

Throws a [`SecurityError`](#239.html_securityerror) exception in cross-origin situations.

The <dfn id="239.html_dom-top" data-anolis-xref="dom-top">`top`</dfn> IDL attribute on the [`Window`](#239.html_window) object of a [`Document`](#239.html_document) in a [browsing context](#239.html_browsing-context) `b` must return the [`WindowProxy`](#239.html_windowproxy) object of its [top-level browsing context](#239.html_top-level-browsing-context) (which would be its own [`WindowProxy`](#239.html_windowproxy) object if it was a [top-level browsing context](#239.html_top-level-browsing-context) itself), if it has one, or its own [`WindowProxy`](#239.html_windowproxy) object otherwise (e.g. if it was a detached [nested browsing context](#239.html_nested-browsing-context)).

The <dfn id="239.html_dom-parent" data-anolis-xref="dom-parent">`parent`</dfn> IDL attribute on the [`Window`](#239.html_window) object of a [`Document`](#239.html_document) in a [browsing context](#239.html_browsing-context) `b` must return the [`WindowProxy`](#239.html_windowproxy) object of the [parent browsing context](#239.html_parent-browsing-context), if there is one (i.e. if `b` is a [child browsing context](#239.html_child-browsing-context)), or the [`WindowProxy`](#239.html_windowproxy) object of the [browsing context](#239.html_browsing-context) `b` itself, otherwise (i.e. if it is a [top-level browsing context](#239.html_top-level-browsing-context) or a detached [nested browsing context](#239.html_nested-browsing-context)).

The <dfn id="239.html_dom-frameelement" data-anolis-xref="dom-frameElement">`frameElement`</dfn> IDL attribute on the [`Window`](#239.html_window) object of a [`Document`](#239.html_document) `d`, on getting, must run the following algorithm:

1.  If `d` is not a [`Document`](#239.html_document) in a [nested browsing context](#239.html_nested-browsing-context), return null and abort these steps.

2.  If the [browsing context container](#239.html_browsing-context-container)'s [`Document`](#239.html_document) does not have the [same](#239.html_same-origin) [effective script origin](#239.html_effective-script-origin) as the [effective script origin](#239.html_effective-script-origin) specified by the [entry settings object](#239.html_entry-settings-object), then throw a [`SecurityError`](#239.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps.

3.  Return the [browsing context container](#239.html_browsing-context-container) for `b`.

#### 5.1.2 Auxiliary browsing contexts

It is possible to create new browsing contexts that are related to a [top-level browsing context](#240.html_top-level-browsing-context) without being nested through an element. Such browsing contexts are called <dfn id="240.html_auxiliary-browsing-context" data-anolis-xref="auxiliary browsing context">auxiliary browsing contexts</dfn>. Auxiliary browsing contexts are always [top-level browsing contexts](#240.html_top-level-browsing-context).

An [auxiliary browsing context](#240.html_auxiliary-browsing-context) has an <dfn id="240.html_opener-browsing-context">opener browsing context</dfn>, which is the [browsing context](#240.html_browsing-context) from which the [auxiliary browsing context](#240.html_auxiliary-browsing-context) was created.

##### 5.1.2.1 Navigating auxiliary browsing contexts in the DOM

The <dfn id="240.html_dom-opener" data-anolis-xref="dom-opener">`opener`</dfn> IDL attribute on the [`Window`](#240.html_window) object, on getting, must return the [`WindowProxy`](#240.html_windowproxy) object of the [browsing context](#240.html_browsing-context) from which the current [browsing context](#240.html_browsing-context) was created (its [opener browsing context](#240.html_opener-browsing-context)), if there is one, if it is still available, and if the current [browsing context](#240.html_browsing-context) has not *[disowned its opener](#240.html_disowned-its-opener)*; otherwise, it must return null. On setting, if the new value is null then the current [browsing context](#240.html_browsing-context) must <dfn id="240.html_disowned-its-opener" data-anolis-xref="disowned its opener">disown its opener</dfn>; if the new value is anything else then the user agent must call the [[DefineOwnProperty]] internal method of the [`Window`](#240.html_window) object, passing the property name "`opener`" as the property key, and the Property Descriptor { [[Value]]: `value`, [[Writable]]: true, [[Enumerable]]: true, [[Configurable]]: true } as the property descriptor, where `value` is the new value.

#### 5.1.3 Secondary browsing contexts

User agents may support <dfn id="241.html_secondary-browsing-context" data-anolis-xref="secondary browsing context">secondary browsing contexts</dfn>, which are [browsing contexts](#241.html_browsing-context) that form part of the user agent's interface, apart from the main content area.

#### 5.1.4 Security

A [browsing context](#242.html_browsing-context) `A` is <dfn id="242.html_familiar-with">familiar with</dfn> a second [browsing context](#242.html_browsing-context) `B` if one of the following conditions is true:

*   Either the [origin](#242.html_origin-0) of the [active document](#242.html_active-document) of `A` is the [same](#242.html_same-origin) as the [origin](#242.html_origin-0) of the [active document](#242.html_active-document) of `B`, or
*   The browsing context `A` is a [nested browsing context](#242.html_nested-browsing-context) with a [top-level browsing context](#242.html_top-level-browsing-context), and its [top-level browsing context](#242.html_top-level-browsing-context) is `B`, or
*   The browsing context `B` is an [auxiliary browsing context](#242.html_auxiliary-browsing-context) and `A` is [familiar with](#242.html_familiar-with) `B`'s [opener browsing context](#242.html_opener-browsing-context), or
*   The browsing context `B` is not a [top-level browsing context](#242.html_top-level-browsing-context), but there exists an [ancestor browsing context](#242.html_ancestor-browsing-context) of `B` whose [active document](#242.html_active-document) has the [same](#242.html_same-origin) [origin](#242.html_origin-0) as the [active document](#242.html_active-document) of `A` (possibly in fact being `A` itself).

* * *

A [browsing context](#242.html_browsing-context) `A` is <dfn id="242.html_allowed-to-navigate">allowed to navigate</dfn> a second [browsing context](#242.html_browsing-context) `B` if the following algorithm terminates positively:

1.  If `A` is not the same [browsing context](#242.html_browsing-context) as `B`, and `A` is not one of the [ancestor browsing contexts](#242.html_ancestor-browsing-context) of `B`, and `B` is not a [top-level browsing context](#242.html_top-level-browsing-context), and `A`'s [active document](#242.html_active-document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#242.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) has its [sandboxed navigation browsing context flag](#242.html_sandboxed-navigation-browsing-context-flag) set, then abort these steps negatively.

2.  Otherwise, if `B` is a [top-level browsing context](#242.html_top-level-browsing-context), and is one of the [ancestor browsing contexts](#242.html_ancestor-browsing-context) of `A`, and `A`'s [`Document`](#242.html_document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#242.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) has its [sandboxed top-level navigation browsing context flag](#242.html_sandboxed-top-level-navigation-browsing-context-flag) set, then abort these steps negatively.

3.  Otherwise, if `B` is a [top-level browsing context](#242.html_top-level-browsing-context), and is neither `A` nor one of the [ancestor browsing contexts](#242.html_ancestor-browsing-context) of `A`, and `A`'s [`Document`](#242.html_document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#242.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) has its [sandboxed navigation browsing context flag](#242.html_sandboxed-navigation-browsing-context-flag) set, and `A` is not the [one permitted sandboxed navigator](#242.html_one-permitted-sandboxed-navigator) of `B`, then abort these steps negatively.

4.  Otherwise, terminate positively!

* * *

An element has a <dfn id="242.html_browsing-context-scope-origin">browsing context scope origin</dfn> if its [`Document`](#242.html_document)'s [browsing context](#242.html_browsing-context) is a [top-level browsing context](#242.html_top-level-browsing-context) or if all of its [`Document`](#242.html_document)'s [ancestor browsing contexts](#242.html_ancestor-browsing-context) all have [active documents](#242.html_active-document) whose [origin](#242.html_origin-0) are the [same origin](#242.html_same-origin) as the element's [`Document`](#242.html_document)'s [origin](#242.html_origin-0). If an element has a [browsing context scope origin](#242.html_browsing-context-scope-origin), then its value is the [origin](#242.html_origin-0) of the element's [`Document`](#242.html_document).

#### 5.1.5 Groupings of browsing contexts

Each [browsing context](#243.html_browsing-context) is defined as having a list of one or more <dfn id="243.html_directly-reachable-browsing-contexts">directly reachable browsing contexts</dfn>. These are:

*   The [browsing context](#243.html_browsing-context) itself.
*   All the [browsing context](#243.html_browsing-context)'s [child browsing contexts](#243.html_child-browsing-context).
*   The [browsing context](#243.html_browsing-context)'s [parent browsing context](#243.html_parent-browsing-context).
*   All the [browsing contexts](#243.html_browsing-context) that have the [browsing context](#243.html_browsing-context) as their [opener browsing context](#243.html_opener-browsing-context).
*   The [browsing context](#243.html_browsing-context)'s [opener browsing context](#243.html_opener-browsing-context).

The transitive closure of all the [browsing contexts](#243.html_browsing-context) that are [directly reachable browsing contexts](#243.html_directly-reachable-browsing-contexts) forms a <dfn id="243.html_unit-of-related-browsing-contexts">unit of related browsing contexts</dfn>.

Each [unit of related browsing contexts](#243.html_unit-of-related-browsing-contexts) is then further divided into the smallest number of groups such that every member of each group has an [active document](#243.html_active-document) with an [effective script origin](#243.html_effective-script-origin) that, through appropriate manipulation of the [`document.domain`](#243.html_dom-document-domain) attribute, could be made to be the same as other members of the group, but could not be made the same as members of any other group. Each such group is a <dfn id="243.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts">unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts</dfn>.

There is also at most one [event loop](#243.html_event-loop) per [unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts](#243.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts) (though several [units of related similar-origin browsing contexts](#243.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts) can have a shared [event loop](#243.html_event-loop)).

#### 5.1.6 Browsing context names

Browsing contexts can have a <dfn id="244.html_browsing-context-name">browsing context name</dfn>. By default, a browsing context has no name (its name is not set).

A <dfn id="244.html_valid-browsing-context-name">valid browsing context name</dfn> is any string with at least one character that does not start with a U+005F LOW LINE character. (Names starting with an underscore are reserved for special keywords.)

A <dfn id="244.html_valid-browsing-context-name-or-keyword">valid browsing context name or keyword</dfn> is any string that is either a [valid browsing context name](#244.html_valid-browsing-context-name) or that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#244.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for one of: `_blank`, `_self`, `_parent`, or `_top`.

These values have different meanings based on whether the page is sandboxed or not, as summarized in the following (non-normative) table. In this table, "current" means the [browsing context](#244.html_browsing-context) that the link or script is in, "parent" means the [parent browsing context](#244.html_parent-browsing-context) of the one the link or script is in, "master" means the nearest [ancestor browsing context](#244.html_ancestor-browsing-context) of the one the link or script is in, "top" means the [top-level browsing context](#244.html_top-level-browsing-context) of the one the link or script is in, "new" means a new [top-level browsing context](#244.html_top-level-browsing-context) or [auxiliary browsing context](#244.html_auxiliary-browsing-context) is to be created, subject to various user preferences and user agent policies, "none" means that nothing will happen, and "maybe new" means the same as "new" if the "[`allow-popups`](#244.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-popups)" keyword is also specified on the [`sandbox`](#244.html_attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute (or if the user overrode the sandboxing), and the same as "none" otherwise.

| Keyword | Ordinary effect | Effect in an [`iframe`](#244.html_the-iframe-element) with... |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sandbox=""` | `sandbox="allow-top-navigation"` |
| --- | --- |
| none specified, for links and form submissions | current | current | current |
| empty string | current | current | current |
| `_blank` | new | maybe new | maybe new |
| `_self` | current | current | current |
| `_parent` if there isn't a parent | current | current | current |
| `_parent` if parent is also top | parent/top | none | parent/top |
| `_parent` if there is one and it's not top | parent | none | none |
| `_top` if top is current | current | current | current |
| `_top` if top is not current | top | none | top |
| name that doesn't exist | new | maybe new | maybe new |
| name that exists and is a descendant | specified descendant | specified descendant | specified descendant |
| name that exists and is current | current | current | current |
| name that exists and is an ancestor that is top | specified ancestor | none | specified ancestor/top |
| name that exists and is an ancestor that is not top | specified ancestor | none | none |
| other name that exists with common top | specified | none | none |
| name that exists with different top, if [familiar](#244.html_familiar-with) and [one permitted sandboxed navigator](#244.html_one-permitted-sandboxed-navigator) | specified | specified | specified |
| name that exists with different top, if [familiar](#244.html_familiar-with) but not [one permitted sandboxed navigator](#244.html_one-permitted-sandboxed-navigator) | specified | none | none |
| name that exists with different top, not [familiar](#244.html_familiar-with) | new | maybe new | maybe new |

Most of the restrictions on sandboxed browsing contexts are applied by other algorithms, e.g. the [navigation](#244.html_navigate) algorithm, not [the rules for choosing a browsing context given a browsing context name](#244.html_the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name) given below.

* * *

An algorithm is <dfn id="244.html_allowed-to-show-a-popup">allowed to show a popup</dfn> if any of the following conditions is true:

*   The [task](#244.html_concept-task) in which the algorithm is running is currently processing an [activation behavior](#244.html_activation-behavior) whose [`click`](#244.html_event-click) event was [trusted](#244.html_concept-events-trusted).

*   The [task](#244.html_concept-task) in which the algorithm is running is currently running the event listener for a [trusted](#244.html_concept-events-trusted) event whose type is in the following list:

    *   `change`
    *   [`click`](#244.html_event-click)
    *   `dblclick`
    *   `mouseup`
    *   `reset`
    *   `submit`
*   The [task](#244.html_concept-task) in which the algorithm is running was [queued](#244.html_queue-a-task) by an algorithm that was [allowed to show a popup](#244.html_allowed-to-show-a-popup), and the chain of such algorithms started within a user-agent defined timeframe.

    For example, if a user clicked a button, it might be acceptable for a popup to result from that after 4 seconds, but it would likely not be acceptable for a popup to result from that after 4 hours.

* * *

<dfn id="244.html_the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name">The rules for choosing a browsing context given a browsing context name</dfn> are as follows. The rules assume that they are being applied in the context of a [browsing context](#244.html_browsing-context), as part of the execution of a [task](#244.html_concept-task).

1.  If the given browsing context name is the empty string or `_self`, then the chosen browsing context must be the current one.

    If the given browsing context name is `_self`, then this is an explicit self-navigation override.

2.  If the given browsing context name is `_parent`, then the chosen browsing context must be the [*parent* browsing context](#244.html_parent-browsing-context) of the current one, unless there isn't one, in which case the chosen browsing context must be the current browsing context.

3.  If the given browsing context name is `_top`, then the chosen browsing context must be the [top-level browsing context](#244.html_top-level-browsing-context) of the current one, if there is one, or else the current browsing context.

4.  If the given browsing context name is not `_blank` and there exists a browsing context whose [name](#244.html_browsing-context-name) is the same as the given browsing context name, and the current browsing context is [familiar with](#244.html_familiar-with) that browsing context, and the user agent determines that the two browsing contexts are related enough that it is ok if they reach each other, then that browsing context must be the chosen one. If there are multiple matching browsing contexts, the user agent should select one in some arbitrary consistent manner, such as the most recently opened, most recently focused, or more closely related.

    If the browsing context is chosen by this step to be the current browsing context, then this is also an explicit self-navigation override.

5.  Otherwise, a new browsing context is being requested, and what happens depends on the user agent's configuration and abilities — it is determined by the rules given for the first applicable option from the following list:

    If the algorithm is not [allowed to show a popup](#244.html_allowed-to-show-a-popup) and the user agent has been configured to not show popups (i.e. the user agent has a "popup blocker" enabled)

    There is no chosen browsing context. The user agent may inform the user that a popup has been blocked.

    If the current browsing context's [active document](#244.html_active-document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#244.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) has the [sandboxed auxiliary navigation browsing context flag](#244.html_sandboxed-auxiliary-navigation-browsing-context-flag) set.

    Typically, there is no chosen browsing context.

    The user agent may offer to create a new [top-level browsing context](#244.html_top-level-browsing-context) or reuse an existing [top-level browsing context](#244.html_top-level-browsing-context). If the user picks one of those options, then the designated browsing context must be the chosen one (the browsing context's name isn't set to the given browsing context name). The default behaviour (if the user agent doesn't offer the option to the user, or if the user declines to allow a browsing context to be used) must be that there must not be a chosen browsing context.
