    If this case occurs, it means that an author has explicitly sandboxed the document that is trying to open a link.

    If the user agent has been configured such that in this instance it will create a new browsing context, and the browsing context is being requested as part of [following a hyperlink](#244.html_following-hyperlinks) whose [link types](#244.html_linkTypes) include the [`noreferrer`](#244.html_link-type-noreferrer) keyword

    A new [top-level browsing context](#244.html_top-level-browsing-context) must be created. If the given browsing context name is not `_blank`, then the new top-level browsing context's name must be the given browsing context name (otherwise, it has no name). The chosen browsing context must be this new browsing context. The creation of such a [browsing context](#244.html_browsing-context) is <dfn id="244.html_a-new-start-for-session-storage">a new start for session storage</dfn>.

    If it is immediately [navigated](#244.html_navigate), then the navigation will be done with [replacement enabled](#244.html_replacement-enabled).

    If the user agent has been configured such that in this instance it will create a new browsing context, and the [`noreferrer`](#244.html_link-type-noreferrer) keyword doesn't apply

    A new [auxiliary browsing context](#244.html_auxiliary-browsing-context) must be created, with the [opener browsing context](#244.html_opener-browsing-context) being the current one. If the given browsing context name is not `_blank`, then the new auxiliary browsing context's name must be the given browsing context name (otherwise, it has no name). The chosen browsing context must be this new browsing context.

    If it is immediately [navigated](#244.html_navigate), then the navigation will be done with [replacement enabled](#244.html_replacement-enabled).

    If the user agent has been configured such that in this instance it will reuse the current browsing context

    The chosen browsing context is the current browsing context.

    If the user agent has been configured such that in this instance it will not find a browsing context

    There must not be a chosen browsing context.

    User agent implementors are encouraged to provide a way for users to configure the user agent to always reuse the current browsing context.

    If the current browsing context's [active document](#244.html_active-document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#244.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) has the [sandboxed navigation browsing context flag](#244.html_sandboxed-navigation-browsing-context-flag) set and the chosen browsing context picked above, if any, is a new browsing context (whether top-level or auxiliary), then all the flags that are set in the current browsing context's [active document](#244.html_active-document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#244.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) when the new browsing context is created must be set in the new browsing context's [popup sandboxing flag set](#244.html_popup-sandboxing-flag-set), and the current browsing context must be set as the new browsing context's [one permitted sandboxed navigator](#244.html_one-permitted-sandboxed-navigator).

### 5.2 The [`Window`](#245.html_window) object

```
[Global]
/*sealed*/ interface Window : EventTarget {
  // the current browsing context
  [Unforgeable] readonly attribute WindowProxy window;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute WindowProxy self;
  [Unforgeable] readonly attribute Document document;
           attribute DOMString name; 
  [PutForwards=href, Unforgeable] readonly attribute Location location;
  readonly attribute History history;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp locationbar;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp menubar;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp personalbar;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp scrollbars;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp statusbar;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp toolbar;
           attribute DOMString status;
  void close();
  readonly attribute boolean closed;
  void stop();
  void focus();
  void blur();

  // other browsing contexts
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute WindowProxy frames;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  [Unforgeable] readonly attribute WindowProxy top;
           attribute WindowProxy? opener;
  readonly attribute WindowProxy parent;
  readonly attribute Element? frameElement;
  WindowProxy open(optional DOMString url = "about:blank", optional DOMString target = "_blank", optional DOMString features = "", optional boolean replace = false);
  getter WindowProxy (unsigned long index);
  getter object (DOMString name);

  // the user agent
  readonly attribute Navigator navigator; 
  readonly attribute External external;
  readonly attribute ApplicationCache applicationCache;

  // user prompts
  void alert(optional DOMString message = "");
  boolean confirm(optional DOMString message = "");
  DOMString? prompt(optional DOMString message = "", optional DOMString default = "");
  void print();

};
Window implements GlobalEventHandlers;
Window implements WindowEventHandlers;
```

`window` . [`window`](#245.html_dom-window)
`window` . [`frames`](#245.html_dom-frames)
`window` . [`self`](#245.html_dom-self)

These attributes all return `window`.

`window` . [`document`](#245.html_dom-document-0)

Returns the [`Document`](#245.html_document) associated with `window`.

`document` . [`defaultView`](#245.html_dom-document-defaultview)

Returns the [`Window`](#245.html_window) object of the [active document](#245.html_active-document).

The [`Window`](#245.html_window) interface must only be exposed to JavaScript if the [JavaScript global environment](#245.html_javascript-global-environment) is a [document environment](#245.html_document-environment).

The <dfn id="245.html_dom-window" data-anolis-xref="dom-window">`window`</dfn>, <dfn id="245.html_dom-frames" data-anolis-xref="dom-frames">`frames`</dfn>, and <dfn id="245.html_dom-self" data-anolis-xref="dom-self">`self`</dfn> IDL attributes must all return the [`Window`](#245.html_window) object's [browsing context](#245.html_browsing-context)'s [`WindowProxy`](#245.html_windowproxy) object.

The <dfn id="245.html_dom-document-0" data-anolis-xref="dom-document">`document`</dfn> IDL attribute must return [the `Window` object's newest `Document` object](#245.html_concept-document-window).

The <dfn id="245.html_dom-document-defaultview" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-defaultView">`defaultView`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`Document`](#245.html_document) interface must return the [`Document`](#245.html_document)'s [browsing context](#245.html_browsing-context)'s [`WindowProxy`](#245.html_windowproxy) object, if there is one, or null otherwise.

* * *

For historical reasons, [`Window`](#245.html_window) objects must also have a writable, configurable, non-enumerable property named <dfn id="245.html_htmldocument">`HTMLDocument`</dfn> whose value is the [`Document`](#245.html_document) interface object.

#### 5.2.1 Security

This section describes a security model that is underdefined, imperfect, and does not match implementations. Work is ongoing to attempt to resolve this, but in the meantime, please do not rely on this section for precision. Implementors are urged to send their feedback on how cross-origin cross-global access to [`Window`](#246.html_window) and [`Location`](#246.html_location) objects should work. See [bug 20701](https://www.w3.org/Bugs/Public/show_bug.cgi?id=20701).

User agents must throw a [`SecurityError`](#246.html_securityerror) exception whenever any properties of a [`Window`](#246.html_window) object are accessed when the [incumbent settings object](#246.html_incumbent-settings-object) specifies an [effective script origin](#246.html_effective-script-origin) that is not the [same](#246.html_same-origin) as [the `Window` object's `Document`](#246.html_concept-document-window)'s [effective script origin](#246.html_effective-script-origin), with the following exceptions:

*   The [`location`](#246.html_dom-location) attribute
*   The `postMessage()` method
*   The [`window`](#246.html_dom-window) attribute
*   The [`frames`](#246.html_dom-frames) attribute
*   The [`self`](#246.html_dom-self) attribute
*   The [`top`](#246.html_dom-top) attribute
*   The [`parent`](#246.html_dom-parent) attribute
*   The [`opener`](#246.html_dom-opener) attribute
*   The [`closed`](#246.html_dom-window-closed) attribute
*   The [`close()`](#246.html_dom-window-close) method
*   The [`blur()`](#246.html_dom-window-blur) method
*   The [`focus()`](#246.html_dom-window-focus) method
*   The [dynamic nested browsing context properties](#246.html_dynamic-nested-browsing-context-properties)

When the [incumbent settings object](#246.html_incumbent-settings-object) specifies an [effective script origin](#246.html_effective-script-origin) that is different than a [`Window` object's `Document`](#246.html_concept-document-window)'s [effective script origin](#246.html_effective-script-origin), the user agent must act as if any changes to that [`Window`](#246.html_window) object's properties, getters, setters, etc, were not present, and as if all the properties of that [`Window`](#246.html_window) object had their [[Enumerable]] attribute set to false.

For members that return objects (including function objects), each distinct [effective script origin](#246.html_effective-script-origin) that is not the same as the [`Window`](#246.html_window) object's [`Document`](#246.html_document)'s [effective script origin](#246.html_effective-script-origin) must be provided with a separate set of objects. These objects must have the prototype chain appropriate for the script for which the objects are created (not those that would be appropriate for scripts whose [global object](#246.html_global-object), as specified by their [settings object](#246.html_settings-object), is the [`Window`](#246.html_window) object in question).

For instance, if two frames containing [`Document`](#246.html_document)s from different [origins](#246.html_origin-0) access the same [`Window`](#246.html_window) object's `postMessage()` method, they will get distinct objects that are not equal.

#### 5.2.2 APIs for creating and navigating browsing contexts by name

`window` = `window` . [`open`](#247.html_dom-open)( [ `url` [, `target` [, `features` [, `replace` ] ] ] ] )

Opens a window to show `url` (defaults to [`about:blank`](#247.html_about:blank)), and returns it. The `target` argument gives the name of the new window. If a window exists with that name already, it is reused. The `replace` attribute, if true, means that whatever page is currently open in that window will be removed from the window's session history. The `features` argument is ignored.

`window` . [`name`](#247.html_dom-name) [ = `value` ]

Returns the name of the window.

Can be set, to change the name.

`window` . [`close`](#247.html_dom-window-close)()

Closes the window.

`window` . [`closed`](#247.html_dom-window-closed)

Returns true if the window has been closed, false otherwise.

`window` . [`stop`](#247.html_dom-window-stop)()

Cancels the document load.

The <dfn id="247.html_dom-open" data-anolis-xref="dom-open">`open()`</dfn> method on [`Window`](#247.html_window) objects provides a mechanism for [navigating](#247.html_navigate) an existing [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) or opening and navigating an [auxiliary browsing context](#247.html_auxiliary-browsing-context).

The method has four arguments, though they are all optional.

The first argument, `url`, must be a [valid non-empty URL](#247.html_valid-non-empty-url) for a page to load in the browsing context. If the first argument is the empty string, then the `url` argument must be interpreted as "[`about:blank`](#247.html_about:blank)". Otherwise, the argument must be [resolved](#247.html_resolve-a-url) to an [absolute URL](#247.html_absolute-url) (or an error), relative to the [API base URL](#247.html_api-base-url) specified by the [entry settings object](#247.html_entry-settings-object) when the method was invoked.

The second argument, `target`, specifies the [name](#247.html_browsing-context-name) of the browsing context that is to be navigated. It must be a [valid browsing context name or keyword](#247.html_valid-browsing-context-name-or-keyword).

The third argument, `features`, has no defined effect and is mentioned for historical reasons only. User agents may interpret this argument as instructions to set the size and position of the browsing context, but are encouraged to instead ignore the argument entirely.

The fourth argument, `replace`, specifies whether or not the new page will [replace](#247.html_replacement-enabled) the page currently loaded in the browsing context, when `target` identifies an existing browsing context (as opposed to leaving the current page in the browsing context's [session history](#247.html_session-history)).

When the method is invoked, the user agent must first select a [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) to navigate by applying [the rules for choosing a browsing context given a browsing context name](#247.html_the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name) using the `target` argument as the name and the [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) of the script as the context in which the algorithm is executed, unless the user has indicated a preference, in which case the browsing context to navigate may instead be the one indicated by the user.

For example, suppose there is a user agent that supports control-clicking a link to open it in a new tab. If a user clicks in that user agent on an element whose [`onclick`](#247.html_handler-onclick) handler uses the [`window.open()`](#247.html_dom-open) API to open a page in an iframe, but, while doing so, holds the control key down, the user agent could override the selection of the target browsing context to instead target a new tab.

If applying [the rules for choosing a browsing context given a browsing context name](#247.html_the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name) using the `target` argument would result in there not being a chosen browsing context, then throw an [`InvalidAccessError`](#247.html_invalidaccesserror) exception and abort these steps.

Otherwise, if `url` is not "[`about:blank`](#247.html_about:blank)", the user agent must [navigate](#247.html_navigate) the selected [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) to the [absolute URL](#247.html_absolute-url) obtained from [resolving](#247.html_resolve-a-url) `url` earlier, with [exceptions enabled](#247.html_exceptions-enabled). If the `replace` is true or if the [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) was just created as part of [the rules for choosing a browsing context given a browsing context name](#247.html_the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name), then [replacement must be enabled](#247.html_replacement-enabled) also. The navigation must be done with the [responsible browsing context](#247.html_responsible-browsing-context) specified by the [incumbent settings object](#247.html_incumbent-settings-object) as the [source browsing context](#247.html_source-browsing-context). If the [resolve a URL](#247.html_resolve-a-url) algorithm failed, then the user agent may either instead [navigate](#247.html_navigate) to an inline error page, with [exceptions enabled](#247.html_exceptions-enabled) and using the same replacement behavior and source browsing context behavior as described earlier in this paragraph; or treat the `url` as "[`about:blank`](#247.html_about:blank)", acting as described in the next paragraph.

If `url` *is* "[`about:blank`](#247.html_about:blank)", and the [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) was just created as part of [the rules for choosing a browsing context given a browsing context name](#247.html_the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name), then the user agent must instead [queue a task](#247.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#247.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `load` at the selected [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context)'s [`Window`](#247.html_window) object, but with its [`target`](#247.html_dom-event-target) set to the selected [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context)'s [`Window` object's `Document`](#247.html_concept-document-window) object (and the `currentTarget` set to the [`Window`](#247.html_window) object).

The method must return the [`WindowProxy`](#247.html_windowproxy) object of the [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) that was navigated, or null if no browsing context was navigated.

* * *

The <dfn id="247.html_dom-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-name">`name`</dfn> attribute of the [`Window`](#247.html_window) object must, on getting, return the current [name](#247.html_browsing-context-name) of the [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context), and, on setting, set the [name](#247.html_browsing-context-name) of the [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) to the new value.

The name [gets reset](#247.html_resetBCName) when the browsing context is navigated to another domain.

* * *

The <dfn id="247.html_dom-window-close" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-close">`close()`</dfn> method on [`Window`](#247.html_window) objects should, if all the following conditions are met, [close](#247.html_close-a-browsing-context) the [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) `A`:

*   The corresponding [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) `A` is [script-closable](#247.html_script-closable).
*   The [responsible browsing context](#247.html_responsible-browsing-context) specified by the [incumbent settings object](#247.html_incumbent-settings-object) is [familiar with](#247.html_familiar-with) the [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) `A`.
*   The [responsible browsing context](#247.html_responsible-browsing-context) specified by the [incumbent settings object](#247.html_incumbent-settings-object) is [allowed to navigate](#247.html_allowed-to-navigate) the [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) `A`.

A [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) is <dfn id="247.html_script-closable">script-closable</dfn> if it is an [auxiliary browsing context](#247.html_auxiliary-browsing-context) that was created by a script (as opposed to by an action of the user), or if it is a [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) whose [session history](#247.html_session-history) contains only one [`Document`](#247.html_document).

The <dfn id="247.html_dom-window-closed" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-closed">`closed`</dfn> attribute on [`Window`](#247.html_window) objects must return true if the [`Window`](#247.html_window) object's [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) has been [discarded](#247.html_a-browsing-context-is-discarded), and false otherwise.

The <dfn id="247.html_dom-window-stop" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-stop">`stop()`</dfn> method on [`Window`](#247.html_window) objects should, if there is an existing attempt to [navigate](#247.html_navigate) the [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) and that attempt is not currently running the [unload a document](#247.html_unload-a-document) algorithm, cancel that [navigation](#247.html_navigate); then, it must [abort](#247.html_abort-a-document) the [active document](#247.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#247.html_browsing-context) of the [`Window`](#247.html_window) object on which it was invoked.

#### 5.2.3 Accessing other browsing contexts

`window` . [`length`](#248.html_dom-length)

Returns the number of [child browsing contexts](#248.html_child-browsing-context).

`window`[`index`]

Returns the indicated [child browsing context](#248.html_child-browsing-context).

The <dfn id="248.html_dom-length" data-anolis-xref="dom-length">`length`</dfn> IDL attribute on the [`Window`](#248.html_window) interface must return the number of [child browsing contexts](#248.html_child-browsing-context) that are [nested through](#248.html_browsing-context-nested-through) elements that are [in the `Document`](#248.html_in-a-document) that is the [active document](#248.html_active-document) of that [`Window`](#248.html_window) object, if that [`Window`](#248.html_window)'s [browsing context](#248.html_browsing-context) shares the same [event loop](#248.html_event-loop) as the [responsible document](#248.html_responsible-document) specified by the [entry settings object](#248.html_entry-settings-object) accessing the IDL attribute; otherwise, it must return zero.

The [supported property indices](#248.html_supported-property-indices) on the [`Window`](#248.html_window) object at any instant are the numbers in the range 0 .. `n`-1, where `n` is the number returned by the [`length`](#248.html_dom-length) IDL attribute. If `n` is zero then there are no [supported property indices](#248.html_supported-property-indices).

To <dfn id="248.html_dom-window-item" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-item">determine the value of an indexed property</dfn> `index` of a [`Window`](#248.html_window) object, the user agent must return the [`WindowProxy`](#248.html_windowproxy) object of the `index`th [child browsing context](#248.html_child-browsing-context) of the [`Document`](#248.html_document) that is nested through an element that is [in the `Document`](#248.html_in-a-document), sorted in the [tree order](#248.html_tree-order) of the elements nesting those [browsing contexts](#248.html_browsing-context).

These properties are the <dfn id="248.html_dynamic-nested-browsing-context-properties">dynamic nested browsing context properties</dfn>.

#### 5.2.4 Named access on the [`Window`](#249.html_window) object

`window`[`name`]

Returns the indicated element or collection of elements.

The [`Window`](#249.html_window) interface [supports named properties](#249.html_support-named-properties). The [supported property names](#249.html_supported-property-names) at any moment consist of the following, in [tree order](#249.html_tree-order), ignoring later duplicates:

*   the [browsing context name](#249.html_browsing-context-name) of any [child browsing context](#249.html_child-browsing-context) of the [active document](#249.html_active-document) whose name is not the empty string,
*   the value of the `name` content attribute for all [`a`](#249.html_the-a-element), [`applet`](#249.html_the-applet-element), [`area`](#249.html_the-area-element), [`embed`](#249.html_the-embed-element), [`form`](#249.html_the-form-element), [`frameset`](#249.html_frameset), [`img`](#249.html_the-img-element), and [`object`](#249.html_the-object-element) elements in the [active document](#249.html_active-document) that have a non-empty `name` content attribute, and
*   the value of the [`id`](#249.html_the-id-attribute) content attribute of any [HTML element](#249.html_html-elements) in the [active document](#249.html_active-document) with a non-empty [`id`](#249.html_the-id-attribute) content attribute.

To [determine the value of a named property](#249.html_determine-the-value-of-a-named-property) `name` when <dfn id="249.html_dom-window-nameditem" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-namedItem">the `Window` object is indexed for property retrieval</dfn>, the user agent must return the value obtained using the following steps:

1.  Let `objects` be the list of [named objects](#249.html_dom-window-nameditem-filter) with the name `name` in the [active document](#249.html_active-document).

    There will be at least one such object, by definition.

2.  If `objects` contains a [nested browsing context](#249.html_nested-browsing-context), then return the [`WindowProxy`](#249.html_windowproxy) object of the [nested browsing context](#249.html_nested-browsing-context) corresponding to the first [browsing context container](#249.html_browsing-context-container) in [tree order](#249.html_tree-order) whose [browsing context](#249.html_browsing-context) is in `objects`, and abort these steps.

3.  Otherwise, if `objects` has only one element, return that element and abort these steps.

4.  Otherwise return an [`HTMLCollection`](#249.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#249.html_document) node, whose filter matches only [named objects](#249.html_dom-window-nameditem-filter) with the name `name`. (By definition, these will all be elements.)

<dfn id="249.html_dom-window-nameditem-filter" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-nameditem-filter">Named objects</dfn> with the name `name`, for the purposes of the above algorithm, are those that are either:

*   [child browsing contexts](#249.html_child-browsing-context) of the [active document](#249.html_active-document) whose name is `name`,
*   [`a`](#249.html_the-a-element), [`applet`](#249.html_the-applet-element), [`area`](#249.html_the-area-element), [`embed`](#249.html_the-embed-element), [`form`](#249.html_the-form-element), [`frameset`](#249.html_frameset), [`img`](#249.html_the-img-element), or [`object`](#249.html_the-object-element) elements that have a `name` content attribute whose value is `name`, or
*   [HTML elements](#249.html_html-elements) that have an [`id`](#249.html_the-id-attribute) content attribute whose value is `name`.

#### 5.2.5 Garbage collection and browsing contexts

A [browsing context](#250.html_browsing-context) has a strong reference to each of its [`Document`](#250.html_document)s and its [`WindowProxy`](#250.html_windowproxy) object, and the user agent itself has a strong reference to its [top-level browsing contexts](#250.html_top-level-browsing-context).

A [`Document`](#250.html_document) has a strong reference to its [`Window`](#250.html_window) object.

A [`Window`](#250.html_window) object [has a strong reference](#250.html_implied-strong-reference) to its [`Document`](#250.html_document) object through its [`document`](#250.html_dom-document-0) attribute. Thus, references from other scripts to either of those objects will keep both alive. Similarly, both [`Document`](#250.html_document) and [`Window`](#250.html_window) objects have [implied strong references](#250.html_implied-strong-reference) to the [`WindowProxy`](#250.html_windowproxy) object.

Each [script](#250.html_concept-script) has a strong reference to its [settings object](#250.html_settings-object), and each [script settings object](#250.html_script-settings-object) has strong references to its [global object](#250.html_global-object), [responsible browsing context](#250.html_responsible-browsing-context), and [responsible document](#250.html_responsible-document).

When a [browsing context](#250.html_browsing-context) is to <dfn id="250.html_discard-a-document">discard a `Document`</dfn>, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Set the [`Document`](#250.html_document)'s *[salvageable](#250.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state to false.

2.  Run any [unloading document cleanup steps](#250.html_unloading-document-cleanup-steps) for the [`Document`](#250.html_document) that are defined by this specification and [other applicable specifications](#250.html_other-applicable-specifications).

3.  [Abort the `Document`](#250.html_abort-a-document).

4.  Remove any [tasks](#250.html_concept-task) associated with the [`Document`](#250.html_document) in any [task source](#250.html_task-source), without running those tasks.

5.  [Discard](#250.html_a-browsing-context-is-discarded) all the [child browsing contexts](#250.html_child-browsing-context) of the [`Document`](#250.html_document).

6.  Lose the strong reference from the [`Document`](#250.html_document)'s [browsing context](#250.html_browsing-context) to the [`Document`](#250.html_document).

Whenever a [`Document`](#250.html_document) object is [discarded](#250.html_discard-a-document), it is also removed from the list of the worker's [`Document`](#250.html_document)s of each worker whose list contains that [`Document`](#250.html_document).

When <dfn id="250.html_a-browsing-context-is-discarded">a *browsing context* is discarded</dfn>, the strong reference from the user agent itself to the [browsing context](#250.html_browsing-context) must be severed, and all the [`Document`](#250.html_document) objects for all the entries in the [browsing context](#250.html_browsing-context)'s session history must be [discarded](#250.html_discard-a-document) as well.

User agents may [discard](#250.html_a-browsing-context-is-discarded) [top-level browsing contexts](#250.html_top-level-browsing-context) at any time (typically, in response to user requests, e.g. when a user force-closes a window containing one or more [top-level browsing contexts](#250.html_top-level-browsing-context)). Other [browsing contexts](#250.html_browsing-context) must be discarded once their [`WindowProxy`](#250.html_windowproxy) object is eligible for garbage collection.

#### 5.2.6 Closing browsing contexts

When the user agent is required to <dfn id="251.html_close-a-browsing-context">close a browsing context</dfn>, it must run the following steps:

1.  Let `specified browsing context` be the [browsing context](#251.html_browsing-context) being closed.

2.  [Prompt to unload](#251.html_prompt-to-unload-a-document) the [active document](#251.html_active-document) of the `specified browsing context`. If the user [refused to allow the document to be unloaded](#251.html_refused-to-allow-the-document-to-be-unloaded), then abort these steps.

3.  [Unload](#251.html_unload-a-document) the [active document](#251.html_active-document) of the `specified browsing context` with the `recycle` parameter set to false.

4.  Remove the `specified browsing context` from the user interface (e.g. close or hide its tab in a tabbed browser).

5.  [Discard](#251.html_a-browsing-context-is-discarded) the `specified browsing context`.

User agents should offer users the ability to arbitrarily [close](#251.html_close-a-browsing-context) any [top-level browsing context](#251.html_top-level-browsing-context).

#### 5.2.7 Browser interface elements

To allow Web pages to integrate with Web browsers, certain Web browser interface elements are exposed in a limited way to scripts in Web pages.

Each interface element is represented by a [`BarProp`](#252.html_barprop) object:

```
interface BarProp {
           attribute boolean visible;
};
```

`window` . [`locationbar`](#252.html_dom-window-locationbar) . [`visible`](#252.html_dom-barprop-visible)

Returns true if the location bar is visible; otherwise, returns false.

`window` . [`menubar`](#252.html_dom-window-menubar) . [`visible`](#252.html_dom-barprop-visible)

Returns true if the menu bar is visible; otherwise, returns false.

`window` . [`personalbar`](#252.html_dom-window-personalbar) . [`visible`](#252.html_dom-barprop-visible)

Returns true if the personal bar is visible; otherwise, returns false.

`window` . [`scrollbars`](#252.html_dom-window-scrollbars) . [`visible`](#252.html_dom-barprop-visible)

Returns true if the scroll bars are visible; otherwise, returns false.

`window` . [`statusbar`](#252.html_dom-window-statusbar) . [`visible`](#252.html_dom-barprop-visible)

Returns true if the status bar is visible; otherwise, returns false.

`window` . [`toolbar`](#252.html_dom-window-toolbar) . [`visible`](#252.html_dom-barprop-visible)

Returns true if the toolbar is visible; otherwise, returns false.

The <dfn id="252.html_dom-barprop-visible" data-anolis-xref="dom-BarProp-visible">visible</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return either true or a value determined by the user agent to most accurately represent the visibility state of the user interface element that the object represents, as described below. On setting, the new value must be discarded.

The following [`BarProp`](#252.html_barprop) objects exist for each [`Document`](#252.html_document) object in a [browsing context](#252.html_browsing-context). Some of the user interface elements represented by these objects might have no equivalent in some user agents; for those user agents, except when otherwise specified, the object must act as if it was present and visible (i.e. its [`visible`](#252.html_dom-barprop-visible) attribute must return true).

<dfn id="252.html_the-location-bar-barprop-object">The location bar `BarProp` object</dfn>

Represents the user interface element that contains a control that displays the URL of the [active document](#252.html_active-document), or some similar interface concept.

<dfn id="252.html_the-menu-bar-barprop-object">The menu bar `BarProp` object</dfn>

Represents the user interface element that contains a list of commands in menu form, or some similar interface concept.

<dfn id="252.html_the-personal-bar-barprop-object">The personal bar `BarProp` object</dfn>

Represents the user interface element that contains links to the user's favorite pages, or some similar interface concept.

<dfn id="252.html_the-scrollbar-barprop-object">The scrollbar `BarProp` object</dfn>

Represents the user interface element that contains a scrolling mechanism, or some similar interface concept.

<dfn id="252.html_the-status-bar-barprop-object">The status bar `BarProp` object</dfn>

Represents a user interface element found immediately below or after the document, as appropriate for the user's media. If the user agent has no such user interface element, then the object may act as if the corresponding user interface element was absent (i.e. its [`visible`](#252.html_dom-barprop-visible) attribute may return false).

<dfn id="252.html_the-toolbar-barprop-object">The toolbar `BarProp` object</dfn>

Represents the user interface element found immediately above or before the document, as appropriate for the user's media. If the user agent has no such user interface element, then the object may act as if the corresponding user interface element was absent (i.e. its [`visible`](#252.html_dom-barprop-visible) attribute may return false).

The <dfn id="252.html_dom-window-locationbar" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-locationbar">`locationbar`</dfn> attribute must return [the location bar `BarProp` object](#252.html_the-location-bar-barprop-object).

The <dfn id="252.html_dom-window-menubar" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-menubar">`menubar`</dfn> attribute must return [the menu bar `BarProp` object](#252.html_the-menu-bar-barprop-object).

The <dfn id="252.html_dom-window-personalbar" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-personalbar">`personalbar`</dfn> attribute must return [the personal bar `BarProp` object](#252.html_the-personal-bar-barprop-object).

The <dfn id="252.html_dom-window-scrollbars" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-scrollbars">`scrollbars`</dfn> attribute must return [the scrollbar `BarProp` object](#252.html_the-scrollbar-barprop-object).

The <dfn id="252.html_dom-window-statusbar" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-statusbar">`statusbar`</dfn> attribute must return [the status bar `BarProp` object](#252.html_the-status-bar-barprop-object).

The <dfn id="252.html_dom-window-toolbar" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-toolbar">`toolbar`</dfn> attribute must return [the toolbar `BarProp` object](#252.html_the-toolbar-barprop-object).

* * *

For historical reasons, the <dfn id="252.html_dom-window-status" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-status">`status`</dfn> attribute on the [`Window`](#252.html_window) object must, on getting, return the last string it was set to, and on setting, must set itself to the new value. When the [`Window`](#252.html_window) object is created, the attribute must be set to the empty string. It does not do anything else.

#### 5.2.8 The [`WindowProxy`](#253.html_windowproxy) object

As mentioned earlier, each [browsing context](#253.html_browsing-context) has a <dfn id="253.html_windowproxy">`WindowProxy`</dfn> object. This object is unusual in that all operations that would be performed on it must be performed on the [`Window`](#253.html_window) object of the [browsing context](#253.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#253.html_active-document) instead. It is thus indistinguishable from that [`Window`](#253.html_window) object in every way until the [browsing context](#253.html_browsing-context) is navigated.

There is no [`WindowProxy`](#253.html_windowproxy) interface object.

The [`WindowProxy`](#253.html_windowproxy) object allows scripts to act as if each [browsing context](#253.html_browsing-context) had a single [`Window`](#253.html_window) object, while still keeping separate [`Window`](#253.html_window) objects for each [`Document`](#253.html_document).

In the following example, the variable `x` is set to the [`WindowProxy`](#253.html_windowproxy) object returned by the [`window`](#253.html_dom-window) accessor on the global object. All of the expressions following the assignment return true, because in every respect, the [`WindowProxy`](#253.html_windowproxy) object acts like the underlying [`Window`](#253.html_window) object.

```
var x = window;
x instanceof Window; // true
x === this; // true
```

### 5.3 Origin

Origins are the fundamental currency of the Web's security model. Two actors in the Web platform that share an origin are assumed to trust each other and to have the same authority. Actors with differing origins are considered potentially hostile versus each other, and are isolated from each other to varying degrees.

For example, if Example Bank's Web site, hosted at `bank.example.com`, tries to examine the DOM of Example Charity's Web site, hosted at `charity.example.org`, a [`SecurityError`](#254.html_securityerror) exception will be raised.

* * *

The <dfn id="254.html_origin-0">origin</dfn> of a resource and the <dfn id="254.html_effective-script-origin">effective script origin</dfn> of a resource are both either opaque identifiers or tuples consisting of a scheme component, a host component, a port component, and optionally extra data.

The extra data could include the certificate of the site when using encrypted connections, to ensure that if the site's secure certificate changes, the origin is considered to change as well.

An [origin](#254.html_origin-0) or [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) can be defined as an <dfn id="254.html_concept-origin-alias" data-anolis-xref="concept-origin-alias">alias</dfn> to another [origin](#254.html_origin-0) or [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin). The value of the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) or [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) is then the value of the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) or [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) to which it is an alias.

These characteristics are defined as follows:

For URLs

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) and [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) of the URL are the origin defined in The Web Origin Concept. [[ORIGIN]](#254.html_refsORIGIN)

For [`Document`](#254.html_document) objects

If a [`Document`](#254.html_document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#254.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) has its [sandboxed origin browsing context flag](#254.html_sandboxed-origin-browsing-context-flag) set

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) is a globally unique identifier assigned when the [`Document`](#254.html_document) is created.

The [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) is initially an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of the [`Document`](#254.html_document).

If a [`Document`](#254.html_document) was served over the network and has an address that uses a URL scheme with a server-based naming authority

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) is an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of [the `Document`'s address](#254.html_the-document's-address).

The [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) is initially an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of the [`Document`](#254.html_document).

If a [`Document`](#254.html_document) was generated from a [`data:` URL](#254.html_data-protocol) found in another [`Document`](#254.html_document) or in a script

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) is an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) specified by the [incumbent settings object](#254.html_incumbent-settings-object) when the [navigate](#254.html_navigate) algorithm was invoked, or, if no [script](#254.html_concept-script) was involved, of the [`Document`](#254.html_document) of the element that initiated the [navigation](#254.html_navigate) to that URL.

The [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) is initially an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) of that same [script settings object](#254.html_script-settings-object) or [`Document`](#254.html_document).

If a [`Document`](#254.html_document) is the initial "[`about:blank`](#254.html_about:blank)" document

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) and [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) of the [`Document`](#254.html_document) are [those it was assigned when its browsing context was created](#254.html_about-blank-origin).

If a [`Document`](#254.html_document) was created as part of the processing for [`javascript:` URLs](#254.html_javascript-protocol)

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) is an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of the [active document](#254.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#254.html_browsing-context) being navigated when the [navigate](#254.html_navigate) algorithm was invoked.

The [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) is initially an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) of that same [`Document`](#254.html_document).

If a [`Document`](#254.html_document) is [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#254.html_an-iframe-srcdoc-document)

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of the [`Document`](#254.html_document) is an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of the [`Document`](#254.html_document)'s [browsing context](#254.html_browsing-context)'s [browsing context container](#254.html_browsing-context-container)'s [`Document`](#254.html_document).

The [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) is initially an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) of the [`Document`](#254.html_document)'s [browsing context](#254.html_browsing-context)'s [browsing context container](#254.html_browsing-context-container)'s [`Document`](#254.html_document).

If a [`Document`](#254.html_document) was obtained in some other manner (e.g. a [`data:` URL](#254.html_data-protocol) typed in by the user or that was returned as the location of an HTTP redirect ([or equivalent](#254.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes) in other protocols), a [`Document`](#254.html_document) created using the [`createDocument()`](#254.html_dom-domimplementation-createdocument) API, etc)

The default behavior as defined in the DOM standard applies. [[DOM]](#254.html_refsDOM).

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) is a globally unique identifier assigned when the [`Document`](#254.html_document) is created, and the [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) is initially an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of the [`Document`](#254.html_document).

The [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin) of a [`Document`](#254.html_document) can be manipulated using the [`document.domain`](#254.html_dom-document-domain) IDL attribute.

For images of [`img`](#254.html_the-img-element) elements

If the image data is [CORS-cross-origin](#254.html_cors-cross-origin)

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) is a globally unique identifier assigned when the image is created.

If the image data is [CORS-same-origin](#254.html_cors-same-origin)

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) is an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of the [`img`](#254.html_the-img-element) element's [`Document`](#254.html_document).

Images do not have an [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin).

For [`audio`](#254.html_the-audio-element) and [`video`](#254.html_the-video-element) elements

If the [media data](#254.html_media-data) is [CORS-cross-origin](#254.html_cors-cross-origin)

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) is a globally unique identifier assigned when the [media data](#254.html_media-data) is [fetched](#254.html_fetch).

If the [media data](#254.html_media-data) is [CORS-same-origin](#254.html_cors-same-origin)

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) is an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of the [media element](#254.html_media-element)'s [`Document`](#254.html_document).

[Media elements](#254.html_media-element) do not have an [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin).

For fonts

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of a downloadable Web font is an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of the [absolute URL](#254.html_absolute-url) used to obtain the font (after any redirects). [[CSSFONTS]](#254.html_refsCSSFONTS) [[CSSFONTLOAD]](#254.html_refsCSSFONTLOAD)

The [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of a locally installed system font is an [alias](#254.html_concept-origin-alias) to the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) of the [`Document`](#254.html_document) in which that font is being used.

Fonts do not have an [effective script origin](#254.html_effective-script-origin).

Other specifications can override the above definitions by themselves specifying the origin of a particular URL, [`Document`](#254.html_document), image, [media element](#254.html_media-element), or font.

* * *

The <dfn id="254.html_unicode-serialization-of-an-origin">Unicode serialization of an origin</dfn> is the string obtained by applying the following algorithm to the given [origin](#254.html_origin-0):

1.  If the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) in question is not a scheme/host/port tuple, then return the literal string "`null`" and abort these steps.

2.  Otherwise, let `result` be the scheme part of the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) tuple.

3.  Append the string "`://`" to `result`.

4.  Apply the IDNA ToUnicode algorithm to each component of the host part of the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) tuple, and append the results — each component, in the same order, separated by "." (U+002E) characters — to `result`. [[RFC5890]](#254.html_refsRFC5890)

5.  If the port part of the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) tuple gives a port that is different from the default port for the protocol given by the scheme part of the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) tuple, then append a ":" (U+003A) character and the given port, in base ten, to `result`.

6.  Return `result`.

The <dfn id="254.html_ascii-serialization-of-an-origin">ASCII serialization of an origin</dfn> is the string obtained by applying the following algorithm to the given [origin](#254.html_origin-0):

1.  If the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) in question is not a scheme/host/port tuple, then return the literal string "`null`" and abort these steps.

2.  Otherwise, let `result` be the scheme part of the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) tuple.

3.  Append the string "`://`" to `result`.

4.  Apply the IDNA ToASCII algorithm to the host part of the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) tuple, with both the AllowUnassigned and UseSTD3ASCIIRules flags set, and append the results to `result`.

    If ToASCII fails to convert one of the components of the string, e.g. because it is too long or because it contains invalid characters, then return the empty string and abort these steps. [[RFC5890]](#254.html_refsRFC5890)

5.  If the port part of the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) tuple gives a port that is different from the default port for the protocol given by the scheme part of the [origin](#254.html_origin-0) tuple, then append a ":" (U+003A) character and the given port, in base ten, to `result`.

6.  Return `result`.

Two [origins](#254.html_origin-0) are said to be the <dfn id="254.html_same-origin">same origin</dfn> if the following algorithm returns true:

1.  Let `A` be the first [origin](#254.html_origin-0) being compared, and `B` be the second [origin](#254.html_origin-0) being compared.

2.  If `A` and `B` are both opaque identifiers, and their value is equal, then return true.

3.  Otherwise, if either `A` or `B` or both are opaque identifiers, return false.

4.  If `A` and `B` have scheme components that are not identical, return false.

5.  If `A` and `B` have host components that are not identical, return false.

6.  If `A` and `B` have port components that are not identical, return false.

7.  If either `A` or `B` have additional data, but that data is not identical for both, return false.

8.  Return true.

#### 5.3.1 Relaxing the same-origin restriction

`document` . [`domain`](#255.html_dom-document-domain) [ = `domain` ]

Returns the current domain used for security checks.

Can be set to a value that removes subdomains, to change the [effective script origin](#255.html_effective-script-origin) to allow pages on other subdomains of the same domain (if they do the same thing) to access each other. (Can't be set in sandboxed [`iframe`](#255.html_the-iframe-element)s.)

The <dfn id="255.html_dom-document-domain" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-domain">`domain`</dfn> attribute on [`Document`](#255.html_document) objects must be initialized to [the document's domain](#255.html_the-document's-domain), if it has one, and the empty string otherwise. If [the document's domain](#255.html_the-document's-domain) starts with a "[" (U+005B) character and ends with a "]" (U+005D) character, it is an IPv6 address; these square brackets must be omitted when initializing the attribute's value.

On getting, the attribute must return its current value, unless the [`Document`](#255.html_document) has no [browsing context](#255.html_browsing-context), in which case it must return the empty string.

On setting, the user agent must run the following algorithm:

1.  If the [`Document`](#255.html_document) has no [browsing context](#255.html_browsing-context), throw a [`SecurityError`](#255.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps.

2.  If the [`Document`](#255.html_document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#255.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) has its [sandboxed `document.domain` browsing context flag](#255.html_sandboxed-document.domain-browsing-context-flag) set, throw a [`SecurityError`](#255.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps.

3.  If the new value is an IPv4 or IPv6 address, let `new value` be the new value. Otherwise, apply the IDNA ToASCII algorithm to the new value, with both the AllowUnassigned and UseSTD3ASCIIRules flags set, and let `new value` be the result of the ToASCII algorithm.

    If ToASCII fails to convert one of the components of the string, e.g. because it is too long or because it contains invalid characters, then throw a [`SecurityError`](#255.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps. [[RFC5890]](#255.html_refsRFC5890)

4.  If `new value` is not exactly equal to the current value of the [`document.domain`](#255.html_dom-document-domain) attribute, then run these substeps:

    1.  If the current value is an IPv4 or IPv6 address, throw a [`SecurityError`](#255.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps.

    2.  If `new value`, prefixed by a "." (U+002E), does not exactly match the end of the current value, throw a [`SecurityError`](#255.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps.

        If the `new value` is an IPv4 or IPv6 address, it cannot match the `new value` in this way and thus an exception will be thrown here.

    3.  If `new value` matches a suffix in the Public Suffix List, or, if `new value`, prefixed by a "." (U+002E), matches the end of a suffix in the Public Suffix List, then throw a [`SecurityError`](#255.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps. [[PSL]](#255.html_refsPSL)

        Suffixes must be compared after applying the IDNA ToASCII algorithm to them, with both the AllowUnassigned and UseSTD3ASCIIRules flags set, in an [ASCII case-insensitive](#255.html_ascii-case-insensitive) manner. [[RFC5890]](#255.html_refsRFC5890)

5.  Release the [storage mutex](#255.html_storage-mutex).

6.  Set the attribute's value to `new value`.

7.  If the [effective script origin](#255.html_effective-script-origin) of the [`Document`](#255.html_document) is an [alias](#255.html_concept-origin-alias), set it to the value of the [effective script origin](#255.html_effective-script-origin) (essentially de-aliasing the [effective script origin](#255.html_effective-script-origin)).

8.  If `new value` is not the empty string, then run these substeps:

    1.  Set the host part of the [effective script origin](#255.html_effective-script-origin) tuple of the [`Document`](#255.html_document) to `new value`.

    2.  Set the port part of the [effective script origin](#255.html_effective-script-origin) tuple of the [`Document`](#255.html_document) to "manual override" (a value that, for the purposes of [comparing origins](#255.html_same-origin), is identical to "manual override" but not identical to any other value).

The <dfn id="255.html_the-document's-domain" data-anolis-xref="the document's domain">domain</dfn> of a [`Document`](#255.html_document) is the host part of the document's [origin](#255.html_origin-0), if the value of that [origin](#255.html_origin-0) is a scheme/host/port tuple. If it isn't, then the document does not have a domain.

The [`domain`](#255.html_dom-document-domain) attribute is used to enable pages on different hosts of a domain to access each others' DOMs.

Do not use the [`document.domain`](#255.html_dom-document-domain) attribute when using shared hosting. If an untrusted third party is able to host an HTTP server at the same IP address but on a different port, then the same-origin protection that normally protects two different sites on the same host will fail, as the ports are ignored when comparing origins after the [`document.domain`](#255.html_dom-document-domain) attribute has been used.

### 5.4 Sandboxing

A <dfn id="256.html_sandboxing-flag-set">sandboxing flag set</dfn> is a set of zero or more of the following flags, which are used to restrict the abilities that potentially untrusted resources have:

The <dfn id="256.html_sandboxed-navigation-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed navigation browsing context flag</dfn>

This flag [prevents content from navigating browsing contexts other than the sandboxed browsing context itself](#256.html_sandboxLinks) (or browsing contexts further nested inside it), [auxiliary browsing contexts](#256.html_auxiliary-browsing-context) (which are protected by the [sandboxed auxiliary navigation browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-auxiliary-navigation-browsing-context-flag) defined next), and the [top-level browsing context](#256.html_top-level-browsing-context) (which is protected by the [sandboxed top-level navigation browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-top-level-navigation-browsing-context-flag) defined below).

If the [sandboxed auxiliary navigation browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-auxiliary-navigation-browsing-context-flag) is not set, then in certain cases the restrictions nonetheless allow popups (new [top-level browsing contexts](#256.html_top-level-browsing-context)) to be opened. These [browsing contexts](#256.html_browsing-context) always have <dfn id="256.html_one-permitted-sandboxed-navigator">one permitted sandboxed navigator</dfn>, set when the browsing context is created, which allows the [browsing context](#256.html_browsing-context) that created them to actually navigate them. (Otherwise, the [sandboxed navigation browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-navigation-browsing-context-flag) would prevent them from being navigated even if they were opened.)

The <dfn id="256.html_sandboxed-auxiliary-navigation-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed auxiliary navigation browsing context flag</dfn>

This flag [prevents content from creating new auxiliary browsing contexts](#256.html_sandboxWindowOpen), e.g. using the [`target`](#256.html_attr-hyperlink-target) attribute, or the [`window.open()`](#256.html_dom-open) method.

The <dfn id="256.html_sandboxed-top-level-navigation-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed top-level navigation browsing context flag</dfn>

This flag [prevents content from navigating their top-level browsing context](#256.html_sandboxLinks) and [prevents content from closing their top-level browsing context](#256.html_sandboxClose).

When the [sandboxed top-level navigation browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-top-level-navigation-browsing-context-flag) is *not* set, content can navigate its [top-level browsing context](#256.html_top-level-browsing-context), but other [browsing contexts](#256.html_browsing-context) are still protected by the [sandboxed navigation browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-navigation-browsing-context-flag) and possibly the [sandboxed auxiliary navigation browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-auxiliary-navigation-browsing-context-flag).

The <dfn id="256.html_sandboxed-plugins-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed plugins browsing context flag</dfn>

This flag prevents content from instantiating [plugins](#256.html_plugin), whether using [the `embed` element](#256.html_sandboxPluginEmbed), [the `object` element](#256.html_sandboxPluginObject), [the `applet` element](#256.html_sandboxPluginApplet), or through [navigation](#256.html_sandboxPluginNavigate) of a [nested browsing context](#256.html_nested-browsing-context), unless those [plugins](#256.html_plugin) can be [secured](#256.html_concept-plugin-secure).

The <dfn id="256.html_sandboxed-origin-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed origin browsing context flag</dfn>

This flag [forces content into a unique origin](#256.html_sandboxOrigin), thus preventing it from accessing other content from the same [origin](#256.html_origin-0).

This flag also [prevents script from reading from or writing to the `document.cookie` IDL attribute](#256.html_sandboxCookies), and blocks access to `localStorage`. [[WEBSTORAGE]](#256.html_refsWEBSTORAGE)

The <dfn id="256.html_sandboxed-forms-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed forms browsing context flag</dfn>

This flag [blocks form submission](#256.html_sandboxSubmitBlocked).

The <dfn id="256.html_sandboxed-pointer-lock-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed pointer lock browsing context flag</dfn>

This flag disables the Pointer Lock API. [[POINTERLOCK]](#256.html_refsPOINTERLOCK)

The <dfn id="256.html_sandboxed-scripts-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed scripts browsing context flag</dfn>

This flag [blocks script execution](#256.html_sandboxScriptBlocked).

The <dfn id="256.html_sandboxed-automatic-features-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed automatic features browsing context flag</dfn>

This flag blocks features that trigger automatically, such as [automatically playing a video](#256.html_attr-media-autoplay) or [automatically focusing a form control](#256.html_attr-fe-autofocus).

The <dfn id="256.html_sandboxed-fullscreen-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed fullscreen browsing context flag</dfn>

This flag prevents content from using the [`requestFullscreen()`](#256.html_dom-element-requestfullscreen) method.

The <dfn id="256.html_sandboxed-document.domain-browsing-context-flag">sandboxed `document.domain` browsing context flag</dfn>

This flag prevents content from using the [`document.domain`](#256.html_dom-document-domain) feature to change the [effective script origin](#256.html_effective-script-origin).

When the user agent is to <dfn id="256.html_parse-a-sandboxing-directive">parse a sandboxing directive</dfn>, given a string `input`, a [sandboxing flag set](#256.html_sandboxing-flag-set) `output`, and optionally an `allow fullscreen flag`, it must run the following steps:

1.  [Split `input` on spaces](#256.html_split-a-string-on-spaces), to obtain `tokens`.

2.  Let `output` be empty.

3.  Add the following flags to `output`:

    *   The [sandboxed navigation browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-navigation-browsing-context-flag).

    *   The [sandboxed auxiliary navigation browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-auxiliary-navigation-browsing-context-flag), unless `tokens` contains the <dfn id="256.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-popups" data-anolis-xref="attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-popups">`allow-popups`</dfn> keyword.

    *   The [sandboxed top-level navigation browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-top-level-navigation-browsing-context-flag), unless `tokens` contains the <dfn id="256.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation" data-anolis-xref="attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-top-navigation">`allow-top-navigation`</dfn> keyword.

    *   The [sandboxed plugins browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-plugins-browsing-context-flag).

    *   The [sandboxed origin browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-origin-browsing-context-flag), unless the `tokens` contains the <dfn id="256.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin" data-anolis-xref="attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin">`allow-same-origin`</dfn> keyword.

        The [`allow-same-origin`](#256.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-same-origin) keyword is intended for two cases.

        First, it can be used to allow content from the same site to be sandboxed to disable scripting, while still allowing access to the DOM of the sandboxed content.

        Second, it can be used to embed content from a third-party site, sandboxed to prevent that site from opening pop-up windows, etc, without preventing the embedded page from communicating back to its originating site, using the database APIs to store data, etc.

    *   The [sandboxed forms browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-forms-browsing-context-flag), unless `tokens` contains the <dfn id="256.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-forms" data-anolis-xref="attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-forms">`allow-forms`</dfn> keyword.

    *   The [sandboxed pointer lock browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-pointer-lock-browsing-context-flag), unless `tokens` contains the <dfn id="256.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-pointer-lock" data-anolis-xref="attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-pointer-lock">`allow-pointer-lock`</dfn> keyword.

    *   The [sandboxed scripts browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-scripts-browsing-context-flag), unless `tokens` contains the <dfn id="256.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-scripts" data-anolis-xref="attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-scripts">`allow-scripts`</dfn> keyword.

    *   The [sandboxed automatic features browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-automatic-features-browsing-context-flag), unless `tokens` contains the [`allow-scripts`](#256.html_attr-iframe-sandbox-allow-scripts) keyword (defined above).

        This flag is relaxed by the same keyword as scripts, because when scripts are enabled these features are trivially possible anyway, and it would be unfortunate to force authors to use script to do them when sandboxed rather than allowing them to use the declarative features.

    *   The [sandboxed fullscreen browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-fullscreen-browsing-context-flag), unless the `allow fullscreen flag` was passed to the [parse a sandboxing directive](#256.html_parse-a-sandboxing-directive) flag.

    *   The [sandboxed `document.domain` browsing context flag](#256.html_sandboxed-document.domain-browsing-context-flag).

* * *

Every [top-level browsing context](#256.html_top-level-browsing-context) has a <dfn id="256.html_popup-sandboxing-flag-set">popup sandboxing flag set</dfn>, which is a [sandboxing flag set](#256.html_sandboxing-flag-set). When a [browsing context](#256.html_browsing-context) is created, its [popup sandboxing flag set](#256.html_popup-sandboxing-flag-set) must be empty. It is populated by [the rules for choosing a browsing context given a browsing context name](#256.html_the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name).

Every [nested browsing context](#256.html_nested-browsing-context) has an <dfn id="256.html_iframe-sandboxing-flag-set">`iframe` sandboxing flag set</dfn>, which is a [sandboxing flag set](#256.html_sandboxing-flag-set). Which flags in a [nested browsing context](#256.html_nested-browsing-context)'s [`iframe` sandboxing flag set](#256.html_iframe-sandboxing-flag-set) are set at any particular time is determined by the [`iframe`](#256.html_the-iframe-element) element's [`sandbox`](#256.html_attr-iframe-sandbox) attribute.

Every [`Document`](#256.html_document) has an <dfn id="256.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set">active sandboxing flag set</dfn>, which is a [sandboxing flag set](#256.html_sandboxing-flag-set). When the [`Document`](#256.html_document) is created, its [active sandboxing flag set](#256.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) must be empty. It is populated by the [navigation algorithm](#256.html_navigate).

Every resource that is obtained by the [navigation algorithm](#256.html_navigate) has a <dfn id="256.html_forced-sandboxing-flag-set">forced sandboxing flag set</dfn>, which is a [sandboxing flag set](#256.html_sandboxing-flag-set). A resource by default has no flags set in its [forced sandboxing flag set](#256.html_forced-sandboxing-flag-set), but other specifications can define that certain flags are set.

In particular, the [forced sandboxing flag set](#256.html_forced-sandboxing-flag-set) is used by the Content Security Policy specification. [[CSP]](#256.html_refsCSP)

* * *

When a user agent is to <dfn id="256.html_implement-the-sandboxing">implement the sandboxing</dfn> for a [`Document`](#256.html_document), it must populate [`Document`](#256.html_document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#256.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) with the union of the flags that are present in the following [sandboxing flag sets](#256.html_sandboxing-flag-set) at the time the [`Document`](#256.html_document) object is created:

*   If the [`Document`](#256.html_document)'s [browsing context](#256.html_browsing-context) is a [top-level browsing context](#256.html_top-level-browsing-context), then: the flags set on the [browsing context](#256.html_browsing-context)'s [popup sandboxing flag set](#256.html_popup-sandboxing-flag-set).

*   If the [`Document`](#256.html_document)'s [browsing context](#256.html_browsing-context) is a [nested browsing context](#256.html_nested-browsing-context), then: the flags set on the [browsing context](#256.html_browsing-context)'s [`iframe` sandboxing flag set](#256.html_iframe-sandboxing-flag-set).

*   If the [`Document`](#256.html_document)'s [browsing context](#256.html_browsing-context) is a [nested browsing context](#256.html_nested-browsing-context), then: the flags set on the [browsing context](#256.html_browsing-context)'s [parent browsing context](#256.html_parent-browsing-context)'s [active document](#256.html_active-document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#256.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set).

*   The flags set on the [`Document`](#256.html_document)'s resource's [forced sandboxing flag set](#256.html_forced-sandboxing-flag-set), if it has one.

### 5.5 Session history and navigation

#### 5.5.1 The session history of browsing contexts

The sequence of [`Document`](#258.html_document)s in a [browsing context](#258.html_browsing-context) is its <dfn id="258.html_session-history">session history</dfn>. Each [browsing context](#258.html_browsing-context), including [nested browsing contexts](#258.html_nested-browsing-context), has a distinct session history. A [browsing context](#258.html_browsing-context)'s session history consists of a flat list of [session history entries](#258.html_session-history-entry). Each <dfn id="258.html_session-history-entry">session history entry</dfn> consists, at a minimum, of a URL, and each entry may in addition have a [state object](#258.html_state-object), a title, a [`Document`](#258.html_document) object, form data, a scroll position, and other information associated with it.

Each entry, when first created, has a [`Document`](#258.html_document). However, when a [`Document`](#258.html_document) is not [active](#258.html_fully-active), it's possible for it to be [discarded](#258.html_discard-a-document) to free resources. The URL and other data in a [session history entry](#258.html_session-history-entry) is then used to bring a new [`Document`](#258.html_document) into being to take the place of the original, should the user agent find itself having to reactivate that [`Document`](#258.html_document).

Titles associated with [session history entries](#258.html_session-history-entry) need not have any relation with the current [`title`](#258.html_the-title-element) of the [`Document`](#258.html_document). The title of a [session history entry](#258.html_session-history-entry) is intended to explain the state of the document at that point, so that the user can navigate the document's history.

URLs without associated [state objects](#258.html_state-object) are added to the session history as the user (or script) navigates from page to page.

* * *

Each [`Document`](#258.html_document) object in a [browsing context](#258.html_browsing-context)'s [session history](#258.html_session-history) is associated with a unique [`History`](#258.html_history-1) object which must all model the same underlying [session history](#258.html_session-history).

The <dfn id="258.html_dom-history" data-anolis-xref="dom-history">`history`</dfn> attribute of the [`Window`](#258.html_window) interface must return the object implementing the [`History`](#258.html_history-1) interface for that [`Window` object's newest `Document`](#258.html_concept-document-window).

* * *

A <dfn id="258.html_state-object">state object</dfn> is an object representing a user interface state.

Pages can [add](#258.html_dom-history-pushstate) [state objects](#258.html_state-object) to the session history. These are then [returned to the script](#258.html_event-popstate) when the user (or script) goes back in the history, thus enabling authors to use the "navigation" metaphor even in one-page applications.

[State objects](#258.html_state-object) are intended to be used for two main purposes: first, storing a preparsed description of the state in the URL so that in the simple case an author doesn't have to do the parsing (though one would still need the parsing for handling URLs passed around by users, so it's only a minor optimization), and second, so that the author can store state that one wouldn't store in the URL because it only applies to the current [`Document`](#258.html_document) instance and it would have to be reconstructed if a new [`Document`](#258.html_document) were opened.

An example of the latter would be something like keeping track of the precise coordinate from which a pop-up [`div`](#258.html_the-div-element) was made to animate, so that if the user goes back, it can be made to animate to the same location. Or alternatively, it could be used to keep a pointer into a cache of data that would be fetched from the server based on the information in the URL, so that when going back and forward, the information doesn't have to be fetched again.

* * *

At any point, one of the entries in the session history is the <dfn id="258.html_current-entry">current entry</dfn>. This is the entry representing the [active document](#258.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#258.html_browsing-context). Which entry is the [current entry](#258.html_current-entry) is changed by the algorithms defined in this specification, e.g. during [session history traversal](#258.html_traverse-the-history).

The [current entry](#258.html_current-entry) is usually an entry for the [address](#258.html_the-document's-address) of the [`Document`](#258.html_document). However, it can also be one of the entries for [state objects](#258.html_state-object) added to the history by that document.

<dfn id="258.html_an-entry-with-persisted-user-state">An entry with persisted user state</dfn> is one that also has user-agent defined state. This specification does not specify what kind of state can be stored.

For example, some user agents might want to persist the scroll position, or the values of form controls.

User agents that persist the value of form controls are encouraged to also persist their directionality (the value of the element's [`dir`](#258.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute). This prevents values from being displayed incorrectly after a history traversal when the user had originally entered the values with an explicit, non-default directionality.

Entries that consist of [state objects](#258.html_state-object) share the same [`Document`](#258.html_document) as the entry for the page that was active when they were added.

Contiguous entries that differ just by fragment identifier also share the same [`Document`](#258.html_document).

All entries that share the same [`Document`](#258.html_document) (and that are therefore merely different states of one particular document) are contiguous by definition.

Each [`Document`](#258.html_document) in a [browsing context](#258.html_browsing-context) can also have a <dfn id="258.html_latest-entry">latest entry</dfn>. This is the entry or that [`Document`](#258.html_document) that was most the recently traversed to. When a [`Document`](#258.html_document) is created, it initially has no [latest entry](#258.html_latest-entry).

User agents may [discard](#258.html_discard-a-document) the [`Document`](#258.html_document) objects of entries other than the [current entry](#258.html_current-entry) that are not referenced from any script, reloading the pages afresh when the user or script navigates back to such pages. This specification does not specify when user agents should discard [`Document`](#258.html_document) objects and when they should cache them.

Entries that have had their [`Document`](#258.html_document) objects discarded must, for the purposes of the algorithms given below, act as if they had not. When the user or script navigates back or forwards to a page which has no in-memory DOM objects, any other entries that shared the same [`Document`](#258.html_document) object with it must share the new object as well.

#### 5.5.2 The [`History`](#259.html_history-1) interface

```
interface History {
  readonly attribute long length;
  readonly attribute any state;
  void go(optional long delta);
  void back();
  void forward();
  void pushState(any data, DOMString title, optional DOMString? url = null);
  void replaceState(any data, DOMString title, optional DOMString? url = null);
};
```

`window` . [`history`](#259.html_dom-history) . [`length`](#259.html_dom-history-length)

Returns the number of entries in the [joint session history](#259.html_joint-session-history).

`window` . [`history`](#259.html_dom-history) . [`state`](#259.html_dom-history-state)

Returns the current [state object](#259.html_state-object).

`window` . [`history`](#259.html_dom-history) . [`go`](#259.html_dom-history-go)( [ `delta` ] )

Goes back or forward the specified number of steps in the [joint session history](#259.html_joint-session-history).

A zero delta will reload the current page.

If the delta is out of range, does nothing.

`window` . [`history`](#259.html_dom-history) . [`back`](#259.html_dom-history-back)()

Goes back one step in the [joint session history](#259.html_joint-session-history).

If there is no previous page, does nothing.

`window` . [`history`](#259.html_dom-history) . [`forward`](#259.html_dom-history-forward)()

Goes forward one step in the [joint session history](#259.html_joint-session-history).

If there is no next page, does nothing.

`window` . [`history`](#259.html_dom-history) . [`pushState`](#259.html_dom-history-pushstate)(`data`, `title` [, `url` ] )

Pushes the given data onto the session history, with the given title, and, if provided and not null, the given URL.

`window` . [`history`](#259.html_dom-history) . [`replaceState`](#259.html_dom-history-replacestate)(`data`, `title` [, `url` ] )

Updates the current entry in the session history to have the given data, title, and, if provided and not null, URL.

The <dfn id="259.html_joint-session-history">joint session history</dfn> of a [top-level browsing context](#259.html_top-level-browsing-context) is the union of all the [session histories](#259.html_session-history) of all [browsing contexts](#259.html_browsing-context) of all the [fully active](#259.html_fully-active) [`Document`](#259.html_document) objects that share that [top-level browsing context](#259.html_top-level-browsing-context), with all the entries that are [current entries](#259.html_current-entry) in their respective [session histories](#259.html_session-history) removed except for the [current entry of the joint session history](#259.html_current-entry-of-the-joint-session-history).

The <dfn id="259.html_current-entry-of-the-joint-session-history">current entry of the joint session history</dfn> is the entry that most recently became a [current entry](#259.html_current-entry) in its [session history](#259.html_session-history).

Entries in the [joint session history](#259.html_joint-session-history) are ordered chronologically by the time they were added to their respective [session histories](#259.html_session-history). Each entry has an index; the earliest entry has index 0, and the subsequent entries are numbered with consecutively increasing integers (1, 2, 3, etc).

Since each [`Document`](#259.html_document) in a [browsing context](#259.html_browsing-context) might have a different [event loop](#259.html_event-loop), the actual state of the [joint session history](#259.html_joint-session-history) can be someone nebulous. For example, two sibling [`iframe`](#259.html_the-iframe-element) elements could both [traverse](#259.html_traverse-the-history) from one unique origin to another at the same time, so their precise order might not be well-defined; similarly, since they might only find out about each other later, they might disagree about the length of the [joint session history](#259.html_joint-session-history).

All the getters and setters for attributes, and all the methods, defined on the [`History`](#259.html_history-1) interface, when invoked on a [`History`](#259.html_history-1) object associated with a [`Document`](#259.html_document) that is not [fully active](#259.html_fully-active), must throw a [`SecurityError`](#259.html_securityerror) exception instead of operating as described below.

The <dfn id="259.html_dom-history-length" data-anolis-xref="dom-history-length">`length`</dfn> attribute of the [`History`](#259.html_history-1) interface must return the number of entries in the [top-level browsing context](#259.html_top-level-browsing-context)'s [joint session history](#259.html_joint-session-history).

The actual entries are not accessible from script.

The <dfn id="259.html_dom-history-state" data-anolis-xref="dom-history-state">`state`</dfn> attribute of the [`History`](#259.html_history-1) interface must return the last value it was set to by the user agent. Initially, its value must be null.
