When the <dfn id="259.html_dom-history-go" data-anolis-xref="dom-history-go">`go(``delta``)`</dfn> method is invoked, if the argument to the method was omitted or has the value zero, the user agent must act as if the [`location.reload()`](#259.html_dom-location-reload) method was called instead. Otherwise, the user agent must [traverse the history by a delta](#259.html_traverse-the-history-by-a-delta) whose value is the value of the method's argument.

When the <dfn id="259.html_dom-history-back" data-anolis-xref="dom-history-back">`back()`</dfn> method is invoked, the user agent must [traverse the history by a delta](#259.html_traverse-the-history-by-a-delta) ?1.

When the <dfn id="259.html_dom-history-forward" data-anolis-xref="dom-history-forward">`forward()`</dfn>method is invoked, the user agent must [traverse the history by a delta](#259.html_traverse-the-history-by-a-delta) +1.

* * *

Each [top-level browsing context](#259.html_top-level-browsing-context) has a <dfn id="259.html_session-history-traversal-queue">session history traversal queue</dfn>, initially empty, to which [tasks](#259.html_concept-task) can be added.

Each [top-level browsing context](#259.html_top-level-browsing-context), when created, must asynchronously begin running the following algorithm, known as the <dfn id="259.html_session-history-event-loop">session history event loop</dfn> for that [top-level browsing context](#259.html_top-level-browsing-context):

1.  Wait until this [top-level browsing context](#259.html_top-level-browsing-context)'s [session history traversal queue](#259.html_session-history-traversal-queue) is not empty.

2.  Pull the first [task](#259.html_concept-task) from this [top-level browsing context](#259.html_top-level-browsing-context)'s [session history traversal queue](#259.html_session-history-traversal-queue), and execute it.

3.  Return to the first step of this algorithm.

The [session history event loop](#259.html_session-history-event-loop) helps coordinate cross-browsing-context transitions of the [joint session history](#259.html_joint-session-history): since each [browsing context](#259.html_browsing-context) might, at any particular time, have a different [event loop](#259.html_event-loop) (this can happen if the user agent has more than one [event loop](#259.html_event-loop) per [unit of related browsing contexts](#259.html_unit-of-related-browsing-contexts)), transitions would otherwise have to involve cross-event-loop synchronisation.

* * *

To <dfn id="259.html_traverse-the-history-by-a-delta">traverse the history by a delta</dfn> `delta`, the user agent must append a [task](#259.html_concept-task) to this [top-level browsing context](#259.html_top-level-browsing-context)'s [session history traversal queue](#259.html_session-history-traversal-queue), the [task](#259.html_concept-task) consisting of running the following steps:

1.  Let `delta` be the argument to the method.

2.  If the index of the [current entry of the joint session history](#259.html_current-entry-of-the-joint-session-history) plus `delta` is less than zero or greater than or equal to the number of items in the [joint session history](#259.html_joint-session-history), then abort these steps.

3.  Let `specified entry` be the entry in the [joint session history](#259.html_joint-session-history) whose index is the sum of `delta` and the index of the [current entry of the joint session history](#259.html_current-entry-of-the-joint-session-history).

4.  Let `specified browsing context` be the [browsing context](#259.html_browsing-context) of the `specified entry`.

5.  If the `specified browsing context`'s [active document](#259.html_active-document)'s [unload a document](#259.html_unload-a-document) algorithm is currently running, abort these steps.

6.  [Queue a task](#259.html_queue-a-task) that consists of running the following substeps. The relevant [event loop](#259.html_event-loop) is that of the `specified browsing context`'s [active document](#259.html_active-document). The [task source](#259.html_task-source) for the queued task is the [history traversal task source](#259.html_history-traversal-task-source).

    1.  If there is an ongoing attempt to navigate `specified browsing context` that has not yet [matured](#259.html_concept-navigate-mature) (i.e. it has not passed the point of making its [`Document`](#259.html_document) the [active document](#259.html_active-document)), then cancel that attempt to navigate the [browsing context](#259.html_browsing-context).

    2.  If the `specified browsing context`'s [active document](#259.html_active-document) is not the same [`Document`](#259.html_document) as the [`Document`](#259.html_document) of the `specified entry`, then run these substeps:

        1.  [Fully exit fullscreen](#259.html_fully-exit-fullscreen).

        2.  [Prompt to unload](#259.html_prompt-to-unload-a-document) the [active document](#259.html_active-document) of the `specified browsing context`. If the user [refused to allow the document to be unloaded](#259.html_refused-to-allow-the-document-to-be-unloaded), then abort these steps.

        3.  [Unload](#259.html_unload-a-document) the [active document](#259.html_active-document) of the `specified browsing context` with the `recycle` parameter set to false.

    3.  [Traverse the history](#259.html_traverse-the-history) of the `specified browsing context` to the `specified entry`.

When the user navigates through a [browsing context](#259.html_browsing-context), e.g. using a browser's back and forward buttons, the user agent must [traverse the history by a delta](#259.html_traverse-the-history-by-a-delta) equivalent to the action specified by the user.

* * *

The <dfn id="259.html_dom-history-pushstate" data-anolis-xref="dom-history-pushState">`pushState(``data``,` `title``,` `url``)`</dfn> method adds a state object entry to the history.

The <dfn id="259.html_dom-history-replacestate" data-anolis-xref="dom-history-replaceState">`replaceState(``data``,` `title``,` `url``)`</dfn> method updates the state object, title, and optionally the URL of the [current entry](#259.html_current-entry) in the history.

When either of these methods is invoked, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `cloned data` be a [structured clone](#259.html_structured-clone) of the specified `data`. If this throws an exception, then rethrow that exception and abort these steps.

2.  If the third argument is not null, run these substeps:

    1.  [Resolve](#259.html_resolve-a-url) the value of the third argument, relative to the [API base URL](#259.html_api-base-url) specified by the [entry settings object](#259.html_entry-settings-object).
    2.  If that fails, throw a [`SecurityError`](#259.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps.
    3.  Compare the resulting [parsed URL](#259.html_parsed-url) to the result of applying the [URL parser](#259.html_url-parser-0) algorithm to [the document's address](#259.html_the-document's-address). If any component of these two URLs differ other than the [path](#259.html_concept-url-path), [query](#259.html_concept-url-query), and [fragment](#259.html_concept-url-fragment) components, then throw a [`SecurityError`](#259.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps.
    4.  If the [origin](#259.html_origin-0) of the resulting [absolute URL](#259.html_absolute-url) is not the same as the [origin](#259.html_origin-0) of the [responsible document](#259.html_responsible-document) specified by the [entry settings object](#259.html_entry-settings-object), and either the [path](#259.html_concept-url-path) or [query](#259.html_concept-url-query) components of the two [parsed URLs](#259.html_parsed-url) compared in the previous step differ, throw a [`SecurityError`](#259.html_securityerror) exception and abort these steps. (This prevents sandboxed content from spoofing other pages on the same origin.)
    5.  Let `new URL` be the resulting [absolute URL](#259.html_absolute-url).

    For the purposes of the comparisons in the above substeps, the [path](#259.html_concept-url-path) and [query](#259.html_concept-url-query) components can only be the same if the [scheme](#259.html_concept-url-scheme) component of both [parsed URLs](#259.html_parsed-url) are [relative schemes](#259.html_concept-url-scheme-relative).

3.  If the third argument is null, then let `new URL` be the URL of the [current entry](#259.html_current-entry).

4.  If the method invoked was the [`pushState()`](#259.html_dom-history-pushstate) method:

    1.  Remove all the entries in the [browsing context](#259.html_browsing-context)'s [session history](#259.html_session-history) after the [current entry](#259.html_current-entry). If the [current entry](#259.html_current-entry) is the last entry in the session history, then no entries are removed.

        This [doesn't necessarily have to affect](#259.html_history-notes) the user agent's user interface.

    2.  Remove any [tasks](#259.html_concept-task) queued by the [history traversal task source](#259.html_history-traversal-task-source) that are associated with any [`Document`](#259.html_document) objects in the [top-level browsing context](#259.html_top-level-browsing-context)'s [document family](#259.html_document-family).

    3.  If appropriate, update the [current entry](#259.html_current-entry) to reflect any state that the user agent wishes to persist. The entry is then said to be [an entry with persisted user state](#259.html_an-entry-with-persisted-user-state).

    4.  Add a [state object](#259.html_state-object) entry to the session history, after the [current entry](#259.html_current-entry), with `cloned data` as the [state object](#259.html_state-object), the given `title` as the title, and `new URL` as the URL of the entry.

    5.  Update the [current entry](#259.html_current-entry) to be this newly added entry.

    Otherwise, if the method invoked was the [`replaceState()`](#259.html_dom-history-replacestate) method:

    1.  Update the [current entry](#259.html_current-entry) in the session history so that `cloned data` is the entry's new state object, the given `title` is the new title, and `new URL` is the entry's new URL.

5.  If the [current entry](#259.html_current-entry) in the session history represents a non-GET request (e.g. it was the result of a POST submission) then update it to instead represent a GET request ([or equivalent](#259.html_concept-http-equivalent-get)).

6.  Set [the document's address](#259.html_the-document's-address) to `new URL`.

    Since this is neither a [navigation](#259.html_navigate) of the [browsing context](#259.html_browsing-context) nor a [history traversal](#259.html_traverse-the-history), it does not cause a [`hashchange`](#259.html_event-hashchange) event to be fired.

7.  Set [`history.state`](#259.html_dom-history-state) to a [structured clone](#259.html_structured-clone) of `cloned data`.

8.  Let the [latest entry](#259.html_latest-entry) of the [`Document`](#259.html_document) of the [current entry](#259.html_current-entry) be the [current entry](#259.html_current-entry).

The `title` is purely advisory. User agents might use the title in the user interface.

User agents may limit the number of state objects added to the session history per page. If a page hits the UA-defined limit, user agents must remove the entry immediately after the first entry for that [`Document`](#259.html_document) object in the session history after having added the new entry. (Thus the state history acts as a FIFO buffer for eviction, but as a LIFO buffer for navigation.)

Consider a game where the user can navigate along a line, such that the user is always at some coordinate, and such that the user can bookmark the page corresponding to a particular coordinate, to return to it later.

A static page implementing the x=5 position in such a game could look like the following:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<!-- this is http://example.com/line?x=5 -->
<title>Line Game - 5</title>
<p>You are at coordinate 5 on the line.</p>
<p>
 <a href="?x=6">Advance to 6</a> or
 <a href="?x=4">retreat to 4</a>?
</p>
```

The problem with such a system is that each time the user clicks, the whole page has to be reloaded. Here instead is another way of doing it, using script:

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<!-- this starts off as http://example.com/line?x=5 -->
<title>Line Game - 5</title>
<p>You are at coordinate <span id="coord">5</span> on the line.</p>
<p>
 <a href="?x=6" onclick="go(1); return false;">Advance to 6</a> or
 <a href="?x=4" onclick="go(-1); return false;">retreat to 4</a>?
</p>
<script>
 var currentPage = 5; // prefilled by server
 function go(d) {
   setupPage(currentPage + d);
   history.pushState(currentPage, document.title, '?x=' + currentPage);
 }
 onpopstate = function(event) {
   setupPage(event.state);
 }
 function setupPage(page) {
   currentPage = page;
   document.title = 'Line Game - ' + currentPage;
   document.getElementById('coord').textContent = currentPage;
   document.links[0].href = '?x=' + (currentPage+1);
   document.links[0].textContent = 'Advance to ' + (currentPage+1);
   document.links[1].href = '?x=' + (currentPage-1);
   document.links[1].textContent = 'retreat to ' + (currentPage-1);
 }
</script>
```

In systems without script, this still works like the previous example. However, users that *do* have script support can now navigate much faster, since there is no network access for the same experience. Furthermore, contrary to the experience the user would have with just a na?ve script-based approach, bookmarking and navigating the session history still work.

In the example above, the `data` argument to the [`pushState()`](#259.html_dom-history-pushstate) method is the same information as would be sent to the server, but in a more convenient form, so that the script doesn't have to parse the URL each time the user navigates.

Applications might not use the same title for a [session history entry](#259.html_session-history-entry) as the value of the document's [`title`](#259.html_the-title-element) element at that time. For example, here is a simple page that shows a block in the [`title`](#259.html_the-title-element) element. Clearly, when navigating backwards to a previous state the user does not go back in time, and therefore it would be inappropriate to put the time in the session history title.

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<TITLE>Line</TITLE>
<SCRIPT>
 setInterval(function () { document.title = 'Line - ' + new Date(); }, 1000);
 var i = 1;
 function inc() {
   set(i+1);
   history.pushState(i, 'Line - ' + i);
 }
 function set(newI) {
   i = newI;
   document.forms.F.I.value = newI;
 }
</SCRIPT>
<BODY ONPOPSTATE="set(event.state)">
<FORM NAME=F>
State: <OUTPUT NAME=I>1</OUTPUT> <INPUT VALUE="Increment" TYPE=BUTTON ONCLICK="inc()">
</FORM>
```

#### 5.5.3 The [`Location`](#260.html_location) interface

Each [`Document`](#260.html_document) object in a [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context)'s session history is associated with a unique instance of a [`Location`](#260.html_location) object.

`document` . [`location`](#260.html_dom-document-location) [ = `value` ]
`window` . [`location`](#260.html_dom-location) [ = `value` ]

Returns a [`Location`](#260.html_location) object with the current page's location.

Can be set, to navigate to another page.

The <dfn id="260.html_dom-document-location" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-location">`location`</dfn> attribute of the [`Document`](#260.html_document) interface must return the [`Location`](#260.html_location) object for that [`Document`](#260.html_document) object, if it is in a [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context), and null otherwise.

The <dfn id="260.html_dom-location" data-anolis-xref="dom-location">`location`</dfn> attribute of the [`Window`](#260.html_window) interface must return the [`Location`](#260.html_location) object for that [`Window`](#260.html_window) object's [`Document`](#260.html_document).

[`Location`](#260.html_location) objects provide a representation of [the address](#260.html_the-document's-address) of the [active document](#260.html_active-document) of their [`Document`](#260.html_document)'s [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context), and allow the [current entry](#260.html_current-entry) of the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context)'s session history to be changed, by adding or replacing entries in the [`history`](#260.html_dom-history) object.

```
[Unforgeable] interface Location {
  void assign(DOMString url);
  void replace(DOMString url);
  void reload();
};
Location implements URLUtils;
```

`location` . [`assign`](#260.html_dom-location-assign)(`url`)

Navigates to the given page.

`location` . [`replace`](#260.html_dom-location-replace)(`url`)

Removes the current page from the session history and navigates to the given page.

`location` . [`reload`](#260.html_dom-location-reload)()

Reloads the current page.

The *relevant [`Document`](#260.html_document)* is the [`Location`](#260.html_location) object's associated [`Document`](#260.html_document) object's [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#260.html_active-document).

When the <dfn id="260.html_dom-location-assign" data-anolis-xref="dom-location-assign">`assign(``url``)`</dfn> method is invoked, the UA must [resolve](#260.html_resolve-a-url) the argument, relative to the [API base URL](#260.html_api-base-url) specified by the [entry settings object](#260.html_entry-settings-object), and if that is successful, must [navigate](#260.html_navigate) the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) to the specified `url`, with [exceptions enabled](#260.html_exceptions-enabled). If the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context)'s [session history](#260.html_session-history) contains only one [`Document`](#260.html_document), and that was the [`about:blank`](#260.html_about:blank) [`Document`](#260.html_document) created when the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) was created, then the navigation must be done with [replacement enabled](#260.html_replacement-enabled).

When the <dfn id="260.html_dom-location-replace" data-anolis-xref="dom-location-replace">`replace(``url``)`</dfn> method is invoked, the UA must [resolve](#260.html_resolve-a-url) the argument, relative to the [API base URL](#260.html_api-base-url) specified by the [entry settings object](#260.html_entry-settings-object), and if that is successful, [navigate](#260.html_navigate) the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) to the specified `url` with [replacement enabled](#260.html_replacement-enabled) and [exceptions enabled](#260.html_exceptions-enabled).

Navigation for the [`assign()`](#260.html_dom-location-assign) and [`replace()`](#260.html_dom-location-replace) methods must be done with the [responsible browsing context](#260.html_responsible-browsing-context) specified by the [incumbent settings object](#260.html_incumbent-settings-object) as the [source browsing context](#260.html_source-browsing-context).

If the [resolving](#260.html_resolve-a-url) step of the [`assign()`](#260.html_dom-location-assign) and [`replace()`](#260.html_dom-location-replace) methods is not successful, then the user agent must instead throw a [`SyntaxError`](#260.html_syntaxerror) exception.

When the <dfn id="260.html_dom-location-reload" data-anolis-xref="dom-location-reload">`reload()`</dfn> method is invoked, the user agent must run the appropriate steps from the following list:

If the currently executing [task](#260.html_concept-task) is the dispatch of a `resize` event in response to the user resizing the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context)

Repaint the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) and abort these steps.

If the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#260.html_active-document) is [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#260.html_an-iframe-srcdoc-document)

[Reprocess the `iframe` attributes](#260.html_process-the-iframe-attributes) of the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context)'s [browsing context container](#260.html_browsing-context-container).

If the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#260.html_active-document) has its [reload override flag](#260.html_reload-override-flag) set

Perform [an overridden reload](#260.html_an-overridden-reload), with the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) being navigated as the [responsible browsing context](#260.html_responsible-browsing-context).

Otherwise

[Navigate](#260.html_navigate) the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) to [the document's address](#260.html_the-document's-address) with [replacement enabled](#260.html_replacement-enabled) and [exceptions enabled](#260.html_exceptions-enabled). The [source browsing context](#260.html_source-browsing-context) must be the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) being navigated.

When a user requests that the [active document](#260.html_active-document) of a [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) be reloaded through a user interface element, the user agent should [navigate](#260.html_navigate) the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) to the same resource as that [`Document`](#260.html_document), with [replacement enabled](#260.html_replacement-enabled). In the case of non-idempotent methods (e.g. HTTP POST), the user agent should prompt the user to confirm the operation first, since otherwise transactions (e.g. purchases or database modifications) could be repeated. User agents may allow the user to explicitly override any caches when reloading. If [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#260.html_active-document)'s [reload override flag](#260.html_reload-override-flag) is set, then the user agent may instead perform [an overridden reload](#260.html_an-overridden-reload) rather than the navigation described in this paragraph (with the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) being reloaded as the [source browsing context](#260.html_source-browsing-context)).

* * *

The [`Location`](#260.html_location) interface also supports the [`URLUtils`](#260.html_urlutils) interface. [[URL]](#260.html_refsURL)

When the object is created, and whenever the [the address](#260.html_the-document's-address) of the *relevant [`Document`](#260.html_document)* changes, the user agent must invoke the object's [`URLUtils`](#260.html_urlutils) interface's [set the input](#260.html_concept-uu-set-the-input) algorithm with [the address](#260.html_the-document's-address) of the *relevant [`Document`](#260.html_document)* as the given value.

The object's [`URLUtils`](#260.html_urlutils) interface's [get the base](#260.html_concept-uu-get-the-base) algorithm must return the [API base URL](#260.html_api-base-url) specified by the [entry settings object](#260.html_entry-settings-object), if there is one, or null otherwise.

The object's [`URLUtils`](#260.html_urlutils) interface's [query encoding](#260.html_concept-uu-query-encoding) is the [document's character encoding](#260.html_document's-character-encoding).

When the object's [`URLUtils`](#260.html_urlutils) interface invokes its [update steps](#260.html_concept-uu-update) with the string `value`, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  If any of the following conditions are met, let `mode` be *normal navigation*; otherwise, let it be *replace navigation*:

    *   The [`Location`](#260.html_location) object's *relevant [`Document`](#260.html_document)* has [completely loaded](#260.html_completely-loaded), or
    *   In the [task](#260.html_concept-task) in which the algorithm is running, an [activation behavior](#260.html_activation-behavior) is currently being processed whose [`click`](#260.html_event-click) event was [trusted](#260.html_concept-events-trusted), or
    *   In the [task](#260.html_concept-task) in which the algorithm is running, the event listener for a [trusted](#260.html_concept-events-trusted) [`click`](#260.html_event-click) event is being handled.
2.  If `mode` is *normal navigation*, then act as if the [`assign()`](#260.html_dom-location-assign) method had been called with `value` as its argument. Otherwise, act as if the [`replace()`](#260.html_dom-location-replace) method had been called with `value` as its argument.

##### 5.5.3.1 Security

This section describes a security model that is underdefined, imperfect, and does not match implementations. Work is ongoing to attempt to resolve this, but in the meantime, please do not rely on this section for precision. Implementors are urged to send their feedback on how cross-origin cross-global access to [`Window`](#260.html_window) and [`Location`](#260.html_location) objects should work. See [bug 20701](https://www.w3.org/Bugs/Public/show_bug.cgi?id=20701).

User agents must throw a [`SecurityError`](#260.html_securityerror) exception whenever any properties of a [`Location`](#260.html_location) object are accessed when the [entry settings object](#260.html_entry-settings-object) specifies an [effective script origin](#260.html_effective-script-origin) that is not the [same](#260.html_same-origin) as the [`Location`](#260.html_location) object's associated [`Document`](#260.html_document)'s [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#260.html_active-document)'s [effective script origin](#260.html_effective-script-origin), with the following exceptions:

*   The [`href`](#260.html_dom-url-href) setter, if the [responsible browsing context](#260.html_responsible-browsing-context) specified by the [entry settings object](#260.html_entry-settings-object) is [familiar with](#260.html_familiar-with) the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) with which the [`Location`](#260.html_location) object is associated
*   The [`replace()`](#260.html_dom-location-replace) method, if the [responsible browsing context](#260.html_responsible-browsing-context) specified by the [entry settings object](#260.html_entry-settings-object) is [familiar with](#260.html_familiar-with) the [browsing context](#260.html_browsing-context) with which the [`Location`](#260.html_location) object is associated
*   Any properties not defined in the IDL for the [`Location`](#260.html_location) object or indirectly via one of those properties (e.g. `toString()`, which is defined via the `stringifier` keyword), if the [effective script origin](#260.html_effective-script-origin) specified by the [entry settings object](#260.html_entry-settings-object) is the [same origin](#260.html_same-origin) as the [`Location`](#260.html_location) object's associated [`Document`](#260.html_document)'s [effective script origin](#260.html_effective-script-origin)

When the [effective script origin](#260.html_effective-script-origin) specified by the [entry settings object](#260.html_entry-settings-object) is different than a [`Location`](#260.html_location) object's associated [`Document`](#260.html_document)'s [effective script origin](#260.html_effective-script-origin), the user agent must act as if any changes to that [`Location`](#260.html_location) object's properties, getters, setters, etc, were not present, and as if all the properties of that [`Location`](#260.html_location) object had their [[Enumerable]] attribute set to false.

For members that return objects (including function objects), each distinct [effective script origin](#260.html_effective-script-origin) that is not the [same origin](#260.html_same-origin) as the [`Location`](#260.html_location) object's [`Document`](#260.html_document)'s [effective script origin](#260.html_effective-script-origin) must be provided with a separate set of objects. These objects must have the prototype chain appropriate for the script for which the objects are created (not those that would be appropriate for scripts whose [settings object](#260.html_settings-object) specifies a [global object](#260.html_global-object) that is the [`Location`](#260.html_location) object's [`Document`](#260.html_document)'s [`Window`](#260.html_window) object).

#### 5.5.4 Implementation notes for session history

*This section is non-normative.*

The [`History`](#261.html_history-1) interface is not meant to place restrictions on how implementations represent the session history to the user.

For example, session history could be implemented in a tree-like manner, with each page having multiple "forward" pages. This specification doesn't define how the linear list of pages in the [`history`](#261.html_dom-history) object are derived from the actual session history as seen from the user's perspective.

Similarly, a page containing two [`iframe`](#261.html_the-iframe-element)s has a [`history`](#261.html_dom-history) object distinct from the [`iframe`](#261.html_the-iframe-element)s' [`history`](#261.html_dom-history) objects, despite the fact that typical Web browsers present the user with just one "Back" button, with a session history that interleaves the navigation of the two inner frames and the outer page.

**Security**: It is suggested that to avoid letting a page "hijack" the history navigation facilities of a UA by abusing [`pushState()`](#261.html_dom-history-pushstate), the UA provide the user with a way to jump back to the previous page (rather than just going back to the previous state). For example, the back button could have a drop down showing just the pages in the session history, and not showing any of the states. Similarly, an aural browser could have two "back" commands, one that goes back to the previous state, and one that jumps straight back to the previous page.

In addition, a user agent could ignore calls to [`pushState()`](#261.html_dom-history-pushstate) that are invoked on a timer, or from event listeners that are not triggered in response to a clear user action, or that are invoked in rapid succession.

### 5.6 Browsing the Web

Features described in this section can at times prove difficult to test in order to assess interoperability. As a result, at present, their test coverage is less than much of the other features with all the stability implications this may have.

#### 5.6.1 Navigating across documents

Certain actions cause the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) to *[navigate](#263.html_navigate)* to a new resource. A user agent may provide various ways for the user to explicitly cause a browsing context to navigate, in addition to those defined in this specification.

For example, [following a hyperlink](#263.html_following-hyperlinks), [form submission](#263.html_concept-form-submit), and the [`window.open()`](#263.html_dom-open) and [`location.assign()`](#263.html_dom-location-assign) methods can all cause a browsing context to navigate.

A *resource* has a URL, but that might not be the only information necessary to identify it. For example, a form submission that uses HTTP POST would also have the HTTP method and payload. Similarly, [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#263.html_an-iframe-srcdoc-document) needs to know the data it is to use.

Navigation always involves <dfn id="263.html_source-browsing-context">source browsing context</dfn>, which is the browsing context which was responsible for starting the navigation.

When a browsing context is <dfn id="263.html_navigate" data-anolis-xref="navigate">navigated</dfn> to a new resource, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Release the [storage mutex](#263.html_storage-mutex).

2.  If the [source browsing context](#263.html_source-browsing-context) is not [allowed to navigate](#263.html_allowed-to-navigate) the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated, then abort these steps.

    If these steps are aborted here, the user agent may instead offer to open the new resource in a new [top-level browsing context](#263.html_top-level-browsing-context) or in the [top-level browsing context](#263.html_top-level-browsing-context) of the [source browsing context](#263.html_source-browsing-context), at the user's option, in which case the user agent must [navigate](#263.html_navigate) that designated [top-level browsing context](#263.html_top-level-browsing-context) to the new resource as if the user had requested it independently.

    Doing so, however, can be dangerous, as it means that the user is overriding the author's explicit request to sandbox the content.

    If the [navigate](#263.html_navigate) algorithm was invoked with <dfn id="263.html_exceptions-enabled">exceptions enabled</dfn>, and it is aborted on this step, then in addition to aborting this algorithm, the user agent must also throw a [`SecurityError`](#263.html_securityerror) exception.

3.  If there is a preexisting attempt to navigate the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context), and the [source browsing context](#263.html_source-browsing-context) is the same as the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated, and that attempt is currently running the [unload a document](#263.html_unload-a-document) algorithm, and the [origin](#263.html_origin-0) of the URL of the resource being loaded in that navigation is not the [same origin](#263.html_same-origin) as the [origin](#263.html_origin-0) of the URL of the resource being loaded in *this* navigation, then abort these steps without affecting the preexisting attempt to navigate the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context).

4.  If a [task](#263.html_concept-task) queued by the [traverse the history by a delta](#263.html_traverse-the-history-by-a-delta) algorithm is running the [unload a document](#263.html_unload-a-document) algorithm for the [active document](#263.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated, then abort these steps without affecting the [unload a document](#263.html_unload-a-document) algorithm or the aforementioned history traversal task.

5.  If the [prompt to unload a document](#263.html_prompt-to-unload-a-document) algorithm is being run for the [active document](#263.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated, then abort these steps without affecting the [prompt to unload a document](#263.html_prompt-to-unload-a-document) algorithm.

6.  Let `gone async` be false.

    The [*handle redirects*](#263.html_navigate-redirect-step) step later in this algorithm can in certain cases jump back to the step labeled [*fragment identifiers*](#263.html_navigate-fragid-step). Since, between those two steps, this algorithm goes from operating synchronously in the context of the calling [task](#263.html_concept-task) to operating asynchronously independent of the [event loop](#263.html_event-loop), some of the intervening steps need to be able to handle both being synchronous and being asynchronous. The `gone async` flag is thus used to make these steps aware of which mode they are operating in.

7.  *Fragment identifiers*: Apply the [URL parser](#263.html_url-parser-0) algorithm to the [absolute URL](#263.html_absolute-url) of the new resource and the [address](#263.html_the-document's-address) of the [active document](#263.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated. If all the components of the resulting [parsed URLs](#263.html_parsed-url), ignoring any [fragment](#263.html_concept-url-fragment) components, are identical, and the new resource is to be fetched using HTTP GET [or equivalent](#263.html_concept-http-equivalent-get), and the [parsed URL](#263.html_parsed-url) of the new resource has a [fragment](#263.html_concept-url-fragment) component that is not null (even if it is empty), then [navigate to that fragment identifier](#263.html_scroll-to-fragid) and abort these steps.

8.  If `gone async` is false, cancel any preexisting but not yet [mature](#263.html_concept-navigate-mature) attempt to navigate the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context), including canceling any instances of the [fetch](#263.html_fetch) algorithm started by those attempts. If one of those attempts has already [created a new `Document` object](#263.html_create-a-document-object), [abort](#263.html_abort-a-document) that [`Document`](#263.html_document) also. (Navigation attempts that have [matured](#263.html_concept-navigate-mature) already have session history entries, and are therefore handled during the [update the session history with the new page](#263.html_update-the-session-history-with-the-new-page) algorithm, later.)

9.  If the new resource is to be handled using a mechanism that does not affect the browsing context, e.g. ignoring the navigation request altogether because the specified scheme is not one of the supported protocols, then abort these steps and proceed with that mechanism instead.

10.  If `gone async` is false, [prompt to unload](#263.html_prompt-to-unload-a-document) the [`Document`](#263.html_document) object. If the user [refused to allow the document to be unloaded](#263.html_refused-to-allow-the-document-to-be-unloaded), then abort these steps.

    If this instance of the [navigation](#263.html_navigate) algorithm gets canceled while this step is running, the [prompt to unload a document](#263.html_prompt-to-unload-a-document) algorithm must nonetheless be run to completion.

11.  If `gone async` is false, [abort](#263.html_abort-a-document) the [active document](#263.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context).

12.  If the new resource is to be handled by displaying some sort of inline content, e.g. an error message because the specified scheme is not one of the supported protocols, or an inline prompt to allow the user to select [a registered handler](#263.html_dom-navigator-registerprotocolhandler) for the given scheme, then [display the inline content](#263.html_read-ua-inline) and abort these steps.

    In the case of a registered handler being used, the algorithm will be reinvoked with a new URL to handle the request.

13.  If the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated is a [nested browsing context](#263.html_nested-browsing-context), then put it in the [delaying `load` events mode](#263.html_delaying-load-events-mode).

    The user agent must take this [nested browsing context](#263.html_nested-browsing-context) out of the [delaying `load` events mode](#263.html_delaying-load-events-mode) when this [navigation](#263.html_navigate) algorithm later [matures](#263.html_concept-navigate-mature), or when it terminates (whether due to having run all the steps, or being canceled, or being aborted), whichever happens first.

14.  This is the step that attempts to obtain the resource, if necessary. Jump to the first appropriate substep:

    If the resource has already been obtained (e.g. because it is being used to populate an [`object`](#263.html_the-object-element) element's new [child browsing context](#263.html_child-browsing-context))

    Skip this step. The data is already available.

    If the new resource is a URL whose [scheme](#263.html_concept-url-scheme) is [`javascript`](#263.html_javascript-protocol)

    [Queue a task](#263.html_queue-a-task) to run <dfn id="263.html_javascript-protocol" data-anolis-xref="javascript protocol">these "`javascript:` URL" steps</dfn>, associated with the [active document](#263.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated:

    1.  If the [origin](#263.html_origin-0) of the [source browsing context](#263.html_source-browsing-context) is not the [same origin](#263.html_same-origin) as the [origin](#263.html_origin-0) of the [active document](#263.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated, then act as if the result of evaluating the script was the void value, and jump to the step labeled *process results* below.

    2.  Apply the [URL parser](#263.html_url-parser-0) to the URL being navigated.

    3.  Let `parsed URL` be the result of the [URL parser](#263.html_url-parser-0).

    4.  Let `script source` be the empty string.

    5.  Append `parsed URL`'s [scheme data](#263.html_concept-url-scheme-data) component to `script source`.

    6.  If `parsed URL`'s [query](#263.html_concept-url-query) component is not null, then first append a "?" (U+003F) character to `script source`, and then append `parsed URL`'s [query](#263.html_concept-url-query) component to `script source`.

    7.  If `parsed URL`'s [fragment](#263.html_concept-url-fragment) component is not null, then first append a "#" (U+0023) character to `script source`, and then append `parsed URL`'s [fragment](#263.html_concept-url-fragment) component to `script source`.

    8.  Replace `script source` with the result of applying the [percent decode](#263.html_percent-decode) algorithm to `script source`.

    9.  Replace `script source` with the result of applying the [UTF-8 decode](#263.html_utf-8-decode) algorithm to `script source`.

    10.  Let `address` be the [address](#263.html_the-document's-address) of the [active document](#263.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated.

    11.  [Create a script](#263.html_create-a-script), using `script source` as the script source, `address` as the script source URL, JavaScript as the scripting language, and the [script settings object](#263.html_script-settings-object) of the [`Window`](#263.html_window) object of the [active document](#263.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated.

        Let `result` be the return value of the [code entry-point](#263.html_code-entry-point) of this [script](#263.html_concept-script). If an exception was thrown, let `result` be void instead. (The result will be void also if [scripting is disabled](#263.html_concept-bc-noscript).)

    12.  *Process results*: If the result of executing the script is void (there is no return value), then the result of obtaining the resource for the URL is [equivalent to](#263.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes) an HTTP resource with an HTTP 204 No Content response.

        Otherwise, the result of obtaining the resource for the URL is [equivalent](#263.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes) to an HTTP resource with a 200 OK response whose [Content-Type metadata](#263.html_content-type) is [`text/html`](#263.html_text/html) and whose response body is the return value converted to a string value.

        When it comes time to [set the document's address](#263.html_set-the-document's-address) in the [navigation algorithm](#263.html_navigate), use `address` as the [override URL](#263.html_override-url).

    The [task source](#263.html_task-source) for this [task](#263.html_concept-task) is the [DOM manipulation task source](#263.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

    So for example a [`javascript:` URL](#263.html_javascript-protocol) in an [`href`](#263.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute of an [`a`](#263.html_the-a-element) element would only be evaluated when the link was [followed](#263.html_following-hyperlinks), while such a URL in the [`src`](#263.html_attr-iframe-src) attribute of an [`iframe`](#263.html_the-iframe-element) element would be evaluated in the context of the [`iframe`](#263.html_the-iframe-element)'s own [nested browsing context](#263.html_nested-browsing-context) when the [`iframe`](#263.html_the-iframe-element) is being set up; once evaluated, its return value (if it was not void) would replace that [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context)'s document, thus also changing the [`Window`](#263.html_window) object of that [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context).

    If the new resource is to be fetched using HTTP GET [or equivalent](#263.html_concept-http-equivalent-get), and there are [relevant application caches](#263.html_relevant-application-cache) that are identified by a URL with the [same origin](#263.html_same-origin) as the URL in question, and that have this URL as one of their entries, excluding entries marked as [foreign](#263.html_concept-appcache-foreign), and whose [mode](#263.html_concept-appcache-mode) is [fast](#263.html_concept-appcache-mode-fast), and the user agent is not in a mode where it will avoid using [application caches](#263.html_application-cache)

    [Fetch](#263.html_fetch) the resource from the [most appropriate application cache](#263.html_concept-appcache-selection) of those that match.

    For example, imagine an HTML page with an associated application cache displaying an image and a form, where the image is also used by several other application caches. If the user right-clicks on the image and chooses "View Image", then the user agent could decide to show the image from any of those caches, but it is likely that the most useful cache for the user would be the one that was used for the aforementioned HTML page. On the other hand, if the user submits the form, and the form does a POST submission, then the user agent will not use an application cache at all; the submission will be made to the network.

    Otherwise

    [Fetch](#263.html_fetch) the new resource, with the *manual redirect flag* set.

    If the steps above invoked the [fetch](#263.html_fetch) algorith, the following requirements also apply:

    If the resource is being fetched using a method other than one [equivalent to](#263.html_concept-http-equivalent-get) HTTP's GET, or, if the [navigation algorithm](#263.html_navigate) was invoked as a result of the [form submission algorithm](#263.html_concept-form-submit), then the [fetching algorithm](#263.html_fetch) must be invoked from the [origin](#263.html_origin-0) of the [active document](#263.html_active-document) of the [source browsing context](#263.html_source-browsing-context), if any.

    Otherwise, if the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated is a [child browsing context](#263.html_child-browsing-context), then the [fetching algorithm](#263.html_fetch) must be invoked from the [browsing context scope origin](#263.html_browsing-context-scope-origin) of the [browsing context container](#263.html_browsing-context-container) of the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) being navigated, if it has one.

15.  If `gone async` is false, return to whatever algorithm invoked the navigation steps and continue running these steps asynchronously.

16.  Let `gone async` be true.

17.  *Handle redirects*: If fetching the resource results in a redirect, and either the URL of the target of the redirect has the [same origin](#263.html_same-origin) as the original resource, or the resource is being obtained using the POST method or a safe method (in HTTP terms), return to [the step labeled *fragment identifiers*](#263.html_navigate-fragid-step) with the new resource, except that if the URL of the target of the redirect does not have a fragment identifier and the URL of the resource that led to the redirect does, then the fragment identifier of the resource that led to the redirect must be propagated to the URL of the target of the redirect.

    So for instance, if the original URL was "`http://example.com/#!sample`" and "`http://example.com/`" is found to redirect to "`https://example.com/`", the URL of the new resource will be "`https://example.com/#!sample`".

    Otherwise, if fetching the resource results in a redirect but the URL of the target of the redirect does not have the [same origin](#263.html_same-origin) as the original resource and the resource is being obtained using a method that is neither the POST method nor a safe method (in HTTP terms), then abort these steps. The user agent may indicate to the user that the navigation has been aborted for security reasons.

18.  Wait for one or more bytes to be available or for the user agent to establish that the resource in question is empty. During this time, the user agent may allow the user to cancel this navigation attempt or start other navigation attempts.

19.  **Fallback in prefer-online mode**: If the resource was not fetched from an [application cache](#263.html_application-cache), and was to be fetched using HTTP GET [or equivalent](#263.html_concept-http-equivalent-get), and there are [relevant application caches](#263.html_relevant-application-cache) that are identified by a URL with the [same origin](#263.html_same-origin) as the URL in question, and that have this URL as one of their entries, excluding entries marked as [foreign](#263.html_concept-appcache-foreign), and whose [mode](#263.html_concept-appcache-mode) is [prefer-online](#263.html_concept-appcache-mode-prefer-online), and the user didn't cancel the navigation attempt during the earlier step, and the navigation attempt failed (e.g. the server returned a 4xx or 5xx status code [or equivalent](#263.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes), or there was a DNS error), then:

    Let `candidate` be the resource identified by the URL in question from the [most appropriate application cache](#263.html_concept-appcache-selection) of those that match.

    If `candidate` is not marked as [foreign](#263.html_concept-appcache-foreign), then the user agent must discard the failed load and instead continue along these steps using `candidate` as the resource. The user agent may indicate to the user that the original page load failed, and that the page used was a previously cached resource.

    This does not affect the *address of the resource from which Request-URIs are obtained*, as used to set [the document's referrer](#263.html_the-document's-referrer) in the [create a Document object](#263.html_create-a-document-object) steps below; they still use the value as computed by the original [fetch](#263.html_fetch) algorithm.

20.  **Fallback for fallback entries**: If the resource was not fetched from an [application cache](#263.html_application-cache), and was to be fetched using HTTP GET [or equivalent](#263.html_concept-http-equivalent-get), and its URL [matches the fallback namespace](#263.html_concept-appcache-matches-fallback) of one or more [relevant application caches](#263.html_relevant-application-cache), and the [most appropriate application cache](#263.html_concept-appcache-selection) of those that match does not have an entry in its [online whitelist](#263.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist) that has the [same origin](#263.html_same-origin) as the resource's URL and that is a [prefix match](#263.html_prefix-match) for the resource's URL, and the user didn't cancel the navigation attempt during the previous step, and the navigation attempt failed (e.g. the server returned a 4xx or 5xx status code [or equivalent](#263.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes), or there was a DNS error), then:

    Let `candidate` be the [fallback resource](#263.html_concept-appcache-fallback) specified for the [fallback namespace](#263.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) in question. If multiple application caches match, the user agent must use the fallback of the [most appropriate application cache](#263.html_concept-appcache-selection) of those that match.

    If `candidate` is not marked as [foreign](#263.html_concept-appcache-foreign), then the user agent must discard the failed load and instead continue along these steps using `candidate` as the resource. [The document's address](#263.html_the-document's-address), if appropriate, will still be the originally requested URL, not the fallback URL, but the user agent may indicate to the user that the original page load failed, that the page used was a fallback resource, and what the URL of the fallback resource actually is.

    This does not affect the *address of the resource from which Request-URIs are obtained*, as used to set [the document's referrer](#263.html_the-document's-referrer) in the [create a Document object](#263.html_create-a-document-object) steps below; they still use the value as computed by the original [fetch](#263.html_fetch) algorithm.

21.  *Resource handling*: If the resource's out-of-band metadata (e.g. HTTP headers), not counting any [type information](#263.html_content-type) (such as the Content-Type HTTP header), requires some sort of processing that will not affect the browsing context, then perform that processing and abort these steps.

    Such processing might be triggered by, amongst other things, the following:

    *   HTTP status codes (e.g. 204 No Content or 205 Reset Content)
    *   Network errors (e.g. the network interface being unavailable)
    *   Cryptographic protocol failures (e.g. an incorrect TLS certificate)

    Responses with HTTP `Content-Disposition` headers specifying the `attachment` disposition type must be handled [as a download](#263.html_as-a-download).

    HTTP 401 responses that do not include a challenge recognized by the user agent must be processed as if they had no challenge, e.g. rendering the entity body as if the response had been 200 OK.

    User agents may show the entity body of an HTTP 401 response even when the response does include a recognized challenge, with the option to login being included in a non-modal fashion, to enable the information provided by the server to be used by the user before authenticating. Similarly, user agents should allow the user to authenticate (in a non-modal fashion) against authentication challenges included in other responses such as HTTP 200 OK responses, effectively allowing resources to present HTTP login forms without requiring their use.

22.  Let `type` be [the sniffed type of the resource](#263.html_content-type-sniffing-0).

23.  If the user agent has been configured to process resources of the given `type` using some mechanism other than rendering the content in a [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context), then skip this step. Otherwise, if the `type` is one of the following types, jump to the appropriate entry in the following list, and process the resource as described there:

    "[`text/html`](#263.html_text/html)"

    Follow the steps given in the [HTML document](#263.html_read-html) section, and then, once they have completed, abort this [navigate](#263.html_navigate) algorithm.

    "`application/xml`"
    "`text/xml`"
    "`image/svg+xml`"
    "[`application/xhtml+xml`](#263.html_application/xhtml+xml)"
    Any other type ending in "`+xml`" that is not an [explicitly supported XML type](#263.html_explicitly-supported-xml-type)

    Follow the steps given in the [XML document](#263.html_read-xml) section. If that section determines that the content is *not* to be displayed as a generic XML document, then proceed to the next step in this overall set of steps. Otherwise, once the steps given in the [XML document](#263.html_read-xml) section have completed, abort this [navigate](#263.html_navigate) algorithm.

    "`text/plain`"

    Follow the steps given in the [plain text file](#263.html_read-text) section, and then, once they have completed, abort this [navigate](#263.html_navigate) algorithm.

    "[`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#263.html_multipart/x-mixed-replace)"

    Follow the steps given in the [multipart/x-mixed-replace](#263.html_read-multipart-x-mixed-replace) section, and then, once they have completed, abort this [navigate](#263.html_navigate) algorithm.

    A supported image, video, or audio type

    Follow the steps given in the [media](#263.html_read-media) section, and then, once they have completed, abort this [navigate](#263.html_navigate) algorithm.

    A type that will use an external application to render the content in the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context)

    Follow the steps given in the [plugin](#263.html_read-plugin) section, and then, once they have completed, abort this [navigate](#263.html_navigate) algorithm.

    An <dfn id="263.html_explicitly-supported-xml-type">explicitly supported XML type</dfn> is one for which the user agent is configured to use an external application to render the content (either a [plugin](#263.html_plugin) rendering directly in the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context), or a separate application), or one for which the user agent has dedicated processing rules (e.g. a Web browser with a built-in Atom feed viewer would be said to explicitly support the `application/atom+xml` MIME type), or one for which the user agent has a dedicated handler (e.g. one registered using [`registerContentHandler()`](#263.html_dom-navigator-registercontenthandler)).

    <dfn id="263.html_set-the-document's-address" data-anolis-xref="set the document's address">Setting the document's address</dfn>: If there is no <dfn id="263.html_override-url">override URL</dfn>, then any [`Document`](#263.html_document) created by these steps must have its [address](#263.html_the-document's-address) set to the URL that was originally to be [fetched](#263.html_fetch), ignoring any other data that was used to obtain the resource (e.g. the entity body in the case of a POST submission is not part of [the document's address](#263.html_the-document's-address), nor is the URL of the fallback resource in the case of the original load having failed and that URL having been found to match a [fallback namespace](#263.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns)). However, if there *is* an [override URL](#263.html_override-url), then any [`Document`](#263.html_document) created by these steps must have its [address](#263.html_the-document's-address) set to that URL instead.

    An [override URL](#263.html_override-url) is set when [dereferencing a `javascript:` URL](#263.html_javascript-protocol) and when performing [an overridden reload](#263.html_an-overridden-reload).

    <dfn id="263.html_create-a-document-object" data-anolis-xref="create a Document object">Creating a new `Document` object</dfn>: when a [`Document`](#263.html_document) is created as part of the above steps, the user agent must additionally run the following algorithm as part of creating the new object:

    1.  Create a new [`Window`](#263.html_window) object, and associate it with the [`Document`](#263.html_document), with one exception: if the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context)'s only entry in its [session history](#263.html_session-history) is the [`about:blank`](#263.html_about:blank) [`Document`](#263.html_document) that was added when the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) was created, and navigation is occurring with [replacement enabled](#263.html_replacement-enabled), and that [`Document`](#263.html_document) has the [same origin](#263.html_same-origin) as the new [`Document`](#263.html_document), then use the [`Window`](#263.html_window) object of that [`Document`](#263.html_document) instead, and change the [`document`](#263.html_dom-document-0) attribute of the [`Window`](#263.html_window) object to point to the new [`Document`](#263.html_document).

    2.  Set [the document's referrer](#263.html_the-document's-referrer) to the *address of the resource from which Request-URIs are obtained* as determined when the [fetch](#263.html_fetch) algorithm obtained the resource, if that algorithm was used and determined such a value; otherwise, set it to the empty string.

    3.  [Implement the sandboxing](#263.html_implement-the-sandboxing) for the [`Document`](#263.html_document).

    4.  If the [active sandboxing flag set](#263.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) of the [`Document`](#263.html_document)'s [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) or any of its [ancestor browsing contexts](#263.html_ancestor-browsing-context) (if any) have the [sandboxed fullscreen browsing context flag](#263.html_sandboxed-fullscreen-browsing-context-flag) set, then skip this step.

        If the [`Document`](#263.html_document)'s [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context) has a [browsing context container](#263.html_browsing-context-container) and either it is not an [`iframe`](#263.html_the-iframe-element) element, or its [`Document`](#263.html_document) does not have the [fullscreen enabled flag](#263.html_fullscreen-enabled-flag) set, then also skip this step.

        Otherwise, set the [`Document`](#263.html_document)'s [fullscreen enabled flag](#263.html_fullscreen-enabled-flag).

24.  *Non-document content*: If, given `type`, the new resource is to be handled by displaying some sort of inline content, e.g. a native rendering of the content, an error message because the specified type is not supported, or an inline prompt to allow the user to select [a registered handler](#263.html_dom-navigator-registercontenthandler) for the given type, then [display the inline content](#263.html_read-ua-inline), and then abort these steps.

    In the case of a registered handler being used, the algorithm will be reinvoked with a new URL to handle the request.

25.  Otherwise, the document's `type` is such that the resource will not affect the browsing context, e.g. because the resource is to be handed to an external application or because it is an unknown type that will be processed [as a download](#263.html_as-a-download). Process the resource appropriately.

* * *

Some of the sections below, to which the above algorithm defers in certain cases, require the user agent to <dfn id="263.html_update-the-session-history-with-the-new-page">update the session history with the new page</dfn>. When a user agent is required to do this, it must [queue a task](#263.html_queue-a-task) (associated with the [`Document`](#263.html_document) object of the [current entry](#263.html_current-entry), not the new one) to run the following steps:

1.  [Unload](#263.html_unload-a-document) the [`Document`](#263.html_document) object of the [current entry](#263.html_current-entry), with the `recycle` parameter set to false.

    If this instance of the [navigation](#263.html_navigate) algorithm is canceled while this step is running the [unload a document](#263.html_unload-a-document) algorithm, then the [unload a document](#263.html_unload-a-document) algorithm must be allowed to run to completion, but this instance of the [navigation](#263.html_navigate) algorithm must not run beyond this step. (In particular, for instance, the cancelation of this algorithm does not abort any event dispatch or script execution occurring as part of unloading the document or its descendants.)

2.  If the navigation was initiated for <dfn id="263.html_entry-update">entry update</dfn> of an entry

    1.  Replace the [`Document`](#263.html_document) of the entry being updated, and any other entries that referenced the same document as that entry, with the new [`Document`](#263.html_document).

    2.  [Traverse the history](#263.html_traverse-the-history) to the new entry.

    This can only happen if the entry being updated is not the [current entry](#263.html_current-entry), and can never happen with [replacement enabled](#263.html_replacement-enabled). (It happens when the user tried to traverse to a session history entry that no longer had a [`Document`](#263.html_document) object.)

    Otherwise

    1.  Remove all the entries in the [browsing context](#263.html_browsing-context)'s [session history](#263.html_session-history) after the [current entry](#263.html_current-entry). If the [current entry](#263.html_current-entry) is the last entry in the session history, then no entries are removed.

        This [doesn't necessarily have to affect](#263.html_history-notes) the user agent's user interface.

    2.  Append a new entry at the end of the [`History`](#263.html_history-1) object representing the new resource and its [`Document`](#263.html_document) object and related state.

    3.  [Traverse the history](#263.html_traverse-the-history) to the new entry. If the navigation was initiated with [replacement enabled](#263.html_replacement-enabled), then the traversal must itself be initiated with [replacement enabled](#263.html_replacement-enabled).

3.  The [navigation algorithm](#263.html_navigate) has now <dfn id="263.html_concept-navigate-mature" data-anolis-xref="concept-navigate-mature">matured</dfn>.

4.  *Fragment identifier loop*: [Spin the event loop](#263.html_spin-the-event-loop) for a user-agent-defined amount of time, as desired by the user agent implementor. (This is intended to allow the user agent to optimize the user experience in the face of performance concerns.)

5.  If the [`Document`](#263.html_document) object has no parser, or its parser has [stopped parsing](#263.html_stop-parsing), or the user agent has reason to believe the user is no longer interested in scrolling to the fragment identifier, then abort these steps.

6.  [Scroll to the fragment identifier](#263.html_scroll-to-the-fragment-identifier) given in [the document's address](#263.html_the-document's-address). If this fails to find [an indicated part of the document](#263.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document), then return to the *fragment identifier loop* step.

The [task source](#263.html_task-source) for this [task](#263.html_concept-task) is the [networking task source](#263.html_networking-task-source).

#### 5.6.2 <dfn id="264.html_navigate-html" data-anolis-xref="navigate-html">Page load processing model for HTML files</dfn>

When an HTML document is to be loaded in a [browsing context](#264.html_browsing-context), the user agent must [queue a task](#264.html_queue-a-task) to [create a `Document` object](#264.html_create-a-document-object), mark it as being an [HTML document](#264.html_html-documents), set its [content type](#264.html_concept-document-content-type) to "`text/html`", create an [HTML parser](#264.html_html-parser), and associate it with the document. Each [task](#264.html_concept-task) that the [networking task source](#264.html_networking-task-source) places on the [task queue](#264.html_task-queue) while the [fetching algorithm](#264.html_fetch) runs must then fill the parser's [input byte stream](#264.html_the-input-byte-stream) with the fetched bytes and cause the [HTML parser](#264.html_html-parser) to perform the appropriate processing of the input stream.

The [input byte stream](#264.html_the-input-byte-stream) converts bytes into characters for use in the [tokenizer](#264.html_tokenization). This process relies, in part, on character encoding information found in the real [Content-Type metadata](#264.html_content-type) of the resource; the "sniffed type" is not used for this purpose.

When no more bytes are available, the user agent must [queue a task](#264.html_queue-a-task) for the parser to process the implied EOF character, which eventually causes a `load` event to be fired.

After creating the [`Document`](#264.html_document) object, but before any script execution, certainly before the parser [stops](#264.html_stop-parsing), the user agent must [update the session history with the new page](#264.html_update-the-session-history-with-the-new-page).

[Application cache selection](#264.html_concept-appcache-init) happens [in the HTML parser](#264.html_parser-appcache).

The [task source](#264.html_task-source) for the two tasks mentioned in this section must be the [networking task source](#264.html_networking-task-source).

#### 5.6.3 <dfn id="265.html_navigate-xml" data-anolis-xref="navigate-xml">Page load processing model for XML files</dfn>

When faced with displaying an XML file inline, user agents must first [create a `Document` object](#265.html_create-a-document-object), following the requirements of the XML and Namespaces in XML recommendations, RFC 7303, DOM, and other relevant specifications. [[XML]](#265.html_refsXML) [[XMLNS]](#265.html_refsXMLNS) [[RFC7303]](#265.html_refsRFC7303) [[DOM]](#265.html_refsDOM)

The actual HTTP headers and other metadata, not the headers as mutated or implied by the algorithms given in this specification, are the ones that must be used when determining the character encoding according to the rules given in the above specifications. Once the character encoding is established, the [document's character encoding](#265.html_document's-character-encoding) must be set to that character encoding.

If the root element, as parsed according to the XML specifications cited above, is found to be an [`html`](#265.html_the-html-element) element with an attribute [`manifest`](#265.html_attr-html-manifest) whose value is not the empty string, then, as soon as the element is [inserted into the document](#265.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document), the user agent must [resolve](#265.html_resolve-a-url) the value of that attribute relative to that element, and if that is successful, must apply the [URL serializer](#265.html_concept-url-serializer) algorithm to the resulting [parsed URL](#265.html_parsed-url) with the *exclude fragment flag* set to obtain `manifest URL`, and then run the [application cache selection algorithm](#265.html_concept-appcache-init) with `manifest URL` as the manifest URL, passing in the newly-created [`Document`](#265.html_document). Otherwise, if the attribute is absent, its value is the empty string, or resolving its value fails, then as soon as the root element is [inserted into the document](#265.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document), the user agent must run the [application cache selection algorithm](#265.html_concept-appcache-init) with no manifest, and passing in the [`Document`](#265.html_document).

Because the processing of the [`manifest`](#265.html_attr-html-manifest) attribute happens only once the root element is parsed, any URLs referenced by processing instructions before the root element (such as `<?xml-stylesheet?>` and `<?xbl?>` PIs) will be fetched from the network and cannot be cached.

User agents may examine the namespace of the root [`Element`](#265.html_element) node of this [`Document`](#265.html_document) object to perform namespace-based dispatch to alternative processing tools, e.g. determining that the content is actually a syndication feed and passing it to a feed handler. If such processing is to take place, abort the steps in this section, and jump to [the next step](#265.html_navigate-non-Document) (labeled *non-document content*) in the [navigate](#265.html_navigate) steps above.

Otherwise, then, with the newly created [`Document`](#265.html_document), the user agent must [update the session history with the new page](#265.html_update-the-session-history-with-the-new-page). User agents may do this before the complete document has been parsed (thus achieving *incremental rendering*), and must do this before any scripts are to be executed.

Error messages from the parse process (e.g. XML namespace well-formedness errors) may be reported inline by mutating the [`Document`](#265.html_document).

#### 5.6.4 <dfn id="266.html_navigate-text" data-anolis-xref="navigate-text">Page load processing model for text files</dfn>

When a plain text document is to be loaded in a [browsing context](#266.html_browsing-context), the user agent must [queue a task](#266.html_queue-a-task) to [create a `Document` object](#266.html_create-a-document-object), mark it as being an [HTML document](#266.html_html-documents), set its [content type](#266.html_concept-document-content-type) to "`text/plain`", create an [HTML parser](#266.html_html-parser), associate it with the document, act as if the tokenizer had emitted a start tag token with the tag name "pre" followed by a single "LF" (U+000A) character, and switch the [HTML parser](#266.html_html-parser)'s tokenizer to the [PLAINTEXT state](#266.html_plaintext-state). Each [task](#266.html_concept-task) that the [networking task source](#266.html_networking-task-source) places on the [task queue](#266.html_task-queue) while the [fetching algorithm](#266.html_fetch) runs must then fill the parser's [input byte stream](#266.html_the-input-byte-stream) with the fetched bytes and cause the [HTML parser](#266.html_html-parser) to perform the appropriate processing of the input stream.

The rules for how to convert the bytes of the plain text document into actual characters, and the rules for actually rendering the text to the user, are defined in RFC 2046, RFC 3676, and subsequent versions thereof. [[RFC2046]](#266.html_refsRFC2046) [[RFC3676]](#266.html_refsRFC3676)

The [document's character encoding](#266.html_document's-character-encoding) must be set to the character encoding used to decode the document.

Upon creation of the [`Document`](#266.html_document) object, the user agent must run the [application cache selection algorithm](#266.html_concept-appcache-init) with no manifest, and passing in the newly-created [`Document`](#266.html_document).

When no more bytes are available, the user agent must [queue a task](#266.html_queue-a-task) for the parser to process the implied EOF character, which eventually causes a `load` event to be fired.

After creating the [`Document`](#266.html_document) object, but potentially before the page has finished parsing, the user agent must [update the session history with the new page](#266.html_update-the-session-history-with-the-new-page).

User agents may add content to the [`head`](#266.html_the-head-element) element of the [`Document`](#266.html_document), e.g. linking to a style sheet or an XBL binding, providing script, giving the document a [`title`](#266.html_the-title-element), etc.

In particular, if the user agent supports the `Format=Flowed` feature of RFC 3676 then the user agent would need to apply extra styling to cause the text to wrap correctly and to handle the quoting feature. This could be performed using, e.g., an XBL binding or a CSS extension.

The [task source](#266.html_task-source) for the two tasks mentioned in this section must be the [networking task source](#266.html_networking-task-source).

#### 5.6.5 <dfn id="267.html_navigate-multipart-x-mixed-replace" data-anolis-xref="navigate-multipart-x-mixed-replace">Page load processing model for `multipart/x-mixed-replace` resources</dfn>

When a resource with the type [`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#267.html_multipart/x-mixed-replace) is to be loaded in a [browsing context](#267.html_browsing-context), the user agent must parse the resource using the rules for multipart types. [[RFC2046]](#267.html_refsRFC2046)

For each body part obtained from the resource, the user agent must run a new instance of the [navigate](#267.html_navigate) algorithm, starting from the *resource handling* step, using the new body part as the resource being navigated, with [replacement enabled](#267.html_replacement-enabled) if a previous body part from the same resource resulted in a [`Document`](#267.html_document) object being [created](#267.html_create-a-document-object), and otherwise using the same setup as the [navigate](#267.html_navigate) attempt that caused this section to be invoked in the first place.

For the purposes of algorithms processing these body parts as if they were complete stand-alone resources, the user agent must act as if there were no more bytes for those resources whenever the boundary following the body part is reached.

Thus, `load` events (and for that matter `unload` events) do fire for each body part loaded.

#### 5.6.6 <dfn id="268.html_navigate-media" data-anolis-xref="navigate-media">Page load processing model for media</dfn>

When an image, video, or audio resource is to be loaded in a [browsing context](#268.html_browsing-context), the user agent should [create a `Document` object](#268.html_create-a-document-object), mark it as being an [HTML document](#268.html_html-documents), set its [content type](#268.html_concept-document-content-type) to the sniffed MIME type of the resource (`type` in the [navigate](#268.html_navigate) algorithm), append an [`html`](#268.html_the-html-element) element to the [`Document`](#268.html_document), append a [`head`](#268.html_the-head-element) element and a [`body`](#268.html_the-body-element) element to the [`html`](#268.html_the-html-element) element, append an element `host element` for the media, as described below, to the [`body`](#268.html_the-body-element) element, and set the appropriate attribute of the element `host element`, as described below, to the address of the image, video, or audio resource.

The element `host element` to create for the media is the element given in the table below in the second cell of the row whose first cell describes the media. The appropriate attribute to set is the one given by the third cell in that same row.

| Type of media | Element for the media | Appropriate attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image | [`img`](#268.html_the-img-element) | [`src`](#268.html_attr-img-src) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video | [`video`](#268.html_the-video-element) | [`src`](#268.html_attr-media-src) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Audio | [`audio`](#268.html_the-audio-element) | [`src`](#268.html_attr-media-src) |
| --- | --- | --- |

Then, the user agent must act as if it had [stopped parsing](#268.html_stop-parsing).

Upon creation of the [`Document`](#268.html_document) object, the user agent must run the [application cache selection algorithm](#268.html_concept-appcache-init) with no manifest, and passing in the newly-created [`Document`](#268.html_document).

After creating the [`Document`](#268.html_document) object, but potentially before the page has finished fully loading, the user agent must [update the session history with the new page](#268.html_update-the-session-history-with-the-new-page).

User agents may add content to the [`head`](#268.html_the-head-element) element of the [`Document`](#268.html_document), or attributes to the element `host element`, e.g. to link to a style sheet or an XBL binding, to provide a script, to give the document a [`title`](#268.html_the-title-element), to make the media [autoplay](#268.html_attr-media-autoplay), etc.

#### 5.6.7 <dfn id="269.html_navigate-plugin" data-anolis-xref="navigate-plugin">Page load processing model for content that uses plugins</dfn>

When a resource that requires an external resource to be rendered is to be loaded in a [browsing context](#269.html_browsing-context), the user agent should [create a `Document` object](#269.html_create-a-document-object), mark it as being an [HTML document](#269.html_html-documents) and mark it as being a <dfn id="269.html_plugin-document">plugin document</dfn>, set its [content type](#269.html_concept-document-content-type) to the sniffed MIME type of the resource (`type` in the [navigate](#269.html_navigate) algorithm), append an [`html`](#269.html_the-html-element) element to the [`Document`](#269.html_document), append a [`head`](#269.html_the-head-element) element and a [`body`](#269.html_the-body-element) element to the [`html`](#269.html_the-html-element) element, append an [`embed`](#269.html_the-embed-element) to the [`body`](#269.html_the-body-element) element, and set the [`src`](#269.html_attr-embed-src) attribute of the [`embed`](#269.html_the-embed-element) element to the address of the resource.

The term [plugin document](#269.html_plugin-document) is used by the Content Security Policy specification as part of the mechanism that ensures [`iframe`](#269.html_the-iframe-element)s can't be used to evade `plugin-types` directives. [[CSP]](#269.html_refsCSP)

Then, the user agent must act as if it had [stopped parsing](#269.html_stop-parsing).

Upon creation of the [`Document`](#269.html_document) object, the user agent must run the [application cache selection algorithm](#269.html_concept-appcache-init) with no manifest, and passing in the newly-created [`Document`](#269.html_document).

After creating the [`Document`](#269.html_document) object, but potentially before the page has finished fully loading, the user agent must [update the session history with the new page](#269.html_update-the-session-history-with-the-new-page).
