User agents may add content to the [`head`](#269.html_the-head-element) element of the [`Document`](#269.html_document), or attributes to the [`embed`](#269.html_the-embed-element) element, e.g. to link to a style sheet or an XBL binding, or to give the document a [`title`](#269.html_the-title-element).

If the [`Document`](#269.html_document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#269.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) has its [sandboxed plugins browsing context flag](#269.html_sandboxed-plugins-browsing-context-flag) set, the synthesized [`embed`](#269.html_the-embed-element) element will [fail to render the content](#269.html_sandboxPluginEmbed) if the relevant [plugin](#269.html_plugin) cannot be [secured](#269.html_concept-plugin-secure).

#### 5.6.8 <dfn id="270.html_navigate-ua-inline" data-anolis-xref="navigate-ua-inline">Page load processing model for inline content that doesn't have a DOM</dfn>

When the user agent is to display a user agent page inline in a [browsing context](#270.html_browsing-context), the user agent should [create a `Document` object](#270.html_create-a-document-object), mark it as being an [HTML document](#270.html_html-documents), set its [content type](#270.html_concept-document-content-type) to "`text/html`", and then either associate that [`Document`](#270.html_document) with a custom rendering that is not rendered using the normal [`Document`](#270.html_document) rendering rules, or mutate that [`Document`](#270.html_document) until it represents the content the user agent wants to render.

Once the page has been set up, the user agent must act as if it had [stopped parsing](#270.html_stop-parsing).

Upon creation of the [`Document`](#270.html_document) object, the user agent must run the [application cache selection algorithm](#270.html_concept-appcache-init) with no manifest, passing in the newly-created [`Document`](#270.html_document).

After creating the [`Document`](#270.html_document) object, but potentially before the page has been completely set up, the user agent must [update the session history with the new page](#270.html_update-the-session-history-with-the-new-page).

#### 5.6.9 <dfn id="271.html_navigate-fragid" data-anolis-xref="navigate-fragid">Navigating to a fragment identifier</dfn>

When a user agent is supposed to navigate to a fragment identifier, then the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Remove all the entries in the [browsing context](#271.html_browsing-context)'s [session history](#271.html_session-history) after the [current entry](#271.html_current-entry). If the [current entry](#271.html_current-entry) is the last entry in the session history, then no entries are removed.

    This [doesn't necessarily have to affect](#271.html_history-notes) the user agent's user interface.

2.  Remove any [tasks](#271.html_concept-task) queued by the [history traversal task source](#271.html_history-traversal-task-source) that are associated with any [`Document`](#271.html_document) objects in the [top-level browsing context](#271.html_top-level-browsing-context)'s [document family](#271.html_document-family).

3.  Append a new entry at the end of the [`History`](#271.html_history-1) object representing the new resource and its [`Document`](#271.html_document) object and related state. Its URL must be set to the address to which the user agent was [navigating](#271.html_navigate). The title must be left unset.

4.  [Traverse the history](#271.html_traverse-the-history) to the new entry, with the *asynchronous events* flag set. This will [scroll to the fragment identifier](#271.html_scroll-to-the-fragment-identifier) given in what is now [the document's address](#271.html_the-document's-address).

If the scrolling fails because the relevant [ID](#271.html_concept-id) has not yet been parsed, then the original [navigation](#271.html_navigate) algorithm will take care of the scrolling instead, as the last few steps of its [update the session history with the new page](#271.html_update-the-session-history-with-the-new-page) algorithm.

* * *

When the user agent is required to <dfn id="271.html_scroll-to-the-fragment-identifier">scroll to the fragment identifier</dfn> and [the indicated part of the document](#271.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document), if any, is [being rendered](#271.html_being-rendered), the user agent must either change the scrolling position of the document using the following algorithm, or perform some other action such that [the indicated part of the document](#271.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document) is brought to the user's attention. If there is no indicated part, or if the indicated part is not [being rendered](#271.html_being-rendered), then the user agent must do nothing. The aforementioned algorithm is as follows:

1.  Let `target` be [the indicated part of the document](#271.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document), as defined below.

2.  If `target` is the top of the document, then [scroll to the beginning of the document](#271.html_scroll-to-the-beginning-of-the-document) for the [`Document`](#271.html_document), and abort these steps. [[CSSOMVIEW]](#271.html_refsCSSOMVIEW)

3.  Use the [scroll an element into view](#271.html_scroll-an-element-into-view) algorithm to scroll `target` into view, with the `align to top flag` set. [[CSSOMVIEW]](#271.html_refsCSSOMVIEW)

4.  If `target` is a [focusable](#271.html_focusable) element, run the [focusing steps](#271.html_focusing-steps) for that element.

<dfn id="271.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document">The indicated part of the document</dfn> is the one that the fragment identifier, if any, identifies. The semantics of the fragment identifier in terms of mapping it to a specific DOM Node is defined by the specification that defines the [MIME type](#271.html_mime-type) used by the [`Document`](#271.html_document) (for example, the processing of fragment identifiers for [XML MIME types](#271.html_xml-mime-type) is the responsibility of RFC7303). [[RFC7303]](#271.html_refsRFC7303)

For HTML documents (and [HTML MIME types](#271.html_html-mime-type)), the following processing model must be followed to determine what [the indicated part of the document](#271.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document) is.

1.  Apply the [URL parser](#271.html_url-parser-0) algorithm to the URL, and let `fragid` be the [fragment](#271.html_concept-url-fragment) component of the resulting [parsed URL](#271.html_parsed-url).

2.  If `fragid` is the empty string, then [the indicated part of the document](#271.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document) is the top of the document; stop the algorithm here.

3.  Let `fragid bytes` be the result of [percent-decoding](#271.html_percent-decode) `fragid`.

4.  Let `decoded fragid` be the result of applying the [UTF-8 decoder](#271.html_utf-8-decoder) algorithm to `fragid bytes`. If the [UTF-8 decoder](#271.html_utf-8-decoder) emits a [decoder error](#271.html_decoder-error), abort the decoder and instead jump to the step labeled *no decoded fragid*.

5.  If there is an element in the DOM that has an [ID](#271.html_concept-id) exactly equal to `decoded fragid`, then the first such element in tree order is [the indicated part of the document](#271.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document); stop the algorithm here.

6.  *No decoded fragid*: If there is an [`a`](#271.html_the-a-element) element in the DOM that has a [`name`](#271.html_attr-a-name) attribute whose value is exactly equal to `fragid` (*not* `decoded fragid`), then the first such element in tree order is [the indicated part of the document](#271.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document); stop the algorithm here.

7.  If `fragid` is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#271.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string `top`, then [the indicated part of the document](#271.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document) is the top of the document; stop the algorithm here.

8.  Otherwise, there is no [indicated part of the document](#271.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document).

For the purposes of the interaction of HTML with Selectors' `:target` pseudo-class, the <dfn id="271.html_target-element">*target element*</dfn> is [the indicated part of the document](#271.html_the-indicated-part-of-the-document), if that is an element; otherwise there is no *[target element](#271.html_target-element)*. [[SELECTORS]](#271.html_refsSELECTORS)

The [task source](#271.html_task-source) for the task mentioned in this section must be the [DOM manipulation task source](#271.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

#### 5.6.10 History traversal

When a user agent is required to <dfn id="272.html_traverse-the-history">traverse the history</dfn> to a `specified entry`, optionally with [replacement enabled](#272.html_replacement-enabled), and optionally with the *asynchronous events* flag set, the user agent must act as follows.

This algorithm is not just invoked when [explicitly going back or forwards in the session history](#272.html_traverse-the-history-by-a-delta) — it is also invoked in other situations, for example when [navigating a browsing context](#272.html_navigate), as part of [updating the session history with the new page](#272.html_update-the-session-history-with-the-new-page).

1.  If there is no longer a [`Document`](#272.html_document) object for the entry in question, [navigate](#272.html_navigate) the [browsing context](#272.html_browsing-context) to the resource for that entry to perform an [entry update](#272.html_entry-update) of that entry, and abort these steps. The "[navigate](#272.html_navigate)" algorithm reinvokes this "traverse" algorithm to complete the traversal, at which point there *is* a [`Document`](#272.html_document) object and so this step gets skipped. The navigation must be done using the same [source browsing context](#272.html_source-browsing-context) as was used the first time this entry was created. (This can never happen with [replacement enabled](#272.html_replacement-enabled).)

    If the resource was obtained usign a non-idempotent action, for example a POST form submission, or if the resource is no longer available, for example because the computer is now offline and the page wasn't cached, navigating to it again might not be possible. In this case, the navigation will result in a different page than previously; for example, it might be an error message explaining the problem or offering to resubmit the form.

2.  If the [current entry](#272.html_current-entry)'s title was not set by the [`pushState()`](#272.html_dom-history-pushstate) or [`replaceState()`](#272.html_dom-history-replacestate) methods, then set its title to the value returned by the [`document.title`](#272.html_document.title) IDL attribute.

3.  If appropriate, update the [current entry](#272.html_current-entry) in the [browsing context](#272.html_browsing-context)'s [`Document`](#272.html_document) object's [`History`](#272.html_history-1) object to reflect any state that the user agent wishes to persist. The entry is then said to be [an entry with persisted user state](#272.html_an-entry-with-persisted-user-state).

4.  If the `specified entry` has a different [`Document`](#272.html_document) object than the [current entry](#272.html_current-entry), then run the following substeps:

    1.  Remove any [tasks](#272.html_concept-task) queued by the [history traversal task source](#272.html_history-traversal-task-source) that are associated with any [`Document`](#272.html_document) objects in the [top-level browsing context](#272.html_top-level-browsing-context)'s [document family](#272.html_document-family).

    2.  If the [origin](#272.html_origin-0) of the [`Document`](#272.html_document) of the `specified entry` is not the [same](#272.html_same-origin) as the [origin](#272.html_origin-0) of the [`Document`](#272.html_document) of the [current entry](#272.html_current-entry), then run the following sub-sub-steps:

        1.  The current [browsing context name](#272.html_browsing-context-name) must be stored with all the entries in the history that are associated with [`Document`](#272.html_document) objects with the [same origin](#272.html_same-origin) as the [active document](#272.html_active-document) *and* that are contiguous with the [current entry](#272.html_current-entry).

        2.  If the browsing context is a [top-level browsing context](#272.html_top-level-browsing-context), but not an [auxiliary browsing context](#272.html_auxiliary-browsing-context), then the browsing context's [browsing context name](#272.html_browsing-context-name) must be unset.

    3.  Make the `specified entry`'s [`Document`](#272.html_document) object the [active document](#272.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#272.html_browsing-context).

    4.  If the `specified entry` has a [browsing context name](#272.html_browsing-context-name) stored with it, then run the following sub-sub-steps:

        1.  Set the browsing context's [browsing context name](#272.html_browsing-context-name) to the name stored with the specified entry.

        2.  Clear any [browsing context names](#272.html_browsing-context-name) stored with all entries in the history that are associated with [`Document`](#272.html_document) objects with the [same origin](#272.html_same-origin) as the new [active document](#272.html_active-document) and that are contiguous with the specified entry.

    5.  If the `specified entry`'s [`Document`](#272.html_document) has any form controls whose autofill field name is "[`off`](#272.html_attr-fe-autocomplete-off)", invoke the [reset algorithm](#272.html_concept-form-reset-control) of each of those elements.

    6.  If the [current document readiness](#272.html_current-document-readiness) of the `specified entry`'s [`Document`](#272.html_document) is "`complete`", [queue a task](#272.html_queue-a-task) to run the following sub-sub-steps:

        1.  If the [`Document`](#272.html_document)'s [page showing](#272.html_page-showing) flag is true, then abort this task (i.e. don't fire the event below).

        2.  Set the [`Document`](#272.html_document)'s [page showing](#272.html_page-showing) flag to true.

        3.  Run any <dfn id="272.html_session-history-document-visibility-change-steps">session history document visibility change steps</dfn> for [`Document`](#272.html_document) that are defined by [other applicable specifications](#272.html_other-applicable-specifications).

            This is specifically intended for use by the Page Visibility specification. [[PAGEVIS]](#272.html_refsPAGEVIS)

        4.  [Fire](#272.html_concept-event-fire) a [trusted](#272.html_concept-events-trusted) event with the name [`pageshow`](#272.html_event-pageshow) at the [`Window`](#272.html_window) object of that [`Document`](#272.html_document), but with its [`target`](#272.html_dom-event-target) set to the [`Document`](#272.html_document) object (and the `currentTarget` set to the [`Window`](#272.html_window) object), using the [`PageTransitionEvent`](#272.html_pagetransitionevent) interface, with the [`persisted`](#272.html_dom-pagetransitionevent-persisted) attribute initialized to true. This event must not bubble, must not be cancelable, and has no default action.

5.  Set [the document's address](#272.html_the-document's-address) to the URL of the `specified entry`.

6.  If the `specified entry` has a URL whose fragment identifier differs from that of the [current entry](#272.html_current-entry)'s when compared in a [case-sensitive](#272.html_case-sensitive) manner, and the two share the same [`Document`](#272.html_document) object, then let `hash changed` be true, and let `old URL` be the URL of the [current entry](#272.html_current-entry) and `new URL` be the URL of the `specified entry`. Otherwise, let `hash changed` be false.

7.  If the traversal was initiated with <dfn id="272.html_replacement-enabled">replacement enabled</dfn>, remove the entry immediately before the `specified entry` in the session history.

8.  If the `specified entry` is not [an entry with persisted user state](#272.html_an-entry-with-persisted-user-state), but its URL has a fragment identifier, [scroll to the fragment identifier](#272.html_scroll-to-the-fragment-identifier).

9.  If the entry is [an entry with persisted user state](#272.html_an-entry-with-persisted-user-state), the user agent may update aspects of the document and its rendering, for instance the scroll position or values of form fields, that it had previously recorded.

    This can even include updating the [`dir`](#272.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute of [`textarea`](#272.html_the-textarea-element) elements or [`input`](#272.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#272.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in either the [Text](#272.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) state or the [Search](#272.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) state, if the persisted state includes the directionality of user input in such controls.

10.  If the entry is a [state object](#272.html_state-object) entry, let `state` be a [structured clone](#272.html_structured-clone) of that state object. Otherwise, let `state` be null.

11.  Set [`history.state`](#272.html_dom-history-state) to `state`.

12.  Let `state changed` be true if the [`Document`](#272.html_document) of the `specified entry` has a [latest entry](#272.html_latest-entry), and that entry is not the `specified entry`; otherwise let it be false.

13.  Let the [latest entry](#272.html_latest-entry) of the [`Document`](#272.html_document) of the `specified entry` be the `specified entry`.

14.  If the *asynchronous events* flag is not set, then run the following steps synchronously. Otherwise, the *asynchronous events* flag is set; [queue a task](#272.html_queue-a-task) to run the following substeps.

    1.  If `state changed` is true, [fire](#272.html_concept-event-fire) a [trusted](#272.html_concept-events-trusted) event with the name [`popstate`](#272.html_event-popstate) at the [`Window`](#272.html_window) object of the [`Document`](#272.html_document), using the [`PopStateEvent`](#272.html_popstateevent) interface, with the [`state`](#272.html_dom-popstateevent-state) attribute initialized to the value of `state`. This event must bubble but not be cancelable and has no default action.

    2.  If `hash changed` is true, then [fire](#272.html_concept-event-fire) a [trusted](#272.html_concept-events-trusted) event with the name [`hashchange`](#272.html_event-hashchange) at the [browsing context](#272.html_browsing-context)'s [`Window`](#272.html_window) object, using the [`HashChangeEvent`](#272.html_hashchangeevent) interface, with the [`oldURL`](#272.html_dom-hashchangeevent-oldurl) attribute initialized to `old URL` and the [`newURL`](#272.html_dom-hashchangeevent-newurl) attribute initialized to `new URL`. This event must bubble but not be cancelable and has no default action.

15.  The [current entry](#272.html_current-entry) is now the `specified entry`.

The [task source](#272.html_task-source) for the tasks mentioned above is the [DOM manipulation task source](#272.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

##### 5.6.10.1 Event definitions

The <dfn id="272.html_event-popstate" data-anolis-xref="event-popstate">`popstate`</dfn> event is fired in certain cases when navigating to a [session history entry](#272.html_session-history-entry).

```
[Constructor(DOMString type, optional PopStateEventInit eventInitDict)]
interface PopStateEvent : Event {
  readonly attribute any state;
};

dictionary PopStateEventInit : EventInit {
  any state;
};
```

`event` . [`state`](#272.html_dom-popstateevent-state)

Returns a copy of the information that was provided to [`pushState()`](#272.html_dom-history-pushstate) or [`replaceState()`](#272.html_dom-history-replacestate).

The <dfn id="272.html_dom-popstateevent-state" data-anolis-xref="dom-PopStateEvent-state">`state`</dfn> attribute must return the value it was initialized to. When the object is created, this attribute must be initialized to null. It represents the context information for the event, or null, if the state represented is the initial state of the [`Document`](#272.html_document).

* * *

The <dfn id="272.html_event-hashchange" data-anolis-xref="event-hashchange">`hashchange`</dfn> event is fired when navigating to a [session history entry](#272.html_session-history-entry) whose URL differs from that of the previous one only in the fragment identifier.

```
[Constructor(DOMString type, optional HashChangeEventInit eventInitDict)]
interface HashChangeEvent : Event {
  readonly attribute DOMString oldURL;
  readonly attribute DOMString newURL;
};

dictionary HashChangeEventInit : EventInit {
  DOMString oldURL;
  DOMString newURL;
};
```

`event` . [`oldURL`](#272.html_dom-hashchangeevent-oldurl)

Returns the URL of the [session history entry](#272.html_session-history-entry) that was previously current.

`event` . [`newURL`](#272.html_dom-hashchangeevent-newurl)

Returns the URL of the [session history entry](#272.html_session-history-entry) that is now current.

The <dfn id="272.html_dom-hashchangeevent-oldurl" data-anolis-xref="dom-HashChangeEvent-oldURL">`oldURL`</dfn> attribute must return the value it was initialized to. When the object is created, this attribute must be initialized to null. It represents context information for the event, specifically the URL of the [session history entry](#272.html_session-history-entry) that was traversed from.

The <dfn id="272.html_dom-hashchangeevent-newurl" data-anolis-xref="dom-HashChangeEvent-newURL">`newURL`</dfn> attribute must return the value it was initialized to. When the object is created, this attribute must be initialized to null. It represents context information for the event, specifically the URL of the [session history entry](#272.html_session-history-entry) that was traversed to.

* * *

The <dfn id="272.html_event-pageshow" data-anolis-xref="event-pageshow">`pageshow`</dfn> event is fired when [traversing](#272.html_traverse-the-history) *to* a [session history entry](#272.html_session-history-entry). The <dfn id="272.html_event-pagehide" data-anolis-xref="event-pagehide">`pagehide`</dfn> event is fired when traversing *from* a [session history entry](#272.html_session-history-entry). The specification uses the [page showing](#272.html_page-showing) flag to ensure that scripts receive these events in a consistent manner (e.g. that they never receive two [`pagehide`](#272.html_event-pagehide) events in a row without an intervening [`pageshow`](#272.html_event-pageshow), or vice versa).

```
[Constructor(DOMString type, optional PageTransitionEventInit eventInitDict)]
interface PageTransitionEvent : Event {
  readonly attribute boolean persisted;
};

dictionary PageTransitionEventInit : EventInit {
  boolean persisted;
};
```

`event` . [`persisted`](#272.html_dom-pagetransitionevent-persisted)

For the [`pageshow`](#272.html_event-pageshow) event, returns false if the page is newly being loaded (and the `load` event will fire). Otherwise, returns true.

For the [`pagehide`](#272.html_event-pagehide) event, returns false if the page is going away for the last time. Otherwise, returns true, meaning that (if nothing conspires to make the page unsalvageable) the page might be reused if the user navigates back to this page.

Things that can cause the page to be unsalvageable include:

*   [`document.open()`](#272.html_dom-document-open)
*   Listening for `beforeunload` events
*   Listening for `unload` events
*   Having [`iframe`](#272.html_the-iframe-element)s that are not salvageable
*   Active `WebSocket` objects
*   [Aborting a `Document`](#272.html_abort-a-document)

The <dfn id="272.html_dom-pagetransitionevent-persisted" data-anolis-xref="dom-PageTransitionEvent-persisted">`persisted`</dfn> attribute must return the value it was initialized to. When the object is created, this attribute must be initialized to false. It represents the context information for the event.

#### 5.6.11 Unloading documents

A [`Document`](#273.html_document) has a <dfn id="273.html_concept-document-salvageable" data-anolis-xref="concept-document-salvageable">*salvageable*</dfn> state, which must initially be true, a <dfn id="273.html_fired-unload">fired unload</dfn> flag, which must initially be false, and a <dfn id="273.html_page-showing">page showing</dfn> flag, which must initially be false.

[Event loops](#273.html_event-loop) have a <dfn id="273.html_termination-nesting-level">termination nesting level</dfn> counter, which must initially be zero.

When a user agent is to <dfn id="273.html_prompt-to-unload-a-document">prompt to unload a document</dfn>, it must run the following steps.

1.  Increase the [event loop](#273.html_event-loop)'s [termination nesting level](#273.html_termination-nesting-level) by one.

2.  Increase the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [ignore-opens-during-unload counter](#273.html_ignore-opens-during-unload-counter) by one.

3.  Let `event` be a new [trusted](#273.html_concept-events-trusted) [`BeforeUnloadEvent`](#273.html_beforeunloadevent) event object with the name `beforeunload`, which does not bubble but is cancelable.

4.  *Dispatch*: [Dispatch](#273.html_concept-event-dispatch) `event` at the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [`Window`](#273.html_window) object.

5.  Decrease the [event loop](#273.html_event-loop)'s [termination nesting level](#273.html_termination-nesting-level) by one.

6.  Release the [storage mutex](#273.html_storage-mutex).

7.  If any event listeners were triggered by the earlier *dispatch* step, then set the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s *[salvageable](#273.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state to false.

8.  If the [`returnValue`](#273.html_dom-beforeunloadevent-returnvalue) attribute of the `event` object is not the empty string, or if the event was canceled, then the user agent should ask the user to confirm that they wish to unload the document.

    The prompt shown by the user agent may include the string of the [`returnValue`](#273.html_dom-beforeunloadevent-returnvalue) attribute, or some leading subset thereof. (A user agent may want to truncate the string to 1024 characters for display, for instance.)

    The user agent must [pause](#273.html_pause) while waiting for the user's response.

    If the user did not confirm the page navigation, then the user agent <dfn id="273.html_refused-to-allow-the-document-to-be-unloaded">refused to allow the document to be unloaded</dfn>.

9.  If this algorithm was invoked by another instance of the "prompt to unload a document" algorithm (i.e. through the steps below that invoke this algorithm for all descendant browsing contexts), then jump to the step labeled *end*.

10.  Let `descendants` be the [list of the descendant browsing contexts](#273.html_list-of-the-descendant-browsing-contexts) of the [`Document`](#273.html_document).

11.  If `descendants` is not an empty list, then for each [browsing context](#273.html_browsing-context) `b` in `descendants` run the following substeps:

    1.  [Prompt to unload](#273.html_prompt-to-unload-a-document) the [active document](#273.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#273.html_browsing-context) `b`. If the user [refused to allow the document to be unloaded](#273.html_refused-to-allow-the-document-to-be-unloaded), then the user implicitly also [refused to allow *this* document to be unloaded](#273.html_refused-to-allow-the-document-to-be-unloaded); jump to the step labeled *end*.

    2.  If the *[salvageable](#273.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state of the [active document](#273.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#273.html_browsing-context) `b` is false, then set the *[salvageable](#273.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state of *this* document to false also.

12.  *End*: Decrease the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [ignore-opens-during-unload counter](#273.html_ignore-opens-during-unload-counter) by one.

When a user agent is to <dfn id="273.html_unload-a-document">unload a document</dfn>, it must run the following steps. These steps are passed an argument, `recycle`, which is either true or false, indicating whether the [`Document`](#273.html_document) object is going to be re-used. (This is set by the [`document.open()`](#273.html_dom-document-open) method.)

1.  Increase the [event loop](#273.html_event-loop)'s [termination nesting level](#273.html_termination-nesting-level) by one.

2.  Increase the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [ignore-opens-during-unload counter](#273.html_ignore-opens-during-unload-counter) by one.

3.  If the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [page showing](#273.html_page-showing) flag is false, then jump to the step labeled *unload event* below (i.e. skip firing the [`pagehide`](#273.html_event-pagehide) event and don't rerun the [unloading document visibility change steps](#273.html_unloading-document-visibility-change-steps)).

4.  Set the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [page showing](#273.html_page-showing) flag to false.

5.  [Fire](#273.html_concept-event-fire) a [trusted](#273.html_concept-events-trusted) event with the name [`pagehide`](#273.html_event-pagehide) at the [`Window`](#273.html_window) object of the [`Document`](#273.html_document), but with its [`target`](#273.html_dom-event-target) set to the [`Document`](#273.html_document) object (and the `currentTarget` set to the [`Window`](#273.html_window) object), using the [`PageTransitionEvent`](#273.html_pagetransitionevent) interface, with the [`persisted`](#273.html_dom-pagetransitionevent-persisted) attribute initialized to true if the [`Document`](#273.html_document) object's *[salvageable](#273.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state is true, and false otherwise. This event must not bubble, must not be cancelable, and has no default action.

6.  Run any <dfn id="273.html_unloading-document-visibility-change-steps">unloading document visibility change steps</dfn> for [`Document`](#273.html_document) that are defined by [other applicable specifications](#273.html_other-applicable-specifications).

    This is specifically intended for use by the Page Visibility specification. [[PAGEVIS]](#273.html_refsPAGEVIS)

7.  *Unload event*: If the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [fired unload](#273.html_fired-unload) flag is false, [fire a simple event](#273.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `unload` at the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [`Window`](#273.html_window) object.

8.  Decrease the [event loop](#273.html_event-loop)'s [termination nesting level](#273.html_termination-nesting-level) by one.

9.  Release the [storage mutex](#273.html_storage-mutex).

10.  If any event listeners were triggered by the earlier *unload event* step, then set the [`Document`](#273.html_document) object's *[salvageable](#273.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state to false and set the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [fired unload](#273.html_fired-unload) flag to true.

11.  Run any [unloading document cleanup steps](#273.html_unloading-document-cleanup-steps) for [`Document`](#273.html_document) that are defined by this specification and [other applicable specifications](#273.html_other-applicable-specifications).

12.  If this algorithm was invoked by another instance of the "unload a document" algorithm (i.e. by the steps below that invoke this algorithm for all descendant browsing contexts), then jump to the step labeled *end*.

13.  Let `descendants` be the [list of the descendant browsing contexts](#273.html_list-of-the-descendant-browsing-contexts) of the [`Document`](#273.html_document).

14.  If `descendants` is not an empty list, then for each [browsing context](#273.html_browsing-context) `b` in `descendants` run the following substeps:

    1.  [Unload](#273.html_unload-a-document) the [active document](#273.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#273.html_browsing-context) `b` with the `recycle` parameter set to false.

    2.  If the *[salvageable](#273.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state of the [active document](#273.html_active-document) of the [browsing context](#273.html_browsing-context) `b` is false, then set the *[salvageable](#273.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state of *this* document to false also.

15.  If both the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s *[salvageable](#273.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state and `recycle` are false, then the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [browsing context](#273.html_browsing-context) must [discard the `Document`](#273.html_discard-a-document).

16.  *End*: Decrease the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [ignore-opens-during-unload counter](#273.html_ignore-opens-during-unload-counter) by one.

This specification defines the following <dfn id="273.html_unloading-document-cleanup-steps">unloading document cleanup steps</dfn>. Other specifications can define more.

1.  Make disappear any `WebSocket` objects that were created by the `WebSocket()` constructor from the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [`Window`](#273.html_window) object.

    If this affected any `WebSocket` objects, then set [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s *[salvageable](#273.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state to false.

2.  If the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s *[salvageable](#273.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state is false, forcibly close any [`EventSource`](#273.html_eventsource) objects that whose constructor was invoked from the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [`Window`](#273.html_window) object.

3.  If the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s *[salvageable](#273.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state is false, empty the [`Document`](#273.html_document)'s [`Window`](#273.html_window)'s [list of active timers](#273.html_list-of-active-timers).

##### 5.6.11.1 Event definition

```
interface BeforeUnloadEvent : Event {
           attribute DOMString returnValue;
};
```

`event` . [`returnValue`](#273.html_dom-beforeunloadevent-returnvalue) [ = `value` ]

Returns the current return value of the event (the message to show the user).

Can be set, to update the message.

There are no [`BeforeUnloadEvent`](#273.html_beforeunloadevent)-specific initialization methods.

The <dfn id="273.html_dom-beforeunloadevent-returnvalue" data-anolis-xref="dom-BeforeUnloadEvent-returnValue">`returnValue`</dfn> attribute represents the message to show the user. When the event is created, the attribute must be set to the empty string. On getting, it must return the last value it was set to. On setting, the attribute must be set to the new value.

#### 5.6.12 Aborting a document load

If a [`Document`](#274.html_document) is <dfn id="274.html_abort-a-document" data-anolis-xref="abort a document">aborted</dfn>, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  [Abort](#274.html_abort-a-document) the [active documents](#274.html_active-document) of every [child browsing context](#274.html_child-browsing-context). If this results in any of those [`Document`](#274.html_document) objects having their *[salvageable](#274.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state set to false, then set this [`Document`](#274.html_document)'s *[salvageable](#274.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state to false also.

2.  Cancel any instances of the [fetch](#274.html_fetch) algorithm in the context of this [`Document`](#274.html_document), discarding any [tasks](#274.html_concept-task) [queued](#274.html_queue-a-task) for them, and discarding any further data received from the network for them. If this resulted in any instances of the [fetch](#274.html_fetch) algorithm being canceled or any [queued](#274.html_queue-a-task) [tasks](#274.html_concept-task) or any network data getting discarded, then set the [`Document`](#274.html_document)'s *[salvageable](#274.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state to false.

3.  If the [`Document`](#274.html_document) has an [active parser](#274.html_active-parser), then [abort that parser](#274.html_abort-a-parser) and set the [`Document`](#274.html_document)'s *[salvageable](#274.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state to false.

User agents may allow users to explicitly invoke the [abort a document](#274.html_abort-a-document) algorithm for a [`Document`](#274.html_document). If the user does so, then, if that [`Document`](#274.html_document) is an [active document](#274.html_active-document), the user agent should [queue a task](#274.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#274.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `abort` at that [`Document`](#274.html_document)'s [`Window`](#274.html_window) object before invoking the [abort](#274.html_abort-a-document) algorithm.

### 5.7 Offline Web applications

#### 5.7.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

In order to enable users to continue interacting with Web applications and documents even when their network connection is unavailable — for instance, because they are traveling outside of their ISP's coverage area — authors can provide a manifest which lists the files that are needed for the Web application to work offline and which causes the user's browser to keep a copy of the files for use offline.

To illustrate this, consider a simple clock applet consisting of an HTML page "`clock.html`", a CSS style sheet "`clock.css`", and a JavaScript script "`clock.js`".

Before adding the manifest, these three files might look like this:

```
EXAMPLE offline/clock/clock1.html
```

```
EXAMPLE offline/clock/clock1.css
```

```
EXAMPLE offline/clock/clock1.js
```

If the user tries to open the "`clock.html`" page while offline, though, the user agent (unless it happens to have it still in the local cache) will fail with an error.

The author can instead provide a manifest of the three files, say "`clock.appcache`":

```
EXAMPLE offline/clock/clock2.appcache
```

With a small change to the HTML file, the manifest (served as [`text/cache-manifest`](#276.html_text/cache-manifest)) is linked to the application:

```
EXAMPLE offline/clock/clock2.html
```

Now, if the user goes to the page, the browser will cache the files and make them available even when the user is offline.

Authors are encouraged to include the main page in the manifest also, but in practice the page that referenced the manifest is automatically cached even if it isn't explicitly mentioned.

With the exception of "no-store" directive, HTTP cache headers and restrictions on caching pages served over TLS (encrypted, using `https:`) are overridden by manifests. Thus, pages will not expire from an application cache before the user agent has updated it, and even applications served over TLS can be made to work offline.

[View this example online](http://www.whatwg.org/demos/offline/clock/live-demo/clock.html).

##### 5.7.1.1 Supporting offline caching for legacy applications

*This section is non-normative.*

The application cache feature works best if the application logic is separate from the application and user data, with the logic (markup, scripts, style sheets, images, etc) listed in the manifest and stored in the application cache, with a finite number of static HTML pages for the application, and with the application and user data stored in Web Storage or a client-side Indexed Database, updated dynamically using Web Sockets, [`XMLHttpRequest`](#276.html_xmlhttprequest), server-sent events, or some other similar mechanism.

This model results in a fast experience for the user: the application immediately loads, and fresh data is obtained as fast as the network will allow it (possibly while stale data shows).

Legacy applications, however, tend to be designed so that the user data and the logic are mixed together in the HTML, with each operation resulting in a new HTML page from the server.

For example, consider a news application. The typical architecture of such an application, when not using the application cache feature, is that the user fetches the main page, and the server returns a dynamically-generated page with the current headlines and the user interface logic mixed together.

A news application designed for the application cache feature, however, would instead have the main page just consist of the logic, and would then have the main page fetch the data separately from the server, e.g. using [`XMLHttpRequest`](#276.html_xmlhttprequest).

The mixed-content model does not work well with the application cache feature: since the content is cached, it would result in the user always seeing the stale data from the previous time the cache was updated.

While there is no way to make the legacy model work as fast as the separated model, it *can* at least be retrofitted for offline use using the [prefer-online](#276.html_concept-appcache-mode-prefer-online) [application cache mode](#276.html_concept-appcache-mode). To do so, list all the static resources used by the HTML page you want to have work offline in an [application cache manifest](#276.html_concept-appcache-manifest), use the [`manifest`](#276.html_attr-html-manifest) attribute to select that manifest from the HTML file, and then add the following line at the bottom of the manifest:

```
SETTINGS:
prefer-online
NETWORK:
*
```

This causes the [application cache](#276.html_application-cache) to only be used for [master entries](#276.html_concept-appcache-master) when the user is offline, and causes the application cache to be used as an atomic HTTP cache (essentially pinning resources listed in the manifest), while allowing all resources not listed in the manifest to be accessed normally when the user is online.

##### 5.7.1.2 Event summary

*This section is non-normative.*

When the user visits a page that declares a manifest, the browser will try to update the cache. It does this by fetching a copy of the manifest and, if the manifest has changed since the user agent last saw it, redownloading all the resources it mentions and caching them anew.

As this is going on, a number of events get fired on the [`ApplicationCache`](#276.html_applicationcache) object to keep the script updated as to the state of the cache update, so that the user can be notified appropriately. The events are as follows:

| Event name | Interface | Fired when... | Next events |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <dfn id="276.html_event-appcache-checking" data-anolis-xref="event-appcache-checking">`checking`</dfn> | [`Event`](#276.html_event) | The user agent is checking for an update, or attempting to download the manifest for the first time. **This is always the first event in the sequence.** | [`noupdate`](#276.html_event-appcache-noupdate), [`downloading`](#276.html_event-appcache-downloading), [`obsolete`](#276.html_event-appcache-obsolete), [`error`](#276.html_event-appcache-error) |
| <dfn id="276.html_event-appcache-noupdate" data-anolis-xref="event-appcache-noupdate">`noupdate`</dfn> | [`Event`](#276.html_event) | The manifest hadn't changed. | Last event in sequence. |
| <dfn id="276.html_event-appcache-downloading" data-anolis-xref="event-appcache-downloading">`downloading`</dfn> | [`Event`](#276.html_event) | The user agent has found an update and is fetching it, or is downloading the resources listed by the manifest for the first time. | [`progress`](#276.html_event-appcache-progress), [`error`](#276.html_event-appcache-error), [`cached`](#276.html_event-appcache-cached), [`updateready`](#276.html_event-appcache-updateready) |
| <dfn id="276.html_event-appcache-progress" data-anolis-xref="event-appcache-progress">`progress`</dfn> | [`ProgressEvent`](#276.html_progressevent) | The user agent is downloading resources listed by the manifest. The event object's `total` attribute returns the total number of files to be downloaded. The event object's `loaded` attribute returns the number of files processed so far. | [`progress`](#276.html_event-appcache-progress), [`error`](#276.html_event-appcache-error), [`cached`](#276.html_event-appcache-cached), [`updateready`](#276.html_event-appcache-updateready) |
| <dfn id="276.html_event-appcache-cached" data-anolis-xref="event-appcache-cached">`cached`</dfn> | [`Event`](#276.html_event) | The resources listed in the manifest have been downloaded, and the application is now cached. | Last event in sequence. |
| <dfn id="276.html_event-appcache-updateready" data-anolis-xref="event-appcache-updateready">`updateready`</dfn> | [`Event`](#276.html_event) | The resources listed in the manifest have been newly redownloaded, and the script can use [`swapCache()`](#276.html_dom-appcache-swapcache) to switch to the new cache. | Last event in sequence. |
| <dfn id="276.html_event-appcache-obsolete" data-anolis-xref="event-appcache-obsolete">`obsolete`</dfn> | [`Event`](#276.html_event) | The manifest was found to have become a 404 or 410 page, so the application cache is being deleted. | Last event in sequence. |
| <dfn id="276.html_event-appcache-error" data-anolis-xref="event-appcache-error">`error`</dfn> | [`Event`](#276.html_event) | The manifest was a 404 or 410 page, so the attempt to cache the application has been aborted. | Last event in sequence. |
| The manifest hadn't changed, but the page referencing the manifest failed to download properly. |
| A fatal error occurred while fetching the resources listed in the manifest. |
| The manifest changed while the update was being run. | The user agent will try fetching the files again momentarily. |

These events are cancelable; their default action is for the user agent to show download progress information. If the page shows its own update UI, canceling the events will prevent the user agent from showing redundant progress information.

#### 5.7.2 Application caches

An <dfn id="277.html_application-cache">application cache</dfn> is a set of cached resources consisting of:

*   One or more resources (including their out-of-band metadata, such as HTTP headers, if any), identified by URLs, each falling into one (or more) of the following categories:

    <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-master" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-master">Master entries</dfn>

    These are documents that were added to the cache because a [browsing context](#277.html_browsing-context) was [navigated](#277.html_navigate) to that document and the document indicated that this was its cache, using the [`manifest`](#277.html_attr-html-manifest) attribute.

    <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-manifest" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-manifest">The manifest</dfn>

    This is the resource corresponding to the URL that was given in a master entry's [`html`](#277.html_the-html-element) element's [`manifest`](#277.html_attr-html-manifest) attribute. The manifest is fetched and processed during the [application cache download process](#277.html_application-cache-download-process). All the [master entries](#277.html_concept-appcache-master) have the [same origin](#277.html_same-origin) as the manifest.

    <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-explicit" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-explicit">Explicit entries</dfn>

    These are the resources that were listed in the cache's [manifest](#277.html_concept-appcache-manifest) in an [explicit section](#277.html_concept-appcache-manifest-explicit).

    <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-fallback" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-fallback">Fallback entries</dfn>

    These are the resources that were listed in the cache's [manifest](#277.html_concept-appcache-manifest) in a [fallback section](#277.html_concept-appcache-manifest-fallback).

    [Explicit entries](#277.html_concept-appcache-explicit) and [Fallback entries](#277.html_concept-appcache-fallback) can be marked as <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-foreign" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-foreign">foreign</dfn>, which means that they have a [`manifest`](#277.html_attr-html-manifest) attribute but that it doesn't point at this cache's [manifest](#277.html_concept-appcache-manifest).

    A URL in the list can be flagged with multiple different types, and thus an entry can end up being categorized as multiple entries. For example, an entry can be a manifest entry and an explicit entry at the same time, if the manifest is listed within the manifest.

*   Zero or more <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-fallback-ns">fallback namespaces</dfn>, each of which is mapped to a [fallback entry](#277.html_concept-appcache-fallback).

    These are URLs used as [prefix match patterns](#277.html_concept-appcache-matches-fallback) for resources that are to be fetched from the network if possible, or to be replaced by the corresponding [fallback entry](#277.html_concept-appcache-fallback) if not. Each namespace URL has the [same origin](#277.html_same-origin) as [the manifest](#277.html_concept-appcache-manifest).

*   Zero or more URLs that form the <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist">online whitelist namespaces</dfn>.

    These are used as prefix match patterns, and declare URLs for which the user agent will ignore the application cache, instead fetching them normally (i.e. from the network or local HTTP cache as appropriate).

*   An <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist-wildcard" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist-wildcard">online whitelist wildcard flag</dfn>, which is either *open* or *blocking*.

    The *open* state indicates that any URL not listed as cached is to be implicitly treated as being in the [online whitelist namespaces](#277.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist); the *blocking* state indicates that URLs not listed explicitly in the manifest are to be treated as unavailable.

*   A <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-mode" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-mode">cache mode flag</dfn>, which is either in the <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-mode-fast" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-mode-fast">*fast*</dfn> state or the <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-mode-prefer-online" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-mode-prefer-online">*prefer-online*</dfn> state.

Each [application cache](#277.html_application-cache) has a <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-completeness" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-completeness">completeness flag</dfn>, which is either *complete* or *incomplete*.

* * *

An <dfn id="277.html_application-cache-group">application cache group</dfn> is a group of [application caches](#277.html_application-cache), identified by the [absolute URL](#277.html_absolute-url) of a resource [manifest](#277.html_concept-appcache-manifest) which is used to populate the caches in the group.

An [application cache](#277.html_application-cache) is <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-newer" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-newer">newer</dfn> than another if it was created after the other (in other words, [application caches](#277.html_application-cache) in an [application cache group](#277.html_application-cache-group) have a chronological order).

Only the newest [application cache](#277.html_application-cache) in an [application cache group](#277.html_application-cache-group) can have its [completeness flag](#277.html_concept-appcache-completeness) set to *incomplete*; the others are always all *complete*.

Each [application cache group](#277.html_application-cache-group) has an <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-status" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-status">update status</dfn>, which is one of the following: *idle*, *checking*, *downloading*.

A <dfn id="277.html_relevant-application-cache">relevant application cache</dfn> is an [application cache](#277.html_application-cache) that is the [newest](#277.html_concept-appcache-newer) in its [group](#277.html_application-cache-group) to be *complete*.

Each [application cache group](#277.html_application-cache-group) has a <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-pending-masters" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-pending-masters">list of pending master entries</dfn>. Each entry in this list consists of a resource and a corresponding [`Document`](#277.html_document) object. It is used during the [application cache download process](#277.html_application-cache-download-process) to ensure that new master entries are cached even if the [application cache download process](#277.html_application-cache-download-process) was already running for their [application cache group](#277.html_application-cache-group) when they were loaded.

An [application cache group](#277.html_application-cache-group) can be marked as <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-obsolete" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-obsolete">obsolete</dfn>, meaning that it must be ignored when looking at what [application cache groups](#277.html_application-cache-group) exist.

* * *

A <dfn id="277.html_cache-host">cache host</dfn> is a [`Document`](#277.html_document) or a `SharedWorkerGlobalScope` object. A [cache host](#277.html_cache-host) can be associated with an [application cache](#277.html_application-cache). [[WEBWORKERS]](#277.html_refsWEBWORKERS)

A [`Document`](#277.html_document) initially is not associated with an [application cache](#277.html_application-cache), but can become associated with one early during the page load process, when steps [in the parser](#277.html_parser-appcache) and in the [navigation](#277.html_navigate) sections cause [cache selection](#277.html_concept-appcache-init) to occur.

A `SharedWorkerGlobalScope` can be associated with an [application cache](#277.html_application-cache) when it is created. [[WEBWORKERS]](#277.html_refsWEBWORKERS)

Each [cache host](#277.html_cache-host) has an associated [`ApplicationCache`](#277.html_applicationcache) object.

* * *

Multiple [application caches](#277.html_application-cache) in different [application cache groups](#277.html_application-cache-group) can contain the same resource, e.g. if the manifests all reference that resource. If the user agent is to <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-selection" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-selection">select an application cache</dfn> from a list of [relevant application caches](#277.html_relevant-application-cache) that contain a resource, the user agent must use the application cache that the user most likely wants to see the resource from, taking into account the following:

*   which application cache was most recently updated,
*   which application cache was being used to display the resource from which the user decided to look at the new resource, and
*   which application cache the user prefers.

* * *

A URL <dfn id="277.html_concept-appcache-matches-fallback" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-matches-fallback">matches a fallback namespace</dfn> if there exists a [relevant application cache](#277.html_relevant-application-cache) whose [manifest](#277.html_concept-appcache-manifest)'s URL has the [same origin](#277.html_same-origin) as the URL in question, and that has a [fallback namespace](#277.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) that is a [prefix match](#277.html_prefix-match) for the URL being examined. If multiple fallback namespaces match the same URL, the longest one is the one that matches. A URL looking for a fallback namespace can match more than one application cache at a time, but only matches one namespace in each cache.

If a manifest `http://example.com/app1/manifest` declares that `http://example.com/resources/images` is a fallback namespace, and the user navigates to `HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM:80/resources/images/cat.png`, then the user agent will decide that the application cache identified by `http://example.com/app1/manifest` contains a namespace with a match for that URL.

#### 5.7.3 The cache manifest syntax

##### 5.7.3.1 Some sample manifests

*This section is non-normative.*

This example manifest requires two images and a style sheet to be cached and whitelists a CGI script.

```
CACHE MANIFEST
# the above line is required

# this is a comment
# there can be as many of these anywhere in the file
# they are all ignored
  # comments can have spaces before them
  # but must be alone on the line

# blank lines are ignored too

# these are files that need to be cached they can either be listed
# first, or a "CACHE:" header could be put before them, as is done
# lower down.
images/sound-icon.png
images/background.png
# note that each file has to be put on its own line

# here is a file for the online whitelist -- it isn't cached, and
# references to this file will bypass the cache, always hitting the
# network (or trying to, if the user is offline).
NETWORK:
comm.cgi

# here is another set of files to cache, this time just the CSS file.
CACHE:
style/default.css
```

It could equally well be written as follows:

```
CACHE MANIFEST
NETWORK:
comm.cgi
CACHE:
style/default.css
images/sound-icon.png
images/background.png
```

Offline application cache manifests can use absolute paths or even absolute URLs:

```
CACHE MANIFEST

/main/home
/main/app.js
/settings/home
/settings/app.js
http://img.example.com/logo.png
http://img.example.com/check.png
http://img.example.com/cross.png
```

The following manifest defines a catch-all error page that is displayed for any page on the site while the user is offline. It also specifies that the [online whitelist wildcard flag](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist-wildcard) is *open*, meaning that accesses to resources on other sites will not be blocked. (Resources on the same site are already not blocked because of the catch-all fallback namespace.)

So long as all pages on the site reference this manifest, they will get cached locally as they are fetched, so that subsequent hits to the same page will load the page immediately from the cache. Until the manifest is changed, those pages will not be fetched from the server again. When the manifest changes, then all the files will be redownloaded.

Subresources, such as style sheets, images, etc, would only be cached using the regular HTTP caching semantics, however.

```
CACHE MANIFEST
FALLBACK:
/ /offline.html
NETWORK:
*
```

##### 5.7.3.2 Writing cache manifests

Manifests must be served using the [`text/cache-manifest`](#278.html_text/cache-manifest) [MIME type](#278.html_mime-type). All resources served using the [`text/cache-manifest`](#278.html_text/cache-manifest) [MIME type](#278.html_mime-type) must follow the syntax of application cache manifests, as described in this section.

An application cache manifest is a text file, whose text is encoded using UTF-8\. Data in application cache manifests is line-based. Newlines must be represented by "LF" (U+000A) characters, "CR" (U+000D) characters, or "CR" (U+000D) "LF" (U+000A) pairs. [[RFC3629]](#278.html_refsRFC3629)

This is a [willful violation](#278.html_willful-violation) of RFC 2046, which requires all `text/*` types to only allow CRLF line breaks. This requirement, however, is outdated; the use of CR, LF, and CRLF line breaks is commonly supported and indeed sometimes CRLF is *not* supported by text editors. [[RFC2046]](#278.html_refsRFC2046)

The first line of an application cache manifest must consist of the string "CACHE", a single U+0020 SPACE character, the string "MANIFEST", and either a U+0020 SPACE character, a "tab" (U+0009) character, a "LF" (U+000A) character, or a "CR" (U+000D) character. The first line may optionally be preceded by a "BOM" (U+FEFF) character. If any other text is found on the first line, it is ignored.

Subsequent lines, if any, must all be one of the following:

A blank line

Blank lines must consist of zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters only.

A comment

Comment lines must consist of zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters, followed by a single "#" (U+0023) character, followed by zero or more characters other than "LF" (U+000A) and "CR" (U+000D) characters.

Comments must be on a line on their own. If they were to be included on a line with a URL, the "#" would be mistaken for part of a fragment identifier.

A section header

Section headers change the current section. There are four possible section headers:

`CACHE:`

Switches to the <dfn id="278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-explicit" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-manifest-explicit">explicit section</dfn>.

`FALLBACK:`

Switches to the <dfn id="278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-fallback" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-manifest-fallback">fallback section</dfn>.

`NETWORK:`

Switches to the <dfn id="278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-network" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-manifest-network">online whitelist section</dfn>.

`SETTINGS:`

Switches to the <dfn id="278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-settings" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-manifest-settings">settings section</dfn>.

Section header lines must consist of zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters, followed by one of the names above (including the ":)" (U+003A) character followed by zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters.

Ironically, by default, the current section is the [explicit section](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-explicit).

Data for the current section

The format that data lines must take depends on the current section.

When the current section is the [explicit section](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-explicit), data lines must consist of zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters, a [valid URL](#278.html_valid-url) identifying a resource other than the manifest itself, and then zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters.

When the current section is the [fallback section](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-fallback), data lines must consist of zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters, a [valid URL](#278.html_valid-url) identifying a resource other than the manifest itself, one or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters, another [valid URL](#278.html_valid-url) identifying a resource other than the manifest itself, and then zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters.

When the current section is the [online whitelist section](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-network), data lines must consist of zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters, either a single "*" (U+002A) character or a [valid URL](#278.html_valid-url) identifying a resource other than the manifest itself, and then zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters.

When the current section is the [settings section](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-settings), data lines must consist of zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters, a [setting](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-setting), and then zero or more U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters.

Currently only one <dfn id="278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-setting" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-manifest-setting">setting</dfn> is defined:

The cache mode setting

This consists of the string "`prefer-online`". It sets the [cache mode](#278.html_concept-appcache-mode) to [prefer-online](#278.html_concept-appcache-mode-prefer-online). (The [cache mode](#278.html_concept-appcache-mode) defaults to [fast](#278.html_concept-appcache-mode-fast).)

Within a [settings section](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-settings), each [setting](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-setting) must occur no more than once.

Manifests may contain sections more than once. Sections may be empty.

URLs that are to be fallback pages associated with [fallback namespaces](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns), and those namespaces themselves, must be given in [fallback sections](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-fallback), with the namespace being the first URL of the data line, and the corresponding fallback page being the second URL. All the other pages to be cached must be listed in [explicit sections](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-explicit).

[Fallback namespaces](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) and [fallback entries](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback) must have the [same origin](#278.html_same-origin) as the manifest itself.

A [fallback namespace](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) must not be listed more than once.

Namespaces that the user agent is to put into the [online whitelist](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist) must all be specified in [online whitelist sections](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-network). (This is needed for any URL that the page is intending to use to communicate back to the server.) To specify that all URLs are automatically whitelisted in this way, a "*" (U+002A) character may be specified as one of the URLs.

Authors should not include namespaces in the [online whitelist](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist) for which another namespace in the [online whitelist](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist) is a [prefix match](#278.html_prefix-match).

[Relative URLs](#278.html_relative-url) must be given relative to the manifest's own URL. All URLs in the manifest must have the same [scheme](#278.html_concept-url-scheme) as the manifest itself (either explicitly or implicitly, through the use of [relative URLs](#278.html_relative-url)). [[URL]](#278.html_refsURL)

URLs in manifests must not have fragment identifiers (i.e. the U+0023 NUMBER SIGN character isn't allowed in URLs in manifests).

[Fallback namespaces](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) and namespaces in the [online whitelist](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist) are matched by [prefix match](#278.html_prefix-match).

##### 5.7.3.3 Parsing cache manifests

When a user agent is to <dfn id="278.html_parse-a-manifest">parse a manifest</dfn>, it means that the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  [UTF-8 decode](#278.html_utf-8-decode) the byte stream corresponding with the manifest to be parsed.

    The [UTF-8 decode](#278.html_utf-8-decode) algorithm strips a leading BOM, if any.

2.  Let `base URL` be the [absolute URL](#278.html_absolute-url) representing the manifest.

3.  Apply the [URL parser](#278.html_url-parser-0) steps to the `base URL`, so that the components from its [parsed URL](#278.html_parsed-url) can be used by the subseqent steps of this algorithm.

4.  Let `explicit URLs` be an initially empty list of [absolute URLs](#278.html_absolute-url) for [explicit entries](#278.html_concept-appcache-explicit).

5.  Let `fallback URLs` be an initially empty mapping of [fallback namespaces](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) to [absolute URLs](#278.html_absolute-url) for [fallback entries](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback).

6.  Let `online whitelist namespaces` be an initially empty list of [absolute URLs](#278.html_absolute-url) for an [online whitelist](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist).

7.  Let `online whitelist wildcard flag` be *blocking*.

8.  Let `cache mode flag` be *fast*.

9.  Let `input` be the decoded text of the manifest's byte stream.

10.  Let `position` be a pointer into `input`, initially pointing at the first character.

11.  If the characters starting from `position` are "CACHE", followed by a U+0020 SPACE character, followed by "MANIFEST", then advance `position` to the next character after those. Otherwise, this isn't a cache manifest; abort this algorithm with a failure while checking for the magic signature.

12.  If the character at `position` is neither a U+0020 SPACE character, a "tab" (U+0009) character, "LF" (U+000A) character, nor a "CR" (U+000D) character, then this isn't a cache manifest; abort this algorithm with a failure while checking for the magic signature.

13.  This is a cache manifest. The algorithm cannot fail beyond this point (though bogus lines can get ignored).

14.  [Collect a sequence of characters](#278.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are *not* "LF" (U+000A) or "CR" (U+000D) characters, and ignore those characters. (Extra text on the first line, after the signature, is ignored.)

15.  Let `mode` be "explicit".

16.  *Start of line*: If `position` is past the end of `input`, then jump to the last step. Otherwise, [collect a sequence of characters](#278.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are "LF" (U+000A), "CR" (U+000D), U+0020 SPACE, or "tab" (U+0009) characters.

17.  Now, [collect a sequence of characters](#278.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are *not* "LF" (U+000A) or "CR" (U+000D) characters, and let the result be `line`.

18.  Drop any trailing U+0020 SPACE and "tab" (U+0009) characters at the end of `line`.

19.  If `line` is the empty string, then jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

20.  If the first character in `line` is a "#" (U+0023) character, then jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

21.  If `line` equals "CACHE:" (the word "CACHE" followed by a ":)" (U+003A) character, then set `mode` to "explicit" and jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

22.  If `line` equals "FALLBACK:" (the word "FALLBACK" followed by a ":)" (U+003A) character, then set `mode` to "fallback" and jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

23.  If `line` equals "NETWORK:" (the word "NETWORK" followed by a ":)" (U+003A) character, then set `mode` to "online whitelist" and jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

24.  If `line` equals "SETTINGS:" (the word "SETTINGS" followed by a ":)" (U+003A) character, then set `mode` to "settings" and jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

25.  If `line` ends with a ":" (U+003A) character, then set `mode` to "unknown" and jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

26.  This is either a data line or it is syntactically incorrect.

27.  Let `position` be a pointer into `line`, initially pointing at the start of the string.

28.  Let `tokens` be a list of strings, initially empty.

29.  While `position` doesn't point past the end of `line`:

    1.  Let `current token` be an empty string.

    2.  While `position` doesn't point past the end of `line` and the character at `position` is neither a U+0020 SPACE nor a "tab" (U+0009) character, add the character at `position` to `current token` and advance `position` to the next character in `input`.

    3.  Add `current token` to the `tokens` list.

    4.  While `position` doesn't point past the end of `line` and the character at `position` is either a U+0020 SPACE or a "tab" (U+0009) character, advance `position` to the next character in `input`.

30.  Process `tokens` as follows:

    If `mode` is "explicit"

    [Resolve](#278.html_resolve-a-url) the first item in `tokens`, relative to `base URL`, with the URL character encoding set to UTF-8; ignore the rest.

    If this fails, then jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

    If the resulting [parsed URL](#278.html_parsed-url) has a different [scheme](#278.html_concept-url-scheme) component than `base URL` (the manifest's URL), then jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

    Let `new URL` be the result of applying the [URL serializer](#278.html_concept-url-serializer) algorithm to the resulting [parsed URL](#278.html_parsed-url), with the *exclude fragment flag* set.

    Add `new URL` to the `explicit URLs`.

    If `mode` is "fallback"

    Let `part one` be the first token in `tokens`, and let `part two` be the second token in `tokens`.

    [Resolve](#278.html_resolve-a-url) `part one` and `part two`, relative to `base URL`, with the URL character encoding set to UTF-8.

    If either fails, then jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

    If the [absolute URL](#278.html_absolute-url) corresponding to either `part one` or `part two` does not have the [same origin](#278.html_same-origin) as the manifest's URL, then jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

    Let `part one` be the result of applying the [URL serializer](#278.html_concept-url-serializer) algorithm to the first resulting [parsed URL](#278.html_parsed-url), with the *exclude fragment flag* set.

    Let `part two` be the result of applying the [URL serializer](#278.html_concept-url-serializer) algorithm to the second resulting [parsed URL](#278.html_parsed-url), with the *exclude fragment flag* set.

    If `part one` is already in the `fallback URLs` mapping as a [fallback namespace](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns), then jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

    Otherwise, add `part one` to the `fallback URLs` mapping as a [fallback namespace](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns), mapped to `part two` as the [fallback entry](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback).

    If `mode` is "online whitelist"

    If the first item in `tokens` is a "*" (U+002A) character, then set `online whitelist wildcard flag` to *open* and jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

    Otherwise, [resolve](#278.html_resolve-a-url) the first item in `tokens`, relative to `base URL`, with the URL character encoding set to UTF-8; ignore the rest.

    If this fails, then jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

    If the resulting [parsed URL](#278.html_parsed-url) has a different [scheme](#278.html_concept-url-scheme) component than `base URL` (the manifest's URL), then jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

    Let `new URL` be the result of applying the [URL serializer](#278.html_concept-url-serializer) algorithm to the resulting [parsed URL](#278.html_parsed-url), with the *exclude fragment flag* set.

    Add `new URL` to the `online whitelist namespaces`.

    If `mode` is "settings"

    If `tokens` contains a single token, and that token is a [case-sensitive](#278.html_case-sensitive) match for the string "`prefer-online`", then set `cache mode flag` to *prefer-online* and jump back to the step labeled *start of line*.

    Otherwise, the line is an unsupported setting: do nothing; the line is ignored.

    If `mode` is "unknown"

    Do nothing. The line is ignored.

31.  Jump back to the step labeled *start of line*. (That step jumps to the next, and last, step when the end of the file is reached.)

32.  Return the `explicit URLs` list, the `fallback URLs` mapping, the `online whitelist namespaces`, the `online whitelist wildcard flag`, and the `cache mode flag`.

The resource that declares the manifest (with the [`manifest`](#278.html_attr-html-manifest) attribute) will always get taken from the cache, whether it is listed in the cache or not, even if it is listed in an [online whitelist namespace](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist).

If a resource is listed in the [explicit section](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-explicit) or as a [fallback entry](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback) in the [fallback section](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-fallback), the resource will always be taken from the cache, regardless of any other matching entries in the [fallback namespaces](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) or [online whitelist namespaces](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist).

When a [fallback namespace](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) and an [online whitelist namespace](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist) overlap, the [online whitelist namespace](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist) has priority.

The [online whitelist wildcard flag](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist-wildcard) is applied last, only for URLs that match neither the [online whitelist namespace](#278.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist) nor the [fallback namespace](#278.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) and that are not listed in the [explicit section](#278.html_concept-appcache-manifest-explicit).

#### 5.7.4 Downloading or updating an application cache

When the user agent is required (by other parts of this specification) to start the <dfn id="279.html_application-cache-download-process">application cache download process</dfn> for an [absolute URL](#279.html_absolute-url) purported to identify a [manifest](#279.html_concept-appcache-manifest), or for an [application cache group](#279.html_application-cache-group), potentially given a particular [cache host](#279.html_cache-host), and potentially given a [master](#279.html_concept-appcache-master) resource, the user agent must run the steps below. These steps are always run asynchronously, in parallel with the [event loop](#279.html_event-loop) [tasks](#279.html_concept-task).

Some of these steps have requirements that only apply if the user agent <dfn id="279.html_shows-caching-progress">shows caching progress</dfn>. Support for this is optional. Caching progress UI could consist of a progress bar or message panel in the user agent's interface, or an overlay, or something else. Certain events fired during the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process) allow the script to override the display of such an interface. (Such events are delayed until after the `load` event has fired.) The goal of this is to allow Web applications to provide more seamless update mechanisms, hiding from the user the mechanics of the application cache mechanism. User agents may display user interfaces independent of this, but are encouraged to not show prominent update progress notifications for applications that cancel the relevant events.

The [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process) steps are as follows:

1.  Optionally, wait until the permission to start the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process) has been obtained from the user and until the user agent is confident that the network is available. This could include doing nothing until the user explicitly opts-in to caching the site, or could involve prompting the user for permission. The algorithm might never get past this point. (This step is particularly intended to be used by user agents running on severely space-constrained devices or in highly privacy-sensitive environments).

2.  Atomically, so as to avoid race conditions, perform the following substeps:

    1.  Pick the appropriate substeps:

        If these steps were invoked with an [absolute URL](#279.html_absolute-url) purported to identify a [manifest](#279.html_concept-appcache-manifest)

        Let `manifest URL` be that [absolute URL](#279.html_absolute-url).

        If there is no [application cache group](#279.html_application-cache-group) identified by `manifest URL`, then create a new [application cache group](#279.html_application-cache-group) identified by `manifest URL`. Initially, it has no [application caches](#279.html_application-cache). One will be created later in this algorithm.

        If these steps were invoked with an [application cache group](#279.html_application-cache-group)

        Let `manifest URL` be the [absolute URL](#279.html_absolute-url) of the [manifest](#279.html_concept-appcache-manifest) used to identify the [application cache group](#279.html_application-cache-group) to be updated.

        If that [application cache group](#279.html_application-cache-group) is [obsolete](#279.html_concept-appcache-obsolete), then abort this instance of the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process). This can happen if another instance of this algorithm found the manifest to be 404 or 410 while this algorithm was waiting in the first step above.

    2.  Let `cache group` be the [application cache group](#279.html_application-cache-group) identified by `manifest URL`.

    3.  If these steps were invoked with a [master](#279.html_concept-appcache-master) resource, then add the resource, along with the resource's [`Document`](#279.html_document), to `cache group`'s [list of pending master entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-pending-masters).

    4.
