If these steps were invoked with a [cache host](#279.html_cache-host), and the [status](#279.html_concept-appcache-status) of `cache group` is *checking* or *downloading*, then [queue a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`checking`](#279.html_event-appcache-checking) that is cancelable at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of that [cache host](#279.html_cache-host). The default action of this event must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that the user agent is checking to see if it can download the application.

    5.  If these steps were invoked with a [cache host](#279.html_cache-host), and the [status](#279.html_concept-appcache-status) of `cache group` is *downloading*, then also [queue a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`downloading`](#279.html_event-appcache-downloading) that is cancelable at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of that [cache host](#279.html_cache-host). The default action of this event must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user the application is being downloaded.

    6.  If the [status](#279.html_concept-appcache-status) of the `cache group` is either *checking* or *downloading*, then abort this instance of the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process), as an update is already in progress.

    7.  Set the [status](#279.html_concept-appcache-status) of `cache group` to *checking*.

    8.  For each [cache host](#279.html_cache-host) associated with an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`, [queue a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) that is cancelable named [`checking`](#279.html_event-appcache-checking) at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [cache host](#279.html_cache-host). The default action of these events must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that the user agent is checking for the availability of updates.

    The remainder of the steps run asynchronously.

    If `cache group` already has an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in it, then this is an <dfn id="279.html_concept-appcache-upgrade" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-upgrade">upgrade attempt</dfn>. Otherwise, this is a <dfn id="279.html_concept-appcache-cache" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-cache">cache attempt</dfn>.

3.  If this is a [cache attempt](#279.html_concept-appcache-cache), then this algorithm was invoked with a [cache host](#279.html_cache-host); [queue a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`checking`](#279.html_event-appcache-checking) that is cancelable at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of that [cache host](#279.html_cache-host). The default action of this event must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that the user agent is checking for the availability of updates.

4.  *Fetching the manifest*: [Fetch](#279.html_fetch) the resource from `manifest URL` with the *synchronous flag* set, and let `manifest` be that resource. HTTP caching semantics should be honored for this request.

    Parse `manifest` according to the [rules for parsing manifests](#279.html_parse-a-manifest), obtaining a list of [explicit entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-explicit), [fallback entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-fallback) and the [fallback namespaces](#279.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) that map to them, entries for the [online whitelist](#279.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist), and values for the [online whitelist wildcard flag](#279.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist-wildcard) and the [cache mode flag](#279.html_concept-appcache-mode).

    The [MIME type](#279.html_mime-type) of the resource is ignored — it is assumed to be [`text/cache-manifest`](#279.html_text/cache-manifest). In the future, if new manifest formats are supported, the different types will probably be distinguished on the basis of the file signatures (for the current format, that is the "`CACHE MANIFEST`" string at the top of the file).

5.  If *fetching the manifest* fails due to a 404 or 410 response [or equivalent](#279.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes), then run these substeps:

    1.  Mark `cache group` as [obsolete](#279.html_concept-appcache-obsolete). This `cache group` no longer exists for any purpose other than the processing of [`Document`](#279.html_document) objects already associated with an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in the `cache group`.

    2.  Let `task list` be an empty list of [tasks](#279.html_concept-task).

    3.  For each [cache host](#279.html_cache-host) associated with an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`, create a [task](#279.html_concept-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) named [`obsolete`](#279.html_event-appcache-obsolete) that is cancelable at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [cache host](#279.html_cache-host), and append it to `task list`. The default action of these events must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that the application is no longer available for offline use.

    4.  For each entry in `cache group`'s [list of pending master entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-pending-masters), create a [task](#279.html_concept-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) that is cancelable named [`error`](#279.html_event-appcache-error) (not [`obsolete`](#279.html_event-appcache-obsolete)!) at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [`Document`](#279.html_document) for this entry, if there still is one, and append it to `task list`. The default action of this event must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that the user agent failed to save the application for offline use.

    5.  If `cache group` has an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) whose [completeness flag](#279.html_concept-appcache-completeness) is *incomplete*, then discard that [application cache](#279.html_application-cache).

    6.  If appropriate, remove any user interface indicating that an update for this cache is in progress.

    7.  Let the [status](#279.html_concept-appcache-status) of `cache group` be *idle*.

    8.  For each [task](#279.html_concept-task) in `task list`, [queue that task as a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task).

    9.  Abort the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process).

6.  Otherwise, if *fetching the manifest* fails in some other way (e.g. the server returns another 4xx or 5xx response [or equivalent](#279.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes), or there is a DNS error, or the connection times out, or the user cancels the download, or the parser for manifests fails when checking the magic signature), or if the server returned a redirect, then run the [cache failure steps](#279.html_cache-failure-steps). [[HTTP]](#279.html_refsHTTP)

7.  If this is an [upgrade attempt](#279.html_concept-appcache-upgrade) and the newly downloaded `manifest` is byte-for-byte identical to the manifest found in the [newest](#279.html_concept-appcache-newer) [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`, or the server reported it as "304 Not Modified" [or equivalent](#279.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes), then run these substeps:

    1.  Let `cache` be the [newest](#279.html_concept-appcache-newer) [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`.

    2.  Let `task list` be an empty list of [tasks](#279.html_concept-task).

    3.  For each entry in `cache group`'s [list of pending master entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-pending-masters), wait for the resource for this entry to have either completely downloaded or failed.

        If the download failed (e.g. the server returns a 4xx or 5xx response [or equivalent](#279.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes), or there is a DNS error, the connection times out, or the user cancels the download), or if the resource is labeled with the "no-store" cache directive, then create a [task](#279.html_concept-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) that is cancelable named [`error`](#279.html_event-appcache-error) at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [`Document`](#279.html_document) for this entry, if there still is one, and append it to `task list`. The default action of this event must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that the user agent failed to save the application for offline use.

        Otherwise, associate the [`Document`](#279.html_document) for this entry with `cache`; store the resource for this entry in `cache`, if it isn't already there, and categorize its entry as a [master entry](#279.html_concept-appcache-master). If applying the [URL parser](#279.html_url-parser-0) algorithm to the resource's URL results in a [parsed URL](#279.html_parsed-url) that has a non-null [fragment](#279.html_concept-url-fragment) component, the URL used for the entry in `cache` must instead be the [absolute URL](#279.html_absolute-url) obtained from applying the [URL serializer](#279.html_concept-url-serializer) algorithm to the [parsed URL](#279.html_parsed-url) with the *exclude fragment flag* set (application caches never include fragment identifiers).

    4.  For each [cache host](#279.html_cache-host) associated with an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`, create a [task](#279.html_concept-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) that is cancelable named [`noupdate`](#279.html_event-appcache-noupdate) at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [cache host](#279.html_cache-host), and append it to `task list`. The default action of these events must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that the application is up to date.

    5.  Empty `cache group`'s [list of pending master entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-pending-masters).

    6.  If appropriate, remove any user interface indicating that an update for this cache is in progress.

    7.  Let the [status](#279.html_concept-appcache-status) of `cache group` be *idle*.

    8.  For each [task](#279.html_concept-task) in `task list`, [queue that task as a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task).

    9.  Abort the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process).

8.  Let `new cache` be a newly created [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`. Set its [completeness flag](#279.html_concept-appcache-completeness) to *incomplete*.

9.  For each entry in `cache group`'s [list of pending master entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-pending-masters), associate the [`Document`](#279.html_document) for this entry with `new cache`.

10.  Set the [status](#279.html_concept-appcache-status) of `cache group` to *downloading*.

11.  For each [cache host](#279.html_cache-host) associated with an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`, [queue a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) that is cancelable named [`downloading`](#279.html_event-appcache-downloading) at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [cache host](#279.html_cache-host). The default action of these events must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that a new version is being downloaded.

12.  Let `file list` be an empty list of URLs with flags.

13.  Add all the URLs in the list of [explicit entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-explicit) obtained by parsing `manifest` to `file list`, each flagged with "explicit entry".

14.  Add all the URLs in the list of [fallback entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-fallback) obtained by parsing `manifest` to `file list`, each flagged with "fallback entry".

15.  If this is an [upgrade attempt](#279.html_concept-appcache-upgrade), then add all the URLs of [master entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-master) in the [newest](#279.html_concept-appcache-newer) [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group` whose [completeness flag](#279.html_concept-appcache-completeness) is *complete* to `file list`, each flagged with "master entry".

16.  If any URL is in `file list` more than once, then merge the entries into one entry for that URL, that entry having all the flags that the original entries had.

17.  For each URL in `file list`, run the following steps. These steps may be run in parallel for two or more of the URLs at a time. If, while running these steps, the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) object's [`abort()`](#279.html_dom-appcache-abort) method [sends a signal](#279.html_send-a-signal) to this instance of the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process) algorithm, then run the [cache failure steps](#279.html_cache-failure-steps) instead.

    1.  If the resource URL being processed was flagged as neither an "explicit entry" nor or a "fallback entry", then the user agent may skip this URL.

        This is intended to allow user agents to expire resources not listed in the manifest from the cache. Generally, implementors are urged to use an approach that expires lesser-used resources first.

    2.  For each [cache host](#279.html_cache-host) associated with an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`, [queue a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task) to [fire](#279.html_concept-event-fire) a [trusted](#279.html_concept-events-trusted) event with the name [`progress`](#279.html_event-appcache-progress), which does not bubble, which is cancelable, and which uses the [`ProgressEvent`](#279.html_progressevent) interface, at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [cache host](#279.html_cache-host). The `lengthComputable` attribute must be set to true, the `total` attribute must be set to the number of files in `file list`, and the `loaded` attribute must be set to the number of files in `file list` that have been either downloaded or skipped so far. The default action of these events must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that a file is being downloaded in preparation for updating the application. [[PROGRESS-EVENTS]](#279.html_refsPROGRESS-EVENTS)

    3.  [Fetch](#279.html_fetch) the resource, from the [origin](#279.html_origin-0) of the URL `manifest URL`, with the *synchronous flag* set and the *manual redirect flag* set. If this is an [upgrade attempt](#279.html_concept-appcache-upgrade), then use the [newest](#279.html_concept-appcache-newer) [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group` as an HTTP cache, and honor HTTP caching semantics (such as expiration, ETags, and so forth) with respect to that cache. User agents may also have other caches in place that are also honored.

        If the resource in question is already being downloaded for other reasons then the existing download process can sometimes be used for the purposes of this step, as defined by the [fetching](#279.html_fetch) algorithm.

        An example of a resource that might already be being downloaded is a large image on a Web page that is being seen for the first time. The image would get downloaded to satisfy the [`img`](#279.html_the-img-element) element on the page, as well as being listed in the cache manifest. According to the rules for [fetching](#279.html_fetch) that image only need be downloaded once, and it can be used both for the cache and for the rendered Web page.

    4.  If the previous step fails (e.g. the server returns a 4xx or 5xx response [or equivalent](#279.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes), or there is a DNS error, or the connection times out, or the user cancels the download), or if the server returned a redirect, or if the resource is labeled with the "no-store" cache directive, then run the first appropriate step from the following list: [[HTTP]](#279.html_refsHTTP)

        If the URL being processed was flagged as an "explicit entry" or a "fallback entry"

        If these steps are being run in parallel for any other URLs in `file list`, then abort these steps for those other URLs. Run the [cache failure steps](#279.html_cache-failure-steps).

        Redirects are fatal because they are either indicative of a network problem (e.g. a captive portal); or would allow resources to be added to the cache under URLs that differ from any URL that the networking model will allow access to, leaving orphan entries; or would allow resources to be stored under URLs different than their true URLs. All of these situations are bad.

        If the error was a 404 or 410 HTTP response [or equivalent](#279.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes)
        If the resource was labeled with the "no-store" cache directive

        Skip this resource. It is dropped from the cache.

        Otherwise

        Copy the resource and its metadata from the [newest](#279.html_concept-appcache-newer) [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group` whose [completeness flag](#279.html_concept-appcache-completeness) is *complete*, and act as if that was the fetched resource, ignoring the resource obtained from the network.

        User agents may warn the user of these errors as an aid to development.

        These rules make errors for resources listed in the manifest fatal, while making it possible for other resources to be removed from caches when they are removed from the server, without errors, and making non-manifest resources survive server-side errors.

        Except for the "no-store" directive, HTTP caching rules that would cause a file to be expired or otherwise not cached are ignored for the purposes of the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process).

    5.  Otherwise, the fetching succeeded. Store the resource in the `new cache`.

        If the user agent is not able to store the resource (e.g. because of quota restrictions), the user agent may prompt the user or try to resolve the problem in some other manner (e.g. automatically pruning content in other caches). If the problem cannot be resolved, the user agent must run the [cache failure steps](#279.html_cache-failure-steps).

    6.  If the URL being processed was flagged as an "explicit entry" in `file list`, then categorize the entry as an [explicit entry](#279.html_concept-appcache-explicit).

    7.  If the URL being processed was flagged as a "fallback entry" in `file list`, then categorize the entry as a [fallback entry](#279.html_concept-appcache-fallback).

    8.  If the URL being processed was flagged as an "master entry" in `file list`, then categorize the entry as a [master entry](#279.html_concept-appcache-master).

    9.  As an optimization, if the resource is an HTML or XML file whose root element is an [`html`](#279.html_the-html-element) element with a [`manifest`](#279.html_attr-html-manifest) attribute whose value doesn't match the manifest URL of the application cache being processed, then the user agent should mark the entry as being [foreign](#279.html_concept-appcache-foreign).

18.  For each [cache host](#279.html_cache-host) associated with an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`, [queue a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task) to [fire](#279.html_concept-event-fire) a [trusted](#279.html_concept-events-trusted) event with the name [`progress`](#279.html_event-appcache-progress), which does not bubble, which is cancelable, and which uses the [`ProgressEvent`](#279.html_progressevent) interface, at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [cache host](#279.html_cache-host). The `lengthComputable` attribute must be set to true, the `total` and the `loaded` attributes must be set to the number of files in `file list`. The default action of these events must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that all the files have been downloaded. [[PROGRESS-EVENTS]](#279.html_refsPROGRESS-EVENTS)

19.  Store the list of [fallback namespaces](#279.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns), and the URLs of the [fallback entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-fallback) that they map to, in `new cache`.

20.  Store the URLs that form the new [online whitelist](#279.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist) in `new cache`.

21.  Store the value of the new [online whitelist wildcard flag](#279.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist-wildcard) in `new cache`.

22.  Store the value of the new [cache mode flag](#279.html_concept-appcache-mode) in `new cache`.

23.  For each entry in `cache group`'s [list of pending master entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-pending-masters), wait for the resource for this entry to have either completely downloaded or failed.

    If the download failed (e.g. the server returns a 4xx or 5xx response [or equivalent](#279.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes), or there is a DNS error, the connection times out, or the user cancels the download), or if the resource is labeled with the "no-store" cache directive, then run these substeps:

    1.  Unassociate the [`Document`](#279.html_document) for this entry from `new cache`.

    2.  [Queue a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) that is cancelable named [`error`](#279.html_event-appcache-error) at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [`Document`](#279.html_document) for this entry, if there still is one. The default action of this event must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that the user agent failed to save the application for offline use.

    3.  If this is a [cache attempt](#279.html_concept-appcache-cache) and this entry is the last entry in `cache group`'s [list of pending master entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-pending-masters), then run these further substeps:

        1.  Discard `cache group` and its only [application cache](#279.html_application-cache), `new cache`.

        2.  If appropriate, remove any user interface indicating that an update for this cache is in progress.

        3.  Abort the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process).

    4.  Otherwise, remove this entry from `cache group`'s [list of pending master entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-pending-masters).

    Otherwise, store the resource for this entry in `new cache`, if it isn't already there, and categorize its entry as a [master entry](#279.html_concept-appcache-master).

24.  [Fetch](#279.html_fetch) the resource from `manifest URL` again, with the *synchronous flag* set, and let `second manifest` be that resource. HTTP caching semantics should again be honored for this request.

    Since caching can be honored, authors are encouraged to avoid setting the cache headers on the manifest in such a way that the user agent would simply not contact the network for this second request; otherwise, the user agent would not notice if the cache had changed during the cache update process.

25.  If the previous step failed for any reason, or if the fetching attempt involved a redirect, or if `second manifest` and `manifest` are not byte-for-byte identical, then schedule a rerun of the entire algorithm with the same parameters after a short delay, and run the [cache failure steps](#279.html_cache-failure-steps).

26.  Otherwise, store `manifest` in `new cache`, if it's not there already, and categorize its entry as [the manifest](#279.html_concept-appcache-manifest).

27.  Set the [completeness flag](#279.html_concept-appcache-completeness) of `new cache` to *complete*.

28.  Let `task list` be an empty list of [tasks](#279.html_concept-task).

29.  If this is a [cache attempt](#279.html_concept-appcache-cache), then for each [cache host](#279.html_cache-host) associated with an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`, create a [task](#279.html_concept-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) that is cancelable named [`cached`](#279.html_event-appcache-cached) at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [cache host](#279.html_cache-host), and append it to `task list`. The default action of these events must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that the application has been cached and that they can now use it offline.

    Otherwise, it is an [upgrade attempt](#279.html_concept-appcache-upgrade). For each [cache host](#279.html_cache-host) associated with an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`, create a [task](#279.html_concept-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) that is cancelable named [`updateready`](#279.html_event-appcache-updateready) at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [cache host](#279.html_cache-host), and append it to `task list`. The default action of these events must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that a new version is available and that they can activate it by reloading the page.

30.  If appropriate, remove any user interface indicating that an update for this cache is in progress.

31.  Set the [update status](#279.html_concept-appcache-status) of `cache group` to *idle*.

32.  For each [task](#279.html_concept-task) in `task list`, [queue that task as a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task).

The <dfn id="279.html_cache-failure-steps">cache failure steps</dfn> are as follows:

1.  Let `task list` be an empty list of [tasks](#279.html_concept-task).

2.  For each entry in `cache group`'s [list of pending master entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-pending-masters), run the following further substeps. These steps may be run in parallel for two or more entries at a time.

    1.  Wait for the resource for this entry to have either completely downloaded or failed.

    2.  Unassociate the [`Document`](#279.html_document) for this entry from its [application cache](#279.html_application-cache), if it has one.

    3.  Create a [task](#279.html_concept-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) that is cancelable named [`error`](#279.html_event-appcache-error) at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [`Document`](#279.html_document) for this entry, if there still is one, and append it to `task list`. The default action of these events must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that the user agent failed to save the application for offline use.

3.  For each [cache host](#279.html_cache-host) still associated with an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) in `cache group`, create a [task](#279.html_concept-task) to [fire a simple event](#279.html_fire-a-simple-event) that is cancelable named [`error`](#279.html_event-appcache-error) at the [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) singleton of the [cache host](#279.html_cache-host), and append it to `task list`. The default action of these events must be, if the user agent [shows caching progress](#279.html_shows-caching-progress), the display of some sort of user interface indicating to the user that the user agent failed to save the application for offline use.

4.  Empty `cache group`'s [list of pending master entries](#279.html_concept-appcache-pending-masters).

5.  If `cache group` has an [application cache](#279.html_application-cache) whose [completeness flag](#279.html_concept-appcache-completeness) is *incomplete*, then discard that [application cache](#279.html_application-cache).

6.  If appropriate, remove any user interface indicating that an update for this cache is in progress.

7.  Let the [status](#279.html_concept-appcache-status) of `cache group` be *idle*.

8.  If this was a [cache attempt](#279.html_concept-appcache-cache), discard `cache group` altogether.

9.  For each [task](#279.html_concept-task) in `task list`, [queue that task as a post-load task](#279.html_queue-a-post-load-task).

10.  Abort the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process).

Attempts to [fetch](#279.html_fetch) resources as part of the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process) may be done with cache-defeating semantics, to avoid problems with stale or inconsistent intermediary caches.

* * *

User agents may invoke the [application cache download process](#279.html_application-cache-download-process), in the background, for any [application cache group](#279.html_application-cache-group), at any time (with no [cache host](#279.html_cache-host)). This allows user agents to keep caches primed and to update caches even before the user visits a site.

* * *

Each [`Document`](#279.html_document) has a list of <dfn id="279.html_pending-application-cache-download-process-tasks">pending application cache download process tasks</dfn> that is used to delay events fired by the algorithm above until the document's `load` event has fired. When the [`Document`](#279.html_document) is created, the list must be empty.

When the steps above say to <dfn id="279.html_queue-a-post-load-task">queue a post-load task</dfn> `task`, where `task` is a [task](#279.html_concept-task) that dispatches an event on a target [`ApplicationCache`](#279.html_applicationcache) object `target`, the user agent must run the appropriate steps from the following list:

If `target`'s [`Document`](#279.html_document) is [ready for post-load tasks](#279.html_ready-for-post-load-tasks)

[Queue](#279.html_queue-a-task) the task `task`.

Otherwise

Add `task` to `target`'s [`Document`](#279.html_document)'s list of [pending application cache download process tasks](#279.html_pending-application-cache-download-process-tasks).

The [task source](#279.html_task-source) for these [tasks](#279.html_concept-task) is the [networking task source](#279.html_networking-task-source).

#### 5.7.5 The application cache selection algorithm

When the <dfn id="280.html_concept-appcache-init" data-anolis-xref="concept-appcache-init">application cache selection algorithm</dfn> algorithm is invoked with a [`Document`](#280.html_document) `document` and optionally a manifest URL `manifest URL`, the user agent must run the first applicable set of steps from the following list:

If there is a `manifest URL`, and `document` was loaded from an [application cache](#280.html_application-cache), and the URL of the [manifest](#280.html_concept-appcache-manifest) of that cache's [application cache group](#280.html_application-cache-group) is *not* the same as `manifest URL`

Mark the entry for the resource from which `document` was taken in the [application cache](#280.html_application-cache) from which it was loaded as [foreign](#280.html_concept-appcache-foreign).

Restart the current navigation from the top of the [navigation algorithm](#280.html_navigate), undoing any changes that were made as part of the initial load (changes can be avoided by ensuring that the step to [update the session history with the new page](#280.html_update-the-session-history-with-the-new-page) is only ever completed *after* this [application cache selection algorithm](#280.html_concept-appcache-init) is run, though this is not required).

The navigation will not result in the same resource being loaded, because "foreign" entries are never picked during navigation.

User agents may notify the user of the inconsistency between the cache manifest and the document's own metadata, to aid in application development.

If `document` was loaded from an [application cache](#280.html_application-cache), and that [application cache](#280.html_application-cache) still exists (it is not now [obsolete](#280.html_concept-appcache-obsolete))

Associate `document` with the [application cache](#280.html_application-cache) from which it was loaded. Invoke, in the background, the [application cache download process](#280.html_application-cache-download-process) for that [application cache](#280.html_application-cache)'s [application cache group](#280.html_application-cache-group), with `document` as the [cache host](#280.html_cache-host).

If `document` was loaded using HTTP GET [or equivalent](#280.html_concept-http-equivalent-get), and, there is a `manifest URL`, and `manifest URL` has the [same origin](#280.html_same-origin) as `document`

Invoke, in the background, the [application cache download process](#280.html_application-cache-download-process) for `manifest URL`, with `document` as the [cache host](#280.html_cache-host) and with the resource from which `document` was parsed as the [master](#280.html_concept-appcache-master) resource.

If there are [relevant application caches](#280.html_relevant-application-cache) that are identified by a URL with the [same origin](#280.html_same-origin) as the URL of `document`, and that have this URL as one of their entries, excluding entries marked as [foreign](#280.html_concept-appcache-foreign), then the user agent should use the [most appropriate application cache](#280.html_concept-appcache-selection) of those that match as an HTTP cache for any subresource loads. User agents may also have other caches in place that are also honored.

Otherwise

The [`Document`](#280.html_document) is not associated with any [application cache](#280.html_application-cache).

If there was a `manifest URL`, the user agent may report to the user that it was ignored, to aid in application development.

#### 5.7.6 Changes to the networking model

When a [cache host](#281.html_cache-host) is associated with an [application cache](#281.html_application-cache) whose [completeness flag](#281.html_concept-appcache-completeness) is *complete*, any and all loads for resources related to that [cache host](#281.html_cache-host) other than those for [child browsing contexts](#281.html_child-browsing-context) must go through the following steps instead of immediately invoking the mechanisms appropriate to that resource's scheme:

1.  If the resource is not to be fetched using the HTTP GET mechanism [or equivalent](#281.html_concept-http-equivalent-get), or if applying the [URL parser](#281.html_url-parser-0) algorithm to both its URL and the [application cache](#281.html_application-cache)'s [manifest](#281.html_concept-appcache-manifest)'s URL results in two [parsed URLs](#281.html_parsed-url) with different [scheme](#281.html_concept-url-scheme) components, then [fetch](#281.html_fetch) the resource normally and abort these steps.

2.  If the resource's URL is [a master entry](#281.html_concept-appcache-master), [the manifest](#281.html_concept-appcache-manifest), [an explicit entry](#281.html_concept-appcache-explicit), or [a fallback entry](#281.html_concept-appcache-fallback) in the [application cache](#281.html_application-cache), then get the resource from the cache (instead of fetching it), and abort these steps.

3.  If there is an entry in the [application cache](#281.html_application-cache)'s [online whitelist](#281.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist) that has the [same origin](#281.html_same-origin) as the resource's URL and that is a [prefix match](#281.html_prefix-match) for the resource's URL, then [fetch](#281.html_fetch) the resource normally and abort these steps.

4.  If the resource's URL has the [same origin](#281.html_same-origin) as the manifest's URL, and there is a [fallback namespace](#281.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) `f` in the [application cache](#281.html_application-cache) that is a [prefix match](#281.html_prefix-match) for the resource's URL, then:

    [Fetch](#281.html_fetch) the resource normally. If this results in a redirect to a resource with another [origin](#281.html_origin-0) (indicative of a captive portal), or a 4xx or 5xx status code [or equivalent](#281.html_concept-http-equivalent-codes), or if there were network errors (but not if the user canceled the download), then instead get, from the cache, the resource of the [fallback entry](#281.html_concept-appcache-fallback) corresponding to the [fallback namespace](#281.html_concept-appcache-fallback-ns) `f`. Abort these steps.

5.  If the [application cache](#281.html_application-cache)'s [online whitelist wildcard flag](#281.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist-wildcard) is *open*, then [fetch](#281.html_fetch) the resource normally and abort these steps.

6.  Fail the resource load as if there had been a generic network error.

The above algorithm ensures that so long as the [online whitelist wildcard flag](#281.html_concept-appcache-onlinewhitelist-wildcard) is *blocking*, resources that are not present in the [manifest](#281.html_concept-appcache-manifest) will always fail to load (at least, after the [application cache](#281.html_application-cache) has been primed the first time), making the testing of offline applications simpler.

#### 5.7.7 Expiring application caches

As a general rule, user agents should not expire application caches, except on request from the user, or after having been left unused for an extended period of time.

Application caches and cookies have similar implications with respect to privacy (e.g. if the site can identify the user when providing the cache, it can store data in the cache that can be used for cookie resurrection). Implementors are therefore encouraged to expose application caches in a manner related to HTTP cookies, allowing caches to be expunged together with cookies and other origin-specific data.

For example, a user agent could have a "delete site-specific data" feature that clears all cookies, application caches, local storage, databases, etc, from an origin all at once.

#### 5.7.8 Disk space

User agents should consider applying constraints on disk usage of [application caches](#283.html_application-cache), and care should be taken to ensure that the restrictions cannot be easily worked around using subdomains.

User agents should allow users to see how much space each domain is using, and may offer the user the ability to delete specific [application caches](#283.html_application-cache).

For predictability, quotas should be based on the uncompressed size of data stored.

How quotas are presented to the user is not defined by this specification. User agents are encouraged to provide features such as allowing a user to indicate that certain sites are trusted to use more than the default quota, e.g. by asynchronously presenting a user interface while a cache is being updated, or by having an explicit whitelist in the user agent's configuration interface.

#### 5.7.9 Application cache API

```
interface ApplicationCache : EventTarget {

  // update status
  const unsigned short UNCACHED = 0;
  const unsigned short IDLE = 1;
  const unsigned short CHECKING = 2;
  const unsigned short DOWNLOADING = 3;
  const unsigned short UPDATEREADY = 4;
  const unsigned short OBSOLETE = 5;
  readonly attribute unsigned short status;

  // updates
  void update();
  void abort();
  void swapCache();

  // events
           attribute EventHandler onchecking;
           attribute EventHandler onerror;
           attribute EventHandler onnoupdate;
           attribute EventHandler ondownloading;
           attribute EventHandler onprogress;
           attribute EventHandler onupdateready;
           attribute EventHandler oncached;
           attribute EventHandler onobsolete;
};
```

`cache` = `window` . [`applicationCache`](#284.html_dom-applicationcache)

(In a window.) Returns the [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object that applies to the [active document](#284.html_active-document) of that [`Window`](#284.html_window).

`cache` = `self` . [`applicationCache`](#284.html_dom-applicationcache)

(In a shared worker.) Returns the [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object that applies to the current shared worker.

`cache` . [`status`](#284.html_dom-appcache-status)

Returns the current status of the application cache, as given by the constants defined below.

`cache` . [`update`](#284.html_dom-appcache-update)()

Invokes the [application cache download process](#284.html_application-cache-download-process).

Throws an [`InvalidStateError`](#284.html_invalidstateerror) exception if there is no application cache to update.

Calling this method is not usually necessary, as user agents will generally take care of updating [application caches](#284.html_application-cache) automatically.

The method can be useful in situations such as long-lived applications. For example, a Web mail application might stay open in a browser tab for weeks at a time. Such an application could want to test for updates each day.

`cache` . [`abort`](#284.html_dom-appcache-abort)()

Cancels the [application cache download process](#284.html_application-cache-download-process).

This method is intended to be used by Web application showing their own caching progress UI, in case the user wants to stop the update (e.g. because bandwidth is limited).

`cache` . [`swapCache`](#284.html_dom-appcache-swapcache)()

Switches to the most recent application cache, if there is a newer one. If there isn't, throws an [`InvalidStateError`](#284.html_invalidstateerror) exception.

This does not cause previously-loaded resources to be reloaded; for example, images do not suddenly get reloaded and style sheets and scripts do not get reparsed or reevaluated. The only change is that subsequent requests for cached resources will obtain the newer copies.

The [`updateready`](#284.html_event-appcache-updateready) event will fire before this method can be called. Once it fires, the Web application can, at its leisure, call this method to switch the underlying cache to the one with the more recent updates. To make proper use of this, applications have to be able to bring the new features into play; for example, reloading scripts to enable new features.

An easier alternative to [`swapCache()`](#284.html_dom-appcache-swapcache) is just to reload the entire page at a time suitable for the user, using [`location.reload()`](#284.html_dom-location-reload).

There is a one-to-one mapping from [cache hosts](#284.html_cache-host) to [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) objects. The <dfn id="284.html_dom-applicationcache" data-anolis-xref="dom-applicationCache">`applicationCache`</dfn> attribute on [`Window`](#284.html_window) objects must return the [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object associated with the [`Window`](#284.html_window) object's [active document](#284.html_active-document). The <dfn id="284.html_dom-sharedworkerglobalscope-applicationcache" data-anolis-xref="dom-SharedWorkerGlobalScope-applicationCache">`applicationCache`</dfn> attribute on `SharedWorkerGlobalScope` objects must return the [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object associated with the worker.

A [`Window`](#284.html_window) or `SharedWorkerGlobalScope` object has an associated [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object even if that [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) has no actual [application cache](#284.html_application-cache).

* * *

The <dfn id="284.html_dom-appcache-status" data-anolis-xref="dom-appcache-status">`status`</dfn> attribute, on getting, must return the current state of the [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) that the [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) is associated with, if any. This must be the appropriate value from the following list:

<dfn id="284.html_dom-appcache-uncached" data-anolis-xref="dom-appcache-UNCACHED">`UNCACHED`</dfn> (numeric value 0)

The [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) is not associated with an [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) at this time.

<dfn id="284.html_dom-appcache-idle" data-anolis-xref="dom-appcache-IDLE">`IDLE`</dfn> (numeric value 1)

The [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) is associated with an [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) whose [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group)'s [update status](#284.html_concept-appcache-status) is *idle*, and that [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) is the [newest](#284.html_concept-appcache-newer) cache in its [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group), and the [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group) is not marked as [obsolete](#284.html_concept-appcache-obsolete).

<dfn id="284.html_dom-appcache-checking" data-anolis-xref="dom-appcache-CHECKING">`CHECKING`</dfn> (numeric value 2)

The [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) is associated with an [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) whose [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group)'s [update status](#284.html_concept-appcache-status) is *checking*.

<dfn id="284.html_dom-appcache-downloading" data-anolis-xref="dom-appcache-DOWNLOADING">`DOWNLOADING`</dfn> (numeric value 3)

The [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) is associated with an [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) whose [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group)'s [update status](#284.html_concept-appcache-status) is *downloading*.

<dfn id="284.html_dom-appcache-updateready" data-anolis-xref="dom-appcache-UPDATEREADY">`UPDATEREADY`</dfn> (numeric value 4)

The [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) is associated with an [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) whose [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group)'s [update status](#284.html_concept-appcache-status) is *idle*, and whose [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group) is not marked as [obsolete](#284.html_concept-appcache-obsolete), but that [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) is *not* the [newest](#284.html_concept-appcache-newer) cache in its group.

<dfn id="284.html_dom-appcache-obsolete" data-anolis-xref="dom-appcache-OBSOLETE">`OBSOLETE`</dfn> (numeric value 5)

The [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) is associated with an [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) whose [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group) is marked as [obsolete](#284.html_concept-appcache-obsolete).

* * *

If the <dfn id="284.html_dom-appcache-update" data-anolis-xref="dom-appcache-update">`update()`</dfn> method is invoked, the user agent must invoke the [application cache download process](#284.html_application-cache-download-process), in the background, for the [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group) of the [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) with which the [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) is associated, but without giving that [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) to the algorithm. If there is no such [application cache](#284.html_application-cache), or if its [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group) is marked as [obsolete](#284.html_concept-appcache-obsolete), then the method must throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#284.html_invalidstateerror) exception instead.

If the <dfn id="284.html_dom-appcache-abort" data-anolis-xref="dom-appcache-abort">`abort()`</dfn> method is invoked, the user agent must <dfn id="284.html_send-a-signal">send a signal</dfn> to the current [application cache download process](#284.html_application-cache-download-process) for the [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group) of the [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) with which the [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) is associated, if any. If there is no such [application cache](#284.html_application-cache), or it does not have a current [application cache download process](#284.html_application-cache-download-process), then do nothing.

If the <dfn id="284.html_dom-appcache-swapcache" data-anolis-xref="dom-appcache-swapCache">`swapCache()`</dfn> method is invoked, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Check that [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) is associated with an [application cache](#284.html_application-cache). If it is not, then throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#284.html_invalidstateerror) exception and abort these steps.

2.  Let `cache` be the [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) with which the [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) is associated. (By definition, this is the same as the one that was found in the previous step.)

3.  If `cache`'s [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group) is marked as [obsolete](#284.html_concept-appcache-obsolete), then unassociate the [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) from `cache` and abort these steps. (Resources will now load from the network instead of the cache.)

4.  Check that there is an application cache in the same [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group) as `cache` whose [completeness flag](#284.html_concept-appcache-completeness) is *complete* and that is [newer](#284.html_concept-appcache-newer) than `cache`. If there is not, then throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#284.html_invalidstateerror) exception and abort these steps.

5.  Let `new cache` be the [newest](#284.html_concept-appcache-newer) [application cache](#284.html_application-cache) in the same [application cache group](#284.html_application-cache-group) as `cache` whose [completeness flag](#284.html_concept-appcache-completeness) is *complete*.

6.  Unassociate the [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) object's [cache host](#284.html_cache-host) from `cache` and instead associate it with `new cache`.

The following are the [event handlers](#284.html_event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#284.html_event-handler-event-type)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#284.html_event-handler-idl-attributes), by all objects implementing the [`ApplicationCache`](#284.html_applicationcache) interface:

| [Event handler](#284.html_event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#284.html_event-handler-event-type) |
| --- | --- |
| <dfn id="284.html_handler-appcache-onchecking" data-anolis-xref="handler-appcache-onchecking">`onchecking`</dfn> | [`checking`](#284.html_event-appcache-checking) |
| <dfn id="284.html_handler-appcache-onerror" data-anolis-xref="handler-appcache-onerror">`onerror`</dfn> | [`error`](#284.html_event-appcache-error) |
| <dfn id="284.html_handler-appcache-onnoupdate" data-anolis-xref="handler-appcache-onnoupdate">`onnoupdate`</dfn> | [`noupdate`](#284.html_event-appcache-noupdate) |
| <dfn id="284.html_handler-appcache-ondownloading" data-anolis-xref="handler-appcache-ondownloading">`ondownloading`</dfn> | [`downloading`](#284.html_event-appcache-downloading) |
| <dfn id="284.html_handler-appcache-onprogress" data-anolis-xref="handler-appcache-onprogress">`onprogress`</dfn> | [`progress`](#284.html_event-appcache-progress) |
| <dfn id="284.html_handler-appcache-onupdateready" data-anolis-xref="handler-appcache-onupdateready">`onupdateready`</dfn> | [`updateready`](#284.html_event-appcache-updateready) |
| <dfn id="284.html_handler-appcache-oncached" data-anolis-xref="handler-appcache-oncached">`oncached`</dfn> | [`cached`](#284.html_event-appcache-cached) |
| <dfn id="284.html_handler-appcache-onobsolete" data-anolis-xref="handler-appcache-onobsolete">`onobsolete`</dfn> | [`obsolete`](#284.html_event-appcache-obsolete) |

#### 5.7.10 Browser state

```
[NoInterfaceObject]
interface NavigatorOnLine {
  readonly attribute boolean onLine;
};
```

`window` . [`navigator`](#285.html_dom-navigator) . [`onLine`](#285.html_dom-navigator-online)

Returns false if the user agent is definitely offline (disconnected from the network). Returns true if the user agent might be online.

The events [`online`](#285.html_event-online) and [`offline`](#285.html_event-offline) are fired when the value of this attribute changes.

The <dfn id="285.html_dom-navigator-online" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-onLine">`navigator.onLine`</dfn> attribute must return false if the user agent will not contact the network when the user follows links or when a script requests a remote page (or knows that such an attempt would fail), and must return true otherwise.

When the value that would be returned by the [`navigator.onLine`](#285.html_dom-navigator-online) attribute of a [`Window`](#285.html_window) or `WorkerGlobalScope` changes from true to false, the user agent must [queue a task](#285.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#285.html_fire-a-simple-event) named <dfn id="285.html_event-offline" data-anolis-xref="event-offline">`offline`</dfn> at the [`Window`](#285.html_window) or `WorkerGlobalScope` object.

On the other hand, when the value that would be returned by the [`navigator.onLine`](#285.html_dom-navigator-online) attribute of a [`Window`](#285.html_window) or `WorkerGlobalScope` changes from false to true, the user agent must [queue a task](#285.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#285.html_fire-a-simple-event) named <dfn id="285.html_event-online" data-anolis-xref="event-online">`online`</dfn> at the [`Window`](#285.html_window) or `WorkerGlobalScope` object.

The [task source](#285.html_task-source) for these [tasks](#285.html_concept-task) is the [networking task source](#285.html_networking-task-source).

This attribute is inherently unreliable. A computer can be connected to a network without having Internet access.

In this example, an indicator is updated as the browser goes online and offline.

```
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html>
 <head>
  <title>Online status</title>
  <script>
   function updateIndicator() {
     document.getElementById('indicator').textContent = navigator.onLine ? 'online' : 'offline';
   }
  </script>
 </head>
 <body onload="updateIndicator()" ononline="updateIndicator()" onoffline="updateIndicator()">
  <p>The network is: <span id="indicator">(state unknown)</span>
 </body>
</html>
```

## 6 Web application APIs

### 6.1 Scripting

#### 6.1.1 Introduction

Various mechanisms can cause author-provided executable code to run in the context of a document. These mechanisms include, but are probably not limited to:

*   Processing of [`script`](#288.html_the-script-element) elements.
*   Navigating to [`javascript:` URLs](#288.html_javascript-protocol).
*   Event handlers, whether registered through the DOM using `addEventListener()`, by explicit [event handler content attributes](#288.html_event-handler-content-attributes), by [event handler IDL attributes](#288.html_event-handler-idl-attributes), or otherwise.
*   Processing of technologies like XBL or SVG that have their own scripting features.

#### 6.1.2 Enabling and disabling scripting

<dfn id="289.html_concept-bc-script" data-anolis-xref="concept-bc-script">Scripting is enabled</dfn> in a *[browsing context](#289.html_browsing-context)* when all of the following conditions are true:

*   The user agent supports scripting.
*   The user has not disabled scripting for this [browsing context](#289.html_browsing-context) at this time. (User agents may provide users with the option to disable scripting globally, or in a finer-grained manner, e.g. on a per-origin basis.) [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/92e02960a6d5f9c71d27c81fd16bd623.jpg)](#289.html_fingerprinting-vector)
*   The [browsing context](#289.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#289.html_active-document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#289.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) does not have its [sandboxed scripts browsing context flag](#289.html_sandboxed-scripts-browsing-context-flag) set.

<dfn id="289.html_concept-bc-noscript" data-anolis-xref="concept-bc-noscript">Scripting is disabled</dfn> in a [browsing context](#289.html_browsing-context) when any of the above conditions are false (i.e. when scripting is not [enabled](#289.html_concept-bc-script)).

* * *

<dfn id="289.html_concept-n-script" data-anolis-xref="concept-n-script">Scripting is enabled</dfn> for a *[node](#289.html_node)* if the [`Document`](#289.html_document) object of the node (the node itself, if it is itself a [`Document`](#289.html_document) object) has an associated [browsing context](#289.html_browsing-context), and [scripting is enabled](#289.html_concept-bc-script) in that [browsing context](#289.html_browsing-context).

<dfn id="289.html_concept-n-noscript" data-anolis-xref="concept-n-noscript">Scripting is disabled</dfn> for a node if there is no such [browsing context](#289.html_browsing-context), or if [scripting is disabled](#289.html_concept-bc-noscript) in that [browsing context](#289.html_browsing-context).

#### 6.1.3 Processing model

##### 6.1.3.1 Definitions

This specification describes three kinds of [JavaScript global environments](#290.html_javascript-global-environment): the <dfn id="290.html_document-environment">document environment</dfn>, the <dfn id="290.html_dedicated-worker-environment">dedicated worker environment</dfn>, and the <dfn id="290.html_shared-worker-environment">shared worker environment</dfn>. The [dedicated worker environment](#290.html_dedicated-worker-environment) and the [shared worker environment](#290.html_shared-worker-environment) are both types of <dfn id="290.html_worker-environment" data-anolis-xref="worker environment">worker environments</dfn>.

Except where otherwise specified, a [JavaScript global environment](#290.html_javascript-global-environment) is a [document environment](#290.html_document-environment).

* * *

A <dfn id="290.html_concept-script" data-anolis-xref="concept-script">script</dfn> has:

A <dfn id="290.html_code-entry-point">code entry-point</dfn>

A code entry-point represents a block of executable code that the script exposes to other scripts and to the user agent. Typically, the code corresponding to the code entry-point is executed immediately after the script is parsed, but for event handlers, it is called each time the handler is invoked.

In JavaScript [`script`](#290.html_the-script-element) blocks, this corresponds to the execution context of the global code.

Optionally, a <dfn id="290.html_muted-errors">muted errors</dfn> flag

A flag which, if set, means that error information will not be provided for errors in this script (used to mute errors for cross-origin scripts, since that can leak private information).

A <dfn id="290.html_settings-object">settings object</dfn>

A [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object), various settings that are shared with other scripts in the same context.

* * *

A <dfn id="290.html_script-settings-object">script settings object</dfn> specifies algorithms for obtaining the following:

A <dfn id="290.html_script-execution-environment">script execution environment</dfn> for each language supported by the user agent

The characteristics of the script execution environment depend on the language, and are not defined by this specification.

In JavaScript, the script execution environment consists of the interpreter, the stack of *execution contexts*, the *global code* and *function code* and the `Function` objects resulting, and so forth.

A <dfn id="290.html_global-object">global object</dfn>

An object that provides the APIs that can be called by the code in scripts that use this [settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object).

This is typically a [`Window`](#290.html_window) object or a `WorkerGlobalScope` object. When a [global object](#290.html_global-object) is an empty object, it can't do anything that interacts with the environment.

If the [global object](#290.html_global-object) is a [`Window`](#290.html_window) object, then, in JavaScript, the ThisBinding of the global execution context for this script must be the [`Window`](#290.html_window) object's [`WindowProxy`](#290.html_windowproxy) object, rather than the global object. [[ECMA262]](#290.html_refsECMA262)

This is a [willful violation](#290.html_willful-violation) of the JavaScript specification current at the time of writing (ECMAScript edition 5, as defined in section 10.4.1.1 Initial Global Execution Context, step 3). The JavaScript specification requires that the `this` keyword in the global scope return the global object, but this is not compatible with the security design prevalent in implementations as specified herein. [[ECMA262]](#290.html_refsECMA262)

A <dfn id="290.html_responsible-browsing-context">responsible browsing context</dfn>

A [browsing context](#290.html_browsing-context) that is assigned responsibility for actions taken by the scripts that use this [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object).

When a script creates and [navigates](#290.html_navigate) a new [top-level browsing context](#290.html_top-level-browsing-context), the [`opener`](#290.html_dom-opener) attribute of the new [browsing context](#290.html_browsing-context)'s [`Window`](#290.html_window) object will be set to the [responsible browsing context](#290.html_responsible-browsing-context)'s [`WindowProxy`](#290.html_windowproxy) object.

A <dfn id="290.html_responsible-document">responsible document</dfn>

A [`Document`](#290.html_document) that is assigned responsibility for actions taken by the scripts that use this [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object).

For example, the [address](#290.html_the-document's-address) of the [responsible document](#290.html_responsible-document) is used to set the [address](#290.html_the-document's-address) of any [`Document`](#290.html_document)s created using [`createDocument()`](#290.html_dom-domimplementation-createdocument).

A <dfn id="290.html_responsible-event-loop">responsible event loop</dfn>

An [event loop](#290.html_event-loop) that is used when it would not be immediately clear what event loop to use.

An <dfn id="290.html_api-referrer-source">API referrer source</dfn>

Either a [`Document`](#290.html_document) (specifically, the [responsible document](#290.html_responsible-document)), or a URL, which is used by some APIs to determine what value to use for the `Referer` (sic) header in calls to the [fetching](#290.html_fetch) algorithm.

An <dfn id="290.html_api-url-character-encoding">API URL character encoding</dfn>

A character encoding used to encode URLs by APIs called by scripts that use this [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object).

An <dfn id="290.html_api-base-url">API base URL</dfn>

An [absolute URL](#290.html_absolute-url) used by APIs called by scripts that use this [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) to resolve [relative URLs](#290.html_relative-url).

An [origin](#290.html_origin-0) and an [effective script origin](#290.html_effective-script-origin)

An instrument used in security checks.

The <dfn id="290.html_relevant-settings-object-for-a-global-object">relevant settings object for a global object</dfn> `o` is the [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) whose [global object](#290.html_global-object) is `o`. (There is always a 1:1 mapping of global objects to script settings objects.)

The <dfn id="290.html_relevant-settings-object-for-a-script">relevant settings object for a script</dfn> `s` is the [settings object](#290.html_settings-object) of `s`.

##### 6.1.3.2 Script settings for browsing contexts

Whenever a new [`Window`](#290.html_window) object is created, it must also create a [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) whose algorithms are defined as follows:

The [script execution environments](#290.html_script-execution-environment)

When the [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) is created, for each language supported by the user agent, create an appropriate execution environment as defined by the relevant specification.

When a [script execution environment](#290.html_script-execution-environment) is needed, return the appropriate one from those created when the [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) was created.

The [global object](#290.html_global-object)

Return the [`Window`](#290.html_window) object itself.

The [responsible browsing context](#290.html_responsible-browsing-context)

Return the [browsing context](#290.html_browsing-context) with which the [`Window`](#290.html_window) object is associated.

The [responsible document](#290.html_responsible-document)

Return the [`Document`](#290.html_document) with which the [`Window`](#290.html_window) is currently associated.

The [responsible event loop](#290.html_responsible-event-loop)

Return the [event loop](#290.html_event-loop) that is associated with the [unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts](#290.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts) to which the [`Window`](#290.html_window) object's [browsing context](#290.html_browsing-context) belongs.

The [API referrer source](#290.html_api-referrer-source)

Return the [`Document`](#290.html_document) with which the [`Window`](#290.html_window) is currently associated.

The [API URL character encoding](#290.html_api-url-character-encoding)

Return the current [character encoding](#290.html_document's-character-encoding) of the [`Document`](#290.html_document) with which the [`Window`](#290.html_window) is currently associated.

The [API base URL](#290.html_api-base-url)

Return the current [base URL](#290.html_document-base-url) of the [`Document`](#290.html_document) with which the [`Window`](#290.html_window) is currently associated.

The [origin](#290.html_origin-0)

Return the [origin](#290.html_origin-0) of the [`Document`](#290.html_document) with which the [`Window`](#290.html_window) is currently associated.

The [effective script origin](#290.html_effective-script-origin)

Return the [effective script origin](#290.html_effective-script-origin) of the [`Document`](#290.html_document) with which the [`Window`](#290.html_window) is currently associated.

##### 6.1.3.3 Calling scripts

Each [unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts](#290.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts) has a <dfn id="290.html_stack-of-script-settings-objects">stack of script settings objects</dfn>, which must be initially empty. When a new [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) is *pushed* onto this stack, the specified [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) is to be added to the stack; when the [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) on this stack that was most recently pushed onto it is to be *popped* from the stack, it must be removed. Entries on this stack can be labeled as <dfn id="290.html_candidate-entry-settings-object" data-anolis-xref="candidate entry settings object">candidate entry settings objects</dfn>.

When a user agent is to <dfn id="290.html_jump-to-a-code-entry-point">jump to a code entry-point</dfn> for a [script](#290.html_concept-script) `s`, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `context` be the [settings object](#290.html_settings-object) of `s`.

2.  [Prepare to run a callback](#290.html_prepare-to-run-a-callback) with `context` as the [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object). If this returns "do not run" then abort these steps.

3.  Make the appropriate [script execution environment](#290.html_script-execution-environment) specified by `context` execute the `s`'s [code entry-point](#290.html_code-entry-point).

4.  [Clean up after running a callback](#290.html_clean-up-after-running-a-callback).

The steps to <dfn id="290.html_prepare-to-run-a-callback">prepare to run a callback</dfn> with a [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) `o` are as follows. They return either "run" or "do not run".

1.  If the [global object](#290.html_global-object) specified by `o` is a [`Window`](#290.html_window) object whose [`Document`](#290.html_document) object is not [fully active](#290.html_fully-active), then return "do not run" and abort these steps.

2.  If [scripting is disabled](#290.html_concept-bc-noscript) for the [responsible browsing context](#290.html_responsible-browsing-context) specified by `o`, then return "do not run" and abort these steps.

3.  Push `o` onto the [stack of script settings objects](#290.html_stack-of-script-settings-objects), and label it as a [candidate entry settings object](#290.html_candidate-entry-settings-object).

4.  Return "run".

The steps to <dfn id="290.html_clean-up-after-running-a-callback">clean up after running a callback</dfn> are as follows:

1.  Pop the current [incumbent settings object](#290.html_incumbent-settings-object) from the [stack of script settings objects](#290.html_stack-of-script-settings-objects).

2.  If the [stack of script settings objects](#290.html_stack-of-script-settings-objects) is now empty, [run the global script clean-up jobs](#290.html_run-the-global-script-clean-up-jobs). (These cannot run scripts.)

3.  If the [stack of script settings objects](#290.html_stack-of-script-settings-objects) is now empty, [perform a microtask checkpoint](#290.html_perform-a-microtask-checkpoint). (If this runs scripts, these algorithms will be invoked reentrantly.)

These algorithms are not invoked by one script directly calling another, but they can be invoked reentrantly in an indirect manner, e.g. if a script dispatches an event which has event listeners registered.

When a JavaScript *SourceElements* production is to be evaluated, the [settings object](#290.html_settings-object) of the [script](#290.html_concept-script) corresponding to that *SourceElements* must be pushed onto the [stack of script settings objects](#290.html_stack-of-script-settings-objects) before the evaluation begins, and popped when the evaluation ends (regardless of whether it's an abrupt completion or not).

The <dfn id="290.html_entry-settings-object">entry settings object</dfn> is the most-recently added [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) in the [stack of script settings objects](#290.html_stack-of-script-settings-objects) that is labeled as a [candidate entry settings object](#290.html_candidate-entry-settings-object). If the stack is empty, or has no entries labeled as such, then there is no [entry settings object](#290.html_entry-settings-object). It is used to obtain, amongst other things, the [API base URL](#290.html_api-base-url) to [resolve](#290.html_resolve-a-url) relative URLs used in scripts running in that [unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts](#290.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts).

The <dfn id="290.html_incumbent-settings-object">incumbent settings object</dfn> is the [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) in the [stack of script settings objects](#290.html_stack-of-script-settings-objects) that was most-recently added (i.e. the last one on the stack). If the stack is empty, then there is no [incumbent settings object](#290.html_incumbent-settings-object). It is used in some security checks.

The WebIDL specification also uses these algorithms. [[WEBIDL]](#290.html_refsWEBIDL)

* * *

Each [unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts](#290.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts) has a <dfn id="290.html_performing-a-microtask-checkpoint">performing a microtask checkpoint</dfn> flag, which must initially be false. It is used to prevent reentrant invocation of the algorithm to [invoke `MutationObserver` objects](#290.html_concept-mo-invoke). For the purposes of [`MutationObserver`](#290.html_mutationobserver) objects, each [unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts](#290.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts) is a distinct [`scripting environment`](#290.html_mutationobserver-scripting-environment).

Each [unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts](#290.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts) has a <dfn id="290.html_global-script-clean-up-jobs-list">global script clean-up jobs list</dfn>, which must initially be empty. A global script clean-up job cannot run scripts, and cannot be sensitive to the order in which other clean-up jobs are executed. The File API uses this to release `blob:` URLs. [[FILEAPI]](#290.html_refsFILEAPI)

When the user agent is to <dfn id="290.html_run-the-global-script-clean-up-jobs">run the global script clean-up jobs</dfn>, the user agent must perform each of the jobs in the [global script clean-up jobs list](#290.html_global-script-clean-up-jobs-list) and then empty the list.

##### 6.1.3.4 Creating scripts

When the specification says that a [script](#290.html_concept-script) is to be <dfn id="290.html_create-a-script" data-anolis-xref="create a script">created</dfn>, given some script source, a script source URL, its scripting language, a [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object), and optionally a `muted errors` flag, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `script` be a new [script](#290.html_concept-script) that this algorithm will subsequently initialize.

2.  If [scripting is disabled](#290.html_concept-bc-noscript) for [browsing context](#290.html_browsing-context) passed to this algorithm, then abort these steps, as if the script source described a program that did nothing but return void.

3.  Obtain the appropriate [script execution environment](#290.html_script-execution-environment) for the given scripting language from the [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) provided.

4.  Parse/compile/initialize the source of the script using the [script execution environment](#290.html_script-execution-environment), as appropriate for the scripting language, and thus obtain `script`'s [code entry-point](#290.html_code-entry-point).

5.  Let `script`'s [settings object](#290.html_settings-object) be the [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) provided.

6.  If the `muted errors` flag was set, then set `script`'s [muted errors](#290.html_muted-errors) flag.

7.  If all the steps above succeeded (in particular, if the script was compiled successfully), [Jump](#290.html_jump-to-a-code-entry-point) to `script`'s [code entry-point](#290.html_code-entry-point).

    Otherwise, [report the error](#290.html_report-the-error) for `script`, with the problematic position (line number and column number), using the [global object](#290.html_global-object) specified by the [script settings object](#290.html_script-settings-object) as the target. If the error is still *[not handled](#290.html_concept-error-nothandled)* after this, then the error may be reported to the user.

##### 6.1.3.5 Killing scripts

User agents may impose resource limitations on scripts, for example CPU quotas, memory limits, total execution time limits, or bandwidth limitations. When a script exceeds a limit, the user agent may either throw a [`QuotaExceededError`](#290.html_quotaexceedederror) exception, abort the script without an exception, prompt the user, or throttle script execution.

For example, the following script never terminates. A user agent could, after waiting for a few seconds, prompt the user to either terminate the script or let it continue.

```
<script>
 while (true) { /* loop */ }
</script>
```

User agents are encouraged to allow users to disable scripting whenever the user is prompted either by a script (e.g. using the [`window.alert()`](#290.html_dom-alert) API) or because of a script's actions (e.g. because it has exceeded a time limit).

If scripting is disabled while a script is executing, the script should be terminated immediately.

User agents may allow users to specifically disable scripts just for the purposes of closing a [browsing context](#290.html_browsing-context).

For example, the prompt mentioned in the example above could also offer the user with a mechanism to just close the page entirely, without running any `unload` event handlers.

##### 6.1.3.6 Runtime script errors

When the user agent is required to <dfn id="290.html_report-the-error" data-anolis-xref="report the error">report an error</dfn> for a particular [script](#290.html_concept-script) `script` with a particular position `line`:`col`, using a particular target `target`, it must run these steps, after which the error is either <dfn id="290.html_concept-error-handled" data-anolis-xref="concept-error-handled">*handled*</dfn> or <dfn id="290.html_concept-error-nothandled" data-anolis-xref="concept-error-nothandled">*not handled*</dfn>:

1.  If `target` is [in error reporting mode](#290.html_in-error-reporting-mode), then abort these steps; the error is *[not handled](#290.html_concept-error-nothandled)*.

2.  Let `target` be <dfn id="290.html_in-error-reporting-mode">in error reporting mode</dfn>.

3.  Let `message` be a user-agent-defined string describing the error in a helpful manner. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/3fec173607d2dca5bb5d344941ddfd12.jpg)](#290.html_fingerprinting-vector)

4.  Let `error object` be the object that represents the error: in the case of an uncaught exception, that would be the object that was thrown; in the case of a JavaScript error that would be an `Error` object. If there is no corresponding object, then the null value must be used instead.

5.  Let `location` be an [absolute URL](#290.html_absolute-url) that corresponds to the resource from which `script` was obtained.
