    The resource containing the script will typically be the file from which the [`Document`](#290.html_document) was parsed, e.g. for inline [`script`](#290.html_the-script-element) elements or [event handler content attributes](#290.html_event-handler-content-attributes); or the JavaScript file that the script was in, for external scripts. Even for dynamically-generated scripts, user agents are strongly encouraged to attempt to keep track of the original source of a script. For example, if an external script uses the [`document.write()`](#290.html_dom-document-write) API to insert an inline [`script`](#290.html_the-script-element) element during parsing, the URL of the resource containing the script would ideally be reported as being the external script, and the line number might ideally be reported as the line with the [`document.write()`](#290.html_dom-document-write) call or where the string passed to that call was first constructed. Naturally, implementing this can be somewhat non-trivial.

    User agents are similarly encouraged to keep careful track of the original line numbers, even in the face of [`document.write()`](#290.html_dom-document-write) calls mutating the document as it is parsed, or [event handler content attributes](#290.html_event-handler-content-attributes) spanning multiple lines.

6.  If `script` has [muted errors](#290.html_muted-errors), then set `message` to "`Script error.`", set `location` to the empty string, set `line` and `col` to 0, and set `error object` to null.

7.  Let `event` be a new [trusted](#290.html_concept-events-trusted) [`ErrorEvent`](#290.html_errorevent) object that does not bubble but is cancelable, and which has the event name `error`.

8.  Initialize `event`'s [`message`](#290.html_dom-errorevent-message) attribute to `message`.

9.  Initialize `event`'s [`filename`](#290.html_dom-errorevent-filename) attribute to `location`.

10.  Initialize `event`'s [`lineno`](#290.html_dom-errorevent-lineno) attribute to `line`.

11.  Initialize `event`'s [`colno`](#290.html_dom-errorevent-colno) attribute to `col`.

12.  Initialize `event`'s [`error`](#290.html_dom-errorevent-error) attribute to `error object`.

13.  [Dispatch](#290.html_concept-event-dispatch) `event` at `target`.

14.  Let `target` no longer be [in error reporting mode](#290.html_in-error-reporting-mode).

15.  If `event` was canceled, then the error is *[handled](#290.html_concept-error-handled)*. Otherwise, the error is *[not handled](#290.html_concept-error-nothandled)*.

###### 6.1.3.6.1 Runtime script errors in documents

Whenever an uncaught runtime script error occurs in one of the scripts associated with a [`Document`](#290.html_document), the user agent must [report the error](#290.html_report-the-error) for the relevant [script](#290.html_concept-script), with the problematic position (line number and column number) in the resource containing the script, using the [global object](#290.html_global-object) specified by the script's [settings object](#290.html_settings-object) as the target. If the error is still *[not handled](#290.html_concept-error-nothandled)* after this, then the error may be reported to the user.

###### 6.1.3.6.2 The [`ErrorEvent`](#290.html_errorevent) interface

```
[Constructor(DOMString type, optional ErrorEventInit eventInitDict)]
interface ErrorEvent : Event {
  readonly attribute DOMString message;
  readonly attribute DOMString filename;
  readonly attribute unsigned long lineno;
  readonly attribute unsigned long colno;
  readonly attribute any error;
};

dictionary ErrorEventInit : EventInit {
  DOMString message;
  DOMString filename;
  unsigned long lineno;
  unsigned long colno;
  any error;
};
```

The <dfn id="290.html_dom-errorevent-message" data-anolis-xref="dom-ErrorEvent-message">`message`</dfn> attribute must return the value it was initialized to. When the object is created, this attribute must be initialized to the empty string. It represents the error message.

The <dfn id="290.html_dom-errorevent-filename" data-anolis-xref="dom-ErrorEvent-filename">`filename`</dfn> attribute must return the value it was initialized to. When the object is created, this attribute must be initialized to the empty string. It represents the [absolute URL](#290.html_absolute-url) of the script in which the error originally occurred.

The <dfn id="290.html_dom-errorevent-lineno" data-anolis-xref="dom-ErrorEvent-lineno">`lineno`</dfn> attribute must return the value it was initialized to. When the object is created, this attribute must be initialized to zero. It represents the line number where the error occurred in the script.

The <dfn id="290.html_dom-errorevent-colno" data-anolis-xref="dom-ErrorEvent-colno">`colno`</dfn> attribute must return the value it was initialized to. When the object is created, this attribute must be initialized to zero. It represents the column number where the error occurred in the script.

The <dfn id="290.html_dom-errorevent-error" data-anolis-xref="dom-ErrorEvent-error">`error`</dfn> attribute must return the value it was initialized to. When the object is created, this attribute must be initialized to null. Where appropriate, it is set to the object representing the error (e.g. the exception object in the case of an uncaught DOM exception).

#### 6.1.4 Event loops

##### 6.1.4.1 Definitions

To coordinate events, user interaction, scripts, rendering, networking, and so forth, user agents must use <dfn id="291.html_event-loop" data-anolis-xref="event loop">event loops</dfn> as described in this section.

There must be at least one [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) per user agent, and at most one [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) per [unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts](#291.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts).

When there is more than one [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) for a [unit of related browsing contexts](#291.html_unit-of-related-browsing-contexts), complications arise when a [browsing context](#291.html_browsing-context) in that group is [navigated](#291.html_navigate) such that it switches from one [unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts](#291.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts) to another. This specification does not currently describe how to handle these complications.

An [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) always has at least one [browsing context](#291.html_browsing-context). If an [event loop](#291.html_event-loop)'s [browsing contexts](#291.html_browsing-context) all go away, then the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) goes away as well. A [browsing context](#291.html_browsing-context) always has an [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) coordinating its activities.

An [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) has one or more <dfn id="291.html_task-queue" data-anolis-xref="task queue">task queues</dfn>. A [task queue](#291.html_task-queue) is an ordered list of <dfn id="291.html_concept-task" data-anolis-xref="concept-task">tasks</dfn>, which are algorithms that are responsible for such work as:

Events

Asynchronously dispatching an [`Event`](#291.html_event) object at a particular [`EventTarget`](#291.html_eventtarget) object is often done by a dedicated task.

Not all events are dispatched using the [task queue](#291.html_task-queue), many are dispatched synchronously during other tasks.

Parsing

The [HTML parser](#291.html_html-parser) tokenizing one or more bytes, and then processing any resulting tokens, is typically a task.

Callbacks

Calling a callback asynchronously is often done by a dedicated task.

Using a resource

When an algorithm [fetches](#291.html_fetch) a resource, if the fetching occurs asynchronously then the processing of the resource once some or all of the resource is available is performed by a task.

Reacting to DOM manipulation

Some elements have tasks that trigger in response to DOM manipulation, e.g. when that element is [inserted into the document](#291.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document).

Each [task](#291.html_concept-task) is associated with a [`Document`](#291.html_document); if the task was queued in the context of an element, then it is the element's [`Document`](#291.html_document); if the task was queued in the context of a [browsing context](#291.html_browsing-context), then it is the [browsing context](#291.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#291.html_active-document) at the time the task was queued; if the task was queued by or for a [script](#291.html_concept-script) then the document is the [responsible document](#291.html_responsible-document) specified by the script's [settings object](#291.html_settings-object).

A [task](#291.html_concept-task) is intended for a specific [event loop](#291.html_event-loop): the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) that is handling [tasks](#291.html_concept-task) for the [task](#291.html_concept-task)'s associated [`Document`](#291.html_document).

When a user agent is to <dfn id="291.html_queue-a-task">queue a task</dfn>, it must add the given task to one of the [task queues](#291.html_task-queue) of the relevant [event loop](#291.html_event-loop).

Each [task](#291.html_concept-task) is defined as coming from a specific <dfn id="291.html_task-source">task source</dfn>. All the tasks from one particular [task source](#291.html_task-source) and destined to a particular [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) (e.g. the callbacks generated by timers of a [`Document`](#291.html_document), the events fired for mouse movements over that [`Document`](#291.html_document), the tasks queued for the parser of that [`Document`](#291.html_document)) must always be added to the same [task queue](#291.html_task-queue), but [tasks](#291.html_concept-task) from different [task sources](#291.html_task-source) may be placed in different [task queues](#291.html_task-queue).

For example, a user agent could have one [task queue](#291.html_task-queue) for mouse and key events (the [user interaction task source](#291.html_user-interaction-task-source)), and another for everything else. The user agent could then give keyboard and mouse events preference over other tasks three quarters of the time, keeping the interface responsive but not starving other task queues, and never processing events from any one [task source](#291.html_task-source) out of order.

* * *

A user agent may have one <dfn id="291.html_storage-mutex">storage mutex</dfn>. This mutex is used to control access to shared state like cookies. At any one point, the [storage mutex](#291.html_storage-mutex) is either free, or owned by a particular [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) or instance of the [fetching](#291.html_fetch) algorithm.

If a user agent does not implement a [storage mutex](#291.html_storage-mutex), it is exempt from implementing the requirements that require it to acquire or release it.

User agent implementors have to make a choice between two evils. On the one hand, not implementing the storage mutex means that there is a risk of data corruption: a site could, for instance, try to read a cookie, increment its value, then write it back out, using the new value of the cookie as a unique identifier for the session; if the site does this twice in two different browser windows at the same time, it might end up using the same "unique" identifier for both sessions, with potentially disastrous effects. On the other hand, implementing the storage mutex has potentially serious performance implications: whenever a site uses Web Storage or cookies, all other sites that try to use Web Storage or cookies are blocked until the first site finishes.

Whenever a [script](#291.html_concept-script) calls into a [plugin](#291.html_plugin), and whenever a [plugin](#291.html_plugin) calls into a [script](#291.html_concept-script), the user agent must release the [storage mutex](#291.html_storage-mutex).

##### 6.1.4.2 Processing model

An [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) must continually run through the following steps for as long as it exists:

1.  Run the oldest [task](#291.html_concept-task) on one of the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop)'s [task queues](#291.html_task-queue), if any, ignoring tasks whose associated [`Document`](#291.html_document)s are not [fully active](#291.html_fully-active). The user agent may pick any [task queue](#291.html_task-queue).

2.  If the [storage mutex](#291.html_storage-mutex) is now owned by the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop), release it so that it is once again free.

3.  If a task was run in the first step above, remove that task from its [task queue](#291.html_task-queue).

4.  If this [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) is not a worker's [event loop](#291.html_event-loop), run these substeps:

    1.  [Perform a microtask checkpoint](#291.html_perform-a-microtask-checkpoint).

    2.  [Provide a stable state](#291.html_provide-a-stable-state).

    3.  If necessary, update the rendering or user interface of any [`Document`](#291.html_document) or [browsing context](#291.html_browsing-context) to reflect the current state.

5.  Otherwise, if this [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) is running for a `WorkerGlobalScope`, but there are no events in the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop)'s [task queues](#291.html_task-queue) and the `WorkerGlobalScope` object's [closing](#291.html_dom-workerglobalscope-closing) flag is true, then destroy the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop), aborting these steps.

6.  Return to the first step of the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop).

* * *

When a user agent is to <dfn id="291.html_perform-a-microtask-checkpoint">perform a microtask checkpoint</dfn>, if the [performing a microtask checkpoint](#291.html_performing-a-microtask-checkpoint) flag is false, then the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let the [performing a microtask checkpoint](#291.html_performing-a-microtask-checkpoint) flag be true.

2.  <dfn id="291.html_perform-a-custom-elements-checkpoint">Perform a custom elements checkpoint</dfn>. [[CUSTOM]](#291.html_refsCUSTOM)

3.  Sort the tables with pending sorts.

4.  [Invoke `MutationObserver` objects](#291.html_concept-mo-invoke) for the [unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts](#291.html_unit-of-related-similar-origin-browsing-contexts) to which the [responsible browsing context](#291.html_responsible-browsing-context) specified by the script's [settings object](#291.html_settings-object) belongs, using the [task wrapper algorithm](#291.html_task-wrapper-algorithm) as the steps to invoke each callback.

    This will typically invoke scripted callbacks, which eventually calls the [clean up after running a callback](#291.html_clean-up-after-running-a-callback) steps, which call this [perform a microtask checkpoint](#291.html_perform-a-microtask-checkpoint) algorithm again, which is why we use the [performing a microtask checkpoint](#291.html_performing-a-microtask-checkpoint) flag to avoid reentrancy.

5.  Let the [performing a microtask checkpoint](#291.html_performing-a-microtask-checkpoint) flag be false.

* * *

When the user agent is to <dfn id="291.html_provide-a-stable-state">provide a stable state</dfn>, if any asynchronously-running algorithms are <dfn id="291.html_await-a-stable-state" data-anolis-xref="await a stable state">awaiting a stable state</dfn>, then the user agent must run their <dfn id="291.html_synchronous-section">synchronous section</dfn> and then resume running their asynchronous algorithm (if appropriate).

A [synchronous section](#291.html_synchronous-section) never mutates the DOM, runs any script, or has any side-effects detectable from another [synchronous section](#291.html_synchronous-section), and thus [synchronous sections](#291.html_synchronous-section) can be run in any order, and cannot [spin the event loop](#291.html_spin-the-event-loop).

Steps in [synchronous sections](#291.html_synchronous-section) are marked with ?.

* * *

The <dfn id="291.html_task-wrapper-algorithm">task wrapper algorithm</dfn>, which is implicitly invoked in the context of an [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) and is used to invoke a given `callback` in a specific way, is as follows:

1.  Invoke `callback` as specified.

The above will change in due course; see [bug 20821](https://www.w3.org/Bugs/Public/show_bug.cgi?id=20821).

* * *

When an algorithm says to <dfn id="291.html_spin-the-event-loop">spin the event loop</dfn> until a condition `goal` is met, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `task source` be the [task source](#291.html_task-source) of the currently running [task](#291.html_concept-task).

2.  Let `old stack of script settings objects` be a copy of the [stack of script settings objects](#291.html_stack-of-script-settings-objects).

3.  Empty the [stack of script settings objects](#291.html_stack-of-script-settings-objects).

4.  [Run the global script clean-up jobs](#291.html_run-the-global-script-clean-up-jobs).

5.  [Perform a microtask checkpoint](#291.html_perform-a-microtask-checkpoint).

6.  Stop the currently running [task](#291.html_concept-task), allowing the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) to resume, but continue these steps asynchronously.

    This causes the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) to move on to the second step of its processing model (defined above).

7.  Wait until the condition `goal` is met.

8.  [Queue a task](#291.html_queue-a-task) to continue running these steps, using the [task source](#291.html_task-source) `task source`. Wait until this task runs before continuing these steps.

9.  Replace the [stack of script settings objects](#291.html_stack-of-script-settings-objects) with the `old stack of script settings objects`.

10.  Return to the caller.

* * *

Some of the algorithms in this specification, for historical reasons, require the user agent to <dfn id="291.html_pause">pause</dfn> while running a [task](#291.html_concept-task) until a condition `goal` is met. This means running the following steps:

1.  If any asynchronously-running algorithms are [awaiting a stable state](#291.html_await-a-stable-state), then run their [synchronous section](#291.html_synchronous-section) and then resume running their asynchronous algorithm. (See the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) processing model definition above for details.)

2.  If necessary, update the rendering or user interface of any [`Document`](#291.html_document) or [browsing context](#291.html_browsing-context) to reflect the current state.

3.  Wait until the condition `goal` is met. While a user agent has a paused [task](#291.html_concept-task), the corresponding [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) must not run further [tasks](#291.html_concept-task), and any script in the currently running [task](#291.html_concept-task) must block. User agents should remain responsive to user input while paused, however, albeit in a reduced capacity since the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop) will not be doing anything.

* * *

When a user agent is to <dfn id="291.html_obtain-the-storage-mutex">obtain the storage mutex</dfn> as part of running a [task](#291.html_concept-task), it must run through the following steps:

1.  If the [storage mutex](#291.html_storage-mutex) is already owned by this [task](#291.html_concept-task)'s [event loop](#291.html_event-loop), then abort these steps.

2.  Otherwise, [pause](#291.html_pause) until the [storage mutex](#291.html_storage-mutex) can be taken by the [event loop](#291.html_event-loop).

3.  Take ownership of the [storage mutex](#291.html_storage-mutex).

##### 6.1.4.3 Generic task sources

The following [task sources](#291.html_task-source) are used by a number of mostly unrelated features in this and other specifications.

The <dfn id="291.html_dom-manipulation-task-source">DOM manipulation task source</dfn>

This [task source](#291.html_task-source) is used for features that react to DOM manipulations, such as things that happen asynchronously when an element is [inserted into the document](#291.html_insert-an-element-into-a-document).

The <dfn id="291.html_user-interaction-task-source">user interaction task source</dfn>

This [task source](#291.html_task-source) is used for features that react to user interaction, for example keyboard or mouse input.

Asynchronous events sent in response to user input (e.g. [`click`](#291.html_event-click) events) must be fired using [tasks](#291.html_concept-task) [queued](#291.html_queue-a-task) with the [user interaction task source](#291.html_user-interaction-task-source). [[DOMEVENTS]](#291.html_refsDOMEVENTS)

The <dfn id="291.html_networking-task-source">networking task source</dfn>

This [task source](#291.html_task-source) is used for features that trigger in response to network activity.

The <dfn id="291.html_history-traversal-task-source">history traversal task source</dfn>

This [task source](#291.html_task-source) is used to queue calls to [`history.back()`](#291.html_dom-history-back) and similar APIs.

#### 6.1.5 Events

##### 6.1.5.1 Event handlers

Many objects can have <dfn id="292.html_event-handlers">event handlers</dfn> specified. These act as non-capture event listeners for the object on which they are specified. [[DOM]](#292.html_refsDOM)

An [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) has a name, which always starts with "`on`" and is followed by the name of the event for which it is intended.

An [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) can either have the value null, or be set to a callback object, or be set to an [internal raw uncompiled handler](#292.html_internal-raw-uncompiled-handler). The [`EventHandler`](#292.html_eventhandler) callback function type describes how this is exposed to scripts. Initially, event handlers must be set to null.

Event handlers are exposed in one of two ways.

The first way, common to all event handlers, is as an [event handler IDL attribute](#292.html_event-handler-idl-attributes).

The second way is as an [event handler content attribute](#292.html_event-handler-content-attributes). Event handlers on [HTML elements](#292.html_html-elements) and some of the event handlers on [`Window`](#292.html_window) objects are exposed in this way.

* * *

An <dfn id="292.html_event-handler-idl-attributes" data-anolis-xref="event handler IDL attributes">event handler IDL attribute</dfn> is an IDL attribute for a specific [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers). The name of the IDL attribute is the same as the name of the [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers).

[Event handler IDL attributes](#292.html_event-handler-idl-attributes), on setting, must set the corresponding [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) to their new value, and on getting, must return the result of [getting the current value of the event handler](#292.html_getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler) in question (this can throw an exception, in which case the getting propagates it to the caller, it does not catch it).

If an [event handler IDL attribute](#292.html_event-handler-idl-attributes) exposes an [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) of an object that doesn't exist, it must always return null on getting and must do nothing on setting.

This can happen in particular for [event handler IDL attribute](#292.html_event-handler-idl-attributes) on [`body`](#292.html_the-body-element) elements that do not have corresponding [`Window`](#292.html_window) objects.

Certain event handler IDL attributes have additional requirements, in particular the `onmessage` attribute of [`MessagePort`](#292.html_messageport) objects.

* * *

An <dfn id="292.html_event-handler-content-attributes" data-anolis-xref="event handler content attributes">event handler content attribute</dfn> is a content attribute for a specific [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers). The name of the content attribute is the same as the name of the [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers).

[Event handler content attributes](#292.html_event-handler-content-attributes), when specified, must contain valid JavaScript code which, when parsed, would match the `FunctionBody` production after automatic semicolon insertion. [[ECMA262]](#292.html_refsECMA262)

When an [event handler content attribute](#292.html_event-handler-content-attributes) is set, the user agent must set the corresponding [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) to an [internal raw uncompiled handler](#292.html_internal-raw-uncompiled-handler) consisting of the attribute's new value and the script location where the attribute was set to this value

When an event handler content attribute is removed, the user agent must set the corresponding [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) to null.

* * *

When an [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) `H` of an element or object `T` implementing the [`EventTarget`](#292.html_eventtarget) interface is first set to a non-null value, the user agent must append an [event listener](#292.html_concept-event-listener) to the list of [event listeners](#292.html_concept-event-listener) associated with `T` with *type* set to the <dfn id="292.html_event-handler-event-type">event handler event type</dfn> corresponding to `H`, *capture* set to false, and *listener* set to [the event handler processing algorithm](#292.html_the-event-handler-processing-algorithm) defined below. [[DOM]](#292.html_refsDOM)

The *listener* is emphatically *not* the [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) itself. Every event handler ends up registering the same *listener*, the algorithm defined below, which takes care of invoking the right callback, and processing the callback's return value.

This only happens the first time the [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers)'s value is set. Since listeners are called in the order they were registered, the order of event listeners for a particular event type will always be first the event listeners registered with `addEventListener()` before the first time the [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) was set to a non-null value, then the callback to which it is currently set, if any, and finally the event listeners registered with `addEventListener()` *after* the first time the [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) was set to a non-null value.

This example demonstrates the order in which event listeners are invoked. If the button in this example is clicked by the user, the page will show four alerts, with the text "ONE", "TWO", "THREE", and "FOUR" respectively.

```
<button id="test">Start Demo</button>
<script>
 var button = document.getElementById('test');
 button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('ONE') }, false);
 button.setAttribute('onclick', "alert('NOT CALLED')"); // event handler listener is registered here
 button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('THREE') }, false);
 button.onclick = function () { alert('TWO'); };
 button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('FOUR') }, false);
</script>
```

The interfaces implemented by the event object do not influence whether an [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) is triggered or not.

<dfn id="292.html_the-event-handler-processing-algorithm">The event handler processing algorithm</dfn> for an [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) `H` and an [`Event`](#292.html_event) object `E` is as follows:

1.  Let `callback` be the result of [getting the current value of the event handler](#292.html_getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler) `H`.

2.  If `callback` is null, then abort these steps.

3.  Process the [`Event`](#292.html_event) object `E` as follows:

    If `E` is an [`ErrorEvent`](#292.html_errorevent) object and the [event handler IDL attribute](#292.html_event-handler-idl-attributes)'s type is [`OnErrorEventHandler`](#292.html_onerroreventhandler)

    [Invoke](#292.html_concept-invoke-event-handler) `callback` with five arguments, the first one having the value of `E`'s [`message`](#292.html_dom-errorevent-message) attribute, the second having the value of `E`'s [`filename`](#292.html_dom-errorevent-filename) attribute, the third having the value of `E`'s [`lineno`](#292.html_dom-errorevent-lineno) attribute, the fourth having the value of `E`'s [`colno`](#292.html_dom-errorevent-colno) attribute, the fifth having the value of `E`'s [`error`](#292.html_dom-errorevent-error) attribute, and with the *callback this value* set to `E`'s `currentTarget`. Let `return value` be the callback's return value. [[WEBIDL]](#292.html_refsWEBIDL)

    Otherwise

    [Invoke](#292.html_concept-invoke-event-handler) `callback` with one argument, the value of which is the [`Event`](#292.html_event) object `E`, with the *callback this value* set to `E`'s `currentTarget`. Let `return value` be the callback's return value. [[WEBIDL]](#292.html_refsWEBIDL)

    In this step, <dfn id="292.html_concept-invoke-event-handler" data-anolis-xref="concept-invoke-event-handler">invoke</dfn> means to run the [jump to a code entry-point](#292.html_jump-to-a-code-entry-point) algorithm.

4.  Process `return value` as follows:

    If the event type is `mouseover`
    If the event type is `error` and `E` is an [`ErrorEvent`](#292.html_errorevent) object

    If `return value` is a WebIDL boolean true value, then cancel the event.

    If the event type is `beforeunload`

    The [event handler IDL attribute](#292.html_event-handler-idl-attributes)'s type is [`OnBeforeUnloadEventHandler`](#292.html_onbeforeunloadeventhandler), and the `return value` will therefore have been coerced into either the value null or a DOMString.

    If the `return value` is null, then cancel the event.

    Otherwise, If the [`Event`](#292.html_event) object `E` is a [`BeforeUnloadEvent`](#292.html_beforeunloadevent) object, and the [`Event`](#292.html_event) object `E`'s [`returnValue`](#292.html_dom-beforeunloadevent-returnvalue) attribute's value is the empty string, then set the [`returnValue`](#292.html_dom-beforeunloadevent-returnvalue) attribute's value to `return value`.

    Otherwise

    If `return value` is a WebIDL boolean false value, then cancel the event.

* * *

The [`EventHandler`](#292.html_eventhandler) callback function type represents a callback used for event handlers. It is represented in Web IDL as follows:

```
[TreatNonCallableAsNull]
callback EventHandlerNonNull = any (Event event);
typedef EventHandlerNonNull? EventHandler;
```

In JavaScript, any `Function` object implements this interface.

For example, the following document fragment:

```
<body onload="alert(this)" onclick="alert(this)">
```

...leads to an alert saying "`[object Window]`" when the document is loaded, and an alert saying "`[object HTMLBodyElement]`" whenever the user clicks something in the page.

The return value of the function affects whether the event is canceled or not: as described above, if the return value is false, the event is canceled (except for `mouseover` events, where the return value has to be true to cancel the event). With `beforeunload` events, the value is instead used to determine the message to show the user.

For historical reasons, the [`onerror`](#292.html_handler-onerror) handler has different arguments:

```
[TreatNonCallableAsNull]
callback OnErrorEventHandlerNonNull = any ((Event or DOMString) event, optional DOMString source, optional unsigned long lineno, optional unsigned long column, optional any error);
typedef OnErrorEventHandlerNonNull? OnErrorEventHandler;
```

Similarly, the [`onbeforeunload`](#292.html_handler-window-onbeforeunload) handler has a different return value:

```
[TreatNonCallableAsNull]
callback OnBeforeUnloadEventHandlerNonNull = DOMString? (Event event);
typedef OnBeforeUnloadEventHandlerNonNull? OnBeforeUnloadEventHandler;
```

* * *

An <dfn id="292.html_internal-raw-uncompiled-handler">internal raw uncompiled handler</dfn> is a tuple with the following information:

*   An uncompiled script body
*   A location where the script body originated, in case an error needs to be reported

When the user agent is to <dfn id="292.html_getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler" data-anolis-xref="getting the current value of the event handler">get the current value of the event handler</dfn> `H`, it must run these steps:

1.  If `H`'s value is an [internal raw uncompiled handler](#292.html_internal-raw-uncompiled-handler), run these substeps:

    1.  If `H` is an element's [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers), then let `element` be the element, and `document` be the element's [`Document`](#292.html_document).

        Otherwise, `H` is a [`Window`](#292.html_window) object's [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers): let `element` be null, and let `document` be the [`Document`](#292.html_document) most recently associated with that [`Window`](#292.html_window) object.

    2.  If `document` is not in a [browsing context](#292.html_browsing-context), or if [scripting is enabled](#292.html_concept-bc-script) for `document`'s [browsing context](#292.html_browsing-context), then return null and abort the algorithm for [getting the current value of the event handler](#292.html_getting-the-current-value-of-the-event-handler).

    3.  Let `body` be the uncompiled script body in the [internal raw uncompiled handler](#292.html_internal-raw-uncompiled-handler).

    4.  Let `location` be the location where the script body originated, as given by the [internal raw uncompiled handler](#292.html_internal-raw-uncompiled-handler).

    5.  If `element` is not null and `element` has a [form owner](#292.html_form-owner), let `form owner` be that [form owner](#292.html_form-owner). Otherwise, let `form owner` be null.

    6.  Let `script settings` be the [script settings object](#292.html_script-settings-object) created for the [`Window`](#292.html_window) object with which `document` is currently associated.

    7.  Obtain the [script execution environment](#292.html_script-execution-environment) for JavaScript from `script settings`.

    8.  If `body` is not parsable as *FunctionBody* or if parsing detects an *early error*, then follow these substeps:

        1.  Set `H`'s value to null.

        2.  [Report the error](#292.html_report-the-error) for the appropriate [script](#292.html_concept-script) and with the appropriate position (line number and column number) given by `location`, using the [global object](#292.html_global-object) specified by `script settings` as the target. If the error is still *[not handled](#292.html_concept-error-nothandled)* after this, then the error may be reported to the user.

        3.  Jump to the step labeled *end* below.

        *FunctionBody* is defined in ECMAScript edition 5 section 13 Function Definition. *Early error* is defined in ECMAScript edition 5 section 16 Errors. [[ECMA262]](#292.html_refsECMA262)

    9.  If `body` begins with a Directive Prologue that contains a Use Strict Directive then let `strict` be true, otherwise let `strict` be false.

        The terms "Directive Prologue" and "Use Strict Directive" are defined in ECMAScript edition 5 section 14.1 Directive Prologues and the Use Strict Directive. [[ECMA262]](#292.html_refsECMA262)

    10.  Using the [script execution environment](#292.html_script-execution-environment) obtained above, create a function object (as defined in ECMAScript edition 5 section 13.2 Creating Function Objects), with:

        Parameter list `FormalParameterList`

        If `H` is an [`onerror`](#292.html_handler-onerror) [event handler](#292.html_event-handlers) of a [`Window`](#292.html_window) object

        Let the function have five arguments, named `event`, `source`, `lineno`, `colno`, and `error`.

        Otherwise

        Let the function have a single argument called `event`.

        Function body `FunctionBody`

        The result of parsing `body` above.

        Lexical Environment `Scope`

        1.  Let `Scope` be the result of NewObjectEnvironment(`document`, the `global environment`).
        2.  If `form owner` is not null, let `Scope` be the result of NewObjectEnvironment(`>form owner`, `Scope`).
        3.  If `element` is not null, let `Scope` be the result of NewObjectEnvironment(`element`, `Scope`).

        NewObjectEnvironment() is defined in ECMAScript edition 5 section 10.2.2.3 NewObjectEnvironment (O, E). [[ECMA262]](#292.html_refsECMA262)

        Boolean flag `Strict`

        The value of `strict`.

        Let `function` be this new function.

    11.  Let `script` be a new [script](#292.html_concept-script).

    12.  Let `script`'s [code entry-point](#292.html_code-entry-point) be `function`.

    13.  Let `script`'s [settings object](#292.html_settings-object) be `script settings`.

    14.  Set `H` to `function`.

2.  *End*: Return `H`'s value.

##### 6.1.5.3 Event firing

Certain operations and methods are defined as firing events on elements. For example, the [`click()`](#292.html_dom-click) method on the [`HTMLElement`](#292.html_htmlelement) interface is defined as firing a [`click`](#292.html_event-click) event on the element. [[DOMEVENTS]](#292.html_refsDOMEVENTS)

<dfn id="292.html_fire-a-simple-event" data-anolis-xref="fire a simple event">Firing a simple event named `e`</dfn> means that a [trusted](#292.html_concept-events-trusted) event with the name `e`, which does not bubble (except where otherwise stated) and is not cancelable (except where otherwise stated), and which uses the [`Event`](#292.html_event) interface, must be created and [dispatched](#292.html_concept-event-dispatch) at the given target.

<dfn id="292.html_fire-a-synthetic-mouse-event" data-anolis-xref="fire a synthetic mouse event">Firing a synthetic mouse event named `e`</dfn> means that an event with the name `e`, which is [trusted](#292.html_concept-events-trusted) (except where otherwise stated), does not bubble (except where otherwise stated), is not cancelable (except where otherwise stated), and which uses the [`MouseEvent`](#292.html_mouseevent) interface, must be created and dispatched at the given target. The event object must have its `screenX`, `screenY`, `clientX`, `clientY`, and `button` attributes initialized to 0, its `ctrlKey`, `shiftKey`, `altKey`, and `metaKey` attributes initialized according to the current state of the key input device, if any (false for any keys that are not available), its `detail` attribute initialized to 1, and its `relatedTarget` attribute initialized to null (except where otherwise stated). The `getModifierState()` method on the object must return values appropriately describing the state of the key input device at the time the event is created.

<dfn id="292.html_fire-a-click-event" data-anolis-xref="fire a click event">Firing a `click` event</dfn> means [firing a synthetic mouse event named `click`](#292.html_fire-a-synthetic-mouse-event), which bubbles and is cancelable.

The default action of these events is to do nothing except where otherwise stated.

##### 6.1.5.4 Events and the [`Window`](#292.html_window) object

When an event is dispatched at a DOM node in a [`Document`](#292.html_document) in a [browsing context](#292.html_browsing-context), if the event is not a `load` event, the user agent must act as if, for the purposes of [event dispatching](#292.html_concept-event-dispatch), the [`Window`](#292.html_window) object is the parent of the [`Document`](#292.html_document) object. [[DOM]](#292.html_refsDOM)

### 6.2 Base64 utility methods

The [`atob()`](#293.html_dom-windowbase64-atob) and [`btoa()`](#293.html_dom-windowbase64-btoa) methods allow authors to transform content to and from the base64 encoding.

```
[NoInterfaceObject]
interface WindowBase64 {
  DOMString btoa(DOMString btoa);
  DOMString atob(DOMString atob);
};
Window implements WindowBase64;
```

In these APIs, for mnemonic purposes, the "b" can be considered to stand for "binary", and the "a" for "ASCII". In practice, though, for primarily historical reasons, both the input and output of these functions are Unicode strings.

`result` = `window` . [`btoa`](#293.html_dom-windowbase64-btoa)( `data` )

Takes the input data, in the form of a Unicode string containing only characters in the range U+0000 to U+00FF, each representing a binary byte with values 0x00 to 0xFF respectively, and converts it to its base64 representation, which it returns.

Throws an [`InvalidCharacterError`](#293.html_invalidcharactererror) exception if the input string contains any out-of-range characters.

`result` = `window` . [`atob`](#293.html_dom-windowbase64-atob)( `data` )

Takes the input data, in the form of a Unicode string containing base64-encoded binary data, decodes it, and returns a string consisting of characters in the range U+0000 to U+00FF, each representing a binary byte with values 0x00 to 0xFF respectively, corresponding to that binary data.

Throws an [`InvalidCharacterError`](#293.html_invalidcharactererror) exception if the input string is not valid base64 data.

The [`WindowBase64`](#293.html_windowbase64) interface adds to the [`Window`](#293.html_window) interface and the `WorkerGlobalScope` interface (part of Web workers).

The <dfn id="293.html_dom-windowbase64-btoa" data-anolis-xref="dom-windowbase64-btoa">`btoa()`</dfn> method must throw an [`InvalidCharacterError`](#293.html_invalidcharactererror) exception if the method's first argument contains any character whose code point is greater than U+00FF. Otherwise, the user agent must convert that argument to a sequence of octets whose `n`th octet is the eight-bit representation of the code point of the `n`th character of the argument, and then must apply the base64 algorithm to that sequence of octets, and return the result. [[RFC4648]](#293.html_refsRFC4648)

The <dfn id="293.html_dom-windowbase64-atob" data-anolis-xref="dom-windowbase64-atob">`atob()`</dfn> method must run the following steps to parse the string passed in the method's first argument:

1.  Let `input` be the string being parsed.

2.  Let `position` be a pointer into `input`, initially pointing at the start of the string.

3.  Remove all [space characters](#293.html_space-character) from `input`.

4.  If the length of `input` divides by 4 leaving no remainder, then: if `input` ends with one or two "=" (U+003D) characters, remove them from `input`.

5.  If the length of `input` divides by 4 leaving a remainder of 1, throw an [`InvalidCharacterError`](#293.html_invalidcharactererror) exception and abort these steps.

6.  If `input` contains a character that is not in the following list of characters and character ranges, throw an [`InvalidCharacterError`](#293.html_invalidcharactererror) exception and abort these steps:

    *   "+" (U+002B)
    *   "/" (U+002F)
    *   [Alphanumeric ASCII characters](#293.html_alphanumeric-ascii-characters)
7.  Let `output` be a string, initially empty.

8.  Let `buffer` be a buffer that can have bits appended to it, initially empty.

9.  While `position` does not point past the end of `input`, run these substeps:

    1.  Find the character pointed to by `position` in the first column of the following table. Let `n` be the number given in the second cell of the same row.

        | Character | Number |
        | --- | --- |
        | A | 0 |
        | B | 1 |
        | C | 2 |
        | D | 3 |
        | E | 4 |
        | F | 5 |
        | G | 6 |
        | H | 7 |
        | I | 8 |
        | J | 9 |
        | K | 10 |
        | L | 11 |
        | M | 12 |
        | N | 13 |
        | O | 14 |
        | P | 15 |
        | Q | 16 |
        | R | 17 |
        | S | 18 |
        | T | 19 |
        | U | 20 |
        | V | 21 |
        | W | 22 |
        | X | 23 |
        | Y | 24 |
        | Z | 25 |
        | a | 26 |
        | b | 27 |
        | c | 28 |
        | d | 29 |
        | e | 30 |
        | f | 31 |
        | g | 32 |
        | h | 33 |
        | i | 34 |
        | j | 35 |
        | k | 36 |
        | l | 37 |
        | m | 38 |
        | n | 39 |
        | o | 40 |
        | p | 41 |
        | q | 42 |
        | r | 43 |
        | s | 44 |
        | t | 45 |
        | u | 46 |
        | v | 47 |
        | w | 48 |
        | x | 49 |
        | y | 50 |
        | z | 51 |
        | 0 | 52 |
        | 1 | 53 |
        | 2 | 54 |
        | 3 | 55 |
        | 4 | 56 |
        | 5 | 57 |
        | 6 | 58 |
        | 7 | 59 |
        | 8 | 60 |
        | 9 | 61 |
        | + | 62 |
        | / | 63 |

    2.  Append to `buffer` the six bits corresponding to `number`, most significant bit first.

    3.  If `buffer` has accumulated 24 bits, interpret them as three 8-bit big-endian numbers. Append the three characters with code points equal to those numbers to `output`, in the same order, and then empty `buffer`.

    4.  Advance `position` by one character.

10.  If `buffer` is not empty, it contains either 12 or 18 bits. If it contains 12 bits, discard the last four and interpret the remaining eight as an 8-bit big-endian number. If it contains 18 bits, discard the last two and interpret the remaining 16 as two 8-bit big-endian numbers. Append the one or two characters with code points equal to those one or two numbers to `output`, in the same order.

    The discarded bits mean that, for instance, `atob("YQ")` and `atob("YR")` both return "`a`".

11.  Return `output`.

### 6.3 <dfn>Dynamic markup insertion</dfn>

APIs for dynamically inserting markup into the document interact with the parser, and thus their behavior varies depending on whether they are used with [HTML documents](#294.html_html-documents) (and the [HTML parser](#294.html_html-parser)) or XHTML in [XML documents](#294.html_xml-documents) (and the [XML parser](#294.html_xml-parser)).

#### 6.3.1 Opening the input stream

The <dfn id="295.html_dom-document-open" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-open">`open()`</dfn> method comes in several variants with different numbers of arguments.

`document` = `document` . [`open`](#295.html_dom-document-open)( [ `type` [, `replace` ] ] )

Causes the [`Document`](#295.html_document) to be replaced in-place, as if it was a new [`Document`](#295.html_document) object, but reusing the previous object, which is then returned.

If the `type` argument is omitted or has the value "[`text/html`](#295.html_text/html)", then the resulting [`Document`](#295.html_document) has an HTML parser associated with it, which can be given data to parse using [`document.write()`](#295.html_dom-document-write). Otherwise, all content passed to [`document.write()`](#295.html_dom-document-write) will be parsed as plain text.

If the `replace` argument is present and has the value "`replace`", the existing entries in the session history for the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object are removed.

The method has no effect if the [`Document`](#295.html_document) is still being parsed.

Throws an [`InvalidStateError`](#295.html_invalidstateerror) exception if the [`Document`](#295.html_document) is an [XML document](#295.html_xml-documents).

`window` = `document` . [`open`](#295.html_dom-document-open)( `url`, `name`, `features` [, `replace` ] )

Works like the [`window.open()`](#295.html_dom-open) method.

[`Document`](#295.html_document) objects have an <dfn id="295.html_ignore-opens-during-unload-counter">ignore-opens-during-unload counter</dfn>, which is used to prevent scripts from invoking the [`document.open()`](#295.html_dom-document-open) method (directly or indirectly) while the document is [being unloaded](#295.html_unload-a-document). Initially, the counter must be set to zero.

When called with two arguments, the [`document.open()`](#295.html_dom-document-open) method must act as follows:

1.  If the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object is not flagged as an [HTML document](#295.html_html-documents), throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#295.html_invalidstateerror) exception and abort these steps.

2.  If the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object is not an [active document](#295.html_active-document), then abort these steps.

3.  Let `type` be the value of the first argument.

4.  If the second argument is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#295.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the value "replace", then let `replace` be true.

    Otherwise, if the [browsing context](#295.html_browsing-context)'s [session history](#295.html_session-history) contains only one [`Document`](#295.html_document), and that was the [`about:blank`](#295.html_about:blank) [`Document`](#295.html_document) created when the [browsing context](#295.html_browsing-context) was created, and that [`Document`](#295.html_document) has never had the [unload a document](#295.html_unload-a-document) algorithm invoked on it (e.g. by a previous call to [`document.open()`](#295.html_dom-document-open)), then let `replace` be true.

    Otherwise, let `replace` be false.

5.  If the [`Document`](#295.html_document) has an [active parser](#295.html_active-parser) whose [script nesting level](#295.html_script-nesting-level) is greater than zero, then the method does nothing. Abort these steps and return the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object on which the method was invoked.

    This basically causes [`document.open()`](#295.html_dom-document-open) to be ignored when it's called in an inline script found during parsing, while still letting it have an effect when called asynchronously.

6.  Similarly, if the [`Document`](#295.html_document)'s [ignore-opens-during-unload counter](#295.html_ignore-opens-during-unload-counter) is greater than zero, then the method does nothing. Abort these steps and return the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object on which the method was invoked.

    This basically causes [`document.open()`](#295.html_dom-document-open) to be ignored when it's called from a `beforeunload` [`pagehide`](#295.html_event-pagehide), or `unload` event handler while the [`Document`](#295.html_document) is being unloaded.

7.  Release the [storage mutex](#295.html_storage-mutex).

8.  Set the [`Document`](#295.html_document)'s *[salvageable](#295.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state to false.

9.  [Prompt to unload](#295.html_prompt-to-unload-a-document) the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object. If the user [refused to allow the document to be unloaded](#295.html_refused-to-allow-the-document-to-be-unloaded), then abort these steps and return the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object on which the method was invoked.

10.  [Unload](#295.html_unload-a-document) the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object, with the `recycle` parameter set to true.

11.  [Abort](#295.html_abort-a-document) the [`Document`](#295.html_document).

12.  Unregister all event listeners registered on the [`Document`](#295.html_document) node and its descendants.

13.  Remove any [tasks](#295.html_concept-task) associated with the [`Document`](#295.html_document) in any [task source](#295.html_task-source).

14.  Remove all child nodes of the document, without firing any mutation events.

15.  Replace the [`Document`](#295.html_document)'s singleton objects with new instances of those objects. (This includes in particular the [`Window`](#295.html_window), [`Location`](#295.html_location), [`History`](#295.html_history-1), [`ApplicationCache`](#295.html_applicationcache), and [`Navigator`](#295.html_navigator), objects, the various [`BarProp`](#295.html_barprop) objects, the two `Storage` objects, the various [`HTMLCollection`](#295.html_htmlcollection) objects, and objects defined by other specifications, like `Selection` and the document's `UndoManager`. It also includes all the Web IDL prototypes in the JavaScript binding, including the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object's prototype.)

    The new [`Window`](#295.html_window) object has a new [script settings object](#295.html_script-settings-object).

16.  Change the [document's character encoding](#295.html_document's-character-encoding) to UTF-8.

17.  If the [`Document`](#295.html_document) is [ready for post-load tasks](#295.html_ready-for-post-load-tasks), then set the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object's [reload override flag](#295.html_reload-override-flag) and set the [`Document`](#295.html_document)'s [reload override buffer](#295.html_reload-override-buffer) to the empty string.

18.  Set the [`Document`](#295.html_document)'s *[salvageable](#295.html_concept-document-salvageable)* state back to true.

19.  Change [the document's address](#295.html_the-document's-address) to the [address](#295.html_the-document's-address) of the [responsible document](#295.html_responsible-document) specified by the [entry settings object](#295.html_entry-settings-object).

20.  If the [`Document`](#295.html_document)'s [iframe load in progress](#295.html_iframe-load-in-progress) flag is set, set the [`Document`](#295.html_document)'s [mute iframe load](#295.html_mute-iframe-load) flag.

21.  Create a new [HTML parser](#295.html_html-parser) and associate it with the document. This is a <dfn id="295.html_script-created-parser">script-created parser</dfn> (meaning that it can be closed by the [`document.open()`](#295.html_dom-document-open) and [`document.close()`](#295.html_dom-document-close) methods, and that the tokenizer will wait for an explicit call to [`document.close()`](#295.html_dom-document-close) before emitting an end-of-file token). The encoding [confidence](#295.html_concept-encoding-confidence) is *irrelevant*.

22.  Set the [current document readiness](#295.html_current-document-readiness) of the document to "`loading`".

23.  If `type` is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#295.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`replace`", then, for historical reasons, set it to the string "`text/html`".

    Otherwise:

    If the `type` string contains a ";" (U+003B) character, remove the first such character and all characters from it up to the end of the string.

    [Strip leading and trailing whitespace](#295.html_strip-leading-and-trailing-whitespace) from `type`.

24.  If `type` is *not* now an [ASCII case-insensitive](#295.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "[`text/html`](#295.html_text/html)", then act as if the tokenizer had emitted a start tag token with the tag name "pre" followed by a single "LF" (U+000A) character, then switch the [HTML parser](#295.html_html-parser)'s tokenizer to the [PLAINTEXT state](#295.html_plaintext-state).

25.  Remove all the entries in the [browsing context](#295.html_browsing-context)'s [session history](#295.html_session-history) after the [current entry](#295.html_current-entry). If the [current entry](#295.html_current-entry) is the last entry in the session history, then no entries are removed.

    This [doesn't necessarily have to affect](#295.html_history-notes) the user agent's user interface.

26.  Remove any [tasks](#295.html_concept-task) queued by the [history traversal task source](#295.html_history-traversal-task-source) that are associated with any [`Document`](#295.html_document) objects in the [top-level browsing context](#295.html_top-level-browsing-context)'s [document family](#295.html_document-family).

27.  Remove any earlier entries that share the same [`Document`](#295.html_document).
28.  If `replace` is false, then add a new entry, just before the last entry, and associate with the new entry the text that was parsed by the previous parser associated with the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object, as well as the state of the document at the start of these steps. This allows the user to step backwards in the session history to see the page before it was blown away by the [`document.open()`](#295.html_dom-document-open) call. This new entry does not have a [`Document`](#295.html_document) object, so a new one will be created if the session history is traversed to that entry.

29.  Finally, set the [insertion point](#295.html_insertion-point) to point at just before the end of the [input stream](#295.html_input-stream) (which at this point will be empty).

30.  Return the [`Document`](#295.html_document) on which the method was invoked.

The [`document.open()`](#295.html_dom-document-open) method does not affect whether a [`Document`](#295.html_document) is [ready for post-load tasks](#295.html_ready-for-post-load-tasks) or [completely loaded](#295.html_completely-loaded).

When called with four arguments, the [`open()`](#295.html_dom-document-open) method on the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object must call the [`open()`](#295.html_dom-open) method on the [`Window`](#295.html_window) object of the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object, with the same arguments as the original call to the [`open()`](#295.html_dom-document-open) method, and return whatever that method returned. If the [`Document`](#295.html_document) object has no [`Window`](#295.html_window) object, then the method must throw an [`InvalidAccessError`](#295.html_invalidaccesserror) exception.

#### 6.3.2 Closing the input stream

`document` . [`close`](#296.html_dom-document-close)()

Closes the input stream that was opened by the [`document.open()`](#296.html_dom-document-open) method.

Throws an [`InvalidStateError`](#296.html_invalidstateerror) exception if the [`Document`](#296.html_document) is an [XML document](#296.html_xml-documents).

The <dfn id="296.html_dom-document-close" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-close">`close()`</dfn> method must run the following steps:

1.  If the [`Document`](#296.html_document) object is not flagged as an [HTML document](#296.html_html-documents), throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#296.html_invalidstateerror) exception and abort these steps.

2.  If there is no [script-created parser](#296.html_script-created-parser) associated with the document, then abort these steps.

3.  Insert an [explicit "EOF" character](#296.html_explicit-eof-character) at the end of the parser's [input stream](#296.html_input-stream).

4.  If there is a [pending parsing-blocking script](#296.html_pending-parsing-blocking-script), then abort these steps.

5.  Run the tokenizer, processing resulting tokens as they are emitted, and stopping when the tokenizer reaches the [explicit "EOF" character](#296.html_explicit-eof-character) or [spins the event loop](#296.html_spin-the-event-loop).

#### 6.3.3 [`document.write()`](#297.html_dom-document-write)

`document` . [`write`](#297.html_dom-document-write)(`text`...)

In general, adds the given string(s) to the [`Document`](#297.html_document)'s input stream.

This method has very idiosyncratic behavior. In some cases, this method can affect the state of the [HTML parser](#297.html_html-parser) while the parser is running, resulting in a DOM that does not correspond to the source of the document (e.g. if the string written is the string "`<plaintext>`" or "`<!--`"). In other cases, the call can clear the current page first, as if [`document.open()`](#297.html_dom-document-open) had been called. In yet more cases, the method is simply ignored, or throws an exception. To make matters worse, the exact behavior of this method can in some cases be dependent on network latency, which can lead to failures that are very hard to debug. **For all these reasons, use of this method is strongly discouraged.**

This method throws an [`InvalidStateError`](#297.html_invalidstateerror) exception when invoked on [XML documents](#297.html_xml-documents).

[`Document`](#297.html_document) objects have an <dfn id="297.html_ignore-destructive-writes-counter">ignore-destructive-writes counter</dfn>, which is used in conjunction with the processing of [`script`](#297.html_the-script-element) elements to prevent external scripts from being able to use [`document.write()`](#297.html_dom-document-write) to blow away the document by implicitly calling [`document.open()`](#297.html_dom-document-open). Initially, the counter must be set to zero.

The <dfn id="297.html_dom-document-write" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-write">`document.write(...)`</dfn> method must act as follows:

1.  If the method was invoked on an [XML document](#297.html_xml-documents), throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#297.html_invalidstateerror) exception and abort these steps.

2.  If the [`Document`](#297.html_document) object is not an [active document](#297.html_active-document), then abort these steps.

3.  If the [insertion point](#297.html_insertion-point) is undefined and either the [`Document`](#297.html_document)'s [ignore-opens-during-unload counter](#297.html_ignore-opens-during-unload-counter) is greater than zero or the [`Document`](#297.html_document)'s [ignore-destructive-writes counter](#297.html_ignore-destructive-writes-counter) is greater than zero, abort these steps.

4.  If the [insertion point](#297.html_insertion-point) is undefined, call the [`open()`](#297.html_dom-document-open) method on the [`document`](#297.html_document) object (with no arguments). If the user [refused to allow the document to be unloaded](#297.html_refused-to-allow-the-document-to-be-unloaded), then abort these steps. Otherwise, the [insertion point](#297.html_insertion-point) will point at just before the end of the (empty) [input stream](#297.html_input-stream).

5.  Insert the string consisting of the concatenation of all the arguments to the method into the [input stream](#297.html_input-stream) just before the [insertion point](#297.html_insertion-point).

6.  If the [`Document`](#297.html_document) object's [reload override flag](#297.html_reload-override-flag) is set, then append the string consisting of the concatenation of all the arguments to the method to the [`Document`](#297.html_document)'s [reload override buffer](#297.html_reload-override-buffer).

7.  If there is no [pending parsing-blocking script](#297.html_pending-parsing-blocking-script), have the [HTML parser](#297.html_html-parser) process the characters that were inserted, one at a time, processing resulting tokens as they are emitted, and stopping when the tokenizer reaches the insertion point or when the processing of the tokenizer is aborted by the tree construction stage (this can happen if a [`script`](#297.html_the-script-element) end tag token is emitted by the tokenizer).

    If the [`document.write()`](#297.html_dom-document-write) method was called from script executing inline (i.e. executing because the parser parsed a set of [`script`](#297.html_the-script-element) tags), then this is a [reentrant invocation of the parser](#297.html_nestedParsing).

8.  Finally, return from the method.

#### 6.3.4 [`document.writeln()`](#298.html_dom-document-writeln)

`document` . [`writeln`](#298.html_dom-document-writeln)(`text`...)

Adds the given string(s) to the [`Document`](#298.html_document)'s input stream, followed by a newline character. If necessary, calls the [`open()`](#298.html_dom-document-open) method implicitly first.

This method throws an [`InvalidStateError`](#298.html_invalidstateerror) exception when invoked on [XML documents](#298.html_xml-documents).

The <dfn id="298.html_dom-document-writeln" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-writeln">`document.writeln(...)`</dfn> method, when invoked, must act as if the [`document.write()`](#298.html_dom-document-write) method had been invoked with the same argument(s), plus an extra argument consisting of a string containing a single line feed character (U+000A).

### 6.4 Timers

The [`setTimeout()`](#299.html_dom-windowtimers-settimeout) and [`setInterval()`](#299.html_dom-windowtimers-setinterval) methods allow authors to schedule timer-based callbacks.

```
[NoInterfaceObject]
interface WindowTimers {
  long setTimeout(Function handler, optional long timeout, any... arguments);
  long setTimeout(DOMString handler, optional long timeout, any... arguments);
  void clearTimeout(long handle);
  long setInterval(Function handler, optional long timeout, any... arguments);
  long setInterval(DOMString handler, optional long timeout, any... arguments);
  void clearInterval(long handle);
};
Window implements WindowTimers;
```

`handle` = `window` . [`setTimeout`](#299.html_dom-windowtimers-settimeout)( `handler` [, `timeout` [, `arguments`... ] ] )

Schedules a timeout to run `handler` after `timeout` milliseconds. Any `arguments` are passed straight through to the `handler`.

`handle` = `window` . [`setTimeout`](#299.html_dom-windowtimers-settimeout)( `code` [, `timeout` ] )

Schedules a timeout to compile and run `code` after `timeout` milliseconds.

`window` . [`clearTimeout`](#299.html_dom-windowtimers-cleartimeout)( `handle` )

Cancels the timeout set with [`setTimeout()`](#299.html_dom-windowtimers-settimeout) identified by `handle`.

`handle` = `window` . [`setInterval`](#299.html_dom-windowtimers-setinterval)( `handler` [, `timeout` [, `arguments`... ] ] )

Schedules a timeout to run `handler` every `timeout` milliseconds. Any `arguments` are passed straight through to the `handler`.

`handle` = `window` . [`setInterval`](#299.html_dom-windowtimers-setinterval)( `code` [, `timeout` ] )

Schedules a timeout to compile and run `code` every `timeout` milliseconds.

`window` . [`clearInterval`](#299.html_dom-windowtimers-clearinterval)( `handle` )

Cancels the timeout set with [`setInterval()`](#299.html_dom-windowtimers-setinterval) identified by `handle`.

Timers can be nested; after five such nested timers, however, the interval is forced to be at least four milliseconds.

This API does not guarantee that timers will run exactly on schedule. Delays due to CPU load, other tasks, etc, are to be expected.

The [`WindowTimers`](#299.html_windowtimers) interface adds to the [`Window`](#299.html_window) interface and the `WorkerGlobalScope` interface (part of Web workers).

Each object that implements the [`WindowTimers`](#299.html_windowtimers) interface has a <dfn id="299.html_list-of-active-timers">list of active timers</dfn>. Each entry in this lists is identified by a number, which must be unique within the list for the lifetime of the object that implements the [`WindowTimers`](#299.html_windowtimers) interface.

* * *

The <dfn id="299.html_dom-windowtimers-settimeout" data-anolis-xref="dom-windowtimers-setTimeout">`setTimeout()`</dfn> method must return the value returned by the [timer initialization steps](#299.html_timer-initialization-steps), passing them the method's arguments, the object on which the method for which the algorithm is running is implemented (a [`Window`](#299.html_window) or `WorkerGlobalScope` object) as the `method context`, and the `repeat` flag set to false.

The <dfn id="299.html_dom-windowtimers-setinterval" data-anolis-xref="dom-windowtimers-setInterval">`setInterval()`</dfn> method must return the value returned by the [timer initialization steps](#299.html_timer-initialization-steps), passing them the method's arguments, the object on which the method for which the algorithm is running is implemented (a [`Window`](#299.html_window) or `WorkerGlobalScope` object) as the `method context`, and the `repeat` flag set to true.

The <dfn id="299.html_dom-windowtimers-cleartimeout" data-anolis-xref="dom-windowtimers-clearTimeout">`clearTimeout()`</dfn> and <dfn id="299.html_dom-windowtimers-clearinterval" data-anolis-xref="dom-windowtimers-clearInterval">`clearInterval()`</dfn> methods must clear the entry identified as `handle` from the [list of active timers](#299.html_list-of-active-timers) of the [`WindowTimers`](#299.html_windowtimers) object on which the method was invoked, where `handle` is the argument passed to the method, if any. (If `handle` does not identify an entry in the [list of active timers](#299.html_list-of-active-timers) of the [`WindowTimers`](#299.html_windowtimers) object on which the method was invoked, the method does nothing.)

* * *

The <dfn id="299.html_timer-initialization-steps">timer initialization steps</dfn>, which are invoked with some method arguments, a `method context`, a `repeat` flag which can be true or false, and optionally (and only if the `repeat` flag is true) a `previous handle`, are as follows:

1.  Let `method context proxy` be `method context` if that is a `WorkerGlobalScope` object, or else the [`WindowProxy`](#299.html_windowproxy) that corresponds to `method context`.

2.  If `previous handle` was provided, let `handle` be `previous handle`; otherwise, let `handle` be a user-agent-defined integer that is greater than zero that will identify the timeout to be set by this call in the [list of active timers](#299.html_list-of-active-timers).

3.  If `previous handle` was not provided, add an entry to the [list of active timers](#299.html_list-of-active-timers) for `handle`.

4.  Let `task` be a [task](#299.html_concept-task) that runs the following substeps:

    1.  If the entry for `handle` in the [list of active timers](#299.html_list-of-active-timers) has been cleared, then abort this [task](#299.html_concept-task)'s substeps.

    2.  Run the appropriate set of steps from the following list:

        If the first method argument is a `Function`

        Call the `Function`. Use the third and subsequent method arguments (if any) as the arguments for invoking the `Function`. Use `method context proxy` as the `thisArg` for invoking the `Function`. [[ECMA262]](#299.html_refsECMA262)

        Otherwise

        1.  Let `script source` be the first method argument.

        2.  Let `script language` be JavaScript.

        3.  Let `settings object` be `method context`'s [script settings object](#299.html_script-settings-object).

        4.  [Create a script](#299.html_create-a-script) using `script source` as the script source, the URL where `script source` can be found, `scripting language` as the scripting language, and `settings object` as the [script settings object](#299.html_script-settings-object).

    3.  If the `repeat` flag is true, then call [timer initialization steps](#299.html_timer-initialization-steps) again, passing them the same method arguments, the same `method context`, with the `repeat` flag still set to true, and with the `previous handle` set to `handler`.

5.  Let `timeout` be the second method argument, or zero if the argument was omitted.

6.  If the currently running [task](#299.html_concept-task) is a task that was created by this algorithm, then let `nesting level` be the [task](#299.html_concept-task)'s [timer nesting level](#299.html_timer-nesting-level). Otherwise, let `nesting level` be zero.

7.  If `nesting level` is greater than 5, and `timeout` is less than 4, then increase `timeout` to 4.

8.  Increment `nesting level` by one.

9.  Let `task`'s <dfn id="299.html_timer-nesting-level">timer nesting level</dfn> be `nesting level`.

10.  Return `handle`, and then continue running this algorithm asynchronously.

11.  If `method context` is a [`Window`](#299.html_window) object, wait until the [`Document`](#299.html_document) associated with `method context` has been [fully active](#299.html_fully-active) for a further `timeout` milliseconds (not necessarily consecutively).

    Otherwise, `method context` is a `WorkerGlobalScope` object; wait until `timeout` milliseconds have passed with the worker not suspended (not necessarily consecutively).

12.  Wait until any invocations of this algorithm that had the same `method context`, that started before this one, and whose `timeout` is equal to or less than this one's, have completed.

    Argument conversion as defined by Web IDL (for example, invoking `toString()` methods on objects passed as the first argument) happens in the algorithms defined in Web IDL, before this algorithm is invoked.

    So for example, the following rather silly code will result in the log containing "`ONE TWO `":

    ```
    var log = '';
    function logger(s) { log += s + ' '; }

    setTimeout({ toString: function () {
      setTimeout("logger('ONE')", 100);
      return "logger('TWO')";
    } }, 100);
    ```

13.  Optionally, wait a further user-agent defined length of time.

    This is intended to allow user agents to pad timeouts as needed to optimise the power usage of the device. For example, some processors have a low-power mode where the granularity of timers is reduced; on such platforms, user agents can slow timers down to fit this schedule instead of requiring the processor to use the more accurate mode with its associated higher power usage.

14.  [Queue](#299.html_queue-a-task) the [task](#299.html_concept-task) `task`.

    Once the task has been processed, if the `repeat` flag is false, it is safe to remove the entry for `handle` from the [list of active timers](#299.html_list-of-active-timers) (there is no way for the entry's existence to be detected past this point, so it does not technically matter one way or the other).

The [task source](#299.html_task-source) for these [tasks](#299.html_concept-task) is the <dfn id="299.html_timer-task-source">timer task source</dfn>.

To run tasks of several milliseconds back to back without any delay, while still yielding back to the browser to avoid starving the user interface (and to avoid the browser killing the script for hogging the CPU), simply queue the next timer before performing work:

```
function doExpensiveWork() {
  var done = false;
  // ...
  // this part of the function takes up to five milliseconds
  // set done to true if we're done
  // ...
  return done;
}

function rescheduleWork() {
  var handle = setTimeout(rescheduleWork, 0); // preschedule next iteration
  if (doExpensiveWork())
    clearTimeout(handle); // clear the timeout if we don't need it
}

function scheduleWork() {
  setTimeout(rescheduleWork, 0);
}

scheduleWork(); // queues a task to do lots of work
```

### 6.5 User prompts

#### 6.5.1 Simple dialogs

`window` . [`alert`](#301.html_dom-alert)(`message`)

Displays a modal alert with the given message, and waits for the user to dismiss it.

A call to the [`navigator.yieldForStorageUpdates()`](#301.html_dom-navigator-yieldforstorageupdates) method is implied when this method is invoked.

`result` = `window` . [`confirm`](#301.html_dom-confirm)(`message`)

Displays a modal OK/Cancel prompt with the given message, waits for the user to dismiss it, and returns true if the user clicks OK and false if the user clicks Cancel.

A call to the [`navigator.yieldForStorageUpdates()`](#301.html_dom-navigator-yieldforstorageupdates) method is implied when this method is invoked.

`result` = `window` . [`prompt`](#301.html_dom-prompt)(`message` [, `default`] )

Displays a modal text field prompt with the given message, waits for the user to dismiss it, and returns the value that the user entered. If the user cancels the prompt, then returns null instead. If the second argument is present, then the given value is used as a default.

A call to the [`navigator.yieldForStorageUpdates()`](#301.html_dom-navigator-yieldforstorageupdates) method is implied when this method is invoked.

The <dfn id="301.html_dom-alert" data-anolis-xref="dom-alert">`alert(``message``)`</dfn> method, when invoked, must run the following steps:

1.  If the [event loop](#301.html_event-loop)'s [termination nesting level](#301.html_termination-nesting-level) is non-zero, optionally abort these steps.

2.  Release the [storage mutex](#301.html_storage-mutex).

3.  Optionally, abort these steps. (For example, the user agent might give the user the option to ignore all alerts, and would thus abort at this step whenever the method was invoked.)

4.  Show the given `message` to the user.

5.  Optionally, [pause](#301.html_pause) while waiting for the user to acknowledge the message.

The <dfn id="301.html_dom-confirm" data-anolis-xref="dom-confirm">`confirm(``message``)`</dfn> method, when invoked, must run the following steps:

1.  If the [event loop](#301.html_event-loop)'s [termination nesting level](#301.html_termination-nesting-level) is non-zero, optionally abort these steps, returning false.

2.  Release the [storage mutex](#301.html_storage-mutex).

3.  Optionally, return false and abort these steps. (For example, the user agent might give the user the option to ignore all prompts, and would thus abort at this step whenever the method was invoked.)

4.  Show the given `message` to the user, and ask the user to respond with a positive or negative response.

5.  [Pause](#301.html_pause) until the user responds either positively or negatively.

6.  If the user responded positively, return true; otherwise, the user responded negatively: return false.

The <dfn id="301.html_dom-prompt" data-anolis-xref="dom-prompt">`prompt(``message``,` `default``)`</dfn> method, when invoked, must run the following steps:

1.  If the [event loop](#301.html_event-loop)'s [termination nesting level](#301.html_termination-nesting-level) is non-zero, optionally abort these steps, returning null.

2.  Release the [storage mutex](#301.html_storage-mutex).

3.  Optionally, return null and abort these steps. (For example, the user agent might give the user the option to ignore all prompts, and would thus abort at this step whenever the method was invoked.)

4.  Show the given `message` to the user, and ask the user to either respond with a string value or abort. The response must be defaulted to the value given by `default`.

5.  [Pause](#301.html_pause) while waiting for the user's response.

6.  If the user aborts, then return null; otherwise, return the string that the user responded with.

#### 6.5.2 Printing

`window` . [`print`](#302.html_dom-print)()

Prompts the user to print the page.

A call to the [`navigator.yieldForStorageUpdates()`](#302.html_dom-navigator-yieldforstorageupdates) method is implied when this method is invoked.

When the <dfn id="302.html_dom-print" data-anolis-xref="dom-print">`print()`</dfn> method is invoked, if the [`Document`](#302.html_document) is [ready for post-load tasks](#302.html_ready-for-post-load-tasks), then the user agent must synchronously run the [printing steps](#302.html_printing-steps). Otherwise, the user agent must only set the <dfn id="302.html_print-when-loaded">print when loaded</dfn> flag on the [`Document`](#302.html_document).

User agents should also run the [printing steps](#302.html_printing-steps) whenever the user asks for the opportunity to [obtain a physical form](#302.html_obtain-a-physical-form) (e.g. printed copy), or the representation of a physical form (e.g. PDF copy), of a document.

The <dfn id="302.html_printing-steps">printing steps</dfn> are as follows:

1.  The user agent may display a message to the user or abort these steps (or both).

    For instance, a kiosk browser could silently ignore any invocations of the [`print()`](#302.html_dom-print) method.

    For instance, a browser on a mobile device could detect that there are no printers in the vicinity and display a message saying so before continuing to offer a "save to PDF" option.

2.  The user agent must [fire a simple event](#302.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `beforeprint` at the [`Window`](#302.html_window) object of the [`Document`](#302.html_document) that is being printed, as well as any [nested browsing contexts](#302.html_nested-browsing-context) in it.

    The `beforeprint` event can be used to annotate the printed copy, for instance adding the time at which the document was printed.

3.  The user agent must release the [storage mutex](#302.html_storage-mutex).

4.  The user agent should offer the user the opportunity to [obtain a physical form](#302.html_obtain-a-physical-form) (or the representation of a physical form) of the document. The user agent may wait for the user to either accept or decline before returning; if so, the user agent must [pause](#302.html_pause) while the method is waiting. Even if the user agent doesn't wait at this point, the user agent must use the state of the relevant documents as they are at this point in the algorithm if and when it eventually creates the alternate form.
