5.  The user agent must [fire a simple event](#302.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `afterprint` at the [`Window`](#302.html_window) object of the [`Document`](#302.html_document) that is being printed, as well as any [nested browsing contexts](#302.html_nested-browsing-context) in it.

    The `afterprint` event can be used to revert annotations added in the earlier event, as well as showing post-printing UI. For instance, if a page is walking the user through the steps of applying for a home loan, the script could automatically advance to the next step after having printed a form or other.

### 6.6 System state and capabilities

#### 6.6.1 The [`Navigator`](#304.html_navigator) object

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator">`navigator`</dfn> attribute of the [`Window`](#304.html_window) interface must return an instance of the [`Navigator`](#304.html_navigator) interface, which represents the identity and state of the user agent (the client), and allows Web pages to register themselves as potential protocol and content handlers:

```
interface Navigator {
  // objects implementing this interface also implement the interfaces given below
};
Navigator implements NavigatorID;
Navigator implements NavigatorLanguage;
Navigator implements NavigatorOnLine;
Navigator implements NavigatorContentUtils;
Navigator implements NavigatorStorageUtils;
Navigator implements NavigatorPlugins;
```

These interfaces are defined separately so that other specifications can re-use parts of the [`Navigator`](#304.html_navigator) interface.

##### 6.6.1.1 Client identification

```
[NoInterfaceObject]
interface NavigatorID {
  readonly attribute DOMString appCodeName; // constant "Mozilla"
  readonly attribute DOMString appName;
  readonly attribute DOMString appVersion;
  readonly attribute DOMString platform;
  readonly attribute DOMString product; // constant "Gecko"
  boolean taintEnabled(); // constant false
  readonly attribute DOMString userAgent;
};
```

In certain cases, despite the best efforts of the entire industry, Web browsers have bugs and limitations that Web authors are forced to work around.

This section defines a collection of attributes that can be used to determine, from script, the kind of user agent in use, in order to work around these issues.

Client detection should always be limited to detecting known current versions; future versions and unknown versions should always be assumed to be fully compliant.

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`appCodeName`](#304.html_dom-navigator-appcodename)

Returns the string "`Mozilla`".

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`appName`](#304.html_dom-navigator-appname)

Returns the name of the browser.

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`appVersion`](#304.html_dom-navigator-appversion)

Returns the version of the browser.

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`platform`](#304.html_dom-navigator-platform)

Returns the name of the platform.

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`product`](#304.html_dom-navigator-product)

Returns the string "`Gecko`".

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`taintEnabled`](#304.html_dom-navigator-taintenabled)()

Returns false.

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`userAgent`](#304.html_dom-navigator-useragent)

Returns the complete User-Agent header.

<dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-appcodename" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-appCodeName">`appCodeName`</dfn>

Must return the string "`Mozilla`".

<dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-appname" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-appName">`appName`</dfn>

Must return either the string "`Netscape`" or the full name of the browser, e.g. "`Mellblom Browsernator`".

<dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-appversion" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-appVersion">`appVersion`</dfn>

Must return either the string "`4.0`" or a string representing the version of the browser in detail, e.g. "`1.0 (VMS; en-US) Mellblomenator/9000`".

<dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-platform" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-platform">`platform`</dfn>

Must return either the empty string or a string representing the platform on which the browser is executing, e.g. "`MacIntel`", "`Win32`", "`FreeBSD i386`", "`WebTV OS`".

<dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-product" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-product">`product`</dfn>

Must return the string "`Gecko`".

<dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-taintenabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-taintEnabled">`taintEnabled()`</dfn>

Must return false.

<dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-useragent" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-userAgent">`userAgent`</dfn>

Must return the string used for the value of the "`User-Agent`" header in HTTP requests, or the empty string if no such header is ever sent.

Any information in this API that varies from user to user can be used to profile the user. In fact, if enough such information is available, a user can actually be uniquely identified. For this reason, user agent implementors are strongly urged to include as little information in this API as possible. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

##### 6.6.1.2 Language preferences

```
[NoInterfaceObject]
interface NavigatorLanguage {
  readonly attribute DOMString? language;
};
```

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`language`](#304.html_dom-navigator-language)

Returns a language tag representing the user's preferred language.

<dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-language" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-language">`language`</dfn>

Must return a valid BCP 47 language tag representing either [a plausible language](#304.html_a-plausible-language) or the user's preferred language. [[BCP47]](#304.html_refsBCP47)

To determine <dfn id="304.html_a-plausible-language">a plausible language</dfn>, the user agent should bear in mind the following:

*   Any information in this API that varies from user to user can be used to profile or identify the user. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)
*   If the user is not using a service that obfuscates the user's point of origin (e.g. the Tor anonymity network), then the value that is least likely to distinguish the user from other users with similar origins (e.g. from the same IP address block) is the language used by the majority of such users. [[TOR]](#304.html_refsTOR)
*   If the user is using an anonymizing service, then the value "`en-US`" is suggested; if all users of the service use that same value, that reduces the possibility of distinguishing the users from each other.

##### 6.6.1.3 Custom scheme and content handlers

```
[NoInterfaceObject]
interface NavigatorContentUtils {
  // content handler registration
  void registerProtocolHandler(DOMString scheme, DOMString url, DOMString title);
  void registerContentHandler(DOMString mimeType, DOMString url, DOMString title);
  void unregisterProtocolHandler(DOMString scheme, DOMString url);
  void unregisterContentHandler(DOMString mimeType, DOMString url);
};
```

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-registerprotocolhandler" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-registerProtocolHandler">`registerProtocolHandler()`</dfn> method allows Web sites to register themselves as possible handlers for particular schemes. For example, an online telephone messaging service could register itself as a handler of the `sms:` scheme, so that if the user clicks on such a link, he is given the opportunity to use that Web site. Analogously, the <dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-registercontenthandler" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-registerContentHandler">`registerContentHandler()`</dfn> method allows Web sites to register themselves as possible handlers for content in a particular [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type). For example, the same online telephone messaging service could register itself as a handler for `text/vcard` files, so that if the user has no native application capable of handling vCards, his Web browser can instead suggest he use that site to view contact information stored on vCards that he opens. [[RFC5724]](#304.html_refsRFC5724) [[RFC6350]](#304.html_refsRFC6350)

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`registerProtocolHandler`](#304.html_dom-navigator-registerprotocolhandler)(`scheme`, `url`, `title`)
`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`registerContentHandler`](#304.html_dom-navigator-registercontenthandler)(`mimeType`, `url`, `title`)

Registers a handler for the given scheme or content type, at the given URL, with the given title.

The string "`%s`" in the URL is used as a placeholder for where to put the URL of the content to be handled.

Throws a [`SecurityError`](#304.html_securityerror) exception if the user agent blocks the registration (this might happen if trying to register as a handler for "http", for instance).

Throws a [`SyntaxError`](#304.html_syntaxerror) exception if the "`%s`" string is missing in the URL.

User agents may, within the constraints described in this section, do whatever they like when the methods are called. A UA could, for instance, prompt the user and offer the user the opportunity to add the site to a shortlist of handlers, or make the handlers his default, or cancel the request. UAs could provide such a UI through modal UI or through a non-modal transient notification interface. UAs could also simply silently collect the information, providing it only when relevant to the user.

User agents should keep track of which sites have registered handlers (even if the user has declined such registrations) so that the user is not repeatedly prompted with the same request.

The arguments to the methods have the following meanings and corresponding implementation requirements. The requirements that involve throwing exceptions must be processed in the order given below, stopping at the first exception thrown. (So the exceptions for the first argument take precedence over the exceptions for the second argument.)

`scheme` ([`registerProtocolHandler()`](#304.html_dom-navigator-registerprotocolhandler) only)

A scheme, such as `mailto` or `web+auth`. The scheme must be compared in an [ASCII case-insensitive](#304.html_ascii-case-insensitive) manner by user agents for the purposes of comparing with the scheme part of URLs that they consider against the list of registered handlers.

The `scheme` value, if it contains a colon (as in "`mailto:`"), will never match anything, since schemes don't contain colons.

If the [`registerProtocolHandler()`](#304.html_dom-navigator-registerprotocolhandler) method is invoked with a scheme that is neither a [whitelisted scheme](#304.html_whitelisted-scheme) nor a scheme whose value starts with the substring "`web+`" and otherwise contains only [lowercase ASCII letters](#304.html_lowercase-ascii-letters), and whose length is at least five characters (including the "`web+`" prefix), the user agent must throw a [`SecurityError`](#304.html_securityerror) exception.

The following schemes are the <dfn id="304.html_whitelisted-scheme" data-anolis-xref="whitelisted scheme">whitelisted schemes</dfn>:

*   `bitcoin`
*   `geo`
*   `im`
*   `irc`
*   `ircs`
*   `magnet`
*   `mailto`
*   `mms`
*   `news`
*   `nntp`
*   `sip`
*   `sms`
*   `smsto`
*   `ssh`
*   `tel`
*   `urn`
*   `webcal`
*   `wtai`
*   `xmpp`

This list can be changed. If there are schemes that should be added, please send feedback.

This list excludes any schemes that could reasonably be expected to be supported inline, e.g. in an [`iframe`](#304.html_the-iframe-element), such as `http` or (more theoretically) `gopher`. If those were supported, they could potentially be used in man-in-the-middle attacks, by replacing pages that have frames with such content with content under the control of the protocol handler. If the user agent has native support for the schemes, this could further be used for cookie-theft attacks.

`mimeType` ([`registerContentHandler()`](#304.html_dom-navigator-registercontenthandler) only)

A [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type), such as `model/vnd.flatland.3dml` or `application/vnd.google-earth.kml+xml`. The [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type) must be compared in an [ASCII case-insensitive](#304.html_ascii-case-insensitive) manner by user agents for the purposes of comparing with MIME types of documents that they consider against the list of registered handlers.

User agents must compare the given values only to the MIME type/subtype parts of content types, not to the complete type including parameters. Thus, if `mimeType` values passed to this method include characters such as commas or whitespace, or include MIME parameters, then the handler being registered will never be used.

The type is compared to the [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type) used by the user agent *after* the sniffing algorithms have been applied.

If the [`registerContentHandler()`](#304.html_dom-navigator-registercontenthandler) method is invoked with a [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type) that is in the [type blacklist](#304.html_type-blacklist) or that the user agent has deemed a privileged type, the user agent must throw a [`SecurityError`](#304.html_securityerror) exception.

The following [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type) are in the <dfn id="304.html_type-blacklist">type blacklist</dfn>:

*   [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#304.html_application/x-www-form-urlencoded)
*   [`application/xhtml+xml`](#304.html_application/xhtml+xml)
*   `application/xml`
*   `image/gif`
*   `image/jpeg`
*   `image/png`
*   `image/svg+xml`
*   [`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#304.html_multipart/x-mixed-replace)
*   [`text/cache-manifest`](#304.html_text/cache-manifest)
*   `text/css`
*   [`text/html`](#304.html_text/html)
*   `text/ping`
*   `text/plain`
*   `text/xml`
*   All types that the user agent supports displaying natively in a [browsing context](#304.html_browsing-context) during [navigation](#304.html_navigate), except for `application/rss+xml` and `application/atom+xml`

This list can be changed. If there are MIME types that should be added, please send feedback.

`url`

A string used to build the URL of the page that will handle the requests.

User agents must throw a [`SyntaxError`](#304.html_syntaxerror) exception if the `url` argument passed to one of these methods does not contain the exact literal string "[`%s`](#304.html_the-s-element)".

User agents must throw a [`SyntaxError`](#304.html_syntaxerror) exception if [resolving](#304.html_resolve-a-url) the `url` argument relative to the [API base URL](#304.html_api-base-url) specified by the [entry settings object](#304.html_entry-settings-object) is not successful.

The resulting [absolute URL](#304.html_absolute-url) would by definition not be a [valid URL](#304.html_valid-url) as it would include the string "`%s`" which is not a valid component in a URL.

User agents must throw a [`SecurityError`](#304.html_securityerror) exception if the resulting [absolute URL](#304.html_absolute-url) has an [origin](#304.html_origin-0) that differs from the [origin](#304.html_origin-0) specified by the [entry settings object](#304.html_entry-settings-object).

This is forcibly the case if the `%s` placeholder is in the scheme, host, or port parts of the URL.

The resulting [absolute URL](#304.html_absolute-url) is the <dfn id="304.html_proto-url">proto-URL</dfn>. It identifies the handler for the purposes of the methods described below.

When the user agent uses this handler, it must replace the first occurrence of the exact literal string "`%s`" in the `url` argument with an escaped version of the [absolute URL](#304.html_absolute-url) of the content in question (as defined below), then [resolve](#304.html_resolve-a-url) the resulting URL, relative to the [API base URL](#304.html_api-base-url) specified by the [entry settings object](#304.html_entry-settings-object) at the time the [`registerContentHandler()`](#304.html_dom-navigator-registercontenthandler) or [`registerProtocolHandler()`](#304.html_dom-navigator-registerprotocolhandler) methods were invoked, and then [navigate](#304.html_navigate) an appropriate [browsing context](#304.html_browsing-context) to the resulting URL using the GET method ([or equivalent](#304.html_concept-http-equivalent-get) for non-HTTP URLs).

To get the escaped version of the [absolute URL](#304.html_absolute-url) of the content in question, the user agent must replace every character in that [absolute URL](#304.html_absolute-url) that is not a character in the URL [default encode set](#304.html_default-encode-set) with the result of [UTF-8 percent encoding](#304.html_utf-8-percent-encode) that character.

If the user had visited a site at `http://example.com/` that made the following call:

```
navigator.registerContentHandler('application/x-soup', 'soup?url=%s', 'SoupWeb?')
```

...and then, much later, while visiting `http://www.example.net/`, clicked on a link such as:

```
<a href="chickenk?wi.soup">Download our Chicken K?wi soup!</a>
```

...then, assuming this `chickenk?wi.soup` file was served with the [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type) `application/x-soup`, the UA might navigate to the following URL:

```
http://example.com/soup?url=http://www.example.net/chickenk%C3%AFwi.soup
```

This site could then fetch the `chickenk?wi.soup` file and do whatever it is that it does with soup (synthesize it and ship it to the user, or whatever).

`title`

A descriptive title of the handler, which the UA might use to remind the user what the site in question is.

This section does not define how the pages registered by these methods are used, beyond the requirements on how to process the `url` value (see above). To some extent, the [processing model for navigating across documents](#304.html_navigate) defines some cases where these methods are relevant, but in general UAs may use this information wherever they would otherwise consider handing content to native plugins or helper applications.

UAs must not use registered content handlers to handle content that was returned as part of a non-GET transaction (or rather, as part of any non-idempotent transaction), as the remote site would not be able to fetch the same data.

* * *

In addition to the registration methods, there are also methods for determining if particular handlers have been registered, and for unregistering handlers.

`state` = `window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`unregisterProtocolHandler`](#304.html_dom-navigator-unregisterprotocolhandler)(`scheme`, `url`)
`state` = `window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`unregisterContentHandler`](#304.html_dom-navigator-unregistercontenthandler)(`mimeType`, `url`)

Unregisters the handler given by the arguments.

The <dfn id="304.html_handler-state-string" data-anolis-xref="handler state string">handler state strings</dfn> are the following strings. Each string describes several situations, as given by the following list.

`new`

The described handler has never been registered for the given scheme or type.

The described handler was once registered for the given scheme or type, but the site has since unregistered it. If the handler were to be reregistered, the user would be notified accordingly.

The described handler was once registered for the given scheme or type, but the site has since unregistered it, but the user has indicated that the site is to be blocked from registering the type again, so the user agent would ignore further registration attempts.

`registered`

An attempt was made to register the described handler for the given scheme or type, but the user has not yet been notified, and the user agent would ignore further registration attempts. (Maybe the user agent batches registration requests to display them when the user requests to be notified about them, and the user has not yet requested that the user agent notify it of the previous registration attempt.)

The described handler is registered for the given scheme or type (maybe, or maybe not, as the default handler).

The described handler is permanently blocked from being (re)registered. (Maybe the user marked the registration attempt as spam, or blocked the site for other reasons.)

`declined`

An attempt was made to register the described handler for the given scheme or type, but the user has not yet been notified; however, the user might be notified if another registration attempt were to be made. (Maybe the last registration attempt was made while the page was in the background and the user closed the page without looking at it, and the user agent requires confirmation for this registration attempt.)

An attempt was made to register the described handler for the given scheme or type, but the user has not yet responded.

An attempt was made to register the described handler for the given scheme or type, but the user declined the offer. The user has not indicated that the handler is to be permanently blocked, however, so another attempt to register the described handler might result in the user being prompted again.

The described handler was once registered for the given scheme or type, but the user has since removed it. The user has not indicated that the handler is to be permanently blocked, however, so another attempt to register the described handler might result in the user being prompted again.

* * *

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-unregisterprotocolhandler" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-unregisterProtocolHandler">`unregisterProtocolHandler()`</dfn> method must unregister the handler described by the two arguments to the method, where the first argument gives the scheme and the second gives the string used to build the URL of the page that will handle the requests.

The first argument must be compared to the schemes for which custom protocol handlers are registered in an [ASCII case-insensitive](#304.html_ascii-case-insensitive) manner to find the relevant handlers.

The second argument must be preprocessed as described below, and if that is successful, must then be matched against the [proto-URLs](#304.html_proto-url) of the relevant handlers to find the described handler.

* * *

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-unregistercontenthandler" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-unregisterContentHandler">`unregisterContentHandler()`</dfn> method must unregister the handler described by the two arguments to the method, where the first argument gives the [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type) and the second gives the string used to build the URL of the page that will handle the requests.

The first argument must be compared to the [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type) for which custom content handlers are registered in an [ASCII case-insensitive](#304.html_ascii-case-insensitive) manner to find the relevant handlers.

The second argument must be preprocessed as described below, and if that is successful, must then be matched against the [proto-URLs](#304.html_proto-url) of the relevant handlers to find the described handler.

* * *

The second argument of the four methods described above must be preprocessed as follows:

1.  If the string does not contain the substring "`%s`", abort these steps. There's no matching handler.

2.  [Resolve](#304.html_resolve-a-url) the string relative to the [API base URL](#304.html_api-base-url) specified by the [entry settings object](#304.html_entry-settings-object).

3.  If this fails, then throw a [`SyntaxError`](#304.html_syntaxerror) exception, aborting the method.

4.  If the resulting [absolute URL](#304.html_absolute-url)'s [origin](#304.html_origin-0) is not the [same origin](#304.html_same-origin) as the [origin](#304.html_origin-0) specified by the [entry settings object](#304.html_entry-settings-object), throw a [`SecurityError`](#304.html_securityerror) exception, aborting the method.

5.  Return the resulting [absolute URL](#304.html_absolute-url) as the result of preprocessing the argument.

###### 6.6.1.3.1 Security and privacy

These mechanisms can introduce a number of concerns, in particular privacy concerns.

**Hijacking all Web usage.** User agents should not allow schemes that are key to its normal operation, such as `http` or `https`, to be rerouted through third-party sites. This would allow a user's activities to be trivially tracked, and would allow user information, even in secure connections, to be collected.

**Hijacking defaults.** User agents are strongly urged to not automatically change any defaults, as this could lead the user to send data to remote hosts that the user is not expecting. New handlers registering themselves should never automatically cause those sites to be used.

**Registration spamming.** User agents should consider the possibility that a site will attempt to register a large number of handlers, possibly from multiple domains (e.g. by redirecting through a series of pages each on a different domain, and each registering a handler for `video/mpeg` — analogous practices abusing other Web browser features have been used by pornography Web sites for many years). User agents should gracefully handle such hostile attempts, protecting the user.

**Misleading titles.** User agents should not rely wholly on the `title` argument to the methods when presenting the registered handlers to the user, since sites could easily lie. For example, a site `hostile.example.net` could claim that it was registering the "Cuddly Bear Happy Content Handler". User agents should therefore use the handler's domain in any UI along with any title.

**Hostile handler metadata.** User agents should protect against typical attacks against strings embedded in their interface, for example ensuring that markup or escape characters in such strings are not executed, that null bytes are properly handled, that over-long strings do not cause crashes or buffer overruns, and so forth.

**Leaking Intranet URLs.** The mechanism described in this section can result in secret Intranet URLs being leaked, in the following manner:

1.  The user registers a third-party content handler as the default handler for a content type.
2.  The user then browses his corporate Intranet site and accesses a document that uses that content type.
3.  The user agent contacts the third party and hands the third party the URL to the Intranet content.

No actual confidential file data is leaked in this manner, but the URLs themselves could contain confidential information. For example, the URL could be `http://www.corp.example.com/upcoming-aquisitions/the-sample-company.egf`, which might tell the third party that Example Corporation is intending to merge with The Sample Company. Implementors might wish to consider allowing administrators to disable this feature for certain subdomains, content types, or schemes.

**Leaking secure URLs.** User agents should not send HTTPS URLs to third-party sites registered as content handlers without the user's informed consent, for the same reason that user agents sometimes avoid sending `Referer` (sic) HTTP headers from secure sites to third-party sites.

**Leaking credentials.** User agents must never send username or password information in the URLs that are escaped and included sent to the handler sites. User agents may even avoid attempting to pass to Web-based handlers the URLs of resources that are known to require authentication to access, as such sites would be unable to access the resources in question without prompting the user for credentials themselves (a practice that would require the user to know whether to trust the third-party handler, a decision many users are unable to make or even understand).

**Interface interference.** User agents should be prepared to handle intentionally long arguments to the methods. For example, if the user interface exposed consists of an "accept" button and a "deny" button, with the "accept" binding containing the name of the handler, it's important that a long name not cause the "deny" button to be pushed off the screen.

**Fingerprinting users.** Since a site can detect if it has attempted to register a particular handler or not, whether or not the user responds, the mechanism can be used to store data. User agents are therefore strongly urged to treat registrations in the same manner as cookies: clearing cookies for a site should also clear all registrations for that site, and disabling cookies for a site should also disable registrations.

###### 6.6.1.3.2 Sample user interface

*This section is non-normative.*

A simple implementation of this feature for a desktop Web browser might work as follows.

The [`registerContentHandler()`](#304.html_dom-navigator-registercontenthandler) method could display a modal dialog box:

![The modal dialog box could have the title 'Content Handler Registration', and could say 'This Web page: Kittens at work http://kittens.example.org/ ...would like permission to handle files of type: application/x-meowmeow using the following Web-based application: Kittens-at-work displayer http://kittens.example.org/?show=%s Do you trust the administrators of the "kittens.example.org" domain?' with two buttons, 'Trust kittens.example.org' and 'Cancel'.](Images/040446c28207b0ba85e445fe86d19fa6.jpg)

In this dialog box, "Kittens at work" is the title of the page that invoked the method, "http://kittens.example.org/" is the URL of that page, "application/x-meowmeow" is the string that was passed to the [`registerContentHandler()`](#304.html_dom-navigator-registercontenthandler) method as its first argument (`mimeType`), "http://kittens.example.org/?show=%s" was the second argument (`url`), and "Kittens-at-work displayer" was the third argument (`title`).

If the user clicks the Cancel button, then nothing further happens. If the user clicks the "Trust" button, then the handler is remembered.

When the user then attempts to fetch a URL that uses the "application/x-meowmeow" [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type), then it might display a dialog as follows:

![The dialog box could have the title 'Unknown File Type' and could say 'You have attempted to access:' followed by a URL, followed by a prompt such as 'How would you like FerretBrowser to handle this resource?' with three radio buttons, one saying 'Contact the FerretBrowser plugin registry to see if there is an official way to handle this resource.', one saying 'Pass this URL to a local application' with an application selector, and one saying 'Pass this URL to the "Kittens-at-work displayer" application at "kittens.example.org"', with a checkbox labeled 'Always do this for resources using the "application/x-meowmeow" type in future.', and with two buttons, 'Ok' and 'Cancel'.](Images/04fefda4f75b5a358a3879ede344869f.jpg)

In this dialog, the third option is the one that was primed by the site registering itself earlier.

If the user does select that option, then the browser, in accordance with the requirements described in the previous two sections, will redirect the user to "http://kittens.example.org/?show=data%3Aapplication/x-meowmeow;base64,S2l0dGVucyBhcmUgdGhlIGN1dGVzdCE%253D".

The [`registerProtocolHandler()`](#304.html_dom-navigator-registerprotocolhandler) method would work equivalently, but for schemes instead of unknown content types.

##### 6.6.1.4 Manually releasing the storage mutex

```
[NoInterfaceObject]
interface NavigatorStorageUtils {
  readonly attribute boolean cookieEnabled;
  void yieldForStorageUpdates();
};
```

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`cookieEnabled`](#304.html_dom-navigator-cookieenabled)

Returns false if setting a cookie will be ignored, and true otherwise.

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`yieldForStorageUpdates`](#304.html_dom-navigator-yieldforstorageupdates)()

If a script uses the [`document.cookie`](#304.html_dom-document-cookie) API, or the `localStorage` API, the browser will block other scripts from accessing cookies or storage until the first script finishes. [[WEBSTORAGE]](#304.html_refsWEBSTORAGE)

Calling the [`navigator.yieldForStorageUpdates()`](#304.html_dom-navigator-yieldforstorageupdates) method tells the user agent to unblock any other scripts that may be blocked, even though the script hasn't returned.

Values of cookies and items in the `Storage` objects of `localStorage` attributes can change after calling this method, whence its name. [[WEBSTORAGE]](#304.html_refsWEBSTORAGE)

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-cookieenabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-cookieEnabled">`cookieEnabled`</dfn> attribute must return true if the user agent attempts to handle cookies according to the cookie specification, and false if it ignores cookie change requests. [[COOKIES]](#304.html_refsCOOKIES)

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-yieldforstorageupdates" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-yieldForStorageUpdates">`yieldForStorageUpdates()`</dfn> method, when invoked, must, if the [storage mutex](#304.html_storage-mutex) is owned by the [event loop](#304.html_event-loop) of the [task](#304.html_concept-task) that resulted in the method being called, release the [storage mutex](#304.html_storage-mutex) so that it is once again free. Otherwise, it must do nothing.

##### 6.6.1.5 Plugins

```
[NoInterfaceObject]
interface NavigatorPlugins {
  readonly attribute PluginArray plugins;
  readonly attribute MimeTypeArray mimeTypes;
  readonly attribute boolean javaEnabled;
};

interface PluginArray {
  void refresh(optional boolean reload = false);
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter Plugin? item(unsigned long index);
  getter Plugin? namedItem(DOMString name);
};

interface MimeTypeArray {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter MimeType? item(unsigned long index);
  getter MimeType? namedItem(DOMString name);
};

interface Plugin {
  readonly attribute DOMString name;
  readonly attribute DOMString description;
  readonly attribute DOMString filename;
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter MimeType? item(unsigned long index);
  getter MimeType? namedItem(DOMString name);
};

interface MimeType {
  readonly attribute DOMString type;
  readonly attribute DOMString description;
  readonly attribute DOMString suffixes; // comma-separated
  readonly attribute Plugin enabledPlugin;
};
```

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`plugins`](#304.html_dom-navigator-plugins) . [`refresh`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-refresh)( [ `refresh` ] )

Updates the lists of supported plugins and MIME types for this page, and reloads the page if the lists have changed.

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`plugins`](#304.html_dom-navigator-plugins) . [`length`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-length)

Returns the number of plugins, represented by [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) objects, that the user agent reports.

`plugin` = `window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`plugins`](#304.html_dom-navigator-plugins) . [`item`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-item)(`index`)
`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`plugins`](#304.html_dom-navigator-plugins)[`index`]

Returns the specified [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object.

`plugin` = `window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`plugins`](#304.html_dom-navigator-plugins) . [`item`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-item)(`name`)
`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`plugins`](#304.html_dom-navigator-plugins)[`name`]

Returns the [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object for the plugin with the given name.

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . `mimeTypes` . [`length`](#304.html_dom-mimetypearray-length)

Returns the number of MIME types, represented by [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) objects, supported by the plugins that the user agent reports.

`mimeType` = `window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . `mimeTypes` . [`item`](#304.html_dom-mimetypearray-item)(`index`)
`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . `mimeTypes`[`index`]

Returns the specified [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) object.

`mimeType` = `window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . `mimeTypes` . [`item`](#304.html_dom-mimetypearray-item)(`name`)
`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . `mimeTypes`[`name`]

Returns the [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) object for the given MIME type.

`plugin` . [`name`](#304.html_dom-plugin-name)

Returns the plugin's name.

`plugin` . [`description`](#304.html_dom-plugin-description)

Returns the plugin's description.

`plugin` . [`filename`](#304.html_dom-plugin-filename)

Returns the plugin library's filename, if applicable on the current platform.

`plugin` . [`length`](#304.html_dom-plugin-length)

Returns the number of MIME types, represented by [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) objects, supported by the plugin.

`mimeType` = `plugin` . [`item`](#304.html_dom-plugin-item)(`index`)
`plugin`[`index`]

Returns the specified [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) object.

`mimeType` = `plugin` . [`item`](#304.html_dom-plugin-item)(`name`)
`plugin`[`name`]

Returns the [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) object for the given MIME type.

`mimeType` . [`type`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-type)

Returns the MIME type.

`mimeType` . [`description`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-description)

Returns the MIME type's description.

`mimeType` . [`suffixes`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-suffixes)

Returns the MIME type's typical file extensions, in a comma-separated list.

`mimeType` . [`enabledPlugin`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-enabledplugin)

Returns the [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object that implements this MIME type.

`window` . [`navigator`](#304.html_dom-navigator) . [`javaEnabled`](#304.html_dom-navigator-javaenabled)

Returns true if there's a plugin that supports the MIME type "`application/x-java-vm`".

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-plugins" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-plugins">`navigator.plugins`</dfn> attribute must return a [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object. The same object must be returned each time.

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-mimetypes" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-mimeTypes">`navigator.mimeTypes`</dfn> attribute must return a [`MimeTypeArray`](#304.html_mimetypearray) object. The same object must be returned each time.

* * *

A [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object represents none, some, or all of the [plugins](#304.html_plugin) supported by the user agent, each of which is represented by a [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object. Each of these [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) objects may be <dfn id="304.html_hidden-plugin" data-anolis-xref="hidden plugin">hidden plugins</dfn>. A [hidden plugin](#304.html_hidden-plugin) can't be enumerated, but can still be inspected by using its name.

The fewer [plugins](#304.html_plugin) are represented by the [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object, and of those, the more that are [hidden](#304.html_hidden-plugin), the more the user's privacy will be protected. Each exposed plugin increases the number of bits that can be derived for fingerprinting. Hiding a plugin helps, but unless it is an extremely rare plugin, it is likely that a site attempting to derive the list of plugins can still determine whether the plugin is supported or not by probing for it by name (the names of popular plugins are widely known). Therefore not exposing a plugin at all is preferred. Unfortunately, many legacy sites use this feature to determine, for example, which plugin to use to play video. Not exposing any plugins at all might therefore not be entirely plausible.

The [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) objects created by a user agent must not be [live](#304.html_live). The set of plugins represented by the objects must not change once an object is created, except when it is updated by the [`refresh()`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-refresh) method.

Each [plugin](#304.html_plugin) represented by a [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) can support a number of [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type). For each such [plugin](#304.html_plugin), the user agent must pick one or more of these [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type) to be those that are <dfn id="304.html_explicitly-supported">explicitly supported</dfn>.

The [explicitly supported](#304.html_explicitly-supported) [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type) of a [plugin](#304.html_plugin) are those that are exposed through the [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) and [`MimeTypeArray`](#304.html_mimetypearray) interfaces. As with [plugins](#304.html_plugin) themselves, any variation between users regarding what is exposed allows sites to fingerprint users. User agents are therefore encouraged to expose the same [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type) for all users of a [plugin](#304.html_plugin), regardless of the actual types supported... at least, within the constraints imposed by compatibility with legacy content.

The [supported property indices](#304.html_supported-property-indices) of a [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object are the numbers from zero to the number of non-[hidden](#304.html_hidden-plugin) [plugins](#304.html_plugin) represented by the object, if any. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-pluginarray-length" data-anolis-xref="dom-PluginArray-length">`length`</dfn> attribute must return the number of non-[hidden](#304.html_hidden-plugin) [plugins](#304.html_plugin) represented by the object. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-pluginarray-item" data-anolis-xref="dom-PluginArray-item">`item()`</dfn> method of a [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object must return null if the argument is not one of the object's [supported property indices](#304.html_supported-property-indices), and otherwise must return the result of running the following steps, using the method's argument as `index`:

1.  Let `list` be the [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) objects representing the non-[hidden](#304.html_hidden-plugin) [plugins](#304.html_plugin) represented by the [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object.

2.  Sort `list` alphabetically by the [`name`](#304.html_dom-plugin-name) of each [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin).

3.  Return the `index`th entry in `list`.

It is important [for privacy](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector) that the order of plugins not leak additional information, e.g. the order in which plugins were installed.

The [supported property names](#304.html_supported-property-names) of a [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object are the values of the [`name`](#304.html_dom-plugin-name) attributes of all the [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) objects represented by the [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object. The properties exposed in this way must not be enumerable. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-pluginarray-nameditem" data-anolis-xref="dom-PluginArray-namedItem">`namedItem()`</dfn> method of a [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object must return null if the argument is not one of the object's [supported property names](#304.html_supported-property-names), and otherwise must return the [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object, of those represented by the [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object, that has a [`name`](#304.html_dom-plugin-name) equal to the method's argument.

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-pluginarray-refresh" data-anolis-xref="dom-PluginArray-refresh">`refresh()`</dfn> method of the [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object of a [`Navigator`](#304.html_navigator) object, when invoked, must check to see if any [plugins](#304.html_plugin) have been installed or reconfigured since the user agent created the [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object. If so, and the method's argument is true, then the user agent must act as if the [`location.reload()`](#304.html_dom-location-reload) method was called instead. Otherwise, the user agent must update the [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object and [`MimeTypeArray`](#304.html_mimetypearray) object created for attributes of that [`Navigator`](#304.html_navigator) object, and the [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) and [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) objects created for those [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) and [`MimeTypeArray`](#304.html_mimetypearray) objects, using the same [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) objects for cases where the [`name`](#304.html_dom-plugin-name) is the same, and the same [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) objects for cases where the [`type`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-type) is the same, and creating new objects for cases where there were no matching objects immediately prior to the [`refresh()`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-refresh) call. Old [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) and [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) objects must continue to return the same values that they had prior to the update, though naturally now the data is stale and may appear inconsistent (for example, an old [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) entry might list as its [`enabledPlugin`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-enabledplugin) a [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object that no longer lists that [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) as a supported [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype)).

* * *

A [`MimeTypeArray`](#304.html_mimetypearray) object represents the [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type) [explicitly supported](#304.html_explicitly-supported) by [plugins](#304.html_plugin) supported by the user agent, each of which is represented by a [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) object.

The [`MimeTypeArray`](#304.html_mimetypearray) objects created by a user agent must not be [live](#304.html_live). The set of MIME types represented by the objects must not change once an object is created, except when it is updated by the [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object's [`refresh()`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-refresh) method.

The [supported property indices](#304.html_supported-property-indices) of a [`MimeTypeArray`](#304.html_mimetypearray) object are the numbers from zero to the number of [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type) [explicitly supported](#304.html_explicitly-supported) by non-[hidden](#304.html_hidden-plugin) [plugins](#304.html_plugin) represented by the corresponding [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object, if any. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-mimetypearray-length" data-anolis-xref="dom-MimeTypeArray-length">`length`</dfn> attribute must return the number of [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type) [explicitly supported](#304.html_explicitly-supported) by non-[hidden](#304.html_hidden-plugin) [plugins](#304.html_plugin) represented by the corresponding [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object, if any. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-mimetypearray-item" data-anolis-xref="dom-MimeTypeArray-item">`item()`</dfn> method of a [`MimeTypeArray`](#304.html_mimetypearray) object must return null if the argument is not one of the object's [supported property indices](#304.html_supported-property-indices), and otherwise must return the result of running the following steps, using the method's argument as `index`:

1.  Let `list` be the [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) objects representing the [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type) [explicitly supported](#304.html_explicitly-supported) by non-[hidden](#304.html_hidden-plugin) [plugins](#304.html_plugin) represented by the corresponding [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object, if any.

2.  Sort `list` alphabetically by the [`type`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-type) of each [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype).

3.  Return the `index`th entry in `list`.

It is important [for privacy](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector) that the order of MIME types not leak additional information, e.g. the order in which plugins were installed.

The [supported property names](#304.html_supported-property-names) of a [`MimeTypeArray`](#304.html_mimetypearray) object are the values of the [`type`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-type) attributes of all the [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) objects represented by the [`MimeTypeArray`](#304.html_mimetypearray) object. The properties exposed in this way must not be enumerable. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-mimetypearray-nameditem" data-anolis-xref="dom-MimeTypeArray-namedItem">`namedItem()`</dfn> method of a [`MimeTypeArray`](#304.html_mimetypearray) object must return null if the argument is not one of the object's [supported property names](#304.html_supported-property-names), and otherwise must return the [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) object that has a [`type`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-type) equal to the method's argument.

* * *

A [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object represents a [plugin](#304.html_plugin). It has several attributes to provide details about the plugin, and can be enumerated to obtain the list of [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type) that it [explicitly supports](#304.html_explicitly-supported).

The [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) objects created by a user agent must not be [live](#304.html_live). The set of MIME types represented by the objects, and the values of the objects' attributes, must not change once an object is created, except when updated by the [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object's [`refresh()`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-refresh) method.

The <dfn id="304.html_reported-mime-types">reported MIME types</dfn> for a [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object are the [MIME types](#304.html_mime-type) [explicitly supported](#304.html_explicitly-supported) by the corresponding [plugin](#304.html_plugin) when this object was last created or updated by [`PluginArray.refresh()`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-refresh), whichever happened most recently.

The [supported property indices](#304.html_supported-property-indices) of a [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object are the numbers from zero to the number of [reported MIME types](#304.html_reported-mime-types). [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-plugin-length" data-anolis-xref="dom-Plugin-length">`length`</dfn> attribute must return the number of [reported MIME types](#304.html_reported-mime-types). [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-plugin-item" data-anolis-xref="dom-Plugin-item">`item()`</dfn> method of a [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object must return null if the argument is not one of the object's [supported property indices](#304.html_supported-property-indices), and otherwise must return the result of running the following steps, using the method's argument as `index`:

1.  Let `list` be the [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) objects representing the [reported MIME types](#304.html_reported-mime-types).

2.  Sort `list` alphabetically by the [`type`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-type) of each [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype).

3.  Return the `index`th entry in `list`.

It is important [for privacy](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector) that the order of MIME types not leak additional information, e.g. the order in which plugins were installed.

The [supported property names](#304.html_supported-property-names) of a [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object are the values of the [`type`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-type) attributes of the [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) objects representing the [reported MIME types](#304.html_reported-mime-types). The properties exposed in this way must not be enumerable. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-plugin-nameditem" data-anolis-xref="dom-Plugin-namedItem">`namedItem()`</dfn> method of a [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object must return null if the argument is not one of the object's [supported property names](#304.html_supported-property-names), and otherwise must return the [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) object that has a [`type`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-type) equal to the method's argument.

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-plugin-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-Plugin-name">`name`</dfn> attribute must return the [plugin](#304.html_plugin)'s name.

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-plugin-description" data-anolis-xref="dom-Plugin-description">`description`</dfn> and <dfn id="304.html_dom-plugin-filename" data-anolis-xref="dom-Plugin-filename">`filename`</dfn> attributes must return user-agent-defined (or, in all likelihood, [plugin](#304.html_plugin)-defined) strings. In each case, the same string must be returned each time, except that the strings returned may change when the [`PluginArray.refresh()`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-refresh) method updates the object.

If the values returned by the [`description`](#304.html_dom-plugin-description) or [`filename`](#304.html_dom-plugin-filename) attributes vary between versions of a [plugin](#304.html_plugin), they can be used both as a fingerprinting vector and, even more importantly, as a trivial way to determine what security vulnerabilities a [plugin](#304.html_plugin) (and thus a browser) may have. It is thus highly recommended that the [`description`](#304.html_dom-plugin-description) attribute just return the same value as the [`name`](#304.html_dom-plugin-name) attribute, and that the [`filename`](#304.html_dom-plugin-filename) attribute return the empty string. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

* * *

A [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) object represents a [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type) that is, or was, [explicitly supported](#304.html_explicitly-supported) by a [plugin](#304.html_plugin).

The [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) objects created by a user agent must not be [live](#304.html_live). The values of the objects' attributes must not change once an object is created, except when updated by the [`PluginArray`](#304.html_pluginarray) object's [`refresh()`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-refresh) method.

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-mimetype-type" data-anolis-xref="dom-MimeType-type">`type`</dfn> attribute must return the [valid MIME type with no parameters](#304.html_valid-mime-type-with-no-parameters) describing the [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type).

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-mimetype-description" data-anolis-xref="dom-MimeType-description">`description`</dfn> and <dfn id="304.html_dom-mimetype-suffixes" data-anolis-xref="dom-MimeType-suffixes">`suffixes`</dfn> attributes must return user-agent-defined (or, in all likelihood, [plugin](#304.html_plugin)-defined) strings. In each case, the same string must be returned each time, except that the strings returned may change when the [`PluginArray.refresh()`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-refresh) method updates the object.

If the values returned by the [`description`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-description) or [`suffxies`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-suffixes) attributes vary between versions of a [plugin](#304.html_plugin), they can be used both as a fingerprinting vector and, even more importantly, as a trivial way to determine what security vulnerabilities a [plugin](#304.html_plugin) (and thus a browser) may have. It is thus highly recommended that the [`description`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-description) attribute just return the same value as the [`type`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-type) attribute, and that the [`suffixes`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-suffixes) attribute return the empty string. [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

Commas in the [`suffixes`](#304.html_dom-mimetype-suffixes) attribute are interpreted as separating subsequent filename extensions, as in "`htm,html`".

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-mimetype-enabledplugin" data-anolis-xref="dom-MimeType-enabledPlugin">`enabledPlugin`</dfn> attribute must return the [`Plugin`](#304.html_dom-plugin) object that represents the [plugin](#304.html_plugin) that [explicitly supported](#304.html_explicitly-supported) the [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type) that this [`MimeType`](#304.html_mimetype) object represents when this object was last created or updated by [`PluginArray.refresh()`](#304.html_dom-pluginarray-refresh), whichever happened most recently.

* * *

The <dfn id="304.html_dom-navigator-javaenabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-navigator-javaEnabled">`navigator.javaEnabled`</dfn> attribute must return true if the user agent supports a [plugin](#304.html_plugin) that supports the [MIME type](#304.html_mime-type) "`application/x-java-vm`". [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/64745a2f2ee97bc037f40c5ff381ec4b.jpg)](#304.html_fingerprinting-vector)

#### 6.6.2 The [`External`](#305.html_external) interface

The <dfn id="305.html_dom-external" data-anolis-xref="dom-external">`external`</dfn> attribute of the [`Window`](#305.html_window) interface must return an instance of the [`External`](#305.html_external) interface. The same object must be returned each time.

```
interface External {
  void AddSearchProvider(DOMString engineURL);
  unsigned long IsSearchProviderInstalled(DOMString engineURL);
};
```

`window` . [`external`](#305.html_dom-external) . [`AddSearchProvider`](#305.html_dom-external-addsearchprovider)( `url` )

Adds the search engine described by the OpenSearch description document at `url`. [[OPENSEARCH]](#305.html_refsOPENSEARCH)

The OpenSearch description document has to be on the same server as the script that calls this method.

`installed` = `window` . [`external`](#305.html_dom-external) . [`IsSearchProviderInstalled`](#305.html_dom-external-issearchproviderinstalled)( `url` )

Returns a value based on comparing `url` to the URLs of the results pages of the installed search engines.

0

None of the installed search engines match `url`.

1

One or more installed search engines match `url`, but none are the user's default search engine.

2

The user's default search engine matches `url`.

The `url` is compared to the URLs of the results pages of the installed search engines using a prefix match. Only results pages on the same domain as the script that calls this method are checked.

Another way of exposing search engines using OpenSearch description documents is using a [`link`](#305.html_the-link-element) element with the [`search`](#305.html_link-type-search) link type.

The <dfn id="305.html_dom-external-addsearchprovider" data-anolis-xref="dom-external-AddSearchProvider">`AddSearchProvider()`</dfn> method, when invoked, must run the following steps:

1.  Optionally, abort these steps. User agents may implement the method as a stub method that never does anything, or may arbitrarily ignore invocations with particular arguments for security, privacy, or usability reasons.

2.  [Resolve](#305.html_resolve-a-url) the value of the method's first argument relative to the [API base URL](#305.html_api-base-url) specified by the [entry settings object](#305.html_entry-settings-object).

3.  If this fails, abort these steps.

4.  Process the resulting [absolute URL](#305.html_absolute-url) as the URL to an OpenSearch description document. [[OPENSEARCH]](#305.html_refsOPENSEARCH)

The <dfn id="305.html_dom-external-issearchproviderinstalled" data-anolis-xref="dom-external-IsSearchProviderInstalled">`IsSearchProviderInstalled()`</dfn> method, when invoked, must run the following steps: [![(This is a fingerprinting vector.)](Images/0a6e6fb7219b8816999de262da48194d.jpg)](#305.html_fingerprinting-vector)

1.  Optionally, return 0 and abort these steps. User agents may implement the method as a stub method that never returns a non-zero value, or may arbitrarily ignore invocations with particular arguments for security, privacy, or usability reasons.

2.  If the [origin](#305.html_origin-0) specified by the [entry settings object](#305.html_entry-settings-object) is an opaque identifier (i.e. it has no host component), then return 0 and abort these steps.

3.  Let `host1` be the host component of the [origin](#305.html_origin-0) specified by the [entry settings object](#305.html_entry-settings-object).

4.  [Resolve](#305.html_resolve-a-url) the `scriptURL` argument relative to the [API base URL](#305.html_api-base-url) specified by the [entry settings object](#305.html_entry-settings-object).

5.  If this fails, return 0 and abort these steps.

6.  Let `host2` be the [host](#305.html_concept-url-host) component of the resulting [parsed URL](#305.html_parsed-url).

7.  If the longest suffix in the Public Suffix List that matches the end of `host1` is different than the longest suffix in the Public Suffix List that matches the end of `host2`, then return 0 and abort these steps. [[PSL]](#305.html_refsPSL)

    If the next domain component of `host1` and `host2` after their common suffix are not the same, then return 0 and abort these steps.

8.  Let `search engines` be the list of search engines known by the user agent and made available to the user by the user agent for which the resulting [absolute URL](#305.html_absolute-url) is a [prefix match](#305.html_prefix-match) of the search engine's URL, if any. For search engines registered using OpenSearch description documents, the URL of the search engine corresponds to the URL given in a `Url` element whose `rel` attribute is "`results`" (the default). [[OPENSEARCH]](#305.html_refsOPENSEARCH)

9.  If `search engines` is empty, return 0 and abort these steps.

10.  If the user's default search engine (as determined by the user agent) is one of the search engines in `search engines`, then return 2 and abort these steps.

11.  Return 1.

## 7 <dfn>User interaction</dfn>

### 7.1 The <dfn id="307.html_attr-hidden" data-anolis-xref="attr-hidden">`hidden`</dfn> attribute

All [HTML elements](#307.html_html-elements) may have the [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) content attribute set. The [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute is a [boolean attribute](#307.html_boolean-attribute). When specified on an element, it indicates that the element is not yet, or is no longer, directly relevant to the page's current state, or that it is being used to declare content to be reused by other parts of the page as opposed to being directly accessed by the user. User agents should not render elements that have the [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute specified. This requirement may be implemented indirectly through the style layer. For example, an HTML+CSS user agent could implement these requirements [using the rules suggested in the Rendering section](#307.html_hiddenCSS).

Because this attribute is typically implemented using CSS, it's also possible to override it using CSS. For instance, a rule that applies 'display: block' to all elements will cancel the effects of the [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute. Authors therefore have to take care when writing their style sheets to make sure that the attribute is still styled as expected.

In the following skeletal example, the attribute is used to hide the Web game's main screen until the user logs in:

```
 <h1>The Example Game</h1>
  <section id="login">
   <h2>Login</h2>
   <form>
    ...
    <!-- calls login() once the user's credentials have been checked -->
   </form>
   <script>
    function login() {
      // switch screens
      document.getElementById('login').hidden = true;
      document.getElementById('game').hidden = false;
    }
   </script>
  </section>
  <section id="game" hidden>
   ...
  </section>
```

The [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute must not be used to hide content that could legitimately be shown in another presentation. For example, it is incorrect to use [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) to hide panels in a tabbed dialog, because the tabbed interface is merely a kind of overflow presentation — one could equally well just show all the form controls in one big page with a scrollbar. It is similarly incorrect to use this attribute to hide content just from one presentation — if something is marked [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute), it is hidden from all presentations, including, for instance, printers.

Elements that are not themselves [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) must not [hyperlink](#307.html_hyperlink) to elements that are [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute). The `for` attributes of [`label`](#307.html_the-label-element) and [`output`](#307.html_the-output-element) elements that are not themselves [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) must similarly not refer to elements that are [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute). In both cases, such references would cause user confusion.

Elements and scripts may, however, refer to elements that are [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) in other contexts.

For example, it would be incorrect to use the [`href`](#307.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute to link to a section marked with the [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute. If the content is not applicable or relevant, then there is no reason to link to it.

It would be fine, however, to use the ARIA `aria-describedby` attribute to refer to descriptions that are themselves [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute). While hiding the descriptions implies that they are not useful alone, they could be written in such a way that they are useful in the specific context of being referenced from the images that they describe.

Similarly, a [`canvas`](#307.html_the-canvas-element) element with the [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute could be used by a scripted graphics engine as an off-screen buffer, and a form control could refer to a hidden [`form`](#307.html_the-form-element) element using its [`form`](#307.html_attr-fae-form) attribute.

Accessibility APIs are encouraged to provide a way to expose structured content while marking it as hidden in the default view. Such content should not be perceivable to users in the normal document flow in any modality, whether using Assistive Technology (AT) or mainstream User Agents.

When such features are available, User Agents may use them to expose the full semantics of [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) elements to AT when appropriate, if such content is referenced indirectly by an [ID reference](#307.html_concept-id) or [valid hash-name reference](#307.html_valid-hash-name-reference). This allows ATs to access the structure of these [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) elements upon user request, while keeping the content hidden in all presentations of the normal document flow. Authors who wish to prevent user-initiated viewing of a [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) element should not reference the element with such a mechanism.

Because some User Agents have flattened hidden content when exposing such content to AT, authors should not reference [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) content which would lose essential meaning when flattened.

For example, it would be incorrect to use the [`href`](#307.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute to link to a section marked with the [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute. If the content is not applicable or relevant, then there is no reason to link to it.

It would be fine, however, to use the ARIA `aria-describedby` attribute to refer to descriptions that are themselves [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute). While hiding the descriptions implies that they are not useful alone, they could be written in such a way that they are useful in the specific context of being referenced from the images that they describe.

Similarly, a [`canvas`](#307.html_the-canvas-element) element with the [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute could be used by a scripted graphics engine as an off-screen buffer, and a form control could refer to a hidden [`form`](#307.html_the-form-element) element using its [`form`](#307.html_attr-fae-form) attribute.

Elements in a section hidden by the [`hidden`](#307.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute are still active, e.g. scripts and form controls in such sections still execute and submit respectively. Only their presentation to the user changes.

The <dfn id="307.html_dom-hidden" data-anolis-xref="dom-hidden">`hidden`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#307.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

### 7.2 Inert subtrees

A node (in particular elements and text nodes) can be marked as <dfn id="308.html_inert">inert</dfn>. When a node is [inert](#308.html_inert), then the user agent must act as if the node was absent for the purposes of targeting user interaction events, may ignore the node for the purposes of text search user interfaces (commonly known as "find in page"), and may prevent the user from selecting text in that node. User agents should allow the user to override the restrictions on search and text selection, however.

For example, consider a page that consists of just a single [inert](#308.html_inert) paragraph positioned in the middle of a [`body`](#308.html_the-body-element). If a user moves their pointing device from the [`body`](#308.html_the-body-element) over to the [inert](#308.html_inert) paragraph and clicks on the paragraph, no `mouseover` event would be fired, and the `mousemove` and [`click`](#308.html_event-click) events would be fired on the [`body`](#308.html_the-body-element) element rather than the paragraph.

When a node is inert, it also can't be [focusable](#308.html_focusable).

An entire [`Document`](#308.html_document) can be marked as <dfn id="308.html_blocked-by-a-modal-dialog">blocked by a modal dialog</dfn> `subject`. While a [`Document`](#308.html_document) is so marked, every node that is [in the `Document`](#308.html_in-a-document), with the exception of the `subject` element and its descendants, must be marked [inert](#308.html_inert). (The elements excepted by this paragraph can additionally be marked [inert](#308.html_inert) through other means; being part of a modal dialog does not "protect" a node from being marked [inert](#308.html_inert).)

Only one element at a time can mark a [`Document`](#308.html_document) as being [blocked by a modal dialog](#308.html_blocked-by-a-modal-dialog).

### 7.3 Activation

`element` . [`click`](#309.html_dom-click)()

Acts as if the element was clicked.

The <dfn id="309.html_dom-click" data-anolis-xref="dom-click">`click()`</dfn> method must [run synthetic click activation steps](#309.html_run-synthetic-click-activation-steps) on the element.

### 7.4 Focus

When an element is *focused*, key events received by the document must be targeted at that element. There may be no element focused; when no element is focused, key events received by the document must be targeted at [the body element](#310.html_the-body-element-0), if there is one, or else at the [`Document`](#310.html_document)'s root element, if there is one. If there is no root element, key events must not be fired.

User agents may track focus for each [browsing context](#310.html_browsing-context) or [`Document`](#310.html_document) individually, or may support only one focused element per [top-level browsing context](#310.html_top-level-browsing-context) — user agents should follow platform conventions in this regard.

Which elements within a [top-level browsing context](#310.html_top-level-browsing-context) currently have focus must be independent of whether or not the [top-level browsing context](#310.html_top-level-browsing-context) itself has the *system focus*.

When a [child browsing context](#310.html_child-browsing-context) is focused, its [browsing context container](#310.html_browsing-context-container) must also have focus.

When an element is focused, the element matches the CSS `:focus` pseudo-class.

#### 7.4.1 Sequential focus navigation and the [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute

The <dfn id="311.html_attr-tabindex" data-anolis-xref="attr-tabindex">`tabindex`</dfn> content attribute allows authors to control whether an element is supposed to be focusable, whether it is supposed to be reachable using sequential focus navigation, and what is to be the relative order of the element for the purposes of sequential focus navigation. The name "tab index" comes from the common use of the "tab" key to navigate through the focusable elements. The term "tabbing" refers to moving forward through the focusable elements that can be reached using sequential focus navigation.

The [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid integer](#311.html_valid-integer).

Each element can have a <dfn id="311.html_specially-focusable">tabindex focus flag</dfn> set, as defined below. This flag is a factor that contributes towards determining whether an element is [focusable](#311.html_focusable), as described in the next section.

If the attribute is specified, it must be parsed using the [rules for parsing integers](#311.html_rules-for-parsing-integers). The attribute's values have the following meanings:

If the attribute is omitted or parsing the value returns an error

The user agent should follow platform conventions to determine if the element's [tabindex focus flag](#311.html_specially-focusable) is set and, if so, whether the element can be reached using sequential focus navigation, and if so, what its relative order should be.

Modulo platform conventions, it is suggested that for the following elements, the [tabindex focus flag](#311.html_specially-focusable) be set:

*   [`a`](#311.html_the-a-element) elements that have an [`href`](#311.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute
*   [`link`](#311.html_the-link-element) elements that have an [`href`](#311.html_attr-link-href) attribute
*   [`button`](#311.html_the-button-element) elements
*   [`input`](#311.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#311.html_attr-input-type) attribute are not in the [Hidden](#311.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state
*   [`select`](#311.html_the-select-element) elements
*   [`textarea`](#311.html_the-textarea-element) elements
*   [Editing hosts](#311.html_editing-host)
*   [Browsing context containers](#311.html_browsing-context-container)

One valid reason to ignore the platform conventions and always allow an element to be focused (by setting its [tabindex focus flag](#311.html_specially-focusable)) would be if the user's only mechanism for activating an element is through a keyboard action that triggers the focused element.

If the value is a negative integer

The user agent must set the element's [tabindex focus flag](#311.html_specially-focusable), but should not allow the element to be reached using sequential focus navigation.

One valid reason to ignore the requirement that sequential focus navigation not allow the author to lead to the element would be if the user's only mechanism for moving the focus is sequential focus navigation. For instance, a keyboard-only user would be unable to click on a text field with a negative [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex), so that user's user agent would be well justified in allowing the user to tab to the control regardless.

If the value is a zero

The user agent must set the element's [tabindex focus flag](#311.html_specially-focusable), should allow the element to be reached using sequential focus navigation, and should follow platform conventions to determine the element's relative order.

If the value is greater than zero

The user agent must set the element's [tabindex focus flag](#311.html_specially-focusable), should allow the element to be reached using sequential focus navigation, and should place the element in the sequential focus navigation order so that it is:

*   before any [focusable](#311.html_focusable) element whose [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute has been omitted or whose value, when parsed, returns an error,
*   before any [focusable](#311.html_focusable) element whose [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute has a value equal to or less than zero,
*   after any element whose [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute has a value greater than zero but less than the value of the [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute on the element,
*   after any element whose [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute has a value equal to the value of the [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute on the element but that is earlier in the document in [tree order](#311.html_tree-order) than the element,
*   before any element whose [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute has a value equal to the value of the [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute on the element but that is later in the document in [tree order](#311.html_tree-order) than the element, and
*   before any element whose [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute has a value greater than the value of the [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute on the element.

An element that has its [tabindex focus flag](#311.html_specially-focusable) set but does not otherwise have an [activation behavior](#311.html_activation-behavior) defined has an [activation behavior](#311.html_activation-behavior) that does nothing.

This means that an element that is only focusable because of its [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) attribute will fire a [`click`](#311.html_event-click) event in response to a non-mouse activation (e.g. hitting the "enter" key while the element is focused).

The <dfn id="311.html_dom-tabindex" data-anolis-xref="dom-tabIndex">`tabIndex`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#311.html_reflect) the value of the [`tabindex`](#311.html_attr-tabindex) content attribute. Its default value is 0 for elements that are focusable and ?1 for elements that are not focusable.

#### 7.4.2 Focus management

An element is <dfn id="312.html_focusable">focusable</dfn> if all of the following conditions are met:

*   The element's [tabindex focus flag](#312.html_specially-focusable) is set.
*   The element is either [being rendered](#312.html_being-rendered) or is a descendant of a [`canvas`](#312.html_the-canvas-element) element that [represents](#312.html_represents) [embedded content](#312.html_embedded-content-2).
*   The element is not [inert](#312.html_inert).
*   The element is not [disabled](#312.html_concept-element-disabled).

In addition, each shape that is generated for an [`area`](#312.html_the-area-element) element, any user-agent-provided interface components of [media elements](#312.html_media-element) (e.g. a play button), and distinct user interface components of form controls (e.g. "up" and "down" buttons on an [`<input type=number>`](#312.html_number-state-(type=number)) spin control), should be [focusable](#312.html_focusable), unless platform conventions dictate otherwise or unless their corresponding element is [disabled](#312.html_concept-element-disabled). (A single [`area`](#312.html_the-area-element) element can correspond to multiple shapes, since image maps can be reused with multiple images on a page.)

Notwithstanding the above, user agents may make *any* element or part of an element focusable, especially to aid with accessibility or to better match platform conventions.

* * *
