The <dfn id="312.html_focusing-steps">focusing steps</dfn> for an element are as follows:

1.  If the element is not [in a `Document`](#312.html_in-a-document), or if the element's [`Document`](#312.html_document) has no [browsing context](#312.html_browsing-context), or if the element's [`Document`](#312.html_document)'s [browsing context](#312.html_browsing-context) has no [top-level browsing context](#312.html_top-level-browsing-context), or if the element is not [focusable](#312.html_focusable), or if the element is already focused, then abort these steps.

2.  If focusing the element will remove the focus from another element, then run the [unfocusing steps](#312.html_unfocusing-steps) for that element.

3.  Make the element the currently focused element in its [top-level browsing context](#312.html_top-level-browsing-context).

    Some elements, most notably [`area`](#312.html_the-area-element), can correspond to more than one distinct focusable area. If a particular area was indicated when the element was focused, then that is the area that must get focus; otherwise, e.g. when using the [`focus()`](#312.html_dom-focus) method, the first such region in tree order is the one that must be focused.

4.  The user agent may apply relevant platform-specific conventions for focusing widgets.

    For example, some platforms select the contents of a text field when that field is focused.

5.  [Fire a simple event](#312.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `focus` at the element.

User agents must synchronously run the [focusing steps](#312.html_focusing-steps) for an element whenever the user moves the focus to a [focusable](#312.html_focusable) element.

The <dfn id="312.html_unfocusing-steps">unfocusing steps</dfn> for an element are as follows:

1.  If the element is an [`input`](#312.html_the-input-element) element, and the [`change`](#312.html_event-input-change) event applies to the element, and the element does not have a defined [activation behavior](#312.html_activation-behavior), and the user has changed the element's [value](#312.html_concept-fe-value) or its list of [selected files](#312.html_concept-input-type-file-selected) while the control was focused without committing that change, then [fire a simple event](#312.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `change` at the element.

2.  Unfocus the element.

3.  [Fire a simple event](#312.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `blur` at the element.

When an element that is focused stops being a [focusable](#312.html_focusable) element, or stops being focused without another element being explicitly focused in its stead, the user agent should synchronously run the [unfocusing steps](#312.html_unfocusing-steps) for the affected element only.

For example, this might happen because the element is removed from its [`Document`](#312.html_document), or has a [`hidden`](#312.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute added. It would also happen to an [`input`](#312.html_the-input-element) element when the element gets [disabled](#312.html_concept-fe-disabled).

#### 7.4.3 Document-level focus APIs

`document` . [`activeElement`](#313.html_dom-document-activeelement)

Returns the currently focused element.

`document` . [`hasFocus`](#313.html_dom-document-hasfocus)()

Returns true if the document has focus; otherwise, returns false.

`window` . [`focus`](#313.html_dom-window-focus)()

Focuses the window. Use of this method is discouraged. Allow the user to control window focus instead.

`window` . [`blur`](#313.html_dom-window-blur)()

Unfocuses the window. Use of this method is discouraged. Allow the user to control window focus instead.

The <dfn id="313.html_dom-document-activeelement" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-activeElement">`activeElement`</dfn> attribute on [`Document`](#313.html_document) objects must return the element in the document that is focused. If no element in the [`Document`](#313.html_document) is focused, this must return [the body element](#313.html_the-body-element-0).

When a [child browsing context](#313.html_child-browsing-context) is focused, its [browsing context container](#313.html_browsing-context-container) is also focused, [by definition](#313.html_bc-focus-ergo-bcc-focus). For example, if the user moves the focus to a text field in an [`iframe`](#313.html_the-iframe-element), the [`iframe`](#313.html_the-iframe-element) is the element with focus in the [parent browsing context](#313.html_parent-browsing-context).

The <dfn id="313.html_dom-document-hasfocus" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-hasFocus">`hasFocus()`</dfn> method on [`Document`](#313.html_document) objects must return true if the [`Document`](#313.html_document)'s [browsing context](#313.html_browsing-context) is focused, and all its [ancestor browsing contexts](#313.html_ancestor-browsing-context) are also focused, and the [top-level browsing context](#313.html_top-level-browsing-context) has the *system focus*. If the [`Document`](#313.html_document) has no [browsing context](#313.html_browsing-context) or if its [browsing context](#313.html_browsing-context) has no [top-level browsing context](#313.html_top-level-browsing-context), then the method will always return false.

The <dfn id="313.html_dom-window-focus" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-focus">`focus()`</dfn> method on the [`Window`](#313.html_window) object, when invoked, provides a hint to the user agent that the script believes the user might be interested in the contents of the [browsing context](#313.html_browsing-context) of the [`Window`](#313.html_window) object on which the method was invoked.

User agents are encouraged to have this [`focus()`](#313.html_dom-window-focus) method trigger some kind of notification.

The <dfn id="313.html_dom-window-blur" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-blur">`blur()`</dfn> method on the [`Window`](#313.html_window) object, when invoked, provides a hint to the user agent that the script believes the user probably is not currently interested in the contents of the [browsing context](#313.html_browsing-context) of the [`Window`](#313.html_window) object on which the method was invoked, but that the contents might become interesting again in the future.

User agents are encouraged to ignore calls to this [`blur()`](#313.html_dom-window-blur) method entirely.

Historically the [`focus()`](#313.html_dom-window-blur) and [`blur()`](#313.html_dom-window-blur) methods actually affected the system focus, but hostile sites widely abuse this behavior to the user's detriment.

#### 7.4.4 Element-level focus APIs

`element` . [`focus`](#314.html_dom-focus)()

Focuses the element.

`element` . [`blur`](#314.html_dom-blur)()

Unfocuses the element. Use of this method is discouraged. Focus another element instead.

Do not use this method to hide the focus ring. Do not use any other method that hides the focus ring from keyboard users, in particular do not use a CSS rule to override the 'outline' property. Removal of the focus ring leads to serious accessibility issues for users who navigate and interact with interactive content using the keyboard.

The <dfn id="314.html_dom-focus" data-anolis-xref="dom-focus">`focus()`</dfn> method, when invoked, must run the following algorithm:

1.  If the element is marked as *[locked for focus](#314.html_locked-for-focus)*, then abort these steps.

2.  Mark the element as <dfn id="314.html_locked-for-focus">locked for focus</dfn>.

3.  Run the [focusing steps](#314.html_focusing-steps) for the element.

4.  Unmark the element as *[locked for focus](#314.html_locked-for-focus)*.

The <dfn id="314.html_dom-blur" data-anolis-xref="dom-blur">`blur()`</dfn> method, when invoked, should run the [unfocusing steps](#314.html_unfocusing-steps) for the element on which the method was called instead. User agents may selectively or uniformly ignore calls to this method for usability reasons.

For example, if the [`blur()`](#314.html_dom-blur) method is unwisely being used to remove the focus ring for aesthetics reasons, the page would become unusable by keyboard users. Ignoring calls to this method would thus allow keyboard users to interact with the page.

### 7.5 Assigning keyboard shortcuts

#### 7.5.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

Each element that can be activated or focused can be assigned a single key combination to activate it, using the [`accesskey`](#316.html_the-accesskey-attribute) attribute.

The exact shortcut is determined by the user agent, based on information about the user's keyboard, what keyboard shortcuts already exist on the platform, and what other shortcuts have been specified on the page, using the information provided in the [`accesskey`](#316.html_the-accesskey-attribute) attribute as a guide.

In order to ensure that a relevant keyboard shortcut is available on a wide variety of input devices, the author can provide a number of alternatives in the [`accesskey`](#316.html_the-accesskey-attribute) attribute.

Each alternative consists of a single character, such as a letter or digit.

User agents can provide users with a list of the keyboard shortcuts, but authors are encouraged to do so also. The [`accessKeyLabel`](#316.html_dom-accesskeylabel) IDL attribute returns a string representing the actual key combination assigned by the user agent.

In this example, an author has provided a button that can be invoked using a shortcut key. To support full keyboards, the author has provided "C" as a possible key. To support devices equipped only with numeric keypads, the author has provided "1" as another possibly key.

```
<input type=button value=Collect onclick="collect()"
       accesskey="C 1" id=c>
```

To tell the user what the shortcut key is, the author has this script here opted to explicitly add the key combination to the button's label:

```
function addShortcutKeyLabel(button) {
  if (button.accessKeyLabel != '')
    button.value += ' (' + button.accessKeyLabel + ')';
}
addShortcutKeyLabel(document.getElementById('c'));
```

Browsers on different platforms will show different labels, even for the same key combination, based on the convention prevalent on that platform. For example, if the key combination is the Control key, the Shift key, and the letter C, a Windows browser might display "<samp>Ctrl+Shift+C</samp>", whereas a Mac browser might display "<samp>^?C</samp>", while an Emacs browser might just display "<samp>C-C</samp>". Similarly, if the key combination is the Alt key and the Escape key, Windows might use "<samp>Alt+Esc</samp>", Mac might use "<samp>??</samp>", and an Emacs browser might use "<samp>M-ESC</samp>" or "<samp>ESC ESC</samp>".

In general, therefore, it is unwise to attempt to parse the value returned from the [`accessKeyLabel`](#316.html_dom-accesskeylabel) IDL attribute.

#### 7.5.2 The <dfn id="317.html_attr-accesskey" data-anolis-xref="attr-accesskey">`accesskey`</dfn> attribute

All [HTML elements](#317.html_html-elements) may have the [`accesskey`](#317.html_the-accesskey-attribute) content attribute set. The [`accesskey`](#317.html_the-accesskey-attribute) attribute's value is used by the user agent as a guide for creating a keyboard shortcut that activates or focuses the element.

If specified, the value must be an [ordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#317.html_ordered-set-of-unique-space-separated-tokens) that are [case-sensitive](#317.html_case-sensitive), each of which must be exactly one Unicode code point in length.

In the following example, a variety of links are given with access keys so that keyboard users familiar with the site can more quickly navigate to the relevant pages:

```
<nav>
 <p>
  <a title="Consortium Activities" accesskey="A" href="/Consortium/activities">Activities</a> |
  <a title="Technical Reports and Recommendations" accesskey="T" href="/TR/">Technical Reports</a> |
  <a title="Alphabetical Site Index" accesskey="S" href="/Consortium/siteindex">Site Index</a> |
  <a title="About This Site" accesskey="B" href="/Consortium/">About Consortium</a> |
  <a title="Contact Consortium" accesskey="C" href="/Consortium/contact">Contact</a>
 </p>
</nav>
```

In the following example, the search field is given two possible access keys, "s" and "0" (in that order). A user agent on a device with a full keyboard might pick `` `Ctrl`+`Alt`+`[S](#317.html_the-s-element)` `` as the shortcut key, while a user agent on a small device with just a numeric keypad might pick just the plain unadorned key `` `0` ``:

```
<form action="/search">
 <label>Search: <input type="search" name="q" accesskey="s 0"></label>
 <input type="submit">
</form>
```

In the following example, a button has possible access keys described. A script then tries to update the button's label to advertise the key combination the user agent selected.

```
<input type=submit accesskey="N @ 1" value="Compose">
...
<script>
 function labelButton(button) {
   if (button.accessKeyLabel)
     button.value += ' (' + button.accessKeyLabel + ')';
 }
 var inputs = document.getElementsByTagName('input');
 for (var i = 0; i < inputs.length; i += 1) {
   if (inputs[i].type == "submit")
     labelButton(inputs[i]);
 }
</script>
```

On one user agent, the button's label might become "<samp>Compose (?N)</samp>". On another, it might become "<samp>Compose (Alt+?+1)</samp>". If the user agent doesn't assign a key, it will be just "<samp>Compose</samp>". The exact string depends on what the [assigned access key](#317.html_assigned-access-key) is, and on how the user agent represents that key combination.

#### 7.5.3 Processing model

An element's <dfn id="318.html_assigned-access-key">assigned access key</dfn> is a key combination derived from the element's [`accesskey`](#318.html_the-accesskey-attribute) content attribute. Initially, an element must not have an [assigned access key](#318.html_assigned-access-key).

Whenever an element's [`accesskey`](#318.html_the-accesskey-attribute) attribute is set, changed, or removed, the user agent must update the element's [assigned access key](#318.html_assigned-access-key) by running the following steps:

1.  If the element has no [`accesskey`](#318.html_the-accesskey-attribute) attribute, then skip to the *fallback* step below.

2.  Otherwise, [split the attribute's value on spaces](#318.html_split-a-string-on-spaces), and let `keys` be the resulting tokens.

3.  For each value in `keys` in turn, in the order the tokens appeared in the attribute's value, run the following substeps:

    1.  If the value is not a string exactly one Unicode code point in length, then skip the remainder of these steps for this value.

    2.  If the value does not correspond to a key on the system's keyboard, then skip the remainder of these steps for this value.

    3.  If the user agent can find a mix of zero or more modifier keys that, combined with the key that corresponds to the value given in the attribute, can be used as the access key, then the user agent may assign that combination of keys as the element's [assigned access key](#318.html_assigned-access-key) and abort these steps.

4.  *Fallback*: Optionally, the user agent may assign a key combination of its choosing as the element's [assigned access key](#318.html_assigned-access-key) and then abort these steps.

5.  If this step is reached, the element has no [assigned access key](#318.html_assigned-access-key).

Once a user agent has selected and assigned an access key for an element, the user agent should not change the element's [assigned access key](#318.html_assigned-access-key) unless the [`accesskey`](#318.html_the-accesskey-attribute) content attribute is changed or the element is moved to another [`Document`](#318.html_document).

User agents might expose elements that have an [`accesskey`](#318.html_the-accesskey-attribute) attribute in other ways as well, e.g. in a menu displayed in response to a specific key combination.

* * *

The <dfn id="318.html_dom-accesskey" data-anolis-xref="dom-accessKey">`accessKey`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#318.html_reflect) the [`accesskey`](#318.html_the-accesskey-attribute) content attribute.

The <dfn id="318.html_dom-accesskeylabel" data-anolis-xref="dom-accessKeyLabel">`accessKeyLabel`</dfn> IDL attribute must return a string that represents the element's [assigned access key](#318.html_assigned-access-key), if any. If the element does not have one, then the IDL attribute must return the empty string.

### 7.6 Editing

#### 7.6.1 Making document regions editable: The [`contenteditable`](#320.html_attr-contenteditable) content attribute

The <dfn id="320.html_attr-contenteditable" data-anolis-xref="attr-contenteditable">`contenteditable`</dfn> attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#320.html_enumerated-attribute) whose keywords are the empty string, `true`, and `false`. The empty string and the `true` keyword map to the *true* state. The `false` keyword maps to the *false* state. In addition, there is a third state, the *inherit* state, which is the *missing value default* (and the *invalid value default*).

The *true* state indicates that the element is editable. The *inherit* state indicates that the element is editable if its parent is. The *false* state indicates that the element is not editable.

`element` . [`contentEditable`](#320.html_dom-contenteditable) [ = `value` ]

Returns "`true`", "`false`", or "`inherit`", based on the state of the [`contenteditable`](#320.html_attr-contenteditable) attribute.

Can be set, to change that state.

Throws a [`SyntaxError`](#320.html_syntaxerror) exception if the new value isn't one of those strings.

`element` . [`isContentEditable`](#320.html_dom-iscontenteditable)

Returns true if the element is editable; otherwise, returns false.

The <dfn id="320.html_dom-contenteditable" data-anolis-xref="dom-contentEditable">`contentEditable`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the string "`true`" if the content attribute is set to the true state, "`false`" if the content attribute is set to the false state, and "`inherit`" otherwise. On setting, if the new value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#320.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`inherit`" then the content attribute must be removed, if the new value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#320.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`true`" then the content attribute must be set to the string "`true`", if the new value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#320.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`false`" then the content attribute must be set to the string "`false`", and otherwise the attribute setter must throw a [`SyntaxError`](#320.html_syntaxerror) exception.

The <dfn id="320.html_dom-iscontenteditable" data-anolis-xref="dom-isContentEditable">`isContentEditable`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return true if the element is either an [editing host](#320.html_editing-host) or [editable](#320.html_editable), and false otherwise.

#### 7.6.2 Making entire documents editable: The [`designMode`](#321.html_designMode) IDL attribute

Documents have a <dfn id="321.html_designMode" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-designMode">`designMode`</dfn>, which can be either enabled or disabled.

`document` . [`designMode`](#321.html_designMode) [ = `value` ]

Returns "`on`" if the document is editable, and "`off`" if it isn't.

Can be set, to change the document's current state. This focuses the document and resets the selection in that document.

The [`designMode`](#321.html_designMode) IDL attribute on the [`Document`](#321.html_document) object takes two values, "`on`" and "`off`". On setting, the new value must be compared in an [ASCII case-insensitive](#321.html_ascii-case-insensitive) manner to these two values; if it matches the "`on`" value, then [`designMode`](#321.html_designMode) must be enabled, and if it matches the "`off`" value, then [`designMode`](#321.html_designMode) must be disabled. Other values must be ignored.

On getting, if [`designMode`](#321.html_designMode) is enabled, the IDL attribute must return the value "`on`"; otherwise it is disabled, and the attribute must return the value "`off`".

The last state set must persist until the document is destroyed or the state is changed. Initially, documents must have their [`designMode`](#321.html_designMode) disabled.

When the [`designMode`](#321.html_designMode) changes from being disabled to being enabled, the user agent must synchronously reset the document's [active range](#321.html_active-range)'s start and end boundary points to be at the start of the [`Document`](#321.html_document) and then run the [focusing steps](#321.html_focusing-steps) for the root element of the [`Document`](#321.html_document), if any.

#### 7.6.3 Best practices for in-page editors

Authors are encouraged to set the 'white-space' property on [editing hosts](#322.html_editing-host) and on markup that was originally created through these editing mechanisms to the value 'pre-wrap'. Default HTML whitespace handling is not well suited to WYSIWYG editing, and line wrapping will not work correctly in some corner cases if 'white-space' is left at its default value.

As an example of problems that occur if the default 'normal' value is used instead, consider the case of the user typing "`yellow??ball`", with two spaces (here represented by "?") between the words. With the editing rules in place for the default value of 'white-space' ('normal'), the resulting markup will either consist of "<samp>yellow&nbsp; ball</samp>" or "<samp>yellow &nbsp;ball</samp>"; i.e., there will be a non-breaking space between the two words in addition to the regular space. This is necessary because the 'normal' value for 'white-space' requires adjacent regular spaces to be collapsed together.

In the former case, "<samp>yellow?</samp>" might wrap to the next line ("?" being used here to represent a non-breaking space) even though "<samp>yellow</samp>" alone might fit at the end of the line; in the latter case, "<samp>?ball</samp>", if wrapped to the start of the line, would have visible indentation from the non-breaking space.

When 'white-space' is set to 'pre-wrap', however, the editing rules will instead simply put two regular spaces between the words, and should the two words be split at the end of a line, the spaces would be neatly removed from the rendering.

#### 7.6.4 Editing APIs

The definition of the terms <dfn id="323.html_active-range">active range</dfn>, <dfn id="323.html_editing-host">editing host</dfn>, and <dfn id="323.html_editable">editable</dfn>, the user interface requirements of elements that are [editing hosts](#323.html_editing-host) or [editable](#323.html_editable), the <dfn id="323.html_execCommand" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-execCommand">`execCommand()`</dfn>, <dfn id="323.html_dom-document-querycommandenabled" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-queryCommandEnabled">`queryCommandEnabled()`</dfn>, <dfn id="323.html_dom-document-querycommandindeterm" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-queryCommandIndeterm">`queryCommandIndeterm()`</dfn>, <dfn id="323.html_dom-document-querycommandstate" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-queryCommandState">`queryCommandState()`</dfn>, <dfn id="323.html_dom-document-querycommandsupported" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-queryCommandSupported">`queryCommandSupported()`</dfn>, and <dfn id="323.html_dom-document-querycommandvalue" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-queryCommandValue">`queryCommandValue()`</dfn> methods, text selections, and the <dfn id="323.html_delete-the-selection">delete the selection</dfn> algorithm are defined in the HTML Editing APIs specification. The interaction of editing and the undo/redo features in user agents is defined by the UndoManager and DOM Transaction specification. [[EDITING]](#323.html_refsEDITING) [[UNDO]](#323.html_refsUNDO)

#### 7.6.5 Spelling and grammar checking

User agents can support the checking of spelling and grammar of editable text, either in form controls (such as the value of [`textarea`](#324.html_the-textarea-element) elements), or in elements in an [editing host](#324.html_editing-host) (e.g. using [`contenteditable`](#324.html_attr-contenteditable)).

For each element, user agents must establish a <dfn id="324.html_concept-spellcheck-default" data-anolis-xref="concept-spellcheck-default">default behavior</dfn>, either through defaults or through preferences expressed by the user. There are three possible default behaviors for each element:

<dfn id="324.html_concept-spellcheck-default-true" data-anolis-xref="concept-spellcheck-default-true">true-by-default</dfn>

The element will be checked for spelling and grammar if its contents are editable.

<dfn id="324.html_concept-spellcheck-default-false" data-anolis-xref="concept-spellcheck-default-false">false-by-default</dfn>

The element will never be checked for spelling and grammar.

<dfn id="324.html_concept-spellcheck-default-inherit" data-anolis-xref="concept-spellcheck-default-inherit">inherit-by-default</dfn>

The element's default behavior is the same as its parent element's. Elements that have no parent element cannot have this as their default behavior.

* * *

The <dfn id="324.html_attr-spellcheck" data-anolis-xref="attr-spellcheck">`spellcheck`</dfn> attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#324.html_enumerated-attribute) whose keywords are the empty string, `true` and `false`. The empty string and the `true` keyword map to the *true* state. The `false` keyword maps to the *false* state. In addition, there is a third state, the *default* state, which is the *missing value default* (and the *invalid value default*).

The *true* state indicates that the element is to have its spelling and grammar checked. The *default* state indicates that the element is to act according to a default behavior, possibly based on the parent element's own [`spellcheck`](#324.html_attr-spellcheck) state, as defined below. The *false* state indicates that the element is not to be checked.

* * *

`element` . [`spellcheck`](#324.html_dom-spellcheck) [ = `value` ]

Returns true if the element is to have its spelling and grammar checked; otherwise, returns false.

Can be set, to override the default and set the [`spellcheck`](#324.html_attr-spellcheck) content attribute.

The <dfn id="324.html_dom-spellcheck" data-anolis-xref="dom-spellcheck">`spellcheck`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return true if the element's [`spellcheck`](#324.html_attr-spellcheck) content attribute is in the *true* state, or if the element's [`spellcheck`](#324.html_attr-spellcheck) content attribute is in the *default* state and the element's [default behavior](#324.html_concept-spellcheck-default) is [true-by-default](#324.html_concept-spellcheck-default-true), or if the element's [`spellcheck`](#324.html_attr-spellcheck) content attribute is in the *default* state and the element's [default behavior](#324.html_concept-spellcheck-default) is [inherit-by-default](#324.html_concept-spellcheck-default-inherit) and the element's parent element's [`spellcheck`](#324.html_dom-spellcheck) IDL attribute would return true; otherwise, if none of those conditions applies, then the attribute must instead return false.

The [`spellcheck`](#324.html_dom-spellcheck) IDL attribute is not affected by user preferences that override the [`spellcheck`](#324.html_attr-spellcheck) content attribute, and therefore might not reflect the actual spellchecking state.

On setting, if the new value is true, then the element's [`spellcheck`](#324.html_attr-spellcheck) content attribute must be set to the literal string "`true`", otherwise it must be set to the literal string "`false`".

* * *

User agents must only consider the following pieces of text as checkable for the purposes of this feature:

*   The [value](#324.html_concept-fe-value) of [`input`](#324.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#324.html_attr-input-type) attributes are in the [Text](#324.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [Search](#324.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [URL](#324.html_url-state-(type=url)), or [E-mail](#324.html_e-mail-state-(type=email)) states and that are *[mutable](#324.html_concept-fe-mutable)* (i.e. that do not have the [`readonly`](#324.html_attr-input-readonly) attribute specified and that are not [disabled](#324.html_concept-fe-disabled)).
*   The [value](#324.html_concept-fe-value) of [`textarea`](#324.html_the-textarea-element) elements that do not have a [`readonly`](#324.html_attr-textarea-readonly) attribute and that are not [disabled](#324.html_concept-fe-disabled).
*   Text in [`Text`](#324.html_text-0) nodes that are children of [editing hosts](#324.html_editing-host) or [editable](#324.html_editable) elements.
*   Text in attributes of [editable](#324.html_editable) elements.

For text that is part of a [`Text`](#324.html_text-0) node, the element with which the text is associated is the element that is the immediate parent of the first character of the word, sentence, or other piece of text. For text in attributes, it is the attribute's element. For the values of [`input`](#324.html_the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#324.html_the-textarea-element) elements, it is the element itself.

To determine if a word, sentence, or other piece of text in an applicable element (as defined above) is to have spelling- and grammar-checking enabled, the UA must use the following algorithm:

1.  If the user has disabled the checking for this text, then the checking is disabled.
2.  Otherwise, if the user has forced the checking for this text to always be enabled, then the checking is enabled.
3.  Otherwise, if the element with which the text is associated has a [`spellcheck`](#324.html_attr-spellcheck) content attribute, then: if that attribute is in the *true* state, then checking is enabled; otherwise, if that attribute is in the *false* state, then checking is disabled.
4.  Otherwise, if there is an ancestor element with a [`spellcheck`](#324.html_attr-spellcheck) content attribute that is not in the *default* state, then: if the nearest such ancestor's [`spellcheck`](#324.html_attr-spellcheck) content attribute is in the *true* state, then checking is enabled; otherwise, checking is disabled.
5.  Otherwise, if the element's [default behavior](#324.html_concept-spellcheck-default) is [true-by-default](#324.html_concept-spellcheck-default-true), then checking is enabled.
6.  Otherwise, if the element's [default behavior](#324.html_concept-spellcheck-default) is [false-by-default](#324.html_concept-spellcheck-default-false), then checking is disabled.
7.  Otherwise, if the element's parent element has *its* checking enabled, then checking is enabled.
8.  Otherwise, checking is disabled.

If the checking is enabled for a word/sentence/text, the user agent should indicate spelling and grammar errors in that text. User agents should take into account the other semantics given in the document when suggesting spelling and grammar corrections. User agents may use the language of the element to determine what spelling and grammar rules to use, or may use the user's preferred language settings. UAs should use [`input`](#324.html_the-input-element) element attributes such as [`pattern`](#324.html_attr-input-pattern) to ensure that the resulting value is valid, where possible.

If checking is disabled, the user agent should not indicate spelling or grammar errors for that text.

Even when checking is enabled, user agents may opt to not report spelling or grammar errors in text that the user agent deems the user has no interest in having checked (e.g. text that was already present when the page was loaded, or that the user did not type, or text in controls that the user has not focused, or in parts of e-mail addresses that the user agent is not confident were misspelt).

The element with ID "a" in the following example would be the one used to determine if the word "Hello" is checked for spelling errors. In this example, it would not be.

```
<div contenteditable="true">
 <span spellcheck="false" id="a">Hell</span><em>o!</em>
</div>
```

The element with ID "b" in the following example would have checking enabled (the leading space character in the attribute's value on the [`input`](#324.html_the-input-element) element causes the attribute to be ignored, so the ancestor's value is used instead, regardless of the default).

```
<p spellcheck="true">
 <label>Name: <input spellcheck=" false" id="b"></label>
</p>
```

This specification does not define the user interface for spelling and grammar checkers. A user agent could offer on-demand checking, could perform continuous checking while the checking is enabled, or could use other interfaces.

## 8 <dfn>The HTML syntax</dfn>

This section only describes the rules for resources labeled with an [HTML MIME type](#325.html_html-mime-type). Rules for XML resources are discussed in the section below entitled "[The XHTML syntax](#325.html_the-xhtml-syntax)".

### 8.1 Writing HTML documents

*This section only applies to documents, authoring tools, and markup generators. In particular, it does not apply to conformance checkers; conformance checkers must use the requirements given in the next section ("parsing HTML documents").*

Documents must consist of the following parts, in the given order:

1.  Optionally, a single "BOM" (U+FEFF) character.
2.  Any number of [comments](#326.html_syntax-comments) and [space characters](#326.html_space-character).
3.  A [DOCTYPE](#326.html_syntax-doctype).
4.  Any number of [comments](#326.html_syntax-comments) and [space characters](#326.html_space-character).
5.  The root element, in the form of an [`html`](#326.html_the-html-element) [element](#326.html_syntax-elements).
6.  Any number of [comments](#326.html_syntax-comments) and [space characters](#326.html_space-character).

The various types of content mentioned above are described in the next few sections.

In addition, there are some restrictions on how [character encoding declarations](#326.html_character-encoding-declaration) are to be serialized, as discussed in the section on that topic.

Space characters before the root [`html`](#326.html_the-html-element) element, and space characters at the start of the [`html`](#326.html_the-html-element) element and before the [`head`](#326.html_the-head-element) element, will be dropped when the document is parsed; space characters *after* the root [`html`](#326.html_the-html-element) element will be parsed as if they were at the end of the [`body`](#326.html_the-body-element) element. Thus, space characters around the root element do not round-trip.

It is suggested that newlines be inserted after the DOCTYPE, after any comments that are before the root element, after the [`html`](#326.html_the-html-element) element's start tag (if it is not [omitted](#326.html_syntax-tag-omission)), and after any comments that are inside the [`html`](#326.html_the-html-element) element but before the [`head`](#326.html_the-head-element) element.

Many strings in the HTML syntax (e.g. the names of elements and their attributes) are case-insensitive, but only for [uppercase ASCII letters](#326.html_uppercase-ascii-letters) and [lowercase ASCII letters](#326.html_lowercase-ascii-letters). For convenience, in this section this is just referred to as "case-insensitive".

#### 8.1.1 The DOCTYPE

A <dfn id="327.html_syntax-doctype" data-anolis-xref="syntax-doctype">DOCTYPE</dfn> is a required preamble.

DOCTYPEs are required for legacy reasons. When omitted, browsers tend to use a different rendering mode that is incompatible with some specifications. Including the DOCTYPE in a document ensures that the browser makes a best-effort attempt at following the relevant specifications.

A DOCTYPE must consist of the following components, in this order:

1.  A string that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#327.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`<!DOCTYPE`".
2.  One or more [space characters](#327.html_space-character).
3.  A string that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#327.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`html`".
4.  Optionally, a [DOCTYPE legacy string](#327.html_doctype-legacy-string) or an [obsolete permitted DOCTYPE string](#327.html_obsolete-permitted-doctype-string) (defined below).
5.  Zero or more [space characters](#327.html_space-character).
6.  A ">" (U+003E) character.

In other words, `<!DOCTYPE html>`, case-insensitively.

* * *

For the purposes of HTML generators that cannot output HTML markup with the short DOCTYPE "`<!DOCTYPE html>`", a <dfn id="327.html_doctype-legacy-string">DOCTYPE legacy string</dfn> may be inserted into the DOCTYPE (in the position defined above). This string must consist of:

1.  One or more [space characters](#327.html_space-character).
2.  A string that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#327.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`SYSTEM`".
3.  One or more [space characters](#327.html_space-character).
4.  A U+0022 QUOTATION MARK or U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (the *quote mark*).
5.  The literal string "[`about:legacy-compat`](#327.html_about:legacy-compat)".
6.  A matching U+0022 QUOTATION MARK or U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (i.e. the same character as in the earlier step labeled *quote mark*).

In other words, `<!DOCTYPE html SYSTEM "about:legacy-compat">` or `<!DOCTYPE html SYSTEM 'about:legacy-compat'>`, case-insensitively except for the part in single or double quotes.

The [DOCTYPE legacy string](#327.html_doctype-legacy-string) should not be used unless the document is generated from a system that cannot output the shorter string.

* * *

To help authors transition from HTML4 and XHTML1, an <dfn id="327.html_obsolete-permitted-doctype-string">obsolete permitted DOCTYPE string</dfn> can be inserted into the DOCTYPE (in the position defined above). This string must consist of:

1.  One or more [space characters](#327.html_space-character).
2.  A string that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#327.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`PUBLIC`".
3.  One or more [space characters](#327.html_space-character).
4.  A U+0022 QUOTATION MARK or U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (the *first quote mark*).
5.  The string from one of the cells in the first column of the table below. The row to which this cell belongs is the *selected row*.
6.  A matching U+0022 QUOTATION MARK or U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (i.e. the same character as in the earlier step labeled *first quote mark*).
7.  If a system identifier is used,
    1.  One or more [space characters](#327.html_space-character).
    2.  A U+0022 QUOTATION MARK or U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (the *third quote mark*).
    3.  The string from the cell in the second column of the *selected row*.
    4.  A matching U+0022 QUOTATION MARK or U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (i.e. the same character as in the earlier step labeled *third quote mark*).

Allowed values for public and system identifiers in an [obsolete permitted DOCTYPE string](#327.html_obsolete-permitted-doctype-string).

| Public identifier | System identifier | System identifier optional? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.0//EN` | `http://www.w3.org/TR/REC-html40/strict.dtd` | Yes |
| `-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN` | `http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/strict.dtd` | Yes |
| `-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Strict//EN` | `http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-strict.dtd` | No |
| `-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.1//EN` | `http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml11/DTD/xhtml11.dtd` | No |

A [DOCTYPE](#327.html_syntax-doctype) containing an [obsolete permitted DOCTYPE string](#327.html_obsolete-permitted-doctype-string) is an <dfn id="327.html_obsolete-permitted-doctype">obsolete permitted DOCTYPE</dfn>. Authors should not use [obsolete permitted DOCTYPEs](#327.html_obsolete-permitted-doctype), as they are unnecessarily long.

#### 8.1.2 Elements

There are five different kinds of <dfn id="328.html_syntax-elements" data-anolis-xref="syntax-elements">elements</dfn>: [void elements](#328.html_void-elements), [raw text elements](#328.html_raw-text-elements), [escapable raw text elements](#328.html_escapable-raw-text-elements), [foreign elements](#328.html_foreign-elements), and [normal elements](#328.html_normal-elements).

<dfn id="328.html_void-elements">Void elements</dfn>

[`area`](#328.html_the-area-element), [`base`](#328.html_the-base-element), [`br`](#328.html_the-br-element), [`col`](#328.html_the-col-element), [`embed`](#328.html_the-embed-element), [`hr`](#328.html_the-hr-element), [`img`](#328.html_the-img-element), [`input`](#328.html_the-input-element), [`keygen`](#328.html_the-keygen-element), [`link`](#328.html_the-link-element), [`meta`](#328.html_the-meta-element), [`param`](#328.html_the-param-element), [`source`](#328.html_the-source-element), [`track`](#328.html_the-track-element), [`wbr`](#328.html_the-wbr-element)

<dfn id="328.html_raw-text-elements">Raw text elements</dfn>

[`script`](#328.html_the-script-element), [`style`](#328.html_the-style-element)

<dfn id="328.html_escapable-raw-text-elements">escapable raw text elements</dfn>

[`textarea`](#328.html_the-textarea-element), [`title`](#328.html_the-title-element)

<dfn id="328.html_foreign-elements">Foreign elements</dfn>

Elements from the [MathML namespace](#328.html_mathml-namespace) and the [SVG namespace](#328.html_svg-namespace).

<dfn id="328.html_normal-elements">Normal elements</dfn>

All other allowed [HTML elements](#328.html_html-elements) are normal elements.

<dfn id="328.html_syntax-tags" data-anolis-xref="syntax-tags">Tags</dfn> are used to delimit the start and end of elements in the markup. [Raw text](#328.html_raw-text-elements), [escapable raw text](#328.html_escapable-raw-text-elements), and [normal](#328.html_normal-elements) elements have a [start tag](#328.html_syntax-start-tag) to indicate where they begin, and an [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) to indicate where they end. The start and end tags of certain [normal elements](#328.html_normal-elements) can be [omitted](#328.html_syntax-tag-omission), as described below in the section on [optional tags](#328.html_syntax-tag-omission). Those that cannot be omitted must not be omitted. [Void elements](#328.html_void-elements) only have a start tag; end tags must not be specified for [void elements](#328.html_void-elements). [Foreign elements](#328.html_foreign-elements) must either have a start tag and an end tag, or a start tag that is marked as self-closing, in which case they must not have an end tag.

The [contents](#328.html_concept-html-contents) of the element must be placed between just after the start tag (which [might be implied, in certain cases](#328.html_syntax-tag-omission)) and just before the end tag (which again, [might be implied in certain cases](#328.html_syntax-tag-omission)). The exact allowed contents of each individual element depend on the [content model](#328.html_content-models) of that element, as described earlier in this specification. Elements must not contain content that their content model disallows. In addition to the restrictions placed on the contents by those content models, however, the five types of elements have additional *syntactic* requirements.

[Void elements](#328.html_void-elements) can't have any contents (since there's no end tag, no content can be put between the start tag and the end tag).

[Raw text elements](#328.html_raw-text-elements) can have [text](#328.html_syntax-text), though it has [restrictions](#328.html_cdata-rcdata-restrictions) described below.

[Escapable raw text elements](#328.html_escapable-raw-text-elements) can have [text](#328.html_syntax-text) and [character references](#328.html_syntax-charref), but the text must not contain an [ambiguous ampersand](#328.html_syntax-ambiguous-ampersand). There are also [further restrictions](#328.html_cdata-rcdata-restrictions) described below.

[Foreign elements](#328.html_foreign-elements) whose start tag is marked as self-closing can't have any contents (since, again, as there's no end tag, no content can be put between the start tag and the end tag). [Foreign elements](#328.html_foreign-elements) whose start tag is *not* marked as self-closing can have [text](#328.html_syntax-text), [character references](#328.html_syntax-charref), [CDATA sections](#328.html_syntax-cdata), other [elements](#328.html_syntax-elements), and [comments](#328.html_syntax-comments), but the text must not contain the character "<" (U+003C) or an [ambiguous ampersand](#328.html_syntax-ambiguous-ampersand).

The HTML syntax does not support namespace declarations, even in [foreign elements](#328.html_foreign-elements).

For instance, consider the following HTML fragment:

```
<p>
 <svg>
  <metadata>
   <!-- this is invalid -->
   <cdr:license xmlns:cdr="http://www.example.com/cdr/metadata" name="MIT"/>
  </metadata>
 </svg>
</p>
```

The innermost element, `cdr:license`, is actually in the SVG namespace, as the "`xmlns:cdr`" attribute has no effect (unlike in XML). In fact, as the comment in the fragment above says, the fragment is actually non-conforming. This is because the SVG specification does not define any elements called "`cdr:license`" in the SVG namespace.

[Normal elements](#328.html_normal-elements) can have [text](#328.html_syntax-text), [character references](#328.html_syntax-charref), other [elements](#328.html_syntax-elements), and [comments](#328.html_syntax-comments), but the text must not contain the character "<" (U+003C) or an [ambiguous ampersand](#328.html_syntax-ambiguous-ampersand). Some [normal elements](#328.html_normal-elements) also have [yet more restrictions](#328.html_element-restrictions) on what content they are allowed to hold, beyond the restrictions imposed by the content model and those described in this paragraph. Those restrictions are described below.

Tags contain a <dfn id="328.html_syntax-tag-name" data-anolis-xref="syntax-tag-name">tag name</dfn>, giving the element's name. HTML elements all have names that only use [alphanumeric ASCII characters](#328.html_alphanumeric-ascii-characters). In the HTML syntax, tag names, even those for [foreign elements](#328.html_foreign-elements), may be written with any mix of lower- and uppercase letters that, when converted to all-lowercase, matches the element's tag name; tag names are case-insensitive.

##### 8.1.2.1 Start tags

<dfn id="328.html_syntax-start-tag" data-anolis-xref="syntax-start-tag">Start tags</dfn> must have the following format:

1.  The first character of a start tag must be a "<" (U+003C) character.
2.  The next few characters of a start tag must be the element's [tag name](#328.html_syntax-tag-name).
3.  If there are to be any attributes in the next step, there must first be one or more [space characters](#328.html_space-character).
4.  Then, the start tag may have a number of attributes, the [syntax for which](#328.html_syntax-attributes) is described below. Attributes must be separated from each other by one or more [space characters](#328.html_space-character).
5.  After the attributes, or after the [tag name](#328.html_syntax-tag-name) if there are no attributes, there may be one or more [space characters](#328.html_space-character). (Some attributes are required to be followed by a space. See the [attributes section](#328.html_syntax-attributes) below.)
6.  Then, if the element is one of the [void elements](#328.html_void-elements), or if the element is a [foreign element](#328.html_foreign-elements), then there may be a single "/" (U+002F) character. This character has no effect on [void elements](#328.html_void-elements), but on [foreign elements](#328.html_foreign-elements) it marks the start tag as self-closing.
7.  Finally, start tags must be closed by a ">" (U+003E) character.

##### 8.1.2.2 End tags

<dfn id="328.html_syntax-end-tag" data-anolis-xref="syntax-end-tag">End tags</dfn> must have the following format:

1.  The first character of an end tag must be a "<" (U+003C) character.
2.  The second character of an end tag must be a "/" (U+002F) character.
3.  The next few characters of an end tag must be the element's [tag name](#328.html_syntax-tag-name).
4.  After the tag name, there may be one or more [space characters](#328.html_space-character).
5.  Finally, end tags must be closed by a ">" (U+003E) character.

##### 8.1.2.3 Attributes

<dfn id="328.html_syntax-attributes" data-anolis-xref="syntax-attributes">Attributes</dfn> for an element are expressed inside the element's start tag.

Attributes have a name and a value. <dfn id="328.html_syntax-attribute-name" data-anolis-xref="syntax-attribute-name">Attribute names</dfn> must consist of one or more characters other than the [space characters](#328.html_space-character), U+0000 NULL, U+0022 QUOTATION MARK ("), U+0027 APOSTROPHE ('), ">" (U+003E), "/" (U+002F), and "=" (U+003D) characters, the [control characters](#328.html_control-characters), and any characters that are not defined by Unicode. In the HTML syntax, attribute names, even those for [foreign elements](#328.html_foreign-elements), may be written with any mix of lower- and uppercase letters that are an [ASCII case-insensitive](#328.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the attribute's name.

<dfn id="328.html_syntax-attribute-value" data-anolis-xref="syntax-attribute-value">Attribute values</dfn> are a mixture of [text](#328.html_syntax-text) and [character references](#328.html_syntax-charref), except with the additional restriction that the text cannot contain an [ambiguous ampersand](#328.html_syntax-ambiguous-ampersand).

Attributes can be specified in four different ways:

Empty attribute syntax

Just the [attribute name](#328.html_syntax-attribute-name). The value is implicitly the empty string.

In the following example, the [`disabled`](#328.html_attr-fe-disabled) attribute is given with the empty attribute syntax:

```
<input disabled>
```

If an attribute using the empty attribute syntax is to be followed by another attribute, then there must be a [space character](#328.html_space-character) separating the two.

Unquoted attribute value syntax

The [attribute name](#328.html_syntax-attribute-name), followed by zero or more [space characters](#328.html_space-character), followed by a single U+003D EQUALS SIGN character, followed by zero or more [space characters](#328.html_space-character), followed by the [attribute value](#328.html_syntax-attribute-value), which, in addition to the requirements given above for attribute values, must not contain any literal [space characters](#328.html_space-character), any U+0022 QUOTATION MARK characters ("), U+0027 APOSTROPHE characters ('), "=" (U+003D) characters, "<" (U+003C) characters, ">" (U+003E) characters, or U+0060 GRAVE ACCENT characters (`), and must not be the empty string.

In the following example, the [`value`](#328.html_attr-input-value) attribute is given with the unquoted attribute value syntax:

```
<input value=yes>
```

If an attribute using the unquoted attribute syntax is to be followed by another attribute or by the optional "/" (U+002F) character allowed in step 6 of the [start tag](#328.html_syntax-start-tag) syntax above, then there must be a [space character](#328.html_space-character) separating the two.

Single-quoted attribute value syntax

The [attribute name](#328.html_syntax-attribute-name), followed by zero or more [space characters](#328.html_space-character), followed by a single U+003D EQUALS SIGN character, followed by zero or more [space characters](#328.html_space-character), followed by a single "'" (U+0027) character, followed by the [attribute value](#328.html_syntax-attribute-value), which, in addition to the requirements given above for attribute values, must not contain any literal "'" (U+0027) characters, and finally followed by a second single "'" (U+0027) character.

In the following example, the [`type`](#328.html_attr-input-type) attribute is given with the single-quoted attribute value syntax:

```
<input type='checkbox'>
```

If an attribute using the single-quoted attribute syntax is to be followed by another attribute, then there must be a [space character](#328.html_space-character) separating the two.

Double-quoted attribute value syntax

The [attribute name](#328.html_syntax-attribute-name), followed by zero or more [space characters](#328.html_space-character), followed by a single U+003D EQUALS SIGN character, followed by zero or more [space characters](#328.html_space-character), followed by a single """ (U+0022) character, followed by the [attribute value](#328.html_syntax-attribute-value), which, in addition to the requirements given above for attribute values, must not contain any literal U+0022 QUOTATION MARK characters ("), and finally followed by a second single """ (U+0022) character.

In the following example, the [`name`](#328.html_attr-fe-name) attribute is given with the double-quoted attribute value syntax:

```
<input name="be evil">
```

If an attribute using the double-quoted attribute syntax is to be followed by another attribute, then there must be a [space character](#328.html_space-character) separating the two.

There must never be two or more attributes on the same start tag whose names are an [ASCII case-insensitive](#328.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for each other.

* * *

When a [foreign element](#328.html_foreign-elements) has one of the namespaced attributes given by the local name and namespace of the first and second cells of a row from the following table, it must be written using the name given by the third cell from the same row.

| Local name | Namespace | Attribute name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actuate` | [XLink namespace](#328.html_xlink-namespace) | `xlink:actuate` |
| `arcrole` | [XLink namespace](#328.html_xlink-namespace) | `xlink:arcrole` |
| `href` | [XLink namespace](#328.html_xlink-namespace) | `xlink:href` |
| `role` | [XLink namespace](#328.html_xlink-namespace) | `xlink:role` |
| `show` | [XLink namespace](#328.html_xlink-namespace) | `xlink:show` |
| `title` | [XLink namespace](#328.html_xlink-namespace) | `xlink:title` |
| `type` | [XLink namespace](#328.html_xlink-namespace) | `xlink:type` |
| `base` | [XML namespace](#328.html_xml-namespace) | `xml:base` |
| `lang` | [XML namespace](#328.html_xml-namespace) | `xml:lang` |
| `space` | [XML namespace](#328.html_xml-namespace) | `xml:space` |
| `xmlns` | [XMLNS namespace](#328.html_xmlns-namespace) | `xmlns` |
| `xlink` | [XMLNS namespace](#328.html_xmlns-namespace) | `xmlns:xlink` |

No other namespaced attribute can be expressed in [the HTML syntax](#328.html_syntax).

Whether the attributes in the table above are conforming or not is defined by other specifications (e.g. the SVG and MathML specifications); this section only describes the syntax rules if the attributes are serialized using the HTML syntax.

##### 8.1.2.4 Optional tags

Certain tags can be <dfn id="328.html_syntax-tag-omission" data-anolis-xref="syntax-tag-omission">omitted</dfn>.

Omitting an element's [start tag](#328.html_syntax-start-tag) in the situations described below does not mean the element is not present; it is implied, but it is still there. For example, an HTML document always has a root [`html`](#328.html_the-html-element) element, even if the string `<html>` doesn't appear anywhere in the markup.

An [`html`](#328.html_the-html-element) element's [start tag](#328.html_syntax-start-tag) may be omitted if the first thing inside the [`html`](#328.html_the-html-element) element is not a [comment](#328.html_syntax-comments).

An [`html`](#328.html_the-html-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`html`](#328.html_the-html-element) element is not immediately followed by a [comment](#328.html_syntax-comments).

A [`head`](#328.html_the-head-element) element's [start tag](#328.html_syntax-start-tag) may be omitted if the element is empty, or if the first thing inside the [`head`](#328.html_the-head-element) element is an element.

A [`head`](#328.html_the-head-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`head`](#328.html_the-head-element) element is not immediately followed by a [space character](#328.html_space-character) or a [comment](#328.html_syntax-comments).

A [`body`](#328.html_the-body-element) element's [start tag](#328.html_syntax-start-tag) may be omitted if the element is empty, or if the first thing inside the [`body`](#328.html_the-body-element) element is not a [space character](#328.html_space-character) or a [comment](#328.html_syntax-comments), except if the first thing inside the [`body`](#328.html_the-body-element) element is a [`meta`](#328.html_the-meta-element), [`link`](#328.html_the-link-element), [`script`](#328.html_the-script-element), [`style`](#328.html_the-style-element), or [`template`](#328.html_the-template-element) element.

A [`body`](#328.html_the-body-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`body`](#328.html_the-body-element) element is not immediately followed by a [comment](#328.html_syntax-comments).

An [`li`](#328.html_the-li-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`li`](#328.html_the-li-element) element is immediately followed by another [`li`](#328.html_the-li-element) element or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`dt`](#328.html_the-dt-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`dt`](#328.html_the-dt-element) element is immediately followed by another [`dt`](#328.html_the-dt-element) element or a [`dd`](#328.html_the-dd-element) element.

A [`dd`](#328.html_the-dd-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`dd`](#328.html_the-dd-element) element is immediately followed by another [`dd`](#328.html_the-dd-element) element or a [`dt`](#328.html_the-dt-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`p`](#328.html_the-p-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`p`](#328.html_the-p-element) element is immediately followed by an [`address`](#328.html_the-address-element), [`article`](#328.html_the-article-element), [`aside`](#328.html_the-aside-element), [`blockquote`](#328.html_the-blockquote-element), [`div`](#328.html_the-div-element), [`dl`](#328.html_the-dl-element), [`fieldset`](#328.html_the-fieldset-element), [`footer`](#328.html_the-footer-element), [`form`](#328.html_the-form-element), [`h1`](#328.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`h2`](#328.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`h3`](#328.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`h4`](#328.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`h5`](#328.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`h6`](#328.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`header`](#328.html_the-header-element), [`hgroup`](#328.html_hgroup), [`hr`](#328.html_the-hr-element), [`main`](#328.html_the-main-element), [`nav`](#328.html_the-nav-element), [`ol`](#328.html_the-ol-element), [`p`](#328.html_the-p-element), [`pre`](#328.html_the-pre-element), [`section`](#328.html_the-section-element), [`table`](#328.html_the-table-element), or [`ul`](#328.html_the-ul-element), element, or if there is no more content in the parent element and the parent element is not an [`a`](#328.html_the-a-element) element.

An [`rb`](#328.html_the-rb-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`rb`](#328.html_the-rb-element) element is immediately followed by an [`rb`](#328.html_the-rb-element), [`rt`](#328.html_the-rt-element), [`rtc`](#328.html_the-rtc-element) or [`rp`](#328.html_the-rp-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

An [`rt`](#328.html_the-rt-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`rt`](#328.html_the-rt-element) element is immediately followed by an [`rb`](#328.html_the-rb-element), [`rt`](#328.html_the-rt-element), [`rtc`](#328.html_the-rtc-element), or [`rp`](#328.html_the-rp-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

An [`rtc`](#328.html_the-rtc-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`rtc`](#328.html_the-rtc-element) element is immediately followed by an [`rb`](#328.html_the-rb-element), [`rtc`](#328.html_the-rtc-element) or [`rp`](#328.html_the-rp-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

An [`rp`](#328.html_the-rp-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`rp`](#328.html_the-rp-element) element is immediately followed by an [`rb`](#328.html_the-rb-element), [`rt`](#328.html_the-rt-element), [`rtc`](#328.html_the-rtc-element) or [`rp`](#328.html_the-rp-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

An [`optgroup`](#328.html_the-optgroup-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`optgroup`](#328.html_the-optgroup-element) element is immediately followed by another [`optgroup`](#328.html_the-optgroup-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

An [`option`](#328.html_the-option-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`option`](#328.html_the-option-element) element is immediately followed by another [`option`](#328.html_the-option-element) element, or if it is immediately followed by an [`optgroup`](#328.html_the-optgroup-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`colgroup`](#328.html_the-colgroup-element) element's [start tag](#328.html_syntax-start-tag) may be omitted if the first thing inside the [`colgroup`](#328.html_the-colgroup-element) element is a [`col`](#328.html_the-col-element) element, and if the element is not immediately preceded by another [`colgroup`](#328.html_the-colgroup-element) element whose [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) has been omitted. (It can't be omitted if the element is empty.)

A [`colgroup`](#328.html_the-colgroup-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`colgroup`](#328.html_the-colgroup-element) element is not immediately followed by a [space character](#328.html_space-character) or a [comment](#328.html_syntax-comments).

A [`thead`](#328.html_the-thead-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`thead`](#328.html_the-thead-element) element is immediately followed by a [`tbody`](#328.html_the-tbody-element) or [`tfoot`](#328.html_the-tfoot-element) element.

A [`tbody`](#328.html_the-tbody-element) element's [start tag](#328.html_syntax-start-tag) may be omitted if the first thing inside the [`tbody`](#328.html_the-tbody-element) element is a [`tr`](#328.html_the-tr-element) element, and if the element is not immediately preceded by a [`tbody`](#328.html_the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#328.html_the-thead-element), or [`tfoot`](#328.html_the-tfoot-element) element whose [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) has been omitted. (It can't be omitted if the element is empty.)

A [`tbody`](#328.html_the-tbody-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`tbody`](#328.html_the-tbody-element) element is immediately followed by a [`tbody`](#328.html_the-tbody-element) or [`tfoot`](#328.html_the-tfoot-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`tfoot`](#328.html_the-tfoot-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`tfoot`](#328.html_the-tfoot-element) element is immediately followed by a [`tbody`](#328.html_the-tbody-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`tr`](#328.html_the-tr-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`tr`](#328.html_the-tr-element) element is immediately followed by another [`tr`](#328.html_the-tr-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`td`](#328.html_the-td-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`td`](#328.html_the-td-element) element is immediately followed by a [`td`](#328.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#328.html_the-th-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`th`](#328.html_the-th-element) element's [end tag](#328.html_syntax-end-tag) may be omitted if the [`th`](#328.html_the-th-element) element is immediately followed by a [`td`](#328.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#328.html_the-th-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

**However**, a [start tag](#328.html_syntax-start-tag) must never be omitted if it has any attributes.

##### 8.1.2.5 Restrictions on content models

For historical reasons, certain elements have extra restrictions beyond even the restrictions given by their content model.

A [`table`](#328.html_the-table-element) element must not contain [`tr`](#328.html_the-tr-element) elements, even though these elements are technically allowed inside [`table`](#328.html_the-table-element) elements according to the content models described in this specification. (If a [`tr`](#328.html_the-tr-element) element is put inside a [`table`](#328.html_the-table-element) in the markup, it will in fact imply a [`tbody`](#328.html_the-tbody-element) start tag before it.)

A single [newline](#328.html_syntax-newlines) may be placed immediately after the [start tag](#328.html_syntax-start-tag) of [`pre`](#328.html_the-pre-element) and [`textarea`](#328.html_the-textarea-element) elements. If the element's contents are intended to start with a [newline](#328.html_syntax-newlines), two consecutive newlines thus need to be included by the author.

The following two [`pre`](#328.html_the-pre-element) blocks are equivalent:

```
<pre>Hello</pre>
```

```
<pre>
Hello</pre>
```

##### 8.1.2.6 Restrictions on the contents of raw text and escapable raw text elements

The text in [raw text](#328.html_raw-text-elements) and [escapable raw text elements](#328.html_escapable-raw-text-elements) must not contain any occurrences of the string "`</`" (U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN, U+002F SOLIDUS) followed by characters that case-insensitively match the tag name of the element followed by one of "tab" (U+0009), "LF" (U+000A), "FF" (U+000C), "CR" (U+000D), U+0020 SPACE, ">" (U+003E), or "/" (U+002F).

#### 8.1.3 Text

<dfn id="329.html_syntax-text" data-anolis-xref="syntax-text">Text</dfn> is allowed inside elements, attribute values, and comments. Extra constraints are placed on what is and what is not allowed in text based on where the text is to be put, as described in the other sections.

##### 8.1.3.1 Newlines

<dfn id="329.html_syntax-newlines" data-anolis-xref="syntax-newlines">Newlines</dfn> in HTML may be represented either as "CR" (U+000D) characters, "LF" (U+000A) characters, or pairs of "CR" (U+000D), "LF" (U+000A) characters in that order.

Where [character references](#329.html_syntax-charref) are allowed, a character reference of a "LF" (U+000A) character (but not a "CR" (U+000D) character) also represents a [newline](#329.html_syntax-newlines).

#### 8.1.4 Character references

In certain cases described in other sections, [text](#330.html_syntax-text) may be mixed with <dfn id="330.html_syntax-charref" data-anolis-xref="syntax-charref">character references</dfn>. These can be used to escape characters that couldn't otherwise legally be included in [text](#330.html_syntax-text).

Character references must start with a U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&). Following this, there are three possible kinds of character references:

Named character references

The ampersand must be followed by one of the names given in the [named character references](#330.html_named-character-references) section, using the same case. The name must be one that is terminated by a ";" (U+003B) character.

Decimal numeric character reference

The ampersand must be followed by a "#" (U+0023) character, followed by one or more [ASCII digits](#330.html_ascii-digits), representing a base-ten integer that corresponds to a Unicode code point that is allowed according to the definition below. The digits must then be followed by a ";" (U+003B) character.

Hexadecimal numeric character reference

The ampersand must be followed by a "#" (U+0023) character, which must be followed by either a "x" (U+0078) character or a "X" (U+0058) character, which must then be followed by one or more [ASCII hex digits](#330.html_ascii-hex-digits), representing a base-sixteen integer that corresponds to a Unicode code point that is allowed according to the definition below. The digits must then be followed by a ";" (U+003B) character.

The numeric character reference forms described above are allowed to reference any Unicode code point other than U+0000, U+000D, permanently undefined Unicode characters (noncharacters), surrogates (U+D800–U+DFFF), and [control characters](#330.html_control-characters) other than [space characters](#330.html_space-character).

An <dfn id="330.html_syntax-ambiguous-ampersand" data-anolis-xref="syntax-ambiguous-ampersand">ambiguous ampersand</dfn> is a U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&) that is followed by one or more [alphanumeric ASCII characters](#330.html_alphanumeric-ascii-characters), followed by a ";" (U+003B) character, where these characters do not match any of the names given in the [named character references](#330.html_named-character-references) section.

#### 8.1.5 CDATA sections

<dfn id="331.html_syntax-cdata" data-anolis-xref="syntax-cdata">CDATA sections</dfn> must consist of the following components, in this order:

1.  The string "`<![CDATA[`".
2.  Optionally, [text](#331.html_syntax-text), with the additional restriction that the text must not contain the string "`]]>`".
3.  The string "`]]>`".

CDATA sections can only be used in foreign content (MathML or SVG). In this example, a CDATA section is used to escape the contents of an `ms` element:

```
<p>You can add a string to a number, but this stringifies the number:</p>
<math>
 <ms><![CDATA[x<y]]></ms>
 <mo>+</mo>
 <mn>3</mn>
 <mo>=</mo>
 <ms><![CDATA[x<y3]]></ms>
</math>
```

#### 8.1.6 Comments

<dfn id="332.html_syntax-comments" data-anolis-xref="syntax-comments">Comments</dfn> must start with the four character sequence U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN, U+0021 EXCLAMATION MARK, U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS (`<!--`). Following this sequence, the comment may have [text](#332.html_syntax-text), with the additional restriction that the text must not start with a single ">" (U+003E) character, nor start with a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-) followed by a ">" (U+003E) character, nor contain two consecutive U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS characters (`--`), nor end with a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-). Finally, the comment must be ended by the three character sequence U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN (`-->`).

### 8.2 Parsing HTML documents

*This section only applies to user agents, data mining tools, and conformance checkers.*

The rules for parsing XML documents into DOM trees are covered by the next section, entitled "[The XHTML syntax](#333.html_the-xhtml-syntax)".

User agents must use the parsing rules described in this section to generate the DOM trees from [`text/html`](#333.html_text/html) resources. Together, these rules define what is referred to as the <dfn id="333.html_html-parser">HTML parser</dfn>.

While the HTML syntax described in this specification bears a close resemblance to SGML and XML, it is a separate language with its own parsing rules.

Some earlier versions of HTML (in particular from HTML2 to HTML4) were based on SGML and used SGML parsing rules. However, few (if any) web browsers ever implemented true SGML parsing for HTML documents; the only user agents to strictly handle HTML as an SGML application have historically been validators. The resulting confusion — with validators claiming documents to have one representation while widely deployed Web browsers interoperably implemented a different representation — has wasted decades of productivity. This version of HTML thus returns to a non-SGML basis.

Authors interested in using SGML tools in their authoring pipeline are encouraged to use XML tools and the XML serialization of HTML.

This specification defines the parsing rules for HTML documents, whether they are syntactically correct or not. Certain points in the parsing algorithm are said to be <dfn id="333.html_parse-error" data-anolis-xref="parse
  error">parse errors</dfn>. The error handling for parse errors is well-defined (that's the processing rules described throughout this specification), but user agents, while parsing an HTML document, may [abort the parser](#333.html_abort-a-parser) at the first [parse error](#333.html_parse-error) that they encounter for which they do not wish to apply the rules described in this specification.

Conformance checkers must report at least one parse error condition to the user if one or more parse error conditions exist in the document and must not report parse error conditions if none exist in the document. Conformance checkers may report more than one parse error condition if more than one parse error condition exists in the document.

Parse errors are only errors with the *syntax* of HTML. In addition to checking for parse errors, conformance checkers will also verify that the document obeys all the other conformance requirements described in this specification.

For the purposes of conformance checkers, if a resource is determined to be in [the HTML syntax](#333.html_syntax), then it is an [HTML document](#333.html_html-documents).

As stated [in the terminology section](#333.html_html-elements), references to [element types](#333.html_element-type) that do not explicitly specify a namespace always refer to elements in the [HTML namespace](#333.html_html-namespace-0). For example, if the spec talks about "a [`div`](#333.html_the-div-element) element", then that is an element with the local name "`div`", the namespace "`http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml`", and the interface [`HTMLDivElement`](#333.html_htmldivelement). Where possible, references to such elements are hyperlinked to their definition.

#### 8.2.1 Overview of the parsing model

![](Images/db9ddf8c2228b9488ee96f7c67e19992.jpg)

The input to the HTML parsing process consists of a stream of [Unicode code points](#334.html_unicode-code-point), which is passed through a [tokenization](#334.html_tokenization) stage followed by a [tree construction](#334.html_tree-construction) stage. The output is a [`Document`](#334.html_document) object.

Implementations that [do not support scripting](#334.html_non-scripted) do not have to actually create a DOM [`Document`](#334.html_document) object, but the DOM tree in such cases is still used as the model for the rest of the specification.

In the common case, the data handled by the tokenization stage comes from the network, but [it can also come from script](#334.html_dynamic-markup-insertion) running in the user agent, e.g. using the [`document.write()`](#334.html_dom-document-write) API.

There is only one set of states for the tokenizer stage and the tree construction stage, but the tree construction stage is reentrant, meaning that while the tree construction stage is handling one token, the tokenizer might be resumed, causing further tokens to be emitted and processed before the first token's processing is complete.

In the following example, the tree construction stage will be called upon to handle a "p" start tag token while handling the "script" end tag token:

```
...
<script>
 document.write('<p>');
</script>
...
```

To handle these cases, parsers have a <dfn id="334.html_script-nesting-level">script nesting level</dfn>, which must be initially set to zero, and a <dfn id="334.html_parser-pause-flag">parser pause flag</dfn>, which must be initially set to false.

#### 8.2.2 The <dfn>input byte stream</dfn>

The stream of Unicode code points that comprises the input to the tokenization stage will be initially seen by the user agent as a stream of bytes (typically coming over the network or from the local file system). The bytes encode the actual characters according to a particular *character encoding*, which the user agent uses to decode the bytes into characters.

For XML documents, the algorithm user agents must use to determine the character encoding is given by the XML specification. This section does not apply to XML documents. [[XML]](#335.html_refsXML)

Usually, the [encoding sniffing algorithm](#335.html_encoding-sniffing-algorithm) defined below is used to determine the character encoding.

Given a character encoding, the bytes in the [input byte stream](#335.html_the-input-byte-stream) must be converted to Unicode code points for the tokenizer's [input stream](#335.html_input-stream), as described by the rules for that encoding's [decoder](#335.html_decoder).

Bytes or sequences of bytes in the original byte stream that did not conform to the encoding specification (e.g. invalid UTF-8 byte sequences in a UTF-8 input byte stream) are errors that conformance checkers are expected to report.

Leading Byte Order Marks (BOMs) are not stripped by the decoder algorithms, they are stripped by the algorithm below.

The decoder algorithms describe how to handle invalid input; for security reasons, it is imperative that those rules be followed precisely. Differences in how invalid byte sequences are handled can result in, amongst other problems, script injection vulnerabilities ("XSS").

When the HTML parser is decoding an input byte stream, it uses a character encoding and a <dfn id="335.html_concept-encoding-confidence" data-anolis-xref="concept-encoding-confidence">confidence</dfn>. The confidence is either *tentative*, *certain*, or *irrelevant*. The encoding used, and whether the confidence in that encoding is *tentative* or *certain*, is [used during the parsing](#335.html_meta-charset-during-parse) to determine whether to [change the encoding](#335.html_change-the-encoding). If no encoding is necessary, e.g. because the parser is operating on a Unicode stream and doesn't have to use a character encoding at all, then the [confidence](#335.html_concept-encoding-confidence) is *irrelevant*.

Some algorithms feed the parser by directly adding characters to the [input stream](#335.html_input-stream) rather than adding bytes to the [input byte stream](#335.html_the-input-byte-stream).

##### 8.2.2.1 Parsing with a known character encoding

When the HTML parser is to operate on an input byte stream that has <dfn id="335.html_a-known-definite-encoding">a known definite encoding</dfn>, then the character encoding is that encoding and the [confidence](#335.html_concept-encoding-confidence) is *certain*.

##### 8.2.2.2 Determining the character encoding

In some cases, it might be impractical to unambiguously determine the encoding before parsing the document. Because of this, this specification provides for a two-pass mechanism with an optional pre-scan. Implementations are allowed, as described below, to apply a simplified parsing algorithm to whatever bytes they have available before beginning to parse the document. Then, the real parser is started, using a tentative encoding derived from this pre-parse and other out-of-band metadata. If, while the document is being loaded, the user agent discovers a character encoding declaration that conflicts with this information, then the parser can get reinvoked to perform a parse of the document with the real encoding.
