Switch to the [script data double escaped dash dash state](#337.html_script-data-double-escaped-dash-dash-state). Emit a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character token.

"<" (U+003C)

Switch to the [script data double escaped less-than sign state](#337.html_script-data-double-escaped-less-than-sign-state). Emit a U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN character token.

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [script data double escaped state](#337.html_script-data-double-escaped-state). Emit a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character token.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Switch to the [script data double escaped state](#337.html_script-data-double-escaped-state). Emit the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) as a character token.

##### 8.2.4.31 <dfn>Script data double escaped dash dash state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"-" (U+002D)

Emit a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character token.

"<" (U+003C)

Switch to the [script data double escaped less-than sign state](#337.html_script-data-double-escaped-less-than-sign-state). Emit a U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN character token.

">" (U+003E)

Switch to the [script data state](#337.html_script-data-state). Emit a U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN character token.

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [script data double escaped state](#337.html_script-data-double-escaped-state). Emit a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character token.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Switch to the [script data double escaped state](#337.html_script-data-double-escaped-state). Emit the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) as a character token.

##### 8.2.4.32 <dfn>Script data double escaped less-than sign state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"/" (U+002F)

Set the [`temporary buffer`](#337.html_temporary-buffer) to the empty string. Switch to the [script data double escape end state](#337.html_script-data-double-escape-end-state). Emit a U+002F SOLIDUS character token.

Anything else

Switch to the [script data double escaped state](#337.html_script-data-double-escaped-state). Reconsume the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character).

##### 8.2.4.33 <dfn>Script data double escape end state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE
"/" (U+002F)
">" (U+003E)

If the [`temporary buffer`](#337.html_temporary-buffer) is the string "`script`", then switch to the [script data escaped state](#337.html_script-data-escaped-state). Otherwise, switch to the [script data double escaped state](#337.html_script-data-double-escaped-state). Emit the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) as a character token.

[Uppercase ASCII letter](#337.html_uppercase-ascii-letters)

Append the lowercase version of the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) (add 0x0020 to the character's code point) to the [`temporary buffer`](#337.html_temporary-buffer). Emit the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) as a character token.

[Lowercase ASCII letter](#337.html_lowercase-ascii-letters)

Append the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the [`temporary buffer`](#337.html_temporary-buffer). Emit the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) as a character token.

Anything else

Switch to the [script data double escaped state](#337.html_script-data-double-escaped-state). Reconsume the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character).

##### 8.2.4.34 <dfn>Before attribute name state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE

Ignore the character.

"/" (U+002F)

Switch to the [self-closing start tag state](#337.html_self-closing-start-tag-state).

">" (U+003E)

Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the current tag token.

[Uppercase ASCII letter](#337.html_uppercase-ascii-letters)

Start a new attribute in the current tag token. Set that attribute's name to the lowercase version of the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) (add 0x0020 to the character's code point), and its value to the empty string. Switch to the [attribute name state](#337.html_attribute-name-state).

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Start a new attribute in the current tag token. Set that attribute's name to a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character, and its value to the empty string. Switch to the [attribute name state](#337.html_attribute-name-state).

U+0022 QUOTATION MARK (")
"'" (U+0027)
"<" (U+003C)
"=" (U+003D)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Treat it as per the "anything else" entry below.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Start a new attribute in the current tag token. Set that attribute's name to the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character), and its value to the empty string. Switch to the [attribute name state](#337.html_attribute-name-state).

##### 8.2.4.35 <dfn>Attribute name state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE

Switch to the [after attribute name state](#337.html_after-attribute-name-state).

"/" (U+002F)

Switch to the [self-closing start tag state](#337.html_self-closing-start-tag-state).

"=" (U+003D)

Switch to the [before attribute value state](#337.html_before-attribute-value-state).

">" (U+003E)

Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the current tag token.

[Uppercase ASCII letter](#337.html_uppercase-ascii-letters)

Append the lowercase version of the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) (add 0x0020 to the character's code point) to the current attribute's name.

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the current attribute's name.

U+0022 QUOTATION MARK (")
"'" (U+0027)
"<" (U+003C)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Treat it as per the "anything else" entry below.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Append the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the current attribute's name.

When the user agent leaves the attribute name state (and before emitting the tag token, if appropriate), the complete attribute's name must be compared to the other attributes on the same token; if there is already an attribute on the token with the exact same name, then this is a [parse error](#337.html_parse-error) and the new attribute must be removed from the token.

If an attribute is so removed from a token, it, along with the value that gets associated with it, if any, are never subsequently used by the parser, and are therefore effectively discarded. Removing the attribute in this way does not change its status as the "current attribute" for the purposes of the tokenizer, however.

##### 8.2.4.36 <dfn>After attribute name state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE

Ignore the character.

"/" (U+002F)

Switch to the [self-closing start tag state](#337.html_self-closing-start-tag-state).

"=" (U+003D)

Switch to the [before attribute value state](#337.html_before-attribute-value-state).

">" (U+003E)

Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the current tag token.

[Uppercase ASCII letter](#337.html_uppercase-ascii-letters)

Start a new attribute in the current tag token. Set that attribute's name to the lowercase version of the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) (add 0x0020 to the character's code point), and its value to the empty string. Switch to the [attribute name state](#337.html_attribute-name-state).

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Start a new attribute in the current tag token. Set that attribute's name to a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character, and its value to the empty string. Switch to the [attribute name state](#337.html_attribute-name-state).

U+0022 QUOTATION MARK (")
"'" (U+0027)
"<" (U+003C)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Treat it as per the "anything else" entry below.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Start a new attribute in the current tag token. Set that attribute's name to the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character), and its value to the empty string. Switch to the [attribute name state](#337.html_attribute-name-state).

##### 8.2.4.37 <dfn>Before attribute value state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE

Ignore the character.

U+0022 QUOTATION MARK (")

Switch to the [attribute value (double-quoted) state](#337.html_attribute-value-(double-quoted)-state).

U+0026 AMPERSAND (&)

Switch to the [attribute value (unquoted) state](#337.html_attribute-value-(unquoted)-state). Reconsume the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character).

"'" (U+0027)

Switch to the [attribute value (single-quoted) state](#337.html_attribute-value-(single-quoted)-state).

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the current attribute's value. Switch to the [attribute value (unquoted) state](#337.html_attribute-value-(unquoted)-state).

">" (U+003E)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the current tag token.

"<" (U+003C)
"=" (U+003D)
"`" (U+0060)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Treat it as per the "anything else" entry below.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Append the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the current attribute's value. Switch to the [attribute value (unquoted) state](#337.html_attribute-value-(unquoted)-state).

##### 8.2.4.38 <dfn>Attribute value (double-quoted) state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

U+0022 QUOTATION MARK (")

Switch to the [after attribute value (quoted) state](#337.html_after-attribute-value-(quoted)-state).

U+0026 AMPERSAND (&)

Switch to the [character reference in attribute value state](#337.html_character-reference-in-attribute-value-state), with the [additional allowed character](#337.html_additional-allowed-character) being U+0022 QUOTATION MARK (").

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the current attribute's value.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Append the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the current attribute's value.

##### 8.2.4.39 <dfn>Attribute value (single-quoted) state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"'" (U+0027)

Switch to the [after attribute value (quoted) state](#337.html_after-attribute-value-(quoted)-state).

U+0026 AMPERSAND (&)

Switch to the [character reference in attribute value state](#337.html_character-reference-in-attribute-value-state), with the [additional allowed character](#337.html_additional-allowed-character) being "'" (U+0027).

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the current attribute's value.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Append the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the current attribute's value.

##### 8.2.4.40 <dfn>Attribute value (unquoted) state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE

Switch to the [before attribute name state](#337.html_before-attribute-name-state).

U+0026 AMPERSAND (&)

Switch to the [character reference in attribute value state](#337.html_character-reference-in-attribute-value-state), with the [additional allowed character](#337.html_additional-allowed-character) being ">" (U+003E).

">" (U+003E)

Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the current tag token.

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the current attribute's value.

U+0022 QUOTATION MARK (")
"'" (U+0027)
"<" (U+003C)
"=" (U+003D)
"`" (U+0060)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Treat it as per the "anything else" entry below.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Append the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the current attribute's value.

##### 8.2.4.41 <dfn>Character reference in attribute value state</dfn>

Attempt to [consume a character reference](#337.html_consume-a-character-reference).

If nothing is returned, append a U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&) to the current attribute's value.

Otherwise, append the returned character tokens to the current attribute's value.

Finally, switch back to the attribute value state that switched into this state.

##### 8.2.4.42 <dfn>After attribute value (quoted) state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE

Switch to the [before attribute name state](#337.html_before-attribute-name-state).

"/" (U+002F)

Switch to the [self-closing start tag state](#337.html_self-closing-start-tag-state).

">" (U+003E)

Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the current tag token.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [before attribute name state](#337.html_before-attribute-name-state). Reconsume the character.

##### 8.2.4.43 <dfn>Self-closing start tag state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

">" (U+003E)

Set the *self-closing flag* of the current tag token. Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the current tag token.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [before attribute name state](#337.html_before-attribute-name-state). Reconsume the character.

##### 8.2.4.44 <dfn>Bogus comment state</dfn>

Consume every character up to and including the first ">" (U+003E) character or the end of the file (EOF), whichever comes first. Emit a comment token whose data is the concatenation of all the characters starting from and including the character that caused the state machine to switch into the bogus comment state, up to and including the character immediately before the last consumed character (i.e. up to the character just before the U+003E or EOF character), but with any U+0000 NULL characters replaced by U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER characters. (If the comment was started by the end of the file (EOF), the token is empty. Similarly, the token is empty if it was generated by the string "`<!>`".)

Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state).

If the end of the file was reached, reconsume the EOF character.

##### 8.2.4.45 <dfn>Markup declaration open state</dfn>

If the next two characters are both "-" (U+002D) characters, consume those two characters, create a comment token whose data is the empty string, and switch to the [comment start state](#337.html_comment-start-state).

Otherwise, if the next seven characters are an [ASCII case-insensitive](#337.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the word "DOCTYPE", then consume those characters and switch to the [DOCTYPE state](#337.html_doctype-state).

Otherwise, if there is an [adjusted current node](#337.html_adjusted-current-node) and it is not an element in the [HTML namespace](#337.html_html-namespace-0) and the next seven characters are a [case-sensitive](#337.html_case-sensitive) match for the string "[CDATA[" (the five uppercase letters "CDATA" with a U+005B LEFT SQUARE BRACKET character before and after), then consume those characters and switch to the [CDATA section state](#337.html_cdata-section-state).

Otherwise, this is a [parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [bogus comment state](#337.html_bogus-comment-state). The next character that is consumed, if any, is the first character that will be in the comment.

##### 8.2.4.46 <dfn>Comment start state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"-" (U+002D)

Switch to the [comment start dash state](#337.html_comment-start-dash-state).

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the comment token's data. Switch to the [comment state](#337.html_comment-state).

">" (U+003E)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the comment token.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the comment token. Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Append the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the comment token's data. Switch to the [comment state](#337.html_comment-state).

##### 8.2.4.47 <dfn>Comment start dash state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"-" (U+002D)

Switch to the [comment end state](#337.html_comment-end-state)

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append a "-" (U+002D) character and a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the comment token's data. Switch to the [comment state](#337.html_comment-state).

">" (U+003E)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the comment token.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the comment token. Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Append a "-" (U+002D) character and the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the comment token's data. Switch to the [comment state](#337.html_comment-state).

##### 8.2.4.48 <dfn id="337.html_comment">Comment state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"-" (U+002D)

Switch to the [comment end dash state](#337.html_comment-end-dash-state)

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the comment token's data.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the comment token. Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Append the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the comment token's data.

##### 8.2.4.49 <dfn>Comment end dash state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"-" (U+002D)

Switch to the [comment end state](#337.html_comment-end-state)

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append a "-" (U+002D) character and a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the comment token's data. Switch to the [comment state](#337.html_comment-state).

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the comment token. Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Append a "-" (U+002D) character and the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the comment token's data. Switch to the [comment state](#337.html_comment-state).

##### 8.2.4.50 <dfn>Comment end state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

">" (U+003E)

Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the comment token.

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append two "-" (U+002D) characters and a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the comment token's data. Switch to the [comment state](#337.html_comment-state).

"!" (U+0021)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [comment end bang state](#337.html_comment-end-bang-state).

"-" (U+002D)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append a "-" (U+002D) character to the comment token's data.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the comment token. Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append two "-" (U+002D) characters and the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the comment token's data. Switch to the [comment state](#337.html_comment-state).

##### 8.2.4.51 <dfn>Comment end bang state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"-" (U+002D)

Append two "-" (U+002D) characters and a "!" (U+0021) character to the comment token's data. Switch to the [comment end dash state](#337.html_comment-end-dash-state).

">" (U+003E)

Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the comment token.

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append two "-" (U+002D) characters, a "!" (U+0021) character, and a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the comment token's data. Switch to the [comment state](#337.html_comment-state).

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the comment token. Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Append two "-" (U+002D) characters, a "!" (U+0021) character, and the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the comment token's data. Switch to the [comment state](#337.html_comment-state).

##### 8.2.4.52 <dfn>DOCTYPE state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE

Switch to the [before DOCTYPE name state](#337.html_before-doctype-name-state).

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Create a new DOCTYPE token. Set its *force-quirks flag* to *on*. Emit the token. Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [before DOCTYPE name state](#337.html_before-doctype-name-state). Reconsume the character.

##### 8.2.4.53 <dfn>Before DOCTYPE name state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE

Ignore the character.

[Uppercase ASCII letter](#337.html_uppercase-ascii-letters)

Create a new DOCTYPE token. Set the token's name to the lowercase version of the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) (add 0x0020 to the character's code point). Switch to the [DOCTYPE name state](#337.html_doctype-name-state).

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Create a new DOCTYPE token. Set the token's name to a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character. Switch to the [DOCTYPE name state](#337.html_doctype-name-state).

">" (U+003E)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Create a new DOCTYPE token. Set its *force-quirks flag* to *on*. Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the token.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Create a new DOCTYPE token. Set its *force-quirks flag* to *on*. Emit the token. Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Create a new DOCTYPE token. Set the token's name to the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character). Switch to the [DOCTYPE name state](#337.html_doctype-name-state).

##### 8.2.4.54 <dfn>DOCTYPE name state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE

Switch to the [after DOCTYPE name state](#337.html_after-doctype-name-state).

">" (U+003E)

Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the current DOCTYPE token.

[Uppercase ASCII letter](#337.html_uppercase-ascii-letters)

Append the lowercase version of the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) (add 0x0020 to the character's code point) to the current DOCTYPE token's name.

U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Append a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character to the current DOCTYPE token's name.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Set the DOCTYPE token's *force-quirks flag* to *on*. Emit that DOCTYPE token. Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

Append the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) to the current DOCTYPE token's name.

##### 8.2.4.55 <dfn>After DOCTYPE name state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE

Ignore the character.

">" (U+003E)

Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit the current DOCTYPE token.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Set the DOCTYPE token's *force-quirks flag* to *on*. Emit that DOCTYPE token. Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

If the six characters starting from the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) are an [ASCII case-insensitive](#337.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the word "PUBLIC", then consume those characters and switch to the [after DOCTYPE public keyword state](#337.html_after-doctype-public-keyword-state).

Otherwise, if the six characters starting from the [current input character](#337.html_current-input-character) are an [ASCII case-insensitive](#337.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the word "SYSTEM", then consume those characters and switch to the [after DOCTYPE system keyword state](#337.html_after-doctype-system-keyword-state).

Otherwise, this is a [parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Set the DOCTYPE token's *force-quirks flag* to *on*. Switch to the [bogus DOCTYPE state](#337.html_bogus-doctype-state).

##### 8.2.4.56 <dfn>After DOCTYPE public keyword state</dfn>

Consume the [next input character](#337.html_next-input-character):

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE

Switch to the [before DOCTYPE public identifier state](#337.html_before-doctype-public-identifier-state).

U+0022 QUOTATION MARK (")

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Set the DOCTYPE token's public identifier to the empty string (not missing), then switch to the [DOCTYPE public identifier (double-quoted) state](#337.html_doctype-public-identifier-(double-quoted)-state).

"'" (U+0027)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Set the DOCTYPE token's public identifier to the empty string (not missing), then switch to the [DOCTYPE public identifier (single-quoted) state](#337.html_doctype-public-identifier-(single-quoted)-state).

">" (U+003E)

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Set the DOCTYPE token's *force-quirks flag* to *on*. Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Emit that DOCTYPE token.

EOF

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state). Set the DOCTYPE token's *force-quirks flag* to *on*. Emit that DOCTYPE token. Reconsume the EOF character.

Anything else

[Parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Set the DOCTYPE token's *force-quirks flag* to *on*. Switch to the [bogus DOCTYPE state](#337.html_bogus-doctype-state).

##### 8.2.4.68 <dfn>CDATA section state</dfn>

Switch to the [data state](#337.html_data-state).

Consume every character up to the next occurrence of the three character sequence U+005D RIGHT SQUARE BRACKET U+005D RIGHT SQUARE BRACKET U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN (`]]>`), or the end of the file (EOF), whichever comes first. Emit a series of character tokens consisting of all the characters consumed except the matching three character sequence at the end (if one was found before the end of the file).

If the end of the file was reached, reconsume the EOF character.

##### 8.2.4.69 Tokenizing character references

This section defines how to <dfn id="337.html_consume-a-character-reference">consume a character reference</dfn>, optionally with an <dfn id="337.html_additional-allowed-character">additional allowed character</dfn>, which, if specified where the algorithm is invoked, adds a character to the list of characters that cause there to not be a character reference.

This definition is used when parsing character references [in text](#337.html_character-reference-in-data-state) and [in attributes](#337.html_character-reference-in-attribute-value-state).

The behavior depends on the identity of the next character (the one immediately after the U+0026 AMPERSAND character), as follows:

"tab" (U+0009)
"LF" (U+000A)
"FF" (U+000C)
U+0020 SPACE
U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN
U+0026 AMPERSAND
EOF
The [additional allowed character](#337.html_additional-allowed-character), if there is one

Not a character reference. No characters are consumed, and nothing is returned. (This is not an error, either.)

"#" (U+0023)

Consume the U+0023 NUMBER SIGN.

The behavior further depends on the character after the U+0023 NUMBER SIGN:

U+0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X
U+0058 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER X

Consume the X.

Follow the steps below, but using [ASCII hex digits](#337.html_ascii-hex-digits).

When it comes to interpreting the number, interpret it as a hexadecimal number.

Anything else

Follow the steps below, but using [ASCII digits](#337.html_ascii-digits).

When it comes to interpreting the number, interpret it as a decimal number.

Consume as many characters as match the range of characters given above ([ASCII hex digits](#337.html_ascii-hex-digits) or [ASCII digits](#337.html_ascii-digits)).

If no characters match the range, then don't consume any characters (and unconsume the U+0023 NUMBER SIGN character and, if appropriate, the X character). This is a [parse error](#337.html_parse-error); nothing is returned.

Otherwise, if the next character is a U+003B SEMICOLON, consume that too. If it isn't, there is a [parse error](#337.html_parse-error).

If one or more characters match the range, then take them all and interpret the string of characters as a number (either hexadecimal or decimal as appropriate).

If that number is one of the numbers in the first column of the following table, then this is a [parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Find the row with that number in the first column, and return a character token for the Unicode character given in the second column of that row.

| Number | Unicode character |
| --- | --- |
| 0x00 | U+FFFD | REPLACEMENT CHARACTER |
| 0x80 | U+20AC | EURO SIGN (€) |
| 0x82 | U+201A | SINGLE LOW-9 QUOTATION MARK (?) |
| 0x83 | U+0192 | LATIN SMALL LETTER F WITH HOOK (?) |
| 0x84 | U+201E | DOUBLE LOW-9 QUOTATION MARK (?) |
| 0x85 | U+2026 | HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS (…) |
| 0x86 | U+2020 | DAGGER (?) |
| 0x87 | U+2021 | DOUBLE DAGGER (?) |
| 0x88 | U+02C6 | MODIFIER LETTER CIRCUMFLEX ACCENT (?) |
| 0x89 | U+2030 | PER MILLE SIGN (‰) |
| 0x8A | U+0160 | LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S WITH CARON (?) |
| 0x8B | U+2039 | SINGLE LEFT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARK (?) |
| 0x8C | U+0152 | LATIN CAPITAL LIGATURE OE (?) |
| 0x8E | U+017D | LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Z WITH CARON (?) |
| 0x91 | U+2018 | LEFT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK (‘) |
| 0x92 | U+2019 | RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK (’) |
| 0x93 | U+201C | LEFT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK (“) |
| 0x94 | U+201D | RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK (”) |
| 0x95 | U+2022 | BULLET (?) |
| 0x96 | U+2013 | EN DASH (–) |
| 0x97 | U+2014 | EM DASH (—) |
| 0x98 | U+02DC | SMALL TILDE (?) |
| 0x99 | U+2122 | TRADE MARK SIGN (?) |
| 0x9A | U+0161 | LATIN SMALL LETTER S WITH CARON (?) |
| 0x9B | U+203A | SINGLE RIGHT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARK (?) |
| 0x9C | U+0153 | LATIN SMALL LIGATURE OE (?) |
| 0x9E | U+017E | LATIN SMALL LETTER Z WITH CARON (?) |
| 0x9F | U+0178 | LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Y WITH DIAERESIS (?) |

Otherwise, if the number is in the range 0xD800 to 0xDFFF or is greater than 0x10FFFF, then this is a [parse error](#337.html_parse-error). Return a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character token.

Otherwise, return a character token for the Unicode character whose code point is that number. Additionally, if the number is in the range 0x0001 to 0x0008, 0x000D to 0x001F, 0x007F to 0x009F, 0xFDD0 to 0xFDEF, or is one of 0x000B, 0xFFFE, 0xFFFF, 0x1FFFE, 0x1FFFF, 0x2FFFE, 0x2FFFF, 0x3FFFE, 0x3FFFF, 0x4FFFE, 0x4FFFF, 0x5FFFE, 0x5FFFF, 0x6FFFE, 0x6FFFF, 0x7FFFE, 0x7FFFF, 0x8FFFE, 0x8FFFF, 0x9FFFE, 0x9FFFF, 0xAFFFE, 0xAFFFF, 0xBFFFE, 0xBFFFF, 0xCFFFE, 0xCFFFF, 0xDFFFE, 0xDFFFF, 0xEFFFE, 0xEFFFF, 0xFFFFE, 0xFFFFF, 0x10FFFE, or 0x10FFFF, then this is a [parse error](#337.html_parse-error).

Anything else

Consume the maximum number of characters possible, with the consumed characters matching one of the identifiers in the first column of the [named character references](#337.html_named-character-references) table (in a [case-sensitive](#337.html_case-sensitive) manner).

If no match can be made, then no characters are consumed, and nothing is returned. In this case, if the characters after the U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&) consist of a sequence of one or more [alphanumeric ASCII characters](#337.html_alphanumeric-ascii-characters) followed by a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;), then this is a [parse error](#337.html_parse-error).

If the character reference is being consumed [as part of an attribute](#337.html_character-reference-in-attribute-value-state), and the last character matched is not a ";" (U+003B) character, and the next character is either a "=" (U+003D) character or an [alphanumeric ASCII character](#337.html_alphanumeric-ascii-characters), then, for historical reasons, all the characters that were matched after the U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&) must be unconsumed, and nothing is returned. However, if this next character is in fact a "=" (U+003D) character, then this is a [parse error](#337.html_parse-error), because some legacy user agents will misinterpret the markup in those cases.

Otherwise, a character reference is parsed. If the last character matched is not a ";" (U+003B) character, there is a [parse error](#337.html_parse-error).

Return one or two character tokens for the character(s) corresponding to the character reference name (as given by the second column of the [named character references](#337.html_named-character-references) table).

If the markup contains (not in an attribute) the string `I'm &notit; I tell you`, the character reference is parsed as "not", as in, `I'm ?it; I tell you` (and this is a parse error). But if the markup was `I'm &notin; I tell you`, the character reference would be parsed as "notin;", resulting in `I'm ? I tell you` (and no parse error).

#### 8.2.5 <dfn>Tree construction</dfn>

The input to the tree construction stage is a sequence of tokens from the [tokenization](#338.html_tokenization) stage. The tree construction stage is associated with a DOM [`Document`](#338.html_document) object when a parser is created. The "output" of this stage consists of dynamically modifying or extending that document's DOM tree.

This specification does not define when an interactive user agent has to render the [`Document`](#338.html_document) so that it is available to the user, or when it has to begin accepting user input.

* * *

As each token is emitted from the tokenizer, the user agent must follow the appropriate steps from the following list, known as the <dfn id="338.html_tree-construction-dispatcher">tree construction dispatcher</dfn>:

If there is no [adjusted current node](#338.html_adjusted-current-node)
If the [adjusted current node](#338.html_adjusted-current-node) is an element in the [HTML namespace](#338.html_html-namespace-0)
If the [adjusted current node](#338.html_adjusted-current-node) is a [MathML text integration point](#338.html_mathml-text-integration-point) and the token is a start tag whose tag name is neither "mglyph" nor "malignmark"
If the [adjusted current node](#338.html_adjusted-current-node) is a [MathML text integration point](#338.html_mathml-text-integration-point) and the token is a character token
If the [adjusted current node](#338.html_adjusted-current-node) is an `annotation-xml` element in the [MathML namespace](#338.html_mathml-namespace) and the token is a start tag whose tag name is "svg"
If the [adjusted current node](#338.html_adjusted-current-node) is an [HTML integration point](#338.html_html-integration-point) and the token is a start tag
If the [adjusted current node](#338.html_adjusted-current-node) is an [HTML integration point](#338.html_html-integration-point) and the token is a character token
If the token is an end-of-file token

Process the token according to the rules given in the section corresponding to the current [insertion mode](#338.html_insertion-mode) in HTML content.

Otherwise

Process the token according to the rules given in the section for parsing tokens [in foreign content](#338.html_parsing-main-inforeign).

The <dfn id="338.html_next-token">next token</dfn> is the token that is about to be processed by the [tree construction dispatcher](#338.html_tree-construction-dispatcher) (even if the token is subsequently just ignored).

A node is a <dfn id="338.html_mathml-text-integration-point">MathML text integration point</dfn> if it is one of the following elements:

*   An `mi` element in the [MathML namespace](#338.html_mathml-namespace)
*   An `mo` element in the [MathML namespace](#338.html_mathml-namespace)
*   An `mn` element in the [MathML namespace](#338.html_mathml-namespace)
*   An `ms` element in the [MathML namespace](#338.html_mathml-namespace)
*   An `mtext` element in the [MathML namespace](#338.html_mathml-namespace)

A node is an <dfn id="338.html_html-integration-point">HTML integration point</dfn> if it is one of the following elements:

*   An `annotation-xml` element in the [MathML namespace](#338.html_mathml-namespace) whose start tag token had an attribute with the name "encoding" whose value was an [ASCII case-insensitive](#338.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`text/html`"
*   An `annotation-xml` element in the [MathML namespace](#338.html_mathml-namespace) whose start tag token had an attribute with the name "encoding" whose value was an [ASCII case-insensitive](#338.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`application/xhtml+xml`"
*   A `foreignObject` element in the [SVG namespace](#338.html_svg-namespace)
*   A `desc` element in the [SVG namespace](#338.html_svg-namespace)
*   A `title` element in the [SVG namespace](#338.html_svg-namespace)

Not all of the tag names mentioned below are conformant tag names in this specification; many are included to handle legacy content. They still form part of the algorithm that implementations are required to implement to claim conformance.

The algorithm described below places no limit on the depth of the DOM tree generated, or on the length of tag names, attribute names, attribute values, [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) nodes, etc. While implementors are encouraged to avoid arbitrary limits, it is recognized that [practical concerns](#338.html_hardwareLimitations) will likely force user agents to impose nesting depth constraints.

##### 8.2.5.1 Creating and inserting nodes

While the parser is processing a token, it can enable or disable <dfn id="338.html_foster-parent" data-anolis-xref="foster
  parent">foster parenting</dfn>. This affects the following algorithm.

The <dfn id="338.html_appropriate-place-for-inserting-a-node">appropriate place for inserting a node</dfn>, optionally using a particular *override target*, is the position in an element returned by running the following steps:

1.  If there was an *override target* specified, then let `target` be the *override target*.

    Otherwise, let `target` be the [current node](#338.html_current-node).

2.  Determine the `adjusted insertion location` using the first matching steps from the following list:

    If [foster parenting](#338.html_foster-parent) is enabled and `target` is a [`table`](#338.html_the-table-element), [`tbody`](#338.html_the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#338.html_the-tfoot-element), [`thead`](#338.html_the-thead-element), or [`tr`](#338.html_the-tr-element) element

    Foster parenting happens when content is misnested in tables.

    Run these substeps:

    1.  Let `last template` be the last [`template`](#338.html_the-template-element) element in the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements), if any.

    2.  Let `last table` be the last [`table`](#338.html_the-table-element) element in the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements), if any.

    3.  If there is a `last template` and either there is no `last table`, or there is one, but `last template` is lower (more recently added) than `last table` in the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements), then: let `adjusted insertion location` be inside `last template`'s [template contents](#338.html_template-contents), after its last child (if any), and abort these substeps.

    4.  If there is no `last table`, then let `adjusted insertion location` be inside the first element in the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements) (the [`html`](#338.html_the-html-element) element), after its last child (if any), and abort these substeps. ([fragment case](#338.html_fragment-case))

    5.  If `last table` has a parent element, then let `adjusted insertion location` be inside `last table`'s parent element, immediately before `last table`, and abort these substeps.

    6.  Let `previous element` be the element immediately above `last table` in the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements).

    7.  Let `adjusted insertion location` be inside `previous element`, after its last child (if any).

    These steps are involved in part because it's possible for elements, the [`table`](#338.html_the-table-element) element in this case in particular, to have been moved by a script around in the DOM, or indeed removed from the DOM entirely, after the element was inserted by the parser.

    Otherwise

    Let `adjusted insertion location` be inside `target`, after its last child (if any).

3.  If the `adjusted insertion location` is inside a [`template`](#338.html_the-template-element) element, let it instead be inside the [`template`](#338.html_the-template-element) element's [template contents](#338.html_template-contents), after its last child (if any).

4.  Return the `adjusted insertion location`.

* * *

When the steps below require the UA to <dfn id="338.html_create-an-element-for-the-token" data-anolis-xref="create an element for the token">create an element for a token</dfn> in a particular `given namespace` and with a particular `intended parent`, the UA must run the following steps:

1.  Create a node implementing the interface appropriate for the element type corresponding to the tag name of the token in `given namespace` (as given in the specification that defines that element, e.g. for an [`a`](#338.html_the-a-element) element in the [HTML namespace](#338.html_html-namespace-0), this specification defines it to be the [`HTMLAnchorElement`](#338.html_htmlanchorelement) interface), with the tag name being the name of that element, with the node being in the given namespace, and with the attributes on the node being those given in the given token.

    The interface appropriate for an element in the [HTML namespace](#338.html_html-namespace-0) that is not defined in this specification (or [other applicable specifications](#338.html_other-applicable-specifications)) is [`HTMLUnknownElement`](#338.html_htmlunknownelement). Elements in other namespaces whose interface is not defined by that namespace's specification must use the interface [`Element`](#338.html_element).

    The [`ownerDocument`](#338.html_dom-node-ownerdocument) of the newly created element must be the same as that of the `intended parent`.

2.  If the newly created element has an `xmlns` attribute *in the [XMLNS namespace](#338.html_xmlns-namespace)* whose value is not exactly the same as the element's namespace, that is a [parse error](#338.html_parse-error). Similarly, if the newly created element has an `xmlns:xlink` attribute in the [XMLNS namespace](#338.html_xmlns-namespace) whose value is not the [XLink Namespace](#338.html_xlink-namespace), that is a [parse error](#338.html_parse-error).

3.  If the newly created element is a [resettable element](#338.html_category-reset), invoke its [reset algorithm](#338.html_concept-form-reset-control). (This initializes the element's [value](#338.html_concept-fe-value) and [checkedness](#338.html_concept-fe-checked) based on the element's attributes.)

4.  If the element is a [form-associated element](#338.html_form-associated-element), and the [`form` element pointer](#338.html_form-element-pointer) is not null, and there is no [`template`](#338.html_the-template-element) element on the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements), and the newly created element is either not [reassociateable](#338.html_category-form-attr) or doesn't have a [`form`](#338.html_attr-fae-form) attribute, and the `intended parent` is in the same [home subtree](#338.html_home-subtree) as the element pointed to by the [`form` element pointer](#338.html_form-element-pointer), [associate](#338.html_concept-form-association) the newly created element with the [`form`](#338.html_the-form-element) element pointed to by the [`form` element pointer](#338.html_form-element-pointer), and suppress the running of the [reset the form owner](#338.html_reset-the-form-owner) algorithm when the parser subsequently attempts to insert the element.

5.  Return the newly created element.

* * *

When the steps below require the user agent to <dfn id="338.html_insert-a-foreign-element">insert a foreign element</dfn> for a token in a given namespace, the user agent must run these steps:

1.  Let the `adjusted insertion location` be the [appropriate place for inserting a node](#338.html_appropriate-place-for-inserting-a-node).

2.  [Create an element for the token](#338.html_create-an-element-for-the-token) in the given namespace, with the intended parent being the element in which the `adjusted insertion location` finds itself.

3.  If it is possible to insert an element at the `adjusted insertion location`, then insert the newly created element at the `adjusted insertion location`.

    If the `adjusted insertion location` cannot accept more elements, e.g. because it's a [`Document`](#338.html_document) that already has an element child, then the newly created element is dropped on the floor.

4.  Push the element onto the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements) so that it is the new [current node](#338.html_current-node).

5.  Return the newly created element.

When the steps below require the user agent to <dfn id="338.html_insert-an-html-element">insert an HTML element</dfn> for a token, the user agent must [insert a foreign element](#338.html_insert-a-foreign-element) for the token, in the [HTML namespace](#338.html_html-namespace-0).

* * *

When the steps below require the user agent to <dfn id="338.html_insert-a-character">insert a character</dfn> while processing a token, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `data` be the characters passed to the algorithm, or, if no characters were explicitly specified, the character of the character token being processed.

2.  Let the `adjusted insertion location` be the [appropriate place for inserting a node](#338.html_appropriate-place-for-inserting-a-node).

3.  If the `adjusted insertion location` is in a [`Document`](#338.html_document) node, then abort these steps.

    The DOM will not let [`Document`](#338.html_document) nodes have [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) node children, so they are dropped on the floor.

4.  If there is a [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) node immediately before the `adjusted insertion location`, then append `data` to that [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) node's data.

    Otherwise, create a new [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) node whose data is `data` and whose [`ownerDocument`](#338.html_dom-node-ownerdocument) is the same as that of the element in which the `adjusted insertion location` finds itself, and insert the newly created node at the `adjusted insertion location`.

Here are some sample inputs to the parser and the corresponding number of [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) nodes that they result in, assuming a user agent that executes scripts.

| Input | Number of [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) nodes |
| --- | --- |
|  
```
A<script>
var script = document.getElementsByTagName('script')[0];
document.body.removeChild(script);
</script>B
```

 | One [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) node in the document, containing "AB". |
|  
```
A<script>
var text = document.createTextNode('B');
document.body.appendChild(text);
</script>C
```

 | Three [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) nodes; "A" before the script, the script's contents, and "BC" after the script (the parser appends to the [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) node created by the script). |
|  
```
A<script>
var text = document.getElementsByTagName('script')[0].firstChild;
text.data = 'B';
document.body.appendChild(text);
</script>C
```

 | Two adjacent [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) nodes in the document, containing "A" and "BC". |
|  
```
A<table>B<tr>C</tr>D</table>
```

 | One [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) node before the table, containing "ABCD". (This is caused by [foster parenting](#338.html_foster-parent).) |
|  
```
A<table><tr> B</tr> C</table>
```

 | One [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) node before the table, containing "A B C" (A-space-B-space-C). (This is caused by [foster parenting](#338.html_foster-parent).) |
|  
```
A<table><tr> B</tr> </em>C</table>
```

 | One [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) node before the table, containing "A BC" (A-space-B-C), and one [`Text`](#338.html_text-0) node inside the table (as a child of a [`tbody`](#338.html_the-tbody-element)) with a single space character. (Space characters separated from non-space characters by non-character tokens are not affected by [foster parenting](#338.html_foster-parent), even if those other tokens then get ignored.) |

* * *

When the steps below require the user agent to <dfn id="338.html_insert-a-comment">insert a comment</dfn> while processing a comment token, optionally with an explicitly insertion position `position`, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Let `data` be the data given in the comment token being processed.

2.  If `position` was specified, then let the `adjusted insertion location` be `position`. Otherwise, let `adjusted insertion location` be the [appropriate place for inserting a node](#338.html_appropriate-place-for-inserting-a-node).

3.  Create a [`Comment`](#338.html_comment-0) node whose `data` attribute is set to `data` and whose [`ownerDocument`](#338.html_dom-node-ownerdocument) is the same as that of the node in which the `adjusted insertion location` finds itself.

4.  Insert the newly created node at the `adjusted insertion location`.

* * *

DOM mutation events must not fire for changes caused by the UA parsing the document. This includes the parsing of any content inserted using [`document.write()`](#338.html_dom-document-write) and [`document.writeln()`](#338.html_dom-document-writeln) calls. [[DOMEVENTS]](#338.html_refsDOMEVENTS)

However, mutation observers *do* fire, as required by the DOM specification.

##### 8.2.5.2 Parsing elements that contain only text

The <dfn id="338.html_generic-raw-text-element-parsing-algorithm">generic raw text element parsing algorithm</dfn> and the <dfn id="338.html_generic-rcdata-element-parsing-algorithm">generic RCDATA element parsing algorithm</dfn> consist of the following steps. These algorithms are always invoked in response to a start tag token.

1.  [Insert an HTML element](#338.html_insert-an-html-element) for the token.

2.  If the algorithm that was invoked is the [generic raw text element parsing algorithm](#338.html_generic-raw-text-element-parsing-algorithm), switch the tokenizer to the [RAWTEXT state](#338.html_rawtext-state); otherwise the algorithm invoked was the [generic RCDATA element parsing algorithm](#338.html_generic-rcdata-element-parsing-algorithm), switch the tokenizer to the [RCDATA state](#338.html_rcdata-state).

3.  Let the [original insertion mode](#338.html_original-insertion-mode) be the current [insertion mode](#338.html_insertion-mode).

4.  Then, switch the [insertion mode](#338.html_insertion-mode) to "[text](#338.html_parsing-main-incdata)".

##### 8.2.5.3 Closing elements that have implied end tags

When the steps below require the UA to <dfn id="338.html_generate-implied-end-tags">generate implied end tags</dfn>, then, while the [current node](#338.html_current-node) is a [`dd`](#338.html_the-dd-element) element, a [`dt`](#338.html_the-dt-element) element, an [`li`](#338.html_the-li-element) element, an [`option`](#338.html_the-option-element) element, an [`optgroup`](#338.html_the-optgroup-element) element, a [`p`](#338.html_the-p-element) element, an [`rb`](#338.html_the-rb-element) element, an [`rp`](#338.html_the-rp-element) element, an [`rt`](#338.html_the-rt-element) element, or an [`rtc`](#338.html_the-rtc-element) element, the UA must pop the [current node](#338.html_current-node) off the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements).

If a step requires the UA to generate implied end tags but lists an element to exclude from the process, then the UA must perform the above steps as if that element was not in the above list.

##### 8.2.5.4 The rules for parsing tokens in HTML content

###### 8.2.5.4.1 The "<dfn id="338.html_insertion-mode:-initial" data-anolis-xref="insertion mode: initial">initial</dfn>" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[initial](#338.html_the-initial-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#338.html_insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, "LF" (U+000A), "FF" (U+000C), "CR" (U+000D), or U+0020 SPACE

Ignore the token.

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#338.html_insert-a-comment) as the last child of the [`Document`](#338.html_document) object.

A DOCTYPE token

If the DOCTYPE token's name is not a [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) match for the string "`html`", or the token's public identifier is not missing, or the token's system identifier is neither missing nor a [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) match for the string "[`about:legacy-compat`](#338.html_about:legacy-compat)", and none of the sets of conditions in the following list are matched, then there is a [parse error](#338.html_parse-error).

*   The DOCTYPE token's name is a [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) match for the string "`html`", the token's public identifier is the [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) string "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.0//EN`", and the token's system identifier is either missing or the [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) string "`http://www.w3.org/TR/REC-html40/strict.dtd`".
*   The DOCTYPE token's name is a [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) match for the string "`html`", the token's public identifier is the [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) string "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN`", and the token's system identifier is either missing or the [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) string "`http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/strict.dtd`".
*   The DOCTYPE token's name is a [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) match for the string "`html`", the token's public identifier is the [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) string "`-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Strict//EN`", and the token's system identifier is the [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) string "`http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-strict.dtd`".
*   The DOCTYPE token's name is a [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) match for the string "`html`", the token's public identifier is the [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) string "`-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.1//EN`", and the token's system identifier is the [case-sensitive](#338.html_case-sensitive) string "`http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml11/DTD/xhtml11.dtd`".

Conformance checkers may, based on the values (including presence or lack thereof) of the DOCTYPE token's name, public identifier, or system identifier, switch to a conformance checking mode for another language (e.g. based on the DOCTYPE token a conformance checker could recognize that the document is an HTML4-era document, and defer to an HTML4 conformance checker.)

Append a [`DocumentType`](#338.html_documenttype) node to the [`Document`](#338.html_document) node, with the `name` attribute set to the name given in the DOCTYPE token, or the empty string if the name was missing; the `publicId` attribute set to the public identifier given in the DOCTYPE token, or the empty string if the public identifier was missing; the `systemId` attribute set to the system identifier given in the DOCTYPE token, or the empty string if the system identifier was missing; and the other attributes specific to [`DocumentType`](#338.html_documenttype) objects set to null and empty lists as appropriate. Associate the [`DocumentType`](#338.html_documenttype) node with the [`Document`](#338.html_document) object so that it is returned as the value of the `doctype` attribute of the [`Document`](#338.html_document) object.

Then, if the document is *not* [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#338.html_an-iframe-srcdoc-document), and the DOCTYPE token matches one of the conditions in the following list, then set the [`Document`](#338.html_document) to [quirks mode](#338.html_quirks-mode):

*   The *force-quirks flag* is set to *on*.
*   The name is set to anything other than "`html`" (compared [case-sensitively](#338.html_case-sensitive)).
*   The public identifier starts with: "`+//Silmaril//dtd html Pro v0r11 19970101//`"
*   The public identifier starts with: "`-//AdvaSoft Ltd//DTD HTML 3.0 asWedit + extensions//`"
*   The public identifier starts with: "`-//AS//DTD HTML 3.0 asWedit + extensions//`"
