##### 8.2.5.5 The rules for parsing tokens <dfn id="338.html_insertion-mode:-in-foreign-content" data-anolis-xref="insertion mode: in foreign content">in foreign content</dfn>

When the user agent is to apply the rules for parsing tokens in foreign content, the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A character token that is U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#338.html_parse-error). [Insert a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character](#338.html_insert-a-character).

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, "LF" (U+000A), "FF" (U+000C), "CR" (U+000D), or U+0020 SPACE

[Insert the token's character](#338.html_insert-a-character).

Any other character token

[Insert the token's character](#338.html_insert-a-character).

Set the [frameset-ok flag](#338.html_frameset-ok-flag) to "not ok".

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#338.html_insert-a-comment).

A DOCTYPE token

[Parse error](#338.html_parse-error). Ignore the token.

A start tag whose tag name is one of: "b", "big", "blockquote", "body", "br", "center", "code", "dd", "div", "dl", "dt", "em", "embed", "h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "h5", "h6", "head", "hr", "i", "img", "li", "listing", "main", "meta", "nobr", "ol", "p", "pre", "ruby", "s", "small", "span", "strong", "strike", "sub", "sup", "table", "tt", "u", "ul", "var"
A start tag whose tag name is "font", if the token has any attributes named "color", "face", or "size"

[Parse error](#338.html_parse-error).

If the parser was originally created for the [HTML fragment parsing algorithm](#338.html_html-fragment-parsing-algorithm), then act as described in the "any other start tag" entry below. ([fragment case](#338.html_fragment-case))

Otherwise:

Pop an element from the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements), and then keep popping more elements from the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements) until the [current node](#338.html_current-node) is a [MathML text integration point](#338.html_mathml-text-integration-point), an [HTML integration point](#338.html_html-integration-point), or an element in the [HTML namespace](#338.html_html-namespace-0).

Then, reprocess the token.

Any other start tag

If the [adjusted current node](#338.html_adjusted-current-node) is an element in the [MathML namespace](#338.html_mathml-namespace), [adjust MathML attributes](#338.html_adjust-mathml-attributes) for the token. (This fixes the case of MathML attributes that are not all lowercase.)

If the [adjusted current node](#338.html_adjusted-current-node) is an element in the [SVG namespace](#338.html_svg-namespace), and the token's tag name is one of the ones in the first column of the following table, change the tag name to the name given in the corresponding cell in the second column. (This fixes the case of SVG elements that are not all lowercase.)

| Tag name | Element name |
| --- | --- |
| `altglyph` | `altGlyph` |
| `altglyphdef` | `altGlyphDef` |
| `altglyphitem` | `altGlyphItem` |
| `animatecolor` | `animateColor` |
| `animatemotion` | `animateMotion` |
| `animatetransform` | `animateTransform` |
| `clippath` | `clipPath` |
| `feblend` | `feBlend` |
| `fecolormatrix` | `feColorMatrix` |
| `fecomponenttransfer` | `feComponentTransfer` |
| `fecomposite` | `feComposite` |
| `feconvolvematrix` | `feConvolveMatrix` |
| `fediffuselighting` | `feDiffuseLighting` |
| `fedisplacementmap` | `feDisplacementMap` |
| `fedistantlight` | `feDistantLight` |
| `fedropshadow` | `feDropShadow` |
| `feflood` | `feFlood` |
| `fefunca` | `feFuncA` |
| `fefuncb` | `feFuncB` |
| `fefuncg` | `feFuncG` |
| `fefuncr` | `feFuncR` |
| `fegaussianblur` | `feGaussianBlur` |
| `feimage` | `feImage` |
| `femerge` | `feMerge` |
| `femergenode` | `feMergeNode` |
| `femorphology` | `feMorphology` |
| `feoffset` | `feOffset` |
| `fepointlight` | `fePointLight` |
| `fespecularlighting` | `feSpecularLighting` |
| `fespotlight` | `feSpotLight` |
| `fetile` | `feTile` |
| `feturbulence` | `feTurbulence` |
| `foreignobject` | `foreignObject` |
| `glyphref` | `glyphRef` |
| `lineargradient` | `linearGradient` |
| `radialgradient` | `radialGradient` |
| `textpath` | `textPath` |

If the [adjusted current node](#338.html_adjusted-current-node) is an element in the [SVG namespace](#338.html_svg-namespace), [adjust SVG attributes](#338.html_adjust-svg-attributes) for the token. (This fixes the case of SVG attributes that are not all lowercase.)

[Adjust foreign attributes](#338.html_adjust-foreign-attributes) for the token. (This fixes the use of namespaced attributes, in particular XLink in SVG.)

[Insert a foreign element](#338.html_insert-a-foreign-element) for the token, in the same namespace as the [adjusted current node](#338.html_adjusted-current-node).

If the token has its *self-closing flag* set, then run the appropriate steps from the following list:

If the token's tag name is "script"

[Acknowledge the token's *self-closing flag*](#338.html_acknowledge-self-closing-flag), and then act as described in the steps for a "script" end tag below.

Otherwise

Pop the [current node](#338.html_current-node) off the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements) and [acknowledge the token's *self-closing flag*](#338.html_acknowledge-self-closing-flag).

An end tag whose tag name is "script", if the [current node](#338.html_current-node) is a `script` element in the [SVG namespace](#338.html_svg-namespace)

Pop the [current node](#338.html_current-node) off the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements).

Let the `old insertion point` have the same value as the current [insertion point](#338.html_insertion-point). Let the [insertion point](#338.html_insertion-point) be just before the [next input character](#338.html_next-input-character).

Increment the parser's [script nesting level](#338.html_script-nesting-level) by one. Set the [parser pause flag](#338.html_parser-pause-flag) to true.

[Process the `script` element](http://www.w3.org/TR/SVGMobile12/script.html#ScriptContentProcessing) according to the SVG rules, if the user agent supports SVG. [[SVG]](#338.html_refsSVG)

Even if this causes [new characters to be inserted into the tokenizer](#338.html_dom-document-write), the parser will not be executed reentrantly, since the [parser pause flag](#338.html_parser-pause-flag) is true.

Decrement the parser's [script nesting level](#338.html_script-nesting-level) by one. If the parser's [script nesting level](#338.html_script-nesting-level) is zero, then set the [parser pause flag](#338.html_parser-pause-flag) to false.

Let the [insertion point](#338.html_insertion-point) have the value of the `old insertion point`. (In other words, restore the [insertion point](#338.html_insertion-point) to its previous value. This value might be the "undefined" value.)

Any other end tag

Run these steps:

1.  Initialize `node` to be the [current node](#338.html_current-node) (the bottommost node of the stack).

2.  If `node`'s tag name, [converted to ASCII lowercase](#338.html_converted-to-ascii-lowercase), is not the same as the tag name of the token, then this is a [parse error](#338.html_parse-error).

3.  *Loop*: If `node` is the topmost element in the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements), abort these steps. ([fragment case](#338.html_fragment-case))

4.  If `node`'s tag name, [converted to ASCII lowercase](#338.html_converted-to-ascii-lowercase), is the same as the tag name of the token, pop elements from the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements) until `node` has been popped from the stack, and then abort these steps.

5.  Set `node` to the previous entry in the [stack of open elements](#338.html_stack-of-open-elements).

6.  If `node` is not an element in the [HTML namespace](#338.html_html-namespace-0), return to the step labeled *loop*.

7.  Otherwise, process the token according to the rules given in the section corresponding to the current [insertion mode](#338.html_insertion-mode) in HTML content.

#### 8.2.6 The end

Once the user agent <dfn id="339.html_stop-parsing" data-anolis-xref="stop parsing">stops parsing</dfn> the document, the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Set the [current document readiness](#339.html_current-document-readiness) to "`interactive`" and the [insertion point](#339.html_insertion-point) to undefined.

2.  Pop *all* the nodes off the [stack of open elements](#339.html_stack-of-open-elements).

3.  If the [list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing](#339.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-when-the-document-has-finished-parsing) is not empty, run these substeps:

    1.  [Spin the event loop](#339.html_spin-the-event-loop) until the first [`script`](#339.html_the-script-element) in the [list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing](#339.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-when-the-document-has-finished-parsing) has its ["ready to be parser-executed"](#339.html_ready-to-be-parser-executed) flag set *and* the parser's [`Document`](#339.html_document) [has no style sheet that is blocking scripts](#339.html_has-no-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts).

    2.  [Execute](#339.html_execute-the-script-block) the first [`script`](#339.html_the-script-element) in the [list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing](#339.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-when-the-document-has-finished-parsing).

    3.  Remove the first [`script`](#339.html_the-script-element) element from the [list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing](#339.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-when-the-document-has-finished-parsing) (i.e. shift out the first entry in the list).

    4.  If the [list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing](#339.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-when-the-document-has-finished-parsing) is still not empty, repeat these substeps again from substep 1.

4.  [Queue a task](#339.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#339.html_fire-a-simple-event) that bubbles named `DOMContentLoaded` at the [`Document`](#339.html_document).

5.  [Spin the event loop](#339.html_spin-the-event-loop) until the [set of scripts that will execute as soon as possible](#339.html_set-of-scripts-that-will-execute-as-soon-as-possible) and the [list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible](#339.html_list-of-scripts-that-will-execute-in-order-as-soon-as-possible) are empty.

6.  [Spin the event loop](#339.html_spin-the-event-loop) until there is nothing that <dfn id="339.html_delay-the-load-event" data-anolis-xref="delay the load
       event">delays the load event</dfn> in the [`Document`](#339.html_document).

7.  [Queue a task](#339.html_queue-a-task) to run the following substeps:

    1.  Set the [current document readiness](#339.html_current-document-readiness) to "`complete`".

    2.  If the [`Document`](#339.html_document) is in a [browsing context](#339.html_browsing-context), create a [trusted](#339.html_concept-events-trusted) event named `load` that does not bubble and is not cancelable and which uses the [`Event`](#339.html_event) interface, and [dispatch](#339.html_concept-event-dispatch) it at the [`Document`](#339.html_document)'s [`Window`](#339.html_window) object, with *target override* set to the [`Document`](#339.html_document) object.

8.  If the [`Document`](#339.html_document) is in a [browsing context](#339.html_browsing-context), then [queue a task](#339.html_queue-a-task) to run the following substeps:

    1.  If the [`Document`](#339.html_document)'s [page showing](#339.html_page-showing) flag is true, then abort this task (i.e. don't fire the event below).

    2.  Set the [`Document`](#339.html_document)'s [page showing](#339.html_page-showing) flag to true.

    3.  [Fire](#339.html_concept-event-fire) a [trusted](#339.html_concept-events-trusted) event with the name [`pageshow`](#339.html_event-pageshow) at the [`Window`](#339.html_window) object of the [`Document`](#339.html_document), but with its [`target`](#339.html_dom-event-target) set to the [`Document`](#339.html_document) object (and the `currentTarget` set to the [`Window`](#339.html_window) object), using the [`PageTransitionEvent`](#339.html_pagetransitionevent) interface, with the [`persisted`](#339.html_dom-pagetransitionevent-persisted) attribute initialized to false. This event must not bubble, must not be cancelable, and has no default action.

9.  If the [`Document`](#339.html_document) has any [pending application cache download process tasks](#339.html_pending-application-cache-download-process-tasks), then [queue](#339.html_queue-a-task) each such [task](#339.html_concept-task) in the order they were added to the list of [pending application cache download process tasks](#339.html_pending-application-cache-download-process-tasks), and then empty the list of [pending application cache download process tasks](#339.html_pending-application-cache-download-process-tasks). The [task source](#339.html_task-source) for these [tasks](#339.html_concept-task) is the [networking task source](#339.html_networking-task-source).

10.  If the [`Document`](#339.html_document)'s [print when loaded](#339.html_print-when-loaded) flag is set, then run the [printing steps](#339.html_printing-steps).

11.  The [`Document`](#339.html_document) is now <dfn id="339.html_ready-for-post-load-tasks">ready for post-load tasks</dfn>.

12.  [Queue a task](#339.html_queue-a-task) to mark the [`Document`](#339.html_document) as <dfn id="339.html_completely-loaded">completely loaded</dfn>.

When the user agent is to <dfn id="339.html_abort-a-parser">abort a parser</dfn>, it must run the following steps:

1.  Throw away any pending content in the [input stream](#339.html_input-stream), and discard any future content that would have been added to it.

2.  Set the [current document readiness](#339.html_current-document-readiness) to "`interactive`".

3.  Pop *all* the nodes off the [stack of open elements](#339.html_stack-of-open-elements).

4.  Set the [current document readiness](#339.html_current-document-readiness) to "`complete`".

Except where otherwise specified, the [task source](#339.html_task-source) for the [tasks](#339.html_concept-task) mentioned in this section is the [DOM manipulation task source](#339.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

#### 8.2.7 Coercing an HTML DOM into an infoset

When an application uses an [HTML parser](#340.html_html-parser) in conjunction with an XML pipeline, it is possible that the constructed DOM is not compatible with the XML tool chain in certain subtle ways. For example, an XML toolchain might not be able to represent attributes with the name `xmlns`, since they conflict with the Namespaces in XML syntax. There is also some data that the [HTML parser](#340.html_html-parser) generates that isn't included in the DOM itself. This section specifies some rules for handling these issues.

If the XML API being used doesn't support DOCTYPEs, the tool may drop DOCTYPEs altogether.

If the XML API doesn't support attributes in no namespace that are named "`xmlns`", attributes whose names start with "`xmlns:`", or attributes in the [XMLNS namespace](#340.html_xmlns-namespace), then the tool may drop such attributes.

The tool may annotate the output with any namespace declarations required for proper operation.

If the XML API being used restricts the allowable characters in the local names of elements and attributes, then the tool may map all element and attribute local names that the API wouldn't support to a set of names that *are* allowed, by replacing any character that isn't supported with the uppercase letter U and the six digits of the character's Unicode code point when expressed in hexadecimal, using digits 0-9 and capital letters A-F as the symbols, in increasing numeric order.

For example, the element name `foo<bar`, which can be output by the [HTML parser](#340.html_html-parser), though it is neither a legal HTML element name nor a well-formed XML element name, would be converted into `fooU00003Cbar`, which *is* a well-formed XML element name (though it's still not legal in HTML by any means).

As another example, consider the attribute `xlink:href`. Used on a MathML element, it becomes, after being [adjusted](#340.html_adjust-foreign-attributes), an attribute with a prefix "`xlink`" and a local name "`href`". However, used on an HTML element, it becomes an attribute with no prefix and the local name "`xlink:href`", which is not a valid NCName, and thus might not be accepted by an XML API. It could thus get converted, becoming "`xlinkU00003Ahref`".

The resulting names from this conversion conveniently can't clash with any attribute generated by the [HTML parser](#340.html_html-parser), since those are all either lowercase or those listed in the [adjust foreign attributes](#340.html_adjust-foreign-attributes) algorithm's table.

If the XML API restricts comments from having two consecutive U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS characters (--), the tool may insert a single U+0020 SPACE character between any such offending characters.

If the XML API restricts comments from ending in a "-" (U+002D) character, the tool may insert a single U+0020 SPACE character at the end of such comments.

If the XML API restricts allowed characters in character data, attribute values, or comments, the tool may replace any "FF" (U+000C) character with a U+0020 SPACE character, and any other literal non-XML character with a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.

If the tool has no way to convey out-of-band information, then the tool may drop the following information:

*   Whether the document is set to *[no-quirks mode](#340.html_no-quirks-mode)*, *[limited-quirks mode](#340.html_limited-quirks-mode)*, or *[quirks mode](#340.html_quirks-mode)*
*   The association between form controls and forms that aren't their nearest [`form`](#340.html_the-form-element) element ancestor (use of the [`form` element pointer](#340.html_form-element-pointer) in the parser)
*   The [template contents](#340.html_template-contents) of any [`template`](#340.html_the-template-element) elements.

The mutations allowed by this section apply *after* the [HTML parser](#340.html_html-parser)'s rules have been applied. For example, a `<a::>` start tag will be closed by a `</a::>` end tag, and never by a `</aU00003AU00003A>` end tag, even if the user agent is using the rules above to then generate an actual element in the DOM with the name `aU00003AU00003A` for that start tag.

#### 8.2.8 An introduction to error handling and strange cases in the parser

*This section is non-normative.*

This section examines some erroneous markup and discusses how the [HTML parser](#341.html_html-parser) handles these cases.

##### 8.2.8.1 Misnested tags: <b><i></b></i>

*This section is non-normative.*

The most-often discussed example of erroneous markup is as follows:

```
<p>1<b>2<i>3</b>4</i>5</p>
```

The parsing of this markup is straightforward up to the "3". At this point, the DOM looks like this:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 1
            *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 2
                *   [`i`](#341.html_the-i-element)
                    *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 3

Here, the [stack of open elements](#341.html_stack-of-open-elements) has five elements on it: [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element), [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element), [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element), [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element), and [`i`](#341.html_the-i-element). The [list of active formatting elements](#341.html_list-of-active-formatting-elements) just has two: [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) and [`i`](#341.html_the-i-element). The [insertion mode](#341.html_insertion-mode) is "[in body](#341.html_parsing-main-inbody)".

Upon receiving the end tag token with the tag name "b", the "[adoption agency algorithm](#341.html_adoptionAgency)" is invoked. This is a simple case, in that the `formatting element` is the [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element, and there is no `furthest block`. Thus, the [stack of open elements](#341.html_stack-of-open-elements) ends up with just three elements: [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element), [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element), and [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element), while the [list of active formatting elements](#341.html_list-of-active-formatting-elements) has just one: [`i`](#341.html_the-i-element). The DOM tree is unmodified at this point.

The next token is a character ("4"), triggers the [reconstruction of the active formatting elements](#341.html_reconstruct-the-active-formatting-elements), in this case just the [`i`](#341.html_the-i-element) element. A new [`i`](#341.html_the-i-element) element is thus created for the "4" [`Text`](#341.html_text-0) node. After the end tag token for the "i" is also received, and the "5" [`Text`](#341.html_text-0) node is inserted, the DOM looks as follows:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 1
            *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 2
                *   [`i`](#341.html_the-i-element)
                    *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 3
            *   [`i`](#341.html_the-i-element)
                *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 4
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 5

##### 8.2.8.2 Misnested tags: <b><p></b></p>

*This section is non-normative.*

A case similar to the previous one is the following:

```
<b>1<p>2</b>3</p>
```

Up to the "2" the parsing here is straightforward:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 1
            *   [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)
                *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 2

The interesting part is when the end tag token with the tag name "b" is parsed.

Before that token is seen, the [stack of open elements](#341.html_stack-of-open-elements) has four elements on it: [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element), [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element), [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element), and [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element). The [list of active formatting elements](#341.html_list-of-active-formatting-elements) just has the one: [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element). The [insertion mode](#341.html_insertion-mode) is "[in body](#341.html_parsing-main-inbody)".

Upon receiving the end tag token with the tag name "b", the "[adoption agency algorithm](#341.html_adoptionAgency)" is invoked, as in the previous example. However, in this case, there *is* a `furthest block`, namely the [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element) element. Thus, this time the adoption agency algorithm isn't skipped over.

The `common ancestor` is the [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element) element. A conceptual "bookmark" marks the position of the [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) in the [list of active formatting elements](#341.html_list-of-active-formatting-elements), but since that list has only one element in it, the bookmark won't have much effect.

As the algorithm progresses, `node` ends up set to the formatting element ([`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)), and `last node` ends up set to the `furthest block` ([`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)).

The `last node` gets appended (moved) to the `common ancestor`, so that the DOM looks like:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 1
        *   [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 2

A new [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element is created, and the children of the [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element) element are moved to it:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 1
        *   [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)

*   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
    *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 2

Finally, the new [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element is appended to the [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element) element, so that the DOM looks like:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 1
        *   [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)
            *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 2

The [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element is removed from the [list of active formatting elements](#341.html_list-of-active-formatting-elements) and the [stack of open elements](#341.html_stack-of-open-elements), so that when the "3" is parsed, it is appended to the [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element) element:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 1
        *   [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)
            *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 2
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): 3

##### 8.2.8.3 Unexpected markup in tables

*This section is non-normative.*

Error handling in tables is, for historical reasons, especially strange. For example, consider the following markup:

```
<table><b><tr><td>aaa</td></tr>bbb</table>ccc
```

The highlighted [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element start tag is not allowed directly inside a table like that, and the parser handles this case by placing the element *before* the table. (This is called *[foster parenting](#341.html_foster-parent)*.) This can be seen by examining the DOM tree as it stands just after the [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element) element's start tag has been seen:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element)

...and then immediately after the [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element start tag has been seen:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
        *   [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element)

At this point, the [stack of open elements](#341.html_stack-of-open-elements) has on it the elements [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element), [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element), [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element), and [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) (in that order, despite the resulting DOM tree); the [list of active formatting elements](#341.html_list-of-active-formatting-elements) just has the [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element in it; and the [insertion mode](#341.html_insertion-mode) is "[in table](#341.html_parsing-main-intable)".

The [`tr`](#341.html_the-tr-element) start tag causes the [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element to be popped off the stack and a [`tbody`](#341.html_the-tbody-element) start tag to be implied; the [`tbody`](#341.html_the-tbody-element) and [`tr`](#341.html_the-tr-element) elements are then handled in a rather straight-forward manner, taking the parser through the "[in table body](#341.html_parsing-main-intbody)" and "[in row](#341.html_parsing-main-intr)" insertion modes, after which the DOM looks as follows:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
        *   [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element)
            *   [`tbody`](#341.html_the-tbody-element)
                *   [`tr`](#341.html_the-tr-element)

Here, the [stack of open elements](#341.html_stack-of-open-elements) has on it the elements [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element), [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element), [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element), [`tbody`](#341.html_the-tbody-element), and [`tr`](#341.html_the-tr-element); the [list of active formatting elements](#341.html_list-of-active-formatting-elements) still has the [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element in it; and the [insertion mode](#341.html_insertion-mode) is "[in row](#341.html_parsing-main-intr)".

The [`td`](#341.html_the-td-element) element start tag token, after putting a [`td`](#341.html_the-td-element) element on the tree, puts a marker on the [list of active formatting elements](#341.html_list-of-active-formatting-elements) (it also switches to the "[in cell](#341.html_parsing-main-intd)" [insertion mode](#341.html_insertion-mode)).

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
        *   [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element)
            *   [`tbody`](#341.html_the-tbody-element)
                *   [`tr`](#341.html_the-tr-element)
                    *   [`td`](#341.html_the-td-element)

The marker means that when the "aaa" character tokens are seen, no [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element is created to hold the resulting [`Text`](#341.html_text-0) node:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
        *   [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element)
            *   [`tbody`](#341.html_the-tbody-element)
                *   [`tr`](#341.html_the-tr-element)
                    *   [`td`](#341.html_the-td-element)
                        *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): aaa

The end tags are handled in a straight-forward manner; after handling them, the [stack of open elements](#341.html_stack-of-open-elements) has on it the elements [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element), [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element), [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element), and [`tbody`](#341.html_the-tbody-element); the [list of active formatting elements](#341.html_list-of-active-formatting-elements) still has the [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element in it (the marker having been removed by the "td" end tag token); and the [insertion mode](#341.html_insertion-mode) is "[in table body](#341.html_parsing-main-intbody)".

Thus it is that the "bbb" character tokens are found. These trigger the "[in table text](#341.html_parsing-main-intabletext)" insertion mode to be used (with the [original insertion mode](#341.html_original-insertion-mode) set to "[in table body](#341.html_parsing-main-intbody)"). The character tokens are collected, and when the next token (the [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element) element end tag) is seen, they are processed as a group. Since they are not all spaces, they are handled as per the "anything else" rules in the "[in table](#341.html_parsing-main-intable)" insertion mode, which defer to the "[in body](#341.html_parsing-main-inbody)" insertion mode but with [foster parenting](#341.html_foster-parent).

When [the active formatting elements are reconstructed](#341.html_reconstruct-the-active-formatting-elements), a [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element is created and [foster parented](#341.html_foster-parent), and then the "bbb" [`Text`](#341.html_text-0) node is appended to it:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): bbb
        *   [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element)
            *   [`tbody`](#341.html_the-tbody-element)
                *   [`tr`](#341.html_the-tr-element)
                    *   [`td`](#341.html_the-td-element)
                        *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): aaa

The [stack of open elements](#341.html_stack-of-open-elements) has on it the elements [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element), [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element), [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element), [`tbody`](#341.html_the-tbody-element), and the new [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) (again, note that this doesn't match the resulting tree!); the [list of active formatting elements](#341.html_list-of-active-formatting-elements) has the new [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element in it; and the [insertion mode](#341.html_insertion-mode) is still "[in table body](#341.html_parsing-main-intbody)".

Had the character tokens been only [space characters](#341.html_space-character) instead of "bbb", then those [space characters](#341.html_space-character) would just be appended to the [`tbody`](#341.html_the-tbody-element) element.

Finally, the [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element) is closed by a "table" end tag. This pops all the nodes from the [stack of open elements](#341.html_stack-of-open-elements) up to and including the [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element) element, but it doesn't affect the [list of active formatting elements](#341.html_list-of-active-formatting-elements), so the "ccc" character tokens after the table result in yet another [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) element being created, this time after the table:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): bbb
        *   [`table`](#341.html_the-table-element)
            *   [`tbody`](#341.html_the-tbody-element)
                *   [`tr`](#341.html_the-tr-element)
                    *   [`td`](#341.html_the-td-element)
                        *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): aaa
        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): ccc

##### 8.2.8.4 Scripts that modify the page as it is being parsed

*This section is non-normative.*

Consider the following markup, which for this example we will assume is the document with URL `http://example.com/inner`, being rendered as the content of an [`iframe`](#341.html_the-iframe-element) in another document with the URL `http://example.com/outer`:

```
<div id=a>
 <script>
  var div = document.getElementById('a');
  parent.document.body.appendChild(div);
 </script>
 <script>
  alert(document.URL);
 </script>
</div>
<script>
 alert(document.URL);
</script>
```

Up to the first "script" end tag, before the script is parsed, the result is relatively straightforward:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`div`](#341.html_the-div-element) `id`="[`a`](#341.html_the-a-element)"
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0):
            *   [`script`](#341.html_the-script-element)
                *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): var div = document.getElementById('a'); ? parent.document.body.appendChild(div);

After the script is parsed, though, the [`div`](#341.html_the-div-element) element and its child [`script`](#341.html_the-script-element) element are gone:

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)

They are, at this point, in the [`Document`](#341.html_document) of the aforementioned outer [browsing context](#341.html_browsing-context). However, the [stack of open elements](#341.html_stack-of-open-elements) *still contains the [`div`](#341.html_the-div-element) element*.

Thus, when the second [`script`](#341.html_the-script-element) element is parsed, it is inserted *into the outer [`Document`](#341.html_document) object*.

Those parsed into different [`Document`](#341.html_document)s than the one the parser was created for do not execute, so the first alert does not show.

Once the [`div`](#341.html_the-div-element) element's end tag is parsed, the [`div`](#341.html_the-div-element) element is popped off the stack, and so the next [`script`](#341.html_the-script-element) element is in the inner [`Document`](#341.html_document):

*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`script`](#341.html_the-script-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): alert(document.URL);

This script does execute, resulting in an alert that says "http://example.com/inner".

##### 8.2.8.5 The execution of scripts that are moving across multiple documents

*This section is non-normative.*

Elaborating on the example in the previous section, consider the case where the second [`script`](#341.html_the-script-element) element is an external script (i.e. one with a [`src`](#341.html_attr-script-src) attribute). Since the element was not in the parser's [`Document`](#341.html_document) when it was created, that external script is not even downloaded.

In a case where a [`script`](#341.html_the-script-element) element with a [`src`](#341.html_attr-script-src) attribute is parsed normally into its parser's [`Document`](#341.html_document), but while the external script is being downloaded, the element is moved to another document, the script continues to download, but does not execute.

In general, moving [`script`](#341.html_the-script-element) elements between [`Document`](#341.html_document)s is considered a bad practice.

##### 8.2.8.6 Unclosed formatting elements

*This section is non-normative.*

The following markup shows how nested formatting elements (such as [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)) get collected and continue to be applied even as the elements they are contained in are closed, but that excessive duplicates are thrown away.

```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<p><b class=x><b class=x><b><b class=x><b class=x><b>X
<p>X
<p><b><b class=x><b>X
<p></b></b></b></b></b></b>X
```

The resulting DOM tree is as follows:

*   DOCTYPE: [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
*   [`html`](#341.html_the-html-element)
    *   [`head`](#341.html_the-head-element)
    *   [`body`](#341.html_the-body-element)
        *   [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)
            *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) `class`="`x`"
                *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) `class`="`x`"
                    *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) `class`="`x`"
                            *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) `class`="`x`"
                                *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                                    *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): X?
        *   [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)
            *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) `class`="`x`"
                *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                    *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) `class`="`x`"
                        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) `class`="`x`"
                            *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                                *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): X?
        *   [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)
            *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) `class`="`x`"
                *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                    *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) `class`="`x`"
                        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) `class`="`x`"
                            *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                                *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                                    *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) `class`="`x`"
                                        *   [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element)
                                            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): X?
        *   [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element)
            *   [`#text`](#341.html_text-0): X?

Note how the second [`p`](#341.html_the-p-element) element in the markup has no explicit [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) elements, but in the resulting DOM, up to three of each kind of formatting element (in this case three [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) elements with the class attribute, and two unadorned [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) elements) get reconstructed before the element's "X".

Also note how this means that in the final paragraph only six [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) end tags are needed to completely clear the list of formatting elements, even though nine [`b`](#341.html_the-b-element) start tags have been seen up to this point.

### 8.3 Serializing HTML fragments

The following steps form the <dfn id="342.html_html-fragment-serialization-algorithm">HTML fragment serialization algorithm</dfn>. The algorithm takes as input a DOM [`Element`](#342.html_element), [`Document`](#342.html_document), or [`DocumentFragment`](#342.html_documentfragment) referred to as `the node`, and either returns a string or throws an exception.

This algorithm serializes the *children* of the node being serialized, not the node itself.

1.  Let `s` be a string, and initialize it to the empty string.

2.  If `the node` is a [`template`](#342.html_the-template-element) element, then let `the node` instead be the [`template`](#342.html_the-template-element) element's [template contents](#342.html_template-contents) (a [`DocumentFragment`](#342.html_documentfragment) node).

3.  For each child node of `the node`, in [tree order](#342.html_tree-order), run the following steps:

    1.  Let `current node` be the child node being processed.

    2.  Append the appropriate string from the following list to `s`:

        If `current node` is an `Element`

        If `current node` is an element in the [HTML namespace](#342.html_html-namespace-0), the [MathML namespace](#342.html_mathml-namespace), or the [SVG namespace](#342.html_svg-namespace), then let `tagname` be `current node`'s local name. Otherwise, let `tagname` be `current node`'s qualified name.

        Append a "<" (U+003C) character, followed by `tagname`.

        For [HTML elements](#342.html_html-elements) created by the [HTML parser](#342.html_html-parser) or `Document.createElement()`, `tagname` will be lowercase.

        For each attribute that the element has, append a U+0020 SPACE character, the [attribute's serialized name as described below](#342.html_attribute's-serialized-name), a "=" (U+003D) character, a U+0022 QUOTATION MARK character ("), the attribute's value, [escaped as described below](#342.html_escapingString) in *attribute mode*, and a second U+0022 QUOTATION MARK character (").

        An <dfn id="342.html_attribute's-serialized-name">attribute's serialized name</dfn> for the purposes of the previous paragraph must be determined as follows:

        If the attribute has no namespace

        The attribute's serialized name is the attribute's local name.

        For attributes on [HTML elements](#342.html_html-elements) set by the [HTML parser](#342.html_html-parser) or by `Element.setAttribute()`, the local name will be lowercase.

        If the attribute is in the [XML namespace](#342.html_xml-namespace)

        The attribute's serialized name is the string "`xml:`" followed by the attribute's local name.

        If the attribute is in the [XMLNS namespace](#342.html_xmlns-namespace) and the attribute's local name is `xmlns`

        The attribute's serialized name is the string "`xmlns`".

        If the attribute is in the [XMLNS namespace](#342.html_xmlns-namespace) and the attribute's local name is not `xmlns`

        The attribute's serialized name is the string "`xmlns:`" followed by the attribute's local name.

        If the attribute is in the [XLink namespace](#342.html_xlink-namespace)

        The attribute's serialized name is the string "`xlink:`" followed by the attribute's local name.

        If the attribute is in some other namespace

        The attribute's serialized name is the attribute's qualified name.

        While the exact order of attributes is UA-defined, and may depend on factors such as the order that the attributes were given in the original markup, the sort order must be stable, such that consecutive invocations of this algorithm serialize an element's attributes in the same order.

        Append a ">" (U+003E) character.

        If `current node` is an [`area`](#342.html_the-area-element), [`base`](#342.html_the-base-element), [`basefont`](#342.html_basefont), [`bgsound`](#342.html_bgsound), [`br`](#342.html_the-br-element), [`col`](#342.html_the-col-element), [`embed`](#342.html_the-embed-element), [`frame`](#342.html_frame), [`hr`](#342.html_the-hr-element), [`img`](#342.html_the-img-element), [`input`](#342.html_the-input-element), [`keygen`](#342.html_the-keygen-element), [`link`](#342.html_the-link-element), [`meta`](#342.html_the-meta-element), [`param`](#342.html_the-param-element), [`source`](#342.html_the-source-element), [`track`](#342.html_the-track-element) or [`wbr`](#342.html_the-wbr-element) element, then continue on to the next child node at this point.

        If `current node` is a [`pre`](#342.html_the-pre-element), [`textarea`](#342.html_the-textarea-element), or [`listing`](#342.html_listing) element, and the first child node of the element, if any, is a [`Text`](#342.html_text-0) node whose character data has as its first character a "LF" (U+000A) character, then append a "LF" (U+000A) character.

        Append the value of running the [HTML fragment serialization algorithm](#342.html_html-fragment-serialization-algorithm) on the `current node` element (thus recursing into this algorithm for that element), followed by a "<" (U+003C) character, a U+002F SOLIDUS character (/), `tagname` again, and finally a U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN character (>).

        If `current node` is a `Text` node

        If the parent of `current node` is a [`style`](#342.html_the-style-element), [`script`](#342.html_the-script-element), [`xmp`](#342.html_xmp), [`iframe`](#342.html_the-iframe-element), [`noembed`](#342.html_noembed), [`noframes`](#342.html_noframes), or [`plaintext`](#342.html_plaintext) element, or if the parent of `current node` is a [`noscript`](#342.html_the-noscript-element) element and [scripting is enabled](#342.html_concept-n-script) for the node, then append the value of `current node`'s `data` IDL attribute literally.

        Otherwise, append the value of `current node`'s `data` IDL attribute, [escaped as described below](#342.html_escapingString).

        If `current node` is a `Comment`

        Append the literal string `<!--` (U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN, U+0021 EXCLAMATION MARK, U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS), followed by the value of `current node`'s `data` IDL attribute, followed by the literal string `-->` (U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN).

        If `current node` is a `ProcessingInstruction`

        Append the literal string `<?` (U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN, U+003F QUESTION MARK), followed by the value of `current node`'s `target` IDL attribute, followed by a single U+0020 SPACE character, followed by the value of `current node`'s `data` IDL attribute, followed by a single ">" (U+003E) character.

        If `current node` is a `DocumentType`

        Append the literal string `<!DOCTYPE` (U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN, U+0021 EXCLAMATION MARK, U+0044 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER D, U+004F LATIN CAPITAL LETTER O, U+0043 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER C, U+0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T, U+0059 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Y, U+0050 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER P, U+0045 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER E), followed by a space (U+0020 SPACE), followed by the value of `current node`'s `name` IDL attribute, followed by the literal string `>` (U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN).

4.  The result of the algorithm is the string `s`.

It is possible that the output of this algorithm, if parsed with an [HTML parser](#342.html_html-parser), will not return the original tree structure.

For instance, if a [`textarea`](#342.html_the-textarea-element) element to which a `Comment` node has been appended is serialized and the output is then reparsed, the comment will end up being displayed in the text field. Similarly, if, as a result of DOM manipulation, an element contains a comment that contains the literal string "`-->`", then when the result of serializing the element is parsed, the comment will be truncated at that point and the rest of the comment will be interpreted as markup. More examples would be making a [`script`](#342.html_the-script-element) element contain a [`Text`](#342.html_text-0) node with the text string "`</script>`", or having a [`p`](#342.html_the-p-element) element that contains a [`ul`](#342.html_the-ul-element) element (as the [`ul`](#342.html_the-ul-element) element's [start tag](#342.html_syntax-start-tag) would imply the end tag for the [`p`](#342.html_the-p-element)).

This can enable cross-site scripting attacks. An example of this would be a page that lets the user enter some font family names that are then inserted into a CSS [`style`](#342.html_the-style-element) block via the DOM and which then uses the [`innerHTML`](#342.html_dom-innerhtml) IDL attribute to get the HTML serialization of that [`style`](#342.html_the-style-element) element: if the user enters "`</style><script>attack</script>`" as a font family name, [`innerHTML`](#342.html_dom-innerhtml) will return markup that, if parsed in a different context, would contain a [`script`](#342.html_the-script-element) node, even though no [`script`](#342.html_the-script-element) node existed in the original DOM.

<dfn id="342.html_escapingString">Escaping a string</dfn> (for the purposes of the algorithm above) consists of running the following steps:

1.  Replace any occurrence of the "`&`" character by the string "`&amp;`".

2.  Replace any occurrences of the U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE character by the string "`&nbsp;`".

3.  If the algorithm was invoked in the *attribute mode*, replace any occurrences of the "`"`" character by the string "`&quot;`".

4.  If the algorithm was *not* invoked in the *attribute mode*, replace any occurrences of the "`<`" character by the string "`&lt;`", and any occurrences of the "`>`" character by the string "`&gt;`".

### 8.4 Parsing HTML fragments

The following steps form the <dfn id="343.html_html-fragment-parsing-algorithm">HTML fragment parsing algorithm</dfn>. The algorithm optionally takes as input an [`Element`](#343.html_element) node, referred to as the <dfn id="343.html_concept-frag-parse-context" data-anolis-xref="concept-frag-parse-context">`context`</dfn> element, which gives the context for the parser, as well as `input`, a string to parse, and returns a list of zero or more nodes.

Parts marked <dfn id="343.html_fragment-case">fragment case</dfn> in algorithms in the parser section are parts that only occur if the parser was created for the purposes of this algorithm (and with a [`context`](#343.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element). The algorithms have been annotated with such markings for informational purposes only; such markings have no normative weight. If it is possible for a condition described as a [fragment case](#343.html_fragment-case) to occur even when the parser wasn't created for the purposes of handling this algorithm, then that is an error in the specification.

1.  Create a new [`Document`](#343.html_document) node, and mark it as being an [HTML document](#343.html_html-documents).

2.  If there is a [`context`](#343.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element, and the [`Document`](#343.html_document) of the [`context`](#343.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element is in [quirks mode](#343.html_quirks-mode), then let the [`Document`](#343.html_document) be in [quirks mode](#343.html_quirks-mode). Otherwise, if there is a [`context`](#343.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element, and the [`Document`](#343.html_document) of the [`context`](#343.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element is in [limited-quirks mode](#343.html_limited-quirks-mode), then let the [`Document`](#343.html_document) be in [limited-quirks mode](#343.html_limited-quirks-mode). Otherwise, leave the [`Document`](#343.html_document) in [no-quirks mode](#343.html_no-quirks-mode).

3.  Create a new [HTML parser](#343.html_html-parser), and associate it with the just created [`Document`](#343.html_document) node.

4.  If there is a [`context`](#343.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element, run these substeps:

    1.  Set the state of the [HTML parser](#343.html_html-parser)'s [tokenization](#343.html_tokenization) stage as follows:

        If it is a [`title`](#343.html_the-title-element) or [`textarea`](#343.html_the-textarea-element) element

        Switch the tokenizer to the [RCDATA state](#343.html_rcdata-state).

        If it is a [`style`](#343.html_the-style-element), [`xmp`](#343.html_xmp), [`iframe`](#343.html_the-iframe-element), [`noembed`](#343.html_noembed), or [`noframes`](#343.html_noframes) element

        Switch the tokenizer to the [RAWTEXT state](#343.html_rawtext-state).

        If it is a [`script`](#343.html_the-script-element) element

        Switch the tokenizer to the [script data state](#343.html_script-data-state).

        If it is a [`noscript`](#343.html_the-noscript-element) element

        If the [scripting flag](#343.html_scripting-flag) is enabled, switch the tokenizer to the [RAWTEXT state](#343.html_rawtext-state). Otherwise, leave the tokenizer in the [data state](#343.html_data-state).

        If it is a [`plaintext`](#343.html_plaintext) element

        Switch the tokenizer to the [PLAINTEXT state](#343.html_plaintext-state).

        Otherwise

        Leave the tokenizer in the [data state](#343.html_data-state).

        For performance reasons, an implementation that does not report errors and that uses the actual state machine described in this specification directly could use the PLAINTEXT state instead of the RAWTEXT and script data states where those are mentioned in the list above. Except for rules regarding parse errors, they are equivalent, since there is no [appropriate end tag token](#343.html_appropriate-end-tag-token) in the fragment case, yet they involve far fewer state transitions.

    2.  Let `root` be a new [`html`](#343.html_the-html-element) element with no attributes.

    3.  Append the element `root` to the [`Document`](#343.html_document) node created above.

    4.  Set up the parser's [stack of open elements](#343.html_stack-of-open-elements) so that it contains just the single element `root`.

    5.  If the [`context`](#343.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element is a [`template`](#343.html_the-template-element) element, push "[in template](#343.html_parsing-main-intemplate)" onto the [stack of template insertion modes](#343.html_stack-of-template-insertion-modes) so that it is the new [current template insertion mode](#343.html_current-template-insertion-mode).

    6.  [Reset the parser's insertion mode appropriately](#343.html_reset-the-insertion-mode-appropriately).

        The parser will reference the [`context`](#343.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element as part of that algorithm.

    7.  Set the parser's [`form` element pointer](#343.html_form-element-pointer) to the nearest node to the [`context`](#343.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element that is a [`form`](#343.html_the-form-element) element (going straight up the ancestor chain, and including the element itself, if it is a [`form`](#343.html_the-form-element) element), if any. (If there is no such [`form`](#343.html_the-form-element) element, the [`form` element pointer](#343.html_form-element-pointer) keeps its initial value, null.)

5.  Place into the [input stream](#343.html_input-stream) for the [HTML parser](#343.html_html-parser) just created the `input`. The encoding [confidence](#343.html_concept-encoding-confidence) is *irrelevant*.

6.  Start the parser and let it run until it has consumed all the characters just inserted into the input stream.

7.  If there is a [`context`](#343.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element, return the child nodes of `root`, in [tree order](#343.html_tree-order).

    Otherwise, return the children of the [`Document`](#343.html_document) object, in [tree order](#343.html_tree-order).

## 9 <dfn id="345.html_xhtml">The XHTML syntax</dfn>

This section only describes the rules for XML resources. Rules for [`text/html`](#345.html_text/html) resources are discussed in the section above entitled "[The HTML syntax](#345.html_syntax)".

### 9.1 Writing XHTML documents

The syntax for using HTML with XML, whether in XHTML documents or embedded in other XML documents, is defined in the XML and Namespaces in XML specifications. [[XML]](#346.html_refsXML) [[XMLNS]](#346.html_refsXMLNS)

This specification does not define any syntax-level requirements beyond those defined for XML proper.

XML documents may contain a `DOCTYPE` if desired, but this is not required to conform to this specification. This specification does not define a public or system identifier, nor provide a formal DTD.

According to the XML specification, XML processors are not guaranteed to process the external DTD subset referenced in the DOCTYPE. This means, for example, that using [entity references](http://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#dt-entref) for characters in XHTML documents is unsafe if they are defined in an external file (except for `&lt;`, `&gt;`, `&amp;`, `&quot;` and `&apos;`).

### 9.2 Parsing XHTML documents

This section describes the relationship between XML and the DOM, with a particular emphasis on how this interacts with HTML.

An <dfn id="347.html_xml-parser">XML parser</dfn>, for the purposes of this specification, is a construct that follows the rules given in the XML specification to map a string of bytes or characters into a [`Document`](#347.html_document) object.

At the time of writing, no such rules actually exist.

An [XML parser](#347.html_xml-parser) is either associated with a [`Document`](#347.html_document) object when it is created, or creates one implicitly.

This [`Document`](#347.html_document) must then be populated with DOM nodes that represent the tree structure of the input passed to the parser, as defined by the XML specification, the Namespaces in XML specification, and the DOM specification. DOM mutation events must not fire for the operations that the [XML parser](#347.html_xml-parser) performs on the [`Document`](#347.html_document)'s tree, but the user agent must act as if elements and attributes were individually appended and set respectively so as to trigger rules in this specification regarding what happens when an element is inserted into a document or has its attributes set, and the DOM specification's requirements regarding mutation observers mean that mutation observers *are* fired (unlike mutation events). [[XML]](#347.html_refsXML) [[XMLNS]](#347.html_refsXMLNS) [[DOM]](#347.html_refsDOM) [[DOMEVENTS]](#347.html_refsDOMEVENTS)

Between the time an element's start tag is parsed and the time either the element's end tag is parsed or the parser detects a well-formedness error, the user agent must act as if the element was in a [stack of open elements](#347.html_stack-of-open-elements).

This is used by the [`object`](#347.html_the-object-element) element to avoid instantiating plugins before the [`param`](#347.html_the-param-element) element children have been parsed.

[[XML]](#347.html_refsXML)

*   `-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//EN`
*   `-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.1//EN`
*   `-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Strict//EN`
*   `-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Frameset//EN`
*   `-//W3C//DTD XHTML Basic 1.0//EN`
*   `-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.1 plus MathML 2.0//EN`
*   `-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.1 plus MathML 2.0 plus SVG 1.1//EN`
