*   `-//WAPFORUM//DTD XHTML Mobile 1.0//EN`

Furthermore, user agents should attempt to retrieve the above external entity's content when one of the above public identifiers is used, and should not attempt to retrieve any other external entity's content.

This is not strictly a [violation](#347.html_willful-violation) of the XML specification, but it does contradict the spirit of the XML specification's requirements. This is motivated by a desire for user agents to all handle entities in an interoperable fashion without requiring any network access for handling external subsets. [[XML]](#347.html_refsXML)

When an [XML parser](#347.html_xml-parser) creates a [`script`](#347.html_the-script-element) element, it must be marked as being ["parser-inserted"](#347.html_parser-inserted) and its ["force-async"](#347.html_force-async) flag must be unset. If the parser was originally created for the [XML fragment parsing algorithm](#347.html_xml-fragment-parsing-algorithm), then the element must be marked as ["already started"](#347.html_already-started) also. When the element's end tag is parsed, the user agent must [perform a microtask checkpoint](#347.html_perform-a-microtask-checkpoint), [provide a stable state](#347.html_provide-a-stable-state), and then [prepare](#347.html_prepare-a-script) the [`script`](#347.html_the-script-element) element. If this causes there to be a [pending parsing-blocking script](#347.html_pending-parsing-blocking-script), then the user agent must run the following steps:

1.  Block this instance of the [XML parser](#347.html_xml-parser), such that the [event loop](#347.html_event-loop) will not run [tasks](#347.html_concept-task) that invoke it.

2.  [Spin the event loop](#347.html_spin-the-event-loop) until the parser's [`Document`](#347.html_document) [has no style sheet that is blocking scripts](#347.html_has-no-style-sheet-that-is-blocking-scripts) and the [pending parsing-blocking script](#347.html_pending-parsing-blocking-script)'s ["ready to be parser-executed"](#347.html_ready-to-be-parser-executed) flag is set.

3.  Unblock this instance of the [XML parser](#347.html_xml-parser), such that [tasks](#347.html_concept-task) that invoke it can again be run.

4.  [Execute](#347.html_execute-the-script-block) the [pending parsing-blocking script](#347.html_pending-parsing-blocking-script).

5.  There is no longer a [pending parsing-blocking script](#347.html_pending-parsing-blocking-script).

Since the [`document.write()`](#347.html_dom-document-write) API is not available for [XML documents](#347.html_xml-documents), much of the complexity in the [HTML parser](#347.html_html-parser) is not needed in the [XML parser](#347.html_xml-parser).

When an [XML parser](#347.html_xml-parser) would append a node to a [`template`](#347.html_the-template-element) element, it must instead append it to the [`template`](#347.html_the-template-element) element's [template contents](#347.html_template-contents) (a [`DocumentFragment`](#347.html_documentfragment) node).

This is a [willful violation](#347.html_willful-violation) of the XML specification; unfortunately, XML is not formally extensible in the manner that is needed for [`template`](#347.html_the-template-element) processing. [[XML]](#347.html_refsXML)

When an [XML parser](#347.html_xml-parser) creates a [`Node`](#347.html_node) object, its [`ownerDocument`](#347.html_dom-node-ownerdocument) must be set to the [`Document`](#347.html_document) of the node into which the newly created node is to be inserted.

Certain algorithms in this specification <dfn id="347.html_feed-the-parser" data-anolis-xref="feed the parser">spoon-feed the parser</dfn> characters one string at a time. In such cases, the [XML parser](#347.html_xml-parser) must act as it would have if faced with a single string consisting of the concatenation of all those characters.

When an [XML parser](#347.html_xml-parser) reaches the end of its input, it must [stop parsing](#347.html_stop-parsing), following the same rules as the [HTML parser](#347.html_html-parser). An [XML parser](#347.html_xml-parser) can also be [aborted](#347.html_abort-a-parser), which must again by done in the same way as for an [HTML parser](#347.html_html-parser).

For the purposes of conformance checkers, if a resource is determined to be in [the XHTML syntax](#347.html_the-xhtml-syntax), then it is an [XML document](#347.html_xml-documents).

### 9.3 Serializing XHTML fragments

The <dfn id="348.html_xml-fragment-serialization-algorithm">XML fragment serialization algorithm</dfn> for a [`Document`](#348.html_document) or [`Element`](#348.html_element) node either returns a fragment of XML that represents that node or throws an exception.

For [`Document`](#348.html_document)s, the algorithm must return a string in the form of a [document entity](http://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-well-formed), if none of the error cases below apply.

For [`Element`](#348.html_element)s, the algorithm must return a string in the form of an [internal general parsed entity](http://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#wf-entities), if none of the error cases below apply.

In both cases, the string returned must be XML namespace-well-formed and must be an isomorphic serialization of all of that node's [relevant child nodes](#348.html_relevant-child-nodes), in [tree order](#348.html_tree-order). User agents may adjust prefixes and namespace declarations in the serialization (and indeed might be forced to do so in some cases to obtain namespace-well-formed XML). User agents may use a combination of regular text and character references to represent [`Text`](#348.html_text-0) nodes in the DOM.

A node's <dfn id="348.html_relevant-child-nodes">relevant child nodes</dfn> are those that apply given the following rules:

For [`template`](#348.html_the-template-element) elements

The [relevant child nodes](#348.html_relevant-child-nodes) are the child nodes of the [`template`](#348.html_the-template-element) element's [template contents](#348.html_template-contents), if any.

For all other nodes

The [relevant child nodes](#348.html_relevant-child-nodes) are the child nodes of node itself, if any.

For [`Element`](#348.html_element)s, if any of the elements in the serialization are in no namespace, the default namespace in scope for those elements must be explicitly declared as the empty string. (This doesn't apply in the [`Document`](#348.html_document) case.) [[XML]](#348.html_refsXML) [[XMLNS]](#348.html_refsXMLNS)

For the purposes of this section, an internal general parsed entity is considered XML namespace-well-formed if a document consisting of an element with no namespace declarations whose contents are the internal general parsed entity would itself be XML namespace-well-formed.

If any of the following error cases are found in the DOM subtree being serialized, then the algorithm must throw an [`InvalidStateError`](#348.html_invalidstateerror) exception instead of returning a string:

*   A [`Document`](#348.html_document) node with no child element nodes.
*   A [`DocumentType`](#348.html_documenttype) node that has an external subset public identifier that contains characters that are not matched by the XML `PubidChar` production. [[XML]](#348.html_refsXML)
*   A [`DocumentType`](#348.html_documenttype) node that has an external subset system identifier that contains both a """ (U+0022) and a "'" (U+0027) or that contains characters that are not matched by the XML `Char` production. [[XML]](#348.html_refsXML)
*   A node with a local name containing a ":" (U+003A).
*   A node with a local name that does not match the XML `Name` production. [[XML]](#348.html_refsXML)
*   An [`Attr`](#348.html_attr) node with no namespace whose local name is the lowercase string "`xmlns`". [[XMLNS]](#348.html_refsXMLNS)
*   An [`Element`](#348.html_element) node with two or more attributes with the same local name and namespace.
*   An [`Attr`](#348.html_attr) node, [`Text`](#348.html_text-0) node, [`Comment`](#348.html_comment-0) node, or [`ProcessingInstruction`](#348.html_processinginstruction) node whose data contains characters that are not matched by the XML `Char` production. [[XML]](#348.html_refsXML)
*   A [`Comment`](#348.html_comment-0) node whose data contains two adjacent U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS characters (-) or ends with such a character.
*   A [`ProcessingInstruction`](#348.html_processinginstruction) node whose target name is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#348.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`xml`".
*   A [`ProcessingInstruction`](#348.html_processinginstruction) node whose target name contains a ":" (U+003A).
*   A [`ProcessingInstruction`](#348.html_processinginstruction) node whose data contains the string "`?>`".

These are the only ways to make a DOM unserializable. The DOM enforces all the other XML constraints; for example, trying to append two elements to a [`Document`](#348.html_document) node will throw a [`HierarchyRequestError`](#348.html_hierarchyrequesterror) exception.

When the algorithm must produce a serialization of a [`template`](#348.html_the-template-element) element, the string returned must contain a serialization of the child nodes of the template element's [`content`](#348.html_dom-template-content) [`DocumentFragment`](#348.html_documentfragment), rather than the [`template`](#348.html_the-template-element) element's children.

### 9.4 Parsing XHTML fragments

The <dfn id="349.html_xml-fragment-parsing-algorithm">XML fragment parsing algorithm</dfn> either returns a [`Document`](#349.html_document) or throws a [`SyntaxError`](#349.html_syntaxerror) exception. Given a string `input` and an optional context element [`context`](#349.html_concept-frag-parse-context), the algorithm is as follows:

1.  Create a new [XML parser](#349.html_xml-parser).

2.  If there is a [`context`](#349.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element, [feed the parser](#349.html_feed-the-parser) just created the string corresponding to the start tag of that element, declaring all the namespace prefixes that are in scope on that element in the DOM, as well as declaring the default namespace (if any) that is in scope on that element in the DOM.

    A namespace prefix is in scope if the DOM `lookupNamespaceURI()` method on the element would return a non-null value for that prefix.

    The default namespace is the namespace for which the DOM `isDefaultNamespace()` method on the element would return true.

    If there is a [`context`](#349.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element, no `DOCTYPE` is passed to the parser, and therefore no external subset is referenced, and therefore no entities will be recognized.

3.  [Feed the parser](#349.html_feed-the-parser) just created the string `input`.

4.  If there is a [`context`](#349.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element, [feed the parser](#349.html_feed-the-parser) just created the string corresponding to the end tag of that element.

5.  If there is an XML well-formedness or XML namespace well-formedness error, then throw a [`SyntaxError`](#349.html_syntaxerror) exception and abort these steps.

6.  If there is a [`context`](#349.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element, and the root element of the resulting [`Document`](#349.html_document) has any sibling nodes, then throw a [`SyntaxError`](#349.html_syntaxerror) exception and abort these steps.

7.  If there is a [`context`](#349.html_concept-frag-parse-context) element, then return the child nodes of the root element of the resulting [`Document`](#349.html_document), in [tree order](#349.html_tree-order).

    Otherwise, return the children of the [`Document`](#349.html_document) object, in [tree order](#349.html_tree-order).

## 10 Rendering

*User agents are not required to present HTML documents in any particular way. However, this section provides a set of suggestions for rendering HTML documents that, if followed, are likely to lead to a user experience that closely resembles the experience intended by the documents' authors. So as to avoid confusion regarding the normativity of this section, RFC2119 terms have not been used. Instead, the term "expected" is used to indicate behavior that will lead to this experience. For the purposes of conformance for user agents designated as [supporting the suggested default rendering](#350.html_renderingUA), the term "expected" in this section has the same conformance implications as the RFC2119-defined term "must".*

### 10.1 Introduction

In general, user agents are expected to support CSS, and many of the suggestions in this section are expressed in CSS terms. User agents that use other presentation mechanisms can derive their expected behavior by translating from the CSS rules given in this section.

In the absence of style-layer rules to the contrary (e.g. author style sheets), user agents are expected to render an element so that it conveys to the user the meaning that the element [represents](#351.html_represents), as described by this specification.

The suggestions in this section generally assume a visual output medium with a resolution of 96dpi or greater, but HTML is intended to apply to multiple media (it is a *media-independent* language). User agent implementors are encouraged to adapt the suggestions in this section to their target media.

* * *

An element is <dfn id="351.html_being-rendered">being rendered</dfn> if it has any associated CSS layout boxes, SVG layout boxes, or some equivalent in other styling languages.

Just being off-screen does not mean the element is not [being rendered](#351.html_being-rendered). The presence of the [`hidden`](#351.html_the-hidden-attribute) attribute normally means the element is not [being rendered](#351.html_being-rendered), though this might be overridden by the style sheets.

* * *

User agents that do not honor author-level CSS style sheets are nonetheless expected to act as if they applied the CSS rules given in these sections in a manner consistent with this specification and the relevant CSS and Unicode specifications. [[CSS]](#351.html_refsCSS) [[UNICODE]](#351.html_refsUNICODE) [[BIDI]](#351.html_refsBIDI)

This is especially important for issues relating to the 'display', 'unicode-bidi', and 'direction' properties.

### 10.2 The CSS user agent style sheet and presentational hints

The CSS rules given in these subsections are, except where otherwise specified, expected to be used as part of the user-agent level style sheet defaults for all documents that contain [HTML elements](#352.html_html-elements).

Some rules are intended for the author-level zero-specificity presentational hints part of the CSS cascade; these are explicitly called out as <dfn id="352.html_presentational-hints">presentational hints</dfn>.

Some of the rules regarding left and right margins are given here as appropriate for elements whose 'direction' property is 'ltr', and are expected to be flipped around on elements whose 'direction' property is 'rtl'. These are marked "<dfn id="352.html_ltr-specific">LTR-specific</dfn>".

These markings only affect the handling of attribute *values*, not attribute names or element names.

* * *

When the text below says that an attribute `attribute` on an element `element` <dfn id="352.html_maps-to-the-pixel-length-property">maps to the pixel length property</dfn> (or properties) `properties`, it means that if `element` has an attribute `attribute` set, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#352.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) doesn't generate an error, then the user agent is expected to use the parsed value as a pixel length for a [presentational hint](#352.html_presentational-hints) for `properties`.

When the text below says that an attribute `attribute` on an element `element` <dfn id="352.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property">maps to the dimension property</dfn> (or properties) `properties`, it means that if `element` has an attribute `attribute` set, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing dimension values](#352.html_rules-for-parsing-dimension-values) doesn't generate an error, then the user agent is expected to use the parsed dimension as the value for a [presentational hint](#352.html_presentational-hints) for `properties`, with the value given as a pixel length if the dimension was an integer, and with the value given as a percentage if the dimension was a percentage.

When a user agent is to <dfn id="352.html_align-descendants">align descendants</dfn> of a node, the user agent is expected to align only those descendants that have both their 'margin-left' and 'margin-right' properties computing to a value other than 'auto', that are over-constrained and that have one of those two margins with a used value forced to a greater value, and that do not themselves have an applicable `align` attribute. When multiple elements are to [align](#352.html_align-descendants) a particular descendant, the most deeply nested such element is expected to override the others. Aligned elements are expected to be aligned by having the used values of their left and right margins be set accordingly.

### 10.3 Non-replaced elements

#### 10.3.1 Hidden elements

```
[](#cb735-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb735-2)
[](#cb735-3)[hidden], area, base, basefont, datalist, head, link,
[](#cb735-4)meta, noembed, noframes, param, rp, script, source, style, template, track, title {
[](#cb735-5)  display: none;
[](#cb735-6)}
[](#cb735-7)
[](#cb735-8)embed[hidden] { display: inline; height: 0; width: 0; }
```

The user agent is expected to force the 'display' property of [`noscript`](#354.html_the-noscript-element) elements for whom [scripting is enabled](#354.html_concept-n-script) to compute to 'none', irrespective of CSS rules.

The user agent is expected to force the 'display' property of [`input`](#354.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#354.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Hidden](#354.html_hidden-state-(type=hidden)) state to compute to 'none', irrespective of CSS rules.

#### 10.3.2 The page

```
[](#cb736-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb736-2)
[](#cb736-3)html, body { display: block; }
```

For each property in the table below, given a [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element, the first attribute that exists [maps to the pixel length property](#355.html_maps-to-the-pixel-length-property) on the [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element. If none of the attributes for a property are found, or if the value of the attribute that was found cannot be parsed successfully, then a default value of 8px is expected to be used for that property instead.

| Property | Source |
| --- | --- |
| 'margin-top' | [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's [`marginheight`](#355.html_attr-body-marginheight) attribute |
| The [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's [container frame element](#355.html_container-frame-element)'s [`marginheight`](#355.html_attr-iframe-marginheight) attribute |
| [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's `topmargin` attribute |
| 'margin-right' | [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's [`marginwidth`](#355.html_attr-body-marginwidth) attribute |
| The [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's [container frame element](#355.html_container-frame-element)'s [`marginwidth`](#355.html_attr-iframe-marginwidth) attribute |
| [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's `rightmargin` attribute |
| 'margin-bottom' | [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's [`marginheight`](#355.html_attr-body-marginheight) attribute |
| The [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's [container frame element](#355.html_container-frame-element)'s [`marginheight`](#355.html_attr-iframe-marginheight) attribute |
| [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's `bottommargin` attribute |
| 'margin-left' | [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's [`marginwidth`](#355.html_attr-body-marginwidth) attribute |
| The [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's [container frame element](#355.html_container-frame-element)'s [`marginwidth`](#355.html_attr-iframe-marginwidth) attribute |
| [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's `leftmargin` attribute |

If the [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element's [`Document`](#355.html_document)'s [browsing context](#355.html_browsing-context) is a [nested browsing context](#355.html_nested-browsing-context), and the [browsing context container](#355.html_browsing-context-container) of that [nested browsing context](#355.html_nested-browsing-context) is a [`frame`](#355.html_frame) or [`iframe`](#355.html_the-iframe-element) element, then the <dfn id="355.html_container-frame-element">container frame element</dfn> of the [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element is that [`frame`](#355.html_frame) or [`iframe`](#355.html_the-iframe-element) element. Otherwise, there is no [container frame element](#355.html_container-frame-element).

The above requirements imply that a page can change the margins of another page (including one from another [origin](#355.html_origin-0)) using, for example, an [`iframe`](#355.html_the-iframe-element). This is potentially a security risk, as it might in some cases allow an attack to contrive a situation in which a page is rendered not as the author intended, possibly for the purposes of phishing or otherwise misleading the user.

* * *

If the [`Document`](#355.html_document) has a [root element](#355.html_root-element), and the [`Document`](#355.html_document)'s [browsing context](#355.html_browsing-context) is a [nested browsing context](#355.html_nested-browsing-context), and the [browsing context container](#355.html_browsing-context-container) of that [nested browsing context](#355.html_nested-browsing-context) is a [`frame`](#355.html_frame) or [`iframe`](#355.html_the-iframe-element) element, and that element has a `scrolling` attribute, then the user agent is expected to compare the value of the attribute in an [ASCII case-insensitive](#355.html_ascii-case-insensitive) manner to the values in the first column of the following table, and if one of them matches, then the user agent is expected to treat that attribute as a [presentational hint](#355.html_presentational-hints) for the aforementioned root element's 'overflow' property, setting it to the value given in the corresponding cell on the same row in the second column:

| Attribute value | 'overflow' value |
| --- | --- |
| `on` | 'scroll' |
| `scroll` | 'scroll' |
| `yes` | 'scroll' |
| `off` | 'hidden' |
| `noscroll` | 'hidden' |
| `no` | 'hidden' |
| `auto` | 'auto' |

* * *

When a [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element has a [`background`](#355.html_attr-background) attribute set to a non-empty value, the new value is expected to be [resolved](#355.html_resolve-a-url) relative to the element, and if this is successful, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#355.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'background-image' property to the resulting [absolute URL](#355.html_absolute-url).

When a [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element has a [`bgcolor`](#355.html_attr-body-bgcolor) attribute set, the new value is expected to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#355.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value), and if that does not return an error, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#355.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'background-color' property to the resulting color.

When a [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element has a [`text`](#355.html_attr-body-text) attribute, its value is expected to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#355.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value), and if that does not return an error, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#355.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'color' property to the resulting color.

When a [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element has a [`link`](#355.html_attr-body-link) attribute, its value is expected to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#355.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value), and if that does not return an error, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#355.html_presentational-hints) setting the 'color' property of any element in the [`Document`](#355.html_document) matching the ':link' pseudo-class to the resulting color.

When a [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element has a [`vlink`](#355.html_attr-body-vlink) attribute, its value is expected to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#355.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value), and if that does not return an error, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#355.html_presentational-hints) setting the 'color' property of any element in the [`Document`](#355.html_document) matching the ':visited' pseudo-class to the resulting color.

When a [`body`](#355.html_the-body-element) element has an [`alink`](#355.html_attr-body-alink) attribute, its value is expected to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#355.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value), and if that does not return an error, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#355.html_presentational-hints) setting the 'color' property of any element in the [`Document`](#355.html_document) matching the ':active' pseudo-class and either the ':link' pseudo-class or the ':visited' pseudo-class to the resulting color.

#### 10.3.3 Flow content

```
[](#cb737-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb737-2)
[](#cb737-3)address, blockquote, center, div, figure, figcaption, footer, form,
[](#cb737-4)header, hr, legend, listing, p, plaintext, pre, xmp {
[](#cb737-5)  display: block;
[](#cb737-6)}
[](#cb737-7)
[](#cb737-8)blockquote, figure, listing, p, plaintext, pre, xmp {
[](#cb737-9)  margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em;
[](#cb737-10)}
[](#cb737-11)
[](#cb737-12)blockquote, figure { margin-left: 40px; margin-right: 40px; }
[](#cb737-13)
[](#cb737-14)address { font-style: italic; }
[](#cb737-15)listing, plaintext, pre, xmp {
[](#cb737-16)  font-family: monospace; white-space: pre;
[](#cb737-17)}
```

The following rules are also expected to apply, as [presentational hints](#356.html_presentational-hints):

```
[](#cb738-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb738-2)
[](#cb738-3)pre[wrap] { white-space: pre-wrap; }
```

In [quirks mode](#356.html_quirks-mode), the following rules are also expected to apply:

```
[](#cb739-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb739-2)
[](#cb739-3)form { margin-bottom: 1em; }
```

* * *

The [`center`](#356.html_center) element, and the [`div`](#356.html_the-div-element) element when it has an [`align`](#356.html_attr-div-align) attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#356.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for either the string "`center`" or the string "`middle`", are expected to center text within themselves, as if they had their 'text-align' property set to 'center' in a [presentational hint](#356.html_presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#356.html_align-descendants) to the center.

The [`div`](#356.html_the-div-element) element, when it has an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#356.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`left`", is expected to left-align text within itself, as if it had its 'text-align' property set to 'left' in a [presentational hint](#356.html_presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#356.html_align-descendants) to the left.

The [`div`](#356.html_the-div-element) element, when it has an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#356.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`right`", is expected to right-align text within itself, as if it had its 'text-align' property set to 'right' in a [presentational hint](#356.html_presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#356.html_align-descendants) to the right.

The [`div`](#356.html_the-div-element) element, when it has an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#356.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`justify`", is expected to full-justify text within itself, as if it had its 'text-align' property set to 'justify' in a [presentational hint](#356.html_presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#356.html_align-descendants) to the left.

The following rules are also expected to apply, as [presentational hints](#357.html_presentational-hints):

```
[](#cb741-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb741-2)
[](#cb741-3)br[clear=left i] { clear: left; }

```

User agents that do not support correct ruby rendering are expected to render parentheses around the text of [`rt`](#357.html_the-rt-element) elements in the absence of [`rp`](#357.html_the-rp-element) elements. [[CSSRUBY]](#357.html_refsCSSRUBY)

* * *

User agents are expected to support the 'clear' property on inline elements (in order to render [`br`](#357.html_the-br-element) elements with [`clear`](#357.html_attr-br-clear) attributes) in the manner described in the non-normative note to this effect in CSS2.1.

The initial value for the 'color' property is expected to be black. The initial value for the 'background-color' property is expected to be 'transparent'. The canvas' background is expected to be white.

* * *

When a [`font`](#357.html_font) element has a `color` attribute, its value is expected to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#357.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value), and if that does not return an error, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#357.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'color' property to the resulting color.

When a [`font`](#357.html_font) element has a `face` attribute, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#357.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'font-family' property to the attribute's value.

When a [`font`](#357.html_font) element has a `size` attribute, the user agent is expected to use the following steps, known as the <dfn id="357.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-font-size">rules for parsing a legacy font size</dfn>, to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#357.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'font-size' property:

1.  Let `input` be the attribute's value.

2.  Let `position` be a pointer into `input`, initially pointing at the start of the string.

3.  [Skip whitespace](#357.html_skip-whitespace).

4.  If `position` is past the end of `input`, there is no [presentational hint](#357.html_presentational-hints). Abort these steps.

5.  If the character at `position` is a "+" (U+002B) character, then let `mode` be *relative-plus*, and advance `position` to the next character. Otherwise, if the character at `position` is a "-" (U+002D) character, then let `mode` be *relative-minus*, and advance `position` to the next character. Otherwise, let `mode` be *absolute*.

6.  [Collect a sequence of characters](#357.html_collect-a-sequence-of-characters) that are [ASCII digits](#357.html_ascii-digits), and let the resulting sequence be `digits`.

7.  If `digits` is the empty string, there is no [presentational hint](#357.html_presentational-hints). Abort these steps.

8.  Interpret `digits` as a base-ten integer. Let `value` be the resulting number.

9.  If `mode` is *relative-plus*, then increment `value` by 3\. If `mode` is *relative-minus*, then let `value` be the result of subtracting `value` from 3.

10.  If `value` is greater than 7, let it be 7.

11.  If `value` is less than 1, let it be 1.

12.  Set 'font-size' to the keyword corresponding to the value of `value` according to the following table:

    | `value` | 'font-size' keyword | Notes |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | 1 | x-small |  |
    | 2 | small |  |
    | 3 | medium |  |
    | 4 | large |  |
    | 5 | x-large |  |
    | 6 | xx-large |  |
    | 7 | xxx-large | *see below* |

    The 'xxx-large' value is a non-CSS value used here to indicate a font size 50% larger than 'xx-large'.

[](#cb742-6)address, blockquote, center, div, figure, figcaption, footer, form,
[](#cb742-7)header, hr, legend, listing, p, plaintext, pre, xmp, article,

[](#cb742-9)colgroup, col, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, td, th, dir, dd, dl, dt,

Input fields (i.e. [`textarea`](#358.html_the-textarea-element) elements, and [`input`](#358.html_the-input-element) elements when their [`type`](#358.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Text](#358.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [Search](#358.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [Telephone](#358.html_telephone-state-(type=tel)), [URL](#358.html_url-state-(type=url)), or [E-mail](#358.html_e-mail-state-(type=email)) state) are expected to present an editing user interface with a directionality that matches the element's 'direction' property.

#### 10.3.7 Sections and headings

```
[](#cb744-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb744-2)
[](#cb744-3)article, aside, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, hgroup, nav, section {
[](#cb744-4)  display: block;
[](#cb744-5)}
[](#cb744-6)
[](#cb744-7)h1 { margin-top: 0.67em; margin-bottom: 0.67em; font-size: 2.00em; font-weight: bold; }
[](#cb744-8)h2 { margin-top: 0.83em; margin-bottom: 0.83em; font-size: 1.50em; font-weight: bold; }
[](#cb744-9)h3 { margin-top: 1.00em; margin-bottom: 1.00em; font-size: 1.17em; font-weight: bold; }
[](#cb744-10)h4 { margin-top: 1.33em; margin-bottom: 1.33em; font-size: 1.00em; font-weight: bold; }
[](#cb744-11)h5 { margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em; font-size: 0.83em; font-weight: bold; }
[](#cb744-12)h6 { margin-top: 2.33em; margin-bottom: 2.33em; font-size: 0.67em; font-weight: bold; }
```

The [`article`](#360.html_the-article-element), [`aside`](#360.html_the-aside-element), [`nav`](#360.html_the-nav-element), and [`section`](#360.html_the-section-element) elements are expected to affect the margins and font size of [`h1`](#360.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) elements, as well as [`h2`](#360.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)–[`h5`](#360.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) elements that follow [`h1`](#360.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) elements in [`hgroup`](#360.html_hgroup) elements, based on the nesting depth. If `x` is a selector that matches elements that are either [`article`](#360.html_the-article-element), [`aside`](#360.html_the-aside-element), [`nav`](#360.html_the-nav-element), or [`section`](#360.html_the-section-element) elements, then the following rules capture what is expected:

```
[](#cb745-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb745-2)
[](#cb745-3)x h1 { margin-top: 0.83em; margin-bottom: 0.83em; font-size: 1.50em; }
[](#cb745-4)x x h1 { margin-top: 1.00em; margin-bottom: 1.00em; font-size: 1.17em; }
[](#cb745-5)x x x h1 { margin-top: 1.33em; margin-bottom: 1.33em; font-size: 1.00em; }
[](#cb745-6)x x x x h1 { margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em; font-size: 0.83em; }
[](#cb745-7)x x x x x h1 { margin-top: 2.33em; margin-bottom: 2.33em; font-size: 0.67em; }
[](#cb745-8)
[](#cb745-9)x hgroup > h1 ~ h2 { margin-top: 1.00em; margin-bottom: 1.00em; font-size: 1.17em; }
[](#cb745-10)x x hgroup > h1 ~ h2 { margin-top: 1.33em; margin-bottom: 1.33em; font-size: 1.00em; }
[](#cb745-11)x x x hgroup > h1 ~ h2 { margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em; font-size: 0.83em; }
[](#cb745-12)x x x x hgroup > h1 ~ h2 { margin-top: 2.33em; margin-bottom: 2.33em; font-size: 0.67em; }
[](#cb745-13)
[](#cb745-14)x hgroup > h1 ~ h3 { margin-top: 1.33em; margin-bottom: 1.33em; font-size: 1.00em; }
[](#cb745-15)x x hgroup > h1 ~ h3 { margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em; font-size: 0.83em; }
[](#cb745-16)x x x hgroup > h1 ~ h3 { margin-top: 2.33em; margin-bottom: 2.33em; font-size: 0.67em; }
[](#cb745-17)
[](#cb745-18)x hgroup > h1 ~ h4 { margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em; font-size: 0.83em; }
[](#cb745-19)x x hgroup > h1 ~ h4 { margin-top: 2.33em; margin-bottom: 2.33em; font-size: 0.67em; }
[](#cb745-20)
[](#cb745-21)x hgroup > h1 ~ h5 { margin-top: 2.33em; margin-bottom: 2.33em; font-size: 0.67em; }
```

#### 10.3.8 Lists

```
[](#cb746-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb746-2)
[](#cb746-3)dir, dd, dl, dt, ol, ul { display: block; }
[](#cb746-4)li { display: list-item; }
[](#cb746-5)

[](#cb746-7)

[](#cb746-12)  margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0;
[](#cb746-13)}
[](#cb746-14)

[](#cb746-16)dir, ol, ul { padding-left: 40px; } /* LTR-specific: use 'padding-right' for rtl elements */
[](#cb746-17)
[](#cb746-18)ol { list-style-type: decimal; }
[](#cb746-19)
[](#cb746-20)dir, ul { list-style-type: disc; }
[](#cb746-21)
[](#cb746-22)dir dir, dir ul,
[](#cb746-23)ol dir, ol ul,
[](#cb746-24)ul dir, ul ul {
[](#cb746-25)  list-style-type: circle;
[](#cb746-26)}
[](#cb746-27)
[](#cb746-28)dir dir dir, dir dir ul,
[](#cb746-29)dir ol dir, dir ol ul,
[](#cb746-30)dir ul dir, dir ul ul,
[](#cb746-31)ol dir dir, ol dir ul,
[](#cb746-32)ol ol dir, ol ol ul,
[](#cb746-33)ol ul dir, ol ul ul,
[](#cb746-34)ul dir dir, ul dir ul,
[](#cb746-35)ul ol dir, ul ol ul,
[](#cb746-36)ul ul dir, ul ul ul {
[](#cb746-37)  list-style-type: square;
[](#cb746-38)}
```

The following rules are also expected to apply, as [presentational hints](#361.html_presentational-hints):

```
[](#cb747-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb747-2)
[](#cb747-3)ol[type=1], li[type=1] { list-style-type: decimal; }
[](#cb747-4)ol[type=a], li[type=a] { list-style-type: lower-alpha; }
[](#cb747-5)ol[type=A], li[type=A] { list-style-type: upper-alpha; }
[](#cb747-6)ol[type=i], li[type=i] { list-style-type: lower-roman; }
[](#cb747-7)ol[type=I], li[type=I] { list-style-type: upper-roman; }
[](#cb747-8)ul[type=disc i], li[type=disc i] { list-style-type: disc; }
[](#cb747-9)ul[type=circle i], li[type=circle i] { list-style-type: circle; }
[](#cb747-10)ul[type=square i], li[type=square i] { list-style-type: square; }
```

When rendering [`li`](#361.html_the-li-element) elements, non-CSS user agents are expected to use the [ordinal value](#361.html_ordinal-value) of the [`li`](#361.html_the-li-element) element to render the counter in the list item marker.

This specification does not yet define the CSS-specific rules for rendering [`li`](#361.html_the-li-element) elements, because CSS doesn't yet provide sufficient hooks for this purpose.

In [quirks mode](#362.html_quirks-mode), the following rules are also expected to apply:

```
[](#cb750-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb750-2)
[](#cb750-3)table {
[](#cb750-4)  font-weight: initial;
[](#cb750-5)  font-style: initial;

[](#cb750-8)  line-height: initial;

[](#cb750-10)  text-align: initial;
[](#cb750-11)}
```

* * *

For the purposes of the CSS table model, the [`col`](#362.html_the-col-element) element is expected to be treated as if it was present as many times as its [`span`](#362.html_attr-col-span) attribute [specifies](#362.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers).

For the purposes of the CSS table model, the [`colgroup`](#362.html_the-colgroup-element) element, if it contains no [`col`](#362.html_the-col-element) element, is expected to be treated as if it had as many such children as its [`span`](#362.html_attr-colgroup-span) attribute [specifies](#362.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers).

For the purposes of the CSS table model, the [`colspan`](#362.html_attr-tdth-colspan) and [`rowspan`](#362.html_attr-tdth-rowspan) attributes on [`td`](#362.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) elements are expected to [provide](#362.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) the *special knowledge* regarding cells spanning rows and columns.

In [HTML documents](#362.html_html-documents), the user agent is expected to force the 'display' property of [`form`](#362.html_the-form-element) elements that are children of [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element), [`thead`](#362.html_the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#362.html_the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#362.html_the-tfoot-element), or [`tr`](#362.html_the-tr-element) elements to compute to 'none', irrespective of CSS rules.

* * *

The [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element's [`cellspacing`](#362.html_attr-table-cellspacing) attribute [maps to the pixel length property](#362.html_maps-to-the-pixel-length-property) 'border-spacing' on the element.

The [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element's [`cellpadding`](#362.html_attr-table-cellpadding) attribute [maps to the pixel length properties](#362.html_maps-to-the-pixel-length-property) 'padding-top', 'padding-right', 'padding-bottom', and 'padding-left' of any [`td`](#362.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) elements that have corresponding [cells](#362.html_concept-cell) in the [table](#362.html_concept-table) corresponding to the [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element.

The [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element's `hspace` attribute [maps to the dimension properties](#362.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'margin-left' and 'margin-right' on the [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element.

The [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element's `vspace` attribute [maps to the dimension properties](#362.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'margin-top' and 'margin-bottom' on the [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element.

The [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element's `height` attribute [maps to the dimension property](#362.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'height' on the [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element.

The [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element's [`width`](#362.html_attr-table-width) attribute [maps to the dimension property](#362.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'width' on the [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element.

The [`col`](#362.html_the-col-element) element's [`width`](#362.html_attr-col-width) attribute [maps to the dimension property](#362.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'width' on the [`col`](#362.html_the-col-element) element.

The [`tr`](#362.html_the-tr-element) element's `height` attribute [maps to the dimension property](#362.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'height' on the [`tr`](#362.html_the-tr-element) element.

The [`td`](#362.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) elements' [`height`](#362.html_attr-tdth-height) attributes [map to the dimension property](#362.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'height' on the element.

The [`td`](#362.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) elements' [`width`](#362.html_attr-tdth-width) attributes [map to the dimension property](#362.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'width' on the element.

* * *

The [`caption`](#362.html_the-caption-element) element unless specified otherwise below, and the [`thead`](#362.html_the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#362.html_the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#362.html_the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#362.html_the-tr-element), [`td`](#362.html_the-td-element), and [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) elements when they have an [`align`](#362.html_attr-div-align) attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#362.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for either the string "`center`" or the string "`middle`", are expected to center text within themselves, as if they had their 'text-align' property set to 'center' in a [presentational hint](#362.html_presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#362.html_align-descendants) to the center.

The [`caption`](#362.html_the-caption-element), [`thead`](#362.html_the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#362.html_the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#362.html_the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#362.html_the-tr-element), [`td`](#362.html_the-td-element), and [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) elements, when they have an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#362.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`left`", are expected to left-align text within themselves, as if they had their 'text-align' property set to 'left' in a [presentational hint](#362.html_presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#362.html_align-descendants) to the left.

The [`caption`](#362.html_the-caption-element), [`thead`](#362.html_the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#362.html_the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#362.html_the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#362.html_the-tr-element), [`td`](#362.html_the-td-element), and [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) elements, when they have an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#362.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`right`", are expected to right-align text within themselves, as if they had their 'text-align' property set to 'right' in a [presentational hint](#362.html_presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#362.html_align-descendants) to the right.

The [`caption`](#362.html_the-caption-element), [`thead`](#362.html_the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#362.html_the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#362.html_the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#362.html_the-tr-element), [`td`](#362.html_the-td-element), and [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) elements, when they have an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#362.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`justify`", are expected to full-justify text within themselves, as if they had their 'text-align' property set to 'justify' in a [presentational hint](#362.html_presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#362.html_align-descendants) to the left.

User agents are expected to have a rule in their user agent stylesheet that matches [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) elements that have a parent node whose computed value for the 'text-align' property is its initial value, whose declaration block consists of just a single declaration that sets the 'text-align' property to the value 'center'.

* * *

When a [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element), [`thead`](#362.html_the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#362.html_the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#362.html_the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#362.html_the-tr-element), [`td`](#362.html_the-td-element), or [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) element has a [`background`](#362.html_attr-background) attribute set to a non-empty value, the new value is expected to be [resolved](#362.html_resolve-a-url) relative to the element, and if this is successful, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#362.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'background-image' property to the resulting [absolute URL](#362.html_absolute-url).

When a [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element), [`thead`](#362.html_the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#362.html_the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#362.html_the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#362.html_the-tr-element), [`td`](#362.html_the-td-element), or [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) element has a `bgcolor` attribute set, the new value is expected to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#362.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value), and if that does not return an error, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#362.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'background-color' property to the resulting color.

When a [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element has a [`bordercolor`](#362.html_attr-table-bordercolor) attribute, its value is expected to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#362.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value), and if that does not return an error, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#362.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'border-top-color', 'border-right-color', 'border-bottom-color', and 'border-right-color' properties to the resulting color.

* * *

The [`table`](#362.html_the-table-element) element's [`border`](#362.html_attr-table-border) attribute [maps to the pixel length properties](#362.html_maps-to-the-pixel-length-property) 'border-top-width', 'border-right-width', 'border-bottom-width', 'border-left-width' on the element. If the attribute is present but parsing the attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#362.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) generates an error, a default value of 1px is expected to be used for that property instead.

Rules marked "<dfn id="362.html_magic-border-selector">only if border is not equivalent to zero</dfn>" in the CSS block above is expected to only be applied if the [`border`](#362.html_attr-table-border) attribute mentioned in the selectors for the rule is not only present but, when parsed using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#362.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers), is also found to have a value other than zero or to generate an error.

* * *

In [quirks mode](#362.html_quirks-mode), a [`td`](#362.html_the-td-element) element or a [`th`](#362.html_the-th-element) element that has a [`nowrap`](#362.html_attr-tdth-nowrap) attribute but also has a [`width`](#362.html_attr-tdth-width) attribute whose value, when parsed using the [rules for parsing dimension values](#362.html_rules-for-parsing-dimension-values), is found to be a length (not an error or a number classified as a percentage), is expected to have a [presentational hint](#362.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'white-space' property to 'normal', overriding the rule in the CSS block above that sets it to 'nowrap'.

#### 10.3.10 Margin collapsing quirks

A node is <dfn id="363.html_concept-rendering-substantial" data-anolis-xref="concept-rendering-substantial">substantial</dfn> if it is a text node that is not [inter-element whitespace](#363.html_inter-element-whitespace), or if it is an element node.

A node is <dfn id="363.html_concept-rendering-blank" data-anolis-xref="concept-rendering-blank">blank</dfn> if it is an element that contains no [substantial](#363.html_concept-rendering-substantial) nodes.

The <dfn id="363.html_concept-rendering-elements-with-margins" data-anolis-xref="concept-rendering-elements-with-margins">elements with default margins</dfn> are the following elements: [`blockquote`](#363.html_the-blockquote-element), [`dir`](#363.html_dir), [`dl`](#363.html_the-dl-element), [`h1`](#363.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`h2`](#363.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`h3`](#363.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`h4`](#363.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`h5`](#363.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`h6`](#363.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements), [`listing`](#363.html_listing), [`multicol`](#363.html_multicol), [`ol`](#363.html_the-ol-element), [`p`](#363.html_the-p-element), [`plaintext`](#363.html_plaintext), [`pre`](#363.html_the-pre-element), [`ul`](#363.html_the-ul-element), [`xmp`](#363.html_xmp)

In [quirks mode](#363.html_quirks-mode), any [element with default margins](#363.html_concept-rendering-elements-with-margins) that is the child of a [`body`](#363.html_the-body-element), [`td`](#363.html_the-td-element), or [`th`](#363.html_the-th-element) element and has no [substantial](#363.html_concept-rendering-substantial) previous siblings is expected to have a user-agent level style sheet rule that sets its 'margin-top' property to zero.

In [quirks mode](#363.html_quirks-mode), any [element with default margins](#363.html_concept-rendering-elements-with-margins) that is the child of a [`body`](#363.html_the-body-element), [`td`](#363.html_the-td-element), or [`th`](#363.html_the-th-element) element, has no [substantial](#363.html_concept-rendering-substantial) previous siblings, and is [blank](#363.html_concept-rendering-blank), is expected to have a user-agent level style sheet rule that sets its 'margin-bottom' property to zero also.

In [quirks mode](#363.html_quirks-mode), any [element with default margins](#363.html_concept-rendering-elements-with-margins) that is the child of a [`td`](#363.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#363.html_the-th-element) element, has no [substantial](#363.html_concept-rendering-substantial) following siblings, and is [blank](#363.html_concept-rendering-blank), is expected to have a user-agent level style sheet rule that sets its 'margin-top' property to zero.

In [quirks mode](#363.html_quirks-mode), any [`p`](#363.html_the-p-element) element that is the child of a [`td`](#363.html_the-td-element) or [`th`](#363.html_the-th-element) element and has no [substantial](#363.html_concept-rendering-substantial) following siblings, is expected to have a user-agent level style sheet rule that sets its 'margin-bottom' property to zero.

#### 10.3.11 Form controls

```
[](#cb751-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb751-2)
[](#cb751-3)input, select, option, optgroup, button, textarea, keygen {
[](#cb751-4)  text-indent: initial;
[](#cb751-5)}
[](#cb751-6)
[](#cb751-7)textarea { white-space: pre-wrap; }
[](#cb751-8)
[](#cb751-9)input[type="radio"], input[type="checkbox"], input[type="reset"], input[type="button"],
[](#cb751-10)input[type="submit"], select, button {
[](#cb751-11)  box-sizing: border-box;
[](#cb751-12)}
```

In [quirks mode](#364.html_quirks-mode), the following rules are also expected to apply:

```
[](#cb752-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb752-2)
[](#cb752-3)input:not([type=image]), textarea { box-sizing: border-box; }
```

Each kind of form control is also given a specific default binding, as described in subsequent sections, which implements the look and feel of the control.

#### 10.3.12 The [`hr`](#365.html_the-hr-element) element

```
[](#cb753-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb753-2)
[](#cb753-3)hr { color: gray; border-style: inset; border-width: 1px; margin: 0.5em auto; }
```

The following rules are also expected to apply, as [presentational hints](#365.html_presentational-hints):

```
[](#cb754-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb754-2)
[](#cb754-3)hr[align=left] { margin-left: 0; margin-right: auto; }
[](#cb754-4)hr[align=right] { margin-left: auto; margin-right: 0; }
[](#cb754-5)hr[align=center] { margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; }
[](#cb754-6)hr[color], hr[noshade] { border-style: solid; }
```

If an [`hr`](#365.html_the-hr-element) element has either a [`color`](#365.html_attr-hr-color) attribute or a [`noshade`](#365.html_attr-hr-noshade) attribute, and furthermore also has a [`size`](#365.html_attr-hr-size) attribute, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#365.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) doesn't generate an error, then the user agent is expected to use the parsed value divided by two as a pixel length for [presentational hints](#365.html_presentational-hints) for the properties 'border-top-width', 'border-right-width', 'border-bottom-width', and 'border-left-width' on the element.

Otherwise, if an [`hr`](#365.html_the-hr-element) element has neither a [`color`](#365.html_attr-hr-color) attribute nor a [`noshade`](#365.html_attr-hr-noshade) attribute, but does have a [`size`](#365.html_attr-hr-size) attribute, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#365.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) doesn't generate an error, then: if the parsed value is one, then the user agent is expected to use the attribute as a [presentational hint](#365.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'border-bottom-width' to 0; otherwise, if the parsed value is greater than one, then the user agent is expected to use the parsed value minus two as a pixel length for [presentational hints](#365.html_presentational-hints) for the 'height' property on the element.

The [`width`](#365.html_attr-hr-width) attribute on an [`hr`](#365.html_the-hr-element) element [maps to the dimension property](#365.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'width' on the element.

When an [`hr`](#365.html_the-hr-element) element has a [`color`](#365.html_attr-hr-color) attribute, its value is expected to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#365.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value), and if that does not return an error, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#365.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'color' property to the resulting color.

#### 10.3.13 The [`fieldset`](#366.html_the-fieldset-element) and [`legend`](#366.html_the-legend-element) elements

```
[](#cb755-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb755-2)
[](#cb755-3)fieldset {
[](#cb755-4)  margin-left: 2px; margin-right: 2px;
[](#cb755-5)  border: groove 2px ThreeDFace;
[](#cb755-6)  padding: 0.35em 0.625em 0.75em;
[](#cb755-7)}
[](#cb755-8)
[](#cb755-9)legend {
[](#cb755-10)  padding-left: 2px; padding-right: 2px;
[](#cb755-11)}
```

The [`fieldset`](#366.html_the-fieldset-element) element is expected to establish a new block formatting context.

If the [`fieldset`](#366.html_the-fieldset-element) element has a child that matches the conditions in the list below, then the first such child is the [`fieldset`](#366.html_the-fieldset-element) element's <dfn id="366.html_rendered-legend">rendered legend</dfn>:

*   The child is a [`legend`](#366.html_the-legend-element) element.
*   The child is not out-of-flow (e.g. not absolutely positioned or floated).
*   The child is generating a box (e.g. it is not 'display:none').

A [`fieldset`](#366.html_the-fieldset-element) element's [rendered legend](#366.html_rendered-legend), if any, is expected to be rendered over the top border edge of the [`fieldset`](#366.html_the-fieldset-element) element as a 'block' box (overriding any explicit 'display' value). In the absence of an explicit width, the box should shrink-wrap. If the [`legend`](#366.html_the-legend-element) element in question has an [`align`](#366.html_attr-legend-align) attribute, and its value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#366.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for one of the strings in the first column of the following table, then the [`legend`](#366.html_the-legend-element) is expected to be rendered horizontally aligned over the border edge in the position given in the corresponding cell on the same row in the second column. If the attribute is absent or has a value that doesn't match any of the cases in the table, then the position is expected to be on the right if the 'direction' property on this element has a computed value of 'rtl', and on the left otherwise.

| Attribute value | Alignment position |
| --- | --- |
| `left` | On the left |
| `right` | On the right |
| `center` | In the middle |

### 10.4 Replaced elements

#### 10.4.1 Embedded content

The [`embed`](#368.html_the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#368.html_the-iframe-element), and [`video`](#368.html_the-video-element) elements are expected to be treated as replaced elements.

A [`canvas`](#368.html_the-canvas-element) element that [represents](#368.html_represents) [embedded content](#368.html_embedded-content-2) is expected to be treated as a replaced element; the contents of such elements are the element's bitmap, if any, or else a transparent black bitmap with the same intrinsic dimensions as the element. Other [`canvas`](#368.html_the-canvas-element) elements are expected to be treated as ordinary elements in the rendering model.

An [`object`](#368.html_the-object-element) element that [represents](#368.html_represents) an image, plugin, or [nested browsing context](#368.html_nested-browsing-context) is expected to be treated as a replaced element. Other [`object`](#368.html_the-object-element) elements are expected to be treated as ordinary elements in the rendering model.

An [`applet`](#368.html_the-applet-element) element that [represents](#368.html_represents) a [plugin](#368.html_plugin) is expected to be treated as a replaced element. Other [`applet`](#368.html_the-applet-element) elements are expected to be treated as ordinary elements in the rendering model.

The [`audio`](#368.html_the-audio-element) element, when it is [exposing a user interface](#368.html_expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user), is expected to be treated as a replaced element about one line high, as wide as is necessary to expose the user agent's user interface features. When an [`audio`](#368.html_the-audio-element) element is not [exposing a user interface](#368.html_expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user), the user agent is expected to force its 'display' property to compute to 'none', irrespective of CSS rules.

Whether a [`video`](#368.html_the-video-element) element is [exposing a user interface](#368.html_expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user) is not expected to affect the size of the rendering; controls are expected to be overlaid above the page content without causing any layout changes, and are expected to disappear when the user does not need them.

When a [`video`](#368.html_the-video-element) element represents a poster frame or frame of video, the poster frame or frame of video is expected to be rendered at the largest size that maintains the aspect ratio of that poster frame or frame of video without being taller or wider than the [`video`](#368.html_the-video-element) element itself, and is expected to be centered in the [`video`](#368.html_the-video-element) element.

Any subtitles or captions are expected to be overlayed directly on top of their [`video`](#368.html_the-video-element) element, as defined by the relevant rendering rules; for [WebVTT](#368.html_webvtt), those are the [rules for updating the display of WebVTT text tracks](#368.html_rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks). [[WEBVTT]](#368.html_refsWEBVTT)

When the user agent starts [exposing a user interface](#368.html_expose-a-user-interface-to-the-user) for a [`video`](#368.html_the-video-element) element, the user agent should run the [rules for updating the text track rendering](#368.html_rules-for-updating-the-text-track-rendering) of each of the [text tracks](#368.html_text-track) in the [`video`](#368.html_the-video-element) element's [list of text tracks](#368.html_list-of-text-tracks) that are [showing](#368.html_text-track-showing) and whose [text track kind](#368.html_text-track-kind) is one of [`subtitles`](#368.html_dom-texttrack-kind-subtitles) or [`captions`](#368.html_dom-texttrack-kind-captions) (e.g., for [text tracks](#368.html_text-track) based on [WebVTT](#368.html_webvtt), the [rules for updating the display of WebVTT text tracks](#368.html_rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks)). [[WEBVTT]](#368.html_refsWEBVTT)

Resizing [`video`](#368.html_the-video-element) and [`canvas`](#368.html_the-canvas-element) elements does not interrupt video playback or clear the canvas.

* * *

The following CSS rules are expected to apply:

```
[](#cb756-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb756-2)
[](#cb756-3)iframe { border: 2px inset; }
[](#cb756-4)video { object-fit: contain; }
```

#### 10.4.2 Images

User agents are expected to render [`img`](#369.html_the-img-element) elements and [`input`](#369.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#369.html_attr-input-type) attributes are in the [Image Button](#369.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, according to the first applicable rules from the following list:

If the element [represents](#369.html_represents) an image

The user agent is expected to treat the element as a replaced element and render the image according to the rules for doing so defined in CSS.

If the element does not [represent](#369.html_represents) an image, but the element already has intrinsic dimensions (e.g. from the [dimension attributes](#369.html_dimension-attributes) or CSS rules), and either:

*   the user agent has reason to believe that the image will become *[available](#369.html_img-available)* and be rendered in due course, or
*   the element has no `alt` attribute, or
*   the [`Document`](#369.html_document) is in [quirks mode](#369.html_quirks-mode)

The user agent is expected to treat the element as a replaced element whose content is the text that the element represents, if any, optionally alongside an icon indicating that the image is being obtained (if applicable). For [`input`](#369.html_the-input-element) elements, the element is expected to appear button-like to indicate that the element is a [button](#369.html_concept-button).

If the element is an [`img`](#369.html_the-img-element) element that [represents](#369.html_represents) some text and the user agent does not expect this to change

The user agent is expected to treat the element as a non-replaced phrasing element whose content is the text, optionally with an icon indicating that an image is missing, so that the user can request the image be displayed or investigate why it is not rendering. In non-graphical contexts, such an icon should be omitted.

If the element is an [`img`](#369.html_the-img-element) element that [represents](#369.html_represents) nothing and the user agent does not expect this to change

The user agent is expected to treat the element as an empty inline element. (In the absence of further styles, this will cause the element to essentially not be rendered.)

If the element is an [`input`](#369.html_the-input-element) element that does not [represent](#369.html_represents) an image and the user agent does not expect this to change

The user agent is expected to treat the element as a replaced element consisting of a button whose content is the element's alternative text. The intrinsic dimensions of the button are expected to be about one line in height and whatever width is necessary to render the text on one line.

The icons mentioned above are expected to be relatively small so as not to disrupt most text but be easily clickable. In a visual environment, for instance, icons could be 16 pixels by 16 pixels square, or 1em by 1em if the images are scalable. In an audio environment, the icon could be a short bleep. The icons are intended to indicate to the user that they can be used to get to whatever options the UA provides for images, and, where appropriate, are expected to provide access to the context menu that would have come up if the user interacted with the actual image.

* * *

All animated images with the same [absolute URL](#369.html_absolute-url) and the same image data are expected to be rendered synchronized to the same timeline as a group, with the timeline starting at the time of the most recent addition to the group.

In other words, the animation loop of an animated image is restarted each time another image with the same [absolute URL](#369.html_absolute-url) and image data begins to animate, e.g. after being inserted into the document.

* * *

The following CSS rules are expected to apply when the [`Document`](#369.html_document) is in [quirks mode](#369.html_quirks-mode):

```
[](#cb757-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb757-2)
[](#cb757-3)img[align=left i] { margin-right: 3px; }
[](#cb757-4)img[align=right i] { margin-left: 3px; }
```

#### 10.4.3 Attributes for embedded content and images

The following CSS rules are expected to apply as [presentational hints](#370.html_presentational-hints):

```
[](#cb758-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb758-2)
[](#cb758-3)iframe[frameborder=0], iframe[frameborder=no i] { border: none; }
[](#cb758-4)
[](#cb758-5)applet[align=left i], embed[align=left i], iframe[align=left i],
[](#cb758-6)img[align=left i], input[type=image i][align=left i], object[align=left i] {
[](#cb758-7)  float: left;
[](#cb758-8)}
[](#cb758-9)
[](#cb758-10)applet[align=right i], embed[align=right i], iframe[align=right i],
[](#cb758-11)img[align=right i], input[type=image i][align=right i], object[align=right i] {
[](#cb758-12)  float: right;
[](#cb758-13)}
[](#cb758-14)
[](#cb758-15)applet[align=top i], embed[align=top i], iframe[align=top i],
[](#cb758-16)img[align=top i], input[type=image i][align=top i], object[align=top i] {
[](#cb758-17)  vertical-align: top;
[](#cb758-18)}
[](#cb758-19)
[](#cb758-20)applet[align=baseline i], embed[align=baseline i], iframe[align=baseline i],
[](#cb758-21)img[align=baseline i], input[type=image i][align=baseline i], object[align=baseline i] {
[](#cb758-22)  vertical-align: baseline;
[](#cb758-23)}
[](#cb758-24)
[](#cb758-25)applet[align=texttop i], embed[align=texttop i], iframe[align=texttop i],
[](#cb758-26)img[align=texttop i], input[type=image i][align=texttop i], object[align=texttop i] {
[](#cb758-27)  vertical-align: text-top;
[](#cb758-28)}
[](#cb758-29)
[](#cb758-30)applet[align=absmiddle i], embed[align=absmiddle i], iframe[align=absmiddle i],
[](#cb758-31)img[align=absmiddle i], input[type=image i][align=absmiddle i], object[align=absmiddle i],
[](#cb758-32)applet[align=abscenter i], embed[align=abscenter i], iframe[align=abscenter i],
[](#cb758-33)img[align=abscenter i], input[type=image i][align=abscenter i], object[align=abscenter i] {
[](#cb758-34)  vertical-align: middle;
[](#cb758-35)}
[](#cb758-36)
[](#cb758-37)applet[align=bottom i], embed[align=bottom i], iframe[align=bottom i],
[](#cb758-38)img[align=bottom i], input[type=image i][align=bottom i],
[](#cb758-39)object[align=bottom i] {
[](#cb758-40)  vertical-align: bottom;
[](#cb758-41)}
```

When an [`applet`](#370.html_the-applet-element), [`embed`](#370.html_the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#370.html_the-iframe-element), [`img`](#370.html_the-img-element), or [`object`](#370.html_the-object-element) element, or an [`input`](#370.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#370.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Image Button](#370.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, has an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#370.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`center`" or the string "`middle`", the user agent is expected to act as if the element's 'vertical-align' property was set to a value that aligns the vertical middle of the element with the parent element's baseline.

The `hspace` attribute of [`applet`](#370.html_the-applet-element), [`embed`](#370.html_the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#370.html_the-iframe-element), [`img`](#370.html_the-img-element), or [`object`](#370.html_the-object-element) elements, and [`input`](#370.html_the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#370.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Image Button](#370.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, [maps to the dimension properties](#370.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'margin-left' and 'margin-right' on the element.

The `vspace` attribute of [`applet`](#370.html_the-applet-element), [`embed`](#370.html_the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#370.html_the-iframe-element), [`img`](#370.html_the-img-element), or [`object`](#370.html_the-object-element) elements, and [`input`](#370.html_the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#370.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Image Button](#370.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state, [maps to the dimension properties](#370.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'margin-top' and 'margin-bottom' on the element.

When an [`img`](#370.html_the-img-element) element, [`object`](#370.html_the-object-element) element, or [`input`](#370.html_the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#370.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Image Button](#370.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state has a `border` attribute whose value, when parsed using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#370.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers), is found to be a number greater than zero, the user agent is expected to use the parsed value for eight [presentational hints](#370.html_presentational-hints): four setting the parsed value as a pixel length for the element's 'border-top-width', 'border-right-width', 'border-bottom-width', and 'border-left-width' properties, and four setting the element's 'border-top-style', 'border-right-style', 'border-bottom-style', and 'border-left-style' properties to the value 'solid'.

The [`width`](#370.html_attr-dim-width) and [`height`](#370.html_attr-dim-height) attributes on [`applet`](#370.html_the-applet-element), [`embed`](#370.html_the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#370.html_the-iframe-element), [`object`](#370.html_the-object-element) or [`video`](#370.html_the-video-element) elements, and [`input`](#370.html_the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#370.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Image Button](#370.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state and that either represents an image or that the user expects will eventually represent an image, [map to the dimension properties](#370.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'width' and 'height' on the element respectively.

#### 10.4.4 Image maps

Shapes on an [image map](#371.html_image-map) are expected to act, for the purpose of the CSS cascade, as elements independent of the original [`area`](#371.html_the-area-element) element that happen to match the same style rules but inherit from the [`img`](#371.html_the-img-element) or [`object`](#371.html_the-object-element) element.

For the purposes of the rendering, only the 'cursor' property is expected to have any effect on the shape.

Thus, for example, if an [`area`](#371.html_the-area-element) element has a [`style`](#371.html_the-style-attribute) attribute that sets the 'cursor' property to 'help', then when the user designates that shape, the cursor would change to a Help cursor.

Similarly, if an [`area`](#371.html_the-area-element) element had a CSS rule that set its 'cursor' property to 'inherit' (or if no rule setting the 'cursor' property matched the element at all), the shape's cursor would be inherited from the [`img`](#371.html_the-img-element) or [`object`](#371.html_the-object-element) element of the [image map](#371.html_image-map), not from the parent of the [`area`](#371.html_the-area-element) element.

### 10.5 Bindings

#### 10.5.1 Introduction

A number of elements have their rendering defined in terms of the 'binding' property. [[BECSS]](#373.html_refsBECSS)

The CSS snippets below set the 'binding' property to a user-agent-defined value, represented below by keywords like *`button`*. The rules then described for these bindings are only expected to apply if the element's 'binding' property has not been overridden (e.g. by the author) to have another value.

Exactly how the bindings are implemented is not specified by this specification. User agents are encouraged to make their bindings set the 'appearance' CSS property appropriately to achieve platform-native appearances for widgets, and are expected to implement any relevant animations, etc, that are appropriate for the platform. [[SELECTORS]](#373.html_refsSELECTORS)

#### 10.5.2 The [`button`](#374.html_the-button-element) element

```
[](#cb759-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb759-2)
[](#cb759-3)button { binding: button; }
```

When the *button* binding applies to a [`button`](#374.html_the-button-element) element, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box rendered as a button whose contents are the contents of the element.

#### 10.5.3 The [`input`](#375.html_the-input-element) element as a text entry widget

```
[](#cb760-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb760-2)
[](#cb760-3)input { binding: input-textfield; }
[](#cb760-4)input[type=password i] { binding: input-password; }
[](#cb760-5)/* later rules override this for other values of type="" */
```

When the *input-textfield* binding applies to an [`input`](#375.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#375.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Text](#375.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [Search](#375.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)), [Telephone](#375.html_telephone-state-(type=tel)), [URL](#375.html_url-state-(type=url)), or [E-mail](#375.html_e-mail-state-(type=email)) state, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box rendered as a text field.

When the *input-password* binding applies, to an [`input`](#375.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#375.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Password](#375.html_password-state-(type=password)) state, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box rendered as a text field whose contents are obscured.

If an [`input`](#375.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#375.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in one of the above states has a [`size`](#375.html_attr-input-size) attribute, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#375.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) doesn't generate an error, then the user agent is expected to use the attribute as a [presentational hint](#375.html_presentational-hints) for the 'width' property on the element, with the value obtained from applying the [converting a character width to pixels](#375.html_converting-a-character-width-to-pixels) algorithm to the value of the attribute.

If an [`input`](#375.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#375.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in one of the above states does *not* have a [`size`](#375.html_attr-input-size) attribute, then the user agent is expected to act as if it had a user-agent-level style sheet rule setting the 'width' property on the element to the value obtained from applying the [converting a character width to pixels](#375.html_converting-a-character-width-to-pixels) algorithm to the number 20.

The <dfn id="375.html_converting-a-character-width-to-pixels">converting a character width to pixels</dfn> algorithm returns (`size`-1)×`avg` + `max`, where `size` is the character width to convert, `avg` is the average character width of the primary font for the element for which the algorithm is being run, in pixels, and `max` is the maximum character width of that same font, also in pixels. (The element's 'letter-spacing' property does not affect the result.)

#### 10.5.4 The [`input`](#376.html_the-input-element) element as domain-specific widgets

```
[](#cb761-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb761-2)
[](#cb761-3)input[type=date i] { binding: input-date; }
[](#cb761-4)input[type=time i] { binding: input-time; }
[](#cb761-5)input[type=number i] { binding: input-number; }
```

When the *input-date* binding applies to an [`input`](#376.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#376.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Date](#376.html_date-state-(type=date)) state, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box depicting a Date control.

When the *input-time* binding applies to an [`input`](#376.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#376.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Time](#376.html_time-state-(type=time)) state, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box depicting a Time control.

When the *input-number* binding applies to an [`input`](#376.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#376.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Number](#376.html_number-state-(type=number)) state, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box depicting a Number control.

These controls are all expected to be about one line high, and about as wide as necessary to show the widest possible value.
