#### 10.5.5 The [`input`](#377.html_the-input-element) element as a range control

```
[](#cb762-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb762-2)
[](#cb762-3)input[type=range i] { binding: input-range; }
```

When the *input-range* binding applies to an [`input`](#377.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#377.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Range](#377.html_range-state-(type=range)) state, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box depicting a slider control.

When the control is wider than it is tall (or square), the control is expected to be a horizontal slider, with the lowest value on the right if the 'direction' property on this element has a computed value of 'rtl', and on the left otherwise. When the control is taller than it is wide, it is expected to be a vertical slider, with the lowest value on the bottom.

Predefined suggested values (provided by the [`list`](#377.html_attr-input-list) attribute) are expected to be shown as tick marks on the slider, which the slider can snap to.

User agents are expected to use the used value of the 'direction' property on the element to determine the direction in which the slider operates. Typically, a left-to-right ('ltr') horizontal control would have the lowest value on the left and the highest value on the right, and vice versa.

#### 10.5.6 The [`input`](#378.html_the-input-element) element as a color well

```
[](#cb763-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb763-2)
[](#cb763-3)input[type=color i] { binding: input-color; }
```

When the *input-color* binding applies to an [`input`](#378.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#378.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Color](#378.html_color-state-(type=color)) state, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box depicting a color well, which, when activated, provides the user with a color picker (e.g. a color wheel or color palette) from which the color can be changed.

Predefined suggested values (provided by the [`list`](#378.html_attr-input-list) attribute) are expected to be shown in the color picker interface, not on the color well itself.

#### 10.5.7 The [`input`](#379.html_the-input-element) element as a checkbox and radio button widgets

```
[](#cb764-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb764-2)
[](#cb764-3)input[type=checkbox i] { binding: input-checkbox; }
[](#cb764-4)input[type=radio i] { binding: input-radio; }
```

When the *input-checkbox* binding applies to an [`input`](#379.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#379.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Checkbox](#379.html_checkbox-state-(type=checkbox)) state, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box containing a single checkbox control, with no label.

When the *input-radio* binding applies to an [`input`](#379.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#379.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#379.html_radio-button-state-(type=radio)) state, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box containing a single radio button control, with no label.

#### 10.5.8 The [`input`](#380.html_the-input-element) element as a file upload control

```
[](#cb765-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb765-2)
[](#cb765-3)input[type=file i] { binding: input-file; }
```

When the *input-file* binding applies to an [`input`](#380.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#380.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [File Upload](#380.html_file-upload-state-(type=file)) state, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box containing a span of text giving the file name(s) of the [selected files](#380.html_concept-input-type-file-selected), if any, followed by a button that, when activated, provides the user with a file picker from which the selection can be changed.

#### 10.5.9 The [`input`](#381.html_the-input-element) element as a button

```
[](#cb766-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb766-2)
[](#cb766-3)input[type=submit i], input[type=reset i], input[type=button i] {
[](#cb766-4)  binding: input-button;
[](#cb766-5)}
```

When the *input-button* binding applies to an [`input`](#381.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#381.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Submit Button](#381.html_submit-button-state-(type=submit)), [Reset Button](#381.html_reset-button-state-(type=reset)), or [Button](#381.html_button-state-(type=button)) state, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box rendered as a button, about one line high, containing the contents of the element's [`value`](#381.html_attr-input-value) attribute, if any, or text derived from the element's [`type`](#381.html_attr-input-type) attribute in a user-agent-defined (and probably locale-specific) fashion, if not.

#### 10.5.10 The [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0) element

```
[](#cb767-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb767-2)
[](#cb767-3)marquee { binding: marquee; }
```

When the *marquee* binding applies to a [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0) element, while the element is [turned on](#382.html_concept-marquee-on), the element is expected to render in an animated fashion according to its attributes as follows:

If the element's [`behavior`](#382.html_attr-marquee-behavior) attribute is in the [scroll](#382.html_attr-marquee-behavior-scroll) state

Slide the contents of the element in the direction described by the [`direction`](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction) attribute as defined below, such that it begins off the start side of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0), and ends flush with the inner end side.

For example, if the [`direction`](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction) attribute is [left](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction-left) (the default), then the contents would start such that their left edge are off the side of the right edge of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0)'s content area, and the contents would then slide up to the point where the left edge of the contents are flush with the left inner edge of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0)'s content area.

Once the animation has ended, the user agent is expected to [increment the marquee current loop index](#382.html_increment-the-marquee-current-loop-index). If the element is still [turned on](#382.html_concept-marquee-on) after this, then the user agent is expected to restart the animation.

If the element's [`behavior`](#382.html_attr-marquee-behavior) attribute is in the [slide](#382.html_attr-marquee-behavior-slide) state

Slide the contents of the element in the direction described by the [`direction`](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction) attribute as defined below, such that it begins off the start side of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0), and ends off the end side of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0).

For example, if the [`direction`](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction) attribute is [left](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction-left) (the default), then the contents would start such that their left edge are off the side of the right edge of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0)'s content area, and the contents would then slide up to the point where the *right* edge of the contents are flush with the left inner edge of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0)'s content area.

Once the animation has ended, the user agent is expected to [increment the marquee current loop index](#382.html_increment-the-marquee-current-loop-index). If the element is still [turned on](#382.html_concept-marquee-on) after this, then the user agent is expected to restart the animation.

If the element's [`behavior`](#382.html_attr-marquee-behavior) attribute is in the [alternate](#382.html_attr-marquee-behavior-alternate) state

When the [marquee current loop index](#382.html_marquee-current-loop-index) is even (or zero), slide the contents of the element in the direction described by the [`direction`](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction) attribute as defined below, such that it begins flush with the start side of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0), and ends flush with the end side of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0).

When the [marquee current loop index](#382.html_marquee-current-loop-index) is odd, slide the contents of the element in the opposite direction than that described by the [`direction`](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction) attribute as defined below, such that it begins flush with the end side of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0), and ends flush with the start side of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0).

For example, if the [`direction`](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction) attribute is [left](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction-left) (the default), then the contents would with their right edge flush with the right inner edge of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0)'s content area, and the contents would then slide up to the point where the *left* edge of the contents are flush with the left inner edge of the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0)'s content area.

Once the animation has ended, the user agent is expected to [increment the marquee current loop index](#382.html_increment-the-marquee-current-loop-index). If the element is still [turned on](#382.html_concept-marquee-on) after this, then the user agent is expected to continue the animation.

The [`direction`](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction) attribute has the meanings described in the following table:

| [`direction`](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction) attribute state | Direction of animation | Start edge | End edge | Opposite direction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [left](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction-left) | ← Right to left | Right | Left | → Left to Right |
| [right](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction-right) | → Left to Right | Left | Right | ← Right to left |
| [up](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction-up) | ↑ Up (Bottom to Top) | Bottom | Top | ↓ Down (Top to Bottom) |
| [down](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction-down) | ↓ Down (Top to Bottom) | Top | Bottom | ↑ Up (Bottom to Top) |

In any case, the animation should proceed such that there is a delay given by the [marquee scroll interval](#382.html_marquee-scroll-interval) between each frame, and such that the content moves at most the distance given by the [marquee scroll distance](#382.html_marquee-scroll-distance) with each frame.

When a [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0) element has a `bgcolor` attribute set, the value is expected to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#382.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value), and if that does not return an error, the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#382.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'background-color' property to the resulting color.

The `width` and `height` attributes on a [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0) element [map to the dimension properties](#382.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'width' and 'height' on the element respectively.

The intrinsic height of a [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0) element with its [`direction`](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction) attribute in the [up](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction-up) or [down](#382.html_attr-marquee-direction-down) states is 200 CSS pixels.

The `vspace` attribute of a [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0) element [maps to the dimension properties](#382.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'margin-top' and 'margin-bottom' on the element. The `hspace` attribute of a [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0) element [maps to the dimension properties](#382.html_maps-to-the-dimension-property) 'margin-left' and 'margin-right' on the element.

The 'overflow' property on the [`marquee`](#382.html_the-marquee-element-0) element is expected to be ignored; overflow is expected to always be hidden.

#### 10.5.11 The [`meter`](#383.html_the-meter-element) element

```
[](#cb768-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb768-2)
[](#cb768-3)meter { binding: meter; }
```

When the *meter* binding applies to a [`meter`](#383.html_the-meter-element) element, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box with a 'height' of '1em' and a 'width' of '5em', a 'vertical-align' of '-0.2em', and with its contents depicting a gauge.

When the element is wider than it is tall (or square), the depiction is expected to be of a horizontal gauge, with the minimum value on the right if the 'direction' property on this element has a computed value of 'rtl', and on the left otherwise. When the element is taller than it is wide, it is expected to depict a vertical gauge, with the minimum value on the bottom.

User agents are expected to use a presentation consistent with platform conventions for gauges, if any.

Requirements for what must be depicted in the gauge are included in the definition of the [`meter`](#383.html_the-meter-element) element.

#### 10.5.12 The [`progress`](#384.html_the-progress-element) element

```
[](#cb769-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb769-2)
[](#cb769-3)progress { binding: progress; }
```

When the *progress* binding applies to a [`progress`](#384.html_the-progress-element) element, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box with a 'height' of '1em' and a 'width' of '10em', and a 'vertical-align' of '-0.2em'.

![](Images/cedb68efa9c4b660d616035359ab53cd.jpg) When the element is wider than it is tall, the element is expected to be depicted as a horizontal progress bar, with the start on the right and the end on the left if the 'direction' property on this element has a computed value of 'rtl', and with the start on the left and the end on the right otherwise. When the element is taller than it is wide, it is expected to depicted as a vertical progress bar, with the lowest value on the bottom. When the element is square, it is expected to be depicted as a direction-independent progress widget (e.g. a circular progress ring).

User agents are expected to use a presentation consistent with platform conventions for progress bars. In particular, user agents are expected to use different presentations for determinate and indeterminate progress bars. User agents are also expected to vary the presentation based on the dimensions of the element.

For example, on some platforms for showing indeterminate progress there is an asynchronous progress indicator with square dimensions, which could be used when the element is square, and an indeterminate progress bar, which could be used when the element is wide.

Requirements for how to determine if the progress bar is determinate or indeterminate, and what progress a determinate progress bar is to show, are included in the definition of the [`progress`](#384.html_the-progress-element) element.

#### 10.5.13 The [`select`](#385.html_the-select-element) element

```
[](#cb770-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb770-2)
[](#cb770-3)select { binding: select; }
```

When the *select* binding applies to a [`select`](#385.html_the-select-element) element whose [`multiple`](#385.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute is present, the element is expected to render as a multi-select list box.

When the *select* binding applies to a [`select`](#385.html_the-select-element) element whose [`multiple`](#385.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute is absent, and the element's [display size](#385.html_concept-select-size) is greater than 1, the element is expected to render as a single-select list box.

When the element renders as a list box, it is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box whose 'height' is the height necessary to contain as many rows for items as given by the element's [display size](#385.html_concept-select-size), or four rows if the attribute is absent, and whose 'width' is the [width of the `select`'s labels](#385.html_width-of-the-select's-labels) plus the width of a scrollbar.

When the *select* binding applies to a [`select`](#385.html_the-select-element) element whose [`multiple`](#385.html_attr-select-multiple) attribute is absent, and the element's [display size](#385.html_concept-select-size) is 1, the element is expected to render as a one-line drop down box whose width is the [width of the `select`'s labels](#385.html_width-of-the-select's-labels).

In either case (list box or drop-down box), the element's items are expected to be the element's [list of options](#385.html_concept-select-option-list), with the element's [`optgroup`](#385.html_the-optgroup-element) element children providing headers for groups of options where applicable.

An [`optgroup`](#385.html_the-optgroup-element) element is expected to be rendered by displaying the element's [`label`](#385.html_attr-optgroup-label) attribute.

An [`option`](#385.html_the-option-element) element is expected to be rendered by displaying the element's [label](#385.html_concept-option-label), indented under its [`optgroup`](#385.html_the-optgroup-element) element if it has one.

The <dfn id="385.html_width-of-the-select's-labels">width of the `select`'s labels</dfn> is the wider of the width necessary to render the widest [`optgroup`](#385.html_the-optgroup-element), and the width necessary to render the widest [`option`](#385.html_the-option-element) element in the element's [list of options](#385.html_concept-select-option-list) (including its indent, if any).

If a [`select`](#385.html_the-select-element) element contains a [placeholder label option](#385.html_placeholder-label-option), the user agent is expected to render that [`option`](#385.html_the-option-element) in a manner that conveys that it is a label, rather than a valid option of the control. This can include preventing the [placeholder label option](#385.html_placeholder-label-option) from being explicitly selected by the user. When the [placeholder label option](#385.html_placeholder-label-option)'s [selectedness](#385.html_concept-option-selectedness) is true, the control is expected to be displayed in a fashion that indicates that no valid option is currently selected.

User agents are expected to render the labels in a [`select`](#385.html_the-select-element) in such a manner that any alignment remains consistent whether the label is being displayed as part of the page or in a menu control.

#### 10.5.14 The [`textarea`](#386.html_the-textarea-element) element

```
[](#cb771-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb771-2)
[](#cb771-3)textarea { binding: textarea; white-space: pre-wrap; }
```

When the *textarea* binding applies to a [`textarea`](#386.html_the-textarea-element) element, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box rendered as a multiline text field.

If the element has a [`cols`](#386.html_attr-textarea-cols) attribute, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#386.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) doesn't generate an error, then the user agent is expected to use the attribute as a [presentational hint](#386.html_presentational-hints) for the 'width' property on the element, with the value being the [textarea effective width](#386.html_textarea-effective-width) (as defined below). Otherwise, the user agent is expected to act as if it had a user-agent-level style sheet rule setting the 'width' property on the element to the [textarea effective width](#386.html_textarea-effective-width).

The <dfn id="386.html_textarea-effective-width">textarea effective width</dfn> of a [`textarea`](#386.html_the-textarea-element) element is `size`×`avg` + `sbw`, where `size` is the element's [character width](#386.html_attr-textarea-cols-value), `avg` is the average character width of the primary font of the element, in CSS pixels, and `sbw` is the width of a scroll bar, in CSS pixels. (The element's 'letter-spacing' property does not affect the result.)

If the element has a [`rows`](#386.html_attr-textarea-rows) attribute, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#386.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) doesn't generate an error, then the user agent is expected to use the attribute as a [presentational hint](#386.html_presentational-hints) for the 'height' property on the element, with the value being the [textarea effective height](#386.html_textarea-effective-height) (as defined below). Otherwise, the user agent is expected to act as if it had a user-agent-level style sheet rule setting the 'height' property on the element to the [textarea effective height](#386.html_textarea-effective-height).

The <dfn id="386.html_textarea-effective-height">textarea effective height</dfn> of a [`textarea`](#386.html_the-textarea-element) element is the height in CSS pixels of the number of lines specified the element's [character height](#386.html_attr-textarea-rows-value), plus the height of a scrollbar in CSS pixels.

User agents are expected to apply the 'white-space' CSS property to [`textarea`](#386.html_the-textarea-element) elements. For historical reasons, if the element has a [`wrap`](#386.html_attr-textarea-wrap) attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#386.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`off`", then the user agent is expected to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#386.html_presentational-hints) setting the element's 'white-space' property to 'pre'.

#### 10.5.15 The [`keygen`](#387.html_the-keygen-element) element

```
[](#cb772-1)@namespace url(http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml);
[](#cb772-2)
[](#cb772-3)keygen { binding: keygen; }
```

When the *keygen* binding applies to a [`keygen`](#387.html_the-keygen-element) element, the element is expected to render as an 'inline-block' box containing a user interface to configure the key pair to be generated.

### 10.6 Frames and framesets

User agent are expected to render [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) elements as a box with the height and width of the viewport, with a surface rendered according to the following layout algorithm:

1.  The `cols` and `rows` variables are lists of zero or more pairs consisting of a number and a unit, the unit being one of *percentage*, *relative*, and *absolute*.

    Use the [rules for parsing a list of dimensions](#388.html_rules-for-parsing-a-list-of-dimensions) to parse the value of the element's `cols` attribute, if there is one. Let `cols` be the result, or an empty list if there is no such attribute.

    Use the [rules for parsing a list of dimensions](#388.html_rules-for-parsing-a-list-of-dimensions) to parse the value of the element's `rows` attribute, if there is one. Let `rows` be the result, or an empty list if there is no such attribute.

2.  For any of the entries in `cols` or `rows` that have the number zero and the unit *relative*, change the entry's number to one.

3.  If `cols` has no entries, then add a single entry consisting of the value 1 and the unit *relative* to `cols`.

    If `rows` has no entries, then add a single entry consisting of the value 1 and the unit *relative* to `rows`.

4.  Invoke the algorithm defined below to [convert a list of dimensions to a list of pixel values](#388.html_convert-a-list-of-dimensions-to-a-list-of-pixel-values) using `cols` as the input list, and the width of the surface that the [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) is being rendered into, in CSS pixels, as the input dimension. Let `sized cols` be the resulting list.

    Invoke the algorithm defined below to [convert a list of dimensions to a list of pixel values](#388.html_convert-a-list-of-dimensions-to-a-list-of-pixel-values) using `rows` as the input list, and the height of the surface that the [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) is being rendered into, in CSS pixels, as the input dimension. Let `sized rows` be the resulting list.

5.  Split the surface into a grid of `w`×`h` rectangles, where `w` is the number of entries in `sized cols` and `h` is the number of entries in `sized rows`.

    Size the columns so that each column in the grid is as many CSS pixels wide as the corresponding entry in the `sized cols` list.

    Size the rows so that each row in the grid is as many CSS pixels high as the corresponding entry in the `sized rows` list.

6.  Let `children` be the list of [`frame`](#388.html_frame) and [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) elements that are children of the [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) element for which the algorithm was invoked.

7.  For each row of the grid of rectangles created in the previous step, from top to bottom, run these substeps:

    1.  For each rectangle in the row, from left to right, run these substeps:

        1.  If there are any elements left in `children`, take the first element in the list, and assign it to the rectangle.

            If this is a [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) element, then recurse the entire [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) layout algorithm for that [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) element, with the rectangle as the surface.

            Otherwise, it is a [`frame`](#388.html_frame) element; create a [nested browsing context](#388.html_nested-browsing-context) sized to fit the rectangle.

        2.  If there are any elements left in `children`, remove the first element from `children`.

8.  If the [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) element [has a border](#388.html_has-a-border), draw an outer set of borders around the rectangles, using the element's [frame border color](#388.html_frame-border-color).

    For each rectangle, if there is an element assigned to that rectangle, and that element [has a border](#388.html_has-a-border), draw an inner set of borders around that rectangle, using the element's [frame border color](#388.html_frame-border-color).

    For each (visible) border that does not abut a rectangle that is assigned a [`frame`](#388.html_frame) element with a `noresize` attribute (including rectangles in further nested [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) elements), the user agent is expected to allow the user to move the border, resizing the rectangles within, keeping the proportions of any nested [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) grids.

    A [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) or [`frame`](#388.html_frame) element <dfn id="388.html_has-a-border">has a border</dfn> if the following algorithm returns true:

    1.  If the element has a `frameborder` attribute whose value is not the empty string and whose first character is either a "1" (U+0031) character, a "y" (U+0079) character, or a "Y" (U+0059) character, then return true.

    2.  Otherwise, if the element has a `frameborder` attribute, return false.

    3.  Otherwise, if the element has a parent element that is a [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) element, then return true if *that* element [has a border](#388.html_has-a-border), and false if it does not.

    4.  Otherwise, return true.

    The <dfn id="388.html_frame-border-color">frame border color</dfn> of a [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) or [`frame`](#388.html_frame) element is the color obtained from the following algorithm:

    1.  If the element has a `bordercolor` attribute, and applying the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#388.html_rules-for-parsing-a-legacy-color-value) to that attribute's value does not result in an error, then return the color so obtained.

    2.  Otherwise, if the element has a parent element that is a [`frameset`](#388.html_frameset) element, then return the [frame border color](#388.html_frame-border-color) of that element.

    3.  Otherwise, return gray.

The algorithm to <dfn id="388.html_convert-a-list-of-dimensions-to-a-list-of-pixel-values">convert a list of dimensions to a list of pixel values</dfn> consists of the following steps:

1.  Let `input list` be the list of numbers and units passed to the algorithm.

    Let `output list` be a list of numbers the same length as `input list`, all zero.

    Entries in `output list` correspond to the entries in `input list` that have the same position.

2.  Let `input dimension` be the size passed to the algorithm.

3.  Let `count percentage` be the number of entries in `input list` whose unit is *percentage*.

    Let `total percentage` be the sum of all the numbers in `input list` whose unit is *percentage*.

    Let `count relative` be the number of entries in `input list` whose unit is *relative*.

    Let `total relative` be the sum of all the numbers in `input list` whose unit is *relative*.

    Let `count absolute` be the number of entries in `input list` whose unit is *absolute*.

    Let `total absolute` be the sum of all the numbers in `input list` whose unit is *absolute*.

    Let `remaining space` be the value of `input dimension`.

4.  If `total absolute` is greater than `remaining space`, then for each entry in `input list` whose unit is *absolute*, set the corresponding value in `output list` to the number of the entry in `input list` multiplied by `remaining space` and divided by `total absolute`. Then, set `remaining space` to zero.

    Otherwise, for each entry in `input list` whose unit is *absolute*, set the corresponding value in `output list` to the number of the entry in `input list`. Then, decrement `remaining space` by `total absolute`.

5.  If `total percentage` multiplied by the `input dimension` and divided by 100 is greater than `remaining space`, then for each entry in `input list` whose unit is *percentage*, set the corresponding value in `output list` to the number of the entry in `input list` multiplied by `remaining space` and divided by `total percentage`. Then, set `remaining space` to zero.

    Otherwise, for each entry in `input list` whose unit is *percentage*, set the corresponding value in `output list` to the number of the entry in `input list` multiplied by the `input dimension` and divided by 100\. Then, decrement `remaining space` by `total percentage` multiplied by the `input dimension` and divided by 100.

6.  For each entry in `input list` whose unit is *relative*, set the corresponding value in `output list` to the number of the entry in `input list` multiplied by `remaining space` and divided by `total relative`.

7.  Return `output list`.

User agents working with integer values for frame widths (as opposed to user agents that can lay frames out with subpixel accuracy) are expected to distribute the remainder first to the last entry whose unit is *relative*, then equally (not proportionally) to each entry whose unit is *percentage*, then equally (not proportionally) to each entry whose unit is *absolute*, and finally, failing all else, to the last entry.

### 10.7 Interactive media

#### 10.7.1 Links, forms, and navigation

User agents are expected to allow the user to control aspects of [hyperlink](#390.html_hyperlink) activation and [form submission](#390.html_form-submission-0), such as which [browsing context](#390.html_browsing-context) is to be used for the subsequent [navigation](#390.html_navigate).

User agents are expected to allow users to discover the destination of [hyperlinks](#390.html_hyperlink) and of [forms](#390.html_the-form-element) before triggering their [navigation](#390.html_navigate).

User agents may allow users to [navigate](#390.html_navigate) [browsing contexts](#390.html_browsing-context) to the resources [indicated](#390.html_resolve-a-url) by the `cite` attributes on [`q`](#390.html_the-q-element), [`blockquote`](#390.html_the-blockquote-element), [`ins`](#390.html_the-ins-element), and [`del`](#390.html_the-del-element) elements.

User agents may surface [hyperlinks](#390.html_hyperlink) created by [`link`](#390.html_the-link-element) elements in their user interface.

While [`link`](#390.html_the-link-element) elements that create [hyperlinks](#390.html_hyperlink) will match the ':link' or ':visited' pseudo-classes, will react to clicks if visible, and so forth, this does not extend to any browser interface constructs that expose those same links. Activating a link through the browser's interface, rather than in the page itself, does not trigger [`click`](#390.html_event-click) events and the like.

#### 10.7.2 The [`title`](#391.html_attr-title) attribute

User agents are expected to expose the [advisory information](#391.html_advisory-information) of elements upon user request, and to make the user aware of the presence of such information.

On interactive graphical systems where the user can use a pointing device, this could take the form of a tooltip. When the user is unable to use a pointing device, then the user agent is expected to make the content available in some other fashion, e.g. by making the element focusable and always displaying the [advisory information](#391.html_advisory-information) of the currently focused element, or by showing the [advisory information](#391.html_advisory-information) of the elements under the user's finger on a touch device as the user pans around the screen.

"LF" (U+000A) characters are expected to cause line breaks in the tooltip; "tab" (U+0009) characters are expected to render as a non-zero horizontal shift that lines up the next glyph with the next tab stop, with tab stops occurring at points that are multiples of 8 times the width of a U+0020 SPACE character.

For example, a visual user agent could make elements with a [`title`](#391.html_attr-title) attribute focusable, and could make any focused element with a [`title`](#391.html_attr-title) attribute show its tooltip under the element while the element has focus. This would allow a user to tab around the document to find all the advisory text.

As another example, a screen reader could provide an audio cue when reading an element with a tooltip, with an associated key to read the last tooltip for which a cue was played.

#### 10.7.3 Editing hosts

The current text editing caret (i.e. the [active range](#392.html_active-range), if it is empty and in an [editing host](#392.html_editing-host)), if any, is expected to act like an inline replaced element with the vertical dimensions of the caret and with zero width for the purposes of the CSS rendering model.

This means that even an empty block can have the caret inside it, and that when the caret is in such an element, it prevents margins from collapsing through the element.

#### 10.7.4 Text rendered in native user interfaces

User agents are expected to honor the Unicode semantics of text that is exposed in user interfaces, for example supporting the bidirectional algorithm in text shown in dialogs, title bars, pop-up menus, and tooltips. Text from the contents of elements is expected to be rendered in a manner that honors [the directionality](#393.html_the-directionality) of the element from which the text was obtained. Text from attributes is expected to be rendered in a manner that honours the [directionality of the attribute](#393.html_directionality-of-the-attribute).

Consider the following markup, which has Hebrew text asking for a programming language, the languages being text for which a left-to-right direction is important given the punctuation in some of their names:

```
<p dir="rtl" lang="he">
 <label>
  ??? ??? ?????:
  <select>
   <option dir="ltr">C++</option>
   <option dir="ltr">C#</option>
   <option dir="ltr">FreePascal</option>
   <option dir="ltr">F#</option>
  </select>
 </label>
</p>
```

If the [`select`](#393.html_the-select-element) element was rendered as a drop down box, a correct rendering would ensure that the punctuation was the same both in the drop down, and in the box showing the current selection.

![](Images/cccd16c9589953da3da1075699378ffc.jpg)

The directionality of attributes depends on the attribute and on the element's [`dir`](#393.html_the-dir-attribute) attribute, as the following example demonstrates. Consider this markup:

```
<table>
 <tr>
  <th abbr="(?" dir=ltr>A
  <th abbr="(?" dir=rtl>A
  <th abbr="(?" dir=auto>A
</table>
```

If the [`abbr`](#393.html_attr-th-abbr) attributes are rendered, e.g. in a tooltip or other user interface, the first will have a left parenthesis (because the direction is 'ltr'), the second will have a right parenthesis (because the direction is 'rtl'), and the third will have a right parenthesis (because the direction is determined *from the attribute value* to be 'rtl').

However, if instead the attribute was not a [directionality-capable attribute](#393.html_directionality-capable-attribute), the results would be different:

```
<table>
 <tr>
  <th data-abbr="(?" dir=ltr>A
  <th data-abbr="(?" dir=rtl>A
  <th data-abbr="(?" dir=auto>A
</table>
```

In this case, if the user agent were to expose the `data-abbr` attribute in the user interface (e.g. in a debugging environment), the last case would be rendered with a *left* parenthesis, because the direction would be determined from the element's contents.

A string provided by a script (e.g. the argument to [`window.alert()`](#393.html_dom-alert)) is expected to be treated as an independent set of one or more bidirectional algorithm paragraphs when displayed, as defined by the bidirectional algorithm, including, for instance, supporting the paragraph-breaking behaviour of "LF" (U+000A) characters. For the purposes of determining the paragraph level of such text in the bidirectional algorithm, this specification does *not* provide a higher-level override of rules P2 and P3\. [[BIDI]](#393.html_refsBIDI)

When necessary, authors can enforce a particular direction for a given paragraph by starting it with the Unicode U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK or U+200F RIGHT-TO-LEFT MARK characters.

Thus, the following script:

```
alert('\u05DC\u05DE\u05D3 HTML \u05D4\u05D9\u05D5\u05DD!')
```

...would always result in a message reading "??? LMTH ????!" (not "??? HTML ????!"), regardless of the language of the user agent interface or the direction of the page or any of its elements.

For a more complex example, consider the following script:

```
/* Warning: this script does not handle right-to-left scripts correctly */
var s;
if (s = prompt('What is your name?')) {
  alert(s + '! Ok, Fred, ' + s + ', and Wilma will get the car.');
}
```

When the user enters "`Kitty`", the user agent would alert "<samp>Kitty! Ok, Fred, Kitty, and Wilma will get the car.</samp>". However, if the user enters "`?? ????`", then the bidirectional algorithm will determine that the direction of the paragraph is right-to-left, and so the output will be the following unintended mess: "<samp lang="">?? ????! derF ,kO, ?? ????, rac eht teg lliw amliW dna.</samp>"

To force an alert that starts with user-provided text (or other text of unknown directionality) to render left-to-right, the string can be prefixed with a U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK character:

```
var s;
if (s = prompt('What is your name?')) {
  alert('\u200E' + s + '! Ok, Fred, ' + s + ', and Wilma will get the car.');
}
```

### 10.8 Print media

User agents are expected to allow the user to request the opportunity to <dfn id="394.html_obtain-a-physical-form">obtain a physical form</dfn> (or a representation of a physical form) of a [`Document`](#394.html_document). For example, selecting the option to print a page or convert it to PDF format. [[PDF]](#394.html_refsPDF)

When the user actually [obtains a physical form](#394.html_obtain-a-physical-form) (or a representation of a physical form) of a [`Document`](#394.html_document), the user agent is expected to create a new rendering of the [`Document`](#394.html_document) for the print media.

### 10.9 Unstyled XML documents

HTML user agents may, in certain circumstances, find themselves rendering non-HTML documents that use vocabularies for which they lack any built-in knowledge. This section provides for a way for user agents to handle such documents in a somewhat useful manner.

While a [`Document`](#395.html_document) is an [unstyled document](#395.html_unstyled-document), the user agent is expected to render [an unstyled document view](#395.html_an-unstyled-document-view).

A [`Document`](#395.html_document) is an <dfn id="395.html_unstyled-document">unstyled document</dfn> while it matches the following conditions:

*   The [`Document`](#395.html_document) has no author style sheets (whether referenced by HTTP headers, processing instructions, elements like [`link`](#395.html_the-link-element), inline elements like [`style`](#395.html_the-style-element), or any other mechanism).
*   None of the elements in the [`Document`](#395.html_document) have any [presentational hints](#395.html_presentational-hints).
*   None of the elements in the [`Document`](#395.html_document) have any [CSS styling attributes](#395.html_css-styling-attribute).
*   None of the elements in the [`Document`](#395.html_document) are in any of the following namespaces: [HTML namespace](#395.html_html-namespace-0), [SVG namespace](#395.html_svg-namespace), [MathML namespace](#395.html_mathml-namespace)
*   The [`Document`](#395.html_document) has no [focusable](#395.html_focusable) elements (e.g. from XLink).
*   The [`Document`](#395.html_document) has no [hyperlinks](#395.html_hyperlink) (e.g. from XLink).
*   There exists no [script](#395.html_concept-script) whose [settings object](#395.html_settings-object) specifies this [`Document`](#395.html_document) as the [responsible document](#395.html_responsible-document).
*   None of the elements in the [`Document`](#395.html_document) have any registered event listeners.

<dfn id="395.html_an-unstyled-document-view">An unstyled document view</dfn> is one where the DOM is not rendered according to CSS (which would, since there are no applicable styles in this context, just result in a wall of text), but is instead rendered in a manner that is useful for a developer. This could consist of just showing the [`Document`](#395.html_document) object's source, maybe with syntax highlighting, or it could consist of displaying just the DOM tree, or simply a message saying that the page is not a styled document.

If a [`Document`](#395.html_document) stops being an [unstyled document](#395.html_unstyled-document), then the conditions above stop applying, and thus a user agent following these requirements will switch to using the regular CSS rendering.

## 11 Obsolete features

### 11.1 Obsolete but conforming features

Features listed in this section will trigger warnings in conformance checkers.

Authors should not specify a [`border`](#397.html_attr-img-border) attribute on an [`img`](#397.html_the-img-element) element. If the attribute is present, its value must be the string "`0`". CSS should be used instead.

Authors should not specify a [`language`](#397.html_attr-script-language) attribute on a [`script`](#397.html_the-script-element) element. If the attribute is present, its value must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](#397.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`JavaScript`" and either the [`type`](#397.html_attr-script-type) attribute must be omitted or its value must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](#397.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`text/javascript`". The attribute should be entirely omitted instead (with the value "`JavaScript`", it has no effect), or replaced with use of the [`type`](#397.html_attr-script-type) attribute.

Authors should not specify the [`name`](#397.html_attr-a-name) attribute on [`a`](#397.html_the-a-element) elements. If the attribute is present, its value must not be the empty string and must neither be equal to the value of any of the [IDs](#397.html_concept-id) in the element's [home subtree](#397.html_home-subtree) other than the element's own [ID](#397.html_concept-id), if any, nor be equal to the value of any of the other [`name`](#397.html_attr-a-name) attributes on [`a`](#397.html_the-a-element) elements in the element's [home subtree](#397.html_home-subtree). If this attribute is present and the element has an [ID](#397.html_concept-id), then the attribute's value must be equal to the element's [ID](#397.html_concept-id). In earlier versions of the language, this attribute was intended as a way to specify possible targets for fragment identifiers in URLs. The [`id`](#397.html_the-id-attribute) attribute should be used instead.

Authors should not, but may despite requirements to the contrary elsewhere in this specification, specify the [`maxlength`](#397.html_attr-input-maxlength) and [`size`](#397.html_attr-input-size) attributes on [`input`](#397.html_the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#397.html_attr-input-type) attributes are in the [Number](#397.html_number-state-(type=number)) state. One valid reason for using these attributes regardless is to help legacy user agents that do not support [`input`](#397.html_the-input-element) elements with `type="number"` to still render the text field with a useful width.

In [the HTML syntax](#397.html_syntax), specifying a [DOCTYPE](#397.html_syntax-doctype) that is an [obsolete permitted DOCTYPE](#397.html_obsolete-permitted-doctype) will also trigger a warning.

#### 11.1.1 Warnings for obsolete but conforming features

To ease the transition from HTML4 Transitional documents to the language defined in *this* specification, and to discourage certain features that are only allowed in very few circumstances, conformance checkers are required to warn the user when the following features are used in a document. These are generally old obsolete features that have no effect, and are allowed only to distinguish between likely mistakes (regular conformance errors) and mere vestigial markup or unusual and discouraged practices (these warnings).

The following features must be categorized as described above:

*   The presence of an [obsolete permitted DOCTYPE](#398.html_obsolete-permitted-doctype) in an [HTML document](#398.html_html-documents).

*   The presence of a [`border`](#398.html_attr-img-border) attribute on an [`img`](#398.html_the-img-element) element if its value is the string "`0`".

*   The presence of a [`language`](#398.html_attr-script-language) attribute on a [`script`](#398.html_the-script-element) element if its value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#398.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`JavaScript`" and if there is no [`type`](#398.html_attr-script-type) attribute or there is and its value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](#398.html_ascii-case-insensitive) match for the string "`text/javascript`".

*   The presence of a [`name`](#398.html_attr-a-name) attribute on an [`a`](#398.html_the-a-element) element, if its value is not the empty string.

*   The presence of a [`maxlength`](#398.html_attr-input-maxlength) attribute on an [`input`](#398.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#398.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Number](#398.html_number-state-(type=number)) state.

*   The presence of a [`size`](#398.html_attr-input-size) attribute on an [`input`](#398.html_the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#398.html_attr-input-type) attribute is in the [Number](#398.html_number-state-(type=number)) state.

Conformance checkers must distinguish between pages that have no conformance errors and have none of these obsolete features, and pages that have no conformance errors but do have some of these obsolete features.

For example, a validator could report some pages as "Valid HTML" and others as "Valid HTML with warnings".

### 11.2 Non-conforming features

Elements in the following list are entirely obsolete, and must not be used by authors:

[`applet`](#399.html_the-applet-element)

Use [`embed`](#399.html_the-embed-element) or [`object`](#399.html_the-object-element) instead.

<dfn id="399.html_acronym">`acronym`</dfn>

Use [`abbr`](#399.html_the-abbr-element) instead.

<dfn id="399.html_bgsound">`bgsound`</dfn>

Use [`audio`](#399.html_the-audio-element) instead.

<dfn id="399.html_dir">`dir`</dfn>

Use [`ul`](#399.html_the-ul-element) instead.

[`frame`](#399.html_frame)
[`frameset`](#399.html_frameset)
<dfn id="399.html_noframes">`noframes`</dfn>

Either use [`iframe`](#399.html_the-iframe-element) and CSS instead, or use server-side includes to generate complete pages with the various invariant parts merged in.

<dfn id="399.html_hgroup">`hgroup`</dfn>

To mark up subheadings, consider putting the subheading into a [`p`](#399.html_the-p-element) element after the [`h1`](#399.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)-[`h6`](#399.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element containing the main heading, or putting the subheading directly within the [`h1`](#399.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements)-[`h6`](#399.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element containing the main heading, but separated from the main heading by punctuation and/or within, for example, a `span class="subheading"` element with differentiated styling.

Headings and subheadings, alternative titles, or taglines can be grouped using the [`header`](#399.html_the-header-element) or [`div`](#399.html_the-div-element) elements.

<dfn id="399.html_isindex-0">`isindex`</dfn>

Use an explicit [`form`](#399.html_the-form-element) and [text field](#399.html_text-(type=text)-state-and-search-state-(type=search)) combination instead.

<dfn id="399.html_listing">`listing`</dfn>

Use [`pre`](#399.html_the-pre-element) and [`code`](#399.html_the-code-element) instead.

<dfn id="399.html_nextid">`nextid`</dfn>

Use GUIDs instead.

<dfn id="399.html_noembed">`noembed`</dfn>

Use [`object`](#399.html_the-object-element) instead of [`embed`](#399.html_the-embed-element) when fallback is necessary.

<dfn id="399.html_plaintext">`plaintext`</dfn>

Use the "`text/plain`" [MIME type](#399.html_mime-type) instead.

<dfn id="399.html_strike">`strike`</dfn>

Use [`del`](#399.html_the-del-element) instead if the element is marking an edit, otherwise use [`s`](#399.html_the-s-element) instead.

<dfn id="399.html_xmp">`xmp`</dfn>

Use [`pre`](#399.html_the-pre-element) and [`code`](#399.html_the-code-element) instead, and escape "`<`" and "`&`" characters as "`&lt;`" and "`&amp;`" respectively.

<dfn id="399.html_basefont">`basefont`</dfn>
<dfn id="399.html_big">`big`</dfn>
<dfn id="399.html_blink">`blink`</dfn>
<dfn id="399.html_center">`center`</dfn>
<dfn id="399.html_font">`font`</dfn>
[`marquee`](#399.html_the-marquee-element-0)
<dfn id="399.html_multicol">`multicol`</dfn>
<dfn id="399.html_nobr">`nobr`</dfn>
<dfn id="399.html_spacer">`spacer`</dfn>
<dfn id="399.html_tt">`tt`</dfn>

Use appropriate elements or CSS instead.

Where the [`tt`](#399.html_tt) element would have been used for marking up keyboard input, consider the [`kbd`](#399.html_the-kbd-element) element; for variables, consider the [`var`](#399.html_the-var-element) element; for computer code, consider the [`code`](#399.html_the-code-element) element; and for computer output, consider the [`samp`](#399.html_the-samp-element) element.

Similarly, if the [`big`](#399.html_big) element is being used to denote a heading, consider using the [`h1`](#399.html_the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements) element; if it is being used for marking up important passages, consider the [`strong`](#399.html_the-strong-element) element; and if it is being used for highlighting text for reference purposes, consider the [`mark`](#399.html_the-mark-element) element.

See also the [text-level semantics usage summary](#399.html_usage-summary) for more suggestions with examples.

* * *

The following attributes are obsolete (though the elements are still part of the language), and must not be used by authors:

<dfn id="399.html_attr-a-charset" data-anolis-xref="attr-a-charset">`charset`</dfn> on [`a`](#399.html_the-a-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-link-charset" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-charset">`charset`</dfn> on [`link`](#399.html_the-link-element) elements

Use an HTTP Content-Type header on the linked resource instead.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-a-coords" data-anolis-xref="attr-a-coords">`coords`</dfn> on [`a`](#399.html_the-a-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-a-shape" data-anolis-xref="attr-a-shape">`shape`</dfn> on [`a`](#399.html_the-a-element) elements

Use [`area`](#399.html_the-area-element) instead of [`a`](#399.html_the-a-element) for image maps.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-a-methods" data-anolis-xref="attr-a-methods">`methods`</dfn> on [`a`](#399.html_the-a-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-link-methods" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-methods">`methods`</dfn> on [`link`](#399.html_the-link-element) elements

Use the HTTP OPTIONS feature instead.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-a-name" data-anolis-xref="attr-a-name">`name`</dfn> on [`a`](#399.html_the-a-element) elements (except as noted in the previous section)
<dfn id="399.html_attr-embed-name" data-anolis-xref="attr-embed-name">`name`</dfn> on [`embed`](#399.html_the-embed-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-img-name" data-anolis-xref="attr-img-name">`name`</dfn> on [`img`](#399.html_the-img-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-option-name" data-anolis-xref="attr-option-name">`name`</dfn> on [`option`](#399.html_the-option-element) elements

Use the [`id`](#399.html_the-id-attribute) attribute instead.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-a-urn" data-anolis-xref="attr-a-urn">`urn`</dfn> on [`a`](#399.html_the-a-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-link-urn" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-urn">`urn`</dfn> on [`link`](#399.html_the-link-element) elements

Specify the preferred persistent identifier using the [`href`](#399.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute instead.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-form-accept" data-anolis-xref="attr-form-accept">`accept`</dfn> on [`form`](#399.html_the-form-element) elements

Use the [`accept`](#399.html_attr-input-accept) attribute directly on the [`input`](#399.html_the-input-element) elements instead.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-area-nohref" data-anolis-xref="attr-area-nohref">`nohref`</dfn> on [`area`](#399.html_the-area-element) elements

Omitting the [`href`](#399.html_attr-hyperlink-href) attribute is sufficient; the [`nohref`](#399.html_attr-area-nohref) attribute is unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-head-profile" data-anolis-xref="attr-head-profile">`profile`</dfn> on [`head`](#399.html_the-head-element) elements

When used for declaring which [`meta`](#399.html_the-meta-element) terms are used in the document, unnecessary; omit it altogether, and [register the names](#399.html_concept-meta-extensions).

When used for triggering specific user agent behaviors: use a [`link`](#399.html_the-link-element) element instead.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-html-version" data-anolis-xref="attr-html-version">`version`</dfn> on [`html`](#399.html_the-html-element) elements

Unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-input-ismap" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-ismap">`ismap`</dfn> on [`input`](#399.html_the-input-element) elements

Unnecessary. Omit it altogether. All [`input`](#399.html_the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#399.html_attr-input-type) attribute in the [Image Button](#399.html_image-button-state-(type=image)) state are processed as server-side image maps.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-input-usemap" data-anolis-xref="attr-input-usemap">`usemap`</dfn> on [`input`](#399.html_the-input-element) elements

Use [`img`](#399.html_the-img-element) instead of [`input`](#399.html_the-input-element) for image maps.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-img-lowsrc" data-anolis-xref="attr-img-lowsrc">`lowsrc`</dfn> on [`img`](#399.html_the-img-element) elements

Use a progressive JPEG image (given in the [`src`](#399.html_attr-img-src) attribute), instead of using two separate images.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-link-target" data-anolis-xref="attr-link-target">`target`</dfn> on [`link`](#399.html_the-link-element) elements

Unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-meta-scheme" data-anolis-xref="attr-meta-scheme">`scheme`</dfn> on [`meta`](#399.html_the-meta-element) elements

Use only one scheme per field, or make the scheme declaration part of the value.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-object-archive" data-anolis-xref="attr-object-archive">`archive`</dfn> on [`object`](#399.html_the-object-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-object-classid" data-anolis-xref="attr-object-classid">`classid`</dfn> on [`object`](#399.html_the-object-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-object-code" data-anolis-xref="attr-object-code">`code`</dfn> on [`object`](#399.html_the-object-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-object-codebase" data-anolis-xref="attr-object-codebase">`codebase`</dfn> on [`object`](#399.html_the-object-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-object-codetype" data-anolis-xref="attr-object-codetype">`codetype`</dfn> on [`object`](#399.html_the-object-element) elements

Use the [`data`](#399.html_attr-object-data) and [`type`](#399.html_attr-object-type) attributes to invoke [plugins](#399.html_plugin). To set parameters with these names in particular, the [`param`](#399.html_the-param-element) element can be used.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-object-declare" data-anolis-xref="attr-object-declare">`declare`</dfn> on [`object`](#399.html_the-object-element) elements

Repeat the [`object`](#399.html_the-object-element) element completely each time the resource is to be reused.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-object-standby" data-anolis-xref="attr-object-standby">`standby`</dfn> on [`object`](#399.html_the-object-element) elements

Optimize the linked resource so that it loads quickly or, at least, incrementally.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-param-type" data-anolis-xref="attr-param-type">`type`</dfn> on [`param`](#399.html_the-param-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-param-valuetype" data-anolis-xref="attr-param-valuetype">`valuetype`</dfn> on [`param`](#399.html_the-param-element) elements

Use the [`name`](#399.html_attr-param-name) and [`value`](#399.html_attr-param-value) attributes without declaring value types.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-script-language" data-anolis-xref="attr-script-language">`language`</dfn> on [`script`](#399.html_the-script-element) elements (except as noted in the previous section)

Use the [`type`](#399.html_attr-script-type) attribute instead.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-script-event" data-anolis-xref="attr-script-event">`event`</dfn> on [`script`](#399.html_the-script-element) elements
<dfn id="399.html_attr-script-for" data-anolis-xref="attr-script-for">`for`</dfn> on [`script`](#399.html_the-script-element) elements

Use DOM Events mechanisms to register event listeners. [[DOM]](#399.html_refsDOM)

<dfn id="399.html_attr-table-datapagesize" data-anolis-xref="attr-table-datapagesize">`datapagesize`</dfn> on [`table`](#399.html_the-table-element) elements

Unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-table-summary" data-anolis-xref="attr-table-summary">`summary`</dfn> on [`table`](#399.html_the-table-element) elements

Use one of the [techniques for describing tables](#399.html_table-descriptions-techniques) given in the [`table`](#399.html_the-table-element) section instead.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-tdth-axis" data-anolis-xref="attr-tdth-axis">`axis`</dfn> on [`td`](#399.html_the-td-element) and [`th`](#399.html_the-th-element) elements

Use the [`scope`](#399.html_attr-th-scope) attribute on the relevant [`th`](#399.html_the-th-element).

<dfn id="399.html_attr-td-scope" data-anolis-xref="attr-td-scope">`scope`</dfn> on [`td`](#399.html_the-td-element) elements

Use [`th`](#399.html_the-th-element) elements for heading cells.

<dfn id="399.html_attr-datasrc" data-anolis-xref="attr-datasrc">`datasrc`</dfn> on [`a`](#399.html_the-a-element), [`applet`](#399.html_the-applet-element), [`button`](#399.html_the-button-element), [`div`](#399.html_the-div-element), [`frame`](#399.html_frame), [`iframe`](#399.html_the-iframe-element), [`img`](#399.html_the-img-element), [`input`](#399.html_the-input-element), [`label`](#399.html_the-label-element), [`legend`](#399.html_the-legend-element), [`marquee`](#399.html_the-marquee-element-0), [`object`](#399.html_the-object-element), [`option`](#399.html_the-option-element), [`select`](#399.html_the-select-element), [`span`](#399.html_the-span-element), [`table`](#399.html_the-table-element), and [`textarea`](#399.html_the-textarea-element) elements
