Use CSS instead.

* * *

The [`border`](#399.html_attr-table-border) attribute on the [`table`](#399.html_the-table-element) element can be used to provide basic fallback styling for the purpose of making tables legible in browsing environments where CSS support is limited or absent, such as text-based browsers, WYSIWYG editors, and in situations where CSS support is disabled or the style sheet is lost. Only the empty string and the value "`1`" may be used as [`border`](#399.html_attr-table-border) values for this purpose. Other values are considered obsolete. To regulate the thickness of such borders, authors should instead use CSS.

### 11.3 Requirements for implementations

#### 11.3.1 The <dfn>`applet`</dfn> element

The [`applet`](#401.html_the-applet-element) element is a Java-specific variant of the [`embed`](#401.html_the-embed-element) element. The [`applet`](#401.html_the-applet-element) element is now obsoleted so that all extension frameworks (Java, .NET, Flash, etc) are handled in a consistent manner.

When the element matches any of the following conditions, it [represents](#401.html_represents) its contents:

*   The element is still in the [stack of open elements](#401.html_stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#401.html_html-parser) or [XML parser](#401.html_xml-parser).
*   The element is not [in a `Document`](#401.html_in-a-document).
*   The element's [`Document`](#401.html_document) is not [fully active](#401.html_fully-active).
*   The element's [`Document`](#401.html_document)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#401.html_active-sandboxing-flag-set) has its [sandboxed plugins browsing context flag](#401.html_sandboxed-plugins-browsing-context-flag) set.
*   The element has an ancestor [media element](#401.html_media-element).
*   The element has an ancestor [`object`](#401.html_the-object-element) element that is *not* showing its [fallback content](#401.html_fallback-content).
*   No Java Language runtime [plugin](#401.html_plugin) is available.
*   A Java runtime [plugin](#401.html_plugin) is available but it is disabled.

Otherwise, the user agent should instantiate a Java Language runtime [plugin](#401.html_plugin), and should pass the names and values of all the attributes on the element, in the order they were added to the element, with the attributes added by the parser being ordered in source order, and then a parameter named "PARAM" whose value is null, and then all the names and values of [parameters](#401.html_concept-param-parameter) given by [`param`](#401.html_the-param-element) elements that are children of the [`applet`](#401.html_the-applet-element) element, in [tree order](#401.html_tree-order), to the [plugin](#401.html_plugin) used. If the [plugin](#401.html_plugin) supports a scriptable interface, the [`HTMLAppletElement`](#401.html_htmlappletelement) object representing the element should expose that interface. The [`applet`](#401.html_the-applet-element) element [represents](#401.html_represents) the [plugin](#401.html_plugin).

The [`applet`](#401.html_the-applet-element) element is unaffected by the CSS 'display' property. The Java Language runtime is instantiated even if the element is hidden with a 'display:none' CSS style.

The [`applet`](#401.html_the-applet-element) element must implement the [`HTMLAppletElement`](#401.html_htmlappletelement) interface.

```
interface HTMLAppletElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString align;
           attribute DOMString alt;
           attribute DOMString archive;
           attribute DOMString code;
           attribute DOMString codeBase;
           attribute DOMString height;
           attribute unsigned long hspace;
           attribute DOMString name;
           attribute DOMString _object; // the underscore is not part of the identifier 
           attribute unsigned long vspace;
           attribute DOMString width;
};
```

The <dfn id="401.html_dom-applet-align" data-anolis-xref="dom-applet-align">`align`</dfn>, <dfn id="401.html_dom-applet-alt" data-anolis-xref="dom-applet-alt">`alt`</dfn>, <dfn id="401.html_dom-applet-archive" data-anolis-xref="dom-applet-archive">`archive`</dfn>, <dfn id="401.html_dom-applet-code" data-anolis-xref="dom-applet-code">`code`</dfn>, <dfn id="401.html_dom-applet-height" data-anolis-xref="dom-applet-height">`height`</dfn>, <dfn id="401.html_dom-applet-hspace" data-anolis-xref="dom-applet-hspace">`hspace`</dfn>, <dfn id="401.html_dom-applet-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-applet-name">`name`</dfn>, <dfn id="401.html_dom-applet-object" data-anolis-xref="dom-applet-object">`object`</dfn>, <dfn id="401.html_dom-applet-vspace" data-anolis-xref="dom-applet-vspace">`vspace`</dfn>, and <dfn id="401.html_dom-applet-width" data-anolis-xref="dom-applet-width">`width`</dfn> IDL attributes must [reflect](#401.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name. For the purposes of reflection, the [`applet`](#401.html_the-applet-element) element's `object` content attribute is defined as containing a URL.

The <dfn id="401.html_dom-applet-codebase" data-anolis-xref="dom-applet-codeBase">`codeBase`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#401.html_reflect) the `codebase` content attribute, which for the purposes of reflection is defined as containing a URL.

#### 11.3.2 The <dfn>`marquee`</dfn> element

The [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element is a presentational element that animates content. CSS transitions and animations are a more appropriate mechanism. [[CSSANIMATIONS]](#402.html_refsCSSANIMATIONS) [[CSSTRANSITIONS]](#402.html_refsCSSTRANSITIONS)

The [task source](#402.html_task-source) for tasks mentioned in this section is the [DOM manipulation task source](#402.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

The [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element must implement the [`HTMLMarqueeElement`](#402.html_htmlmarqueeelement) interface.

```
interface HTMLMarqueeElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString behavior;
           attribute DOMString bgColor;
           attribute DOMString direction;
           attribute DOMString height;
           attribute unsigned long hspace;
           attribute long loop;
           attribute unsigned long scrollAmount;
           attribute unsigned long scrollDelay;
           attribute boolean trueSpeed;
           attribute unsigned long vspace;
           attribute DOMString width;

           attribute EventHandler onbounce;
           attribute EventHandler onfinish;
           attribute EventHandler onstart;

  void start();
  void stop();
};
```

A [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element can be <dfn id="402.html_concept-marquee-on" data-anolis-xref="concept-marquee-on">turned on</dfn> or <dfn id="402.html_concept-marquee-off" data-anolis-xref="concept-marquee-off">turned off</dfn>. When it is created, it is [turned on](#402.html_concept-marquee-on).

When the <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-start" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-start">`start()`</dfn> method is called, the [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element must be [turned on](#402.html_concept-marquee-on).

When the <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-stop" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-stop">`stop()`</dfn> method is called, the [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element must be [turned off](#402.html_concept-marquee-off).

When a [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element is created, the user agent must [queue a task](#402.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#402.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `start` at the element.

* * *

The <dfn id="402.html_attr-marquee-behavior" data-anolis-xref="attr-marquee-behavior">`behavior`</dfn> content attribute on [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) elements is an [enumerated attribute](#402.html_enumerated-attribute) with the following keywords (all non-conforming):

| Keyword | State |
| --- | --- |
| `scroll` | <dfn id="402.html_attr-marquee-behavior-scroll" data-anolis-xref="attr-marquee-behavior-scroll">scroll</dfn> |
| `slide` | <dfn id="402.html_attr-marquee-behavior-slide" data-anolis-xref="attr-marquee-behavior-slide">slide</dfn> |
| `alternate` | <dfn id="402.html_attr-marquee-behavior-alternate" data-anolis-xref="attr-marquee-behavior-alternate">alternate</dfn> |

The *missing value default* is the [scroll](#402.html_attr-marquee-behavior-scroll) state.

* * *

The <dfn id="402.html_attr-marquee-direction" data-anolis-xref="attr-marquee-direction">`direction`</dfn> content attribute on [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) elements is an [enumerated attribute](#402.html_enumerated-attribute) with the following keywords (all non-conforming):

| Keyword | State |
| --- | --- |
| `left` | <dfn id="402.html_attr-marquee-direction-left" data-anolis-xref="attr-marquee-direction-left">left</dfn> |
| `right` | <dfn id="402.html_attr-marquee-direction-right" data-anolis-xref="attr-marquee-direction-right">right</dfn> |
| `up` | <dfn id="402.html_attr-marquee-direction-up" data-anolis-xref="attr-marquee-direction-up">up</dfn> |
| `down` | <dfn id="402.html_attr-marquee-direction-down" data-anolis-xref="attr-marquee-direction-down">down</dfn> |

The *missing value default* is the [left](#402.html_attr-marquee-direction-left) state.

* * *

The <dfn id="402.html_attr-marquee-truespeed" data-anolis-xref="attr-marquee-truespeed">`truespeed`</dfn> content attribute on [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) elements is a [boolean attribute](#402.html_boolean-attribute).

* * *

A [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element has a <dfn id="402.html_marquee-scroll-interval">marquee scroll interval</dfn>, which is obtained as follows:

1.  If the element has a `scrolldelay` attribute, and parsing its value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#402.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) does not return an error, then let `delay` be the parsed value. Otherwise, let `delay` be 85.

2.  If the element does not have a [`truespeed`](#402.html_attr-marquee-truespeed) attribute, and the `delay` value is less than 60, then let `delay` be 60 instead.

3.  The [marquee scroll interval](#402.html_marquee-scroll-interval) is `delay`, interpreted in milliseconds.

* * *

A [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element has a <dfn id="402.html_marquee-scroll-distance">marquee scroll distance</dfn>, which, if the element has a `scrollamount` attribute, and parsing its value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#402.html_rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) does not return an error, is the parsed value interpreted in CSS pixels, and otherwise is 6 CSS pixels.

* * *

A [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element has a <dfn id="402.html_marquee-loop-count">marquee loop count</dfn>, which, if the element has a `loop` attribute, and parsing its value using the [rules for parsing integers](#402.html_rules-for-parsing-integers) does not return an error or a number less than 1, is the parsed value, and otherwise is ?1.

The <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-loop" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-loop">`loop`</dfn> IDL attribute, on getting, must return the element's [marquee loop count](#402.html_marquee-loop-count); and on setting, if the new value is different than the element's [marquee loop count](#402.html_marquee-loop-count) and either greater than zero or equal to ?1, must set the element's `loop` content attribute (adding it if necessary) to the [valid integer](#402.html_valid-integer) that represents the new value. (Other values are ignored.)

A [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element also has a <dfn id="402.html_marquee-current-loop-index">marquee current loop index</dfn>, which is zero when the element is created.

The rendering layer will occasionally <dfn id="402.html_increment-the-marquee-current-loop-index">increment the marquee current loop index</dfn>, which must cause the following steps to be run:

1.  If the [marquee loop count](#402.html_marquee-loop-count) is ?1, then abort these steps.

2.  Increment the [marquee current loop index](#402.html_marquee-current-loop-index) by one.

3.  If the [marquee current loop index](#402.html_marquee-current-loop-index) is now equal to or greater than the element's [marquee loop count](#402.html_marquee-loop-count), [turn off](#402.html_concept-marquee-off) the [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element and [queue a task](#402.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#402.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `finish` at the [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element.

    Otherwise, if the [`behavior`](#402.html_attr-marquee-behavior) attribute is in the [alternate](#402.html_attr-marquee-behavior-alternate) state, then [queue a task](#402.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#402.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `bounce` at the [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element.

    Otherwise, [queue a task](#402.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#402.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `start` at the [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) element.

* * *

The following are the [event handlers](#402.html_event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#402.html_event-handler-event-type)) that must be supported, as [event handler content attributes](#402.html_event-handler-content-attributes) and [event handler IDL attributes](#402.html_event-handler-idl-attributes), by [`marquee`](#402.html_the-marquee-element-0) elements:

| [Event handler](#402.html_event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#402.html_event-handler-event-type) |
| --- | --- |
| <dfn id="402.html_handler-marquee-onbounce" data-anolis-xref="handler-marquee-onbounce">`onbounce`</dfn> | `bounce` |
| <dfn id="402.html_handler-marquee-onfinish" data-anolis-xref="handler-marquee-onfinish">`onfinish`</dfn> | `finish` |
| <dfn id="402.html_handler-marquee-onstart" data-anolis-xref="handler-marquee-onstart">`onstart`</dfn> | `start` |

* * *

The <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-behavior" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-behavior">`behavior`</dfn>, <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-direction" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-direction">`direction`</dfn>, <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-height" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-height">`height`</dfn>, <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-hspace" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-hspace">`hspace`</dfn>, <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-vspace" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-vspace">`vspace`</dfn>, and <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-width" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-width">`width`</dfn> IDL attributes must [reflect](#402.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

The <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-bgcolor" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-bgColor">`bgColor`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#402.html_reflect) the `bgcolor` content attribute.

The <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-scrollamount" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-scrollAmount">`scrollAmount`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#402.html_reflect) the `scrollamount` content attribute. The default value is 6.

The <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-scrolldelay" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-scrollDelay">`scrollDelay`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#402.html_reflect) the `scrolldelay` content attribute. The default value is 85.

The <dfn id="402.html_dom-marquee-truespeed" data-anolis-xref="dom-marquee-trueSpeed">`trueSpeed`</dfn> IDL attribute must [reflect](#402.html_reflect) the [`truespeed`](#402.html_attr-marquee-truespeed) content attribute.

#### 11.3.3 Frames

The <dfn id="403.html_frameset">`frameset`</dfn> element acts as [the body element](#403.html_the-body-element-0) in documents that use frames.

The [`frameset`](#403.html_frameset) element must implement the [`HTMLFrameSetElement`](#403.html_htmlframesetelement) interface.

```
interface HTMLFrameSetElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString cols;
           attribute DOMString rows;
};
HTMLFrameSetElement implements WindowEventHandlers;
```

The <dfn id="403.html_dom-frameset-cols" data-anolis-xref="dom-frameset-cols">`cols`</dfn> and <dfn id="403.html_dom-frameset-rows" data-anolis-xref="dom-frameset-rows">`rows`</dfn> IDL attributes of the [`frameset`](#403.html_frameset) element must [reflect](#403.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

The [`frameset`](#403.html_frameset) element exposes as [event handler content attributes](#403.html_event-handler-content-attributes) a number of the [event handlers](#403.html_event-handlers) of the [`Window`](#403.html_window) object. It also mirrors their [event handler IDL attributes](#403.html_event-handler-idl-attributes).

The [`onblur`](#403.html_handler-onblur), [`onerror`](#403.html_handler-onerror), [`onfocus`](#403.html_handler-onfocus), [`onload`](#403.html_handler-onload), [`onresize`](#403.html_handler-onresize), and [`onscroll`](#403.html_handler-onscroll) [event handlers](#403.html_event-handlers) of the [`Window`](#403.html_window) object, exposed on the [`frameset`](#403.html_frameset) element, replace the generic [event handlers](#403.html_event-handlers) with the same names normally supported by [HTML elements](#403.html_html-elements).

* * *

The <dfn id="403.html_frame">`frame`</dfn> element defines a [nested browsing context](#403.html_nested-browsing-context) similar to the [`iframe`](#403.html_the-iframe-element) element, but rendered within a [`frameset`](#403.html_frameset) element.

A [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element is said to be an <dfn id="403.html_active-frame-element">active `frame` element</dfn> when it is [in a `Document`](#403.html_in-a-document) and its parent element, if any, is a [`frameset`](#403.html_frameset) element.

When a [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element is created as an [active `frame` element](#403.html_active-frame-element), or becomes an [active `frame` element](#403.html_active-frame-element) after not having been one, the user agent must create a [nested browsing context](#403.html_nested-browsing-context), and then [process the `frame` attributes](#403.html_process-the-frame-attributes) for the first time.

When a [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element stops being an [active `frame` element](#403.html_active-frame-element), the user agent must [discard](#403.html_a-browsing-context-is-discarded) the [nested browsing context](#403.html_nested-browsing-context).

Whenever a [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element with a [nested browsing context](#403.html_nested-browsing-context) has its `src` attribute set, changed, or removed, the user agent must [process the `frame` attributes](#403.html_process-the-frame-attributes).

When the user agent is to <dfn id="403.html_process-the-frame-attributes">process the `frame` attributes</dfn>, it must run the first appropriate steps from the following list:

If the element has no `src` attribute specified, and the user agent is processing the [`frame`](#403.html_frame)'s attributes for the first time

[Queue a task](#403.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#403.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `load` at the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element.

Otherwise

1.  If the value of the `src` attribute is the empty string, let `url` be the string "[`about:blank`](#403.html_about:blank)".

    Otherwise, [resolve](#403.html_resolve-a-url) the value of the `src` attribute, relative to the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element.

    If that is not successful, then let `url` be the string "[`about:blank`](#403.html_about:blank)". Otherwise, let `url` be the resulting [absolute URL](#403.html_absolute-url).

2.  [Navigate](#403.html_navigate) the element's [child browsing context](#403.html_child-browsing-context) to `url`.

Any [navigation](#403.html_navigate) required of the user agent in the [process the `frame` attributes](#403.html_process-the-frame-attributes) algorithm must be completed as an explicit self-navigation override and with the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element's document's [browsing context](#403.html_browsing-context) as the [source browsing context](#403.html_source-browsing-context).

Furthermore, if the [active document](#403.html_active-document) of the element's [child browsing context](#403.html_child-browsing-context) before such a [navigation](#403.html_navigate) was not [completely loaded](#403.html_completely-loaded) at the time of the new [navigation](#403.html_navigate), then the [navigation](#403.html_navigate) must be completed with [replacement enabled](#403.html_replacement-enabled).

Similarly, if the [child browsing context](#403.html_child-browsing-context)'s [session history](#403.html_session-history) contained only one [`Document`](#403.html_document) when the [process the `frame` attributes](#403.html_process-the-frame-attributes) algorithm was invoked, and that was the [`about:blank`](#403.html_about:blank) [`Document`](#403.html_document) created when the [child browsing context](#403.html_child-browsing-context) was created, then any [navigation](#403.html_navigate) required of the user agent in that algorithm must be completed with [replacement enabled](#403.html_replacement-enabled).

When a [`Document`](#403.html_document) in a [`frame`](#403.html_frame) is marked as [completely loaded](#403.html_completely-loaded), the user agent must [queue a task](#403.html_queue-a-task) to [fire a simple event](#403.html_fire-a-simple-event) named `load` at the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element.

The [task source](#403.html_task-source) for the [tasks](#403.html_concept-task) above is the [DOM manipulation task source](#403.html_dom-manipulation-task-source).

When there is an [active parser](#403.html_active-parser) in the [`frame`](#403.html_frame), and when anything in the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) is [delaying the load event](#403.html_delay-the-load-event) of the [`frame`](#403.html_frame)'s [browsing context](#403.html_browsing-context)'s [active document](#403.html_active-document), the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) must [delay the load event](#403.html_delay-the-load-event) of its document.

When the browsing context is created, if a `name` attribute is present, the [browsing context name](#403.html_browsing-context-name) must be set to the value of this attribute; otherwise, the [browsing context name](#403.html_browsing-context-name) must be set to the empty string.

Whenever the `name` attribute is set, the nested [browsing context](#403.html_browsing-context)'s [name](#403.html_browsing-context-name) must be changed to the new value. If the attribute is removed, the [browsing context name](#403.html_browsing-context-name) must be set to the empty string.

The [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element must implement the [`HTMLFrameElement`](#403.html_htmlframeelement) interface.

```
interface HTMLFrameElement : HTMLElement {
           attribute DOMString name;
           attribute DOMString scrolling;
           attribute DOMString src;
           attribute DOMString frameBorder;
           attribute DOMString longDesc;
           attribute boolean noResize;
  readonly attribute Document? contentDocument;
  readonly attribute WindowProxy? contentWindow;

  [TreatNullAs=EmptyString] attribute DOMString marginHeight;
  [TreatNullAs=EmptyString] attribute DOMString marginWidth;
};
```

The <dfn id="403.html_dom-frame-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-frame-name">`name`</dfn>, <dfn id="403.html_dom-frame-scrolling" data-anolis-xref="dom-frame-scrolling">`scrolling`</dfn>, and <dfn id="403.html_dom-frame-src" data-anolis-xref="dom-frame-src">`src`</dfn> IDL attributes of the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element must [reflect](#403.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name. For the purposes of reflection, the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element's `src` content attribute is defined as containing a URL.

The <dfn id="403.html_dom-frame-frameborder" data-anolis-xref="dom-frame-frameBorder">`frameBorder`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element must [reflect](#403.html_reflect) the element's `frameborder` content attribute.

The <dfn id="403.html_dom-frame-longdesc" data-anolis-xref="dom-frame-longDesc">`longDesc`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element must [reflect](#403.html_reflect) the element's `longdesc` content attribute, which for the purposes of reflection is defined as containing a URL.

The <dfn id="403.html_dom-frame-noresize" data-anolis-xref="dom-frame-noResize">`noResize`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element must [reflect](#403.html_reflect) the element's `noresize` content attribute.

The <dfn id="403.html_dom-frame-contentdocument" data-anolis-xref="dom-frame-contentDocument">`contentDocument`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element must return the [`Document`](#403.html_document) object of the [active document](#403.html_active-document) of the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element's [nested browsing context](#403.html_nested-browsing-context), if any and if its [effective script origin](#403.html_effective-script-origin) is the [same origin](#403.html_same-origin) as the [effective script origin](#403.html_effective-script-origin) specified by the [incumbent settings object](#403.html_incumbent-settings-object), or null otherwise.

The <dfn id="403.html_dom-frame-contentwindow" data-anolis-xref="dom-frame-contentWindow">`contentWindow`</dfn> IDL attribute must return the [`WindowProxy`](#403.html_windowproxy) object of the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element's [nested browsing context](#403.html_nested-browsing-context).

The <dfn id="403.html_dom-frame-marginheight" data-anolis-xref="dom-frame-marginHeight">`marginHeight`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element must [reflect](#403.html_reflect) the element's `marginheight` content attribute.

The <dfn id="403.html_dom-frame-marginwidth" data-anolis-xref="dom-frame-marginWidth">`marginWidth`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`frame`](#403.html_frame) element must [reflect](#403.html_reflect) the element's `marginwidth` content attribute.

#### 11.3.4 Other elements, attributes and APIs

User agents must treat [`acronym`](#404.html_acronym) elements in a manner equivalent to [`abbr`](#404.html_the-abbr-element) elements in terms of semantics and for purposes of rendering.

```
partial interface HTMLAnchorElement {

           attribute DOMString charset;
           attribute DOMString name;
           attribute DOMString shape;
};
```

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-a-coords" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-coords">`coords`</dfn>, <dfn id="404.html_dom-a-charset" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-charset">`charset`</dfn>, <dfn id="404.html_dom-a-name" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-name">`name`</dfn>, and <dfn id="404.html_dom-a-shape" data-anolis-xref="dom-a-shape">`shape`</dfn> IDL attributes of the [`a`](#404.html_the-a-element) element must [reflect](#404.html_reflect) the respective content attributes of the same name.

```
};
```

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-area-nohref" data-anolis-xref="dom-area-noHref">`noHref`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`area`](#404.html_the-area-element) element must [reflect](#404.html_reflect) the element's [`nohref`](#404.html_attr-area-nohref) content attribute.

* * *

```
partial interface HTMLBodyElement {
```

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-body-text" data-anolis-xref="dom-body-text">`text`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`body`](#404.html_the-body-element) element must [reflect](#404.html_reflect) the element's [`text`](#404.html_attr-body-text) content attribute.

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-body-link" data-anolis-xref="dom-body-link">`link`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`body`](#404.html_the-body-element) element must [reflect](#404.html_reflect) the element's [`link`](#404.html_attr-body-link) content attribute.

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-body-alink" data-anolis-xref="dom-body-aLink">`aLink`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`body`](#404.html_the-body-element) element must [reflect](#404.html_reflect) the element's [`alink`](#404.html_attr-body-alink) content attribute.

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-body-vlink" data-anolis-xref="dom-body-vLink">`vLink`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`body`](#404.html_the-body-element) element must [reflect](#404.html_reflect) the element's [`vlink`](#404.html_attr-body-vlink) content attribute.

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-body-bgcolor" data-anolis-xref="dom-body-bgColor">`bgColor`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`body`](#404.html_the-body-element) element must [reflect](#404.html_reflect) the element's [`bgcolor`](#404.html_attr-body-bgcolor) content attribute.

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-body-background" data-anolis-xref="dom-body-background">`background`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`body`](#404.html_the-body-element) element must [reflect](#404.html_reflect) the element's [`background`](#404.html_attr-background) content attribute. (The [`background`](#404.html_attr-background) content is *not* defined to contain a URL, despite rules regarding its handling in the rendering section above.)

* * *

```

};
```

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-br-clear" data-anolis-xref="dom-br-clear">`clear`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`br`](#404.html_the-br-element) element must [reflect](#404.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

```
partial interface HTMLMetaElement {
           attribute DOMString scheme;
};
```

User agents may treat the [`scheme`](#404.html_attr-meta-scheme) content attribute on the [`meta`](#404.html_the-meta-element) element as an extension of the element's [`name`](#404.html_attr-meta-name) content attribute when processing a [`meta`](#404.html_the-meta-element) element with a [`name`](#404.html_attr-meta-name) attribute whose value is one that the user agent recognizes as supporting the [`scheme`](#404.html_attr-meta-scheme) attribute.

User agents are encouraged to ignore the [`scheme`](#404.html_attr-meta-scheme) attribute and instead process the value given to the metadata name as if it had been specified for each expected value of the [`scheme`](#404.html_attr-meta-scheme) attribute.

For example, if the user agent acts on [`meta`](#404.html_the-meta-element) elements with [`name`](#404.html_attr-meta-name) attributes having the value "eGMS.subject.keyword", and knows that the [`scheme`](#404.html_attr-meta-scheme) attribute is used with this metadata name, then it could take the [`scheme`](#404.html_attr-meta-scheme) attribute into account, acting as if it was an extension of the [`name`](#404.html_attr-meta-name) attribute. Thus the following two [`meta`](#404.html_the-meta-element) elements could be treated as two elements giving values for two different metadata names, one consisting of a combination of "eGMS.subject.keyword" and "LGCL", and the other consisting of a combination of "eGMS.subject.keyword" and "ORLY":

```
<!-- this markup is invalid -->
<meta name="eGMS.subject.keyword" scheme="LGCL" content="Abandoned vehicles">
<meta name="eGMS.subject.keyword" scheme="ORLY" content="Mah car: kthxbye">
```

The suggested processing of this markup, however, would be equivalent to the following:

```
<meta name="eGMS.subject.keyword" content="Abandoned vehicles">
<meta name="eGMS.subject.keyword" content="Mah car: kthxbye">
```

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-meta-scheme" data-anolis-xref="dom-meta-scheme">`scheme`</dfn> IDL attribute of the [`meta`](#404.html_the-meta-element) element must [reflect](#404.html_reflect) the content attribute of the same name.

| <dfn id="404.html_dom-document-vlinkcolor" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-vlinkColor">`vlinkColor`</dfn> | [`vlink`](#404.html_attr-body-vlink) |
| <dfn id="404.html_dom-document-alinkcolor" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-alinkColor">`alinkColor`</dfn> | [`alink`](#404.html_attr-body-alink) |
| <dfn id="404.html_dom-document-bgcolor" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-bgColor">`bgColor`</dfn> | [`bgcolor`](#404.html_attr-body-bgcolor) |

* * *

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-document-anchors" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-anchors">`anchors`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#404.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#404.html_document) node, whose filter matches only [`a`](#404.html_the-a-element) elements with [`name`](#404.html_attr-a-name) attributes.

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-document-applets" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-applets">`applets`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](#404.html_htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#404.html_document) node, whose filter matches only [`applet`](#404.html_the-applet-element) elements.

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-document-clear" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-clear">`clear()`</dfn>, <dfn id="404.html_dom-document-captureevents" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-captureEvents">`captureEvents()`</dfn>, and <dfn id="404.html_dom-document-releaseevents" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-releaseEvents">`releaseEvents()`</dfn> methods must do nothing.

* * *

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-document-all" data-anolis-xref="dom-document-all">`all`</dfn> attribute must return an [`HTMLAllCollection`](#404.html_htmlallcollection-0) rooted at the [`Document`](#404.html_document) node, whose filter matches all elements.

The object returned for [`all`](#404.html_dom-document-all) has several unusual behaviors:

*   The user agent must act as if the ToBoolean() operator in JavaScript converts the object returned for [`all`](#404.html_dom-document-all) to the false value.

*   The user agent must act as if, for the purposes of the `==` and `!=` operators in JavaScript, the object returned for [`all`](#404.html_dom-document-all) compares as equal to the `undefined` and `null` values. (Comparisons using the `===` operator, and comparisons to other values such as strings or objects, are unaffected.)

*   The user agent must act such that the `typeof` operator in JavaScript returns the string `undefined` when applied to the object returned for [`all`](#404.html_dom-document-all).

These requirements are a [willful violation](#404.html_willful-violation) of the JavaScript specification current at the time of writing (ECMAScript edition 5). The JavaScript specification requires that the ToBoolean() operator convert all objects to the true value, and does not have provisions for objects acting as if they were `undefined` for the purposes of certain operators. This violation is motivated by a desire for compatibility with two classes of legacy content: one that uses the presence of [`document.all`](#404.html_dom-document-all) as a way to detect legacy user agents, and one that only supports those legacy user agents and uses the [`document.all`](#404.html_dom-document-all) object without testing for its presence first. [[ECMA262]](#404.html_refsECMA262)

* * *

```
partial interface Window {
  void captureEvents(long dummy);
  void releaseEvents(long dummy);
};
```

The <dfn id="404.html_dom-window-captureevents" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-captureEvents">`captureEvents()`</dfn> and <dfn id="404.html_dom-window-releaseevents" data-anolis-xref="dom-window-releaseEvents">`releaseEvents()`</dfn> methods must do nothing.

* * *

The [`hgroup`](#404.html_hgroup) element does not have [strong native semantics](#404.html_strong-native-semantics) or [default implicit ARIA semantics](#404.html_default-implicit-aria-semantics). User agents must not implement accessibility layer semantics for the [`hgroup`](#404.html_hgroup) element that obfuscates or modifies the semantics of its children.

## 12 IANA considerations

### 12.1 <dfn>`text/html`</dfn>

This registration has been filed successfully with IANA.

Type name:

text

Subtype name:

html

Required parameters:

No required parameters

Optional parameters:

`charset`

The `charset` parameter may be provided to definitively specify the [document's character encoding](#406.html_document's-character-encoding), overriding any [character encoding declarations](#406.html_character-encoding-declaration) in the document. The parameter's value must be one of the [labels](#406.html_encoding-label) of the [character encoding](#406.html_encoding) used to serialize the file. [[ENCODING]](#406.html_refsENCODING)

Encoding considerations:

8bit (see the section on [character encoding declarations](#406.html_character-encoding-declaration))

Security considerations:

Entire novels have been written about the security considerations that apply to HTML documents. Many are listed in this document, to which the reader is referred for more details. Some general concerns bear mentioning here, however:

HTML is scripted language, and has a large number of APIs (some of which are described in this document). Script can expose the user to potential risks of information leakage, credential leakage, cross-site scripting attacks, cross-site request forgeries, and a host of other problems. While the designs in this specification are intended to be safe if implemented correctly, a full implementation is a massive undertaking and, as with any software, user agents are likely to have security bugs.

Even without scripting, there are specific features in HTML which, for historical reasons, are required for broad compatibility with legacy content but that expose the user to unfortunate security problems. In particular, the [`img`](#406.html_the-img-element) element can be used in conjunction with some other features as a way to effect a port scan from the user's location on the Internet. This can expose local network topologies that the attacker would otherwise not be able to determine.

HTML relies on a compartmentalization scheme sometimes known as the *same-origin policy*. An [origin](#406.html_origin-0) in most cases consists of all the pages served from the same host, on the same port, using the same protocol.

It is critical, therefore, to ensure that any untrusted content that forms part of a site be hosted on a different [origin](#406.html_origin-0) than any sensitive content on that site. Untrusted content can easily spoof any other page on the same origin, read data from that origin, cause scripts in that origin to execute, submit forms to and from that origin even if they are protected from cross-site request forgery attacks by unique tokens, and make use of any third-party resources exposed to or rights granted to that origin.

Interoperability considerations:

Rules for processing both conforming and non-conforming content are defined in the published specification.

Published specification:

[http://www.w3.org/TR/html](http://www.w3.org/TR/html)

Applications that use this media type:

Web browsers, tools for processing Web content, HTML authoring tools, search engines, validators.

Fragment identifier considerations:

Fragment identifiers used with text/html resources either refer to the indicated part of the document or provide state information for in-page scripts. Detailed processing for fragment identifiers is defined in the "Navigating to a fragment identifier" section ([http://www.w3.org/TR/html/browsers.html#scroll-to-fragid](http://www.w3.org/TR/html/browsers.html#scroll-to-fragid)).

Restrictions on usage:

No restrictions apply.

Provisional registration? (standards tree only):

No.

Additional information:

1.  Deprecated alias names for this type: N/A
2.  Magic number(s): No sequence of bytes can uniquely identify an HTML document. More information on detecting HTML documents is available in the MIME Sniffing specification. [[MIMESNIFF]](#406.html_refsMIMESNIFF)
3.  File extension(s): "html" and "htm" are commonly used.
4.  Macintosh file type code: TEXT
5.  Object Identifiers: N/A

Person & email address to contact for further information:

Robin Berjon <robin@berjon.com>

Intended usage:

Common

Author:

Ian Hickson <ian@hixie.ch>

Change controller:

W3C

### 12.2 <dfn>`multipart/x-mixed-replace`</dfn>

Type name:

multipart

Subtype name:

x-mixed-replace

Required parameters:

*   `boundary` (defined in RFC2046) [[RFC2046]](#407.html_refsRFC2046)

Optional parameters:

No optional parameters.

binary

Security considerations:

Subresources of a [`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#407.html_multipart/x-mixed-replace) resource can be of any type, including types with non-trivial security implications such as [`text/html`](#407.html_text/html).

Interoperability considerations:

None.

Published specification:

Rules for processing this type in Web browsers are described in [http://www.w3.org/TR/html/browsers.html#read-multipart-x-mixed-replace](http://www.w3.org/TR/html/browsers.html#read-multipart-x-mixed-replace).

Applications that use this media type:

This type is intended to be used in resources generated by Web servers, for consumption by Web browsers.

Fragment identifier considerations:

Fragment identifiers used with multipart/x-mixed-replace resources apply to each body part as defined by the type used by that body part.

Restrictions on usage:

No restrictions apply.

Provisional registration? (standards tree only):

No.

Additional information:

1.  Deprecated alias names for this type: N/A
2.  Magic number(s): No sequence of bytes can uniquely identify it.
3.  File extension(s): No specific file extensions are recommended for this type.
4.  Macintosh file type code: No specific Macintosh file type codes.

### 12.3 <dfn>`application/xhtml+xml`</dfn>

This registration has been filed successfully with IANA.

Type name:

application

Subtype name:

xhtml+xml

Required parameters:

None.

Optional parameters:

charset

Same as for application/xml. [[RFC7303]](#408.html_refsRFC7303)

profile

Deprecated as the notion of XHTML profiles has been obsoleted in HTML5. See section 8 of RFC 3236 for additional information about how this parameter was defined.

Encoding considerations:

binary

Security considerations:

The considerations for "text/html" as specified in [http://www.w3.org/TR/html](http://www.w3.org/TR/html) and for 'application/xml' as specified in RFC 7303, also hold for 'application/xhtml+xml'. [[RFC7303]](#408.html_refsRFC7303)

Interoperability considerations:

Rules for processing both conforming and non-conforming content are defined in [http://www.w3.org/TR/html](http://www.w3.org/TR/html).

Published specification:

Labeling a resource with the application/xhtml+xml type asserts that the resource is an XML document that likely has a root element from the HTML namespace. Thus, the relevant specifications are the XML specification, the Namespaces in XML specification, and [http://www.w3.org/TR/html](http://www.w3.org/TR/html). [[XML]](#408.html_refsXML) [[XMLNS]](#408.html_refsXMLNS)

Applications that use this media type:

Web browsers, tools for processing Web content, HTML authoring tools, search engines, validators.

Fragment identifier considerations:

Same as for application/xml. [[RFC7303]](#408.html_refsRFC7303)

Restrictions on usage:

No restrictions apply.

No.

2.  Magic number(s): No sequence of bytes can uniquely identify an XHTML document. More information on detecting XHTML documents is available in the MIME Sniffing specification. [[MIMESNIFF]](#408.html_refsMIMESNIFF)
3.  File extension(s): "`xhtml`" and "`xht`" are sometimes used as extensions for XML resources that have a root element from the [HTML namespace](#408.html_html-namespace-0).
4.  Macintosh file type code: TEXT.

### 12.4 <dfn>`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`</dfn>

This registration has been filed successfully with IANA.

Type name:

application

Subtype name:

x-www-form-urlencoded

Required parameters:

No parameters

Optional parameters:

No parameters

Encoding considerations:

7bit

Security considerations:

In isolation, an [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#409.html_application/x-www-form-urlencoded) payload poses no security risks. However, as this type is usually used as part of a form submission, all the risks that apply to HTML forms need to be considered in the context of this type.

These risks fall into multiple categories that pertain to the same-origin policy and cross-origin reach of HTML forms ([http://www.w3.org/TR/cors/#security](http://www.w3.org/TR/cors/#security)), general HTML application threats ([http://www.w3.org/TR/html/single-page.html#writing-secure-applications-with-html](http://www.w3.org/TR/html/single-page.html#writing-secure-applications-with-html)), and not relying on client-side validation for anything other than user feedback ([http://www.w3.org/TR/html/single-page.html#security-forms](http://www.w3.org/TR/html/single-page.html#security-forms)).

Interoperability considerations:

Rules for generating and processing [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#409.html_application/x-www-form-urlencoded) payloads are defined in this specification.

Published specification:

[http://www.w3.org/TR/html](http://www.w3.org/TR/html) is the relevant specification. Algorithms for [encoding](#409.html_application/x-www-form-urlencoded-encoding-algorithm) and [decoding](#409.html_application/x-www-form-urlencoded-decoding-algorithm) are defined.

Applications that use this media type:

Web browsers and servers.

Fragment identifier considerations:

Fragment identifiers have no meaning with the application/x-www-form-urlencoded type.

Restrictions on usage:

This type is only intended to be used to describe HTML form submission payloads.

Provisional registration? (standards tree only):

No.

Additional information:

1.  Deprecated alias names for this type: N/A
2.  Magic number(s): There is no reliable mechanism for recognising such payloads.
3.  File extension(s): N/A
4.  Macintosh file type code: N/A.
5.  Object Identifiers: N/A

Person & email address to contact for further information:

Robin Berjon <robin@berjon.com>

Intended usage:

Common

Ian Hickson <ian@hixie.ch>

W3C

### 12.5 <dfn>`text/cache-manifest`</dfn>

This registration has been filed successfully with IANA.

Type name:

text

Subtype name:

cache-manifest

Required parameters:

No parameters

Optional parameters:

`charset`

The `charset` parameter may be provided. The parameter's value must be "`utf-8`". This parameter serves no purpose; it is only allowed for compatibility with legacy servers.

Encoding considerations:

8bit

Security considerations:

Cache manifests themselves contain no executable content and pose no immediate risk unless sensitive information is included within the manifest.

Implementations however, are required to follow specific rules when populating a cache based on a cache manifest, to ensure that certain origin-based restrictions are honoured. Failure to correctly implement these rules can result in information leakage, cross-site scripting attacks, and the like.

Caching mechanisms are typically subjects of poisoning attacks and the one that this file type supports is no exception. The published specification includes steps intended to mitigate such issues (notably non-malicious cache poisoning from captive portals) but implementers are advised to exercise caution in caching.

Additionally, the permanence of this caching mechanism requires care to be taken with respect to users' privacy ([http://www.w3.org/TR/html/single-page.html#expiring-application-caches](http://www.w3.org/TR/html/single-page.html#expiring-application-caches)) and storage resources ([http://www.w3.org/TR/html/single-page.html#disk-space](http://www.w3.org/TR/html/single-page.html#disk-space)).

Interoperability considerations:

Rules for processing both conforming and non-conforming content are defined in the [HTML specification](http://www.w3.org/TR/html/).

Published specification:

[http://www.w3.org/TR/html/](http://www.w3.org/TR/html/) is the relevant specification.

Applications that use this media type:

Web browsers.

Fragment identifier considerations:

Fragment identifiers have no meaning with the text/cache-manifest type.

Restrictions on usage:

No restrictions apply.

Provisional registration? (standards tree only):

No.

Additional information:

1.  Deprecated alias names for this type: N/A
2.  Magic number(s): "CACHE MANIFEST" followed by [ \t\r\n]
3.  File extension(s): "appcache", "manifest"
4.  Macintosh file type code: No specific Macintosh file type codes are recommended.
5.  Object Identifiers: N/A

Intended usage:

### 12.6 <dfn id="411.html_scheme-web" data-anolis-xref="scheme-web">`web+` scheme prefix</dfn>

This section describes a convention for use with the IANA URI scheme registry. It does not itself register a specific scheme. [[RFC4395]](#411.html_refsRFC4395)

URI scheme name:

Schemes starting with the four characters "`web+`" followed by one or more letters in the range `a`-`z`.

Status:

permanent

URI scheme syntax:

Scheme-specific.

URI scheme semantics:

Scheme-specific.

Encoding considerations:

All "`web+`" schemes should use UTF-8 encodings where relevant.

Applications/protocols that use this URI scheme name:

Scheme-specific.

Interoperability considerations:

The scheme is expected to be used in the context of Web applications.

Security considerations:

Any Web page is able to register a handler for all "`web+`" schemes. As such, these schemes must not be used for features intended to be core platform features (e.g. network transfer protocols like HTTP or FTP). Similarly, such schemes must not store confidential information in their URLs, such as usernames, passwords, personal information, or confidential project names.

Contact:

Ian Hickson <ian@hixie.ch>

Author/Change controller:

Ian Hickson <ian@hixie.ch>

References:

Custom scheme and content handlers, HTML Living Standard: [http://www.whatwg.org/specs/web-apps/current-work/#custom-handlers](#411.html_custom-handlers)

An asterisk (*) in a cell indicates that the actual rules are more complicated than indicated in the table above.

? Categories in the "Parents" column refer to parents that list the given categories in their content model, not to elements that themselves are in those categories. For example, the [`a`](#413.html_the-a-element) element's "Parents" column says "phrasing", so any element whose content model contains the "phrasing" category could be a parent of an [`a`](#413.html_the-a-element) element. Since the "flow" category includes all the "phrasing" elements, that means the [`th`](#413.html_the-th-element) element could be a parent to an [`a`](#413.html_the-a-element) element.

### All Interfaces

*This section is non-normative.*

### Events

*This section is non-normative.*

List of events

| Event | Interface | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `abort` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) when the download was aborted by the user |
| `afterprint` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) after printing |
| `beforeprint` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) before printing |
| `beforeunload` | [`BeforeUnloadEvent`](#419.html_beforeunloadevent) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) when the page is about to be unloaded, in case the page would like to show a warning prompt |
| `blur` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at nodes losing focus |
| `change` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at controls when the user commits a value change |
| [`click`](#419.html_event-click) | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at an element before its [activation behavior](#419.html_activation-behavior) is run |
| `DOMContentLoaded` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at the [`Document`](#419.html_document) once the parser has finished |
| `error` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at elements when network and script errors occur |
| `focus` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at nodes gaining focus |
| [`hashchange`](#419.html_event-hashchange) | [`HashChangeEvent`](#419.html_hashchangeevent) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) when the fragment identifier part of [the document's address](#419.html_the-document's-address) changes |
| `input` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at controls when the user changes the value |
| `invalid` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at controls during form validation if they do not satisfy their constraints |
| `load` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) when the document has finished loading; fired at an element containing a resource (e.g. [`img`](#419.html_the-img-element), [`embed`](#419.html_the-embed-element)) when its resource has finished loading |
| `message` | `MessageEvent` | Fired at an object when the object receives a message |
| [`offline`](#419.html_event-offline) | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) when the network connections fails |
| [`online`](#419.html_event-online) | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) when the network connections returns |
| [`pagehide`](#419.html_event-pagehide) | [`PageTransitionEvent`](#419.html_pagetransitionevent) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) when the page's entry in the [session history](#419.html_session-history) stops being the [current entry](#419.html_current-entry) |
| [`pageshow`](#419.html_event-pageshow) | [`PageTransitionEvent`](#419.html_pagetransitionevent) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) when the page's entry in the [session history](#419.html_session-history) becomes the [current entry](#419.html_current-entry) |
| [`popstate`](#419.html_event-popstate) | [`PopStateEvent`](#419.html_popstateevent) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) when the user navigates the [session history](#419.html_session-history) |
| [`readystatechange`](#419.html_event-readystatechange) | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at the [`Document`](#419.html_document) when it finishes parsing and again when all its subresources have finished loading |
| `reset` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at a [`form`](#419.html_the-form-element) element when it is [reset](#419.html_concept-form-reset) |
| `submit` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at a [`form`](#419.html_the-form-element) element when it is [submitted](#419.html_concept-form-submit) |
| `unload` | [`Event`](#419.html_event) | Fired at the [`Window`](#419.html_window) object when the page is going away |

See also [media element events](#419.html_mediaevents), and [application cache events](#419.html_appcacheevents).

[URL]

**Note:** URLs can be used in numerous different manners, in many differing contexts. For the purpose of producing strict URLs one may wish to consider [[RFC3986]](#420.html_refsRFC3986) [[RFC3987]](#420.html_refsRFC3987). The W3C URL specification defines the term URL, various algorithms for dealing with URLs, and an API for constructing, parsing, and resolving URLs. Developers of Web browsers are advised to keep abreast of the latest URL developments by tracking the progress of [https://url.spec.whatwg.org/](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/). We expect that the W3C URL draft will evolve along the Recommendation track as the community converges on a definition of URL processing.

Most of the URL-related terms used in the HTML specification (**URL**, **[absolute URL](#420.html_absolute-url)**, **[relative URL](#420.html_relative-url)**, **relative schemes**, **scheme component**, **scheme data**, **username**, **password**, **host**, **port**, **path**, **query**, **fragment**, **[percent encode](#420.html_percent-encode)**, **get the base**, and **[UTF-8 percent encode](#420.html_utf-8-percent-encode)**) can be straightforwardly mapped to the terminology of [[RFC3986]](#420.html_refsRFC3986) [[RFC3987]](#420.html_refsRFC3987). The [`URLUtils`](#420.html_urlutils) (formerly known as `URL`) collection of attributes (e.g. `href` and `protocol`) and its required definitions (**[input](#420.html_the-input-element)**, **query encoding**, **url**, **update steps**, **set the input**) are considered common practice nowadays. Some of the URL-related terms are still being refined (e.g. **[URL parser](#420.html_url-parser-0)**, **parse errors**, **URL serializer**, **[default encode set](#420.html_default-encode-set)**, and **[percent decode](#420.html_percent-decode)**).

As a word of caution, there are notable differences in the manner in which Web browsers and other software stacks outside the HTML context handle URLs. While no changes would be accepted to URL processing that would break existing Web content, some important parts of URL processing should therefore be considered as implementation-defined (e.g. parsing file: URLs or operating on URLs that would be syntax errors under the [[RFC3986]](#420.html_refsRFC3986) [[RFC3987]](#420.html_refsRFC3987) syntax).

[URL](http://www.w3.org/TR/url/) (URL: [http://www.w3.org/TR/url/](http://www.w3.org/TR/url/)), E. Arvidsson, M.[tm] Smith. W3C.

Thanks also to everyone who has ever posted about HTML to their blogs, public mailing lists, or forums, including all the contributors to the [various W3C HTML WG lists](http://www.w3.org/html/wg/lists/) and the [various WHATWG lists](http://www.whatwg.org/mailing-list).

Special thanks to Richard Williamson for creating the first implementation of [`canvas`](#421.html_the-canvas-element) in Safari, from which the canvas feature was designed.

Special thanks also to the Microsoft employees who first implemented [`contenteditable`](#421.html_attr-contenteditable) and other features first widely deployed by the Windows Internet Explorer browser.

Special thanks and $10,000 to David Hyatt who came up with a broken implementation of the [adoption agency algorithm](#421.html_adoptionAgency) that the editor had to reverse engineer and fix before using it in the parsing section.

Thanks to the many sources that provided inspiration for the examples used in the specification.

The image of two cute kittens in a basket used in the context menu example is based on [a photo](http://www.flickr.com/photos/digidreamgrafix/8370087640/) by [Alex G](http://www.flickr.com/photos/digidreamgrafix/). ([CC BY 2.0](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/))

The Blue Robot Player sprite used in the canvas demo is based on [a work](http://johncolburn.deviantart.com/art/Blue-Robot-Player-Sprite-323813997) by [JohnColburn](http://johncolburn.deviantart.com/). ([CC BY-SA 3.0](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/))

Thanks also to the Microsoft blogging community for some ideas, to the attendees of the W3C Workshop on Web Applications and Compound Documents for inspiration, to the #mrt crew, the #mrt.no crew, and the #whatwg crew, and to Pillar and Hedral for their ideas and support.
